Ego te triumphare fecit de inimico tuo, & tu de plebe meodas meis inimicis triumphum. Nonne propterea Maximus destiturus est, quia ante ipsos expeditionis dies cum audisset Romae Synagogam incensam, edictum Romanum miserat quasi vindex disciplinae publicae? Unde populus Christianus ait: Nihil boni huic imminet. Rex iste Iudaeus factus est: defensorem istum disciplinae audiuimus, quem mox Christus probauit, qui pro peccatoribus mortuus est. Si de sermone hoc dictum est, quid de vltione dicetur? Hic leigitur statim a Francis, a Saxonum gente, in Sicilia, Siciae, Batauione, vbique denique terrarum victus est. Quid pio commune cum perfido? Abolenda cum impio sunt etiam impietatis exempla. Quod ille nocuit, & quo victus offendit, hoc non sequidebet, sed damnare qui vicit. Itaque illa tibi non quasi ingrato recensui, sed quasi iure collata enumeraui, ut his admonitus cui plus collatum est, plus diligas.
units.tr: And what will Christ say to you hereafter? Do you not remember what David was commanded by the prophet Nathan, from the same God? "I chose you from among your brothers, a lesser one, and made you emperor over the first of nations. I placed one of the fruit of your seed upon the imperial throne. I subjected the barbarian nations to you, I gave you peace, I brought your enemy captive into your power. You had no grain for the feeding of your armies; by the hand of your enemies themselves I opened the gates for you, I unlocked the granaries; your enemies gave you the supplies they had prepared for themselves. I confounded the plans of your enemy so that he would strip himself bare. I bound the usurper of the empire himself and tied up his mind, so that although he still had the chance to flee, yet, as if fearing that someone might perish from you, he shut himself in with all his men. I gathered together for the completion of your victory his count and his army from the other side of nature, whom I had earlier scattered lest they join together in alliance of war. And your army, drawn from many untamed nations of foreigners, I ordered to keep the faith, the peace and the harmony of a single people. When the greatest danger was that the faithless counsels of the barbarians would penetrate the Alps, I bestowed victory upon you within the very rampart of the Alps, so that you might conquer without loss. I made you triumph over your enemy, and you have given triumph to my enemies from the people of mine." Was it not for this reason that Maximus was going to desist? For on the very days before his expedition, when he had heard that the Synagogue at Rome had been burned, he had sent a Roman edict as if he were the avenger of public discipline. Whence the Christian people said: "Nothing good threatens this man. The king has become a Jew. We have heard of a defender of discipline who was soon condemned by Christ, who died for sinners." If this was said of that speech, what will be said of the vengeance? He was conquered at once by the Franks, by the Saxon people, in Sicily, at Siscia, at Batavia, in short, everywhere on earth. What has the pious in common with the faithless? The examples of impiety must also be abolished along with the impious. What harmed him, and by which he was defeated, that ought not to be followed, but the one who conquered ought to be condemned. Therefore I have not recited those benefits to you as to an ungrateful man, but have listed them as conferred by right, so that, reminded by these things, you may love more the one to whom more has been given.

units.la: Denique hoc respondenti Simoni dixit Dominus Iesus: Recte iudicasti. Statimque conuersus ad mulierem quae pedes eius vnguento vnxit, typum Ecclesiae gerens, ait Simoni: Propter quod dico tibi: Remissa sunt peccata eius multa, quoniam dilexit multum. Cui autem minus dimittitur, minus diligit. Haec est mulier quae domum Pharisaei intrauit, & eiecit Iudaeum, Christum acquisiuit. Ecclesia enim Synagogam exclusit. Cur iterum tentatur vt apud Christi famulum, hoc est de pectore fidei, de domo Christi Synagoga excludat Ecclesiam? Haec ego Imperator amore & studio tui in hunc sermonem contuli.
units.tr: Finally, to Simon's answer the Lord Jesus said: "You have judged rightly." And immediately turning to the woman who anointed his feet with ointment, bearing the figure of the Church, he said to Simon: "Therefore I say to you, her many sins are forgiven, because she loved much; but to whom less is forgiven, the same loves less." This is the woman who entered the house of the Pharisee, drove out the Jew, and won Christ. For the Church has shut out the Synagogue. Why is it again attempted, that in the presence of the servant of Christ, that is, from the breast of faith, the Synagogue should shut the Church out of the house of Christ? I have spoken these things to you, Emperor, out of love and zeal for you.

units.la: Debeo enim beneficiis tuis, quibus me petente liberasti plurimos de exiliis, de carceribus, de vltimae necis poenis, vt malle debeam pro salute tua etiam offensionem tui animi non timere, (nemo maiore fiducia vitur, quam qui ex affectu diligit: Nemo certe debet laedere qui sibi consulit,) totannorum conceptam cuiuscunque sacerdotii gratiam vno momento amittam. Et tamen non damnum gratiae deprecor, sed salutis periculum. Quanquam quantum est Imperator, vt quaerendum aut vindicandum non putes, quod in hunc diem nemo vnquam vindicauit? Graue est fidem tuam pro Iudaeis periclitari. Gedeon cum occidisset sacratum vitulum, dixerunt Gentiles: Dii ipsi iniuriam suam vindicent. Quis habet Synagogam vindicare? Christus quem occiderunt, quem negauerunt? An Deus pater vindicabit eos qui nec patrem recipiunt, qui filium non receperunt?
units.tr: For I owe a debt to your kindnesses, by which at my request you have freed many from exile, from prisons, from the penalties of final death; so that I ought to prefer, for the sake of your safety, not to fear even the offence of your mind. (No one trusts with greater confidence than one who loves from affection; certainly no one ought to injure one who looks to his own good.) In a single moment I would lose the favour of whatever priesthood I have held for years. And yet I do not plead for the loss of favour, but for the danger to salvation. Yet how great is it, Emperor, that you do not think it must be inquired into or avenged, something that to this day no one has ever avenged? It is a grave thing that your faith should be imperilled for the sake of the Jews. When Gideon had destroyed the sacred calf, the Gentiles said: "Let the gods themselves avenge their own wrong." Who is to avenge the Synagogue? Christ, whom they killed and denied? Or will God the Father avenge those who do not receive the Father, who did not receive the Son? Who is to have the heresy of the Valentinians avenged? How does your piety avenge it, when it has ordered them to be shut out and not allowed to gain the opportunity of meeting together? If I set before you Josiah, a king approved by God, you will condemn in those people what was approved in him. Surely, if too little trust is placed in me...

units.la: Quis habet Valentinianorum haeresim vindicari? quam pietas tua quomodo vindicat, cum eos excludi iusserit, nec conueniendi vsurpare copiam? Si Iosiam tibi obiiciam regem Deo probatum, hoc in istis damnabis quod in illo probatum est. Certe si mihi parum fidei defertur, iube adesse quos putaueris episcopos, tractetur Imperator quid salua fide agi debeat. Si de causis pecuniariis comitem tuos consulis, quanto magis in causa religionis Sacerdotes Domini aequum est consulas? Consideret clementia tua quantas insidiatores habeat Ecclesia, quantos exploratores. Leuem rimam si offenderint, figent aculeum. Secundum homines loquor. Caeterum plus hominibus Deus timetur, qui etiam Imperatoribus iure praefertur. Si amico suo aliquis, si parenti aut propinquo deferendum existimat, recte ego & deferendum Deo, & eum praeferendum omnibus iudicaui.
units.tr: Who would claim that the heresy of the Valentinians should be avenged? How does your piety avenge it, when you have ordered them to be shut out and have not taken up the opportunity to meet with them? If I set before you King Josiah, who was approved by God, you will condemn in these men what was approved in him. Certainly, if you give me too little credence, command the bishops you think fit to be present, and let the Emperor be instructed on what ought to be done while the faith is kept safe. If you consult your counts about financial matters, how much more fitting is it that you consult the priests of the Lord in a matter of religion? Let your clemency consider how many ambushers and how many spies the Church has. If they find a small crack, they will drive in the sting. I speak in human terms. Yet God is to be feared more than men, and by right He is preferred even to emperors. If anyone thinks that he must give way to a friend, or to a parent or relative, I have rightly judged that one must give way to God and prefer Him to all.

units.la: Consule tibi Imperator, aut patere me consulere mihi. Quid respondebo postea si compertum fuerit datas hinc aut bonitate aliquos Christianorum aut gladio, aut fustibus, aut plumbis necato? Quomodo hoc purgabo factum? Quomodo excusabo apud episcopos? qui nunc quia per triginta & innumeros annos presbyteri quidam gradu functi, vel ministri Ecclesiae retrahuntur a munere sacro, & eur iae deputantur, graviter gemunt. Nam cum ii qui vobis militant, certo militiae tempore seruentur, quanto magis etiam nos considerare debetis, qui Deo militant? Quomodo, inquam, hoc excusabo apud episcopos, qui queruntur de clericis, & impressione graui vastari scribunt ecclesias? Hoc tamen in noticiam clementiae tuae peruenire volui, de hoc vt placet arbitrio tuo consulere, & temperare dignaberis. Illud autem quod me angit, & iure angit, excludeatque eiice: Ipse facis quicquid fieri iussisti. Aut si ille facturus non est, malo te magis esse clementem, quam illum non fecisse quod iussus est. Habes in quibus Domini adhuc debes circa imperium Romanum inuitare clementiam, habes quibus amplius quam tibi speres. Illorum gratia, illorum salus te in hoc sermone conueniat, ne causam tuam alieno committas iudicio. Integra adhuc tibi sunt omnia. In hoc me ego Deo nostro prote obligo, nec verearis sacramentum. Nunquid Deo displicere poterit, quod pro eius emendatur honoris ticentia? Nihil mutaueris certe in illa epistola, sive missa, sive nondum missa est: dictari iube aliam, quae plena fidei, plena pietatis sit. Tibi integrum sit emendare, mihi non est integrum dissimulare. Antiochenis tuam donasti iniuriam, inimici tui filias reuocasti, nutriendas apud affinem dedisti matri hostis tui, misisti de aerario tuo sumptus. Haec tanta pietas, tanta erga Deum fides fidei hoc facto obfuscabitur? Tu igitur qui armatis pepercisti hostibus, & seruasti inimicos tuos, ne quæso tanto studio putes vindicandum in Christianos. Nunc Imperator rogo vt non aspernanter acceperis me, & pro te & pro me timentem. Sancti enim vox est: Vt quid factus sum videre contritionem populi mei, vt offendam incurram Dei? Ego certe quod honorificentius fieri potuit, feci: vt me magis audires in regia, ne si necesse esset, audires in Ecclesia.
units.tr: Take counsel for yourself, Emperor, or allow me to take counsel for myself. What will I answer afterwards if it is discovered that some of the Christians have been put to death from here, whether by the sword, by clubs, or by lead weights? How will I clear this deed? How will I excuse it before the bishops, who now groan heavily because certain men who have served as elders for thirty and countless years, or ministers of the Church, are being drawn away from their sacred office and handed over to the workhouse? For since those who serve you as soldiers are kept to a fixed term of service, how much more must you consider us, who serve God? How, I say, will I excuse this before the bishops, who complain about the clergy and write that the churches are being laid waste by a heavy assault? Nevertheless, I wished this to come to the notice of your clemency, so that you may consult on it as your judgment pleases and deign to moderate it. But that which troubles me, and rightly troubles me, you should both reject and cast out: you yourself do whatever you have ordered to be done. Or if he is not going to do it, I prefer that you be more merciful than that he should not have done what he was ordered to do. You have, in the matter of the Roman empire, those for whom you ought still to invoke the Lord's clemency; you have those for whom you may hope for more than yourself. Let the grace of these people and their salvation meet you in this discourse, so that you do not entrust your cause to another's judgment. All things are still whole for you. In this I bind myself to our God, and I, for my part, bind myself by a solemn pledge in His name; do not fear the oath. Can what is done for the sake of the honour of God displease God? Certainly you have altered nothing in that letter, whether it has been sent or not yet sent: order another to be dictated, one full of faith and full of piety. It is in your power to amend; it is not in my power to keep silent. You remitted the wrong to the Antiochenes, you recalled your enemy's daughters, you gave them to a kinswoman to be brought up, you sent money from your treasury to your enemy's mother. Will this great piety and this great faith toward God be obscured by a single deed? You, therefore, who spared the armed enemy and preserved your foes, do not, I beg, think that the Christians must be avenged with such zeal. Now, Emperor, I ask that you receive me not with scorn, since I fear both for you and for myself. For it is the word of the saint: "How can I bear to see the destruction of my people? How can I, lest I incur the displeasure of God?" I, at least, have done what could be done with greater honour: so that you would hear me in the palace, lest, if it became necessary, you should hear me in the Church.

units.la: EPISTOLA XXX.
units.tr: LETTER XXX.

units.la: Diui Ambrosii ad Valentinianum, eundem rogantis atque conuenientis, ne ad petitionem Gentilium aras eorum Imperatoris decreto instaurari iubeat, ostendentisque ex tali decreto, primum Deo, deinde patri & fratri iniurias irrogari.
units.tr: The letter of St Ambrose to Valentinian, in which he asks and urges him not to order, at the petition of the Gentiles, that their altars be restored by imperial decree, and shows that from such a decree injury is done first to God, then to his father and brother.

units.la: Beatissimo principi & Christianissimo Imperatori Valentiniano. Cum omnes homines qui sub ditione Romana sunt, vobis militent Imperatoribus terrarum atque principibus, tum ipsi vos omnipotenti Deo & sacræ fidei militatis. Aliter enim salus tuta esse non poterit, nisi vnusquisque Deum verum, hoc est Deum Christianorum, à quo cuncta reguntur (ipse enim solus verus est Deus) intima mente veneretur. Dii enim gentium dæmonia, sicut Scriptura dicit. Huic igitur Deo vero quisquis militat, & qui intimo colendum recipit affectu, non dissimulationem, non conuenientiam, sed fidei studium & devotionis impendit. Postremo si non ista, consensum saltem aliquem non debet colendis idolis & prophanis cæremoniarum cultibus exhibere. Nemo enim Deum fallit, cui omnia etiam cordis occulta manifesta sunt. Ergo cum à te Imperator Christianissime fides Deo vero sit exhibenda, cum ipsius fidei studium, cautio atque devotio, miror quomodo aliquibus in spem venerit, quod debeas aras Diis gentium tuo instaurare præcepto, ad vsus quoque sacrificiorum prophanorum præbere sumptum. Quod enim iam dudum vel fisco vel arcæ est vindicatum, de tuo magis conferre videbere, quam de suo reddere. Et de dispendiis queruntur, qui nunquam nostro sanguini pepercerunt, qui ipsa Ecclesiarum ædificia subruerunt. Petunt etiam vt illis priuilegia deferas, qui loquendi & docendi nostris communem vsum Iuliani lege proxima denegarunt: & priuilegia illa quibus sæpe decepti sunt etiam Christiani. Nonnullos enim illis priuilegiis partim per imprudentiam, partim propter publicarum necessitatum molestias declinandas irretire voluerunt, & quia non omnes fortes inueniuntur, etiam sub principibus Christianis plerique sunt lapsi. Sed hæc si iam sublata non essent, auferenda tuo imperio comprobarem. At cum per totum fere orbem à pluribus retro principibus inhibita interdictaque sint, Romæ autem à fratre clementiæ tuæ augustæ memoriæ Gratiano fidei veræ ratione sublata sint, & datis antiquata rescriptis: ne quaso vel fideliter statuta conuellas, vel fraterna præcepta rescindas. De negociis ciuilibus si quid statuitur, nemo putat esse temerandum, & præceptum de religione calcatur? Nullus obrepat iuniori ætati tuæ, siue ille Gentilis est qui ista depoposcit, non debet mentem tuam vinculis suæ superstitionis innectere, sed proprio studio docere & admonere te debet; quemadmodum veræ fidei studere debeas, quando ille tanto motu veri fana defendit.
units.tr: To the most blessed prince and most Christian Emperor Valentinian. Although all men who are under Roman rule serve you as emperors and princes of the earth, you yourself serve almighty God and the sacred faith. For safety cannot be secure unless each man venerates with inner mind the true God, that is, the God of the Christians, by whom all things are governed (for he alone is the true God). The gods of the nations are demons, as Scripture says. Whoever serves this true God, and receives him to be worshipped with inward affection, does not offer dissimulation or compliance, but zeal and devotion of faith. Finally, if not these things, he ought at least not to give any consent to the worship of idols and the profane rites of ceremonies. For no one deceives God, to whom even the hidden thoughts of the heart are manifest. Therefore, since, most Christian Emperor, true faith must be shown to the true God by you, and since zeal, caution and devotion belong to that faith, I wonder how it has come into some men's hope that you should, by your command, restore altars to the gods of the Gentiles and furnish expenses for the uses of profane sacrifices. For what has long since been claimed by the treasury or the chest, you will seem to be contributing from your own resources rather than returning what is someone else's. And they complain about losses, those who never spared our blood, who overthrew the very buildings of the churches. They also ask that you grant privileges to those who, by the law of Julian recently passed, denied our people the common use of speaking and teaching; and privileges by which even Christians have often been deceived. For some they wished to ensnare with those privileges, partly through imprudence, partly to avoid the troubles of public necessities, and because not all are found to be brave, many even under Christian princes have fallen. But if these things had not already been abolished, I would approve that they be removed by your authority. But since they have been forbidden and prohibited throughout almost the whole world by many earlier princes, and at Rome were abolished by your brother of clement memory, Gratian of august memory, on the ground of the true faith, and were annulled by the rescripts issued, I beg you, do not either overturn what has been faithfully established, or rescind the commands of your brother. If something is decreed in civil affairs, no one thinks it should be violated; and will a command concerning religion be trampled underfoot? Let no one creep up on your younger age. Whether he is a Gentile who has demanded these things, he ought not bind your mind with the chains of his superstition, but ought to teach and admonish you by his own zeal, how you ought to be zealous for the true faith, since he defends his false gods with such great eagerness.

units.la: Deferendum meritis clarorum virorum & ego suadeo, sed Deum certum est omnibus præferendum. Si de re militari est consulendum, debet exercitati in præliis viri expectari sententia, consilium comprobari: quando de religione tractatus est, Deum cogita: Nullius iniuria est, cui Deus omnipotens antefertur. Habet ille sententiam suam. Inuitum non cogitis colere quod nolit, hoc idem vobis liceat Imperator, & vnusquisque patienter ferat si non extorqueatur Imperatori, quod moleste ferret, si ei extorquere cuperet Imperator. Ipsis gentilibus displicere consueuit prævaricantis affectus. Libere enim debet defendere vnusquisque fidele mentis suæ & seruare propositum. Quod si aliqui nomine Christiani tale aliquid decernendum putant, mentem tuam vocabula nuda non capiant, nomina cassa non fallant. Quisquis hoc suadet, sacrificat, & quisquis hoc statuit. Tolerabilius tamen est vnius sacrificium, quam lapsus omnium. Totus hic Christianorum periclitatur senatus. Si hodie gentilis aliquis Imperator, quod absit, aram statueret simulacris, & eo conuenire cogeret Christianos, vt sacrificantibus interessent, vt oppleret anhelitus & ora fidelium cinis ex ara, fauilla de sacrilegio, fumus ex busto, & in ea curia sententiam diceret, vbi iurati ad aram simulacri in sententiam cogerentur: (propterea enim interpretantur aram locatam, vt eius sacramento, vt ipsi putant, vnusquisque conuentus consuleret in medium, cum curia maiore iam Christianorum numero sit relicta) persecutionem esse crederet Christianus, qui cogeretur tali optione ad senatum venire: quod fit plerumque nam etiam iniuriis conuenire cogantur. Te ergo Imperatore Christiani in aram iurare cogentur? Quid est iurare, nisi eius, quem testaris fidei tuæ præsulem, diuinam potentiam conf iteri? Te Imperatore hoc petitur & postulatur, vt aram iubeas eleuari, sumptum sacrisiciis prophanis dari? Sed hoc non potest sine sacrilegio decerni. Vnde rogo te ne id decernas, statuas, vel in eius modi decreta subscribas. Conuenio fidem tuam Christi sacerdos. Omnes conuenireMUS episcopi, nisi incredibile hoc & repentinum ad aures peruenisset hominum, quod tale aliquid esset vel in consistorio suggestum tuo, vel à senatu petitum: sed absit vt hoc senatus petiisse dicatur. Pauci Gentiles communi vtuntur nomine. Nam & ante biennium fere cum hoc pe-tere tere tentarent, misit ad me sanctus Damasus Romanæ Ecclesiæ Sacerdos, iudicio Dei electum libellum, quem Christiani senatores dederunt, & quidem innumeri, postulantes nihil se tale mandasse, non congruere Gentilium istiusmodi petitionibus, non præbere consensum, quæsti etiam publice priuatimque se non conuenturos ad curiam, si tale aliquid decerneretur. Dignum est temporibus vestris, hoc est Christianis temporibus, vt dignitas Christianis senatoribus abrogetur, quo Gentilibus senatoribus prophanæ deferatur voluntatis effectus? Hunc libellum ego fratri clementiæ vestræ direxi. Vnde constitit non senatum aliquid de superstitionis impensis mandasse legatis.
units.tr: I too advise that the merits of distinguished men be given weight, but it is certain that God must be placed before all. If counsel is to be taken on a military matter, the opinion of men experienced in battles should be awaited and their advice approved; when the question concerns religion, think of God: no one is wronged when Almighty God is put first. Let him keep his opinion. You do not compel the unwilling to worship what he does not want; let the same be allowed to you, Emperor, and let each man bear it patiently, if nothing be extorted from the Emperor which he would take ill if the Emperor wished to extort it from him. The Gentiles themselves are wont to dislike the feelings of one who betrays. For each man ought freely to defend the faith of his mind and keep his purpose. But if some under the name of Christians think that something of this kind should be decreed, let not bare words capture your mind, let empty names not deceive. Whoever urges this, sacrifices; and whoever decides it, sacrifices. Yet the sacrifice of one man is more bearable than the fall of all. The whole senate of the Christians is in peril here. If today some Gentile emperor, which God forbid, were to set up an altar to images and compel Christians to gather there so that they might attend the sacrifices, so that the breath and mouths of the faithful were filled with ash from the altar, with the spark of sacrilege, with smoke from the burnt offering, and he were to pronounce a sentence in that senate where those sworn at the altar of the image would be compelled to vote (for they explain that the altar was set up for this purpose, so that by its oath, as they think, each assembly should be consulted in the middle, since the greater number of Christians had already been left out of the senate), a Christian would believe it to be persecution if he were compelled to come to the senate under such a choice; which indeed often happens, for they are compelled to assemble even with insults. Under you as Emperor, then, will Christians be compelled to swear at an altar? What is swearing, except to confess the divine power of him whom you call as witness to your faith? Under you as Emperor, is this asked and demanded, that you order an altar to be raised and money to be given for profane sacrifices? But this cannot be decreed without sacrilege. Therefore I beg you not to decree it, nor to establish it, nor to subscribe to decrees of this kind. I approach your faith as a priest of Christ. I would have convened all the bishops, had not this unexpected and incredible report reached men's ears, that something of this sort had been either proposed to your consistory, or sought from the senate. But far be it that the senate is said to have sought this. Only a few Gentiles use the common name. For about two years ago, when they were trying to seek this, the holy Damasus, priest of the Roman Church, sent to me a petition chosen by God's judgment, which Christian senators had given in, and indeed countless ones, asking that they had ordered nothing of the kind, that it did not agree with the petitions of Gentiles of this sort, that they did not give consent, and they declared, both publicly and privately, that they would not come to the senate house if anything of this kind were decreed. Is it fitting in your times, that is, in Christian times, that the dignity of Christian senators be taken away, so that the will of pagan senators be carried out in profane matters? I have sent this petition to your brother of clement memory. From it, it is clear that the senate did not order anything about expenses for superstition to the envoys.

units.la: Sed fortasse dicatur: Cur dudum non interfuerint senatui, cum ista peterentur? Satis loquuntur quid velint, qui non interfuerunt: satis locuti sunt, qui apud Imperatorem locuti sunt. Et miramur tamen, si priuatis resistendi Romæ eripiunt libertatem, qui nolunt esse liberum tibi non iubere quod non probas, non seruare quod non sentis. Et ideo memor legationis proximæ mandatæ mihi, conuenio iterum fidem tuam, conuenio mentem tuam, ne vel respondendum secundum huiusmodi petitionem Gentilium censeas, vel in eiusmodi responsa sacrilegium subscriptionis adiungas. Certe refer ad parentem pietatis tuæ principem Theodosium, quem super omnibus fere maioribus causis consulere consuesti. Nihil maius est religione, nihil sublimius de. Si ciuilis causa esset, diuersæ parti responsio seruaretur. Causa religionis est, Episcopus conuenio. Detur mihi exemplum missæ relationis, vt & ego plenius respondeam, & sic de omnibus consultus clementiæ tuæ parens respondere dignetur. Certe si aliud statuitur, episcopi hoc æquo animo pati & dissimulare non possumus. Licebit tibi ad Ecclesiam conuenire, sed illic non inuenies sacerdotem, aut inuenies resistentem.
units.tr: But perhaps it will be said: Why did they not attend the senate when these things were being sought? Those who were not present speak sufficiently about what they wish; those who spoke before the Emperor have spoken enough. And yet we wonder, if those who do not want you to be free to command what you do not approve, and not to keep what you do not think, take away from private persons at Rome the liberty of resisting. And so, mindful of the recent embassy entrusted to me, I again approach your faith, I approach your mind, lest you think either that a reply should be given according to this petition of the Gentiles, or add the sacrilege of a signature to such replies. Certainly refer the matter to the prince Theodosius, your father of piety, whom you are accustomed to consult on almost all the greater affairs. Nothing is greater than religion, nothing more sublime. If it were a civil matter, a response would be given to the opposing party. It is a matter of religion, and I, a bishop, approach you. Let a copy of the sent report be given to me, so that I may answer more fully, and so that your father of clemency, consulted on all these things, may deign to reply. Certainly, if something else is decided, we bishops cannot bear it and overlook it with an equal mind. You will be free to come to the Church, but there you will not find a priest, or you will find one who resists.

units.la: Quid respondebis sacerdoti dicenti tibi: Munera tua non quærit Ecclesia, quia templa Gentilium muneribus adornasti? Ara Christi dona tua respuit, quoniam aram simulacris fecisti. Vox enim tua, manus tua, & subscriptio tua, opus est tuum. Obsequium tuum Dominus Iesus recusat & respuit, quoniam idolis obsecutus es. Dixit enim tibi: Non potestis duobus Dominis seruire. Priuilegia tua sacratæ Deo Virginis non habent, & vindicant virgines Vestæ? Cur sacerdotes Dei requiris, quibus petitiones prophanas Gentilium prætulisti? Alieni erroris societatem suscipere non possumus. Quid respondebis his verbis? Puerum esse te lapsum? Omnis ætas perfecta Christo est. Omnis Deo plena pueritia fidei comprobatur.
units.tr: What will you reply to the priest who says to you: The Church does not seek your gifts, because you have adorned the temples of the Gentiles with your gifts? Christ's altar rejects your offerings, since you have made an altar to images. For your voice, your hand, and your signature are your work. The Lord Jesus refuses and rejects your compliance, since you have yielded to idols. For he said to you: You cannot serve two masters. Do your privileges not belong to the virgins consecrated to God, and do they claim the Vestal virgins? Why do you seek the priests of God, when you have preferred the profane petitions of the Gentiles to them? We cannot take up fellowship in another's error. What will you reply to these words? That you have fallen as a boy? Every age is perfect to Christ. Every boyhood full of God is proved by faith.

units.la: Paruuli etiam Christum intrepido aduersus persecutores ore confessi sunt. Quid respondebis germano tuo? Nonne tibi dicit: Victum me esse non credidi, quia te Imperatorem reliqui: mori non dolui, quia te heredem habebam: imperio me decedere non ingemui, quia imperia mea, præsertim de religione diuina, omnibus seculis mansura credebam. Hos ego titulos piæ virtutis erexeram, has de seculo manubias, hæc spolia de diabolo, has ego de aduersario omnium exuuias offerebam, in quibus æterna victoria est. Quid mihi plus potuit manus hostis auferre? Abrogasti decreta mea: quod adhuc ille, qui contra me leuauit arma, non fecit. Nunc grauius telum corpore recipio, quod a fratre mea statuta damnantur. Meliore parte mei apud te periclitor. Illa enim mors corporis, ista virtutis est. Nunc mihi abrogatur imperium, & quod est grauius, abrogatur a tuis, abrogatur a meis, & id abrogatur, quod in me etiam mei aduersarii prædicarunt. Si volens acquieuisti, damnasti fidem meam. Si inuitus cessisti, prodidisti tuam. Ergo, quod grauius est, & in te periclitor.
units.tr: Even small children confessed Christ with a fearless voice before their persecutors. What will you answer your brother? Does he not say to you: "I did not believe I had been defeated, because I left you as emperor; I did not grieve at dying, because I had you as my heir; I did not lament leaving the throne, because I believed my empire, especially concerning the divine religion, would last for all ages. These were the titles of holy virtue that I had raised up, these the spoils from the world, these the trophies from the devil, these the booty taken from the adversary of all, in which lies eternal victory. What more could the hand of an enemy take from me? You have annulled my decrees, which even he who raised arms against me has not done. Now I receive a more grievous wound than in my body, in that my statutes are condemned by my brother. I am in danger in the better part of me before you. For that death was of the body, but this is of virtue. Now my rule is revoked, and what is more grievous, it is revoked by your people, revoked by mine, and what is revoked is what even my adversaries praised in me. If you consented willingly, you condemned my faith. If you yielded unwillingly, you betrayed your own. Therefore, what is more grievous, I am in danger in you as well."

units.la: Quid respondebis etiam patri? qui te maiore dolore conueniet, dicens: De me fili pessime iudicasti, qui putasti quod ego Gentilibus conuenientiam præstitissem. Nemo ad me detulit aram esse in illa Romana curia, nunquam tantum nefas credidi, quod in communi illo Christianorum Gentiliumque concilio sacrificarent Gentiles, hoc est, insultarent Gentiles præsentibus Christianis, & inuiti Christiani interesse sacrificiis cogerentur. Multa & diuersa crimina me imperante commissa sunt, vltus sum quæcunque sunt deprehensa: si quis tunc latuit, debet ergo dicere me probasse, quod ad me nemo detulerat? De me pessime iudicasti, si mihi superstitio aliena, non fides mea seruauit imperium. Vnde cum aduertas Imperator, Deo primum, deinde Patri & fratri iniurias irrogari, si quid tale decernas, peto vt id facias, quod salutis tuæ apud Deum intelligis profuturum.
units.tr: What will you answer also your father? He will meet you with still greater grief, saying: "You judged me very badly, son, when you thought I had made a concession to the Gentiles. No one reported to me that there was an altar in that Roman court; I never believed such a great wickedness, that in that common council of Christians and Gentiles the Gentiles would sacrifice, that is, that the Gentiles would insult the Christians present, and that Christians, unwilling, would be forced to take part in the sacrifices. Many and various crimes were committed in my reign; I punished whatever was discovered. If anyone then lay hidden, must it therefore be said that I approved what no one had reported to me? You judged me very badly, if it was another's superstition, not my faith, that preserved my empire. Therefore, since you perceive, Emperor, that wrongs are being inflicted first on God, then on your father and brother, if you decree anything of this kind, I ask that you do what you understand will profit your salvation before God."

units.la: EPISTOLA XXXII.
units.tr: Letter 32.

units.la: Diui Ambrosii ad Valentinianum Imperatorem, recusantis certare cum Auxentio Arriano in consistorio Imperatore iudicaturo, ex eo quod in causa fidei Episcopi de laicis in Ecclesia, & non laici de Episcopis in consistorio decebant iudicare.
units.tr: Of Saint Ambrose to the Emperor Valentinian, refusing to contend with Auxentius the Arian before the Emperor sitting in consistory as judge, on the ground that in matters of faith bishops ought to judge laymen in the Church, and laymen ought not to judge bishops in the consistory.

units.la: Clementissimo Imperatori & beatissimo Augusto Valentiniano Ambrosius Episcopus. Dalmatius me tribunus & notarius mandato, vt allegauit, clementiæ conuenit tuæ, postulans vt & ipse iudices legerem, sicut elegisset Auxentius. Nec tamen expressit eorum nomina, qui fuerunt postulati: sed id addidit, quod in consistorio esset futura certatio, arbitrio pietatis iudicio tuæ. Cui rei respondeo, vt arbitror, competenter. Nec quisquam contumacem iudicare nu debet, hoc cum asseram, quod augustæ memoriæ Pater tuus non solum sermone respondit, sed etiam legibus suis sanxit, in causa fidei vel Ecclesiastici alicuius ordinis cum iudicare debere, qui nec munere impar sit, nec iure dissimilis: Hæc enim verba rescripti sunt: hoc est, sacerdotes de sacerdotibus voluit iudicare.
units.tr: To the most merciful Emperor and most blessed Augustus Valentinian, Ambrose, bishop. Dalmatius the tribune and notary came to me with a mandate, as he alleged, from your clemency, demanding that I should read out the judges as Auxentius had chosen them. He did not, however, name those who had been proposed, but added that the contest would take place in the consistory at the discretion of your piety's judgment. To this I reply, as I think, appropriately. Nor ought anyone to judge a man who is refusing to answer, since I maintain this: your father of august memory not only declared in words but also enacted in his laws that in a case of faith, or of some ecclesiastical order, a judge ought to be one who is neither unequal in office nor dissimilar in rank. For these were the words of the rescript; that is, he wished priests to judge priests.

units.la: Quin etiam si alias quoque argueretur Episcopus, & morum esset examinanda causa, etiam hanc voluit ad episcopale iudicium pertinere. Quis igitur contumaciter respondit clementiæ tuæ? Ille qui te patri similem esse desiderat, an qui vult esse dissimilem? Nisi forte viis quibusdam tanti Imperatoris existimatur sententia, cuius & fides confessionis constantia comprobata est, & sapientia melioratæ reipublicæ profectibus prædicatur. Quando audisti, clementissime Imperator, in causa fidei laicos de Episcopo iudicasse? Ita ergo quadam adulatione curuamur, vt sacerdotalis iuris simus immemores, & quod Deus donauit mihi, hoc ipse aliis putem esse credendum? Si docendus est Episcopus a laico, quid sequetur? Laicus ergo disputet, & Episcopus audiat, Episcopus discatà laico. At certe si vel Scripturarum seriem diuinarum, vel vetera tempora retractemus, quis est qui abnuat in causa fidei, in causa inquam, fidei Episcopos solere de Imperatoribus Christianis, non Imperatores de Episcopis iudicare? Eris Deo fauente etiam senectutis maturitate prouectior, & tunc de hoc censebis, qualis ille Episcopus sit, qui laicis ius sacerdotale substernit. Pater tuus Deo fauente vir maturioris ætui dicebat: Non est meum iudicare inter Episcopos, tua nunc dicit clementia, Ego debeo iudicare? Et ille baptizatus in Christo inhabilem se ponderi tanti putabat esse iudicii: Clementia tua, cui adhuc emerenda Baptismatis sacramenta seruantur, arrogat de fide iudicium, cum fidei ipsius sacramenta non nouerit? Quales autem elegerit iudices, possumus existimationi relinquere, quando eorum nomina timet prodere. Veniant plane, si qui sunt ad Ecclesiam, audiant cum populo: non vt quisquam iudex resideat, sed vnusquisque de suo affectu habeat examen, eligat quem sequatur. Agitur de istius Ecclesiæ sacerdote: Si audierit illum populus, & putauerit melius disputare, sequatur fidem eius: non inuidebo. Omitto, quia iam ipse populus vindicabit: taceo, quia eum quem habet, de patre tuæ clementiæ postulauit: taceo, quia patet pietatis tuæ quietem futuram spospondit, si electus susciperet sacerdotium. Hanc fidem secutus sum promissorum.
units.tr: Indeed, even if a bishop were accused on other grounds, and his moral conduct were to be examined, he wished that this too should belong to episcopal judgment. Who, then, has answered your clemency with insolence? He who wishes you to be like your father, or he who wishes you to be unlike him? Unless perhaps by some kind of flattery the opinion of so great an Emperor is thought of little account, whose constancy in confessing the faith has been proved, and whose wisdom is praised for the advancement of the improved commonwealth. When did you ever hear, most merciful Emperor, of laymen judging a bishop in a matter of faith? Are we, then, so bent by a certain flattery that we forget the law of the priesthood, and that what God has given to me I should think ought to be entrusted to others? If a bishop is to be taught by a layman, what will follow? Let the layman dispute and the bishop listen; let the bishop learn from the layman. But surely if we review the sequence of the divine Scriptures or the ancient times, who would deny that in matters of faith, I say, in matters of faith, bishops have customarily judged Christian emperors, and emperors have not judged bishops? God willing, you too will grow more mature with the ripeness of old age, and then you will judge what sort of bishop he is who puts the priestly right beneath laymen. Your father, God favouring, a man of more mature age, used to say: It is not for me to judge between bishops. Does your clemency now say, I ought to judge? And he, baptized in Christ, thought himself unfit to bear the weight of so great a judgment: does your clemency, for whom the sacraments of baptism are still to be earned, claim a judgment about faith, when it has not learned the sacraments of that faith itself? As for the kind of judges he has chosen, we may leave that to public opinion, since he fears to name their names. Let them certainly come, if there are any, to the Church and hear with the people; not that any judge should sit there, but that each man, from his own feeling, should make his own examination and choose whom he will follow. The matter concerns the priest of that Church: if the people hear him and think he argues better, let them follow his faith; I shall not grudge it. I pass over this, because the people themselves will assert their right; I say nothing of the fact that he has demanded the one he has from your clemency's father; I say nothing of the fact that it is clear that he promised quiet for your piety if the chosen man should undertake the priesthood. I have followed this faith of promises.

units.la: Quod si de aliquorum peregrinorum assentatione se iactat, ibi fit Episcopus, vnde sunt ii, qui episcopatus putant nomine esse donandum. Nam ego nec Episcopum noui, nec vnde sit scio. Vbi illud constituimus, Imperator, quod iam ipse tuum iudicium declarasti, imo etiam dedisti leges, ne cui esset liberum aliud iudicare? Quod cum præscripsisti aliis, præscripsisti & tibi. Leges enim Imperator fert, quas primus ipse custodiat. Visne igitur experiar, vt incipiant ii, qui iudices eliguntur, aut aduersus tuam venire sententiam, aut certe excusare, quod Imperatoris tam seuero, & tam districto imperio non potuerint obu-iare? Sed hoc contumacis, non modesti est sacerdotis. Ecce Imperator legem tuam iam ex parte rescindis, sed vtinam non ex parte, sed in vniuersum. Legem enim tuam nollem esse supra Dei legem. Dei lex nos docuit quid sequamur, humanæ leges hoc docere non possunt.
units.tr: But if he boasts of the flattery of some foreigners, then he is a bishop of the place from which those come who think the episcopate ought to be granted by name. For I do not know this bishop, nor do I know where he is from. What have we settled there, Emperor, since you yourself have already declared your judgment, indeed have even issued laws that no one should be free to judge otherwise? What you have prescribed for others, you have prescribed for yourself as well. For an emperor brings laws which he himself should first observe. Do you wish me then to try whether those who are chosen as judges will begin either to act against your sentence, or at least to excuse themselves on the ground that they could not resist the commands of so strict and severe an emperor? But this is the mark of a contumacious priest, not of a modest one. Behold, Emperor, you are now partly rescinding your law; would that you did so not partly but entirely. For I would not want your law to stand above the law of God. The law of God has taught us what to follow; human laws cannot teach this.

units.la: Extorquere solent timidis commutationem, fidem inspirare non possunt. Quis erit igitur ille, qui cum legat per tot prouincias vno momento esse mandatum, vt quicunque obuiauerit Impe-ratori, feriatur gladio: Quicunque Dei templum non tradiderit, protinus occidatur? Quis, inquam, est qui possit vel vnus, vel inter paucos dicere Imperatori, lex tua mihi non probatur. Non permittitur hoc dicere sacerdotibus, permittitur laicis? Et iudicabit de fide, qui aut gratiam sperat, aut metuit offensam? Deinde ipse committam vt eligam iudices laicos, qui cum tenuerint fidei veritatem, aut proscribantur, aut necentur, quod lex de fide lata decernit? E-go igitur aut præuaricationi offeram homines, aut pœnæ? Non tanti est Ambrosius, vt propter se deiiciat Sacerdotium. Non tanti est vnius vita, quanti est dignitas omnium sacerdotum, quorum de consilio ista dictauì, intimantibus ne forte etiam Gentilis esset aliquis aut Iudæus, qui ab Auxentio esset electus, quibus traderemus de Christo triumphum, si de Christo iudicium committeremus. Quid illos aliud, nisi Christi iniuriam audire delectat? Quid illis aliud potest placere nisi (quod absit) vt Christi diuinitas denegetur? Cum iis plane bene conuenit Arriano, qui creaturam Christum dicit, quod etiam Gentiles ac Iudæi promptissime confitentur. Hoc scriptum est in Ariminensi Synodo: meritoque concilium illud exhorreo, sequens tractatum concilii Niceni, à quo me nec mors, nec gladius poterit separare. Quam fidem etiam parens clementiæ tuæ Theodosius beatissimus Imperator & sequitur, & probauit. Hanc fidem Galliæ tenent, hanc Hispaniæ, & cum ipsa diuini Spiritus confessione custodiunt. Si tractandum est, tractare in Ecclesia didici: quod majomaiores fecerunt mei. Si conferendum de fide, Sacerdotum debet esse ista collatio, sicut factum est sub Constantino Augustæ memoriæ Principe, qui nullas leges ante præmisit, sed liberum dedit iudicium sacerdotibus. Factum est etiam sub Constantino Augustæ memoriæ Imperatore paternæ dignitatis hærede. Sed quod bene coepit, aliter consummatum. Nam episcopi sinceram primo scripserant fidem: sed dum volunt quidam de fide intra palatium iudicare, id egerunt, ut circumscriptionibus illa episcoporum iudicia mutarentur. Qui tamen inflexam statim revocauere sententiam. Et certe maior numerus Arimini, Niceni concilii fidem probauit, Arriana decreta damnauit. Si ad Synodum pronocat Auxentius, ut de fide disputet: licet non sit necesse propter unum tot episcopos fatigari, qui etiam si Angelus de coelo esset, paci ecclesiarum non deberet præferri: cum audiero synodum congregari, & ipse non decero. Tolle igitur legem; si vis esse certamen. Venissem Imperator ad consistorium clementiae tuae, ut haec coram suggererem, si me vel episcopi vel populus permisissent, dicentes de fide in ecclesia coram populo debere tractari. Atque utinam Imperator non denunciasset, ut quo vellem pergerem. Quotidie prodibam, nemo me asseruabat. Debuisti me quo volueras destinare, quem ipse omnibus offerebam. Nunc mihi a sacerdotibus dicitur: Non multum interest, utrum velens relinquas, an tradas altare Christi. Cum enim reliqueris, trades. Atque utinam liquido mihi pateret, quod Arrianis ecclesia minima traderetur: Sponte me offerrem tuae pietatis arbitrio. Sed si ego solus instrepo, cur etiam de aliis omnibus inuadendis ecclesiis est præceptum? Utinam confirmetur, ut ecclesiis nullus molestus sit: opto ut de me, qualis videtur, sententia proferatur. Dignanter igitur Imperator accipe, quod ad consistorium venire non potui. Ego in consistorio nisi pro te stare non didici: & intra palatium certare non possum, qui palatii secreta nec quæro, nec noui. Ego Ambrosius Episcopus hunc libellum obtuli clementissimo Imperatori, & beatissimo Augusto Valentiniano.
units.tr: Laws are accustomed to extort a change from the timid; they cannot inspire faith. Who, then, will be the man who, when he reads that throughout so many provinces a command has been issued in a single moment that whoever meets the Emperor shall be struck down with the sword; whoever does not hand over the temple of God shall be put to death at once? Who, I ask, is there who could, alone or among a few, say to the Emperor, "Your law does not please me"? Is this permitted to priests, and permitted to laymen? And will one judge about faith who either hopes for favour or fears offence? Then shall I myself commit the choice of lay judges, who, when they hold to the truth of the faith, are either proscribed or put to death, as the law passed concerning faith decrees? Shall I, then, offer men either to prevarication or to punishment? Ambrose is not so important that the priesthood should be cast down on his account. The life of one man is not worth as much as the dignity of all the priests, on whose counsel I have dictated these things, warning lest perhaps there might be some Gentile or Jew chosen by Auxentius, to whom we would hand over the triumph over Christ if we committed to them the judgment about Christ. What else does it delight them to hear but an insult to Christ? What else can please them but (God forbid) the denial of Christ's divinity? Indeed, Arianism agrees well with them, since it calls Christ a creature, which even Gentiles and Jews most readily confess. This is written in the Synod of Ariminum; and I rightly abhor that council, following the decision of the Council of Nicaea, from which neither death nor the sword will be able to separate me. This faith your clemency's father, the most blessed Emperor Theodosius, also followed and approved. Gaul holds this faith, Spain holds it, and together with it they keep the confession of the divine Spirit. If there is to be a discussion, I have learned to discuss it in the Church, as my elders did. If there is to be a conference about faith, that conference ought to be of priests, as happened under Constantine, the prince of blessed memory, who sent out no laws beforehand but gave the priests free judgment. It also happened under Constantine of blessed memory, the heir of his father's dignity. But what was well begun was finished otherwise. For the bishops had at first written a sound faith; but while certain men wished to judge the faith within the palace, they brought it about by circumventions that those episcopal judgments were changed. Yet these men soon revoked the sentence they had bent. And certainly the greater number at Ariminum approved the faith of the Council of Nicaea and condemned the Arian decrees. If Auxentius appeals to a synod so that he may dispute about faith, although it is not necessary to wear out so many bishops for the sake of one man, who, even if he were an angel from heaven, ought not to be preferred to the peace of the churches, I shall not refuse when I hear that a synod is being assembled. Therefore remove the law, if you wish there to be a contest. I would have come to the consistory of your clemency to put these things before you in person, if the bishops or the people had allowed me, saying that matters of faith ought to be treated in the Church, before the people. And would that the Emperor had not announced that I should go wherever I wished. I would go out every day; no one was keeping me back. You ought to have sent me where you wished, I who offered myself to all. Now I am told by the priests: "It makes little difference whether you give up of your own will or hand over the altar of Christ. For when you have abandoned it, you will hand it over." And would that it were clear to me that the smallest church was being given to the Arians: I would of my own accord offer myself to the judgment of your piety. But if I alone make a noise, why has an order also been given to seize all the other churches? I would that it were confirmed that no one is troubled in the churches; I desire that the sentence be pronounced about me as it seems fit. Therefore, Emperor, graciously accept that I could not come to the consistory. I do not learn to stand in the consistory except on your behalf, and I cannot contend within the palace, I who neither seek nor know the palace's secrets. I, Ambrose, bishop, have offered this little book to the most merciful Emperor and most blessed Augustus Valentinian.

units.la: ORATIO
units.tr: ORATION

units.la: Divi Ambrosii in Auxentium de Basilicis tradendis invehentis, suasque ad constantiam atque tolerantiam exhortantis.
units.tr: Of Saint Ambrose, against Auxentius, concerning the surrender of the basilicas, exhorting them to constancy and endurance.

units.la: VIdeo vos præter solitum subito esse turbatos, atque asseruantes mei Miror quid hoc sit, nisi forte, quia tribunos me vidistis aut audiuistis Imperiali mandato esse conuentum, ut quo vellem abirem hinc, & si qui vellent, sequendi potestatem haberent. Metuistis ergo ne ecclesiam desererem, & damnas saluti meae timeo, vos relinquerem? Sed quid & ipse mandauerim, potuistis auertere: deserendae ecclesiae mihi voluntatem subesse non posse, quia plus Dominum mundi, quam saeculi huius Imperatorem timerem. Sane si me vis aliqua abduceret ab ecclesia, carnem meam exturbari posse non mentem. Paratum me esse ut si ille faceret, quod solet esse regiae potestatis, ego subire quod sacerdotis esse consueuit. Quid ergo turbamini? Volens nunquam vos deleram, coactus repugnare non noui. Dolere potero, potero flere, potero gemere: aduersus arma, milites, Gothos quoque lachrymae meae arma sunt. Talia enim munimenta sunt sacerdotis. Aliter nec debeo, nec possum resistere. Fugere autem & relinquere Ecclesiam non soleo, ne quis grauioris poenae metu factum interpretetur. Scitis & vos ipsi quod Imperatoribus soleam deferre, non credere, supplicii me libenter offerre, nec metuere quae parantur. Vtinam essem securus, quod Ecclesia haereticis minime traderetur: ad palatium Imperatoris irem libenter, si hoc congrueret sacerdotis officio, ut in palatio magis certarem, quam in Ecclesia. Sed in consistorio non reus solet Christus esse, sed iudex. Causam fidei in Ecclesia agendam quis abnuat? Si quis confidit, huc veniat. Inclinatum iam vel Imperatoris iudicium, quod lata lege patefecit, quo impugnat fidem, vel sperata ambientium quorundam studia non requirat. Non committo ut quisquam vendat iniuriam Christi. Circumfusi milites, armorum strepitus, quibus vallata est Ecclesia, fidem non terrent meam, sed mentem exagitant: ne dum metenetis, perniciosum aliquid vestrae oboriatur saluti. Ego enim iam didici non timere, sed vobis timere plus coepi. Sinite quaeso vestrum sacerdotem congredi, habemus aduersarium qui lacessit. Aduersarius enim noster diabolus, sicut leo rugiens circuit quaerens quem devoret, ut Apostolus dixit. Accepit sine dubio, accepit (non fallimur, sed admonemur) tentandi huiusmodi potestatem, ne forte corporis mei vulneribus possim a fidei intentione revocari. Legitis & vos, quia multiplici tentavit sanctam Iob diabolus: ad postremum potestatem huiusmodi petiit & accepit, ut tentaret corpus eius: quod perfudit vulneribus. Cum esset propositum ut ecclesiae vasa iam traderemus, hoc responsi reddidi: Me si de meis aliquid posceretur, aut fundus, aut domus, aut aurum, aut argentum, id quod mei iuris esset, libenter offerre: templo Dei nihil posse decerpere: nec tradere illud, quod custodiendum non tradendum acceperim. Deinde consulere me etiam Imperatoris salutí, quia nec mihi expediret tradere, nec illi accipere. Accipiat enim vocem liberi sacerdotis, si vult sibi esse consultum, recedat a Christi iniuria. Haec plena humilitatis sunt, & (ut arbitror) plena afsectus eius, quem Imperatori debet sacerdos. Sed quia lucta nobis est non solum aduersus carnem & sanguinem, sed etiam (quod gravius est) aduersus spiritualia nequitia, quae sunt in coelestibus, tentator ille diabolus per ministros suos certamen auget, vulneribus corporis mei experiendum arbitratur. Scio fratres vulnera haec, quae pro Christo excipimus, non esse vulnera quibus vita amittitur, sed propagatur. Sinite quaeso esse certamen, spectatores vos esse decet. Considerate quia si quem habet ciuitas tas vel athletam, vel altetius nobilis artis peritum, optat offerre certamini. Cur in maioribus rebus repudiatis, quod vel in minoribus velle consuestis? Non metuit arma, non Barbaros, qui mortem non timet, qui nulla carnis voluptate retinetur. Certe si Dominus huic vos certamini deputauit, frustra peruigiles tot noctibus & diebus custodias exhibetis. Implebitur Christi voluntas. Omnipotens enim noster est Dominus Iesus. hæc est fides nostra, Et ideo quod fieri mandat, implebitur: nec conuenit nos diuinæ obuiare sententiæ. Audistis quod hodie lectum sit: Pullum sibi asinæ Saluator per Apostolos iussit adduci, mandauitque vt si quis resisteret, diceretur: Dominus operam eius desiderat. Quid si & nunc pullum istum asinæ, hoc est, eius animalis quod grauem sarcinam portare consuevit, sicut est humana conditio, cui dicitur: Venite ad me omnes qui laboratis & onerati estis, & ego vos reficiam. tollite iugum meum, quia leue est; quid si, inquam, pullum istum ad se modo iussit adduci, missis Apostolis, illis qui iam exuti corpore incomprehensibilem oculis nostris Angelorum speciem gerunt? Nonne si ab aliquo resistatur, dicent: Dominus operam eius desiderat? Si resistat vel vitæ huius cupiditas, si resistat cor & sanguis, si resistat conuersatio corporalis, quia aliquibus forsitan grati videmur: sed qui vos hic diligit, multo amplius diliget si sinat fieri hostiam Christi: quia dissolui, & cum Christo esse, multo melius, etsi manere in carne, magis necessarium propter vos. Nihil est ergo quod veteamini fratres dilectissimi. Scio enim, quia quicquid passus fuero, pro Christo patiar. Et legi quod eos timere non debeam, qui possunt carnem occidere. Et audiui dicentem: Qui perdiderit animam suam propter me, inueniet eam. Ergo si vult Dominus, certum est quod nullus obsistat. Quod si adhuc nostra differt certamina, quid veremini? Seruum Christi non custodia corporalis, sed Domini prouidentia sepire consueuit. Turbati estis, quia apertas reperistis geminas fores, quas captus oculis quidam dum hospitium proprium repetit, patefecisse memoratur. In quo cognoscite, quod nihil suffragetur humana custodia. Ecce vnus, qui videndi munus amisit, soluit vestra vniuersa munimina, & custodias lusit. Dominus autem misericordiæ suæ custodiam non amisit. Nonne ante biduum, vt meministis, etiam illud repertum est, quod à parte læua Basilicæ ingressus quidam peruius fuit, quem putabitis clausum esse atque munitum? Sepserunt nempe armati Basilicam, explorabant hos atque illos aditus. Cæcitate perfusi sunt, vt quod apertum erat, videre non possent. Itaque per plurimas noctes quod apertum fuerit, non ignoratis. Definite ergo sollicitari: quia hoc erit quod Christus iubet, & hoc esse expedit. Denique exempla vobis legis proferam. Helisæus quærebatur à rege Syriæ, missus erat exercitus qui eum caperet. Circumuallatus erat vndique. Cæpit timere eius seruulus, quia seruulus erat, hoc est; non erat liberæ mentis, & liberæ potestatis. Petiuit aperiri eius oculos sanctus Propheta, & ait: Respice, & vide quanto plures sint pro nobis, quam contra eos. Et respexit, & vidit Angelorum millia. Aduertitis igitur, quod seruulos Christi ii magis custodiant qui non videntur, quam qui videntur. Sed & illi si custodiunt, vestris custodiunt orationibus aduocati. Legistis nempe eos ipsos qui Helisæum quærebant, ingressos esse Samariam ad eum ipsum, quem capere gestiebant, cui non solum non potuerunt nocere, sed ipsius aduersus quem venerant, intercessione seruati sunt. Petrus quoque Apostolus vtriusque rei vobis edit exemplum. Nam vbi eum Herodes quæsiuit & cepit, recepit in carcerem. Non enim recesserat Dei seruulus, sed feteratur timoris ignarus. Orabat pro eo Ecclesia, sed Apostolus in carcere quiescebat, quod est iudicium non timentis. Missus est angelus, qui dormientem excitaret, per quem Petrus productus è carcere, mortem ad tempus euasit. Idem Petrus postea victo Simone cum præcepta Dei populo seminaret, doceret castimoniam, excitauit animos Gentilium: quibus eum quærentibus, Christianæ animæ deprecatæ sunt vt paulisper cederet. Et quamuis esset cupidus passionis, tamen contemplatione populi precantis inflexus est. Rogabatur enim vt ad instituendum & confirmandum populum se reseruare. Quid multa? Nocte muro egredi coepit, & videns sibi in porta Christum occurrere, vrbemque ingredi, ait: Domine, quo vadis? Respondit Christus, Venio Romam iterum crucifigi. Intellexit Petrus ad suam crucem diuinum pertinere responsum. Christus enim non poterat iterum crucifigi, qui carnem passionis susceptæ mortis exterat. Quod enim mortuus est, peccato mortuus est semel: quod autem viuit, viuit Deo. Intellexit ergo Petrus quod iterum Christus crucifigendus esset in seruulo. Itaque sponte remeauit, interrogantibus Christianis respônsum reddidit, statimq; correptus, per crucem suam honorificauit Dominum Iesum. Videtis igitur quod in seruulis suis pati velit Christus. Quid si & huic seruulo dicit: Illum volo sic manere, tu autem me sequere: & de hac arbore gustare vult fructum? Nam si illius cibus erat vt faceret voluntatem patris, idem cibus illius est vt nostris passionibus epuletur? Nonne (vt de ipso Domino sumamus exemplum) quando voluit, passus est: & cum quæreretur, inuentus est? Quando autem hora non venerat passionis, per medium quærentium transibat, & videntes eum tenere non poterant. Quo vtique euidenter ostendit, quia quando Dominus vult, vbi vult, inuenitur & capitur. Quando autem differt, etiam si quærentium manibus occurrat & obstruatur, non tenetur. Ego ipse non quotidie vel visitandi gratia prodibam, vel pergebam ad martyres? Non regiam palatii prætexebam eundo atque redeundo? Et tamen nemo me tenuit, cum exturbanti dimissi haberent, vt prodiderunt postea, voluntatem, dicentes: Exi de ciuitate, & vade quo vis. Expectabam fore magnum aliquid, vt gladium pro Christi nomine, aut incendium. Atrilli delicias mihi pro passionibus obtulerunt: sed athleta Christi non delicias, sed passiones suas exigit. Nemo ergo vos turbet quod aut carcerem præparauerant, aut dura, vt videbatur sibi, Auxentii ipsius qui se dicit Episcopum, ore iactata. Plerique narrabant percussores præmissos, poenam mortis esse decretam: nec illa timeo, & ista non desero. Quo enim abibo, vbi non omnia plena gemitus sint atque lachrymarum, quando per Ecclesias iubentur eiici Catholici sacerdotes, resistentes gladio feriri, curiales proscribi omnes, nisi mandatum impleuerint? Et haec Episcopi manu scripta, & ore dictata: quàse vt probaret doctissimum, vetus non omisit exemplum. Legimus enim in Propheta quod viderit falcem volantem. Hanc imitatus Auxentius gladium volantem per omnes vrbes direxit. Et Satanas transfigurat se in Angelum lucis, & in malum imitatur eius potentiam. Tu Domine Iesu vno momento mundum redemisti, Auxentius vno momento tot populos, quod in ipso est, trucidabat, alios gladio, alios sacrilegio. Meam Basilicam petit cruento ore, sanguinolentis manibus. Cui bene praesens respondit lectio: Peccatori autem dixit Deus: Quare tu enarras iustitias meas? id est, non conuenit paci & furori, non conuenit Christo & Belial. Meministis etiam quod lectum est hodie, Nabuthe sanctum virum possessorem vineae suae interpellatum petitione regia vt vineam suam daret, vbi rex succisis vitibus olus vile sereret, eumq; respondisse: Absit vt ego patrum meorum tradam hereditatem. Regemq, contristatum esse quod sibi esset alienum ius relatione iusta negatum, sed muliebri consilio deceptum Nabuthe, vites suas vel proprio cruore defendisse. Si ille vineam non tradidit suam, nos trademus Ecclesiam Christi? Quid igitur a me responsum est contumaciter? Dixi enim conuentus: Absit a me vt tradam Christi hereditatem. Si ille patrum haereditatem non tradidit, ego tradam Christi haereditatem? Sed & hoc addidi: Absit vt tradam hereditatem patrum, hoc est, haereditatem Dionysii qui in exilio in causa fidei defunctus est, haereditatem Eustorgii confessoris, haereditatem Myrocliis, atq; omnium retro fidelium Episcoporum. Respondi ego quod sacerdotis est: quod Imperatoris est, faciat Imperator. Peius est vt animam mihi quà fidem auferat. At cui tradam? Praesens lectio Euangelii docere nos debet, quid petatur, à quib. petatur. Audistis nempe legi quod cum Christus super pullu asinae sederet, clamabant pueruli, & molestè ferebant Iudaei. Deniq; interpellauerunt Dominum Iesum dicentes vt faceret eos tacere, respondit: Si hi tacebunt, lapides clamabunt. Deinde ingressus templum, eiecit nummularios, & cathedras, & columbas vendentes in templo Dei. Lectio nempe ista nulla nostra dispositione recitata est, sed casu, quae praesentib. bene aptatur temporibus. Semper ergo Christi laudes, verbera pfidorum sunt. Et nunc cum laudatur Christus dicunt haeretici quia seditio commouetur: dicunt haeretici quia his mors paratur, & vere mortem habent in laudibus Christi. Quomodo enim laudes eius ferre possunt, cuius infirmitatem praedicant? Itaq; & hodie cum laudatur Christus, Arrianorum amentia verberatur. Gerasenii praesentiâ Christi ferre nõ poterant, isti peiores Gerasenis nec laudationem Christi sustinere possunt: Vident pueros Christi gloriâ concinentes, quia scriptum est, Ex ore infantium & lactantium perfecisti laudem: Irridենt istam aetatulam fidei plenam, cum dicunt: Ecce quid clamant? sed respondit iis Christus: Si hi tacuerint, lapides clamabunt, hoc est, fortiores clamabunt, clamabunt & iuvenes, clamabunt & maturiores, clamabunt & senes, isti lapides ad illum iam solidati lapidem, de quo scriptum est: lapidem quem reprobauerunt aedificantes, hic factus est in caput anguli. His igitur laudationibus inuitatus templum suum Christus ingreditur, & flagellum prehendit, & eiicit de templo nummularios. Non patitur enim in suo templo pecuniae esse vernaculos, non patitur in suo templo esse eos qui vendant cathedras. Quid sunt cathedrae? Nisi honores? Quid sunt columbae nisi simplices, mentes vel animae fidem candidam & puram sequentes? Ego ergo inducam in templum quem Christus excludit? Iubetur enim exire qui dignitates vendit & honores. Iubetur enim exire qui vendere vult simplices mentes fidelium? Ergo Auxentius eiicitur, Mercurinus excluditur. Vnum portentum est, duo nomina. Etenim ne cognosceretur quis esset, mutauit sibi vocabulum: vt quia hic fuerat, Auxentius Episcopus Arrianus, ad decipiendam plebem, quam ille tenerat, se vocaret Mercurinũ. Mutauit ergo vocabulum, sed perfidiam non mutauit. Exuit lupum, & induit lupum. Nihil prodest quod mutauit nomen, quid sit agnoscitur. Alius in Scythiae partibus dicebatur, alius hic vocatur. Nomina pro regionib. habet. Habet ergo iam duo nomina: & si hinc alio perrexerit, habebit & tertium. Quomodo enim patietur vt maneat ei vocabulum ad tanti sceleris indicium? Minora fecit in Scythia, & ita erubuit vt mutaret vocabulum. Sceleratiora hic ausus est, & volet, quocunq; perrexerit, nomine suo prodi. Tantorum populorum sanguinem manu sua scribet & poterit confiteri animo? Paucos excludebat Dominus Iesus de templo suo, Auxentius nullum reliquit. De templo suo Iesus flagello eiicit, Auxentius gladio. Iesus flagello, Mercurianus securi. Pius Dominus flagello exturbat sacrilegos, nequam persequitur pios ferro. De quo bene dixistis hodie: Leges suas secum ferat. Feret, etiam si nolit. Feret conscientiam suam, & si non fert chartulam: feret sanguine inscriptam animam suam, etsi atramento inscriptam epistolam non feret. Scripta est Iuda culpa tua graphio ferreo & vngue adamantino, & scripta in pectore tuo: hoc est, ibi scripta, unde processit. Is mihi etiam audet mentionem facere retractandi, plenus sanguinis cruoris? Qui quos non potuerit sermone decipere, eos gladio putat esse feriendos, cruentas leges ore dictans, manu scribens, & putans quod lex fidem hominibus imperare. Non audiuit, & id quod hodie dictum est: Quoniam non iustificatur homo ex operibus legis? Aut, per legem legi mortuus sum, vt Deo viuam? id est, per legem spiritualem interpretationem legis est mortuus corporali. Et nos per legem Domini nostri Iesu Christi moriamur huic legi, quae sancit decreta perfidiae. Non lex Ecclesiam congregauit, sed fides Christi. Lex enim non est ex fide, iustus autem ex fide viuit. Iustum ergo fides non lex facit, quia non est per legem iustitiarum, sed per fidem Christi. Qui autem fidem repudiat, & legis iura praescribit, ipse se testatur iniustum, quia iustus ex fide viuit. Hanc ergo legem quisquam sequatur, qua firmatur Ariminense concilium, in quo creatura dictus est Christus: sed aiunt: Misit Deus filium suum factum ex muliere littere; factum sub lege. Ergo factum legunt, hoc est creatum. Nonne hoc ipsum considerant quod proposuerunt, quia factus dicitur Christus, sed ex muliere, hoc est, secundum partum virginis factus est, qui secundum diuinam generationem ex patre natus est? Legerunt & hodie, quia Christus nos redemit de maledicto legis, factus pro nobis maledictum. Nunquid maledictum Christus secundum diuinitatem est? Sed quare maledictum dicatur; Apostolus te docet, dicens, quia scriptum est: Maledictus omnis qui pendet in ligno: Hoc est, qui in carne sua nostram carnem, in suo corpore nostras infirmitates & nostra maledicta suscepit, ut crucifigeret. Non enim maledictus, sed in te maledictus. Denique habes alibi: Qui peccatum non cognouit, sed pro nobis peccatum factus est: qui nostra peccata suscepit, ut sacramento sua passionis aboleret. Haec ergo fratres coram ipso apud vos plenius disputatem, sed certus non ignaros vos esse fidei, vestrum refugit examen, & Gentiles quosdam quatuor aut quinque ferme homines elegit cognitores sibi, si tamen aliquos eligit: quos vellem adesse in coetu omnium, non vt de Christo iudicent; sed vt maiestatem audiant Christi. Tamen illi iam de Auxentio pronunciauerunt, cui tractanti quotidie non crediderunt. Quae maior eius condemnatio, quam quod sine aduersario apud iudices suos victus est? Ergo & ipsorum sententiam contra Auxentium iam tenemus; & quod Gentes elegit, iure damnandus est, quia Apostoli praecepta dimisit, cum Apostolus dicat: Audet aliquis vestrum aduersus alterum habens negocium, iudicari apud iniquos, & non apud sanctos? Aut nescitis quoniam sancti de hoc mundo iudicabunt? Et infra ait: Si non est inter vos sapiens quisquam, qui possit iudicare inter fratres, sed frater cum fratre iudicio contendit, & hoc apud infideles? Vides quia quod ille obtulit, contra auctoritatem Apostoli sit? Vos eligite, vtrum Auxentium, aut Paulum sequi debeatis magistrum? Sed quid dicam de Apostolo, cum ipse Dominus clamet per prophetam: Audite me populus meus, qui scitis iudicium, quorum in corde lex mea est. Deus dicit: Audite me populus meus, qui scitis iudicium; Auxentius dicit: Nescitis iudicium. Videtis quia iam Deum contemnit in vobis, qui sententiam coelestis refutat oraculi? Audite me, inquit, populus meus, dicit Dominus. Non dicit, audite gentes; non dicit, audite Iudaei. Iam enim populus Dei qui fuerat, populus erroris est factus. Et qui populus erroris erat, populus Dei esse coepit, quia in Christum credidit. Iste ergo populus iudicat, cuius in corde lex diuina est, non humana: Lex non atramento scripta, sed spiritu Dei viui: non in charta operata, sed in corde signata: Lex gratiae non cruoris. Quis igitur vobis iniuriam facit, qui reculat vestram, an qui eligit audientiam? Conclusus undique ad veritatem patrum suorum confugit. De Imperatore vult inuidiam commouere, dicens iudicare debere adolescentem catechumenum sacrae lectionis ignarum, & in consistorio iudicare. Quasi vero superiore anno, quando ad palatium suum petitus, cum praesentibus primatibus ante consistorium tractaretur; cum Imperator Basilicam vellet eripere, ego tunc aulae contemplatione regalis infractus sim, constantiam non tenuerim Sacerdotis, aut immunito iure discesserim. Nonne meminerunt, quod vbi me cognouit populus palatium petisse, ita irruit, vt vim eius ferre non possent, quando Comiti militari cum expeditis ad fugandam multitudinem egresso obtulerunt omnes se neci pro fide Christi? Non tunc rogatus sum, vt populum multo sermone mulcerem? sponderem fidem, quod Basilicam Ecclesiae nullus inuaderet? Et cum pro beneficio meum sit officium postulatum, tamen quod populus ad palatium venisset, mihi inuidia commota est. In hanc igitur inuidiam me redire desiderant. Reuocaui populum, & tamen inuidiam non euasi: quam quidem inuidiam ego temperandam arbitror, non timendam. Quid enim timeamus pro Christi nomine? nisi forte illud mouere me debet quod aiunt, ergo non debet Imperator vnam Basilicam accipere ad quam procedat: & plus vult Ambrosius posse quam Imperator, vt Imperatori prodeundi facultatem neget? Quod cum dicunt, apprehendere sermones nostros gestiunt, sicut Iudaei qui Christum versuto sermone tentabant, dicentes: Magister, licet tributum dare Caesari aut non? Semperne de Caesare seruulis Dei inuidia commouetur? Et hoc ad calumniam sibi arcessit impietas, vt imperiale nomen obtendat? Et isti possunt dicere, quod eorum non habeant sacrilegium, quorum imitantur magisterium: Et tamen videte, quanto priores Arriani sunt quam Iudaei. Illi quaerebant vtrum soluendum putaret Caesari ius tributi, isti Imperatori volunt dare ius Ecclesiae. Sed vt perfidi suum sequuntur authorem, ita & nos, quae nos Dominus & author noster docuit, respondeamus. Considerans enim Iesus dolum Iudaeorum dixit ad eos: Quid me tentatis? Ostendite mihi denarium. Et cum dedissent, dixit: cuius imaginem habet & inscriptionem? Respondentes dixerunt: Caesaris. Et ait illis Iesus: Reddite quae sunt Caesaris, Caesari: & quae sunt Dei, Deo. Ergo & ego dico illis, qui mihi obiiciunt: Ostendite mihi denarium. Iesus Caesaris denarium vidit, & ait: Reddite Caesari quae Caesaris sunt, & quae Dei sunt, Deo. Nunquid de Ecclesiae Basilicis occupandis possunt denarium offerre Caesaris? Sed in Ecclesia vnam imaginem noui, hoc est, imaginem Dei visibilis, de qua dixit Deus: Faciamus hominem ad imaginem & similitudinem nostram. Illam imaginem, de qua scriptum est: quia Christus splendor gloriae, & imago substantiae eius. In ista imagine patrem cerno; sicut dixit ipse Dominus Iesus: Qui me vidit, vidit & Patrem. Non enim haec imago a patre est separata, quae Vnitatem me docuit Trinitatis, dicens: Ego & Pater vnum sumus. Et infra: Omnia quaecunque habet Pater, mea sunt. Et de Spiritu sancto, dicens: Quia spiritus Christi sit, & de Christo accepit, sicut scriptum est: Ille de meo accipiet, & annunciabit vobis. Quid igitur? non humiliter responsum a nobis est? Si tributum petit, non negamus. Agri Ecclesiae sol-uunt unt tributum. Si agros desiderat Imperator, potestatem habet vindicandorum, nemo nostrum interuenit. Potest pauperibus collatio populi redundare. Non faciant de agris inuidiam, tollat eos si libitum est. Imperatori non dono, sed non nego. Aurum quaerunt, possum dicere: Argentum & aurum non quaero. Sed inuidiam faciunt, quia aurum erogatur. Necego hanc inuidiam perhorresco. Habeo aerarios: Aerarii mei, pauperes Christi sunt. Hunc noui congregare thesaurum. Vtinam hoc mihi semper crimen adscribam, quia aurum pauperibus erogatur. Quod si obiiciunt, quod defensionem ab iis requiram, non nego, sed etiam ambio. Habeo defensionem, sed in orationibus pauperum. Caeci illi, & claudi, debiles & senes, robustis bellatoribus fortiores sunt. Denique munera pauperum Deum obligant, quia scriptum est: Qui largitur pauperi, Deo foenerat. Praesidia bellatorum diuinam saepe gratiam non merentur. Hymnorum quoque meorum carminibus deceptum populum ferunt. Plane nec hoc abnuo. Grande carmen istud est, & quo nihil potentius. Quid enim potentius quam confessio Trinitatis, quae quotidie totius populi ore celebratur? Certatim omnes studeant fidem fateri, Patrem & Filium & Spiritum sanctum norunt versibus praedicare. Facti sunt igitur omnes magistri, qui vix poterant esse discipuli. Quid igitur obaudientius potest esse, quam vt Christi sequamur exemplum, qui specie inuentus vt homo, humiliauit semetipsum factus obediens usque ad mortem? Denique omnes per obedientiam liberauit. Sicut enim per inobedientiam vnius hominis peccatores constituti sunt plurimi, ita & per vnius obedientiam iusti constituentur multi. Si ergo ille obediens, accipiant obedientiae magisterium, cui nos inhaeremus, dicentes iis, qui nobis de Imperatore inuidiam faciunt: Soluimus quae sunt Caesaris Caesari, & quae sunt Dei Deo. Tributum Caesaris est, non negatur. Ecclesia Dei est, Caesari utique non debet addici: quia ius Caesaris esse non potest Dei templum. Quod cum honorificentia Imperatoris nemo dictum potest negare. Quid enim honorificentius, quam vt Imperator Ecclesiae filius esse dicatur? Quod cum dicitur, sine peccato dicitur, cum gratia dicitur. Imperator enim bonus intra Ecclesiam, non supra Ecclesiam est. Bonus enim Imperator quaerit auxilium Ecclesiae, non refutat. Haec vt humiliter dicimus, ita constanter exponimus. Sed incendia aliqui, gladium, deportationem minantur. Didicimus Christi seruuli non timere. Non timentibus nunquam est grauis terror. Denique scriptum est: Sagittae infantium factae sunt plagae eorum. Satis igitur propositis respondsum videtur. Nunc illos interrogo quod Saluator interrogauit: Baptismus Ioannis de caelo est, an ex hominibus? Et non potuerunt respondere ei Iudaei. Si Baptismum Ioannis non soluerunt Iudaei, Auxentius soluit baptismum Christi? Non enim istud ex hominibus est baptisma, sed de caelo, quod retulit consilii magni Angelus, vt iustificemur Deo. Cur igitur rebaptizandos Auxentius fideles populos putat, baptizatos in nomine Trinitatis, cum Apostolus dicat: vna fides, vnum baptisma? Et se hominum dicit aduersarium esse, non Christi, cum consilium Dei spernat, & condemnet baptisma, quod Christus nobis ad redimenda nostra peccata donauit.
units.tr: I see that you are unusually upset and are saying that I am being tried. I wonder what this is about, unless perhaps you saw or heard that tribunes had come to me with an imperial order to leave here as I wished, and that anyone who wanted could follow me. So did you fear that I would desert the Church, and that I would abandon you to save myself? But you could have guessed what I myself had ordered: my will could not include deserting the Church, since I fear the Lord of the world more than the Emperor of this age. Indeed, if some force were to drag me away from the Church, it could only drive out my flesh, not my mind. I am ready, if he did what is customary for royal power, to undergo what is customary for a priest. Why then are you troubled? I would never willingly abandon you, and when compelled I have not known how to resist. I can grieve, I can weep, I can groan. My tears are weapons against armed soldiers and even against the Goths. Such are the defences of a priest. I ought not, and cannot, resist in any other way. Nor am I accustomed to flee and leave the Church, lest anyone interpret the act as fear of a heavier punishment. You yourselves know that I am accustomed to yield to the Emperors, not to trust them, and to offer myself willingly to punishment, and not to fear what is being prepared. I wish I were sure that the Church would not be handed over to heretics. I would gladly go to the Emperor's palace, if it fitted the office of a priest to contend more in the palace than in the Church. But in the consistory it is not Christ who is accustomed to be the accused, but the judge. Who would refuse to have the cause of the faith pleaded in the Church? If anyone trusts his case, let him come here. The Emperor's judgment, which he has revealed by a law that attacks the faith, is already biased, and the hoped-for zeal of certain men who seek favour does not need to be consulted. I will not allow anyone to sell the injury done to Christ. The soldiers gathered around, the clash of arms by which the Church is surrounded, do not terrify my faith, but they stir up my mind, so that, while you are fearful, something harmful to your salvation may arise. For I have already learned not to fear, but I have begun to fear more for you. Please allow your priest to contend; we have an adversary who provokes us.
