Let us therefore discern what God has made and what man has made; and let us neither hate the man on account of the error, nor love the error on account of the man. Therefore, with one mind, let us pursue in the man the evil of pride, so that the man himself may first be freed from his enemy, namely error. Our almighty Redeemer will grant the life of charity and justice; he will grant to us, though placed far from us, the unity of his Spirit, by whose skill the Church, bound together like a citadel built in the manner of the world's four quarters, with its sides of wood that does not rot, joined by the bitumen of charity, may not be disturbed by the hostility of any spirit, or by the swelling of any wave that comes from outside. But just as we must pray that by his governing grace no wave coming from without may trouble us, so, dear brothers, we must pray with our whole bowels that the right hand of his providence may drain from within us the surplus of this opinion. For the adversary, the Devil, who rages against the humble, roaring like a lion, goes about seeking whom he may devour, does not now, as we see, go about the sheepfolds, but he so strongly fixes his teeth in certain necessary members of the Church that no one doubts that, unless the Lord of all, by his providence, brings together the flock of pastors in unanimous agreement, he will tear the whole fold to pieces, which God forbid, more quickly. Consider, dear brothers, what follows from this nearby, whose such perverse beginnings break out even among priests. For since he is near of whom it is written, He is king over all the sons of pride, I am compelled to say, not without great grief, that our brother and fellow bishop John, despising the commands of the Lord, the precepts of the Apostles, and the rules of the Fathers, tries to outstrip him by pride in the name. And may almighty God show to your blessedness how I am tormented by a grievous sighing over this consideration: that he who was once most modest to me, he who was beloved by all, he who seemed occupied with almsgiving, prayers and fasting, has, from that in which he sat in ashes, from that humility which he put forward, taken up boasting, so that he tries to ascribe to himself the whole universe; and by the proud speech of that very pomp, he strives to subject to himself the members that all cohere to the one Head, namely Christ. Nor is it any wonder, since that tempter, who knows that pride is the beginning of every sin, used it first of all in the first man, and now places it at the end of virtues for certain men, so that those who seemed somewhat to have escaped his most cruel hands by good pursuits of life, he sets, at the very goal of a good work and, as it were, at the very conclusion of perfection, a snare. Hence we must pray earnestly, and implore almighty God with constant prayers, that he may turn this error away from his mind, and warn him of this evil of pride and confusion, which divides the Church from unity and humility. And, with the Lord's favour, we must run and provide with all our strength, lest, through the poison of one man's word, the living members of Christ's body should die. For if this is permitted to be said freely, the honour of all the Patriarchs is denied. And when perhaps he who is called Universal perishes in error, no Bishop will be found to have remained in the state of truth. I therefore beg you to keep the Churches constantly and without prejudice, just as you received them; and let not this temptation of Diabolical usurpation claim anything for itself in you. Stand firm, stand secure, and do not presume ever to give or to accept letters with the false name of Universal. Forbid all Bishops subject to your care from the defilement of this arrogance, so that the Churches may recognise you as Patriarchs of the universal Church, not only in good works, but also in the authority of the truth. But if any adversity should perhaps follow, we must, persisting together, show it even by dying, because in condemning the name of universality we do not especially love anything of our own. Let us say with Paul: For me to live is Christ, and to die is gain. Let us hear what the first of all shepherds says: If you suffer for righteousness' sake, you will be blessed. For believe me: the honour which we have taken up for the preaching of the truth, if the need of necessity demands it, we shall more confidently give up for that same truth which we hold. But pray, as your most dear blessedness befits, so that I may show by my works what I dare to say to you.

units.la: EPISTOLA XXXVIII.
units.tr: EPISTLE XXXVIII.

units.la: De pace sancta Ecclesia ab eo per Universale nomen turbata. De synodo per Pelagium Papam cassata. Exemplum proponit Diaboli contra Deum superbientis. Et de superbia eius himia.
units.tr: On the holy peace of the Church, disturbed by his use of the title "Universal". On the synod annulled by Pope Pelagius. He sets forth the example of the devil, who was proud against God. And on his arrogance.

units.la: Ioanni Episcopo Constantinopolitano. Eo tempore quo fraternitas vestra in sacerdotalem honorem provecta est, quantam Ecclesiarum pacem atque concordiam inuenerit, revolit. Sed quoniam, quove tumore nescio, novum sibi conata est nomen arripere, unde omnium fratrum corda potuissent ad scandalum peruenire: Quæ inter tehementer admiror, quia nec ad Episcopatum venire potuisses, fugisse velle te memini. Quem tamen adeptum ita exercere desideras, ac si ad eum ambitioso desiderio cucurrisses. Quid enim indignum te esse fateberis, vt Episcopus dici debuisses, ad hoc quandoque perductus, vt despectis fratribus Episcopus appelari solus vocari. Et quidem hac de re sanctæ memoriæ decessoris mei Pelagii gravis ad sanctitatem vestram scripta transmissa sunt. In quibus synodi quæ apud vos de fratris quondam & consacerdotis nostri Gregorii causa congregata est: propter nefandum elationis vocabulum, a te dissoluit; & Archidiaconum, quem iuxta morem ad vestigia Dominorum transmiserat, missarum solemnia vobiscum celebrare prohibuit. Post eius vero obitum, cum indignus ego ad Ecclesiæ regimen adductus sum, & antea per alios responsales meos, & nunc per communem filium meum Sabinianum Diaconum alloqui fraternitatem vestram, vt a tali se præsumptione compesceret, non quidem scripto, sed nudo sermone curavi. Et si emendari nollet, cum missarum solemnia cum fraternitate vestra celebrare prohibui, vt sanctitatem vestram prius sub quadam verecundiæ reuerentia pulsassem: quatenus si emendari nefandus ac profanus tumor verecunde non posset, tunc ad ea debuissem, quæ sunt districta atque canonica, peruenire. Eo quia rescanda vulnera prius leui manu palpanda sunt: rogo, deprecor, & quanta possum dulcedine exposco, vt fraternitas vestra cunctis sibi adulantibus, atque erroris nomen deferentibus contradicat, ne stulto ac superbo vocabulo appellari consentiat. Vere enim flens dico, atque ex intimo viscerum dolore peccatis meis deputo, quod ille meus frater nuncupatus ad humilitatem reduci non valuit; qui ad hoc in Episcopatus gradu constitutus est, vt aliorum animas ad humilitatem reducat, quod ille qui veritatem docet alios, semetipsum docere, nec me quoque deprecante consensit. Perpende rogo, quia in hac præsumptione temeraria pax totius turbatur Ecclesiæ, & gratiæ contradicitur communiter omnibus effusæ. In qua nimirum ipse crescere tantum potes, quantum penes temetipsum decreueris. Tantoque maior efficieris, quanto te a superbi & stulti vocabuli usurpatione restringis. Atqui in tantum profecis, in quantum tibi non studueris derogando fratribus arrogare. Humilitatem ergo frater charissime totis visceribus dilige, per quam sanctorum fratrum concordia; & sanctæ vniuersalis Ecclesiæ vnitas valeat custodiri. Certe Paulus Apostolus cum audiret quosdam dicere: Ego sum Pauli, ego Apollo, ego vero Cephæ: hanc dilaceratio nem corporis Domini, per quam membra eius aliis quodammodo se capitibus sociabant, vehementissime exhorrescens exclamauit, dicens: Nunquid Paulus pro vobis crucifixus est, aut in nomine Pauli baptizati estis? Sic ergo ille membra Domini corporis certis extra Christum quasi capitibus, & ipsis quidem Apostolis subiici particulariter cuitauit: tu quid Christo vniuersalis sanctæ Ecclesiæ capiti in extremi iudicii esse dicturus examine, qui cuncta eius membra tibimet conaris vniuersalis appellatione supponere? Quis rogo in hoc tam peruerso vocabulo, nisi ille admirandum proponitur, qui despectis Angelorum legionibus secum socialiter constitutis, ad culmen conatus est singularitatis erumpere, vt & nihil subesse, & solus omnibus præesse videretur? Qui etiam dixit: In cælum conscendam, super astra cæli exaltabo solium meum. Sedebo in monte testamenti, in lateribus aquilonis. Ascendam super altitudinem nubium, similis ero Altissimo. Quid enim fratres tui omnes vniuersalis Ecclesiæ Episcopi, nisi astra cœli sunt? quorum vita simul & lingua inter peccata errorésque hominum quasi inter noctis tenebras lucent. Quibus dum cupis temetipsum vocabulo elationis præponere, eorumque nomen tui comparatione calcare; quid aliud dicis, nisi in cælum conscendam, super astra cœli exaltabo solium meum? An non vniuersi Episcopi nubes sunt, qui & verbis prædicationis pluunt, & bonorum operum luce & miraculis coruscant? quos dum vestra fraternitas despiciens, sub se premere conatur: quid aliud dicit nisi hoc, quod ab antiquo hoste dicitur: Ascendam super altitudinem nubium? Quæ cuncta ego cum flens conspicio, & occulta Dei iudicia pertimesco, augentur lachrymæ, gemitus sein meo corde non capiunt, quod ille vir sanctissimus Dominus Ioannes, tantæ abstinentiæ atque humilitatis, suorum familiarium seductione linguarum ad tantam superbiam erupit, vt in appetitu peruersi nominis illi esse conetur similis, qui dum superbe esse similis Deo voluit, etiam donatæ similitudinis gratiam amisit, & veram beatitudinem perdidit, quia falsam gloriam quæsuit. Certe Petrus Apostolus primum membrum Sanctæ & Vniuersalis Ecclesiæ est. Paulus, Andreas, Ioannes, quid aliud quam singularium sunt plebium capita? & tamen sub vno capite omnes membra sunt Ecclesiæ. Atque vt cuncta breui cingulo orationis astringam: Sancti ante legem; sancti sub lege; sancti sub gratia, omnes hi perficientes corpus Domini, in membris sunt Ecclesiæ constituti, & nemo se vnquam vocare Vniuersalem voluit. Vestra autem sanctitas agnoscat quantum apud se tumeat, quæ illo nomine vocari appetit, quo vocari nullus præsumpsit, qui veraciter sanctus fuit. Nunquid non, sicut vestra fraternitas hovit, per venerandum Chalcedonense Concilium huius Apostolicæ sedis Antistites, cui Deo auctore disponenti deseruio; Vniuersales oblato honore vocati sunt? Sed tamen nullus vnquam tali vocabulo appellari voluit; nullus sibi hoc temerarium nomen arripuit: ne si sibi in pontificatus gradu gloriam singularitatis arriperet, hanc omnibus fratribus denegasse videretur. Sed hæc scio, quia vestræ sanctitati ab illis oriuntur, qui vobis deceptiosa familiaritate deseruiunt, contra quos peto, vt vestra fraternitas solertet inuigilet, nec se eorum verbis fallendum præbeat. Tanto enim maiores hostes credendi sunt, quanto magis laudibus adulantur. Relinque tales, etsi omnino deceptur sunt, saltem terrenorum hominum.
units.tr: To John, Bishop of Constantinople. At the time when your brotherhood was raised to the priestly office, I recall what peace and harmony you found among the churches. But since, from some swelling of pride I know not what, you have tried to seize a new title, by which the hearts of all the brothers could come to scandal, I marvel greatly at this, for I remember that you wished to flee even when you could not be brought to the episcopate. Yet now that you have obtained it, you wish to exercise it as if you had run to it with an ambitious desire. For what unworthiness will you confess yourself to have, that you should be called a bishop, you who were at last brought to this, so that, the brothers being despised, you alone should be called and named the bishop? Indeed, in this matter, a serious letter of my predecessor, Pelagius of holy memory, was sent to your holiness. In it, the synod which was gathered among you concerning the case of our former brother and fellow priest Gregory was dissolved by you on account of the abominable word of arrogance. And you forbade the archdeacon, whom he had sent to the feet of the lords according to custom, to celebrate the solemnities of the Masses with you. After his death, when I, though unworthy, was brought to the government of the Church, I first addressed your brotherhood through my other agents, and now through our common son, Sabinianus the deacon, and I took care to urge you, not in writing but by mere word, to restrain yourself from such presumption. And if you were unwilling to amend, I forbade you to celebrate the solemnities of the Masses with your brotherhood. I wished first to strike at your holiness with a certain modest reverence, so that if the wicked and profane swelling could not be amended with modesty, then I should have proceeded to those measures which are strict and canonical. For wounds that must be cut should first be touched with a light hand. I ask, I beseech, and with all the sweetness I can, I entreat that your brotherhood, against all who flatter you and bear the name of error, should resist, and not consent to be called by a foolish and proud title. For I say with truest weeping, and I reckon it with the deepest sorrow of my bowels as among my sins, that this brother of mine, so called, has not been able to be brought back to humility. He was placed in the rank of bishop so that he might lead the souls of others back to humility, yet he has not consented, even at my entreaty, to teach himself, though he who teaches others the truth ought to do so. Consider, I beg you, that in this rash presumption the peace of the whole Church is disturbed, and the grace poured out in common upon all is contradicted. In this you can indeed grow only as much as you determine within yourself. And you will become greater in proportion as you restrain yourself from usurping that proud and foolish title. Indeed, you have advanced only so far as you have not sought to arrogate to yourself by belittling your brothers. Therefore, dearest brother, love humility with your whole heart, through which the concord of the holy brothers and the unity of the holy universal Church may be preserved. Surely the Apostle Paul, when he heard some saying, "I am of Paul, I am of Apollos, I am of Cephas," shuddering most vehemently at this laceration of the body of the Lord, by which its members were in a manner joining themselves to different heads, cried out, saying: "Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?" So he took care that the members of the Lord's body should not be subjected particularly to certain heads outside Christ, even to the Apostles themselves. What will you say before the judgment of the last day, before Christ, the head of the whole holy Church, you who try to place all its members under yourself by the name of "universal"? Who, I ask, is set forth as the admirable one in this so perverse a title, except him who, having despised the legions of angels joined with him in fellowship, tried to break out to the summit of singularity, so that he might seem to be subject to nothing and to rule over all alone? He also said: "I will ascend into heaven; above the stars of heaven I will exalt my throne. I will sit on the mount of the covenant, in the sides of the north. I will ascend above the height of the clouds; I will be like the Most High." For what are all your brothers, the bishops of the universal Church, but the stars of heaven, whose life and tongue shine among the sins and errors of men as lights in the darkness of night? While you desire to place yourself above them by the word of pride, and to trample their name under your own comparison, what else do you say but: "I will ascend into heaven; above the stars of heaven I will exalt my throne"? Are not all bishops clouds, which rain with the words of preaching and gleam with the light of good works and with miracles? When your brotherhood, looking down on them, tries to press them under itself, what else does it say than what is said by the ancient enemy: "I will ascend above the height of the clouds"? When I look upon all these things with weeping, and fear the hidden judgments of God, my tears increase, and my groaning cannot be contained in my heart, that this most holy man, Lord John, of such abstinence and humility, has by the seduction of the tongues of his familiars broken out into such great pride, so that in his desire for the perverse name he tries to be like him who, while he willed to be proudly like God, also lost the grace of the likeness given to him, and lost true blessedness, because he sought false glory. Surely the Apostle Peter is the first member of the holy and universal Church. Paul, Andrew, John: what else are they than heads of particular peoples? And yet all are members of the Church under one head. And to bind everything in a short girdle of speech: the holy men before the law, the holy men under the law, the holy men under grace, all of whom completed the body of the Lord, were established as members of the Church, and no one ever wished to call himself universal. But your holiness should recognize how much it swells within itself, since it seeks to be called by that name by which no one who was truly holy presumed to be called. Did not the bishops of this Apostolic See, to whom I, by God's disposition, am a servant, as your brotherhood knows, through the venerable Council of Chalcedon, when honour was offered, get called universal? Yet no one ever wished to be called by such a title; no one seized for himself this rash name, lest, if he claimed for himself in the rank of pontiff the glory of singularity, he should seem to have denied this to all the brothers. But I know these things arise from those who serve you with deceitful familiarity; against them I beg that your brotherhood watch carefully and not allow itself to be deceived by their words. For they are to be believed to be the greater enemies the more they flatter with praises. Leave such men, even if they are wholly deceived, at least to earthly men,

units.la: homim hominum, & non sacerdotum corda decipiant. Sine mortuos sepelire mortuos suos. Vos autem cum Propheta dicite: Auertantur retrorsum, qui dicunt mihi euge, euge. Et rursus: Oleum autem peccatoris non impinguet caput meum. Unde & bene quidam sapiens admonet: Multi sint pacifici tui, consiliarius autem sit unus tibi de mille. Corrumpunt enim bonos mores colloquia mala. Antiquus enim hostis cum robusti cor irrumpere non valeat, subiectas & infirmas personas quaerit, & quasi contra alta moenia scalis appositis ascendit. Sic Adam per subiectam mulierem decepit. Sic beato Iob cum filios occidit, infirmam mulierem reliquit: ut qui eius cor per se minime poterat, saltem si posset per mulieris verba penetraret. Quicunque ergo iuxta vos infirmi, ac seculares sunt, in fide semper persuasione, atque adulatione frangantur: quia inde aeternas Dei inimicitias pariunt, unde ipsi peruersi amatores videntur. Certe olim clamabatur per Apostolum Ioannem: Filioli, nouissima hora est, secundum quod veritas predixit. Pestilentia & gladius per mundum saevit, gentes insurgunt in gentes, terra concutitur, orbis cum habitatoribus suis terra dehiscente sorbetur. Omnia enim quae praedicta sunt, fiunt. Rex superbiae prope est, & quod dici nefas est, sacerdotum est praeparatus exitus, quia ceruici militant elationis, qui ab hoc positi fuerant, ut ducatum praberent humilitatis. Sed hac in re, etiam si nostra lingua minime contradicat, illius virtus contra elationem, in ultionem erigitur, qui superbiae vitio per semetipsum specialiter aduersatur. Hinc enim scriptum est: Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam. Hinc rursus dicitur: Immundus est apud Deum, qui exaltat cor. Hinc contra superbientem hominem scriptum est: quid superbis terra & cinis? Hinc per semetipsam veritas dicit: Omnis qui se exaltat, humiliabitur. Quae ut nos ad viam vitae per humilitatem reduceret, in semetipsa dignata est, quod nos admonet, demonstrare dicens: Discite a me quia mitis sum, & humilis corde. Ad hoc namque unigenitus Dei filius formam infirmitatis nostrae suscepit: ad hoc invisibilis, non solum visibilis, sed etiam despectus apparuit, ad hoc contumeliarum ludibria, illusionum probra, passionum tormenta toleravit, ut superbum non esse hominem doceret humilis Deus. Quanta igitur humilitatis virtus est, propter quam solam veraciter edocendam, is qui sine aestimatione magnus est, usque ad passionem mortis factus est parvus? Quia enim originem perditionis nostrae se praebuit superbia Diaboli, instrumentum redemptionis nostrae inuenta est humilitas Dei. Hostis quippe noster inter omnia conditus, videri supra omnia voluit elatus. Redemptor autem noster magnus manens supra omnia, fieri inter omnia dignatus est parvus. Quid ergo nos Episcopi dicimus, qui honoris locum ex Redemptoris nostri humilitate suscepimus, & tamen superbiam hostis ipsius imitamur? Ecce nouimus creatorem nostrum de suae celsitudinis culmine, ut humano generi daret gloriam, descendisse: & nos de infimis creati, de fratrum minoratione quaerimus gloriam. Humiliavit se usque ad nostrum pulverem Dei, & in caelos os suum posuit, & super terram lingua pertransit pulvis humanus, & non erubescit: non metuit extolli homo putredo, & filius hominis vermis. Reducamus ad animum frater charissime hoc quod per sapientissimum Salomonem dicitur: Ante contritionem praecedit superbia, & ante ruinam exaltabitur cor. Vbi e diverso subiungitur, ante gloriam humiliabitur. Humiliemur ergo in mente, si ad solidam conamur venire celsitudinem. Nequaquam per elationis fumum oculi cordis obscuratur: qui quanto magis excreuerit, tanto celerius euanescit. Pensemus quid nos praecepta admonent Redemptoris nostri, dicentis: Beati pauperes spiritu, quoniam ipsorum est regnum caelorum. Hinc etiam per Prophetam dicit: Super quem requiescet Spiritus meus, nisi super humilem & quietum, & trementem sermones meos? Certe cum Dominus ad humilitatis viam adhuc infirmantium discipulorum corda reduceret, dixit: Si quis vult inter vos primus esse, erit omnium minimus. Qua in re aperte cognoscitur, quoniam ille veraciter sublimis est, qui in suis cogitationibus humiliatur. Formidemus ergo in illorum numerum adscribi, qui primas in synagogis cathedras quaerunt, & salutationes in foro, & vocari ab hominibus Rabbi. Quo contra discipulis Dominus dicit: vos autem nolite vocari Rabbi. Vnus enim magister vester est, vos autem omnes fratres. Et patrem nolite vocare vobis super terram, vnus est enim pater vester. Quid ergo frater charissime in illo terribili examine venientis iudicis dicturus es, qui non solum pater, sed etiam generalis pater in mundo vocari appetis? Cauetur ergo malorum praua suggestio, fugiatur omnis instigatio scandali. Oportet quidem ut veniant scandala; verumtamen vae homini illi per quem scandalum venit. Ecce ex hoc nefando elationis vocabulo Ecclesia scinditur, fratrum omnium corda ad scandalum provocantur. Nunquid nam mente excidit, quod veritas dicit: Qui scandalizauerit unum de pusillis istis, qui in me credit, expedit ei ut suspendatur mola asinaria in collo eius, & demergatur in profundum maris? Scriptum vero est: Charitas non quaerit quae sua sunt. Ecce vestra fraternitas sibi arrogat etiam aliena. Rursum scriptum est: Honore invicem praevenientes. Et tu conaris eum omnibus tollere, quem tibi illicite desideras singulariter vsurpare. Vbi est, frater charissime, quod scriptum est: Pacem habete cum omnibus & sanctimoniam, sine qua nemo videbit Deum. Vbi est quod scriptum est: Beati pacifici, quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur? Considerare vos conuenit, ne qua radix amaritudinis sursum germinans impediat, & per illam coinquinantur multi. Quod tamen si considerare negligimus, contra tantae elationis tumorem iudicia superna vigilabunt. Et nos quidem in quos talis tantaque per autum nefarium culpa committitur, seruamus quod veritas præcepit, dicens: si peccauerit in te frater tuus, vade & corripe eum inter te & ipsum solum. Si te audierit, lucratus eris fratrem tuum. Si autem te non audierit, adhibe tecum adhuc vnum vel duos, vt in ore duorum vel trium testium stet omne verbum: quod si non audierit eos, dic Ecclesiæ. Si autem Ecclesiam non audierit, sit tibi sicut Ethnicus & publicanus. Ego itaque per Responsales meos semel & his verbis humilibus hoc quod in tota Ecclesia peccatur, corripere studui: nunc per me ipsum scribo. Quicquid facere humiliter debui, omisi. Sed si in mea correptione despicitor, restat vt Ecclesiam debeam adhibere. Hæc itaque dicens, omnipotens Deus fraternitati vestræ indicet, quanto circa vos amore constringor: quantumque in hac causa non contra vos, sed pro vobis lugeo. In qua tamen præceptis Euangelicis, institutionibus canonum, utilitatibus fratrum personam præponere non possum, nec eius quem multum amo. Scripta autem sanctitatis vestræ dulcissima atque suauissima de causa Presbyterorum Ioannis & Athanasii suscepi, de qua vobis in subsequentibus Domino adiuuante respondebo: quia sub tantis tribulationibus circumfusus Barbarorum gladiis premor, vt non dico multa tractare, sed mihi respirare vix liceat. Dat. Kalendas Ianuarii, Indict. XIII. Anno Dom. 594.
units.tr: men's hearts, and not the hearts of priests, deceive. Let the dead bury their own dead. But you, with the Prophet, should say: Let them be turned back who say to me, Aha, aha. And again: Let the oil of the sinner not anoint my head. Hence a certain wise man also rightly advises: Let your peacemakers be many, but let your counsellor be one in a thousand. For evil conversations corrupt good manners. For the ancient enemy, when he cannot break into the heart of a strong man, seeks out weak and submissive persons, and climbs as if against high walls with scaling ladders. Thus Adam was deceived through the woman who was subject to him. Thus, when he had killed Job's sons, he left his wife, a weak woman, so that he who could not penetrate Job's heart by himself might at least, if he could, get in through the words of his wife. Therefore, whoever among you are weak and secular, let them be broken in faith by persuasion and flattery, since these men produce eternal enmities of God, by which they themselves appear to be perverse lovers. Certainly, long ago the Apostle John cried out: Little children, it is the last hour, as the truth foretold. Pestilence and sword rage through the world, nations rise against nations, the earth is shaken, and the world with its inhabitants is swallowed up as the earth gapes open. For all that has been foretold is coming to pass. The king of pride is near, and (it is unlawful to say it) the end is prepared by priests, because those who were placed in this office to give the lead in humility are serving as soldiers under the yoke of arrogance. But in this matter, even if our tongue does not contradict it, the power of him who specially opposes the vice of pride rises up in vengeance against arrogance. For it is written: God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble. Again it is said: He who exalts his heart is unclean before God. Against the proud man it is written: Why are you proud, earth and ashes? Truth itself says: Everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled. That truth, in order to lead us back to the way of life through humility, deigned to show this in himself, admonishing us and saying: Learn from me, for I am meek and lowly in heart. For this reason the only-begotten Son of God took on the form of our weakness; for this he appeared invisible, yet not only visible but also despised; for this he endured the mockeries of insults, the reproaches of scorn, the torments of suffering, so that God, being humble, might teach that man ought not to be proud. How great, then, is the virtue of humility, for the sake of which alone, to be truly taught, he who is great beyond measure was made small even unto the death of the Cross? For as the pride of the Devil provided the origin of our ruin, so the humility of God was found to be the instrument of our redemption. Our enemy, created above all things, wished to appear exalted above all things. Our Redeemer, though remaining great above all things, deigned to become small among all things. What, then, do we bishops say, who have received the place of honour from the humility of our Redeemer, and yet imitate the pride of his enemy? Behold, we know that our Creator came down from the summit of his loftiness so as to give glory to the human race; and we, created from the lowest, seek glory from the diminishing of our brothers. He humbled himself even to our dust, the dust of God, and placed his mouth in the heavens, and human dust passes over the earth with its tongue, and is not ashamed. Man, who is rottenness, does not fear to be exalted, and the son of man, a worm. Let us call to mind, most beloved brother, what the most wise Solomon says: Before destruction goes pride, and before ruin the heart is lifted up. Where, on the other side, it is added: Before glory goes humility. Let us therefore be humbled in mind, if we seek to come to a solid height. The eyes of the heart are never darkened by the smoke of exaltation; the more it grows, the more quickly it vanishes. Let us consider what the precepts of our Redeemer admonish, saying: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Hence also through the Prophet he says: On whom shall my Spirit rest, but on the humble and quiet, and him who trembles at my words? Certainly, when the Lord was still leading the hearts of the weak disciples back to the way of humility, he said: If anyone wishes to be first among you, he shall be the least of all. In this matter it is clearly seen that he is truly exalted who is humbled in his own thoughts. Let us therefore fear to be counted among those who seek the first chairs in the synagogues, and greetings in the marketplaces, and to be called Rabbi by men. Against this the Lord says to his disciples: But you, do not be called Rabbi. For one is your teacher, and you are all brothers. And call no one on earth your father, for one is your Father. What, then, most beloved brother, will you say at that terrible judgment of the coming Judge, you who desire to be called not only father, but even universal father in the world? Let the evil suggestion of wicked men be guarded against; let every incitement to scandal be fled. It is necessary indeed that offences come; but woe to that man through whom the offence comes. Behold, through this accursed title of exaltation the Church is torn apart, and the hearts of all the brothers are provoked to scandal. Has it then slipped from your mind what truth says: Whoever shall offend one of these little ones who believe in me, it would be better for him that a millstone were hung about his neck and he were drowned in the depth of the sea? But it is written: Charity does not seek its own. Behold, your brotherhood claims even what belongs to others for itself. Again it is written: Preferring one another in honour. And you try to take away from all that honour which you unlawfully desire to seize for yourself alone. Where is it, most beloved brother, that it is written: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no one shall see God? Where is it written: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the sons of God? It behoves you to consider, lest any root of bitterness, springing up, hinder, and through it many be defiled. But if we neglect to consider this, against the swelling of such great pride the heavenly judgments will keep watch. As for us, against those in whom such a great and wicked fault is committed through pride, we keep what the truth has commanded, saying: If your brother sins against you, go and correct him between you and him alone. If he hears you, you will have gained your brother. But if he does not hear you, take with you one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may stand. And if he refuses to hear them, tell the Church. But if he does not hear the Church, let him be to you as a heathen and a tax collector. Therefore I have, through my Responsales, once and in these humble words, sought to correct what is sinned in the whole Church; now I write in my own person. What I ought to have done humbly, I have omitted. But if I am despised in my correction, it remains that I must bring in the Church. Saying these things, may almighty God show your brotherhood how strongly I am bound to you in love, and how much in this cause I grieve not against you, but for you. Yet in this matter I cannot place the person, even of him whom I love greatly, before the precepts of the Gospel, the institutions of the canons, and the advantage of the brothers. But I have received your most sweet and pleasant writings concerning the cause of the Presbyters John and Athanasius, to which, with the Lord helping, I will reply in what follows; for I am so beset by such great tribulations, pressed by the swords of the Barbarians, that I scarcely have leave to breathe, let alone to treat many matters. Given on the Kalends of January, Indiction XIII, in the year of the Lord 594.

units.la: EPISTOLA XXXIX.
units.tr: EPISTLE XXXIX.

units.la: De superbia Ioannis Episcopi vitanda.
units.tr: On avoiding the pride of John the Bishop.

units.la: Sabiniano Diacono. De causa fratris nostri viri reuerendissimi Ioannis Episcopi Constantinopolitani, duas Epistolas facere nolui. Sed vna breuiter facta est, quæ utrumque habere videretur admixtum, id est, & rectitudinem & blandimentum. Tua itaque dilectio eam epistolam, quam nunc direxi, propter voluntatem Imperatoris dare studes. Nam de subsequenti talis alia transmittitur, de qua eius superbia non lætetur. Ad hoc enim usque peruenit, vt sub occasione Ioannis Presbyteri gesta huc transmitteret, in quibus se pene per omnem versum Vniuersalis Patriarcham nominaret. Sed spero in omnipotentem Deum, quia hypocrismi illius superna maiestas soluet. Miror autem quomodo dilectionem tuam fallere potuit, vt permitteres Dominum Imperatori persuaderi, quatenus ad me sua scripta de hac causa transmitteret, in quibus admonerer, vt cum eo pacem habere debuissem. Qui si iustitiam tenere vult, illum debuit admonere, vt se a superbo vocabulo compesceret, & protinus inter nos pax fieret. Tamen qua id calliditate prædicto fratre nostro Ioanne factum sit, minime suspicor, pensasti. Idcirco enim hoc ille fecit, vt audiretur Dominus Imperator, & ille in sua vanitate confirmatus esse videretur: aut non a me audiretur, & eius animus contra me irritaretur. Sed nos rectam vitam tenemus, nihil in hac causa aliud nisi omnipotentem Dominum metuentes. Vnde tua dilectio in nullo tepidet: omnis quam in hoc seculo videt alta esse contra veritatem, despiciat, in omnipotentis Dei gratia, atque Beati Petri Apostoli adiutorio confidat. Vocem veritatis recolat dicentis: Maior est qui in cælis est, quam qui in mundo, & in hac causa quicquid agendum est, cum summa auctoritate agat. Postquam enim desendi ab inimicorum gladiis nullo modo possumus: postquam pro utilitate reipublicæ argentum aurum, mancipia, vestes perdidimus; nimis ignominiosum est, vt per eos etiam fidem perdamus. In isto enim scelesto vocabulo consentire, nihil est aliud quam fidem perdere. Vade sicut tibi iam transactis epistolis scripsi, nunquam cum eo procedere præsumas.
units.tr: To Sabinianus, Deacon. Concerning the cause of our brother, the most reverend man John, Bishop of Constantinople, I have been unwilling to write two letters. Instead one has been written briefly, which seems to contain both uprightness and flattery mixed together. Therefore, your Affection is eager to give the letter which I have now sent, on account of the Emperor's wishes. For another letter of such a kind is being sent after it, at which his pride should not rejoice. For he has gone so far that, under the pretext of the cause of John the Presbyter, he has sent here records in which he calls himself "Universal Patriarch" in almost every line. But I trust in almighty God that the heavenly majesty will dissolve that hypocrisy of his. I am surprised, however, how he was able to deceive your Affection, so that you allowed the Lord Emperor to be persuaded to send me his writings on this cause, in which I was to be admonished that I ought to keep peace with him. If he wishes to hold to justice, he ought to have urged him to restrain himself from that proud title, and at once peace would have come about between us. Yet by what cunning this was done by the aforesaid brother of ours, John, I by no means suspect; you have considered it. For he did this so that the Lord Emperor might be heard, and so that he himself might seem confirmed in his vanity; or so that he would not be heard by me, and his mind would be provoked against me. But we keep a right life, fearing nothing in this cause except almighty God. Wherefore let your Affection not grow lukewarm in any way: let it despise everything that it sees in this world raised up against the truth, and trust in the grace of almighty God and the help of the blessed Apostle Peter. Let it call to mind the voice of truth saying: "He who is in heaven is greater than he who is in the world"; and whatever must be done in this cause, let it be done with the highest authority. For since we can in no way be defended from the swords of our enemies, since we have lost silver, gold, slaves and clothing for the advantage of the commonwealth, it is far too shameful that through them we should also lose the faith. For to consent to that wicked title is nothing other than to lose the faith. Go, as I have already written to you in the earlier letters: never presume to proceed with him.

units.la: REGESTI LIB. VI. EPIST. IV.
units.tr: Register, Book 6, Letter 4

units.la: De custodienda charitate & vnitate sanctæ Ecclesiæ, de pastoralis muneris difficultatibus, & de Vniuersalis nomine reiiciendo.
units.tr: On keeping the charity and unity of the holy Church, on the difficulties of the pastoral office, and on rejecting the title "Universal."

units.la: Cyriaco Episcopo Constantinopolitano. Communes filios Georgium Presbyterum & Theodorum Diaconum vestrum, ea quæ decet charitate suscepimus, vosque ab Ecclesiasticarum rerum cura ad animarum regimen venisse gaudemus: quia iuxta veritatis vocem, qui in modico fidelis est, & in maiori fidelis erit; & bene ministranti seruo dicitur: quia in pauca fuisti, supra multa te constituam. Cui etiam mox de æterna retributione subiungitur: intra in gaudium Domini tui. In scriptis autem vestris vos magnopere requiem quæsisse narratis. Sed post hoc ad pastoralem sollicitudinem vos congrue venisse ostenditis: quia sicut locus regiminis desiderantibus negandus est, ita fugientibus offerendus est. Et sicut scriptum est: Nec quisquam sumit sibi honorem, sed qui vocatur a Deo tanquam Aaron. Et rursus idem prædicator egregius dicit: Si unus pro omnibus mortuus est, ergo omnes mortui sunt; & unus pro omnibus mortuus est Christus: superest vt & ei qui viuunt, iam non sibi viuant, sed ei qui pro eis mortuus est, & resurrexit. Et pastori sanctæ Ecclesiæ dicitur: Simon Ioannis amas me? Pasce oues meas. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quia si is qui valet, omnipotentis Dei oues recte pascere, ostendit se pastorem summum minime amare. Si enim vnigenitus patris pro explenda utilitate omnium de deserto patris egressus est ad publicum nostrum, nos quid dicturi sumus, si secretum nostrum præponimus utilitati proximorum? Quies itaque nobis & ex corde appetenda est, & tamen pro multorum lucro aliquando postponenda. Nam sicut toto desiderio debemus occupationem fugere, ita si desit qui prædicet, occupationis onus liberi necesse
units.tr: To Cyriacus, Bishop of Constantinople. We have received with the affection that befits them our common sons, George the Presbyter and Theodore the Deacon, your men, and we rejoice that you have passed from the care of Church affairs to the governance of souls. For according to the word of truth, "He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much," and to the good servant it is said: "Because you have been faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things." Immediately after this it is added concerning eternal reward: "Enter into the joy of your Lord." In your letters, however, you tell us that you have greatly sought rest. But after this you show that you have come properly to the pastoral care, since, just as the place of government must be denied to those who desire it, so it must be offered to those who flee from it. And as it is written: "No man takes this honour to himself, but he who is called by God, as Aaron was." And again the same outstanding preacher says: "If one died for all, then all have died; and Christ died for all, so that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for him who died for them and rose again." And to the pastor of the holy Church it is said: "Simon, son of John, do you love me? Feed my sheep." From these words it is gathered that if a man who is able to feed the sheep of Almighty God rightly shows that he does not love the chief Shepherd, [he is in error]. For if the Only-begotten of the Father, to accomplish the benefit of all, went forth from the Father's bosom into our public life, what are we to say if we put our own privacy before the advantage of our neighbours? Rest, therefore, must be sought by us from the heart, and yet for the gain of many it must sometimes be set aside. For just as we ought with all our desire to flee from business, so if there is no one to preach, the free man must of necessity bear the burden of the office on his shoulders.

units.la: Ioannis Episcopi: mirum est] (marginal glosses are not separately legible on this scan) necesse est humero subire. Quod ex duorum Prophetarum opere docemur, quorum vnus prædicationis officium vitare conatus est, & alter appetiit. Nam mittenti se Domino Hieremias respondit dicens: A, a, a, Domine Deus nescio loqui, quia puer ego sum. Et cum omnipotens Deus personam ad prædicandum quæreret, dicens: Quem mittam & quis ibit ex vobis? vltro se Esaias obtulit dicens: Ecce ego, mitte me. En ab vtrisque exterius diuersa vox prodiit, sed non à diuerso fonte dilectionis emanauit. Duo quippe sunt præcepta caritatis, Dei videlicet amor, & proximi. Per actiuam igitur vitam prodesse proximis cupiens Esaias, officium prædicationis appetiit; per contemplatiuam vero Hieremias amori conditoris sui sedulo inhærere desiderans, ne mitti ad prædicandum debeat, contradicit. Quod ergo laudabiliter vnus appetiit, hoc laudabiliter alter expauit. Iste ne tacitæ considerationis lucra loquendo perderet; ille damna studiosi operis tacendo sentiret. Sed hoc in vtrisque est subtiliter intuendum; quia & is qui recusauit, plene non restitit, & is qui mitti voluit, ante se per altaris calculum purgatum vidit; ne aut non purgatus adire quisquam sacra ministeria audeat, aut quem superna gratia elegit, sub humilitatis specie superbe contradicat. Magno autem desiderio vos in epistolis vestris inuenio serenitatem mentis quærere, & repulsa perturbatione ad tranquillitatem cogitationis anhelare. Sed qua ratione ad hoc vestra fraternitas pertingere possit, ignoro. Qui enim regendam nauem suscipit, tanto amplius necesse est vigilet, quanto amplius littus relinquit; vt aliquando futuras procellas ex signis prævideat, aliquando venientes aut directo clauo si prauæ sint superet, aut si vehementer intumescunt, dato in obliquum latere irruentes declinet; & sæpe solus vigilet, cum cuncti illi quibus nulla nauis cura commissa est, quiescunt. Quomodo autem suscepto pastorali onere habere serenitatem cogitationum potestis, cum scriptum sit: Ecce gigantes gemunt sub aquis? Iuxta Ioannis etenim vocem, aquæ populi sunt. Et gigantes sub aquis gemere est, quia quisquè in hoc mundo quasi corporis mole, ordine potestatis excreuerit, tanto pondera maioris tribulationis sentit, quanto super se regendorum populorum curam susceperit. Si sancti Spiritus virtus afflictam mentem afflauerit, protinus hoc quod Israelitico populo corporaliter factum est, nobis spiritaliter contingit. Scriptum quippe est: Filij Israel ambulauerunt per siccum & medium mare. Et per Prophetam Dominus pollicetur dicens: Cum transieris per aquas, tecum ero, & flumina non operient te. Illos enim flumina operiunt, quos actiones huius seculi mentis perturbatione confundunt. Nam qui sancti Spiritus gratiam tenet in mente, transit aquas, & tamen fluminibus non operitur; quia etiam inter medias populorum turmas sic peragit gressus sui itineris, vt non submittat actionibus seculi caput mentis. Ego quoq; qui indignus ad locum regiminis veni, infirmitatis meæ conscius, secretiora loca petere aliquando decreueram: sed superna mihi iudicia aduersarii conspiciens, iugo conditoris subdidi ceruicem cordis; hoc præcipue perpendens, quia quælibet occulta loca sine Dei gratia animam saluare non possunt; quod aliquando in ipsis quoq; conspicimus errantibus electorum. Nam Lot in ipsa peruersa ciuitate fuit iustus, in monte peccauit. Sed ista cur dicimus, cum maiora nouerimus? Quid enim Paradiso iucundius? Quid cœlo securius? & tamen homo ex Paradiso, & angelus de cœlo peccando cecidit. Illius ergo nobis virtus quærenda est, & gratia postulanda, sine quo nusquam à periculo & culpa, cum quo nusquam sine iustitia esse non possumus. Curandum ergo est vt pertubatio cogitationum non exuperet animum: nam repelli funditus nullatenus potest.
units.tr: John the Bishop: it is remarkable [marginal note; the rest of this gloss is not legible] must bear it on the shoulder. We are taught this from the work of two prophets, one of whom tried to avoid the office of preaching, and the other sought it. For when the Lord sent him, Jeremiah answered, saying: "Ah, ah, ah, Lord God, I cannot speak, for I am a child." And when Almighty God, seeking a person to preach, said: "Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?" Isaiah offered himself without being asked, saying: "Here I am, send me." Behold, from the two of them there came forth outwardly different voices, but they did not flow from a different source of love. For there are two precepts of charity, namely the love of God and the love of neighbour. Isaiah, therefore, desiring to benefit his neighbours through the active life, sought the office of preaching; but Jeremiah, earnestly desiring to cling to the love of his Creator in contemplation, resisted being sent to preach. What one sought with praise, the other feared with praise. The one did not want to lose by speaking the gains of quiet contemplation; the other did not want to feel by silence the losses of diligent work. But in both cases this must be carefully noted: he who refused did not resist completely, and he who wished to be sent saw himself first purified by the live coal from the altar, so that no one would dare to approach the holy ministries unpurified, and so that a man whom heavenly grace has chosen does not proudly contradict under the appearance of humility. But in your letters I find that you seek with great longing serenity of mind, and that after your rejection you pant after tranquillity of thought. But by what method your brotherhood may attain this, I do not know. For he who takes up the steering of a ship must watch the more carefully the more he leaves the shore: so that at times he may foresee future storms from the signs, and at times, when they are coming, either overcome them with the rudder held straight if they are fierce, or, if they swell violently, turn aside by putting the ship's side obliquely to the onrushing waves; and often he alone keeps watch while all those to whom no care of the ship has been entrusted are at rest. But how can you have serenity of thought, having taken up the pastoral burden, since it is written: "Behold, the giants groan beneath the waters"? For according to the word of John, the waters are the peoples. And for giants to groan beneath the waters means that whoever in this world has grown in the bulk of his body, as it were, and in the order of power, feels the weight of greater tribulation in proportion as he has undertaken the care of governing peoples. If the power of the Holy Spirit has breathed upon a troubled mind, straightway what was done bodily for the Israelite people happens to us spiritually. For it is written: "The children of Israel walked through the dry land and the midst of the sea." And through the Prophet the Lord promises, saying: "When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and the rivers shall not overwhelm you." For those are overwhelmed by the rivers whom the affairs of this age confound by disturbance of mind. But he who holds the grace of the Holy Spirit in his mind passes through the waters, and yet is not overwhelmed by the rivers; for even amid the crowds of peoples he so carries on the steps of his journey that he does not bow the head of his mind to worldly affairs. I too, who have come unworthily to the place of government, aware of my weakness, had at one time decided to seek more secret places; but seeing the heavenly judgements of the adversary, I submitted the neck of my heart to the yoke of the Creator, weighing especially this: that no hidden places can save the soul without the grace of God, which we sometimes see even in the erring of the elect. For Lot was just in that perverse city, and he sinned on the mountain. But why do we say these things, when we know greater examples? For what is more delightful than Paradise? What is safer than heaven? And yet man fell from Paradise, and the angel fell from heaven, through sin. Therefore we must seek his strength and ask for his grace, without which we can never be free from danger and fault, and with which we can never be without righteousness. Care must therefore be taken that the disturbance of thoughts does not overcome the mind, for it can by no means be driven out utterly.

units.la: Quisquis enim est in loco regiminis, aliquando necesse est habeat etiam terrena cogitare, & exteriorum quoque curam gerere, vt grex commissus valeat ad ea quæ sibi sunt expleda subsistere. Sed magnopere semper prouidendum est, ne hæc eadem cura modum transeat, vt cum cor licenter admittitur, nimis excrescere non permittatur. Vnde recte per Ezechielem Prophetam dicitur: Sacerdotes caput suum non radant; neq; comam suam nutriant, sed tondentes attondeant capita sua.
units.tr: Whoever is in a place of government must at some time also think about earthly things and bear care for outward matters as well, so that the flock committed to him may be able to stand firm in what is needful for it. But always great foresight must be exercised lest this same care pass its measure, so that when the heart is admitted to it, it is not allowed to grow excessively. Hence it is rightly said through the prophet Ezekiel: "Priests shall not shave their heads, nor let their hair grow long, but they shall trim their heads."

units.la: Quid enim per significationem sunt capilli in capite, nisi cogitationes in mente, qui dum supra cerebrum infatigabiliter oriuntur, curas vitæ ante capite, nisi cogitationes in mente? qui dum supra cerebrum membrorum oriuntur, cuius vitæ præsentis designant, quæ ex sensu negligenti, quia importune aliquando prodeunt, quasi à nobis non sentientibus procedunt. Quia igitur cuncti qui præsunt, habere quidem sollicitudines exteriores debent, nec tamen eis vehementer iucumbere; sacerdotes recte & caput prohibentur radere, & comam nutrire, ut cogitationes carnales de vita subditorum, nec à se funditus amputent, nec rursus ad crescendum nimis relaxent. Vbi & bene dicitur: Tondentes tondeant capita sua: ut videlicet curæ temporalis sollicitudines, & quantum necesse est prodeant, & tamen recidantur citius, ne immoderatius exerescant. Dum igitur & per administratam exteriorem providentiam corporum vita protegitur, & rursus per immoderatam cordis intentio non impeditur, capilli in capite sacerdotis & servantur ut cutem cooperiant, & resecantur ne oculos claudant. Præterea epistolas vestras directas plenas fide suscepimus; atq; omnipotenti Deo gratias agimus, qui incosutilem tunicam desuper contextam, videlicet Ecclesiam suam vicaria confessione fidelium in vnitate gratiæ ab omni erroris scissione custodit, & contra pereuntis mundi, vt ita dicam, tot culparum diluuium, ex multis lignis arcam construit, in qua omnipotentis Dei electi seruentur ad vitam. Nam cum vicissim nobis fidei nostræ confessionem transmittimus, & caritatem nostram erga nos ostendimus; quid aliud in sancta Ecclesia agimus, nisi arcam bitumine linimus; ne vnda erroris intret, & vel spiritales quosq; tanquam homines, vel carnales tanquam animalia occidat? Sed cum sapienter à vobis recta fides prolata sit; restat vt procul dubio debeatis pacem cordium prudentius custodire, propter hoc quod veritas dicit: Habere sal in vobis, & pacem habere inter vos: Et Paulus Apostolus admonet dicens: Solliciti seruare vnitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis: qui rursus ait: Pacem sequimini cum omnibus & sanctimonium Ghtonomiam, fine qua nemo videbit Deum. Quam videlicet pacem tum vobiscum veraciter habebitis; & profani nominis superbiam declinetis, iuxta quod idem magister gentium dicit: O Timothee depositum custodi, deuitans profanas vocum nouitates. Nimis quippe iniquum est, si hi qui praedicatores humilitatis facti sunt, de vani nominis elatione glorientur, cum verus praedicator dicat: Mihi autem absit gloriari, nisi in cruce Domini nostri Iesu Christi. Ille ergo vere gloriosus est, qui non de temporali potentia, sed pro Christi nomine de sua passione gloriatur. In hoc itaque vos medullitus amplectimur. In hoc sacerdotes vos esse recognoscimus, si repulsa vanitate verborum, sanctitatis locum cum sancta humilitate teneatis. Ecce enim in hefandi appellatione nominis scandalizari sumus, & non minimas querelas seruamus in mente, & promittimus in voce. Vestra autem fraternitas nouit, quia veritas dicit: si offers munus tuum ad altare, & ibi recordatus fueris, quia frater tuus habet aliquid aduersum te: relinque ibi munus tuum, & vade prius reconciliari fratri tuo, & tunc veniens offeres munus tuum. Quapropter re pensandum est, quia cum omnis culpa oblato sacrificio deleatur, tantum est malum scandali alieno corde generati, ut ab eo qui peccauerit, hoc ipsum sacrificium Dominus accipiat, quod delere peccatum solet. Curate ergo cordis vestri scandalum festine detegere, ut possit omnipotens Deus oblationis vestrae sacrificium acceptabile habere. Praeterea cum recta a vobis fides veraciter & subtiliter sit prolata, inter eos, quos per sanctissimas generales Synodos damnandos esse censuistis, Eudoxium quendam vos damnasse reperimus: cuius nomen in Latina lingua neque in synodis, neque in libris beatae memoriae Episcoporum Epiphanii, Augustini, & Philastrii, quos contra haereticos praecipue disputasse nouimus, positum reperimus. Quod si quis eum veraciter de catholicis patribus damnat, eius procul dubio sententiam sequimur. Vos tamen si in synodica vestra Epistola eos quoque damnare nominatim voluistis, qui extra sanctas synodos per patrum scripta damnantur, multo scriptis suis vestra fraternitas minus polluit; si autem eos, quos generales synodi recipiunt, hunc unum amplius. Sed inter haec sciendum est, quia ut nobis liceat rectam fidem libere fateri, & cuncta quae agenda sunt, concorditer in pace disponere, pro serenissimorum Dominorum vita, propria quoque sobole incessanter orandum est, ut omnipotens Deus eorum pedibus barbaras nationes subiiciat, longa eis & felicia tempora concedat, quatenus per Christianum imperium ea quae in Christo est fides, regnent.
units.tr: For what are the hairs on the head, in the figurative sense, but the thoughts of the mind? As they grow without ceasing above the brain, so the cares of this present life spring up, as it were without our noticing, because they break out at unwelcome moments. Since therefore all who rule ought to have outward cares, yet must not be deeply absorbed in them, priests are rightly forbidden both to shave the head and to let the hair grow, so that they neither cut off carnal thoughts about the lives of their subjects entirely nor let them grow too freely. And well is it said: Shearing, let them shear their heads, that is, the anxieties of temporal care should appear as far as necessary, yet be cut back quickly, lest they grow up immoderately. Thus, while the life of the body is protected by the outward care that is administered, and the heart is not hindered by an immoderate attention, the hairs on the priest's head are both kept, to cover the skin, and trimmed, so that they do not close the eyes. Moreover, we have received your letters, sent to us full of faith, and we give thanks to almighty God, who keeps his Church, the seamless tunic woven from above, in the unity of grace through the vicarious confession of the faithful, free from every tear of error, and who, against the deluge of sins that overwhelms the passing world, builds an ark of many planks, in which the elect of almighty God are preserved to life. For when in turn we send to you the confession of our faith and show our love towards you, what else do we do in holy Church but smear the ark with pitch, so that the wave of error may not enter and slay those who are spiritual as men, or those who are carnal as beasts? But since you have wisely set forth the right faith, it remains that you should, beyond doubt, keep the peace of hearts more prudently, because the truth says: Have salt in yourselves, and have peace among yourselves. And the Apostle Paul admonishes, saying: Be eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace; and again he says: Follow peace with all men, and holiness [ἁγιασμόν], without which no one shall see God. Indeed, you will truly keep this peace with us, and you will avoid the pride of a profane name, in accordance with what the same teacher of the Gentiles says: O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane novelties of words. For it is exceedingly unjust if those who have become preachers of humility boast of the exaltation of an empty name, when the true preacher says: But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ. He therefore is truly glorious who glories not in temporal power but, for the name of Christ, in his own suffering. In this, then, we embrace you from the heart. In this we acknowledge you to be priests, if, having rejected the vanity of words, you hold the place of holiness with holy humility. For behold, we are scandalized by the hateful use of that name, and we keep no small complaints in our mind, while we make promises with our voice. Your brotherhood, however, knows that the truth says: If thou offer thy gift at the altar, and there thou remember that thy brother hath anything against thee: leave there thy offering before the altar, and go first to be reconciled to thy brother, and then coming thou shalt offer thy gift. Wherefore it must be weighed that, since every sin is blotted out by the offering of a sacrifice, the evil of scandal generated in another's heart is so great that the Lord accepts from the one who has sinned this very sacrifice which usually blots out sin. Take care, therefore, to lay bare quickly the scandal of your heart, so that almighty God may find the sacrifice of your offering acceptable. Furthermore, since the right faith has been set forth by you truly and carefully, we find that among those whom you judged should be condemned by the most holy general Synods, you have condemned a certain Eudoxius; his name we find placed neither in the Synods nor in the books of the blessed bishops of memory, Epiphanius, Augustine and Philastrius, whom we know to have disputed especially against heretics. If anyone truly condemns him among the Catholic Fathers, we beyond doubt follow his judgment. Yet if in your synodal letter you wished to condemn by name also those who are condemned outside the holy Synods through the writings of the Fathers, your brotherhood is the less defiled by his writings; but if those whom the general Synods receive, then this one more. But in the meantime it must be known that, so that we may be free to confess the right faith and to arrange in peace, in harmony, all the things that are to be done, prayer must also be offered without ceasing for the life of the most serene Lords and for their own offspring, that almighty God may subject barbarous nations under their feet, grant them long and happy times, so that through the Christian empire they may reign, the faith which is in Christ.

units.la: EPISTOLA XXIIII.
units.tr: EPISTLE XXIV.

units.la: De Cyriaco Episcopo Constantinopolitano, & profano vocabulo Vniuersalis, quo temere vtebatur.
units.tr: Concerning Cyriacus, Bishop of Constantinople, and the profane term "Universal", which he used rashly.

units.la: ANASTASIO Episcopo Antiocheno. Desideratam suauissimae vestrae sanctitatis epistolam communi filio meo Sabiniano Diacono deferente suscepi, in qua non linguae sed animae verba profluebant. Et non mirum si bene loquitur, qui perfecte viuit. Quia enim per magistrum Spiritum in schola cordis per praecepta vitae didicistis terrena cuncta despicere, ad caelestem patriam festinare; quantum vos in bono profecistis, tantum bona etiam de aliis sentitis. Dum vero in scriptis vestrae beatitudinis multa de me dici laudabilia audirem, intellexi studium, quia commemorare voluistis non quid sum, sed quid esse debeam. Illud vero quod me dicitis motum membrorum debere reminisci, & maligno spiritui quaerenti animas cribrare pro nulla causa locum dare; ego quidem me semper malis moribus fuisse recolo, atque eosdem in me mores si possum vincere ac delere, summopere festino. Si tamen, ut vos creditis, aliquid boni habui in omnipotentis Dei adiutorio confido, quia oblitus non sum. Sed sanctitas vestra, ut video, in praemissis verbis dulcedinis, & subsequenti hoc verbo epistolam suam api esse similem voluit, quae mel simul & aculeum portat, ut me & melle satiaret, & aculeo pungeret. Sed inter haec ego ad meditandam Salomonis vocem redeo, quia meliora sunt vulnera diligentis, quam inimici blandientis oscula. Quod vero dicitis pro nulla causa dare nos locum scandalo debere, haec mihi & piissimus Dominus filius noster, pro cuius vita incessanter orandum est, iam saepius scripsit, & quod ille ex potestate, scio quia hoc vos ex amore dicitis. Nec miratus sum vos in vestris epistolis impetialia verba posuisse, quia habent inter se maximam cognationem amor & potestas. Nam utraque principaliter praesunt, utraque per auctoritatem semper loquuntur. Et quidem in suscipienda fratris & consacerdotis nostri Cyriaci synodica epistola dignum non fuit, ut pro causa profani vocabuli moras facerem, ne vnitatem sanctae Ecclesiae perturbarem: Sed tamen de eodem superstitioso & superbo eum admonere studui, dicens: quia pacem habere nobiscum non posset, nisi elationem praedicti verbi corrigeret, quam primus apostata inuenit. Vos tamen eadem causam nullam esse dicere non debetis, quia si hanc aequanimiter portamus, vniuersae Ecclesiae fidem corrumpimus. Scitis enim quanti non solum haeretici, sed etiam haeresiarchae de Constantinopolitana Ecclesia sunt egressi. Et ut de honoris vestri iniuria taceam, si vnus Episcopus vocatur Vniversalis, vniuersa Ecclesia corruit, si vnus vniuersus cadit. Sed absit haec stultitia. abiit haec leuitas absque uiribus meis. In omnipotenti autem Domino confido, quia quod promisit, citius implerurus est. Omnis qui se exaltat, humiliabitur. Haec occupatus in multis ad Epistolarum vestrarum dicta in breuitate respondi. Nam quae modo loqui per scripta non debeo, in animo signata manent. Peto vt me beatitudo vestra in suis sanctis orationibus semper ad memoriam reducat, quatenus a malis me temporalibus & aeternis vestrae intercessiones eripiant. Pro serenissimo autem Domino Imperatore studiose & feruenter orate, quia valde est eius vita mundo necessaria. Cesso autem amplius dicere, quia & vos non dubitatis scire.
units.tr: To Anastasius, Bishop of Antioch. I received your longed-for letter, which my fellow son Sabinianus, the deacon, brought, and in it the words flowed not from the tongue but from the soul. It is no wonder that he speaks well who lives well. For since, under the Spirit as teacher, in the school of the heart, you have learned through the precepts of life to despise all earthly things and to hasten toward the heavenly homeland, so far as you have advanced in good, so far also do you think well of others. When I heard in your blessed writing that many praiseworthy things were said about me, I understood your zeal, for you wished to recall not what I am but what I ought to be. As to what you say, that I should remember the movements of my limbs and should in no case give place to the evil spirit who seeks to sift souls, I indeed recall that I have always been of bad morals, and I hasten greatly to conquer and blot out these same morals in myself as far as I can. Yet if, as you believe, I have any good in me, I trust in the help of almighty God that I have not forgotten it. But your holiness, as I see, wished in the preceding words of sweetness, and in the word that follows, that your letter should be like a bee, which carries honey and a sting together, so that it might both satisfy me with honey and prick me with the sting. Yet in the meantime I return to ponder the saying of Solomon, that the wounds of a lover are better than the deceitful kisses of an enemy. As to what you say, that we must give no place to scandal in any cause, this our most pious lord and son, for whose life we must pray without ceasing, has already written to me many times, and I know that he says this from power, and you say it from love. Nor was I surprised that in your letters you used imperious words, since love and power have a very close kinship. For both preside in chief, and both always speak with authority. And indeed, in receiving the synodal letter of our brother and fellow priest Cyriacus, it was not fitting that I should delay for the sake of the profane term, lest I disturb the unity of the holy Church. Yet I took care to admonish him about that same superstitious and proud term, saying that he could not have peace with us unless he corrected the arrogance of that word, which the first apostate invented. Yet you ought not to say that there is no cause for this, since if we bear it calmly we corrupt the faith of the whole Church. For you know how many not only heretics but even heresiarchs have gone out from the Church of Constantinople. And to say nothing of the injury to your own honour: if one bishop is called Universal, the whole Church falls, if the one who is universal falls. But far be this folly, far be this levity, from me, without my strength. I trust in the almighty Lord, however, that He will sooner fulfil what He has promised. Whoever exalts himself will be humbled. Occupied with many matters, I have briefly answered the points of your letters. For what I ought not now to say in writing remains sealed in my mind. I ask that your blessedness, in your holy prayers, always keep me in remembrance, so that your intercessions may rescue me from evils both temporal and eternal. Pray earnestly and fervently for our most serene lord the Emperor, for his life is very necessary to the world. I cease to say more, since you too do not doubt to know it.

units.la: EPISTOLA XXVIII.
units.tr: EPISTOLA XXVIII.

units.la: De submouendo profano vocabulo, vt pax Ecclesiæ conseruetur, & scandala multorum auferantur.
units.tr: On removing the profane term, so that the peace of the Church may be preserved and the scandals of many may be taken away.

units.la: CYRIACO Episcopo Constantinopolitano. Scripta beatitudinis vestræ suscepimus, quæ nobis non linguæ, sed animæ verba loquebantur. Aperiebant enim mentem, quæ tamen mihi clausa non erat, quia per memetipsum suauitatis ipsius experimentum tenebam. Vnde omnipotenti Deo incessanter gratias refero, quia si erga nos in corde vestro virtutum mater charitas permanet, bonorum operum ramos nunquam amittitis, qui ipsam bonitatis radicem tenetis. Oportet ergo vt mihi atque omnibus fratribus vestris eiusdem charitatis pulchritudinem in hoc primum opere monstretis, vt verbum superbiæ, per quod grave scandalum in Ecclesiis generatur, auferre festinetis, hoc modis omnibus implentes, quod scriptum est: Sollicti seruare vnitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis. Et rursus: Nullam occasionem dare aduersario maledicti gratia. Tunc enim ostensa charitas vera est, si per typhum superbiæ inter nos schisma non fuerit. Ego eiam Iesum testem invoco in anima mea, quia a summo vsque ad vltimum nulli hominum dare scandali occasionem volo. Omnes magnos esse, & honorabiles cupio, quorum tamen honor, honori omnipotentis Dei non detrahat: nam quisquis se contra Deum honorari appetit, mihi honorabilis non est. Sed vt cognoscatis quam erga vestram beatitudinem habeam voluntatem, dilectissimum filium meum Anatholium Diaconum ad piissimorum Dominorum vestigia transmisi, qui eorum pietati ac vestræ fraternitati satisfaciat, quia nulli in hac causa nocere appeto, sed humilitatem Deo placitam, & Sanctæ Ecclesiæ concordiam custodire. Et quia hostis omnipotentis Dei Antichristus iuxta est, studiose cupio ne proprium quid inueniat non solum in moribus, sed etiam nec in vocabulo sacerdotum. Ea ergo, quæ nouo modo introducta sunt, ipso ordine quo illata sunt, auferantur, & pax nobis illibata in Domino permanebit.
units.tr: To Cyriacus, Bishop of Constantinople. We have received the writings of your Blessedness, which spoke to us not with words but with the heart. They revealed your mind, which was not in fact closed to me, since I already knew the sweetness of it from my own experience. For this reason I give unceasing thanks to almighty God, because if the charity which is the mother of virtues remains towards us in your heart, you will never lose the branches of good works, since you hold the very root of goodness. It is therefore fitting that you show to me and to all your brethren the beauty of this same charity, first in this matter, by hastening to remove the word of pride through which grave scandal is generated in the Churches, and so in every way fulfilling what is written: Be eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. And again: Give the adversary no occasion to speak reproachfully. For then our charity is shown to be true, if no schism arises among us through the pride of arrogance. I also call Jesus to witness in my soul that I wish to give no occasion of scandal to any man, from the highest to the lowest. I desire that all should be great and honoured, yet let their honour not detract from the honour of almighty God; for whoever seeks to be honoured against God is not honourable to me. But so that you may know the goodwill I bear towards your Blessedness, I have sent my most beloved son, the deacon Anatolius, to the feet of your most pious Lords, to satisfy their piety and your brotherhood, since I desire to harm no one in this cause, but to keep the humility pleasing to God and the concord of the Holy Church. And since Antichrist, the enemy of almighty God, is near, I earnestly desire that he find nothing of his own, not only in morals but not even in the title of the priests. Therefore let those things which have been introduced in a new way be removed in the same order in which they were brought in, and peace will remain unbroken among us in the Lord.

units.la: Nam quæ erit inter nos dulcedo, quæ caritas, si nosmetipsos voce refouemus, & rebus pungimur? Hoc ergo vestra Sanctitas agat, vt bona quæ dicitis, non in cordis medulla sentiamus, quatenus dum in vnanimitate corda fuerint sacerdotum, pro piissimorum Dominorum vita desperantes tanto citius exaudire mereamur, quanto & orationes vestras ante Dei oculos pax illuminat, & discordiæ macula non obscurat.
units.tr: For what sweetness or what charity can there be between us if we cherish ourselves with words while we are pricked by deeds? Let your Holiness therefore see to it that we do not feel in the marrow of our hearts the good things you say, so that, while the hearts of the priests are united in one accord, we may deserve to be heard all the sooner for the life of our most pious Lords, despairing of nothing, since peace illumines your prayers before the eyes of God and the stain of discord does not darken them.

units.la: EPISTOLA XXX.
units.tr: LETTER XXX.

units.la: Defendit se temere indiscretum nominatum fuisse, quod Cyriacum Episcopum Constantinopolitanum, qui Vniuersalem se nominabat, reprehenderit.
units.tr: He defends himself against being called rashly indiscreet for having rebuked Cyriacus, Bishop of Constantinople, who styled himself Universal.

units.la: MAVRITIO AVGVSTO. Dominorum pietas prouida ne quid fortasse scandali in vnitate sanctæ Ecclesiæ ex sacerdotum dissensione generari potuisset, semel ac bis me admonere dignata est, vt responsales fratris & Consacerdotis mei Cyriaci benigne suscipererem, eaque ad remeandum citius relaxarem. Et licet piissime Domine apte & prouide cuncta præcipiatis, ego tamen inuenio quia eorum iudicio indiscretus esse ex hac tali admonitione reprehendor. Nunquid nam ex profano ac superbo vocabulo meus non in modico est animus vulneratus, tantæ indiscretionis esse potui, vt nescirem quid vnitati fidei, quid concordiæ Ecclesiasticæ deberem, & fratris mei responsales & synodicam epistolam suscipere cuiuslibet causæ amaritudine interuenientè recusarem? Absit hoc. Nimis mihi fuerat desipuisse, sic sapere. Aliud namque est quod conseruandæ vnitatis fidei, atque aliud quod debemus comprimendæ elationi. Distinguenda ergo erant tempora, ne prædicti fratris mei ex quolibet articulo charitatis turbaretur. Vnde & Responsales eius cum magno affectu suscepi, quicquid debui charitatis exhibui, meliusque eos quam consuetudo prisca fuerat honoraui, & mecum feci eos sacra missarum solennia celebrare, quia sicut meus Diaconus ad exhibenda sancta mysteria illi non debet ministrare, qui elationis culpam aut commisit aut commissam ab aliis ipse non corrigit, ita ministri illius in celebratione missarum mihi adesse debuerunt, qui custodiente Deo, in superbiæ errorem non cecidi. Eundem vero fratrem & consacerdotem meum studiose admonere, curaui, vt si habere pacem omnium concordiamq; desiderat, ab stulti vocabuli se appellatione compescat. De qua re mihi in suis iussionibus Dominorum pietas præcepit dicens; vt pro appellatione friuoli nominis inter nos scandalum generari non debeat. Sed rogo vt Imperialis pietas penseт, quia alia sunt friuola valde innoxia, atq; alia vehementer nociua. Nunquid non cum se Antichristus veniens Deum dixerit, friuolum valde erit, sed tamen nimis perniciosum? Si quantitatem sermonis attendimus, duæ sunt syllabæ; si vero pondus iniquitatis, vniuersa pernicies. Ego autem fidenter dico, quia quisquis se Vniuersalem sacerdotem vocat, vel vocari desiderat, in elatione sua Antichristum præcurrit, quia superbiendo se ceteris præponit. Nec dispari superbia ad errorem ducitur; quia sicut peruersus ille, Deus videri vult super omnes homines; ita quisquis iste est, qui solus sacerdos appellari appetit, super ceteros sacerdotes se extollit. Sed quoniam veritas dicit: Omnis qui se exaltat, humiliabitur, scio quia quælibet elatio tanto citius rumpitur, quanto amplius influitur. Illis ergo pietas vestra præcipiat, ne quod per appellationem friuoli nominis scandalum gignant, quiin superbiæ typhum ceciderunt. Nam peccator ego, qui auctore Deo humilitatem teneo, admonendus ad humilitatem non sum. Omnipotens autem Deus serenissimi Domini nostri vitam & ad pacem Sanctæ Ecclesiæ, & ad vtilitatem reipublicæ Romanæ per tempora longa custodiat. Certi enim sumus, quia si vos viuitis, qui cœli Dominum timetis, nulla contra veritatem superba prævalere permittetis.
units.tr: TO MAURICE AUGUSTUS. The providence of my most pious lords has deigned twice to admonish me, lest any scandal arise from the disagreement of the priests against the unity of the holy Church, that I should kindly receive the representatives of my brother and fellow priest Cyriacus, and dismiss them quickly so they might return. And although, most pious Lords, you order all things wisely and providently, I find that in your judgement I am reproved as indiscreet for this admonition. Can it be that my mind, not a little wounded by this profane and proud title, could have been so lacking in discretion that I did not know what I owed to the unity of the faith and the concord of the Church, and, through some bitterness arising from the quarrel, refused to receive my brother's representatives and the synodal letter? Far from it. It would have been too foolish of me to be so wise. For one thing is what we must keep in the unity of the faith, and another is what we must do to restrain pride. The times therefore had to be distinguished, lest my said brother be disturbed over some point of charity. So I received his representatives with great affection, showed them every courtesy of charity, and honoured them more than the old custom had required; and I had them celebrate the solemn rites of the Mass with me. For just as my deacon ought not to minister in the holy mysteries to one who has either committed the fault of pride or does not correct it when committed by others, so his ministers ought to be present with me at the celebration of the Masses, since, by God's keeping, I have not fallen into the error of pride. I took care, moreover, to admonish that same brother and fellow priest of mine earnestly, that if he desires peace and concord with all, he should refrain from the use of that foolish title. On this matter your pious Lordships, in your orders to me, have instructed that for the sake of a frivolous name no scandal should arise between us. But I ask that Your Imperial piety weigh the fact that some frivolities are quite harmless, while others are exceedingly harmful. Will not the frivolity be great, yet at the same time most pernicious, when the coming Antichrist calls himself God? If we consider the length of the word, it has two syllables; but if we weigh its iniquity, it is a total ruin. I say with confidence that whoever calls himself, or desires to be called, the Universal Priest, in his pride runs ahead of Antichrist, since by exalting himself he sets himself above the others. Nor is it by a lesser pride that he is led into error; for just as that perverse one wishes to be seen as God above all men, so whoever he is who seeks to be called the sole priest raises himself above the other priests. But since the truth says: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, I know that every such elation is broken all the sooner, the more it is inflated. Let your piety therefore instruct those who have fallen into the whirlwind of pride not to cause scandal by means of this frivolous name. For I, a sinner, who by God's guidance hold to humility, have no need to be admonished to humility. May almighty God preserve the life of our most serene Lord for a long time, both for the peace of the holy Church and for the welfare of the Roman commonwealth. For we are certain that if you, who fear the Lord of heaven, are alive, you will permit no proud thing to prevail against the truth.

units.la: EPISTOLA XXXI.
units.tr: EPISTLE XXXI.

units.la: De responsalibus Cyriaci Episcopi in causa fidei admissis. De suo Diacono cum eo non prosequuto. De damnatione Eudoxii sibi incognita. De historia Sozomeni ab Apostolica sede reprobata.
