De anima Ada, quod in peccato mortua est. Dicit quoq; eam per pœnitentiam salvatum. Et quod Diabolus cor hominis ingreditur.
units.tr: On the representatives of Cyriacus, Bishop, admitted in a matter of faith. On his deacon, who was not to join in communion with him. On the condemnation of Eudoxius, unknown to him. On the history of Sozomen, rejected by the Apostolic See. On the soul of Adam, that it died in sin. He also says that it was saved through repentance, and that the Devil enters the heart of man.

units.la: EVLOGIO Episcopo Alexandrino, & Anastasio Episcopo Antiocheno. Charitas qua vobis valde constrictus sum; tacere me minimè permittit, vt sanctitas vestra quæcunq; apud nos aguntur, agnoscat, & falsis rumoribus non decepta, suæ iustitiæ atq; rectitudinis viam, sicut persecte cœpit, perfectius teneat. Responsales siquidem fratris & Coepiscopi nostri Cyriaci venientes, eius ad me synodicam detulerunt epistolam. Et quidem inter nos & ipsum sicut vestra beatitudo nouit, propter appellationem profani nominis est grauis discordia, sed in causa fidei transmissos responsales eius existimaui esse suscipiendos, ne culpa elationis quæ in Constantinopolitana Ecclesia perne contra omnes sacerdotes exorta est, dissensionem fidei & rixam Ecclesiasticæ faceret vnitati. Eosdem vero Responsales, quia hoc omnino humiliter precabantur, missarum solennia mecum celebrare feci, quia sicut & serenissimo Domino Imperatori nostro intimare studui, responsales fratris & consacerdotis nostri Cyriaci mihi communicare debuerunt; quia auctore Deo in elationis errorem non cecidi. Meus vero Diaconus cum prædicto fratre nostro Cyriaco missarum solennia celebrare non debet: quia per profanum vocabulum culpam superbiæ aut commisit, aut sequitur: nec si, quod absit, procedit ei in tali elatione posito, vanitatem stulti nominis confirmare videamur. Eundem vero fratrem admonere studui, vt se à tali elatione corrigat: quia si hanc non correxerit, pacem nobiscum nullo modo habebit. Præterea idem frater noster omnia in suis synodicis catholicè, Deo auctore, locutus est. Quendam vero Eudoxium damnauit, quem neque in synodis damnatum inuenimus, neque à decessoribus eius in suis synodicis reprobatum. Et canones quidem Constantinopolitani Concilii Eudoxianos damnant, sed quis fuerit eorum auctor Eudoxius, minimè dicunt. Romana autem Ecclesia eosdem canones vel gesta synodi illius hactenus non habet, nec accipit: in hoc autem eandem synodum accepit, quod est per eam contra Macedonium definitum. Reliquas vero hæreses quæ illic memoratæ sunt, ab aliis tam patribus damnatas reprobat. De Eudoxianis vero nihil hactenus agnouit. In historia autem Sozomeni de quodam Eudoxio, qui Constantinopolitanæ Ecclesiæ Episcopatum arripuisse dicitur, aliqua narrantur. Sed ipsam quoque historiam sedes Apostolica suscipere recusat, quoniam multa mentitur, & Theodorum Mopsuestiæ nimium laudas.
units.tr: To Eulogius, Bishop of Alexandria, and Anastasius, Bishop of Antioch. My love for you, by which I am greatly bound, does not allow me to remain silent, so that your holiness may learn what is done among us, and, not deceived by false rumours, may hold more perfectly to the path of your justice and uprightness, which you have begun so well. The representatives of our brother and fellow bishop Cyriacus have come and brought me his synodal letter. Indeed, between us and him, as your blessedness knows, there is a serious discord over the use of a profane title. But since his representatives were sent in a matter of faith, I judged that they should be received, lest the fault of pride, which has arisen in the Church of Constantinople against all priests, should turn the dispute over faith and the quarrel into a breach of ecclesiastical unity. Since these same representatives begged me most humbly for this, I have seen to it that they celebrate the solemn rites of the Mass with me. For, as I have also taken care to make known to our most serene lord the Emperor, the representatives of our brother and fellow priest Cyriacus ought to have communion with me, since by the grace of God I have not fallen into the error of arrogance. My deacon, however, must not celebrate the solemn rites of the Mass with that brother of ours, Cyriacus, because by using the profane title he has either committed, or is following, the fault of pride; nor, should he (which God forbid) advance in such an exalted position, would we seem to confirm the vanity of that foolish name. I have taken care to admonish that same brother to correct himself of such arrogance, because if he does not correct it, he will in no way have peace with us. Moreover, this same brother of ours has spoken in all his synodal letters in a catholic manner, by God's guidance. Indeed, he condemned a certain Eudoxius, whom we find neither condemned in the synods nor rejected by his predecessors in their synodal letters. The canons of the Council of Constantinople do condemn the Eudoxian canons, but they do not say who the author of them was, Eudoxius. The Roman Church, however, has not so far had or received those canons or the acts of that synod; yet it has received the same synod in this respect, that what was defined by it against Macedonius is accepted. As for the other heresies mentioned there, it rejects them as condemned by the other fathers. Concerning the Eudoxians, however, it has so far acknowledged nothing. In the history of Sozomen, some things are related about a certain Eudoxius who is said to have seized the episcopate of the Church of Constantinople. But the Apostolic See itself refuses to accept that history, since it tells many lies and praises Theodore of Mopsuestia too highly.

units.la: EPISTOLÆ.
units.tr: EPISTLES.

units.la: laudat, atque vsque ad diem obitus sui magnum doctorem Ecclesiæ fuisse perhibet. Restat ergo vt si quis illam historiam recipit, synodo, quæ piæ memoriæ Iustiniani temporibus de tribus capitulis facta est contradicat. Qui vero huic contradicere non valet, illam historiam necesse est vt repellat. In latina vero lingua de hoc Eudoxio nunc vsque neque in Philastro, neque in beato Augustino, qui multa de hæresibus conscripserunt, neque in aliis patribus aliquid inuenimus. Charitas igitur vestra, si quis apud Græcos probatorum patrum, de eo sermonem fecit, sibi mihi Epistolis monstrefcat. Præterea ante triennium, cogente causa monachorum Isauriæ, qui hæretici accusabantur, satisfaciens mihi quondam frater & consacerdos meus Dominus Ioannes literas misit, quibus nitebatur ostendere eos Ephesinæ synodi diffinitionibus contradixisse, & velut ex eadem synodo certa nobis, quibus ipsi obsisterent, capitula destinauit. Inter alia autem scriptum illic continebatur de Ade anima, quia in peccato mortua non fuerit, eo quod Diabolus in cor hominis non ingrediatur, & si quis hoc dixisset, anathema esset. Quæ cum mihi relecta fuissent, valde contristatus sum.
units.tr: He praises him, and maintains that he was a great teacher of the Church up to the day of his death. It follows, then, that whoever accepts that history must contradict the synod held in the time of Justinian of blessed memory concerning the Three Chapters. But whoever cannot contradict that synod must necessarily reject the history. In the Latin language, however, we have found nothing about this Eudoxius up to now, neither in Philastrius nor in blessed Augustine, who wrote much about heresies, nor in any other Fathers. Therefore, if any approved Father among the Greeks has written about him, let your Charity show me this by letter. Moreover, three years ago, when the case of the monks of Isauria, who were accused of heresy, required it, my former brother and fellow priest, Lord John, satisfied me by sending letters in which he tried to show that they had contradicted the decisions of the Synod of Ephesus. As if from that same synod, he sent me certain articles to which they were opposed. Among other things, there was written there concerning Adam's soul that it "was not dead in sin, because the Devil does not enter into the heart of man, and if anyone said this, he would be anathema." When these were read back to me, I was very distressed.

units.la: Si enim Adæ, qui primus peccauit, anima in peccato mortua non est, quomodo de ligno vetito illi dictum est: In quacunque die comederitis ex eo, morte moriemini? Et certe comedit Adam & Eua de ligno vetito, & tamen in carne suo vltra nongentos annos postmodum vixerunt. Constat itaque quia in carne non est mortuus. Si ergo in anima mortuus non est, quod dici nefas est, falsam sententiam de illo protulit Deus qui dixit, quia qua die comederet, moreretur. Sed absit hic error, absit à vera fide. Nos enim primum hominem, qua die peccauit, anima mortuum dicimus, atq; per hunc omne genus humanum in hac mortis & corruptionis pœna damnatum. Per secundum vero hominem & modo à morte animæ, & postmodum ab omni corruptione carnis in æterna resurrectione liberari nos posse confidimus.
units.tr: For if the soul of Adam, who first sinned, is not dead in sin, how is it that the words were spoken to him about the forbidden tree: "In whatever day you eat of it, you shall surely die"? And certainly Adam and Eve ate of the forbidden tree, and yet they lived afterwards in the flesh for more than nine hundred years. It is clear, then, that he did not die in the flesh. If, therefore, he did not die in the soul, which is impious to say, then God, who said that on the day he ate he would die, pronounced a false sentence about him. But far be this error, far be it from the true faith. For we say that the first man, on the day he sinned, died in soul, and through him the whole human race was condemned to this penalty of death and corruption. Through the second man, we trust that we can be freed both now from the death of the soul, and afterwards from all corruption of the flesh in the eternal resurrection.

units.la: Sic autem & prædictis Responsalibus diximus: Adæ animam in peccatis mortuam dicimus, non à substantia viuendi, sed à qualitate viuendi. Quia enim aliud est substantia, atq; aliud qualitas, non est eius anima ita mortua, vt non esset; sed ita mortua vt beata non esset. Qui tamen Adam postmodum per pœnitentiam ad vitam rediit. Quod vero Diabolus cor hominis ingrediatur, si Euangelio creditur non negatur. Ibi enim scriptum est: Et post buccellam introiuit in eum Satbanas.
units.tr: Indeed, we also said in the aforementioned replies: we say that Adam's soul was dead in sins, not with respect to its substance of living, but with respect to its quality of living. For since substance is one thing and quality another, his soul was not so dead that it did not exist, but so dead that it was not blessed. Yet Adam afterwards returned to life through repentance. As for the Devil entering the heart of man, this is not denied, if we believe the Gospel. For there it is written: "And after the morsel, Satan entered into him."

units.la: Et rursus ibi dicitur: Cum Diabolus iam misisset in cor Iudæ, vt traderet eum Iudæ. Hoc autem qui negat in Pelagianam hæresim cadit. Quia ergo perscrutantes Ephesinam synodum, nihil in ea tale inuenimus contineri, de Rauennati quoq; Ecclesia vetustum valde Codicem eiusdem synodi ad nos deferri fecimus, & synodo quam habemus, eum ita concordare inuenimus, vt in nullo discreparet, & nihil aliud contineret in definitione anathematis & reprobationis, nisi quod duodecim capitula beatæ memoriæ Cyrilli reprobant. Hanc autem totam rationem multo latius subtiliusq; prædictis Responsalibus eius in præsenti positis reddidimus, atque ei plenissime satisfecimus.
units.tr: And again there it is said: "When the Devil had already put it into the heart of Judas to betray him." But whoever denies this falls into the Pelagian heresy. Therefore, since we carefully examined the Synod of Ephesus and found nothing of this kind contained in it, we had a very old codex of the same synod brought to us from the Church of Ravenna as well. We found that it agrees with the synod we have so closely that it differs in nothing, and contains in its definition of anathema and rejection nothing other than the rejection of the twelve chapters of blessed Cyril of memory. We have set out this whole reasoning far more widely and subtly in the replies aforementioned, now placed before him, and we have fully satisfied him.

units.la: Igitur ne vel hæc, vel alia similia illic surrepant, quæ sanctam Ecclesiam scandalizent, necesse nobis fuit hæc ipsa sanctitati vestræ indicare. Et quamuis fratrem & coepiscopum nostrum Cyriacum nouerimus orthodoxum, tamen propter alios cauti esse debemus, vt antequam ad publicum prodeant, errorum semina concülcentur. Scripta autem vestræ sanctitatis communi filio Sabiniano Diacono veniente suscepi. Sed quia harum lator iam ad egrediendum paratus retineri non potuit, ad hæc responsali meo Diacono veniente respondebo.
units.tr: Therefore, so that neither these nor other similar things may creep in there and scandalise the holy Church, it was necessary for us to point these very matters out to your holiness. And although we know our brother and fellow bishop Cyriacus to be orthodox, nevertheless we ought to be cautious on account of others, so that the seeds of error may be trampled before they come out into the open. I received your holiness's writings through our common son, the deacon Sabinianus. But since the bearer of these was already prepared to leave and could not be detained, I shall reply to these when my deacon, my messenger, arrives.

units.la: REGESTI LIB. VII. EPIST. XI.
units.tr: REGESTI LIB. VII. EPIST. XI.

units.la: Delege Imperatoris, & quod ex militari habitu nullus nisi ante triennium probatus, suscipiendus sit.
units.tr: Concerning the Emperor's law, and that no one who has served in the army should be received unless he has first been tested for three years.

units.la: Eusebio Thessalonicensi; Urbicio Diracitano, Constantino Mediolanensi, & Andreæ Nicopoli, Ioanni Corinthi, Ioanni primæ Iustinianæ, Ioanni Cretensi Scoritano, Ioanni Larissæ Mariano Rauennæ, Ioanni Caralitano Sardiniæ, & omnibus Episcopis Siciliæ. Legem, quam piissimus Imperator dedit, ne fortasse hi qui militiæ vel rationibus sunt publicis obligati, dum causarum suarum periculum fugiunt, ad Ecclesiasticum habitum veniant, vel in monasterium conuertantur, vestræ studui fraternitati transmittere: hoc maxime exhortans, quod hi qui sæculi actionibus implicati sunt, in clero Ecclesiæ præpropere suscipiendi non sunt: quia dum in Ecclesiastico habitu non diff similiter quàm vixerant, viuunt; nequaquam studeant sæculum fugere, sed mutare. Quod si etiam tales quoque monasterium petunt, suscipiendi nullo modo sunt, nisi prius rationibus publicis absoluti fuerint.
units.tr: To Eusebius of Thessalonica; Urbicius of Diracium, Constantine of Milan, Andrew of Nicopolis, John of Corinth, John of Prima Justiniana, John of Crete at Scorita, John of Larissa, Marianus of Ravenna, John of Caralis in Sardinia, and all the bishops of Sicily. I have sent to your brotherhood the law which our most pious Emperor has given, lest perhaps those who are bound to military service or to public accounts, while they flee the danger of their lawsuits, should come to the ecclesiastical habit or be turned into monasteries. I exhort you especially in this, that those who are entangled in the affairs of the world must not be hastily received into the clergy of the Church; for while they live in the ecclesiastical habit without differing at all from how they lived before, they do not seek to flee the world but only to change its guise. And if such men also seek a monastery, they must by no means be received unless they have first been released from public obligations.

units.la: Si qui vero ex militaribus numeribus in monasteriis conuerti festinant, non sunt temere suscipiendi, nisi eorum vita fuerit subtiliter inquisita. Et iuxta normam regularem debent in suo habitu per triennium probari, & tunc monachicum habitum Deo auctore suscipere. Qui si ita sint probati atque suscepti, & pro anima sua pœnitentiam de perpetratis culpis agere studeant, pro eorum vita & lucro cœlesti, non est eorum conuersio renuenda. Qua de re etiam serenissimus & Christianissimus Imperator, mihi credite, omni modo placatur, & libenter eorum conuersionem suscipit, quos in rationibus publicis implicatos non esse cognoscit.
units.tr: If, however, any who serve in the military units hasten to be converted into monasteries, they are not to be received rashly, unless their life has been carefully examined. According to the rule, they ought to be proved for three years in their own habit, and only then to take up the monastic habit, with God's help. If they have been so proved and received, and strive to make satisfaction for their sins committed, for the sake of their soul and their heavenly gain, their conversion is not to be refused. On this matter, too, the most serene and most Christian Emperor, believe me, is in every way pleased, and gladly accepts the conversion of those whom he knows not to be entangled in public accounts.

units.la: EPISTOLA LXX.
units.tr: LETTER LXX.

units.la: Iubet ob superbiam Ioannis Episcopi Constantinopolitani, & Cyriaci qui superbum Vniuersalis nomen usurpabant, ne quisquam in illorum subscriptionibus hanc vocem, Vniuersalis, adjiciat.
units.tr: He orders that, on account of the pride of John, Bishop of Constantinople, and of Cyriacus, who used the proud title of Universal, no one should add the word "Universal" to their signatures.

units.la: Eusebio Thessalonicensi, Vrbico Dirachino, Andreæ Nicopolitano, Ioanni Corinthio, Ioanni primæ Iustinianæ, Ioanni Cretensi, Ioanni Larisseo & Excodicano, aliisque compluribus Episcopis. Suscepti regiminis statura constringimur, officii nostri sollicitudinem vigilanter extendere, & fratrum nostrorum animos sermone admonitionis instruere, vt nec ignorantes præsumptio prava decipere, nec scientes dissimulatio quædam valeat excusare. Cognoscat siquidem fraternitas vestra, Ioannem quondam Constantinopolitanæ ciuitatis Antistitem contra Deum, contra pacem Ecclesiæ in omnium despectu & iniuria sacerdotum, modestiæ ac mensuræ suæ terminos excessisse, & illicite in synodo superbum ac pestiferum Oecumenicum, hoc est, Vniuersalis sibi vocabulum vsurpare. Quod beatæ recordationis Pelagius decessor meus agnoscens, omnia gesta eiusdem synodi, præter illa quæ illic de causa venerandæ memoriæ Gregorii Episcopi Antiocheni sunt habita, valida omnino distinctione cassauit, distinctissima illum increpatione corripiens, vt se a nouo & temerario superstitionis homine cohiberet, adeo vt suum illi Diaconum nisi tantum nefas emendaret, procedere prohiberet.
units.tr: To Eusebius of Thessalonica, Urbicus of Dyrrachium, Andreas of Nicopolis, John of Corinth, John of Prima Justiniana, John of Crete, John of Larissa and Excodicanus, and to several other Bishops. By the standard of the office I have undertaken, I am bound to extend the care of my duty watchfully, and to instruct the minds of our brothers by a word of admonition, so that wicked presumption may not deceive the ignorant, nor a certain dissimulation excuse those who know better. Let your brotherhood know that John, once Bishop of the city of Constantinople, has, against God and against the peace of the Church, and in contempt and injury of all the priests, gone beyond the limits of his modesty and measure, and has unlawfully, in a synod, usurped for himself the proud and pestilent title of Oecumenical, that is, Universal. Pelagius of blessed memory, my predecessor, recognising this, quashed all the acts of that same synod, except those that were transacted there concerning the cause of the venerable Gregory, Bishop of Antioch, by a most emphatic annulment, rebuking him with the sharpest reproof, so that he might restrain himself from being a new and rash man of superstition; and he forbade him to advance so far that he would not correct his own deacon for so great a wickedness.

units.la: Cuius nos rectitudinis Zelo per omnia inhærentes, statuta ipsius sine refragatione Deo protegente seruamus; quia dignum est vt recto decessoris sui viam gressibus inoffensis incedat, quem de eodem loco ad reddendam rationem æterni iudicis tribunal expectat. In quare ne quid omittere, quod ad pacem Ecclesiæ pertinet videremur, nostris tundem sanctissimum Ioannem scriptis semel iterumque conuenimus, vt amoto superbiæ vocabulo cordis sui elationem ad humilitatem quam Magister & Dominus noster docuit, inclinaret. Quem quoniam neglexisse comperimus, hæc eadem & beatissimum fratrem & Consacerdotem nostrum Cyriacum successorem ipsius concordiæ studio non destitimus admonere.
units.tr: Adhering in all things to the zeal of this rectitude, and with God protecting us, we keep his decrees without objection; for it is right that he who awaits the tribunal of the eternal Judge, to render an account from that same place, should walk the path of his predecessor with unfaltering steps. Therefore, lest we should seem to have neglected anything that pertains to the peace of the Church, we have summoned the most holy John by our writings once and again, so that, the name of pride being put aside, he might bend the elation of his heart to the humility which our Master and Lord taught. Since we have found that he has neglected this, we have not ceased, out of zeal for harmony, to admonish the same things to his most blessed brother and fellow priest Cyriacus, his successor.

units.la: Sed quia hoc iam vt videmus, mundi huius termino propinquante, in præcursione sua apparuit humani generis inimicus, vt ipsos qui ei contradicere bene atque humiliter viuendo debuerunt, per hoc superbiæ vocabulum præcursores habeat sacerdotes; hortor atque suadeo vt nullus vestrum hoc nomen aliquando recipiat, nullus consentiat, nullus scribat, nullus vbi fuerit scriptum admittat, vel subscriptionem suam adiuciat; sed sicut omnipotentis Dei ministros decet, integrum se ab huiuscemodi venenata infectione custodiat, & callido insidiatori in se locum non præbeat, quoniam & hoc in totius Ecclesiæ itinerarium ac discissionem, & sicut diximus, in omnium vestrum despectum fiet.
units.tr: But because, as we now see, the enemy of the human race has appeared in his forerunner role, with the end of this world drawing near, so that he may have priests as his forerunners, through this proud title, men who ought to have resisted him by living well and humbly, I urge and advise that none of you ever accept this name, that none consent to it, that none write it, that none admit it wherever it has been written, or add his own signature to it. Rather, as becomes the ministers of almighty God, let each keep himself whole from this kind of poisonous infection, and not give the crafty deceiver any place in himself; for this would also become a path and a division of the whole Church and, as we have said, to the contempt of all of you.

units.la: Nam si vnus, vt putat, vniversalis est, restat vt vos Episcopi non sitis. Præterea peruenit ad nos, quod fraternitas vestra, ad vrbem Constantinopolim sit conuocata. Et quamuis piissimus noster Imperator agi illic illicita non permittat, tamen ne peruersi homines conuentus vestri occasione reperta, aut pro huius nominis superstitione locum surreptionis requirant, aut ob aliam rem facere synodum cogitent; quatenus hoc in ea callidis machinationibus inducant, quamuis sine Apostolicæ sedis auctoritate atque consensu nullas quæcunque acta fuerint vires habeant: veruntamen coram omnipotenti Deo contestor & admoneo, vt nullius vestrum illic quibuslibet blandimentis, quibuslibet præmiis, quibuslibet terroribus tangatur assensus: sed pro æterni iudicii consideratione aduersus praua desideria salubriter atque vnanimiter vos exhibete, & pastorali constantia atque Apostolicæ auctoritate suffulti prædonem irruentem, lupum excludite, & in discissionem Ecclesiæ sæuienti non cedite, nec de hac re quacunque surreptione synodum patiamini, quæ ne legitima quidem, nec synodus dicenda est, celebrari. Hoc quoque pariter admonemus, vt si forte nil actum de huius peruersi nominis mentione fuerit, sed de alia re forte synodus colligitur, omnino sitis cauti, circumspecti, vigilantes atque sollicitи, ne quid illic contra locum aliquem vel personam prætiudicialiter siue illicite, vel aduersus canones censeatur. Sed si quid incidentis vtilitatis causa tractandum est, sic causa de qua agitur formam accipiat, vt statuta vetera nulla conuellat. Vnde iterum, coram Deo & sanctis ipsius admonemus, vt hæc omnia summo studio, & tota mentis intentione seruetis. Nam si quis (quod non credimus) scripta præsentia aliqua in parte neglexerit, a Beati Petri Apostolorum Principis pace se nouerit segregatum. Ita ergo fraternitas vestra agat, vt cum pastor pastorum in iudicio venerit, de loco regiminis quem accepit, reatum habere non possit.
units.tr: For if one man, as he thinks, is universal, it follows that you bishops are not bishops. Moreover, word has reached us that your brotherhood has been summoned to the city of Constantinople. And although our most pious Emperor does not permit unlawful acts to be done there, nevertheless, lest wicked men, seizing the occasion of your gathering, either seek a place for fraud on account of the superstition of this name, or plan to hold a synod for some other reason, so as to lead you into their crafty schemes there, although whatever acts may be done without the authority and consent of the Apostolic See have no force: nevertheless, I call God Almighty to witness and admonish that none of you be moved to assent there by any flatteries, any rewards, or any terrors; but in consideration of the eternal judgment, stand firm against wicked desires, salutarily and unanimously, and supported by pastoral constancy and Apostolic authority, drive out the robber who rushes in, the wolf; and do not yield to him who rages toward the division of the Church, nor suffer a synod to be convened on this matter by any fraud, which ought not to be called lawful, nor even a synod. We likewise admonify this as well: if perhaps nothing has been done concerning the mention of this perverse name, but a synod is gathered perhaps for some other business, you must be altogether cautious, circumspect, watchful, alert and attentive, lest anything there be judged to the prejudice of any place or person, whether unlawfully, or against the canons. But if something useful must be treated on the occasion of what has arisen, let the matter under discussion take such a form that it overturns no ancient statutes. Hence again, before God and his saints, we admonish you to observe all these things with the highest zeal and entire intention of mind. For if anyone (which we do not believe) neglects any part of these present writings, let him know that he has been cut off from the peace of Blessed Peter, Prince of the Apostles. Therefore let your brotherhood so act that, when the shepherd of shepherds comes to judgment, it may be unable to have any guilt concerning the place of rule which it has received.

units.la: REGESTI LIB. XI. EPIST. XLVII.
units.tr: REGESTI LIB. XI. EPIST. XLVII.

units.la: De pace & vnitate sancta Ecclesia, & de Vniuersalis vocabulo fugiendo.
units.tr: Concerning peace and the holy unity of the Church, and concerning the avoidance of the title "Universal."

units.la: Cyriaco Patriarchæ Constantinopolitano. Quanta sit pacis virtus, carissime frater, ex voce Dominica diligentius intuentes, quæ ait: Pacem meam relinquo vobis, pacem meum do vobis; ita in eius nos decet dilectione persistere, vt locum præbere discordiæ nullo modo debeamus. Sed quia in radice ipsius viuere aliter non valeamus nisi mente & actu humiliatem, quam ipse auctor pacis docuit, teneamus; cum ea caritate qua dignum est suademus, vt profanam elationem quæ animabus semper aduersa est, cordis pede calcantes, peruersi superbiq; vocabuli scandalum Ecclesiæ auferte de medio festinetis: ne a pacis nostræ societate diuisi inueniri possitis. Sed vnus in nobis spiritus, vna mens, vna caritas, vna in Christo, qui sua membra esse nos voluit, sit compago concordiæ. cordiæ. Nam quàm durum, quàm indecens, quàm crudele, quamq; à sacerdotali proposito sit extraneum, pacem illum quàm aliis prædicat non habere, sanctitas vestra consideret: & suos de superbia fratres scandalizare abstineat. Sed hæc magis studeat, vt vanæ aut superfluæ elationis autorem, humilitatis quàm ense prosternere: quatenus ex eiusmodi victoria, suum vos habitaculum sancti Spiritus gratia sibi vendicet, & aperte impleatur in vobis quod scriptum est: Templum Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos. Præsentium vero portitorem dilectissimum communem filium Bonifacium Diaconum vobis in omnibus commendamus, vt quocunq; necesse fuerit, solatia vestræ sicut decet inueniat sanctitatis.
units.tr: To Cyriacus, Patriarch of Constantinople. Dearest brother, if we look more carefully at the Lord's word, we see how great the power of peace is, for he says: "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you." So we ought to persist in his love in such a way that we must in no way give room to discord. But since we cannot live in its root unless we hold in mind and deed the humility that the author of peace himself taught, we urge you with the charity that is fitting: trampling underfoot with the heel of the heart the profane elation that is always hostile to souls, hasten to remove from the midst the scandal of the perverse and proud title, lest you be found divided from the fellowship of our peace. Rather, let there be one spirit in us, one mind, one charity, one in Christ, who willed us to be his members, and let it be the bond of concord. For let your holiness consider how hard, how unseemly, how cruel, and how foreign to the priestly purpose it is that he should not have the peace which he preaches to others; let him refrain from scandalizing his brothers by pride. Rather, let him strive to overthrow the author of vain or superfluous elation by the weapon of humility rather than by the sword, so that from such a victory the grace of the Holy Spirit may claim you as its own dwelling, and what is written may be openly fulfilled in you: "The temple of God is holy, which you are." We commend to you in all things the bearer of these presents, our most beloved common son, the deacon Boniface, so that wherever he has need he may find the consolations of your holiness, as is fitting.

units.la: B. AGOBARDI LVG- DVNENSIS ARCHIEPISCOPI, ET PRIMATIS AQVI- TANIÆ
units.tr: B. Agobard, Archbishop of Lyons, and Primate of Aquitaine

units.la: TRACTATVS DE COMPARATIONE UTRIUSQVE REGIMINIS Ecclesiastici & Politici, & in quibus Ecclesiæ dignitas præfulgeat Imperiorum Maiestati: & de Monarchia Imperii Ro- mani contra diuisionem Ludouici Pii Imperatoris.
units.tr: A TREATISE ON COMPARING THE ECCLESIASTICAL AND THE POLITICAL GOVERNMENTS, AND IN WHICH RESPECTS THE DIGNITY OF THE CHURCH SHINES FORTH ABOVE THE MAJESTY OF EMPIRES; AND ON THE MONARCHY OF THE ROMAN EMPIRE AGAINST THE DIVISION OF THE EMPEROR LOUIS THE PIOUS.

units.la: Clementissimo Domino & Christianissimo ac per hoc omni laude dignissimo Imperatori LVDOVICO, Agobardus.
units.tr: To the most merciful Lord and most Christian Emperor LOUIS, and therefore worthy of all praise, Agobard.

units.la: VBet vestra prudentissima solertia contra commotiones huius temporis paratum esse vtrumq; ordinem, Militarem videlicet, & Ecclesiasticum; id est, & eos qui seculari militia, & illos qui sacris ministerium inseruiunt, & illos quidem, ad certandum ferro, istos autem ad disceptandum verbo; vt similes similibus obsistere valeant. In qua re summopere sciendum est, quod in congressione armorum, plus expectanda est iustitia superni regiminis, quam robur brachiorum. In altercatione autem sermonum plus expectanda est veritas, quam copia verborum. Propterquod orandum est ab ouibus tota intentione mentis, vt ille; de quo vos dicitis; Dominus illuminatio mea, & salus mea; quia illuminatio vestra est, illustret faciem suam super vos; & quia salus vestra est, saluum vos faciat in sua misericordia, vt huic orationi congruenter vos subiugatis: Domine, non confundar, quoniam inuocaui te: Ego igitur seruulus vester cum cognouissem ex vestro sacro præcepto iussum mihi esse ad vestram præsentiam properare ita paratum, vt cum ceteris Ecclesiasticis viris contra iniustos reprehensores iusta reprehensionis oppositionem adhibere possemus, visum mihi est vt in Dei & vestro seruitio, de anteriorum Patrum actibus & sensibus, hæc verba, quæ supter adnexa sunt, gloriosissimæ excellentiæ vestræ mitterem; Quatenus sancta Religio vestra pie perpendere dignetur, cuius reuerentiæ debitores estis ad vestrum quotidianum profectum erga sedem Apostolicam. Denique beatus Pelagius Papa cum quosdam redarguERET Episcopos, eo quod nomen eius reticerent in actione sacri mysterii in solemniis Missarum, in principio scilicet vbi dicere solemus inprimis; quas tibi offerimus pro Ecclesia tua sancta Catholica, quam pacificare, custodire, adunare, & regere digneris toto orbe terrarum, vna cum famulo tuo Papa nostro, ait ad eosdem Episcopos: Diuisionem vestram à generali Ecclesia, quam tolerabiliter ferte non possumus, vehementer stupeo. Cum enim beatissimus Augustinus dominica sententia memor, quæ fundamentum Ecclesiæ in Apostolicis sedibus collocauit, in Schismate esse dicit, quicunq; se à præsule earundem sedium auctoritate vel communione suspenderit, nec aliam manifestet esse Ecclesiam; nisi qui in pontificalibus Apostolicarum sedium est solidata radicibus, quomodo vos ab vniuerso orbis communione separatos esse noui creditis, si mei inter sacra mysteria secundum consuetudinem nominis memoriam reticetis, in quo licet indigno, Apostolicæ sedi per successionem Episcopatus præsenti tempore videtis consistere firmitatem. Beatissimus quoque Leo Papa ad vniuersos Vienensis Provinciæ Episcopos, de auctoritate & priuilegio Apostolicæ sedis, ita scribit: Diuina cultum religionis, quem in omnes gentes, omnesq; nationes Dei voluit gratia coruscare, ita Dominus noster Iesus Christus humani generis Saluator instituit, vt veritas quæ antea Legis & Prophetarum praeconio continebatur, post Apostolicam tubam in salutem vniuersitatis exiret, sicut scriptum est; In omnem terram exiuit sonus eorum, & in fines orbis terræ verba eorum. Sed huius muneris sacramentum, ita Dominus ad omnium Apostolorum officium pertinere voluit, vt in beatissimo Petro Apostolorum omnium summo principaliter collocaret, vt ab ipso, quasi quodam capite, dona sua; velut in corpus omne diffunderet, ut exertem se mysterii intelligeret esse diuini, qui antea fuisset à Petri soliditate retedu-re. Hunc enim in consortium individuae unitatis assumptum, id quod ipse erat, voluit nominari, dicendo: Tu es Petrus, & super hanc petram aedificabo Ecclesiam meam; ut aeterni templi aedi-ficatio mirabili munere gratia Dei in petri soliditate consisteret, hanc Ecclesiam suam firmitate corroborans, ut illam nec humana temeritas posset appetere, nec porta contra illam inferi praevalerent. Verum hanc petrae istius sacratissimam firmitatem, in Deo, ut diximus, aedificante constructam, nemo impia vult praesumptione violare, quisquis eius potestati attentat infringere, fauendo cupiditatibus suis, & id quod accepit à veteribus non sequendo. Haec beatus Leo, sed & alii multi huiusmodi docentes, ut illius stabilis Petrae sempiterna soliditas, super quam Dominus salvator noster propriam fundavit Ecclesiam, à Solis ortu usque ad occasum, Primatus sui apicem successorum suorum auctoritate, tam per se, quam per vicarios suos firmiter obtineret. Ex quibus beatus Anastasius Papa ad Imperatorem scribens, docet, quod pro Christo fungatur legatione, qui pro pace precatur Ecclesiae. Et ipsum Imperatorem admonet, ut constitutis Apostolicae sedis obtemperet. Certe, clementissime Domine, si nunc Gregorius Papa irrationabiliter & ad pugnandum venit, merito & pugnatus & repulsus recedet; si autem pro quiete & pace populi & vestra laborare nititur, bene & rationabiliter obtemperandum est illi, non repugnandum.
units.tr: Since your most prudent diligence has arranged that both orders stand prepared against the disturbances of this time, namely the military and the ecclesiastical, that is, both those who serve in secular warfare and those who minister in sacred things; the former indeed to contend with the sword, the latter to dispute with the word; so that each may be able to withstand its like. In this matter it must be chiefly borne in mind that in the clash of arms we ought to look for justice from the supreme government more than for the strength of arms, and in the contest of words we ought to look for truth more than for abundance of words. Therefore the sheep must pray with their whole intention of mind that He of whom you speak, "The Lord is my light and my salvation," because he is your light, may let his face shine upon you, and because he is your salvation, may save you in his mercy; so that in keeping with this prayer you may submit yourselves: Lord, let me not be confounded, for I have called upon you. I, therefore, your servant, having learned from your sacred command that I was ordered to hasten to your presence, so prepared that together with the other ecclesiastical men I might be able to set a just opposition against unjust accusers, thought it right, in the service of God and of you, to send to your glorious excellency, from the deeds and opinions of the earlier Fathers, these words which are annexed below; so that your holy religion may deign to weigh them piously, you to whose reverence you are indebted for your daily progress toward the Apostolic See. Thus, when the blessed Pope Pelagius rebuked certain bishops because they omitted his name in the celebration of the sacred mystery in the solemnities of the Masses, namely at the beginning, where we are accustomed to say first: which we offer to you for your holy Catholic Church, which you deign to pacify, guard, gather, and govern throughout the whole world, together with your servant our Pope, he said to the same bishops: I am greatly astonished at your division from the universal Church, which we cannot bear with patience. For since the most blessed Augustine, mindful of the Lord's saying which placed the foundation of the Church in the Apostolic sees, says that whoever has withdrawn himself from the authority and communion of the prelate of those sees is in schism, and shows no other to be the Church except the one that is established in the pontifical roots of the Apostolic sees; how do you believe yourselves separated from the communion of the whole world, if you omit my name in the sacred mysteries according to the custom of naming, in which, though unworthy, you see the firmness of the Apostolic see standing at present by succession of the episcopate? The most blessed Pope Leo also, writing to all the bishops of the Province of Vienne, concerning the authority and privilege of the Apostolic see, writes thus: The divine worship of religion, which God willed to shine forth among all peoples and all nations, our Lord Jesus Christ, the Saviour of the human race, so ordained, that the truth which before was contained in the proclamation of the Law and the Prophets should, after the Apostolic trumpet, go forth for the salvation of the whole world, as it is written: Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world. But the Lord willed that the sacrament of this office should pertain to the duty of all the Apostles, yet so that he principally placed it in the most blessed Peter, the chief of all the Apostles, so that from him, as from a kind of head, his gifts might flow out into the whole body; that he who had formerly been cut off from the solidity of Peter might understand that he was excluded from the divine mystery. For he, taken into fellowship of indivisible unity, willed to be named by what he himself was, saying: "You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church"; so that the building of the eternal temple, by the wondrous gift of God's grace, might stand upon the solidity of Peter, strengthening this his Church with such firmness that neither human rashness could assail it nor the gates of hell prevail against it. But this most sacred firmness of that rock, built by God, as we have said, no impious presumption wishes to violate; whoever attempts to break its power, favouring his own desires and not following what he has received from the ancients. These things the blessed Leo teaches, and many others teaching in like manner, so that the everlasting solidity of that stable Rock, upon which our Saviour Lord founded his own Church, from the rising of the sun to its setting, might firmly hold the summit of its primacy, through the authority of his successors, both in person and through their vicars. Among these, the blessed Pope Anastasius, writing to the Emperor, teaches that he who prays for the peace of the Church discharges an embassy for Christ; and he admonishes the Emperor himself to obey the decrees of the Apostolic see. Surely, most merciful Lord, if now Pope Gregory comes irrationally and for fighting, he will deservedly depart both fought against and repulsed; but if he strives to labour for the quiet and peace of the people and of you, he is to be obeyed well and reasonably, not resisted.

units.la: Si enim quod vestra voluntate & potestate, cum consensu totius Imperii vestri factum est, & postea in Apostolicae sedè roboratum, hoc vult in pristinum reducere statum, satis rationabilis & opportunus est eius adventus. Quia nullatenus quod ita est constitutum à vobis, debetis mutare: necenim sine graui periculo & reatu animae fieri potest in his sacratissimis diebus Paschalibus. Perlatae sunt ad me litterae istius Apostolici, praecipientes, ut ieiunia & orationes cum abstinentia faceremus; si forte omnipotens Dominus, effectum conatui eius praestare dignetur; quatenus apud vos obtineri possit; ut pax & concordia pristina domui & Regno vestro restituatur. Quod ego audiens, compunctus, faciem cordis mei quantum valui, ad Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum leuani, vehementer exoptans, ut sine sanguinis effusione tam iniustus tumultus per benignissimam omnipotentiam eius sedaretur. Dignetur sublimis prudentia vestra pie perpendere, quod Apostolus dicit: In novissimis diebus instabunt tempora periculosa. Quae pericula beatus Papa Gregorius suo iam tempore, quando adhuc status idem multo & incomparabiliter melior erat quam nunc ita deplorat dicens: Tantu quippe in hoc loco huius mundi fluctibus quatior, ut vetustā ac putrescente navem, quam regendam occulta Dei dispensatione suscepi, ad portum dirigere nullatenus possim. Nunc ex adverso fluctus irruunt, nunc ex latere cumuli spumosi maris intumescunt, nunc a tergo tempestas insequitur; inter haec omnia turbatus cogor modo in ipsa clavum adversitate dirigere, modo curvato navis latere minas fluctuum ex obliquo declinare; ingemisco, quia sentio quod negligente me crescit sentina vitiorum, & tempestate fortiter obviante, iam iamque putrida naufragium tabulae sonant. Heu, heu, si tunc iam putrescebat navis Ecclesiae, & si eius tabulae iam putridae erant, quid nunc est! Haec verba, piissime Domine beatissimi Doctoris, propterea ad memoriam vestram reducere praesumpsi, ut quia nemo dubitat vos, multo inestabiliter plus esse amatorem Regni caelestis, quam terreni; permansuri, quam transituri, & iuxta vestram lanctam fidem, spem & charitatem de nullo alio opere potestis tam chare Deum placare, quam de sollicitudine & administratione Pacis, & unitatis Ecclesiae, vestra solertissima Religio elaboret; ut omnis anima fidelis proficiat in fide, & cognitione Dei, quae res omnibus rebus Deo charior est, huius rei nisus merita vestra appropinquare faciat Apostolicis meritis.
units.tr: For if what was done by your will and power, with the consent of your whole Empire, and afterwards confirmed in the Apostolic see, he wishes to bring back to its former state, his coming is reasonable enough and opportune. For in no way ought you to change what has thus been established by you, since without grave danger and guilt to the soul it cannot be done in these most sacred days of Easter. Letters from that Apostolic man have been brought to me, instructing us to hold fasts and prayers with abstinence, if perhaps almighty God may deign to grant the success of his endeavour, so that it may be obtained among you that former peace and concord may be restored to your house and kingdom. Hearing this, I, pricked in heart, lifted up the face of my heart as far as I could to Jesus Christ our Lord, earnestly desiring that by his most gracious omnipotence such unjust tumult might be calmed without the shedding of blood. May your exalted prudence deign to weigh piously what the Apostle says: "In the last days perilous times will come." Those perils the blessed Pope Gregory already lamented in his own time, when the state was still the same but much and incomparably better than now, saying: "I am so tossed in this place by the waves of this world, that I cannot direct to harbour the old and rotting ship which I have received to govern by God's hidden dispensation. Now the waves rush in from the front, now from the side the foaming heaps of the sea swell, now the storm follows from behind; amid all these things, troubled, I am compelled now to steer the helm itself against the adversity, now with the ship's side bent to turn aside the threats of the waves obliquely; I groan, because I feel that through my negligence the bilge of vices grows, and with the storm strongly opposing, the rotten planks already creak with shipwreck. Alas, alas, if already then the ship of the Church was rotting, and if its planks were already rotten, what is it now!" I have presumed to bring these words of the most blessed Doctor back to your memory, most pious Lord, for because no one doubts that you are a lover of the heavenly kingdom far more than of the earthly, of things that remain rather than of things that pass away, and that according to your holy faith, hope and charity, you can please God by no other work so dearly as by the care and administration of peace and of the unity of the Church, for which your most diligent piety labours; so that every faithful soul may advance in faith and in the knowledge of God, which thing is dearer to God than all things, may the endeavour of this matter, by your merits, bring you near to the Apostolic merits.

units.la: RESCRIPTVM AD EPISTOLAM SYNODALEM EPISCOPORVM FRANCORVM EX GERMANIA ET GALLIA CONGREGATORVM, PRO CAVSA LVDOVICI PII IMPERATORIS.
units.tr: LETTER OF THE ROMAN PONTIFF IN REPLY TO THE SYNODAL LETTER OF THE BISHOPS OF THE FRANKS ASSEMBLED FROM GERMANY AND GAUL, ON BEHALF OF THE EMPEROR LOUIS THE PIOUS.

units.la: ROMANO Pontifici scribentes contrariis tum in praefatione hominibus appellastis, Fratrem videlicet, & Papam, dum congruentius esset solam ei paternam reverentiam exhibere, aduentu quoque eius comperto, lamentari vos dicitis, credentes omnibus, Principi scilicet subiectis futurum, & optasse occursum vestrum nobis non negandum, nisi sacra iussio Imperialis praevenisset; quae verba reprehensibilia sunt uno quidem modo, quia iussio Apostolicae sedis non minus vobis sacra videri debuerat, quam illa quam dicitis Imperialem; deinde quia veritate caret, quod dicitis illam praevenisse; non enim illa praevenit, sed nostra, id est, Pontificalis. Neque ignorare debueratis, maius esse Regimen animarum, quod est Pontificale, quam Imperiale, quod est temporale. Beatus Gregorius Nazianzenus nō hoc timuit coram Imperatoribus in Ecclesia praedicare. Sic enim ipsis Imperatoribus loquitur, dicens: Suscipite suscipiritis libertatem verbi, Ideo tamen accipite quod tot sacri sacerdotali vos vestra subiecit potestati, atq; ipsis tribunalibus subdisti dedit enim & nobis potestatem, dedit principatum multo pociorem primipatibus vestris? aut nunquid ipsum vobis videtur, si ederet Spiritus carnis, si a terrenis caelestia superentur, si divinis praeferantur humana? Quare igitur vos, sicut veri Sacerdotes, divini videlicet cultus ministri, non humani, non respondetis Imperatori, cuius sacra vobis dicitur iussione praeuentos, sicut ipsdem beatus Gregorius alloquitur Imperatorem praesentem? dicens: Patienter, quaeso, accipe libertatem nostram, scio te omnem esse gregis mei a Christo mihi summo Pastore annumeratum, & a sancto Spiritu consignatum; scio te inter sacra altaria cum veneratione subiici manus Sacerdotum; Scio re beate Trinitatis cultum, fidemque non tuam, sed nostra praedicatione seruare. Et post aliqua: Memento semper quod una tibi natura est, eademque substantia cum omnibus qui tibi subiecti sunt; tamen animo esto cum Deo, & non tam dominari te mundo, quam dominari tibi Christum gloriare. Quare etiam nunc commorantes cum Imperatore, intermittentes illus issimas adulationes, non ei praedicat cum beato Augustino? dicentes: Felices dicimus Imperatores si iuste imperant, si inter linguas subiectorum honoratum, non extollantur; & se homines esse meminerint, si suam potestatem ad Dei cultum maxime dilatandum maiestati eius famulantur, si Deum timent, diligunt, colunt. Si plurimum amant illud regnum, ubi non timent habere consortes; si tardius vindicant, & cognoscunt; si tandem vindicam, pro necessitate regendi tuendaque Republica, non propter sui natura minuitarum odio exerunt; si eandem veniam non ad impunitatem iniquitatis, sed ad spem correctionis indulgent; si quando aspere coguntur plerumque decernere, misericordia lenitate, & beneficiorum largitate compensant; si luxuria a tetu castigatio, qua nihil posset esse liberior; si malunt cupiditatibus, quam quibuslibet gentibus imperare; & si haec omnia faciunt, non propter ardorem inanis gloriae, sed propter charitatem felicitatis aeternae; si pro suis peccatis humilitatis & miserationis & orationis sacrificium Deo suo vere immolare non negligunt; talis Christianos Imperatores dicimus esse fideles, interim ipse, postea re ipsa futuros, cum id quod expectamus adueneri. Vos autem econtrario quia non vultis esse veri aedificatores, estis procul dubio veri decepti, sicut scriptum est: Populi qui beatum te dicunt, ipsi te decipiunt, & viam gressuum tuorum dissipant.
units.tr: In writing to the Roman Pontiff, you addressed him in your preface with contrary terms, calling him "brother" and "Pope," when it would have been more fitting to show him only paternal reverence. You also say that when you learned of his coming, you lamented, believing that everything would be subject to the Prince, and that you had wished for a meeting with you, which should not have been refused us, had not the sacred Imperial command intervened. These words are blameworthy in one respect, because the command of the Apostolic See ought to have seemed no less sacred to you than the one you call Imperial. They are also false in saying that the Imperial command intervened; for it did not intervene, but ours did, that is, the Pontifical one. Nor should you have been ignorant that the government of souls, which is Pontifical, is greater than the Imperial, which is temporal. Blessed Gregory Nazianzen did not fear to preach this before emperors in the church. For he speaks thus to the emperors themselves: Receive the freedom of the word. Yet accept this, that the sacred priesthood has placed you under its power and subjected you to the tribunals themselves; for it has given us power, a principate far greater than your princely rule. Or do you think it is unfitting if the Spirit rules the flesh, if heavenly things are set above earthly, if divine things are preferred to human? Why then do you, as true priests, that is ministers of divine worship and not of human affairs, not answer the Emperor, by whose sacred command you are said to have been anticipated, as the same blessed Gregory addresses the Emperor who was present? He says: Patiently, I beg you, accept our freedom. I know that you are numbered among all my flock by Christ, the highest Shepherd to me, and sealed by the Holy Spirit. I know that you, among the holy altars, bow with reverence to the hands of priests. I know that you keep the worship of the blessed Trinity and the faith by our preaching, not by your own. And after some words: Always remember that you have one nature and the same substance as all who are subject to you; yet be of a mind with God, and glory not so much that you rule the world as that Christ rules you. Why then, still dwelling with the Emperor, do you not, setting aside those most shameless flatteries, preach to him with blessed Augustine, saying: We call emperors happy if they rule justly, if they are not puffed up by the praises of their subjects, if they remember that they are men, if they serve their power chiefly for enlarging the worship of God, if they fear, love and honour God; if they love most that kingdom where they fear to have fellows; if they are slow to take vengeance and are well informed before they do; if they exercise punishment, when needed for ruling and defending the commonwealth, not out of hatred of the vices of others; if they grant pardon not to licence wrongdoing but in hope of correction; if, when harshly compelled to decree something, they make up for it by gentleness of mercy and generosity of benefits; if they curb luxury, which could be nothing freer; if they prefer to rule their lusts rather than any peoples; and if they do all this, not from the ardour of empty glory but from love of eternal happiness; if they do not neglect to offer to their God the true sacrifice of humility, mercy and prayer for their own sins. Such emperors we call Christian and faithful, though they are so only in hope now, and will be so in reality later, when what we expect has come. But you, on the contrary, because you do not wish to be true builders, are without doubt truly deceived, as it is written: "Those who call you blessed, they themselves deceive you, and scatter the way of your steps.

units.la: Deinde postquam dixistis vos laetatos esse de adventu nostro, iterum intulistis, quoniam diu relatione magno maerore affectos, quod utique facit instabilitas mentis; verum est omnino: quoniam qui haesitat similis est fluctui maris qui a vento movetur. Sed inter has haesitationes nimis stolide vos iudicatis immemores esse Pastoralis officii, & districtissimae moderationis; deinde sicut scriptum est, cum sit timidus nequitia, dat testimonium condemnata. Adiungens (quod omni verecundia dignum est) dicentes nos venire propter quandam praesumptionem & omnis rationis carentem excommunicationem faciendam, & admonentes nos nimis inuolutis & confusis sermonibus & sententiis, ut neque nostrae voluntatis: neque alterius hortatu praesumpsione prorumpamus; ea quod (ut dicitis) pertineat ad iniuriam ac debellationem Imperialis potestatis, & ad Domini rationem & reprehensionem nostrae auctoritatis, dicite; quis, quae sunt ista portenta verborum? & quid potius pertinet ad dehonestationem Imperialis potestatis opera digna excommunicatione, an ipsa excommunicatio? sed quia haec verba vestra exaggerate laboriosum est; eo quod plenaque sint nauseae tantum illud si gitos, ut dicatis quomodo potuit fieri, ut manente Apostolicae sedis honore, mea tantum poenitentia causa reprehensionis & vituperationis remaneat? Nullo modo enim si ita potest, ut is qui locum beati Petri tenet, exhonoratur sine crimine, dum taxatur; cathedra eius honorata permanet.
units.tr: Then, after saying that you rejoiced at our arrival, you added again that you had been greatly grieved by the report, which indeed is the effect of an unstable mind. This is entirely true: "he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven by the wind." But amid these hesitations you judge, very foolishly, that you have forgotten the pastoral office and the strictest moderation. Then, as it is written, "since the coward is wicked, he bears witness against himself," you add (which deserves all shame) that we are coming to pronounce some excommunication on account of a certain presumption lacking all reason. You admonish us with very tangled and confused words and sentences not to rush forward either by our own will or by the urging of another, since (as you say) this pertains to the injury and overthrow of Imperial power, and to a charge against the Lord and a censure of our authority. Tell us: what are these monstrous words? And which is more fitting to dishonour the Imperial power, deeds worthy of excommunication, or excommunication itself? But since it is laborious to go over these words of yours, which are so full of nausea that you say how it could happen that, while the honour of the Apostolic See remains, only my penance should remain the cause of blame and reproach? For in no way, if it can be so, is the one who holds the place of blessed Peter dishonoured without crime while he is censured; his see remains honoured.

units.la: In tantum autem honoranda est Cathedra Pontificalis, & propter Cathedram sedentis in illa, ut etiam de Caipha crudelitate & incredulitate impio dicat Evangelista: Hoc autem a semetipso non dixit, sed cum esset pontifex anni illius prophetavit, quia Iesu moriturum erat pro gente. Unde constat etiam impium Caiphan propter Cathedram honoratum esse prophetam. Vos autem fideles & culorem pietatis Pontificem dehonestandum praedicatis absque iniuria Sedis, quod omnino falsum est. Bene autem subiungitis, Memorem me esse debere veritatis iudicandi causa fidei suae suum Imperatori. Quod si feci, in hoc volo vitare periurium; si annunciavero ei omnia quae contra unitatem & pacem Ecclesiae & Regni committit; quod si non fecero, perierunt ea, sicut & vos; (sed tamen iuravi.) Vos tamen, quia procul dubio iuratis & teneratis, promittentes ei erga illam omnia fideliter vos agere, & nunc videntes illum agere contra fidem, & praecipitari in perniciem, non revocatis eum, quantum ex vobis est; perturbatis quia pro eius salute; secundum fidem non laboratis.
units.tr: The Pontifical See is to be honoured so greatly, and on account of the one who sits in it, that the Evangelist even says of the impious and unbelieving Caiaphas: "Now this he did not say of himself, but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was to die for the nation." Hence it is clear that the impious Caiaphas was also honoured as a prophet on account of the See. But you, who are faithful and call the Pontiff a pillar of piety, declare him to be dishonoured without injury to the See, which is altogether false. You rightly add that I must be mindful of the truth, so as to judge in the cause of faith, and to report to the Emperor his own affairs. If I have done so, I wish in this to avoid perjury; if I have announced to him all that he commits against the unity and peace of the Church and the Kingdom, well; but if I have not done so, those things have perished, as you have too (but yet I have sworn). Yet you, because without doubt you have sworn and held to it, promising him that you would act faithfully towards that oath, and now seeing him act against the faith and rushing to destruction, do not recall him, as far as lies in you. You are troubled, because for his salvation you do not labour according to faith.

units.la: Deinde promittitis mihi venerabilem receptionem, si tamen ita ad illum venero, ut eius voluntas est. Haec non in libris divinis, sed in vestris conscientiis legitis, qui omnia faciebatis propter temporalem retributionem, eo quod gius harundines vento agitatae, & omnes aurae vos doctam Pensare, pensare Farres; quam longe est metis vestrae ab illa petitione, qua in celebrationibus Missarum dicere Deo non voluntate, sed voce, da nobis pro amore tuo prosperia mundi despectere, & nullum eius adversa formidare. Nam si ex corde haec petieritis, iam dedisset ille qui dixit: Petite & dabitur vobis. Deinde dicitis illam primam divisionem Regni, quam inter filios suos fecerat Imperator nunc iuxta Regum opportunitatem esse mutatam: quod omnino duplicitet falsum est; yno quidem modo, quia non est opportunitas, eo quod sit causa & origo contubationis & dissensionis;
units.tr: Then you promise me a venerable reception, if indeed I come to him in such a way as is his will. You read this not in the divine books but in your own consciences, you who did everything for temporal reward, since, like reeds shaken by the wind, you are carried about by every breeze and weigh up, weigh up, the wheat. How far your mind is from that petition by which, in the celebration of the Masses, we say to God, not with the will alone but with the voice: "Grant us, for your love, to despise the prosperity of the world, and not to fear its adversities." For if you asked this from the heart, he who said "Ask, and it will be given you" would already have granted it. Then you say that the first division of the kingdom, which the Emperor had made among his sons, has now been changed according to the convenience of the kings. This is false in two ways: in one way, because there is no convenience in it, since it is the cause and origin of disturbance and dissension;

units.la: D commotionis & depraedationis, & omnium malorum, quae per singula dicere longum est; extra periuria innumera, & fidei ac pacis expulsiones: alio vero modo, quia nec dum scitis vtrum sit commutata aut per verum Regem & Dominum manet illibata. Ista enim commutatio, quam vos dicitis, iuxta rerum opportunitatem factam, inde cognoscitur; quia non fuerit per Deum, quia multorum peccatorum causa existit. Illud namque quod per voluntatem Dei fit, plerumque causa est pressurae, & persecutionis; sicut factum est aduersum sanctos Apostolos, & Martyres, qui non propter aliud passi sunt nisi propter defensionem & confirmationem Euangelicae veritatis. Causa autem peccatorum & scelerum esse non potuit, sicut vestra diuisio est, quam dicitis fuisse opportunam.
units.tr: of commotion and plunder, and of all the evils that would take too long to list one by one; besides countless perjuries and the expulsions of faith and peace. In the other way, because you do not yet know whether it has been changed, or whether it remains unimpaired under the true King and Lord. That change, which you say was made according to the convenience of affairs, is known to be not from God, since it is the cause of many sins. For what happens by the will of God is often the cause of pressure and persecution, as happened to the holy Apostles and Martyrs, who suffered for nothing else than the defence and confirmation of the evangelical truth. But the cause of sins and crimes could not have been this division of yours, which you say was expedient.

units.la: Deinde quod grandi super alio dicitis, quia si reuertenter venerimus ad Imperatorem, per ipsum cognoscemus omnem rei veritatem, quare opportune & vtiliter mutatio sit diuisio: hoc loqui cogit vos magnitudo superbiae, aestimantes solos suos posse rerum cognoscere causas. Vere dico vobis, quia non solum studus, sed & infelix est, qui non intelligit quantos & quales fructus malorum protulit vestra commutatio, & de cuius thesauro maligni cordis processit, & pro quo reos laudatores & defensores estis huius malignitatis. Deinde subiungitis, quia nisi secundum voluntatem vestram venero, non habeo Ecclesias vestras consentaneas, sed in tantum contrarias, vt nihil mihi in vestris parochiis agere vel disponere liceat, nec quempiam excommunicare vobis obsistentibus. Vere verum est quod veritas dicit; malus homo de malo thesauro cordis sui profert mala. Quare mihi contrarii cum Ecclesiis vestris esse debetis in legatione pacis, & vnitatis, quod Christi donum & ministerium est? an ignoratis Angelorum cantu promissam esse pacem in terra hominibus bonae voluntatis? per Apostolum autem tribulationem & angustiam in omnem animam hominis operantis malum? Hic apparet, quod congruat vobis illud quod Scriptura dicit: Arma & gladii in via peruersi. Vos conamini obsistere peruersitatibus vestris, nobis, qui legatione fungimur pacis: nam quicunque inter vos membra Christi sunt, non cum potestis abscindere a corpore capitis quod est Christus; nam & si vos datis operam separandi a corpore vos ipsos, tamen sicut semper fuit, est & erit; vt vnguentum illud, Spiritus videlicet sanctus, qui descendit a capite Christi in barbam, quae est Apostolorum chorus: & de hac barba in ora vestimenti, quae est capitium tunicae, Ecclesiae, scilicet Christi, quod capit caput, vt inhabitet Christus per fidem in corde eius, in omnibus vbique & videlicet seruet vnitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis. Haec idcirco dicimus, vt noveritis non vos posse diuidere Ecclesiam Gallicanam & Germanicam ab vnitate tunicae, quae subiacet capicio, sublimioribus videlicet membris Ecclesiae, qui proximiores sunt barbae Apostoli, scilicet, ac per hoc Apostolicis sedibus; sicut barba non potest esse nisi in capite. Deinde dicitis, rem ridiculam subinferentes, & quod potius tacere, quam dicere maluimus: si autem non egeritis, assensum consilio nostro non praebueritis, honoris vestri periculo subiacebitis: si potius maluistis, id est magis voluistis tacere, quam dicere: quare non tacuistis? consuetudo est in vobis vt id quod minus est, vincat quod maius est: maior voluntas exitit in vobis tacere minor autem dicere, & tamen minor vicit maiorem, credendum est omnino, quoniam in discordiarum amaritudinibus victrix est cupiditas, victa continentia. Illud vero quod mirari nos cognoscimus, periculum grandius.
units.tr: Next, as to what you say at length about another matter, namely that if we return to the Emperor, we shall learn from him the whole truth of why the division was made at a suitable and useful time: this is the arrogance of your pride speaking, since you think only yourselves able to know the causes of things. I tell you truly, he is not only foolish but also unhappy who does not understand what great and what kinds of fruits your change has produced, out of whose treasure of a malicious heart it came, and for which you are the accomplices, praisers and defenders of this malice. Then you add: unless I come according to your will, I do not have your Churches in agreement with me, but so much opposed that I am not permitted to do or arrange anything in your parishes, nor to excommunicate anyone while you resist. Truly, what the truth says is true: an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart brings forth evil things. Therefore you ought to be opposed to me in the embassy of peace and unity, which is the gift and ministry of Christ. Or do you not know that peace on earth to men of good will was promised by the song of the angels? And through the Apostle, tribulation and anguish upon every soul of man who works evil? Here it appears that what Scripture says fits you: Arms and swords are in the way of the perverse. You try to resist us, who act as ambassadors of peace, with your perversities. For whoever among you are members of Christ, you cannot cut off from the body of the head, which is Christ. Even if you take pains to separate yourselves from the body, it always was, is and will be as it is; like that ointment, namely the Holy Spirit, which descended from the head of Christ onto the beard, which is the company of the Apostles, and from this beard onto the hem of the garment, which is the collar of the tunic, that is, the Church of Christ, which covers the head, so that Christ may dwell through faith in its heart, in all places everywhere, and so keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. We say this so that you may know that you cannot separate the Gallican and German Churches from the unity of the tunic which lies beneath the collar, that is, from the more exalted members of the Church, who are nearer to the beard of the Apostle, and therefore to the Apostolic sees; just as a beard cannot exist except on the head. Then you say, adding a ridiculous thing, and one which we would rather have kept silent than said: but if you do not act, and do not give assent to our counsel, you will be exposed to danger to your honour. If you preferred, that is, were more willing, to keep silent rather than speak, why did you not keep silent? It is your custom that the lesser should overcome the greater: in you the greater will was to keep silent and the lesser to speak, and yet the lesser has overcome the greater. It must be wholly believed that in the bitterness of discord desire is victorious and restraint is defeated. But what we perceive as more to be wondered at is the greater danger.

units.la: Quis explicare poterit quantum sit absurdum, quantumque inconueniens & ridiculum, cum vestra communicatio non sit propter crimen, homicidium scilicet, sacrilegium, aut furtum, vel aliquid huiusmodi, sed nisi ita venerimus, sicut ipsi vultis, cui rei in argumento adiungitis iuramentum, & non recordamini erubescentes, qui periuri peieratum degradare non possunt, etiam si essem? Deniq; vos non me scitis esse peieratum; de vobis autem nemo quis dubitet hoc esse? In hac re memor esse debuerat solertia vestra; quia quicunque cloacam commouet, quanto amplius commouerit, tanto ampliorem fetorem exhalari facit. Quod autem de sequentibus me fratribus, & Coepiscopis similiter promittitis agendum, & additis irretractabiliter; miranda in hoc praesumptio vestra cognoscitur. Nunquid quod in parte agitur, retractari apud vniuersitatem non poterit? Numquid quod apud homines a rectitudine deviantes agitur, apud meliores, recti videlicet, tenaces, retractari non debet? aut quod in praesenti maliciose iudicatur, Dei iudicio retractandum non erit? quod vestrae minae continent; nunquam adhuc ab initio Ecclesiae factum est. Nam si etiam ego fuissem periurus, aptandum vobis erat illud Euangelium: Neg tu times Deum, cum in eadem damnatione sis!
units.tr: Who can explain how absurd, how inappropriate and how ridiculous it is, since your communion is not withheld on account of a crime, namely homicide, sacrilege, theft or anything of that kind, but unless we come exactly as you wish, to which matter you add an oath, and you do not remember, blushing, that perjurers cannot depose a perjurer, even if I were one? Moreover, you do not know me to be a perjurer, and who could doubt this about you? In this matter your shrewdness ought to have been mindful: whoever stirs a sewer, the more he stirs it, the greater the stench he makes rise. As for your promise that you will act in the same way as my brothers and fellow bishops, and you add irrevocably; your presumption in this is seen to be astonishing. Can what is done in part not be revoked before the whole body? Must what is done among men who deviate from rectitude not be revoked before better men, namely the upright and steadfast? Or what is maliciously judged in the present must not be revoked by the judgement of God? That your threats contain this has never yet been done from the beginning of the Church. For if I too had been a perjurer, that Gospel would have fitted you: Do you not fear God, since you are under the same condemnation?

units.la: Audite haec, omnes gentes, audiat terra & plenitudo eius a solis ortu & occasu ab Aquilone, & mari, & sciant, & recogitent pariter domini & Imperatoris Ludovici filios iuste fuisse, & esse indignatos, & bene sentire & intendere ad expurgandum paternum palatium a sordibus facinorum, & iniquis factionibus; & regnum ab amarissimis & tumultuosis inquietudinibus, tantum vt inter eos germana fides & fraterna sinceritas Deo digna & omni fideli populo beneplacita perseveraret, & inviolabiliter perseueret. Igitur cum praedictus Dominus & Imperator quietus esset in domo, & florens in palatio suo, cum adhuc iuvenem coniugem sub sui reverentia custodiret, & secundum Apostolum Iam [illegible, ~40 letters] illi persoluerent; in processu vero dierum cum coepissent haec primum tempestare, deinde [illegible, ~12 letters] ac per hoc & mulier resoluit in lasciviam, cessantibus licitis conversationibus [illegible, ~10 letters] ad illicita, adsumit sibimet aptas personas ad perpetranda turpia, & primi[illegible, ~8 letters], deinde impedientes.
units.tr: Hear this, all peoples; let the earth and all that is in it hear, from the rising and setting of the sun, from the north and the sea, and let them know and consider that the sons of the lord and Emperor Louis were justly and rightly indignant, and that they meant well and set out to cleanse the paternal palace of the filth of crimes and of wicked factions, and the kingdom of the most bitter and tumultuous disturbances, so that a true faith and brotherly sincerity, worthy of God and pleasing to every faithful people, might persist among them and continue inviolably. Therefore, while the said lord and Emperor was at rest in his house and flourishing in his palace, and while he still kept his young wife under his protection and reverence, and, according to the Apostle, [illegible passage] they rendered to him; but in the course of days, when these things began first to rage, then [illegible passage], and so the woman, in consequence, dissolved into wantonness, licit intercourse having ceased [illegible passage] to illicit things, she takes to herself suitable persons to commit shameful acts, and first [illegible passage], then hindering.

units.la: Cognouerunt autem hoc initio pauci, deinde plures, ad postremum autem multitudo palatii, & regni, ac finium terrae; quam rem irridebant minores, doctissimi [illegible, ~6 letters] clari viri intolerandum iudicantes: Concitati itaque sunt spiritus filiorum imperatoris zelo, videntes maculatum stratum paternum, sordidatum Palatium, confusum regnum, & obscuratum nomen Francorum, quod hactenus clarum fuerat in toto orbe: & surgentes singuli uno & pio consensu in emendatione scelerum conuenerunt simul, & aliis comprehensis, aliis effugatis, auctore vero malorum a Palatio exclusa, inclusaque in custodia [illegible, ~8 letters] induto habitu sanctimoniali, reddiderunt Patrem quieti & aliquantulum honestati. Caeterum minimam filiorum remissionem bene acta dissoluerentur, per carnalium blanditias, & scelestos fauores, atque indecoras adulationes, iterum mulier tanquam legitima domina renocata est in Palatium, & praelata Consiliis & Consiliariis, cuius instigationibus [illegible, ~6 letters] Barbaris, & caepit duris cornibus ventilare filios & conturbare populos; Sicque [illegible, ~8 letters] mortalibus, ut non tam persecuti, iniuste sustinerent persecutiones quam persecutores inuiti & coacti exercerent, & non solum exercerent, sed & sustinerent, dum violentissime in diversa & contraria iuramenta compelluntur. Attendite & videte si factum est vn-quam huiusmodi. Iuratum est ergo Imperatori iuniori; & iterum ipso faciente, aliqui ex ipsis iurauerunt Regis [illegible, ~4 letters] & ad postremum pene omnes compulsi sunt iurare Puero, & ne ibi quidem remansit, sed quasi nihil horum fuisset, adhuc exorta sunt iuramenta. Nunquid super hu non visitabo, dicit Dominus, & in gente tali non remanebit despectio Dei, & pollutio nominis eius? sicut scriptum est, non periurabis nec pollues nomen Domini Dei tui? Ecce patefactis abyssis stultitiarum, ad quid peruentum est. Cum enim deberent exercitum mittere aduersus exteras gentes, & ipse Imperator aduersus barbaras nationes dimicare, ut eas fidei subiugaret ad dilatandum terminum Regni fidelium (sic namq; orat vniuersalis Ecclesia in solemnitis, illis orationibus, diebus passionis Dominicae pro Imperatoribus, ut Deus subiectas faciat barbaras nationes;) nunc econtrario omne regnum cum extremitatibus suis conspirat in vnum in medio sui, diversa tamen intentione, dum alii parantur ad intestina viscera dispendia, alii ad pacandam si fieri potest iniustissimam discordiam, qui omnes pia mente perpendere debuerant, quod dicitur in praedictis orationibus, vbi Sacerdos admonet, dicens: Oremus & pro Christianissimo Imperatore nostro, ut Deus & Dominus subditus illi faciat omnes barbaras nationes ad nostram perpetuam pacem. Domus ergo Dei, quae est Ecclesia Dei viui, columna & firmamentum veritatis, orat ut Christianissimo Imperatori, barbari subiiciantur, non ut subiecti conturbentur & barbarizentur. Neque enim Christianismi Imperatoris est subiectos exturbare, & vnitos diuidere. O Domine Deus, coeli ac terrae, cur permisisti fidelissimum & Christianissimum seruum tuum Imperatorem nostrum in tantam deuenire negligentiam, ut videre nolit quibus malis circundatus sit; diligit enim odientes se & odit diligentes se. Quid si verum est, quod plerique, qui subtilius intelligere videntur affirmant; quod scilicet sint aliqui in latere eius, qui inaniter expectant exterminium filiorum eius. Quod si viderint, collatum habent inter se, ut in Imperatorem mittant manum, & dispertiant sibi regnum; hoc verum verum sit ipsi norunt, multi tamen sunt, qui non ambigunt illos, de quibus dicitur, ita incumbere regno tanquam parieti inclinato, & maceriae impulsae. Unde constat, quia nisi Deus subuenit, aut exteris dabitur regnum, aut in multos tyrannos dispertietur, aut forsitan Antichristo, qui praeparabitur, quod in hoc assimilatur; quoniam Imperator qui aduersus barbarorum Reges bella iusta disponere debuerat, aduersus dilectiones sui filios iniusta agere parat. Dicunt etiam aliqui, quod Domina Palatii seniioris, extra illa, quae de eius occultis & non occultis dicuntur, ludat pueriliter, expectantibus etiam aliquibus de ordine sacerdotali; & plerisque concludentibus, qui secundum formam, quam Apostolus scribit de eligendis Episcopis dicens: Domui suae bene praepositum, filios habentem subditos cum omni castitate, quia si quis domui suae praeesse nescit, quomodo Ecclesiae Dei diligentiam habebit? Praedicare debuerant Dominae ludenti; si qua Regina [illegible, ~6 letters] regere non nouit, quomodo de honestate Palatii curam habebit? aut quomodo gubernaculum regni diligenter exercebit? Reducere quoque eiad memoriam debuerant, quod supra [illegible, ~8 letters] inuenitur aptari potest quantum tamen ad exteriorem sensum pertinet, quod ... Scriptura dicit: Mulier diligens, corona est viro suo; & putredo in ossibus eius, qua confusione res agitur. Et iterum: Testa perstillantia in die frigoris, & litigiosa mulier comparantur: qui retinet eam, quasi qui retinet ventum & oleum dextera sua exercet. Sed forte dicturus est aliquis; haec non est litigiosa, tamen sed blanda. Quibus verbis respondendum est, non esse maius litigium, quam bonis Patris bonos filios irritare, exacerbare, exhonorare, & penitus a Patre alienare velle, quia quia proprie solam pulchritudinem a viro inofficiose diligi fertur; inculcandum vtrique fuerit quod iterum eadem Scriptura dicit: fallax gratia & vana est pulchritudo; mulier timens Dominum ipsa laudabitur. Nunc igitur omnes timentes, & amantes Deum, Regem quoque & Regnum, pacata societate, rebus mundi vtentes, rebus diuinis fruentes, omni conamine dare operam debent, ut exprimatur vulnus iniquitatis, & obducatur cicatrix sanitatis, absque sanguinis effusione, absque strage interfectionis, absque amaritudine iurgiorum, absque turbulentia. turbulenta & fœtida commixtione spirituum immundorum: ut vere dicatur de Ecclesia huius regni, hæc est domus Dei, & porta Cœli. Porta autem infert eam prænabunt aduersus eam. Et rursum: Dominus Deus tuus in medio tui fortis, ipse laudabit, gaudebit super te in lætitia, silebit in dilectione tua, & exultabit super te in laude: fugas quæ à lege recesserant congregabo quia ex te erant, ut non vitrabuntur super te opprobrium, & dicat omnis Apostolus, Amen, Amen, & hymnum Deo.
units.tr: This, however, was first known to a few, then to more, and at last to the whole body of the court, the kingdom, and the lands of the realm. The lesser people made light of it, while the most learned and distinguished men judged it intolerable. Stirred by zeal, the sons of the emperor rose up, seeing their father's bed defiled, the palace soiled, the kingdom in confusion, and the name of the Franks, once famous throughout the world, darkened.
