Sed quia ciuitas illa ad Deum toto corde conuersa, nequaquam iuxta minacem Domini sententiam excidii est euersione deleta. Cum ergo Deus omnipotens non modo verax, sed & ipsa sit veritas, inuiolato consilii sui manente proposito, exterioris iudicii sui sæpe variat ordinem, iuxta humani siue probi, siue improbi meriti qualitatem, quatenus & à prauitate correctus, quod Deus iuste minatur, euadat & prolapsus in culpam, nullatenus quæ pollicetur bona percipiat. Hinc est, quod per Ieremiam dicit: Bonas facite vias vestras & studia vestra, & audite vocem Domini Dei vestri, & pœnitebit Dominum mali, quod locutus est aduersum vos. Hinc est, quod ad Heli quoque per virum Dei Dominus ait: Loquens locutus sum, ut domus tua, & domus patris tui ministraret in conspectu meo usque in sempiternum. Nunc autem, dicit Dominus, absit hoc à me, sed quicunque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum, qui autem contemnunt me, erunt ignobiles.
units.tr: No one who frequents the threshold of the Church is ignorant that Jonah, sent by the Lord to Nineveh, cried out, saying: "Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown." But because that city turned to God with its whole heart, it was by no means destroyed by overthrow in accordance with the threatening sentence of the Lord. Since, therefore, almighty God is not only truthful but is truth itself, while his purpose of counsel remains inviolate, he often varies the order of his outward judgment according to the quality of human merit, whether good or bad, so that the one who has been corrected from wickedness escapes what God justly threatens, and the one who has fallen into guilt by no means receives the good things he promises. Hence it is that through Jeremiah he says: "Make your ways and your doings good, and hear the voice of the Lord your God, and the Lord will repent of the evil which he has spoken against you." Hence also the Lord said to Eli through the man of God: "I spoke, so that your house and the house of your father should minister before me for ever. But now, says the Lord, far be this from me; but whoever glorifies me, I will glorify him, and those who despise me shall be dishonoured."

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: Regius Aduocatus.

units.la: Recte plane cuncta proposueras, perspicuis roborasti testimoniis Scripturarum, attamen ad superiora paulisper reuertere, & iuxta tuæ sponsionis elogium de Domini mei Regis iniuria rationem redde.
units.tr: You have certainly set out everything correctly and supported it with clear testimonies of Scripture. Still, go back a little to what went before, and, as your promise required, give an account of the wrong done to my lord the King.

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.

units.la: Glorioso Regi in eligendo Pontificem, absit vt nos intulerimus iniuriam, cum ad hoc nos, sicut superius dictum est, necessitas impulerit, non rapina, adhoc, inquam, nos inuitos traxit imminens periculum ciuilis belli, non lædendi, vel minuendi huiusmodi Imperii.
units.tr: As for choosing a Pontiff against the glorious King, far be it from us to have done him any wrong. As was said above, necessity drove us to it, not plunder. I say, we were drawn against our will by the imminent danger of civil war, not with any intention of injuring or diminishing this empire.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: Regius Aduocatus.

units.la: Ciuile bellum obiicis, imminens periculum in tua allegationis defensione prætendis; dicatur etiam, si placet quod cœlum rueret, terra subcicinium pateretur: perge adhuc addens, quod pontus aresceret, terram diluuium inundaret. Quid mihi omnia hæc dum constet, quia quidquid accideret, nullo modo sancti Papæ sententiam debuisti infringere, nulla ratione synodalis decreti mysterium liquit violare? Sicut enim Scriptura perhibet, melius est vt oriatur scandalum, quam vt veritas relinquatur. Nam si hoc bellum timuissent beati Martyres, fierent proculdubio sanctæ militiæ desertores.
units.tr: You bring up civil war and use the imminent danger as a defence of your argument. Let it be said, if you like, that heaven would fall and the earth would open up beneath us. Go on and add that the sea would dry up and the flood would overwhelm the land. What does all this matter to me? Whatever might happen, you ought in no way to have overturned the judgment of the holy Pope, and by no reasoning to have broken the sanctity of a synodal decree. For as Scripture says, it is better that a scandal arise than that the truth be abandoned. If the blessed martyrs had feared this war, they would undoubtedly have become deserters of the holy army.

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.

units.la: Non ignoras, quod inter omnes sanctos Martyres Petrus & Paulus in Apostolici Senatus culmine possident principatum.
units.tr: You are not unaware that among all the holy martyrs, Peter and Paul hold the chief place in the summit of the Apostolic Senate.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: Regius Aduocatus.

units.la: Hoc sicut negare sacrilegium est, ita etiam affirmare superfluum.
units.tr: To deny this would be sacrilege, just as to affirm it is superfluous.

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.

units.la: Eorum sunt nobis tenenda vestigia, eorum forma iuris est actibus imprimenda, sub eorum magistra debemus viuere disciplina.
units.tr: We must follow their footsteps; we must stamp their pattern on our conduct; under their teaching we ought to live.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: Regius Aduocatus.

units.la: Hoc vtique clarum est, perspicuum est, sed quid à te portenti, quid præstigii sub hoc funiculo inductionis alatur ignoro.
units.tr: This is certainly clear and plain. But what monstrous trick or sleight of hand is being nourished under this thread of inference, I do not know.

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.

units.la: Tolle præstigium, intellige veritatem, times me tanquam tibi tendiculas substruentem: audi Paulum de capite suo Petro veraciter perhibentem: Petrus, antequam venirent quidam à Iacobo, cum Gentilibus edebat; cum autem venissent, subtrahebat se & segregabat, timens eos qui ex circumcisione erant. Cernimus ergo Petrum non rigidum, sed discretum. Timebat enim Iudæos, ne per occasionem Gentium à Fide recederent Christianorum, & ne perderet gregem creditum, boni pastoris est imitatus exemplum: factus est enim Iudæis tanquam Iudæus, vt Iudæos lucrifaceret. Sicut Christus apparuit in forma carnis peccati, vt à peccatis hominem liberaret: & cum legem Moysi non ambigeret abolendam, consulens tamen adhuc rudibus & infirmis fratribus, tenuit ad tempus vmbram legis, vt eos quoque proueheret ad perfectæ noscendam plenitudinem veritatis. In hoc ergo beatus Petrus discretionis nobis regulam dedit, quatenus aliquando, vbi tamen non plurimum noceat, declinemus aliquantulum à tramite rectitudinis, vt consulere valeamus infirmis.
units.tr: Drop the trickery and understand the truth. You are afraid of me as though I were laying snares for you. Hear Paul truthfully speaking of Peter, the head of the Church: Before certain men came from James, Peter ate with the Gentiles; but when they came, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing those who were of the circumcision. We see, then, that Peter was not rigid but discerning. For he feared the Jews, lest through the stumbling of the Gentiles they should fall away from the faith of the Christians, and lest he lose the flock committed to him. He imitated the example of a good shepherd: he became to the Jews as a Jew, that he might win the Jews. Just as Christ appeared in the form of sinful flesh, to free man from sins, and though he did not doubt that the law of Moses was to be abolished, yet, consulting the still untaught and weak brethren, he kept for a time the shadow of the law, so that he might also lead them on to know the fullness of the perfect truth. In this, then, the blessed Peter gave us a rule of discretion: that now and then, where it does not do much harm, we may turn aside a little from the path of uprightness, so that we may be able to help the weak.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: Regius Aduocatus.

units.la: Qui dicis, quod Petrus aliquando legem Iudaicam tenuit, cur non dicis quod in eadem Epistola legitur, nimirum quia Paulus in facie eum reprehendit: In faciem, inquit, ei restiti, quia reprehensibilis erat. Eique dixit: Si tu, cum sis Iudæus, Gentiliter, & non Iudaicè viuis, quomodo cogis Gentes Iudaizare? Cum ergo illud permisisti, istud quare silentio suppresisti.
units.tr: You who say that Peter at one time kept the Jewish law, why do you not mention what is read in the same Epistle? Namely, that Paul rebuked him to his face. I withstood him to his face, he says, because he was to be blamed. And he said to him: If you, though you are a Jew, live as a Gentile and not as a Jew, how do you compel the Gentiles to live as Jews? Since you have allowed the one, why have you kept the other in silence?

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.

units.la: Quod Petrus egit compassione misericordiæ, hoc Paulus arguit pro magisterio disciplinæ: ille, quod fecit dispensatiue, vt infirmis tolleret scandalum; hoc iste atripuit, ne indiscretus quilibet passim adduceret in exemplum: sin Petro dicamus, vt periculo imminente discreti Pauli sermonibus instruantur, vt sanis rebus vita nostra mere deseruiat rectitudini.
units.tr: What Peter did out of compassion and mercy, Paul rebuked in the interest of the discipline of teaching. Peter did it by way of dispensation, to take away offence from the weak; Paul insisted on the reverse, lest any indiscreet person should cite it everywhere as an example. But if we speak of Peter, let it be so that, when danger threatens, the discerning are instructed by the words of Paul, so that our life may serve purely the uprightness of sound things.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: Regius Aduocatus.

units.la: Laudo quidem redditam rationem, sed cum duorum Apostolorum propositueris magisterium, mirum cur prætermisso Paulo, solum Petrum adduxeris in exemplum.
units.tr: I certainly approve the account you have given. But since you have set forth the teaching of two Apostles, it is strange why, passing over Paul, you have brought forward Peter alone as an example.

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.

units.la: Noli, frater, pueriliter currere, imo noli volare, sed perge; pro gravitate quippe negocii prudentia est quoque moderanda sermonis. Audi etiam consequenter & Paulum, discretionis aureæ lineam nostris oculis opponentem, eiusdemque dispensatiuæ compassionis auctorem. Sicut enim Apostolicorum Actuum testatur historia, perambulat Paulus Syriam, & Ciliciam, confirmans Ecclesias, perueniitque in Derben & Lystram: & ecce discipulus quidam erat nomine Timotheus, filius mulieris viduæ Fidelis, pater autem gentilis. Hunc ergo, vt ad compendium veniamus, Apostolus circumcidit, quoniam Iudæos, imo Iudæis, qui in illis erant regionibus, timuit. Cur itaque circumcidit Fidelem hominem, non Iudæum, qui videlicet incircumcisus erat, & natione gentilis, nisi vt discretionis studio deseruiret, ne Iudæi Fideles in scandalum corruentes à Fide recederent? Hoc etiam nunc ad memoriam redit, quoniam aliquando iuxta morem Nazaræorum comam ex voto nutriuit, & postquam nauigasset in Syriam, in Cenchris positus caput iuxta legis mandata totondit. Refert adhuc Lucas sacræ Scriptor historiæ: Cum venissemus, inquit, Ierosolymam, libenter susceperunt nos fratres, & sequenti die Iacobus, & omnes seniores, qui cum eo erant, Euangelio illius comprobato dixerunt ei: Vides frater, quot millia sunt in Iudæis, qui crediderunt in Christo, & omnes amulatores sunt legis. Audierunt autem de te, quod discessionem doceas à Moyse eorum, qui per Gentes sunt Iudæorum, dicens non debere eos circumcidere filios suos, nec secundum consuetudinem ingredi. Quid ergo est? vtique oportet conuenire multitudinem; audient enim te superuenisse. Hoc ergo fac quod tibi dicimus. Sunt nobis quatuor viri votum habentes super se, hos assumptis sanctifica te cum ipsis, & impende in illis, vt radant capita; & scient omnes, quia qua de te audierunt, falsa sunt, sed ambulas & ipse custodiens legem. Tunc Paulus assumptis viris, posteriori die purificatus cum illis intrauit in templum, annuncians expletionem dierum purificationis, donec offerretur pro vnoquoque eorum oblatio. Cur itaque Paulus iuxta ceremonias Iudæorum caput rasit, nudipedalia exercuit, sacrificia obtulit, & legem destruens, legis præcepta seruauit? cur, inquam, hæc omnia nisi vt his qui ex Iudæis Fideles exiterant, scandalum tolleretur? formam suscepit ægritudinis, vt morbos auferret ægrotis; seruauit ceremonias legis, de quibus tamen in Epistola dicit: Quæ mihi fuerunt lucra, facta sunt detrimenta, & propter Christum arbitror velut stercora. Circumcidit hominem, & tamen hoc terribiliter clamat: Dico, inquit, vobis, quia si circumcidamur, Christus nihil nobis proderit. Quod, quæso, maius peccatum esse poterit, quam Christum perdere, Christianæ religionis regulam violare, Iudaicæ legis ritus inducere, nouam Euangelii gratiam impugnare? Et tamen hæc Apostolus Paulus in superficie fecisse conspicitur, ne in ipsis nouæ Fidei rudimentis mentes adhuc tenerae scandala paterentur. Quantum namque in exterioribus cernitur, Cherinthus, & Ebion nil pene peius inueniuntur egisse, quam Paulus, qui nimirum in Christum credentes, propter hoc solum à Patribus anathematizati sunt, quia legis ceremonias Christi Euangelio miscuerunt, & sic noua confessi sunt, vt vetera non mutarent. Sed ecce cum dicitur, quoniam Iacobus & omnes seniores hoc Paulo consilium dederunt: omnes ergo discipuli, quod Paulus fecit, pariter fecerunt; vnumque scilicet habent in hoc meritum, & qui fecit, & qui faciendi dedere consilium. Si ergo ipsi principes mundi, quorum legibus parent non modo regna terrarum, sed ipsa etiam celsitudo cœlorum, non dubitauere pro paucis, qui tunc erant hominibus, in tam periculoso negotio condescendere: cur nobis vtique paruulis, & infra eorum vestigia longe iacentibus non licuit innumerabili Romanæ vrbis multitudini subuenire? Sed quid Apostolos loquimur scandalum cauisse debilium, & nouiter conuersorum, cum & ipse illorum Magister & Dominus, cuius nimirum omnia secula substernuntur imperio, ad nostræ imitationis exemplum, scandalum præcauerit Iudæorum? Simon, inquit, Reges terræ à quibus accipiunt tributum, à filiis suis, an ab alienis? quo respondente, ab alienis: Iesus subiungit: Ergo liberi sunt filii. Vt autem non scandalizemus eos, vade ad mare, mitte hamum, & cum piscem, qui primus ascenderit, tolle, & aperto ore eius inuenies staterem, illum sumens da eis pro me & te. Ad molliendum ergo rigorem rectitudinis, ad tuendam virtutem discretionis, si tibi Petrus non sufficit ad exemplum, iungé & Paulum. Quod si procaci contumaciæ nequeunt vterque sufficere, pudeat te vltra Idum per dicacitatis ineptiam prosilire: Finis enim legis Christus ad iustitiam omni credenti.
units.tr: Do not, brother, run about like a child; indeed, do not fly, but go on. Given the seriousness of the matter, the prudence of your speech must be moderated too. Hear next also Paul, who sets before our eyes the golden line of discretion and is the author of the same dispensing compassion. For as the history of the Apostolic Acts bears witness, Paul travelled through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches, and came to Derbe and Lystra. And behold, a certain disciple was there named Timothy, the son of a faithful widow, but his father was a Gentile. This man, to be brief, the Apostle circumcised, because he feared the Jews, or rather, the Jews who were in those regions. Why then did he circumcise a faithful man, not a Jew, who was indeed uncircumcised and a Gentile by birth, unless it was to serve the aim of discretion, lest Jewish believers, stumbling at the offence, should fall away from the faith? This also comes back to mind now: at one time, in keeping with the custom of the Nazarites, he let his hair grow in accordance with a vow, and after he had sailed to Syria, he shaved his head at Cenchreae in accordance with the commands of the law. Luke, the writer of the sacred history, goes on: When we came to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly. And the next day James and all the elders who were with him, when they had heard his account of the Gospel, said to him: "You see, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews who have believed in Christ, and they are all zealous for the law. But they have heard about you, that you teach the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their sons nor to walk according to the custom. What then is to be done? They will certainly hear that you have come. So do what we tell you. We have four men who have a vow upon them; take these, purify yourself with them, and pay their costs, so that they may shave their heads; and all will know that the things they have heard about you are false, but that you yourself also walk, keeping the law." Then Paul took the men, and the next day, purified with them, he entered the temple, announcing the completion of the days of purification, until the offering was made for each of them. Why, then, did Paul, in accordance with the ceremonies of the Jews, shave his head, perform the rites of purification, offer sacrifices, and, although he was destroying the law, keep the precepts of the law? Why, I ask, all these things, unless it was to remove offence from those who had become faithful from among the Jews? He took on the form of weakness so as to remove the diseases of the sick. He kept the ceremonies of the law, of which nevertheless he says in his Epistle: What things were gain to me, these I have counted loss, and for Christ I consider them as dung. He circumcised a man, and yet he cries out terribly: I say to you, that if you are circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing. What greater sin, I ask, could there be than to lose Christ, to violate the rule of the Christian religion, to bring in the ritual of the Jewish law, and to attack the new grace of the Gospel? And yet the Apostle Paul is seen to have done these things only on the surface, so that tender minds in the very first stages of the new faith should not suffer offence. For as far as outward things are concerned, Cerinthus and Ebion are found to have done almost nothing worse than Paul, who, believing in Christ, were nonetheless anathematized by the Fathers for this alone: that they mixed the ceremonies of the law with the Gospel of Christ and so professed new things that they did not change the old. But see, when it is said that James and all the elders gave this counsel to Paul, then all the disciples together did what Paul did; so they share the merit in this, both he who did it and those who advised him to do it. If, then, the very princes of the world, by whose laws not only the kingdoms of the earth but even the height of heaven obey, did not hesitate to yield, for the sake of the few who were then men, in so perilous a matter, why was it not permitted to us, who are very small and lie far below their footsteps, to help the countless multitude of the city of Rome? But why do we speak of the Apostles having guarded against the offence of the weak and the newly converted, when their own Master and Lord, to whose empire all ages are subject, guarded against the offence of the Jews as an example for our imitation? Simon, he said, do the kings of the earth take tribute from their own sons or from strangers? When he answered, from strangers, Jesus added: Then the sons are free. But so that we do not offend them, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up; when you open its mouth you will find a coin; take it and give it to them for me and for you. To soften the rigour of uprightness and to maintain the virtue of discretion, if Peter is not enough for you as an example, add Paul as well. But if both together cannot suffice against your insolent obstinacy, let it shame you to leap beyond due measure in the silliness of your contentiousness: For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: The Royal Advocate.

units.la: Discretionis virtutem tot Scripturarum testimoniis approbatam improbare non possumus; sed absit, vt vlla virtus sit tam sublimis, tamue præcipua, cuius tuendæ studio in anathematis barathrum corruere debeamus. Nam cum omne, quod nobis ex diuina lege præcipitur, ad hoc procul dubio tendat, vt nos Creatori nostro societate æterna coniungat; si nos abeo, quod absit, per maledictionis sententiam contingat abscedere, quæ virtus, quæ discretio, quæ, sicut dicitur, pia compassio tam incomparabile damnum nobis poterit compensare? Sane si propter hoc solum virtus appetitur, vt omnipotentis Dei societas acquiratur, qualis iam illa virtus esset, quæ nos à diuini gubernii societate repellat?
units.tr: We cannot disapprove of the virtue of discretion, which is so widely confirmed by the testimonies of Scripture; but far be it that any virtue should be so lofty or so pre-eminent that, in pursuing it, we must fall into the pit of anathema. For since everything that is commanded us by the divine law undoubtedly aims at this, that it joins us to our Creator in eternal fellowship, if through the sentence of malediction we should, which God forbid, be cut off from that fellowship, what virtue, what discretion, or what (as it is called) pious compassion could make up to us for so incomparable a loss? Indeed, if a virtue is sought for this reason alone, that the fellowship of the almighty God may be obtained, what kind of virtue would that be which repels us from the fellowship of the divine government?

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: The Defender of the Roman Church.

units.la: Hæc cur prosequaris, quia nobis occulta sunt, euidenter expone.
units.tr: Explain plainly why you pursue these things, since they are hidden from us.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: Regius Aduocatus.

units.la: Synodalis enim decreti pagina, quam cum Concilii totius assensu beatus Nicolaus Papa constituit, cui quippe manus articulum indidit, quam tot Episcoporum venerandus celebrisque conuentus subscriptione firmauit, anathematis vinculo iuxta morem carere non potuit. Unde vos pro compassione, vel condescensione, nescio quam dicitis furentis populi, nequaquam vos metipsos debaretis tam inenodabiliter sententiae nexibus irretire. Ridiculum quippe est, sic obrutum de voragine marini fluctus eruere, vt ipse compellatur exceptor undosis procellarum spumantium cumulis subsidere.
units.tr: For the page of the synodal decree, which blessed Pope Nicholas drew up with the assent of the whole council, and to which he set his own hand, and which such a venerable and celebrated gathering of bishops confirmed with their signatures, could not, as is customary, be free of the bond of anathema. Therefore, when you speak of some compassion or indulgence toward I know not what raging people, you should by no means entangle yourselves so inextricably in the knots of that sentence. For it is absurd to drag a man out of the whirlpool of the sea when he is so overwhelmed that the very one who rescues him is pulled down by the waves and the heaped-up foam of the storms.

units.la: Defensor Romanae Ecclesiae.
units.tr: Defensor Romanae Ecclesiae.

units.la: Cum haec inconsultius loqueris, Antabatarum aduersum me more confligis, qui nimirum dum clausis semper oculis pugnant, alios quidem vulnerant, sed quomodo seipsos a vulneribus tueantur, ignorant. Dicis, quia nequaquam debemus in anathema corruere, etiamsi per hoc valeamus infirmis fratribus subuenire. Huc vibrasti gladium, tentasti vulnus infligere, sed tibimet vbi clypeum opponeres, non vidisti. Nunquid tibi iam de memoria excidit, quod superius protuli, quoniam beatus Paulus in Epistola sua dicit, quia si circumdamur, Christus nihil nobis proderit? Et tamen quod tam districte praebuit, ipse pro charitate fratrum infirmantium, ne scandalum paterentur, impleuit. Quod enim maius siue deterius poterit quis anathema subire, quam cui negatum est, Christum pro sui reatus damnatione prodesse? Nam cui Christus non prodest, proculdubio anathema est: nihilque est aliud anathema aliquem fieri, nisi a Christi, in quo benedicuntur omnes Gentes, societate repelli. Si ergo Paulus hoc anathema pro charitate fratrum subuenire non timuit; imo prorsus euasit, cum non qualemcunque hominem, sed Christianum vtique discipulum circumcidit; tu, quaso, vbi cordis oculos amisisti, qui, quod Apostolus fecit, non faciendum esse testatus ipse enim dicit: Quaecunque scripta sunt, ad nostram doctrinam scripta sunt.
units.tr: When you speak so carelessly, you fight against me in the manner of the Antabatae, who, as they always fight with their eyes shut, wound others indeed, but do not know how to protect themselves from wounds. You say that we must by no means fall into anathema, even if by this we might be able to help weak brethren. You have brandished the sword here and tried to inflict a wound, but you did not see where to set your shield for yourself. Has it not slipped from your memory what I cited above, that the blessed Paul says in his Epistle: if we are surrounded, Christ will profit us nothing? And yet what he laid down so strictly, he himself fulfilled for the sake of the charity of weak brethren, so that they would not suffer offence. For what greater or worse thing can anyone undergo than anathema, to whom it is denied that Christ profits him for the condemnation of his guilt? For to whom Christ does not profit, he is undoubtedly anathema; and to be made anathema is nothing other than to be cast out from the fellowship of Christ, in whom all nations are blessed. If therefore Paul did not fear to take upon himself this anathema for the sake of the charity of the brethren, nay rather he wholly escaped it, since he circumcised not just any man but a Christian disciple; I ask you, where have you lost the eyes of your heart, that you deny what the Apostle did should be done, when he himself testifies: Whatever things were written, were written for our instruction.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: Regius Aduocatus.

units.la: Verisimile est, quod sicut Paulus Coapostolum suum Petrum de Iudaizandi reditum vsurpatione corripuit; ita nihilominus & in semetipsum, postquam discipulum circumcidetat, reprehendari nec mihi hoc aliter vnquam poterit persuaderi, nisi fortassis in eius verbis aliquatenus valeat inueniri.
units.tr: It is likely that just as Paul rebuked his fellow apostle Peter for the return to Judaizing, so also he rebuked himself after he had circumcised the disciple; nor can I ever be persuaded otherwise, unless perhaps something in his words can be found to support it to some extent.

units.la: Defensor Romanae Ecclesiae.
units.tr: Defensor Romanae Ecclesiae.

units.la: Vt nullus ambiguitatis nexus in tua mente remaneat, vt nulla cor tuum super hoc negotio deinceps caligo confundat, audi quid idem Paulus ad Romanos dicat: Veritatem dico in Christo, non mentior, testimonium mihi perhibente conscientia mea in Spiritu sancto, quoniam tristitia est mihi magna & continuus dolor cordis mei: optabam enim ipse anathema esse a Christo pro fratribus meis, qui sunt cognati mei secundum carnem, qui sunt Israelita. Ecce Paulus cum non sit sicut nos, necessitate coactus, sponte ac voluntarie desiderat anathema esse pro fratribus; & tu mihi proponis anathema timendum, vbi me perspicis, & inevitabili prorsus necessitate fuisse constrictum, & charitatis studio, ne tanta fratrum multitudo corrueret, inclinatum: Audi etiam quod Moyses pro populo Israelitico postulans dicat: Obsecro Domine, peccauit populus iste peccatum maximum, fecerunt que sibi Deos aureos: & dimitte eis hanc noxam, aut si non facis, dele me de libro tuo quem scripsisti. Quod nimirum pleniter fiet, cum reprobis in iudicio dicet: Ite maledicti in ignem aeternum. Ecce hic Paulus optat anathema pro fratribus fieri: ecce illic Moyses postulat ex Dei libro pro populo, quem duebat, charitate deleri: & sola Romana Ecclesia, quae pietatem & charitatem toto terrarum orbe spiritualiter & principaliter docet, ex imminentibus vibratio vndique gladiis filios suos, quos quotidie per sacri baptismatis mysterium generat, liberare non auderet? Maledictus vir, ait Saul, qui comederit panem vsque ad vesperam, donec vlciscar me de inimicis meis. In hoc, sicut legitur, anathema Ionathas excidit, sed cum ab imminenti mortis sententia, charitas, qua pro populo strenue dimicauerat, liberauit. Vis audire, quid etiam de ipso Iesu, totius benedictionis auctore, idem Apostolus dicat? Christus, inquit, vt vos liberaret a maledicto legis, factus est maledictum. Si ergo ipse auctor benedictionis aeternae, vt nos a vinculo maledictionis absoluerete, maledictioni non dedignatus est subiacere: si sancti quique vel noui, vel Veteris Testamenti, dum sui capitis imitantur exemplum, vt infirmis subuenire fratribus in periculis concupiscunt, anathema subire sententiam nullatenus perhorrescunt: cur vni mihi niteris imputare peccatum, & charitatem ad hoc me induxisse non perspicis, quae operit multitudinem peccatorum? Quomodo autem me cuiusliber hominis sententia ligat, quem charitas ipsa, quae Deus est, liberat? Erubescat igitur humani anathematis imputator, cum per charitatis gratiam mecum sit aeternae benedictionis indulgentia.
units.tr: So that no knot of ambiguity may remain in your mind, so that no darkness may henceforth confuse your heart on this matter, hear what the same Paul says to the Romans: I speak the truth in Christ, I do not lie, my conscience bearing me witness in the Holy Spirit, that I have great sorrow and continual grief in my heart; for I could wish that I myself were anathema from Christ for my brethren, who are my kinsmen according to the flesh, who are Israelites. Behold, Paul, though he is not as we are, compelled by necessity, desires anathema for the brethren of his own accord and willingly; and you set before me anathema as something to be feared, when you see that I was bound by an altogether inevitable necessity and inclined by zeal for charity, lest so great a multitude of brethren should fall. Hear also what Moses, pleading for the people of Israel, says: I beseech you, Lord, this people has sinned a very great sin, and they have made for themselves golden gods; and forgive them this offence, or if you do not, blot me out of your book which you have written. Which surely will be fully fulfilled when he says to the reprobate at judgment: Depart, you accursed, into eternal fire. Behold, here Paul wishes anathema to come upon the brethren; behold, there Moses asks, out of love for the people he led, to be blotted out of God's book; and shall the Roman Church alone, which teaches piety and charity spiritually and chiefly throughout the whole world, not dare to free her sons, whom she daily begets through the mystery of holy baptism, from the swords brandished on every side and hanging over them? Cursed be the man, said Saul, who eats bread until evening, until I avenge myself on my enemies. In this, as we read, Jonathan fell under the curse, but charity, by which he had bravely fought for the people, freed him from the imminent sentence of death. Do you want to hear what the same Apostle says about Jesus himself, the author of all blessing? Christ, he says, that he might redeem us from the curse of the law, was made a curse. If therefore the very author of eternal blessing did not disdain to submit to a curse, so that he might absolve us from the bond of malediction; and if the holy men of both the New and the Old Testament, following the example of their Head, desire to help weak brethren in dangers, and in no way shrink from undergoing the sentence of anathema; why do you strive to impute sin to me alone, and do not see that charity has led me to this, which covers the multitude of sins? Moreover, how can the sentence of any human being bind me, whom charity itself, which is God, sets free? Let the one who imputes human anathema therefore blush, since through the grace of charity the indulgence of eternal blessing is with me.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: The Royal Advocate.

units.la: Cuicumque in disputatione certanti veritas ipsa defecerit, ineptum est adhuc per ambages, atque versutias pertinaciter niti; ridiculum est diutius verbis prolixioribus immorari: de vinculo siquidem anathematis, quo te hactenus arbitrabar astringi, ita te nauiter expedisti, vt nihil de caetero tibi valeat obiici, nihil super hoc capitulo rationabiliter possit opponi. Verumtamen adhuc video mihi materiam superesse, quam tibi valeam non sine causa reluctatori obiicere. Dicis, qui necessitate constricti, & velut angusti temporis breui spacio coartati nequaquam potuistis tuistis in electione Pontificis expectare consensum regiæ maiestatis. Quod profecto friuolum esse suspicuum est. Constat enim tres plus minus menses interim decurrisse, ex quo sanctæ memoriæ Papa Nicolaus occubuit, usque ad Kalend. Octobr. cum iste successit. Videamus ergo si per tam morosam longitudinem, trimestris videlicet spacii, non potuerit ab aula regia pragmaticæ sanctionis vobis apocha reportari.
units.tr: When a man who is contending in a disputation has been abandoned by the truth itself, it is pointless to keep pressing stubbornly through circumlocutions and tricks, and ridiculous to linger longer over wordy verbiage. As for the bond of anathema, by which I had supposed you were bound until now, you have so vigorously freed yourself from it that nothing more can be objected against you and nothing reasonable can be raised against you on this point. Yet I still see that some material remains which I can, not without cause, throw at you as you struggle. You say that you, bound by necessity and confined, as it were, within the narrow span of a short time, could by no means wait for the consent of the royal majesty in the election of the Pope. This is surely suspected to be frivolous. For it is established that about three months passed in the meantime, from the death of Pope Nicholas of holy memory until the first of October, when this man succeeded. Let us see, then, whether within so long a delay, namely a space of three months, the approval of the pragmatic sanction could not have been obtained for you from the royal court.

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defender of the Roman Church.

units.la: Ecce compellis me vulgato sermone depromere, quod Imperialis palatii reverentia decreuerant silentio praeterire: sed iuxta vestræ scilicet exactionis instantiam iam proferatur in medium opus egregium vestrum, seculis omnibus inauditum. Rectores enim aulæ regiæ cum nonnullis Teutonici regni sanctis (ut vita loquar) Episcopis conspirantes contra Romanam Ecclesiam Concilium collegistis, quo Papam quasi per synodalem sententiam condemnastis, & omnia quæ ab eo fuerunt statuta, quasi incredibili prorsus audacia præsumpsistis. In quo nimirum non dicam iudicio, sed præiudicio idipsum quoque priuilegium, quod Regi prædictus Papa contulerat, si dicere liceat, vacuastis. Nam dum, quidquid ille constituit, vestra sententia decernente destruitur; consequenter etiam id, quod ab eo Regi præstitum fuerat, aboletur. Sed absit à nobis, ut propter cuiuslibet hominis insolentiam Rex, qui innocens erat, quantum ad nos, rem sui iuris amittat, & quem auctore Deo votis omnibus præstolamur ad Imperiale fastigium, non permittemus ob alienam culpam regiæ dignitatis incurrere detrimentum. Sed ut totam inauditæ calamitatis nostræ percurramus historiam, Stephanus Cardinalis presbyter Apostolicæ Sedis, vir videlicet tantæ grauitatis & honestatis nitore conspicuus, tantis denique, sicut non obscurum est, virtutum floribus insignitus, cum Apostolicis libris ad aulam regiam missus, ab aulicis administratoribus non est admissus, sed per quinque fere dies, ad beati Petri & Apostolicæ Sedis iniuriam, præforibus mansit exclusus. Quod ille, vtpote vir grauis & patiens æquanimiter tulit: Legati tamen officium, quo fungebatur, implere non potuit. Clausum itaque signatumque mysterium Concilii, cuius erat gerulus, retulit, quia regiis eum præsentari conspectibus Curialium plectenda temeritas non permisit. In qua nimirum inopinatæ præsumptionis audacia tanta disputandi videtur inesse materia, vt & Demosthenis eloquentiam vincat, & copiam Tullianæ facultatis excedat. Vnde si vellemus iniuriam nostram distinctius persequi, iure possemus obtendere, quia vos Romanæ Ecclesiæ vosmetipsos dono priuastis, qui scilicet ei præiudicii vestri gratis contumeliam intulistis. Ille quippe fœdus amicitiæ violat, qui gratis amicum per offensionis molestiam pulsat. Nam & Dominus Iudæis per Ieremiam ait: Ecce feriam domui Israel, & domui Iuda fœdus nouum, non secundum pactum, quod pepigi cum patribus eorum, pactum quod irritum fecerunt. Ille ergo irritum reddit beneficii pactum, qui prior violat amicitiæ sacramentum. Veruntamen Romana Ecclesia non vult exaggerare, quod pertulit, sed perseuerare cupit in muhere, quod regio culmini liberaliter prorogauit.
units.tr: Look, you compel me to bring out in plain speech what the reverence of the Imperial palace had decided to pass over in silence. But since you press so insistently, let your outstanding work, unheard of in every age, now be brought into the open. You, the rulers of the royal court, conspiring with some holy bishops of the Teutonic kingdom (to speak plainly), gathered a council against the Roman Church, by which you condemned the Pope as if by a synodal sentence, and presumed, with an utterly incredible audacity, to overturn everything he had decreed. In this you have, I will not say judged, but prejudged, and, if I may say so, emptied of force that very privilege which the said Pope had granted to the King. For while whatever he established is destroyed by your decree, it follows that what had been granted to the King by him is also abolished. But far be it from us that the King, who is innocent so far as we are concerned, should lose his rights because of the insolence of any man. And whom we, with all our prayers, await to the Imperial summit under God's guidance, we will not permit to suffer loss of royal dignity through another's fault. But to run through the whole history of our unheard-of calamity: Stephen, a cardinal priest of the Apostolic See, a man conspicuous for such gravity and brightness of honour, and indeed, as is not obscure, adorned with such flowers of virtue, was sent to the royal court with Apostolic letters, but was not admitted by the court administrators, and for nearly five days remained shut out before the doors, to the injury of blessed Peter and the Apostolic See. He, as a serious man who endured patiently, bore this calmly; yet he could not carry out the office of legate which he held. Therefore he brought back the sealed and closed mystery of the Council, of which he was the bearer, because the punishable rashness of the courtiers did not permit him to be presented before the royal eyes. In this unexpected audacity of presumption there seems to be so much matter for debate that it surpasses the eloquence of Demosthenes and exceeds the copiousness of Tullian ability. Hence, if we wished to pursue our injury more distinctly, we could rightly allege that you have deprived yourselves of the gift of the Roman Church, you who have gratuitously inflicted the insult of your prejudgment upon her. For he who violates the bond of friendship is the one who gratuitously strikes a friend with the annoyance of offence. And the Lord says to the Jews through Jeremiah: "Behold, I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah, not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers, a covenant which they broke." Therefore he who first violates the sacrament of friendship makes the covenant of benefit void. Nevertheless the Roman Church does not wish to magnify what she has suffered, but desires to persevere in the gift which she has generously extended to the royal majesty.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: The Royal Advocate.

units.la: Quod Domino nostro Regi reuerenter adscribis innocentiam, digne facis: quod autem administratoribus aulæ publicæ deuoluis è diuerso calumniam, videtur iniustum. Quicquid enim circa vos in huiusmodi calibus actum est, ad hoc nos Regium munus impulit, Imperiale præceptum, non propriæ libertatis arbitrium.
units.tr: You rightly attribute innocence to our Lord the King with reverence; but it seems unjust that you, on the other hand, throw the blame onto the administrators of the public court. For whatever has been done around you in such matters, it was the royal office and the Imperial command that impelled us, not the choice of our own liberty.

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defender of the Roman Church.

units.la: Et ego tibi secundum cordis tui duritiem respondebo: dico enim quod Dei omnipotentis obtemperare sermonibus aliquando peccatum est.
units.tr: And I will answer you according to the hardness of your heart: for I say that to obey the words of Almighty God is at some time a sin.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: The Royal Advocate.

units.la: Ad hoc quod asseris, mens humana concutitur, & Christianæ pietatis ferre non valet audiens.
units.tr: As to what you assert, the human mind is shaken, and cannot bear to hear it as Christian piety requires.

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defender of the Roman Church.

units.la: Quia hoc tantopere miraris, illud etiam consequenter adiicio, quia propter hoc, quod Deo quidam promptus obediuit, funditus periit: alius ob id, quod obtemperare contemplit, ad cumulum gratiæ plenioris ascendit.
units.tr: Since you wonder so greatly at this, I add the following consequence as well: because of this, that one man readily obeyed God, he perished utterly; another, because he hesitated to obey, rose to the heap of fuller grace.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: The Royal Advocate.

units.la: Incredibile est valde quod dicis, veruntamen si vales exemplis approbare quod loqueris, dic, quia vnquam Deo obediuit, ac propterea periit?
units.tr: What you say is very hard to believe. But if you can support your claim with examples, tell me: has anyone ever obeyed God and for that reason perished?

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defender of the Roman Church.

units.la: Non te latet quod Iudæ Ischarioti, qui iam accepto consilio eum traditurus erat, ait Dominus: Quod facis, fac citius. Postmodum quoque cum ad eius osculum accedere præsumpsisset, adiicit: Amice, ad quid venisti? subauditur, perfice. Sed quia miser hic sermonibus efficaciter obediuit, irreuocabiliter periit.
units.tr: You are not unaware that the Lord said to Judas Iscariot, who had already taken counsel and was about to betray him: What you do, do quickly. Afterwards, when Judas had presumed to approach for his kiss, the Lord added: Friend, why have you come? (understood: do it). But because this wretched man obeyed the words effectively, he perished beyond recall.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: The Royal Advocate.

units.la: Huius propositionis ratione reddita, redde consequenter alterius, quis scilicet Dei omnipotentis obedientiam spreuit, & propter hoc copiosiorem gratiam meruit.
units.tr: Having given the reason for this proposition, now give the other in turn: who, namely, despised the obedience of Almighty God and for this merited a more abundant grace?

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defender of the Roman Church.

units.la: Si placet hoc in memoriam reuoca, quod Dominus ad Ieremiam dixit: Vade ad domum Rechabitarum, & loquere eis, & introduces in domum Domini in vnam exhedram thesaurorum, & dabis eis bibere vinum. Et paulo post Propheta subiungit: Et posui coram filiis Rehabitarum, scyphos plenos vino & calices, & dixi ad eos, bibite vinum. Qui responderunt: Non bibemus vinum, quia Ionadab pater noster praecepit nobis dicens: non bibetis vinum vos & filii vestri vsque in sempiternum. Vnde postmodum Ieremias ait eis: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus exercituum: non deficiet vir de stirpe Ionadab filii Rechab stans in conspectu meo cunctis diebus. At ecce ille male obediens, perfunctus obedientiæ munere cucurrit ad laqueum: isti feliciter inobedientes, perpetuum sui Conditoris mertere conspectum. Hoc etiam ad hoc valet, quod superius dictum est, quia cum Papam sine consensu regis eligimus, non debetis quod extrinsecus actum est, diiudicare, sed potius quo animo, & qua intentione sit factum, diligenter attendere.
units.tr: If you please, recall what the Lord said to Jeremiah: Go to the house of the Rechabites, speak to them, and bring them into the house of the Lord, into one of the chambers of the treasuries, and give them wine to drink. A little later the prophet adds: And I set before the sons of the Rechabites bowls full of wine and cups, and I said to them, drink wine. They answered: We will not drink wine, for Jonadab our father commanded us, saying: you and your sons shall never drink wine for ever. Hence Jeremiah afterwards said to them: Thus says the Lord of hosts: there shall not fail a man of the stock of Jonadab son of Rechab, standing before me all the days. Yet behold, that man who obeyed badly, having performed his duty of obedience, ran to the noose; while these, happily disobedient, were to behold the face of their Creator for ever. This also bears on what was said above: when we elect a Pope without the consent of the king, you must not judge what is done outwardly, but rather attend carefully to the spirit and intention with which it is done.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: The Royal Advocate.

units.la: Hæc argumenta nobis domestica sunt, & numquam deficiunt, quia de promptuariis proferuntur, semper enim possumus in parui operis exhibitione delinquere, sed quia occulta est, ad puræ mentis debemus patrocinium confugere.
units.tr: These arguments are familiar to us and never run out, for they are drawn from our storeroom. We can always err in the performance of some small work; but since the intention is hidden, we must take refuge in the defence of a pure mind.

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defender of the Roman Church.

units.la: Censéne semper debere iuxta rerum, atque verborum superficiem iudicari? quid enim iuxta verborum strepitum magis est absonum, quam cum Deus Pater & Filius & Spiritus sanctus mediatorem Dei & hominum, dicitur tradidisse? Ecce Christum tradidit Iudas, tradidit & Deus Pater: aliquid non quasi similis casus videtur? ergo ne traditor est Iudas, & traditor Deus Pater?
units.tr: Do you think things must always be judged by the outward surface of deeds and words? For what sounds more absurd, going by the mere noise of the words, than to say that God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit delivered up the Mediator between God and men? Judas delivered up Christ; God the Father also delivered him up. Does not the case seem similar? Is Judas therefore a traitor, and is God the Father a traitor?

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: The Royal Advocate.

units.la: Vnde probas, quia Pater & Filius & Spiritus sanctus tradiderint Saluatorem?
units.tr: From what do you prove that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit delivered up the Saviour?

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defender of the Roman Church.

units.la: Audi Apostolum dicentem: Qui proprio Filio suo non pepercit, sed pro omnibus nobis tradidit illum. Cum & Salomon ait: Cum sis iussus & omnia iusse dispensas, ipsum qui non debet puniri, condemnas. Quod autem se Filius tradidit, idem dicit Apostolus: Qui me dilexit, & tradidit semetipsum pro me. Quod autem & Spiritus sanctus tradidit Filium, Sapientia perhibet dicens: Vnigenitus est enim spiritus Sapientia, & non liberauit maledictum a labiis suis. Maledicti apud veteres dicebantur omnes, qui suspendebantur in ligno. Christus autem, vt Apostolus dicit, vt nos liberaret a maledicto, factus est maledictum. Spiritus ergo sanctus non liberauit maledictum a labiis suis, quia quæ per ora Prophetarum de Christi passione locutus est, non cohibuit, sed super eum sine dimissione compleri cuncta permisit. Ergo secundum te, qui non de cordis intentione, sed semper ex operum vis superficie iudicare: si Pater tradidit Filium, & ipse se tradidit Filius, & Spiritus sanctus, Iudas quid male fecit? Facta est traditio a Patre, facta est a Filio, neconon a Spiritu sancto, facta est a Iuda: vna res a pluribus facta est, sed eadem res in operatoribus decernenda est. Quod enim Deus omnipotens ex charitate, hoc Iudas fecit ex cupiditate acquirendæ pecuniæ. Quod Deus fecit ad salutis nostræ remedium, hoc ille fecit ad explendum insatiabilis auaritiæ votum. Vides ergo, quia non quod homo faciat, debemus attendere; sed quo animo & voluntate faciat, diligenter examinare. Nam si sola duntaxat exteriora perpendimus, inuenimus ipsum Dominum Saluatorem & dixisse quod prohibet, & fecisse aliter quod iubet. Quisquis, ait, dixerit fratri suo, fatue, reus erit gehennæ ignis: & tamen ipso Resurrectionis suæ die duobus de se dubitantibus loquentibus ait: O stulti & tardi corde ad credendum! dixerat etiam in monte Discipulis: Si quis te percusserit in dexteram maxillam, præbe illi & alteram. In passione vero positus percutienti se in maxillam puero sacerdotis non modo non alteram præbuit, sed insuper dixit: Si male locutus sum, exprobra de malo: si autem bene, cur me cædis? Et quomodo iam verum est, quod de illo Lucas ait: Quod cœpit facere & docere, si quod docuit, non implevit? Sed proculdubio intelligendum est, hoc eum præcepisse ad præparationem cordis, non autem ad ostensionem operis. Quomodo enim paratus corde non fuit in maxillam alteram cædi, qui pro hominum salute decreuerat toto corpore crucifigi? Paulus etiam palma percussus iussione Pontificis, ait: Percutiet te Deus, paries dealbate. Quod minus intelligentibus videtur in verbo conuiciari, sed in sensu prophetici retinet oraculi sacramentum. Paries enim dealbatus hypocrisis est, sacerdotalem sub hoc nomine præferens dignitatem, sed occultans intrinsecus luteam malitiæ turpitudinem; nam quod hominis ministeris fuit, mirabiliter custodiuit. Cum enim illi diceretur: Principi sacerdotum maledicis? respondit, Nescivi, frater, quia princeps esset sacerdotum. Scriptum est enim: Principi populi tui non maledices. Vbi patenter ostenditur, quanta idem tranquillitate dixisset, quod iratus intulisse videbatur. Quibus Scripturarum testimoniis quid aliud edocemur, nisi quia non iuxta verba nuda semper debemus sententias iudicare, sed quo animo, qua mentis intentione proferantur, suspicere?
units.tr: Hear the Apostle saying: He who did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all. Solomon also says: Since you are commanded and order all things, you condemn him who ought not to be punished. That the Son also delivered himself up, the Apostle says the same: He loved me and delivered himself up for me. That the Holy Spirit delivered up the Son, Wisdom bears witness, saying: For the Spirit of wisdom is only-begotten, and has not released the curse from his lips. All who hang upon a tree were called accursed by the ancients. Christ, as the Apostle says, that he might free us from the curse, was made a curse. The Holy Spirit therefore did not release the curse from his lips, because what he spoke through the mouths of the prophets concerning the passion of Christ he did not restrain, but allowed everything to be fulfilled upon him without omission. So according to you, who judge not from the intention of the heart but always from the surface force of the deeds: if the Father delivered up the Son, and the Son delivered himself up, and the Holy Spirit did, what wrong did Judas do? The delivering up was done by the Father, done by the Son, likewise by the Holy Spirit, and done by Judas: one act was done by several, but the same act must be judged in its agents. For what God Almighty did out of love, Judas did out of greed for acquiring money. What God did as a remedy for our salvation, he did to satisfy the vow of insatiable avarice. You see, therefore, that we must attend not to what a man does, but carefully examine with what mind and will he does it. For if we weigh only the outward things, we find that the Lord and Saviour himself both said what he forbids and did otherwise than he commands. Whoever, he says, shall say to his brother, Fool, shall be liable to the fire of hell. Yet on the very day of his resurrection, when two disciples doubted concerning him, he said: O foolish men and slow of heart to believe! He had also said to the disciples on the mountain: If anyone strikes you on the right cheek, offer him the other also. Yet in his passion, when a servant of the high priest struck him on the cheek, he not only did not offer the other, but said: If I have spoken evil, bear witness to the evil; but if well, why do you strike me? And how is it true what Luke says of him: What he began to do and to teach, if he did not fulfil what he taught? But without doubt it must be understood that he commanded this for the preparation of the heart, not for the display of the deed. For how could he not be ready in heart to be struck on the other cheek, who had decided to be crucified with his whole body for the salvation of men? Paul also, struck on the mouth by the order of the high priest, said: God will strike you, whitewashed wall. This seems to those who do not understand to be mere abuse in words, but in its sense it keeps the mystery of a prophetic oracle. For a whitewashed wall is hypocrisy, which presents the dignity of the priesthood under this name but hides inwardly the filthy uncleanness of malice. For what belonged to the office of a minister he carefully preserved. When it was said to him: Do you revile the high priest of God? he answered: I did not know, brothers, that he was high priest. For it is written: You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people. Here it is plainly shown how calmly he said what he seemed to have said in anger. What else are we taught by these testimonies of Scripture, except that we must not always judge sentences by the bare words, but must look to the spirit and the intention of mind with which they are spoken?

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: The Royal Advocate.

units.la: Dubia quæ proponis, luculenter elucidas per exempla quæ subiicis: sed quæso te ut ad superiora paulisper redeas, & cum non calumnieris, vobis præiudicium intulisse, qui regiæ ditioni parcuntur patenter exponas.
units.tr: You clear up the doubts you raise very clearly, using the examples you add. But I beg you to go back a little to what came before, and to set out plainly how you have shown that we, who spare the royal authority, have not been prejudiced, without making any false accusation.

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defender of the Roman Church.

units.la: Recte plane, ordinabiliter & congruenter, postquam omnis vestræ partis obiectio non rhetoricis argumentis, vel coloribus oratoriis, non denique dialecticis syllogismis, sed viuæ potius atque perspicuæ veritatis est ratione purgata: versa vice iam dignum est, ut de vestris excessibus vel breuiter disseratur. Enimuero damnatio Papæ tam grauis & inexpiabilis, ut non humano, sed diuino duntaxat sit tractanda iudicio. Reges autem nostros tum ætatis infirmitas, tum fragilitas sexus excusat: quibus utique non reatus adscribitur, sed eorum consiliariis, ut dignum est, imputatur. Omissis itaque peruersitatibus cæteris, ut quid ignorante Roma, reprobum Dominum in Romanum Pontificem eligere præsumpsistis?
units.tr: Quite rightly, orderly and fittingly, now that every objection from your side has been cleansed, not by rhetorical arguments, oratorical colours or dialectical syllogisms, but by the reasoning of living and plain truth, it is right that your excesses also be discussed briefly. Indeed the condemnation of a Pope is so grave and inexpiable that it must be handled not by human judgement alone but by divine judgement. Our kings, however, are excused by their youth and the frailty of their sex; blame is not assigned to them but, as is fitting, imputed to their counsellors. Setting aside your other perversities, why did you presume, with Rome ignorant, to elect a reprobate man as Roman Pontiff?

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: The Royal Advocate.

units.la: Electionem quidem, ut palam est fecimus, sed longe prius Gerardo comite, aliisque Romanis, ut videbatur, ciuibus infatigabiliter insistentibus ad hoc inducti sumus. Nam & Abbas Monasterii quod dicitur, Cliuus Scauri, non defuit. Non ergo, ut asseris, ignorante Roma, sed præsente, atque petente, Romani Pontificis electio facta est.
units.tr: We did make the election, as is plain, but long before that we were drawn into it by Count Gerard and other Roman citizens, who, as it seemed, pressed the matter tirelessly. For the abbot of the monastery called Clivus Scauri was not wanting either. So the election of the Roman Pontiff was not made, as you assert, with Rome ignorant, but with Rome present and asking for it.

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defender of the Roman Church.

units.la: In hoc pro me facis, dum Gerardo sub anathemate constituto te communicasse testaris, nam ut de Abbate & alias interim sileamus, de Gerardo liceat tantummodo dicere, Ecclesiæ hominem non fuisse, & Christi nequaquam pertinuisse Fidelibus. Illud enim unum caput anathemati, maledictionique subiacuit, omnium fere Pontificum, quicunque Romanæ Ecclesiæ eius temporibus præfuerunt: demum paulo antequam moreretur, propter Comitem Angum & Archiepiscopum, quos à beati Petri Liminibus reduntes inuasit, spoliauit, & usque ad mille Papienses monetæ libras appendentia rapuit. Propter hoc itaque in plenaria Synodo, Papa Nicolao præsidente, excommunicatus est, & extinctis luminaribus sub perpetuo fuit anathemate condemnatus. Perpendat igitur sancta Synodus, si illius, eiusque complicum rata iure videatur electio, qui tam terribiliter est ab Ecclesiæ visceribus Euangelica atque canonica falce præcisus, ut ne in morte quidè de Christianitatis fuerit titulo reformatus, & si per eum ordinari Romanam Ecclesiam dignum fuit, qui eius semper cruentue extitit inimicus; quia eam semper est feraliter persecutus. Et quomodo summam debet Ecclesiam ordinare, cui cuiuscunque limen Ecclesiæ non licet attingere? Clamat Dominus ad Israel: Anathema in medio tui Israel, non poteris stare contra hostes tuos, donec deleatur ex te, qui hoc contaminatus est scelere. Et hoc quare? Quoniam Achan filius Charmi de anathemate Hiericho ducentos duntaxat argenti siclos, regulamque auream quinquaginta siclorum, & coccineum abstulerat pallium. Et ob hanc vilem videlicet summam auctor sceleris non modo lapidatur, sed & lapidum acervis obruitur. Si propter illum hominem, qui duntaxat vnum sacrilegium fraude commiserat, Israel ante suorum hostium faciem ruituras erat: quomodo stabit Ecclesia, si per virum tot criminibus inuolutum fuerit ordinata? præferrin cum & talem elegerit, in quem, reste mundo, omnium vitiorum sententia confluxit. Pseudoepiscopi Apostolorum Antichristi aduersarium Christi, amici puellarum mangonem Ecclesiarum. Quid igitur istorum iusto videbitur examine præferendus? vtrum is quem elegit vnus vir perpetuæ maledictionis anathemate condemnatus; an ille potius, quem Cardinales Episcopi vnanimiter vocauerunt, quem Clerus elegit, quem populus expetiuit, non ab extremitate terrarum, sed intra mœnia Romanorum, & in ipsius Sedis Apostolicæ gremio.
units.tr: In this you help my case, since you testify that you held communion with Gerard, who was placed under anathema. To say nothing for now of the abbot and others, let me say only this about Gerard: he was not a man of the Church, and he did not belong in any way to the faithful of Christ. That one charge subjected him to anathema and curse, a charge that almost all the Popes who presided over the Roman Church in his times were also under. Finally, shortly before he died, on account of Count Angus and the Archbishop, whom he attacked as they returned from the threshold of the blessed Peter, he despoiled them and seized up to a thousand pounds of Pavian coin in value. For this reason he was excommunicated in a full synod, with Pope Nicholas presiding, and, with the candles extinguished, he was condemned under perpetual anathema. Let the holy synod therefore weigh whether the election of him and his accomplices can rightly be thought valid, since he was cut off so terribly from the bowels of the Church by the Gospel and canonical sickle that, even in death, he was not restored to the title of Christianity; and whether it was fitting for the Roman Church to be ordained through a man who was always her bloody enemy, since he always persecuted her savagely. And how can one who may not so much as touch the threshold of any church ordain the Church? The Lord cries out to Israel: "Anathema is in the midst of you, Israel; you cannot stand against your enemies until the one who is defiled by this crime is destroyed from among you." And why? Because Achan, son of Carmi, had taken from the devoted things of Jericho only two hundred shekels of silver, a golden wedge of fifty shekels, and a scarlet cloak. And for this paltry sum, of course, the author of the crime was not only stoned but buried under a heap of stones. If Israel was going to fall before the face of its enemies on account of that one man, who had committed only one sacrilege by fraud, how will the Church stand if she is ordained through a man entangled in so many crimes? Or rather, since he chose such a man, into whom, as it were, the verdict of every vice has flowed. Pseudo-bishops of the Apostles, Antichrist's adversary of Christ, friend of harlots, hireling of the churches. Which of these, then, shall be preferred by a just examination? He whom one man chose, a man condemned by the anathema of perpetual curse? Or rather he whom the cardinal bishops unanimously called, whom the clergy elected, whom the people desired, not from the ends of the earth but within the walls of Rome and in the very bosom of the Apostolic See.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: The Royal Advocate.

units.la: Tot ate rationibus redditis possumus sortassis adhibere consensum, si semel emissam decreret Regiam maiestatem mutare sententiam: principali quippe gloriæ velut inconstantiæ nævus imprimitur, si quodcunque suæ constitutionis edictum leniter annulletur.
units.tr: With so many reasons given, we might perhaps give our assent, if his royal majesty were to decree a change of a sentence once issued. For a blemish of inconstancy, as it were, is stamped upon the principal glory if any edict of his constitution is lightly annulled.

units.la: Defensor Romanæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Defender of the Roman Church.

units.la: Quis nesciat Rege Deum esse maiorem, & tamen dicere non erubescit: Pœnitet me, quod constitutus Saul Regem. Et per Samuelem ei denuntiat, dicens: Projecit te Dominus ne sis Rex super Israel. Si poenitere se Deus asseruit, qui futura cuncta cognouerat: cur homo suam mutare in melius sententiam erubescat, qui qualis & ipse quoque sit futurus ignorat? Ille de bono factus est malus; iste (videlicet Cadalous) dolosus de malo, vtique quod iam erat, sit quotidie diaboli mors deterior.
units.tr: Who does not know that God is greater than a king, and yet does not blush to say: "It repents me that I set up Saul as king"? And through Samuel he declares to him: "The Lord has rejected you, so that you shall not be king over Israel." If God, who had known all future things, asserted that he repented, why should a man blush to change his opinion for the better, when he does not know what he himself will be? The former was made bad from good; this one, Cadalus, crafty from bad, becoming daily something worse than what he already was, a death worse than the devil's.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: The Royal Advocate.

units.la: Quam inconsulte nunc loqueris, qui diabolum deteriorari posse testaris, qui certe tam malus est, vt deterior esse non possit.
units.tr: How ill-advised your words now are, you who declare that the devil can become worse, when he is surely so wicked that he cannot be any worse.

units.la: Defensor Romanae Ecclesiae.
units.tr: The Defender of the Roman Church.

units.la: Meatior si quod proposui, Scripturae testimoniis comprobare non valeo. Nam Isaia teste, dicebat superbus in mundi principio: Ascendam super altitudinem nubium, similis ero Altissimo. Paulus autem dicit, in fine mundi reniens aduersatur & extollitur supra omne quod dicitur Deus, aut quod colitur. Qui ergo tunc affectauit Deo se similem esse; in fine mundi iam deterior factus qui vult prior eminere. Per quod manifesto colligitur diabolum adhuc in deteriora posse corruere: & quia Diabolus interpretatur deorsum fluens, Gedalum a cadendo dictus ruinam populi sonat, ipsisque nominibus aptissime inuicem concordant. Dic ergo: quomodo iste Pontifex esset, quem non populus Romanus, sed vnus homo cum suis complicibus, idemque non Romanus, sed suburbanus (sempe Gerardus Galeria Dominus Est Galeriis oppidulum prope Vrbem situm, ideoque suburbanum appellatum) & non Ecclesiae filius, sed maledictus & anathematizatus elegit? Illene esset tuo iudicio Pontifex qui suam vendidit, vt Romanam Ecclesiam obtineret? qui Romanos occidit in ore gladii, vt Romanus Pontifex fieret? Dices me non debuisse Pontificem sine consensu Regis eligere, & magni pendendum mihi fuisse, vt populus non periret. Ecce hinc beatus Augustinus Hipponensi ecclesiae, Valerio viuente, praeficitur: ecce illinc Ambrosius octauo die postquam baptizatus est, perceptis cunctis ecclesiasticis gradibus Episcopus ordinatur. In quibus vtique ob nihil aliud canonicae auctoritatis ordo deseritur, nisi dunt axat vt saluti populi consulatur, Et tu mihi dicis in seruando populo ipsi Regi me debuisse consulere, vt sibimet in dando consensu vnius epistolae gloria proueniret. Nam vnde postmodum Romanus Imperator fieret, si tunc se Romanus populus mutuis vulneribus peremisset? Porro autem, quia in constituendo Pontifice Romana Ecclesia a charitate regia non recessit, hoc etiam indicio est, quia cum in Clero suo religiosis viris & sapientibus abundaret, non de propriis, sed eum, qui Regi tanquam domesticus & familiaris erat, elegit.
units.tr: If what I have proposed cannot be confirmed by the testimonies of Scripture, then I am lying. For, according to Isaiah, the proud one said at the beginning of the world: "I will ascend above the height of the clouds; I will be like the Most High." Paul also says that at the end of the world he will oppose and exalt himself above everything that is called God or worshipped. So he who then aimed to be like God, now at the end of the world, having become worse, wants to stand out above the rest. From this it is clearly gathered that the devil can still fall into worse things. And since "Diabolus" means "flowing downwards," and "Gedalum," named from falling, signifies the ruin of the people, the names themselves agree very aptly with one another. Tell me, then, what sort of pope was he whom not the Roman people but one man, with his accomplices, chose, and that man not a Roman but a suburban (namely Gerard, lord of Galeria, a small town situated near the City, and therefore called suburban), and not a son of the Church but one cursed and anathematized? Would he, in your judgment, be a pope who sold his own soul in order to obtain the Roman Church? Who slew the Romans by the edge of the sword, so that he might become Roman pope? You will say that I ought not to have elected a pope without the king's consent, and that I should have given great weight to ensuring the people did not perish. Look: here blessed Augustine was set over the church of Hippo while Valerius was still living; there Ambrose, eight days after he was baptized, was ordained bishop, having received all the ecclesiastical grades. In these cases the order of canonical authority was surely set aside for no other reason than to provide for the safety of the people. And you tell me that in saving the people I ought to have consulted the king himself, so that the glory of giving consent by a single letter would fall to him. For whence would a Roman emperor later arise, if the Roman people had destroyed itself by mutual wounds? Moreover, that the Roman Church did not depart from royal goodwill in choosing its pope is also shown by this: although it abounded in religious and wise men among its own clergy, it chose not one of its own, but the man who was, as it were, a household servant and intimate of the king.

units.la: Regius Aduocatus.
units.tr: The Royal Advocate.

units.la: Quisquis veritati, postquam patefacta claruit, obstinate renititur, Dei omnipotentis aduersarius non immerito iudicatur, cuius aduersum se iram extinguibiliter prouocat, si veritatem quae ipse est, pertinaciter & arroganter impugnat. Nam vt ipse disputationis tuae velut epilogum faciam, cum inter nos quaestio moueretur, vtrum sine Regis assensu Romani Pontificis fieri posset electio, recensitis historiarum catalogis, tantam Romanorum Imperatorum atque Pontificum copiam coacernauit, & velut nubem mihi testium opposuisti, vt his conspectis, ne multum quidem me aduersum te super hoc vlterius facere libuisset. De anathemate vero, quod Nicolaus Papa constituit, in quo etiam, vt veram fatear, totam victoriae vim intentio nostra poluerat, tam inuictis Scripturarum testimoniis, tam lucidis certe modo beatorum Apostolorum, modo ipsius Domini Saluatoris tuae disputationis assertiose purgauit exemplis, vt & nos catenus ignota doceret, & vos ab illius sententiae vinculo patenter absolueret. Deinde a Domini nostri Regis, quam dicebamus, iniuria, quae scilicet nos aduersum vos acrius accendebat, tam strenue le purgauit oratio, vt euidenti claresat iudicio, quia in eo, quod sibi Pontificem populus Romanus elegit, maiestati regiae potissimum ministrauit; nec ei, sicut dicebatur, priuilegium tulit, sed potius roborauit, dum non de Romana Ecclesia, sed ex aula regia Sacerdotem ad Apostolicae sedis culmen tuexit. Postremo de electione Parmensis Episcopi quid dicimus? loquar, an sileam? Sed iuxta Scripturam conceptum sermonem tenere quis possit? Et certe vbi nuda veritas cernitur, temporis ignominia est, si commentae fallaciae deseruitur. Ipsi plane liquido nouimus anathematizatum esse Gerardum, nec ignoramus eius instinctu potissimum hunc Episcopum in hoc negocium fuisse pellectum; & vt ita loquar, arbor quae de venenata radice anathematis oritur, antequam perniciosum protrumpat in fructum; modis omnibus ne noceat, euellatur, testante veritate, quae dicit: Omnis arbor quae non facit fructum bonum, excidetur & in ignem mittetur.
units.tr: Whoever stubbornly resists the truth once it has been brought to light is rightly judged an adversary of almighty God, whose wrath against himself he surely provokes if he obstinately and arrogantly assails the truth, which is God himself. To sum up your argument, as it were: when we were debating whether the election of a Roman Pontiff could take place without the king's assent, you went through the catalogues of history and heaped up such a multitude of Roman emperors and popes, and set them before me like a cloud of witnesses, that when I saw them I hardly wished to press the matter any further against you. As for the anathema which Pope Nicholas laid down, on which, to confess the truth, all the force of our case had rested, your discourse cleared it away with such unconquerable testimonies of Scripture, and with such clear examples, first of the blessed Apostles and then of the Lord and Saviour himself, that it taught us things we had not known and freed you plainly from the bond of that sentence. Next, concerning the injury done to our lord the King, which I mentioned, and which indeed sharpened our anger against you, your speech defended him so vigorously that it is clear from the evident judgment of the matter that in the election of a Pontiff by the Roman people, the royal majesty was chiefly served. Nor did it take away a privilege from him, as was alleged, but rather confirmed it, since it was from the royal court, and not from the Roman Church, that the priest was raised to the summit of the apostolic see. Finally, what shall we say about the election of the Bishop of Parma? Shall I speak or be silent? Yet who could keep to the speech he had composed according to Scripture? And certainly, where bare truth is seen, it is a disgrace to the age if one clings to a feigned deceit. We clearly know that Gerard was anathematized, and we are not unaware that this bishop was lured into the business chiefly by his instigation; and, to speak plainly, the tree that springs from the poisonous root of anathema must be uprooted by every means before it bursts into harmful fruit, as the truth attests, which says: Every tree that does not bring forth good fruit shall be cut down and cast into the fire.

units.la: Defensor Romanae Ecclesiae.
units.tr: Defender of the Roman Church.

units.la: Ecce audiuit beatitudo vestra, venerabiles Patres, quoniam qui inspector est mendium, confoederat nos in concertatione verborum, videt enim nos non malitiae causa confligere, sed inueniendae veritatis studio deseruire; ideoq; dignatus est motam inter nos sopire querelam, & suam nobis inspirare concordiam. Pax enim nostra, quae fecit vtrumque vnum conflauit, & in eodem sensu corda unorum. Agamus ei gratias, qui prius sagenam Petri periclitari permisit, & turbine ventorum, & procellis undarum: sed ecce vt regrediens manum tetendit, Petrum erexit, ventis imperauit, & discrimina marina compescuit, confestim mare, quod in cumulos erigebatur, obruitur, tempestatis procella sedatur, ventorum turbo repriuitur, & aurea coeli facies serenatur.
units.tr: Behold, your blessedness has heard, venerable Fathers, that he who is the overseer of lies has made us come to blows in a war of words; for he sees that we are not fighting out of malice but are labouring in the pursuit of finding the truth. Therefore he has deigned to calm the quarrel that has arisen between us and to breathe into us his own concord. For it is our peace, which has made both one and joined the hearts of both in one sense. Let us give thanks to him who first allowed Peter's net to be endangered by the whirlwind and the storms of the waves; but see how, returning, he stretched out his hand, raised Peter up, commanded the winds, and quelled the perils of the sea: at once the sea, which was heaped up in mountains, is overwhelmed, the fury of the storm is quieted, the whirlwind of the winds is driven back, and the golden face of the sky is made clear.

units.la: Clausula dictionis.
units.tr: Conclusion of the address.

units.la: A modo igitur, dilectissimi, illinc regalis aulae Consiliarii, hinc sedis Apostolicae comministri, vtraque pars in hoc vno studio conspiremus laborantes, vt summum Sacerdotium & Romanum simul confoederetur Imperium, quatenus humanum genus, quod per hos duos apices in vtraque substantia regitur, nullis, quod absit, partibus, quod per Cadaloum nuper factum est, rescindatur, sicq; mundi vertices in perpetuae charitatis vnione occurrant, vt in inferiora membra per eorum discordiam non resiliant, & quatenus ab vno Mediatore Dei & hominum haec duo, regnum scilicet, & Sacerdotium diuino sunt conflata mysterio; ita sublimes istae duae personae tanta sibimet vnanimitate iungantur, vt quodam mutuae charitatis glutino, & Rex in Romano Pontifice, & Romanus Pontisex inveniatur in Rege, salvo scilicet suo priuilegio Papae, quod nemo praeter eum vsurpare permittetur. Caeterum & ipse delinquentes, cum causa dictauerit, forensi lege coerceat, & Rex cum suis Episcopis super animarum statu prolata sacrorum canonum auctoritate, decernat. Ille tanquam pater paterno semper iure praeemineat; iste velut vnicus ac singularis filius in amoris illius amplexibus requiescat. Attalus plene Rex Asiae & Nicomedes Rex Bythiniae in tantum Romanam Rempublicam dilexere, vt vterque moriens Romanum populum testamenti reliquerit heredem. Sanctae ergo Ecclesiae Principes quam propensiori inuicem debent charitate congruere, quibus iunctum est, charitatem praecipue Christiano populo praedicare; vt ex eorum, quae procedat ex pace, concordia, sancta vniuersalis gratuletur Ecclesia, ac gemino vtriusque studio Christianae religionis resloreat disciplina. Verum nos piscatoris nostri nauiculam ex hiatu Scyllae voragiis extrahentes, dum successorem Petri, fide labente vestigio mersum ad litora quieta deducimus, pium Redemptori nostro coleusma canentes: Te Deum laudamus: Te Dominum confitemur.
units.tr: From now on, therefore, beloved brethren, let us, the counsellors of the royal court on the one side and the fellow-servants of the Apostolic See on the other, both work together in this one endeavour: that the supreme priesthood and the Roman Empire be joined together, so that the human race, which is governed in both its substances by these two summits, may not be torn apart (God forbid) in any part, as was recently done through Cadalus, and so that the heads of the world may meet in a bond of lasting charity, lest they recoil from one another through discord and harm the members below. And since these two, namely kingship and priesthood, were joined together by divine mystery through the one Mediator between God and men, let these two lofty persons be united with such unanimity that, by a kind of glue of mutual charity, the King may be found in the Roman Pontiff and the Roman Pontiff in the King, saving of course the privilege of the Pope, which no one but he shall be permitted to usurp. Moreover, let him (the King) restrain by the forensic law those who offend, when the case has been laid before him, and let the King, with his Bishops, decree concerning the state of souls, by the authority of the sacred canons, once it has been pronounced. The one, as a father, shall always excel by paternal right; the other, as the only and unique son, shall rest in the embraces of that father's love. Attalus, king of Asia in full, and Nicomedes, king of Bithynia, so loved the Roman Commonwealth that each, when dying, left the Roman people as heir of his estate. Therefore the princes of the holy Church ought to agree with one another in the greater charity, since they are bound above all to preach charity to the Christian people; so that from their concord, which arises from peace, the holy universal Church may rejoice, and by the twofold zeal of both the discipline of the Christian religion may be restored. But while we draw our fisherman's little boat out of the jaws of Scylla's whirlpools, and while we bring to the quiet shore the successor of Peter, who had sunk when his faith faltered, we sing a devout hymn to our Redeemer: We praise you, O God; we acknowledge you as Lord.

units.la: B. BERNHARDI ABBATIS CLAREVALLENSIS
units.tr: B. BERNARD, ABBOT OF CLAIRVAUX

units.la: EPISTOLA AD LOTHARIVM IMPERATOREM,
units.tr: LETTER TO THE EMPEROR LOTHAIR,

units.la: De recuperandis Imperii iuribus contra iniustos prouinciarum eius vsurpatores & detentores.
units.tr: On recovering the rights of the Empire against the unjust usurpers and holders of its provinces.

units.la: Othario Dei gratia Romanorum Imperatori Augusto, Bernhardus Abbas de Claraualle, si quid potest peccatoris oratio. Benedictus Deus qui vos elegit, & erexit coram salutis nobis, ad laudem & gloriam nominis sui, & reparandum Imperii decus, ad subueniendum Ecclesiae suae in tempore malo, postremo ad operandum etiam nunc salutem in medio terrae.
