Decima ratio eorū est haec, omnis purus viator, qui potest actuale peccatum & mortale contra legem committere, potest incurrere haereticā prauitatē, quia talis potest damnabiliter excaecari, cum vt habetur Sapien. 2. malitia peccatorum eos excaecat, de impiis enim ibi scribitur: Excaecauit eos malitia eorum, & ita in tantam deduci poterunt caecitatem, vt catholicam abnegent veritatem, sed Papa potest peccatum actuale & mortale committere, secundum quod Bonifacius martyr, prout legitur di. 44. c. si Papa, & Simachus Papa, vt habetur 9. q. 3. c. aliorum, testantur aperte, qp etiam Ecclesia catholica insinuat euidenter, cum pro ipsius spirituali salute preces ad Deum fundere nō desistat, ergo Papa potest incurrere haeretica prauitatem. Vndecima ratio eorum est haec, illi, qui exponendis scripturis sunt praeferendi Papae, possunt errare contra fidem, igitur multomagis ille potest errare contra fidem. Consequentia patet. Tum quia tenet per locum à minori. Tū quia ille, qui nō potest errare contra fidē, praeferendus est in expositione diuinarum scripturarū illi, qui potest errare. Tū quia sicut mendax est veraci nullatenus praeponendus, ita qui contra ea, quae fidei sunt, potest mentiri, nullo modo praeponendus est illi, qui mentiri nō potest, antecedēs autē probatur aperte. Nā sicut allegatū est prius, secundū qp habetur in decr. di. 20. c. 1. tractatores scripturarū diuinarū in expositione scripturae sunt Pontificibus summis praeferendi, dicti aut tractatores possunt errare contra fidē secundū qp prius de B. Cypriano & Augustī. ac etiā Hieronymo probatum extitit. Origenes tractator diuinae scripturae non minus errauit aperte & in haereticam incidit prauitatē, ergo multomagis summi Pontifices, qui saepe sunt illiterati & sanctarum diuinarum scripturarum ignari, possunt in haereticam incidere prauitatem. Duodecima ratio est haec, qui potest de haeresi accusari, & pro haeretico condemnari, potest contra fidem errare catholicam, & prauitate haeretica maculari, hoc patens est de se: quia de crimine, quod quis non valet committere, nulla est accusatio, Papa autē potest de haeresi accusari, & pro haeresi potest condemnari, secundū qp ex superioribus probatur aperte, ergo Papa potest haereticari, Papa aut potest actum haereticalem committere, patet p exemplum de B. Marcellino & de Siluestro secundo, ergo Papa potest haereticari. Tredecima ratio est haec, de nulla persona est licitum affirmare ipsam non posse errare contra fidem, de qua ipsam non posse errare neque per scripturam sacram nec per doctrinam ecclesiae vel sanctorum, neqṡ per rationem in dicta doctrina fundata potest ostendi, sed qp Papa nō possit errare cōtra fidē, nullo prędictoū modorū potest ostendi. Si n. posset ostendi, optime probaretur p illas auctoritates Saluatoris: Vobiscū sum omnibus diebus vsq; ad consummationem seculi. Luc. 22. Simon ecce Sathanas expetiuit vos vt cribraret sicut triticum, ego autem rogaui pro te vt non deficiat fides tua, & tu aliquando conuersus confirma fratres tuos, sed per illas auctoritates non potest ostendi, quod Papa non possit errare contra fidem, non per primam: quia auctoritas non intelligitur de Papa: cum vacante sede nullus sit Papa, & ita non dicit Christus pro Papa, sed pro ecclesia militante, vobiscum sum omnibus diebus vsque ad consummationem seculi. Item Christus non solum intellexit se permansurū cum ecclesia militante vsq; ad consummationē seculi p fidē solūmodo: sed etiā p caritatem & bonā vitam. Constat aut, quod Christus non est cū Papa per caritatem & bonam vitam: cum Papa sit nepharius extra caritatem existens, ergo de Papa non debent verba prędicta intelligi. Nec secunda auctoritas potest de Papa intelligi, vt Christus rogauerit, vt fides Papae non deficeret. Tum quia sedes Apostolica saepe vacat, & tamen tunc non deficit fides, pro qua Christus rogauit. Tu quia Papa potest renunciare Papatui, vel deponi, & postea contra fidem errare; cum nullo tempore deficiat fides, pro qua rogauit Christus. Verba vero praedicta dicit Christus beato Petro pro persona ipsius Petri: quia fides eius finaliter non deficit, licet ad tempus defecerit, propter quod dicit sibi Christus: Et tu aliquando conuersus, postquam scilicet fides tua defecerit, ergo tu ad fidem rediens confirma fratres tuos. Eadem etiam verba, scil. ego pro te rogaui, vt non deficiat fides tua, dicit Christus Petro pro congregatione fidelium: quia fides Petri fuit, & est in congregatione fidelium absque interruptione vsque ad consummationem seculi duratura. Nam fides, quam beatus Petrus tenuit, praedicauit & docuit, nunquam deficiet, sed in aliquibus Christianis clericis vel laicis, viris vel mulieribus, vsque ad finem seculi remanebit. Quartadecima ratio est haec, qui potest haereticorum & haeresis fautor & defensor existere, potest haeretica prauitate foedari: imo talis haeresiarcha est censendus, teste Vrbano Papa, qui vt habetur 24. q. 3. cap. qui aliorum, ait: Qui aliorum errorem defendit, multo est damnabilior illis qui errant: quia non solum ille errat, sed etiam alios offendicula erroris praeparat & confirmat. Vnde qui magister erroris est, non tantum haereticus, sed haeresiarcha dicendus est, sed Papa non potest haereticorum prauitatis haereticae fautor & defensor existere. Quod per duo exempla probatur. Primum est de Anastasio, qui fuit fautor Fotini & Achatii haereticorum, secundum quod habetur distinct. 19. ca. Anastasius. Secundum exemplum ponunt aliqui de Ioh. 22. qui Nicolai Tertii & decretalis suae, quae incipit: Exiit qui seminat, necnon & Clementis IX. & decretalis suae, quae incipit: Exiuit de Paradiso, fautor fuit aliquando & defensor, & tamen in dictis decretalibus, Exiit & Exiuit, plures haereses de paupertate Christi & Apostolorum eius, necnon & de voto abdicationis proprietatis omnium temporalium in speciali, & etiam in communi loquendo continentur, vt nonnulli dicunt & scribunt.
units.tr: The fifth reason is this: nothing repels error against faith and grace more than any ecclesiastical dignity. Therefore a person is no more confirmed against error and heresy by an ecclesiastical dignity than by faith and grace. But no mere wayfarer is confirmed in the faith by faith and grace, since he can still err and be infected with heretical depravity. Therefore no one is confirmed in the faith by an ecclesiastical dignity, not even the papal one, so that he cannot afterwards be defiled by heretical depravity. The sixth reason is this: a pope who has been justly deposed, and a pope who has freely resigned the papacy, can both err against the faith. Therefore a pope before deposition or voluntary resignation can err against the faith. The antecedent is plain. For if a deposed pope, and one who has resigned the papacy, could not err against the faith, it would follow that some mere wayfarer, burdened with many sins and other than a pope, could not err against the faith. The consequence is proved thus: a wayfarer does not acquire the power to err against the faith through a meritorious act. But both the deposition of a pope and a voluntary resignation can be meritorious. For when a pope worthy of deposition accepts his deposition, or patiently endures it for God's sake, he merits by it. So if John XXII, when he was being deposed from the papacy, had patiently borne it for love of God, he would have had merit with God. It is also probable that Pope Symmachus, who clung to the papacy with eleven thousand..., and Celestine V, who merited before God by resigning the papacy, did so. Therefore neither deposition nor resignation of this kind acquires the power to err against the faith, and so a pope before deposition or resignation has the power to err against the faith. Student. This argument seems to take up one false assertion, namely that a pope can err against the faith before deposition. For it seems, according to the law, that as soon as a pope errs against the faith he is at once deposed. Master. Some answer that instance by saying that deposition is twofold, namely by man and by law. Before deposition by man, a pope can err against the faith and fall into heretical depravity, and the argument above concerns that deposition, since first he becomes a heretic and afterwards, converted and repentant, can be deposed by man and accept the deposition meritoriously. Before deposition by law, however, a pope can err against the faith out of simplicity or ignorance, but he is not counted among the heretics. Therefore, although he has strayed from the faith through ignorance or simplicity (provided he is ready to be corrected), he is not deprived of the papacy. But if he obstinately clings to an error against the faith, he is deposed by the very fact, and is stripped of all authority by law, though not by man but by law. Student. Add other reasons. Master. The seventh reason of theirs is this: no one who has received a dignity unworthily, illegitimately and unjustly is confirmed in the faith by it. But it happens that someone unworthy ascends to the papacy illicitly and unjustly, through ambition and simony and other impious and unjust means. Therefore such a man is in no way confirmed in the faith by the papacy. The eighth reason of theirs is this: that state through which the one who assumes it is confirmed in the faith, and in which no one can err, should not be shunned by a perfect man but desired with all longing. For such a state is either wholly secure from every spiritual danger, or is less perilous than the state in which one is not confirmed in the faith, since it is more imperfect and more prone to sin on account of the lack of faith. But the papacy is not to be desired, it is to be shunned, and it is no less perilous than other states in which it is possible to err against the faith. For this reason Saint Clement also refused to become pope. Therefore no one is confirmed in the faith by the papacy. The ninth reason of theirs is this: one who cannot err against the faith does not need the skill of others in this mortal life in order to define and determine doubts that arise against the faith. Just as one who cannot err in geometry or another discipline would hardly need the counsel of others to resolve doubts in that discipline, so too the congregation of the faithful, since it cannot err against the faith, does not need the wisdom of other Christians to define those things that agree with catholic truth. But the pope, to declare and define the many doubts that arise about the catholic faith, needs the skill of others. Otherwise general councils would have been gathered in vain to declare doubts and root out heresies, and in vain would he call learned men into the sacred page. Therefore the pope can err against the faith. The tenth reason of theirs is this: every mere wayfarer who can commit an actual and mortal sin against the law can fall into heretical depravity, for such a man can be blinded to his damnation. As is said in Wisd. 2. the malice of sinners blinds them, for it is written of the wicked there: Their malice has blinded them. And so they may be brought into such great blindness that they deny catholic truth. But the pope can commit an actual and mortal sin, as Boniface the martyr testifies, as is read in dist. 44, c. Si Papa, and Pope Symmachus, as found in 9, q. 3, c. Aliorum, testify openly. The catholic Church also clearly implies this, since it does not cease to pour out prayers to God for his spiritual salvation. Therefore the pope can fall into heretical depravity. The eleventh reason of theirs is this: those who are to be preferred to the pope in expounding the Scriptures can err against the faith. Therefore much more can the pope err against the faith. The consequence is plain, both because it holds by the argument from the lesser, and because one who cannot err against the faith is to be preferred in the exposition of the divine Scriptures to one who can err. And because just as a liar is by no means to be preferred to a truthful man, so one who can lie against what pertains to the faith is in no way to be preferred to one who cannot lie. The antecedent is plainly proved. For as was said before, according to what is held in decr. dist. 20, c. 1, the expositors of the divine Scriptures are to be preferred to the highest pontiffs in expounding Scripture. Yet these expositors can err against the faith, as was proved earlier about Saint Cyprian, Augustine and also Jerome. Origen, an expositor of the divine Scripture, erred no less openly and fell into heretical depravity. Therefore much more can the supreme pontiffs, who are often unlettered and ignorant of the holy divine Scriptures, fall into heretical depravity. The twelfth reason is this: one who can be accused of heresy and condemned as a heretic can err against the catholic faith and be stained with heretical depravity. This is plain in itself, because there is no accusation of a crime that a man cannot commit. But the pope can be accused of heresy and condemned for heresy, as is clearly proved from what was said above. Therefore the pope can be made a heretic. Moreover the pope can commit a heretical act, as is shown by the examples of Saint Marcellinus and of Silvester II. Therefore the pope can be made a heretic. The thirteenth reason is this: it is not lawful to affirm of any person that he cannot err against the faith, unless it can be shown from sacred Scripture, from the teaching of the Church or the saints, or from reason founded on that teaching, that he cannot err. But that the pope cannot err against the faith cannot be shown by any of these means. For if it could be shown, it would be best proved by those sayings of the Saviour: I am with you always, even to the end of the age. Luke 22. Behold, Satan has demanded to sift you like wheat, but I have prayed for you that your faith may not fail, and when you have returned, strengthen your brethren. But it cannot be shown from those sayings that the pope cannot err against the faith. Not from the first, because the saying is not understood of the pope, since when the see is vacant there is no pope. So Christ does not speak of the pope but of the militant Church: I am with you all days, even to the end of the age. Likewise Christ meant not only that he would remain with the militant Church to the end of the age through faith alone, but also through love and a good life. But it is certain that Christ is not with the pope through love and a good life, since the pope is a barren man standing outside charity. Therefore those words cannot be understood of the pope. Nor can the second saying be understood of the pope, that Christ prayed that the pope's faith would not fail. First, because the apostolic see is often vacant, and yet the faith, for which Christ prayed, does not fail at that time. Second, because the pope can resign the papacy or be deposed, and afterwards err against the faith, while the faith for which Christ prayed never fails at any time. Indeed Christ spoke those words to blessed Peter for Peter's own person, because his faith does not fail in the end, although it failed for a time. For this reason Christ says to him: And you, when you have returned, that is, after your faith has failed, strengthen your brethren once you are returning to the faith. The same words, namely I have prayed for you that your faith may not fail, Christ also speaks to Peter on behalf of the congregation of the faithful, because the faith of Peter was, and is, in the congregation of the faithful, to last without interruption to the end of the age. For the faith that blessed Peter held, preached and taught will never fail, but will remain in some Christians, clergy or laity, men or women, until the end of the age. The fourteenth reason is this: one who can be a supporter and defender of heretics and heresy can be defiled by heretical depravity. Indeed such a man is to be counted a heresiarch, as Pope Urban testifies, who says, as is held in 24, q. 3, cap. Qui aliorum: He who defends the error of others is far more damnable than those who err, for not only does he err himself, but he also prepares and confirms the stumbling blocks of error for others. Hence he who is the teacher of error is to be called not merely a heretic but a heresiarch. But the pope cannot be a supporter and defender of the heretical depravity of heretics. This is proved by two examples. The first is that of Anastasius, who was a supporter of the heretics Photinus and Acacius, as is held in distinct. 19, c. Anastasius. The second example some give from John XXII, who at one time was a supporter and defender of the decretal of Nicholas III that begins Exiit qui seminat, and also of the decretal of Clement V that begins Exiit de Paradiso. Yet in the said decretals, Exiit and Exiit, many heresies concerning the poverty of Christ and of his Apostles are contained, and also concerning the vow of renouncing all ownership of temporal goods, both in particular and in common, as some say and write.

units.la: Disc. Isti malitiose contra dominum Ioh. 22. procedunt, nituntur enim, quod vel fuit vel est haereticus, monstrare. Mag. Volo te scire, quod nonnulli putant non malitiose, sed veraciter & infallibiliter demonstratur, quod Ioh. 22. vel fuit vel est modo haereticus: quia (vt asserunt) nulla potest tergiuersatione negari, quando doctrina sua de paupertate Christi & Apostolorum eius, & de abdicatione proprietatis omnium temporalium in speciali & etiam in communi & de paupertate euangelica, doctrinae Nicolai Tertii, & aliorum summorum Pontificum aduersetur, cum ergo omnia praedicta ad fidem pertineant, vel ad bonos mores, necesse est quod altera istarum doctrinarum continetur sub haeretica prauitate, aut ergo doctrina Ioh. 22. est haeretica: aut doctrina Nicolai Tertii, & aliorum summorum Pontificum cum eo concordantium circa praedicta, est haeretica, si doctrina Ioh. 22. est haeretica: cum enim diffinierit solenniter eam esse tenendam, sequitur quod pertinax & haereticus est censendus. Si autem doctrina Nicolai Tertii, & aliorum summorum Pontificum est haeretica, ergo Iohan. 22. quando eam per declarationem suam solenniter approbauit, & multipliciter mandauit, fuit haereticus reputandus: quia prauitatis haereticae defensor & fautor, vnde nonnulli ex praedictis formant decimamquintam rationem sic. Qui circa ea, quae fidei sunt, est sibiipsi contrarius, potest errare circa fidem, Papa autem potest circa ea, quae fidei sunt, esse sibiipsi contrarius, hanc probant per exemplum de Ioh. 22. qui sibi contrarius inuenitur, cum prius approbat doctrinam Nicolai Tertii de paupertate Christi & Apostolorum eius, & de abdicatione proprietatis Christi omnium temporalium in speciali & in communi; & postea contradicit eidem.
units.tr: Pupil: Those men proceed maliciously against Pope John XXII, for they strive to show that he was or is a heretic. Teacher: I want you to know that some think it is not malicious but truly and infallibly demonstrated that John XXII was or is now a heretic. They say that this cannot be denied by any evasion, since his doctrine on the poverty of Christ and his Apostles, on the renunciation of all temporal property both individually and in common, and on evangelical poverty, runs counter to the doctrine of Nicholas III and of other supreme pontiffs. Since all these matters pertain either to faith or to good morals, one of these two doctrines must be contained under heretical depravity. Either the doctrine of John XXII is heretical, or the doctrine of Nicholas III and the other supreme pontiffs who agreed with him on these points is heretical. If John XXII's doctrine is heretical, then since he solemnly decreed that it must be held, it follows that he must be judged obstinate and a heretic. If, however, the doctrine of Nicholas III and the other supreme pontiffs is heretical, then John XXII, when he solemnly approved it by his declaration and commanded it in many ways, must be regarded as a heretic, since he was a defender and promoter of heretical depravity. Hence some of those mentioned above form the fifteenth argument thus: whoever is self-contradictory in matters that pertain to the faith can err concerning the faith; the Pope can be self-contradictory in matters that pertain to the faith; they prove this by the example of John XXII, who is found to contradict himself, since he first approved the doctrine of Nicholas III on the poverty of Christ and his Apostles and on the renunciation of all temporal property of Christ, both individually and in common, and afterwards contradicted the same doctrine.

units.la: CAP. IV.
units.tr: CHAP. IV.

units.la: I- n quo ponitur opinio, quae in contrarium arguit, probando, quod Papa canonice electus non potest manens Papa errare a fide & haereticari. Et hoc probatur octo rationibus, ad quas respondetur capitulo sequenti.
units.tr: Here is set out the opinion that argues the contrary, proving that a Pope canonically elected cannot, while remaining Pope, err from the faith and become a heretic. This is proved by eight arguments, to which the following chapter replies.

units.la: DIscipulus. Quamuis rationes, quae impugnare videntur sacratissimum patrem nostrum dominum Papam, non putem concludere, licet sint difficiles ad soluendum (de quarum solutione sollicite cogitabo) tamen aliae quaedam efficaces apparent. Vnde & probabile mihi videtur, quod non est impossibile, quod Papa primo intret canonice, & postea efficiatur haereticus, verum quia veritas exagitata magis splendescit in lucem, peto vt in contrarium allegare nitaris. Mag. Pro assertione contraria, quam tenet (vt dicitur) Ioh. 22. & etiam frater G. (vt fertur) multis modis arguitur. Primo sic. In illa communitate non potest esse iudicium certum sine vacillatione de dubiis, quae emergunt, circa quae dubia & fundamenta eorum quilibet in illa communitate existens potest errare, sed in ecclesia militante est iudicium certum absque vacillatione de dubiis, quae circa fidem emergunt, aliter enim nulli determinationi, diffinitioni seu declarationi ecclesiae militantis circa ea, quae fidei sunt, esset firmiter adhaerendum, quia illi, qui potest errare, non est indubitata fide credendum, ergo non quilibet in ecclesia militante potest errare, ergo est aliquis in ecclesia militante, qui errare non potest; & non alius quam Papa, ergo Papa circa ea, quae fidei sunt non potest errare. Secundo sic. Ille ad quem sunt omnes causae fidei deferendae, non potest contra fidem errare, nec haereticam incurrere prauitatem, sed si quis errauerit contra fidem, de his, quae fidei sunt, recte diffinire non poterit, sed ad summum Pontificem sunt omnes causae fidei deferendae & diffiniendae per ipsum 24. q. 1. cap. quoties, extra de baptismo cap. maiores, ergo Papa errare non potest contra fidem. Tertio sic. Cuius scripturae inter scripturas canonicas computantur, contra fidem errare non potest: quia qui potest contra fidem errare, potest à fidelibus reprobari, auctore autem reprobato reprobantur scripta eius, extr. de haret. cū Celestinus, scripturæ aut, quæ reprobari possunt, non sunt inter catholicas scripturas numerandæ, ille ergo, cuius scripturæ sunt censendæ canonicæ contra fidē errare non potest, scripturæ autem Papæ & decretales eius inter scripturas canonicas nuncupantur, teste August. qui lib. 2. de doctrina Christiana, prout habetur dist. 19. c. in canonicis, ait: in canonicis scripturis ecclesiarum catholicarum, quam plurimum diuinarum scripturarum solertissimus indagator auctoritatē sequatur, inter quas sane illa sunt, quas Apostolica sedes habere, & ab ea accipere meruerunt epistolas, cui etiam concordat Agatho Papa, prout habetur ead. di. c. sic omnes, omnes Apostolicæ sedis sanctiones accipiēda sunt tanquā ipsius diuina voce Petri firmata. ergo Papa, cuius scripta sunt tam autentica, contra fidem errare non potest. Quarto sic, non minoris auctoritatis, dignitatis, sanctitatis, firmitatis putandus est summus Pontifex in noua lege, quā fuerit sacerdos summus aut Iudex in veteri lege, sed summus Pontifex aut Iudex in veteri lege tantæ fuit auctoritatis & firmitatis habendus, q; nulli licebat de eius diffinitione aut iudicio, in quacunque causa ardua dubitare, vel ei quasi contraire, teste ipso Deo, qui, vt habetur Deuter. 17. dixit populo vniuerso, si difficile & ambiguum apud te iudicium esse prospexeris, & iudicū intra portas tuas videris verba variari, surge & ascende ad locum, quem elegerit Dominus Deus tuus, veniesque ad sacerdotes Leuitici generis ad iudicem, qui fuerit illo tempore quaerescue ab eis, qui iudicabunt tibi iudicii veritatem & faciens quodcunque dixerint, qui præsunt loco quem elegerit Dominus & docuerint te iuxta legem eius, sequerisq; sententiam eorum: nec declinabis ad dexteram, neque ad sinistram, qui autem superbierit nolens obedire sacerdotis imperio, qui eo tempore ministrat Domino Deo tuo, ex decreto iudicis morietur homo ille, & auferes malum de Israel, cunctusque populus audiens timebit, vt nullus deinceps intumescebat superbia. Ex his verbis colligitur, quod in veteri lege dignus erat morte, qui in quacunque conclusione difficili & ambigua sacerdotis & iudicis imperio minime obedisset. Ex quo sequitur, quod nulli dubitare licebat, aq; sacerdos & iudex recte diffiniuisset, ergo multo magis in noua lege, quæ perfectiores noscitur habere ministros, nulli licet dubitare catholico, an Papa de inquisitione fidei recte diffinit, q; nō esset verum, si Papa contra fidem posset errare. Disc. Auctoritas Deuter. allegata non videtur ad propositum: quia illa non loquitur de causa fidei, sed de causis ciuilibus & criminalibus. Mag. Hoc non impedit rationem, quia ille, de cuius iudicio in causis criminalibus & ciuilibus non est aliqualiter dubitandum, de eius etiam iudicio in causa fidei est nullatenus trepidandum, nam qui in huiusmodi causis non potest errare, & in causa fidei errare non poterit, eo quod omnis, qui contra fidem potest errare, & in aliis poterit deuiare: cum ei rantum in fide Christi, in aliis minime sit credendum, quia sicut sacri canones potestantur, infideles & hæretici nec iudicare nec testimonium ferre in causis fidelium valent quoquo modo. Disc. De hoc postea collocutionem tecum habebo: ideo ad alias rationes transi. Mag. Quinto sic arguitur. Constitutus in dignitate, qui huic confert innocentiæ sanctitatem, hæreticari non potest; sed Papatus confert Papæ innocentiæ sanctitatem, teste Symacho Papa, qui vt habetur dist. 40. c. Nihil nos, ait: quis sanctum dubiter esse quem apex tanta potestatis extollit, in quo si desint bona acquisita per meritum sufficiunt, quæ à loci predecessore testantur, aut enim claros ad hec fastigia erigit, aut qui erigunt illustrat. Ex his verbis intelligitur, quod quæ dignitas Papatus extollit (etsi malus prius extiterit) sanctitate illustrat, quare nisi renunciauerit Papatui, hæreticari non potest. Sexto: si Papa contra fidem potest errare, & hæretica infici prauitate, eadem ratione & multo fortius quilibet Christianus poterit hæresi damnari, vbi autem quilibet de aliquo collegio hæreticari potest, etiam totum collegium hæreticari valebit, quare sequeretur, quod tota congregatio fidelium potest incurrere hæreticam prauitatem; quod doctrinæ euangelicæ aduersatur aperte. Septimo sic: qui potest errare contra fidem, potest contra præcepta aliquid imperare, ei autem, qui potest contra diuina præcepta imperare, non est necesse in omnibus obedire: quia secundum sententiam beati Petri Act. 5. potius obediendum est Deo, quam contra Deum iubenti. Si ergo Papa potest errare contra fidem, non est necesse Papæ in omnibus obedire: quia sacris canonibus obuiare videtur. Gregor. enim, vt habetur dist. 19. c. nulli, ait: nulli fas est vel velle vel posse transgredi Apostolicæ sedis præcepta, & idem Greg. vt habetur dist. 19. c. 1. præceptis Apostolicis non superbia resistatur, sed per obedientiam quæ à sacra Romana ecclesia & Apostolica auctoritate iussa sunt salutifere impleantur. Ex his verbis patet, quod præceptis Papæ est in omnibus obediendum, & per consequens errare non potest. Octauo sic: si Papa potest hæreticari, posset ab homine iudicari, sed Papa non potest ab homine iudicari, sicut sacri canones attestantur, ergo Papa hæreticari non potest.
units.tr: Disciple. Although the arguments that seem to attack our most holy father the Lord Pope do not, I think, prove their conclusion, and although they are difficult to solve (I will think carefully about their solution), other arguments nonetheless appear forceful. So it seems to me probable that it is not impossible for a Pope first to enter canonically and afterwards become a heretic. But since truth, when it is shaken, shines more brightly, I ask you to set out the opposite case. Master. The opposite view, which (as it is said) John XXII holds, and which (as it is reported) Brother G. also holds, is argued in many ways. First, thus. In that community there cannot be a certain judgment, free from wavering, on doubtful matters that arise; and concerning these doubts and their grounds, any member of that community may err. But in the militant Church there is a certain judgment, free from wavering, on the doubts that arise concerning the faith; otherwise no determination, definition or declaration of the militant Church concerning matters of faith could be firmly adhered to, since one who can err is not to be believed with undoubting faith. Therefore not every member of the militant Church can err. Therefore there is someone in the militant Church who cannot err, and it is none other than the Pope. Therefore the Pope cannot err concerning matters of faith. Second, thus. He to whom all causes of faith are to be referred cannot err against the faith or fall into heretical depravity; but if anyone has erred against the faith, he will not be able to define rightly concerning the matters of faith. All causes of faith are to be referred to the supreme Pontiff and defined by him: 24 q. 1 cap. quoties; extra, de baptismo, cap. maiores. Therefore the Pope cannot err against the faith. Third, thus. Those whose writings are counted among the canonical Scriptures cannot err against the faith. For whoever can err against the faith can be rejected by the faithful, and when the author is rejected, his writings are rejected too: extr. de haeret., cum Celestinus. Writings that can be rejected are not to be numbered among the catholic Scriptures. Therefore he whose writings are to be judged canonical cannot err against the faith. But the writings of the Pope and his decretals are called canonical Scriptures, as Augustine attests in lib. 2 de doctrina Christiana, where it is found in dist. 19 c. in canonicis: "In the canonical Scriptures of the catholic churches, the most skilful investigator of the divine Scriptures follows authority, among which indeed are those epistles which the Apostolic See has deserved to have and to receive from it." Pope Agatho agrees with this, as found in the same distinction, c. sic omnes: "All the sanctions of the Apostolic See are to be received as confirmed by the divine voice of Peter himself." Therefore the Pope, whose writings are so authentic, cannot err against the faith. Fourth, thus. The supreme Pontiff in the new law must be thought of as no less authoritative, dignified, holy and firm than the high priest or judge was in the old law. But the high priest or judge in the old law was to be held of such authority and firmness that it was not lawful for anyone to doubt his definition or judgment in any difficult cause, or to contradict it. God himself bears witness to this, for, as it is written in Deut. 17., he said to the whole people: "If you see that a judgment is difficult and ambiguous among you, and that the words of the judges within your gates vary, arise and go up to the place which the Lord your God shall choose; and you shall come to the priests of the Levitical race and to the judge who will be in that time, and ask of them, and they shall declare to you the truth of the judgment; and you shall do whatever they say, those who preside in the place which the Lord shall choose, and who teach you according to his law; and you shall follow their sentence. You shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left. But the man who is proud and refuses to obey the command of the priest, who at that time ministers to the Lord your God, or of the judge, that man shall die; and you shall take away the evil from Israel. And all the people, hearing it, shall fear, so that no one afterwards shall be puffed up with pride."* From these words it is gathered that in the old law anyone who did not obey the command of the priest or judge in any difficult and ambiguous question was worthy of death. From this it follows that no one was allowed to doubt, and that the priest and judge had rightly defined. Much more, then, in the new law, which is known to have more perfect ministers, no Catholic may doubt whether the Pope rightly defines in the inquiry into the faith. That would not be true if the Pope could err against the faith. Disciple. The authority of Deuteronomy cited does not seem to bear on the point, because it does not speak of a cause of faith but of civil and criminal causes. Master. This does not hinder the argument. He whose judgment in civil and criminal causes is in no way to be doubted, is also in no way to be feared in his judgment in a cause of faith. For he who cannot err in such causes will not be able to err in a cause of faith, since everyone who can err against the faith can also go astray in other matters; and so he is to be believed only in the faith of Christ, and not at all in other matters. For, as the sacred canons attest, unbelievers and heretics are of no force in any way to judge or to give testimony in causes concerning the faithful. Disciple. I will have a discussion with you about this later; so let us pass on to the other arguments. Master. Fifth, the argument goes thus. One who is established in a dignity which bestows on him the holiness of innocence cannot be made a heretic. But the papacy bestows on the Pope the holiness of innocence, as Pope Symmachus witnesses, who, as is found in dist. 40 c. Nihil nos, says: "Who may doubt that he is holy whom so great a height of power exalts, in whom, if good qualities acquired by merit are lacking, those qualities which are attested in his predecessor's place suffice; for either he raises to these heights men who are famous, or those whom he raises he makes famous." From these words it is understood that the dignity of the papacy, which exalts a man (even if he was bad before), illumines him with holiness. Therefore, unless he renounces the papacy, he cannot be made a heretic. Sixth: if the Pope can err against the faith and be infected with heretical depravity, then for the same reason, and much more strongly, any Christian can be condemned for heresy. Now where anyone in a college can be made a heretic, the whole college too may be made a heretic. It would follow that the whole congregation of the faithful could fall into heretical depravity, which plainly conflicts with the evangelical teaching. Seventh, thus. One who can err against the faith can command something contrary to the precepts. But one who can command something against the divine precepts need not be obeyed in all things, because, according to the saying of blessed Peter in Acts 5., we ought to obey God rather than men commanding against God. If therefore the Pope can err against the faith, it is not necessary to obey the Pope in all things, since this seems to oppose the sacred canons. For Gregory, as found in dist. 19 c. nulli, says: "It is not lawful for anyone either to wish or to be able to transgress the precepts of the Apostolic See." And the same Gregory, as found in dist. 19 c. 1: "Let no one resist the Apostolic precepts out of pride, but let what has been commanded by the holy Roman Church and by Apostolic authority be fulfilled in obedience, for salvation." From these words it is plain that the precepts of the Pope are to be obeyed in all things, and consequently that he cannot err. Eighth, thus. If the Pope can be made a heretic, he could be judged by a man. But the Pope cannot be judged by a man, as the sacred canons attest. Therefore the Pope cannot be made a heretic.

units.la: In quo ponuntur responsiones ad precedentes quarti capituli rationes.
units.tr: In which replies are given to the arguments of the preceding fourth chapter.

units.la: Disc. Quauis illæ rationes videatur mihi difficiles; tñ conclusioni nequeo assentire. Vnde qualiter respondeatur ad eas declara. Mag. Ad primā earū respondetur, q; in illa communitate, quæ nō est sibi ipsi relicta, sed est præseruata ab eo, qui errare nō potest; potest esse iudicium certum de dubiis, licet quilibet de illa communitate sigillatim possit errare, & hoc, qa nullo eorū specialiter pseruatur; q n possit errare sicut communitas pseruatur, sic est de ecclesia militante: quia quilibet in ecclesia militante in manu consilii sui relinquitur, vt secundum suæ voluntatis arbitrium manere possit in fide, gratia, affinitate diuina, vel à fide catholica deuiare, communitas autem Christianorum sic præseruatur à Deo, quod si vnus à fide exorbitauerit, alius firmus in fide diuino munere permanebit, vnde si papa contra fidem errauerit, alius Christianus, vir vel mulier, minime à fide recedet. Discipul. Nonne talis modus arguendi valet, quilibet Christianus potest errare contra fidem, ergo tota Christianorum communitas potest errare contra fidem. Magist. Talis modus arguendi (vt multi dicunt) non valet, sed est fallacia figuræ dictionis, quia sæpe à nomine, quod non est collectivum, ad nomen collectivum est fallacia figuræ dictionis, sicut hoc, quilibet de populo potest sustentari de vno pane in die, ergo populus potest sustentari de vno pane in die. Et sicut hoc, vtraq; pars contradictionis potest esse vera, ergo contradictoria possunt esse vera. Discip. Non placet mihi, quod circa rationalem scientiam te diffundas, ideo refer quomodo ad alias rationes respondetur. Mag. Ad secundam rationem respondetur, quod quamuis ad hæreticum causæ sint minime deferendæ, ad illum tamen, qui hæreticus potest fieri, antequam efficiatur hæreticus, sunt causæ fidei deferendæ. Et ideo licet possit in prauitatem labi hæreticam, antequam tamen labatur, sunt causæ fidei deferendæ ad ipsum, sed si hæreticam incurrerit prauitatem, tunc non est ad ipsum quæstio fidei deferenda. Ad tertiam rationem dicitur, quod illæ scripturæ & decretales papæ inter scripturas canonicas, hoc est authenticas & venerationè dignas, sunt recipiendæ, quæ scripturæ diuinæ aut sacris authoritatibus patrum sanctorum non inveniuntur aduersæ, & de huiusmodi sanctionibus, scripturis & epistolis papæ loquitur Aug. & Agatho papa, & alii sancti patres, scripturæ autem & epistolæ papæ, quæ sacræ paginæ & sacris dogmatibus contradicunt, sunt à cunctis fidelibus respuendæ, teste Gratiano, qui dist. 19. c. hoc autem, ait: hoc autem (scilicet quod decretales papæ authoritatis sint cum canonibus) intelligendum est de illis sanctionibus vel decretalibus epistolis, in quibus nec præcedentium patrum decretis nec euangelicis præceptis aliquid contrarium inuenitur, & ibidem § quia ergo, ait: Quia ergo illicite & non canonice, sed contra decretum prædecessorum & successorum suorum hæc rescripta dedit, vt probat Felix & Gelasius, qui Achatium ante Anastasium excommunicauerunt, & Hormisda, qui ab ipso Anastasio tertium eundem Achatium postea damnauit, ideo à Romana ecclesia repudiatur & à Deo percussus esse legitur. Ex his verbis colligitur, quod papa potest scribere decretales, quæ non sunt à catholicis acceptandæ, quod quidam exemplo probare conantur, nam decretales seu etiam scripta Ioh. 22. decretalibus & rescriptis Gregorii 9. Innoc. 4. Alexand. 4. Nicolai 3. & Clementis 5. & quorundam aliorum summorum pontificum, & ad ea quæ ad dogmata fidei spectant, obviant & repugnant, contraria autem non sunt à catholicis recipienda, ergo vel scripta Iohan. 22. vel prædictorum summorum pontificum sunt à catholicis respuenda. Ad quartam rationem respondetur, quod summo pontifici in veteri lege & iudici oportebat omnes in talibus difficultatibus & ambiguis obedire, quando iuxta legem diuinam & veritatem iudices iudicabant, si autem contra diuinam legem aliquid præcepissent, non fuisset obediendum eisdem, sicut ex li. Deuteron. c. 13. & 17. colligitur euidenter. Quod autem sacerdotes summi veteris legis, & etiam iudices principales poterant contra legem Dei iubere, & contra fidem veritatem errare, constat ex hoc, quod plures eorum à veritate iudicii & fidei deuiauerunt, sicut per plura exempla possset ostendi, quod plures summi pontifices sacerdotes circa tempora Machabeorum legem Domini reliquerunt. Vrias enim sacerdos obediens regi Achas contra legem extrexit altare, sicut habetur 4. regum 16. Summi etiam sacerdotes tempore Christi in multis contra legem errauerunt, iudices etiam Hebræorum nonnulli post Iosue contra legem egerunt, & omnes reges præter Dauid Ezechiam & Iosiam, idololatriam commiserunt, quare & summi sacerdotes & iudices in veteri lege contra legem potuerunt iubere: in quo etiā non erat obediendum eisdem: & consimiliter est de summo pontifice tenendum, quod errare potest contra legem diuinam: si tamen non errauerit, eius est standum sententiæ. Ad quintam dicitur, quod papatus officiū non necessario confert suscipienti sanctitatem, plures enim summi pontifices in officio exercentes flagitia & enormia commiserunt. Beatus enim Marcellinus idololatrauit. Anastasius secundus hæresim fautoriam hæreticorum incurrit. Stephanus papa Formosum papam defunctum persequebatur inique, omnes ordinationes eius irritas discernendo. Quin etiam corpus Formosi in concilio positū, & papali veste exutum, laicali habitu indui: & duobus digitis dextexæ eius abscissis manus eius in Tiberim amputari præcepit. Sergius 4. papa Formosum papam de sepulchro extractum, & in lede pontificali habitu sacerdotali indutū ipsum decollari præcepit, & in Tiberim iactari, & omnes per Formosum papa ordinatos deordinauit iniquè. Ioh. 3. venator & lubricus fœminas publicè tenuit, Iohanni Diacono Cardinali nasum, & cuidam subdiacono manum amputari præcepit, qui tandē extitit papatu privatus. Benedictus septimus depræda ta primū ecclesia sancti Petri Iohanni Cardinali Diacono oculos eruit, Syluester secundus Dæmones in papatu consuluit. Liquet ergo quod papatus non confert innocentiæ sanctitatem. Ad decretum autē Symachi respondetur, quod nequaquam Symachus papa intendit astruere, quod nemo possit esse papa, nisi sanctus: cum constet multos scelestissimos viros fuisse in summo pontificio residentes, sed vult asserere Symachus papa, quod ad papatus officiū sublimatus præsumendus est esse sanctus, etiam licet prius fuisset malus, nisi contrarium euidenter appareat, & ideo non dicit ipsum esse sanctū, sed quis sanctum esse dubitet? quasi dicat nemo debet dubitare male suspicando, sed præsumere, quod assumptus ad papatū sit sanctus, nisi contrariū constiterit euidenter, & sic exponit Glo. idem, dicens: & si quandoq; forte Apostoli non essent boni, semp præsumuntur esse boni, obiiciens in contrariū ait: sed nōne in cōtrarium est 19. dist. Anastasius & 26. di. c. 1. § nunc autē? ad q̄ obiectionē respōdēs ait: sed tamē nō dicitur hic q̄ sancti sint, sed q̄ sancti præsumuntur, donec contrariū constet, & infra, q̄ hoc dicitur quod præsupraesumuntur semper benefacere: intelligitur de hiis quae bene possunt retorqueri ad bonum & ad malum: quia semper in dubio pro ipsius facto praesumitur, sed certe hoc idem est in quolibet sacerdote, vt 13. q. 3. absit, & eadem dist. c. 1. & c. 16. q. 1. si clericatus, respondeo: hoc verum est, sed tamen hoc magis praesumitur pro papa, vt 93. dist. c. q. unde sacrilegii instar esset disputare de facto suo, vt 18. q. 4. c. qui autem. Ad sextam rationem respondetur, sicut ad primam, quod non est vniuersaliter verum, quod si quilibet de collegio potest errare, quod totum collegium potest errare, sed quandoque collegium specialiter praeseruatur, si etiam Dominus aliquis temporalis posset aliquod monasterium conseruare impediendo omnes similiter occidi; quamuis nullam vnam singularem personam, quamdiu essent multi, vellet defendere, sed si contingeret omnes occidi praeter vnum, illum defenderet quousque alius sibi in eodem monasterio iungeretur; & ex tunc illum sibiipsi relinqueret: talis Dominus monasterium conseruaret, & tamen nullum de monasterio conseruaret, nisi tantum ad tempus. Ad septimam rationem respondetur, quod non est obediendum papae, si aliquid praecipit contra legem Dei vel bonos mores, si enim praeciperet fornicari, aut idolis immolare, vel daemones inuocare, aut fidem Christi negare, vel aliquid de se malum, non esset sibi obediendum, sacri autem Canones loquuntur in casu, in quo papa praecepit aliquid licitum ad suum spectans officium. Ad vltimam respondetur, quod in casu potest papa iudicari ab homine.
units.tr: Pupil. Although those arguments seem to me difficult, I cannot assent to the conclusion. So explain how they are to be answered. Master. To the first of them it is answered that in that community which is not left to itself but is preserved by him who cannot err, there can be a certain judgment on doubtful matters, even though each individual member of that community may err, because none of them is specially preserved. Yet it is not so with the community as a whole. This is the case in the Church militant: each member of the Church militant is left to the counsel of his own will, so that by his own choice he may remain in the faith, in grace, in fellowship with God, or may turn aside from the Catholic faith. But the community of Christians is so preserved by God that if one has strayed from the faith, another will remain firm in the faith by the gift of God. Hence, if the Pope should err against the faith, another Christian, man or woman, will by no means fall away from the faith. Pupil. Does not this form of argument hold: any Christian can err against the faith, therefore the whole community of Christians can err against the faith? Master. This form of argument (as many say) does not hold, but is the fallacy of figure of speech, because it is often a move from a word that is not collective to a collective word, which is a fallacy of figure of speech. For example: any one of the people can be fed on one loaf in a day, therefore the people can be fed on one loaf in a day. And likewise: either part of a contradiction can be true, therefore contradictories can both be true. Pupil. I do not like it that you wander off into logic; so tell me instead how the other arguments are answered. Master. To the second argument it is answered that, although causes of faith must by no means be brought to a heretic, they must be brought to the one who can become a heretic before he becomes one. Therefore, although he may slide into heretical depravity, yet before he slides, the causes of faith must be brought to him. But if he has fallen into heretical depravity, then the question of faith is no longer to be put to him. To the third argument it is said that those writings and decretals of the Pope are to be received among the canonical writings, that is, the authentic and worthy of reverence, which are not found to be opposed to Holy Scripture or to the authority of the holy Fathers. Augustine and Pope Agatho and other holy Fathers speak of such decrees, writings and letters of the Pope. But the writings and letters of the Pope which contradict the sacred page and the sacred doctrines are to be rejected by all the faithful, as Gratian witnesses, who, in Dist. 19, c. Hoc autem, says: This (namely, that the papal decretals have the authority of the canons) is to be understood of those decrees or decretal letters in which nothing contrary is found either to the decrees of the earlier Fathers or to the precepts of the Gospel. And in the same place, under the paragraph Quia ergo, he says: Because he gave these rescripts unlawfully and not canonically, but against the decree of his predecessors and successors, as Felix and Gelasius prove, who excommunicated Acacius before Anastasius, and Hormisdas, who afterwards condemned the same Acacius, the third after Anastasius himself, therefore he is rejected by the Roman Church and is read to have been struck down by God. From these words it is gathered that the Pope can write decretals which are not to be accepted by Catholics. Some try to prove this by example, for the decretals or writings of John XXII, and the decretals and rescripts of Gregory IX, Innocent IV, Alexander IV, Nicholas III and Clement V, and of certain other supreme pontiffs, which bear on matters of the faith and oppose and contradict it, are not to be received by Catholics. Therefore either the writings of John XXII or those of the aforesaid supreme pontiffs are to be rejected by Catholics. To the fourth argument it is answered that in the Old Law the high priest and the judge had to be obeyed by everyone in such difficulties and ambiguities, when the judges judged according to the divine law and truth. But if they had commanded anything against the divine law, they were not to be obeyed, as is clearly gathered from Deuteronomy 13 and 17. That the high priests of the Old Law, and also the chief judges, could command against the law of God and err against the faith and truth, is clear from the fact that many of them strayed from the truth of judgment and from the faith. As many examples could show, many high priests in the times of the Maccabees forsook the law of the Lord. Urijah the priest, obeying King Ahaz, built an altar contrary to the law, as is found in 4 Kings 16. The high priests at the time of Christ also erred in many things against the law. Some of the judges of the Hebrews after Joshua acted against the law, and all the kings except David, Hezekiah and Josiah committed idolatry. Wherefore the high priests and judges in the Old Law could also command against the law, and in that case too they were not to be obeyed. Likewise must it be held of the supreme pontiff, that he can err against the divine law; yet if he has not erred, his sentence is to be followed. To the fifth it is said that the office of the papacy does not necessarily confer holiness on the one who takes it up, for many supreme pontiffs, while exercising the office, committed crimes and outrages. Blessed Marcellinus, for instance, practised idolatry. Anastasius II incurred the heresy of favouring heretics. Pope Stephen unjustly persecuted the deceased Pope Formosus, declaring all his ordinations void. Moreover, the body of Formosus was placed in a council, stripped of the papal vestments, dressed in lay clothing, and, with two fingers of his right hand cut off, his hand was ordered to be thrown into the Tiber. Pope Sergius III had Formosus, dragged from his tomb and placed on the papal throne, dressed in priestly vestments, beheaded and thrown into the Tiber, and he unjustly deposed all whom Formosus had ordained. John III, a hunter and a lecher, openly kept women; he ordered the nose of John, a deacon and cardinal, to be cut off, and the hand of a certain subdeacon, and at last he was deprived of the papacy. Benedict VII, having first plundered the church of St Peter, gouged out the eyes of John, a deacon and cardinal. Sylvester II consulted demons during his papacy. It is therefore clear that the papacy does not confer holiness of innocence. As for the decree of Symmachus, it is answered that Pope Symmachus by no means intended to assert that no one could be pope unless he were holy, since it is established that many most wicked men have sat in the supreme pontificate. Rather Pope Symmachus wishes to assert that one raised to the papal office is to be presumed holy, even if he was wicked before, unless the contrary clearly appears. Therefore he does not say that he is holy, but: who can doubt that he is holy? as if to say that no one ought to doubt by evil suspicion, but to presume that one who has been raised to the papacy is holy, unless the contrary has clearly been established. The same is explained by the Gloss, which says: And if at some time the Apostles were not good, they are always presumed to be good. Objecting to the contrary, it says: But is it not the contrary in Dist. 19, Anastasius, and in Dist. 26, c. 1, under the paragraph Nunc autem? Answering this objection, it says: Yet it is not said here that they are holy, but that they are presumed holy until the contrary is established; and further on, that this is said of the thing that is presumed to always do well is to be understood of those things which can be turned to good or to evil, because in doubt one is always presumed in favour of the deed itself. But certainly this is the same for any priest, as in 13 q. 3, Absit, and in the same distinction c. 1, and c. 16, q. 1, Si clericatus. I answer: this is true, but it is presumed more strongly in favour of the Pope, as in 93 Dist., c. Unde; so it would be like sacrilege to dispute about his deed, as in 18 q. 4, c. Qui autem. To the sixth argument it is answered, as to the first, that it is not universally true that if each member of a college can err, the whole college can err. But sometimes a college is specially preserved. Suppose some temporal lord could preserve a monastery by preventing all its members from being killed in the same way. Although he would not defend any single individual so long as there were many, yet if it happened that all but one were killed, he would defend that one until another was joined to him in the same monastery, and from then on he would leave him to himself. Such a lord would preserve the monastery, and yet he would preserve no one in it except for a time. To the seventh argument it is answered that the Pope is not to be obeyed if he commands anything against the law of God or good morals. For if he commanded fornication, or sacrifice to idols, or the invoking of demons, or the denial of the faith of Christ, or anything evil in itself, he would not be obeyed. But the sacred canons speak of the case in which the Pope commands something lawful that pertains to his office. To the last, it is answered that in that case the Pope can be judged by a man.

units.la: CAP. VI.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI.

units.la: Vbi proponitur secunda quaestio huius libri, scilicet vtrum collegium Cardinalium possit haeretica pravitate maculari. Quod non, decem rationibus hic probatur: ad quas respondetur cap. 8. huius.
units.tr: Here the second question of this book is put forward, namely whether the college of Cardinals can be tainted with heretical depravity. That it cannot is proved here by ten arguments, to which replies are given in chapter 8 of this book.

units.la: Discipulus. Post praedicta de papa cupio scire, quid de collegio cardinalium sentiant litterati, auscilicet omnes existiment, quod collegium Cardinalium possit haeretica pravitate respergi. Magister. De hoc sunt opiniones contrariae, nam aliqui arbitrantur, quod totum collegium cardinalium haereticari non potest, & huius opinionis videtur esse frater G. qui (vt a quibusdam de ordine Fratrum Minorum audiuit) hoc in quodam processu facto contra Fratrem M. asserit manifeste. Pro hac autem assertione multis modis arguitur. Primo sic: ecclesia Romana haereticari non potest, 24. q. 1. c. 6 pudenda & c. a recta & c. memor, vbi dicit Sixtus papa: Memor sum sub illius nomine praesidere ecclesiae, cuius confessio a Domino Iesu Christo glorificata est: Et cuius fides nullam haeresim vnquam fouet, sed omnes quidem haereses destruit, ista autem ecclesia (cui praefuit Sixtus) fuit ecclesia Romana, ergo ecclesia Romana haereticari non potest, sed illa Romana ecclesia non est papa: quia papa praest Romanae ecclesiae, nullus autem sibiipsi praeesse potest, ergo papa non est Romana ecclesia, quae haereticari non potest, nec vniuersalis ecclesia est Romana ecclesia: quia Romana ecclesia est magistra aliarum ecclesiarum & caput, vniuersalis autem ecclesia non est caput aliarum ecclesiarum, sed est totum corpus, nec potest dici, quod Romana ecclesia est populus Romanus, vel clerus cum populo, vel totus clerus, comprehendens totum collegium Cardinalium tanquam partem, nam ad Romanam ecclesiam spectat de aliis ecclesiis ordinare, sicut ex sacris canonibus colligitur euidenter, hoc autem non pertinet ad populum Romanum, nec ad clerum & populum, nec ad totum clerum Romanum qui comprehendit collegium Cardinalium tanquam partem, ergo per ecclesiam Romanam solummodo collegium Cardinalium debet intelligi: & per consequens idem collegium haereticari non potest. Secundo sic: sedes Apostolica haereticari non potest, teste Eusebio papa, qui, vt habetur 24. q. 1. c. in sede, ait: In sede Apostolica extra maculam semper est seruata catholica religio, sedes autem Apostolica non est papa, qui praesidet Apostolicae sedi: nec est populus Romanus, nec clerus, ergo est collegium Cardinalium, ergo collegium Cardinalium haereticari non potest. Tertio sic. Illud collegium, quod solummodo (& non aliud) habet potestatem eligendi summum pontificem, qui est caput ecclesiae, haereticari non potest: quia si illud collegium esset haereticum, esset priuatum potestate eligendi summum pontificem: quia haeretici summum pontificem non debent eligere, & per consequens tota ecclesia careret potestate eligendi summum pontificem: quod est inconueniens reputandum, sed ad solum collegium Cardinalium spectat potentia eligendi summum pontificem, vt ex decreto Nicolai papae, quod ponitur dist. 79. colligitur, ergo collegium Cardinalium haereticari non potest. Quarto sic: illud collegium, ad quod spectat papam, si exorbitauerit a fide, corrigere & iudicare, non potest contra fidem errare: quia si potest contra fidem errare, non est papa eorum subiectus iudicio: immo etiam alii Christiani non essent necessario eorum subiecti iudicio in causa fidei; quia posset ab eis, si errarent, appellare, ergo multo fortius papa non esset eorum subiectus iudicio, sed collegium Cardinalium potest de papa haeretico iudicare, quod probatur exemplo eorum: qui Anastasium secundum, vt habetur dist. 19. repudiauerunt propter haereticam pravitatem, illi autem fuerunt Cardinales, ergo ad Cardinales spectat papam de pravitate haeretica iudicare, & per consequens collegium Cardinalium haereticari non potest. Quinto, illud collegium haereticari non potest, quo haereticato collegio tota multitudo Christianorum haereticaretur: quia, vt habetur 6. q. 1. c. verum. capite languente faciliter reliqua membra corporis inficiuntur, collegium autem Cardinalium est caput Christianitatis, ergo haereticato collegio Cardinalium faciliter haereticaretur tota Christianitas, sed tota Christianitas haereticari non potest, ergo collegium Cardinalium haereticari non potest. Sexto sic: si collegium Cardinalium posset haereticari, multo magis quodlibet aliud collegium potest haereticari, & ita nullum esset collegium Christia-
units.tr: Pupil: After what has been said about the pope, I want to know what learned men think about the college of Cardinals, whether they all hold that the college of Cardinals can be tainted with heretical depravity. Master: On this there are opposing opinions. Some think that the whole college of Cardinals cannot be made heretical, and Brother G. seems to hold this opinion. (As I have heard from some of the Order of Friars Minor, he plainly asserts it in a certain proceeding brought against Brother M.) For this assertion there are many arguments. First, thus: the Roman Church cannot be made heretical (24 q. 1 c. 6 pudenda and c. a recta and c. memor), where Pope Sixtus says: I am mindful that I preside under the name of that Church whose confession has been glorified by the Lord Jesus Christ, and whose faith never fosters any heresy, but indeed destroys all heresies. But the Church over which Sixtus presided was the Roman Church. Therefore the Roman Church cannot be made heretical. But that Roman Church is not the pope, because the pope presides over the Roman Church, and no one can preside over himself. Therefore the pope is not the Roman Church, which cannot be made heretical. Nor is the universal Church the Roman Church, because the Roman Church is the teacher and head of the other churches, whereas the universal Church is not the head of the other churches but is the whole body. Nor can it be said that the Roman Church is the Roman people, or the clergy with the people, or the whole Roman clergy comprising the college of Cardinals as a part. For it belongs to the Roman Church to ordain for the other churches, as is clearly gathered from the sacred canons, and this does not pertain to the Roman people, nor to the clergy and people, nor to the whole Roman clergy, which comprises the college of Cardinals as a part. Therefore by the Roman Church only the college of Cardinals must be understood, and consequently that same college cannot be made heretical. Second, thus: the Apostolic See cannot be made heretical, as Pope Eusebius testifies, who, as is found in 24 q. 1 c. in sede, says: In the Apostolic See the Catholic religion has always been preserved free from stain. But the Apostolic See is not the pope, who presides over the Apostolic See; nor is it the Roman people, nor the clergy. Therefore it is the college of Cardinals. Therefore the college of Cardinals cannot be made heretical. Third, thus: that college which alone (and no other) has the power to elect the supreme pontiff, who is the head of the Church, cannot be made heretical. For if that college were heretical, it would be deprived of the power to elect the supreme pontiff, because heretics ought not to elect a supreme pontiff; and consequently the whole Church would lack the power to elect a supreme pontiff, which must be regarded as an absurdity. But the power of electing the supreme pontiff belongs to the college of Cardinals alone, as is gathered from the decree of Pope Nicholas, which is given in dist. 79. Therefore the college of Cardinals cannot be made heretical. Fourth, thus: that college to which it belongs to correct and judge the pope, should he stray from the faith, cannot err against the faith. For if it could err against the faith, the pope would not be subject to its judgment. Indeed, other Christians too would not necessarily be subject to its judgment in matters of faith, since they could appeal from it if it erred. Therefore, much more strongly, the pope would not be subject to its judgment. But the college of Cardinals can judge a heretical pope. This is proved by the example of those who rejected Anastasius II, as is found in dist. 19, on account of his heretical depravity. Those men were Cardinals. Therefore it belongs to the Cardinals to judge the pope for heretical depravity, and consequently the college of Cardinals cannot be made heretical. Fifth, that college cannot be made heretical, since, if the college were made heretical, the whole multitude of Christians would be made heretical. For, as is found in 6 q. 1 c. verum, when the head is sick the remaining members of the body are easily infected. But the college of Cardinals is the head of Christendom. Therefore, if the college of Cardinals were made heretical, the whole of Christendom would easily be made heretical. But the whole of Christendom cannot be made heretical. Therefore the college of Cardinals cannot be made heretical. Sixth, thus: if the college of Cardinals could be made heretical, much more could any other college be made heretical, and so there would be no college of Christians that could not incur heretical depravity. Therefore the whole of Christendom could be tainted with heretical depravity, which is by no means to be conceded. Therefore the college of Cardinals cannot be made heretical.

units.la: nostianorum, quod non posset haereticam pravitatem incurrere, ergo tota Christianitas potest haeretica pravitate respergi: quod est minime concedendum, ergo collegium Cardinalium haereticari non potest. Septimo sic: Illud collegium haereticari non potest, cui nullus Christianus in his, quae fidei sunt, audet resistere, nec contra ipsum fidem catholicam defendere: quia tali collegio haereticato tota fides periclitaretur, sed collegio Cardinalium nullus audet in his, quae fidei sunt, resistere Christianus, nec contra idem collegium aliquid tangens fidem defendere, ergo &c. Octavo sic: Collegium Cardinalium est nobilius & dignius collegio episcoporum, nam Cardinales in Romana curia ipsis praeferuntur, sed collegium ipsorum episcoporum succedit collegio Apostolorum, quod haereticari non potuit, ergo nec collegium episcoporum potest haereticari: & per consequens multo fortius nec collegium Cardinalium. Nono sic: Illud collegium, quod de haeresi accusari nullatenus potest, non potest haereticari, sed collegium Cardinalium accusari non potest de haeresi, nisi ab inferioribus, inferiores autem superiores accusare non possunt, secundum Canonicas sanctiones, ergo collegium Cardinalium de haeresi accusari non potest: & per consequens haereticari nequit. Decimo sic: Illud collegium, in cuius fide salvantur simplices, haereticari non potest: quia illo haereticato collegio simplices salvari nequirent, sed simplices salvantur in fide maiorum, inter maximos autem maximi sunt Cardinales, ergo simplices salvantur in fide Cardinalium, ergo collegium Cardinalium haereticari non potest.
units.tr: Seventh, thus: that college cannot be made heretical against which no Christian dares to resist in matters of faith, nor defend the Catholic faith against it. For if that college were made heretical, the whole faith would be endangered. But no Christian dares to resist the college of Cardinals in matters of faith, nor to defend the faith against that same college when it touches on the faith. Therefore etc. Eighth, thus: the college of Cardinals is more noble and worthy than the college of bishops, for the Cardinals are placed before the bishops in the Roman court. But the college of bishops succeeds the college of Apostles, which could not be made heretical. Therefore neither can the college of bishops be made heretical, and consequently, much more strongly, neither can the college of Cardinals. Ninth, thus: that college which cannot in any way be accused of heresy cannot be made heretical. But the college of Cardinals can be accused of heresy only by its inferiors, and inferiors cannot accuse their superiors, according to the canonical sanctions. Therefore the college of Cardinals cannot be accused of heresy, and consequently cannot be made heretical. Tenth, thus: that college in whose faith the simple are saved cannot be made heretical. For if that college were made heretical, the simple could not be saved. But the simple are saved in the faith of their betters, and among the greatest, the greatest are the Cardinals. Therefore the simple are saved in the faith of the Cardinals, and therefore the college of Cardinals cannot be made heretical.

units.la: CAP. VII.
units.tr: CAP. VII.

units.la: In quo secundum opinionem aliorum ad oppositum arguitur decem rationibus, probando quod collegium Cardinalium possit haeretica pravitate foedari: ad quas respondetur, c. 9. huius.
units.tr: In which, according to the opinion of others, the contrary is argued with ten reasons, proving that the college of Cardinals may be tainted with heretical depravity. These reasons are answered in chapter 9 of this work.

units.la: DIscip. Narra assertionem contrariam cum motivis suis. Mag. Quidam indubitanter tenent, quod collegium Cardinalium in fide est nullatenus confirmatum: sicut nec collegium Monachorum & aliorum clericorum, & ideo haereticari potest, nec est certum, quod nunquam contra fidem errabit: sicut nec est certum, quod errabit contra fidem. Isti assertores hanc assertionem multis rationibus fulcire nituntur. Quarum prima est haec: Nulli particulari collegio per summum pontificem voluntarie & ad placitum instituto debet attribui, quod contra fidem errare non potest. Quia quod aliquod collegium contra fidem errare non posset, aliter probari non potest, nisi quia Christus promisit fidelibus catholicam fidem usque ad finem seculi permansuram. Verba autem Christi promittentis fidem usque ad finem seculi permansuram de nullo collegio particulari a summo pontifice instituto debent intelligi: quia Christus promissionem suam in ordinatione summi pontificis nequaquam instituit, collegium autem Cardinalium est collegium particulare a summo pontifice voluntarie & ad placitum institutum. Quia nec a Christo nec ab Apostolis legitur institutum: eo quod nec in scriptura sacra nec in gestis Apostolorum de Cardinalibus aliqua mentio reperitur. Ergo temerarium est dicere, quod collegium Cardinalium nunquam contra fidem errabit. Secundo: Illud collegium, quod summus pontifex potest destruere vel cassare, non est illa ecclesia, quae errare non potest, quia illa ecclesia, quae non potest errare, non potest esse nulla. Et per consequens a summo pontifice destrui & cassari non potest, summus autem pontifex sicut collegium Cardinalium instituit, ita posset illud collegium destruere vel cassare: quia posset Cardinalibus morientibus alios minime subrogare, nec in hoc diceretur praecepti divini transgressor; eo quod de Cardinalibus creandis nullum invenitur praeceptum divinum, ergo collegium Cardinalium non est illa ecclesia, quae contra fidem errare non potest. Tertio sic: Illa ecclesia, quae contra fidem errare non potest, post tempora Apostolorum non incepit, quia ecclesiae, quae erat temporibus Apostolorum, promisit Christus se cum ea usque ad finem seculi permansurum, cum dicitur Matt. ultim. vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem seculi. In quibus verbis Christus innuit manifeste: quod ab illo tempore usque ad finem seculi nunquam ecclesia a fide catholica esset recessura, & illa ecclesia, quae errare non potest, post tempora Apostolorum nequaquam incepit, collegium autem Cardinalium post tempora Apostolorum incepit, ergo collegium Cardinalium non est illa ecclesia, quae contra fidem errare non potest. Quarto sic: Illud, quod est inferius papa, non est ecclesia, quae contra fidem errare non potest, quia sicut papa contra fidem potest errare, ita omne collegium inferius ipso potest contra fidem errare, collegium autem Cardinalium est inferius papa, ergo potest contra fidem errare.
units.tr: Disciple. Set out the contrary assertion together with its grounds. Master. Some hold without doubt that the college of Cardinals is in no way confirmed in the faith, just as the college of monks and of other clergy is not; and therefore it can fall into heresy, and it is not certain that it will never err against the faith, just as it is not certain that it will err against the faith. The advocates of this assertion strive to support it with many arguments. The first is this: no particular college instituted by the supreme pontiff by his own will and pleasure ought to be credited with being unable to err against the faith. For that some college could not err against the faith cannot be proved in any other way than because Christ promised the faithful that the Catholic faith would remain until the end of the age. But the words of Christ promising that the faith would remain until the end of the age must not be understood of any particular college instituted by the supreme pontiff, because Christ did not at all establish his promise in the appointment of the supreme pontiff, whereas the college of Cardinals is a particular college instituted by the supreme pontiff by his will and pleasure. Nor is it read that it was instituted by Christ or by the Apostles, since no mention of Cardinals is found either in Holy Scripture or in the Acts of the Apostles. Therefore it is rash to say that the college of Cardinals will never err against the faith. Second: that college which the supreme pontiff can destroy or annul is not that church which cannot err, for the church which cannot err cannot be nothing; and consequently it cannot be destroyed or annulled by the supreme pontiff. But the supreme pontiff, just as he instituted the college of Cardinals, could likewise destroy or annul that college: he could, when Cardinals die, decline to appoint others in their place, and he would not be called a transgressor of a divine precept, since no divine precept about creating Cardinals is found. Therefore the college of Cardinals is not that church which cannot err against the faith. Third: that church which cannot err against the faith did not begin after the times of the Apostles, because Christ promised that he would remain with the church which existed in the times of the Apostles until the end of the age, when it is said in Matt. ultim.: "I am with you all days, even to the end of the age." In these words Christ clearly signified that from that time until the end of the age the church would never depart from the Catholic faith. The church which cannot err did not begin at all after the times of the Apostles, but the college of Cardinals began after the times of the Apostles; therefore the college of Cardinals is not that church which cannot err against the faith. Fourth: that which is inferior to the pope is not the church which cannot err against the faith, because just as the pope can err against the faith, so every college inferior to him can err against the faith; but the college of Cardinals is inferior to the pope; therefore it can err against the faith.

units.la: Discip. Per hanc rationem probaretur, quod tota congregatio fidelium potest contra fidem errare, quia tota est inferior papa. Mag. Respondetur quod non procedit ratio de tota congregatione fidelium: quia quando sedes Apostolica non vacat, tota congregatio fidelium non est inferior papa, quia comprehendit papam: sed tota fidelium multitudo praeter papam est inferior papa, & de illa conceditur, quod potest errare contra fidem, quia secundum eos fides potest in solo summo pontifice permanere. Discipul. Compleas alias rationes. Magist. Quinta ratio est haec, de illa sola ecclesia firmiter est tenendum, quod non potest contra fidem errare, de qua firmiter est credendum, quod extra ipsam non est salus, sed extra collegium Cardinalium potest esse salus, multi enim salvantur, qui Cardinales non sunt, ergo collegium Cardinalium non est illa ecclesia, quae errare non potest. Sexto sic: sicut omnis persona, quae potest errare in moribus, potest etiam errare contra fidem, ita etiam omne collegium, quod potest peccare contra bonos mores, potest peccare contra fidem, si enim essent duo vel tres Cardinales tantummodo non esset necesse quod aliquis eorum esset in caritate; nimo potest quilibet eorum esse in peccato mortali, constat autem, quod nonnunquam viri sceleratissimi ad Cardinalatus officium assumuntur, ergo idem collegium potest contra fidem errare. Septimo sic: Illud collegium, quod potest errare contra minora & faciliora, potest etiam errare contra maiora & difficiliora, minus autem & facilius est eligere summum pontificem, quam caulas fidei diffinire, collegium vero Cardinalium potest errare contra electionem summi pontificis, manifeste enim erravit, quando mulierem in papam elegit, potest etiam papam per symoniam eligere, sicut aperte insinuat Glo. di. 59. c. si quis pecunia, ergo collegium Cardinalium in diffiniendo causas fidei potest errare. Octauo collegium Cardinalium nec sanctitate nec fidei firmitate collegium Apostolorum excedit, haec consideratibus vitam & mores eorum est tam nota, quod probatione non indiget, sed collegium Apostolorum potuit errare, & errauit, tempore enim passionis Christi nullus eorum fixus in fide remansit, ergo collegium Cardinalium potest errare contra fidem. Discip. Ista ratio non videtur concludere, quia collegium Apostolorum, licet ante missionem sancti Spiritus erraverit, tamen post dictam missionem non erravit. Magist. Non videtur illis, quod hoc impediat argumentum: quia collegium Apostolorum non solum post missionem sancti Spiritus, sed etiam ante passionem Christi uberiori gratia sanctitatis & veritatis illuminatione maiori praefulgebat, quam collegium Cardinalium, ipsos ei ante Christus multipliciter commendauit, dicens Matt. 5. Vos estis lux mundi, vos estis sal terrae, & Ioh. 15. Iam non dicam vos seruos, quia seruus nescit quid faciat Dominus eius, vos autem dixi amicos, quia omnia quaecunque audiui a patre meo nota feci vobis. Et de firmitate eos commendauit, Luc. 22. dicens: vos estis qui permansistis mecum in tentationibus meis, si ergo Apostoli, qui comparantur cedris, secundum beatumGreg. a fide poterant deuiare: temerarie Cardinales (qui in omni veto doctrinae tanquam arundines agitantur,) dicuntur non posse a veritatis tramite aberrare. Nono sic: nulla dignitas ecclesiastica viatorem sanctificat, nec inobliquabilem a fide constituit, haec ex auctoritatibus allegatis supius approbatur aperte, quod etiam ex verbis Chryl. quae ponuntur di. 19. c. multi, colligitur, ait enim non locus sanctificat hominem, & infra: qui bene sederit super cathedram, honorem cathedrae accipit: qui autem male sederit, iniuriam cathedrae facit. Ex his verbis datur intelligi, quod dignitas ecclesiastica non attribuit sanctitatem: & per consequens non confert impossibilitatem errandi contra fidem, sed tota multitudo Cardinalium ante dignitatem Cardinalatus adeptam potuit errare contra fidem, ergo eadem multitudo post dignitatem Cardinalatus adeptam, potest contra fidem errare.Decimo sic: collegium eminentius & superius collegio Cardinalium sc. collegium archiepiscoporum & episcoporum, potest errare contra fidem, ergo multo magis collegium Cardinalium potest errare contra fidem. Hic esse nt duo praenotanda. Primum sc. quod collegium archiepiscoporum & episcoporum est eminentius collegio Cardinalium; quod ex hoc ostenditur, quod olim Cardinales Romanae ecclesiae ad archiepiscopatus electi & assumpti fuerunt, secundum quod ex Registro Innocentii, & gestis Romanorum pontificum habetur, non debet autem aliquis eligi de statu maiori ad minorem, licet econuerso, ergo statu archiepiscoporum est maior statu Cardinalium. Secundum praenotandum est: quod collegium aut communitas archiepiscoporum & episcoporum potest contra fidem errare, quod patet ex hoc, quia Christus non promisit, quod fides catholica esset in episcopis vsq; ad finem seculi permansura. Undecimo sic: de vna sola ecclesia militante dicitur, quod non potest errare contra fidem, collegium autem Cardinalium non est ista ecclesia, licet sit pars huius ecclesiae: sicut etiam ecclesia Parisiensis est pars istius ecclesiae, ergo congregatio Cardinalium potest errare contra fidem.Confirmatur haec ratio: quia quod competit toti ecclesiae, non est attribuendum parti ecclesiae, etiam principali, nisi hoc possit per rationem necessariam vel auctoritatem apertam ostendi, collegium autem Cardinalium est pars ecclesiae, quae errare non potest contra fidem, ergo non posse errare contra fidem non debet attribui collegio Cardinalium: cum nec per rationem necessariam, nec per auctoritatem apertam possit ostendi. Duodecimo sic: Illud collegium, quod contra fidem errare non potest, non indiget aliorum consilio pro conclusionibus fidei terminandis, collegium autem Cardinalium saepe in conclusionibus fidei terminandis aliorum consilio orthodoxorum indiget, aliter enim pro conclusionibus huiusmodi superfluum esset generalia concilia celebrare, ergo concilium Cardinalium potest contra fidem errare.
units.tr: Disciple. By this reasoning it would be proved that the whole congregation of the faithful can err against the faith, because the whole is inferior to the pope. Master. It is answered that the argument does not hold of the whole congregation of the faithful.
