When the Apostolic See is not vacant, the whole congregation of the faithful is not inferior to the pope, since it includes the pope; but the whole multitude of the faithful apart from the pope is inferior to the pope, and of that it is granted that it can err against the faith, because according to them the faith can remain in the supreme pontiff alone. Disciple. Give the other arguments as well. Master. The fifth argument is this: that church alone must firmly be held not to be able to err against the faith outside which we must firmly believe there is no salvation; but outside the college of Cardinals there can be salvation, for many are saved who are not Cardinals; therefore the college of Cardinals is not that church which cannot err. Sixth: just as every person who can err in morals can also err against the faith, so every college which can sin against good morals can sin against the faith. For if there were only two or three Cardinals, it would not be necessary for any one of them to be in charity; indeed any one of them may be in mortal sin. But it is evident that sometimes most wicked men are admitted to the office of Cardinal; therefore the same college can err against the faith. Seventh: that college which can err in lesser and easier matters can also err in greater and more difficult matters. But choosing the supreme pontiff is less and easier than defining the causes of faith, and the college of Cardinals can err in the election of the supreme pontiff: for it manifestly erred when it elected a woman as pope, and it can also elect a pope through simony, as the gloss plainly hints at in dist. 59 c. si quis pecunia. Therefore the college of Cardinals can err in defining the causes of faith. Eighth: the college of Cardinals does not surpass the college of the Apostles either in holiness or in firmness of faith. Their life and morals are so well known to those who consider them that they need no proof. But the college of the Apostles could err, and did err, for at the time of Christ's passion none of them remained steadfast in the faith; therefore the college of Cardinals can err against the faith. Disciple. This argument does not seem to conclude, because the college of the Apostles, although it erred before the mission of the Holy Spirit, did not err after that mission. Master. It does not seem to those authors that this hinders the argument. For the college of the Apostles, not only after the mission of the Holy Spirit but even before the passion of Christ, shone with a greater grace of holiness and a greater illumination of truth than the college of Cardinals. Christ commended them to himself in many ways beforehand, saying in Matt. 5: You are the light of the world, you are the salt of the earth; and in John 15: No longer do I call you servants, for a servant does not know what his lord is doing; but I have called you friends, because all things that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you. And he commended their firmness in Luke 22, saying: You are those who have remained with me in my trials. If therefore the Apostles, who are compared to cedars, could, according to blessed Gregory, stray from the faith, then the Cardinals (who are tossed about like reeds in every wind of doctrine) are rashly said not to be able to wander from the path of truth. Ninth: no ecclesiastical dignity sanctifies the one who holds it, nor makes him unable to be turned aside from the faith. This is clearly approved above by the authorities cited, and it is also gathered from the words of Chrysostom which are set down in dist. 19 c. multi, for he says: place does not sanctify a man, and below: he who sits well upon the chair receives the honour of the chair; but he who sits badly does injury to the chair. From these words it is understood that ecclesiastical dignity does not confer holiness, and consequently does not confer the impossibility of erring against the faith. But the whole multitude of Cardinals, before attaining the dignity of the Cardinalate, could err against the faith; therefore the same multitude, after attaining the dignity of the Cardinalate, can err against the faith. Tenth: the college more eminent and superior to the college of Cardinals, namely the college of archbishops and bishops, can err against the faith; therefore much more can the college of Cardinals err against the faith. Here two things are to be noted beforehand. The first is that the college of archbishops and bishops is more eminent than the college of Cardinals. This is shown by the fact that formerly Cardinals of the Roman church were chosen and raised to archbishoprics, as is held from the Register of Innocent and the Acts of the Roman pontiffs; but no one ought to be chosen from a higher rank to a lower one, although the reverse is allowed; therefore the rank of archbishops is higher than the rank of Cardinals. The second thing to be noted is that the college or community of archbishops and bishops can err against the faith. This is evident from the fact that Christ did not promise that the Catholic faith would remain in bishops until the end of the age. Eleventh: of the one church militant alone it is said that it cannot err against the faith; but the college of Cardinals is not that church, although it is part of this church, just as the church of Paris is also part of it. Therefore the assembly of Cardinals can err against the faith. This argument is confirmed thus: what belongs to the whole church is not to be attributed to a part of the church, even a principal part, unless this can be shown by necessary reason or by clear authority. But the college of Cardinals is a part of the church which cannot err against the faith; therefore the inability to err against the faith ought not to be attributed to the college of Cardinals, since it can be shown neither by necessary reason nor by clear authority. Twelfth: that college which cannot err against the faith does not need the counsel of others in reaching conclusions of faith. But the college of Cardinals often needs the counsel of orthodox others in reaching conclusions of faith, for otherwise it would be superfluous to hold general councils for such conclusions; therefore the council of Cardinals can err against the faith.

units.la: CAP. VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: Soluit rationes sexti capituli tenendo, quod collegium Cardinalium possit errare, ubi nota, quod ecclesia Romana & sedes Apostolica multipliciter sumuntur.
units.tr: It answers the arguments of the sixth chapter, holding that the college of Cardinals can err. Note here that the Roman church and the apostolic see are taken in many senses.

units.la: Discip. Durum mihi videtur afferre, collegium Cardinalium posse contra fidem errare: & tamen rationes ad hoc inductae apparent difficiles, quamobrem qualiter ad rationes utriusque partis respondetur, ostende. Et primo quomodo respondetur ad rationes pro prima assertione. Magist. Ad primam istarum respondetur, quod Romana ecclesia multipliciter accipitur, aliquando enim accipitur pro vniuersali ecclesia: aliquando pro papa: aliquando pro clero & Romano populo: aliquando pro collegio Cardinalium. Illa autem ecclesia Romana, quae errare non potest, est vniuersalis ecclesia: & non collegium Cardinalium. Discip. Circa illam materiam non dicas hoc amplius: quia de ea postea te interrogabo, sed dic quomodo respondetur ad secundam rationem. Mag. Ad secundam dicunt quidam: quod per sedem Apostolicam aliquando intelligitur papa: aliquando diocesis sua: aliquando papa cum collegio Cardinalium: aliquando vniuersalis ecclesia, illa autem sedes Apostolica, quae errare non potest contra fidem, lecundum aliquos, est vniuersalis ecclesia, secundum quosdam vero, est Romana diœcesis. Discip. De hoc etiam ad præsens supersedeas, & dic ad tertiam rationem. Magist. Ad tertiam rationem respondetur, quod sicut Imperator (qui aliquando habuit potestatem eligendi summum pontificem vt habetur in decre. di. 83. c. Adrianus & c. in synodo,) potuit hæreticam incurrere prauitatem, ita etiam illud collegium, quod nunc habet potestatem eligendi summum pontifi€, potest prauitate hæretica maculari. Discip. Si illud collegium hæreticaretur, nullus haberet potestatem eligendi summum pontificem: & ita in ecclesia Dei de eligendo summo pontifice non esset sufficienter prouisum. Mag. Respondetur, quod sufficienter prouisum est, quia si collegium Cardinalium hæreticaretur, electio deuolueretur ad Romanos, si autem (sicut dicunt aliqui) esset possibile, quod omnes Romani hæreticarentur, potestas eligendi summum pontificem deuolueretur ad alios orthodoxos Discip. De hoc tecum post collocutione habebo, narra, quomodo respondetur ad quartam rationem. Mag. Respondetur ad illam rationem distinguendo: quia aut papa publice & notorie incidit in hæresim manifestam explicite iam damnatam, & in illo casu non solum collegium Cardinalium (si in fide permanserit) sed etiam diœcesanus loci, in quo moratur papa, haberet papam effectum hæreticum iudicare, & tunc negatur maior illius rationis, quia sicut papa effectus hæreticus est subiectus iudicio diœcesani fidelis, qui tamen potest errare: ita etiam papa effectus hæreticus est subiectus iudicio collegii Cardinalium in fide manentium, quod tamen potest hæreticari: quo hæreticato non haberet de papa iudicare, aut papa incidit in hæresim damnatam solummodo implicite, & tunc non collegium Cardinalium, sed collegium generale habet iudicare de ipso. Discip. Quomodo potest aliquis, qui errare potest, de papa hæretico iudicare? Magist. Respondetur quod sicut episcopi & inquisitores hæreticæ prauitatis, de quibus non est dubium, quin possint errare contra fidem, si tamen non erraverint, sed in fide permanserint orthodoxa, possunt de aliquo alio, ita & de papa eff. &c. hæretico iudicare. Discip. Dic ad alias rationes. Magist. Ad quintam respondetur, quod hæreticato collegio Cardinalium non propter hoc hæreticatur tota multitudo Christianorum, quod autem dicitur capite languente &c. hoc de multis membris continet veritatem, non tamen semper de omnibus membris verificatur, tempore enim Anastasii tertii caput (scilicet Anastasius, qui fuerat papa) languebat hæretica prauitate, & tamen multa membra sana & integra permanebant. Ad sextam rationem respondetur dupliciter, vno modo, concedendo quod nullum est collegium neq; prælatorum, neq; religiosorum, neq; laicorum, neq; clericorum, neq; virorum, neq; mulierum, quod non possit errare contra fidem, collegium tamen vniuersaliter Christianorum, quod de facto comprehendit viros & mulieres, Deus nunquam permittet contra fidem errare, aliter dicitur; quod totum collegium Romanæ diœcesis non potest errare contra fidem, neque valet consequentia: collegium Cardinalium potest errare contra fidem, ergo quodlibet aliud Collegium particulare potest errare contra fidem. Interdum est aliqua prærogatiua, quæ competit toti, q non est attributa parti, & ideo licet secundum istos tota Romana diœcesis non possit errare contra fidem: tamen collegium Cardinalium, quod est pars diœcesis, poterit errare contra fidem. Ad septimam respondetur, quod si collegium Cardinalium contra fidem erraret, inuenirentur alii Christiani, qui eis auderent resistere: quia timor mortis eos nequaquam retraheret à confessione & defensione catholicæ veritatis, sicut temporibus imperatorum, qui erat Domini mundi & multo maiores potentiæ temporalis, quam sint cardinales, multi sancti martyres confitebantur fidem catholicam & pro viribus defensabant. Discip. Nunc non inuenirentur tales. Mag. Dicitur quod sic, si enim nunc quamplurimi seculares se pro defensione temporalium contra totum collegium Cardinalium opponunt, non est incredibile reputandum, quin aliqui se exponerent pro defensione fidei, si collegium Cardinalium fidem catholicam expugnaret. Discip. Dic quomodo respondetur ad octauam rationem. Mag. Ad octauam rationem dicitur, quod collegium episcoporum potest errare contra fidem, nec est certum nec per scripturam diuinam, nec per doctrinam vniuersalis ecclesiæ, nec per doctr. nam sanctorum, quod omnes episcopi tempore Antichristi vel aliquo alio tempore à fide catholica minime errabunt: imo existimant aliqui, quamuis ad hoc fundamentum solidum haberi non possit, quod sicut pontifices & Pharisæi crucifixerunt Christum, ita episcopi & religiosi & clerici erunt principales sectatores Antichristi, nec aliquis clericus vel religiosus sibi opponet. Disc. Hoc est temerarie dictum, etiam esto quod non sit certum, an aliqui clerici Antichristo resistant: ideo transi & indica, quomodo respondetur ad rationem nonam. Mag. Ad nonam dicitur, quod collegium Cardinalium posset accusari de hæresi, & cum dicitur, inferiores superiorem accusare non possunt, hoc negatur in multis casibus. Ad decimam respondetur, quod simplices non saluarentur in fide Cardinalium, sed saluarentur si hæreticarentur in side Apostolorum, vel aliorum sanctorum, qui credebant explicite illud, quod simplices credunt implicite, vnde quod dicitur, quod simplices saluantur in fide maiorum, vel in ecclesia, debet intelligi, quod saluantur in illa fide, quæ fuit in Apostolis explicite, & adhuc est in maioribus, si maiores non sunt simplices in lege diuina, & sunt catholici & fideles, si enim soli illiterati, vel parua habentes notitiam in lege diuina essent catholici, & omnes episcopi & religiosi ac clerici essent hæretici, quamuis illiterati, non crederent explicite multa, quæ spectant ad fidem: credentes tamen illam esse veram fidem, quam prædicauerunt Apostoli, pro qua sancti martyres sunt occisi, saluarentur in fide maiorum, scilicet Apostolorum & aliorum sanctorum, qui credebant explicite, quod credunt isti implicite.
units.tr: Disciple: It seems hard to me to assert that the college of Cardinals can err against the faith, and yet the arguments brought forward for this seem difficult. So show me how replies are made to the arguments on each side, and first how the arguments for the first assertion are answered. Master: To the first of these it is answered that the Roman church is taken in many ways. Sometimes it is taken for the universal church, sometimes for the pope, sometimes for the clergy and the Roman people, and sometimes for the college of Cardinals. The Roman church that cannot err is the universal church, not the college of Cardinals. Disciple: Do not say anything more on that subject, because I will question you about it later. Tell me instead how the second argument is answered. Master: To the second some say that by "the apostolic see" sometimes the pope is understood, sometimes his diocese, sometimes the pope together with the college of Cardinals, and sometimes the universal church. According to some, that apostolic see which cannot err against the faith is the universal church, but according to others it is the Roman diocese. Disciple: Set this aside for now as well, and tell me about the third argument. Master: To the third argument it is answered that just as the Emperor (who at one time had the power of electing the supreme pontiff, as is held in Decretum, dist. 83, cap. Adrianus and cap. In synodo,) could fall into heretical depravity, so also that college which now has the power of electing the supreme pontiff can be stained with heretical depravity. Disciple: If that college became heretical, no one would have the power of electing the supreme pontiff, and so in the church of God there would not be sufficient provision for electing the supreme pontiff. Master: It is answered that sufficient provision is made, because if the college of Cardinals became heretical, the election would pass to the Romans. But if (as some say) it were possible that all the Romans became heretical, the power of electing the supreme pontiff would pass to other orthodox men. Disciple: I will have a further discussion with you about this later. Tell me how the fourth argument is answered. Master: That argument is answered by a distinction. Either the pope has publicly and notoriously fallen into a manifest heresy that has already been explicitly condemned, and in that case not only the college of Cardinals (if it has remained in the faith) but also the diocesan of the place where the pope resides would have the power to judge the heretical pope. And then the major premise of that argument is denied. For just as a heretical pope is subject to the judgment of a faithful diocesan, who nevertheless can err, so also a heretical pope is subject to the judgment of the college of Cardinals that remains in the faith, which nevertheless can become heretical. Once that college has become heretical, it would not have the power to judge the pope. Or else the pope has fallen into a condemned heresy only implicitly, and in that case it is not the college of Cardinals but a general council that has the power to judge him. Disciple: How can anyone who can err judge a heretical pope? Master: It is answered that just as bishops and inquisitors of heretical depravity, who undoubtedly can err against the faith, can nevertheless judge someone else if they have not erred but have remained in the orthodox faith, so also they can judge a heretical pope and so on. Disciple: Go on to the other arguments. Master: To the fifth argument it is answered that when the college of Cardinals becomes heretical, the whole multitude of Christians is not thereby made heretical. What is said, that when the head is sick the members are sick too, contains truth about many members, but it is not always verified of all members. For in the time of Anastasius III the head (namely Anastasius, who had been pope) was sick with heretical depravity, and yet many members remained sound and whole. To the sixth argument there is a twofold answer. In one way, by conceding that there is no college, whether of prelates, religious, laymen, clergy, men or women, that cannot err against the faith; but the college of Christians taken universally, which in fact includes men and women, God will never permit to err against the faith. Otherwise it is said: the whole college of the Roman diocese cannot err against the faith, and the consequence does not hold that the college of Cardinals can err against the faith, therefore any other particular college can err against the faith. Sometimes there is a prerogative that belongs to the whole and is not assigned to a part. So, although according to these men the whole Roman diocese cannot err against the faith, nevertheless the college of Cardinals, which is a part of the diocese, can err against the faith. To the seventh argument it is answered that if the college of Cardinals were to err against the faith, other Christians would be found who would dare to resist them, because fear of death would by no means draw them back from confessing and defending the Catholic truth. So in the times of the emperors, who were lords of the world and far greater in temporal power than the cardinals are, many holy martyrs confessed the Catholic faith and defended it to the best of their strength. Disciple: Now such men would not be found. Master: It is said that they would, for if at present very many laymen oppose the whole college of Cardinals in defence of temporal goods, it is not incredible to think that some would expose themselves in defence of the faith if the college of Cardinals attacked the Catholic faith. Disciple: Tell me how the eighth argument is answered. Master: To the eighth argument it is said that the college of bishops can err against the faith. It is certain neither from divine Scripture, nor from the teaching of the universal church, nor from the teaching of the saints, that all bishops will in no way depart from the Catholic faith in the time of Antichrist or at any other time. Indeed some think, although no solid foundation for this can be had, that just as the pontiffs and Pharisees crucified Christ, so the bishops, religious and clergy will be the principal followers of Antichrist, and no clergyman or religious will oppose him. Disciple: This is rashly said, even granting that it is not certain whether any clergy will resist Antichrist. So pass over it and show me how the ninth argument is answered. Master: To the ninth it is said that the college of Cardinals could be accused of heresy, and when it is said that inferiors cannot accuse a superior, this is denied in many cases. To the tenth it is answered that simple people would not be saved in the faith of the Cardinals, but they would be saved if they were to become heretics in the faith of the Apostles or of other saints, who believed explicitly what simple people believe implicitly. Hence what is said, that simple people are saved in the faith of their elders or in the church, must be understood to mean that they are saved in that faith which was explicit in the Apostles and is still in their elders, provided the elders are not simple in divine law and are Catholic and faithful. For if only the unlettered, or those with little knowledge of divine law, were Catholic, and all bishops, religious and clergy were heretics, then even though they were unlettered and did not explicitly believe many things that pertain to the faith, yet believing that to be the true faith which the Apostles preached and for which the holy martyrs were killed, they would be saved in the faith of their elders, namely of the Apostles and the other saints, who believed explicitly what these men believe implicitly.

units.la: CAP. IX.
units.tr: CAP. IX.

units.la: Soluit rationes septimi capituli defendendo pro prima opinione, quod collegium Cardinalium haereticari non potest.
units.tr: Answers the arguments of the seventh chapter, defending for the first opinion that the college of Cardinals cannot be heretical.

units.la: Discipulus. Audiui, quomodo tenentes aliam assertionem respondeant ad rationes pro prima assertione, nunc affecto scire, quomodo primi assertores niituntur soluere rationes inductas pro secunda assertione. Magist. Ad primam dicitur, quod sicut secundum patres sanctos Christus immediate dedit papatum Romanę ecclesiae, & tamen de hoc nulla mentio in scriptura diuina habetur, ita Christus promisit, quod Romana ecclesia esset vsq; ad finem seculi duratura, Romana autem ecclesia est collegium Cardinalium, cum vero dicitur, collegium Cardinalium est constitutum a summo pontifice. Respondetur, quod quamuis ita sit, tamen succedit priori collegio, quod errare non potuit: & ideo nec ipsum potest errare contra fidem. Ad secundam dicitur, quod summus pontifex non potest collegium Cardinalium destruere vel cassare, sicut nec potest statutum ecclesiae immutares. q. l quae ad poenitentiam. Ad tertiam autem dicitur, quod collegium Cardinalium succedit illi ecclesiae, quae temporibus Apostolorum errare non potuit, & ideo non potest errare. Ad quartam conceditur, aliqua ecclesia inferior papa non potest errare contra fidem, sicut ecclesia Romana, cui praesidet papa, est inferior papa, & tamen non potest errare in fide. Ad quintam dicitur, quod nullus, qui est sic extra collegium Cardinalium, in his, q concedit collegium Cardinalium, aduersatur eidem, potest saluari, quis saluari possit, licet non sit Cardinalis. Ad sextam dicitur, q collegium totum Cardinalium, etiam si non essent nisi duo, non possent errare contra bonos mores, qa praeseruarentur a Deo. Ad septimam dicitur, quod sicut aliquando ecclesia praeseruatur circa maiora & non circa minora, ita congregatio a Deo praeseruatur, ne fidei catholicae iacturam sustineat, quam tamen Deus patitur in multis pressuris & angustiis corporalibus tribulari: ita collegium Cardinalium praeseruatur, ne erret in electione summi pontificis. Ad octauam dicitur, quod nec ex sanctitate, nec ex fidei firmitate Cardinalium maiori, quam habuerunt Apostoli, est quod collegium Cardinalium errare non potest, sed ex promissione Christi, unde illud argumentum, si valeret concluderet, quod omni tempore post Apostolos potuit congregatio fidelium errare contra fidem, quia in congregatione fidelium post tempora Apostolorum nec maior sanctitas nec maior fidei firmitas quam in Apostolis fuit inuenta. Ad nonam dicitur, quod dignitas ecclesiastica nec sanctificat nec inobliquabilem in fide instituit aliquam personam, tamen Christus praeseruat ab errore contra fidem aliquod collegium habens aliquam specialem dignitatem, quemadmodum religio Christiana nec sanctificat nec inobliquabilem reddit aliquam personam, Christus tamen praeseruat collegium suscipientium religionem Christianam ne erret contra fidem. Ad decimam dicitur dupliciter, uno modo, quod collegium archiepiscoporum & episcoporum non potest contra fidem errare, & isti concedunt, quod praeter congregationem fidelium sunt plura collegia particularia, quae contra fidem errare non possunt, sc. collegium Cardinalium & collegium episcoporum. Aliter dicitur, quod collegium Cardinalium, quantum ad aliqua, est eminentius collegio episcoporum, licet quantum ad aliqua sit inferius ipso, & ideo licet Cardinales valeant eligi ad episcopatus, poterit tamen collegium episcoporum vel ipsorum cardinalium esse confirmatum in fide. Ad undecimam dicitur, quod de una sola ecclesia militante in generali asseritur, quod non potest contra fidem errare, cum hoc tamen stat, quod sit aliqua ecclesia particularis, quae non possit errare contra fidem, sicut conceditur quod congregatio fidelium errare non potest, & tamen simul cum hoc conceditur, quod concilium generale contra fidem errare non potest. Ad ultimam dicitur, quod collegium Cardinalium in quaestionibus fidei terminandis requirit aliorum concilium, ut magis autenticetur per consensum plurium determinatio eorum.
units.tr: Student. I have heard how those who hold the other assertion reply to the arguments brought for the first assertion; now I wish to know how the authors of the first assertion undertake to answer the arguments brought for the second assertion. Master. To the first it is said that, just as according to the holy Fathers Christ immediately gave the papacy to the Roman Church, and yet no mention of this is found in divine Scripture, so Christ promised that the Roman Church would endure until the end of the age. The Roman Church, however, is the college of Cardinals. But when it is said that the college of Cardinals was established by the supreme pontiff, the reply is that, although this is so, it nonetheless succeeds the earlier college, which could not err; and therefore it too cannot err against the faith. To the second it is said that the supreme pontiff cannot destroy or annul the college of Cardinals, just as he cannot change a statute of the Church (C. 1, q. 1, "Quae ad poenitentiam"). To the third it is said that the college of Cardinals succeeds that Church which in the times of the Apostles could not err, and therefore it cannot err. To the fourth it is granted that some church inferior to the pope cannot err against the faith; just as the Roman Church, over which the pope presides, is inferior to the pope, and yet cannot err in the faith. To the fifth it is said that no one who is outside the college of Cardinals and opposes the college of Cardinals in those things which it grants can be saved; but whether one can be saved, although he is not a Cardinal, is another question. To the sixth it is said that the whole college of Cardinals, even if there were only two of them, could not err against good morals, because they would be preserved by God. To the seventh it is said that, just as sometimes the Church is preserved in greater matters and not in lesser ones, so the congregation is preserved by God lest it sustain loss of the Catholic faith, although God allows it to be troubled in many distresses and bodily straits; so the college of Cardinals is preserved lest it err in the election of the supreme pontiff. To the eighth it is said that the college of Cardinals cannot err neither from the holiness nor from the firmness of faith of the Cardinals, which is greater than that which the Apostles had, but from the promise of Christ. Hence that argument, if it were valid, would conclude that at every time after the Apostles the congregation of the faithful could have erred against the faith, because in the congregation of the faithful after the times of the Apostles neither greater holiness nor greater firmness of faith was found than in the Apostles. To the ninth it is said that ecclesiastical dignity neither sanctifies nor makes any person unbendable in the faith; yet Christ preserves from error against the faith a college having some special dignity, just as the Christian religion neither sanctifies nor renders any person unbendable, yet Christ preserves the college of those who take up the Christian religion from erring against the faith. To the tenth it is said in two ways. In one way, that the college of archbishops and bishops cannot err against the faith, and these men concede that, besides the congregation of the faithful, there are several particular colleges which cannot err against the faith, namely the college of Cardinals and the college of bishops. In another way it is said that the college of Cardinals, in some respects, is more eminent than the college of bishops, although in some respects it is inferior to it; and therefore, although Cardinals may be eligible to bishoprics, the college of bishops or of the Cardinals themselves may nevertheless be confirmed in the faith. To the eleventh it is said that of the one church militant in general it is asserted that it cannot err against the faith; yet with this it stands that there may be some particular church which could not err against the faith, just as it is conceded that the congregation of the faithful cannot err, and yet at the same time it is conceded that a general council cannot err against the faith. To the last it is said that the college of Cardinals, in terminating questions of faith, requires the agreement of others, so that their determination is made more authentic by the consent of several.

units.la: CAP. X.
units.tr: CHAPTER X.

units.la: In quo ponitur alia quaestio incidens ex precedentis tractatione, utrum sc. Papa cum collegio Cardinalium simul possit haeretica pravitate maculari, & circa hanc ponuntur duae opiniones.
units.tr: In which another question arising from the previous discussion is raised, namely whether the pope together with the College of Cardinals can be stained by heretical depravity, and two opinions on this are set out.

units.la: Discip. Exiguitati meae videtur, quod ad rationem septimam, octauam & nonam sufficienter respon sum extitit, sed ad rationes alias responsiones nequaquam intelligo: quarum tamen vsq; ad tepu discussionem maiorem volo differri, nunc autem occasione praedictorum scire desidero, quid sentiunt Scholastici de collegio Cardinalium vna cum papa sc. an papa & hi Cardinales simul possint pravitate haeretica irretiri? Magi. Circa hoc sunt diuersae opiniones. Qui enim dicunt, quod papa non potest errare contra fidem, etiam illi qui asserunt, quod collegium Cardinalium non potest contra fidem errare, habent dicere consequenter, quod papa vna cum collegio Cardinalium non potest contra fidem errare, cuius ratio videtur esse praecipua: quia ecclesia Romana non potest contra fidem errare, ecclesia autem Romana est papa vna cum collegio Cardinalium, ergo &c.
units.tr: Disciple: To my slight understanding, the seventh, eighth and ninth reasons seem to have been sufficiently answered, but I do not understand the answers to the other reasons. I want their fuller discussion deferred until a later time, but now, prompted by what has been said, I wish to know what the Scholastics think about the College of Cardinals together with the pope. That is, can the pope and these Cardinals together be entangled in heretical depravity? Master: On this point there are different opinions. Those who say that the pope cannot err against the faith, and also those who assert that the College of Cardinals cannot err against the faith, must consequently say that the pope together with the College of Cardinals cannot err against the faith. The chief reason for this seems to be that the Roman Church cannot err against the faith, and the Roman Church is the pope together with the College of Cardinals; therefore, etc.

units.la: Item sedes Apostolica errare non potest contra fidem, sedes autem Apostolica papam & collegium Cardinalium tantum modo comprehendit, ergo &c. Alii asserunt manifeste, quod papa vna cum collegio Cardinalium potest errare contra fidem, quorum rationes fundamentales tactae sunt prius. Tum, quia si papa cum Cardinalibus non potest contra fidem errare, frustra ad quaestiones fidei terminandas generalia concilia congregarentur. Tum quia, de vna sola ecclesia habetur ex scriptura diuina, quod errare non potest. Tum quia extra papam & Cardinales est salus. Tum quia omnes possent simul crimine irretiri, ergo omnes etiam possent simul contra fidem errare.
units.tr: Likewise, the Apostolic See cannot err against the faith, but the Apostolic See comprehends only the pope and the College of Cardinals; therefore, etc. Others plainly assert that the pope together with the College of Cardinals can err against the faith, and their fundamental reasons were touched on earlier. (1) If the pope with the Cardinals cannot err against the faith, general councils would be convened in vain to settle questions of faith. (2) Divine Scripture teaches that only one church cannot err. (3) Salvation lies outside the pope and the Cardinals. (4) All of them could be entangled in crime at the same time, and therefore all of them could also err together against the faith.

units.la: CAP. XI.
units.tr: CAP. XI.

units.la: In quo ponitur tertia quaestio principalis huius, utrum ecclesia Romana, seu sedes Apostolica valeat haeretica infici pravitate, & circa hoc sunt 4. principales assertiones, sed subdividitur in duas.
units.tr: In which the third principal question of this book is set out, whether the Roman church, or the apostolic see, can be infected with heretical depravity; and on this there are four principal assertions, but it is subdivided into two.

units.la: Discip. Ut cerno, proposita mea interrogatio dependet ex alia: an scilicet ecclesia Romana seu sedes Apostolica valeat haeretica infici pravitate, ideo de illa differere non postponas. Mag. Ex praedictis potes euidenter elicere, quod circa illam interrogationem tuam non omnes consentiunt. Unde quidam dicunt absque distinctione, quod nec ecclesia Romana, nec sedes Apostolica potest errare contra fidem: intelligentes per Romanam ecclesiam & sedem Apostolicam, papam tantum vel collegium Cardinalium tantummodo, vel simul papam & Cardinales. Alii dicunt, quod ecclesia Romana contra fidem errare non potest, intelligentes per Romanam ecclesiam, clerum Romanum, qui papam & Cardinales & alios clericos comprehendit. Alii dicunt, quod ecclesia Romana, quae comprehendit omnes clericos in quibusdam mundi partibus constitutos, errare non potest. Et quidam istorum dicunt, quod licet aliqui clerici possent errare contra fidem, tamen maior pars nunquam contra fidem errabit. Alii vero dicunt, quod multitudo clericorum potest errare; sed semper aliqui clerici in fide manebunt. Alii autem de ecclesia Romana distinguunt dicentes, quod aliquando papa, quandoque collegium Cardinalium, aliquoties papa cum Cardinalibus, quandoque totus clerus Romanus, interdum tota Romana dioecesis, nonnunquam tota congregatio fidelium nomine Romana ecclesia importatur. Et de ecclesia Romana illo ultimo modo dicta dicunt, quod non potest errare, de papa autem & Cardinalibus, de tota Romana dioecesi, quae est distincta ab aliis dioecesibus in provinciis aliis constitutis, concedunt quod potest errare contra fidem. Nec est certum nec perscriptum, nec per doctrinam vniuersalis ecclesiae, quod ciuitas Romana cum tota regione, quae spectat ad episcopatum Romanum, cum venerit Antichristus, sibi minime adhaerebit: nec etiam ante tempora Antichristi tota discedet a fide Catholica.
units.tr: Disciple. As I see it, my question depends on another: namely, whether the Roman church or the apostolic see can be infected with heretical depravity. So do not put off explaining that to me. Master. From what has been said you can clearly gather that not all agree about your question. Some say, without distinction, that neither the Roman church nor the apostolic see can err against the faith, understanding by the Roman church and the apostolic see only the pope, or only the college of cardinals, or the pope and the cardinals together. Others say that the Roman church cannot err against the faith, understanding by the Roman church the Roman clergy, which includes the pope, the cardinals and the other clerics. Others say that the Roman church, which comprises all the clerics established in certain parts of the world, cannot err. Some of these add that although some clerics could err against the faith, yet the greater part will never err against it. Others, however, say that the multitude of clerics can err, but that some clerics will always remain in the faith. Still others distinguish concerning the Roman church, saying that sometimes the pope, sometimes the college of cardinals, sometimes the pope with the cardinals, sometimes the whole Roman clergy, at other times the whole Roman diocese, and occasionally the whole congregation of the faithful is meant by the name Roman church. Of the Roman church taken in that last sense they say that it cannot err; but of the pope and the cardinals, and of the whole Roman diocese, which is distinct from the other dioceses established in other provinces, they concede that it can err against the faith. Yet it is neither certain nor written down, nor taught by the universal church, that the city of Rome with the whole region which belongs to the Roman bishopric will not at all cling to Antichrist when he comes, nor that before the time of Antichrist the whole of it will fall away from the Catholic faith.

units.la: CAP. XII.
units.tr: CAP. XII.

units.la: In quo probatur, quod vniuersalis ecclesia potest Romana ecclesia appellari, duabus rationibus.
units.tr: In which it is shown, by two arguments, that the universal Church can be called the Roman Church.

units.la: Discipul. Miror quod isti dicunt, totam Romanam ecclesiam aliquando congregationem fidelium importare, vnde si hoc possunt trahere ex scripturis authenticis, aperire digneris. Mag. Quod per Romanam ecclesiam congregatio fidelium valet importari, ex scriptura niituntur ostendere. Primo sic: Omnis ecclesia Romanorum potest ecclesia Romana appellari, sed omnes fideles possunt appellari Romani. Unde & beatus Paulus extra totam Italiam natus, antequam Romam venisset, se esse Romanum ciuem asseruit, Actor. 6. ergo tota congregatio fidelium potest Romana ecclesia appellari. Secundo arguunt sic: Illa ecclesia, quae non habet maculam neq; rugam neq; aliud huiusmodi, potest Romana ecclesia appellari, teste Pelagio papa, qui, ut habetur dist. 22. c. quamuis, loquens de Romana ecclesia ait: Est ergo prima Apostoli Petri sedes Romana ecclesia, non habens maculam neq; rugam nec aliquid huiusmodi. Vbi dicit Glo. Ord. quod vbicunq; sunt boni, est Romana ecclesia. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod tota congregatio bonorum, vbicunque sint, potest ecclesia Romana appellari, & per consequens tota congregatio fidelium potest ecclesia Romana appellari.
units.tr: Disciple. I marvel at what these men say, that the whole Roman Church sometimes signifies the congregation of the faithful. If they can draw this from authentic Scriptures, please deign to show me. Master. They undertake to show from Scripture that the Roman Church can be taken to signify the congregation of the faithful. First, thus: every congregation of the Romans can be called the Roman Church, but all the faithful can be called Romans. Hence also blessed Paul, born outside all Italy, asserted that he was a Roman citizen before he came to Rome (Acts 6.); therefore the whole congregation of the faithful can be called the Roman Church. Secondly, they argue thus: that church which has no spot, nor wrinkle, nor anything of the kind, can be called the Roman Church, as Pope Pelagius testifies, who, as is found in dist. 22, c. quamuis, speaking of the Roman Church, says: "The Roman Church is therefore the first see of the Apostle Peter, not having spot, nor wrinkle, nor anything of the kind." Where the Glossa Ordinaria says: "Wherever there are good people, there is the Roman Church." From these words it is clear that the whole congregation of the good, wherever they may be, can be called the Roman Church, and consequently the whole congregation of the faithful can be called the Roman Church.

units.la: CAP. XIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIII.

units.la: In quo probatur quod ecclesia Romana vt distinguitur a tota congregatione fidelium, non potest contra fidem errare, & hoc octo rationibus & quibusdam authoritatibus, ad quas respondetur infra cap. 14.
units.tr: In which it is proved that the Roman church, as distinguished from the whole congregation of the faithful, cannot err against the faith, and this by eight arguments and certain authorities, to which replies are given below in chapter 14.

units.la: Discipulus. Circa interrogationem propositam considero sententias hominum multipliciter variari, de quibus duas tantummodo pertractes ad praesens. Primo enim allega pro prima sententia, qua asseritur, quod Romana ecclesia, quae distinguitur a congregatione fidelium, sicut pars a suo toto, non potest contra fidem errare, postea pro assertione contraria allegare conaberis. Mag. Quod ecclesia Romana (quae distinguitur a tota congregatione fidelium, sicut pars a suo toto) contra fidem errare non possit, multis modis ostenditur. Primo sic: Illa ecclesia, quae voce euangelica Domini & Saluatoris nostri caeteris ecclesiis est praelata, contra fidem errare non potest, quia (ut habetur actor. 5.)
units.tr: Pupil. Regarding the question proposed, I observe that the opinions of men vary in many ways, and of these I shall treat only two for the present. For first you adduce arguments for the first opinion, which holds that the Roman church, distinguished from the congregation of the faithful as a part is from its whole, cannot err against the faith, and afterwards you will try to adduce arguments for the contrary assertion. Master. That the Roman church (which is distinguished from the whole congregation of the faithful as a part is from its whole) cannot err against the faith is shown in many ways. First, thus: that church which, by the evangelical voice of our Lord and Saviour, has been preferred to the other churches cannot err against the faith, because (as is written in Acts 5.)

units.la: Ss opus Dei dissolui non potest ab hominibus, si autem illa ecclesia, quae voce divina caeteris ecclesiis est praelata, contra fidem erraret, desineret esse caput aliarum ecclesiarum, & ita opus Dei dissolveretur.
units.tr: If the work of God cannot be dissolved by men, but that church which by the divine voice has been preferred to the other churches were to err against the faith, it would cease to be the head of the other churches, and so the work of God would be dissolved.

units.la: Sed Romana ecclesia, quae distincta est contra alias ecclesias; & per consequens contra totam congregationem fidelium (sicut pars contra suum totum) voce Domini caeteris ecclesiis est praelata, teste Pelagio, qui, ut habetur dist. 21. c. quamuis, ait: quamuis per orbem catholica ecclesia constituta unus thalamus Christi sint, tamen sancta Romana ecclesia catholica & apostolica nullis Synodicis constitutionibus caeteris ecclesiis praelata est, sed Evangelica voce Domini & Salvatoris nostri principatum obtinuit, ergo haec ecclesia Romana errare non potest. Secundo sic: Illa ecclesia contra fidem errare non potest, quae privilegium super alias ecclesias non potest amittere, quia eo ipso, quod aliqua quaecunque ecclesia haereticetur, omne privilegium super quoscunque orthodoxos amitteret, cum omnes haeretici quibuscunque catholicis sint minores. 24. q. 1. c. si autem, ecclesia autem Romana super alias ecclesias privilegium non potest amittere: imo esset haereticus reputandus, qui privilegium auferre sibi conaretur: cum & assertione illius, qui potest veritatem habere, non sit inter haereticos numerandus. Sed qui privilegium Romanae ecclesiae auferre conatur, in haeretica labitur pravitatem, teste Nicolao papa, qui, ut habetur 22. dist. c. omnes, loquens de Romana ecclesia, quae est distincta contra alias ecclesias, ait: non est dubium, quia quisquis cuiuslibet ecclesiae ius suum detrahit, iniustitiam facit. Qui autem Romana ecclesia privilegium ab ipso summo omnium ecclesiarum pontifice traditum auferre conatur, hic procul dubio in haeresim labitur, & cum ille vocetur iniustus, hic est dicendus haereticus. Ex quibus verbis habetur, quod qui conatur auferre privilegium ecclesiae Romanae, haereticus est censendus, & per consequens tale privilegium a Romana ecclesia auferri non potest. Et per consequens ipsa haereticari non potest, quia eo ipso, quo haereticaretur, omne privilegium perderet. Tertio sic: Illa ecclesia contra fidem errare non potest, sine qua nulla ecclesia catholica valet regi: quia Deus ecclesiam universaliter non rectam nunquam usque in finem seculi dereliquit. Igitur nec usque in finem seculi derelinquet illa ecclesia, sine qua nulla ecclesia regitur, sed sine ecclesia Romana non esset ecclesia catholica rite disposita, teste Anacleto papa, qui, ut habetur di. 22. c. sacrosanctam, ait: haec vero Apostolica sedes caput & cardo, ut praefatum est, a Domino & non ab alio constituta est, & sicut cardine ostium regitur, sic huius sancta Apostolica sedis auctoritate omnes ecclesiae (Domino disponente) reguntur, ergo haec sedes Apostolica, quae est Romana ecclesia, contra fidem errare non potest. Quarto sic: illa ecclesia contra fidem errare non potest, a qua quicunque dissentit non est inter episcopos computandus catholicos: quia propter dissensionem ab haereticis nemo a numero catholicorum excludedus est, sed quicunque ab ecclesia Romana dissentit, non est de catholicis episcopis reputandus, teste beato Ambro. qui, ut habetur 24. q. 1. c. aduocauit, ait: aduocauit ad se Cyprianum episcopum Satirum, nec ullam putauit veram nisi veram fidei gratiam, percunctatus quaeque est eum, utrum nam de catholicis episcopis esset, hoc est, si cum ecclesia Romana communicaret. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod nemo potest esse ex catholicis episcopis, nisi cum ecclesia Romana communicet, igitur Romana ecclesia errare non potest. Quinto: Illa ecclesia errare non potest, extra quam nemo salvatur, sed extra Romanam ecclesiam nemo potest salvari, teste Hiero. qui, ut habetur 24. q. 1. c. quantum vetus, loquens de Romana ecclesia ait: Ego nullum praemium nisi Christum sequens beatitudini tuae, id est, cathedra Petri communione, consortio & super illam Petram fundatam ecclesiam scio, quicunque extra hanc domum agnum comederit profanum est, si quis in Archa Noe non fuerit, peribit diluvio regnante. Et infra: quicunque non colligit mecum, dispergit. Ex quibus datur intelligi, quod quicunque non fuerit per conformitatem & unitatem fidei intra Romanam ecclesiam, de qua loquitur Hieron. salvari nequit. ergo Romana ecclesia de qua loquitur Hiero. contra fidem errare non potest: quia si erraret, qui esset intra eam, minime salvaretur. Sexto. Illa ecclesia non potest contra fidem errare, a qua omnis Christianus discedens, est inter schismaticos computandus, sed quicunque a Romana ecclesia discedit, est inter schismaticos computandus, seu computatur: quia extra ecclesiam reputatur, teste Cypria. qui, ut legitur di. 93. c. qui cathedram Petri, ait: qui cathedram Petri, super quam fundata est ecclesia, deserit, in ecclesia se esse non confidat, & Innocentius tertius, ut recitatur extra, de maioritate & obedientia, omnes ab ovili Christi asserit alienos: & per consequens schismaticos, qui Petri successores & magistros non cognoscunt & pastores, ergo Romana ecclesia contra fidem errare non potest. Septimo sic: Corpus sine membris consistere non potest, ecclesia autem fidelium est corpus mysticum, ergo ecclesia sine membris esse non potest, membrum autem principale noscitur esse caput, ecclesia vero Romana est caput totius ecclesiae Dei, ergo ecclesia Dei sine ecclesia Romana esse non potest, illa autem ecclesia, sine qua ecclesia Dei esse non potest, non potest errare contra fidem, ergo ecclesia Romana contra fidem errare non potest. Octavo sic: Illa ecclesia non potest contra fidem errare, quam nulla malitia valet extinguere, sed ecclesiam Romanam nulla malitia valet extinguere, teste Pelagio papa, qui, ut habetur 24. q. 1. c. pudenda, ait: cum ecclesia una sit, nullam aliam esse constat, nisi quae in Apostolica est radice fundata, & infra recitans verba Aug. subiungit: si nullo modo recte potest dici ecclesia, in qua schisma est, restat ut quoniam ecclesia nulla esse non potest, ea sit, quam in Apostolica sedis per successiones eorum constitutam, nulla hominum malitia, etiam si nota, excludi non possit, sed pro temporis ratione iudicatur tolerandā, nullo modo valet extinguere. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod ecclesiam in radice sedis Apostolicae constitutam per successionem episcoporum, quae est Romana ecclesia, nulla malitia hominum valet extinguere, ergo papa contra fidem errare non potest. Conclusionem praedictam, quod ecclesia Romana errare non potest, auctoritatibus fulcire nituntur, ait enim Hieronymus 24. q. 1. cap. a recta: Haec sancta & Apostolica mater ecclesiarum omnium Christi ecclesia, quae per Dei omnipotentis gratiam a tramite Apostolicae traditionis nunquam errasse probatur, nec haereticis novitatibus damnata succumbit, sed ut ab exorexordio normam fidei suscepit ab auctoribus Apostolorum Christi principibus illibata fide hactenus manet, & ibidem Hieronym. vt habetur 24. q. 1. c. haec est fides, ait: sancta Romana ecclesia (quae semper immaculata permansit) Domino providente & beato Petro opem ferente in futuro seculo permanebit sine vlla haereticorum insultatione firma & immobilis omni tempore perstitet. Ex his videtur, quod Romana ecclesia nunquam contra fidem erravit, nec errabit.
units.tr: But the Roman church, which is distinct from the other churches and, consequently, from the whole congregation of the faithful (as a part from its whole), has been preferred to the other churches by the voice of the Lord, as Pelagius testifies, who, as is found in dist. 21. c. quamuis, says: although the catholic church, established throughout the world, is one bridal chamber of Christ, yet the holy Roman catholic and apostolic church has not been preferred to the other churches by any synodical decrees, but has obtained the primacy by the evangelical voice of our Lord and Saviour. Therefore this Roman church cannot err. Second, thus: that church cannot err against the faith which cannot lose its privilege over the other churches, because if any church whatever were to be declared heretical, it would lose every privilege over all orthodox churches, since all heretics are lesser than any catholics. 24. q. 1. c. si autem says that the Roman church cannot lose its privilege over the other churches; indeed, whoever tried to take that privilege away from it should be judged a heretic, since one who asserts what may be true is not to be numbered among heretics. But whoever tries to take away the privilege of the Roman church falls into heretical wickedness, as Pope Nicholas testifies, who, as is found in 22. dist. c. omnes, speaking of the Roman church, which is distinct from the other churches, says: there is no doubt that whoever takes away from any church its right does an injustice. But whoever tries to take away from the Roman church the privilege handed down to it by the supreme pontiff of all churches himself, he without doubt falls into heresy, and whereas the former is called unjust, the latter must be called a heretic. From these words it is clear that whoever tries to take away the privilege of the Roman church is to be judged a heretic, and consequently such a privilege cannot be taken away from the Roman church. And consequently it cannot itself be made heretical, because by the very fact that it were made heretical it would lose every privilege. Third, thus: that church cannot err against the faith without which no catholic church can be governed, because God has never forsaken the universal church, which is not upright, until the end of the age. Therefore neither will he forsake until the end of the age that church without which no church is governed. But without the Roman church a catholic church would not be duly ordered, as Pope Anacletus testifies, who, as is found in dist. 22. c. sacrosanctam, says: this Apostolic see, as has been said, is the head and hinge, and was established by the Lord and by no other, and just as a door is governed by its hinge, so by the authority of this holy Apostolic see all churches are governed (the Lord so disposing). Therefore this Apostolic see, which is the Roman church, cannot err against the faith. Fourth, thus: that church cannot err against the faith from which whoever dissents is not to be counted among the catholic bishops, because no one is to be excluded from the number of catholics on account of dissent from heretics; but whoever dissents from the Roman church is not to be reckoned among the catholic bishops, as blessed Ambrose testifies, who, as is found in 24. q. 1. c. advocavit, says: he summoned to himself Cyprian, the bishop Satyrus, and he thought nothing true except the grace of the true faith, inquiring of each one whether he was among the catholic bishops, that is, whether he communicated with the Roman church. From these words it is clear that no one can be among the catholic bishops unless he communicates with the Roman church; therefore the Roman church cannot err. Fifth: that church cannot err outside of which no one is saved; but outside the Roman church no one can be saved, as Jerome testifies, who, as is found in 24. q. 1. c. quantum vetus, speaking of the Roman church, says: I, following no other reward than Christ, know of no church but yours, blessed one, that is, the communion of the chair of Peter, and the church founded upon that Rock. Whoever eats the lamb outside this house is profane; if anyone is not in the ark of Noah, he will perish when the flood reigns. And further: whoever does not gather with me, scatters. From these words it is clear that whoever is not, through conformity and unity of faith, within the Roman church, of which Jerome speaks, cannot be saved. Therefore the Roman church of which Jerome speaks cannot err against the faith, because if it did err, whoever was within it would by no means be saved. Sixth: that church cannot err against the faith from which every Christian who departs is counted among the schismatics; but whoever departs from the Roman church is counted, or is reckoned, among the schismatics, because he is regarded as outside the church, as Cyprian testifies, who, as is read in dist. 93. c. qui cathedram Petri, says: whoever deserts the chair of Peter, upon which the church is founded, let him not trust that he is in the church; and Innocent III, as cited in Extra, de maioritate et obedientia, asserts that all who do not acknowledge the successors and teachers of Peter, and his ministers, are strangers to the fold of Christ, and consequently schismatics. Therefore the Roman church cannot err against the faith. Seventh, thus: a body cannot exist without its members, but the church of the faithful is the mystical body; therefore the church cannot exist without members. Now the principal member is known to be the head, and the Roman church is the head of the whole church of God; therefore the church of God cannot exist without the Roman church. But that church without which the church of God cannot exist cannot err against the faith; therefore the Roman church cannot err against the faith. Eighth, thus: that church cannot err against the faith which no malice is able to extinguish; but the Roman church is one which no malice is able to extinguish, as Pope Pelagius testifies, who, as is found in 24. q. 1. c. pudenda, says: since the church is one, it is clear that there is no other except that which is founded on the Apostolic root; and further, quoting the words of Augustine, he adds: if in no way can that be rightly called a church in which there is schism, it remains that the church which is established in the Apostolic see through the succession of its bishops, which cannot be excluded by any malice of men, even if known, but is tolerated for reasons of time, cannot by any means be extinguished. From these words it is clear that the church established at the root of the Apostolic see through the succession of bishops, which is the Roman church, cannot be extinguished by any malice of men; therefore the pope cannot err against the faith. They strive to support the aforesaid conclusion, that the Roman church cannot err, with authorities. For Jerome says in 24. q. 1. c. a recta: this holy and Apostolic mother of all churches, the church of Christ, which by the grace of almighty God is proved never to have erred from the path of Apostolic tradition, nor yields, condemned by heretical novelties, but from the beginning received the norm of the faith from the authors, the chief Apostles of Christ, remains until now with its faith unimpaired; and in the same place Jerome, as is found in 24. q. 1. c. haec est fides, says: the holy Roman church (which has always remained spotless), God providing and blessed Peter bringing aid, will remain in the future age without any insult from heretics, firm and immovable, standing at all times. From these things it appears that the Roman church never erred against the faith, nor will it err.

units.la: CAP. XIV.
units.tr: CAP. XIV.

units.la: In quo ponitur quaedam alia quaestio incidens ex praecedenti tertia quaestione principali, à quo scilicet Romana ecclesia super omnes alias obtinuit principatum, de qua quinque assertiones, seu conclusiones ponit, quae iuvant praecedentis capituli assertionem, & quae probantur sigillatim in capitulis sequentibus.
units.tr: In which another question is raised, arising from the third principal question of the preceding chapter, namely from what source the Roman Church obtained principality over all the others; on this there are five assertions or conclusions, which support the assertion of the preceding chapter and which are proved separately in the following chapters.

units.la: Discipulus. Si non fallor, ad sciendum an Romana ecclesia possit contra fidem errare, confert non modicum indagare, à quo Romana ecclesia super omnes alias obtinuit principatum. Quia si habuerit principatum à Deo, non videtur quod possit isto principatu priuari, nisi à solo Deo. Et ita vsque in finem seculi est habitura principatum, & per consequens nunquam contra fidem errabit. Si autem habuerit principatum ab homine, non video quare ipsa non possit errare contra fidem, sicut aliae ecclesiae particulares. Nunc igitur peto, vt (aliqualiter à principali proposito digrediendo) de hac re cures disserere, quid Scholastici sentiant indicando. Bene enim postea ad propositum principale faciam te reuerti. Mag. De principatu ecclesiae Romanae diuersi diuersas & aduersas affirmant sententias, quibusdam dicentibus, quod nec beatus Petrus, nec aliquis successor eius, nec Romana ecclesia super alias habuit à Deo seu à Christo principatum: imo dicunt, quod nec beatus Petrus ex ordinatione Christi superior fuit aliis Apostolis, nec aliquis Episcopus ex ordinatione Christi est superior alio. Vnde quinque assertiones circa hanc materiam probare nituntur. Prima est, quod beatus Petrus ex ordinatione Christi non habuit super alios Apostolos principatum. Secunda, quod Petrus non fuit Romanus episcopus. Tertia quod beatus Petrus ex ordinatione Apostolorum super alios Apostolos papatum obtinuit. Quarta est, quod ex ordinatione Christi nullus sacerdos supra alios habet maiorem potestatem. Quinta est, quod Romana ecclesia ab ipso Constantino Imperatore super omnes alias ecclesias primatum accepit.
units.tr: Student. If I am not mistaken, to know whether the Roman Church can err against the faith, it matters not a little to inquire from what source the Roman Church obtained principality over all the others. For if it has received its principality from God, it does not seem that it could be deprived of that principality except by God alone; and so it will have that principality until the end of the age, and consequently will never err against the faith. But if it has received its principality from man, I do not see why it should not be able to err against the faith, just as other particular churches can. I therefore ask you now, digressing somewhat from the main subject, to set out for me what the Schoolmen think on this matter. I will afterwards bring you back to the principal subject without fail. Master. Writers differ widely and hold conflicting opinions about the principality of the Roman Church. Some say that neither blessed Peter, nor any of his successors, nor the Roman Church received principality over the others from God or from Christ. Indeed they say that blessed Peter was not, by the ordinance of Christ, superior to the other Apostles, and that no bishop is, by the ordinance of Christ, superior to another. Hence they seek to prove five assertions about this matter. The first is that blessed Peter did not have principality over the other Apostles by the ordinance of Christ. The second, that Peter was not the bishop of Rome. The third, that blessed Peter obtained the papacy over the other Apostles by the ordinance of the Apostles. The fourth, that by the ordinance of Christ no priest has greater power than the others. The fifth, that the Roman Church received primacy over all other churches from the Emperor Constantine himself.

units.la: CAP. XV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XV.

units.la: In quo ponitur & probatur prima conclusio, scilicet quod beatus Petrus non habuit super alios Apostolos ex ordinatione Christi principatum, tribus rationibus, & aliquibus auctoritatibus: Ad oppositum huius ponitur opinio contraria capitulo 16. immediate sequenti.
units.tr: In which the first conclusion is set out and proved, namely that Saint Peter did not have a primacy over the other apostles by the ordinance of Christ, by three arguments and some authorities. The opposing opinion is put in the immediately following chapter 16.

units.la: Discipul. De istis conclusionibus valde miror, quod quis literatus tenere praesumit: Verumtamen ad excitanda ingenia motiua eorum audire desidero, quia ex ipsis forsitan veritas clarius elucescet. Magist. Primam assertionem; quod videlicet beatus Petrus super alios Apostolos ex ordinatione Christi non habuit principatum, auctoritatibus scripturae diuinae & sanctorum probare nituntur. Talem autem possunt facere rationem. Beatus Petrus super illos à Christo non habuit principatum, qui aequalem potestatem seu principatum potestati Petri seu primatui receperunt à Christo, quia par super parem nullum noscitur habere principatum, Apostoli autem potestatem aequalem beati Petri potestati receperunt à Christo &c. Hinc auctoritatibus scripturae diuinae & sanctorum moliuntur ostendere. Primo autem hanc declarare conantur auctoritate Christi dicentis cunctis Apostolis, Matth. 18. Amen dico vobis, quaecunque ligaueritis super terram, erunt ligata & in coelis. Ex quibus verbis dicunt manifeste patere, quod potestas ligandi & soluendi aequalis potestati beati Petri fuit data Apostolis à Christo, beatus autem Petrus nullam potestatem, in qua dicatur alios excellere, recepit à Christo, nisi potestatem ligandi & soluendi, ergo beatus Petrus & omnes alii Apostoli aequalem potestatem habuerunt à Christo. Hoc etiam Iohann. Euangelista (recitans verba Saluatoris) videtur asserere 20. c. dicens: Dixit iterum, pax vobis, sicut misit me pater, & ego mitto vos. Hoc cum dixisset, insufflauit & dixit: accipite Spiritum sanctum, quorum remiseritis peccata, remittuntur eis. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod Christus claues, quas promiserat beato Petro, tunc dedit omnibus Apostolis, & cum beato Petro dixit: tibi dabo claues regni coelorum: omnibus Apostolis in persona Petri promisit claues regni coelorum, quare cum claues promissae, & postea datae beato Petro eius potestatem designent, sequitur quod alii Apostoli aequalem potestatem cum beato Petro acceperunt à Christo, & ita Petrus potestatem seu principatum aut primatum super alios Apostolos à Christo non habuit. Amplius: Recipere potestatem super alios, quam non debet in eos recipiens exercere, est superfluum, vanum & inutile reputandum in operibus autem Christi nihil superfluum, vanū & inutile poteritrepeiri. Christus autem non dedit B. Petro aliam potestatem super alios Apostolos, q; in eos debuit exercere: imo talem potestatē B. Petro & omnibus aliis Apostolis super alios Apostolos interdixit, dicens Mat. 20. Scitis quia principes gentium dominantur eorū, & qui maiores sunt potestatem exercent in eos, non ita erit inter vos, & Mar. 10. ita legitur: Iesus autem vocans eos ait illis: Scitis quod hi, qui videntur principari gentibus, dominantur eis, & principes eorum potestatem habent ipsorum: non ita est autem in vobis, Luc. 22. c. recitat verba Christi dicens: Reges gentium dominantur eorum, & qui potestatem habent super eos benefici vocantur: vos autem non sic. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod nullus Apostolus debuit potestatem in alios exercere, ergo nec beatus Petrus habuit à Christo potestatem super alios Apostolos seu primatum. Discip. Istæ duæ auctoritates non videntur facere ad propositum, nam verba Christi prædicta debet intelligi de potestate temporali: beatus autē Petrus non habuit à Christo sup alios Apostolos potestatē temporalē, sed spiritualem, quare p auctoritates premissas probari nō potest, nisi q beatus Petrus non habuit potestatē temporalem sup alios Apostolos, qualē reges & principes gentium noscuntur habere. Mag. Hanc rationem nituntur excludere ostendentes, q Christus cuilibet Apostolo super alios Apostolos potestatem temporalē & spiritualem interdixit. Nam, teste Hilario, vt habetur extra de verb. significationibus, intelligentia dictorū ex causis est assumeda dicendi. Verba ergo Christi premissa ex causa dicendi debent intelligi, Christus autē dixit verba pdicta occasione accepta ex contentione Apostolorū, quis eorū videretur esse maior. Ita enim legitur Luc. 22. Facta est contentio inter eos, quis eorū videretur esse maior. Dixit autē eis &c. Inter eos autem non fuit contentio de maioritate temporali, sed spirituali. Ergo Christus potestatē interdicens eisdē sub potestate non solū temporalē, sed etiā spirituale comprehendit, ergo B. Petrus potestatē super alios Apostolos nec tēporalē nec spirituale accepit à Christo. Rursus: si aliqua potestas vel principatus fuit data B. Petro à Christo sup alios Apostolos, data fuit sibi p illa verba Ioh. vlt. Pasce oues meas, sed p illa verba nulla fuit data potestas spiritualis vel principatus sup alios Apostolos, ergo principatū super alios Apostolos nō accepit à Christo. Maior huius rationis conceditur. Minor probatur: q a spiritualiter pascere oues non contingit nisi tripliciter sc. salutari doctrina, & vita exemplari, & disciplina seu correctione regulari, sed quilibet istorum modorū pascendi oues Christi, communis fuit omnibus Apostolis. Vniuersi enim Apostoli oēs oues Christi doctrina pascere debuerunt, ipsa veritate testante, q omnibus præcepit Apostolis, Mat. vlt. dicens: Euntes ergo docete oēs gentes baptizantes eos in nomine Patris & Filii & Spiritus sancti, docentes eos seruare omnia quecunq; mandaui vobis. Oēs etiā debuerunt pascere vita exéplari, ipsis Christo dicente Mat. 5. Vos estis lux mundi, & sequitur: Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus, vt videant opera vestra bona, & glorificent patrē vestrum qui in cœlis est. De modo pascendi correctione & disciplina regulari habetur Iohan. 20. vbi Christus dixit omnibus Apostolis: Quorum remiseritis peccata remittuntur eis: & quorum retinueritis, retenta sunt, vbi videtur Christus omnibus Apostolis potestatem corrigendi alios commisisse. Discip. Ista ratio non concludit, quia beato Petro fuit collata potestas corrigendi cunctos Christianos non solum in foro conscientiæ, sed etiam in foro ecclesiæ: aliis autem Apostolis, cum Christus dixit eis, Quorum remiseritis peccata &c. potestas corrigendi in foro conscientiæ tantum fuit commissa. Mag. Hanc responsionem ipsi improbare niteruntur hoc modo: Vbi Christus ordinauit modum corrigendi in foro ecclesiæ, nihil speciale beato Petro commisit, sed potestatem corrigendi in foro ecclesiæ commisit non solum beato Petro, sed communitati ecclesiæ dicens Matth. 18. Si peccauerit in te frater tuus, vade & corripe eum inter te & ipsum solum, si te audierit, lucratus eris fratrem tuum: si autem te non audierit, adhibe tecum vnum vel duos: vt in ore duorum vel trium stet omne verbum, quod si non audierit eos, dic ecclesiæ, si autem ecclesiam non audierit, sit tibi sicut Ethnicus & publicanus. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod Christus dedit ecclesiæ potestatem corrigendi in foro ecclesiæ, & non alicui Apostolo in speciali. Discip. In his verbis agitur de correctione fraterna, & non de correctione iudiciali in foro ecclesiæ. Magist. Respondent isti, quod in principio allegationis ait Christus de fraterna correctione, quæ debet præcedere saltem correctionem iudicialem, in fine autem loquitur de correctione iudiciali in foro ecclesiæ, cum dixit: & si non audierit eos, dic ecclesiæ, si autem ecclesiam non audierit, sit tibi sicut Ethnicus & publicanus. Discip. Quomodo potest stare, quod Christus potestatem corrigendi in foro ecclesiæ solummodo commiserit ecclesiæ, cum Apostolus Paulus Corinthum excommunicauit, & in epistola ad Timotheum primo asserit se quosdam Sathanæ tradidisse? Mag. Ad hoc respondetur, quod ex commissione Christi sola communitas fidelium habuit potestatem corrigendi in foro ecclesiæ, Christus tamen non arctauit communitatem fidelium ad certum modum corrigendi, quando scilicet posset per se totam, quando esset expediens, vel per aliquam singularem personam, quæ gereret vicem communitatis, corrigere delinquentes & ita dicunt beatū Paulum potestatē corrigendi accepisse à cōitate fidelium vnius puinciæ vel diuersarū prouinciarum. Discip. Secundū hoc sequitur, q Christus non reliquit aliquod caput ecclesiæ. Mag. Concedūt isti, q Christus non reliquit caput ecclesiæ, q ex ordine Christi haberet potestatē coercendi delinquentes in foro ecclesiæ: nec tñ insufficienter, puidit ecclesiæ: q a ordinando q ecclesia haberet potestatē corrigendi, disposuit q ecclesia sibi vnū caput vel plura secundū diuersitatē puinciarum eligeret: imo dicunt q pro bono comunitatis ecclesiæ est, q in potestate ecclesiæ sit sibi vnū caput vel plura eligere, quod etiam vel quæ quādo expediens videretur ecclesiæ posset deponere, cum ergo Christus optime proꝑiderit ecclesiæ, in potestate posuit ecclesiæ sibi vnum caput vel plura eligere, sicut enim sæpe expedit communitati, vnum caput habere: ita interdum potest esse expediens communitati regi à pluribus. Sicut enim nonnunquam expedit rectorem habere perpetuum, ita aliquando expedit rectorem habere non perpetuum, sed ad tempus habere. Et ideo in quibusdam communitatibus secularibus non improvide ordinatur, quod rectores annis singulis vel post tres menses vel alium numerum mensium vel annorum vel dierum suum resignent officium, vel penitus deponantur: in quibusdam communitatibus non vnus solus, sed plures præficiuntur regentes. Ratio autem prædictorum assignatur; quia in providendo regimini alicuius communitatis non solum conditionem & mores subditorum, sed etiam mores & conditiones præficiendorum oportet attendere. Et ideo quia potest contingere, quod in communitate non inueniatur aliquis idoneus, vt solus regimen super communitatem accipiat; in tali casu non vnus, sed plures communitatem vtiliter gubernabunt.
units.tr: Disciple. I am greatly surprised that any learned person presumes to hold these conclusions. Nevertheless, I would like to hear their arguments, so that the minds of their supporters may be stirred, and perhaps the truth may shine out more clearly from them. Master. They try to prove the first assertion, namely that Saint Peter did not have a primacy over the other apostles by the ordinance of Christ, by the authority of divine Scripture and the saints. They make the following argument. Christ did not give Saint Peter a primacy over those who received from Christ a power or primacy equal to Peter's power or primacy, since no one is known to have a primacy over his equal. But the apostles received from Christ a power equal to Saint Peter's power, and so on. They then try to show this from the authority of divine Scripture and the saints. First, they try to establish this by the authority of Christ, who said to all the apostles, Matt. 18. Verily I say unto you, whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven. From these words they say it is clear that the power of binding and loosing, equal to the power of Saint Peter, was given to the apostles by Christ; but Saint Peter received from Christ no power in which he could be said to excel the others, except the power of binding and loosing. Therefore Saint Peter and all the other apostles had an equal power from Christ. John the Evangelist also seems to affirm this in chapter 20, when he recounts the words of the Saviour: Then said Jesus to them again, Peace be unto you: as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you. And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost: whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them. From these words it is understood that Christ then gave to all the apostles the keys which he had promised to Saint Peter, and when he said to Peter, I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven, he promised the keys of the kingdom of heaven to all the apostles in the person of Peter. Therefore, since the keys promised and afterwards given to Saint Peter signify his power, it follows that the other apostles received from Christ a power equal to that of Peter, and so Peter did not have from Christ a power or primacy over the other apostles. Furthermore: to receive a power over others which the recipient ought not to exercise over them is to be counted superfluous, vain and useless; but nothing in the works of Christ can be found superfluous, vain or useless. Now Christ did not give Saint Peter any power over the other apostles which he ought to exercise over them; indeed he forbade Saint Peter and all the other apostles such a power over the other apostles, saying in Matt. 20. Ye know that the princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and they that are great exercise authority upon them. But it shall not be so among you. And Mark 10. reads thus: But Jesus called them to him, and saith unto them, Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them. But so shall it not be among you. Luke 22. recounts the words of Christ, saying: The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors. But ye shall not be so. From these words it is understood that no apostle ought to exercise power over the others; therefore neither did Saint Peter have from Christ a power or primacy over the other apostles. Disciple. These two authorities do not seem to bear on the point, for the words of Christ quoted above must be understood of temporal power; but Saint Peter did not have from Christ over the other apostles a temporal power but a spiritual one. Therefore the authorities cited cannot prove anything, except that Saint Peter did not have over the other apostles a temporal power of the kind that kings and princes of the Gentiles are known to have. Master. They try to exclude this argument by showing that Christ forbade every apostle any power over the other apostles, both temporal and spiritual. For, as Hilary testifies, and as is found in the Extra, On the meaning of words, the understanding of sayings is to be drawn from the occasion of speaking. The words of Christ quoted above must therefore be understood from the occasion of speaking, and Christ spoke them on the occasion of a dispute among the apostles as to which of them seemed to be greatest. For so it reads in Luke 22.: And there was also a strife among them, which of them should be accounted the greatest. And he said unto them, etc. But the dispute among them was not about temporal greatness but spiritual. Therefore Christ, in forbidding them power, comprehended under the word power not only temporal but also spiritual power; therefore Saint Peter received from Christ no power over the other apostles, neither temporal nor spiritual. Again: if any power or primacy over the other apostles was given to Saint Peter by Christ, it was given to him by those words of John's last chapter, Feed my sheep; but by those words no spiritual power or primacy over the other apostles was given, therefore he did not receive a primacy over the other apostles from Christ. The major of this argument is granted. The minor is proved thus: to feed sheep spiritually can happen only in three ways, namely by wholesome teaching, by exemplary life, and by regular discipline or correction. But each of these ways of feeding the sheep of Christ was common to all the apostles. For all the apostles were bound to feed all the sheep of Christ by teaching, the truth itself testifying, which Christ commanded to all the apostles in Matt. last chapter, saying: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you. All were also bound to feed by exemplary life, Christ himself saying in Matt. 5.: Ye are the light of the world; and it follows: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven. Concerning the manner of feeding by correction and regular discipline, it is written in John 20, where Christ said to all the apostles: Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them; and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained; where it seems that Christ committed to all the apostles the power of correcting others. Disciple. This argument does not conclude, because a power of correcting all Christians, not only in the forum of conscience but also in the forum of the Church, was conferred on Saint Peter; but to the other apostles, when Christ said to them, Whose soever sins ye remit, etc., only a power of correcting in the forum of conscience was committed. Master. They try to disprove this answer in the following way. Where Christ ordained the manner of correcting in the forum of the Church, he committed nothing special to Saint Peter, but he committed the power of correcting in the forum of the Church not only to Saint Peter but to the whole community of the Church, saying in Matt. 18.: If thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother. But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established. And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the Church: but if he neglect to hear the Church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.
