Again, the greatest falling away of Christians from the faith will occur in the time of Antichrist; but in his time many faithful Christian men will remain, the truth itself bearing witness, which, as is found in Matthew 24, speaking of the persecution to come in the time of Antichrist, says: "There shall arise false Christs and false prophets, and shall show great signs and wonders, insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive even the elect." From these words it is gathered that in the time of Antichrist there will be some holy and elect men who will by no means be led into error, which the blessed John in the Apocalypse seems to attest in various places. These, among other things, clearly refute the aforesaid assertion of its improbability. DISCIPLE. Although I have no doubt about the conclusion, nevertheless, that I may understand the truth more clearly, and have occasion to think about the many matters that pertain to this subject, would you please explain how these arguments can be answered?

units.la: CAP. XXXIV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXIV.

units.la: Ubi respondetur ad duas precedentes rationes, quibus probatur quod non tota multitudo virorum contra fidem errare possit.
units.tr: Where a reply is given to the two preceding arguments, by which it is proved that the whole multitude of men cannot err against the faith.

units.la: MAGIST. Vis ut tibi quid sentiam de praedictis aperiam. DISCIP. Nolo ut quod tenes in mente, reueles: sed responsiones aliquas, quae cogitari vel teneri potuerint a quocunque, non differas recitare. MAGIST. Hoc pacto ut omnia quae narrabo non aliter accipiantur, nisi quod aliquis quaestionum difficilium indagator potest dicendo computare consona veritati, quomodo ad praedictas instantias respondere contingat ostendam. Volo etiam quod dicenda fratri MAGIST. & eius sequacibus nequaquam imponas, sicut in praecedentibus multas recitaui sententias, quae assertionibus domini Iohann. & suorum sequacium obuiant manifeste; quas tamen frater MAGIST. & sui sequaces minime opinantur: immo nonnullas impugnare nituntur, ita in parte futura operis huius (si tu volueris) plura referam, quae frater MAG. & sui sequaces satagunt improbare. DISCIP. Quod istum modum teneas, a principio acceptaui. quia sententias contrarias quorumcunque catholicorum & haereticorum & interdum alia, quae a nullo Christiano tenentur, licet possint habere catholicos & haereticos defendentes, te desidero recitare. sic enim multiplicius & efficacius exercitabimus studiorum ingenia. MAGIST. Peractis suppositis memoratis quomodo ad instantias allegatas poterit responderi, tuae curiositati satagam explanare. Ad primam dupliciter dicitur vel dici potest. primo, quod verba Christi praefata, erit tunc tribulatio magna, &c. ad literam intellecta de persecutione facta per Titum & Vespasianum non debent intelligi, manifeste videtur posse probari. Primo, quia tribulatio facta per diluuium, quando in vniuerso mundo octo sc. animae tantum modo saluabantur, erat multo maior quam facta per Titum & Vespasianum; eo quod multae animae tunc saluatae fuerunt. DISC. Verba Christi praedicta non intelliguntur de tribulatione generali vniuersorum mortalium, qualis fuit illa, quae fuit facta per diluuium: sed de tribulatione particulari & speciali Iudaeorum, quorum non fuit maior, quam illa, quae fuit facta per Romanos. MAG. Haec responsio potest dupliciter impugnari. Christus enim ibidem non loquitur de tribulatione speciali tantum modo Iudaeorum, sed loquitur etiam de tribulatione aliarum gentium & regnorum. & praemittit ibidem dicens: consurget gens contra gentem &c. quae verba de Iudaea tantum modo, quae fuit unicum regnum, non possunt intelligi. igitur Christus cum dicit: erit enim tunc tribulatio magna &c. de tribulatione Iudaeorum, quam intulerunt Romani, non debent intelligi. intelligitur ergo vel de tribulatione generali cunctorum viuentium, vel de tribulatione alicuius gentis specialis, vel aliarum gentium determinatarum. non possunt intelligi de tribulatione generali: quia illa, quae facta fuit per diluuium, maior fuit, quam illa quam fecerunt Romani. nec possunt intelligi de tribulatione in speciali gentis vel gentium facta per Romanos: quia tribulatio Sodomorum, in qua omnes perierunt, maior fuit
units.tr: MASTER. You want me to set out what I think of the foregoing. DISCIPLE. I do not want you to reveal what you hold in your own mind, but please do not hold back from reciting any replies that anyone could think up or hold. MASTER. On this condition, that everything I say is taken only as the view of one who investigates difficult questions, and that it may be reckoned consistent with the truth, I will show how it may be possible to reply to the aforesaid objections. I also ask that you do not attribute to Brother Master and his followers what I recite, just as in the earlier part I recited many opinions which plainly oppose the assertions of Master John and his followers, although Brother Master and his followers by no means hold them; indeed, they strive to attack some of them. So in the later part of this work (if you wish) I will report more that Brother Master and his followers labour to refute. DISCIPLE. I accepted from the beginning that you would keep to this method, because I want you to recite the opposing opinions of whatever Catholics and heretics there are, and sometimes others that no Christian holds, even though Catholics and heretics may defend them. In this way we will exercise the wits of our studies more widely and effectively. MASTER. With the aforesaid suppositions settled, I will take care to explain to your curiosity how the alleged objections may be answered. To the first it is or can be answered in two ways. First, that the words of Christ quoted above, there will then be great tribulation, etc., must not be understood literally of the persecution made by Titus and Vespasian; this seems clearly provable. First, because the tribulation made by the flood, when in the whole world only eight souls, namely, were saved, was much greater than that made by Titus and Vespasian, inasmuch as many souls were saved then. DISC. The words of Christ above are not understood of the general tribulation of all mortals, such as was that made by the flood, but of the particular and special tribulation of the Jews, of which there was none greater than that which was made by the Romans. MAG. This reply can be attacked in two ways. For Christ there speaks not only of the special tribulation of the Jews, but also of the tribulation of other nations and kingdoms, and he says just before it: nation shall rise against nation, etc. These words cannot be understood of Judea alone, which was a single kingdom. Therefore when Christ says for then there will be great tribulation, etc., they must not be understood of the tribulation of the Jews which the Romans inflicted. It is understood, then, either of the general tribulation of all living things, or of the tribulation of some special nation, or of certain other determinate nations. They cannot be understood of a general tribulation, because the one made by the flood was greater than the one the Romans made. Nor can they be understood of a tribulation of a nation or nations in particular, made by the Romans, because the tribulation of Sodom, in which all perished, was greater

units.la: fuit foit quam tribulatio per Romanos illata. ergo verba Christi praedicta de tribulatione, quae facta est per Romanos, non debent intelligi. DISCIP. De qua ergo tribulatione debent intelligi? MAGIST. Debet dici, quod verba illa specialiter debent intelligi de tribulatione fidelium, qui scil. rectam fidem tenent de Deo: inter quos quidam sunt electi, & alii per poenam aeternam sunt praescit. Et non de quacunque tribulatione, sed de tribulatione, quae sub Antichristo erit, quando tanta tribulationem habebunt, quantam certe fidem tenentes nunquam habuerunt, licet saepe infideles maiorem tribulationem habuerint, & sicut forsitan sunt habituri. Tribulatio autem facta per diluvium respectu infidelium erat maior, quam erit tribulatio Antichristi respectu fidelium: quia tunc omnes infideles pariter perierunt: sed respectu fidelium non erit tanta tempore Antichristi; quia non omnes fideles tunc peribunt. Maior etiam fuit tribulatio Sodomorum, quando quinque civitates subversae fuerunt, quam erit tribulatio fidelium tempore Antichristi. & ita saepe maior fuit tribulatio infidelium, quam erit illa tribulatio, quam Christus praedixit futuram: quamvis forsitan erit tanta, quod fideles pauci remanebunt firmi in fide. Et an isti fideles erunt viri vel mulieres, solus Deus novit, & illi, quibus Deus specialiter revelavit.
units.tr: than the tribulation brought by the Romans. Therefore the words of Christ quoted above about the tribulation made by the Romans should not be understood. DISCIPLE. Of what tribulation, then, ought they to be understood? MASTER. It must be said that those words should be understood especially of the tribulation of the faithful, who hold the true faith concerning God, among whom some are elect and others are foreknown to eternal punishment. And not of just any tribulation, but of the tribulation that will be under Antichrist, when they will suffer such tribulation as those holding the true faith have certainly never suffered, although unbelievers have often suffered greater tribulation, and perhaps will do so again. The tribulation made by the flood was greater with respect to unbelievers than the tribulation of Antichrist will be with respect to the faithful, because then all unbelievers perished together; but with respect to the faithful it will not be so great in the time of Antichrist, because not all the faithful will perish then. The tribulation of Sodom was also greater, when the five cities were overthrown, than the tribulation of the faithful in the time of Antichrist will be. And so often the tribulation of unbelievers has been greater than that tribulation which Christ foretold would come, although perhaps it will be so great that only a few faithful will remain firm in the faith. Whether those faithful will be men or women, God alone knows, and those to whom God has specially revealed it.

units.la: Ad secundam rationem potest dici, quod electi comprehendunt viros & mulieres. & ideo per hoc, quod iuxta promissionem Christi tempore Antichristi remanebunt electi, non potest concludi, quod illi electi erunt viri, quia mulieres tunc poterunt esse electae. DISCIP. Videtur quod illi qui tenent praedictam assertionem, non multum reputant stabilitatem ecclesiae & constantiam Christianorum. MAGIST. Est quaedam assertio, quae affirmatur aperte, quod temerarium est asserere omni tempore futuros Christianos, qui erunt constantiores in fide quam Iudaei fuerunt.
units.tr: To the second argument it can be said that the elect comprise men and women. And so from the fact that, according to Christ's promise, the elect will remain in the time of Antichrist, it cannot be concluded that those elect will be men, since women could then be elect too. DISCIPLE. It seems that those who hold the aforesaid assertion do not think much of the stability of the Church and the constancy of Christians. MASTER. There is an assertion that is openly affirmed, that it is rash to assert that at all times there will be Christians more constant in the faith than the Jews were.

units.la: quamvis enim fuerunt in fide constantissimi, & aliqui firmi in fide sint futuri; tamen nescitur ab aliquo viatore (nisi alicui Deus revelaverit) an multitudo catholicorum ad illam paucitatem deveniet, in qua fuit tempore Noe & temporibus Patriarcharum & in veteri lege: & an Saraceni & alii infideles omnes regiones Christianorum & fidelium occupabunt. Ideo aliquid in talibus diffinire, & de futuris aliquid temere divinare vanum est.
units.tr: For although they were most constant in the faith, and some will be firm in the faith, yet no wayfarer knows (unless God has revealed it to someone) whether the multitude of Catholics will fall to that small number in which it was at the time of Noah, in the times of the patriarchs, and under the old law; or whether the Saracens and other unbelievers will occupy all the regions of Christians and the faithful. Therefore to define anything about such matters, and to divine rashly about the future, is vain.

units.la: Poterit enim Deus exigentibus Christianorum demeritis permittere omnes ab infidelibus subiugari: & (paucis exceptis) ad sectam eorum converti; qui postea poterit (si voluerit) sua pietate totum mundum ad fidem convertere. Quemadmodum per paucos apostolos sive discipulos magnam partem mundi fidei subiugavit. Et ideo sunt quidam dicentes, quod si Saraceni & alii infideles Christianitatem inuaserit, temere Christiani praesumant se per dimidiam potentiam protegentes, si terras suas disseminatas iam vbiq; terrarum haeresibus, symoniis, persecutionibus, diffamationibus & calumniis, innocentum violentis iudiciis, guerris, dissensionibus, & discordiis, rerum & dominiorum ac iurium occupationibus & invasionibus alienorum, ambitionibus, acceptionibus personarum, distributionibus impiis & iniquis bonorum, iracundia & invidia, iniustitiis ac aliis vitiis spiritualibus ac carnalibus innumerabilibus, quibus tota vel fere tota Christianitas videtur infecta, neglexerint expurgare.
units.tr: For God, because of the demerits of Christians, may permit all of them to be subjugated by unbelievers, and (a few excepted) converted to their sect; afterwards he can, if he wills, convert the whole world to the faith by his mercy, just as through a few apostles or disciples he brought a great part of the world under the faith. And so there are some who say that if the Saracens and other unbelievers invade Christendom, Christians rashly presume to protect themselves with half their strength, if they have neglected to cleanse their lands, now everywhere scattered with heresies, simonies, persecutions, defamations and calumnies, violent judgments against the innocent, wars, dissensions and discords, the occupation and invasion of others' property, domains and rights, ambitions, partiality towards persons, impious and unjust distributions of goods, anger and envy, injustices, and countless other spiritual and carnal vices, with which the whole, or nearly the whole, of Christendom seems infected.

units.la: Omnibus enim haereticis & fautoribus eorum ac nequitiis aliis inuolutis extinctis; terrisque omnium Christianorum ab infidelibus occupatis: poterit Deus etiam per duos aut per tres vel plures (quos elegerit) orthodoxos multiplicare plusquam fuerint unquam Christianos ac terram sanctam: & maiores quam unquam habuerint regiones (infidelibus extirpatis) eorum subdere ditioni. Quid autem de praedictis eveniet, nolunt dicere se spiritum prophetiae habere; nec reputant divinare. Et ideo concedunt, quemadmodum etiam praedixisti, quod non est credendum, quod infideles nunquam totam Christianitatem nullatenus occupabunt. neutrum enim est certum, nisi Deo & cui Deus revelabit.
units.tr: For when all heretics, their supporters and other wicked people are wrapped up and extinguished, and the lands of all Christians are occupied by unbelievers, God can also multiply, through two or three or more orthodox men whom he chooses, more people than Christians have ever been, and the holy land too; and he can subject to their rule greater regions than they have ever had, the unbelievers having been exterminated. What will happen of these things they are unwilling to say, since they do not claim to have the spirit of prophecy, nor do they think they divine. And so they concede, as you also have said, that it is not to be believed that unbelievers will never occupy the whole of Christendom. For neither outcome is certain, except to God and to whomever God reveals it.

units.la: Quamvis dicant nonnulli, quod tempore Antichristi tanta erit persecutio & extinctio catholicorum, quod omnis regio in universo orbe erit per infidelibus vel per apostatas occupata. Et an simile quid eveniet vel non eveniet ante tempus Antichristi, dicunt quod per scripturam divinam vel doctrinam vniversalis ecclesiae sciri non potest.
units.tr: Although some say that in the time of Antichrist the persecution and extermination of Catholics will be so great that every region in the whole world will be occupied by unbelievers or apostates, they also say that whether something similar will or will not happen before the time of Antichrist cannot be known from divine Scripture or from the teaching of the universal Church.

units.la: DISCIP. Certum est, quod fides Christi usque in finem seculi permanebit. ergo certum est, quod nunquam infideles totam Christianitatem occupabunt. MAGIST. Respondent dicentes: male arguis, quia fides catholica Christi poterit remanere in catholicis dispersis & latitantibus in terris ab infidelibus occupatis: quemadmodum nunc Iudaei aliqui & Saraceni etiam publice in terris Christianorum manent.
units.tr: DISCIP. It is certain that the faith of Christ will remain until the end of the age; therefore it is certain that unbelievers will never occupy the whole of Christendom. MAGIST. They reply, saying: "Your argument is faulty, because the Catholic faith of Christ can remain among Catholics scattered and hiding in lands occupied by unbelievers, just as now some Jews and even Saracens remain openly in the lands of Christians."

units.la: CAP. XXXV.
units.tr: CAP. XXXV.

units.la: Vbi probatur quinque rationibus, quod tota multitudo fidelium usum rationis habentium potest contra fidem errare.
units.tr: Where it is proved by five arguments that the whole multitude of the faithful, who have the use of reason, can err against the faith.

units.la: DISCIP. Istam assertionem tam absurdam aestimo, quod ipsam dignam reprobatione maiori non censeo. Ideo ipsa dimissa ad complendam materiam, quam incepi, volo te aliam magis rationabilem pertractare. Quaeso enim, ut mihi reveles, an aliqui sentiant, quod tota multitudo Christianorum valeat haeretica pravitate foedari. MAGIST. Iudaei, Saraceni, & etiam Pagani firmissime tenent, fidem Christianam esse erroneam. DISCIP. Non intendo quaequaerere de illis, sed de Christianis: sub Christianis etiam haereticos comprehendendo. MAG. Nescio aliquem Christianum, qui hoc teneat. DISCIP. Licet nescias Christianum aliquem hoc tenere, tamen pro hoc aliquas rationes excogitare nitaris. MAGIST. Ad quaestionem falsam nulla ratio nisi sophistica potest adduci. DISCIP. Concedo quod pro assertione praedicta nulla valet ratio nisi sophistica allegari: tamen saepe rationes apparentes & difficiles ad soluendum pro falsis inducuntur. unde qualescunque inuenire conaris. MAGIST. Quod tota multitudo Christianorum vsum rationis habentium possit contra fidem errare, tali ratione probatur. quantum ad possibilitatem errandi & peccandi idem iudicium est habendum de multis & paucis arbitrii libertatem & peccabilitatem habentibus: sed parua multitudo Christianorum propter libertatem arbitrii & peccabilitatem potest contra fidem errare. ergo propter eandem causam tota multitudo Christianorum potest contra fidem errare. Confirmatur haec ratio, quia vbi est eadem causa, debet esse idem effectus. causa quare Christianus potest contra fidem errare, est; quia nemo credit nisi volens, eo quod articuli fidei non sunt de se euidentes. sed illa causa repetitur in tota multitudine Christianorum: & articuli fidei sunt inuidentes toti multitudini. & ideo illa non credit, nisi volens. ergo ita poterit tota multitudo Christianorum errare, sicut vnus solus. Secunda ratio talis est. Illa multitudo, quae non est confirmata in fide, potest contra fidem errare; sicut illa multitudo vsum rationis habentium, quae non est confirmata in gratia, potest peccare. tota autem multitudo Christianorum non est confirmata in fide: quia nullus Christianus in hac vita est confirmatus in fide. ergo multo fortius tota multitudo non est confirmata in fide. & ergo tota potest contra fidem errare. Tertia ratio est haec. Illa multitudo quando est sola, potest contra fidem errare, quae valet errare contra fidem, postquam sibi alii sunt adiuncti, per quos nihil necessario veritatis aut virtutis diminuitur, sed magis accrescit: quia eadem multitudo est fortior cum aliis sibi conferentibus, quam sola. sed tota multitudo Christianorum, quae nunc est (illa manente integra, nec vno ex ea penitus pereunte) postquam multi alii fuerunt Christiani, sacerdotes & episcopi, poterit contra fidem errare. ergo eadem multitudo, si sola manserit, nullo alio effecto Christiano, antequam aliquis alius fidem susceperit, poterit contra fidem errare. Erit haec est possibilis, tota multitudo Christianorum errabit contra fidem. Quarta ratio est haec. nulla auctoritate videtur posse probari, quin possibile sit omnes Christianos, praeter duos episcopos contra fidem errare: quia omnes promissiones Christi de fide vsque ad finem seculi durature saluari possunt, si omni tempore ad minus duo episcopi catholici fuerint in fide. Ponatur ergo, quod omnes Christiani efficiantur haeretici praeter duos episcopos. quo posito probatur quod illi duo episcopi (antequam aliquis alius efficiatur catholicus) possunt contra fidem errare, sic: Non maior cura esset Deo de illis duobus episcopis, eo quod essent fideles soli: quam fuerit de duobus primis parentibus, quando erant. Sed primi parentes, quando erant soli fideles, potuissent contra fidem errare. ergo & illi episcopi possent contra fidem errare. Quinta ratio probat specialiter, quod tota multitudo virorum & mulierum vsum rationis habentium potest contra fidem errare: quia illa tota multitudo potest contra fidem errare, qua errante saluantur omnes promissiones Christi de fide vsque ad finem seculi permansura. sed errante tota multitudine Christianorum virorum & mulierum vsum rationis habentium, possunt saluari promissiones Christi de fide Christi mansura. Nam Christus vere est spiritualiter cum paruulis baptizatis per gratiam & virtutes. Fides etiam beati Petri, pro qua Christus rogauit, nequaquam deficeret, quia repperiretur in paruulis. Paruuli enim habent habitum fidei. ergo errante tota multitudine Christianorum vsum rationis habentium, possunt saluari promissiones Christi per paruulos baptizatos. ergo temerarium est asserere, quod nunquam tota multitudo Christianorum vsum rationis habentium contra fidem errabit.
units.tr: DISCIP. I judge this assertion so absurd that I do not think it deserves any strong refutation. So I will set it aside and, to finish the subject I began, I want you to treat another, more reasonable question. Please tell me whether some people think that the whole multitude of Christians could be corrupted by heretical depravity. MAGIST. The Jews, the Saracens and even the pagans firmly hold that the Christian faith is erroneous. DISCIP. I do not mean to ask about them, but about Christians, and by Christians I include heretics too. MAG. I do not know of any Christian who holds this. DISCIP. Even if you know of no Christian who holds it, you are still trying to devise some arguments for it. MAGIST. No argument except a sophistical one can be brought for a false question. DISCIP. I grant that no argument except a sophistical one can be alleged for the aforesaid assertion; yet arguments that look plausible and are hard to answer are often put forward even for falsehoods. So produce whatever kind you can find. MAGIST. That the whole multitude of Christians, who have the use of reason, can err against the faith is proved by this argument. As regards the possibility of erring and sinning, the same judgment must be made of many and of few who have freedom of will and are capable of sin. But a small multitude of Christians, because of freedom of will and capacity for sin, can err against the faith. Therefore, for the same cause, the whole multitude of Christians can err against the faith. This argument is confirmed thus: where the cause is the same, the effect must be the same. The reason why a Christian can err against the faith is that no one believes unless willing, since the articles of faith are not self-evident. But this cause is found in the whole multitude of Christians, and the articles of faith are not evident to the whole multitude. Therefore it does not believe unless willing. So the whole multitude of Christians can err just as one man alone can. The second argument is this. That multitude which is not confirmed in the faith can err against the faith, just as that multitude of rational beings which is not confirmed in grace can sin. But the whole multitude of Christians is not confirmed in the faith, because no Christian in this life is confirmed in the faith. Therefore, much more strongly, the whole multitude is not confirmed in the faith, and so the whole can err against the faith. The third argument is this. That multitude which, when it is alone, can err against the faith, is also able to err against the faith after other people have been joined to it, through whom nothing of truth or virtue is necessarily lessened but rather increased, since the same multitude is stronger with others contributing to it than alone. But the whole multitude of Christians that now exists (that multitude remaining intact, with none of its members wholly perishing), after many others have become Christians, priests and bishops, can err against the faith. Therefore the same multitude, if it remains alone, with no other person having become a Christian, before anyone else has taken up the faith, can err against the faith. And so, if this is possible, the whole multitude of Christians will err against the faith. The fourth argument is this. By no authority can it seem to be proved that it is not possible for all Christians, except two bishops, to err against the faith, since all the promises of Christ that the faith will endure to the end of the age can be saved if at every time at least two catholic bishops have been in the faith. Suppose, then, that all Christians become heretics except two bishops. Granting this, it is proved that those two bishops (before anyone else becomes catholic) can err against the faith, as follows. God would not have had greater care for those two bishops, because they alone were faithful, than He had for the first two parents when they were the only ones. But the first parents, when they alone were faithful, could have erred against the faith. Therefore those bishops also could have erred against the faith. The fifth argument proves specifically that the whole multitude of men and women who have the use of reason can err against the faith, because that whole multitude can err against the faith, if its erring would still leave intact all the promises of Christ concerning the faith that are to endure to the end of the age. But if the whole multitude of Christian men and women who have the use of reason were to err, the promises of Christ concerning the faith could still be saved and remain in force. For Christ is truly present spiritually with the baptized infants through grace and the virtues. The faith of the blessed Peter, for which Christ prayed, would by no means fail, because it would be found in the infants, for infants have the habit of faith. Therefore, if the whole multitude of Christian men and women who have the use of reason were to err, the promises of Christ could be saved through the baptized infants. Therefore it is rash to assert that the whole multitude of Christians who have the use of reason will never err against the faith.

units.la: Explicit liber quintus.
units.tr: Here ends the fifth book.

units.la: INCIPIT LIBER SEXTVS, IN QVO AGITVR DE PVNI- TIONE ET POENIS HAERETICORVM ET maxime Papæ, si efficiatur haereticus. Et habet iste liber duas partes. in prima de Papa mendaciter diffamato de haeresi agitur usque ad capitulum 66. In secunda de eodem veraciter diffamato.
units.tr: BOOK SIX BEGINS, IN WHICH IT IS TREATED OF THE PUNISHMENT AND PENALTIES OF HERETICS, AND ESPECIALLY OF THE POPE, SHOULD HE BECOME A HERETIC. This book has two parts. The first, concerning a Pope falsely defamed of heresy, runs up to chapter 66. The second concerns the same man truly defamed.

units.la: CAP. I.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: Quaerit, an Papa habeat iudicem superiorem in terris, ubi ponuntur quatuor modi respondendi. duo tamen sunt principales, & primus modus dicendi probatur sex auctoritatibus & tribus rationibus. ad quas respondetur infra 62. c. huius, scilicet quod Papa non habeat superiorem in terris.
units.tr: He asks whether the Pope has a superior judge on earth. Four ways of answering are set out, but two of them are the principal ones. The first way of speaking is supported by six authorities and three reasons, to which an answer is given below in chapter 62 of this book: namely, that the Pope has no superior on earth.

units.la: DISCIP. Solutiones praedictarum rationum per memetipsum satagam invenire, & ideo qui possunt haeretici, te interrogare desistam, nonnulla de puniendis haereticis amodo quaesiturus. Porro quia istud opus volui fieri principaliter propter dissensionem inter sanctissimum patrem dominum Iohann. Papam. 22. & quosdam qui ipsum de pravitate haeretica diffamant, cum quibus convenio in hoc, quod Papa potest haeretica labe respergi, licet praedictum dominum virum catholicum reputem & fidelem. Ideo principaliter in hoc sexto libro, qualiter quis (si efficiatur haereticus) ferendus sit, investigare curabo. Veruntamen quia Papa valet de haeresi mendaciter infamari, primo inquiram de Papa super crimine haeresis mendaciter diffamato. Secundo (sc. infra c. 66.) de Papa vere haeretica labe foedato. In primis autem cupio scire, an Papa habeat iudicem superiorem in terris, unde de hac re unam velis vel plures assertiones cum suis motivis mihi referre. MAGIST. Circa interrogationem tuam discrepant literati: quibusdam dicentibus, quod papa non habet superiorem in terris: aliis dicentibus, quod licet nulla persona in terris sit superior papa, universalis tamen ecclesia & concilium generale est supra papam. Asserentium autem papam non habere superiorem in terris, quidam dicunt, quod cum quis semel est canonice ad papatum assumptus, nisi abrenunciaverit spontanea voluntate papatui, nunquam poterit nisi per divinam potentiam a papatu iuste privari, etiam si efficiatur haereticus. Alii dicunt, quod quamuis papa non habeat superiorem in terris, quamdiu est papa; si tamen efficiatur haereticus, ipso facto iure divino non humano est papatu privatus, & inferior factus catholicis. DISC. Allega primo pro assertione, in qua diversi conveniunt. sc. quod papa non habeat iudicem superiorem in terris. MAGIST. Hoc auctoritatib. & rationib. nonnulli probare conantur. hoc enim Inno. papa ut habetur. 9. q. 3. c. nemo, sentire videtur. ait enim: nemo iudicabit primam sedem iusticiam temperare desiderantem. neque enim ab Augusto, neque ab omni clero, neq; à Regibus, neq; à populo iudex iudicabitur. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod etiam universalis ecclesia non est papa superior, cui clerus & papa, qui secundum praedicta verba Innoc. papam nequeant iudicare, ecclesiam universalem constituant. Ex quo sequitur, quod etiam concilium generale non est supra papam. Item Simachus papa, ut habetur eisdem causa & quaestione, ca. aliorum hominum Deus causas voluit per homines terminare, licet sedis istius praesulem suo (sine quaestione) seruauit arbitrio. Ex quo habetur, quod solus Deus est superior sedis apostolicae. DISC. Dicerent alii, quod Simachus loquitur de aliis causis, quam de causis haereticis. & ideo non obstantibus verbis eiusdem, papa habet superiorem in causis haeresis. MAGIST. Ista responsio impugnatur; quia sicut ex dictis sanctorum patrum colligitur, ubi canon non excipit, nec nos debemus excipere. cum ergo canon Simachi papae causam haeresis nequaquam excipiat, nec nos causam haeresis debemus excipere. Hoc etiam patet, quia verba indistincte prolata generaliter debet intelligi, ut papa in omni causa divino seruetur arbitrio. Tertia auctoritas ad praedictam assertionem est Antheri papae, qui, ut in praedictis c. & q.c. facta, ait: facta subditorum iudicantur a nobis: nostra vero a Deo iudicantur. papa ergo superiorem iudicem non habet in terris. Quarta auctoritas est Constantini imperatoris, qui, ut legitur. 15. q. 1. c. futura, praesidens sanctae synodo, quae apud Nicenam congregata est, cum querelam quorundam aspiceret contra se deferendam, ait: vos a nemine diudicari potestis, quia Dei solius iudicio seruamini. dii etenim vocati estis: & idcirco non potestis ab hominibus iudicari. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod clerici non possunt a laicis iudicari. & per consequens multo fortius caput clericorum summus pontifex nequaquam potest ab alio iudicari. Quinta auctoritas ad idem est Gelasii papae, & habetur. 9. q. 3. c. ipsi, & loquens de apostolica sede, ait: ipsi sunt sibi canones, qui appellationes totius ecclesiae ad huius sedis examen voluerunt deferre, ab ipsa vero nunquam prorsus appellari debere sanxerunt: ac per hoc illam de tota ecclesia iudicare, ipsam ad nullius commeare iudicium, nec de eius vnquam praeceperunt iudicio iudicare. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod de summo pontifice non licet toti ecclesiae iudicare; sed ipse habet de tota ecclesia iudicare. cum ergo nec persona, nec aliqua congregatio in terris sit superior tota ecclesia; nec papa, qui est supra totam ecclesiam, potest alia congregatio vel persona superior reperiri. Sexta auctoritas est Nicolai papae, qui, ut habetur causa & quaest. praedictu, ca. patet, ait: patet perfecto sedis apostolicae, cuius auctoritate maius non est iudicium a nemine forte retractandum, nec cuiquam de eius iudicio iudicare. Ex quibus habetur, quod nulli licet de summo pontifice iudicare: & per consequens non habet superiorem in terris.
units.tr: STUDENT. I shall try to find the solutions to the aforesaid reasons myself, and so, heretics though they may be, I will stop questioning you and seek only a few points about the punishment of heretics from now on. Moreover, I wanted this work to be done chiefly because of the disagreement between the most holy father, Lord John XXII, and certain people who defame him of heretical depravity. I agree with them on this point, that the Pope can be stained by the blot of heresy, though I regard the said lord as a Catholic man and a faithful one. So in this sixth book I shall take care to investigate chiefly how someone (should he become a heretic) is to be dealt with. Yet since the Pope can be falsely defamed of heresy, I shall first inquire about the Pope falsely defamed of the crime of heresy. Second (namely below, chapter 66), I shall inquire about the Pope truly befouled with the stain of heresy. But first I want to know whether the Pope has a superior judge on earth, so you may give me one or more assertions about this matter, with their grounds. MASTER. Learned men disagree about your question. Some say that the Pope has no superior on earth; others say that although no person on earth is superior to the Pope, the universal Church and a general council are nonetheless above the Pope. Of those who assert that the Pope has no superior on earth, some say that once a man has been canonically raised to the papacy, he can never be justly deprived of it, except by divine power, unless he voluntarily renounces the papacy, even if he becomes a heretic. Others say that although the Pope has no superior on earth as long as he is Pope, yet if he becomes a heretic he is, by that very fact, deprived of the papacy by divine law, not by human law, and is made inferior to Catholics. STUDENT. First, state the assertion on which the various parties agree, namely that the Pope has no superior judge on earth. MASTER. Some try to prove this by authorities and reasons. Pope Innocent seems to hold this view, as is found in 9 q. 3 c. Nemo. For he says: No one shall judge the first see, which desires to temper justice. For it will not be judged by Augustus, nor by all the clergy, nor by kings, nor by the people. From these words it is understood that even the universal Church is not superior to the Pope, since the clergy and the Pope, who according to the words of Innocent cannot judge the Pope, constitute the universal Church. From this it follows that even a general council is not above the Pope. Likewise Pope Symmachus, as found in the same cause and question, c. Aliorum hominum: God willed that the causes of other men be settled by men, although he reserved the prelate of this see to his own judgment, beyond question. From this it is held that God alone is superior to the apostolic see. STUDENT. Others would say that Symmachus is speaking of other causes, not of the causes of heresy, and so, despite his words, the Pope has a superior in cases of heresy. MASTER. That answer is refuted, because, as is gathered from the sayings of the holy fathers, where the canon makes no exception, neither must we make one. Since the canon of Pope Symmachus makes no exception for the cause of heresy, neither must we make an exception for the cause of heresy. This is also clear because words spoken without distinction must be understood generally, so that the Pope is preserved in every cause under divine judgment. The third authority for the said assertion is that of Pope Anterus, who, as in the aforesaid chapter and in the question Facta, says: The deeds of subjects are judged by us; our deeds, however, are judged by God. Therefore the Pope has no superior judge on earth. The fourth authority is that of the Emperor Constantine, who, as we read in 15 q. 1 c. Futura, presiding over the holy synod assembled at Nicaea, when he saw a complaint of certain men brought against himself, said: You can be judged by no one, since you are preserved for the judgment of God alone. For you have been called gods, and therefore you cannot be judged by men. From these words it is gathered that clerics cannot be judged by laymen, and consequently, much more strongly, the head of the clergy, the supreme pontiff, can by no means be judged by another. The fifth authority on the same point is that of Pope Gelasius, found in 9 q. 3 c. Ipsi, who, speaking of the apostolic see, says: The canons themselves have ordained that the appeals of the whole Church should be brought to the examination of this see, but that no appeal should ever be made from it at all. Thus they have decreed that it should judge the whole Church, but should never come under the judgment of anyone, nor ever be ordered to submit to judgment. From these words it is understood that the supreme pontiff may not be judged by the whole Church, but he himself has the right to judge the whole Church. Therefore, since neither a person nor any assembly on earth is superior to the whole Church, and the Pope, who is above the whole Church, cannot be found to have any superior person or assembly. The sixth authority is that of Pope Nicholas, who, as found in the same cause and question, c. Patet, says: It is plain that the judgment of the apostolic see, by whose authority there is no greater judgment, is not to be called in question by anyone, nor is anyone to pass judgment on its judgment. From these words it is held that it is not lawful for anyone to judge the supreme pontiff, and consequently he has no superior on earth.

units.la: DISCIP. Puto, quod qui posset ad istas auctoritates rationabiliter respondere, omnes alias eandem rationem praetendentes seu sententiam sine difficultate dissolueret. Ideo istae sufficiant. Signes tamen, ubi poterunt aliae inveniri, quae sonare videntur, quod papa non habet iudicem in terris superiorem.
units.tr: STUDENT. I think that whoever could answer these authorities reasonably would dissolve without difficulty all the others that put forward the same reasoning or opinion. So let these suffice. Nevertheless, point out where other passages can be found that seem to sound as if the Pope has no superior judge on earth.

units.la: MAGIST. Ad hoc poterit allegari auctoritas Nicolai papae, di. 21. nunc autem, & di. 23. contradictionem, & 2. q. 7. Petrus. DISCIP. Pro eadem assertione rationes adducas. MAGIST. Prima ratio talis est: a quo non licet appellare, non habet superiorem in terris: quia ab omni inferiore ad superiorem licitum est appellare. 2. q. 5. placuit. Sed a papa appellare non licet. 9. q. 3. cap. ipsi & c. cuncta. Ergo papa non habet superiorem in terris. Secunda ratio talis est: Ille, qui est omnibus superior, non habet superiorem: quia non potest respectu eiusdem vel eorundem esse superior & inferior. Sed papa est omnibus catholicis superior, cum sit omnium caput. Ergo non habet iudicem superiorem. Tertia ratio est haec: Qui non potest ab aliquo accusari, non habet iudicem superiorem. Sed papa non potest ab aliquo accusari: quia pastor ab omnibus accusari non potest. 6. q. 1. ouis. & 2. q. 7. Petrus. Omnes autem catholici sunt oves curae & regimini papae commissae. Ipsum igitur accusare non possunt, & per consequens a nemine potest iudicari.
units.tr: MASTER. For this, the authority of Pope Nicholas may be cited, in d. 21 Nunc autem, and d. 23 Contradictionem, and 2 q. 7 Petrus. STUDENT. Bring forward reasons for the same assertion. MASTER. The first reason is this: from whom it is not lawful to appeal, he has no superior on earth, because it is lawful to appeal from every inferior to a superior (2 q. 5 Placuit). But it is not lawful to appeal from the Pope (9 q. 3 c. Ipsi and c. Cuncta). Therefore the Pope has no superior on earth. The second reason is this: he who is superior to all has no superior, because he cannot be both superior and inferior with respect to the same person or persons. But the Pope is superior to all Catholics, since he is the head of all. Therefore he has no superior judge. The third reason is this: he who cannot be accused by anyone has no superior judge. But the Pope cannot be accused by anyone, because a shepherd cannot be accused by all (6 q. 1 Ouis, and 2 q. 7 Petrus). Yet all Catholics are sheep committed to the care and rule of the Pope. Therefore they cannot accuse him, and consequently he cannot be judged by anyone.

units.la: CAP. II.
units.tr: Chapter II.

units.la: Ubi ponitur opinio contraria, scil. quod papa habeat iudicem etiam ordinarium in terris: & circa hoc sunt duo modi ponendi. & primus modus probatur unica ratione, cuius maior probatur capitulo 3. sc. quod papa nullam habeat iurisdictionem coactivam. Secunda ratio ad probandum idem notatur capitulo 4. tertia & quarta ponuntur capitulo 5, etiam ibidem probatur exemplo Ioh. 12.
units.tr: Here the contrary opinion is set out, namely that the pope has a judge on earth, even an ordinary one, and there are two ways of putting this. The first way is proved by a single argument, whose major premise is proved in chapter 3, namely that the pope has no coercive jurisdiction. A second argument for the same point is given in chapter 4. A third and fourth are set out in chapter 5, and there is also proof from the example of John 12.

units.la: DISCIP. Nolim multiplicare rationes pro hac parte: sed motivum dicentium, quod papa superiorem habet in terris, enarra. MAGIST. Quod papa etiam manens papa habeat iudicem superiorem in terris, nonnulli etiam multis rationibus probare nituntur. Modi tamen ponendi sunt diversi. Quidam enim dicunt, quod imperator, vel aliquis alius iudex & princeps secularis, aut populus seu multitudo aliqua, est iudex ordinarius papae. Alii vero dicunt, quod nec ecclesia universalis, nec aliqua alia congregatio aut persona habeat potestatem requirendi vel coercendi papam, nisi in duobus casibus. Primus est, si papa fuerit de haeresi graviter infamatus, licet falso. Secundus est, si in aliquo crimine, de quo scandalizetur ecclesia, sit notorie deprehensus, & ipse se incorrigibilem ostendat. DISCIP. Prosequere primo primam opinionem, & quamvis putem eam haereticam, qualiter tamen assertores ipsius eam fundare conantur, & quomodo ad rationes & auctoritates in contrarium respondere nitantur, gratia exercitii, ut acutius veritatem intelligam, scire desidero. MAGIST. Pro praedicta opinione vel assertione potest primo sic argui. Ille, qui nullam habet iurisdictionem coactivam, imperatori, aut regi, vel alii principi, aut populo est subiectus, quia qui nulli alteri est praepositus, alicui est subiectus. Aliter autem nullum ordinem ad alios homines nec superioritatis nec inferioritatis haberet. Ubi autem non est ordo, ibi est confusio. Confusio autem inter homines inveniri non debet. Qui autem quantum ad iurisdictionem coactivam, nulli est praepositus, quantum ad iurisdictionem coactivam alicui est subiectus. Sed papa ex ordinatione Christi super alios nullam habet iurisdictionem coactivam. Ergo quantum ad iurisdictionem coactivam alicui est subiectus: & non nisi imperatori, aut regi, vel principi. Ergo alicui praedictorum est papa subiectus; & ita aliquis praedictorum est iudex ordinarius papae.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. I would not multiply arguments for this side, but explain the reasoning of those who say that the pope has a superior on earth. TEACHER. That even while he remains pope, the pope has a superior judge on earth, some people try to prove by many arguments. Yet the ways of putting it differ. Some say that the emperor, or some other judge and secular prince, or the people or some multitude, is the pope's ordinary judge. Others say that neither the universal Church nor any other assembly or person has the power to call the pope to account or restrain him, except in two cases. The first is if the pope has been gravely accused of heresy, even falsely. The second is if he is openly caught in some crime that scandalises the Church, and he shows himself incorrigible. DISCIPLE. Go on first with the first opinion. Although I think it heretical, I wish to learn, for the sake of practice, how its advocates try to ground it, and how they try to answer the arguments and authorities against it, so that I may understand the truth more keenly. TEACHER. In support of this opinion or assertion one may first argue as follows. He who has no coercive jurisdiction is subject to the emperor, or the king, or another prince, or the people, for he who is set over no one is subject to someone. Otherwise he would have no order of superiority or inferiority in relation to other men. Where there is no order, there is confusion, and confusion should not be found among men. Now the one who, as far as coercive jurisdiction goes, is set over no one, is subject to someone as far as coercive jurisdiction goes. But the pope, by Christ's ordinance, has no coercive jurisdiction over others. Therefore, as far as coercive jurisdiction goes, he is subject to someone, and to none but the emperor, the king or a prince. Therefore the pope is subject to one of these, and so one of these is the pope's ordinary judge.

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: Chapter III.

units.la: In quo probatur minor assumpta in ratione pro opinione prima ca. praecedentis, scil. quod papa super alios non habet iurisdictionem coactivam. & hoc rationibus & auctoritatibus. & est valde notandum.
units.tr: In which the minor premise assumed in the argument for the first opinion of the preceding chapter is proved, namely that the pope has no coercive jurisdiction over others. This is proved by arguments and authorities, and it is very much to be noted.

units.la: DISC. Quamvis asserere, quod papa super alios non habet iurisdictionem coactivam, sit haereticum reputandum (ut arbitror) dicit in quomodo praedicti assertores hoc probare nituntur. MAG. Hoc auctoritate scripturae divinae & sanctorum moliuntur ostendere. Primo auctoritate Christi dicentis apostolis
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Although to assert that the pope has no coercive jurisdiction over others must, I think, be reckoned heretical, tell me how those who put this forward try to prove it. TEACHER. They strive to show it by the authority of divine Scripture and of the saints. First, by the authority of Christ speaking to the apostles:

units.la: Matth. 20. Scitis quia principes gentium dominantur eorum: & qui maiores sunt potestatis exercent in eos: non ita erit inter vos; sed quicunque inter vos voluerit maior esse, sit minister vester. & quicunque voluerit inter vos primus esse, erit vester seruus. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod maioritas & primitas illius, qui est maior & primus inter omnes discipulos Christi (cuiusmodi sunt omnes Christiani) in ministrando & seruiendo consistit. & per consequens iurisdictionem coactiuam super alios nullatenus habet. DISCIP. Ministerium & seruitium Papae consistit in regendo & gubernando gregem sibi commissum: quod nequaquam facere posset, nisi iurisdictionem coactiuam haberet. Nec obuiat, quia Papa debet esse minister & seruus seruorum Dei, nam etiam iudex temporalis puniendo malefactores minister est, iuxta sententiam apostoli ad Rom. 13. MAGIST. Secundum hanc responsionem debent Christum excludere, cum sic ministerium & seruitium imponit maiori. & ideo suis discipulis exercendi potestatem in alios interdixit dicens: qui maiores sunt, potestatem exercent in illos: non ita erit inter vos &c. Ex quibus colligitur, quod Christus ministro & seruo aliorum Christianorum potestatem exercendi in alios interdicit. & ita ab eo iurisdictionem coactiuam excludit: quia inutilis & superflua est iurisdictio coactiua, quae non debet potestatem in maleficos exercere. Cum vero dicis, quod iudex temporalis est minister secundum apostolum: Respondetur, quod male allegas apostolum; quia non dicit apostolus, quod est minister subditorum: sed dicit, quod est minister Dei. Christus enim voluit, quod inter Christianos esset minister non solum Dei, sed etiam aliorum. DISCIP. Probant ne aliter, quod Papa non habet iurisdictionem coactiuam super alios. MAGIST. Hoc etiam probant sic. Papa non habet iurisdictionem coactiuam maiorem, quam habuerit Christus, cuius est Vicarius. sed Christus non habuit inquantum homo mortalis iurisdictionem coactiuam.
units.tr: Matth. 20. You know that the princes of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those who are greater exercise power over them. It shall not be so among you; but whoever wishes to be greater among you, let him be your minister; and whoever wishes to be first among you, let him be your servant. From these words it is made clear that the greatness and primacy of the one who is greatest and first among all Christ's disciples (and all Christians are such) consists in ministering and serving, and consequently he has no coercive jurisdiction over others at all. DISCIPLE. The ministry and service of the pope consists in ruling and governing the flock committed to him, which he could by no means do unless he had coercive jurisdiction. Nor does it stand in the way that the pope ought to be the minister and servant of the servants of God, for even a temporal judge, in punishing evildoers, is a minister, according to the saying of the apostle Rom. 13. TEACHER. By this reply they must exclude Christ himself, since service and ministry are thus laid upon the greater. And so he forbade his disciples to exercise power over others, saying: Those who are greater exercise power over them; it shall not be so among you, etc. From this it is gathered that Christ forbids a minister and servant of other Christians to exercise power over others, and so he excludes coercive jurisdiction from him, since coercive jurisdiction, which ought not to exercise power over wrongdoers, is useless and superfluous. As for your saying that a temporal judge is a minister according to the apostle, the answer is that you wrongly cite the apostle, for the apostle does not call him a minister of the subjects but a minister of God. For Christ willed that among Christians there should be a minister not only of God but also of others. DISCIPLE. Do they prove in some other way that the pope has no coercive jurisdiction over others? TEACHER. They prove this also as follows. The pope does not have greater coercive jurisdiction than Christ had, whose vicar he is. But Christ, as a mortal man, did not have coercive jurisdiction.

units.la: Tum quia iurisdictio coactiua sine diuitiis vel adiutorio habentium diuitias conuenienter exerceri non potest. & per consequens inutiliter retineretur. Christus autem omnes diuitias necessarias ad iurisdictionem coactiuam exercendam, quo ad Deum, penitus abdicauit victu & vestitu contentus. Adiutorio etiam diuitum ad eandem iurisdictionem exercendam minime vtebatur. ergo iurisdictionem coactiuam inquantum homo mortalis non habuit: Tum quia ipso testante, ministrare venit non ministrari, ergo non venit iurisdictionem coactiuam exercere. ergo eam non habuit. Tum quia Christus opus, quod sibi pater imposuit, consummauit, ipso testante, qui ait Iohann. 17. consummaui opus, quod dedisti mihi vt facerem. Christus autem iurisdictionem coactiuam nequaquam exercuit. ergo iurisdictionem coactiuam a patre non accepit inquantum erat homo mortalis: quia si eam accepisset, & nequaquam exercuisset, de malitia vel negligentia fuisset merito arguendus: quia officium sine opere renuisset.
units.tr: Again, because coercive jurisdiction cannot be conveniently exercised without the riches or the help of those who have riches; and so it would be kept to no purpose. But Christ, as far as God is concerned, entirely renounced all the riches necessary for exercising coercive jurisdiction, being content with food and clothing. Nor did he make use at all of the help of the rich for exercising the same jurisdiction. Therefore he did not have coercive jurisdiction as a mortal man. Again, because, as he himself testifies, he came to minister, not to be ministered to; therefore he did not come to exercise coercive jurisdiction, and so he did not have it. Again, because Christ completed the work which the Father had laid upon him, as he himself testifies, who says in John 17: I have finished the work which you gave me to do. But Christ never exercised coercive jurisdiction. Therefore he did not receive coercive jurisdiction from the Father as a mortal man, for if he had received it and never exercised it, he would rightly be charged with malice or negligence, since he would have refused the office by not performing the work.

units.la: DISCIP. Hic errant aperte; quia euangelica testatur historia, quod Christus iurisdictionem exercuit coactiuam, cum Christus de templo vendentes & ementes violenter eiecit, vt legitur Matth. 21. Mar. 11. Lu. 19. & Iohann. 2. MAGIST. Ipsi asserunt te hic errare propter duo. Primo, quia eiicere vendentes de templo & alia facere, quae tunc Christus exercuit, ad iurisdictionem coactiuam non pertinent: nec tunc Christus officium praelati vel summi sacerdotis exercuit, sed officiu hostiariorum tunc assumpsit, teste Magistro sententiarum, qui, vt habetur li. 4. di. 3. ait: hoc officium (scilicet hostiariorum) Deus in sua persona suscepit, quando flagello de funiculis facto vendentes & ementes de templo eiecit. ipse enim se hostiarium significans dicit: Ego sum hostium: per me si quis introierit &c. Praedictum ergo officium, quod Christus tunc exercuit, ad hostiarios spectat. hostiarii autem ex officio suo nullam iurisdictionem coactiuam noscuntur habere. ergo per illud exemplum probare non potest, quod Christus iurisdictionem habuit coactiuam. Secundo dicunt te errare: quia Christus inquantum summus sacerdos, si habuerit iurisdictionem, non habuit eam nisi respectu fidelium & in eum credentium. quia ad eum de his quae foris erat, inquantum summus sacerdos, non pertinebat iudicare. Christus autem eiecit tunc infideles de templo. ergo hoc non fecit inquantum sacerdos, sed inquantum hostiarius; cuius est absque iurisdictione non solum malos fideles, sed etiam infideles de templo eiicere. Ex his verbis concludunt, quod Christus inquantum sacerdos nunquam iurisdictionem coactiuam exercuit. ergo non habuit.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Here they are clearly in error, for the gospel history testifies that Christ did exercise coercive jurisdiction when he violently drove out of the temple those who sold and bought, as is read in Matth. 21. Mar. 11. Lu. 19. & Iohann. 2. TEACHER. They maintain that you are wrong here for two reasons. First, because driving the sellers out of the temple, and the other things Christ then did, do not belong to coercive jurisdiction; nor did Christ then exercise the office of a prelate or high priest, but took up the office of a doorkeeper, as the Master of the Sentences testifies, who, as is found in book 4, distinction 3, says: God took up this office (namely that of doorkeeper) in his own person when he drove out of the temple, with a scourge made of cords, those who sold and bought. For he himself, signifying that he is the doorkeeper, says: I am the door; by me if anyone enters, etc. The office which Christ then exercised therefore belongs to doorkeepers, and doorkeepers, by their office, are known to have no coercive jurisdiction. Therefore that example cannot prove that Christ had coercive jurisdiction. Secondly, they say you are wrong, because Christ, as high priest, if he had jurisdiction, had it only with respect to the faithful and those who believe in him, since it did not belong to him as high priest to judge those outside. But Christ then drove the unbelievers out of the temple. Therefore he did not do this as priest but as doorkeeper, whose office is to drive out of the temple, without any jurisdiction, not only wicked believers but also unbelievers. From these words they conclude that Christ, as priest, never exercised coercive jurisdiction, and therefore did not have it.

units.la: DISCIP. Licet Christus habuit iurisdictionem coactiuam, eam tamen nequaquam exercuit, quia inter suos discipulos non erant malefici, inter quos debuerit iurisdictionem coactiuam exercere. nec tamen propter hoc caruit iurisdictione tali, sicut si rex non haberet subditos, nisi bonos, propter hoc non careret iurisdictione. MAGIST. Istud excludunt per hoc, quod nonnulli discipuli Christi graviter deliquerunt apostatantes a fide, quam susceperant. Iohann. enim 6. sic legitur: Multi discipulorum eius abierunt retro. non enim propter defectum materiae, sed propter iurisdictionis coactiuae carentiam Christus in delinquentes potestatem aut vindictam nequaquam exercuit. Ex his verbis concludunt, quod Christus inquantum summus pontifex, iurisdictionem non habuit coactiuam. ergo nec Papa iurisdictionem obtinet coactiuam. Quod etiam auctoritatibus probare niituntur. Origenes enim super illud Matt. 20. Reges gentium dominantur eorum &c. ait: Scitis quia principes gentium dominantur eorum, & non contenti tantum regere suos subditos, violenter eis dominari niituntur. inter vos autem, qui est maior, non etiam hoc corporalia, quomodo sicut omnia corporalia in necessitate sunt posita, spiritualia autem in voluntate: sic & qui principes sunt spirituales & praelati, principatus eorum in dilectione debet esse penitus, non in timore. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod totus praelatorum principatus ecclesiae, & per consequens summi pontificis in voluntate & dilectione, non in timore, debet consistere. ergo diligi debent, non timeri. qui autem iurisdictione coactiua vtuntur, à malis timentur; teste apostolo ad Rom. 13. qui ait sic: si autem malefeceris, time: scilicet potestatem: ergo prælati iurisdictione coactiva uti non debent. Hoc etiam Chrysostom. ibidem sententiam videtur. ait enim: principes mundi non sunt, ut dominentur minoribus suis, & eos seruituti subiiciant & expoliant, & usque ad mortem eis vtantur ad suam voluntatem & gloriam. principes autem ecclesiae sunt, ut minoribus seruiant & ministrent en quæcunque acceperint à Christo, ut suas utilitates negligant, & illorum procurent. Ex quibus verbis patet distinctio inter principes seculares & principes ecclesiarum, quia principes seculares suis subditis dominantur: principes autem ecclesiae minoribus seruiunt & ministrant. ergo in eos iurisdictionem coactiuam exercere non valent. His etiam Ambrof. correspondet, qui vt recitatur 23. q. 8. c. conuenior, ait: dolere potero, flere potero, gemere potero: aduersus arma, milites Gothosque, lachryma mea arma mea sunt. talia enim instrumenta sunt sacerdotis. aliter autem nec debent nec possunt resistere. Ex quibus verbis videtur, quod sacerdos orationibus & lachrymis debet malis resistere, & non per potentiam temporalem. & per consequens non habet iurisdictionem coactiuam. Quod etiam Chrysostom. in li. suo Dialogorum, qui de dignitate sacerdotali int. titulatur, li. 2. c. 3. super illud Apocal. 2. & ad Corinth. 1. non dominantur fidei nostra, apertissime sentire videtur. Ait enim: hi, qui foris sunt, iudices malignes quosque cum subditerint, ostendunt in eis plurimam potestatem in eos inuites à priorum nostrorum prauitate compescunt. in ecclesia vero non coactum, sed acquiescentem oportet ad meliora conuerti: quia nec nobis à legibus data est talis potestas, ut auctoritate sententiae cohibeamus homines à delictu. clarius dici non posset, quod ecclesia non habet iurisdictionem coactiuam, cum in ecclesia nullus debeat ad meliora cogi, nec aliquis debeat cohiberi per iudicialem sententiam à delictis. Item, ad habentem iurisdictionem coactiuam spectat negociis secularibus implicari, quia ad ipsum spectat contentiones & lites dirimere. contentiones autem, lites & rixæ inter negocia seculària computantur; ext. nec clerici vel monachi se negociis secularibus se immiscentes. c. 1. Sed ad summum pontificem non pertinet secularibus negociis implicari, teste apostolo, 2. ad Timoth. 2. qui ait: nemo militans Deo implicat se negociis secularibus. ergo ad summum pontificem ex ordinatione non pertinet iurisdictio coactiua. Item, papa non habet maiorem iurisdictionem ex ordinatione Christi, quam habuit beatus Petrus & alii apostoli. Sed beatus Petrus & alii apostoli iurisdictionem coactiuam à Christo minime acceperunt. ergo nec papa habet iurisdictionem coactiuam ex ordinatione Christi. Maior est manifesta. Minor probatur auctoritate beati Bernardi, qui li. ad Eugenium papam ait: non monstrabunt, puto, qui hic dicerent, vbi aliquando quispiam apostolorum iudex sederit hominum. & parum post: sterilisse denique lege apostolos iudicandos, sedisse iudicantes non legő, & illud non fuit. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod apostoli iudices hominum non fuerunt. quod G eg. sentire videtur. tractans enim illa verba apostoli: secularia igitur iudicia si habueritis &c. in Moralibus ait: hi terrenas causas, qui exteriorum rerum sapientiam perceperunt. qui autem spiritualibus dotati sunt, terrenis non debent negociis implicari, ut dum non cogunter inferiora bona disponere, valeant bonis superioribus deseruire. Cum ergo apostoli maximis bonis fuerunt dotati, ipsi non erant circa causas hominum & lites aliqualiter occupati. quod Gl. s. super illud 1. Corinth. 6. secularia ergo iudicia si habueritis &c. aperte sentire videtur. ait enim: Contemptos vel contemptibiles. (i.e. aliquos sapientes, qui tamen sunt minoris meriti) constituite ad iudicandum. apostoli enim circumeuntes talibus non vacabant. sapientes igitur, qui in locis consistebant fideles & sancti, non qui huc atque illuc propter consilium discurrebant, tanquam negociorum examinatores esse volunt. his verbis ostenditur, quod apostoli causas hominem terminandis minime insistebant. Ex quo infertur, quod non acceperant iurisdictionem coactiuam à Christo, quia omne officium iniunctum eis à Christo diligentissime perfecerunt. DISCIP. In scriptura diuina habetur aperte, quod beatus Petrus iurisdictionem habuit coactiuam, cum ex potestate officii Ananiam & Saphyram morti tradiderit, teste beato Gregorio in Dialogo, qui, vt recitatur 21. q. 8. c. Petrus, ait: Petrus qui Tabitam mortuam orando suscitauit, Ananiam & Saphiram mentientes morti increpando tradidit. neque enim orasse in eorum extinctione legitur, sed solummodo culpam, quam perpetrauerant, increpasse. onstat ergo quod aliquando talia ex potestate exhibebantur; aliquando ex postulatione, dum & ipsa vitam increpando abstulit, & illi reddidit orando. Ex quibus verbis habetur, quod beatus Petrus ex potestate visus est nisi coactiua. MAGIS F. Ad hoc respondent, quod verba Greg. male intelligis. non enim asserit Greg. quod beatus Petrus ex potestate officii sui prædictos Ananiam & Saphiram morti tradiderit. tunc enim iudex in causa sanguinis extitisset, quod vniuersis clericis noscitur interdictum. sed beatus Petrus non ex potestate officii, sed ex potestate faciendi miracula (quam Deus personæ non officio papatus concesserat) morti tradidit supradictos. nonnunquam autem facit absque oratione miracula: & ita ex hoc probari non potest, quod Petrus iurisdictionem habuit coactiuam.
units.tr: STUDENT. Christ did have coercive jurisdiction, but He never exercised it, because among His disciples there were no wrongdoers over whom He ought to have exercised it. Nor did He lack such jurisdiction for that reason, any more than a king who had only good subjects would for that reason lack jurisdiction. MASTER. Your opponents refute this by pointing out that some of Christ's disciples sinned gravely by falling away from the faith they had embraced. John 6 reads: Many of his disciples went back. So Christ did not exercise power or vengeance against these offenders because of any lack of material, but because He lacked coercive jurisdiction. From these words they conclude that Christ, as high priest, had no coercive jurisdiction, and therefore the Pope does not possess coercive jurisdiction either. They also try to prove this by authorities. Origen, commenting on Matthew 20, The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, etc., says: You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over their subjects, and not content merely to rule their subjects, they strive to dominate them by force. But among you, whoever is greater, let him be ... Bodily things are subject to necessity, but spiritual things to the will; so also those who are spiritual rulers and prelates, their rule ought to rest entirely on love, not on fear. From these words it is to be understood that the whole rule of the prelates of the Church, and consequently of the high priest, must consist in will and love, not in fear. Therefore they ought to be loved, not feared. But those who use coercive jurisdiction are feared by the wicked, as the Apostle witnesses in Romans 13, who says: But if you do evil, fear, namely the power. Therefore prelates ought not to use coercive jurisdiction. Chrysostom also seems to hold this opinion in the same place. For he says: The rulers of the world are not there to lord it over their inferiors, to subject them to slavery and plunder them, and to use them until death for their own will and glory. But the rulers of the Church are there to serve and minister to their inferiors with whatever they have received from Christ, neglecting their own advantages and seeking theirs. From these words the distinction between secular rulers and rulers of the churches is plain: secular rulers dominate their subjects, but the rulers of the Church serve and minister to their inferiors. Therefore they cannot exercise coercive jurisdiction over them. Ambrose agrees with this, who, as is quoted in 23 q. 8 c. Convenior, says: I can grieve, I can weep, I can groan; against arms, soldiers and Goths, my tears are my arms. For such are the instruments of a priest. Otherwise they ought not and cannot resist. From these words it appears that a priest ought to resist evil by prayers and tears, and not by temporal power, and consequently does not have coercive jurisdiction. Chrysostom also seems most plainly to hold this in his book of Dialogues on the priestly dignity, which is entitled On the Priesthood, book 2, chapter 3, on the words of Revelation 2 and 1 Corinthians: Not lording it over your faith. For he says: Those outside, when they subject wicked judges, show that they have much power over them, and restrain them against their will from the wickedness of our predecessors. But in the Church one must not be compelled, but must be turned to better things by consent. For such power has not been given to us by laws, that by the authority of a sentence we should restrain men from sin. It could not be said more clearly that the Church does not have coercive jurisdiction, since in the Church no one ought to be compelled to better things, nor should anyone be restrained from offences by a judicial sentence. Again, it belongs to one who has coercive jurisdiction to be involved in secular business, because it is his task to settle disputes and lawsuits. But disputes, lawsuits and quarrels are counted among secular business; see the decretal Nec clerici vel monachi se negotiis secularibus immiscentes, c. 1. But it does not pertain to the high priest to be involved in secular business, as the Apostle witnesses in 2 Timothy 2, who says: No one serving God entangles himself in secular business. Therefore by ordinance the high priest does not have coercive jurisdiction. Again, the Pope does not have greater jurisdiction by the ordinance of Christ than blessed Peter and the other apostles had. But blessed Peter and the other apostles did not at all receive coercive jurisdiction from Christ. Therefore the Pope does not have coercive jurisdiction by the ordinance of Christ either. The major premise is evident. The minor is proved by the authority of blessed Bernard, who in his book to Pope Eugene says: I think those who say here will not point out where any of the apostles ever sat as a judge of men. And a little later: Finally, I do not read that the apostles were ever taught by law to judge, nor that they sat as judges, and that was not so. From these words it is to be understood that the apostles were not judges of men. Gregory seems to hold this too, for in treating the words of the Apostle, If then you have secular judgments, etc., in his Moralia he says: Those who have grasped the wisdom of external things judge earthly causes. But those who are endowed with spiritual gifts ought not to be entangled in earthly business, so that, not being compelled to manage lower goods, they may be free to serve higher ones. Since the apostles, therefore, were endowed with the greatest gifts, they were not themselves occupied in any way with men's causes and lawsuits. Gloss also seems plainly to hold this on 1 Corinthians 6, If then you have secular judgments, etc. For it says: Appoint to judge those who are despised or contemptible (that is, some wise men who nevertheless are of lesser merit). For the apostles, travelling about, did not have time for such things. Therefore the wise men who remained in the places, faithful and holy, not those who ran here and there for counsel, are the ones they wish to be examiners of business. By these words it is shown that the apostles did not at all devote themselves to deciding men's causes. From this it follows that they did not receive coercive jurisdiction from Christ, since they most diligently carried out every office enjoined on them by Christ. STUDENT. In divine Scripture it is plainly stated that blessed Peter had coercive jurisdiction, since by the power of his office he handed Ananias and Sapphira over to death. This is attested by blessed Gregory in the Dialogues, who, as is quoted in 21 q. 8 c. Petrus, says: Peter, who raised the dead Tabitha by prayer, handed Ananias and Sapphira over to death by rebuking them for lying. For it is not read that he prayed for their death, but only that he rebuked the sin they had committed. It is clear, therefore, that sometimes such things were done by power, and sometimes by request, since he took away their life by rebuke and restored it to them by prayer. From these words it is held that blessed Peter seemed to act by a power that was coercive. MASTER. To this they reply that you misunderstand the words of Gregory. For Gregory does not assert that blessed Peter handed those named, Ananias and Sapphira, over to death by the power of his office. For then he would have been a judge in a case of blood, which is known to be forbidden to all clerics. But blessed Peter handed them over to death not by the power of his office, but by the power of working miracles, which God had granted to the person of Peter, not to the papal office. Miracles are sometimes worked without prayer; and so it cannot be proved from this that Peter had coercive jurisdiction.

units.la: CAP. IV.
units.tr: CAP. IV.

units.la: In quo ponitur secunda ratio principalis ad probandum dictum prima opinionis recitata, a. scilicet quod Papa habeat superiorem in terris, & hoc specialiter, quod huiusmodi sit aliquis secularis.
units.tr: In which the second principal argument is set out to prove the aforesaid first opinion, namely that the Pope has a superior on earth, and specifically that this superior is some secular ruler.

units.la: DISCIP. Circa hanc rationem primam te nimium dilatasti: ideo complea alias rationes, nam de potestate Papae in mtractatu secundo de doctrina domini Papae magis diffuse tractabimus.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. You have spent too long on this first argument. So go on to the other arguments, since we will treat the power of the Pope more fully in the second treatise, on the doctrine of the lord Pope.

units.la: MAG. Secunda ratio ad probandum, quod imperator vel princeps alius secularis, aut populus sit ordinarius iudex Papae, talis est. Papa non est magis exemptus a iurisdictione imperatoris, quam fuit Christus. sed Christus, in quantum homo mortalis, subiectus fuit iurisdictioni imperatoris: ergo & Papa modo modo simili. & per consequens imperator est iudex ordinarius domini Papae. Maior istius rationis probatione videtur nullatenus indigere, quia vicarius non est maior illo, cuius est vicarius; sicut nec servus maior est domino; nec discipulus maior est magistro. Minor probatur auctoritate Christi dicentis ad Pilatum Ioan. 19. non haberes adversum me potestatem ullam, nisi tibi datum esset desuper: propterea qui tradidit me tibi, maius peccatum habet. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod Pilatus iurisdictionem habuit coactivam super Christum: quia de potestate coactiva intelliguntur verba Christi, cum ad verba Pilati dicentis: mihi non loqueris? nescis quia potestatem habeo dimittere te? respondit. constat autem quod Pilatus loquebatur de potestate coactiva. ergo Christus locutus est de eadem.
units.tr: MASTER. The second argument to prove that the emperor, or some other secular prince, or the people, is the ordinary judge of the Pope runs as follows. The Pope is no more exempt from the jurisdiction of the emperor than Christ was. But Christ, insofar as he was a mortal man, was subject to the jurisdiction of the emperor. Therefore the Pope too, in a similar way, is subject to it, and consequently the emperor is the ordinary judge of the lord Pope. The major premise of this argument seems to need no proof at all, since a vicar is not greater than the one whose vicar he is, just as a servant is not greater than his lord, nor a disciple greater than his teacher. The minor premise is proved by the authority of Christ speaking to Pilate: "You would have no power at all against me, unless it were given you from above; therefore he who delivered me to you has the greater sin" (John 19). From these words it is gathered that Pilate had coercive jurisdiction over Christ, because Christ's words refer to coercive power, since they answer Pilate's words, "Do you not speak to me? Do you not know that I have power to release you?" It is certain that Pilate was speaking of coercive power. Therefore Christ too spoke of the same power.

units.la: DISCIP. Duplex est potestas coercendi, scilicet ordinata & usurpata. Christus autem concessit Pilatum habuisse potestatem usurpatam, quam Pilatus forte credidit ordinatam; sed in hoc erravit. MAG. Istam responsionem niuntur excludere: Primo auctoritate B. Augustini, qui super verba praedicta ait: dicamus ergo quod dixit, quod & apostolus docuit quia non est potestas nisi a Deo & quia plus peccat qui innocentem ad occidendum potestatem tradit, iudice quam potestas ipsa, si eum timore alterius potestatis maioris occidit. talem quippe Deus dederat illi potestatem, ut esset ipse etiam sub Caesaris potestate. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod sub tali potestate Caesaris & Pilati erat Christus in quantum homo mortalis, de quali potestate loquitur apostolus ad Rom. 13. cum dixit: non est potestas nisi a Deo. Sed apostolus non loquitur de potestate usurpata, sed ordinata, cum dicat aperte: qui potestati resistit, Dei ordinationi resistit, quae verba de potestate ordinata, non usurpata, debent intelligi. nam qui potestati usurpatae resistit, nequaquam Dei ordinationi resistit: quia tunc secundum apostolum sibi damnationem acquireret, quod est erroneum.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. There are two kinds of power to coerce, namely ordained and usurped. Christ, however, granted that Pilate had a usurped power, which Pilate perhaps believed to be ordained, but in this he was mistaken. MASTER. They try to rule out this answer. First, by the authority of St Augustine, who, on the words cited above, says: "Let us say, then, what he said, which the Apostle also taught: that there is no power except from God, and that he sins more who hands an innocent man over to be killed, the judge, than the power itself does, if he kills him out of fear of another, greater power. For God had given that power to him, so that he himself should also be under the power of Caesar." From these words it is gathered that Christ, insofar as he was a mortal man, was under such a power of Caesar and of Pilate, the kind of power of which the Apostle speaks in Romans 13 when he says: "There is no power except from God." But the Apostle is not speaking of usurped power but of ordained power, since he plainly says: "He who resists the power resists the ordinance of God." These words must be understood of ordained power, not usurped. For he who resists usurped power does not by any means resist the ordinance of God, since then, according to the Apostle, he would bring damnation upon himself, which is false.

units.la: tunc enim nec invasori Papatus nec alicui tyranno liceret resistere. loquitur ergo apostolus de potestate ordinata, non usurpata. Ergo Christus de potestate sic locutus est. Et ita concessit, quod Pilatus super ipsum potestatem habuerit ordinatam. Insinuat tamen, quod ista potestate ordinata abutebatur, cum dicit: qui tradidit me tibi, maius peccatum habet, quasi diceret: tu habes peccatum sufficiens dando in me non confessum, neque legitime convictum de crimine digno morte, quia tamen ex timore hoc facis, & alii me tibi ex malitia & invidia tradiderunt: ideo illi maius peccatum habent. & ita Pilatus potestatem ordinariam super Christum, in quantum erat mortalis, habuit. Quod Theophilus super illud Ioh. 8. A temetipso hoc dicis, an alii dixerunt tibi de me, sentire videtur, dicens: ac si diceret Christus: scilicet si hoc ex teipso loqueris, pande signa rebellionis mea, aut si ab aliis percepisti, inquisitionem fac ordinariam. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod Pilatus habuit potestatem ordinariam inquirendo de criminibus Christo impositis; qui autem potestatem habet inquirendi ordinarie de aliquo infamato, habet iurisdictionem coactivam super eundem. ergo Pilatus habuit super Christum iurisdictionem coactivam. Item Bernardus ad episcopum & archiepiscopum Senonensem ait: cum autem, inquit, Romani praesidis potestatem Christus super se quoque fateatur celitus ordinatam, &c. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod potestas Pilati non fuit usurpata, sed caelitus ordinata; & ideo super Christum iurisdictionem coactivam habuit, quam tamen in Christum exercere minime potuisset iuste, nisi Christus coram eo legitime (quantum iudici constare potest) fuisset convictus de crimine.
