Ista assertio videtur contradictionem concludere. vna enim pars alteri apparet repugnare. si enim nulla persona super Papam de haeresi diffamatum habet iurisdictionem, nulla persona valebit iure de ipso inquirere, quia non ad inferiorem, nec ad parem, sed ad superiorem iurisdictionem habentem officium inquisitionis spectare dinoscitur. MAG. Ad illam obiectionem respondetur: quia inquisitio ad superiorem spectat, ita et citatio pertinet ad superiorem, non enim par vel inferior potest regulariter suum superiorem citare, sed citare est iurisdictionem habentis. Et tamen, hoc non obstante, potest in casu quis iurisdictionem minime habens super alium, citare eum. Si autem dubitatur probabiliter, an iudex haberet iurisdictionem super aliquem, tamen ipsum debet & potest citare, & citatus ire tenetur & ostendere, quod citatio non tenet. Quod si non fecerit, poterit ipsum excommunicare. & propter contumaciam iudex, qui nullam habet iurisdictionem super ipsum, iurisdictionem super eum haberet, quantum ad hoc, quod ipsum potest excommunicationis sententia innodare; extra de appel. duobus. Sic dicitur de inquisitione, dicendum, quod licet inquirere regulariter ad superiorem pertineat, si tamen probabiliter dubitatur de aliquo, qui non potest recurrere ad superiorem, an habeat super alium iurisdictionem & potestatem inquirendi, & non aliter, nisi inquirendo (an scilicet super alium habeat iurisdictionem) ad veritatem poterit peruenire; licebit sibi de ipso inquirere, vt cognoscat, an ille ad eius iurisdictionem pertineat. Sic dicunt, quod est in proposito: quia eo ipso, quod Papa de haeresi tam grauiter diffamatur; quod talis infamia absque scandalo ecclesiae & periculo fidei dissimulari aut tolerari non posset, praelati possunt probabiliter dubitare: an Papa sit catholicus vel haereticus. Quia de diffamato dubitandum est ante examinationem causae, an fama veritati innitatur. Et per consequens dubitandum est, an diffamatus crimen, super quo diffamatur, commiserit. Si autem praelati probabiliter dubitant, an Papa de haeresi diffamatus sit catholicus vel haereticus, sequitur, quod probare habent, an Papa sit de iurisdictione ipsorum effectus. Nam si fama est falsa, non est de iurisdictione ipsorum: quia Papa manens Papa propter falsam infamiam non est de iurisdictione quorumcunque. falsa enim infamia nullam iurisdictionem tribuit. Si autem fama continet veritatem, Papa talis diffamatus est vere haereticus. si autem vere haereticus, est de iurisdictione catholicorum. Sicut igitur praelati catholici probabiliter dubitant, an Papa de haeresi diffamatus sit catholicus vel haereticus, ita dubitant probabiliter, an sit de iurisdictione ipsorum effectus. Ex quo autem probabiliter dubitant, an sit de iurisdictione ipsorum effectus, ipsi tenentur de ipso inquirere, an scilicet Papa de haeresi sic diffamatus sit haereticus vel catholicus. Ergo in hoc casu praelati catholici habent potestatem inquirendi de Papa super haeresi mendaciter diffamato, licet in rei veritate iurisdictionem non habeant super ipsum: sicut potest quis citare alium, cuius tamen in rei veritate non est iudex.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. The allegations set out above nearly drive me to perplexity. For it seems hard to me to assert that all people have jurisdiction, power or authority over their minister: the members over the head, the sons over the father, the disciples over the master, the subjects over the prelate; especially since an unjust and false infamy ought not to confer jurisdiction, nor can it do so. And so it seems serious to say that a Pope, lyingly defamed of heresy, is made subject to the judgment of any person or persons on account of such infamy; especially since it seems scarcely possible that the whole Catholic faith should rest in the Pope alone, even for a short time. On the other hand, the zeal for the Christian faith troubles me keenly, not to say that no inquiry or judgment ought to be made concerning a Pope defamed of the crime of heresy. Therefore, since I hold it probable that the Pope can fall into heretical depravity, and if no inquiry can be made into him, the whole faith could be imperilled. Wherefore, if some men strive to resolve this perplexity, reveal it to me. MASTER. There is a certain assertion that, on account of no false infamy, the Church has jurisdiction over the Pope. Yet if the Pope has been so defamed of heresy that it could not be tolerated without scandal to the Church or danger to the faith, not only the universal Church or a general council but also the bishops have power to inquire into him. And if they find him manifestly heretical, they must restrain him, or denounce his depravity to others. DIS. This assertion seems to conclude a contradiction. For one part appears to contradict the other. If no person has jurisdiction over a Pope defamed of heresy, no person will be able by right to inquire into him, since the office of inquiry is recognised as belonging not to an inferior, nor to an equal, but to one who has superior jurisdiction. MAG. To that objection the answer is this: just as inquiry belongs to a superior, so does citation; for an equal or inferior cannot ordinarily cite his superior, since to cite belongs to one who has jurisdiction. Yet, notwithstanding this, in a case someone who has no jurisdiction over another may cite him. And if it is probably doubted whether a judge has jurisdiction over someone, nevertheless he ought and may cite him, and the person cited is bound to appear and to show that the citation does not hold. If he does not do so, the judge may excommunicate him; and on account of contumacy the judge, who has no jurisdiction over him, would have jurisdiction over him to this extent, namely that he can bind him by the sentence of excommunication (Extra, de appellationibus, Duobus). So it is said of inquiry, and it must be said that, although to inquire ordinarily belongs to a superior, yet if it is probably doubted of someone, who cannot have recourse to a superior, whether he has power and jurisdiction to inquire over another, and the truth cannot otherwise be reached except by inquiring (namely whether he has jurisdiction over the other), it will be lawful for him to inquire into that person, so as to know whether that person belongs to his jurisdiction. They say that this is the case in point: for by the very fact that the Pope is so gravely defamed of heresy, and such infamy could not be overlooked or tolerated without scandal to the Church and danger to the faith, prelates can probably doubt whether the Pope is Catholic or heretical. For a man who is defamed must be doubted, before the examination of the cause, whether the report rests on truth. And consequently it must be doubted whether the defamed man has committed the crime of which he is defamed. If, then, prelates probably doubt whether a Pope defamed of heresy is Catholic or heretical, it follows that they must determine whether the Pope is subject to their jurisdiction. For if the report is false, he is not subject to their jurisdiction: since a Pope who remains Pope is not subject to the jurisdiction of anyone on account of a false infamy; for a false infamy confers no jurisdiction. But if the report contains the truth, a Pope so defamed is truly heretical; and if truly heretical, he is subject to the jurisdiction of Catholics. Therefore, just as Catholic prelates probably doubt whether a Pope defamed of heresy is Catholic or heretical, so they probably doubt whether he is made subject to their jurisdiction. And since they probably doubt whether he is subject to their jurisdiction, they are bound to inquire into him, namely whether a Pope so defamed is heretical or Catholic. Therefore in this case Catholic prelates have power to inquire into a Pope lyingly defamed of heresy, although in the truth of the matter they have no jurisdiction over him, just as one may cite another over whom, in truth, one is not judge.

units.la: CAP. XV.
units.tr: CAP. XV.

units.la: In quo ostenditur, quod de Papa super crimine haeresis diffamato catholici potestatem habent inquirendi veritatem, & quod ad eo inquisitio est facienda.
units.tr: In which it is shown that Catholics have power to inquire into the truth about a Pope defamed of the crime of heresy, and that such an inquiry ought to be made concerning him.

units.la: DISCIP. Ex praedictis mihi data est occasio manifesta quaerendi. ante tamen expostulo, vt ostendas, quib. rationib. vel auctoritatib. possit assertio supradicta muniri. MAG. Per rationes fundatas in scriptura diuina & dictis sanctorum patrum praedicta assertio videtur posse probari. Quam tamen exemplo patentissimo, vt nonnullis apparet, quidam monstrare nituntur. Nam sicut allegatum est supra, de beato Marcellino Papa de haeresi diffamato, eo quod actum haeretica Idolatriae videtur commisisse, plures episcopi conuenerunt, & inquisitionem de ipso fecerunt. & inquisitione facta (quia ipsum no deprehenderunt haereticum) ipsum iudicare nolebant, sicut nec poterant. Ex quo datur intelligi, quod de Papa de haeresi diffamato catholici potestatem habent inquirere, an fama contineat veritatem. DIS. Notum fuit, quod B. Marcellinus commiserat Idolatriam: & per consequens quod esset haereticus. & ita non est simile de Papa Marcellino, & de Papa mendaciter de haeresi diffamato. MAG. Istam rationem excludunt dicentes, quod quamuis esset notum apud fideles, & etiam apud quosdam catholicos, quod B. Marcellinus sacrificasset Idolis; tamen hoc non erat notorium apud episcopos, qui ad concilium conuenerunt: nec erat notorium apud quosdam, quod ipse esset haereticus. & ideo dubitabant episcopi, an esset haereticus. & forte magis credebant, quod esset haereticus, quia tamen nesciuerunt veritatem, ipse fuit de haeresi diffamatus. & conuenerunt catholici, & inquisierunt solicite veritatem. Si autem veritate sciuissent, superflue conuenissent, vel inquisiuissent. inquisierunt ergo de facto Papae; & ita de Papa infamato de haeresi est inquisitio facienda. DIS. Adhuc instat contra dictum exemplum: quia B. Marcellinus non fuit infamatus de haeresi, sed de idolatria tantummodo. & ita exemplum positum nequaquam concludit intentum illorum. MAG. Istam instantiam excludunt dicentes, quod eo ipso, quod fuit diffamatus de idolatria, fuit diffamatus de haeresi. quia omnis idolatra, de quo nesciturn timore mortis vel sponte immolauerit idolis, de haeresi est suspectus. & ita diffamare aliquem de idolatria antequam constet ipsum idolatrare solum timore mortis, est ipsum infamare de haeresi. Cum ergo B. Marcellinus commiserit idolatriam, antequam rediret, & poenitentiam ageret, & confiteretur se idolatrasse timore mortis tantummodo, nesciebatur an praeuitatem haereticam incurrisset. & ita constat, quod B. Marcellinus fuit de haeresi diffamatus. Item, vt dicunt illi: esto quod B. Marcellinus non fuerit de haeresi diffamatus; habent tamen intentum, per dictum exemplum, quia catholici potestatem habent inquirendi de Papa de haeresi diffamato. nam non est maior ratio, quod catholici habeant maiorem potestatem inquirendi de Papa de crimine Idolatriæ diffamato, quàm de Papa super crimine hæresis diffamato. Cùm ergo catholici habeant potestatem inquirendi de Papa super crimine idolatriæ diffamato, sequitur quod habent potestatem inquirendi de Papa super crimine hæresis diffamato. DIS. Dicerent aliqui, ꝗ certum est vel fuit beatum Marcellinum idolatrasse, & ideo potuerunt catholici inquirere merito de facto eius. Sed si Papa aliquis esset diffamatus de hæresi, non esset propter hoc certum ipsum sensisse hæreticam pravitatem. & ita non est simile de beato Marcellino & de Papa super hæresi diffamato.
units.tr: DISCIP. From what has been said, I have a clear occasion to ask. First, however, I request that you show by what reasons or authorities the assertion stated above can be supported. MAG. The assertion above seems capable of proof by reasons grounded in divine Scripture and in the sayings of the holy Fathers. Some, however, try to demonstrate it by a most obvious example. For, as was cited above, concerning blessed Marcellinus, Pope, who was defamed of heresy because he seemed to have committed the heretical act of idolatry, several bishops assembled and made an inquiry into him. When the inquiry was made, they did not find him to be a heretic, and so they were unwilling to judge him, as indeed they could not. From this it is to be understood that Catholics have power to inquire, concerning a Pope defamed of heresy, whether the report contains the truth. DIS. It was known that blessed Marcellinus had committed idolatry, and consequently that he was a heretic. Therefore the case of Pope Marcellinus is not like that of a Pope falsely defamed of heresy. MAG. Those who maintain the assertion exclude this objection, saying that although it was known among the faithful, and even among some Catholics, that blessed Marcellinus had sacrificed to idols, yet this was not notorious among the bishops who came together for the council, nor was it notorious to some that he was a heretic. Hence the bishops doubted whether he was a heretic. And perhaps they rather believed that he was a heretic; yet because they did not know the truth, he was defamed of heresy. Catholics therefore assembled and diligently inquired into the truth. If they had known the truth, they would have assembled and inquired in vain. They therefore inquired into the Pope's case in fact; and so an inquiry is to be made concerning a Pope infamed of heresy. DIS. Still, there is an objection to the example given: blessed Marcellinus was not defamed of heresy, but only of idolatry. So the example adduced does not at all prove what they intend. MAG. Those who maintain the assertion exclude this objection too, saying that by the very fact that he was defamed of idolatry, he was defamed of heresy, because every idolater who has not been shown to have sacrificed to idols solely from fear of death is suspected of heresy. Thus to defame someone of idolatry, before it is established that he idolatrized only from fear of death, is to defame him of heresy. Since blessed Marcellinus committed idolatry before he returned, did penance, and confessed that he had idolatrized from fear of death alone, it was not known whether he had incurred the heretical depravity. And so it is plain that blessed Marcellinus was defamed of heresy. Again, as they say: even if blessed Marcellinus had not been defamed of heresy, they still gain their point from this example, because Catholics have power to inquire about a Pope defamed of heresy. For there is no greater reason that Catholics should have power to inquire into a Pope defamed of the crime of idolatry than into a Pope defamed of the crime of heresy. Since, therefore, Catholics have power to inquire into a Pope defamed of the crime of idolatry, it follows that they have power to inquire into a Pope defamed of the crime of heresy. DIS. Some would reply that it is certain, or was certain, that blessed Marcellinus had idolatrized, and therefore Catholics could rightly inquire into his deed. But if some Pope were defamed of heresy, it would not for that reason be certain that he had held heretical depravity. So the case of blessed Marcellinus is not like that of a Pope defamed of heresy.

units.la: MAG. Istam instantiam dicunt esse malam: quia inquisitio non debet esse de certis, sed de dubiis. qui enim scit, certificari non debet. & per consequens superflue quis inquirit propter sua vel aliorum dubia excludeda. Sicigitur quia fuit certum & notorium episcopis, qui convenerant ad concilium, beatum Marcellinum idolatrasse, de hoc non quæsierunt; sed inquisierunt, quod erat eis ignotum, an timore mortis idolatrauerit. Item, si Papa aliquam hæresim prædicaret & esset notorium, de hoc non esset inquisitio facienda: sed esset inquisitio facienda, an pertinaciam errori adiungeret. & ita dum Papa super crimine hæresis diffamatur, est inquisitio per catholicos facienda. Quam etiam assertionem pluribus rationibus isti confirmare nituntur: quarum prima talis est. Ad unumquemque prælatum & pastores spectat cognoscere, quæ oves sunt suæ, & qui sunt sibi subiecti, aliter enim exempli pastoris summi dicentis Iohan. 10. Ego sum pastor bonus & cognosco oves meas, erit nullatenus imitator. nec præceptum Salomonis implebit dicentis Prouer. 27. Diligenter agnosce vultum pecoris tui, tuosque greges considera. Debet ergo prælatus cognoscere, qui sunt subiecti sui. ergo quando dubitatur de aliquo, an sit subiectus alicuius prælati, idem prælatus constringitur, ne forte subditus suus per negligentiam pereat, & secum alios pertrahat in interitum, diligenter inquirere & investigare, an ad gregem suum pertineat. Sed si Papa de hæresi graviter diffamatus sit, prælati debent probabiliter dubitare, an Papa totaliter diffamatus sit de iurisdictione eorum effectus: quia dubitare habent, an sit hæreticus, licet non statim debeant credere ipsum esse hæreticum. ergo in hoc casu tenentur inquirere, an Papa taliter diffamatus sit de iurisdictione ipsorum. hoc autem facere possunt nequaquam, nisi inquirendo an sit factus hæreticus. ergo tenentur inquirere, an Papa taliter diffamatus incurrit hæreticam pravitatem. Secunda ratio est. ad illum spectat scire, qui sunt subditi sui, ad quæ spectat corrigere omnium subditorum suorum excessus. sed ad prælatos catholicos spectat corrigere omnium subditorum suorum excessus, ut sacri canones protestantur aperte. ergo ad ipsos spectat scire de omnibus qui sunt subditi sui. ergo ad ipsos pertinet inquirere de illis, de quibus dubitatur, an sint sibi subditi, utrum in rei veritate sint subditi sui vel non. Si autem Papa graviter de hæresi diffamatur, probabiliter dubitant, an sit subiectus catholicorum: quia probabiliter dubitatur, an sit hæreticus. ergo ad catholicos pertinet inquirere, an Papa de hæresi diffamatus sit eis subiectus. Tertia ratio est hæc. prælati catholici tenentur ex officio suo oves suas contra luporum rabiem custodire. ergo tenentur subditos suos contra hæreticorum insidias conseruare: & per consequens, quando nunciatur prælatis catholicis per publicam famam, quod aliquis niititur gregem suum invadere, & corrumpere per hæreticam pravitatem, debent inquirere diligenter veritatem, ipso domino præcipiente Deut. 23. si audieris in una urbium, quas dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi habitandam, dicentes aliquos: egressi sunt filii Belial de medio tui, & averterunt habitatores urbis tuæ, atque dixerunt: eamus & seruiamus diis alienis, quos ignoratis. quare sollicite & diligenter inquire veritate rei, spectata. si inueneris certum esse quod dicitur, & abominationem hanc operè perpetratam, statim percuties habitatores urbis illius in ore gladii. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod sia prouidis & honestis Papa, vel quicunque alius, publice diffamatur, quod velit catholicos à fide auertere orthodoxæ veritas diligenter inquirenda. Ergo de Papa super crimine hæresis graviter diffamato est inquisitio facienda. DISCIP. Prælati non habent inquirere, nisi de illis, quos constat esse subditos suos. & ita de Papa non habent inquirere.
units.tr: MAG. Those who maintain the assertion say this objection is faulty, because an inquiry ought to concern not things that are certain but things that are doubtful. For whoever knows something need not be certified of it, and consequently a man inquires in vain into what is already settled, either for himself or for others. Thus, since it was certain and notorious to the bishops who had come together for the council that blessed Marcellinus had idolatrized, they did not inquire into this; they inquired into what was unknown to them, namely whether he had idolatrized from fear of death. Likewise, if a Pope were to preach some heresy and this were notorious, there would be no need to inquire into that; but there would need to be an inquiry whether he added obstinacy to the error. So while a Pope is defamed of the crime of heresy, an inquiry is to be made by Catholics. They try to confirm this assertion by several reasons, of which the first is this: it belongs to every prelate and minister to know which sheep are his and who are subject to him. Otherwise he will in no way be an imitator of the supreme Shepherd, who says in John 10: I am the good shepherd, and I know my sheep; nor will he fulfil the precept of Solomon, who says in Proverbs 27: Diligently know the face of your flock, and consider your herds. A prelate must therefore know who are subject to him. Therefore, when there is doubt about someone, whether he is subject to some prelate, that same prelate is bound, lest his subject perish through negligence and draw others with him to destruction, to inquire and investigate diligently whether he belongs to his flock. But if a Pope has been gravely defamed of heresy, the prelates ought reasonably to doubt whether the Pope, so defamed, has fallen from their jurisdiction, because they must doubt whether he is a heretic, although they ought not immediately to believe that he is a heretic. Therefore in this case they are bound to inquire whether the Pope, so defamed, is outside their jurisdiction. They can in no way do this unless by inquiring whether he has become a heretic. Therefore they are bound to inquire whether the Pope, so defamed, has fallen into heretical depravity. The second reason is this: it belongs to him who must know who are his subjects, and to whom it belongs to correct the offences of all his subjects. But it belongs to Catholic prelates to correct the offences of all their subjects, as the sacred canons plainly declare. Therefore it belongs to them to know all who are their subjects. Therefore it pertains to them to inquire about those about whom it is doubtful whether they are subject to them, whether in truth they are their subjects or not. But if a Pope is gravely defamed of heresy, they reasonably doubt whether he is subject to Catholics, because it is reasonably doubtful whether he is a heretic. Therefore it pertains to Catholics to inquire whether the Pope, defamed of heresy, is subject to them. The third reason is this: Catholic prelates are bound by their office to guard their sheep against the rage of wolves. Therefore they are bound to preserve their subjects against the snares of heretics. Consequently, when it is reported to Catholic prelates by public rumour that someone is attempting to invade their flock and corrupt it by heretical depravity, they ought to inquire diligently into the truth, the Lord himself commanding in Deut. 23: If you hear in one of the cities which the Lord your God will give you to dwell in, that some say: "The sons of Belial have gone out from among you, and have turned away the inhabitants of your city, saying, Let us go and serve other gods whom you do not know," then you shall inquire carefully and diligently into the matter. If you find it certain that this is said, and that this abomination has been committed, you shall at once strike the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword. From these words it is to be understood that when a Pope or anyone else, whether honest or dishonest, is publicly defamed of wanting to turn Catholics away from the orthodox faith, the truth must be diligently inquired into. Therefore an inquiry is to be made concerning a Pope gravely defamed of the crime of heresy. DISCIP. Prelates are not bound to inquire except into those whom it is certain are their subjects. And so they are not bound to inquire about a Pope.

units.la: MAGIST. Respondetur tibi, quod quilibet prælatus debet inquirere de omnibus, qui gregem suum invadunt, siue sint subditi, siue non. saltem ad resistendum eisdem. quemadmodum rex debet omnes repellere, qui regnum suum invadunt, quamuis sint de alio regno. & quilibet etiam nullam habens iurisdictionem debet pro patria omnes invadentes pro posse repellere, quamuis nullam super eis iurisdictionem habeat. Et ex hoc quarta ratio sic formatur. Non minus sollicite debent prælati catholici gregem suum contra spirituales inimicos defendere, & ea, quæ ad defensionem pertinent, exercere: quam reges & principes eorum subditos debent terras suas contra invadentes iniuste defendere, licet de eorum iurisdictione nequaquam existant. ergo multo fortius & animosius debent prælati contra inimicos spirituales greges suos defendere, & ea facere, quæ ad spiritualem defensionem spectare noscuntur. Sed ad defensionem noscitur pertinere inuestigare sollicite, qui sunt isti hostes spirituales, qui gregem nituntur invadere: maxime si est publica fama per viros honestos & prouidos suscitata, quod aliqui volunt dominicum gregem invadere. Ergo Papa per viros prouidos & honestos de hæresi publicæ diffamatur, catholici deberent diligenter inquirere veritatem.
units.tr: MAGISTER. It is answered to you that every prelate ought to inquire into all who invade his flock, whether they are subject to him or not, at least so as to resist them. Just as a king ought to drive off all who invade his kingdom, even though they are from another kingdom; and anyone at all, even one who has no jurisdiction, ought to repel by all means in his power, on behalf of his country, all who invade it, although he has no jurisdiction over them. And from this the fourth reason is framed thus. Catholic prelates ought to defend their flock against spiritual enemies no less diligently, and to carry out those things which pertain to its defence, than kings and princes ought to defend their lands against unjust invaders, even though those invaders are in no way under their jurisdiction. Therefore prelates ought much more strongly and boldly to defend their flocks against spiritual enemies, and to do those things which are known to belong to spiritual defence. But it is known to pertain to defence to inquire carefully who these spiritual enemies are who strive to invade the flock, especially if there is public report, raised by honest and prudent men, that some wish to invade the Lord's flock. Therefore, since the Pope is publicly reported by prudent and honest men to be a heretic, Catholics ought to inquire diligently into the truth.

units.la: Quinta ratio talis est. cui periculosum est renunciare iuri suo, ei periculosum est non inquirere, ad quos extendutur iura sua, qn dubitatur de aliquib. an extendantur ad ipsos. Sed platis religiosis periculosum iolum est renunciare, aut cedere iuri suo, quod in causa Dei susceperunt à Deo, teste B. Cypriano, qui vt recitatur. f. q. 1. c. quam periculosum sit, ait: quam periculosum sit in diuinis rebus, vt quis cedat iuri suo & potestati scriptura diuina declarat, cum Esau primatus suos perdiderit, nec inde recipere vel petere postmodum potuit quod semel concessit. Ergo periculosum est praelatis catholicis non solicite inquirere, ad quos extenduntur iura eorum in causis Dei, quando de aliquibus dubitatur, an potestati catholicorum sint subiecti. si autem Papa publice per vitos prouidos & honestos de haeresi diffametur, probabiliter dubitandum est, an sit potestati catholicorum subiectus: ergo de hoc in hoc casu debent catholici quaerere veritatem diligenter. Et ita habent de Papa taliter diffamato inquisitionem facere diligentem.
units.tr: The fifth reason is this. For one to whom it is dangerous to renounce his right, it is also dangerous not to inquire to whom his rights extend, when it is doubted whether they extend to certain persons. But for religious prelates it is dangerous to renounce or yield up the right which they have received from God in the cause of God, as blessed Cyprian witnesses, who, as is quoted in Decr. 1, q. 1, c. "Quam periculosum sit," says: how dangerous it is in divine matters for anyone to yield his right and power, the divine Scripture declares, since Esau lost his primacy and could afterwards neither recover nor seek again what he had once granted. Therefore it is dangerous for Catholic prelates not to inquire carefully to whom their rights in the causes of God extend, when it is doubted whether certain persons are subject to the power of Catholics. But if the Pope is publicly reported by honest and prudent men to be a heretic, it must be probably doubted whether he is subject to the power of Catholics; therefore in this case Catholics ought to seek the truth diligently. And so they ought to make a diligent inquiry concerning a Pope so reported.

units.la: CAP. XVI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVI.

units.la: In quo consequenter agitur de appellatione à summo pontifice pro causa haeresis interiecta, & ponuntur duo modi dicendi. primus est, quod in nullo casu est deferendum appellationi contra summum pontificem, & probatur duabus auctoritatibus & sex rationibus, ad quas respondetur capitulo 55. secundus modus dicendi ponitur capitulo sequenti, scilicet 17.
units.tr: In which the question is pursued, in order, of appeal from the supreme pontiff on account of heresy having been lodged; and two ways of speaking are set out. The first is that in no case is an appeal against the supreme pontiff to be entertained; this is proved by two authorities and six arguments, to which an answer is given in chapter 55. The second way of speaking is set out in the following chapter, namely chapter 17.

units.la: DISCIP. Audiui rationes, quibus ostenditur, quod potestatem habent catholici inquirendi de Papa super crimine haeresis diffamato: occasione quarum accidit mihi voluntas indagandi specialiter, an propter appellationem aliquorum contra Papam pro causa haeresis interiecta catholici habent potestatem inquirendi de summo pontifice. Cum enim appellatio sit diffamatoria Papae: videtur, quod si praelati habeant potestatem inquirendi de Papa super crimine haeresis diffamato, quod etiam propter talem appellationem eandem obtinent potestatem. Vnde de hoc quid sentiant literati, indicare digneris. MAGIST. Circa hoc sunt assertiones contrariae, quibusdam dicentibus quod in nullo casu est appellationi contra summum pontificem deferendum: Aliis dicentibus, quod appellationi pro causa haeresis contra summum pontificem interiectae debent praelati deferre. & per consequens oportet eos de iure de tali appellatione cognoscere.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. I have heard the reasons by which it is shown that Catholics have the power to inquire into a Pope who has been publicly accused of the crime of heresy. On the strength of these, a wish has come over me to investigate in particular whether, because some have appealed against the Pope on account of heresy, Catholics have the power to inquire into the supreme pontiff. For since an appeal is a defamation of the Pope, it seems that if prelates have the power to inquire into a Pope accused of heresy, they also hold the same power on account of such an appeal. So please be good enough to tell me what the learned think about this. MASTER. On this point opinions conflict. Some say that appeal against the supreme pontiff must be admitted in no case. Others say that prelates ought to admit an appeal made against the supreme pontiff on account of heresy, and consequently that they are bound by law to hear such an appeal.

units.la: DIS. Motiua primae assertionis allega. MAG. Prima assertio auctoritatibus & rationibus videtur posse probari. Prima auctoritas est Gelasii Papae. & ponitur. 9. q. 3. c. ipsi, qui ait; ipsi sunt canones, qui appellationes totius ecclesiae ad huius sedis examen voluerunt deferre: ab ipso vero nunquam prorsus appellari debere sanxerunt. Secunda est eiusdem ca. sequenti, qui ait: Contra per multa dum nouit ecclesia, quod sacrosancta Romana ecclesia fas de omnibus habeat iudicandi: nec cuiquam de eius licet iudicare iudicio: siquidem ad illam de qualibet mundi parte appellandum est: ab ipsa autem nemo est appellare permissus. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod in nullo à Papa appellare licet, quia canones supradicti absolute sine omni discussione vel distinctione affirmant, quod à Romana ecclesia appellare non licet: ergo nec eos debemus distinguere.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Set out the arguments for the first opinion. MASTER. The first opinion seems capable of proof by authorities and reasons. The first authority is that of Pope Gelasius, cited in 9 q. 3 c. ipsi, who says: "The canons themselves have willed that the appeals of the whole Church be brought to the examination of this see, and have decreed that no appeal may ever be made from it at all." The second is from the same chapter that follows, which says: "Since the Church knows through many examples that the most holy Roman Church has the right to judge concerning all things, and that no one may judge its judgment; for appeal must be made to it from every part of the world, but it is permitted to appeal from it to no one." From these words it is gathered that one may in no case appeal from the Pope, because the aforesaid canons affirm absolutely, without any discussion or distinction, that it is not lawful to appeal from the Roman Church. Therefore we ought not to distinguish them either.

units.la: DIS. Pro eadem assertione rationes adducas. MAG. Prima ratio talis est. ab illo, qui non habet superiorem in terris, appellare non licet 2. q. 8. c. anteriorum. sed Papa non habet superiorem in terris: cum ipse sit caput & iudex omnium Christianorum. ergo à Papa appellare non licet. Secunda ratio est haec: qui licite pro causa haeresis appellat ab aliquo, est totaliter a iurisdictione ipsius exemptus: quia omnis appellans in eo, super quo appellat, est exemptus à iurisdictione illius à quo appellat, extra de appell. cum causamus. & c. propositum. qui autem appellat super causa haeresis, appellat super tota iurisdictione illius, à quo appellat. quia si est haereticus, nullam habet iurisdictionem omnino. ergo qui appellat ab aliquo super causa haeresis, à iurisdictione ipsius est exemptus omnino. sed nullus Christianus est exemptus à iurisdictione Papae, ergo non licet appellare ab ipso. Tertia ratio est haec: ab illo appellare non licet, à cuius obedientia non licet recedere. quia appellans recedit ab obedientia illius, à quo appellat. sed nulli Christiano licet recedere ab obedientia Papae. di. 13. c. praeceptis. ergo nulli Christiano licet à summo pontifice appellare. Quarto sic. ab illo appellare non licet, ad quem est ab omnibus (si oppressi fuerint) appellandum. quia non licet eidem in eadem causa appellare ab aliquo ad ipsum. sed omni Christiano in causis haeresis (si oppressus fuerit) licet appellare ad Papam. 2. q. 6. ca. quisquis c. omnis. & ca. ad Romanam. ergo nulli Christiano licet in causa haeresis appellare à Papa. Quinto sic, sicut imperator primatum habet in temporalibus, ita Papa in spiritualibus primatum noscitur obtinere. sed nulli pro aliqua causa temporali licet appellare ab imperatore, secundum leges ergo nulli licet appellare pro causa spirituali à Papa. & per consequens pro causa haeresis non est à Papa appellandum. Sexto sic. ab illo, ad quem sunt omnes causae fidei deferendae, non est pro causa fidei appellandum. sed omnes causae fidei sunt ad summum pontificem deferendae. 24. q. 1. c. quotiens. & extra, de baptismo & eius effectu. maiores. 2. dt. 17. multis. pro causa ergo fidei non est à summo pontifice appellandum. Ex quo concluditur, quod si contingeret aliquem contra Papam temere appellare, tali appellationi esset minime deferendum, & non esset de Papa aliqualiter inquirendum, necaliquid aliter innouandum.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Give the arguments for the same opinion. MASTER. The first argument runs thus: it is not lawful to appeal from one who has no superior on earth (2 q. 8 c. anteriorum). But the Pope has no superior on earth, since he is the head and judge of all Christians. Therefore it is not lawful to appeal from the Pope. The second argument is this: one who lawfully appeals from someone on account of heresy is wholly exempt from his jurisdiction, because every appellant is exempt, in the matter over which he appeals, from the jurisdiction of the one from whom he appeals (extra, de appell., cum causam, and c. propositum). But whoever appeals on the ground of heresy appeals concerning the whole jurisdiction of the one from whom he appeals, because if that man is a heretic he has no jurisdiction at all. Therefore whoever appeals from someone on the ground of heresy is altogether exempt from his jurisdiction. But no Christian is exempt from the jurisdiction of the Pope. Therefore it is not lawful to appeal from him. The third argument is this: it is not lawful to appeal from one whose obedience it is not lawful to leave, because the appellant withdraws from the obedience of the one from whom he appeals. But it is not lawful for any Christian to withdraw from the obedience of the Pope (13 d. c. praeceptis). Therefore no Christian may appeal from the supreme pontiff. Fourth, it is not lawful to appeal from one to whom all may appeal (if they have been oppressed), because it is not permitted to appeal to the same person in the same cause from someone else. But every Christian, in causes of heresy, if he has been oppressed, may appeal to the Pope (2 q. 6 c. quisquis; c. omnis; and c. ad Romanam). Therefore no Christian may in a cause of heresy appeal from the Pope. Fifth: just as the emperor holds the primacy in temporal matters, so the Pope is known to hold the primacy in spiritual matters. But by the laws no one may appeal from the emperor in any temporal cause. Therefore no one may appeal from the Pope in any spiritual cause, and consequently in a cause of heresy one may not appeal from the Pope. Sixth: it is not lawful to appeal in a cause of faith from one to whom all causes of faith are to be referred. But all causes of faith are to be referred to the supreme pontiff (24 q. 1 c. quotiens; and extra, de baptismo et eius effectu, maiores; 2 d. 17 multis). Therefore in a cause of faith one may not appeal from the supreme pontiff. From this it follows that if anyone should rashly appeal against the Pope, such an appeal ought in no way to be admitted, and there should be no inquiry into the Pope in any way, nor any other innovation made.

units.la: CAP. XVII.
units.tr: CAP. XVII.

units.la: Ponit opinionem contrariam capitulo praecedenti positam sub tribus conclusionibus. Quarum prima tres habet partes, quae in hoc capitulo suo ordine pertractantur. Secunda vero pertractatur capitulo octavo, & sequentibus. Tertia capitulo 45.
units.tr: Sets out the opposing opinion, put forward against the preceding chapter, under three conclusions. The first of these has three parts, which are treated in this chapter in their proper order. The second is treated in chapter eight and those following. The third in chapter 45.

units.la: DISC: Itae allegationes pro assertione praedicta videntur fortes, quarum virtutes magis adiuvertam, si recitaueris, quomodo respondetur ad illas, & qualiter assertio contraria sulciatur. Unde primo assertionem contrariam munire nitaris. Secundo narra, quomodo ad rationes praescriptas respondetur. MAG. Assertionem contrariam melius intelliges, si tibi fuerit per particulas explicata. DIS. Hoc peto ut facias: MAG. In assertione contraria medullitus explicata tres continentur conclusiones, quarum prima est, quod a Papa catholico, quamuis de haeresi publice diffamato, pro causa haeresis directe appellare non licet: nisi forte aliquis deceptus haberet iustam causam credendi Papam esse haereticum. Secunda conclusio est: quod a Papa haeretico licet appellare. Tertia conclusio est: quod si aliquis de facto appellaret a Papa catholico, antequam constaret appellationem eius non esse legitimam, esset eiusdem appellationi deferendum.
units.tr: DISC: These arguments for the aforesaid assertion seem strong, and I would better appreciate their force if you were to recount how they are answered and how the contrary assertion is supported. Therefore first try to fortify the contrary assertion; second, relate how the foregoing arguments are answered. MAG. You will understand the contrary assertion better if it is explained to you piece by piece. DIS. That is what I ask you to do. MAG. In the contrary assertion, when it has been thoroughly explained, three conclusions are contained. The first is that one may not appeal directly from a Catholic Pope, although he is publicly defamed of heresy, on account of heresy; unless perhaps someone who has been deceived has a just reason for believing the Pope to be a heretic. The second conclusion is that one may appeal from a heretical Pope. The third conclusion is that if anyone should in fact appeal from a Catholic Pope, before it is established that his appeal is not lawful, the same appeal is to be deferred to.

units.la: DIS: Istas tres conclusiones cupio per ordinem pertractari. primam autem cupio explicari: quia plures partes continere videtur, quas non bene intelligo: imo etiam quare illud adverbium directe ponitur. MAG. Bene dicis, quod praedicta conclusio tenet plures partes: quia tres continet explicite vel implicite. quarum prima est, quod qui non est deceptus de fidelitate Papae (quia videlicet non habet probabilem causam credendi Papam esse haereticum) non debet ab eo directe pro causa haeresis appellare, sibi videlicet haeresim imponendo vel ipsum de haeresi accusando, aut quomodo libet diffamando.
units.tr: DIS: I wish these three conclusions to be treated in order, but I wish the first to be explained, since it seems to contain several parts which I do not well understand; and indeed I would like to know why the adverb "directly" is added. MAG. You rightly say that the said conclusion holds several parts, for it contains three, explicitly or implicitly. The first is that whoever is not deceived about the Pope's faithfulness (that is, has no probable reason for believing the Pope to be a heretic) ought not to appeal directly from him on account of heresy, that is, by charging him with heresy, or by accusing him of heresy, or by defaming him in any way whatever.

units.la: DISCIP. Non requisito pro nunc plures allegationes, pro tribus allegationibus supradictis, quia de aliquibus earum postea occasionem loquendi habebo. ideo ad secundam conclusionem principalem te converte, & ad probandum, quod licet a Papa haeretico appellare, allegare coneris. MAG. Antequam adverterentur allegationes, quod a Papa haeretico liceat appellare, expedit tibi (forte ut melius eas intelligas) modum ponendi explicite aperiri. DIS. Hoc volo.
units.tr: DISCIP. I do not now ask for more arguments for the three aforesaid conclusions, since I shall have occasion to speak of some of them later. So turn to the second principal conclusion, and try to prove by argument that one may appeal from a heretical Pope. MAG. Before the arguments are advanced that one may appeal from a heretical Pope, it is useful for you (perhaps so that you may understand them better) that the manner of proposing them be set out explicitly. DIS. That is what I want.

units.la: CAP. XVIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVIII.

units.la: In quo ponitur, quod a Papa haeretico liceat appellare. ubi nota appellationis multiplicem significationem & acceptionem, & quid sit appellatio.
units.tr: In which it is laid down that it is lawful to appeal from a heretical Pope. Note the manifold meaning and usage of the word "appeal," and what an appeal is.

units.la: DISCIP. Non requisito pro nunc plures allegationes, pro tribus allegationibus supradictis; quia de aliquibus earum postea occasionem loquendi habebo. Ideo ad secundam conclusionem principalem te converte, & ad probandum, quod licet a Papa haeretico appellare, allegare coneris. {ionibus}, quae fiunt ext. iudicium ab aduersario, ne aliquid fiat in praeiudicium appellantis super eo, pro quo appellat. Tales appellationes quasi prouocationes sunt ad causam & talibus appellationibus est deferendum. 14. bone & tales appellationes faciunt clerici frequenter inter se, & in electionibus pro aliis negotiis ecclesiae supra, de electis & confirmationibus, bona auditionis: & infra, de his quae fi. a maio. par. capituli.c.1. Ex quibus colligitur, quod appellatio plures habet significationes. Aliqua enim appellatio est, quae continet querelam iniquae sententiae, & fit a iudice. Aliqua autem est appellatio, quae continet querelam aliquae sententiae, quae quandoque non est a iudice, sed est etiam prouocatio quaedam ad causam, ne aliquid fiat illicite.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. I do not now require more arguments beyond the three given above, since I shall have occasion to speak of some of them later. So turn to the second principal conclusion, and try to prove that it is lawful to appeal from a heretical Pope. {ionibus}, which are made against a judgment by an opponent, so that nothing be done to the prejudice of the appellant in the matter for which he appeals. Such appeals are, as it were, challenges to the cause, and such appeals must be deferred to. 14. Good. Clerics often make such appeals among themselves, and in elections and other church affairs: see above, De electis et confirmationibus, bona auditionis; and below, De his quae fiunt a maiore parte capituli, c. 1. From this it is gathered that appeal has several meanings. For one kind of appeal contains a complaint of an unjust sentence and is made to a judge. Another kind of appeal contains a complaint about some sentence which is not always from a judge, but is also a kind of challenge to the cause, so that nothing be done unlawfully.

units.la: DISCIP. Applica ista ad propositum. MAGIST. Dicunt assertores praedicti, quod largissime uti nolunt nomine appellationis, ne videantur concedere, quod appellans ab haeretico papa eo ipso quod appellat habeat papam haereticum pro iudice: quia eo ipso, quod aliquis appellat, habet ipsum pro non iudice; quem tamen ad causam prouocare intendit, ne in praeiudicium appellantis & omnium catholicorum papali utatur officio.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Apply these things to the matter in hand. MASTER. The aforesaid advocates say that they are unwilling to use the word "appeal" in its broadest sense, lest they seem to concede that an appellant from a heretical pope, by the very fact that he appeals, has the heretical pope as his judge. For by the very fact that someone appeals, he holds the other not to be a judge; yet he intends to provoke him to the cause, so that the Pope does not exercise his papal office to the prejudice of the appellant and of all Catholics.

units.la: DISCIP. Hoc ultimo dictum videtur contraria includere. nam si licet appellare a papa haeretico, maxime liceret appellare ab ipso si (aliquo licite coram ipso contendente) super quaestione fidei contra fidem diffinitiuam proferret sententiam: puta si aliquis accusans alium, quod teneret, Christum non fuisse natum de virgine; si papa daret sententiam diffinitiuam pro eo, quod Christus non fuit natus de virgine, liceret actori a papae sententia appellare. talis autem appellatio esset appellatio propriissime dicta: quia esset prouocatio iniquae sententiae querelam continens. ergo isti non tantum debent loqui de appellatione largissime sumpta, sed etiam de appellatione strictissime sumpta.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. What was said last seems to imply contrary things. For if it is lawful to appeal from a heretical pope, it would be most lawful to appeal from him if, while a dispute is being carried on lawfully before him, he should pronounce a definitive sentence against the faith on a question of faith: for example, if someone accusing another of holding that Christ was not born of a virgin, the Pope should give a definitive sentence that Christ was not born of a virgin, the plaintiff would be permitted to appeal from the Pope's sentence. Such an appeal would be an appeal in the strictest sense, since it would be a provocation containing a complaint of an unjust sentence. Therefore these men must speak not only of appeal taken in the broadest sense, but also of appeal taken in the strictest sense.

units.la: MAGIST. Ista obiectio, ut dicunt, est tam frivola, quod responsione non eget. nam quamuis dicant se nolle loqui de appellatione largissime sumpta, non propter hoc dicunt, se nunquam velle loqui de appellatione stricte sumpta, porro ex obiectione praedicta datur mihi occasio explicandi modum ponendi eorum.
units.tr: MASTER. This objection, as they say, is so trifling that it needs no answer. For although they say they do not wish to speak of appeal in the broadest sense, they do not therefore say that they never wish to speak of appeal in the strict sense. But from the objection just made I am given an occasion of explaining their manner of proceeding.

units.la: DISCIP. Explica.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Explain it.

units.la: MAGIST. Duo dicunt. Primum est, quod a papa haeretico in casu licet appellationem stricte sumptam emittere. illam appellationem videlicet, quae est prouocatio iniquae sententiae querelam continens. puta si aliquibus litigantibus coram ipso super quaestione fidei pro altero istorum accusatore vel accusato diffinitiuam contra fidem proferret sententiam. Secundum est: quod si papa fiat haereticus, ex causa quacunque etiam qui non litigat coram ipso potest appellare contra ipsum. & ista appellatio est prouocatio: & non erit propria dicta appellatio.
units.tr: MASTER. They say two things. The first is that, in a case, it is lawful to make an appeal in the strict sense from a heretical pope; namely that appeal which is a provocation containing a complaint of an unjust sentence. For example, if, while some litigants are before him on a question of faith, he were to pronounce a definitive sentence against the faith in favour of one of these, either the accuser or the accused. The second is this: that if a pope becomes a heretic, for whatever cause, then even someone who is not litigating before him can appeal against him. And that appeal is a provocation, and will not be an appeal properly so called.

units.la: DISCIP. Probabilitatem videtur habere, quod si papa in praeiudicium litigantis coram ipso super quaestione fidei iniquam contra fidem catholicam diffinitiuam proferret sententiam, liceret eidem a tali iniqua sententia appellare. sed alii appellare non liceret: quia sua non interest contra eum cum non sit probata sententia. Item, quamuis nunc (de crimine commisso extra iudicium) possit aliquis accusari, non est contra eum tamen appellandum. Quamuis ergo papa extra iudicium factus haereticus de haeresi valeat accusari, non tamen est appellandum ab ipso: sicut neque est appellandum a quolibet criminoso, licet quilibet criminosus valeret accusari.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. It seems probable that if the pope, to the prejudice of a litigant before him on a question of faith, were to pronounce an unjust and definitive sentence against the Catholic faith, it would be lawful for that litigant to appeal from such an unjust sentence. But it would not be lawful for another to appeal, because his interest is not involved against him, since the sentence has not been proved. Likewise, although someone may now be accused of a crime committed outside a judicial proceeding, it is not necessary to appeal against him. Therefore, although a pope who has become a heretic outside a judicial proceeding can be accused of heresy, one must not appeal from him, just as one must not appeal from every criminal, even though every criminal can be accused.

units.la: MAGIST. Ad primam istarum obiectionum respondetur, quod quaestio fidei est quaestio communis, & ad omnes pertinet Christianos. di. 96. c. vnam, vbi Nicolaus papa ait: vbi namque legistis imperatores antecessores vestros synodalibus conuentibus interfuisse, nisi forsitan de quibusdam, vbi de fide tractatum est, quae vniuersalis est, quae omnium communis, quae non solum ad clericos, verumetiam ad laicos & ad omnes omnino pertinet Christianos. ideo non solum licitum, sed etiam cuiuslibet catholici interest contra iniquam sententiam papae contra fidem prolatam appellare: quia talis sententia cuilibet Christiano praeiudicium noscitur generare. Ad secundam respondetur, quod nunquam ad vnum finem fit accusatio criminosi, & appellatio ab aliquo criminoso. accusatur enim criminosus, vt de commisso crimine puniatur: sed appellatur ab aliquo, ne aliquid in futurum in praeiudicium appellantis attemptet. & ideo si papa haereticus omnino cessaret a papali officio renunciando papatui, posset de haeresi accusari: sed non esset necesse appellare ab ipso. sed si papa haereticus a papali non cessaret officio, cum hoc redundat in praeiudicium cuiuslibet Christiani, quilibet Christianus ab ipso vel contra ipsum poterit appellare; ipsum ad causam & iudicium pronocando.
units.tr: MASTER. To the first of these objections it is answered that a question of faith is a common question, and pertains to all Christians (Dist. 96, c. Unam, where Pope Nicholas says: "For where have you read that your predecessors, the emperors, were present at synodal assemblies, except perhaps in those matters where faith was treated, which is universal, which is common to all, and which pertains not only to clerics but also to laymen and to all Christians without exception?"). Therefore it is not only lawful, but it is also in the interest of every Catholic, to appeal against an unjust sentence against the faith pronounced by the pope, because such a sentence is known to bring prejudice to every Christian. To the second it is answered that an accusation of a criminal and an appeal from someone are never made for one and the same end. For a criminal is accused so that he may be punished for the crime committed; but one appeals from someone so that he may not attempt anything in future to the prejudice of the appellant. And therefore, if a heretical pope were wholly to cease from the papal office by renouncing the papacy, he could be accused of heresy, but there would be no need to appeal from him. But if a heretical pope did not cease from the papal office, since this redounds to the prejudice of every Christian, any Christian may appeal from him, or against him, provoking him to the cause and to judgment.

units.la: DISCIP. Ad quid distinguitur inter appellationem, quae fit post diffinitiuam sententiam & appellationem quae fit extra iudicium: MAGIST. Ideo distinguitur, quia in appellatione, quae fit post diffinitiuam sententiam, non oportet in speciali allegare causam, sed sufficit dicere sententiam esse iniquam. Unde si duo litigarent coram papa super aliqua certa quaestione fidei (puta si vnus accusaret alium, quod esset haereticus, quia pertinaciter asseruisset visuram non esse peccatum, vel Christum non contingenter sed necessitate absoluta fuisse passum & crucifixum, aut apostolos nunquam post missionem spiritus sancti per vnam diem integram duxisse vitam communem cum aliis, aut legem Christianam non esse veram vel sanctam, vel Christum falsum prophetam fuisse) & papa diffinitiuam daret sententiam pro eo, quod non esset haereticus, quia assertio sua esset catholica, liceret a papa actori appellare, allegando solummodo, quod sententia sua esset iniqua & contra fidem catholicam; nec oporteret specialiter explicare, in quo sua sententia fidei obuiaret.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Why is a distinction drawn between an appeal which is made after a definitive sentence and an appeal which is made outside a judicial proceeding? MASTER. It is distinguished because in an appeal made after a definitive sentence it is not necessary to allege the cause specifically, but it is enough to say that the sentence is unjust. Hence, if two men were litigating before the pope on some definite question of faith (for example, if one accused the other of being a heretic, because he had obstinately asserted that fornication is not sin, or that Christ suffered and was crucified not contingently but by absolute necessity, or that the apostles never lived a common life with others for one entire day after the mission of the Holy Spirit, or that the Christian law is not true or holy, or that Christ was a false prophet), and the pope were to give a definitive sentence in favour of the one who was not a heretic, because his assertion was catholic, it would be lawful for the plaintiff to appeal from the pope, alleging only that his sentence was unjust and contrary to the Catholic faith; nor would it be necessary to explain specifically in what way his sentence opposed the faith.

units.la: Si autem extra iudicium, aut ante sententiam diffinitiuam voluerit quis appellare, oportet quod causam tale in speciali alleget: quae si esset probata, deberet legitima reputari. non enim sufficit in tali appellatione dicere ad hoc vt legitima reputetur, quod papa est haereticus; sed oportet exprimere, in quo est haereticus puta quod est haereticus, quia pertinaciter docet aut tenet fidem Christianam non esse veram, aut Christum non descendisse de Dauid, aut in Christo non fuisse duas substantias, aut aliquid huiusmodi, quod fidei obviat orthodoxae.
units.tr: But if someone wishes to appeal outside a judicial proceeding, or before a definitive sentence, he must allege the cause in particular; and if this were proved, it ought to be regarded as lawful. For in such an appeal it is not enough, in order that it be regarded as lawful, to say that the pope is a heretic; but it is necessary to state in what respect he is a heretic: for example, that he is a heretic because he obstinately teaches or holds that the Christian faith is not true, or that Christ did not descend from David, or that in Christ there were not two natures, or anything of this kind which opposes the orthodox faith.

units.la: CAP. XIX.
units.tr: CHAP. XIX.

units.la: In quo probatur, quod a papa haeretico in aliquo casu licet appellare, 13. rationibus & nota quod propter illum terminum licet moveantur plures difficultates infra capitulo 23. & sequentibus usque ad 28.
units.tr: In which it is proved that one may in some case appeal from a heretical pope, by thirteen reasons. Note that on account of this term several difficulties arise, see below chapter 23 and following, up to 28.

units.la: DISCIP. Modum ponendi illorum aliqualiter incipio aduertere: tamen ut eum magis intelligam, primo probare conetis, quod a papa haeretico in aliquo casu licet appellare, & postea de eadem materia plura interrogabo. MAGIST. Quia manifesta (sed aliqui de eis dubitauerunt) sunt primo probanda, ut per ipsa ad ignotorum perueniatur notitiam: ideo primo (supposito casu apertissimo) ostenditur, quod a papa haeretico licet appellare. DISCIP. Pone casum tuum possibilem. MAGIST. Ponitur quod aliquis accuset alium coram papa, quod est haereticus eo quod tenet & asserit, fidem Christianam falsam & legem Saracenorum esse tenendam, & Christum falsum fuisse prophetam & damnandum. quo accusato & lite contestata papa proferret sententiam difinitiuam, quod accusatus non est haereticus, quia omnia praedicta, quae dicit & asserit, continent veritatem.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. I begin to grasp the method of these matters somewhat, but so that I may understand it better, first try to prove that one may in some case appeal from a heretical pope, and afterwards I will question you further on the same subject. MASTER. Things that are plain (though some have doubted them) must be proved first, so that through them we may arrive at knowledge of what is unknown. So first, taking a most obvious case, it is shown that one may appeal from a heretical pope. DISCIPLE. Set out your case, as a possible one. MASTER. Suppose that someone accuses another before the pope of being a heretic, because he holds and asserts that the Christian faith is false, that the law of the Saracens is to be held, and that Christ was a false prophet and deserves to be condemned. The accusation having been made and the case joined, the pope pronounces a definitive sentence that the accused is not a heretic, because everything he says and asserts contains the truth.

units.la: DISCIP. Quamuis iste casus nunquam contigerit, & nunquam forte euenient; tamen durum mihi videtur asserere, quod sit impossibilis. nam apparet, quod neque ex scriptura diuina, nec ex doctrina ecclesiae potest ostendi aperte, quod nullus papa futurus erit Antichristus: quod etiam de tribu Dan (de qua nonnulli Antichristum aestimant nascituru) multi forte Christiani mediantibus parentibus diuersis ad fidem traxerunt iam dudum originem, de quibus posset procreari Antichristus. Et adhuc posset forte de illa tribu aliquis fidem Christianam suscipere, de quo possit nasci filius, qui primo valeret eligi in summum pontificem: & postea posset se patefacere ostendere Antichristum, & ita nescitur, an aliquis Christianus futurus papa de tribu Dan tracturus originem erit Antichristus. Constat autem, quod Antichristus manifeste docebit, quod lex Christianorum est falsa; & quod Christus fuit falsus propheta. casus autem praedictus non videtur impossibilis, quia nescitur quod nullus papa futurus sectam Saracenorum accipiet. posset enim accidere, quod papa, qui fuisset primo catholicus, inciperet reputare sectam Saracenorum esse meliorem lege Christianorum; qui tantam posset contrahere primo amicitiam occultam cum Saracenis, quod eorum potentia ad se vocata auderet patenter asserere, legem Christianam esse falsam & iniquam, & ad legem Saracenorum suscipiendam cogere Christianos. Cum autem constet, Christianos clericos & religiosos ad sectam Saracenorum fuisse conuersos, non videtur quin etiam posset papa ad tantam infamiam deuenire. Cum enim papa non sit confirmatus in fide, sicut nec caeteri: ideo quantum ad possibilitatem conuertendi se ad Saracenos de ipso & de aliis idem videtur esse tenendum. Posito ergo casu praedicto pro assertione praefata saragas allegare. MAG. Quod a papa praedicto modo haeretico liceat appellare, multis modis ostenditur.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Although this case has never happened and perhaps never will, still it seems harsh to me to assert that it is impossible. For it appears that neither from divine Scripture nor from the teaching of the Church can it be clearly shown that no future pope will be Antichrist. Likewise, from the tribe of Dan (from which some reckon that Antichrist will be born), many Christians, through parents of different descent, have long since drawn their origin to the faith, and from such people Antichrist could be born. And perhaps, again, someone from that tribe might take up the Christian faith, and a son born of him might first be capable of being elected supreme pontiff; and afterwards he could reveal himself and show himself to be Antichrist. So it is not known whether some future Christian pope, deriving his origin from the tribe of Dan, will be Antichrist. It is agreed, however, that Antichrist will openly teach that the law of the Christians is false and that Christ was a false prophet. Nor does the aforesaid case seem impossible, since it is not known that no future pope will embrace the sect of the Saracens. For it could happen that a pope who had at first been Catholic might begin to regard the sect of the Saracens as better than the law of the Christians; and he might at first form so secret a friendship with the Saracens that, once their power was summoned to his side, he would dare to declare openly that the Christian law is false and unjust, and compel the Christians to accept the law of the Saracens. Since it is established that Christian clergy and religious have been converted to the sect of the Saracens, it does not seem that the pope could not also fall into such infamy. For since the pope is not confirmed in the faith, any more than the others are, it seems that the same should be held of him and of others, as regards the possibility of his turning to the Saracens. Therefore, granting the aforesaid case, to support the assertion above I shall adduce reasons. MASTER. That one may appeal from a pope who is heretical in the aforesaid manner is shown in many ways.

units.la: Primo sic: a papa a iure depositus est licitum pro causa fidei appellare, sed propria diffinitione pronuncians, fidem Christianam esse falsam, & legem Saracenorum esse tenendam, est de iure depositus. ergo a tali licet appellare. DISCIP. De isto modo, an scilicet papa haereticus sit ipso iure depositus, post inquiram. ideo aliam rationem inducas. MAG. Secunda ratio talis est: ab omni iudice vel pro iudice se gerente, qui iudicem habet superiorem, licet contra iniquam sententiam ipsius appellare. sed papa diffinitiue pronuncians legem Christianorum esse falsam habet iudicem superiorem. ergo a tali papa licet appellare. Maior ostenditur auctoritate Iulii papae, quae ponitur. 2. q. 6. c. placuit.
units.tr: First, thus: it is lawful to appeal on a matter of faith from a man who has been lawfully deposed; but a pope who by his own definitive sentence pronounces the Christian faith false and the law of the Saracens to be held is deposed by law. Therefore one may appeal from such a man. DISCIPLE. Concerning this way, namely whether a heretical pope is deposed by law itself, I will ask afterwards. So bring forward another argument. MASTER. The second argument is this: from every judge, or from one acting as judge, who has a superior judge, one may appeal against his unjust sentence. But a pope who definitively pronounces the law of the Christians to be false has a superior judge. Therefore one may appeal from such a pope. The major premise is shown by the authority of Pope Julius, which is cited in 2 q. 6 c. placuit,

units.la: qui ait: placuit ut a quibuscumque iudicibus ecclesiasticis, ad alios iudices ecclesiasticos, vbi maior est auctoritas (si prouocatum fuerit) audientia non negetur. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod a minori auctoritate ad maiorem appellare licet. Minor probatur: tum quia omnis haereticus habet iudicem superiorem, cum sit minor omni catholico. 24. q. 1. si autem. Tum quia vniuersalis ecclesia est maior papa, sicut orbis est maior vrbe, di. 93. c. legimus. Tum quia concilium generale est supra papam, ut notatur in Glos. di. 19. Anastasius. Tertio sic: ab illo licet pro causa fidei appellare, qui nec iudex, nec testis, nec accusator in causa fidei vel alia esse potest. hoc patet, quia ab illo, qui se gerit pro iudice, & tamen iudex esse non potest, licet appellare. sed papa pronuncians legem esse falsam, non potest esse iudex, nec testis, nec accusator, quia est haereticus. haeretici autem iudices esse non possunt, cum nihil habet potestatis, aut iuris, 24. q. 1. c. dicimus. nec possunt esse testes, ext. de haeret. c. 1. nec possunt esse accusatores. 2. q. 7. ca. aliani. & c. pagani. & c. non potest. ergo a papa pronunciante legem Christianam esse falsam, appellare licet. Quarto sic: ab omni apostata, qui se pro iudice in causa fidei gerit, licet appellare, saltem si aliter causa fidei vitiata subleuari non potest. sed papa diffinitiue pronuncians fidem Christianam esse falsam, est manifestus apostata a fide Christiana. ergo si gerit se pro iudice in causa fidei, licet appellare ab ipso. Quinto sic: omnis causa vitiata est per appellationis remedium subleuanda, teste Fabiano papa, qui, ut habetur 2. q. 6. c. ait: licet appellare & vitiatam causam appellationis remedio subleuare. & ca. licet, ait: licet in criminalib. causis appellare: nec vox appellandi denegetur ei, qui in suppliciis definiuerit sententia. sed papa diffinitiue pronunciante pro reo lege Christianam esse falsam, causa fidei est apertissime vitiata. ergo licet actori in tali iniqua sententia lata contra fidem catholicam appellare.
units.tr: who says: "It has been resolved that from whatever ecclesiastical judges, to other ecclesiastical judges where the authority is greater, a hearing shall not be denied if appeal has been made." From these words it is gathered that one may appeal from a lesser authority to a greater. The minor premise is proved: first, because every heretic has a superior judge, since he is inferior to every Catholic (24 q. 1 si autem); second, because the universal Church is greater than the pope, as the world is greater than the city (dist. 93 c. legimus); third, because a general council is above the pope, as is noted in the gloss on dist. 19, Anastasius. Thirdly, thus: one may appeal on a matter of faith from one who cannot be judge, witness or accuser in a matter of faith or any other. This is plain, because one may appeal from one who acts as judge but cannot be judge. But a pope pronouncing the law to be false cannot be judge, witness or accuser, because he is a heretic. Heretics cannot be judges, since they have no power or right (24 q. 1 c. dicimus); nor can they be witnesses (Extra, de haeret. c. 1); nor can they be accusers (2 q. 7 c. aliani, c. pagani, c. non potest). Therefore one may appeal from a pope who pronounces the law of the Christians to be false. Fourthly, thus: one may appeal from every apostate who acts as judge in a matter of faith, at least if the cause of faith otherwise cannot be relieved from its defect. But a pope who definitively pronounces the Christian faith false is a manifest apostate from the Christian faith. Therefore, if he acts as judge in a matter of faith, one may appeal from him. Fifthly, thus: every defective cause is to be relieved by the remedy of appeal, as Pope Fabian witnesses, who, as is found in 2 q. 6 c., says: "It is permitted to appeal and to relieve a defective cause by the remedy of appeal." And c. licet says: "It is permitted to appeal in criminal causes, nor is the voice of appealing denied to one whose sentence has been pronounced in matters of punishment." But when the pope, pronouncing definitively against the accused, declares the Christian law to be false, the cause of faith is most obviously defective. Therefore it is lawful for the plaintiff to appeal against such an unjust sentence, given against the Catholic faith.

units.la: DISCIP.
units.tr: DISCIPLE.

units.la: DISC. Per istam rationem liceret à papa pro quacunq; sententia in aliis causis, quam in causa fidei appellare, si omnis causa vitiata per appellationis remedium poterit subleuari. MAG. Respondetur q; omnis causa vitiata per appellationis remedium poterit subleuari, quando ferens iniquā sententiam habet iudicem superiorē. ergo &c. DISC. Video quod haec ratio fundatur in aliis rationibus unde alias rationes adducas. MAG. Sexta ratio talis est. ab eo est licitum p causa haeresis appellare, qui potest de haeresi accusari. sed papa potest de haeresi accusari. ergo licet à papa pro haeresi appellare. DISC. Ista ratio aequaliter probat, quod à papa licet pro omni haeresi appellare, & non solū in casu praedicto. MAG. Omnes rationes allegatae & allegandae secundum rei veritatem concludunt, q à papa haeretico licet appellare, qualicunq; haeresi fuerit maculatus. unde ille casus non est positus, nisi ut rationes potentiores & probabiliores videantur. DISC. Alias rationes adducas. MAG. Septima ratio talis est. ab illo licet appellare, à cuius obedientia licet recedere. sed ab obedientia & à communione papae haeretici pronunciantis legem Christianam esse falsam, licet recedere, exemplo illorum Romanorū, q pro minori excessu, q pro fautoria haereticorum damnatorum à communione & ab obedientia Anastasii etiam laudabiliter sese abegerunt, ut habetur di.19. Anastasius. ergo à papa pronunciante diffinitiue legem Christianam esse falsam, licet appellare. Octauo sic: ab illa sententia licet appellare, quam licet publice impugnare: quia appellare videtur esse quidam modus specialis impugnandi iniquam sententiam. sed sententiam papae pronunciantis fidem Christianam esse falsam, & Christum fuisse falsum prophetam, licet illi, contra quem lata est sententia, sicut & omnibus Christianis, publice impugnare. sicut enim omnibus licet publice confiteri Christum, ipso dicente Matt. 10. omnis ergo qui confitebitur me coram omnibus hominibus, confitebor & ego eum coram patre meo, qui in coelis est: sic licet oēs blasphemos Christi impugnare. papa autem pronuncians legem Christi esse falsam, & Christum falsum fuisse prophetam, est blasphemus Christi, ergo licet cuilibet ipsum impugnare; & per consequens licet ab ipso appellare. Nono sic: ab illo appellare licet, si in causa fidei se pro iudice gesserit, qui in causa fidei iudex esse non debet. sed papa diffinitiue pronuncians Christum falsum fuisse prophetam, nullā debet exercere potentiam in Christianos. Ergo ab eo licet appellare. Maior videtur certa. minor probatur: Quia nullus blasphemus Christi debet exercere potestatem in Christianos, teste Inno. tertio, qui in concilio generali, ut habetur ext. de Iudeis, cum sit, ait: cum sit nimis absurdum, ut blasphemus Christi in Christianos vim potestatis exerceat &c. sed papa diffinitiue pronuncians Christum fuisse falsum prophetam, est blasphemus Christi. ergo in Christianos vim potestatis exercere nō debet. DISC. Ista ratio non videtur concludere, quia Inno. tertius loquitur de Iudaeis. Papa autem, licet pronunciaret Christum falsum fuisse prophetam, non esset propter hoc Iudaeus. ergo per dictum ca. non potest pbari, q non possit in Christianos vim potestatis exercere, quamdiu ab ecclesia toleratur. MAG. Haec tua responsio p hoc excluditur, quod licet Inno. loquitur in illo capit. de Iudaeis, statuens q eis officia publica nullatenus committantur. Statuti tamen sui rationem assignans asserit manifeste, q nullus blasphemus Dei, seu Christi, debet in Christianos vim potestatis exercere. & q ideo Iudaeis non sunt officia publica committenda. vbi autem est eadem ratio, debet esse idem ius. cum ergo papa diffinitiue pronuncians Christum fuisse falsum prophetam, sit manifeste blasphemus Christi: sequitur euidenter, q sicut Iudaei propter hoc, quod sunt blasphemi Christi, non debent in Christianos vim potestatis exercere, ita papa diffinitiue Christum pronuncians falsum prophetam fuisse, propter hoc quod est blasphemus Christi, non debet in Christianos vim potestatis exercere. Decimo sic: ab illo in causa haeresis licite appellatur, si se gerit pro iudice, & iniquā profert sententiam contra fidem, ad quem in causa fidei non licet prouocare. quia ad illum se gerentem pro iudice licite prouocatur, quod ab aliquo appellare non licet. sed ad papam diffinitiue pronunciantem legem Christi esse falsam, & legem Sarracenorum esse tenendam, nequaq; licite prouocatur, cum sint alterius fidei, quam catholici: ad iudicium autem hominis alterius fidei catholicis prouocare non licet, testante consilio Carthaginen. ut habetur 2. q. 6. ca. catholicus: catholicus, qui causam suam siue iustam siue iniustam ad iudicium alterius iudicis prouocat, excommunicetur. ergo ad papam pronunciantem diffinitiue legem Sarracenorum esse tenendam, prouocare non licet, & per consequens licet appellare ab ipso. Vndecimo sic: ab excommunicato pro iudice se gerente licet appellare. sed papa pronuncians diffinitiue fidem Christianam esse falsam, est excommunicatus, sicut & ille, qui incidit in haeresim iam damnatam, teste Glo. 24 q.1. c. qui ait: hic est casus, in quo papa incidit in canonem latae sententiae. ergo ab ipso appellare licet. Duodecimo sic: contra illam sententiam appellare licet, quae nec est tenenda, nec est seruanda, nec timenda; quia illa sententia, à qua non licet appellare, est timenda. sed sententia diffinitiua, qua papa pronunciat legem Christianam esse falsam, nec est seruanda, nec est timenda, nec tenenda, quia sententia contra legem diuinam prolata non est timenda: sicut nec aliquod pactum contra leges Dei est tenendum. ergo à tali sententia appellare licet. Tredecimo sic. ab illo est licitum appellare, qui potest licite recusari. sed pronuncians legem Christianorum esse falsam, in omni causa fidei potest licite recusari. talis autem papa Christianorum omnium & totius legis Christianae esset inimicus manifestus. ergo à tali licet in causa fidei appellare.
units.tr: DISC. By this reasoning, one could appeal from the Pope in any other kind of case, not only in a case of faith, if every case corrupted by an unjust sentence can be relieved by the remedy of appeal. MAG. The answer is that every case corrupted by an unjust sentence can be relieved by appeal when the judge who gives the unjust sentence has a superior judge. Therefore etc. DISC. I see that this reasoning rests on other reasons; bring forward the others. MAG. The sixth reason is this: it is lawful to appeal in a case of heresy from one who can be accused of heresy. But the Pope can be accused of heresy. Therefore it is lawful to appeal from the Pope on account of heresy. DISC. This reasoning equally proves that one may appeal from the Pope for any heresy whatever, and not only in the case just mentioned. MAG. All the reasons already alleged, and those still to be alleged, rightly conclude that one may appeal from a heretical Pope, whatever heresy he is stained with. That case has therefore been put only so that the reasons may appear stronger and more probable. DISC. Bring forward other reasons. MAG. The seventh reason is this: one may appeal from one whose obedience it is lawful to renounce. But it is lawful to withdraw from the obedience and communion of a Pope who pronounces the Christian law to be false, as the Romans did, who, for a lesser offence than this, that is, for favouring condemned heretics, rightly cut themselves off from the communion and obedience of Anastasius, as is recorded in Dist. 19, "Anastasius." Therefore one may appeal from a Pope who definitively pronounces the Christian law to be false. The eighth reason: one may appeal from a sentence which may be openly opposed, because appealing seems to be a particular way of opposing an unjust sentence. But it is lawful for the one against whom a sentence is pronounced, as for all Christians, to oppose publicly a Pope who pronounces the Christian faith false and Christ to have been a false prophet. For just as everyone may publicly confess Christ, since he himself says in Matt. 10, Everyone therefore who shall confess me before men, I will confess him also before my Father who is in heaven, so it is lawful to oppose all blasphemers of Christ. But a Pope who pronounces the law of Christ false, and Christ to have been a false prophet, is a blasphemer of Christ. Therefore it is lawful for anyone to oppose him, and consequently it is lawful to appeal from him. The ninth reason: one may appeal from a man who has acted as judge in a case of faith when he ought not to be judge in a case of faith. But the Pope, who definitively pronounces that Christ was a false prophet, ought not to exercise any power over Christians. Therefore one may appeal from him. The major premise seems certain. The minor is proved thus: no blasphemer of Christ ought to exercise power over Christians, as Pope Innocent III testifies in the general council, as recorded in the Decretals, De Iudaeis, cum sit, where he says: since it is most absurd that a blasphemer of Christ should exercise the force of power over Christians, etc. But a Pope who definitively pronounces that Christ was a false prophet is a blasphemer of Christ. Therefore he ought not to exercise the force of power over Christians. DISC. This argument does not seem to conclude, because Innocent III is speaking of Jews. A Pope, however, even if he pronounced that Christ was a false prophet, would not on that account be a Jew. Therefore from the said chapter it cannot be proved that he could not exercise the force of power over Christians, so long as the Church tolerates him. MAG. Your answer is refuted by this, that although Innocent speaks in that chapter about Jews, ruling that public offices must by no means be entrusted to them, yet in giving the reason for his ruling he plainly asserts that no blasphemer of God or of Christ ought to exercise the force of power over Christians, and that therefore public offices are not to be entrusted to Jews. Where the reason is the same, the right must be the same.
