Ad secundam dicitur, quod sententiarum, quæ non possunt transire in rem iudicatam, duplex differentia reperitur. quædam enim est sententia talis, à qua si non appellat ille, contra quam fuerit lata, eo ipso ipse parere censetur. talis est sententia lata contra fidem. & ideo à tali sententia necesse est appellare, ne is, contra quem fertur, fautor prauitatis hæreticæ reputetur. Alia est sententia, quæ transire non potest in rem iudicatam: cui tamen ille, contra quem fertur, non censetur parere, licet non appellaret. & à tali sententia non est necesse appellare. & de tali est sermo in decretis. 2. q. 6. diffinitiua. Ad tertiam respondetur consimiliter, quod in illa causa, contra quam non potest præscriptio currere, non est necesse appellare: nisi ille, contra quem fertur, sensetur parere ex hoc, quod non appellat. talis autem est causa fidei. ideo si feratur iniqua sententia contra fidem, necesse est appellare, ne non appellans favere hæresi iudicetur. Ad quartam respondetur, quod causa fidei est magis priuilegiata, quam causa matrimonii: & ideo non semper est necesse appellare. Et per hoc patet responsio etiam ad quintam rationem.
units.tr: Disciple. The arguments by which it is shown that it is not necessary to appeal from the sentence of a Pope who pronounces definitively that the Christian faith is false seem to me as weighty as the arguments alleged for the contrary position. I therefore ask you to set out how each side is answered. Yet first answer the arguments proving that appeal is not necessary. Master. To the first of these it is said that there is no need to appeal from a sentence passed against the laws and canons, because this is provided for in law. But it is not provided for in law that there is no need to appeal from a sentence of the Pope pronouncing the law of Christ to be false. To the second it is said that there is a twofold difference among sentences which cannot pass into res judicata. For there is one kind of sentence from which, if he against whom it was passed does not appeal, he is by that very fact considered to submit to it. Such is a sentence passed against the faith, and therefore it is necessary to appeal from such a sentence, lest he against whom it is passed be regarded as a supporter of heretical depravity. There is another sentence which cannot pass into res judicata, yet he against whom it is passed is not considered to submit to it even if he does not appeal; and from such a sentence there is no need to appeal. And it is of such a sentence that the decretals speak, 2. q. 6, definitive. To the third it is answered similarly that in a case against which prescription cannot run, there is no need to appeal, unless he against whom it is passed is deemed to submit by the very fact that he does not appeal. But a case of faith is such a case. Therefore, if an unjust sentence is passed against the faith, it is necessary to appeal, lest one who does not appeal be judged to favour heresy. To the fourth it is answered that a cause of faith is more privileged than a cause of marriage, and therefore it is not always necessary to appeal. And by this the reply to the fifth argument is also made plain.

units.la: CAP. XXX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXX.

units.la: Ponit responsiones ad rationes 28. capituli probantes, quod necesse sit in forma, quem appellare etiam infra tempus statutum à iure à sententia Papæ haretici.
units.tr: Gives the replies to the arguments of chapter 28, which prove that a person must appeal, even within the time fixed by law, from a sentence of the Pope pronounced against a heretic.

units.la: DIscIP. Istæ responsiones videntur mihi valde debiles: quas tamen pro nunc nolo amplius pertractari, imo dic quomodo ad rationes in contrarium respondetur. MAG. Ad primam respondetur, quod quando sententia transit in rem iudicatam (nisi fuerit appellatione suspensa) tunc qui à sententia iniqua infra tempus statutum à iure absq; causa rationabili neglexerit appellare, per interpretationem iuris latæ sententiæ parere videtur. Sed quando sententia iniqua nullo modo potest transire in rem iudicatam, nec aliquo modo potest firmitatem sententiæ obtinere, ille, qui à tali sententia non appellat, non intelligitur per interpretationem iuris parere eidem. talis est sententia Papæ lata contra fidem: quia nullo modo potest transire in rem iudicatam, nec unquam potest aliquis per talem sententiam obligari, imo non est necesse appellare: sed sufficit absque verbo appellandi vel facto pro loco & tempore sententiam detestari. & eo ipso intelligitur quis eidem sententiæ dissentire; & talis dissensus loco appellationis est habendus. Ad secundam dicitur, quod remedium appellationis est ad præsidium innocentiæ institutum, quando aliter quam per appellationem non potest innocentia esse tuta. Sed quando innocentia potest aliter esse secura, quam per remedium appellationis, non est simpliciter necessaria appellatio: licet nonnunquam possit esse vtilis, etiam licet innocentia possit esse aliter tuta. nunc autem innocentia catholici, contra quæ Papa pronunciaret legem Christianam esse falsam, aliter quam per appellationis remedium potest esse tuta: quia de iure talis sententia ipsum nequit aliquo modo ligare. ideo de iure sufficit catholico absq; verbo appellandi talem sententiam verbo vel facto impugnare, & ei nullatenus obedire. DIscIP. Quid si de facto catholicus non est tutus, nisi appellaret à tali sententia Papæ. MAG. In hoc casu tenetur propter defensionem fidei & suæ innocentiæ appellare, si enim taliter damnatu à Papa alii Christiani nollent defendere, nisi vocem appellationis emitteret, necesse esset quod appellaret, non quod de iure teneatur, sed quia aliter de facto tutus esse non potest. Ad tertiâ respondetur, quòd si quis debet uti aliquo, utendum est eo ad illum usum, ad quem institutum est. medicina enim instituta est ad sanitatem consequendam. & imo qui debet uti medicina, debet uti ipsa ad sanitatem consequendâ: non tamen debet quis omni tempore uti medicina intentione sanitatis consequendæ, quia hoc sæpe esset impedimentum sanitatis, & inductiuum infirmitatis. sic qui debet uti appellatione, debet uti ipsa, ut ab oppressione releuetur, vel ne irrationabiliter opprimatur. non tamen est necesse semper uti appellationis remedio, si alio modo ab oppressione quis valeat releuari, & imo ab iniqua sententia Papæ pronunciantis fidem Christianam esse falsam non est absolute necesse appellare: licet in casu quando oppressus aliter releuari non posset, esset appellare necesse.
units.tr: STUDENT. These replies seem to me very weak; yet for now I do not want them discussed further. Rather, tell me how the arguments to the contrary are answered. MASTER. To the first it is answered that when a sentence becomes res iudicata (unless it has been suspended by appeal), then one who, within the time fixed by law and without reasonable cause, has neglected to appeal from an unjust sentence is understood by interpretation of law to submit to it. But when an unjust sentence can in no way become res iudicata, nor in any way obtain the force of a sentence, the one who does not appeal from such a sentence is not understood by interpretation of law to submit to it. Such is a sentence of the Pope pronounced against the faith: for it can in no way become res iudicata, and no one can ever be bound by such a sentence; indeed, there is no need to appeal, but it is enough, without any word or act of appeal, to detest the sentence by word or deed, according to place and time. By that very fact one is understood to dissent from the sentence, and such dissent is to be held in place of appeal. To the second it is said that the remedy of appeal was instituted as a protection of innocence, when innocence cannot be kept safe except through appeal. But when innocence can be kept safe otherwise than by the remedy of appeal, appeal is not absolutely necessary, although at times it may be useful even though innocence could be kept safe in another way. Now, however, the innocence of a Catholic, against whom the Pope would pronounce that the Christian law is false, can be kept safe otherwise than by the remedy of appeal, because by law such a sentence cannot bind him in any way. Therefore, by law, it is enough for a Catholic, without any word of appeal, to oppose such a sentence by word or deed and in no way to obey it. STUDENT. What if, in fact, a Catholic is not safe unless he appeals from such a sentence of the Pope? MASTER. In this case he is bound, for the defence of the faith and of his innocence, to appeal; for if, having been so condemned by the Pope, other Christians were unwilling to defend him unless he uttered the word of appeal, it would be necessary for him to appeal, not because he is bound by law, but because otherwise he cannot be safe in fact. To the third it is answered that if someone ought to use something, it must be used for the purpose for which it was instituted. For medicine was instituted to obtain health; and indeed, one who ought to use medicine ought to use it to obtain health; yet one ought not to use medicine at all times with the intention of obtaining health, because this would often be an obstacle to health and an inducement to sickness. So too, one who ought to use appeal ought to use it so as to be relieved from oppression, or lest he be oppressed unreasonably. Yet it is not always necessary to use the remedy of appeal, if one can be relieved from oppression in another way; and indeed, from an unjust sentence of the Pope declaring the Christian faith to be false, it is not absolutely necessary to appeal, although in the case where the oppressed person could not otherwise be relieved, appeal would be necessary.

units.la: CAP. XXXI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXI.

units.la: Capitulum 31. probat, quod appellare cuilibet Christiano à Papa sententiam hæreticam proferente licet, quatuor rationibus.
units.tr: Chapter 31 proves, by four arguments, that any Christian may appeal to a higher authority from a sentence pronounced by the Pope that is heretical.

units.la: DIscIP. Postquam asseruisti, quantum volui, an ille, contra quem Papa diffinitiuam fert sententiam, quod lex Christiana est falsa, posset licite appellare à tali iniqua sententia, & ibidem recitasti, quod licet cuilibet Christiano à tali sententia appellare: sed motiua illius assertionis minime adduxisti, ideo rogo vt eandem assertionem fulcire nitaris. MAG. Quod cuilibet Christiano à tali sententia licet appellare, videtur multis modis posse probari. Primo sic: à sententia lata contra alium licet cuilibet appellare, cui per talem sententiam fit præiudicium manifestum, extra de sent. & re iudic. c. cum super. sed per sententiam Papæ (quod lex Christiana est falsa) latam contra alium fit cuilibet Christiano præiudicium manifestum quia cum teste apostolo vna sit fides omnium, sententia lata contra fidem est in præiudicium cuiuslibet Christiani: ergo à tali sententia lata contra alium licet Christiano cuilibet appellare.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Since you have shown at length, as I wished, that someone against whom the Pope pronounces a definitive sentence that the Christian law is false may lawfully appeal from such an unjust sentence, and since you stated there that any Christian may appeal from such a sentence, you have not yet offered the grounds for that assertion. So I ask you to make an effort to support it. MASTER. That any Christian may appeal from such a sentence can be proved in many ways. First, as follows. Anyone may appeal from a sentence passed against another person if the sentence causes him manifest prejudice (Extra, De sententia et re iudicata, c. Cum super). But a sentence of the Pope, passed against another person, that the Christian law is false, causes manifest prejudice to every Christian. For, as the Apostle witnesses, there is one faith for all, so a sentence passed against the faith is to the prejudice of every Christian. Therefore any Christian may appeal from such a sentence passed against another.

units.la: DIscIP. Non videtur, quod per talem sententiam aliis præiudicium generetur: quia res inter alios acta, aliis non nocet in multis casibus, secundum quod Glossa notat extra de fid. instrum. cap. inter dilectos. ergo sententia iniqua contra fidem lata contra aliquem, aliis catholicis non nocet: & per consequens non interest eorum à tali sententia appellare.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. It does not seem that such a sentence causes prejudice to others, because a matter transacted between others does not harm those who are not parties in many cases, as the Gloss notes (Extra, De fide instrumentorum, c. Inter dilectos). Therefore an unjust sentence against the faith, passed against one person, does not harm other Catholics, and consequently it is not in their interest to appeal from such a sentence.

units.la: MAG. Respondetur, quod illa regula, Res inter alios acta, aliis non nocet, fallit in multis casibus, secundum quod Glossa notat, & de sent. & re iudic. cap. quamuis, nocet enim, vt ibid. dicit Glossa cum causa sunt connexa, & per consequens multo magis, cum causa est vna & eadem: cuiusmodi est causa fidei, quæ omnibus est communis. & imo cum fides catholica condemnatur, omnibus catholicis præiudicium generatur. quare omnibus licet (si voluerint) à tali sententia appellare. DIscIP. Alia motiua adducas.
units.tr: MASTER. It is answered that the rule, "a matter transacted between others does not harm those who are not parties," fails in many cases, as the Gloss notes (De sententia et re iudicata, c. Quamvis). For it does harm when the causes are connected, as the same Gloss says there, and so much more when the cause is one and the same. Such is the cause of the faith, which is common to all. Indeed, when the Catholic faith is condemned, prejudice is caused to all Catholics. Hence it is lawful for all of them, if they wish, to appeal from such a sentence. DISCIPLE. Bring forward your other grounds.

units.la: MAG. Secundo sic arguitur. cuilibet licet (appellando & defendendo) suam prosequi iniuriam. sed per talem iniquam sententiam Papæ cuilibet catholico fit iniuria. ergo cuilibet licet à tali sententia appellare. Tertio sic vnusquisq; catholicus magis tenetur defendere fidem catholicam, quam filios consanguineos vel parentes, quia fides est illis omnibus præferenda. ergo non minus licet appellare, seu prouocare pro fide catholica condemnata, quam pro patente filio vel consanguineo condemnato. Sed mulier, licet non possit pro filio agere, pro filio tamen condemnato licet appellare. 1.quaest.6.cap.non solent, vbi sic dicitur: quod si mulier ex pietate prouocauerit, dicendum est hanc audiri debere. vbi dicit Gloss. super verbo pro filio: pro filio condemnato, pro consanguineo possunt appellare alii. ergo multo magis pro fide catholica condemnata, licet cuilibet Christiano catholico appellare seu prouocare.
units.tr: MASTER. Secondly, the argument runs thus. Anyone may (by appealing and defending himself) pursue his own wrong. But by such an unjust sentence of the Pope every Catholic suffers a wrong. Therefore it is lawful for anyone to appeal from such a sentence. Thirdly, every Catholic is more bound to defend the Catholic faith than his children or his parents, because the faith is to be preferred to all of them. Therefore it is no less lawful to appeal, or to call for review, on behalf of the condemned faith than on behalf of a condemned son or kinsman. But a woman, although she may not act on behalf of a son, may nevertheless appeal on behalf of a condemned son (C. 1, q. 6, c. Non solent), where it is said: "If a woman out of piety has appealed, it must be held that she ought to be heard." Where the Gloss says, on the words pro filio: "On behalf of a condemned son, or of a kinsman, others may appeal." Therefore, much more on behalf of the condemned Catholic faith, it is lawful for any Catholic Christian to appeal or call for review.

units.la: Quarto sic: non minus licet appellare a sententia inferente iniuriam, quae maxime est a catholicis vindicanda, quam a sententia inferente iniuriam, quae minus est a catholicis vindicanda. quia appellatio vel est vindicta quaedam, vel via quaedam ad vindictam inferendam. sed iniuria illata per sententiam iniquam Papae diffinitiue pronunciantis legem Christianam esse falsam, est magis vindicanda a catholicis, quam quaecunque iniuria propria alicui illata per sententiam iudicis inserioris. ergo si licet appellare a sententia iudicis inferioris iniqua, qua sententiatur, aliquem esse priuandum bonis suis temporalibus, vel puniendum in persona, multo magis licet cuilibet catholico appellare a sententia Papae pronunciantis legem Christianam esse falsam. Maior istius rationis apparet. Minor (scilicet quod iniuria illata per talem sententiam Papae magis vindicanda est, &c.) probatur, quia illa est iniuria Christi & Dei directe. iniuria autem Dei est magis vindicanda quam propria, teste beato Gregorio, qui, vt habetur 23.quaest.4.cap.si is, sic air: Si is qui praelatus est dominico debitori culpas impune dimittit, non mediocriter profecto offendit, qui debita coelestis regis & domini sua praesumptione resoluit. ea namque, quae in nobis committuntur, facile possumus dimittere: ea vero quae in Deum commissa sunt, cum magna discretione, nec tamen sine poenitentia possumus relaxare. Et Chrysostomus super Matth. ait: In propriis iniuriis esse quempiam patientem laudabile est: iniurias autem Dei dissimulare, nimis est impium. Augustin. etiam, vt habetur 23.quaest.4.cap.si ea, ait: Si ea de quibus vehementer offenditur Deus, insequi vel vlcisci differimus, ad iracscendum vtique deitatis patientiam prouocamus. Ex quibus patet, quod iniuria Dei est praecipue & magis, quam propria vindicanda. & ita si licet a sententia inferioris iudicis inferente iniuriam propriam appellare, multo magis licet a sententia inferente Deo iniuriam (cuiusmodi est sententia illa Papae, qua condemnatur fides catholica) appellare.
units.tr: Fourthly, it is no less lawful to appeal from a sentence inflicting an injury which Catholics ought most of all to avenge than from a sentence inflicting an injury which Catholics ought less to avenge. For an appeal is either a kind of vengeance or a way of inflicting vengeance. But the injury inflicted by an unjust sentence of the Pope, who definitively pronounces that the Christian law is false, is more to be avenged by Catholics than any private injury inflicted on someone by the sentence of a lower judge. Therefore, if it is lawful to appeal from an unjust sentence of a lower judge, by which someone is sentenced to be deprived of his temporal goods or punished in his person, then much more is it lawful for any Catholic to appeal from a sentence of the Pope pronouncing that the Christian law is false. The major premise of this argument is evident. The minor premise (namely, that an injury inflicted by such a sentence of the Pope is more to be avenged, etc.) is proved as follows: that injury is directly an injury to Christ and to God. But an injury to God is more to be avenged than a private one, as witnessed by blessed Gregory, who says (C. 23, q. 4, c. Si is): "If a prelate who is set over the Lord's debtors lets their faults go unpunished, he surely offends not a little, since by his presumption he dissolves the debts owed to the heavenly King and Lord. For the wrongs committed against us we can readily forgive; but those committed against God we may remit only with great discernment, and not without penance." And Chrysostom on Matthew says: "It is praiseworthy for someone to be patient in his own injuries; but to overlook injuries to God is extremely impious." Augustine also, as is found in C. 23, q. 4, c. Si ea, says: "If we delay in pursuing or avenging the things by which God is gravely offended, we surely provoke the patience of the Deity to anger." From these things it is clear that an injury to God is to be avenged above all and more than one's own. And so, if it is lawful to appeal from the sentence of a lower judge who inflicts a private injury, much more is it lawful to appeal from a sentence which inflicts an injury on God, such as that sentence of the Pope by which the Catholic faith is condemned.

units.la: CAP. XXXII.
units.tr: CAP. XXXII.

units.la: Dat tres instantias contra assumpta in ratione quarta capituli praecedentis, vbi etiam notatur quorum interest iniuriam vindicare.
units.tr: Gives three objections against the premises assumed in the fourth argument of the preceding chapter, where it is also noted who has an interest in avenging an injury.

units.la: DISCIP. Haec vltima ratio tripliciter videtur deficere. Primo: quia auctoritates non loquuntur de omnibus Christianis, sed tantummodo de praelatis, qui debent Dei iniuriam vindicare. Secundo, quia si concluderet, probaretur per illam, quod necesse esset cuilibet catholico a tali sententia appellare, sicut quilibet catholicus tenetur iniuriam Dei vindicare. Tertio, quia ex ipso sequeretur, quod quilibet criminosus excommunicatus & infamis, potest propriam insequi iniuriam. ergo multo magis iniuriam illatam Deo, si ratio procedit. Haec sunt, quae rationem illam impedire videntur. tu autem dic qualiter potest responderi ad ipsa.
units.tr: DISCIPULUS. This last argument seems to fail in three ways. First, because the authorities do not speak of all Christians, but only of prelates, who ought to avenge the injury done to God. Second, because if it were a valid conclusion, it would follow from it that every Catholic would have to appeal from such a sentence, just as every Catholic is bound to avenge the injury done to God. Third, because from the same premise it would follow that any criminal, excommunicated and infamous person may pursue his own injury; therefore, much more the injury done to God, if the argument holds. These are the things which seem to hinder that argument. But you, Master, say how these points can be answered.

units.la: MAG. Ad primam istarum posset aliquis dicere, quod superius auctoritates allegatae insinuant iniuriam esse vindicandam a praelatis: etiam manifestant, quod omnes catholici inquantum licet & expedit pro gradu & officio vniuscuiusque debent iniuriae illatae Deo occurrere. Et ideo appellare ab iniqua sententia non solum conuenit praelatis, sed etiam subditis. eo enim ipso, quod praelati debent iniuriam Dei vindicare, licebit subditis, sed plus non possunt vel statui eorum non competit a tali sententia appellare, quia minus est appellare, quam vindictam exercere. si ergo praelati debent vindictam exercere in eos, qui iniuriantur Deo, licebit eis a tali sententia appellare. Ad secundam dicitur, quod per dictam rationem non probaretur, quod aliquis teneatur a tali sententia appellare; nisi quando non potest conuenienter aliter, quam appellando, tali iniquae sententiae obviare. & in hoc casu conceditur, quod necesse est a tali sententia appellare. nec intendunt illi, qui dicunt, non esse necesse appellare a tali sententia iniqua, quod in nullo casu fit necesse appellare: sed non est regulariter necesse appellare ab aliqua sententia iniqua: quia quando regulariter est necesse appellare, hoc est, ne talis sententia transeat in rem iudicatam. ob hanc autem causam nunquam est necesse appellare a sententia lata contra fidem. sed ob aliam causam potest alicui incumbere necessitas appellandi: puta si aliter propter maliciam vel negligentiam vel imperitiam aliorum vel ob aliam causam non posset talem sententiam iniquam impugnare. Ad tertiam potest dici, quod si non esset alius, quam criminosus & infamis, qui vellet causam fidei prosequi contra Papam pronunciantem, fidem Christi esse falsam, criminosis & infamibus liceret a tali sententia appellare, & prosequi suam appellationem, essentq; tales audiendi. Idemq; posset dici de inimicis in fauorem fidei Christianae. tales tamen ad testificandum non essent aliquatenus admittendi. si autem essent alii boni famae & non inimici, non essent praedicti audiendi, si a tali sententia appellarent. & tamen essent audiendi, si propriam prosequerentur iniuriam: quia non essent alii, qui eorum prosequerentur iniuriam.
units.tr: MAGISTER. To the first of these one might say that the authorities cited above do indeed indicate that the injury is to be avenged by prelates, but they also make clear that all Catholics, insofar as it is lawful and expedient, must according to the rank and office of each one oppose the injury done to God. And so appealing from an unjust sentence belongs not only to prelates but also to subjects. For by the very fact that prelates ought to avenge the injury done to God, it will be permitted to subjects too; but they may not do more, nor does it befit their station to appeal from such a sentence, since appealing is less than exercising vengeance. If therefore prelates ought to exercise vengeance against those who injure God, it will be lawful for them to appeal from such a sentence. To the second it is said that the said argument would not prove that anyone is bound to appeal from such a sentence, except when he cannot suitably oppose such an unjust sentence in any way other than by appealing. And in this case it is granted that it is necessary to appeal from such a sentence. Nor do those who say that it is not necessary to appeal from such an unjust sentence mean that it is never necessary to appeal in any case; but it is not generally necessary to appeal from any unjust sentence, because it is generally necessary to appeal when the sentence would otherwise pass into a judgment that cannot be challenged. For this reason, however, it is never necessary to appeal from a sentence pronounced against the faith. But for another reason a necessity to appeal may fall upon someone: for example, if otherwise, owing to the malice or negligence or inexperience of others, or for some other cause, he could not challenge such an unjust sentence. To the third it may be said that if there were no one other than a criminal and infamous person who wished to pursue the cause of the faith against a Pope pronouncing that the faith of Christ is false, then criminals and infamous persons would be allowed to appeal from such a sentence and to pursue their appeal, and such persons would have to be heard. The same could be said of enemies, in favour of the Christian faith. Such persons, however, are not to be admitted to give testimony in any way. But if there were others of good repute and not enemies, the aforesaid persons would not have to be heard if they appealed from such a sentence. And yet they would have to be heard if they pursued their own injury, because there would be no others to pursue their injury for them.

units.la: CAP. XXXIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXIII.

units.la: In quo ponitur quæstio, si liceat appellare à sententia quacunque Papæ hæretica, ad quam respondetur sub duplici opinione. & secundam prosequitur, scilicet quod ab omni sententia Papæ, qualemcunque hæresim contineat, sive damnatam explicite, sive implicite, licet appellare. & probatur quatuor rationibus.
units.tr: In which the question is raised whether it is lawful to appeal from any heretical sentence of the Pope, to which an answer is given under a twofold opinion. And it follows the second, namely that from every sentence of the Pope, whatever heresy it contains, whether condemned explicitly or implicitly, it is lawful to appeal. And this is proved by four arguments.

units.la: DISCIP. Satis disputauimus, an licet a sententia Papæ appellare, si diffinitiue pronunciaret contra catholicos fidem Christianam esse falsam. ideo ad interrogationem aliam me conuerto, an à sententia quacunque Papæ qualemcunque hæresim continente liceat appellare. vnde de hoc vnam vel plures narra sententias. MAG. Tenentes, quod nunquam licet appellare a Papa, dicerent, quod nulli liceret a tali sententia appellare. Alii autem dicerent, quod ab omni sententia Papæ (qualemcunque hæresim contineat, sive damnatam explicite, sive solummodo implicite) licet appellare. DISCIP. Pro ista secunda sententia nitaris allegare. MAG. Quod a tali sententia liceat appellare, sic probatur. ab omni sententia Papæ licet appellare, quam licitum est impugnare. Sed talem sententiam licet impugnare: quia licet omnem hæresim damnatam explicite vel implicite impugnare. ergo a tali sententia licet appellare.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. We have disputed enough whether it is lawful to appeal from a sentence of the Pope if he should define and pronounce against Catholics that the Christian faith is false. So I turn to another question: whether it is lawful to appeal from any sentence of the Pope containing whatever heresy. Tell me one or more opinions on this. MASTER. Those holding that it is never lawful to appeal from the Pope would say that no one may appeal from such a sentence. Others, however, would say that from every sentence of the Pope (whatever heresy it contains, whether condemned explicitly or only implicitly) it is lawful to appeal. DISCIPLE. You seem to want to argue for this second opinion. MASTER. That it is lawful to appeal from such a sentence is proved thus: it is lawful to appeal from every sentence of the Pope which it is lawful to attack. But it is lawful to attack such a sentence, because it is lawful to attack every heresy, whether condemned explicitly or implicitly. Therefore it is lawful to appeal from such a sentence.

units.la: Secundo sic: idem videtur esse in paruis, quod in magnis. extra de præben. cap. maioribus. & 24. q. vltima. c. fi. ergo idem iuris est in hæresi quæ videtur maxima, & in hæresi quæ videtur parua. sed a Papa diffinitiue pronunciante & declarante maximam hæresim esse tenendam (quod fides Christiana videlicet esset falsa) licet appellare. ergo a Papa pronunciante quamcunque hæresim cuicunque catholicæ veritati aduersantem esse tenendam licet appellare. Tertio sic: idem iuris est in parte, quod in toto. ergo idem iuris est de hæresi, quæ partem fidei catholicæ videtur destruere, & de hæreti quæ totam negat catholicam fidem. sed a Papa pronunciante totam fidem Christi esse falsam licet appellare. ergo a Papa pronunciante quamcunque hæresim cuicunque catholicæ veritati aduersantem esse tenendam, licet appellare. Quarto sic: ratio, quare a Papa pronunciante fidem Christianam esse falsam, licet appellare, est, quia talis Papa est hæreticus & destruit catholicam fidem. sed Papa pronuncians diffinitiue quamcunque hæresim esse tenendam, est hæreticus & destruit catholicam fidem. vbi autem est eadem ratio, debet esse idem ius. ergo a Papa quamcunque hæresim pronunciante diffinitiue esse tenendam licet appellare. Pro ista assertione possunt adduci rationes supra c. 18. inductæ: quia illæ probant, quod ab omni Papa hæretico licet appellare, quamuis patentius quodammodo concludant, quod a Papa pronunciante fidem catholicam Christianam esse falsam, licet appellare, &c.
units.tr: Secondly, thus: the same seems to hold in small matters as in great. Extra, De praebendis, chapter Maioribus; and 24 q. last, c. fin. Therefore the same law holds for a heresy which seems very great as for one which seems small. But it is lawful to appeal from the Pope when he defines and declares the greatest heresy to be held (namely that the Christian faith is false). Therefore it is lawful to appeal from the Pope when he pronounces that any heresy opposed to any Catholic truth is to be held. Thirdly, thus: the same law holds for a part as for the whole. Therefore the same law holds for a heresy which seems to destroy part of the Catholic faith and for a heretic who denies the whole Catholic faith. But it is lawful to appeal from the Pope when he pronounces the whole faith of Christ to be false. Therefore it is lawful to appeal from the Pope when he pronounces that any heresy opposed to any Catholic truth is to be held. Fourthly, thus: the reason why it is lawful to appeal from the Pope when he pronounces the Christian faith to be false is that such a Pope is a heretic and destroys the Catholic faith. But a Pope who defines that any heresy whatever is to be held is a heretic and destroys the Catholic faith. Where the reason is the same, the law ought to be the same. Therefore it is lawful to appeal from a Pope who defines that any heresy whatever is to be held. For this assertion the arguments adduced above in chapter 18 can be brought forward: for those prove that it is lawful to appeal from every heretical Pope, although in a somewhat more open way they conclude that it is lawful to appeal from a Pope who pronounces the Christian Catholic faith to be false, etc.

units.la: CAP. XXXIV.
units.tr: CAP. XXXIV.

units.la: Inquirit, si Papa non pronunciaret aliquam hæresim diffinitiue sed tantummodo prædicaret vel doceret publice, vtrum ab ipso liceat appellare, & notatur ibi de hæresi, cuius oppositum tenetur quis explicite vel implicite credere: & hoc in responsione.
units.tr: He inquires whether, if the Pope does not define some heresy as such but merely preaches or teaches it publicly, one may appeal from him; and here it is noted concerning heresy, the contrary of which one is bound to believe either explicitly or implicitly: and this is in the answer.

units.la: DISCIP. Ex prædictis aduertro quod secundum istos non refert ad hoc, quod liceat ab hæretico appellare, an Papa diffinitiue pronunciat fidem Christianam esse falsam, vel quamcunque hæresim, quæ fidei obuiat orthodoxæ; quamuis etiam plures tenerent, talem assertionem fidei catholicæ nullatenus repugnare. MAG. Verum dicis, quia indubitanter tenent, quod cum hæresis quantumcunque à Christianis etiam eruditis & in scriptura sacra peritis reputetur catholica, est à quolibet catholico scienti eam veritati contrariari catholicæ impugnanda, & ideo licet omni catholico à Papa pronunciante diffinitiue quamcunque hæresim esse tenendam appellare. DISCIP. Quid si Papa non pronunciat diffinitiue aliquam hæresim esse tenendam, sed publice docet & tenet vel prædicat aliquam hæresim esse tenendam: nunquid appellare licet ab ipso?
units.tr: DISCIPULUS. From what has been said above, I observe that according to these men it makes no difference to the question whether one may appeal from a heretic whether the Pope defines that the Christian faith, or any heresy opposed to the orthodox faith, is false; although many would hold that such an assertion does not in any way contradict the Catholic faith. MAGISTER. You say truly, for they hold without doubt that whenever a heresy, however much it is regarded as Catholic by Christians, even learned ones and those skilled in Holy Scripture, is contrary to Catholic truth, it is to be attacked by any Catholic who knows it; and therefore every Catholic may appeal from the Pope when he defines any heresy as something to be held. DISCIPULUS. What if the Pope does not define that some heresy is to be held, but publicly teaches, holds or preaches that some heresy is to be held: may one appeal from him?

units.la: MAG. Respondetur, quod appellare licet; qualiter tamen & quando liceat appellare oportet attendere diligenter. aut enim Papa docet, prædicat, dogmatizat, aut asserit hæresim contrariam veritati catholicæ, quam tenetur explicite tenere, & tunc statim licet appellare non solum à doctrina iniqua, etiam à docente tanquam hæretico: quia talis Papa sine examinatione maiori est hæreticus reputandus. Si enim Papa asserit non esse in diuinis tres personas distinctas, tamen tenetur explicite credere Patrem & Filium & spiritum Sanctum esse distinctas personas; statim Papa censendus est hæreticus. Aut Papa prædicat vel dogmatizat hæresim contrariam veritati, quam non tenetur explicite credere: puta si prædicaret Dauid non fuisse filium Isay, vel Ieroboam non fuisse regem Israel: & tunc non est statim appellandum à Papa. Sed si de assertione oritur scandalum, est subtiliter indagandum, an paratus sit corrigi suam assertionem reuocando. Si autem non est paratus corrigi, tunc licet appellare, impugnando videlicet doctrinam hæreticam & docentem hæresim, si fuerit pertinax deprehensus.
units.tr: MAGISTER. The answer is that one may appeal; yet how and when one may appeal must be considered carefully. For either the Pope teaches, preaches, dogmatizes or asserts a heresy contrary to Catholic truth, which one is bound to hold explicitly, and then one may at once appeal, not only from the wicked doctrine but also from the teacher as a heretic, because such a Pope is to be reckoned a heretic without any further examination. For if the Pope asserts that there are not three distinct persons in the divine nature, although one is bound to believe explicitly that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are distinct persons, the Pope is at once to be judged a heretic. Or the Pope preaches or dogmatizes a heresy contrary to the truth which one is not bound to believe explicitly: for example, if he were to preach that David was not the son of Jesse, or that Jeroboam was not king of Israel; and then one must not appeal from the Pope at once. But if offence arises from the assertion, it must be carefully investigated whether he is ready to be corrected by retracting his assertion. If, however, he is not ready to be corrected, then one may appeal, namely by attacking the heretical doctrine and the teacher of heresy, if he is found obstinate.

units.la: CAP. XXXV.
units.tr: CAP. XXXV.

units.la: Capitulum 35. dat vnam instantiam probando, quod ab ipso non sit appellandum propter talem dogmatizationem, ad quam etiam respondetur ibidem, vbi etiam notatur, qualis possit esse vel fieri talis appellatio.
units.tr: Chapter 35 gives one instance, proving that one should not appeal from the Pope himself on account of such teaching; this is also answered in the same place, where it is further noted what kind of appeal such an appeal could be or become.

units.la: DISCIP. Non videtur, quod in hoc casu sit appellandum à Papa: sed magis videtur, quod accusandus est Papa. nam appellatio seu prouocatio vel fit à iudice, vel se gerente pro iudice, vel fit extra iudicium, ne aliquid fiat in praeiudicium appellantis super eo quod appellat. Sed primo modo non est appellandum à Papa, si docet aut praedicat haereticam prauitatem: quia docendo, vel praedicando non tenet locum iudicis, nec se gerit pro iudice, sed se gerit pro doctore, vel praedicatore, vel assertore. Nec secundo modo est in hoc casu appellandum à Papa: quia talis appellatio est respectu alicuius futuri ne fiat, sicut quando aliquis appellat, ne electio aliqua fiat in praeiudicium appellantis, talis appellatio respicit electionem futuram, ne videlicet fiat. sed assertio Papae haeretica, quam praedicauit, aut docuit, est praeterita. ergo à Papa taliter praedicante non est appellandum secundo modo.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. It does not seem that in this case one should appeal from the Pope; rather, it seems that the Pope is to be accused. For an appeal or challenge is made either by a judge, or by one acting as judge, or outside of judgment, so that nothing is done to the prejudice of the appellant regarding the matter appealed. But in the first way, one may not appeal from the Pope if he teaches or preaches heretical depravity, because in teaching or preaching he does not hold the place of a judge, nor does he act as a judge, but acts as a teacher, preacher, or asserter. Nor in this case is one to appeal from the Pope in the second way, because such an appeal concerns something future, so that it may not happen: as when someone appeals so that some election may not be made to the prejudice of the appellant, such an appeal looks to the future election, that it may not take place. But the heretical assertion of the Pope, which he preached or taught, is past. Therefore one should not appeal from the Pope, while preaching in this way, in the second manner.

units.la: MAG. Dicunt nonnulli, sicut tactum est prius, quod non intendunt loqui de appellatione stricte, secundum quod in iure positivo accipitur, quando dicunt, quod non licet appellare à Papa docente haereticam prauitatem: sed intendunt loqui de appellatione largissime, secundum quod omnis impugnatio facto vel verbo Papae docentis haereticam prauitatem, potest dici appellatio, & isto modo licet appellare à Papa haeresim praedicante: quia licet cuilibet catholico talem haeresim impugnare, & Papa, si fuerit pertinax, accusare. DISCIP. Isti loquuntur improprie, cum dicunt: quod omnis impugnatio Papae potest dici appellatio, quia manifestum est, quod omnis accusatio est impugnatio, accusatio autem distinguitur ab appellatione. ergo non omnis impugnatio est appellatio. MAG. Isti, prout dixi, de proprietate locutionis in hac materia non curant. DISCIP. Quare? MAGIST. Quia, vt dixi prius, non reputant esse necessarium absolute appellare, quantum est de iure, in quocunque casu ab haretico Papa vel haeresim praedicante, notando appellationé, quando verbum appellandi emittitur. sed si quis voluerit vocare appellationem, omnem impugnationem Papae haeretici, sic dicunt quod necesse est appellare. si autem dicat quis, quod non sit vtendum appellatione in isto sensu, de verbis contendere nolunt. & imo in hoc sistunt, quod Papa praedicans haeresim praedicto modo est à catholicis impugnandus.
units.tr: MASTER. Some say, as was touched on before, that they do not intend to speak of appeal strictly, in the sense in which it is taken in positive law, when they say that one may not appeal from a Pope teaching heretical depravity; rather they intend to speak of appeal in the very broad sense, in which every challenge, by deed or word, to a Pope teaching heretical depravity can be called an appeal, and in this way one may appeal from a Pope preaching heresy, since it is permitted to any Catholic to challenge such heresy and to accuse the Pope, if he is found obstinate. DISCIPLE. These men speak improperly when they say that every challenge to the Pope can be called an appeal, since it is plain that every accusation is a challenge, but accusation is distinguished from appeal. Therefore not every challenge is an appeal. MASTER. These men, as I said, do not care about the proper use of language in this matter. DISCIPLE. Why? MASTER. Because, as I said before, they do not think it absolutely necessary, by law, in any case against a heretical Pope or one preaching heresy, to appeal, marking the appeal when the word "appeal" is uttered. But if someone wishes to call every challenge to a heretical Pope an appeal, they say that it is then necessary to appeal. If, however, someone says that the word appeal should not be used in that sense, they are unwilling to quarrel over words. Indeed, they insist on this: that a Pope preaching heresy in the aforesaid manner is to be challenged by Catholics.

units.la: CAP. XXXVI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXVI.

units.la: In quo proponitur talis quaestio, si Papam haereticum impugnantes sint à catholicis defendendi, & respondetur sub duplici opinione. Prima probatur in hoc capitulo duabus rationibus. Secunda probatur capitulo 37, huius nouem rationibus.
units.tr: In which the following question is put: whether Catholics are to defend those who attack a heretical Pope; and the answer is given under a twofold opinion. The first is proved in this chapter by two arguments; the second is proved in chapter 37 by nine arguments.

units.la: DISCIP. Ex praemissis intelligo, quod dicentium, licere catholicis appellare à Papa haeretico: Dicunt quidam, quod non est necesse verbum appellandi emittere, licet aliquando expediat. Quidam vero dicunt, quod hoc est necesse. Primi autem diuersas patiuntur difficultates notabiles propter varias significationes, quas nomini appellationis attribuunt. omnes autem praedicti in hoc conueniunt, quod omnem doctrinam Papae haereticam licet fidelibus impugnare. imo omisso vocabulo appellationis & appellantis, volo in quibusdam interrogationibus, quas tibi de materia praecedenti proponam, vti vocabulo impugnationis & impugnantis. In primis autem interrogo, an impugnantes Papam haereticum sint à catholicis aliis defendendi, etiam contra Papam taliter impugnantes punire volentem.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. From what has been said above I understand that those who say it is lawful for Catholics to appeal from a heretical Pope say different things. Some say that it is not necessary to use the word "appeal," although at times it is expedient; others say that it is necessary. The first group, however, labour under notable difficulties because of the various meanings they attach to the word "appeal." All of them, however, agree that it is lawful for the faithful to attack any heretical teaching of the Pope. Indeed, leaving aside the terms "appeal" and "appellant," I wish to use the terms "attack" and "one who attacks" in some questions which I shall put to you on the preceding matter. First, then, I ask whether those who attack a heretical Pope are to be defended by other Catholics, even against the Pope if he wishes to punish those who thus attack him.

units.la: MAGIST. Circa hanc interrogationem sunt assertiones contrariae. vna est, quod impugnantes Papam haereticum, qui verbum appellandi nequaquam emittunt, non sunt à catholicis defendendi. Alia est contraria, scilicet quod sunt à catholicis defendendi.
units.tr: MASTER. On this question there are contrary assertions. One is that those who attack a heretical Pope, without ever uttering the word "appeal," are not to be defended by Catholics. The other, the contrary, is that they are to be defended by Catholics.

units.la: DISCIP. Pro istis assertionibus contrariis te libenter audio allegare. MAGIST. Prima assertio videtur posse probari tali ratione. Maius est defendere impugnantes Papam haereticum, quam eorum impugnationi differre. sed catholici non tenentur differre impugnationi Papae haretici, nisi impugnantes interposuerint appellationem legitimam. ergo nec tenentur talitet impugnantes defendere. Secundo sic: per impugnationem non eximitur impugnans à iurisdictione praelati, quem impugnat, sed propter appellationem legitimam eximitur appellans à iurisdictione praelati, à quo appellat. ergo per solam impugnationem Papae haretici non eximitur impugnans à iurisdictione Papae: sed per appellationem Papae eximitur, catholici autem non debent defendere contra Papam, nisi solos exemptos à iurisdictione Papae. ergo licet tenentur defendere appellantes, non tamen tenentur defendere impugnantes, qui non appellant.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. I gladly hear you put forward arguments for these contrary assertions. MASTER. The first assertion seems capable of being proved by the following argument. It is a greater thing to defend those who attack a heretical Pope than to defer to the attack of a heretical Pope. But Catholics are not bound to defer to the attack of a heretical Pope unless those who attack him have lodged a lawful appeal. Therefore neither are they bound to defend such attackers. Secondly, thus: by an attack the attacker is not freed from the jurisdiction of the prelate whom he attacks; but by a lawful appeal the appellant is freed from the jurisdiction of the prelate from whom he appeals. Therefore by the mere attack on a heretical Pope the attacker is not freed from the jurisdiction of the Pope; but by an appeal from the Pope he is freed. Catholics, however, ought to defend against the Pope only those who are exempt from the Pope's jurisdiction. Therefore, although they are bound to defend appellants, they are not bound to defend those who attack without appealing.

units.la: Cap.
units.tr: Chapter.

units.la: DIALOGVS. CAP. XXXVII.
units.tr: DIALOGUE. CHAPTER XXXVII.

units.la: In quo ponitur & probatur secunda opinio, 9. rationibus probans, quod impugnantes Papam haereticum debitis circumstantiis, licet non appellent, sunt à catholicis defendendi.
units.tr: In which the second opinion is set out and proved by nine arguments: that those who attack a heretical Pope, provided the circumstances are right, are to be defended by Catholics even though they do not appeal.

units.la: DISCIP. Sufficiant istae allegationes pro assertione praedicta. ideo pro contraria allegare conabor. MAGIST. Quod omnes impugnantes Papam haereticum circumstantiis debitis, licet non appellent, sunt à catholicis defendendi, videtur multis rationibus posse probari. Est autem prima ratio talis: qui secrete & rite legitime causam omnium fidelium prosequuntur, sunt ab omnibus fidelibus defendendi: qui enim negocium alicuius gerit utiliter, auxilium & favorem ab eo meretur: aliter enim erit ingratus & nequam, non reddens bonum pro bono. Sed impugnantes Papam haereticum, causam omnium fidelium prosequuntur: quia causa fidei est causa omnium catholicorum. ergo sunt ab omnibus catholicis defendendi. Secundo sic: magis tenentur catholici & fideles defendere prosequentes causam fidei, quae est causa omnium, quam teneatur Papa defendere illos, qui causas proprias prosequuntur. sed Papa debet defendere illos, qui causas proprias prosequuntur, teste Zepherino Papa, qui, ut habetur 2. q. 6. c. ad Romanam, sic: ad Romanam Ecclesiam maxime ab oppressis est appellandum & concurrendum quasi ad matrem, ut eius uberibus nutriantur, & auctoritate defendantur, & a suis oppressionibus releventur. ergo multo magis impugnantes Papam haereticum, ad quoscunque concurrerint orthodoxos, sunt ab eis defendendi. Tertio sic: magis sunt defendendi à catholicis impugnantes haereticam pravitatem (ne propter impugnationem huiusmodi patiatur) quam sint socii à sociis. sed socius socium debet defendere, teste Ambrosio, qui in libro de officiis, ut legitur 23. q. 3. c. non inferenda, ait: qui non repellit à socio iniuriam (si potest) tam est in vitio quam ille qui facit. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod socius socium debet contra iniuriantem defendere. ergo multo magis catholici debent impugnantes haereticam pravitatem (ne propter impugnationem huiusmodi iniuriam patiantur) defendere. Quarto sic: non minus tenentur catholici defendere impugnantes haereticam pravitatem, quam Ecclesia teneatur defendere scelerator & impios, qui ad eam confugiunt, cum boni magis defendendi sunt quam mali. sed Ecclesia tenetur defendere malos fugientes ad ipsam, 17. q. 4. c. frater vester. & c. sicut. Et in multis aliis decretis sanctorum patrum idem habetur. ergo multo magis catholici tenentur defendere impugnantes haereticam pravitatem.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Let these allegations be enough for the assertion above. So I will try to bring forward arguments for the opposite view. MASTER. That all who attack a heretical Pope, under due circumstances and even without appealing, are to be defended by Catholics, can be proved by many arguments. The first argument runs like this: those who pursue the cause of all the faithful, secretly and properly and lawfully, are to be defended by all the faithful. For whoever carries on another's business to good effect deserves help and favour from him; otherwise he would be ungrateful and wicked, not returning good for good. But those who attack a heretical Pope pursue the cause of all the faithful, because the cause of the faith is the cause of all Catholics. Therefore they are to be defended by all Catholics. Secondly, thus: Catholics and the faithful are more bound to defend those who pursue the cause of the faith, which is the cause of all, than the Pope is bound to defend those who pursue their own causes. But the Pope is bound to defend those who pursue their own causes, as Pope Zephyrinus witnesses, who says, as it is found in 2 q. 6 c. Ad Romanam: To the Roman Church those oppressed must appeal and resort above all, as to a mother, that they may be nourished at her breasts, be defended by her authority, and be relieved from their oppressions. Therefore, much more, those who attack a heretical Pope, wherever they have resorted to orthodox men, are to be defended by them. Thirdly, thus: those who attack heretical wickedness are more to be defended by Catholics (lest they suffer injury on account of such an attack) than companions are to be defended by their companions. But a companion ought to defend a companion, as Ambrose witnesses, who in his book On Duties, as it is read in 23 q. 3 c. Non inferenda, says: He who does not repel an injury from a companion, if he can, is as much at fault as the one who does it. From these words it is gathered that a companion ought to defend a companion against one who injures him. Therefore, much more, Catholics ought to defend those who attack heretical wickedness (lest on account of such an attack they suffer injury). Fourthly, thus: Catholics are bound to defend those who attack heretical wickedness no less than the Church is bound to defend wicked and impious criminals who flee to her, since good men are more to be defended than bad. But the Church is bound to defend evil men fleeing to her, 17 q. 4 c. Frater vester and c. Sicut. And the same is found in many other decrees of the holy Fathers. Therefore, much more, Catholics are bound to defend those who attack heretical wickedness.

units.la: DISCIP. Quod Ecclesia defendat malos fugientes ad ipsam, est ex privilegio speciali, quale non habent impugnantes haereticam pravitatem. MAG. Haec responsio impugnatur, quia ubi est eadem ratio, debet esse idem ius. sed ratio, quare Ecclesia defendit malos fugientes ad ipsam, est ut honor Ecclesiae conservetur. 17. q. 4. c. reum. honor autem Ecclesiae, & utiliter omnium catholicorum, & etiam Dei magis conservatur per defensionem impugnantium haereticam pravitatem, quam per defensionem malorum quantumcunque, ad Ecclesiam confugerint. ergo magis defendendi sunt, quam tales mali praedicti. DISCIP. Alias rationes adducas. MAG. Quinto videtur probari posse eadem assertio sic: fides catholica magis defendenda est, quam patria. unusquisque autem debet defendere patriam, iuxta illud Catonis: Pugna pro patria, &c. cui Ambrosius concordat primo de officiis, qui, ut legitur 23. quaest. tertia, cap. fortitudo. ait: Fortitudo, quae bello tuetur à barbaris patriam, vel domi defendit infirmos, vel à latronib. socios, plena iustitia est. ergo multo magis fides catholica est ab omnibus catholicis defendenda. non autem defenditur fides, nisi defensentur impugnantes haereticam pravitatem. ergo omnes catholici pro loco & tempore impugnantes haereticam pravitatem debent defendere. Sexto sic: hoc debet quilibet catholicus impugnantibus Papam haereticum facere, sine quo dilectio Dei & proximi non habetur. sed absque defensione impugnantium Papam haereticum dilectio Dei & proximi non habetur. quod non dilectio Dei, patet: quia quod non fit impugnantibus Papam haereticum propter Deum, non fit Deo, iuxta illud Christi Matth. 25. Quam diu non fecistis uni de minoribus istis, nec mihi fecistis. ubi Christus asserit manifeste, quod opera misericordiae, quae non fiunt suis fidelibus, intelliguntur non fieri sibi: propter quorum omissionem impii deputabuntur aeternis supplicis. ergo defensio, quae non exhibetur impugnantibus Papam haereticum, intelligitur non exhiberi Deo. qui autem non exhibet defensionem debitam honori divino, Deum non diligit: ergo qui non defendit impugnantes haereticam pravitatem, caret dilectione divina. nec etiam habetur dilectio proximi, si impugnantes haereticam pravitatem minime defenduntur: quia qui proximo in sua necessitate non subvenit, charitatem proximi minime habet; impugnantes autem Papam haereticum, maxime indigent defensione. ergo qui eos negligunt defendere, charitatem ad ipsos nullatenus habent.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. That the Church defends evil men fleeing to her arises from a special privilege, which those who attack heretical wickedness do not have. MASTER. This answer is refuted, because where the reason is the same, the right ought to be the same. But the reason why the Church defends evil men fleeing to her is so that the honour of the Church may be preserved (17 q. 4 c. Reum). But the honour of the Church, and the advantage of all Catholics, and also of God, is preserved more by defending those who attack heretical wickedness than by defending evil men, however many, who have fled to the Church. Therefore they are more to be defended than those evil men just mentioned. DISCIPLE. Bring forward other arguments. MASTER. Fifthly, the same assertion seems capable of proof thus: the Catholic faith is to be defended more than one's country. Now each person ought to defend his country, according to that saying of Cato: Fight for your country, etc., with which Ambrose agrees in the first book On Duties, which, as it is read in 23 q. 3, c. Fortitudo, says: Fortitude, which in war protects the country from barbarians, or at home defends the weak, or protects companions from robbers, is full justice. Therefore, much more, the Catholic faith is to be defended by all Catholics. But the faith is not defended unless those who attack heretical wickedness are defended. Therefore all Catholics, according to place and time, ought to defend those who attack heretical wickedness. Sixthly, thus: every Catholic ought to do this for those who attack a heretical Pope, without which the love of God and of neighbour is not present. But without the defence of those who attack a heretical Pope, the love of God and of neighbour is not present. That the love of God is not present is plain: because what is not done for those who attack a heretical Pope for God's sake is not done to God, according to that saying of Christ in Matthew 25: As long as you did not do it to one of these least, you did not do it to me. Where Christ plainly asserts that works of mercy which are not done to his faithful ones are understood not to be done to him, and on account of their omission the impious will be consigned to eternal punishments. Therefore the defence which is not given to those who attack a heretical Pope is understood not to be given to God. But he who does not give the defence due to the divine honour does not love God. Therefore he who does not defend those who attack heretical wickedness lacks the divine love. Nor is love of neighbour present if those who attack heretical wickedness are not defended at all, because he who does not help his neighbour in his need does not have love for his neighbour; but those who attack a heretical Pope have the greatest need of defence. Therefore those who neglect to defend them have no love for them whatsoever.

units.la: Septimo sic arguitur. non defendere Christum, & non defendere discipulos Christi veritatem catholicam nunciantes, ad idem genus criminis pertinet: sic spernere Christum & spernentes discipulos Christi. sed spernere Christum & spernere discipulos Christi ad culpam spectat consimilem, ipso Christo testante, qui, ut habetur Lucae 10. dixit discipulis suis: Qui vos spernit, me spernit. hoc etiam patet: quia non defendere alium est quidam modus specialis contemnendi. qui enim non defendit, spernit. non defendere enim, quem quis potest, ex contemptu procedit: sicut defendere ex amore procedit. sed omnes catholici Christum debent defendefendere, quando possunt, testante Augustin. qui turbam asserit graviter deliquisse, quia Christum, cum duceretur ad mortem, non defendit. qua, vt habetur 23. quaest. 3. ostendit Propheta, nec illos immunes esse a scelere, qui permiserunt principibus Christum interficere: & cum pro multitudine timerentur, & possent illos a facto & se a consensu liberare, ergo etiam illi, qui discipulos Christi veritatem catholicam nunciantes non defendunt, non sunt immunes a scelere reputandi. tales autem sunt discipuli Christi Papam haereticum impugnantes, qui veritatem profitentur catholicam. ergo tales sunt ab omnibus catholicis defendendi.
units.tr: Seventhly, the argument goes thus. Not to defend Christ and not to defend the disciples of Christ who proclaim the Catholic truth belong to the same kind of crime, just as to despise Christ and to despise the disciples of Christ do. But to despise Christ and to despise the disciples of Christ pertains to a like guilt, Christ himself testifying, who, as it is found in Luke 10, said to his disciples: He who despises you despises me. This is also plain, because not to defend another is a certain special mode of contempt. For he who does not defend, despises. For not to defend someone whom one can defend proceeds from contempt, just as to defend proceeds from love. But all Catholics ought to defend Christ when they can, as Augustine testifies, who asserts that the crowd gravely sinned because it did not defend Christ when he was led to death; which, as it is found in 23 q. 3, the Prophet shows, nor are those free from crime who allowed the princes to kill Christ; and although they were feared because of the multitude, and could have freed themselves from the deed and from consent. Therefore, those too who do not defend the disciples of Christ who proclaim the Catholic truth are not to be reckoned free from crime. But such are the disciples of Christ who attack a heretical Pope, who profess the Catholic truth. Therefore such are to be defended by all Catholics.

units.la: Octauo: qui miseriae alicuius compatitur, subuenit sibi, & defendit eum cum potest. sed sanum membrum & verum corporis Christi mystici compatitur alteri membro in periculo constituto: cum videamus iuxta Apostolum, quod si quid patitur vnum membrum corporis naturalis, compatiuntur omnia membra, 1. ad Corinth. 12. ergo si aliqui patiuntur propter impugnationem catholicae veritatis, omnia membra sana corporis Christi mystici compatiuntur eisdem, & per consequens eis subueniunt, & ipsos defendunt, si possunt.
units.tr: Eighthly: whoever sympathises with another's misery helps him and defends him when he can. But a sound member and a true member of the mystical body of Christ sympathises with another member placed in danger, since we see, according to the Apostle, that if one member of the natural body suffers, all the members suffer with it, 1 Corinthians 12. Therefore, if some suffer on account of the attack on Catholic truth, all the sound members of the mystical body of Christ suffer with them, and consequently help them and defend them, if they can.

units.la: Nono sic: Opera misericordiae sunt omnibus impendenda. ergo defensio (cum sit opus misericordiae) est omnibus impendenda. & per consequens defensio impugnantibus Papam haereticum est praestanda.
units.tr: Ninthly, thus: works of mercy are to be bestowed on all. Therefore defence (since it is a work of mercy) is to be bestowed on all. And consequently the defence of those who attack a heretical Pope is to be rendered.

units.la: CAP. XXXVIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXVIII.

units.la: Ponit quatuor instantias contra rationem nonam capituli immediate precedentis, scil. as- serentis, quod opera misericordiae omnibus sint impendenda, quae solvun- tur capitulo immediate sequenti.
units.tr: It sets out four objections against the ninth reason of the immediately preceding chapter, namely the assertion that works of mercy are to be bestowed on all people; these objections are answered in the immediately following chapter.

units.la: DISCIP. Peristam rationem probaretur, quod impugnantes catholicam fidem vel veritatem, essent a catholicis defendendi, quia opera misericordiae non solum bonis, sed etiam malis oportet catholicos exhibere. cum ergo defensio sit opus misericordiae, oportet catholicos defensare haereticos veritatem catholicam impugnantes. Item, opera misericordiae nequaquam cadunt sub praecepto (tunc enim qui non daret eleemosynam, aut non redimeret captivos, peccaret mortaliter) si ergo defensio est opus misericordiae: catholici ad talem defensionem de necessitate salutis minime astringuntur. Amplius, sicut punire delinquentes pertinet solummodo ad iudices seculares vel ecclesiasticos: ita defendere bonos ad superiores & potestates publicas noscitur pertinere. ergo non ad omnes catholicos pertinet defendere Papam haereticum.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. If the reason I gave were to be proved, namely that Catholics ought to defend those who attack the Catholic faith or truth, it would be because works of mercy must be shown by Catholics not only to the good but also to the wicked. Therefore, since defence is a work of mercy, Catholics must defend heretics who attack Catholic truth. Likewise, works of mercy do not at all fall under a precept (for then whoever did not give alms, or did not ransom captives, would sin mortally); so if defence is a work of mercy, Catholics are by no means bound to such defence by necessity of salvation. Furthermore, just as punishing offenders belongs only to secular or ecclesiastical judges, so defending the good is known to belong to superiors and public authorities. Therefore it does not belong to all Catholics to defend the heretical Pope.

units.la: Rursus, oppressorum defensio exhibetur, cum illatae vel inferendae iniuriae pulsantur. (sed iniurias propulsare ad viros perfectos minime pertinet: tum quia prima veritas talibus ait, Matth. 5. Ego autem dico vobis non resistere malo: tum quia armis iniuria propulsatur, viris autem persectis, sicut clericis, non licet arma movere. ergo saltem ad viros perfectos minime spectat impugnantes Papam haereticum defendere. Ista sunt, quae rationem factam de operibus misericordiae & nonnullas alias (vt mihi videtur) impediunt. ideo quomodo respondetur ad ea, gestio scire.
units.tr: Again, the defence of the oppressed is exercised when injuries that have been inflicted or are about to be inflicted are repelled. (But repelling injuries does not belong at all to perfect men: first, because the first Truth says to such men, Matt. 5: "But I say to you, do not resist evil"; second, because injury is repelled by arms, and it is not lawful for perfect men, such as clerics, to take up arms.) Therefore, at least for perfect men, it by no means pertains to defending those who attack the heretical Pope. These are the things which, as it seems to me, hinder the argument made from works of mercy and several others. I long therefore to know how these objections are answered.

units.la: CAP. XXXIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXIX.

units.la: Ponit responsiones ad obiectiones precedentis capituli, vbi etiam ponuntur 3. valde notanda, & quomodo malis impendenda sunt opera misericordiae, & qui & quando teneantur homines ad opera misericordiae.
units.tr: It gives answers to the objections of the preceding chapter, where three things worth noting are also set out, and how works of mercy are to be bestowed on the wicked, and who and when people are bound to works of mercy.

units.la: MAGIST. Dicunt nonnulli, quod istae obiectiones tuam insipientiam manifestant, & quod non intelligis assertionem praedictam, ostendunt. Ad cuius euidetiam tria debent esse notanda, quorum primum est: quod sicut diuersa sunt opera iustitiae, quorum quaedam omnibus subditis & praepositis possunt congrue convenire: sicut cum subditus siue praepositus alienum habet de necessitate iustitiae restituere habet, nisi ex causa rationali excusetur. Quaedam vero sunt opera iustitiae, quae non conveniunt omnibus, sed solum praepositis: sicut iudicare iuste non competit nisi superiori. Sic sunt quaedam opera misericordiae & beneficientiae, quae omnibus competere possunt, sicut orare, intercedere pro aliquo, & nonnulla alia. quaedam vero sunt opera misericordiae, quae non omnibus competere debent, cuiusmodi est opus nonnunquam alios armis defendere. Secundo dicunt esse notandum, quod licet praecepta affirmativa obligent semper, non tamen pro semper, & ideo semper remanet quilibet obligatus ad opera misericordiae, quae sibi competunt proximis exhibenda; non tamen tenetur quilibet talia opera misericordiae omni tempore exercere: sed hoc loco & tempore oportunis aliis circumstantiis debite observatis. Tertio dicunt esse notandum, quod multis modis potest quis defendere. vno modo armis violentiae resistendo, alio modo, verbis pro alio allegando vel impugnare nolentes verbis exhortatoriis, praeceptoriis vel prohibitoriis seu aliis quibuscunque a violentia reprehendendo: alio modo, occultando vel non prodendo, aut in domum vel locum tutum recipiendo: aliisq; modis pluribus, quos longum esset enarrare, conuenit alios defendere. DISCIP. Narra, quomodo ad obiectiones meas per ista notabilia respondetur. MAG. Ad primam dicunt, quod quamuis interdum etiam oporteat malis opera miserimisericordiæ exhibere; non tamen opera omnia misericordiæ sunt omnibus malis & impiis exhibenda. Intercedere enim apud iudicem pro puniendis reis, est opus misericordiæ: & tamen pro sceleratis incorrigibilib. liberandis nullus intercedere debet. 23. q. 4. c. est iniusta. & ideo licet haereticis impugnantibus catholicam veritatem sint quaedam opera misericordiæ impendenda, defensio tamen, quæ in fauorem haereticæ prauitatis, vel in præiudicium fidei Christianæ potest aliqualiter redundare, est omnino substrahenda: quæ tamen catholicis Papam haereticum impugnantibus in fauorem fidei orthodoxæ à fidelibus est præbenda. Ad secundam potest dici, quod omnia opera misericordiæ pro aliquo tempore cadunt sub præcepto, quemadmodum amor proximi, ex quo omnia opera misericordiæ procedere debent, cadit sub præcepto. & ideo defensio impugnantium Papam haereticum circumstantiis debitis obseruatis, cadit sub præcepto, licet tale præceptum non intelligitur pro omni tempore obligare. DISCIP. Pro quo tempore secundum istos obligat hoc præceptum? MAG. Respondetur, quod sicut dare eleemosynam tenetur de necessitate ille, qui potest, cum ex parte indigentis apparet euidens & vrgens necessitas, nec scit alium, quem probabiliter credit velle & posse necessitate habenti iuxta indigentiam subuenire: sic tunc tenetur quilibet, qui potest modo defensionis sibi congruo & possibili impugnantes Papam haereticum defendere, quando tali defensione necessario indigent, nec apparet alius, qui eis velit & possit tutionem impendere. sicut etiam quando imminet periculum fidei, essent praelatiá subditis arguendi, & fides catholica esset fideliter confitenda. sic quando ex omissione defensionis impugnantium Papam haereticum, periculum fidei immineret, vel subtraheretur honor Dei, essent impugnantes Papam haereticum ab omnibus, qui possunt, si non appareret alius, qui eos protegeret, defendendi. & quicunque eis in aliquo casu, videlicet praedictorum, defensionem debitam denegaret in peccatum mortale, & fautoriam prauitatis haereticæ laberetur, nec possent aliqui, nisi per solam impotentiam, excusari.
units.tr: MASTER. Some say that these objections reveal your foolishness and show that you do not understand the aforesaid assertion. To make its clarity evident, three points must be noted. The first is this: just as the works of justice are diverse, some of which can suitably belong to all subjects and superiors alike (for example, when a subject or superior is under an obligation of justice to make restitution of what belongs to another, unless he is excused by a reasonable cause), while some works of justice do not belong to everyone but only to superiors (for example, to judge justly belongs only to a higher authority), so too there are some works of mercy and beneficence that can belong to all, such as praying and interceding for someone and several others, while there are some works of mercy that ought not to belong to everyone, of which kind is sometimes the work of defending others by arms. Second, they say it must be noted that, although affirmative precepts always bind, they do not bind for always. Therefore everyone always remains bound to the works of mercy that are due to his neighbours, yet no one is bound to exercise every such work of mercy at all times, but only in this place and at this time, with other circumstances duly observed. Third, they say it must be noted that one can defend in many ways: by resisting violence with arms; in another way, by pleading for another with words, or by rebuking, with words of exhortation, command or prohibition, or with any other means, those who are unwilling to be attacked by violence; in another way, by concealing or not betraying, or by receiving into a house or a safe place; and by many other means, which would take too long to recount, it is fitting to defend others. DISCIPLE. Tell me how, by means of these points, my objections are answered. MASTER. To the first they say that although it sometimes behoves one to show works of mercy even to the wicked, yet not all works of mercy are to be shown to all the wicked and impious. For to intercede before a judge for the punishment of criminals is a work of mercy, and yet no one ought to intercede for the liberation of incorrigible criminals (23. q. 4. c. est iniusta). And therefore, although certain works of mercy are to be bestowed on heretics who attack catholic truth, the defence which could in some way redound to the favour of heretical depravity or to the prejudice of the Christian faith must be entirely withheld; yet that defence, which is to be given by the faithful to catholics who attack the heretical Pope, is given in favour of the orthodox faith. To the second it can be said that all works of mercy fall under a precept for some time, just as love of neighbour, from which all works of mercy ought to proceed, falls under a precept. And therefore the defence of those who attack the heretical Pope, with the due circumstances observed, falls under the precept, although such a precept is not understood to bind at all times. DISCIPLE. According to them, for what time does this precept bind? MASTER. It is answered that just as the one who is able is bound of necessity to give alms when the need of the one in want is plain and pressing, and he knows no other whom he reasonably believes willing and able to help the needy according to their want, so then everyone who is able is bound, by a means of defence suitable and possible for him, to defend those who attack the heretical Pope whenever they stand in necessary need of such defence, and no other appears who is willing and able to give them protection. Likewise, when danger to the faith threatens, prelates should be rebuked by their subjects, and the catholic faith should be faithfully confessed. So too, when through the omission of defence the danger to the faith would threaten, or the honour of God would be taken away, those who attack the heretical Pope should be defended by all who are able, if no other appears who would protect them. And whoever in any such case, namely those mentioned, denies due defence to them commits mortal sin and falls into favouring heretical depravity, and no one can be excused except by sheer inability.

units.la: DISCIP. De ista in septimo huius inquiram. ideo refer, quomodo ad aliam instantiam respondetur.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. I will inquire into this in the seventh part of this book. So tell me how the other objection is answered.

units.la: MAG. Ad illam instantiam respondetur seu dicitur, quod aliquod genus defensionis solummodo pertinet ad iurisdictionem habentes; quemadmodum ad eosdem pertinet tantummodo regulariter petere, plectere delinquentes: sed praeter talem defensionem, sicut dictum est in tertio notabili suprascripto, sunt multi alii modi defendendi Papam haereticum impugnantes, qui aliis à iudicibus competere possunt. Saepe enim aliqui à violentiis aliorum solum precibus defenduntur. Unde de tali modo defensionis habetur dist. 87. c. eos, vbi sic legitur: eos, qui ad Ecclesiam consugiunt, tradi non oportet, sed loci sancti reverentia & intercessione defendi. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod nonnunquam eo ipso, quod aliqui non traduntur, vel pro eis intercedit, defenduntur. multis etiam aliis modis potest quis defendi, qui non solum ad iurisdictionem habentes, sed etiam ad quoscunque alios pertinere noscuntur. possunt ergo catholici nullam iurisdictionem habentes, & etiam maiores multis modis defendere Papam haereticum impugnantes. quia interdum non tradendo, occultando ab eorum persecutione verbis molestantes multifariis revocando, & aliis modis quos longum esset enarrare. Et per idem respondetur ad quartam: quia praeter defensionem, quae fit armis, multi sunt alii modi defendendi impugnantes praedictos. cum vero accipis, quod iniuriam propulsare ad viros perfectos minime pertinet: negatur de multis modis iniuriam propulsandi. & cum allegas auctoritatem Christi, respondetur secundum August. super Ioan. vt legitur 23. q. 1. c. paratus, quod dictum Christi præceptum magis est ad præparationem cordis, quam ad opus. cum autem dicis, quod armis iniuria propulsatur, verum dicis: sed praeter istum modum pulsandi iniuriam sunt multi alii, viris perfectis & clericis congruentes.
units.tr: MASTER. To that objection it is answered, or said, that one kind of defence belongs only to those who hold jurisdiction, just as it belongs to them alone, as a rule, to demand and punish offenders. But apart from such defence, as was said in the third point noted above, there are many other ways of defending those who attack the heretical Pope, and these can belong to others besides judges. For often some are defended from the violence of others by prayers alone. Hence concerning this kind of defence we read in dist. 87, c. eos, where it is written thus: those who flee to the Church are not to be handed over, but are to be defended by reverence for the holy place and by intercession. From these words it is gathered that sometimes people are defended simply by the fact that they are not handed over, or that someone intercedes for them. Many other ways too exist by which one may be defended, which are known to pertain not only to those holding jurisdiction but also to anyone whatever. Therefore Catholics who hold no jurisdiction, and even the greater ones, can defend those who attack the heretical Pope in many ways: because sometimes by not handing them over, by concealing them from their persecution, by rebuking their harassers with words, by recalling them, and by other means which would take too long to describe. And the same answer serves for the fourth objection: since, apart from the defence that is made by arms, there are many other ways of defending the aforesaid attackers. As for your claim that repelling injury is in no way proper to perfect men, it is denied, since there are many ways of repelling injury. And when you cite the authority of Christ, it is answered, following Augustine on John, as is read in 23. q. 1. c. paratus, that the precept of Christ concerns the preparation of the heart rather than the work. As for your saying that injury is repelled by arms, you speak truly; but besides that way of repelling injury there are many others, fitting for perfect men and for clergy.

units.la: CAP. XL.
units.tr: CHAPTER XL.

units.la: In quo assignatur alia ratio, quae est 10. pro opinione secunda cap. 37. recitata, probans quod quilibet catholicus taliter impugnantes tenetur de necessitate salutis defendere modo sibi possibili, & ista ratio sumitur ex his, quae dicta sunt in capitulo 39. vbi respondebatur ad obiectiones per tria notanda, & alia ibidem dicta.
units.tr: In which another argument is set out, the tenth, for the second opinion recited in chapter 37, proving that every Catholic is bound, of necessity to salvation, to defend in whatever way is possible for him those who attack the Pope in such a manner; and this argument is drawn from what has been said in chapter 39, where replies to the objections were given under three points to be noted, along with other things said there.

units.la: DISCIP. Considero ex praedictis, quod isti largissime nomine defensionis vtuntur, cum dicunt, quod impugnantes Papam haereticum sunt à catholicis defendendi. & ideo magis quam priusassertionem praedictam intelligo. adhuc tamen vellem scire; si amplius, quam prius, saepe dicta assertio explicatur.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. From what has been said I consider that these men use the word "defence" very broadly when they say that those who attack a heretical Pope are to be defended by Catholics.
