But they do not seem to show that those who do not know the Pope to be a heretic are bound to defend him against those who attack him for heretical wickedness. So I ask what the learned openly think about this.

units.la: MAG. Rationes illae saltem multae non tantum de scientibus Papam esse haereticum: sed de nescientibus (tamen dubitantibus) videntur procedere. vnde nonnulli putant, quod sicut si aliquis de facto a Papa catholico appellaret, ipsi haeresim imponendo antequam constaret appellationem huiusmodi non esse legitimam esset appellationi deferendum eiusdem. ita si aliquis impugnant Papam haereticum, alii catholici nescientes ipsum esse haereticum, & ignorantes an ipsum impugnantes veraciter & iuste impugnent, tenentur, si possunt, taliter impugnantes defendere.
units.tr: TEACHER: Those arguments, at least many of them, seem to apply not only to those who know the Pope to be a heretic, but also to those who do not know it, though they doubt it. Hence some think that just as, if someone were to appeal from a Catholic Pope and charge him with heresy, the appeal must be granted a hearing before it is established that the appeal is not lawful, so too, if some people attack a heretical Pope, other Catholics who do not know that he is a heretic, and who are ignorant whether those attacking him are truly and justly attacking him, are bound, if they can, to defend those who attack him in this way.

units.la: DISCIP. Secundum ista, quæ dicis, hic est locus congruus pertractandi conclusionem tertiam illorum, qui dicunt, quod licet appellare à summo Pontifice, quam supra c. 17. recitasti: & nunc iterum replicasti. ideo pro illa conclusione primo satagas allegare.
units.tr: STUDENT: Following what you say, this is a fitting place to examine the third conclusion of those who say that it is lawful to appeal from the Supreme Pontiff, which you recited above in chapter 17 and have now repeated. So, for that conclusion, first make your case.

units.la: MAGIST. Quod deferendum sit appellationi à Papa catholico pro causa hæresis interiectæ, antequam constet ipsam non esse legitimam, multis modis videtur posse probari. Primo sic: non minus deferendum est appellationi pro causa hæresis interiectæ, quam aliis appellationibus pro gravaminibus spiritualibus. & leuibus interiectis, quia appellatio pro causa fidei interiecta spectat ad ius publicum & utilitatem communem. ergo non minori privilegio gaudere debet, quam appellatio interiecta pro utilitate privata. sed aliis appellationibus est deferendum, quamuis non constet, quod non sint legitimæ, eo quod causa allegata non est probata. ergo multo fortius appellationi à Papa pro causa hæresis interiectæ est deferendum, dummodo non constet, quod non est legitima.
units.tr: TEACHER: That an appeal against a Catholic Pope on the ground of heresy must be granted a hearing, before it is established that the appeal is not lawful, can be proved in many ways. First, thus: an appeal made on the ground of heresy must be granted a hearing no less than other appeals made on account of spiritual grievances, even slight ones, because an appeal lodged on behalf of the faith concerns public right and the common good. Therefore it ought to enjoy no lesser privilege than an appeal lodged for private advantage. But other appeals must be granted a hearing, even though it is not established that they are not lawful, because the cause alleged has not been proved. Therefore, much more strongly, an appeal against the Pope on the ground of heresy must be granted a hearing, provided it is not established that it is unlawful.

units.la: DISCIP. Tardiores exemplis apertis sæpe moventur. ideo pone exemplum apertum de appellatione à Papa catholico interiecta.
units.tr: STUDENT: Slower minds are often moved by plain examples. So give a plain example of an appeal lodged against a Catholic Pope.

units.la: MAG. Sicut in principio istius materiæ tibi apertius indicavi, tenentes istam assertionem, quod appellationi à Papa catholico est deferendum, antequam constet appellationem non esse legitimam, nolunt ad strictissimam significationem appellationis artari, sed utuntur nomine appellationis, quo poterunt largius, scilicet pro prouocatione largissime sumpta: imo etiam usus permittit pro recusatione. intendunt ergo quod appellationi seu prouocationi à Papa catholico, vel recusationi, quando allegatur causa, quæ si esset probata, deberet legitima reputari, tali appellationi vel recusationi est omnino deferendum. Tali modo loquendi suppositio, ponatur, quod aliquis appellet à Papa, vel recuset eum allegando, & se velle probare firmiter offerendo, quod Papa tenuit & asseruit fidem Christianam esse falsam & fictam. & ideo non potest nec debet officium papatus exercere. Quo posito dicunt isti, quod tali appellationi seu prouocationi vel recusationi, quantumcunq; causa allegata sit falsa, quia tamen est talis, quæ si esset probata, deberet legitima reputari, antequam allegans eam fuerit de calumnia convictus, vel in probatione defecerit, aut per aliam exceptionem legitimam, vel alium modum congruum appareat repellendus, tam Papa quàm alii catholici debent tali appellationi vel recusationi deferre circa taliter appellantem vel recusantem, priusquam eum malitiose constiterit processisse, nihil penitus innouando: imo pro tempore illo à iurisdictione summi Pontificis est exemptus. hoc exemplo posito probatur, quod modo prædicto tam summus Pontifex, quam alii tali appellationi vel recusationi deferre tenentur.
units.tr: TEACHER: As I indicated to you more plainly at the beginning of this subject, those who hold this assertion, that an appeal against a Catholic Pope must be granted a hearing before it is established that the appeal is not lawful, do not want to be confined to the strictest meaning of appeal. Instead they use the word "appeal" as widely as they can, taking "appeal" in its broadest sense, and common usage even allows it to cover "recusation" (challenging a judge). They therefore intend that an appeal, or challenge, against a Catholic Pope, or a recusation of him, where the cause alleged is such that, if it were proved, it ought to be held lawful, must wholly be granted a hearing. In this manner of speaking, let it be supposed that someone appeals from the Pope, or recuses him, alleging the cause and firmly offering to prove that the Pope has held and asserted that the Christian faith is false and feigned, and that therefore he cannot and must not exercise the office of the papacy. Given this, these people say that such an appeal or challenge or recusation, however false the cause alleged may be, must be granted a hearing by the Pope and by other Catholics, against the one appealing or recusing, until he has been convicted of calumny, or has failed in his proof, or is shown to be rejected by some other lawful exception or suitable means. This is because, as long as the cause is of such a kind that, if it were proved, it ought to be held lawful, it must be granted a hearing, and until it is clear that the appellant has acted maliciously, no change may be made at all. Indeed, for that time the one appealing is exempt from the jurisdiction of the Supreme Pontiff. With this example laid down, it is proved that in the above manner the Supreme Pontiff, as well as others, is bound to grant a hearing to such an appeal or recusation.

units.la: Et primo sic: secundum leges fauore religionis multa constituuntur contra rationem, quod lano intellectui inconsonum veritati dinoscitur, quia religio Christiana maiori fauore dinoscitur esse digna, quam quæcunque causa priuata. Ex quo concluditur, quod verba iuris in fauorem religionis amplianda sunt, & nullatenus restringenda. & per consequens omnia iura canonica & ciuilia in fauorem edita appellantis interpretanda sunt largissime: quia appellans pro religione Christiana & fide catholica se asserit appellare. constat autem secundum iura canonica & ciuilia, quod appellationi illius, qui pro re alia, quam pro fide, si talem causam allegat, quæ si esset probata, deberet legitima reputari, iudex, à quo appellat, & alii deferre tenentur. ergo per eadem iura probatur, quod appellans à Papa allegans quod Papa tenet & asserit fidem Christianam esse falsam: Papa & alii appellationi eius vel recusationi deferre tenentur, quia si hæc causa esset probata, deberet legitima reputari. si enim talis appellans probaret legitime Papam tenere fidem Christianam esse falsam, Papa nec super illum, nec super alium iurisdictionem haberet.
units.tr: And first, thus: according to the laws, for the sake of religion, many things are established against reason, things which are recognised as plainly at odds with the understanding of truth, because the Christian religion is recognised as deserving greater favour than any private cause. From this it follows that the words of the law must be extended in favour of religion, and by no means restricted. And consequently all canon and civil laws enacted in favour of the appellant must be interpreted very broadly, because the appellant asserts that he appeals for the Christian religion and the Catholic faith. Now it is established, according to canon and civil law, that a judge from whom someone appeals, and others, are bound to grant a hearing to the appeal of one who appeals for some other matter than the faith, if he alleges a cause which, if it were proved, ought to be held lawful. Therefore by the same laws it is proved that the appellant who, against the Pope, alleges that the Pope holds and asserts that the Christian faith is false, must be granted a hearing by the Pope and others, in respect of his appeal or recusation, because if this cause were proved, it ought to be held lawful. For if such an appellant were to prove lawfully that the Pope holds the Christian faith to be false, the Pope would have no jurisdiction over him or over anyone else.

units.la: Secunda ratio talis est. sicut appellationi, vel recusationi legitimæ, deferendum est: ita etiam omni appellationi & recusationi, quam non constat illegitimam esse, deferendum est, antequam constet eum frustratorie seu malitiose procedere: & licet pro causa, quam allegat, ab aliquo appellare vel alium recusare: & quia sic omni appellationi vel recusationi legitimæ deferendum est. sed catholico licet à Papa appellare, vel Papam recusare, si Papa asserit fidem Christianam esse falsam. ergo si pro causa hac quis appellat, appellationem vel recusationem non esse legitimam, nisi constiterit causam allegatam esse falsam. igitur deferendum est appellationi vel recusationi huiusmodi.
units.tr: The second argument is this. Just as a lawful appeal or recusation must be granted a hearing, so too every appeal and recusation which is not clearly unlawful must be granted a hearing, until it is established that the appellant is acting deceptively or maliciously. And although someone appeals from or recuses another on account of the cause he alleges, all lawful appeals or recusations must be granted a hearing. But it is lawful for a Catholic to appeal from the Pope, or to recuse him, if the Pope asserts that the Christian faith is false. Therefore, if someone appeals on this cause, the appeal or recusation is not unlawful, unless it is established that the cause alleged is false. Therefore an appeal or recusation of this kind must be granted a hearing.

units.la: Tertia ratio talis est. si appellationi, vel recusationi huiusmodi est minime deferendum, aut hoc est, quia causa assignata, si esset probata, non deberet legitima reputari; aut quia ille, à quo appellat vel qui recusatur, est talis persona, à qua pro causa tali appellare non licet; vel quia appellans vel recusans est talis persona, cui specialiter est interdictum à iure, ne pro tali causa appellaret, vel quia appellans vel recusans infra tempus statutum à iure non appellat vel non recusat, vel suam appellationem vel recusationem hequaquam prosequitur; vel quia in forma appellationis aliqua deberent inferri, quæ omittuntur. Quia si aliqua appellatio vel recusatio repellitur, aut est repellenda propter causam legitimam, si etiam esset probata; vel propter defectum appellationis, aut prosecutionis, aut propter omissionem temporis à iure statuti; vel propter conditionem personæ, à qua appellatur vel recusatur; vel propter conditionem personæ appellantis vel recusantis. sed propter primum non est dicendum, quod tali appellationi vel recusationi est minime deferendum: quia causa assignata, quod Papa videlicet tenet & asserit fidem Christianam esse falsam, est talis, quae si esset probata, deberet ab omnibus catholicis sufficiens & legitima reputari. Nec propter secundum: quia a Papa, si asserit & tenet fidem Christianam esse falsam; licet appellare; imo est ab omnibus catholicis cuitandus. Nec propter tertium est tali appellationi vel recusationi minime deferendum: quia ponatur, quod appellans seu recusans sit bonae famae, quando appellat vel recusat, & talis contra quem nihil obiici potest: imo ponatur, quod sit rex; vel Episcopus, vel talis opinionis & famae, quod contra personam non possit exceptio legitima allegari. Nec propter quartum est tali appellationi vel recusationi a iudice minime deferendum: tum quia, sicut probatum est, tali appellanti, vel recusanti non potest currere tempus, cum non sit simpliciter necesse appellare pro tali causa: tum quia ponitur, quod infra tempus statutum a iure appellet vel recusat, & appellationem vel recusationem prosequitur. Nec propter quintum est tali appellationi vel recusationi minime deferendum. tum quia in hoc casu in favorem fidei Christianae non est necesse observare subtilitates iuris; tum quia ponatur, quod talis appellans vel recusans nihil de contingentibus & subtilitatibus iuris obmittat. Patet igitur, quod nulla ratio potest allegari, quare tali appellationi sit minime deferendum. quia nec ex parte causae assignatae, nec ex parte appellantis, nec ex parte personae a qua appellatur, nec ex parte temporis, nec ex parte formae appellationis. & ita dicendum est secundum ipsos, quod tali appellationi seu recusationi est deferendum omnino.
units.tr: The third argument is this. If an appeal or recusation of this kind is not to be granted a hearing at all, this must be either because the cause assigned, if it were proved, ought not to be held lawful; or because the person from whom one appeals, or who is recused, is such that it is not lawful to appeal from him on such a cause; or because the appellant or the one recusing is a person specifically forbidden by law to appeal on such a cause; or because the appellant or the one recusing does not appeal or recuse within the time fixed by law, or does not pursue his appeal or recusation at all; or because certain things which ought to be included in the form of the appeal are omitted. For if any appeal or recusation is rejected, it must be rejected either on account of a lawful cause, even if it were proved; or on account of a defect in the appeal, or in its pursuit, or on account of the omission of the time fixed by law; or on account of the condition of the person from whom one appeals or who is recused; or on account of the condition of the person appealing or recusing. But it cannot be said, on the first ground, that such an appeal or recusation must in no way be granted a hearing, because the cause assigned, namely that the Pope holds and asserts that the Christian faith is false, is of such a kind that, if it were proved, it ought by all Catholics to be held sufficient and lawful. Nor on the second ground: because it is lawful to appeal from the Pope if he asserts and holds that the Christian faith is false; indeed all Catholics ought to avoid him. Nor on the third ground may such an appeal or recusation be refused a hearing, because let it be supposed that the appellant or the one recusing is of good repute when he appeals or recuses, and that nothing can be objected against him; indeed let it be supposed that he is a king, or a bishop, or of such standing and reputation that no lawful exception can be alleged against his person. Nor on the fourth ground may such an appeal or recusation be refused a hearing by the judge: partly because, as has been proved, the time cannot run against such an appellant or recusant, since it is not absolutely necessary to appeal on such a cause; and partly because it is supposed that he appeals or recuses within the time fixed by law and pursues his appeal or recusation. Nor on the fifth ground may such an appeal or recusation be refused a hearing: partly because in this case, for the sake of the Christian faith, it is not necessary to observe the subtleties of law; and partly because it is supposed that such an appellant or recusant omits nothing of the formalities and subtleties of law. It is clear, therefore, that no reason can be alleged why such an appeal should in no way be refused a hearing: neither on the part of the cause assigned, nor on the part of the appellant, nor on the part of the person from whom one appeals, nor on the part of the time, nor on the part of the form of the appeal. And so, according to these people, it must be said that such an appeal or recusation must wholly be granted a hearing.

units.la: Discip. Potest dici, quod ratio dari vel reddi, quare tali appellationi est minime deferendum ex parte causae, quia causa est falsa, eo quod Papa est catholicus secundum casum.
units.tr: Disciple. It may be said that a reason can be given why such an appeal should by no means be admitted, on the side of the cause: the cause is false, since the Pope is in this case a Catholic.

units.la: Mag. Ista responsio friuola reputatur, quia falsitas causae non impedit, quo minus appellationi vel recusationi sit deferendum, antequam falsitas sit probata; vel offerens se probaturum causam in probatione defecerit. aliter enim nunquam esset aliqua appellatio reprobanda; an iudex vel alius rationabiliter detulisset; quod tamen constat esse falsum. si enim iudex iustam contra aliquem proferret sententiam; si ille duxerit appellandum, allegans quod sententia est iniqua, iudex, quamvis sciat appellationem iniquam & causam esse falsam: quia tamen adhuc non est probata causa esse falsa, nec etiam appellans in probatione defecit, iudex appellationi suae deferre tenetur: qui tamen postquam de iniqua appellatione fuerit convictus, exigente iustitia est graviter puniendus.
units.tr: Master. That answer is regarded as frivolous, because the falsity of a cause does not prevent an appeal or a recusation from being admitted, before the falsity has been proved, or before the party offering to prove the cause has failed in the proof. Otherwise no appeal would ever be rightly rejected, and a judge would never have acted reasonably in any matter, which is plainly false. If a judge pronounced a just sentence against someone, and that person chose to appeal, alleging that the sentence was unjust, the judge, even if he knows the appeal is unjust and the cause false, must still admit the appeal, because the cause has not yet been proved false and the appellant has not failed in the proof. Yet once the unjust appeal has been proved against him, justice requires that he be severely punished.

units.la: Discip. Alias rationes adducas. Magist. Quarta ratio pro assertione praedicta talis est. illius appellationi vel recusationi est deferendum, qui appellat, vel recusat ex causa, quae si esset probata, deberet legitima reputari; cuius accusatio vel testimonium contra superiorem in eadem causa debet admitti. Sed qui voluerit Papam de praedicta haeresi accusare, vel contra eum testificari: si alius est persona idonea, eius est accusatio & etiam testificatio admittenda. ergo si ex eadem causa duxerit appellandum, vel eundem iudicem duxerit recusandum, eius appellationi vel recusationi est deferendum. Maior est manifesta: quia aeque levibus causis vel aequalibus contingit contra aliquem appellare & recusare ipsum, ex quibus contingit eum accusare vel contra eum testimonium ferre. saepe enim licet aliquem iudicem recusare vel testificari contra ipsum, ut patet. Minor etiam videtur certa: quia constat, quod Papa potest de haeresi accusari secundum iura, & per consequens contingit contra ipsum de haeresi testimonium ferri: quod maxime veritatem habet, si Papa tenet fidem Christianam esse falsam.
units.tr: Disciple. Bring forward other reasons. Master. The fourth reason for the aforesaid assertion is this. An appeal or recusation must be admitted when it is made by someone who appeals or recuses on a ground which, if it were proved, ought to be held lawful; and the accusation or testimony of such a person against a superior in the same cause must be admitted. But whoever wishes to accuse the Pope of the aforesaid heresy, or to bear witness against him, if he is a suitable person, his accusation and testimony must be admitted. Therefore, if he appeals or recuses the same judge on the same ground, his appeal or recusation must be admitted. The major premise is plain, because appealing against someone or recusing him happens on grounds as slight or equal to those on which one may accuse him or bear witness against him. Indeed it is often lawful to recuse a judge or to testify against him, as is clear. The minor premise also seems certain, because it is agreed that the Pope may be accused of heresy under the laws, and consequently testimony may be given against him on this charge. This holds most strongly if the Pope holds that the Christian faith is false.

units.la: Quinta ratio est haec: ille, cuius appellationi, vel recusationi merito non deferetur, de appellatione iniqua vel frustratoria vituperandus censetur. quia solummodo appellationi vel recusationi frustratoriae vel iniquae est minime deferendum. Sed qui appellat vel recusat Papam pro iudice se gerente, scilicet offerens probaturum, quod Papa tenet & asserit fidem Christianam esse falsam, ante examinationem causae & antequam convincatur de falsi criminis impositione, vel in probatione defecerit, non est vituperandus, iuxta sententiam sapientis, qui, ut habetur Ecclesiast. 11. ait: Priusquam interrogesl, ne vituperes quenquam. ergo tali appellationi vel recusationi (antequam ostendatur iniqua) est deferendum.
units.tr: The fifth reason is this. The person whose appeal or recusation is not rightly admitted is judged worthy of blame for an unjust or frivolous appeal, since only a frivolous or unjust appeal or recusation is by no means to be admitted. But whoever appeals from or recuses the Pope as a judge, namely offering to prove that the Pope holds and asserts the Christian faith to be false, before the examination of the cause and before he is convicted of the crime of false accusation, or before he has failed in the proof, is not to be blamed, according to the saying of the wise man, who, as is found in Ecclesiastes 11, says: "Before you inquire, do not blame anyone." Therefore such an appeal or recusation (until it is shown to be unjust) must be admitted.

units.la: Sexta ratio talis est: in dubiis via securior est tenenda, extra de regulis iuris, estote. & extra de homicidio, ad audientiam. Sed deferre appellationi vel recusationi Papae ex causa praedicta est securior via. nam ex hoc, quod tali appellationi vel recusationi defertur, nullum periculum imminet, neque fidei Christianae, nec summo Pontifici, si est innocens. si autem talibus appellationibus vel recusationibus minime est deferendum, magna pericula possent fidei catholicae imminere. posset etiam Papa absque metu strictis iudicii, & poenae condignae, catholicae fidei corrumpere puritatem. ergo (securiorem viam sequendo) in favorem fidei Christianae talibus est appellationibus vel recusationibus deferendum.
units.tr: The sixth reason is this. In doubtful matters the safer course is to be taken, see the extravagant on the rules of law, "estote," and the extravagant on homicide, "ad audientiam." But to admit an appeal or recusation of the Pope on the aforesaid ground is the safer course. For from admitting such an appeal or recusation no danger threatens either the Christian faith or the supreme Pontiff, if he is innocent. If, however, such appeals or recusations are by no means admitted, great dangers could threaten the Catholic faith. The Pope could also, without fear of strict judgment and of due punishment, corrupt the purity of the Catholic faith. Therefore, by following the safer course, such appeals or recusations must be admitted in favour of the Christian faith.

units.la: Discip. Videtur quod talis via non sit securior: quia summo Pontifici, si talibus esset appellationibus & recusationib. deferendum, multiplicia & magna imminerent dispendia. posset enim quilibet Papam catholicum tanquam haereticum recusare. ex quo fama summi Pontificis multipliciter laederetur, & ipse suam innocentiam declarando modis variis vexaretur.
units.tr: Disciple. It seems that this course is not the safer one, because if such appeals and recusations were admitted, many and great losses would threaten the supreme Pontiff. For anyone could recuse a Catholic Pope as a heretic, whereby the reputation of the supreme Pontiff would be harmed in many ways, and he himself would be harassed in various ways by having to declare his innocence.

units.la: Magist. Ista responsio impugnatur: quia talis via non est securior, quod sic probatur: illa via, quae est in favorem fidei Christianae, & non probabile dispendium summi Pontificis innocentis, est securior, quam illa via, quae potest vergere in notabil· dispendium fidei orthodoxae & periculum & in fauorem Papae praultate haeretica macular.sed deferre huiusmodi appellationib.& recusationibus interiectis ex causa praedicta (antequam legitime constet causam esse falsam) est in fauorem fidei Christianae, & non est in personae dispendium vel periculum summi Pontificis innocentis : Quia summo Pontifici innocenti plurimae viae patent omne periculum euadendi. non deferre autem huiusmodi appellationibus & recusationibus potest vergere in notabile dispendium fidei orthodoxae, & in fauorem Papae haeretici. Poterit enim libere Papa haereticus praultate haeretica corrumpere orthodoxos, si nemo contra eum est super crimine haeresis audiendus. deferre igitur huiusmodi appellationibus & recusationibus est via securior,& ideo est tenenda.
units.tr: Master. This answer is refuted, because the course is in fact the safer one. This is proved as follows. The course which is in favour of the Christian faith, and which involves no probable loss to an innocent supreme Pontiff, is safer than the course which could tend towards a notable loss to the orthodox faith and a danger, and which brands the Pope with heretical depravity in his favour. But to admit such appeals and recusations made on the aforesaid ground (before it is lawfully established that the cause is false) is in favour of the Christian faith, and is not a loss or danger to the person of the innocent supreme Pontiff. For many ways lie open to an innocent supreme Pontiff to escape every danger. Not to admit such appeals and recusations, however, could tend towards a notable loss to the orthodox faith, and in favour of a heretical Pope. For a heretical Pope could freely corrupt the orthodox with heretical depravity, if no one may be heard against him on a charge of heresy. Therefore to admit such appeals and recusations is the safer course, and so it is to be followed.

units.la: DISCIP. Ista ratio videtur deficere dupliciter. Primo quia (sicut ego dixi) deferre appellationibus & recusationibus huiusmodi, potest vergere in personale periculum summi Pontificis innocentis: quia quilibet poterit eum diffamare & multipliciter fatigare.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. This argument seems to fail in two ways. First, because (as I have said) admitting appeals and recusations of this kind may tend towards a personal danger to the innocent supreme Pontiff, since anyone could defame him and harass him in many ways.

units.la: Secundo deficit: quia quamuis non sit talibus appellationibus & recusationibus deferendum,non tamen poterit Papa haereticus libere praultate haeretica corrumpere orthodoxos: quia si aliqui,qui sint minime repellendi,eum accusare voluerint de haeretica praultate, eis non debet audientia denegari.
units.tr: Second, it fails because, although such appeals and recusations are not to be admitted, a heretical Pope could still not freely corrupt the orthodox with heretical depravity, since if certain persons, who are by no means to be repelled, wish to accuse him of heretical depravity, a hearing must not be denied them.

units.la: MAGIST. Prima instantia tua friuola multis apparet:quia sicut quemadmodum notatur extra, de praesumptionibus.cap.quia verisimile, quia sicut de nemine praesumendum est, quod bona sua iactet, supra de renunciatione, super hoc. & supra. de re. spol. sollicite: ita de nemine praesumendum est quod gratis confusioni & totius amissioni honoris ac poenae praultatis haereticae se exponat.Sed qui appellaret a Papa, vel ipsum tanquam haereticum recusaret, eidem imponendo quod Christianam fidem asserat esse falsam,se confusioni Papae ac totius amissioni honoris ac poenae praultatis haereticae se exponeret. Talis enim propter tanti criminis impositionem tantae personae omnibus praedictis esset dignissimus. De nemine ergo qui fuerit bonae discretionis & famae est praesumendum, quod tale quid velit mendaciter imponere summo Pontifici. Quare quantumcunque talibus appellationibus & recusationibus deferatur, probabile periculum nequaquam imminer summo Pontifici innocenti. Quia nullatenus oportet probabiliter formidare, quod vnquam aliquis tantum crimen summo Pontifici innocenti audebit imponere. Et si contingeret, quod semel vel bis aliquis ad tantam deuenirent insaniam: quod mendaciter tale crimen imponerent summo Pontifici innocenti,& propter hoc ab ipso appellarent vel recusarent eundem,non essent propter hoc tales appellationes vel recusationes regulariter repellendae. Quia sicut in legibus statuendis, ita in interpretatione legum ea quae frequenter, & non quae raro accidunt, sunt pensanda.quare cum raro vel nunquam accidat, quod aliquis appellando, vel recusando Papam sibi imponat,quod fidem abnegauerit Christianam,cum ista sit causa, quae si esset probata, deberet legitima reputari. concluditur quod iura, quae asserunt, quod est appellationibus & recusationibus deferendum,in quibus assignatur causa, si esset probata, deberet legitima reputari ad appellationem & recusationem Papae, in qua pro causa assignatur, quod Papa fidem Christianam asserit esse falsam,sunt omnimode extendenda. Et instantia tua secunda per rationem quartam superius sedam repellitur.nam ostensum est,quod cuilibet licet accusare Papam de haeretica praultate, & eius appellationi & recusationi pro causa haeresis est omnimode deferendum:cum minus sit appellare vel iudicem recusare,quam accusare eundem,
units.tr: MASTER. Your first objection appears frivolous to many, because just as it is noted in the extravagant on presumptions, chapter "quia verisimile," that no one is presumed to boast of his own goods (see above, on renunciation, "super hoc," and above, on restitution of spoils, "sollicite"), so no one is presumed to expose himself willingly to shame, the total loss of honour, and the punishment due to a heretical depravity. But whoever should appeal from the Pope, or recuse him as a heretic, by charging him that he asserts the Christian faith to be false, would expose himself to the Pope's shame, to the total loss of honour, and to the punishment of heretical depravity. For such a man, on account of imputing so great a crime to so great a person, would be most worthy of all these penalties. Therefore no one of sound judgment and good reputation is to be presumed to wish to lie and impute such a thing to the supreme Pontiff. Wherefore, however much such appeals and recusations are admitted, there is in no way a probable danger threatening the innocent supreme Pontiff. For there is no reason at all to fear with probability that anyone will ever dare to impute so great a crime to an innocent supreme Pontiff. And if it should happen that once or twice some men came to such madness as falsely to charge an innocent supreme Pontiff with such a crime, and on that ground appealed from him or recused him, such appeals or recusations would not on that account be rightly rejected as a general rule. For just as in enacting laws, so in interpreting them, what happens frequently, and not what happens rarely, is to be weighed. Therefore, since it rarely or never happens that someone, in appealing from or recusing the Pope, charges him with having abandoned the Christian faith, and since this is a cause which, if it were proved, ought to be held lawful, it follows that the laws which state that appeals and recusations are to be admitted when the cause given would, if proved, be held lawful, must be extended in every way to an appeal and recusation of the Pope in which the cause given is that the Pope asserts the Christian faith to be false. And your second objection is refuted by the fourth reason set out above. For it has been shown that it is lawful for anyone to accuse the Pope of heretical depravity, and that his appeal and his recusation on the ground of heresy must in every way be admitted, since appealing from a judge or recusing him is a lesser thing than accusing him.

units.la: CAP. XLVI.
units.tr: CHAPTER 46.

units.la: Inquo ponitur & probatur conclusio contraria duabus rationibus probando scilicet,quod non sit deferendum tali appellationi contra summum Pontificem, ad quas respondetur capitulo immediate sequenti.
units.tr: In which the contrary conclusion is set out and proved by two reasons, namely that such an appeal against the supreme Pontiff ought not to be admitted; these are answered in the immediately following chapter.

units.la: DISCIP. Ex quo allegasti pro assertione dicente, quod deferendum est appellationi seu recusationi Papae,antequam constet talem appellationem vel recusationem non esse legitimam: quia causa videlicet allegata non est probata, licet talis sit, quod si esset probata, deberet legitima reputari:peto vt pro assertione contraria aliquas allegationes adducas.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Since you have alleged, in support of the assertion that an appeal or recusation against the Pope ought to be admitted before it is established that such an appeal or recusation is not legitimate (because the cause alleged is not proved, although it may be such that, if it were proved, it ought to be regarded as legitimate), I ask that you adduce some allegations for the contrary assertion.

units.la: MAGIST.Quod nescientes & dubitantes talem appellationem vel recusationem non esse legitimam eis deferre non debeant:maxime si Papa sciens causam esse falsam non deferret eidem, videtur posse probari.
units.tr: MASTER. That those who do not know, and who doubt, that such an appeal or recusation is not legitimate ought not to admit it, seems capable of being proved, especially if the Pope, knowing the cause to be false, did not admit it.

units.la: Primo sic: praeceptis Papae oportet non solum in certis, sed etiam in dubiis obedire: cum etiam in dubiis praecepto regis sacrilegi miles debeat obedire; teste Augustin. qui, vt habetur 23. quaest. 1. cap. quid culpatur, ait: vir iustus si forte etiam sub rege & homine sacrilego militet; recte potest illo iubente bellare: si vice pacis ordinem seruans quod sibi iubetur vel non esse contra Dei praeceptum certum est, vel vtrum sit certum non est ita vt fortasse reum faciat regem iniquitas imperandi,innocentem autem militem ostendat ordo seruiendi.Ex quib.verbis colligitur quod miles regi sacrilego in dubiis obedire tenetur.ergo multo magis in dubiis est obediendum summo Pontifici. ex quo concluditur, quod dubitantes talem appellationem vel recusationem icusationem esse legitimam, si Papa non defert ei, & aliis mandat ne deferant, ipsi ei obedire debent.
units.tr: First, thus: one must obey the commands of the Pope not only in certain matters but also in doubtful ones, since a soldier ought to obey even in doubtful matters the command of a sacrilegious king; as Augustine witnesses, who, as is found in 23 q. 1 c. "Quid culpatur," says: "A just man, if perchance he serves under a king and a sacrilegious man, may rightly wage war at his command, keeping the order of peace as far as it concerns him; it is certain that what is commanded him is either not contrary to the precept of God, or it is not certain whether it is contrary; so that perhaps the iniquity of the one commanding makes the king guilty, while the order of serving shows the soldier to be innocent." From these words it is gathered that a soldier is bound to obey a sacrilegious king in doubtful matters. Therefore, much more in doubtful matters must obedience be given to the supreme Pontiff. From this it follows that those who doubt whether such an appeal or recusation is legitimate, if the Pope does not admit it and orders others not to admit it, ought themselves to obey him.

units.la: Secundo sic: nulli clerico licet ante tempus sententiae ab Episcopo suo discedere. 8. quaest. 4. propter nullam appellationem vel recusationem ante decisionem causae licet catholicis ab obedientia Papae recedere. ergo post recusationem vel appellationem huiusmodi est in omnibus obediendum Papae, sicut prius. ergo si Papa praecipit tali appellationi vel recusationi nequaquam deferri, dubitantes talem appellationem vel recusationem non esse legitimam, tenentur ei non deferre. aliter oporteret catholicos nescientes Papam haereticum esse ab obedientia ipsius recedere, quod nullatenus est tenendum.
units.tr: Second, thus: it is lawful for no clergyman to depart from his bishop before the time of sentence (8 q. 4). Likewise, on account of no appeal or recusation before the decision of the cause is it lawful for Catholics to withdraw from obedience to the Pope. Therefore, after such a recusation or appeal, the Pope is to be obeyed in all things, as before. Therefore, if the Pope commands that such an appeal or recusation not be admitted at all, those who doubt whether such an appeal or recusation is legitimate are bound not to admit it. Otherwise it would be necessary for Catholics who do not know that the Pope is a heretic to withdraw from obedience to him, which by no means is to be held.

units.la: CAP. XLVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XLVII.

units.la: Vbi ponitur responsio ad rationes praecedentis capituli probantes, tali appellationi non esse de- ferendum. vbi nota de ignorantia.
units.tr: Where a reply is given to the arguments of the preceding chapter which prove that such an appeal is not to be obeyed. Note here concerning ignorance.

units.la: DISCIP. Non puto, quod fortiores rationes, quam sint istae duae, pro assertione praedicta valeant inveniri. ideo plures non adducas: sed dic quomodo respondetur ad istas.
units.tr: Disciple. I do not think that stronger arguments than these two can be found for the assertion just made. So do not bring forward more, but tell me how these are answered.

units.la: MAGIST. Ad primam respondetur de dubiis distinguendo. nam sicut distinguitur de ignorantia, prout legitur. i. quaest. 4. cap. crimen. §. notandum, quod alia est ignorantia facti, alia est iuris. Ignorantia facti, alia est eius quod oportet scire, & alia eius quod non oportet scire. Et similiter ignorantia iuris, alia est iuris naturalis, alia civilis. Sic est alia dubitatio facti, & alia dubitatio iuris. & alia dubitatio facti quod oportet scire, & similiter alia est dubitatio quod quis scire non tenetur. & alia est iuris, quod quis scire tenetur. & alia est dubitatio iuris quod quis scire non tenetur. Per hoc respondetur ad primam rationem, quod quaedam sunt dubia, quae oportet scire: & quaedam sunt dubia quae non oportet scire. In dubiis autem, quae non oportet scire, est obediendum superiori. & in tali casu loquitur Augustin. in verbis superius allegatis. In dubiis vero, quae oportet scire, non est semper obediendum superiori. Si enim Rex vel alius praeciperet adorari Machometum, vel servare legem Iudaeorum, quamvis subditus dubitaret tale praeceptum esse contra legem Dei & iniquum, nullatenus excusaretur a peccato obediendo, sicut Iudaei & alii minime excusantur, licet non sciant se malefacere. Sic dicunt in proposito, quod si aliquis dubitet, an sit obediendum Papae praecipienti, quod tali appellationi vel recusationi minime deferatur, dubitat de illo, quod oportet scire & nullatenus dubitare. quilibet enim capax rationis scire tenetur, quod magis favendum est legi divinae quam cuicunque mortali. & ideo occurrendum est magis, ubi imminet periculum legis divinae quam ubi imminet periculum hominis cuiuscunque mortalis. Quare quilibet scire tenetur, quod in derogationem & subversionem legis divinae nulli oportet obedire praelato. Tenentur etiam quilibet scire, quod si non esset deferendum appellationi vel recusationi huiusmodi, antequam constet eam non esse legitimam, posset legis divinae subversio imminere. Posset enim libere Papa haereticus absque resistentia legem divinam subvertere, & introducere sectam catholicae fidei adversantem: quia quilibet scire tenetur, quod tali praecepto est minime obediendum. Et ideo si dubitans obediat, a peccato minime excusatur, quia dubitat ubi dubitare non debet.
units.tr: Master. To the first I reply by distinguishing doubts. For just as a distinction is drawn about ignorance, as one reads in I Qu. 4, ch. Crimen, §. Notandum, that there is ignorance of fact and ignorance of law, and that ignorance of fact is of two kinds, of what one ought to know and of what one ought not to know, and likewise ignorance of law is of natural law or of civil law, so too there is doubt of fact and doubt of law, and doubt of fact is either of what one ought to know or of what one is not bound to know, and doubt of law is either of what one is bound to know or of what one is not bound to know. By this the first argument is answered: some doubts are such that one ought to know them, and some are such that one ought not to know them. In doubts which one ought not to know, one must obey the superior, and it is in such a case that Augustine speaks in the words cited above. In doubts which one ought to know, however, one must not always obey the superior. For if a king or anyone else were to order that Muhammad be worshipped, or that the law of the Jews be kept, then even though the subject doubted that such a command was contrary to the law of God and unjust, he would by no means be excused from sin by obeying, just as the Jews and others are not at all excused, although they do not know that they do wrong. So they say in the present case: if anyone doubts whether he must obey the Pope when he orders that such an appeal or refusal not be given effect, he doubts about something which he ought to know and should by no means doubt. For every person capable of reason is bound to know that the law of God is to be favoured more than any mortal whatever. And therefore one must resist more where the danger threatens the law of God than where the danger threatens any mortal man. Hence everyone is bound to know that one ought in no way to obey a prelate in derogation of or subversion of the law of God. Everyone is also bound to know that, if such an appeal or refusal were not to be given effect before it is established that it is not lawful, the subversion of the divine law could threaten. For the Pope, if he were a heretic, could freely subvert the divine law without resistance and introduce a sect hostile to the Catholic faith, since everyone is bound to know that such a command must in no way be obeyed. And therefore if one who doubts obeys, he is not excused from sin at all, because he doubts where he ought not to doubt.

units.la: DISCIP. Omnino videtur irrationabiliter dictum, quod quilibet tenetur scire, quod tali praecepto Papae non sit obediendum: cum pauci vel nulli hoc teneant. ea autem quae quilibet tenetur scire, cognoscuntur esse contraria his quae paucis sunt ignota. ergo non quilibet tenetur scire, quod non est obediendum tali praecepto summi Pontificis. Quod etiam ratione videtur posse probari: quia spectantia ad mores, quae quilibet scire tenetur, vel pertinent ad ius naturale vel ad ius divinum. Ea vero quae sunt de iure positivo, non quilibet tenetur scire: sed non obedire tali praecepto non pertinet ad ius naturale: quia tunc naturaliter esset votum. nec pertinet ad ius divinum: quia ius divinum in scripturis sacris habetur, in tota autem scriptura divina nulla de hoc fit mentio. ergo non spectat ad ius divinum.
units.tr: Disciple. It seems altogether unreasonably said that everyone is bound to know that such a command of the Pope is not to be obeyed, since few or none hold this. But those things which everyone is bound to know are known to be contrary to those things which are unknown to few. Therefore not everyone is bound to know that one must not obey such a command of the supreme Pontiff. This can also seem to be proved by reason: matters of conduct which everyone is bound to know pertain either to natural law or to divine law. But matters of positive law not everyone is bound to know. Yet not to obey such a command does not pertain to natural law, for then it would be known by nature. Nor does it pertain to divine law, for divine law is contained in the holy Scriptures, and in the whole divine Scripture there is no mention of this. Therefore it does not belong to divine law.

units.la: MAGIST. Respondetur, quod sicut natura humana est corrupta per peccatum, ita & cognitio humana in multis per varia vicia quo ad multa penitus est amissa. & ideo si nulli vel pauci tenent, quod non est obediendum tali praecepto Papae, hoc ex corruptione accidit vitiorum. pauci enim vel nulli inveniuntur, qui velint pro veritate indignationem incurrere summi Pontificis. si autem summus Pontifex hoc teneret, omnes vel multi de hoc nullatenus dubitarent: si etiam vellent ad conscientiam suam recurrere, invenirent esse tenendum, quod nulli mortali est obediendum in subversione legis divinae, & per consequens quod tali praecepto Papae cum possit esse in subversionem legis divinae non est obediendum quoquo modo.
units.tr: Master. The answer is that just as human nature has been corrupted by sin, so human knowledge in many respects, by various vices, has been wholly lost as regards many things. And therefore if none or few hold that one must not obey such a command of the Pope, this comes about from the corruption of vices. For few or none are found who are willing to incur the displeasure of the supreme Pontiff for the sake of the truth. But if the supreme Pontiff held this, all or many would by no means doubt it; and if they were willing to have recourse to their conscience, they would find that it must be held that no mortal is to be obeyed in the subversion of the divine law, and consequently that a command of the Pope, since it may be in subversion of the divine law, is in no way to be obeyed.

units.la: Cum vero dicis, quod spectantia ad mores, quae quilibet scire tenetur, vel pertinent ad ius naturale, vel ad ius divinum: dicitur quod verum est aliquo modo: quia vel sunt principia, aut conclusiones iuris naturalis vel divini, aut sequuntur similiter ex iure naturali & divino. & ita est de assertione ista: non est obediendum huiusmodi praecepto Papae, quia sequitur ex his, qui sunt ex dictamine iuris naturalis, & ex aliquibus contentis in iure divino. & quia per rationem naturalem scitur, quod quilibet debet præferre legem, quam reputat diuinam, omni mortali. per legem autem diuinam scitur, quod lex Christiana est lex diuina, igitur per rationem & legem diuinam similiter scitur, quod lex Christiana est omni homini præferenda. & per consequens nulli præcepto Papæ in derogationem vel subuersionem legis Christianæ est aliqualiter obediendum. & ita spectat quodammodo ad ius naturale & ad ius diuinum. Cum vero probatur, quod non pertinet ad ius naturale: quia tunc esset naturaliter notum. Respondetur, quod non est verum: quia multa spectant ad ius naturale, tanquam ad conclusiones, quæ non sunt naturaliter nota. cum autem dicis, quod de hoc in iure diuino nulla fit mentio. Respondetur, quod de hoc non fit mentio vocaliter in iure diuino: in iure tamen diuino (sicut conclusio) virtualiter continetur.
units.tr: As for your saying that matters of conduct which everyone is bound to know pertain either to natural law or to divine law, it is said that this is true in a certain way, because they are either principles or conclusions of natural or divine law, or they follow in like manner from natural and divine law. And so it is with this assertion: such a command of the Pope is not to be obeyed, because it follows from those things which come from the dictate of natural law and from certain things contained in divine law. And because by natural reason it is known that everyone ought to prefer the law which he judges to be divine to every mortal, and by divine law it is known that the Christian law is the divine law, therefore by reason and divine law it is likewise known that the Christian law is to be preferred by every man. And consequently in no way is any command of the Pope, in derogation or subversion of the Christian law, to be obeyed. And so it pertains in some measure both to natural law and to divine law. As for your proof that it does not pertain to natural law, because then it would be known by nature, the answer is that this is not true, for many things pertain to natural law as conclusions which are not known by nature. As for your saying that no mention is made of this in divine law, the answer is that it is not mentioned expressly in divine law, but in divine law it is nevertheless contained virtually, as a conclusion.

units.la: Disc ip. Dic quomodo respondetur ad rationem secundam.
units.tr: Disciple. Tell me how you answer the second argument.

units.la: Mag. Dicitur, quod non est generaliter verum, quod nulli clerico licet ante tempus sententiæ ab Episcopo suo discedere, teste Gloss. 2. q. 7. c. sacerdotes, quæ ait: Si prælati sunt hæretici vel excommunicati, vel non seruant canones, vel simoniaci vel notorii fornicatores, tunc potest recedi ab eis 16. q sin. sane. & 23 dist. nullus. Ex quibus verbis patet, quod licet clericis in casu ante tempus sententiæ latæ ab homine ab Episcopo suo vel prælato recedere. & ideo quandoque à Papa ante sententiam latam ab homine licet discedere.
units.tr: Master. It is said that it is not generally true that no cleric may leave his bishop before the time of a sentence, as the Gloss says on II Qu. 7, ch. Sacerdotes, which states: "If the prelates are heretics or excommunicated, or do not keep the canons, or are simoniacal or notorious fornicators, then one may withdraw from them" (XVI Qu. 1, Sin sane, and XXIII dist. Nullus). From these words it is plain that in such a case clerics may withdraw from their bishop or prelate before the time of a sentence pronounced by a man, and therefore sometimes one may withdraw from the Pope before a sentence pronounced by a man.

units.la: Disc ip. Ista responsio non videtur apparens: quia quamuis clerico liceat quandoque ante tempus sententiæ latæ ab homine, id est, ab Episcopo suo vel Prælato recedere: hoc tamen non licet ante tempus sententiæ latæ à iure. unde si Prælati sint hæretici, vel excommunicati, vel simoniaci, vel notorii fornicatores, licet sententia non sit lata contra eos ab homine, sententia tamen lata est à iure. sed propter appellationem vel recusationem alicuius nulla est sententia lata contra Papam à iure neque ab homine. ergo non obstante tali appellatione & recusatione est Papæ obediendum, sicut prius. & ita si præcipit ne appellationi vel recusationi huiusmodi deferatur, obediendum est.
units.tr: Disciple. This reply does not seem to hold, for although a cleric may sometimes withdraw from his bishop or prelate before the time of a sentence pronounced by a man, he may not do so before the time of a sentence pronounced by law. Hence, if prelates are heretics, or excommunicated, or simoniacal, or notorious fornicators, then even if no sentence has been pronounced against them by a man, a sentence has nevertheless been pronounced by law. But by reason of an appeal or refusal of anyone, no sentence is pronounced against the Pope either by law or by a man. Therefore, notwithstanding such an appeal and refusal, the Pope is to be obeyed as before, and so if he commands that such an appeal or refusal not be given effect, he is to be obeyed.

units.la: Mag. Dicitur quod secundum iura & dictamen rectæ rationis ante sententiam latam ab homine vel à iure non licet alicui simpliciter à suo Prælato recedere. veruntamen sicut sæpe per accusationem vel recusationem suspensa est iurisdictio alicuius & potestas, vel quantum ad aliquam causam determinatam, vel quantum ad omnem causam: ita proprer appellationem, vel recusationem potest potestas Papæ suspendi quo ad quædam præcepta, ne videlicet aliquid præcipiat aut determinet esse in præiudicium appellantis vel etiam recusantis. & quemadmodum propter appellationem & recusationem huiusmodi est suspesa potestas Papæ quo ad præcepta in præiudicium appellantis: ita omnes subditi Papæ scientes appellationem vel recusationem huiusmodi interiectam, licet nesciant causam esse legitimam, absoluti sunt ab obedientia Papæ quo ad præcepta in præiudicium appellantis & recusantis, & ideo sicut tunc Papa non debet præcipere aliquid in præiudicium appellationis vel recusationis huiusmodi, ita subditi sui quo ad hoc nullatenus sibi obedire tenentur.
units.tr: Mag. It is said that, according to the laws and the dictate of right reason, before a sentence has been pronounced against him by a man or by law, it is not lawful for anyone simply to withdraw from his own prelate. Nevertheless, just as often by accusation or recusation the jurisdiction and power of someone is suspended, either as to some particular case or as to every case, so also by reason of an appeal or a recusation the power of the Pope can be suspended as to certain precepts, namely that he may not command or determine anything to the prejudice of the appellant or even of the one who recuses. And just as by reason of such an appeal and recusation the power of the Pope is suspended as to precepts to the prejudice of the appellant, so all the subjects of the Pope who know that such an appeal or recusation has been lodged, although they may not know that the cause is lawful, are absolved from obedience to the Pope as to precepts to the prejudice of the appellant and the recusant. And therefore, just as the Pope ought not then to command anything to the prejudice of such an appeal or recusation, so his subjects are in no way bound to obey him in this matter.

units.la: CAP. XLVIII.
units.tr: CAP. XLVIII.

units.la: Vbi inquiritur, à quo possit quis suspendi, & quid importetur nomine suspensionis.
units.tr: Where it is inquired by whom a person can be suspended, and what is meant by the name of suspension.

units.la: Disc ip. Miror quod dicitur, potestatem Papæ posse suspendi per appellationem vel recusationem cuiuscunq; cum nullus debeat suspendi, nisi ab homine, vel à iure. Papa autem ab homine suspendi non potest, cum nullus sit eo superior: nec potest suspendi à iure, quia quicunq; suspensus est à iure, vel est suspensus à iure naturali, vel à iure diuino, vel à iure positiuo. sed potestas Papæ per huiusmodi appellationem vel recusationem non est suspensa à iure naturali: cum appellationes vel recusationes non sunt à iure naturali, sed ab inuentione humana. nec est suspensa à iure diuino propter idem: nec à iure positiuo, quoniam in toto iure positiuo de tali suspensione nulla penitus mentio reperitur.
units.tr: Objection. I am surprised that it is said that the power of the Pope can be suspended by the appeal or refusal of anyone, since no one ought to be suspended except by a man or by law. But the Pope cannot be suspended by a man, since there is no one above him. Nor can he be suspended by law, because whoever is suspended by law is suspended either by natural law, or by divine law, or by positive law. But the power of the Pope is not suspended by natural law through such an appeal or refusal, since appeals and refusals do not come from natural law but from human invention. Nor is it suspended by divine law for the same reason, nor by positive law, since no mention whatever of such a suspension is found in the whole of positive law.

units.la: Mag. Isti de vocabulo suspensionis volunt contendere. & ideo qualitercunque accipiatur in iure, ipsi in hoc casu vtuntur nomine suspensionis scilicet quod importat potestatem in alium ex causa minime exercendam. Et isto modo dicunt potestatem Papæ aliquo modo suspensam per talem appellationem vel recusationem: quia scilicet Papa de necessitate salutis tenetur non exercere potestatem in appellantem vel recusantem in præiudicium appellationis vel recusationis ipsius. Et ita suspensio est à iure naturæ: quia est ex dictamine naturali. dictat enim ratio naturalis, quod si aliquis appellat vel recusat iudicem ex causa, quæ si esset probata, deberet legitima reputari, iudex, antequam appellans vel recusans de malicia conuincatur, non debet potestatem exercere in ipsum in præiudicium appellationis, vel recusationis ipsius. & cum dicis quod appellationes & recusationes non sunt à iure naturali, sed ab inuentione humana: respondetur, quod ex hoc non sequitur, quod talis suspensio non sit à iure. quia sicut licet peccatum non sunt à iure naturali, cohibitio tamen peccatorum sic est à iure naturali pro statu naturæ corruptæ, licet non pro statu institutæ. Similiter posset dici, quod talis suspensio est à iure diuino, quia ex iure diuino potest ostendi, quod Papa non debet in talem potestatem suam (in suæ appellationis vel recusationis præiudicium) exercere:
units.tr: Reply. These men want to quarrel about the word "suspension". And so, however it is understood in law, they in this case use the name of suspension to mean that which implies a power over another that ought in no way to be exercised for the cause in question. In this way they say that the power of the Pope is in some sense suspended by such an appeal or refusal, because the Pope is bound, by necessity of salvation, not to exercise his power against the appellant or the one refusing, to the prejudice of that appeal or refusal. And so the suspension is from the law of nature, because it arises from the dictate of nature. For natural reason dictates that if anyone appeals or refuses a judge on a ground which, if it were proved, ought to be held lawful, the judge, before the appellant or the one refusing is convicted of malice, ought not to exercise his power against him to the prejudice of the appeal or refusal. And when you say that appeals and refusals are not from natural law but from human invention, the answer is that it does not follow from this that such a suspension is not from law. For although sins are not from natural law, the restraint of sins is nonetheless from natural law in the state of corrupted nature, though not in the state in which man was created. Similarly it could be said that such a suspension is from divine law, because from divine law it can be shown that the Pope ought not to exercise his power against such a person to the prejudice of his own appeal or refusal:

units.la: CAP. XLIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XLIX.

units.la: Dicit quod Papa tenetur deferri appellationi tali contra eum facta, & probatur tribus rationibus.
units.tr: He says that the Pope is bound to defer to such an appeal made against him, and this is proved by three arguments.

units.la: DISCIP. Apparet quod isti per talem suspensionem non aliud intelligunt, nisi quod Papa tali appellationi vel recusationi deferre tenetur: ideo omittamus verbum suspensionis, & conare probare, quod Papa tali appellationi vel recusationi deferre tenetur, appellantem videlicet & recusantem propter appellationem vel recusationem, nullatenus molestando ante decisionem causae.
units.tr: PUPIL. It seems that those who speak of such a suspension mean nothing other than that the Pope is bound to defer to such an appeal or recusation. So let us drop the word "suspension" and try to prove that the Pope is bound to defer to such an appeal or recusation, that is, that he must not molest the appellant or the one recusing in any way on account of the appeal or recusation before the case is decided.

units.la: MAG. Quod Papa teneatur tali appellationi vel recusationi deferre, videtur posse probari primo sic: Papa in his quae sunt ad alterum, non debet dominium vel potentiam contra iusticiam vel misericordiam exercere, iuxta illud beati Petri: Non dominantes in clero, sed si Papa appellationi vel recusationi huiusmodi non deferret, erga appellantem vel recusantem, nec iusticiam nec misericordiam, sed dominium & potentiam exerceret, quod non iusticiam; patet, quia ad iusticiam minime spectat appellationi vel recusationi non deferre, antequam constet eam non esse legitimam. nec exercet misericordiam, constat: quia nulla misericordiam facit taliter appellanti vel recusanti minime appellationi vel recusationi deferendo. exercet ergo potentiam & dominium absque ratione. imo contra rationem. ergo damnabiliter peccat. Secundo sic: si Papa non tenetur tali appellationi vel recusationi deferre, aut hoc est, quia nulli appellationi vel recusationi pro causa haeresis interiectae deferre tenetur, aut quia scit talem appellationem vel recusationem esse iniquam, & causam assignatam esse falsam. Non propter primum, quia si causa assignata esset vera, puta quod teneret fidem Christianam esse falsam, tali appellationi vel recusationi deferre deberet. nec propter secundum; quia falsitas causae non impedit, quo minus quis appellationi vel recusationi deferre deberet, dummodo sit talis, quae si esset probata, deberet legitima reputari. relinquitur ergo, quod Papa tali appellationi vel recusationi deferre tenetur. Tertio sic: iudex debet illi appellationi, aut recusationi deferre (quamvis sciat causam esse iniquam & causam assignatam esse falsam) cui alii deferre tenentur. sed alii a Papa tali appellationi vel recusationi deferre tenentur. ergo etiam Papa debet deferre eidem. ad hoc etiam possunt allegari rationes supra capitulo 45. inductae.
units.tr: MASTER. That the Pope is bound to defer to such an appeal or recusation can perhaps be proved first as follows. In matters concerning another, the Pope ought not to exercise lordship or power against justice or mercy, according to the saying of blessed Peter: "not lording it over the clergy" (1 Pet. 5). But if the Pope did not defer to such an appeal or recusation, he would exercise towards the appellant or the one recusing neither justice nor mercy, but lordship and power, which is not justice. This is clear, because it does not belong to justice at all not to defer to an appeal or recusation before it is established that it is not legitimate. Nor does he exercise mercy, which is also evident, since by not deferring to the appeal or recusation he shows no mercy to the one appealing or recusing. Therefore he exercises power and lordship without reason, indeed against reason, and so he sins damnably. Second, as follows: if the Pope is not bound to defer to such an appeal or recusation, this is either because he is not bound to defer to any appeal or recusation made on account of an alleged heresy, or because he knows the appeal or recusation to be unjust and the cause alleged to be false. Not because of the first, since if the cause alleged were true, for instance that he held the Christian faith to be false, he ought to defer to such an appeal or recusation. Nor because of the second, for the falsity of the cause does not prevent a man from being bound to defer to an appeal or recusation, provided it is of such a kind that, if it were proved, it would have to be reckoned legitimate. It follows, therefore, that the Pope is bound to defer to such an appeal or recusation. Third, as follows: a judge ought to defer to that appeal or recusation (even though he knows the cause to be unjust and the alleged cause to be false) which others are bound to defer to. But others besides the Pope are bound to defer to such an appeal or recusation. Therefore the Pope too ought to defer to the same. The reasons adduced above in chapter 45 can also be alleged for this.

units.la: CAP. L.
units.tr: CHAPTER L.

units.la: Quaerit, an nescientes Papam esse haereticum tenentur ipsum de haeresi impugnantes defendere? quaerebatur superius cap. 55. & acceptis in bona modificatione vocabulis respondetur sub conclusione, quod sic. quod probatur unica ratione. in capitulo vero sequenti ponuntur decem alia. ubi etiam ab aliis probatur quaedam alia conclusio, scilicet quod tales etiam si ducantur ad mortem, sunt liberandi a catholicis, ubi etiam notatur, si latro ductus ad mortem debeat liberari. etiam nota ibidem, de quo magis sit praesumendum in tali impugnatione.
units.tr: It is asked whether those who do not know the Pope to be a heretic are bound to defend him when they attack him for heresy? This was asked above in chapter 55, and, with the terms taken in a good sense, it is answered under a conclusion that it is so. This is proved by one reason alone. In the following chapter, ten other reasons are set out, where another conclusion is also proved by others, namely that such men, even if they are led to death, are to be freed by Catholics; and it is noted there whether a robber led to death ought to be freed. Note also in the same place what is to be presumed more strongly in such an attack.

units.la: DISCIP. Post praedicta ad interrogationem, quam supra proposui, an nescientes Papam esse haereticum tenentur impugnantes Papam de haeretica pravitate defendere, volo redire. Porro quia fundamenta aemulorum summi Pontificis discutere cupio, diligenter unum autem de fundamentis eorum est: quod appellantes, recusantes, accusantes, & testificantes contra Papam de haeretica pravitate, ac adhaerentes & fauentes eisdem sunt a cunctis catholicis & nescientibus Papam esse haereticum defendendi. Ideo posco, ut ostendas, quomodo possit probari, quod impugnantes Papam de haeretica pravitate, sunt tuendi a cunctis catholicis, quando non constat legitimis documentis, quod taliter impugnantes inique procedunt. Volo autem sub nomine impugnantium comprehendere appellantes, recusantes, accusantes, testificantes contra Papam & adhaerentes & praebentes auxilium, consilium & fauorem supradictis & impugnationi eorum. Volo etiam uti nomine defensionis largissime pro defensione scilicet, quae fit quocunque modo, verbo vel facto, vel taciturnitate vel omissione, secundum quod dicitur aliquis alium defendere, qui eum non producit vel non manifestat.
units.tr: DISCIPULUS. After what has been said, I wish to return to the question I put forward above: whether those who do not know the Pope to be a heretic are bound to defend against the charge of heretical depravity those who attack the Pope for it. Since I wish to examine the foundations of the adversaries of the supreme Pontiff, and one of their foundations is this: that those who appeal, refuse, accuse, and testify against the Pope concerning heretical depravity, and those who adhere to and favour them, are to be defended by all Catholics who do not know the Pope to be a heretic, I therefore ask you to show how it can be proved that those who attack the Pope for heretical depravity are to be protected by all Catholics, when it is not established by legitimate documents that those who so attack act unjustly. I wish, moreover, to include under the name of attackers those who appeal, refuse, accuse, and testify against the Pope, and those who adhere to them and give aid, counsel, and favour to them and to their attack. I also wish to use the word defence very broadly, for that defence which is made in any way whatever, by word or deed, by silence or by omission, in the sense that someone is said to defend another who does not bring him forward or does not reveal him.

units.la: MAGIST. Sic acceptis vocabulis impugnationis & defensionis, quod omnes catholici teneantur defendere impugnantes Papam etiam catholicum de haeretica pravitate (antequam constet legitimis documentis eos malitiose procedere) ostenditur primo quadam ratione, quae tacta est prius cap. 44. quae talis est. Qui occasionem damni dat, damnum dedisse videtur, extra, de iniuriis & damno dato, si culpa. ergo similiter qui occasionem persequendi vel molestandi vel iniuriandi dat, persecutionem vel molestiam vel iniuriam intulisse videtur: sed non defendens impugnantes Papam de haeretica pravitate (cum potest) occasionem persequendi vel molestandi vel iniuriandi dat: quia si defenderet (ex quo potest) persecutionem cutionem {a}tutionem vel molestiam vel iniuriam illatam, vel inferendam excluderet. Ergo talis non defendens prædictos prædicta intulisse videtur vel dignoscitur. Sed nullus debet impugnantibus Papam de hæretica prauitate, antequam constiterit eos malitiose procedere, persecutionem aut molestiam vel iniuriam irrogare. Ergo quilibet, qui potest, eos tenetur defendere. Discip. Dare occasionem damni vel persecutionis aut iniuriæ aut nocumenti, contingit dupliciter: aut positiue aliquid agendo, vel loquendo; vel negatiue aliquid omittendo. Qui primo modo dat occasionem damni, damnum dedisse videtur, & reprehensibilis reputatur, qui autem dat occasionem damni vel persecutionis, vel nocumenti, vel molestiæ siue iniuriæ aliquid omittendo, non videtur damnum vel molestiā intulisse, nec culpabilis est tenendus. Tunc enim quicunq; non iuuaret alium vel non ditaret, & ex hoc accideret damnū alterius, videretur damnū dedisse, & esset reprehensibilis iudicandus, quod est nimis durum. Magist. Ista responsio assertionibus sanctorum patrum obuiare videtur: quia ipsi intelligunt, q; non solum damnum dat, qui occasionem damni dat aliquid faciendo vel loquendo, sed etiā qui occasionē damni dat aliquid omittendo, & quod inde tenetur saltem in conspectu Dei. Hoc auctoritatibus multis videtur posse probari. Greg. enim nonus, ut legitur extra, de iniuriis & damno dato, si culpa, ait: si culpa tua datu est damnū vel iniuria irrogata seu aliis irrogantibus opē ferre distulisti: aut hoc imperitia tua seu negligentia euenerit, iure super hīs satisfacere te oportet: nec ignorantia te excusat, si scire debuisti ex facto tuo inde iniuriā verisimiliter posse contingere vel iacturā. Ex quibus verbis colligitur euidenter, quod non solū damnum intelligitur dare, q; verbo vel facto occasionem damni dat, sed etiā qui per negligentiā aliquid omittendo occasionē damni dat, intelligitur damnum dare, & ex hoc culpabilis iudicatur. Item, qui occasionē mortis dat, solumodo omittendo aliquid, reus homicidii iudicatur, teste Ambrosio, qui, ut habetur 86. di. pasce, ait: quisquis enim pascendo hominem seruare poteris (si non pauperi) occidisti. Ergo consimiliter qui occasionem damni dat vel nocumenti, solummodo aliquid omittendo, hic damnum vel nocumentū dare videtur, & exinde reus & culpabilis est tenendus. Disc. Quamuis allegationes istæ magnam apparentiā videantur habere, modo video tamen, q; generaliter, qui occasionē damni dat aliquid omittendo sit culpabilis iudicandus: cū etiam absq; culpa possit quis occasionem damni dare aliquid faciendo. 23. q. 5. c. de occidendis. Et ita ex hoc, q; aliquis non defendit eos, qui Papā de hæretica prauitate impugnant, quamuis ex hoc quod non defendit, sequitur damnum vel nocumentum eorū, non potest inferri, q; talis non defendens sit culpabilis reputandus. Magist. Ista responsionem vel obiectionem nonnulli niuntur excludere. Ad cuius euidentiam prædictæ regulæ, scilicet qui occasionē damni dat &c. intellectum exponunt. Et primo quidem, quando aliquis dat occasionē damni solummodo aliqd omittendo. Secundo, quando quis dat occasionem damni aliquid faciendo vel loquendo. Quantū ad primū dicunt: quod si aliquis dat occasionem damni solummodo aliquid omittendo, aut tenetur illud facere, & tunc ex tali omissione culpā incurrit. Hinc in Exodo legitur, & recitatur extra, de iniuriis & damno dato: si bos alienus cornupeta esset ab heri & nudius tertius, & non custodierit Dominus eius, reddet bouem pro boue. Vbi dicit Glos. super verbo, non custodierit: supple, & alterius bouem occiderit, unde tenetur, quia culpa sine negligentia damnū datum est, qui debuit diligentiam exhibere. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod ideo Dominus bouis, non custodiendo tenetur, si bos suus damnum fecerit, quia debuit diligentiā adhibere, ex quo sciuit bouem suum cornupetam. Si autē quis dat occasionem damni, solummodo aliquid omittendo, si non tenebatur facere quod omisit: qualecunq; damnum acciderit ex occasione data, ille qui occasionem damni dedit, est immunis à culpa. Quod Exo. 21. Lex Diuina insinuare videtur, vbi sic legitur: si bos cornupeta percusserit virum aut mulierem, & mortui fuerint, lapidibus obruetur, & non comedentur carnes eius. Dominus quoq; bouis innocens erit, quod si bos cornupeta fuerit ab heri & nudius tertius, & contestati sunt Dominum eius, nec eum incluserit, occideritque virum & mulierem, & bos lapidibus obruetur, & dominum illius occident. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod si ex non reclusione bouis, quando Dominus ipsum recludere non tenetur, mors viri vel mulieris accidit, Domino non recludenti minime imputatur. Et ita qui occasionem damni dat aliquid omittendo, quod facere non tenetur, culpabilis minime iudicatur. Secundo dicunt, quod si quis dat occasionem damni aliquid faciendo, aut dat operam rei licitæ, aut rei illicitæ, si rei illicitæ, omne damnum, quod sequitur, ei imputatur. Si dat operam rei licitæ, aut adhibet diligentiam quam debet, sibi nullum damnum (quod sequitur) imputatur. Si autem non adhibet diligentiam debitam, tunc damnum quod sequitur ei imputatur. Discip. Ista valde rationabilia mihi videntur: sed non video, quomodo ad propositum debeant applicari. Magist. Nonnullis apparet, quod demonstratiue potest ostendi, quod impugnantes Papam de hæretica prauitate sunt à catholicis defendendi. Vt tamen ratio eorum magis appareat, probant primo istam conclusionem: quod videlicet taliter impugnantes Papam de prauitate hæretica, si quæruntur vel ducuntur ad mortem, sunt à morte corporali per catholicos, (si valuerint) liberandi. Et ex conclusione ista inferunt, quod ab omni persecutione & periculo sunt à catholicis eruendi. Discip. Proba primo, quod tales sunt à morte corporali liberandi. Mag. Hoc ostenditur auctoritate Salomonis, quæ allegata est supra, qui sic ait: erue eos qui ducuntur ad mortem &c. Hoc Aug. ut legitur 23. q. 4. c. ipsa pietas, videtur asserere manifeste dicens: q; si duo fuerint in domo ruitura, si possumus, ambos liberare tenemur. Quia, ut dicit ibidem, nisi faceremus, crudeles iudicaremur. Si etiam duo fuerit in aliqua domo ruitura, & neutet vult exire: si unus vult interficere seipsum, si alter fuerit liberatus, illum unum à morte liberare debemus. Similiter si multi essent in domo ruitura: & si unus solus liberaretur, omnes alii seipsos præcipitio vellent occidere, illum unum eruere debemus. Ergo quilibet tenetur alium etiam inuitum & nonlente à morte liberare si potest, etiam si ob talem liberationē vnius alii vellent seipsos occidere. Ergo multo fortius, si qs inuite & iniuste trahitur ad mortē, alii, qui possunt eum à morte liberare, tenetur. Ex quo sequitur, qp, qui possunt, debent quæsitos ad mortē defendere. Et ita si quis vult impugnantes Papā de prauitate hæretica quærere ad mortē, catholici q possunt vel armis resistendo, si competit ipsorū personis, vel quærentes eos ad mortē verbis monitoriis, aut supplicatoriis, & aliis modis, qbus possunt à tanta nequitia cõpescendo vel quæsitos ad mortē occultando, vel non tradendo eos debet defendere. Disc. Per istā rationē quicunq; videret latrones & homicidas & alios malefactores damnatos à iudice duci ad mortē eos si posset liberare deberet. Mag. Ad istam respondetur, qp secus est de illis, q seruato ordine iudiciario condemnatur ad mortē, & de illis qui absq; causæ cognitione, propter hoc, qp volunt superiore impugnare, mortis periculo exponuntur. Primi enim non sunt liberandi à morte: quia semp præsumitur, p his, quæ fiunt à iudice & pro sententia eius, nisi fuerit legitime reprobata vel p appellationem vel per alium modū congruenté suspensa. Et ideo tales damnati non sunt à morte liberandi, nisi à sententia iudicis appellatū existeret. Tunc enim liberandi essent ab illo, qui posset. Secundi vero liberandi sunt ab illis, q cõuenienter possunt. Et ideo si Papa mandaret aliquos capi & duci ad mortē propter hoc qp eum de prauitate hæretica impugnare, p causa, pro qua licet superiore impugnare niteruntur, liberandi essent. Quia in hoc casu sumendum esset pro impugnantib' Papā, & non p Papa. Quod autem præsumendū esset pro impugnantibus Papā ostenditur. Quia sicut vnusquisq; præsumitur bonus, nisi probetur contrariū, ita de quolibet præsumendū est, qp bene agit nisi contrariū constiterit p legitima documenta. Et ideo si quis facit illud, qp bene fieri potest, psumendum est, qp bene facit, anteqũ contrariū constiterit. Quia ea quæ bene & male fieri possunt, in meliorē partem interpretanda sunt. Cū ergo possibile sit, qp aliquis rite & iuste ac veraciter impugnet Papam de hæretica prauitate, præsumendū est de quolibet impugnante Papā de prauitate hæretica, qp rite & iuste faciat, anteqũ constet contrariū p impugnantibus. Ergo Papā de prauitate hæretica impugnātes præsumendum est anteqũ legitimis documentis constiterit, qp non maliciose impugnant neq; iniquē. Quod autē non sit præsumendū, p Papa, qui ante iudiciū præciperet taliter impugnantes neci tradi, vel etiā carceri mancipari, aut alias dure tractari, pbatur. Nam nõ est præsumendū pro illo, q iudiciū subterfugit: imo psumendū est contrariū, extra, de præsumpt. nullū. & ii.q.i. Christianum. & 3.q.9. decreuimus, & di.74. honorati. Sed Papa qui mandaret taliter impugnantes ipsum neci tradi vel dure tractari iudicium subterfugeret. Ergo non esset præsumendum pro illo, sed contra ipsum. Discip. Istæ allegationes duplicitep videntur deficere. Quia pro illo est minime præsumendum, qui iudicium subterfugit, quando tenetur stare in iudicio. Papa autem non tenetur stare in iudicio. Ergo si iudicium subterfugit, non est propter hoc præsumendum contra ipsum. Secundo deficiunt: quia non est præsumendum pro illo, qui præsumitur ex inuidia, & non ex charitate procedere. Sed qui Papam de prauitate hæretica impugnaret, præsumendum esset quod non ex charitate, sed ex inuidia impugnaret, quemadmodum præsumitur accusationem potius fieri causa inuidiæ quam charitatis, 6.q.1.c.si omnia. in textu & Gloss. & 2.q.7. si quis Episcopus. vbi canon notat accusationem, illaudabilem actionem. Ergo pro impugnantibus Papam de hæretica prauitate est nullatenus præsumendum: sed præsumendum est contra eos, sicut contra detractores. Magist. Ad primam istarum instantiarum nonnulli respondere niteruntur dicentes, quod Papa tenetur stare in iudicio, si apparuerint aliqui (q legitima exceptione repelli non possunt) qui eum voluerint de prauitate hæretica accusare. Cum enim, vt dicunt, constet aperte, quod potest de hæresi accusari, patenter infertur, quod aliqui sunt, qui valent Papam de hæresi accusare. Ex quibus sequitur euidenter, quod Papa in tali casu iudicio stare tenetur. Et ideo si iudicium subterfugit, reddit se suspectum, & est contra ipsum merito præsumendum.
