Idem ius est de haeresi minima & de maxima, quia idem est ius in paruis & in magnis, sic etiā deferendum est pro causa minima, sicut pro maxima interiectae appellationi, furtum etiam committitur in re minima sicut in maxima, sed si aliquis Papa haereticus effectus diceret se Christum & verum Deum, sicut Christus fuit verus Deus, voce Christi esset Papatu priuatus, cū dicit: Nolite ire post illos, illis n. verbis Christus nullū praecepit esse sequendum, qui diceret se Christū & Deum, & per consequens eisdem verbis Papa Papatu priuauit, si praesumeret se Christum & verū Deum, ergo cōsimiliter Christus eisdē verbis Papatu priuauit omne Papam, qui in quamcunq; etiā minimam haeresim laberetur. Et p hoc respondent ad instantiā memorata dicentes, q verba Christi praedicta debent intelligi tā de illis, qui dicturi erant se dignitate Christi habere, q̄ de omnibus haereticis asserentib. sese doctrinam veram astruere. Per secundam etiam instantiam intentum probare niteruntur, quia si Papa est sequendus; aut sequendus est quantum ad doctrinam, aut quantū ad praecepta, sed neutro modo Papa haereticus est sequendus, ergo non est verus Papa. Maior videtur aperta, minor probatur, quod non sit sequendus quo ad doctrinam, patet, quia nulla haeretica doctrina est sequenda. Quod etiam non sit sequēdus, quantum ad praecepta, patet, quia vnum de principalibus praeceptis Papae est, vt subiecti eius doctrinam seruent: si ergo Papa haereticus non est sequendus, quo ad doctrinam, nec etiam quo ad praecepta est sequendus, & per hoc patet responsio ad instantiam, quam adducis. Ad tertiam respondetur, quod Papa non est in omnibus sequendus, si enim male viuit, eius vita nullatenus est sequenda, & ideo si docet aliquid absque omni pertinacia contra fidem, in hoc minime est sequendus. Papa tamen manet Papa, quantum autem ad illa, quae contra fidem docet irreuocabiliter, non est sequendus, & ideo si aliquid irreuocabiliter docet contra fidem, sic eo ipso non est verus Papa, & est Papatu priuatus, si autem aliquid docet contra fidem & paratus est corrigi, non est Papatu priuatus. Disc. Quomodo scietur hoc, quod Papa docet aliquid irreuocabiliter contra fidem, & aliquid non irreuocabiliter? Mag. Ad hoc dicitur, quod hoc iudicari debet per verba & per opera eius, quandoque enim conuincendus est per verba, quae dicit: quandoque per opera quae agit, sicut ex quarto huius potes aduertere.
units.tr: Ioan. 3. against the faith, he would be deprived of the papacy. For whoever teaches false doctrine, whether obstinately or not obstinately, is not to be followed in this; and so one who came in the name of Christ, saying, I am the Pope and vicar of Christ, and held doctrine contrary to the faith in whatever way, one would not go after him, and consequently he would be deprived of the papacy, which is wholly contrary to the truth. Mag. Some people think your objections are trivial, supposing that by them they prove demonstratively the conclusion intended. For through the first they show (as it seems to them clearly) that a Pope, if he becomes a heretic, is deprived of the papacy by the voice of Christ; for they make this argument: the same law applies to the smallest heresy as to the greatest, because the same law holds for small matters and great, and so an appeal is to be rejected in a minor case as in a major one; theft is also committed in a small thing as in a great one. But if a Pope who has become a heretic were to say that he is Christ and true God, just as Christ was true God, he would be deprived of the papacy by the voice of Christ when he says: Do not go after them; for by those words Christ commanded that no one who called himself Christ and God should be followed. Consequently, by those same words, the Pope has deprived himself of the papacy if he presumes to call himself Christ and true God. Therefore, in the same way, by those same words, Christ deprived of the papacy every Pope who fell into any heresy, however small. And in answer to the objection mentioned, they say that the words of Christ above must be understood both of those who would claim to have the dignity of Christ and of all heretics who assert that they teach true doctrine. Through the second objection too they try to prove their point, because if the Pope is to be followed, he is to be followed either as to doctrine or as to precepts; but a heretical Pope is to be followed in neither way; therefore he is not a true Pope. The major premise seems clear; the minor is proved thus: that he is not to be followed as to doctrine is evident, because no heretical doctrine is to be followed. That he is not to be followed as to precepts is also evident, because one of the principal precepts of the Pope is that his subjects keep his doctrine. If, then, a heretical Pope is not to be followed as to doctrine, neither is he to be followed as to precepts; and by this the answer to the objection you raise is plain. To the third, it is answered that the Pope is not to be followed in everything; for if he lives wickedly, his life is in no way to be followed, and so if he teaches anything contrary to the faith without any obstinacy, he is in no way to be followed in that. The Pope nevertheless remains Pope. But as to those things which he teaches contrary to the faith irrevocably, he is not to be followed; and so if he irrevocably teaches anything contrary to the faith, by that very fact he is not a true Pope and is deprived of the papacy; but if he teaches something contrary to the faith and is ready to be corrected, he is not deprived of the papacy. Disc. How will it be known whether the Pope teaches something irrevocably contrary to the faith, and something not irrevocably? Mag. To this it is said that this must be judged by his words and his works; for sometimes he must be convicted by the words he speaks, and sometimes by the deeds he does, as you may observe from the fourth part of this book.

units.la: Discipul. Sunt ne plures rationes pro assertione praedicta? Magist. Secunda ratio in sacra Scriptura fundata est talis, vniuersi pseudoprophetae & pseudochristi a cunctis fidelibus sunt vitandi, ipsa veritate testante, quae vt habetur Matthaei 24. ait: Surgent enim pseudochristi & pseudoprophetae, & dabunt signa magna & prodigia, ita vt in errorem inducantur (si fieri potest) etiam electi, ecce praedixi vobis, si ergo dixerint vobis: ecce in deserto est: nolite exire, ecce in penetralibus: nolite credere. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod pseudoprophetae & pseudochristi sunt vitandi. Sed Papa, si efficiatur haereticus, inter pseudoprophetas & pseudochristos est censendus, ergo vera voce Christi quam cito sic scitur esse talis a cunctis catholicis est vitandus. Et per consequens voce Christi est Papatu priuatus: quia verus Papa a catholicis nullatenus est vitandus.
units.tr: Disciple. Are there several arguments for the assertion stated above? Master. The second argument is grounded in Holy Scripture as follows: all false prophets and false christs are to be avoided by all the faithful, as the truth itself testifies in Matthew 24, where it says: For there shall arise false christs and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders, insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect. Behold, I have told you before. Wherefore if they shall say unto you, Behold, he is in the desert; go not forth: behold, he is in the secret chambers; believe it not. From these words it is clear that false prophets and false christs are to be avoided. But if the Pope becomes a heretic, he must be counted among the false prophets and false christs. Therefore, by the voice of Christ, as soon as he is known to be such, he is to be avoided by all Catholics. And consequently, by the voice of Christ, he is deprived of the papacy, since a true Pope is by no means to be avoided by Catholics.

units.la: Tertia ratio est talis, qui est de medio fidelium auferendus, non est verus Papa: cum verus Papa sit a cunctis fidelibus honorandus. Sed Papa haereticus etiam si signa faceret, & praediceret aliqua, & ita euenirent, est de medio fidelium auferendus: eo quod sententia diuina lata est contra ipsum, Deuteronom. 13. vbi sic legitur: Si surrexerit in medio tui propheta, aut qui somnium dicat se vidisse, & praedixerit signum, atque portentum, & euenerit quod est & dixerit tibi: eamus & sequamur Deos alienos, quos ignoras, & seruiamus eis, non audies verba prophetae illius aut somniatoris, quia tentat vos Dominus Deus vester, & infra: propheta autem ille aut fictor somniorum interficietur, quia locutus est, vt vos auerteret a Domino Deo vestro, qui eduxit vos de terra Aegypti, & redemit vos de domo seruitutis, vt errare te faceret de via, quam praecepit tibi Dominus Deus, & auferes malum de medio tui. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod quicunque nullo excepto visus fuerit a via Domini, & a veritate catholica fideles auertere, est de medio fidelium auferendus. Sed Papa, si est haereticus & prauitatem docuerit haereticam, a fide conatur fideles auertere, ergo est de medio fidelium auferendus, & per consequens verus Papa minime est censendus. Discipulus. Si Papa doceret seruire diis falsis vel colere idola, videtur quod eo ipso non esset reputandus verus Papa: sed propter quamlibet haeresim non videtur, quod sit statim Papatu priuatus. Magister. Hic concedis, quod est aliqua haeresis, quam si Papa incurreret, statim ipso facto est Papatu priuatus voce Dei, ergo pro omni haeresi cui pertinaciter adhaeserit, est ipso facto per diuinam sententiam Papatu priuatus. Quia de haeresi vna & alia quantum ad hoc consimiliter est dicendum.
units.tr: The third argument is this: whoever must be removed from the midst of the faithful is not a true Pope, since a true Pope is to be honoured by all the faithful. But a heretical Pope, even if he worked signs and foretold certain things and they came to pass, must be removed from the midst of the faithful, because a divine sentence has been pronounced against him in Deuteronomy 13, where it is read thus: If there arise in the midst of thee a prophet, or one that saith he hath seen a dream, and he foretell a sign or wonder, and the thing come to pass whereof he spake, saying, Let us go after other gods, which thou hast not known, and let us serve them; thou shalt not hearken unto the words of that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams: for the Lord your God proveth you... And that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death; because he hath spoken to turn you away from the Lord your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, to thrust thee out of the way which the Lord thy God commanded thee to walk in. So shalt thou put the evil away from the midst of thee. From these words it is gathered that whoever, without exception, is seen to turn the faithful away from the way of the Lord and from Catholic truth, is to be removed from the midst of the faithful. But the Pope, if he is a heretic and teaches a heretical perversity, seeks to turn the faithful away from the faith. Therefore he must be removed from the midst of the faithful, and consequently a true Pope is by no means to be counted such. Disciple. If the Pope were to teach the serving of false gods or the worship of idols, it seems that by that very fact he would not be regarded as a true Pope; but it does not seem that he is at once deprived of the papacy on account of any heresy whatever. Master. Here you concede that there is some heresy which, if the Pope fell into it, would at once, by that very fact, deprive him of the papacy by the voice of God. Therefore, for every heresy to which he has obstinately adhered, he is by that very fact deprived of the papacy by divine sentence. For what is said of one heresy and of another must be said alike in this respect.

units.la: Quarta ratio est haec, Antichristus non est verus Christi vicarius, sed Papa haereticus est veracter Antichristus, teste beato Iohanne in canonica sua 1. c. 9. ait: omnis spiritus qui soluit Iesum ex Deo non est, & hic est Antichristus, & de eo audistis quoniam iam venit. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod quicunque negat fidem Christi Antichristus est censendus; Papa ergo haereticus est Antichristus, & per consequens non est verus vicarius Christi. Ex quo sequitur, quod est Papatu priuatus.
units.tr: The fourth argument is this: Antichrist is not the true vicar of Christ, but a heretical Pope is truly Antichrist. The blessed John, in his Epistle 1, chapter 9, testifies to this: Every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that spirit of Antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come. From these words it is clear that whoever denies the faith of Christ is to be counted Antichrist. Therefore a heretical Pope is Antichrist, and consequently is not the true vicar of Christ. From this it follows that he is deprived of the papacy.

units.la: Quinta ratio est hæc, ille non est verus Papa, cui fideles minime communicare debent, quia Papæ est communicandum & obediendum, sed Papæ hæretico minime fideles communicare debent, ergo Papa hæreticus non est verus Papa. Maior est manifesta. Minor probatur auctoritate B. Ioh. qui in canonica sua ait: Si quis venerit ad vos, & hanc doctrinam suam non affert, nolite recipere eum in domum: nec aue ei dixeritis, qui enim dixerit ei aue, communicat operibus eius malis, quæ verba Beda, ut legitur 24. q. 1. c. omnis, exponens ait: Si quis venit ad vos, & hanc doctrinam non affert: nolite recipere eum in domum, nec aue ei dixeritis, qui enim dixit illi aue, communicat illius operibus malis, hac enim Iohan. de schismatibus fuge hereticis deuitandis, quae verbis docuit & factis exhibuit, narrat enim de illo auditor eius sanctissimus vir & martyr fortissimus Polycarpus Smirneorum antistes, quod tempore quodam cum apud Ephesum balnea lauandi gratia fuisset ingressus, & vidisset ibi Cherintum: exiit continuo, & discessit non lotus, dicens: Fugiamus hinc, ne balnea ipsa corruant, in quibus Cherintus lauatur inimicus veritatis. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod ei qui non affert doctrinam Christi, est nullatenus communicandum, Papa autem hæreticus non affert doctrinam Christi, ergo ei nullatenus est communicandum: & per consequens non est verus Papa.
units.tr: The fifth argument is this: he is not a true Pope with whom the faithful ought by no means to have communion, since the Pope is to be communicated with and obeyed. But the faithful ought by no means to have communion with a heretical Pope; therefore a heretical Pope is not a true Pope. The major premise is evident. The minor is proved by the authority of the blessed John, who in his Epistle says: If there come any unto you, and bring not this doctrine, receive him not into your house, neither bid him God speed: for he that biddeth him God speed is partaker of his evil deeds. Bede, as it is read in 24 q. 1 c. Omnis, expounding these words, says: If anyone comes to you and does not bring this doctrine, do not receive him into your house, nor say to him, God speed; for he who says to him, God speed, shares in his evil works. By this John teaches, in words and shows by deeds, that heretics must be shunned in schism. For his hearer, the most holy man and most brave martyr Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, relates of him that on a certain occasion, when he had gone into the baths at Ephesus to wash, and saw Cerinthus there, he immediately went out and departed unwashed, saying: "Let us flee from here, lest the baths themselves fall down, in which Cerinthus, the enemy of the truth, is washing." From these words it is clear that one who does not bring the doctrine of Christ is by no means to be communicated with. But a heretical Pope does not bring the doctrine of Christ; therefore he is by no means to be communicated with, and consequently he is not a true Pope.

units.la: Disc. Beatus Iohannes non loquitur de Papa hæretico: sed de aliis hæreticis, quibus non est communicandum. Magist. Hæc responsio impugnatur, primo, quia beatus Iohannes inter Papam non asserentem doctrinam Christi & alium non distinguit: sed dat pro regula generali, quod quicunq; non attulerit doctrinam Christi non est communicandum eidem. Secundo ostenditur ex ratione beati Ioh. quod regula sua magis intelligenda est de Papa hæretico, quam de aliis hæreticis. Affirmatur enim pro ratione, quare hæreticus est vitandus, & non est dicendum ei aue, dicit: qui enim dixerit sibi aue: communicat operibus suis malis. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod qui dicit aue hæretico, communicat suis operibus malignis, sed operibus malis neque Papæ hæretici neque aliorum hæreticorum communicandum est, eo quod propter dignitatem, qua fungitur Papa hæreticus, magis nocere valeret fidei orthodoxæ, si fautores, sequaces & defensores haberet quam alii hæretici, teste beato Augustino, ut legitur distinct. 83. c. nemo, ait: nemo quippe in ecclesia Dei amplius nocet, quam qui peruerse agens nomen vel ordinem sanctitatis vel sacerdotis habet, delinquentem namque hunc redarguere nullus præsumit: & in exemplum culpa vehementer extenditur, quando pro reuerentia ordinis peccator honoratur. Ex quibus verbis infertur, quod nemo amplius nocere potest ecclesiæ Dei, quam Papa peruersè & hæretsim dogmatizans, si pro reuerentia Papalis officii honoratur. Si ergo operibus malis aliorum hæreticorum catholici communicare non debent: multo magis communicare non debent operibus malis Papæ hæretici, & per consequens ei dicere aue non debent: quia secundum beatum Ioh. qui dicit cuicunque hæretico aue, communicat operibus illius malignis.
units.tr: Disciple. The blessed John does not speak of a heretical Pope, but of other heretics, with whom communion is not to be held. Master. This answer is refuted, first, because the blessed John does not distinguish between a Pope who does not assert the doctrine of Christ and anyone else; he gives as a general rule that whoever does not bring the doctrine of Christ is not to be communicated with. Secondly, it is shown from the reason given by the blessed John that his rule is to be understood more of a heretical Pope than of other heretics. For a reason is given why the heretic is to be avoided and is not to be greeted: for he that biddeth him God speed is partaker of his evil deeds. From these words it is clear that whoever greets a heretic shares in his wicked deeds. But neither the heretical Pope nor other heretics are to be shared in their evil deeds, and this holds all the more for the heretical Pope, because by reason of the dignity which the heretical Pope holds, he could do more harm to the orthodox faith, if he had supporters, followers and defenders, than other heretics could. So the blessed Augustine teaches, as it is read in distinction 83, c. Nemo: For no one does more harm in the Church of God than he who, acting perversely, bears the name or order of holiness or of the priesthood; for no one presumes to rebuke such an offender; and the fault is greatly extended as an example when a sinner is honoured out of reverence for his order. From these words it follows that no one can do more harm to the Church of God than a Pope who perversely teaches heresy, if he is honoured out of reverence for the papal office. If therefore Catholics ought not to communicate with the evil deeds of other heretics, much less ought they to communicate with the evil deeds of a heretical Pope, and consequently they ought not to bid him God speed, because according to the blessed John whoever bids any heretic God speed shares in his wicked deeds.

units.la: Discip. Alias rationes adducas. Magist. Sexta ratio est hæc. Ille non est verus Papa, qui neque in spiritualibus, neque in temporalibus debet esse iudex fidelium, quia verus Papa est verus Iudex omnium Christianorum. Sed Papa hæreticus neque in spiritualibus, neque in temporalibus debet esse Iudex fidelium. Quia non in temporalibus, patet per Apostolum, qui primæ ad Cor. 6. Corinthios reprehendit, quod coram infidelibus litigabant, dicens sic: Non est inter vos sapiens quisquam, qui possit iudicare inter fratrem suum? sed frater cum fratre contendit in iudicio: & hoc apud infideles. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi: quod fideles etiam pro temporalibus non debent coram infidelibus contendere, si inter se sapientem habuerint, qui inter ipsos sciat & valeat iudicare. Ex quo concluditur, quod multo fortius infidelis in spiritualibus non debet esse iudex fidelium, Papa autem hæreticus est infidelis, ergo non debet esse iudex fidelium: & per consequens non est verus Papa.
units.tr: Disciple. Bring forward other arguments. Master. The sixth argument is this: he is not a true Pope who ought to be the judge of the faithful neither in spiritual nor in temporal matters, since a true Pope is the true judge of all Christians. But a heretical Pope ought to be the judge of the faithful neither in spiritual nor in temporal matters. That he ought not in temporal matters is clear from the Apostle, who in 1 Corinthians 6 rebuked the Corinthians because they went to law before unbelievers, saying: Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints? ... Is there not a wise man among you, who shall be able to judge between his brethren? But brother goeth to law with brother, and that before the unbelievers. From these words it is gathered that even in temporal matters the faithful ought not to contend before unbelievers, if they have among themselves a wise man who knows and is able to judge between them. From this it is concluded that much more an unbeliever ought not to be the judge of the faithful in spiritual matters. But the heretical Pope is an unbeliever; therefore he ought not to be the judge of the faithful, and consequently he is not a true Pope.

units.la: Septima ratio est talis, ille qui tanquam proprio iudicio condemnatus est, est a fidelibus euitandus, Papa hæreticus tanquam proprio iudicio condemnatus est, ergo est a fidelibus euitandus, teste Apostolo, qui ad Titum 3. ait: Hæreticum hominem post vnam & secundam correctionem deuita, sciens, quod subuersus est, qui eiusmodi est & delinquit cum sit proprio iudicio condemnatus, ergo est euitandus. Quod etiam Ambros. vt habetur 24. q. 1. c. quae dignior, asserit manifeste ita dicens: fides ergo in primis ecclesia quaerenda mandatur: in qua si Christus habitator fit, haud dubie sit legendum. Si vero perfidus populus aut preceptor hereticus deformet ecclesia habitaculum, vitanda hereticorum communio; fugienda synagoga censetur; exutiendus pedum pulvis, ne satisceentibus perfidiæ sterilis siccitatibus tanquam humi arida arenosaque mentis tua vestigium polluatur. Nam sicut corporeas infirmitates populi fidelis suscipere in se debet euangelii predicator, iuxta quod scriptum est: quis infirmatur & ego non infirmor? & ita si qua est ecclesia, quae fidem respuat, nec Apostolica predicationis fundamenta possideat, ne, quem labe perfidiæ possit aspergere, deserenda est. Quod Apostolus quoque asseruit euidenter, dicens, hæreticum hominem post vnam & alteram correctionem deuita. Ex quibus verbis potest intelligi, quod Papa hæreticus etiam absque omni humana sententia est vitandus. Ratio enim, quare Ambrosius asserit hæreticos esse deuitandos, est, ne quos labe perfidiæ scil. prauitatis hæreticæ possit aspergere. Papa autem hæreticus inter omnes hæreticos efficacius, fortius, celerius, & vniuersalius potest aspergere prauitate hæretica populos Christianos, ergo Papa hæreticus ante omnem humanam sententiam est a catholicis (tanquam diuina condemnatus sententia) deuitādus; & per consequens verus Papa minime est censendus. Disc. Verba Apostoli videntur ostendere, quod Papa hæreticus non est sententia diuina condemnatus, cum dicat Apostolus hæreticum hominem post primam & secundam correctionem deuita, aperte insinuans, quod ante primam & secundam correctionem non est a fidelibus deuitandus. Ex quo infertur, quod Papa hæreticus ante primam & secundam correctionem diuina sententia non est condemnatus. Mag. Ad istam obiectionem respondetur, quod prima & secunda correctio minime requiruntur ad condemnationem Papæ hæretici, necpræcedunt condemnationem eius: quia absq; omni correctione Papa hereticus est damnatus, cum correctio sententiam damnationis nequaquam contineat, & nullus absque omni sententia diuina & humana est vitandus. Si Papa hæreticus post primam & secundam correctionem sic est vitandus, constat quod ante correctionem primam & secundam Papa hæreticus aliqua sententia diuina vel humana extitit condemnatus, & ita prima & secunda correctio non præcedunt sententiam condemnationis Papæ hæretici: sed sæpe quando aliquis fit hæreticus, quia negat veritatem, quam non tenetur explicite credere ad hoc, quod sciatur esse damnatus diuina sententia, & per consequens, vt constet, quod est à catholicis deuitandus, requiritur prima & secunda correctio: quia sæpe aliter constare non potest, quod est prauitate hæretica irretitus, quandoq; enim per primam correctionem minime innotescit, quod errans contra fidem pertinaciter errat, & ideo adhuc non constat, quod est vitandus. Per secundam autem correctionem constat an paratus sit corrigi, vel in sua sententia pertinaciter perseuerare, & ideo tunc scitur an sit diuina sententia condemnatus, & per consequens an sit à fidelibus euitandus. Per primam ergo & secundam correctionem intelligit Apostolus omnem correctionem, in qua innotescit errantem esse in sua sententia pertinacem, & per consequens qua constat illum esse diuina sententia condemnatum, & à catholicis deuitandum.
units.tr: The seventh reason is this: whoever has been condemned by his own judgment is to be avoided by the faithful. The Pope, being a heretic, has been condemned by his own judgment. Therefore he is to be avoided by the faithful. The Apostle bears witness to this in Titus 3, where he says: "Avoid a heretical man after a first and second admonition, knowing that such a man is subverted and sins, being condemned by his own judgment." Ambrose also asserts this plainly, as found in 24 q. 1 c. quae dignior, saying: "Therefore the faith is first to be sought in the Church, and where Christ dwells there, beyond doubt, one must read. But if a faithless people or a heretical teacher defiles the dwelling of the Church, the communion of heretics is to be avoided, the synagogue is to be shunned, and the dust of the feet is to be shaken off, lest the dry dust of faithlessness cling to you and your footprint be polluted as on barren and sandy ground. For just as the preacher of the gospel must take upon himself the bodily weaknesses of the faithful people, according to what is written, 'Who is weak, and I am not weak?', so if there is a church which rejects the faith and does not hold the foundations of apostolic preaching, it is to be abandoned, lest one be stained by the blemish of its faithlessness." The Apostle also clearly asserts this, saying: "Avoid a heretical man after a first and second admonition." From these words it can be understood that a heretical Pope is to be avoided by Catholics even without any human sentence. For the reason Ambrose gives for saying that heretics are to be avoided is lest they stain us with the blemish of heretical depravity. But a heretical Pope, more effectively, more strongly, more swiftly and more widely than any other heretic, can stain Christian peoples with heretical depravity. Therefore a heretical Pope, before any human sentence, is to be avoided by Catholics as one condemned by divine sentence; and consequently he is by no means to be counted a true Pope. Student: The words of the Apostle seem to show that a heretical Pope is not condemned by divine sentence, since the Apostle says, "Avoid a heretical man after the first and second admonition," clearly implying that before the first and second admonition he is not to be avoided by the faithful. From this it follows that a heretical Pope is not condemned by divine sentence before the first and second admonition. Master: To this objection the answer is that the first and second admonition are by no means required for the condemnation of a heretical Pope, nor do they precede his condemnation; for a heretic is condemned even without any admonition, since admonition by no means contains the sentence of condemnation, and no one is to be avoided without any divine or human sentence. If a heretical Pope is to be avoided after the first and second admonition, it is plain that before the first and second admonition he was already condemned by some divine or human sentence; and so the first and second admonition do not precede the sentence condemning a heretical Pope. But often, when someone becomes a heretic by denying a truth which he is not explicitly bound to believe, the first and second admonition are required in order that it may be known that he has been condemned by divine sentence, and consequently, so that it may be established that he is to be avoided by Catholics. For often it cannot otherwise be established that he is entangled in heretical depravity; for sometimes by the first admonition it does not become known that one who errs against the faith errs stubbornly, and so it is not yet established that he is to be avoided. But by the second admonition it is established whether he is ready to be corrected or persists stubbornly in his opinion, and then it is known whether he has been condemned by divine sentence and consequently whether he is to be avoided by the faithful. Therefore by the first and second admonition the Apostle means every admonition in which it becomes known that the erring man is stubborn in his opinion, and so by which it is established that he has been condemned by divine sentence and is to be avoided by Catholics.

units.la: Disc. Sunt ne plures rationes pro assertione prædicta? Mag. Octaua ratio est hæc, Qui est anathematizatus, non est verus Papa: quia talis est ab ecclesia separatus. Verus autem Papa est ab ecclesia minime separatus, cum sit caput ecclesiæ, caput autem ab ecclesia separatum non est amplius caput, sicut nec caput à corpore separatum est amplius caput, quemadmodum homo mortuus non est homo, vt dicit Aristoteles, caput est capitati caput. Sed Papa hæreticus est anathematizatus, teste Apostolo, qui ad Gal. ca. 1. ait: licet nos autem angelus de cælo euangelizet vobis præterquam, quod euangelizauimus vobis, anathema sit sicut prædiximus, & nunc iterum dico: si quis vobis euangelizauerit præter id quod accepistis, anathema sit, ergo Papa hæreticus non est papa. Discip. Videtur quod ista ratio non concludit: quia Apostolus non concludit, quod talis euangelizator anathema est, sed dicit, anathema sit, insinuás quod talis non est anathematizatus, sed anathematizandus, & ita papa hæreticus non est anathematizatus, sed anathematizandus. Mag. Respondetur quod verba Apostoli non recte intelligis, non enim dicit Apostolus Anathema sit, quia euangelizator hæreticalis doctrinæ est anathematizandus, non anathematizatus. Sed ideo dicit, anathema sit, quia vult verba sua intelligi conditionaliter, scil. si aliquis euangelizaret contra Apostolicam doctrinam, sequitur quod sit anathema, ita quod talis conditionalis est vera, si aliquis euangelizaret contra doctrinam Apostoli, ipse est anathema. Aliter dicitur, & prædictis non obuiat, cum dicit Apostolus, anathema sit, hoc est tanquam anathema sit habendus, & per consequens talis est ab ecclesia fidelium separatus.
units.tr: Student: Are there more reasons for the assertion just made? Master: The eighth reason is this: whoever is anathematized is not a true Pope, because such a man is separated from the Church. But a true Pope is by no means separated from the Church, since he is the head of the Church; and a head separated from the Church is no longer a head, just as a head separated from the body is no longer a head, as a dead man is no longer a man, as Aristotle says: "the head is the head of one who has a head." But a heretical Pope is anathematized, as the Apostle bears witness, who says in Gal. 1: "But even if an angel from heaven should preach to you otherwise than what we have preached to you, let him be anathema. As we said before, so now I say again: if anyone preaches to you otherwise than what you have received, let him be anathema." Therefore a heretical Pope is not a Pope. Student: It seems that this reasoning does not follow, because the Apostle does not conclude that such a preacher is anathema; he says, "let him be anathema," implying that such a man is not anathematized but is to be anathematized, and so a heretical Pope is not anathematized but is to be anathematized. Master: The answer is that you do not rightly understand the Apostle's words. For the Apostle does not say "let him be anathema" because a preacher of heretical doctrine is to be anathematized rather than anathematized. Rather he says "let him be anathema" because he wishes his words to be understood conditionally: if anyone should preach against apostolic doctrine, it follows that he is anathema; so that the conditional is true: if anyone should preach against the doctrine of the Apostle, he is anathema. It is also said otherwise, and this does not conflict with what has been said: when the Apostle says "let him be anathema," he means that he is to be held as anathema, and consequently such a man is separated from the community of the faithful.

units.la: Disc. Alias audiam libenter rationes. Mag. Nona ratio est talis, homo alterius secta non debuit esse rex fidelium constitutorum sub veteri lege, papa autem est caput omnium constitutorum sub noua lege, ergo nullus alterius secta potest esse verus papa, sed papa verus est caput omnium Christianorum, papa autem hæreticus est alterius secta, ergo hæreticus non est verus papa. Quod autem homo alterius secta non debuit esse rex fidelium constitutorum sub veteri lege, lex diuina manifestat apertius, cum dicat Deuter. 16. Non poteris alterius gentis hominem regem facere, qui non sit frater tuus, ergo cōsimiliter homo alterius secta non est verus papa.
units.tr: Student: I would gladly hear other reasons. Master: The ninth reason is this: a man of another sect ought not to have been king of the faithful who were constituted under the old law; but the Pope is the head of all who are constituted under the new law. Therefore no one of another sect can be a true Pope. But the true Pope is the head of all Christians, and a heretical Pope is of another sect; therefore a heretic is not a true Pope. That a man of another sect ought not to have been king of the faithful constituted under the old law the divine law shows more plainly, since it says in Deut. 16: "You shall not make a man of another nation king, who is not your brother." Therefore likewise a man of another sect is not a true Pope.

units.la: Decima ratio est hæc, nemo alterius secta est verus propheta & doctor Christianorum, ergo multo magis nemo alterius secta est verus papa catholicorum, papa autem hæreticus est alterius secta, ergo non est verus papa. Quod autem nemo alterius secta possit esse propheta aut doctor catholicorum diuinis testimoniis videtur aperte probari. Ait enim Dominus Moysi Deut. 18. Prophetam suscitabo eis de medio fratrum suorum similem tui, & ponam verba mea in ore eius. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod verus papa & doctor omnium Christianorum catholicorum est de medio tantummodo fidelium suscitandus, & ita alterius secta esse non potest, & per consequens homo alterius secta non est verus papa, cum verus papa sit propheta verus, id est doctor fidelium, quia verbo pascere debet catholicos, Christo dicente Petro: pasce oues meas.
units.tr: The tenth reason is this: no one of another sect is a true prophet and teacher of Christians; therefore much more no one of another sect is a true Pope of Catholics. But a heretical Pope is of another sect; therefore he is not a true Pope. That no one of another sect can be a prophet or teacher of Catholics seems plainly proved by divine testimonies. For the Lord said to Moses in Deut. 18: "I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brothers, like you, and I will put my words in his mouth." From these words it is gathered that the true Pope and teacher of all Catholic Christians is to be raised up only from among the faithful themselves; and so he cannot be of another sect, and consequently a man of another sect is not a true Pope, since the true Pope is a true prophet, that is, a teacher of the faithful, because he ought to feed Catholics with the Word, Christ saying to Peter: "Feed my sheep."

units.la: Vndecima ratio est hæc, verus papa est verus pastor ouium Christi, papa autem hæreticus non est verus pastor ouium Christi, ergo papa hæreticus non est verus papa. Maior est manifesta: quia est successor B. Petri, qui fuit verus papa à Christo constitutus. Minor probatur, quia verus pastor ouium Christi est sequendus, teste ipso Christo, qui, vt legitur Ioh. 10. de vero pastore loquens, ait: Oues eius vocem audiunt, & proprias oues vocat nominatim & educit eas & cum proprias oues emiserit ante eas vadit & oues ei sequuntur, ita patet, quod verus pastor est sequendus, papa autem hæreticus non est sequendus, ergo non est verus pastor. Item, fur non est verus pastor: quia veritas (vbi prius) furem à vero pastore distinguit. Sed papa hæreticus est fur: quia papa hæreticus tanquam fur non venit nisi vt furetur & mactet & perdat, ergo papa hæreticus non est verus pastor, & per consequens non est verus papa.
units.tr: The eleventh reason is this: the true Pope is the true shepherd of Christ's sheep; but a heretical Pope is not the true shepherd of Christ's sheep; therefore a heretical Pope is not a true Pope. The major is manifest, since he is the successor of St. Peter, who was constituted true Pope by Christ. The minor is proved, because the true shepherd of Christ's sheep is to be followed, as Christ himself witnesses, who, as we read in John 10, speaking of the true shepherd, says: "His sheep hear his voice, and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out; and when he has brought out his own sheep, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him." It is thus plain that the true shepherd is to be followed; but a heretical Pope is not to be followed; therefore he is not a true shepherd. Likewise, a thief is not a true shepherd, because the truth (in the passage cited above) distinguishes the thief from the true shepherd. But a heretical Pope is a thief, because a heretical Pope, like a thief, comes only to steal and kill and destroy; therefore a heretical Pope is not a true shepherd, and consequently is not a true Pope.

units.la: Duodecima ratio est hæc, qui non est de corpore ecclesiæ militantis, non est verus papa: eo quod verus papa est verum caput ecclesiæ. Sed papa hæreticus (nulla etiam contra eum humana lata sententia) non est de corpore ecclesiæ quantumcunque putetur esse de corpore ecclesiæ, ergo papa hæreticus non est papa. Maior est euidens. Minor ostenditur sic. Nullus hæreticus est de corpore ecclesiæ, ergo papa hæreticus non est de corpore ecclesiæ. Antecedens probatur aperte auctoritate Greg. afferentis, quod licet mali catholici pertineant ad ecclesiam, quæ comprehendit bonos & malos, hæretici tamen non sunt de societate ecclesiæ. Ait enim Greg. in omelia de parabola zizaniorum: cum negligenter agerent prapositi ecclesiæ, & dormitionem mortis acciperent Apostoli, venit diabolus & superseminauit eos, quos malos filios Deus interpretatur. Sed recte quaeritur, utrum haeretici sint an male viuentes catholici, possunt enim dici mali filii & haeretici, qui ex eodem semine euangelii & Christi nomine procreati prauis opinionibus ad falsa dogmata conuertuntur. Sed quod dicit eos in medio tritici seminatos, quo videntur illi significari, qui vnius conditionis sunt, veruntamen quoniam Dominus agrum non ecclesiam, sed hunc mundum interpretatur, intelliguntur haeretici, qui non societate vnius ecclesiæ vel vnius fidei, sed societate solius nominis Christiani in hoc mundo permiscentur bonis, vt illi qui in eadem fide mali sunt palea potius, quam zizania reputentur, quia palea etiam fundamentum idem habet cum frumento radicemque communem. In illa palea sane sagenaque, qua concluduntur & mali & boni, non absurde intelliguntur mali catholici, aliud mare magnum, quod significat ipsum mundum, aliud sagena, qua vnius fidei vel vnius ecclesiæ communionem videtur ostendere.
units.tr: The twelfth argument is this: whoever is not of the body of the militant Church is not a true pope, because a true pope is the true head of the Church. But a heretical pope (even without any human sentence pronounced against him) is not of the body of the Church, however much he may be thought to be, therefore a heretical pope is not pope. The major premise is evident. The minor is shown thus. No heretic is of the body of the Church; therefore a heretical pope is not of the body of the Church. The antecedent is plainly proved by the authority of Gregory, who asserts that although bad Catholics belong to the Church, which comprises both good and bad, heretics are nevertheless not in the fellowship of the Church. For Gregory says in his homily on the parable of the tares: when the leaders of the Church were acting carelessly and the Apostles fell into the sleep of death, the devil came and sowed among them those whom God calls evil sons. But it is rightly asked whether they are heretics or badly living Catholics, for those can be called evil sons and heretics who, born of the same seed of the gospel and in the name of Christ, are turned by depraved opinions to false doctrines. But when he says they were sown in the midst of the wheat, by which those who share one condition seem to be signified, nevertheless, since the Lord interprets the field not as the Church but as this world, heretics are understood to be those who are mixed among the good in this world not by fellowship in one Church or one faith, but by fellowship in the name of Christian alone. Thus those who are evil in the same faith should be reckoned chaff rather than tares, because chaff also has the same foundation as the wheat and a common root. In that chaff, and in the net in which both evil and good are enclosed, the evil Catholics are not absurdly understood; the great sea, which signifies the world itself, is one thing, and the net, which seems to show the communion of one faith or one Church, is another.

units.la: Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod absque omni humana sententia omnes haeretici sunt a corpore ecclesiæ separati, nec sunt de ecclesia, licet quidam eorum putentur esse de ecclesia, quia quod sunt haeretici ignoratur, dicit enim Gregorius, quod haeretici non societate vnius ecclesiæ vel vnius fidei, sed societate solius nominis Christiani in hoc mundo permiscentur bonis. Ex quo patenter habetur, quod haeretici non sunt de corpore ecclesiæ eiusdem cum bonis. Item omnes qui sunt de corpore ecclesiæ militantis, siue sunt boni, siue mali, in vna sagena concluduntur. Sed haeretici cum catholicis licet sint in vno mari, quia in vno mundo, non tamen sunt in vna sagena, secundum Greg. ergo haeretici non sunt de corpore ecclesiæ. Quod etiam sic probatur, ecclesia Christi est regnum Christi, sed soli catholici spectant ad regnum Christi, teste beato August. qui super Ioh. ait: fideles Christiani sunt regnum, quod non colligitur sed emitur sanguine Christi. Et alibi super Iohan. ait: quid enim regnum eius, nisi credentes? Ex quibus verbis patet, quod haeretici non sunt de regno Christi, licet mali catholici sint de regno Christi. Quod autem regnum Christi sit ecclesia, asserit euidenter Gregor. qui in omelia de communi virginum ait: sciendum vobis est, quod sape in sacro eloquio regnum coelorum praesentis temporis ecclesia dicitur, de quo in alio loco Dominus dicit: Mittet filium hominis angelos suos & colligent de regno eius omnia scandala. Cum ergo haeretici non sunt de regno Christi, quod comprehendit bonos & malos, sequitur quod non sunt de corpore ecclesiæ militantis. Et ita Papa haereticus non est de corpore ecclesiæ militantis. Item quod haeretici non sunt de corpore ecclesiæ, sic probatur, qui est extra ecclesiam, non est de corpore ecclesiæ, sed omnes haeretici sunt extra ecclesiam, ergo non sunt de corpore ecclesiæ. Maior est euidens, minor probatur multis modis. Primo modo, qui nouiter veniunt vel redeunt ad ecclesiam catholicam prius extra ecclesiam exiterunt, sed haeretici suas haereses delinquentes veniunt & redeunt ad ecclesiam, 1. q. 7. si qui voluerint, & c. quoties, & c. salubberrimi, & c. conuenientibus, ergo haeretici non sunt de corpore ecclesiæ. Item, qui sunt alibi, quam in ecclesia catholica, non sunt de corpore ecclesiæ, sed haeretici sunt alibi quam in ecclesia catholica 1. q. 7. c. qui in qualibet, & c. si qui presbyteri, ergo haeretici non sunt de corpore ecclesiæ. Item, qui exiit de ecclesia non est de corpore ecclesiæ, omnes autem haeretici, quando efficiuntur haeretici, exeunt de ecclesia, 1. qu. 1. si quis de ecclesia, ergo haeretici non sunt de corpore ecclesiæ, etiam nulla lata humana sententia contra ipsos. Item ecclesia catholica ab ecclesia haereticorum distinguitur, ergo haeretici non sunt intra ecclesiam catholicam, & ita Papa haereticus non est de corpore ecclesiæ catholicæ. Item, ecclesia catholica est congregatio fidelium, sed Papa haereticus, quantumcunque reputetur Papa (etiam absque omni humana sententia) non est de congregatione fidelium, ergo ante omnem humanam sententiam, eo ipso, quod est haereticus, vere est extra ecclesiam, & non est de corpore ecclesiæ. Item, aut haeretici eo ipso quod sunt haeretici, sunt absque humana sententia extra ecclesiam: aut solummodo sunt extra ecclesiam per humanam sententiam: si detur primum, habetur intentum quod Papa eo ipso, quod est haereticus ante omnem humanam sententiam est vere extra ecclesiam, sicut haeretici sunt extra ecclesiam secundo modo per humanam sententiam: ergo haeretici, qui praecesserunt talem humanam sententiam, fuerunt intra ecclesiam, quod non modicum inconueniens est censendum eo, quod ex illis verbis manifeste sequitur, quod aliquando fuit vna ecclesia catholicorum & haereticorum: imo sequitur, quod possit adhuc esse vna ecclesia catholicorum & haereticorum, quia omnis humana sententia, qua haeretici extra ecclesiam exclusi fuerunt, posset per illos, qui eandem auctoritatem habent, quam habebant, qui talem tulerunt sententiam, reuocari, & ita reuocata humana sententia possunt haeretici in sua perfidia persistentes reuerti ad ecclesiæ vnitatem, & impossibile est censendum: quia si reuocata humana sententia, qua haeretici ab ecclesia exclusi fuerunt, redirent ad ecclesiæ catholicæ vnitatem; aut redirent ad ecclesiæ catholicæ vnitatem, aut alterius ecclesiæ quam catholicæ, si redirent ad vnitatem ecclesiæ catholicæ: ergo intra ecclesiam catholicam includuntur haeretici: & sic ecclesia catholica ita esset infidelium sicut fidelium, quod impossibile est censendum, si autem redirent ad aliam ecclesiam quam catholicam, & redirent ad vnitatem, a qua per humanam sententiam exclusi fuerant, ergo catholici essent de alia ecclesia, quam de ecclesia catholica. Quod etiam est inconueniens reputandum. Omnis autem haereticus siue Papa siue alius eo ipso, quod est haereticus, etsi nulla contra eum proferatur sententia, vere est extra ecclesiam catholicam. Ex quo sequitur, quod Papa haereticus eo ipso, quod est haereticus, non est de corpore ecclesiæ, & per consequens non est caput ecclesiæ, & ita Papa haereticus non est verus Papa.
units.tr: From these words it is gathered that, apart from any human sentence, all heretics are separated from the body of the Church and are not of the Church, although some of them may be thought to be of the Church, because the fact that they are heretics is unknown. For Gregory says that heretics are mixed among the good in this world not by fellowship in one Church or one faith, but by fellowship in the name of Christian alone. From this it is plainly held that heretics are not of the body of the Church together with the good. Again, all who are of the body of the militant Church, whether good or bad, are enclosed in one net. But heretics, although they are in one sea with the Catholics because they are in one world, are not in one net, according to Gregory; therefore heretics are not of the body of the Church. This is also proved thus: the Church of Christ is the kingdom of Christ, but only Catholics belong to the kingdom of Christ, as the blessed Augustine witnesses, who says in his commentary on John: the faithful Christians are the kingdom, which is not gathered but bought with the blood of Christ. And elsewhere on John he says: for what is his kingdom, except believers? From these words it is clear that heretics are not of the kingdom of Christ, although bad Catholics are of the kingdom of Christ. That the kingdom of Christ is the Church, Gregory plainly asserts in his homily on the common life of virgins, where he says: you must know that often in sacred speech the kingdom of heaven of the present time is called the Church, of which the Lord says in another place: The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all the offences. Since, therefore, heretics are not of the kingdom of Christ, which comprises good and bad, it follows that they are not of the body of the militant Church. And so a heretical pope is not of the body of the militant Church. Again, that heretics are not of the body of the Church is proved thus: whoever is outside the Church is not of the body of the Church; but all heretics are outside the Church; therefore they are not of the body of the Church. The major is evident; the minor is proved in many ways. First, those who newly come to or return to the Catholic Church previously went out from the Church; but heretics, renouncing their heresies, come and return to the Church, 1. q. 7. si qui voluerint, & c. quoties, & c. salubberrimi, & c. conuenientibus, therefore heretics are not of the body of the Church. Again, those who are anywhere other than in the Catholic Church are not of the body of the Church; but heretics are elsewhere than in the Catholic Church, 1. q. 7. c. qui in qualibet, & c. si qui presbyteri, therefore heretics are not of the body of the Church. Again, whoever has gone out of the Church is not of the body of the Church; but all heretics, when they become heretics, go out of the Church, 1. qu. 1. si quis de ecclesia, therefore heretics are not of the body of the Church, even without any human sentence passed against them. Again, the Catholic Church is distinguished from the Church of the heretics; therefore heretics are not within the Catholic Church, and so a heretical pope is not of the body of the Catholic Church. Again, the Catholic Church is the congregation of the faithful; but a heretical pope, however much he may be reckoned pope (even without any human sentence), is not of the congregation of the faithful; therefore, before any human sentence, by the very fact that he is a heretic, he is truly outside the Church and is not of the body of the Church. Again, either heretics, by the very fact that they are heretics, are outside the Church without any human sentence, or they are outside the Church only through a human sentence. If the first is granted, the point intended is had: the pope, by the very fact that he is a heretic, before any human sentence, is truly outside the Church, just as heretics are outside the Church in the second way, through a human sentence. Therefore the heretics who preceded such a human sentence were within the Church, which is by no means a small absurdity, since it clearly follows from those words that there was once one Church of Catholics and heretics; indeed, it follows that there could still be one Church of Catholics and heretics, because any human sentence by which heretics were excluded from the Church could be revoked by those who have the same authority as those who pronounced it, and so, the human sentence being revoked, heretics persisting in their perfidy could return to the unity of the Church. And this is impossible to hold, because if heretics, once the human sentence excluding them from the Church is revoked, returned to the unity of the Catholic Church, then either they return to the unity of the Catholic Church or to the unity of some Church other than the Catholic one. If they return to the unity of the Catholic Church, then heretics are included within the Catholic Church, and so the Catholic Church would be of unbelievers as much as of believers, which is impossible to hold. But if they return to a Church other than the Catholic one, and return to the unity from which they had been excluded by human sentence, then Catholics would be of another Church than the Catholic Church, which is also to be reckoned absurd. But every heretic, whether pope or other, by the very fact that he is a heretic, even if no sentence is pronounced against him, is truly outside the Catholic Church. From this it follows that a heretical pope, by the very fact that he is a heretic, is not of the body of the Church, and consequently is not the head of the Church, and so a heretical pope is not a true pope.

units.la: Tertiadecima ratio principalis est haec, verus Papa habet potestatem & ius super omnes catholicos, sed Papa haereticus nil potestatis vel iuris omnino habet, ergo Papa haereticus non est verus Papa. Maior est euidens. Minor ostenditur auctoritate Cypriani, qui vt legitur 24. q. 1. ca. didicimus, ait: did.c mus omnes omnino haereticos & schismaticos nihil habere potestatis aut iuris. Discipulus. Bene probatur, quod Papa haereticus non est verus Papa: & quod est papatu priuatus. Sed non probatur per auctoritatem praedictam, quod papa haereticus sit per diuinam sententiam papatu priuatus. Quod beatus Cyprianus non dicit, didicimus ex scriptura diuina omnes omnino haereticos; sed sine determinatione ait: didicimus, &c. Potuit autem in canonibus sacris addiscere, quod omnes omnino haeretici nihil habeant potestatis aut iuris, quia licet per scripturam diuinam haeretici non sunt omni potestate priuati: sunt tamen per sacros canones omni potestate ac iure nudati. Magister. Videtur nonnullis, quod si sequentia beati Cypriani pensares subtiliter, inuenires quod beatus Cyprianus asserit manifeste, se in sacra scriptura didicisse: omnes omnino haereticos & schismaticos nihil habere potestatis. Nam ad probandum verba praedicta subdit: inuenimus in tali facinore non solum duces & auctores, sed etiam participes eorum poenis destinari, nisi a communione eorum se separauerint, praecipiente per Moysen Domino & dicente: Separamini a tabernaculo hominum istorum durissimorum, & nolite tangere de omnibus quae sunt eorum, ne simul pereatis in peccatis eorum, & quod locutus per Moysen Dominus fuerat, impleuit, vt quisquis se a Chore & Datan & Abiron non separasset, poenas statim ipsa communione persolueret. Quo exemplo ostenditur, & probatur obnoxios omnes poenae, & per consequens culpae futuros, qui se schismaticis contraprepositos & sacerdotes irreligiosa temeritate miscuerunt. Sicut etiam per Oseam prophetam Spiritus sanctus contestatur & dicit: Sacrificia eorum tanquam panis luctus, omnes qui manducant ea contaminabuntur: docens scilicet & ostendens, omnes cum auctoribus suis supplicius mergi, qui fuerunt eorum peccatis contaminati.
units.tr: The thirteenth principal argument is this: a true pope has power and right over all Catholics, but a heretical pope has no power or right at all. Therefore a heretical pope is not a true pope. The major premise is evident. The minor is shown by the authority of Cyprian, who, as we read in 24. q. 1. ca. didicimus, says: we have learned that all heretics and schismatics without exception have no power or right. Disciple: It is well proved that a heretical pope is not a true pope, and that he is deprived of the papacy. But it is not proved by the said authority that a heretical pope is deprived of the papacy by divine sentence. Blessed Cyprian does not say, "we have learned from divine Scripture that all heretics without exception"; he says without qualification, we have learned, etc. He could have learned in the sacred canons that all heretics without exception have no power or right, because although heretics are not stripped of all power by divine Scripture, they are nonetheless stripped of all power and right by the sacred canons. Master: It seems to some that if you weigh what follows in blessed Cyprian closely, you will find that he plainly asserts that he learned in sacred Scripture that all heretics and schismatics without exception have no power. For to prove these words he adds: we find that in such a crime not only the leaders and authors but also their accomplices are condemned to punishments, unless they separate themselves from their communion, the Lord commanding through Moses and saying: "Separate yourselves from the tents of these most hard men, and do not touch anything that belongs to them, lest you perish together in their sins." And what the Lord had spoken through Moses he fulfilled, so that whoever did not separate himself from Korah, Dathan and Abiram was at once punished by that very communion. By this example it is shown and proved that all who have joined themselves to schismatics, who were set over them in opposition, and to priests with irreligious rashness, will be liable to punishment and therefore to guilt. So also the Holy Spirit testifies through the prophet Hosea and says: Their sacrifices will be like the bread of mourning; all who eat of them will be defiled, teaching and showing that all who were defiled by their sins perish with their authors in punishment.

units.la: Et infra: si autem foris cuncti haeretici & schismatici sunt, Spiritum sanctum non habent, & ideo apud nos manus eis imponitur, vt hic accipiatur, quod illic non est nec dari potest, manifestum est, nec remissionem peccatorum per eos dari posse, quos constat Spiritum sanctum non habere. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod beatus Cyprianus ad declarationem assertionis, scilicet quod omnes omnino haeretici & schismatici nihil habent potestatis aut iuris, auctoritates diuinae scripturae adducit. Ex quo sequitur euidenter, quod in scriptura diuina didicit, quod omnes haeretici nihil habeant potestatis aut iuris, haec a scriptura accipere diuina dicuntur. Item, quod beatus Cyprianus intelligat se in scriptura diuina didicisse, quod haeretici nihil habent potestatis aut iuris, ex aliis verbis eius colligitur. Nam, vt habetur 1. quaestion. 1. cap. si quis, idem Cyprianus ait: si quis de ecclesia haeretica praesumptione exierit, a semetipso est damnatus, cum huiusmodi (secundum Apostolum) nec cibum quidem debemus accipere. Declaratur hoc in libro Regum tertio, vbi cum homo Dei ad Hieroboam missus esset, qui peccata sua exprobraret, atque vltionem suturam praediceret; panem apud ipsum edere & aquam bibere prohibitus est. Et infra: an debet quisquam dicere sacramentum salutare, & gratiam coelestem communem cum haereticis esse posse, cum quibus nec terrestris cibus, nec secularis potus debet esse communis. Ex quibus verbis aperte colligitur, quod beatus Cyprianus in scriptura diuina se fundauit asserens, quod haereticorum communio est vitanda, & per consequens nihil potestatis aut iuris habet. Ex quo sequitur euidenter, quod sicut papa haereticus per scripturam diuinam communione fidelium est priuatus, ita per scripturam diuinam est omni potestate & ecclesiastica dignitate nudatus, cum vero etiam papa communicandum est; nullus etiam a communione veri papae fugere tenetur, ergo ille, qui est communione fidelium auctoritate diuinae scripturae priuatus, non est verus papa.
units.tr: And further on: But if all heretics and schismatics outside are without the Holy Spirit, and therefore hands are laid on them with us so that what is not there and cannot be given there may be received here, it is clear that forgiveness of sins cannot be given by those whom it is known do not have the Holy Spirit. From these words it is gathered that blessed Cyprian, to declare his assertion that all heretics and schismatics without exception have no power or right, brings forward the authorities of divine Scripture. From this it follows plainly that when he says he learned in divine Scripture that all heretics have no power or right, he means that these things are taken from Scripture. Again, from his other words it is gathered that blessed Cyprian understood that he had learned in divine Scripture that heretics have no power or right. For, as we find in 1. quaest. 1. cap. si quis, the same Cyprian says: if anyone has presumptuously gone out of the heretical church, he is condemned by himself, since, according to the Apostle, we ought not even to take food with such persons. This is illustrated in the third book of Kings, where when the man of God was sent to Jeroboam, to rebuke his sins and foretell the coming punishment, he was forbidden to eat bread or drink water with him. And further on: Can anyone say that the saving sacrament and heavenly grace can be shared with heretics, when neither earthly food nor common drink ought to be shared with them? From these words it is clearly gathered that blessed Cyprian founded himself on divine Scripture in asserting that communion with heretics is to be avoided, and therefore that they have no power or right. From this it plainly follows that just as a heretical pope is deprived of the communion of the faithful by divine Scripture, so he is stripped of all power and ecclesiastical dignity by divine Scripture. Yet even a pope must be communed with, and no one is bound to flee from the communion of a true pope. Therefore he who is deprived of the communion of the faithful by the authority of divine Scripture is not a true pope.

units.la: Quartadecima ratio est haec. Ad verum papam sunt causae fidei deferendae, 24. q. 1. c. quotiens, sed ad Papam haereticum non sunt causae fidei deferendae: quia ad aduersarium fidei, causae fidei sunt minime deferendae. Papa autem haereticus est aduersarius fidei Christianae, ergo ad Papam haereticum non sunt causae fidei deferendae. Et ideo Papa haereticus non est verus Papa. Disc. Ista ratio videtur fortis, si ex iure diuino haberet papa verus, quod ad ipsum sint quaestiones fidei deferendae. Quia non video quod hoc (sc. quod ad papam haereticum non sunt causae fidei deferendae) probari indigeat. Et ideo proba mihi, quod ex iure diuino verus papa illam praerogatiuam obtineat, quod ad ipsum sint causae fidei deferendae. Mag. Hoc videtur posse probari per hoc, quod eodem iure habet verus Papa, quod ad ipsum sint quaestiones fidei deferendae, ex quo iure super omnes fideles dignoscitur habere principatum. Sed verus papa ex iure diuino super omnes fideles obtinet principatum dist. 21. quamuis, & distinct. 22. c. omnes, & c. sacrosanctam, igitur de iure diuino habet, quod ad ipsum sunt causae fidei deferendae.
units.tr: The fourteenth argument is this. Matters of faith are to be referred to a true pope, 24. q. 1. c. quotiens, but matters of faith are not to be referred to a heretical pope, because matters of faith are by no means to be referred to an adversary of the faith. But a heretical pope is an adversary of the Christian faith; therefore matters of faith are not to be referred to a heretical pope. And so a heretical pope is not a true pope. Disciple: This argument seems strong if a true pope had by divine right that matters of faith should be referred to him. For I do not see why this (namely, that matters of faith are not to be referred to a heretical pope) should need proof. So prove to me that by divine right a true pope enjoys that prerogative, that matters of faith are referred to him. Master: This seems to be provable from the fact that by the same right a true pope has that matters of faith are referred to him, since by that right he is recognized as having primacy over all the faithful. But a true pope by divine right holds primacy over all the faithful, dist. 21. quamuis, and dist. 22. c. omnes, and c. sacrosanctam; therefore by divine right it is his that matters of faith are referred to him.

units.la: Decima quinta ratio est haec. Ille, cui secundum legem diuinam catholici debent se opponere maxime in his, quae ad religionem pertinent Christianam non est verus Papa: cum verus papa sit caput omnium Christianorum, praecipue in his, quae spectant ad religionem specialiter Christianam. Sed papae haeretico secundum legem diuinam catholici se opponere astringuntur. Unde & Dominus per Ezechiel prophetam ca. 13. illos qui non resistunt haereticis acriter reprehendit, dicens: non ascendistis ex aduerso, nec opposuistis vos murum pro domo Israel, vt staretis in pralio in die Domini, ex aduerso enim ascendere & pro domo Israel se murum opponere est pro defensione catholicae veritatis, cuicunque haretico domum Israel (quae est ecclesia) cupienti destruere, totis viribus obuiare, quod cuiden ter Vrbanus Papa videtur innuere, qui vt legitur 1. q. 3. c. Saluator, ait: Saluator praedixit in euangelio circa finem seculi pseudo Apostolos & pseudoprophetas surgere & multos seducere, & fideles suos in mundo multas habituros pressuras, sed tamen portas inferni non praevaliturus. Proinde, vt ait Apostolus; Oportet esse haereses, vt qui probati sunt, manifesti fiant: oportet & nos cum propheta ex aduerso conjurgere & murum pro domo Israel opponere. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod contra quascunque haereses insurgentes oportet catholicos ex aduerso consurgere, & se murum opponere pro defensione fidei orthodoxae. Ergo si Papa fiat haereticus, & fidem molitus fuerit destruere orthodoxam, oportet catholicos ei animosius obviare. Et per consequens haereticus non est verus Papa censendus, secundum testimonium sacrarum scriptura-rum.
units.tr: The fifteenth argument is this. He to whom Catholics, according to divine law, must oppose themselves, especially in matters that pertain to the Christian religion, is not a true pope, since a true pope is the head of all Christians, especially in those things that concern the Christian religion in particular. But Catholics are bound by divine law to oppose a heretical pope. Hence also the Lord, through the prophet Ezekiel, chapter 13, sharply rebukes those who do not resist heretics, saying: You have not gone up against them, nor set up a wall for the house of Israel, that you might stand in battle on the day of the Lord. For to go up against them and to set up a wall for the house of Israel is to defend Catholic truth, and to withstand with all one's strength any heretic who desires to destroy the house of Israel (which is the Church). Pope Urban seems clearly to hint at this, who, as we read in 1. q. 3. c. Salvator, says: The Saviour foretold in the Gospel that near the end of the age false apostles and false prophets would arise and lead many astray, and that his faithful would have many trials in the world, yet the gates of hell would not prevail. Therefore, as the Apostle says, "there must be heresies, that those who are approved may be made manifest"; we too must, with the prophet, rise up against them and set up a wall for the house of Israel. From these words it is made clear that Catholics ought to rise up against whatever heresies arise and set themselves up as a wall in defense of the orthodox faith. Therefore if a pope becomes a heretic and labours to destroy the orthodox faith, Catholics ought to resist him with greater courage. And consequently a heretic is not to be judged a true pope, according to the testimony of the sacred Scriptures.

units.la: CAP. LXVII.
units.tr: CAP. LXVII.

units.la: In quo contraria assertio, sive opinio illi priori septem rationibus probatur, scilicet quod Papa haereticus non fit iure divino Papatu privatus.
units.tr: In which the contrary assertion, or opinion, is proved against the former one by seven reasons, namely that a Pope who becomes a heretic is not deprived of the Papacy by divine right.

units.la: Disc. Pro ista assertione fortiter allegasti: & puto quod apparentiores rationes pro ipsa non est facile invenire, ideo ut mihi detur occasio cogitandi pro assertione contraria aliquas rationes excogitare conare. Mag. Quod Papa haereticus non sit iure divino Papatu privatus, videtur multis modis posse probari. Primo sic: sicut Papa est caput fidelium, qui sunt sub nova lege, ita summus sacerdos quantum ad illa, quae spectant ad legem divinam caput erat fidelium, qui erant sub veteri lege constituti. Sed summus sacerdos in veteri lege quamvis erraret a fide, non fuisset sacerdotio summo iure divino privatus. Quia ut videtur plures summi sacerdotes in antiqua lege deviaverunt a fide, & tamen postea summo sacerdotio fungebantur. Ergo licet Papa erraret a fide, & efficeretur haereticus, non esset iure divino Papatu privatus. Confirmatur haec ratio: quia non magis per scripturam divinam probari potest, quod Papa haereticus est Papatu privatus, quam quod summus sacerdos veteris legis effectus haereticus fuerit sacerdotio summo privatus. Quod rationes sumptae ex scriptura divina maxime ex Veteri Testamento non magis concludunt de summo sacerdote novae legis, quam veteris. Sed summus sacerdos in antiqua lege effectus haereticus non fuit iure divino sacerdotio summo privatus. Secunda ratio est haec, Papa non est deterioris conditionis, quam alii praelati & episcopi, sed alii praelati & episcopi, si fiant haeretici, non sunt iure divino omni dignitate privati. Maior videtur certa. Minor probatur: quia si episcopi & alii praelati effecti haeretici essent iure divino omni dignitate privati, non possent absque nova electione ad suas recipi dignitates, vel saltem suas dignitates minime retinerent. Sed non nulli praelati effecti haeretici absque nova electione ad suas dignitates recepti fuerunt vel retinuerunt eadem l. quaest. 7. maximum, & qu. 1. omnes cuiuslibet, & 6. quam quidam. Ergo & Papa quamvis efficiatur haereticus Papalem retinet dignitatem, & ita nequaquam est iure divino Papatu privatus. Tertio, non deterioris conditionis est Papa, quam Imperator vel princeps secularis. Sed Imperator effectus haereticus iure divino non est imperiali dignitate privatus. Nec reges, nec principes seculares si efficiantur haeretici, iure divino suis dignitatibus sunt privati. Ergo nec Papa haereticus est iure divino dignitate Papali privatus. Maior videtur certa. Minor ostenditur manifeste. Nam in veteri lege multi reges idololatrae & haeretici effecti fuerunt, & tamen veri reges remanserunt. Iulianus quoque apostata haereticus de Christiano fuit effectus: Et tamen fuit verus Imperator ii. quaestion. 3. cap. Iulianus. Ergo principes seculares haeretici nequaquam suis dignitatibus iure divino priuantur. Ergo nec Papa quamvis efficiatur haereticus, iure divino Papatu est privatus. Quarto; si Papa haereticus esset iure divino Papatu privatus: hoc non esset propter aliam causam, nisi quia haereticus catholicis praeesse non potest. Sed haereticos & infideles praefuisse catholicis, & catholicos infidelibus obediisse in sacris literis & aliis scripturis autenticis legitur manifeste. Ioseph enim seruiuit & obediuit Pharaoni: & Daniel Nabuchodonosor: & Christiani plures fidelibus Imperatoribus seruierunt. Ergo non est contra legem divinam, quod haereticus vel infidelis fidelibus praesit, ergo non est contra sacram Scripturam, quod Papa haereticus remaneat verus Papa. Quinto sic: Ad quem pertinet institutio alicuius, ad eundem destitutio spectat eiusdem, extra, de haereticis, cum ex incerto. Sed Papa non instituitur iure divino, sed eligentium electione canonica & concordi. Ergo nec Papa destituitur iure divino: sed si est destituendus, oportet quod ipsum destituant electores. Sexto sic: Illa assertio nullatenus est tenenda, ad quam sequi potest totius ecclesiasticae Hierarchiae confusio, cui tota ecclesia subuenire non posset. Sed si Papa haereticus iure divino esset Papatu privatus, posset sequi totius ecclesiasticae Hierarchiae confusio, posset enim Papa esse occultus haereticus, cuius ordinationes, promotiones, consecrationes, & cetera facta eius nullius essent momenti, si iure divino esset Papatu privatus, & ita si Papa occulte efficitur haereticus, nullus praelatus per ipsum factus esset verus praelatus. Et per consequens totus ordo ecclesiasticus esset confusus, quare nullus esset verus praelatus: nec tota ecclesia Dei, quae de occultis iudicare non potest, valeret tali confusioni ecclesiastici ordinis obviare, ergo non est tenendum, quod Papa haereticus statim iure divino sit Papatu privatus. Septimo sic: Illa poena Papae haeretico per scripturam divinam minime est inflicta, de qua in tota Scriptura nulla mentio reperitur, sed de poena privationis officii & beneficii nulla penitus in Scriptura sacra mentio reperitur, ergo per Scripturam sacram Papa haereticus Papatu nullatenus est privatus.
units.tr: Student. You have argued strongly for that position, and I think it is not easy to find more plausible reasons for it. So let me have the chance to think about it, and I will try to work out some reasons for the opposite position. Master. That a Pope who becomes a heretic is not deprived of the Papacy by divine right can be proved in many ways. (1) First, as the Pope is the head of the faithful who live under the new law, so the high priest was, with respect to those matters that pertain to the divine law, the head of the faithful who were established under the old law. But the high priest under the old law, although he strayed from the faith, was not deprived of the high priesthood by divine right. For it seems that several high priests in the old law strayed from the faith and yet afterwards continued to serve as high priest. Therefore, even if the Pope strayed from the faith and became a heretic, he would not be deprived of the Papacy by divine right. This reasoning is confirmed: it cannot be proved from divine Scripture any more that a Pope who becomes a heretic is deprived of the Papacy than that a high priest of the old law who became a heretic was deprived of the high priesthood. And arguments drawn from divine Scripture, especially from the Old Testament, conclude no more about the high priest of the new law than about the old. But a high priest of the old law who became a heretic was not deprived of the high priesthood by divine right. (2) The second reason is this: the Pope is not in a worse condition than other prelates and bishops, but other prelates and bishops, if they become heretics, are not deprived of all dignity by divine right. The major premise seems certain. The minor is proved thus: if bishops and other prelates who became heretics were deprived of all dignity by divine right, they could not be restored to their dignities without a new election, or at least they would not keep their dignities at all. But some prelates who became heretics were restored to their dignities, or kept them, without a new election, as in the case of Q. 7, Maximum, and Q. 1, Omnes cuiuslibet, and 6, Quam quidam. Therefore the Pope too, although he becomes a heretic, keeps the Papal dignity, and so he is by no means deprived of the Papacy by divine right. (3) Thirdly, the Pope is not in a worse condition than an emperor or a secular prince. But an emperor who became a heretic was not deprived of imperial dignity by divine right. Nor are kings or secular princes, if they become heretics, deprived of their dignities by divine right. Therefore a Pope who becomes a heretic is not deprived of Papal dignity by divine right either. The major premise seems certain. The minor is shown plainly. For in the old law many kings became idolaters and heretics, and yet they remained true kings. Julian the Apostate, too, was made a heretic from a Christian, and yet he was a true emperor, II, Q. 3, cap. Iulianus. Therefore heretical secular princes are in no way deprived of their dignities by divine right. Therefore neither is the Pope, even if he becomes a heretic, deprived of the Papacy by divine right. (4) Fourthly: if a Pope who was a heretic were deprived of the Papacy by divine right, this would be for no other cause than that a heretic cannot preside over Catholics. But it is plainly read in the sacred letters and other authentic writings that heretics and unbelievers have presided over Catholics, and Catholics have obeyed unbelievers. For Joseph served and obeyed Pharaoh, and Daniel served Nebuchadnezzar, and many Christians served faithful emperors. Therefore it is not contrary to divine law for a heretic or unbeliever to preside over the faithful, and so it is not contrary to Holy Scripture for a Pope who is a heretic to remain a true Pope. (5) Fifthly: whoever has the power to institute something has the power to depose it, Extra, de haereticis, cum ex incerto. But the Pope is not instituted by divine right, but by the canonical and united election of the electors. Therefore the Pope is not deposed by divine right either; but if he must be deposed, it is necessary that the electors depose him. (6) Sixthly: that assertion must by no means be held which can lead to the confusion of the whole ecclesiastical hierarchy, a confusion the whole Church could not remedy. But if a Pope who became a heretic were deprived of the Papacy by divine right, the confusion of the whole ecclesiastical hierarchy could follow. For a Pope could be a secret heretic, and his ordinations, promotions, consecrations, and other acts would be of no account if he were deprived of the Papacy by divine right. And so, if a Pope secretly became a heretic, no prelate made by him would be a true prelate. And consequently the whole ecclesiastical order would be thrown into confusion, since there would be no true prelate; nor could the whole Church of God, which cannot judge hidden things, prevent such confusion of the ecclesiastical order. Therefore it must not be held that a Pope who becomes a heretic is at once deprived of the Papacy by divine right. (7) Seventhly: that punishment has not been inflicted on a heretical Pope by divine Scripture of which no mention is found in the whole of Scripture; but no mention at all of the penalty of deprivation of office and benefice is found in Holy Scripture. Therefore by Holy Scripture a heretical Pope is in no way deprived of the Papacy.

units.la: CAP. LXVIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER 68.

units.la: In quo ad septem rationes precedentis capituli respondetur: vbi nota differentiam inter Papam haereticum, & summum sacerdotem haereticum veteris legis.
units.tr: Here the seven arguments of the preceding chapter are answered. Note the difference between a heretical Pope and a heretical high priest of the old law.

units.la: Disc. Ista assertio pure est negativa, & ideo cum asserit, quod in sacris literis minime reperitur Papam haereticum ipso facto esse Papatu priuatum, videtur, quod contra proteruum probari non posset, nisi per singula loca Scripturae sacrae, praesertim tractantia de haereticis vel infidelibus discurrendo, hoc autem nolo quod faciAS, ideo cum pro ista parte rationes vt mihi videtur allegaueris fortiores, quaeso vt indices qualiter ad ipsas respondere contingat, de rationibus allegatis etiam pro alia parte tecum post completionem istius Dialogi collocutionem habebo. Mag. Ad primam istarum rationum dupliciter respondetur, dicitur enim vno modo, quod summus sacerdos veteris legis eo ipso efficiebatur haereticus, fuit sacerdotio summo priuatus, nec tunc erat verus summus Pontifex secundum rei veritatem, licet exiterit secundum opinionem hominum summus sacerdos.
