This follows from the example of King Nebuchadnezzar, who, though he was neither a cleric nor a prelate of the Church, enacted a law that no one should presume to blaspheme the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego; and this is clearly gathered from what was said earlier, where it was shown that laymen can enact laws for the faith. Stud. Can laymen restrain transgressors of their precepts and laws of this kind? Mast. The answer is that such transgressors, who are exempt from the jurisdiction of laymen, such as clerics, cannot be restrained as a rule; yet in a case they can.

units.la: CAP. XCV.
units.tr: CAP. XCV.

units.la: In quo agitur consequenter de quaestione fidei secundo modo non totaliter diuulgata, sed tamen ab ecclesia approbata, quomodo illa spectat ad laicos.
units.tr: In which it is discussed, in sequence, how a question of faith of the second kind, not fully published but nonetheless approved by the Church, pertains to the laity.

units.la: Disc. De hac materia interrogabo te, ideo postquam disseruisti de quaestione fidei, vbi aliquid apud omnes orthodoxos tanquā catholicum diuulgatum in quaestione vertitur, dic an quaestio fidei spectet ad laicos, cum aliquid catholicum non totaliter diuulgatum, sed tamen ab ecclesia explicite approbatum in quaestione vertitur. Mag. Respondetur, quod talis quaestio fidei postquam laicis cōstiterit veritas huiusmodi quaestionis sic spectat ad eos, quod pro loco & tempore veritatem tenentur simpliciter confiteri, sc. cum honor Dei & utilitas proximi hoc exposcit. Secundo talis quaestio sic spectat ad laicos, quod tales omnes praedicantes, docentes, tenentes pertinaciter contra veritatē huiusmodi quaestionis vitare tenentur, & eis nullatenus obedire. Vnde quamuis audirent & scirent Papam praedicare & docere, Pilatum nō misisse Christum ad Herodem tempore passionis, aut Apostolos & alios credentes, de quib. fit mentio Act. 4. fuisse proprietarios & Dominos portionum sibi assignatarum; aut Christum inquantum homo mortalis fuisse regem in temporalibus, non debent propter hoc statim Papam tanquā haereticum euitare, quantumcunq; constaret eis, quod tales sunt inter haereses damnatas explicite computandae, si tamen scirent eum diffinitiue docere ipsum tanquam haereticum vitare debent. Discipulus. Video quod opinio istorum in hac parte dependet ab illis, quae dicta sunt libro quarto, in quo tractatur, quomodo de pertinacia debeat quis conuinci. Magister. Verum dicis, quod non constat laicis aliquam assertionem, de qua est quaestio, esse catholicam & haereticam simul: cum hoc constat, quod docens praedicans & tenens contra catholicam veritatem est pertinax in sua assertione. Et per omnia dicunt de quaestione fidei secundo modo dicta: sicut dictum est de quaestione primo modo dicta, quia illis duobus suppositis, eisdem modis pertinet quaestio fidei, secundo modo dicta ad laicos, quibus modis pertinet ad eos quaestio fidei primo modo dicta. Veruntamen quamuis assertio fidei vtroq; modo praedictis modis spectat ad laicos, principalius tamen spectat ad praelatos ecclesiae, quibus ex officio incumbit magis intelligere catholicas veritates, & eas frequentius aliis propalare, ac circa punitionem haereticorum magis diligenter insistere.
units.tr: Disc. On this matter I shall question you. So, since you have discussed questions of faith, where something that is published among all the orthodox as Catholic is in dispute, tell me whether a question of faith pertains to the laity when something Catholic, not fully published but nonetheless explicitly approved by the Church, is in dispute. Mag. The answer is that such a question of faith, once the truth of this kind of question has become clear to the laity, pertains to them in such a way that, according to place and time, they are bound plainly to confess the truth, namely when the honour of God and the advantage of their neighbour demand it. Second, such a question pertains to the laity in such a way that they are bound to avoid, and by no means obey, all who preach, teach or stubbornly hold anything against the truth of this question. Hence, although they might hear and know that the Pope preaches and teaches that Pilate did not send Christ to Herod at the time of the passion, or that the Apostles and other believers, mentioned in Act. 4., were not owners and lords of the portions assigned to them, or that Christ, insofar as he was a mortal man, was not a king in temporal affairs, they ought not on that account immediately to avoid the Pope as a heretic, however clearly it might be established for them that such views are to be counted explicitly among the condemned heresies. Yet if they knew that he teaches this definitively, they ought to avoid him as a heretic. Discipulus. I see that the opinion of these men on this point depends on what was said in libro quarto, where it is treated how someone ought to be convicted of obstinacy. Magister. You speak truly. It is not established for the laity that any assertion under dispute is both Catholic and heretical at once; but it is established that one who teaches, preaches and holds something against Catholic truth is obstinate in his assertion. And everything said about the question of faith in the second way applies in all respects as was said of the question in the first way, because, given those two suppositions, the question of faith in the second way pertains to the laity in the same ways as the question of faith in the first way does. Nevertheless, although an assertion of faith in both of the aforesaid ways pertains to the laity, it pertains more principally to the prelates of the Church, to whom it belongs by office to understand Catholic truths more fully, to make them known to others more often, and to devote greater diligence to the punishment of heretics.

units.la: CAP. XCVI.
units.tr: CAP. XCVI.

units.la: In quo agitur de quaestione fidei tertio modo dicta, an talis spectet ad laicos & quomodo.
units.tr: In which the question of faith taken in the third sense is discussed: whether it belongs to the laity, and how.

units.la: Disc. Dic de quaestione fidei tertio modo dicta, an spectat ad laicos. Mag. Dicitur, quod quādo aliquid, quod non est ab ecclesia explicite approbatum, nec per consequens eius contrarium est explicite condemnatum, vertitur in quaestionem, laici non tenentur publice confitendo, ordinando, statuendo, prohibendo, praecipiendo, se de tali intromittere quaestione, nisi euidenter aduerterent, quod aliter graue periculum fidei, vel reipublicae immineret. Si quis vero aperte cognosceret, quod ex tali quaestione fidei seditiones, bella, & schismata prouenirent, nisi laici per potentiam temporalem occurrerent, ad ipsos talis quaestio fidei pertineret. Quod sic ostenditur, quia pax aliter haberi non poterit, est ad regale prouidentiam recurrendum. Igitur si ex quaestione fidei (modo praedicto) oriuntur sectae, seditiones & schismata in communis pacis dispendiū, quae absque laicorum potentia sedari non possunt, ad regale seu laicale potentiā oportet recurrere, & per consequens in hoc casu saltem talis quaestio spectat ad laicos. Antecedens istius rationis testimoniis & exemplis probatur aperte. Oniae enim sacerdos, vt legitur 2. Machabaeor. 4. ad regem infidelem se contulit, non vt ciuium accusator, sed vt communem vtilitatem (apud semetipsum) immensae multitudinis considerans, videbat enim sine regali prouidentia impossibilem rebus pacem dari. Item, vt legitur dist. 17. cap. consilia §. hinc etiam, Theodorus rex aduertens seditiones & dissensiones in clero propter Simachum papam commisit potestati pontificum, vt sine propositum vellent audire negotium, siue nollent, quod magis putarent vtile deliberarent, dummodo venerandi prouisione pax consilii in Romana ciuitate daretur. Ex quibus aliisque quamplurimis patet, quod quando ex quaestione fidei oriuntur diuisiones, sectae & schismata, quae absque laicorum sententia sedari non possunt, necesse est pro pace recurrere ad prouidentiam laicalem.
units.tr: Disc. Tell me whether the question of faith taken in the third sense belongs to the laity. Mag. It is said that when something has not been explicitly approved by the Church, and consequently its contrary has not been explicitly condemned, and it becomes a matter of dispute, laymen are not bound to meddle in such a question by publicly confessing, ordaining, decreeing, forbidding or commanding, unless they clearly perceive that otherwise a grave danger to the faith or to the commonwealth is imminent. But if anyone clearly knew that from such a question of faith seditions, wars and schisms would arise, unless the laity intervened with temporal power, then such a question of faith would belong to them. This is shown as follows: since peace cannot otherwise be had, recourse must be made to royal providence. Therefore, if from a question of faith (in the aforesaid manner) sects, seditions and schisms arise, to the detriment of the common peace, and these cannot be quelled without the power of the laity, it is necessary to resort to royal or lay power, and consequently in this case at least such a question belongs to the laity. The antecedent of this argument is clearly proved by testimonies and examples. For Onias the priest, as we read in 2 Maccabees 4, went to the unbelieving king, not as an accuser of his fellow citizens, but considering, in his own mind, the common advantage of an immense multitude; for he saw that without royal providence peace could not be given to affairs. Likewise, as we read in dist. 17, cap. consilia, §. hinc etiam, King Theodoric, noticing seditions and dissensions among the clergy on account of Pope Symmachus, committed the matter to the power of the bishops, so that whether they wished to hear the business or not, they should deliberate what they judged more useful, provided that by the providence of the venerable council peace might be given in the Roman city. From these and very many other examples it is plain that when divisions, sects and schisms arise from a question of faith, and cannot be quelled without the sentence of the laity, it is necessary, for the sake of peace, to resort to lay providence.

units.la: CAP. XCVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XCVII.

units.la: In quo probatur, quod in casu aliquo spectat ad laicos coertio Papae haeretici, etiam si minime fuerint requisiti a prelatis ecclesiae, vbi etiam pon- itur opinio contraria, pro qua arguitur, & rationes pro eadem soluuntur.
units.tr: In which it is proved that in a certain case the coercion of a heretical Pope belongs to the laity, even if the prelates of the Church have not asked for it. The contrary opinion is also set out, with the arguments advanced for it, and the arguments for that opinion are answered.

units.la: Discipul. In capitulo 93. dixisti, quod tria sunt declaranda circa opinionem dicentem, coertionem papae haeretici & quorumcunque haereticorum in casu speciali ad laicos pertinere, de duobus autem primis sumus satis breuiter expediti, ideo modo tractemus de tertio, in quo scilicet casu spectat ad laicos coertio papae haretici & aliorum haereticorum. Magist. Sicut dictum est prius, secundum quandam opinionem non eodem modo est de haereticis omnibus sentiendum, nam haereticorum quidam sunt laici, & alii sunt clerici, laici haeretici etiam quantum ad crimen haeresis sunt de foro iudicis saecularis, haeretici autem clerici non sunt de foro iudicis saecularis, nisi in specialibus casibus. Discipul. Intendo primo probare, quod haeretici laici sunt de foro iudicis saecularis. Magist. Ad hoc allegatum est supra cap. 93. Discipul. Peto vt ad eandem assertionem aliquas alias rationes cogitare nitaris. Magist. Hoc videtur posse probari. Primo sic: Ille, qui est minister Domini regis, praecipue habet iudicare peccata, quae subditi sui committunt in Deum, reges autem sunt ministri Dei, quibus dicitur Sapient. 6. cum esset ut minister regis illius, non recte iudicasti &c. ergo ad reges pertinet praecipue punire peccata, quae subditi sui committunt in Deum, haeresis autem est peccatum in Deum, ergo ad reges spectat haereticos sibi subiectos debita animaduersione punire. Secundo: ille habet punire haereticos subiectos sibi, cuius est omne malum iudicare vel dissipare, sed hoc interest regis, teste Salomone Prouerbio. 20. cum dicit, rex qui sedet in solio iudicii, dissipat omne malum intuitu suo, ergo ad ipsum spectat omnes haereticos sibi subiectos debite punire. Tertio sic: Ad eosdem spectat haereticos in noua lege punire ad quos in veteri lege idololatras & blasphemos condigna poena punire spectabat. Sed ad reges in veteri testamento spectabat haereticos, idololatras, blasphemos condigna poena punire, ergo & hoc spectat ad reges in nouo testamento. Maior videtur apparens. Minor probatur exemplis apertis, nam de rege Aza loquitur 3. Regum 15. quod fecit rectum in conspectu Domini, sicut Dauid pater eius, & abstulit effeminatos de terra, purgauitq; vniuersas sordes idolorum, quae fecerunt patres eius, insuper & Maachatn matrem suam, ne esset princeps in sacris Priapi amouit, & in luco eius, quem consecrauerat, subuertit, specum eius, & confregit simulachrum turpissimum. Ex his verbis habetur aperte, quod rex Aza de idololatris, qui erant inter haereticos computandi, zelo Dei fecit iustitiam. Item, vt patet 3. Reg. 18. Helias omnes prophetas Baal occidit. Quarto sic: Si laici quoad crimen haeresis a iurisdictione regum & principum sunt exempti, aut ista exemptio est a iure diuino, aut a iure humano, non a iure diuino, quia de tali exemptione in scripturis sacris (in quibus continetur ius diuinum) nihil penitus inuenitur, igitur talis exemptio non est a iure diuino, nec a iure humano, quia si est a iure humano, aut est a iure Canonico, aut a iure ciuili, videlicet regum & principum saecularium aut pontificum vel vniuersitatum, nō est talis exemptio a iure Canonico: quia conditores iuris Canonici sic non debent minuere iurisdictionem saecularium, extra de iudiciis, nouit, itaq; non debent subdiros saecularium ab eorum iurisdictione eximere, nec talis exemptio est a iure ciuili saecularium: quia in iure ciuili de tali exemptione non legitur, & ita laici a iurisdictione regum & principum quo ad crimen haeresis minime sunt exempti. Quinto sic: non minus est de foro iudicis saecularis laicus haereticus quam clericus haereticus, sed clericus haereticus quam cito degradatus est, est sic de foro iudicis saecularis, quod est per eum debite puniendus, ergo laicus semper est de foro iudicis saecularis: & per consequens ideo laicus potest & debet punire laicos haereticos. Discip. Tenent ne omnes, quod laici quo ad crimen haeresis sunt sub foro iudicis saecularis anequam a iudice ecclesiastico foro iudicis saecularis relinquantur. Magist. Multi tenunt, quod non. Disc. Pro ista assertione aliquas allegationes adducas. Mag. Ista assertio videtur expresse de intentione Lucii papae, qui, vt habetur extra de haereticis ad abolendam, ait: laicus autem nisi (prout dictum est abiurata haeresi & satisfactione exhibita confestim ad fidem catholicam confugit orthodoxam,) iudicis saecularis arbitrio relinquatur, debitam recepturus pro qualitate facinorum vltionem. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod laicus index laicum haereticum punire non debet, antequam sibi ab ecclesiastico iudice relinquatur. Huic etiam Glo. concordare videtur dicens: Laici enim per ecclesiam damnandi sunt de haeresi: sed iudex saecularis illos punire debet, ergo haretici antequam per ecclesiam fuerunt condemnati non spectant ratione haeresis ad forum iudicis saecularis. Item sicut causae seculares non spectant ad iudices ecclesiasticos: sic nec causae ecclesiasticae pertinent ad iudices saeculares, sed haeresis est causa ecclesiastica, teste Glo. quae 2. q. 1. notat: causarum alia ecclesiastica, alia saecularis, & ecclesiasticarum alia est spiritualis, alia criminalis, alia ciuilis. Spiritualis est vbi ageretur de decimis vel matrimonio. Criminalis vero vbi agitur de crimine ecclesiastico scilicet haeresis vel vsurarum, cuius examinatio spectat ad iudicem ecclesiasticum, infra c. si quis cum clerico, & 6. quaest. 1. cap. 1. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod ecclesiastica causa spectat [?]tat ad iudicem ecclesiasticum: & per consequens non spectat ad iudicem secularem, causa autem haeresis est causa ecclesiastica, sicut in verbis praedictis habetur expresse, igitur causa haeresis non spectat ad iudicem secularem, & ita iudex secularis laicos haereticos, antequam fuerint per ecclesiam condemnati, punire non debet. Discip. Quamuis istam assertionem secundam reputem consonam veritati, tamen qualiter contingat respondere ad motiua istius assertionis secundae, libenter audirem. Magist. Respondetur quod secundum Greg. vt recitatur dist. 29. c. regulae: Regula sanctorum patrum pro tempore & loco & persona ac negocio (instantene cessitate) traditae sunt, cui concordat Isidor. vt habetur dist. eadem c. 1. dicens: Sciendum est quod plura capitula tam ex persona, ex loco & ex tempore consideranda sunt, quorum modi (quia medullitus non indagantur) in errorem labyrinthum nonnulli intricando impingunt: cum ante iudicantem intelligant, ideo auctoritates Lucii papae & maiorum dicta, ex qua causa & fine & quo tempore intelligenda sunt, videre oportet, quo viso patebit, quod iudices seculares laicos haereticos sibi subditos poterunt coercere. Dicitur ergo quod ideo Lucius papa negat laicum haereticum, nisi ad fidem confugerit orthodoxam, seculars iudicis arbitrio relinquendum: quia pro tempore, & forte semper fuit ita, quod iudices seculares de haereticis, antequam essent a iudice ecclesiastico condemnati, nullatenus intromiserunt, propter negligentiam igitur secularium iudicum, ecclesiae se de haereticis laicis intromisit inquirendo & convincendo ipsos: sed nullam poenam voluit eis inferre, sed voluit quod poena debita inferretur per iudicem secularem. Sicut igitur iudex ecclesiasticus saepe propter negligentiam iudicis secularis nonnunquam compellit eundem iustitiam exercere: ita & modo facit ecclesia laicos punire haereticos, quos tamen iudices seculares possent debite coercere. Cum igitur dicit Glos. quod laici per ecclesiam condemnandi sunt de haeresi, verum dicit de facto: quia iudices seculares quamuis de iure possent inquirere & corrigere laicos haereticos sibi subiectos, id tamen de facto saepe omittunt, & ideo ne haretici laici remaneant impuniti in praeiudicium fidelium & periculum fidei orthodoxae, iudex ecclesiasticus supplet negligentiam iudicum secularium, & desipsis inquirit, eosque quos convincit damnat, iniungens iudici seculari, quod eos debita poena percellat. Et ad hoc insinuandum Glossa praedicta post verba praescripta immediate post subiungit: hoc verum, nisi vbi traditur laicus curiae seculari, sed clericus solummodo, infra de verborum significatione c. nouimus: quia laicus semper est de foro seculari. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod laicus non est exemptus a foro seculari, pro crimine haeresis, sed cum iudex secularis laicos haereticos negligeret coercere, damnandi sunt primo a iudice ecclesiastico: & postea compellendus est iudex secularis punire eosdem, & propter hoc subiungit Glossa ibidem: sed in casu isto executio fit solummodo per secularem iudicem, hoc est, quod quamuis condemnatio valeat fieri per iudicem ecclesiasticum supplentem in hoc negligentiam iudicis secularis, tamen executio punitionis fieri debet a seculari iudice tantummodo. Cum vero alia Glossa dicit, quod causa haeresis est causa ecclesiastica, conceditur quantum ad clericos haereticos, quia clerici haeretici non sunt de foro iudicis secularis, nisi in quibusdam casibus determinatis, quantum ad laicos autem causa haeresis est causa secularis & etiam causa ecclesiastica: quia iudex secularis habet punire laicos haereticos: & ideo est causa secularis, est etiam aliquo modo causa ecclesiastica: quia iudex ecclesiasticus supplendo negligentiam iudicis secularis, potest haereticos laicos condemnare. Discipul. Istud apparentia videtur carere, nam crimen haeresis nullo modo est crimen seculare. Cum, quia committitur directe in Deum. Tum quia est peccatum in religionem Christianam solummodo. Tum quia apud iudices seculares paganos non esset crimen, igitur nullo modo est crimen seculare, ergo est solummodo crimen ecclesiasticum. Ex quo patenter infertur, quod solummodo ad ecclesiasticum iudicem spectat, & non ad secularem. Magist. Licet crimen sit ecclesiasticum, & non seculare: tamen spectat ad iudicem secularem, quia ad iudicem secularem non tantum spectat crimina secularia punire, sed etiam crimina commissa in Deum & in personas & in res ecclesiasticas, hoc enim habet omnis lex & secta, quod reges & principes distincti a sacerdotibus non solum puniunt crimina secularia, sed etiam crimina quae reputant in Deum vel in Deos suos & in sectam commissa, propter hoc etiam reges in veteri testamento idololatras puniebant, Imperatores etiam iudices paganorum Christianos tanquam contra Deos suos & sectam graviter delinquentes acerbissime persecuti sunt. Sic etiam reges Christiani homicidas sacerdotum & furantes res ecclesiasticas plectunt poena debita, & tamen homicidium sacerdotis & furtum rei ecclesiasticae sunt crimina ecclesiastica, ergo multa crimina ecclesiastica ad secularem iudicem spectant, & ita per hoc, quod crimen haeresis est crimen ecclesiasticum & in Deum committitur, probari non potest quod ad iudicem secularem minime spectat. Huic August. concordare videtur, prout legitur 23. q. 5. si propterea, ait: Si propterea persecutor non fuit Nabuchodonosor rex, quia scelus in sanctum Danielem commissum vindicauit iustissime: quomodo vindicandum est a regibus, quod Christi sacramenta exsufflantur, si prophetae membra, quia in periculum missa sunt, sic vindicari meruerunt? Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod multo magis vindicandum est a regibus peccatum, quod in Deum committitur, quam peccatum quod in prophetam vel in sacerdotem committitur. Si igitur rex potest & debet absque inquisitione praelatorum punire homicidam sacerdotis sibi subiectum; multo magis potest & debet debita animaduersione ferire sibi subiectos, si per prauitatem haereticam Dei offenderint maiestatem.
units.tr: Discipul. In chapter 93 you said that three things must be explained concerning the opinion that the coercion of a heretical Pope, and of any heretics whatever, belongs to the laity in a special case. Of the first two we have been dealt with briefly enough, so now let us treat the third: namely, in what case the coercion of a heretical Pope and of other heretics belongs to the laity. Magist. As was said before, according to a certain opinion, not all heretics are to be judged in the same way. For some heretics are laymen and others are clergy. Lay heretics, so far as the crime of heresy is concerned, belong to the court of the secular judge, but clerical heretics do not belong to the court of the secular judge, except in special cases. Discipul. I intend first to prove that lay heretics belong to the court of the secular judge. Magist. For this, the authority cited above in chapter 93 has been given. Discipul. I ask you to think of some other arguments for the same assertion. Magist. This seems capable of being proved. First, thus: he who is the minister of the Lord's king chiefly has the duty of judging the sins which his subjects commit against God. Kings, however, are ministers of God, of whom it is said in Wisdom 6: "Since you were ministers of his kingdom, you did not judge rightly," and so on. Therefore it belongs chiefly to kings to punish the sins which their subjects commit against God. Heresy, however, is a sin against God. Therefore it belongs to kings to punish with due correction the heretics subject to them. Second: he has the power to punish heretics subject to him who has the charge of judging or scattering every evil. But this concerns the king, as Solomon says in Proverbs 20: "A king who sits on the throne of judgment scatters all evil by his look." Therefore it belongs to him to punish duly all heretics subject to him. Third, thus: it belongs to the same persons to punish heretics under the new law as it belonged to punish idolaters and blasphemers with fitting penalty under the old law. But in the Old Testament it belonged to kings to punish heretics, idolaters and blasphemers with fitting penalty. Therefore this too belongs to kings under the New Testament. The major premise seems evident. The minor is proved by clear examples. For 1 Kings 15 speaks of King Asa, that he "did what was right in the sight of the Lord, as David his father had done, and he removed the effeminate men out of the land, and purged all the idols which his fathers had made. Moreover, Maachah his mother, he removed her from being queen, because she had made an idol in a grove; and Asa cut down her idol and burned it at the brook Kidron." From these words it is plainly to be gathered that King Asa, from zeal for God, did justice upon idolaters, who were to be counted among heretics. Likewise, as appears in 1 Kings 18, Elijah slew all the prophets of Baal. Fourth, thus: if laymen are exempt from the jurisdiction of kings and princes so far as the crime of heresy is concerned, this exemption is either from divine law or from human law. It is not from divine law, because nothing at all is found about such an exemption in the holy Scriptures, in which the divine law is contained. Therefore such an exemption is neither from divine law nor from human law; for if it is from human law, it is either from canon law or from civil law, that is, of secular kings and princes, or of the Pontiffs or of communities. It is not such an exemption from canon law, because the framers of canon law ought not thus to diminish the jurisdiction of secular rulers (Extra de iudiciis, Nouit), and so they ought not to take the subjects of secular rulers out from under their jurisdiction. Nor is such an exemption from the civil law of secular rulers, because no such exemption is read in the civil law. And so laymen are in no way exempt from the jurisdiction of kings and princes so far as the crime of heresy is concerned. Fifth, thus: a lay heretic is no less under the court of the secular judge than a clerical heretic. But a clerical heretic, as soon as he has been degraded, is so under the court of the secular judge that he must be duly punished by him. Therefore a layman is always under the court of the secular judge, and consequently a layman can and ought to punish lay heretics. Discip. Do not all hold that laymen, so far as the crime of heresy is concerned, are under the court of the secular judge, unless they have first been handed over to the secular court by the ecclesiastical judge? Magist. Many hold that they are not. Disc. Adduce some arguments for that assertion. Mag. This assertion seems clearly to be the intention of Pope Lucius, who, as found in Extra de haereticis ad abolendam, says: "A layman, however, unless (as has been said) he abjures his heresy, makes satisfaction, and at once flees to the orthodox Catholic faith, shall be left to the judgment of the secular judge, to receive due vengeance according to the quality of his crimes." From these words it is to be understood that a lay judge ought not to punish a lay heretic before he has been handed over to him by the ecclesiastical judge. The Gloss also seems to agree with this, saying: "Laymen are to be condemned for heresy by the Church, but the secular judge ought to punish them." Therefore heretics, before they have been condemned by the Church, do not, by reason of heresy, belong to the court of the secular judge. Likewise, just as secular cases do not belong to ecclesiastical judges, so ecclesiastical cases do not belong to secular judges. But heresy is an ecclesiastical cause, as the Gloss says on 2 q. 1, where it notes: "Of causes, some are ecclesiastical and some secular, and of ecclesiastical causes some are spiritual, some criminal, and some civil. A cause is spiritual where tithes or marriage are at issue. A cause is criminal where an ecclesiastical crime is in question, namely heresy or usury, whose examination belongs to the ecclesiastical judge (see below, c. Si quis cum clerico, and 6 q. 1, c. 1)." From these words it is to be understood that an ecclesiastical cause belongs to the ecclesiastical judge, and consequently not to the secular judge. But the cause of heresy is an ecclesiastical cause, as is expressly stated in the words just quoted. Therefore the cause of heresy does not belong to the secular judge, and so the secular judge ought not to punish lay heretics before they have been condemned by the Church. Discip. Although I think this second assertion agrees with the truth, I would gladly hear how one may answer the arguments in support of it. Magist. The answer is this. According to Gregory, as is cited in dist. 29, c. Regula: "The rule of the holy fathers was given according to time, place, person and matter, as the pressure of the situation required." This agrees with Isidore, as found in the same dist., c. 1, where he says: "It must be understood that many chapters are to be considered in respect of person, place and time, and since their manner is not thoroughly investigated, some, by entangling themselves in a labyrinth of error, stumble; for they understand before judging." Therefore the authorities of Pope Lucius and of the elders, and their sayings, must be understood in the light of the cause, the purpose and the time for which they were given; and once this is seen, it will be plain that secular judges may coerce lay heretics subject to them. It is said, then, that Pope Lucius denies that a lay heretic, unless he flees to the orthodox faith, is to be left to the judgment of the secular judge, because at that time, and perhaps always, it was the case that secular judges did not meddle at all with heretics before they had been condemned by an ecclesiastical judge. Through the negligence of the secular judges, the Church therefore intruded itself into the matter of lay heretics, by inquiring into and convicting them; but it did not wish to inflict any penalty on them. It wished rather that the due penalty be inflicted by the secular judge. Just as the ecclesiastical judge, because of the negligence of the secular judge, sometimes compels him to exercise justice, so now the Church makes itself responsible for punishing lay heretics, whom however the secular judges could duly coerce. When the Gloss therefore says that laymen are to be condemned for heresy by the Church, it speaks of the fact: for although secular judges could by right inquire into and correct the lay heretics subject to them, they often in fact neglect to do so. Therefore, so that lay heretics may not remain unpunished to the prejudice of the faithful and to the danger of the orthodox faith, the ecclesiastical judge makes up for the negligence of the secular judges, inquires into them himself, condemns those whom he convicts, and enjoins on the secular judge that he strike them with due penalty. To make this clear, the aforesaid Gloss immediately after the words quoted adds: "This is true, unless the layman is handed over to the secular court, but only the cleric is, see below, de verborum significatione, c. Nouimus, because a layman is always under the secular court." From these words it is to be understood that a layman is not exempt from the secular court for the crime of heresy; but when the secular judge neglects to coerce lay heretics, they are first to be condemned by the ecclesiastical judge, and afterwards the secular judge is to be compelled to punish them. For this reason the Gloss adds in the same place: "But in this case the execution is carried out only by the secular judge." That is, although condemnation may be brought about by the ecclesiastical judge, supplying in this the negligence of the secular judge, yet the execution of punishment must be carried out by the secular judge alone. When another Gloss says that the cause of heresy is an ecclesiastical cause, this is granted with regard to clerical heretics, because clerical heretics are not under the court of the secular judge except in certain determined cases; but with regard to laymen, the cause of heresy is both a secular cause and also an ecclesiastical cause in a certain way. It is a secular cause because the secular judge has the power to punish lay heretics; and it is also in a way an ecclesiastical cause, because the ecclesiastical judge, supplying the negligence of the secular judge, can condemn lay heretics. Discipul. That seems to me to lack force, for the crime of heresy is in no way a secular crime. For, first, it is committed directly against God; second, it is a sin only against the Christian religion; third, before pagan secular judges it would not be a crime at all. Therefore it is in no way a secular crime, and so it is only an ecclesiastical crime. From this it is plainly inferred that it belongs only to the ecclesiastical judge and not to the secular judge. Magist. Although the crime is ecclesiastical and not secular, it nevertheless belongs to the secular judge. For it belongs to the secular judge not only to punish secular crimes, but also crimes committed against God, against persons, and against ecclesiastical property. Every law and sect has this feature: that kings and princes, distinct from priests, punish not only secular crimes but also those crimes which they regard as committed against God or their gods and against their sect. For this reason kings in the Old Testament also punished idolaters; and the emperors, as judges of the pagans, persecuted Christians most bitterly as those who sinned gravely against their gods and their sect. Likewise Christian kings punish with due penalty the murderers of priests and those who steal ecclesiastical property, and yet the murder of a priest and the theft of ecclesiastical property are ecclesiastical crimes. Therefore many ecclesiastical crimes belong to the secular judge, and so from the fact that the crime of heresy is an ecclesiastical crime and is committed against God, it cannot be proved that it in no way belongs to the secular judge. Augustine seems to agree with this, as is read in 23 q. 5, Si propterea, where he says: "If Nebuchadnezzar the king was not a persecutor for this reason, that he most justly avenged the crime committed against the holy Daniel, how should it be avenged by kings that the sacraments of Christ are spat upon, if the members of the prophets have deserved to be avenged in this way because they were sent into danger?" From these words it is to be understood that a sin committed against God must much more be avenged by kings than a sin committed against a prophet or a priest. If, then, a king can and ought, without inquiry by the prelates, to punish a murderer of a priest subject to him, much more can and ought he to strike with due correction those subject to him who by heretical perversity have offended the majesty of God.

units.la: CAP. XCVIII.
units.tr: CAP. XCVIII.

units.la: In quo quaeritur, an Papa haereticus, seu quivis alter clericus possit per iudicem secularem coerceri etiam si a prælatis ecclesiæ minime fuerit requisitus, & recitantur tres opiniones & prima probatur auctoritatibus, ad quas respondetur ca. 100. in principio. Dictum vero secundæ & tertiæ opinionis probatur cap. sequenti.
units.tr: This chapter asks whether a heretical Pope, or any other clergyman, may be restrained by a secular judge even if the prelates of the Church have not asked him to do so. It sets out three opinions. The first is supported by authorities, to which an answer is given in chapter 100 at the beginning. The statement of the second and third opinions is supported in the following chapter.

units.la: Discip. Postquam indagavimus de haereticis laicis, an iudicio regum & secularium iudicum absque inquisitione prælatorum ecclesiæ sint subiecti, vertamus stylum ad clericos: & specialiter ad papam haereticum, an in aliquo casu papa vel clericus alius haereticus per iudicem secularem debeat coerceri, si iudex secularis super hoc a prælatis ecclesiæ minime fuerit requisitus. Mag. Circa hoc sunt opiniones diversæ, quarum una est, quod nec de clericis haereticis nec quibuscunque aliis laici nisi per prælatos ecclesiæ fuerint requisiti, in nullo casu intromittere se debent. Alia opinio est, quod laici, deficiente ecclesiastica potestate, de clericis etiam de papa haeretico possunt diffinitiam proferre sententiam, & executioni eandem sententiam demandare. Tertia opinio est hæc, quod deficiente ecclesiastica potestate laici possunt & debent papam haereticum, & eadem ratione alios clericos haereticos detinere, & ne virus suæ iniquitatis effundant in alios prohibere: sed diffinitiuam contra ipsum vel ipsos non debent nec possunt proferre sententiam: nec per consequens sententiam executioni mandare. Discipul. Pro prima opinione, quam puto veram, allega. Magist. Hæc videtur sententia Lucii papæ esse, qui, ut habetur extra de haereticis, ad abolendam, ait: Statuimus de haereticis, ut Comites, Barones, Rectores & Consules civitatum, & aliorum locorum, iuxta monitionem episcoporum (præstito corporaliter sacramento) promittant quod fideliter & efficaciter (cum ab eis fuerint requisiti) ecclesiam contra haereticos & horum complices adiuvabunt bona fide secundum posse suum, si vero illud observare noluerint, honore, quem obtinent, spolientur, & ad illos nullatenus assumantur (eis nihilominus excommunicatione ligandis) terra eorum interdicto ecclesiæ supponendi, civitas autem quæ hiis institutis duxerit resistendum vel (contra monitionem episcopi) punire neglexerit resistentes, aliarum careat civitatum commercio, & episcopali sede noverit dignitate privandam. Ex his verbis datur intelligi, quod laici & iudices seculares de punitione clericorum se intromittere non debent, nisi per prælatos ecclesiæ fuerint requisiti. Cui concilium generale sub Innocen. 3. papa celebratum, ut legitur supradicto c. excommunicamus, concordare videtur, in quo sic scribitur: moneantur, inquit, & inducatur, & si necesse fuerit per censuram ecclesiasticam compellantur seculi potestates (quibuscunque fungantur officiis) ut sicut reputari cupiunt & haberi fideles, ita pro defensione fidei præstent publice iuramentum: quod de terris suæ iurisdictioni subiectis univer sos haereticos ab ecclesia damnatos bona fide pro viribus exterminare studebunt: ita quod a modo quandocunque aliquis in potestatem sive per potentiam temporalem assumptus fuerit, hoc teneatur totum iuramentum firmare, si vero Dominus temporalis requisitus & monitus ab ecclesia terram suam purgare neglexerit ab haeretica feritate, per metropolitanum vel comprovinciales episcopos excommunicationis vinculo innodetur &c. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi quod punitio haereticorum non spectat ad laicos, nisi fuerint per ecclesiam requisiti.
units.tr: Disciple: Now that we have examined whether heretical laymen are subject to the judgment of kings and secular judges without the investigation of the prelates of the Church, let us turn our pen to the clergy, and in particular to a heretical Pope: may a Pope or any other heretical clergyman be restrained by a secular judge in any case, if the secular judge has not been asked to do so by the prelates of the Church? Master: On this there are differing opinions. One is that laymen must not interfere at all with heretical clergy, or with anyone else, unless they have been asked to do so by the prelates of the Church. Another opinion is that laymen, when ecclesiastical power is lacking, may pronounce a definitive sentence even on clergy, and even on a heretical Pope, and commit that sentence to execution. The third opinion is this: when ecclesiastical power is lacking, laymen may and must detain a heretical Pope, and for the same reason other heretical clergy, and prevent them from pouring out the poison of their wickedness upon others; but they may not and cannot pronounce a definitive sentence against him or them, and consequently cannot commit a sentence to execution. Disciple: For the first opinion, which I think is true, give your reasons. Master: This seems to be the view of Pope Lucius, who, as is found in the Extra decretals, On Heretics, Ad abolendam, says: "We decree concerning heretics that counts, barons, rulers and consuls of cities and other places, at the admonition of the bishops, shall swear an oath with their bodily hand that they will faithfully and effectually, when they have been asked, aid the Church against heretics and their accomplices in good faith and to the best of their power. If they are unwilling to keep this, they shall be stripped of the honour they hold, and shall never be admitted to any office; they shall also be bound with excommunication, and their land shall be placed under an interdict of the Church. A city which has decided to resist these institutions, or which (despite the bishop's admonition) has neglected to punish those who resist, shall be deprived of commerce with other cities, and shall know that it will be stripped of episcopal dignity." From these words it may be understood that laymen and secular judges ought not to interfere in the punishment of clergy unless they have been asked to do so by the prelates of the Church. The general council held under Pope Innocent III, as read in the aforementioned chapter Excommunicamus, seems to agree with this, where it is written: "Let the secular powers, whatever offices they hold, be admonished and instructed, and if necessary compelled by ecclesiastical censure, so that, just as they wish to be reckoned and regarded as faithful, they may publicly take an oath for the defence of the faith: that they will strive in good faith and to the best of their strength to drive out of the lands subject to their jurisdiction all heretics condemned by the Church; so that whenever anyone is raised to authority, whether by temporal power or by force, he shall be bound to confirm this whole oath. If a temporal lord, when asked and admonished by the Church, neglects to cleanse his land of heretical wildness, he shall be bound with the chain of excommunication by the metropolitan or the neighbouring bishops," and so on. From these words it may be understood that the punishment of heretics does not belong to laymen unless they have been asked to do so by the Church.

units.la: CAP. XCIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XCIX.

units.la: In quo quaeritur consequenter, an laici deficiente ecclesiastica potestate, habeant Papam haereticum seu alios clericos haereticos detinere & prohibere ne suam pravitatem in alios diffundant.
units.tr: In which it is further asked whether laymen, when ecclesiastical power fails, may hold a heretical pope or other heretical clergy and prohibit them from spreading their wickedness among others.

units.la: Discipul. Ista mihi sufficiant pro assertione prædicta, præsertim cum clerici a iurisdictione laicorum sint exempti, sane quia opinio secunda & tertia in hoc concordant, quod laici deficiente ecclesiastica potestate habent papam haereticum & eadem ratione alios clericos haereticos detinere: & etiam prohibere, ut non valeant in alios haereticam infundere pravitatem, de hoc solo omissis aliis, in quibus discrepant opiniones prædictæ, dicere non postponas. Magist. Assertionem dictam magis intelliges, si fuerit declaratum, quomodo intelligant ecclesiasticam posse deficere potestatem.
units.tr: Disciple. Let these things suffice for the aforesaid assertion, especially since the clergy are exempt from the jurisdiction of laymen. Indeed, the second and third opinions agree that when ecclesiastical power fails, laymen have the right to hold a heretical pope, and for the same reason to detain other heretical clergy and also to prohibit them from infusing their heretical wickedness into others. Do not hesitate to tell me about this point alone, setting aside the others on which the aforesaid opinions differ. Master. You will understand the assertion better if it is made clear how they understand that ecclesiastical power can fail.

units.la: Disc. Dic quomodo hoc debet intelligi. Mag. Quod papa effecto haeretico ecclesiastica potestas deficiat quatuor modis potest intelligi, videlicet per impotentiam, per malitiam, per damnabilem negligentiam & per ignorantiam. Per impotentiam quidem, si papa haereticus tanta vteretur potentia temporali, ut nullus platus ecclesiæ (nec illius dioecesis in qua papa haereticus moraretur) nec alius posset ad brachium seculare recurrere: utpote si omnes prælatos catholicos teneret in vinculis, vel aliis modis impediret, ne ad seculare volarent auxilium. Alio modo potest ecclesiastica potestas deficedeficere per impotentiam, puta si aliqui prælati catholici impotentes & pauperes requirerent laicos aliquos pro papa hæretico coercendo, & illi nollent eos iuuare. Secundo modo potest intelligi deficere potestas ecclesiastica per malitiam: puta si omnes prælati ecclesiæ & clerici papæ hæretico adhærerent eius errores vel personam pro viribus defendendo. Tertio potest deficere ecclesiastica potestas per damnabilem negligentiam, vtpote si prælati & clerici qui possent per se (invocato auxilio brachii secularis) papam hæreticum coercere: & tamen conculcationem fidei nullatenus attendentes, vel non accusantes ipsum permittant libere in suis erroribus remanere. Quarto potest deficere ecclesiastica potestas per ignorantiam: vtpote si prælati ecclesiæ, saltem multi qui possent papam hæreticum coercere, nescirent ipsum in prauitatem hæreticam incidisse. Istis quatuor modis (papa hæretico existente) potest intelligi potestas ecclesiastica deficere. Discipul. Intelligo quomodo dicunt ecclesiasticam potestatem posse deficere, ideo nunc allega pro assertione prædicta. Magist. Quod deficiente ecclesiastica potestate aliquo prædictorum modorum laici valeant papam hæreticum captiuare, & ne prauitate hæretica inficiat alios prohibere, multis modis, tam scilicet aliorum testimoniis, quam rationibus videtur posse probari. Hoc enim Glossa distin. 17. c. non licuit, sententialiter & verbaliter videtur asserere, ait enim: Vbicunque deficit ecclesiastica potestas, semper recurritur ad brachium seculare, siue ergo deficiat ecclesiastica potestas per impotentiam, siue per malitiam, siue per damnabilem negligentiam, coercio papæ hæretici, ne valeat fideles inficere, ad laicos aliquos pertinebit. Item hæc videtur sententia Isidor. qui, vt legitur 23. quaest. 5. c. principes, ait: Principes nonnunquam intra ecclesiam potestatis adepta culmina tenent, vt per eandem potestatem disciplinam ecclesiasticam muniant, vbi dicit Gloss. in hæc verba: Et ecce laici habent iurisdictionem multipliciter intra ecclesiam, quandoque in personis, cum sint incorrigibiles, vt 23. distinct. eos qui, & infra eadem de legislatoribus. Item quandoque propter ambitionem aliquius, vt 79. distinct. c. fi quis pecuniam. Item cum fidem volunt subuertere, 8. dist. quo iure, & eadem cap. 1. & 17. distinct. vbi licuit, & infra. Item cum falsarius est clericus, & extra de crimine falsi, ad falsariorum, & cum schisma faciunt: & cum contemnunt excommunicationem, vt infra de legislatoribus, & vbicunque ecclesiastica potestas deficit, vt hic, & cum tributum petunt ab ecclesia, vt infra ca. q. 8. c. conuenior.
units.tr: Disc. Tell me how this is to be understood. Mag. That ecclesiastical power may fail when the pope has become a heretic can be understood in four ways: through inability, through malice, through culpable negligence, and through ignorance. Through inability, if a heretical pope wielded such temporal power that no prelate of the Church (nor of the diocese where the heretical pope lived) and no one else could appeal to the secular arm; for example, if he kept all the Catholic prelates in chains or otherwise prevented them from flying to the aid of the secular power. In another way ecclesiastical power can fail through inability: for instance, if some Catholic prelates, being powerless and poor, asked laymen to restrain a heretical pope, and the laymen were unwilling to help them. In the second way, ecclesiastical power can be understood to fail through malice: for instance, if all the prelates of the Church and all the clergy adhered to the pope, defending his errors or his person as far as they could. Thirdly, ecclesiastical power can fail through culpable negligence: for instance, if the prelates and clergy, who could themselves (by invoking the aid of the secular arm) restrain the heretical pope, yet in no way heeding the trampling of the faith, or not accusing him, allowed him to remain freely in his errors. Fourthly, ecclesiastical power can fail through ignorance: for instance, if the prelates of the Church, or at least many of those who could restrain the heretical pope, did not know that he had fallen into heretical wickedness. In these four ways, with the pope being a heretic, ecclesiastical power can be understood to fail. Discipul. I understand how they say ecclesiastical power can fail; now therefore bring forward your arguments for the aforesaid assertion. Magist. That when ecclesiastical power fails in any of the aforesaid ways, laymen may take a heretical pope captive and prohibit him from infecting others with heretical wickedness, can be proved in many ways, both by the testimonies of others and by reasons. For the Gloss on distin. 17. c. non licuit seems to assert this both in substance and in words; it says: Wherever ecclesiastical power fails, recourse is always had to the secular arm; so whether ecclesiastical power fails through inability, or through malice, or through culpable negligence, the restraint of a heretical pope, lest he be able to infect the faithful, will pertain to some laymen. Likewise this seems to be the opinion of Isidore, who, as is read in 23. quaest. 5. c. principes, says: Princes sometimes hold the heights of power attained within the Church, so that by that same power they may fortify ecclesiastical discipline; where the Gloss says on these words: And behold, laymen have jurisdiction in many ways within the Church, sometimes over persons, since they are incorrigible, as in 23 dist. "eos qui," and below in the same place on legislators. Likewise sometimes on account of someone's ambition, as in 79 dist. c. "si quis pecuniam." Likewise when they wish to subvert the faith, 8 dist. "quo iure," and the same chapter, and 1 and 17 dist. "ubi licuit," and below. Likewise when a cleric is a forger, Extra "de crimine falsi," "ad falsariorum"; and when they make a schism; and when they despise excommunication, as below "de legislatoribus"; and wherever ecclesiastical power fails, as here; and when they demand tribute from the Church, as below C. q. 8 c. "conuenior."

units.la: Ex quibus verbis habetur non solum sententialiter, sed etiam verbaliter, quod vbicunque ecclesiastica potestas deficit, laici habent iurisdictionem intra ecclesiam, hoc est super clericos & deficiente per consequens ecclesiastica potestate sive per impotentiam siue per malitiam siue per ignorantiam, laici super papam hæreticum obtinent potestatem, sed & ex eisdem verbis colliguntur diuersæ rationes, quare papa hæreticus ad iurisdictionem pertinet laicorum, quod debet intelligi, deficiente ecclesiastica potestate. Quarum prima est: quia papa hæreticus est incorrigibilis, ex hoc enim quod est pertinax, debet incorrigibilis reputari: etiam cum omnes incorrigibiles debeant coerceri deficiente ecclesiastica potestate est papa hæreticus per laicos coercendus. Secunda ratio assignatur ambitio, nam papa hæreticus per ambitionem occupans Apostolicam sedem (ne totus ordo ecclesiasticus confundatur & fides periclitetur) deficiente ecclesiastica potestate coerceri debet per prouidentiam laicorum. Tertia ratio propter hoc quod papa hæreticus fidem subuertere cupit, potestate ecclesiastica deficiente, est a laicis prohibendus. Quarta propter hoc, quod excommunicationem contemnit, ne excommunicatione cum eo catholici maculentur, per principes seculi quando ecclesiastica potestas deficit coerceri debet. Item Isidor. vbi prius, dicit in hæc verba: ceterum intra ecclesiam potestates necessariæ non essent, nisi vt quod sacerdotes non prævalent efficere per sermonem doctrinæ, potestas imperet per disciplinam terrorem, sæpe enim per regnum terrenum cœleste regnum proficit: vt qui intra ecclesiam positi contra fidem & disciplinam agunt, rigore principum terreantur, ipsamque disciplinam, quam vtilitas ecclesiæ exercere non prævalet, ceruicibus super horum potestas principalis imponat. Ex quibus verbis colligitur euidenter, quod quando circa correctionem eorum, qui contra fidem & disciplinam agunt, deficit ecclesiastica potestas, tales sunt per principes comprimendi. Si igitur papa est hæreticus, & sacerdotes per doctrinæ sermonem eum non valent vel nolunt corrigere: per potestates publicas comprimi debet. Item Pelagius papa, vt habetur 23. quaest. 5. c. quali, ait: Hoc etiam diuina & humana leges statuerunt, vt ab ecclesiastica vnitate diuisi & eius pacem iniquissime perturbantes, a secularibus potestatibus etiam comprimantur, nec quicquam maius est, vnde Deo sacrificium possitis offerre, quam si ordinetis vt hi qui in suam & aliorum perniciem debachantur, competenti debeant vigore compesci. Ex quibus verbis euidenter habetur, quod secundum leges diuinas ab ecclesiæ vnitate diuisi & eius pacem perturbantes per seculares debent comprimi potestates, papa autem hæreticus ab vnitate ecclesiæ est diuisus, cuius pacem iniquissime nititur perturbare, quia dum fides ecclesiæ corrumpitur & laceratur, vera pax ecclesiæ perturbatur, igitur papa hæreticus, vbi deficeret ecclesiastica potestas, esset per potestates publicas compescendus.
units.tr: From these words it is held not only in substance but also in words that wherever ecclesiastical power fails, laymen have jurisdiction within the Church, that is, over the clergy; and so, when ecclesiastical power consequently fails, whether through inability, through malice, or through ignorance, laymen obtain power over a heretical pope. From the same words, various reasons are also gathered for why a heretical pope falls under the jurisdiction of laymen, which must be understood as applying when ecclesiastical power fails. (1) The first is that a heretical pope is incorrigible; for from the fact that he is obstinate he must be regarded as incorrigible, and since all incorrigible persons ought to be restrained when ecclesiastical power fails, the heretical pope is to be restrained by laymen. (2) The second reason assigned is ambition: a heretical pope who occupies the apostolic see by ambition (lest the whole ecclesiastical order be confounded and the faith endangered) must be restrained, when ecclesiastical power fails, by the providence of laymen. (3) The third is that, because a heretical pope desires to subvert the faith, he is to be prohibited by laymen when ecclesiastical power fails. (4) The fourth is that, because he despises excommunication, lest Catholics be defiled by association with him, he must be restrained by the princes of the world when ecclesiastical power fails. Likewise Isidore, in the passage cited above, says in these words: Otherwise, powers would not be necessary within the Church, except that what priests cannot effect by the word of doctrine, the power may enforce by the terror of discipline; for often the heavenly kingdom profits through an earthly kingdom, so that those who, placed within the Church, act against faith and discipline may be terrified by the rigour of princes, and that discipline which the usefulness of the Church does not prevail to exercise, the principal power may impose upon their necks. From these words it is clearly gathered that when ecclesiastical power fails in correcting those who act against faith and discipline, such persons are to be restrained by princes. If therefore the pope is a heretic, and the priests either cannot or will not correct him by the word of doctrine, he ought to be restrained by public powers. Likewise Pope Pelagius, as is found in 23. quaest. 5. c. quali, says: Divine and human laws have also decreed that those who are divided from the unity of the Church and most iniquitously disturb its peace should be restrained even by secular powers; nor is there anything greater by which you can offer sacrifice to God than if you ordain that those who rage to their own and others' destruction ought to be restrained with due vigour. From these words it is clearly held that, according to divine laws, those divided from the unity of the Church and disturbing its peace are to be restrained by secular powers. But the heretical pope is divided from the unity of the Church, and he strives most iniquitously to disturb its peace, because while the faith of the Church is corrupted and torn, the true peace of the Church is disturbed. Therefore the heretical pope, where ecclesiastical power would fail, would have to be restrained by public powers.

units.la: Discip. Quæ sunt illæ leges diuinæ, quibus statuitur, quod ab ecclesiæ vnitate diuisi & eius pacem iniquissime perturbantes, sunt per potestates publicas comprimendi? Magist. Respondetur, quod illæ leges diuinæ specialiter de hæreticis perturbantibus ecclesiam habentur Deut. 13. & 17. nam Deut. 13. non solum sacerdotibus, sed etiam generaliter omnibus & specialiter in potestate constitutis sic præcipitur: Si surrexerit in medio tui propheta, aut qui somnium dicat se vidisse, & prædixerit signum & portentum, & venerit quod locutus est, & dixerit tibi: Eamus & sequamur Deos alienos quos ignoras, & seruiamus eis, non audies verba Prophetæ illius aut somniatoris: quia tentat vos Dominus Deus vester, vt palam sciat vtrum diligatis eum, aut non in toto corde & in tota anima vestra, & post ait: Propheta autem antem ille aut fictor somniorum interficietur: quia locutus est ut vos auerteret à Domino Deo vestro, qui eduxit vos de terra Ægypti, & redemit vos de domo seruitutis, ut errare te faceret de via quam præcepit tibi Dominus Deus tuus: & auferes malum de medio tui, ibi immediate subiungitur: si voluerit te persuadere frater tuus Filius matris tuæ, aut Filius tuus, vel Filia, siue vxor tuæ, quæ est in sinu tuo, aut amicus quem diliges vt animam tuam, dicens: exeamus & seruiamus diis alienis quos ignoras tu & patres tui cunctarum in circuitu gentium, quæ iuxta vel procul sunt ab initio vsque ad finem terræ, non acquiesces ei, neque audias neque parcat ei oculus tuus & misereris, & auscultes eum: sed statim interficies eum, & post sic legitur: si audieris in vna vrbium tuarum, quas Deus tuus dabit tibi ad habitandum, dicentes aliquos, egressi sunt filii Belial, & euerterunt habitatores urbis atque dixerunt: eamus, seruiamus diis alienis quos ignoratis, quare sollicite & diligenter (rei veritate perspecta) si inueneris certum esse quod dicitur, & abominationem hanc opere perpetratam, statim percuties habitatores urbis eius in ore gladii. Item Deuteronomo 17. sic scribitur: Cum reperti fuerint intra vnam portarum tuarum, quas Dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi, aut vir aut mulier, qui faciunt malum in conspectu Domini Dei tui, vt transgrediantur pactum eius, vt vadant & seruiant diis alienis & adorent eos & solem & lunam & omnem militiam cœli quam non præcepi, & hoc tibi fuerit nunciatum, audiensque inquisieris diligenter, & verum esse repereris abominationem factam esse in Israel, educes virum & mulierem, quæ rem sceleratissimam perpetrauit ad portas ciuitatis tuæ & lapidibus obruentur. Hæ sunt leges diuinæ contra omnes auertentes & conantes auertere à veritate legis diuinæ, inter quos constat hæreticos computandos indistincte cunctos constringentes catholicos, vt viriuersos à lege Dei apostatantes delere conentur, quæ leges non esse ordinem iuris in hoc obseruandum aperte declarant, vt scilicet quicunque viri vel mulieres, vel sacerdotes, vel non sacerdotes, vel prophetæ, id est doctores, vel alii de prauitate hæretica, seu apostasia à fide accusantur vel etiam diffamantur, omni diligentia & sollicitudine veritas inquiratur per quoscunque fideles, ad quos accusatio vel diffamatio talis peruenerit, si non sint superiores, qui velint vel possint inquirere de veritate, iustitia minime differatur, sed tales maledicti pro suis demeritis puniantur. Discipul. Talis inquisitio & punitio non debet fieri per quoscunque: sed solummodo per iudices, quibus talia ex officio suscepto incumbunt. Magist. Conceditur quod talia primo spectant ad iudices: si tamen iudices non possunt vel nolunt in hos iustitiam exercere, ad subiectos spectat facere de hoc iustitiæ complementum, propter quod verba prædicta legum, non ad iudices tantummodo pertinent, sed indistincte ad cunctos catholicos diriguntur, vt intelligant viriuersi fideles, quod huiusmodi iustitia in nullo casu debet differri: sed quicunque fideles subditi vel alii iustitiam facere debent, si tantam habuerint potestatem vt queant leges diuinas executioni mandare, propter quod Helias propheta, quamuis non esset sacerdos nec iudex, iussit populo, non iudicibus, apprehendere prophetas Baal: quos comprehensos duxit ad torrentem Cyson, & interfecit eos ibi, vt legitur 3. Regum 18. ergo leges diuinæ prædictæ non solum iudices, sed subiectos vniuersos constringunt: ordine tamen quodam, vt primo ad talem iustitiam faciendam iudices obligentur, secundo autem subiecti, si iudices non possunt vel nolunt iustitiam exercere.
units.tr: Student: What are those divine laws by which it is laid down that those who have been separated from the unity of the Church and who most wickedly disturb its peace are to be restrained by the public powers? Master: It is answered that those divine laws concerning heretics who disturb the Church are found specifically in Deut. 13 and 17. For Deut. 13 commands this not only to priests but generally to everyone, and especially to those placed in authority, in these words: "If a prophet or one who claims to have seen a dream arises in your midst, and he foretells a sign or a wonder, and what he spoke comes to pass, and he says to you, 'Let us go and follow other gods, whom you do not know, and serve them,' you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or dreamer, for the LORD your God tests you, to know openly whether you love him with your whole heart and your whole soul." Afterwards it says: "But that prophet or dream-maker shall be put to death, because he has spoken to turn you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, to make you stray from the way which the LORD your God commanded you; so you shall take away the evil from your midst." Immediately after this it continues: "If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or daughter, or the wife of your bosom, or a friend whom you love as your own soul, should try to persuade you secretly, saying, 'Let us go and serve other gods, which you and your fathers have not known, gods of the peoples round about you, near or far, from one end of the earth to the other,' you shall not consent to him or listen to him; your eye shall not pity him, you shall not spare him or conceal him, but you shall surely kill him." And then it is read: "If you hear that in one of your cities, which the LORD your God gives you to dwell in, some men, sons of Belial, have gone out and have led astray the inhabitants of the city, saying, 'Let us go and serve other gods, which you have not known,' then you shall inquire carefully and diligently; if, the truth having been examined, you find it certain that this is said and this abomination has been done, you shall at once put the inhabitants of that city to the sword." Likewise Deut. 17 is written thus: "When there are found within one of your gates, which the LORD your God gives you, a man or a woman who does evil in the sight of the LORD your God, so as to transgress his covenant, and goes and serves other gods and worships them, or the sun, or the moon, or any host of heaven, which I have not commanded; and when it is reported to you, and you hear and inquire diligently and find it true that this abomination has been done in Israel, you shall bring out that man or woman who has committed this most wicked thing to the gates of your city, and they shall be stoned with stones." These are the divine laws against all who turn away, or try to turn away, from the truth of the divine law, and it is clear that among these must be counted all heretics, who trouble the Catholics without distinction, so that they seek to destroy everyone who apostatises from the law of God. These laws plainly declare that the order of law to be observed is this: whatever men or women, whether priests or non-priests, or prophets (that is, teachers), or others, are accused or even defamed of heretical depravity or apostasy from the faith, the truth is to be inquired into with all diligence and care by whatever faithful persons such an accusation or defamation reaches, if there are no superiors who are willing or able to inquire into the truth; justice must not be delayed in any way, but such accursed persons must be punished according to their deserts. Student: Such inquiry and punishment ought not to be carried out by just anyone, but only by judges, to whom such matters belong by virtue of their office. Master: It is granted that such matters first belong to judges. If, however, the judges cannot or will not exercise justice against these men, it falls to subjects to bring about the completion of justice. For this reason the aforesaid words of the laws do not pertain to judges alone, but are addressed without distinction to all Catholics, so that all the faithful may understand that justice of this kind must in no case be delayed. Rather, any faithful subjects or others must act, if they have such power that they can put the divine laws into execution. Thus the prophet Elijah, although he was neither a priest nor a judge, ordered the people, not the judges, to seize the prophets of Baal; he led them, once seized, down to the brook Kishon and slew them there, as is read in 3 Kings 18. Therefore the aforesaid divine laws bind not only judges but all subjects. Yet there is a certain order: judges are bound first to carry out such justice, and subjects second, if the judges cannot or will not exercise justice.

units.la: Discipul. Istæ leges diuinæ cum pertineant non ad moralia, sed ad iudicialia legis diuinæ antiquæ fideles sub lege libertatis constitutos nequaquam constringunt. Magist. In legibus supradictis aliquid est morale & aliquid est iudiciale, morale est, quod fideles hæreticis & apostaticis à fide cupientibus alios & lege Dei auertere, nullo modo consentire tenebantur, sed eis obuiare & resistere modis sibi conuenientibus, legemque diuinam obseruare, defendere & tueri tenebantur. Iudiciale autem erat, quod occidi debebant, licet ergo fideles sub lege libertatis constituti ad id, quod est iudiciale in legibus memoratis minime astringantur: quia ratione illarum legum non tenentur hæreticos aut à fide apostatantes neci tradere corporali: ad illa tamen quæ in illis legibus moralia sunt cuncti Christiani necessario sunt astricti, & ideo nec hæreticis consentire debent nec fauere nec obedire: sed ipsis resistere pro viribus & prohibere, ne fidem corrumpere valeant orthodoxam principes seculi: & propter eorum negligentiam vel malitiam ad id omnes Christiani tenentur.
units.tr: Student: Since these divine laws belong not to the moral but to the judicial part of the ancient law of God, they do not bind the faithful who are placed under the law of liberty. Master: In the laws cited above there is something moral and something judicial. What is moral is that the faithful were bound never to consent in any way to heretics and to those who, desiring to turn others away from the law of God, have apostatised from the faith; rather, they were bound to oppose and resist them by suitable means, and to observe, defend and protect the divine law. What is judicial is that these men had to be put to death. Therefore, although the faithful who live under the law of liberty are not bound by what is judicial in the laws mentioned, since by virtue of those laws they are not obliged to hand heretics or those who apostatise from the faith over to bodily death, yet all Christians are necessarily bound to what is moral in those laws. For this reason they ought neither to consent to heretics, nor to favour them, nor to obey them, but to resist them with all their strength and to prevent them from being able to corrupt the orthodox faith; and all Christians are bound to this, on account of the negligence or malice of the secular princes.

units.la: Discipul. Nunquid aliquis doctorum ab ecclesia receptorum tenet prædictas leges veteris testamenti nunc à catholicis vniuersis esse seruandas? Magist. Beatus Cyprianus, vt legitur 23. q. 5. c. si audieris, hoc videtur expresse sentire, ait enim: si audieris in vna ex ciuitatibus, quas Dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi inhabitare illic dicentes, eamus & seruiamus diis alienis, quos non nouisti, interficies, nesciisque omnes qui sunt in ciuitate in cede gladii, & incendes ciuitatem igni: & erit sine habitaculo, in æternum non reedificabitur, etiam nunc vt auertatur Dominus ab indignatione irae suae & dabit tibi misericordiam, & miserebitur tui & multiplicabit te, si audieris vocem Domini Dei tui & obseruaueris præcepta, cuius præcepti & vigoris memor Mathathias interfecit eum qui ad aram sacrificaturus accesserat, quod si ante aduentum Christi circa Deum colendum & idola spernenda hæc præcepta seruata sunt: quanto magis sunt post aduentum Christi circa Deum colendum seruanda, quando ille veniens non solum verbis hortatus fit, sed etiam factis. Ex quibus verbis colligitur quod leges præscriptæ sunt magis seruandæ post aduentum Christi quam ante, quod intelligendum est de moralibus, quæ in prædictis legibus continentur.
units.tr: Student: Does any of the teachers received by the Church hold that the aforesaid laws of the Old Testament are now to be observed by all Catholics? Master: Blessed Cyprian, as is read in 23 q. 5 c. si audieris, seems expressly to hold this. For he says: "If you hear that in one of the cities which the LORD your God gives you to dwell in, men say, 'Let us go and serve other gods, whom you have not known,' you shall slay them, and you shall put to the sword all who are in the city, and you shall burn the city with fire, and it shall be a desolation for ever, and it shall not be rebuilt. Then the LORD will turn from the heat of his anger and will show you mercy, and have compassion on you and multiply you, if you hear the voice of the LORD your God and keep his commandments." Mindful of the force of this precept, Mattathias slew the man who was about to approach the altar to sacrifice. If these precepts were observed before the coming of Christ, in worshipping God and despising idols, how much more must they be observed after the coming of Christ, since he, when he came, exhorted us not only by words but also by deeds. From these words it is gathered that the prescribed laws are to be observed even more after the coming of Christ than before, which must be understood of the moral parts contained in the aforesaid laws.

units.la: Disc. Quamuis ista moralia seruanda sunt à iudicibus, non tamen ab omnibus. Mag. Contra hoc videtur Glossa in praeallegato capitulo: quae super verbo necabit, ibi ait: Tu quicunque fis. Et sic quandoque qui non est iudex potest punire maleficos, ut infra eo q. ultim. legit. ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod non solum ad iudices, verum etiam ad alios pertinet in hoc casu, scilicet cum volunt subvertere haereticI fidem, & non apparet qui eis resistat, punire maleficos. Et ita cum papa est haereticus, & clerici non possunt vel nolunt ipsum coercere, ipsius coercio spectat ad laicos, quamuis per clericos non fuerint requisiti. Discip. Si plura testimonia maiorum sonant eandem assertionem, ipsa non differas allegare. Magist. Hoc Pelagius papa, ut legitur 23. q. 5. c. non vos, sentire videtur, cum dicit: malum autem schisma esse & per exteras etiam potestates huiusmodi opprimi debere homines & canonica scriptura auctoritas & paternarum nostrarum regularum veritas docet, igitur haeretici etiam clerici sunt per potestates exteras comprimendi, & per consequens papa haereticus (si potestas deficiat clericorum) per principes laicorum compesci deberet. Item papa Pelagius infra eo cap. de Liguribus scribens Narsoprincipi ait: regulae patrum hoc specialiter constituerunt, ut si qua ecclesiastici officii persona, cui subiectum est, resisterit, vel seorsum turbas collegerit, aut aliud altare erexerit, seu schisma fecerit, iste excommunicetur atque damnetur, omnes schismaticos etiam per exteras potestates opprimendo. Quod si forte hoc contempserit, & permanserit divisiones & schismata faciendo, per potestates publicas opprimatur. Ecce Domine, quia animus noster forte timidus est, nec persequi videatur, de patrum auctoritate vobis haec breviter scribenda curavi: cum mille alia exempla & constitutiones sint, quibus evidenter cognoscitur, ut facientes scissuras in sancta ecclesia, non solum exilio sed etiam inscriptione rerum & dura custodia per publicas potestates debeant coerceri. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod episcopi, de quibus fuit sermo in capitulo supradicto Pelagii, si excommunicationem & damnationem contemnendo scissuras & schismata fecerint, quales sunt episcopi haeretici, auctoritate canonum sanctorum patrum debent per potestates publicas coerceri, ergo si papa fiat haereticus, quantumcunque praelati ecclesiae noluerint vel non potuerint ad ipsum coercendum auxilium invocare brachii saecularis, publicae potestates non solum auctoritate divinae legis, & rationis simul ex lege divina & naturali dictamine rationis acceptae: sed auctoritate constitutionum patrum sanctorum possunt & debent papam haereticum coercere. Item Augustin. ut legitur 11. q. 3. cap. Imperatores, scribens Donatistis, qui erant clerici & quidam eorum episcopi, ait: ipse Nabuchodonosor post miraculum trium puerorum commotus atque commutatus pro veritate contra errorem edictum proposuit, ut quicunque blasphemarent Deum Sydrach, Misach & Abdenago, in interitum irent & domus eorum in ruinam, & non vultus ut aliquid tale contra vos iubeant Imperatores Christiani, cum sciant a nobis, quos rebaptizatis, Christum exsufflari? Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod quemadmodum Nabuchodonosor rex infidelis edictum proposuit contra blasphemantes Deum verum, sic possunt imperatores Christiani punire clericos haereticos & episcopos Christum exsufflantes, sed Nabuchodonosor tale poterat edictum proponere a sacerdotibus minime requisitus, ergo imperatores possunt punire clericos haereticos, & ita si papa fuerit haereticus, & praelati non velint ipsum vel non poterint ipsum coercere, est per laicos comprimendus. Item Glossa 23. dist. dicit, quod clerici propter haeresim facti sunt de foro iudicis saecularis.
units.tr: Disciple: Although these moral precepts are to be observed by judges, they are not binding on everyone. Master: The Gloss on the chapter cited above seems to say otherwise. On the word "shall kill" it says: "Whoever you are." So sometimes someone who is not a judge can punish evildoers, as is read below in the last question. From these words it is understood that this applies not only to judges but also to others in the case where heretics want to subvert the faith and no one appears to resist them. So when the pope is a heretic, and the clergy cannot or will not restrain him, his restraint belongs to the laity, even though the clergy have not asked for it. Disciple: If several testimonies of the elders affirm the same assertion, do not hold back from citing them. Master: Pope Pelagius seems to hold this, as is read in 23 q. 5 c. non vos, when he says: "Schism is evil, and both the authority of canonical Scripture and the truth of our fathers' rules teach that men of this kind ought to be suppressed even by foreign powers." Therefore heretical clergy too are to be restrained by foreign powers, and consequently a heretical pope (if the power of the clergy fails) ought to be restrained by the princes of the laity. Likewise Pope Pelagius, writing to the prince Narses in the same chapter, "de Liguribus," says: "The rules of the fathers have specifically laid down that if any person of ecclesiastical office, to whom he is subject, resists, or gathers crowds apart, or erects another altar, or makes a schism, he is to be excommunicated and condemned, all schismatics being suppressed even by foreign powers. But if perhaps he despises this and persists in making divisions and schisms, let him be suppressed by public powers." Behold, Lord, since our spirit is perhaps timid and seems not to pursue the matter, I have taken care to write these things to you briefly from the authority of the fathers. There are a thousand other examples and constitutions by which it is clearly known that those who make rents in holy Church should be restrained not only by exile but also by confiscation of goods and harsh custody by public powers. From these words it is understood that the bishops mentioned in the above chapter of Pelagius, if they make rents and schisms by despising excommunication and condemnation, as heretical bishops do, ought to be restrained by public powers on the authority of the holy canons of the fathers. Therefore if the pope becomes a heretic, however much the prelates of the Church have been unwilling or unable to invoke the help of the secular arm to restrain him, public powers not only can but ought to restrain the heretical pope. They have this right by the authority of divine law, by reason joined with the natural dictate of reason received from divine law, and also by the authority of the constitutions of the holy fathers. Likewise Augustine, as is read in 11 q. 3 c. Imperatores, writing to the Donatists, who were clergy and some of them bishops, says: "Nebuchadnezzar himself, moved and changed after the miracle of the three boys, set forth an edict in defence of the truth against error, that whoever blasphemed God, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, should go to destruction and their houses to ruin. Will not Christian emperors order anything of the kind against you, since they know that Christ is breathed upon by us, whom you rebaptize?" From these words it is understood that just as the unbelieving king Nebuchadnezzar set forth an edict against those who blasphemed the true God, so Christian emperors can punish heretical clergy and bishops who breathe upon Christ. Nebuchadnezzar could set forth such an edict without being asked by priests at all; therefore emperors can punish heretical clergy. And so if the pope is a heretic and the prelates do not want to restrain him, or cannot, he is to be restrained by laymen. Likewise the Gloss on 23 dist. says that "clergy, on account of heresy, have come under the jurisdiction of the secular judge."

units.la: Discipul. Si pro assertione ista rationes aliquas cogitasti, ipsas adducas in medium. Magist. Assertio supradicta multis videtur rationibus posse probari: quarum prima est haec.
