Similiter si quis docuerit, quod Christus non sit natus de virgine: vel quod non fuit passus: vel quod non resurrexerit: vel quod non est unus Deus: vel quod non sunt tres personae in Deo: Iudex secularis tenetur scire, quod talis est haereticus, & ita sicut iudex secularis multa ad fidem spectantia orthodoxam credere tenetur explicite, ita in multis casibus per seipsum potest cognoscere, quid est tenendum in causa haereticae pravitatis. Alio modo potest cognoscere de causa haereticae pravitatis requirendo consilium peritorum, quemadmodum de multis criminibus contingit ex informatione aliorum, in quibus nesciret per seipsum, quid rectum, quid obliquum, nisi per informationem aliorum discutere, cum enim coram iudice aliquis accusatur de salsa moneta: nescit discernere per seipsum an moneta, de qua fit quaestio, sit vera & falsa, & ideo antequam sententiam proferat, requirit monetarios, quos iuramento vel alio modo astringit, ut sibi de tali moneta indicent veritatem, & ita in pluribus casibus iudex secularis, qui non habet omnes artes & naturas rerum scire de consilio aliorum profert sententiam, quia in talibus casibus quam pluribus per seipsum non posset cognoscere, quomodo oporteat iudicare. Sic dicunt de iudice seculari in casibus multis respectu causae pravitatis haereticae: quia in multis casibus indigeret consilio in sacris literis peritorum. Si enim aliquis Christianus accusaretur coram iudice seculari in Biblia minime erudito: quod pertinaciter asseruit beatum Paulum fuisse conversum ante passionem Christi, quemadmodum quidam magnus canonista dixit, & in scripturis suis reliquit, quod beatus Paulus fuit unus de duodecim Apostolis, qui sequebantur Christum antequam pateretur: Iudex secularis nesciret per seipsum dare sententiam: sed de requisito consilio peritorum in Scripturis sacris; ex quibus penderet quaestio supradicta, posset scire dare sententiam. Ubi autem iudex secularis, nec per consilium suum posset scire aperte, quae esset veritas in aliqua quaestione mota de fide, in tali casu se intromittere non deberet. Ad propositum igitur applicando dicitur, quod si Papa haereticus teneret fidem Christianam esse falsam, non esse tres personas distinctas in divinis, aut aliquid huiusmodi, quod iudex secularis per seipsum, vel per consilium peritorum posset aperte cognoscere esse haereticum: secure posset Papam haereticum iudicare, si clerici nollent vel non possent ipsum debite coercere: Cum vero dicitur, quod ad iudicem secularem non pertinet causa fidei vel Dei: Respondetur, quod dicere causam fidei vel Dei nullo modo spectare ad iudicem secularem, vel laicos, omnino esset insanum, & est verbum clericorum avarorum & superborum; qui ideo ab ecclesia Dei laicos conantur excludere, ut ipsis laicis exclusis possent ab ecclesia laicorum Domini reputari, cum (sicut saepe allegatum est) in Scriptura sacra nunquam laici ab ecclesia nomine excludantur, sed ubicunque in Scripturis sacris nomen ecclesiae viros & mulieres & laicos comprehendat. Causa igitur fidei & Dei secundum istos spectat ad laicos. Et sicut Deus est Deus clericorum, ita est Deus laicorum.
units.tr: Disciple. This matter was discussed above in the first book, so pass over it and show how the second argument, adduced above in chapter 91, is answered. Master. It is answered that sometimes it belongs to the secular judge to take cognizance of a case of heretical wickedness, and this in two ways. In one way he does so himself, since he too is bound to know many things, and by these he can judge many cases of heretical wickedness even without the counsel of other experts. For if some Christian says that the Christian faith is false and wicked, the secular judge need not ask anyone's advice to know whether such a person is to be condemned as a heretic. He is bound to know that such a person is to be regarded as a heretic and condemned for heresy. Likewise, if someone teaches that Christ was not born of a virgin, or that he did not suffer, or that he did not rise again, or that there is not one God, or that there are not three persons in God, the secular judge is bound to know that such a person is a heretic. Just as the secular judge is bound to believe explicitly many matters pertaining to the orthodox faith, so in many cases he can know by himself what is to be held in a case of heretical wickedness. In another way he can take cognizance of a case of heretical wickedness by seeking the counsel of experts, as often happens with many crimes through the information of others. In these he would not know by himself what is right and what wrong, and could only sort it out through others' information. For when someone is accused before a judge of false coinage, the judge cannot tell by himself whether the coin in question is genuine or counterfeit. So before pronouncing sentence he asks the moneyers, binding them by oath or some other means, to tell him the truth about such coin. In this way, in many cases, the secular judge, who does not have all the arts and natures of things at his command, pronounces sentence on the counsel of others, because in such cases he could not by himself know how he ought to judge. So they say that the secular judge, in many cases concerning heretical wickedness, would need the counsel of those skilled in the sacred writings. If some Christian were accused before a secular judge who was not at all learned in the Bible, of stubbornly asserting that the blessed Paul was converted before Christ's passion, as a certain great canonist said and left in his writings, namely that the blessed Paul was one of the twelve apostles who followed Christ before he suffered, the secular judge would not know by himself how to pass sentence. But with the counsel of experts in the holy Scriptures, on which the aforesaid question depends, he could know how to pass sentence. Where, however, the secular judge could not clearly know, even with his own counsel, what the truth is in some question about the faith, he ought not to intrude in such a case. Applying this to the matter at hand, it is said that if a heretical Pope held that the Christian faith was false, or that there are not three distinct persons in the divine nature, or something of that kind, which the secular judge could clearly recognize as heretical either by himself or through the counsel of experts, then the secular judge could safely judge the heretical Pope, if the clerics were unwilling or unable to restrain him duly. But when it is said that a cause of faith or of God does not pertain to the secular judge, it is answered that to say a cause of faith or of God pertains in no way to the secular judge or to laymen would be utterly insane. It is the word of greedy and proud clerics, who try to exclude laymen from the Church of God, so that with the laymen excluded they might be regarded as the Church of the Lord's laity. For, as has often been alleged, in Holy Scripture laymen are never excluded from the name church. Wherever the name church occurs in the Scriptures, it embraces men, women and laity. Therefore, according to these men, the cause of faith and of God pertains to laymen. And just as God is the God of clerics, so he is the God of laymen.

units.la: Sic causa fidei quae spectat ad clericos, etiam spectat ad laicos. Si etiam causa fidei & Dei nullo modo spectaret ad laicos: laici nec fidem Domini defendere, nec haereticos euitare, nec in persecutione fidei praelatis assistere, nec in aliquo se intromittere de haereticis etiam per ecclesiam condemnatis deberent; quae sunt insana censenda. Causa igitur quae est causa Dei, aliquo modo spectat ad laicos: principalius tamen spectat ad praelatos ecclesiae, quia praelati ecclesiae non solum haereticos laicos coercent, sed etiam clericos possunt debite coercere: de quibus laici iudicare non possunt, nisi clerici noluerint vel non potuerint castigare. Secundario autem causa fidei spectat ad laicos: quia laici etiam clericos, imo Papam haereticum possunt & debent (ne virus suae perfidiae transferant in alios) prohibere, si eum clerici noluerint vel non potuerint coercere.
units.tr: Thus a cause of faith that pertains to clerics also pertains to laymen. If the cause of faith and of God in no way pertained to laymen, laymen would be bound neither to defend the Lord's faith, nor to avoid heretics, nor to assist the prelates in the persecution of the faith, nor to meddle at all with heretics, even those already condemned by the Church. These things are to be deemed insane. So the cause which is the cause of God pertains to laymen in some way. Yet it pertains chiefly to the prelates of the Church, because the prelates of the Church not only restrain lay heretics but can also duly restrain clerics, whom laymen cannot judge unless the clerics are unwilling or unable to correct them. Secondarily, however, the cause of faith pertains to laymen, because laymen can and ought (lest they pass the poison of their perfidy on to others) to forbid even clerics, indeed even a heretical Pope, if the clerics are unwilling or unable to restrain him.

units.la: Discipulus. Dic, quomodo respondetur ad auctoritates supra adductas. Magister. Respondetur, quod cum de causis fidei agitur: & sacerdotes Christi suum officium digne & sollicite exequuntur: Imperatores & reges debent voluntatem suam sacerdotibus Christi, recipiendo eorum informationem & consilia eorum iudicio in his, quae ad ipsos pertinent iudicare, subdere, non praeferre, vbi autem sacerdotes auerterentur a fide, vel in causis Dei essent damnabiliter negligentes: Imperatores & reges voluntatem suam sacerdotibus non subdere, sed praeferre debent. Et sic intelligenda sunt verba Felicis Papae; qui per sua verba honorem Dei intendebat. Et ideo quia esset contra honorem Dei quod reges voluntatem suam subderet sacerdotibus haereticis & negligentibus seu laborantibus ad subuersionem fidei orthodoxae, noluit Felix Papa, quod reges in hoc casu suo subderent sacerdotib. voluntatem. Ad auctoritatem Nicolai Papae dicitur, quod verba eius non possunt nec debent sine omni exceptione intelligi, tunc enim clerici incorrigibiles & haeretici per ecclesiam condemnati, & traditi curiae seculari per iudices seculares nullo modo iudicari deberent, quae tamen constat falsa esse. Verba igitur Nicolai Papae cum exceptionibus suis debent intelligi. Potissima autem exceptio est, quando Papa est haereticus: & clerici nolunt vel non possunt corrigere, igitur cum ista exceptione potissime verba Nicolai debent intelligi. Ad tertiam auctoritatem respondetur, quod Theodosius minor scribens synodo Ephesinae noluit, quod Candidianus Comes de piis degradationibus, quae in eadem synodo tractabantur, se intromittere attentaret, quia eius impia dogmata, de quibus tractabatur, poterant sufficienter terminari per sacerdotes, qui convenerant, cum vero dicit : illicitum est enim eum, qui non est in ordine sanctissimorum episcoporum ecclesiasticis intromisceri tractatibus : respondetur quod haec verba non possunt nec debent intelligi, sicut prima facie sonant, tum quia nunquam magister Theologiae aut alius literatus in decretis & scripturis diuinis, qui non esset episcopus, deberet interesse ecclesiasticis tractatibus: tum quia etiam Imperatores non deberent interesse concilio generali, in quo tractaretur de quaestione fidei; quae salsa sunt & absurda, debent igitur verba praedicta, sicut praecedentia, intelligi. quia illicitum est eum, qui non sit in ordine episcoporum, tanquam sit episcopus, ecclesiasticis intermisceri tractatibus: & quando per episcopos rite & ordinate tractantur; vbi autem episcopi convenirent in subuersionem fidei catholicae, deberet laicus catholicus non solum eis praeesse, sed eos debite coercere; quando per alios clericos coerceri non possunt. Ad quartam auctoritatem respondetur, quod Imperatores non debent indebite vsurpare, quae solis sacerdotibus conueniunt, sed detinere Papam haereticum (quando clerici nollent vel non possent eum corrigere) non conuenit solis sacerdotibus: sed competit laicis orthodoxis, ideo &c. Ad quintam auctoritatem dicitur, quod Imperator catholicus est filius (secundum Iohannem Papam) ecclesiae catholicae non haereticae, & non est praesul ecclesiae catholicae, sed praesul, hoc est superior est & Iudex ecclesiae haereticae: quando clerici nolunt vel non possunt ecclesiam haereticam corrigere. Et ideo quoad religionem competit ei discere a catholicis, non docere, tanquam habens praedicandi officium, quia habet priuilegia potestatis suae, ad quae ministrandum legibus publicis diuinitus constitutus est, nec inquantum solummodo Imperator, sed inquantum Imperator Christianus est: non solum ad administrandum legibus secularib. debet intendere, sed eii incumbit haereticos clericos, etiam Papam haereticum (quando ecclesiae potestas deficit) coercere. Et ideo Imperator circa dispositionem coelestis ordinis nihil vsurparet indebite, quia ad sacerdotes catholicos, non autem haereticos Deus voluit, quae in ecclesia dispensanda sunt pertinere principaliter: non ad seculi potestates principaliter, nec etiam non principaliter quantum ad sacramenta ecclesiae dispensanda. Quantum vero ad clericos ordinatos (qui haeretici facti sunt) corrigendos & recipiendos, si remanserint in errore: de errore non debent se Imperatores intromittere, nisi supplendo malitiam, vel negligentiam, aut impotentiam, vel ignorantiam sacerdotum. Verba igitur haec Iohannis Papae sane debent intelligi, vt in detrimentum fidei orthodoxae nullo modo redundent. Disc. Quomodo possent in detrimentum redundare? Magister. Respondetur, quod verba Iohannis Papae in detrimentum fidei redundarent, si in nullo casu Imperator vel Iudex saecularis posset Papam haereticum coercere, sed si Papa esset haereticus, & omnes clerici vna cum Papa, exceptis duobus vel tribus episcopis, quos Papa haereticus in vinculis detineret, in multitudine populi Christiani periclitaretur fides, nisi laici possent compescere haereticos & catholicos liberare. Discipulus. Dic, quomodo respondetur ad auctoritatem Cypriani. Magister. Respondetur, quod beatus Cyprianus loquitur in casu, in quo Pontifices non sunt haeretici, nec in suo officio negligentes.
units.tr: Disciple. Tell me how the authorities cited above are answered. Master. The answer is that when matters of faith are at issue, and the priests of Christ carry out their office worthily and diligently, emperors and kings ought to make their own will subject to the priests of Christ, accepting their instruction and submitting their counsels to the priests' judgment in those matters which belong to the priests to judge. They should not put their own will above the priests. But where the priests turn away from the faith, or are culpably negligent in the cause of God, emperors and kings ought not to subject their will to the priests but to set it above them. This is how the words of Pope Felix must be understood, for by them he was aiming at the honour of God. And so, because it would be against the honour of God for kings to subject their will to heretical priests, or to priests who are negligent or who labour to overthrow the orthodox faith, Pope Felix did not want kings in such a case to subject their will to the priests. As for the authority of Pope Nicholas, the answer is that his words cannot and must not be understood without any exception. For if they were, heretical clergy who were incorrigible and had been condemned by the Church, and handed over to the secular authority, could in no way be judged by secular judges. Yet that is plainly false. Therefore the words of Pope Nicholas must be understood together with their exceptions. The chief exception is this: when the Pope himself is a heretic, and the clergy are unwilling or unable to correct him. So the words of Nicholas are best understood with this exception in view. As for the third authority, the answer is that the younger Theodosius, writing to the Council of Ephesus, did not want Candidianus the Count to presume to meddle in the pious depositions which were being dealt with at that council, because the impious doctrines under discussion could be sufficiently settled by the priests who had gathered. But when he says, it is unlawful for one who is not in the order of the most holy bishops to meddle in ecclesiastical proceedings, the answer is that these words cannot and must not be understood as they sound at first sight. For one thing, no master of theology or other learned man versed in the decrees and divine Scriptures who was not a bishop would ever be allowed to take part in ecclesiastical proceedings; and for another, emperors would not be allowed to attend a general council at which a question of faith was being treated. Both of these are false and absurd. So the words quoted must be understood in the same way as the words that precede them: it is unlawful for one who is not in the order of bishops to meddle in ecclesiastical proceedings as though he were a bishop, and this applies when such matters are handled properly and in good order by the bishops. But where bishops gathered to overthrow the catholic faith, a catholic layman ought not only to preside over them but also to restrain them duly, when they cannot be restrained by other clergy. As for the fourth authority, the answer is that emperors ought not to usurp unduly what belongs only to priests; but to hold a heretical Pope in check (when the clergy are unwilling or unable to correct him) does not belong only to priests, but is the business of orthodox laymen; therefore, and so on. As for the fifth authority, it is said that the catholic emperor is (according to Pope John) a son of the catholic and not of the heretical Church, and he is not the prelate of the catholic Church, but a prelate, that is, he is superior and judge of the heretical Church, when the clergy are unwilling or unable to correct that heretical Church. Therefore, in matters of religion, it is his business to learn from catholics, not to teach as though he held the office of preaching; for he has the privileges of his power, to the administration of which he is divinely appointed by public laws, and this not merely as emperor but as a Christian emperor. He ought not only to attend to the administration of the secular laws, but it is also incumbent on him to restrain heretical clergy, even a heretical Pope, when the power of the Church fails. Therefore an emperor, concerning the arrangement of the heavenly order, would usurp nothing unduly, since God willed that the things to be dispensed in the Church pertain principally to catholic priests, and not to heretical ones, and not principally to the powers of this world, nor even secondarily as regards the dispensing of the sacraments of the Church. But as regards clergy who have been ordained and have become heretics, to be corrected and received back if they remain in error: emperors ought not to meddle with the error itself, except by supplying the malice, negligence, incapacity or ignorance of the priests. So these words of Pope John must certainly be understood in such a way that they in no way redound to the detriment of the orthodox faith. Disc. How could they redound to its detriment? Master. The answer is that the words of Pope John would redound to the detriment of the faith if in no case could an emperor or secular judge restrain a heretical Pope. But if the Pope were a heretic, and all the clergy along with the Pope, except two or three bishops whom the heretical Pope kept in chains, then the faith would be in peril among the multitude of Christian people, unless laymen could curb the heretics and free the catholics. Disciple. Tell me how the authority of Cyprian is answered. Master. The answer is that the blessed Cyprian is speaking of a case in which the bishops are not heretics, nor negligent in their office.

units.la: Discipulus. Video quod omnes auctoritates de hac materia vno modo exponuntur: quia videlicet intelligendae sunt, quando non deficit potestas ecclesiastica, quando autem deficeret potestas ecclesiastica, non habet locum, ideo dic, quomodo ad rationem tertiam respondetur. Mag. Respondetur, quod omne crimen ecclesiasticum spectat in aliquo casu ad iudicem secularem, aliter non omnis pater filium pro crimine haeresis coercere posset, aliter etiam Iudex laicus clericum condemnatum pro haeresi & curiae traditum seculari iudicare non posset. Disc. Executio sententiae latae contra clericum pro crimine ecclesiastico, puta pro crimine haeresis, spectat ad laicum, sed examinatio causae & sententiae pronunciatio non spectat ad laicum. Vnde illa punitio haereticorum fit auctoritate ecclesiae, & ita eam magis fecit ecclesia, quam iudex secularis. Magister. Videtur nonnullis, quod minime habeas sacrorum canonum intellectum, quia Iudex secularis puniendo clericos ab ecclesia condemnatos & curiae seculari traditos: non est tantum executor sententiae per ecclesiasticum Iudicem latae, tunc enim nullam poenam posset infligere, nisi per ecclesiasticum Iudicem taxatam, quod salsum est. Iudex igitur secularis non est in hoc casu merus executor: & per consequens habet in hoc casu de clerico haeretico iudicare. Ad conuincendum tamen ipsum de haeretica prauitate, sufficit quod conuictus fuerit in alio iudicio, & ideo solum sibi iudicialiter debitam poenam imponit, & ita videtur, quod crimen ecclesiasticum in aliquo casu ad iudicem secularem spectat, quare tunc potissime spectat, cum Papa esset haereticus, & clerici nollent vel non possent coercere eundem. Ad decretum autem (2. quaestion. 1. cap. si quis in hoc) respondetur, quod decretum illud loquitur in casu, quando tota potestas ecclesiastica non deficit. Quando autem tota potestas ecclesiastica deficit, aliter esset tenendum. Discipulus. Hoc videtur contra iura, dicit enim Glossa 11. quaestion. 1. cap. 1. quod propter negligentiam iudicis ecclesiastici clericus non potest conueniri coram laico, licet econuerso propter defectum iudicis secularis, causa secularis coram iudice ecclesiastico sit tractanda. Magister. Respondetur, quod Glossa loquitur in casu, in quo non tota ecclesiastica potestas deficeret, licet enim episcopus negligeret facere iustitiam de clerico, non esset ad secularem iudicem recurrendum, quia ad Papam posset haberi recursus, sed si nullus esset Papa, & nullus clericus esset, qui posset & nollet de clerico publice delinquente iustitiam facere, deberent laici iustitiam adhibere, & sic etiam vbi tantum periculum fidei immineret, esset clericus per laicos detinendus. Ad rationem vero, qua probatur, quod crimen ecclesiasticum ad iudicem secularem non spectat: Respondetur, quod ad decentiam iudicis, qui per seipsum ex consuetudine audit & examinat, & diffinit causas, spectat quod habeat noticiam illarum legum & iurium: secundum quae est in causis huiusmodi iudicandum. Et ideo qui ex consuetudine per seipsum audit, examinat & diffinit in causis criminalibus & ecclesiasticis (& maxime de crimine haeresis) decet vt non solum in notitia canonum; sed etiam in scripturis diuinis sit peritus & exercitatus. Sed non est simpliciter necessarium, quod ille, qui non ex consuetudine per seipsum huiusmodi causas examinat, sed aliis committit, notitiam habeat, praesertim excellentem legum & iurium notitiam: secundum quae oportet iudicem iudicare in huiusmodi, sed sufficit quod habeat peritiam iudicandi. Aliter enim quis non posset eligi in summum Pontificem, nisi esset in scripturis diuinis excellens: cum tamen constet, saepe in sacra pagina simplices fuisse ad Papatum assumptos, constat enim, quod ad summum Pontificem sunt causae fidei deferendae 24. quaestion. 1. quotiens. In causis enim fidei potissime & principalissime oportet secundum sacras literas iudicare, ergo si iudex in talibus causis debet habere noticiam praecellentem iuris, secundum quod posset iudicare, nullus posset eligi in summum Pontificem, nisi esset excellens in sanctarum notitia scripturarum. Item nullus posset eligi in episcopum, nisi haberet notitiam decretorum & decretalium: quia secundum decreta & decretales oportet in causis ecclesiasticis iudicare, videtur ergo dicendum, quod cum aliquis tractat aliquas causas aliis committendo, & de consiliis aliorum, non est necesse quod habeat legum (secundum quas debet iudicare) notitiam excellentem, ergo qui aliquae causae non spectant ad iudicem, nisi in casu speciali, qui raro accidit: non est necesse, quod iudex iuris secundum quod iudicare debet notitiam habeat praecellentem, causae autem fidei in casu speciali, & qui raro accidit spectant ad iudicem seculare: vt sc. iudex secularis per seipsum causam fidei examinet, & in ea diffiniat absq; consilio aliorum in sacra pagina peritorum, hoc enim nunquam debet facere, nisi quando omnes in sacris literis eruditi, quorum posset consilium habere, aperte contra fidem errarent, & ideo non est necesse, quod iudex secularis notitiam habeat praecellentem scripturae diuinae: sed sufficit sibi pro multis casib. (qui tamen raro vel nunquam accidunt) quod aliquale notitiam explicitam fidei habeat orthodoxae, quam habere tenetur, quemadmodum oēs Christiani aliqua credere tenentur explicite, quae debent tam firmiter credere, & si oēs clerici mundi in sacra pagina eruditi contraria affirmarent, docerent, praedicarent, assererēt & tenerent, laici credere non debent, sed eos redarguere, reprobare & acriter reprehendere tenentur explicite, omnes laici Christiani ratione vtentes, quales debent esse iudices, in quibuscunque causis habent sufficientem peritiam iudicandi in talibus causis de clericis quibuscunque. Magister. Mirabile est, quod idiota de clerico, imperitus de perito, illiteratus de litterato in his, quae ad sacras literas spectant, debeat & valeat iudicare; & tamen si ad hoc aliqua exempla possunt adduci, libenter scirem. Magister. Ad hoc probandum exempla plurima allegarentur. Si omnes eruditi in sacra pagina vna cum Papa & cardinalibus omnibus praedicarent, assererent & docerent fidem Christianam esse falsam & malam: & legem Iudaeorum vel Sarracenorum esse seruandam: laici illiterati per notitiam fidei, quam in ecclesia didicerunt, essent iudices eorum idonei, quantum est ex parte scientiae vel peritiae seu notitiae: licet aliqui non essent iudices eorum idonei propter carentiam iurisdictionis & potestatis. Item si omnes clerici mundi asserrerent Christum non fuisse crucifixum, vel non esse venturum ad iudicium, vel animas reproborum non esse in inferno, vel aliquid huiusmodi, quod omnes Christiani ecclesiastici & laici credere tenentur explicite; puri illiterati, quantum est ex parte notitiae essent iudices eorum idonei. Disc p. Tu ponis exempla, quae nunquam acciderunt.
units.tr: Student. I see that all the authorities on this matter are explained in one way: namely, that they are to be understood when ecclesiastical power is not lacking, but when ecclesiastical power would fail, they do not apply. So tell me how the third argument is answered. Master. The answer is that every ecclesiastical crime falls, in some case, under the secular judge. Otherwise not every father could restrain his son for the crime of heresy, and a lay judge could not judge a cleric condemned for heresy and handed over to the secular arm. Student. The execution of a sentence passed against a cleric for an ecclesiastical crime, such as heresy, belongs to the layman, but the examination of the case and the pronouncement of the sentence do not belong to the layman. Therefore that punishment of heretics is carried out by the authority of the Church, and so the Church, rather than the secular judge, has made it. Master. It seems to some that you do not grasp the sense of the sacred canons at all. For a secular judge who punishes clerics condemned by the Church and handed over to the secular court is not merely the executor of a sentence passed by an ecclesiastical judge. In that case he could inflict no penalty except one fixed by the ecclesiastical judge, which is absurd. So the secular judge in this case is not a mere executor, and consequently in this case he has the right to judge a heretical cleric. Yet to convict him of heretical depravity it is enough that he has been convicted in another trial, and so he imposes only the penalty due to him by law. Thus it appears that an ecclesiastical crime does, in some case, fall under the secular judge. This is especially so when the Pope would be a heretic and the clerics were unwilling or unable to restrain him. As for the decree (2. quaestion. 1. cap. si quis in hoc), the answer is that this decree speaks of the case where the whole ecclesiastical power is not lacking. When the whole ecclesiastical power fails, the matter must be held otherwise. Student. This seems contrary to the laws. For the Gloss says (11. quaestion. 1. cap. 1.) that because of the negligence of an ecclesiastical judge a cleric cannot be sued before a layman, although conversely, because of the failure of a secular judge, a secular case may be tried before an ecclesiastical judge. Master. The answer is that the Gloss speaks of a case in which the whole ecclesiastical power is not lacking. For although a bishop might neglect to do justice regarding a cleric, one would not have to resort to the secular judge, since recourse could be had to the Pope. But if there were no Pope, and no cleric who could and would do justice regarding a cleric publicly guilty of wrongdoing, then the laity ought to apply justice. Likewise, where such great danger to the faith threatened, the cleric would be restrained by the laity. As for the argument by which it is proved that an ecclesiastical crime does not belong to the secular judge, the answer is this. It is fitting for a judge, who by custom hears, examines and decides cases himself, that he should know those laws and rights according to which such cases are to be judged. Therefore whoever by custom hears, examines and decides criminal and ecclesiastical cases himself (especially the crime of heresy) should be skilled and practised not only in knowledge of the canons but also in the divine Scriptures. But it is not strictly necessary that one who does not personally examine such cases by custom, but commits them to others, should have knowledge, especially an outstanding knowledge of the laws and rights according to which a judge must judge such matters. It is enough that he has skill in judging. Otherwise no one could be chosen as supreme Pontiff unless he were outstanding in the divine Scriptures. Yet it is well known that simple men have often been raised to the papacy in the sacred page. For it is established that questions of faith are referred to the supreme Pontiff (24. quaestion. 1. quotiens). In matters of faith especially and chiefly, one must judge according to the sacred letters. Therefore, if a judge in such cases ought to have an outstanding knowledge of the law by which he could judge, then no one could be chosen as supreme Pontiff unless he were outstanding in knowledge of the holy Scriptures. Likewise no one could be chosen bishop unless he had knowledge of the decrees and decretals, since in ecclesiastical cases one must judge according to the decrees and decretals. It seems, then, that we must say that when someone handles cases by committing them to others and taking the advice of others, he is not obliged to have outstanding knowledge of the laws according to which he must judge. Therefore, since some cases belong to the judge only in a special case, which rarely occurs, it is not necessary that a judge have outstanding knowledge of the law according to which he must judge. Cases of faith, however, in a special case which rarely occurs, belong to the secular judge, so that the secular judge himself examines a matter of faith and decides it without the counsel of others skilled in the sacred page. For he should never do this unless all those learned in the sacred letters, whose counsel he could have, were openly erring against the faith. Therefore it is not necessary that the secular judge have outstanding knowledge of the divine Scripture. It is enough for him, in many cases (which nonetheless rarely or never occur), that he have some explicit knowledge of the orthodox faith, which he is bound to have, just as all Christians are bound to believe some things explicitly. They must believe these as firmly as they can. Even if all the clerics of the world, learned in the sacred page, were to affirm, teach, preach, assert and hold the contrary, the laity ought not to believe them. Rather, they are bound explicitly to refute, reprove and sharply rebuke them. All Christian laymen who use reason, such as judges ought to be, have sufficient skill to judge in such cases concerning any clerics whatever. Master. It is remarkable that a layman should be able, and have the right, to judge a cleric; an unskilled man a skilled one; an unlettered man a lettered one in those matters which pertain to the sacred letters. Yet if examples can be brought forward for this, I would gladly know them. Master. Many examples could be cited to prove this. Suppose all those learned in the sacred page, together with the Pope and all the cardinals, were to preach, assert and teach that the Christian faith is false and evil, and that the law of the Jews or the Saracens is to be kept. Then unlettered laymen, through the knowledge of the faith which they learned in the Church, would be suitable judges of them, so far as knowledge, skill or understanding is concerned, although some would not be suitable judges of them because they lack jurisdiction and power. Likewise, if all the clerics of the world were to assert that Christ was not crucified, or that he will not come to judgment, or that the souls of the reprobate are not in hell, or something of this kind, which all Christians, clerical and lay, are bound to believe explicitly, then mere unlettered people would be suitable judges of them, so far as knowledge is concerned. Student. You put forward examples which never happened.

units.la: Magister. Respondetur, quod propter duo talia ponuntur exempla, primo, quia talia licet nunquam acciderunt, tamen possunt accidere, secundo, quia per exempla tam aperte manuducitur intellectus ad discernendum, quod in aliis est tenendum.
units.tr: Master. The answer is that two such examples are given for two reasons. First, although such things have never happened, they could happen. Second, because through examples the understanding is led so clearly to discern what must be held in other cases.

units.la: Disc. Puto me intelligere responsionem datam ad rationem illam, ideo dic quomodo respondetur ad rationem quartam. Mag. Respondetur, quod maiores causae sunt ad maius iudicium deferendae, qui iustitia & veritas in maiori iudicio poterit inueniri, & iudicium maius non deficit. Quando autem non inueniretur maius iudicium, tunc maiores causae essent ad iudicium inferius deferendae. Et ideo si Papa & omnes clerici (ad quos posset haberi recursus) contra fidem errarent, aperte docentes vel tenentes aliquid contra aliquam veritatem, quam eodem modo omnes clerici tenentur credere explicite: huiusmodi causa non ad Papam haereticum, sed ad laicos catholicos esset omnino deferenda.
units.tr: Student. I think I understand the answer given to that argument. So tell me how the fourth argument is answered. Master. The answer is that greater cases are to be referred to a greater judgment, since justice and truth can be found in a greater judgment, and a greater judgment does not fail. But if no greater judgment could be found, then the greater cases would have to be referred to a lower judgment. Therefore, if the Pope and all the clerics (to whom recourse could be had) were to err against the faith, openly teaching or holding something against some truth which all clerics are equally bound to believe explicitly, such a case must be referred entirely not to the heretical Pope but to the Catholic laity.

units.la: Cum vero accipitur, quod causa haeresis est inter causas maximas computanda: Respondetur, quod causa haeresis sicut causa fidei duplex est, quandoq; n. vocatur causa haeresis, quando quaestio agitatur de aliquo, quod manifestum est esse haeresim, quia est haeresis explicite condemnata, & haec causa haeresis vel causa fidei inter causas maximas minime computatur, quia haec causa ad episcopos spectat, & inquisitores haereticae pravitatis, & ideo haec causa in casu speciali potest competere laicis super Papam haereticum: quem clerici nolunt, vel non possunt coercere. Alia est causa haeresis siue fidei, quando quaestio de aliquo efficitur, quod non est certum esse haeresim: quia non est haeresis explicite condemnata: nec eius contrarium est veritas catholica explicite approbata, & talis causa haeresis vel fidei inter causas maximas computatur, nec diffinitio seu determinatio talis causae, vnquam spectat ad laicos illiteratos, sed solummodo spectat ad ecclesiam vniuersalem & concilium generale. netale, vel Romanum Pontificem, & ita talis causa nunquam deferenda est ad iudicium m seculare, & ideo quantum ad talem causam, iudicium ecclesiasticum maius est iudicio seculari, sicut scribit Gregorius Nazianzenus. Si tamen iudicium ecclesiasticum propter infidelitatem clericorum deficeret, talis causa tunc minime est tractanda.
units.tr: When it is objected that the cause of heresy must be counted among the greatest causes, the answer is that the cause of heresy, like the cause of faith, is twofold. For it is called a cause of heresy when the question concerns something that is manifestly heresy, because it has been explicitly condemned as heresy; and this kind of cause of heresy or faith is by no means counted among the greatest causes, because such a cause belongs to the bishops and the inquisitors of heretical depravity, and so in a special case it can fall to laymen against a heretical Pope, whom the clergy are unwilling or unable to restrain. The other kind of cause of heresy or faith is when the question concerns something which is not certainly heresy, because it has not been explicitly condemned as heresy, nor has its contrary been explicitly approved as Catholic truth. Such a cause of heresy or faith is counted among the greatest causes, and the definition or determination of such a cause never belongs to unlettered laymen, but only to the universal Church and a general council, or to the Roman Pontiff. Therefore such a cause must never be referred to the secular judgment, and so, as far as such a cause is concerned, ecclesiastical judgment is greater than secular judgment, as Gregory Nazianzen writes. If, however, ecclesiastical judgment should fail on account of the unbelief of the clergy, such a cause is then in no way to be handled.

units.la: Ad quintam rationem respondetur, quod licet potestas iudiciaria sacerdotalis & secularis sint potestates distinctae, non tamen taliter sunt distinctae, quod nunquam una habeat iudicare de alia, & quod nulla causa, quae spectat ad unam potestatem in nullo casu spectat ad aliam potestatem, quia hoc est expresse contra canonicas sanctiones, quibus asseritur manifeste, quod potestas ecclesiastica nonnunquam habet de potestate seculari iudicare, nonnunquam habet iudicare de causis spectantibus ad iudicem secularem, ergo per distinctionem istarum potestatum non potest probari, quod in nullo casu spectat ad iudicem secularem de Papa haeretico iudicare.
units.tr: To the fifth objection the answer is that although the judicial power of the priesthood and that of the secular power are distinct powers, they are not so distinct that one can never judge the other, or that no cause which belongs to one power belongs in any case to the other power. For this is expressly contrary to the canonical sanctions, which plainly affirm that ecclesiastical power sometimes has the right to judge concerning secular power, and sometimes has the right to judge causes which pertain to the secular judge. Therefore it cannot be proved from the distinction of these powers that in no case does it belong to the secular judge to judge a heretical Pope.

units.la: Ad sextam rationem respondetur, quod sicut ad Imperatores, qui erant pagani, spectabat non in quantum erant pagani, sed in quantum erant homines, Deum colere & idola relinquere: ita ad Imperatores & reges, qui erant pagani, non inquantum erant pagani, sed inquantum erant Imperatores & reges, pertinebat catholicos defendere, propter quod ad Imperatores & reges Christianos, qui succedunt Imperatoribus & regibus paganis, non in paganismo, sed in Imperiali & regali dignitate, spectat etiam Papam haereticum, quem clerici nolunt vel non possunt, corrigere vel coercere.
units.tr: To the sixth objection the answer is that just as the emperors, who were pagans, were bound to worship God and abandon idols not in so far as they were pagans but in so far as they were men, so it pertained to the emperors and kings who were pagans, not in so far as they were pagans but in so far as they were emperors and kings, to defend Catholics. On account of this, the Christian emperors and kings who succeed the pagan emperors and kings, not in their paganism but in their imperial and royal dignity, also have the duty to correct or restrain a heretical Pope, whom the clergy are unwilling or unable to correct or restrain.

units.la: Ad rationem septimam respondetur, quod in eadem causa contigit uti legibus diversis, & in causa consimili unus iudex tenetur uti aliquibus legibus, quibus alius uti non tenetur. In eadem ergo causa seculari aliis legibus utitur iudex in Italia, & aliis legibus iudex in Francia, & ideo licet Papa vel iudices ecclesiastici non teneantur uti legibus imperialibus, seu secularibus in causa haeresis: tamen iudices seculares in huiusmodi causa, quando spectat ad eos, uti possunt & legibus divinis & ecclesiasticis & etiam secularibus, quae non sunt contrariae divinae legi vel ecclesiasticis, ad quas omnes catholici astringuntur.
units.tr: To the seventh objection the answer is that in the same cause it happens that different laws are used, and in a similar cause one judge is bound to use certain laws which another is not bound to use. In the same secular cause, therefore, a judge in Italy uses one set of laws and a judge in France another. And so, although the Pope or ecclesiastical judges are not bound to use imperial or secular laws in a cause of heresy, nevertheless secular judges in such a cause, when it belongs to them, may use both divine and ecclesiastical laws, and also secular laws which are not contrary to divine or ecclesiastical law, to which all Catholics are bound.

units.la: Ad octavam rationem respondentur eadem, quae dicta sunt in responsione ad rationem quintam, quod una causa fidei, quae est de aliquo, quod nec est explicite condemnatum nec explicite approbatum, nunquam pertinet ad distinctionem iudicis secularis.
units.tr: To the eighth objection the same answer is given as was given to the fifth objection: a cause of faith which concerns something neither explicitly condemned nor explicitly approved never falls within the competence of the secular judge.

units.la: Explicit liber sextus.
units.tr: Here ends the sixth book.

units.la: INCIPIT LIBER SEPTIMVS, IN QVO TRACTATVR DE CRE- DENTIBUS, FAUTORIBUS, DEFENSORIBUS & RECEPTATORIBUS HAERETICORUM.
units.tr: BOOK SEVEN, IN WHICH IS TREATED OF THE BELIEVERS, FAVOURERS, DEFENDERS AND RECEIVERS OF HEretics.

units.la: CAP. I.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: Vbi ponitur differentia credentium haereticis: & assignatur duplex, quarum quaeli- bet sub se plures continet, per quas etiam aperitur, qui vere sint credentes haereticis censendi.
units.tr: Where the difference between believers and heretics is laid down, a twofold difference is assigned, each part of which contains several kinds beneath it, and through these it is also made clear who are truly to be counted as believers in heretics.

units.la: DIscipulus: Hactenus de punitione (& praecipue Papae, si efficeretur haereticus) quamplurima quaesiui, licet multa omiserim, post hoc opus sollicite mentem tuam inquiram, nunc vero de credentibus, fautoribus, defensoribus & receptatoribus haereticorum inuestigare propono, & primo de credentibus, de quibus ante omnia disseras, qui sunt censendi credentes. Magister. Nonnullis apparet, quod credentes possunt in duplici differentia reperiri, quidam enim explicite haereticorum credunt erroribus, quemadmodum Arriani credebant explicite, quod filius Dei non est verus Deus, sicut error Arriani haeretici, & de his videtur loqui Gregorius (ut habetur extra de haereticis, excommunicamus) cum sic ait: Credentes autem eorum erroribus haereticos similiter iudicamus. Alii vero videntur esse credentes; qui licet non credant explicite haereticorum erroribus, credunt tamen haereticis, censentes eos inter catholicos reputandos, & eorum doctrinam catholicam reputant: sed in quo explicite discrepent a doctrina catholica ignorant, & isto modo videtur mihi, quod illi qui ad haereticos causa addisceendi accedunt, quia secundum leges minus puniuntur quam Doctores, inter credentes debeant numerari. Disc. Distinctionem de credentibus, siue vera sit, siue falsa intelligo, & ideo de utroque membro te interrogare intendo, dic ergo inprimis de primis credentibus: an omnes sint inter haereticos computandi: cum hoc auctoritas superius allegata videatur asserere, cum indistincte non distinguendo inter hos haereticos credentes & illos dicat, credentes autem eorum (scil. haereticorum) erroribus haereticos similiter iudicamus. Magister. Est quaedam assertio, quod non debet dici indistincte, quod omnes credentes explicite haereticorum erroribus sunt censendi haeretici, sed illi tantum, qui scienter & explicite credunt haereticorum erroribus. Unde eis distinguendum apparet: Credentium enim haereticorum erroribus, quidam sciunt ipsos errores ab ecclesia condemnatos: quidam vero nesciunt, quod sunt ab ecclesia condemnati, & istorum quidam adhaerent pertinaciter talibus erroribus: quidam vero non adhaerent pertinaciter, sed corrigi sunt parati, primi credentes tes haereticorum erroribus (absque alia examinatione) sunt inter haereticos computandi. Cuius ratio assignatur: quia errans contra fidem, qui non est paratus corrigi, est inter haereticos computandus 24. quaestio. 3. dixit Apostolus, sed credens haereticorum erroribus, quos scit ab ecclesia condemnatos, non est paratus corrigi, quia quilibet errans contra fidem debet esse paratus corrigi per doctrinam ecclesiae: aliter est pertinax reputandus, sed qui scit errorem aliquem ab ecclesia condemnatum: & tamen credit eidem errori, non est paratus corrigi per doctrinam ecclesiae, ergo talis est pertinax reputandus. Discipulus. Secundum ista quicunque crederet errori damnato contra fidem a Papa Romano, esset haereticus reputandus, & ita per consequens nullo modo licet sententiae summi Pontificis contraire. Magister. Respondetur, quod sententiae catholicae a Romano Pontifice latae contra errorem infidelium nulli licet absque haeretica pravitate resistere, sed sententiae erroneae Papae contra fidem debet quilibet catholicus (qui scit sententiam eius esse erroneam) obviare. Discipul. Si licet sententiae Romani Pontificis obviare, & Romanos Pontifices non semper sequi, schisma sequetur inter Christianos, quod est omnino vitandum, ergo quilibet tenetur (saltem propter schisma vitandum) acquiescere sententiae Papae. Magister. Respondetur, quod si sententia Papae fuerit erronea contra fidem, schisma sequetur tale, quale semper fuit inter haereticos & catholicos, quale schisma catholici compescendo haereticos sedare debent, si possunt; si autem non possunt, propter nullum schisma vitandum debent acquiescere sententiae falsae; licet in casu, quo viderent periculosam oriri turbationem absque utilitate fidelium cessare deberet (saltem ad tempus) a divulgatione catholicae veritatis. Discipulus. Si non est credendum Papae in his quae fidei sunt, cui credetur? Magister. Respondetur, quod credetur scripturae divinae, & doctrinae quam universalis ecclesia hactenus tenuit, praedicavit & docuit, scriptura enim divina & doctrina praecedentium patrum ab universali ecclesia approbata, doctrinae Papae posterioris est anteponenda, quod in decretis (distinct. 19. c. secundum ecclesiam) insinuari videtur expresse, ubi sic legitur he autem (scil. decretales epistolae) sunt pari auctoritatis cum canonibus, & per consequens quod est eis adhibenda fides. Hoc autem intelligendum est de illis sanctionibus vel decretalibus epistolis, in quibus nec praecedentium patrum decretis vel euangelicis praeceptis aliquid contrarium invenitur. Anastasius enim secundus favore Anastasii Imperatoris Achatius post sententiam in se prolatam sacerdotes & Levitas ordinavit: acceptis officiis rite fungi debere decreuit, de cuius constitutione eadem distinct. §. quia ergo, subiungitur: quia ergo illicite & non canonice, sed contra Dei decreta praedecessorum & successorum suorum haec rescripta dedit, ut probat Felix & Gelasius, qui Achacium ante excommunicaverunt, & Ormisda qui ab ipso Anastasio tertius eundem Anastasium postea damnavit, ideo ab ecclesia Romana repudiatur, & a Deo percussus fuisse legitur. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod si Papa constitutionem condiderit in his, quae ad doctrinam fidei spectant, doctrinae praecedentium patrum contrariam, non est sibi credendum: sed talis eius constitutio est a fidelibus reprobanda: suntq; credentes & scientes doctrinam suam dogmatibus orthodoxorum praecedentium patrum esse contrariam inter haereticos computandi, quemadmodum ipse Papa, si aliquid tale diffinitive tenet, est haereticorum numero aggregandus. Discipulus. Quid si aliqui scientes talem diffinitionem Papae esse obviantem diffinitioni ecclesiae: & tamen credentes in corde determinationem ecclesiae esse veram, exterius ore vel timore, vel ambitione, vel aliqua alia causa tenent aut docent diffinitionem Papae determinationi ecclesiae contrariam. Magister. Respondetur, quod licet tales apud Deum sint deteriores haereticis, eo quod negant agnitam veritatem (& ideo peccant in Spiritum sanctum) tamen apud Deum non sunt haeretici: quia mentaliter contra fidem minime errant, hoc tamen non obstante, si coram ecclesia probatum fuerit, quod ipsi non ignorant determinationem ecclesiae, & tamen tenent diffinitionem Papae contrariam ecclesiae (quae de manifestis iudicat, non de occultis) debet eos haereticos reputare, & tanquam haereticos condemnare, etiam si post assereret, se hanc diffinitionem Papae contrariam determinationi ecclesiae nunquam corde tenuisse, quia tali assertioni eorum de occultis cordium fidem tenetur minime adhibere.
units.tr: Student: Hitherto I have asked very many things about punishment, especially about the Pope, should he become a heretic. Although I have passed over much, I will now carefully examine your mind after this work. Now, however, I propose to investigate believers, favourers, defenders and receivers of heretics. And first, about believers, you should discuss before all else who are to be regarded as believers. Master. Some think that believers can be found in a twofold distinction. For some believe explicitly the errors of heretics, just as the Arians explicitly believed that the Son of God is not true God, which is the error of the heretic Arius. Gregory seems to speak of these (as is found in Extra, de haereticis, Excommunicamus) when he says: Those who believe their errors we likewise judge to be heretics. Others, however, seem to be believers who, although they do not explicitly believe the errors of heretics, nevertheless believe the heretics, judging them to be reckoned among Catholics and regarding their teaching as Catholic. But they do not know where it explicitly differs from Catholic doctrine. In this way it seems to me that those who go to heretics for the sake of learning, since by the laws they are punished less than teachers, ought to be numbered among believers. Student. I understand the distinction concerning believers, whether it is true or false, and so I intend to question you about both parts. Tell me first about the first kind of believers: whether all of them are to be counted among heretics, since the authority cited above seems to assert this, when, without distinguishing between these heretical believers and those others, it says: Those who believe their errors (namely of the heretics) we likewise judge to be heretics. Master. There is a view that it should not be said without distinction that all who explicitly believe the errors of heretics are to be regarded as heretics, but only those who knowingly and explicitly believe the errors of heretics. Hence a distinction seems necessary. For among those who believe the errors of heretics, some know that these errors have been condemned by the Church; others do not know that they have been condemned by the Church. Of these, some cling stubbornly to such errors; others do not cling stubbornly but are ready to be corrected. The first kind, who believe the errors of heretics, are to be counted among heretics without any further examination. The reason is assigned: because one who errs against the faith and is not ready to be corrected is to be counted among heretics (24. quaestio 3, dixit Apostolus). But one who believes the errors of heretics, which he knows have been condemned by the Church, is not ready to be corrected, since anyone who errs against the faith ought to be ready to be corrected by the teaching of the Church; otherwise he must be reckoned obstinate. But one who knows that some error has been condemned by the Church, and yet believes that same error, is not ready to be corrected by the teaching of the Church. Therefore such a person must be reckoned obstinate. Student. According to this, whoever believed an error condemned by the Roman Pontiff as contrary to the faith would be reckoned a heretic, and so in no way would it be lawful to oppose the sentence of the supreme Pontiff. Master. The answer is that no one may lawfully resist, without heretical wickedness, the Catholic sentences passed by the Roman Pontiff against the error of unbelievers; but any Catholic who knows that the Pope's sentence against the faith is erroneous ought to oppose it. Student. If it is lawful to oppose the sentence of the Roman Pontiff, and not always to follow the Roman Pontiffs, schism will follow among Christians, which must be entirely avoided. Therefore everyone is bound (at least to avoid schism) to acquiesce in the Pope's sentence. Master. The answer is that if the Pope's sentence is erroneous against the faith, such schism will follow as has always existed between heretics and Catholics. Catholics ought to quell such schism by restraining the heretics, if they can. If they cannot, then for the sake of avoiding no schism they ought to acquiesce in a false sentence; although, in the case where they saw that a dangerous disturbance would arise without any benefit to the faithful, they ought to cease (at least for a time) from publishing Catholic truth. Student. If the Pope is not to be believed in matters of faith, whom shall we believe? Master. The answer is that we shall believe Divine Scripture and the doctrine which the universal Church has hitherto held, preached and taught. For Divine Scripture and the doctrine of the earlier Fathers, approved by the universal Church, are to be preferred to the doctrine of a later Pope. This seems to be expressly hinted at in the Decretum (Distinctio 19, c. Secundum ecclesiam), where it is read thus: These (namely the decretal letters) are of equal authority with the canons, and consequently that faith is to be given to them. This, however, must be understood of those sanctions or decretal letters in which nothing contrary to the decrees of the earlier Fathers or to the evangelical precepts is found. For Anastasius II, out of favour to the Emperor Anastasius, ordained priests and Levites for Acacius after the sentence pronounced against him, and decreed that they should lawfully perform the offices they had received. Concerning this constitution the same distinction continues in the paragraph Quia ergo: Because he gave these rescripts unlawfully and not canonically, but against the decrees of God and of his predecessors and successors, as Felix and Gelasius prove, who excommunicated Acacius before, and Hormisdas, who, third from Anastasius himself, afterwards condemned that same Anastasius, therefore he is repudiated by the Roman Church, and it is read that he was struck down by God. From these words it is understood that if a Pope should issue a constitution in matters that pertain to the doctrine of faith, contrary to the doctrine of the earlier Fathers, he is not to be believed. Rather, such a constitution is to be rejected by the faithful. Those who believe, and know that his doctrine is contrary to the dogmas of the orthodox earlier Fathers, are to be counted among heretics, just as the Pope himself, if he holds anything of this kind definitively, is to be numbered with heretics. Student. What if some, knowing that such a definition of the Pope opposes the definition of the Church, yet in their heart believing the decision of the Church to be true, outwardly hold or teach, through fear or ambition or some other cause, a definition of the Pope contrary to the decision of the Church? Master. The answer is that although such persons are worse than heretics before God, because they deny a truth they have acknowledged (and therefore sin against the Holy Spirit), nevertheless before God they are not heretics, because mentally they do not err at all against the faith. Yet notwithstanding this, if it is proved before the Church that they are not ignorant of the decision of the Church and yet hold the Pope's definition contrary to the Church's (which judges of manifest things, not of hidden ones), the Church must regard them as heretics and condemn them as heretics, even if afterwards they assert that they never held this definition of the Pope contrary to the decision of the Church in their heart. For their assertion about the hidden things of the heart is by no means to be given credence.

units.la: CAP. II.
units.tr: CHAP. II.

units.la: Ubi inquiritur de propositione ambigua habente duos sensus, unum sc. catholicum, alterum vero haereticum, quam Papa sub sensu haeretico diffinis tenendam, utrum talis diffinitio assertioni credens sit haereticus censendus, & respondetur secundum duplicem opinionem.
units.tr: Where it is asked about an ambiguous proposition with two senses, one Catholic and the other heretical, which the Pope defines to be held in the heretical sense: whether one who believes such a definition is to be judged a heretic; and the answer is given according to two opinions.

units.la: Discip. Quid si determinatio Papae est ambigua habens diversos sensus: quorum unus est haereticalis de intentione Papae, quem in aliis scriptis posterioribus vel prioribus explicat manifeste: alius autem sensus talis determinationis seu diffinitionis Papae est catholicus: nunquid credens tali determinationi Papae putans suum sensum catholicum, esse de intentione Papae, est haereticus reputandus, si scit alium sensum ab ecclesia esse condemnatum? Magister. Una assertio tenet, quod talis est haereticus reputandus, quod tali ratione videtur posse probari. Sicut nihil differt in vitio dicere bonum malum, & malum dicere bonum, ita non videtur distare in vitio dicere scripturam catholicam esse haereticam, & dicere scripturam haereticam esse catholicam, quod Esaias propheta ca. 5. videtur testari, cum hoc facientibus imprecatur væ damnationis æternæ, dicens: Væ, qui dicitis malum bonum, & bonum malum, ponentes tenebras lucem, & lucem tenebras, amarum dulce, & dulce amarum. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod quemadmodum utrque damnabili crimine irretitur, scil. qui dicit malum esse bonum, & qui dicit bonum esse malum: ita utrque damnabilis est, scil. & qui ponit tenebras, hoc est prauitatem haereticam esse lucem, id est catholicā veritatem: & qui dicit lucem, id est catholicam veritatem, esse tenebras, id est haereticā prauitatem, sed qui dicit scripturam catholicam esse haereticam, trahendo eam videlicet ad sensum haereticum, & aliter exponendo, quam sensus Spiritus sancti effiagitat: est haereticus censendus, 24. qu. 3. haeresis, igitur ille, qui scripturam haereticam trahit ad sensum catholicum eius errorem exponendo, haereticus est censendus, & ita qui determinationem Papæ secundum mentem eius haereticam reputat catholicam, sciens, quod ille sensus, qui secundum rei veritatem est de mente Papæ, est damnatus, debet haereticus iudicari: licet nesciat, quod ille sit sensus Papæ haeretici. Alia assertio, quæ tenet, quod talis sic exponens determinationem Papæ haereticam, & trahit eam ad sensum catholicum, quem putat esse de mente Papæ, non est haereticus iudicandus, videtur tali ratione posse probari. Ille qui non errat contra fidem, non est haereticus iudicandus, licet erret contra intentionem alicuius haeretici vel catholici, sed qui determinationem Papæ habentem diversos sensus, unum catholicum & alium haereticum, trahit ad sensum catholicum, putans eum esse de mente Papæ, quamvis non sit, non errat contra fidem, sed tantum contra mentem Papæ: quia tenet quicquid spectat ad fidem, in hoc tamen errat, quod putat sensum catholicum esse de mente Papæ: qui tamen non est, ergo talis non est haereticus reputandus. Discipul. Quæ prædictarum assertionum sit verior, post consummationem istius operis sollicite indagabo, nunc autem dicam pectet mortaliter ille, qui trahit determinationem Papæ, secundum mentem Papæ haereticam ad sensum catholicum: quem tamen non credit esse de intentione Papæ: sed credit quod haereticus sensus est de mente Papæ. Magister. Respondetur, quod talis qui non tantummodo recitando, sed exterius affirmando trahit determinationem haereticam ad sensum catholicum, quem non credit esse de mente taliter determinantis, peccat mortaliter, quia committit crimen mendacii, sive adulando, sive timore, sive ambitione taliter mentiatur: nec potest a peccato mortali quomodolibet excusari, quia omne tale mendacium est peccatum mortale, & si ex desiderio complacendi Papæ haeretico mendacium tale procedat, grauius est, quam si ex timore solummodo emanaret, quare in pusillanimo timore aliquo modo diminuit peccatum, in illo autem, qui homini placere desiderat, per crimen mendacii, crimen adulationis aut cupiditatis, aut ambitionis adiungitur, & ideo talis grauius & multiplicius peccat.
units.tr: Disciple. What if the Pope's determination is ambiguous and has several senses: one of them heretical in the Pope's intention, which he plainly explains in other writings, earlier or later, and another sense of that determination or definition which is Catholic? Is one who believes that determination of the Pope, thinking his Catholic sense to be the Pope's intention, to be counted a heretic, if he knows that the other sense has been condemned by the Church? Master. One opinion holds that such a person is to be counted a heretic, and this seems to be provable by the following reasoning. Just as there is no difference in wickedness between calling good evil and calling evil good, so there seems to be no difference in wickedness between calling Catholic Scripture heretical and calling heretical Scripture Catholic. The prophet Isaiah seems to bear witness to this in chapter 5, when he pronounces a woe of eternal damnation on those who do it, saying: Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter. From these words it is gathered that, just as both are caught in a damnable crime, namely the one who says evil is good and the one who says good is evil, so both are damnable: namely the one who puts darkness, that is, heretical depravity, for light, that is, Catholic truth; and the one who calls light, that is, Catholic truth, darkness, that is, heretical depravity. But one who calls Catholic Scripture heretical, by dragging it, that is, to a heretical sense and expounding it otherwise than the sense of the Holy Spirit requires, is to be counted a heretic (24. qu. 3. haeresis). Therefore he who, by expounding his error, drags the heretical Pope's determination to a Catholic sense, is to be counted a heretic; and so one who regards the Pope's determination, according to its heretical meaning, as Catholic, knowing that the sense which in the truth of the matter is the Pope's meaning has been condemned, ought to be judged a heretic, even if he does not know that this is the sense of the heretical Pope. Another opinion, which holds that one who thus expounds the Pope's heretical determination and drags it to a Catholic sense, which he thinks is the Pope's meaning, is not to be judged a heretic, seems to be provable by the following reasoning. One who does not err against the faith is not to be judged a heretic, even if he errs against the intention of some heretic or Catholic. But one who drags the Pope's determination, which has several senses, one Catholic and another heretical, to the Catholic sense, thinking it to be the Pope's meaning, although it is not, does not err against the faith but only against the Pope's meaning. For he holds whatever pertains to the faith; in this alone he errs, that he thinks the Catholic sense to be the Pope's meaning, which it is not. Therefore such a person is not to be counted a heretic. Disciple. I will diligently inquire, after the completion of this work, which of these opinions is the truer. For now, tell me: does one who, in the Pope's determination, drags the heretical sense of the Pope to a Catholic sense, which he does not believe to be the Pope's intention, but believes the heretical sense to be the Pope's meaning, sin mortally? Master. The answer is that such a person, who not merely in reciting but in openly affirming drags a heretical determination to a Catholic sense, which he does not believe to be the meaning of the one who so determined, sins mortally, because he commits the crime of lying, whether he so lies out of flattery, fear, or ambition. Nor can he in any way be excused from mortal sin, because every such lie is a mortal sin; and if such a lie proceeds from a desire to please the heretical Pope, it is graver than if it came only from fear. For in timid fear the sin is somewhat lessened, but in one who desires to please a man, the crime of flattery, or of greed or ambition, is added to the crime of lying; and therefore such a person sins more gravely and in more ways.

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CAP. III.

units.la: In quo agitur de eis, qui assertionem in omni sensu haereticam traherent ad sensum catholicum, scientes tamen quod in rei veritate talis assertio in omni sensu, quem posset habere, est haeretica & respondetur secundum duplicem opinionem.
units.tr: In which those are discussed who would bend an assertion that is heretical in every sense towards a Catholic sense, while knowing that in the truth of the matter such an assertion, in whatever sense it might bear, is heretical; and the answer is given according to a twofold opinion.

units.la: Discipulus. Post interrogationem de trahentibus diffinitionem Papæ haereticam, habentem diversos sensus, unum haereticum, & alium catholicum, ad sensum catholicum: peto ut dicas, quid sentiendum esset de illis, qui diffinitionem Papæ haereticam in omni sensu, quem talis diffinitio posset habere, de virtute verborum traherent ad aliquem sensum catholicum, scientes quod quilibet illorum sensuum, qui secundum rei veritatem possunt elici ex verbis determinationis Papæ, est haereticus. Magister. Respondetur, quod est quaedam assertio dicens, quod tales essent credentes errori Papæ haeretici, & etiam haeretici reputandi, nisi sollicite quaererent veritatem, & parati essent corrigi, quam cito veritatem inuenirent. Quod enim tales credentes haereticorum errori debeant haeretici reputari, videtur sic posse probari. Ille, qui credit haereticorum errori, qui nullum potest habere sensum catholicum, est inter credentes haereticorum errorem merito computandus, sed ille, qui pertinaciter defendit haereticorum errorem, qui nullum potest habere sensum catholicum, est haereticus reputandus, 24. quaestion. 3. qui aliorum. Cum ergo per positum tales credant errori, qui nullum potest habere sensum catholicum, inter credentes sunt merito computandi. Et per illud patet, quod tales nisi sollicite quaerant veritatem parati corrigi, cum inuenerint, sunt haeretici iudicandi, quoniam errans contra fidem, nisi quaerat veritatem paratus corrigi cum inuenerit, est inter haereticos numerandus, 24. quaestion. 3. dicit Apostolus. Ex quo infertur, quod qui exponerent & traherent determinationem Papæ haereticam in omni sensu, quem potest habere de virtute verborum ad sensum catholicum, si simul cum hoc non persequerentur & molestarent qualitercunque diffinitionem Papæ haereticam impugnantes, essent inter haereticos reputandi: quia non quaererent cauta sollicitudine veritatem. Alia est assertio, quæ de trahentibus taliter diffinitionem Papæ haereticam ad sensum catholicum dicit esse distinguendum, quia aut tales sunt periti in arte distinguendi assertiones ambiguas diversos sensus habentes: aut in tali arte sunt minime eruditi. Primi excusari non possunt de crimine mendacii, nec de crimine haereticæ prauitatis: sed sunt censendi sibiipsis contrarii, quemadmodum haeretici saepe reperiuntur sibiipsis contrarii, quia secundum Augustinum 24. quaestion. sept. cap. quod autem: Haretici adeo calumniandi cupiditate cecantur, ut non attendant, quod sint inter se contraria, quae loquuntur, & ideo cum tales sint periti in arte distinguendi assertiones ambiguas, praesumptio est violenta, quod tenens assertionem Papae haereticam sub aliquo sensu, quem sonat: & quod simul cum hoc tanquam contrarii sibiipsis tenent catholicam veritatem. Si autem tales non sunt periti in arte distinguendi assertiones ambiguas, non sunt statim haeretici iudicandi, sed si pertinaciter defenderent talem assertionem esse sub tali sensu sustinendam, deberent haeretici iudicari. Discipulus. Quomodo convincetur talis de pertinacia? Magister. Respondetur, quod de pertinacia convincetur, si postquam ostensum sibi fuerit evidenter, quod assertio Papae haeretici talem sensum habere non potest, adhuc in sua opinione permanserit. Dicitur etiam, quod multis aliis modis potest convinci de pertinacia, puta si de veritate (quando convenienter potest) renuit informari: si impugnatores haereticae pravitatis persequitur vel molestat: si alios minis, praeceptis, poenis, vel alio quovis modo compellit ad suam opinionem pertinaciter defendendam, & forte aliquibus aliis modis, de quibus dictum est supra libro quarto, est de pertinacia convincendus. Discipulus. Quid si aliquis promittit vel iurat, quod tenebit semper talem assertionem haereticam, & intendit tenere sub sensu catholico: quem tamen sensum catholicum de virtute verborum habere non potest. Magister. Respondetur, quod talis est haereticus iudicandus: quia ex quo tenet assertionem haereticam in omni sensu, quem de virtute verborum habere potest, & promittit seu iurat quod semper tenebit eandem, non est paratus corrigi, & per consequens haereticus est censendus.
units.tr: Disciple. After the question about those who bend a heretical definition of the Pope, which has various senses, one heretical and another Catholic, towards the Catholic sense, I ask you to say what should be thought of those who, while knowing that each of the senses which can truly be drawn from the words of the Pope's determination is heretical, would by the force of the words bend the heretical definition of the Pope, in every sense it could bear, towards some Catholic sense. Teacher. The answer is that there is one view which holds that such people, who believe the error of a heretical Pope, should also be regarded as heretics, unless they diligently seek the truth and are ready to be corrected as soon as they find it. That those who believe such things should be reckoned heretics can apparently be proved as follows. One who believes the error of heretics, which has no possible Catholic sense, is rightly counted among those who believe the error of heretics; but one who stubbornly defends the error of heretics, which has no possible Catholic sense, is to be regarded as a heretic (24. quaest. 3. qui aliorum.). Since, then, by the supposition, such people believe an error which has no possible Catholic sense, they are rightly counted among believers. And from this it is plain that such people, unless they diligently seek the truth and are ready to be corrected when they find it, are to be judged heretics; for one who errs against the faith, unless he seeks the truth and is ready to be corrected when he finds it, is to be numbered among heretics (24. quaest. 3. dicit Apostolus.). From this it follows that those who would expound and bend the heretical definition of the Pope, in every sense it can bear by the force of the words, towards a Catholic sense, and who at the same time did not pursue and harass in any way those who attack the heretical definition of the Pope, would be reckoned among heretics, because they would not seek the truth with careful diligence. There is another view, which says that those who bend the heretical definition of the Pope towards a Catholic sense in this way must make a distinction, because either such people are skilled in the art of distinguishing ambiguous assertions that have various senses, or they are quite unlearned in that art. The first cannot be excused of the crime of lying or of heretical depravity; they are to be judged self-contradictory, just as heretics are often found to be self-contradictory, since according to Augustine (24. quaest. 7. cap. quod autem): Heretics, blinded by the desire to calumniate, do not notice that the things they say are contrary to one another. And therefore, since such people are skilled in distinguishing ambiguous assertions, there is a strong presumption that one who holds the heretical assertion of the Pope under some sense which it sounds like, and at the same time holds the Catholic truth as though contrary to himself, is doing so. But if such people are not skilled in distinguishing ambiguous assertions, they are not to be judged heretics at once; yet if they stubbornly defended that such an assertion must be upheld in such a sense, they ought to be judged heretics. Disciple. How is such a person convicted of obstinacy? Teacher. The answer is that he is convicted of obstinacy if, after it has been clearly shown to him that the assertion of the heretical Pope cannot have such a sense, he still remains in his opinion. It is also said that he can be convicted of obstinacy in many other ways: for example, if he refuses to be instructed in the truth (when that can fittingly be done); if he persecutes or harasses those who attack heretical depravity; if he compels others by threats, commands, punishments, or any other means to defend his opinion obstinately; and perhaps in some other ways, of which something was said above in book four, he is to be convicted of obstinacy. Disciple. What if someone promises or swears that he will always hold such a heretical assertion, and intends to hold it in a Catholic sense, which nevertheless he cannot have from the force of the words? Teacher. The answer is that such a person is to be judged a heretic, because since he holds a heretical assertion in every sense it can bear by the force of the words, and promises or swears that he will always hold the same, he is not ready to be corrected, and consequently he is to be regarded as a heretic.

units.la: CAP. IV.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: In quo agitur de praelatis inferioribus Papae statutum tale non approbando, sed suis tantummodo praecipiendo, ne ipsum reprobare audeant, & ut de persona Papae semper reuerenter loquantur, ubi etiam nota, si quando aliquem liceat ludificare, & ad huiusmodi quaesitum etiam respondetur sub duplici opinione, ibidem etiam nota de iuramento, de mendacio & peccato infidelitatis.
units.tr: In which it is discussed whether inferior prelates may obey the Pope's decree without approving it, merely ordering their subjects not to dare to condemn it and always to speak of the Pope's person with reverence. Note also when it is lawful to deceive someone, and two opinions are given in reply to this question. Note also here concerning the oath, lying and the sin of unbelief.

units.la: Discipulus. Ponatur quod Papa diffiniret aliquam assertionem haereticam esse tenendam, tanquam catholicam: & alius praelatus (puta archiepiscopus, vel episcopus, vel alius sciens diffinitionem Papae esse haereticam) ordinet, statuat, praecipiat, aut mandet sub graui poena, quod nullus subditorum suorum audeat diffinitionem Papae aliqualiter reprobare, sed de ea, & etiam de persona Papae, quilibet subditus suus loquatur omnino reuerenter, nomen tamen Papae in tali ordinatione, statuto, praecepto vel mandato nullatenus exprimendo, nunquid talis praelatus est credens errori Papae & haereticus reputandus? Magister. Circa hoc sunt diuersae opiniones, vna est, quod talis praelatus est credens errori Papae & haereticus reputandus, quod enim inter credentes errori Papae debeat computari, ex hoc probatur, quod statuit diffinitionem Papae nullatenus reprobandam: sed quod de ea cum reuerentia est loquendum, error autem est reprobandus, & non est cum reuerentia de errore loquendum, ergo talis ordinans, statuens, praecipiens siue mandans credit diffinitionem Papae esse tenendam, & per consequens inter credentes errori Papae est merito computandus. Quod vero talis praelatus sit haereticus reputandus, tali ratione probatur. Credens errori contra fidem & ad eundem errorem tenendum alios minis compellit, statutis & praeceptis, est haereticus computandus, vt ex his quae dicta sunt libro quarto, videtur posse probari, talis autem praelatus est credens errori Papae: & ad eundem errorem tenendum alios compellit statutis & praeceptis, ergo non est solum credens errori Papae: sed haereticus est censendus. Alia est opinio; quod si praelatus inferior, puta archiepiscopus aut aliquis praelatus, praecise talibus verbis vel aequipollentibus vtatur: statuo, mando, vel praecipio, vel sub poena excommunicationis, vel etiam carceris, vt nullus mihi subiectus diffinitiones Domini summi Pontificis audeat reprobare: vel ex eo de persona Papae qualitercunque male loqui, sed loquatur cum omnimoda reuerentia de eisdem, talis praelatus sine maiori examinatione, non est inter credentes errori Papae, nec inter haereticos computandus. Cuius ratio assignatur: quia propter verba generalia talia, quae ita possunt intelligi de diffinitionibus catholici Papae, sicut de diffinitionibus Papae haretici, non est aliquis inter credentes erroribus Papae haereticus, vel haereticos computandus: sed praedicta ita possunt intelligi de diffinitionibus Papae catholici, sicut de diffinitionibus Papae haretici, ergo propter talia verba generalia non est aliquis inter credentes vel haereticos computandus. Discipulus. Ista regula esset apparens; si, quando fit tale statutum, esset aliquis Papa catholicus, sicut est Papa haereticus. Magister.
