Primum istorum declaratur sic, sicut ille, qui nullam veritatem catholicam explicite credit, quamvis credat in genere fidem catholicam esse veram, non est catholicus reputandus: sic ille, qui nullam errorem contrarium veritati catholicae explicite credit, non est inter haereticos computandus, sed ille, qui credit aliquos catholicos, qui tamen sunt haeretici: & nescit in speciali aliquem errorem eorum nulli errori contrario fidei explicite credit, ergo talis non est inter haereticos computandus nomine haereticorum stricte sumpto. Secundum, scilicet quod large accipiendo nomen haereticorum pertinaciter credentes haereticis, licet nullum errorem ipsorum in speciali & explicite credant, sunt haeretici iudicandi, sic videtur posse probari, tenentes pertinaciter errorem, ex quo & quibusdam veris, quae negari non possunt, sequitur haeresis manifesta, possunt haeretici nuncupari large accipiendo vocabulum, sed tales credunt errorem, ex quo & quibusdam veris sequitur haeresis manifesta, verbi gratia: si aliquis haereticus teneret pertinaciter animas reproborum in inferno minime cruciari, & quod animae sanctae non vident Deum in coelo, & quod omnia de necessitate eveniunt, credentes pertinaciter talem esse catholicum tenerent errorem: ex quo & quodam vero (quod negari non potest) sequitur haeresis manifesta. Sequitur enim: talis, puta Martinus vel Iacobus, est catholicus: & Martinus vel Iacobus tenent irrevocabiliter, quod animae reproborum non cruciantur in inferno: & quod animae sanctorum in coelo non vident Deum: & quod omnia de necessitate eveniunt, ergo animae reproborum non cruciantur in inferno: nec animae sanctorum in coelo vident Deum: & omnia de necessitate eveniunt. Conclusio ista concludit haereses manifestas: & isti credentes (de quibus est sermo) pertinaciter explicite tenent maiorem, & minor potest aperte probari, ergo isti credentes large sumpto vocabulo sunt haeretici iudicandi. Alius modus ponendi potest esse, quod tales credentes nec uno modo nec alio modo sunt haeretici reputandi: quia sicut nullus est reputandus catholicus, nisi habeat fidem de veritate incommutabili, quae falsificari non potest: ita nullus est haereticus reputandus, nisi adhaereat errori, qui verificari non potest, tales autem credentes non adhaerent nisi erroribus, qui verificari non possunt, si enim Iacobus vel Iohannes hodie est haereticus: cras posset esse catholicus, ergo tales non sunt haeretici reputandi.
units.tr: Student. Having seen the errors of heretics that believers hold explicitly, let us consider the believers who are themselves heretics, namely those who regard themselves as Catholics, though they do not know where they differ from sound Catholic doctrine: whether such persons are to be counted as heretics, and by what punishment they ought to be punished. Master. On this matter there can be different ways of speaking. One is this: such persons, if they explicitly believe no heretical error and do not know in particular what their errors are, are not to be counted among heretics, speaking strictly of heretics. Taking the term broadly, however, those who obstinately hold implicitly errors that savour of manifest heresy are to be judged heretics. The first of these is shown thus: just as one who explicitly believes no Catholic truth, although he believes in general that the Catholic faith is true, is not to be regarded as Catholic, so one who explicitly believes no error contrary to Catholic truth is not to be counted among heretics. But one who believes that some Catholics are heretics, and does not know in particular any of their errors, explicitly believes no error contrary to the faith; therefore such a person is not to be counted among heretics, taking the name of heretic strictly. The second, namely that, taking the name of heretic broadly, those who obstinately trust heretics, although they do not explicitly believe any of their errors in particular, are to be judged heretics, seems capable of being proved thus. Those who obstinately hold an error from which, together with certain truths that cannot be denied, manifest heresy follows, may be called heretics in the broad sense of the word. But such believers hold an error from which, together with certain truths, manifest heresy follows. For example: if some heretic obstinately held that the souls of the reprobate are not tormented in hell, that the holy souls do not see God in heaven, and that all things happen of necessity, and if believers obstinately regarded such a man as Catholic, they would hold an error from which, together with a certain truth that cannot be denied, manifest heresy follows. For it follows: such a man, say Martin or James, is Catholic; and Martin or James irrevocably holds that the souls of the reprobate are not tormented in hell, that the souls of the saints in heaven do not see God, and that all things happen of necessity; therefore the souls of the reprobate are not tormented in hell, nor do the souls of the saints in heaven see God, and all things happen of necessity. This conclusion yields manifest heresies; and the believers of whom we speak explicitly and obstinately hold the major premise, and the minor can be plainly proved; therefore these believers, taking the word broadly, are to be judged heretics. Another way of putting it may be that such believers are to be regarded as heretics in neither the one sense nor the other, because just as no one is to be regarded as Catholic unless he has faith in the unchangeable truth, which cannot be falsified, so no one is to be regarded as heretic unless he adheres to an error which cannot be made true. Such believers, however, adhere only to errors which cannot be made true; for if James or John is a heretic today, he could be a Catholic tomorrow; therefore such persons are not to be regarded as heretics.

units.la: CAP. IX.
units.tr: CHAP. IX.

units.la: Agit de taliter credentibus, &c. precedenti modo expresso, quomodo graviter peccent, ubi etiam notatur de ignorantia supina, & quomodo cognosci possit, quando quis ea laborat: ibidem etiam notatur de criminosis quomodo in iudicio sint audiendi.
units.tr: This chapter deals with those who believe in the manner already described, and how they sin gravely. It also notes supine ignorance, and how one may recognise when someone labours under it. Here it is further noted how criminals are to be heard in court.

units.la: Discipul. Ista difficultas, an scilicet tales credentes sint censendi haeretici, videtur mihi magis esse de nomine, quam de re, ideo ipsa dimissa dic, an omnes credentes haereticis modo praedicto (licet in speciali nullum sciant errorem ipsorum) graviter peccent: & an sint acriter puniendi. Magist. Respondetur, quod si tales credentes sciant haereticos esse damnatos, graviter & mortaliter peccant, si autem nesciant eos esse damnatos, nec sciunt quod sunt haeretici, & non laborant ignorantia crassa & supina, non peccant mortaliter, si vero laborant ignorantia crassa & supina, peccant mortaliter. Discipul. Quomodo scietur, qui credentes haereticis, quos nesciunt esse haereticos, laborant ignorantia crassa & supina & qui non? Magist. Respondetur, quod illi dicuntur esse credentes haereticis ignorantia crassa & supina sive damnabili laborantes, qui nolunt scire vel non curant, quos putant catholicos esse, & quos haereticos. Discipul. Et quomodo scietur, quod aliqui credentes haereticis nolunt scire ipsos esse haereticos? Magist. Respondetur quod illi nolunt scire esse aliquos hæreticos, qui veram informationem de hæreticorum perfidia nolunt audire, unde si sint aliqui scientes hæreticorum perfidiam, qui laborant, & parati sunt ostendere, quod sunt prauitate infecti hæretica, qui nolunt eos audire: & multo magis qui tales volentes eos de hæreticorum perfidia informare, repellunt, persequuntur & molestant, ignorantia damnabili & affectata laborant.
units.tr: Disciple. This question, whether such believers are to be counted heretics, seems to me to be more a matter of names than of substance. So set it aside and tell me this: do all who believe heretics in the way described (even though they know nothing of the particular errors of those heretics) sin gravely, and are they to be punished severely? Master. The answer is that if such believers know that the heretics have been condemned, they sin gravely and mortally. If they do not know that the heretics have been condemned, and do not know that they are heretics, and are not labouring under gross and supine ignorance, they do not sin mortally. If, however, they are labouring under gross and supine ignorance, they sin mortally. Disciple. How will it be known which believers of heretics, whom they do not know to be heretics, labour under gross and supine ignorance, and which do not? Master. The answer is that those are said to believe heretics in culpable, gross and supine ignorance who are unwilling to know, or do not care, whether those whom they think to be Catholics are Catholics or heretics. Disciple. And how will it be known that some who believe heretics are unwilling to know that those men are heretics? Master. The answer is that those are unwilling to know that some men are heretics who refuse to hear true information about the perfidy of heretics. Hence, if there are some who know the perfidy of heretics, who are labouring to show, and are ready to show, that certain people are infected with heretical depravity, and those people refuse to hear them, then, much more, those who repel, persecute and harass such persons who wish to inform them about the perfidy of heretics are labouring under culpable and deliberate ignorance.

units.la: Discip. Videtur quod tales repellentes, persequentes, & molestantes eos, qui cupiunt eos informare de illis, quos putant catholicos esse, & ostendere quod sunt hæretici, non peccant: imo faciunt quod debent, nam ex quo putant tales catholicos esse, reputare debent illos esse detractores: qui eos cupiunt de prauitate hæretica diffamare. Detractores autem repellere, molestare, & persequi non est peccatum, sed virtus, teste Psalmista: Detrahentem secreto proximo suo, hunc persequebar. Cui Salomon concordare videtur, qui Proverbio. 25. ait: Ventus aquilo dissipat pluvias, & facies tristis linguam detrahentem. Et Proverbio. 4. c. Labia detrahentium sint procul à te. Et c. 3. dicit: Cum detractoribus non miscearis. Quibus consonat illud Ecclesiast. 20. Sepi aures spinis, & noli audire linguam nequam. Ex quibus aliisque quamplurimis testimoniis scripturarum sacrarum patenter colligitur: quod detractores non sunt audiendi, sed compellendi & molestandi, quod Anteros papa (ut habetur 6. quæst. 1. ca. ex merito) aperte insinuat dicens: cauteat itaque vnusquisque ne aut linguam, aut aures habeat prurientes: id est, ne aut aliis ipse detrahat, aut alios detrahentes audiat.
units.tr: Disciple. It seems that those who repel, persecute and harass those who wish to inform them about those whom they think to be Catholics, and to show that these are heretics, do not sin. Indeed they do what they ought. For since they think these men to be Catholics, they ought to regard those who wish to defame them for heretical depravity as slanderers. Yet to repel, harass and persecute slanderers is not a sin but a virtue, as the Psalmist witnesses: Whoever secretly slanders his neighbour, him I persecuted. Solomon seems to agree with this, who says in Proverbs 25: The north wind drives away rain, and a sad face (drives away) a slandering tongue. And in Proverbs 4: Let the lips of slanderers be far from you. And in chapter 3 he says: Do not mix yourself with slanderers. To this agrees that passage in Ecclesiasticus 20: Hedge your ears with thorns, and do not listen to a wicked tongue. From these and very many other testimonies of the holy Scriptures it is plainly gathered that slanderers are not to be heard, but compelled and harassed. Anterus the pope (as is found in 6 q. 1, c. ex merito) clearly hints at this, saying: Let each one therefore take care that he has neither a tongue nor ears that itch, that is, that he neither slander others himself nor listen to those who slander.

units.la: Hoc etiam ex octaua Synodo probatur, prout legitur 11. q. 3. capitu. non solum, colligitur euidenter, quod non solum ille reus est, qui falsum de aliquo profert, sed etiam is qui aurem criminibus cito præbet. Quæ etiam Augustin. sentire videtur, ut habetur eisdem cap. & q. c. in cunctis, scribens archiepiscopo Mediolanensi in hæc verba: sanctitas vestra debet mentem suam à maledicorum hominum rumoribus atque obtrectationibus disiungere. Ex quibus aliisque quamplurimis patenter infertur, quod detractores, calumniatores, diffamatores, & criminum impositores non sunt aliqualiter audiendi, sed omnimode repellendi. Igitur si apparent aliqui, qui volunt alios informare de papa, quod sit prauitate hæretica irretitus, quantumcunque papa esset hæreticus: illi, qui nescirent papam esse hæreticum, non debent tales informatores audire. Ex quo sequitur, quod tales propter quod nolunt de perfidia papæ hæretici informari: non essent dicendi ignorantia damnabili ignorantes. Hæc inter alia mouent me ad tenendum, quod volentes ignorantes papam vel alios prauitatem hæreticam incurrisse de veritate informare, non sunt aliquo modo audiendi: sed tanquam detractores repellendi, qualiter tamen contingat ad ista responderi, explana. Magist. Ad omnes auctoritates, quibus suadetur, detractores esse minime audiendos: respondetur vnico verbo, quod omnes debent intelligi, quando sciuntur esse detractores, quia illi de quibus scitur quod detractionis vitio sunt infecti, absque magna causa audiri non debent, cum volunt de aliis aliquid narrare sinistrum, illi autem de quibus ignoratur an sint detractores, sunt omnino audiendi: præcipue cum aliquid, quod in dispendium potest vergere boni communis, cupiunt enarrare, & multo magis sunt audiendi illi, qui hactenus discreti & bonæ famæ reputati fuerunt, si intendunt aliquid sinistrum de aliquo referare, quare si tales laborant ostendere, quod papa est hæretica prauitate maculatus, sunt audiendi omnino.
units.tr: This is also proved from the eighth Synod, as is read in 11 q. 3, cap. non solum. It is plainly gathered that not only is he guilty who utters a falsehood about someone, but also he who readily lends his ear to accusations. St Augustine also seems to think this, as is found in the same chapter and question, cap. & q. c. in cunctis, writing to the archbishop of Milan in these words: Your holiness ought to keep your mind apart from the rumours and detractions of evil men. From these and very many other sources it is plainly inferred that slanderers, calumniators, defamers and imposers of crimes are not to be heard in any way, but are to be repelled in every way. Therefore, if some appear who wish to inform others that the pope is entangled in heretical depravity, however much the pope might be a heretic, those who did not know that the pope was a heretic ought not to hear such informers. It follows from this that those who, because they are unwilling to be informed of the pope's heretical perfidy, should not be called ignorant with culpable ignorance. These and other considerations lead me to hold that those who wish to inform ignorant people of the truth, that the pope or others have fallen into heretical depravity, are not to be heard in any way, but are to be repelled as slanderers. Explain, however, how these matters can be answered. Master. To all the authorities by which it is urged that slanderers are by no means to be heard, the answer is in one word: all of them must be understood to apply when slanderers are known to be such. For those who are known to be infected with the vice of detraction are not to be heard, without a great cause, when they wish to relate something unfavourable about others. But those whose slander is not known are to be heard entirely, especially when they wish to relate something that may turn to the detriment of the common good. Much more are those to be heard who have hitherto been regarded as discreet and of good repute, if they intend to report something unfavourable about someone. Therefore, if such persons labour to show that the pope is stained with heretical depravity, they are to be heard entirely.

units.la: Discipul. Non obstante ista responsione generali dic quomodo ad auctoritates singulariter respondetur.
units.tr: Disciple. Notwithstanding this general answer, tell me how the authorities are answered one by one.

units.la: Magister. Respondetur, ad primam dicitur, quod Psalmista loquebatur de illo, quem sciebat esse detrahentem, & ideo tanquam malum iuste persequebatur eundem. Ad secundam dicitur, quod auditor per faciem tristem debet repellere illum, quem esse trahentem agnoscit. Ad tertiam per idem respondetur, quod labia detrahentium, quos scit esse detrahentes, debent esse procul à quolibet bono viro. Ad quartam respondetur, quod nullus debet scienter cum detractoribus commisceri. Ad quintam, quod non est audienda lingua nequam, quæ scitur esse nequam. Ad sextam de Antero papa respondetur, quod nemo debet scienter audire aliis detrahentes. Ad alia respondetur, quod autem cito præbere criminibus contingit dupliciter: vel absque credulitate solummodo audiendo; vel adhibendo fidem & credendo, primo modo nemo debet cito aurem præbere criminibus, quando narrantur ab illis, quos scit mendosos, falsos, detractores, vel in quocunque crimine irretitos: quia omnes tales debet habere suspectos, ne falso vel mendaciter vel mala intentione crimina referre nitantur, & ideo illos debet repellere, & quantum sibi competit pro gradu suo & officio ad correctionem & punitionem eorum tenetur fideliter laborare. Si vero criminum relatores non fuerint antea aliquo crimine, puta nec detractione, nec mendacio, nec aliquo alio irretiti, cito eis auris est præbenda, solummodo audiendo & ad cautelam in memoria retinendo. Sed secundo modo, scilicet fidem adhibendo & credendo nullus debet aurem cito præbere criminibus, hoc enim vitio criminali minime caret. Ad vltimam auctoritatem respondetur, quod vir sanctus mentem suam ab obtrectationibus & rumoribus illorum hominum, quos sciuit esse maledicos, debet disiungere, non solummodo eis fidem minime adhibendo, sed nec eos absque causa magna aliqualiter audiendo. Discipulus. Quare dicitur, quod tales absque causa magna audiri non debent: cum per hoc innuatur, quod ex causa magna detractores & maledici debeant audiri? Magist. Respondetur quod quemadmodum nullus criminosus est regulariter ad accusandum & testificandum in iudicio admittendus, tamen in quibusdam criminibus enormibus ad accusandum & denunciandum deberet admitti, licet nunquam fides ei debeat adhiberi, nisi per legitima documenta suae assertionis probauerit veritatem, ita detractores regulariter audiri non debent: in casu tamen magno pro magno periculo euitando, praesertim si aliqua indicia veritatis praecederent, deberent audiri ad aperiendum vias inuestigandi citius veritatem, nullus tamen debet 5 credere eis.
units.tr: Master. The answer to the first is that the Psalmist was speaking of one whom he knew to be a slanderer, and so he rightly pursued him as an evil man. To the second it is said that a hearer ought to repel with a sad face the one whom he recognises to be a slanderer. To the third the same answer is given: the lips of slanderers, whom one knows to be slanderers, ought to be far from every good man. To the fourth the answer is that no one ought knowingly to mix with slanderers. To the fifth, that a wicked tongue, which is known to be wicked, is not to be listened to. To the sixth, concerning Anterus the pope, the answer is that no one ought knowingly to listen to those who slander others. To the other authorities the answer is that to lend a ready ear to accusations happens in two ways: either by merely listening without belief, or by giving credence and believing. In the first way, no one ought readily to lend his ear to accusations when they are related by those whom he knows to be liars, false, slanderers, or entangled in some crime whatsoever, because one ought to regard all such persons with suspicion, lest they strive to report crimes falsely, lyingly or with evil intent. Therefore one ought to repel them, and as far as lies within one's rank and office, one is bound to labour faithfully for their correction and punishment. But if the reporters of crimes have not previously been entangled in any crime, such as slander, lying or any other, then an ear is to be lent to them readily, merely by listening and by keeping their words in mind as a precaution. In the second way, however, that is, by giving credence and believing, no one ought readily to lend his ear to accusations, for this is by no means free of criminal vice. To the last authority the answer is that a holy man ought to keep his mind apart from the detractions and rumours of those men whom he knows to be evil-speakers, not only by giving them no credence at all, but also by not listening to them in any way without a great cause. Disciple. Why is it said that such persons are not to be heard without a great cause, since this implies that slanderers and evil-speakers ought to be heard for a great cause? Master. The answer is that just as no criminal is ordinarily admitted to accuse or give testimony in court, yet in certain enormous crimes he ought to be admitted to accuse and denounce, although credence should never be given to him unless he has proved the truth of his assertion by lawful proofs, so slanderers ordinarily are not to be heard. Yet in a great case, to avoid great danger, especially if some signs of the truth precede, they ought to be heard, in order to open the ways of inquiring more quickly into the truth. Nevertheless, no one ought to believe them.

units.la: CAP. X.
units.tr: CAP. X.

units.la: Vbi inuestigatur de his, qui impugnant Papam haereticum, vtrum tales sint audiendi etiam ab ignorantibus Papam esse haereticum, & respondetur, quod sic, & probatur p. rationibus.
units.tr: Where it is investigated concerning those who attack the Pope as a heretic, whether such men are to be heard even by those who do not know that the Pope is a heretic; and it is answered that they are, and this is proved by several arguments.

units.la: Discipulus, Licet Dominum summum pontificem nunc Dei prouidentia in cathedra sancti Petri sedentem, Dominum videlicet Iohannem 22. catholicum atque sanctum ab omni haeretica prauitate alienum absque omni dubitatione existimem, & ideo omnia quae dicta sunt de papa haeretico & dicentur, de ipso nullo modo intelligam, quia tamen probabiliter existimo, quod papa (cum non sit confirmatus neque in gratia neque in fide) in haereticam valeat incidere prauitatem, 10 in quo cum Fratre Michaele quondam generali Ministro Fratrum Minorum complicibusque suis conuenio, qui (vt audio) probare nituntur, quod in his, quae proponunt contra Dominum summum pontificem, sunt a catholicis audiendi: eorumque scripta contra doctrinam ipsius & personam eius a fidelibus sunt videnda, & cum deliberatione prouida discutienda & examinanda, quod & Dominus noster summus pontifex de scriptis eorum fecisse dignoscitur, cum ad scripta eorum etiam sub Bulla subtiliter & sufficienter respondit: peto vt motiua dicentium, quod volentes informare ignorantes papam esse haereticum de erroribus eiusdem papae haeretici atque pertinacia eius, si periti & bonae famae reputati ante fuerunt, sint ab ignorantibus papam esse haereticum audiendi, forsitan enim pro tempore, quo aliquis papa futurus efficeretur haereticus, posset esse vtilius vel ad probandum vel ad improbandum, expedit enim nonnunquam scire motiua impugnantium veritatem. Magist. Mihi videtur, quod intendis ponere casum, quod papa in rei veritate sit haereticus, & quod aliqui catholici satagunt eius errores & perfidiam publicare. Discipul. Ita est vt dicis: vnde procedas ac si papa esset haereticus, quamuis in rei veritate non sit. Magist. Quod catholici imponentes papae (quantumcunque fuerit haereticus) prauitatem haereticam sint ab ignorantibus papam esse haereticum audiendi: illi praecipue, qui antea bonae famae fuerunt, videtur multis modis posse probari, primo quidem sic. Illi, qui sunt pro aliqua causa ab aliquibus defendendi, sunt multo fortius audiendi ab eisdem, cum minus sit audire aliquos, quam defendere eosdem, sed catholici imponentes papae haereticam prauitatem, sunt etiam ab ignorantibus papam esse haereticum, defendendi, ergo multo fortius audiri debent ab eisdem. Discipul. Video, quod ratio ista dependet ab illis, quae dicta sunt, supra libro 7. a. c. 37. vsque ad c. 55. quia per illa videtur minor posse probari, ideo istam rationem noli amplius pertractare: sed si aliquas cogitasti, adducas. Magist. Secunda ratio ad eandem conclusionem talis est, velox ad audiendum debet praebere aures illis, qui errores & perfidiam papae haeretici impugnare nituntur, sed omnis homo debet esse velox ad audiendum, tardus vero ad loquendum, ergo &c. 40
units.tr: Disciple. Although I consider our lord, the supreme pontiff now sitting in the chair of St Peter by the providence of God, namely Lord John XXII, to be Catholic and holy and free from every heretical depravity beyond all doubt, and therefore I shall in no way understand everything that has been said and will be said about a heretical pope as applying to him, nevertheless I think it probable that the Pope (since he has not been confirmed either in grace or in the faith) may fall into heretical depravity. On this point I agree with Brother Michael, formerly Minister General of the Friars Minor, and his associates, who (as I hear) strive to prove that those who bring charges against our lord the supreme pontiff are to be heard by Catholics. Their writings against his doctrine and person are to be read by the faithful and examined and discussed with careful deliberation. Our lord the supreme pontiff is known to have done this with their writings too, since he replied to them thoroughly and sufficiently even under a Bull. I ask that the arguments of those who say, wishing to inform those who do not know that the Pope is a heretic, about the errors and obstinacy of that heretical pope, should be heard by those who do not know he is a heretic, provided they were reckoned skilled and of good repute beforehand. For perhaps, at the time when some future pope becomes a heretic, it could be more useful either to prove or to disprove the matter, for it is sometimes expedient to know the arguments of those who attack the truth. Master. It seems to me you intend to posit the case that the Pope is in fact a heretic, and that some Catholics are labouring to make public his errors and perfidy. Disciple. It is as you say. So proceed as if the Pope were a heretic, although in fact he is not. Master. That Catholics who charge the Pope (however much of a heretic he may be) with heretical depravity are to be heard by those who do not know he is a heretic, especially those who were previously of good repute, seems capable of being proved in many ways. First, indeed, thus. Those who are to be defended by some people for some cause are much more strongly to be heard by those same people, since hearing someone is less than defending him. But Catholics who charge the Pope with heretical depravity are to be defended even by those who do not know the Pope is a heretic. Therefore they must be heard all the more strongly by the same people. Disciple. I see that this argument depends on what was said above, in book 7, chapters 37 to 55, because through those chapters the minor premise seems capable of being proved. So do not pursue this argument further, but if you have thought of others, bring them forward. Master. The second argument for the same conclusion is this. A man must be quick to hear those who strive to attack the errors and perfidy of a heretical pope. But every man ought to be quick to hear and slow to speak. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Discipul. Ista auctoritas beati Iacobi pro istis non facit: quia homo velox debet esse ad audiendum bona: non autem ad audiendum mala, ergo per hanc auctoritatem probari non potest, quod ignorantes papam esse haereticum debeant audire illos, qui volunt eius errores & perfidiam publicare. Magist. Respondetur, quod auctoritas beati Iacobi non tantum de bonis, sed etiam de malis audiendis debet intelligi, quia dicit beatus Iacobus: debet esse quisque velox ad audiendum: sicut debet esse tardus ad loquendum, nam eodem modo proportionabiliter debet intelligi, quod beatus Iacobus dicit, sit omnis homo velox ad audiendum mala, non vt credat vel approbet: sed vt caueat & euitet. Et ex hoc potest tertia ratio formari, homo debet esse velox ad audiendum illa quae scire potest esse vtilia sibi & toti communitati, sed scire papam esse haereticum (quando est haereticus) potest esse vtile cuilibet fideli & toti communitati fidelium: quia per hoc facilius & melius eius malitiae resisterent, ergo quilibet debet libenter audire volentes errores & perfidiam papae haeretici publicare. 50 Quarta ratio est haec. Illa debet homo catholicus libenter audire, quae debet velle scire, illa autem quae cauenda sunt, debet catholicus velle scire, quia cauenda nisi sciantur cauERI non possunt, non tantum autem debet catholicus cauere peccatum in se: sed etiam debet quantum in se est cauere pericula, quae communitati vel fidei imminere dicuntur, si autem papa infectus fuerit haeretica prauitate: periculum imminet fidei orthodoxae, & per consequens offerentes se ad prodendum & ad monstrandum perfidiam papae haeretici, debent libenter audiri. 60 Quinta ratio est haec. Hoc debet catholicus libenter inquirere, cuius veritatem (cum non sciat) tenetur inquirere, sed si catholicis etiam ignorantibus papam esse haereticum nunciatur eius perfidia, ipsi tenentur veritatem inquirere, ergo tales nunciantes papam haereticum debent audiri. Maior videtur probatione minime indigere. Minor auctoritatibus diuinae scripturae videtur posse probari, nam sicut supra allegatum existit, Deut. 13. sic legitur: Si audieris in vna vrbium tuarum, quas Dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi ad habitandum, dicentes aliquos; egressi sunt filii Belial de medio tui: & adverterunt habitatores vrbis tuae atque dixerunt: exeamus & seruiamus diis alienis quos ignoratis, quare sollicite & diligenter rei veritatem perspecta. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod cum aliqui dicunt, quod aliqui volunt fidem corrumpere, veritas est sollicite inquirenda, ergo si aliqui asserunt papam haereticum velle fidem corrumpere orthodoxam: illi fideles & ignorantes papam tali respersum perfidia, debent sollicite quaerere veritatem, quod etiam Iob. 29. innuitur, cum ipsemet Iob dicit: causam quam nesciebam diligentissime inuestigabam. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod cum alicuius causae, quae potest esse in detrimentum omnium, veritas ignoratur, debet diligentissime inuestigari, hinc Salomon Prouerbio. 25. ait: gloria regum est inuestigare sermonem, quod verum est, cum periculum imminet publicae utilitatis. Discipul. Istae auctoritates nihil faciunt pro conclusione intenta, quia auctoritates praedictae & consimiles de praelatis & iudicibus siue regentibus (duntaxat) debent intelligi, quia illorum & non aliorum est inquirere subditorum excessus, cum mala fama de eis exierit secundum canonicas sanctiones. Magist. Dicunt alii, quod verba auctoritatum praedictarum, & etiam sacrorum canonum, quibus asseritur, quod praelati ad corrigendos subditorum excessus debent assurgere, nequaquam intelligis, quia correctio est duplex, vna est potestatiue per publicam punitionem, & haec pertinet ad praelatos, & in sublimitatibus constitutos, alia est per simplicem monitionem, & haec pertinet ad omnes charitatem habentes, quia vnicuique praecipitur amouere malum cuiuslibet subditi & praelati (si potest) sic inquisitio siue inuestigatio peccati alterius, vna est potestatiua & iudicialis, qua quis compellit alios ex officio, vel potest compellere dicere veritatem de peccato, & etiam de mala intentione alterius: vel etiam periculi, quod potest sibi & aliis imminere, alia est per simplicem interrogationem absque omni praecepto & solennitate, seu compulsione & punitione nolentium, quam scirent dicere veritatem, & ista inquisitio, seu inuestigatio peccati vel periculi (quod sibi potest & aliis imminere) spectat ad omnes, qui curam de se & aliis habere debent, omnes autem non solum de ipsis: sed etiam de proximis, quos (sicut seipsos debent diligere) tenentur aliquam curam & sollicitudinem pro loco & tempore (& cum aliis circumstantiis determinatis requisitis) habere, iuxta illud Apostoli ad Romanos 12. sollicitudine non pigri, quod non tantum dicitur ad praelatos, sed etiam ad subditos, quorum est aliquam sollicitudinem non solum pro se, sed etiam pro omnibus aliis inferioribus, aequalibus & superioribus, quando conuenienter possunt, habere.
units.tr: Disciple. That saying of blessed James does not support your case, because a man ought to be quick to hear good things, not evil things. Therefore this authority cannot prove that those who do not know the Pope is a heretic must hear those who wish to make public his errors and perfidy. Master. The reply is that the authority of blessed James must be understood as applying not only to good things but also to evil things to be heard. For blessed James says: "Let every man be quick to hear, as he ought to be slow to speak." In the same way, proportionally, what blessed James says must be understood: every man should be quick to hear evil things, not so that he believes or approves them, but so that he may be on guard and avoid them. From this a third argument can be formed. A man ought to be quick to hear those things which he can know to be useful to himself and to the whole community. But to know that the Pope is a heretic (when he is one) can be useful to every faithful person and to the whole community of the faithful, because by this means they could more easily and effectively resist his wickedness. Therefore everyone ought willingly to hear those who wish to make public the errors and perfidy of a heretical pope. The fourth argument is this. A Catholic ought willingly to hear those things which he ought to wish to know. Now a Catholic ought to wish to know those things against which he must be on guard, since things to be guarded against cannot be avoided unless they are known. A Catholic is bound not only to guard against sin in himself but, as far as he can, also to guard against the dangers which are said to threaten the community or the faith. If the Pope has been infected with heretical depravity, danger threatens the orthodox faith. Consequently, those who offer themselves to reveal and show the perfidy of a heretical pope ought to be willingly heard. The fifth argument is this. A Catholic ought willingly to inquire into the truth of a matter which he is bound to inquire into though he does not know it. But if Catholics, even those who do not know the Pope is a heretic, are told of his perfidy, they are bound to inquire into the truth. Therefore those who announce that the Pope is a heretic ought to be heard. The major premise seems to need no proof. The minor seems capable of being proved from the authorities of divine Scripture. For, as was cited above, Deuteronomy 13 reads thus: "If you hear, in one of your cities which the Lord your God gives you to dwell in, some saying that children of Belial have gone out from among you, and the inhabitants of your city have turned aside and said, 'Let us go and serve other gods, whom you do not know', then you shall inquire carefully and diligently into the truth of the matter." From these words it is given to understand that when some say that certain people wish to corrupt the faith, the truth is to be inquired into diligently. Therefore, if some assert that the Pope, a heretic, wishes to corrupt the orthodox faith, then the faithful who do not know that the Pope is stained with such perfidy ought to seek the truth diligently. This is also hinted at in Job 29, where Job himself says: "The cause which I did not know I investigated most diligently." From these words it is gathered that when the truth of a matter which may be to the detriment of all is unknown, it ought to be investigated most diligently. Hence Solomon says in Proverbs 25: "It is the glory of kings to investigate a matter," which is true when danger threatens the public good. Disciple. These authorities do nothing for the conclusion intended, because the above-mentioned authorities and similar ones must be understood only of prelates and judges or rulers, since it belongs to them and not to others to inquire into the faults of subjects, when an ill report of them has arisen according to the canonical sanctions. Master. Others say that you do not understand the words of the above-mentioned authorities, or of the sacred canons, which state that prelates must rise up to correct the faults of their subjects. For correction is twofold. One is by power, through public punishment, and this belongs to prelates and those set in high positions. The other is by simple admonition, and this belongs to all who have charity, since it is commanded to everyone to remove the evil of any subject or prelate (if he can). Likewise, the inquiry or investigation of another's sin is twofold. One is by power and judicially, by which someone compels others by virtue of office, or can compel them to tell the truth about a sin, or even about another's evil intention, or about a danger which may threaten himself and others. The other is by simple questioning, without any command, solemnity, compulsion, or punishment of the unwilling, to find out whether they will tell the truth. This inquiry or investigation of a sin or danger (which may threaten himself and others) concerns everyone who ought to have care for himself and others. Now all are bound to have some care and concern not only for themselves but also for their neighbours, whom they ought to love as themselves, for place and time (and with the other determined circumstances required). So the saying of the Apostle to the Romans 12 applies: "not slothful in zeal" ("sollicitudine non pigri"). This is said not only to prelates but also to subjects, who ought to have some concern not only for themselves but also for all others, inferiors, equals and superiors, when they can do so fittingly.

units.la: Discipul. Ista responsio apparentiam videtur habere, si quilibet teneretur pro omnibus superioribus & aliis aliquam sollicitudinem & causam habere, & ideo indica si hoc potest aliquo modo probari.
units.tr: Disciple. That answer seems plausible, if everyone is bound to have some concern and care for all superiors and others. So tell me whether this can be proved in any way.

units.la: Magist. Hoc Apostolus in diuersis locis insinuare videtur. Nam 1. Corinth. 12. expresse, vt apparet, probare conatur, quod exemplo membrorum corporis, quorum quodlibet aliquam sollicitudinem videtur habere de alio debet esse sollicitus. Vnde ibidem Apostolus: Non sit schisma in corpore: sed in idipsum pro se inuicem sollicita sint membra, & si quid patitur vnum membrorum: compatiuntur omnia membra, siue dum gloriatur vnum membrorum: congaudent omnia membra. Ex quibus verbis colligitur euidenter, quod cum simus membra vnius corporis, quilibet pro omnibus debet esse sollicitus, hoc dicit Glos. non sit schisma, id est discordantia in corpore humano vel in ecclesia, vbi debet esse vnitas, sed omnia membra potius sollicita sint, ita vt tendant in idipsum: id est in id sollicitudinis, quod sit ipsum indifferens, vt non minus pro alio quam pro seipso sollicita sint. Ex quibus aperte colligitur, quod omnes de omnibus sollicitudinem debent habere, quod etiam Apostolus ad Ephes. 4. aperte insinuare videtur, cum dicit: digne ambuletis vocatione qua vocati estis cum omni humilitate & mansuetudine, cum patientia supportantes inuicem in charitate, solliciti seruare vnitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis. Ex quibus patenter habetur, quod sicut omnes se debent inuicem supportare, ita pro inuicem debent esse solliciti, ne vnitas in eis rumpatur, vnitas autem spiritus in catholicis rumpitur, si papa efficeretur haereticus, ergo omnes, qui sunt membra corporis Christi, debent esse solliciti, ne fides catholica, quae est fundamentum vnitatis spiritus, & omnium bonorum spiritualium, corrumpatur, & ita omnes tenentur audire illos, qui volunt perfidiam papae haeretici satagentis fidem corrumpere orthodoxam ad occupandum periculo fidei publicare. Discipul. Debent ergo catholici aliquas occupationes dimittere & intendere illis, qui volunt perfidiam papae haeretici diuulgare? Magist. Non dicunt isti, quod omnes teneantur omnes alias occupationes dimittere: sed dicunt, quod iudicandum est de audientia danda illis, qui volunt perfidiam papae haeretici publicare: sicut iudicandum est de aliis actibus affirmatiuis, qui cadunt sub praecepto, quod non obligant ad semper: sed loco & tempore cum circumstantiis debitis requisitis, & ideo non est facile certam regulam dare in speciali, quo tempore tenetur quis de necessitate salutis audire illos, qui volunt perfidiam papae haeretici diuulgare.
units.tr: Master. The Apostle seems to hint at this in several places. In 1 Corinthians 12 he clearly tries to prove, by the example of the members of the body, that each member, which seems to have some concern for the others, ought to be anxious about them. Hence the Apostle says in the same place: "There should be no schism in the body, but the members should have care for one another in the same way. If one member suffers, all the members suffer with it; if one member is honoured, all the members rejoice with it." From these words it is plainly gathered that, since we are members of one body, each one ought to be concerned for all. The gloss says: "no schism, that is, discord in the human body or in the Church, where there ought to be unity; rather, let all the members be concerned, so that they tend to the same thing, that is, to a concern which is the same, so that they are no less concerned for another than for themselves." From this it is openly gathered that all ought to have concern for all. The Apostle also seems plainly to suggest this in Ephesians 4, when he says: "walk worthily of the calling to which you have been called, with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love, eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace." From these words it is plainly held that, just as all ought to bear with one another, so they ought to be concerned for one another, lest unity among them be broken. But the unity of the Spirit among Catholics is broken if the pope should become a heretic. Therefore all who are members of the body of Christ ought to be concerned lest the Catholic faith, which is the foundation of the unity of the Spirit and of all spiritual goods, be corrupted. And so all are bound to listen to those who wish to expose the faithlessness of the heretical pope, who is striving to corrupt the orthodox faith and so to expose the faith to danger. Disciple. Ought then Catholics to set aside their occupations and attend to those who wish to make known the faithlessness of the heretical pope? Master. Those men do not say that everyone is bound to set aside all other occupations. They say that judgment must be made about giving a hearing to those who wish to publish the faithlessness of the heretical pope, just as judgment must be made about other affirmative acts which fall under a precept but do not oblige at every moment; they oblige at the proper place and time, with the required circumstances. Therefore it is not easy to give a fixed rule in particular as to the time when one is bound, by necessity of salvation, to listen to those who wish to publish the faithlessness of the heretical pope.

units.la: Potest tamen dici, quod tunc ad hoc tenetur vnusquisque, quando non habet rationabilem excusationem, quare tunc eos minime audire teneatur. Si enim sit aliis occupationibus vtilibus & vrgentibus occupatus, potest rationabiliter respondere: modo mihi non vacat audire, si autem non sit aliqualiter occupatus, nec impeditus: se excusare non potest, si autem dimittit illos audire, vel qa de periculo fidei minime curat, aut qa reputat facta fidei ad se nullatenus pertinere, vel quia reputat papam catholicum, vt ei conei complaceat aut saltem ei nullatenus displiceat, non audiendo peccat mortaliter, & inter credentes damnabiliter papæ hæretico (licet nulli errori eius explicite credat) est merito computandus.
units.tr: Yet it can be said that each person is bound to this at the time when he has no reasonable excuse for not listening to them then. For if he is occupied with other useful and pressing business, he can reasonably reply, "I have no time to listen now." But if he is not occupied in any way, nor hindered, he cannot excuse himself. If he refuses to hear them, either because he cares nothing for the danger to the faith, or because he thinks that matters of faith do not concern him at all, or because he thinks the pope is Catholic and wishes to please him, or at least not to displease him in any way, then by not listening he sins mortally. Among believers he is rightly counted, to his damnation, as one who believes the heretical pope (although he does not explicitly believe any of his errors).

units.la: Disc. Cerno, quod isti non damnant omnes istos, qui nolunt audire eos, qui volunt perfidiam papæ hæretici diuulgare: sed tantummodo illos, qui absque rationabili causa eos audire recusant, putantes quod nec timor papæ, quem reputant catholicum: nec dilectio ad ipsum: nec odium ad publicantes perfidiam eius: nec aliquid tale eos valeat excusare: sed solummodo vtilior occupatio, cui sunt intenti, aut alicuius periculi maioris vitatio, diuulgationis inutilitas vel aliud simile eosdem apud Deum valeat excusare, & ad istam intentionem aliquas rationes (si quas audisti vel vidisti, aut etiam cogitasti sine magna discussione causa abbreuiationis breuiter tangendo) allega. Magist.
units.tr: Disciple. I see that these men do not condemn all those who are unwilling to hear those who wish to publish the faithlessness of the heretical pope, but only those who refuse to hear them without a reasonable cause. They think that neither fear of the pope, whom they regard as Catholic, nor love for him, nor hatred of those who publish his faithlessness, nor anything of that kind can excuse such people. Only a more useful occupation to which they are devoted, or the avoidance of some greater danger, or the uselessness of publishing, or something similar, could excuse them before God. For this purpose, bring forward some reasons, whatever you have heard or seen or even thought, touching on them briefly without a long discussion for the sake of brevity. Master.

units.la: Sexta ratio est haec. Qui non est ex se sufficiens ad agendum recte ea, quae incumbunt sibi, aliorum qui eum cupiunt informare debet audire consilia, sed quilibet debet esse sollicitus, sicut probatum existit, de fide catholica, ne per quemcunque aliqualiter subuertatur: debetque corrumpere fidem volentibus quantum sibi licet pro gradu suo & officio obuiare viriliter, ergo si non est sufficienter informatus de illis, qui volunt fidem destruere, debet audire eorum consilia, & informationes, qui eum cupiunt de talibus informare. Minor ex his quae dicta sunt supra in ratione quinta videtur posse probari. Maior autem auctoritatibus diuinae scripturae insinuatur aperte. Eccles. 32. sic scribitur: fili sine consilio nihil facies: & post factum non poenitebis, & Prouerbior. 13. c. vbi ait Salomo. qui autem sapiens est audit consilia, & idem in eodem ait: qui autem cum consilio agunt, reguntur sapientia, & vt legitur Tobiae 4. Tobias filium suum instruens ait: consilium autem a sapiente semper perquire.
units.tr: The sixth reason is this. One who is not sufficient in himself to act rightly in what falls to him must hear the counsels of others who seek to inform him. But everyone ought to be concerned, as has been proved, for the Catholic faith, lest it be subverted by anyone at all. And one who is able ought to resist manfully, as far as it is permitted him according to his rank and office, those who wish to corrupt the faith. Therefore, if he is not sufficiently informed about those who wish to destroy the faith, he ought to hear their counsels and information, and also those who seek to inform him of such things. The minor premise can be proved from what was said above in the fifth reason. The major premise is plainly suggested by the authority of divine Scripture. Ecclesiasticus 32 reads: "Son, do nothing without counsel, and you will not repent after the deed." Proverbs 13 says, where Solomon speaks: "but he who is wise listens to counsels," and again in the same place: "but those who act with counsel are governed by wisdom." And as is read in Tobit 4, Tobit instructing his son says: "always seek counsel from a wise man."

units.la: Ex quibus aliisque verbis quam pluribus colligitur euidenter, quod in arduis negotiis non solum audienda, sed etiam requirenda sunt consilia peritorum, cum ergo negotium fidei, quando scilicet fides catholica impugnatur praecipue ab illo, qui plurimos trahere potest ad suos errores, cuiusmodi est papa haereticus, sit arduissimum negotium: in hoc casu oportet non solum audire, sed requirere consilium & informationes eorum qui perfidiam papæ haeretici non ignorant, vndecunque innotuit eis.
units.tr: From these and very many other words it is plainly gathered that in difficult affairs not only should counsels be heard, but the counsels of experts should also be sought. Since therefore the matter of faith is a most difficult affair, namely when the Catholic faith is attacked, especially by one who can draw very many to his errors, as the heretical pope can, in this case it is necessary not only to hear but to seek the counsel and information of those who do not ignore the faithlessness of the heretical pope, from whatever source it has come to their knowledge.

units.la: Discipul. Quamuis antea cogitauerim, quod rationes istae nequaquam discuterentur prolixe: volo tamen contra istam mouere duas instantias, quarum prima est: quod quamuis in arduis peritorum sunt informationes & consilia requirenda: non tamen sunt requirenda, nisi ab his, ad quos huiusmodi spectant negotia. Negotium autem fidei quando papa esset haereticus, non spectat nisi tantummodo ad praelatos, & non ad simplices nec ad laicos, vnde ad religiosos pauperes & ad alios, nisi essent Cardinales vel Patriarchae aut episcopi, nullatenus pertinaret, & ideo alii non tenerentur audire volentes perfidiam papae haeretici declarare: praesertim si fuerit a superioribus eis iniunctum vel praeceptum, quod eos audire non debeant. Secunda instantia est, quod quamuis in arduis sint consilia requirenda, non oportet consilia quaerere, nisi quando videtur periculum imminere, & ideo illi qui nesciunt papam esse haereticum, cum non sentiant ex perfidia papae haeretici aliquod periculum imminere: non tenentur eos audire, qui volunt eos de perfidia papae haeretici informare, hae sunt instantiae quae rationem praedictam totaliter videntur refellere: & tamen quomodo respondere contingat ad ipsas, enarra. Magist. Putant nonnulli, quod istae instantiae ex ignorantia intelligentiae scripturarum emanant, primam autem instantiam dicunt absurditatem perniciosam & periculosam & haereticalem ac etiam stultissimam continere, quae est illorum assertio & inuentio, qui suam desidiam, immo nequitiam pessimam palliare nituntur, est autem haec absurditas, quod negotium fidei, quando papa esset haereticus, nullo modo spectat ad simplices & pauperes, sed solummodo ad praelatos, puta Cardinales, archiepiscopos, & episcopos: & non ad pauperes religiosos, nec ad laicos, nec ad clericos sub episcopis constitutos, quam absurditatem Diabolicam arbitrantur ex astutia Diaboli ad subuersionem fidei adinuentam, quomodo enim defensio patriae pertinebit ad omnes, si defensio fidei, quae est amplius quam patriam defendere, non spectat ad omnes? aut quomodo defensio propriae vitae pertinebit ad subiectos simplices & pauperes, si defensio fidei, quae debet esse vnicuique cárior, quam vita corporalis non spectat ad omnes?
units.tr: Disciple. Although I had thought beforehand that these arguments would by no means be discussed at length, I nevertheless wish to raise two objections against them. The first is this: although in difficult matters the information and counsel of experts must be sought, yet they need be sought only from those to whom such matters belong. But the matter of faith, if the pope were a heretic, belongs only to prelates, and not to simple people or laymen. Hence it would in no way pertain to poor religious and others, unless they were cardinals, patriarchs or bishops. So others would not be bound to listen to those who wish to declare the faithlessness of the heretical pope, especially if their superiors had enjoined or commanded them not to hear such people. The second objection is that although counsels must be sought in difficult matters, it is not necessary to seek counsel unless danger seems to threaten. So those who do not know that the pope is a heretic, since they do not perceive any danger threatening from his faithlessness, are not bound to listen to those who wish to inform them of it. These are the objections which seem to overturn the aforesaid reason entirely. Yet explain how it may be possible to answer them. Master. Some think that these objections arise from ignorance of the understanding of the Scriptures. They say that the first objection contains a pernicious, dangerous, heretical and most foolish absurdity. It is the assertion and invention of those who strive to cloak their sloth, or rather their most wicked wickedness. The absurdity is this: that the matter of faith, if the pope were a heretic, in no way pertains to simple and poor people, but only to prelates, namely cardinals, archbishops and bishops, and not to poor religious, nor to laymen, nor to clergy placed under bishops. They judge this a diabolical absurdity, devised by the devil's cunning for the subversion of the faith. For how will the defence of the fatherland pertain to everyone, if the defence of the faith, which is far more than defending the fatherland, does not pertain to everyone? Or how will the defence of one's own life pertain to simple and poor subjects, if the defence of the faith, which ought to be dearer to each person than bodily life, does not pertain to everyone?

units.la: Discipul. An negotium fidei spectat ad omnes, discussum est libro 6. ideo de hoc ad praesens pertranseas: & tantummodo dic, quomodo respondetur ad hoc, quod dicitur quod si superiores iniunxerint subditis ne audiant illos, qui volunt perfidiam papae haeretici diuulgare, non debent eos audire. Magist. Respondetur, quod in hoc casu est magna cautela & prudentia procedendum, & forma mandati est diligentissime inspicienda: aliaeque circumstantiae subtiliter sunt pensandae. Ad cuius cutidentiam dicitur esse sciendum, quod sicut ex sacris canonibus 3. quaest. 3. si quis episcopus & c. non enim, & c. si Dominus, & aliis innumeris colligitur euidenter, non esse superioribus obediendum in omnibus, si enim aliquid praecipiunt, quod est contrarium scripturis diuinis, aut iuri naturali, aut vergat in patens dispendium honoris vel fidei orthodoxae, vel communis boni, aut in salutis spiritualis & corporalis detrimentum: non debent eis subditi obedire: sed sententiam beati Gregorii debent in memoria retinere, qui (vt legitur 2. quaest. 7. capitul. admonendi,) ait: Admonendi sunt subditi, ne plus quam expediat sint subiecti: ne dum student plus quam necesse hominibus subiici compellantur vitia eorum venerari, & ita in dispendium communis boni subditi superioribus nullatenus debent obedire. Per hoc ad propositum respondetur. Quod si subditis mandati... mandant superiores, nedum vt tales volentes perfidiâ Papæ hæretici declarare, nullatenus audiant, nullam causam rationabilem (quare audire non debeant) assignantes: subditi (tanquam sinceri fidei zelatores & fidem omni homini præferentes) eis rescribent, quod eos intendunt audire ad instar prælati, cui mandat Alexander tertius, vt habetur extr. de haereticis c. si quando, quod si mandatum apostolicum adimplere non debeat, causam rationabilē (quare adimplere nō valeat) per literas studeat intimare: ita in hoc casu subditi debent suis superioribus intimare, quod eorum mandatum adimplere non debeant, dum tamen in audiendo tales nullum sit periculum. Non audiendo enim posset grande fidei periculum imminere. Si autem in tali mandato causa rationabilis exprimatur, quare subditi audire non debeant volentes Papæ haeretici perfidiam declarare, quia sunt de calumnia, mendaciis vel detractione aut inimicitia conuicti, non essent (saltem in publico) audiendi: nisi verisimiliter appareat, quod vias scirent dare probabiles, quibus perfidia Papæ haeretici panderetur. In omnibus enim talibus non voluntatem prælatorum, qui forte timore, ambitione, vel cupiditate essent corrupti, sed honorem Dei, & defensionem fidei deberent attendere, & illud dictum Pet. Actor. 5. obedire oportet Deo magis quam hominibus, memoriter retinere. Discip.
units.tr: Disciple. Whether the business of the faith concerns everyone was discussed in book 6, so you may pass over that point for now. Tell me only how to answer the objection that if superiors order subjects not to listen to those who wish to make known the perfidy of a heretical pope, they ought not to listen to them. Master. The answer is that in this case great caution and prudence must be exercised, the form of the command must be examined most carefully, and the other circumstances must be weighed finely. For the sake of this caution, it should be known that, as is clearly gathered from the sacred canons, 3. quaest. 3, si quis episcopus, etc., non enim, etc., si Dominus, and from countless others, subjects are not bound to obey superiors in all things. If superiors command something contrary to the divine Scriptures or to the natural law, or tending to the manifest loss of honour, of the orthodox faith, or of the common good, or to the detriment of spiritual or bodily salvation, subjects must not obey them. Rather, they ought to keep in mind the saying of blessed Gregory, who (as we read in 2. quaest. 7, cap. admonendi) says: Subjects are to be admonished not to be more subject than is expedient, lest, while they strive to submit to men more than necessary, they be compelled to venerate their vices. Thus, to the point, subjects may in no way obey superiors to the detriment of the common good. By this the question is answered. But if superiors order subjects not merely not to listen to those who wish to declare the perfidy of a heretical pope, but give no reasonable cause why they should not listen, then the subjects (as sincere zealots of the faith, who prefer the faith to every man) should write back to them that they intend to listen, in the manner of the prelate to whom Alexander III commands, as we have it in extr. de haereticis, c. si quando, that if he ought not to carry out an apostolic mandate, he should take care to make known by letter the reasonable cause why he cannot carry it out. So in this case subjects should inform their superiors that they ought not to carry out their command, provided that in listening to such men there is no danger. For by not listening a great danger to the faith could threaten. If, however, a reasonable cause is stated in such a command why subjects should not listen to those who wish to declare the perfidy of a heretical pope, namely that these men are convicted of calumny, lies, slander or enmity, they would not be (at least in public) to be listened to, unless it appeared likely that they knew how to offer plausible ways by which the perfidy of a heretical pope might be laid open. For in all such cases one must attend not to the will of the prelates, who may perhaps be corrupted by fear, ambition or greed, but to the honour of God and the defence of the faith, and keep in memory the saying of Peter in Acts 5: We ought to obey God rather than men. Disciple.

units.la: Dic ad secundam instantiam. Magist. Respondetur quod non solum arduis in negociis, vbi peritia propria non suppetit: tunc sunt peritorum consilia requirenda, quando quis videret periculum imminere: sed etiam quando eminens periculum nunciatur; maxime si à fide dignis & prouidis intimatur non volentibus denunciato periculo obuiare, attendat illud apostoli 1. ad Thessal. 15. Cum dixerint pax & securitas, tunc & repentinus superueniet etiam interitus, (scil. Fidei orthodoxæ. Sicut in corporibus infirmorum postquam conualuerint, forte superueniet nonnullorum interitus corporalis. Discip. Breuiter tange alias rationes. Magist. Septima ratio est, quæ ex prædictis accipit fulcimentum. Quæ potest sic formari. Illi debent audiri, qui grande periculum omnibus imminere asserunt & affirmant, ne audire nolentes cum eos apprehendit periculum necessitate dicant intra se illud Sapient. 5. Poenitentiam agentes & præangustia spiritus gementes his scilicet qui nobis nunciauerunt pericula quæ super euenerunt nobis: bi sunt quos aliquando habuimus in derisum & in similitudinem improperii nos insensati vitam illorum existimabamus sine honore. Vnde de nolentibus audire pericula nunciantes dicitur Ezech. 33. audiens autem quisquis ille est sonitum buccinae & non obseruauerit venerit que gladius & tulerit eum: sanguis ipsius super caput ipsius erit: sonum buccinae audiuit, & non se obseruauit, sanguis eius in ipso erit. Ille audit sonum buccinae, qui audit in confuso, quod sunt aliqua imminentia pericula putantes: sed non obseruat se quicunque in speciali ad occurrendum periculis annunciantibus renuit informari. Et ideo cum periculum apprehendit ipsum, se per ignorantiam non potest excusare: sed sanguis ipsius super caput eius erit, sicut sunt aliqui volentes catholicos de perfidia Papæ haeretici informare, & grandia pericula futura populo Christiano prædicunt. Ergo qui non audierint diligenter informationes eorum, nequaquam poterunt per ignorantiam excusari, si Papa haereticus infecerit populum Christianum. Discip. Auctoritas Ezechiæ loquitur de speculatore super specula, seu populum constituto. Et ideo si episcopus vel prælatus, qui est speculator super subditos constitutus nunciaret Papam esse haereticum, & illi informationes nolint audire non essent per ignorantiam excusati. Secus est de illis, qui nunciant Papam esse haereticū, & non sunt speculatores super populum constituti. Quia tales audiri non debent. Magist. Dicitur quod ista responsio non impedit rationem prædictam: quia licet prædicta verba Ezechielis principaliter intelligantur de speculatoribus super populum constitutis: tamen debent etiam de quibuscunque nunciantibus imminentia pericula Papæ vel personæ cuiuscunque intelligi. Cuius ratio assignatur, quia propter charitatem & amicitiam, qua vnusquisque debet proximum suum diligere, sicut seipsum, quilibet quantum ad simplicem admonitionem & informationem ac simplicem instructionem mutuamque defensionem, & subuentionem, quantum licet cuicunque pro gradu suo & officio debet esse alterius speculator, custos, defensor, protector, adiutor, informator, consiliarius, & instructor: licet nullus debeat super proximum suum iurisdictionem, potestatem aut auctoritatem indebite vsurpare. Cum ergo quilibet debeat speculatorem nunciantem gladium venientem audire: quod non est verum tantum modo de speculatore, qui iurisdictione & potestate fungitur super alios, sed de quocunque speculatore ingruentia pericula aduertente: sequitur quod qui nunciant pericula, quæ intendit Papa haereticus, licet non sint prælati, debent audiri. Octava ratio est hæc. Vnusquisque tenetur audire illum, qui eum informare tenetur. Sicut discipulus tenetur audire doctorem: qui doctor tenetur discipulum informare. Et filius tenetur audire patrem: qui filium debet instruere. Sic etiam vicinus debet vicinum audire: si vicinus vicinum informare tenetur, qu sacra scriptura insinuare videtur Eccl. 23. vbi scribitur, vbi auditus non est, non effundas sermonē. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, qu vbi auditores nequaquā tenetur audire, nullus tenetur sermone effundere. Quare vbi aliquis tenetur sermone effundere, ibi sunt aliqui qui tenentur sermonem audire. Sed scientes Papam haereticum niti fidem orthodoxa corrumpere, & seducere fideles de necessitate salutis tenentur (certis circumstantiis obseruatis) instruere fideles ignorantes de perfidia & intentione iniqua Papæ haeretici, vt se obseruent & pro loco, & tempore, modis sibi conuenientibus eidem haeretico toto posse resistant. Ergo & ignorantes Papam esse haereticum debent audire eos, qui eos volunt de perfidia & iniquis conaminibus Papæ haeretici informare. Quod autem scientes Papam esse haereticum tenentur ignorantibus eius perfidiam reuelare, probatur ex hoc, quia non minus debet vnusquisque praeseruare (si potest) proximum à morte spirituali, quam à morte corporali. Sed si videt alium volentem proximum suum neci tradere corporali, debet hoc ei vt sibi præcaueat intimare. Ergo multo magis si scit Papam hæreticum satagere omnes Christianos occidere spiritualiter eos inficiendo hæretica prauitate: debet inescios, (si conuenienter potest) de iniqua malitia Papæ hæretici informare. Nona ratio est hæc. Si quis tenetur peccata vitare, ita (si potest) tenetur pericula tam corporalia quam spiritualia tam in se quantum in aliis præcauere. Sed propter hoc quod quilibet tenetur vitare peccata debet corrigentem se audire. Ergo similiter tenetur audire illum, qui pericula tam corporalia quam spiritualia denunciare conatur. Sed declarantes perfidiam Papæ hæretici & pericula omnium fidelium, tam corporalia quam spiritualia denunciare noscuntur. Ergo audire eis negare non debet.
units.tr: Tell me the second objection. Master. The answer is that counsel of experts must be sought not only in difficult matters, where one's own skill is lacking, when one sees a danger impending, but also when a imminent danger is announced, especially if it is announced by trustworthy and prudent men to those who are unwilling to meet the announced danger. Let them heed the saying of the Apostle, 1 Thess. 15: When they say, "peace and security," then sudden destruction will come upon them (namely of the orthodox faith). Just as in the bodies of the sick, after they have recovered, perhaps the death of some bodily part will come upon them. Disciple. Briefly touch on the other reasons. Master. The seventh reason is one that receives support from what has been said. It may be formed thus: those ought to be listened to who assert and affirm that a great danger threatens everyone, lest those who refuse to listen, when danger seizes them, say to themselves that saying of Wisdom 5: Repenting and groaning with anguish of spirit, these are they whom we once held in derision and as a byword of reproach. We fools thought their life madness and their end without honour. Hence of those who refuse to listen to men announcing dangers it is said in Ezek. 33: But whoever hears the sound of the trumpet and does not take warning, and the sword comes and takes him away, his blood shall be upon his own head. He heard the sound of the trumpet, and did not take warning; his blood shall be upon him. He hears the sound of the trumpet who hears in a confused way that some dangers are impending, but thinks about them; yet he does not take warning who refuses to be informed in particular so as to meet the dangers announced. Therefore, when the danger seizes him, he cannot excuse himself through ignorance, but his blood will be upon his own head, just as there are some who wish to inform Catholics about the perfidy of a heretical pope and foretell great dangers to the Christian people. Therefore those who have not carefully listened to their information will in no way be able to excuse themselves through ignorance, if the heretical pope has infected the Christian people. Disciple. The authority of Ezekiel speaks of a watchman set upon a watch-tower, or of one appointed over the people. So if a bishop or prelate, who is appointed as watchman over his subjects, were to announce that the pope is a heretic, and they were unwilling to hear his information, they would not be excused through ignorance. It is otherwise with those who announce that the pope is a heretic and are not appointed watchmen over the people; such men ought not to be heard. Master. It is said that this answer does not weaken the foregoing reason, because although the words of Ezekiel are principally understood of watchmen appointed over the people, yet they must also be understood of whoever announces impending dangers, whether concerning the pope or any person whatever. The reason given is this: on account of the charity and friendship by which each person ought to love his neighbour as himself, everyone, as far as simple admonition, information, simple instruction and mutual defence and aid go, and as far as is lawful for anyone according to his rank and office, ought to be the watchman, guardian, defender, protector, helper, informer, counsellor and instructor of another, although no one ought to usurp unjustly jurisdiction, power or authority over his neighbour. Since, then, everyone ought to hear a watchman announcing the sword coming, and this is true not only of a watchman who exercises jurisdiction and power over others, but of any watchman who notices impending dangers, it follows that those who announce dangers which the heretical pope intends ought to be heard, even if they are not prelates. The eighth reason is this. Everyone is bound to hear the one who is bound to inform him, as a disciple is bound to hear a teacher, and the teacher is bound to inform the disciple; and a son is bound to hear his father, who ought to instruct his son. So also a neighbour ought to hear a neighbour, if a neighbour is bound to inform a neighbour, which Holy Scripture seems to indicate in Ecclus. 23, where it is written: Where there is no hearer, do not pour out your words. From these words it is gathered that where hearers are in no way bound to listen, no one is bound to pour out words. Therefore where someone is bound to pour out words, there are some who are bound to hear them. But those who know that the heretical pope strives to corrupt the orthodox faith and to seduce the faithful are bound, from the necessity of salvation (with certain circumstances observed), to instruct the faithful who are ignorant of the perfidy and wicked intention of the heretical pope, so that they may take heed and, according to place and time and in ways suitable to themselves, resist that heretic with all their power. Therefore those who are ignorant that the pope is a heretic ought also to listen to those who wish to inform them about the perfidy and wicked attempts of the heretical pope. That those who know the pope to be a heretic are bound to reveal his perfidy to those ignorant of it is proved from this: each person ought no less to preserve (if he can) his neighbour from spiritual death than from bodily death. But if he sees another wishing to hand his neighbour over to bodily death, he ought to warn him of this so that he may take precautions. Therefore much more, if he knows that the heretical pope is labouring to kill all Christians spiritually by infecting them with heretical depravity, he ought to inform the unwitting (if he can do so suitably) of the wicked malice of the heretical pope. The ninth reason is this. If someone is bound to avoid sins, then, if he can, he is bound to guard against dangers, both bodily and spiritual, both in himself and in others. But because everyone is bound to avoid sins, he ought to hear one who corrects him. Therefore likewise he is bound to hear the one who strives to announce dangers, both bodily and spiritual. But those who declare the perfidy of the heretical pope and announce the dangers of all the faithful, both bodily and spiritual, are known to do so. Therefore he ought not to refuse to hear them.

units.la: CAP. XI.
units.tr: CAP. XI.

units.la: Vbi inquiritur de eis, qui laborant ignorantia damnabili, nolentes scil. scire Papam esse hæreticum, qui tamen vere est hæreticus, & qualiter sint tenendi, & qualiter puniendi.
units.tr: Where it is inquired about those who labour under culpable ignorance, namely those unwilling to know that the Pope is a heretic, although he truly is a heretic, and how they are to be treated and how punished.

units.la: Discipulus. Quantum intelligo omnes rationes prædictæ, etiam forte omnes aliæ quæ possunt fieri ad conclusionem eandem, duobus fundamentis inniti videntur. Quorum primum est, quod vnusquisque tenetur proximos suos sicut seipsum diligere, & eis facere quod vellet sibi fieri. Secundum est, quod fides catholica est omni homini præferenda, vt ob timorem, amorem, & fauorem, vel gratiam cuiuscunq; mortalis nullatenus omittatur, quod ad saluationem, exaltationem & dilatationem fidei Christianæ noscitur pertinere. Quare pro conclusione prædicta desine allegare: quia aliæ rationes eandem virtutem forte cum prædictis habent. Nunc dic qua pœna secundum assertionem prædictam ignorantes ignorantia damnabili Papam esse hæreticum, & de eius perfidia nolentes informari, sunt plectendi, & an sint hæretici vel credentes, aut fautores Papæ hæretici reputandi. Magist. Respondetur, quod ad sciendum qua pœna ignorantes ignorantia damnabili Papam esse hæreticum: quia nolunt scire, vel etiam quia non curant aut contemnunt scire, sint plectendi, oportet primo videre, an sint hæretici credentes, an fautores vel defensores Papæ hæretici iudicandi.
units.tr: Disciple. As far as I understand, all the aforementioned arguments, and perhaps all the others that can be brought to the same conclusion, seem to rest on two foundations. The first is that everyone is bound to love his neighbours as himself and to do to them what he would wish done to himself. The second is that the Catholic faith is to be preferred to every man, so that for fear, love, favour or the grace of any mortal it is in no way neglected, since it is known to pertain to the salvation, exaltation and spread of the Christian faith. Therefore, for the aforesaid conclusion, stop alleging, since the other arguments perhaps have the same force as those already given. Now tell me, according to the aforesaid assertion, what punishment is to be inflicted on those who through culpable ignorance do not know that the Pope is a heretic, and who are unwilling to be informed of his perfidy, and whether they are to be regarded as heretics, or as believers, or as supporters of the heretical Pope. Master. It is answered that, to know what punishment is to be inflicted on those who through culpable ignorance do not know that the Pope is a heretic, whether because they are unwilling to know, or also because they do not care or despise knowing, we must first see whether they are to be judged heretical believers, or supporters or defenders of the heretical Pope.

units.la: Disc. Ab hoc primo incipias. Magist. Non tamen apparet, quod tales non sunt hæretici stricte accipiendo hæreticorum vocabulum. Nec sunt proprie fautores vel defensores Papæ hæretici. Quia fautio & similiter defensio aliquem actum positiuum exteriorem importare videntur. Tales autem ignorantes per hoc solummodo, quod nolunt vel non curant aut contemnunt scire Papam esse hæreticum, nullum actum exteriorem exercent. Ergo propter hoc solummodo non sunt fautores vel defensores Papæ hæretici iudicandi. Dicitur ergo quod sunt credentes, non quidem explicite erroribus Papæ (cum nesciant eum errare) sed sunt credentes ipsi Papæ hæretico ipsum esse catholicum damnabiliter reputantes. Et isto modo videtur accipi nomen credentium extr. de hereticis excommunicamus primo. Aliter autem accipitur nomen credentium eodem capitulo excommunicamus 2. Quod vero tales Papam esse catholicum, quando est hæreticus damnabiliter, reputantes credentes valeant nuncupari, videtur posse probari. Nam omnes damnabiliter errantes (& potissime ex adhæsione ad personam Papæ hæretici) vel sunt credentes, vel fautores, vel defensores, vel receptatores. Non enim plures inveniuntur, qui propter crimen ex adhæsione ad personas hæreticorum secundum iura sunt puniendi. Sed qui damnabiliter reputat Papam esse catholicum, qui est hæreticus, non est ex hoc solummodo fautor vel defensor Papæ hæretici, sicut dictum est prius. Nec est propter hoc receptator Papæ hæretici. Ergo propter hoc solummodo debet inter credentes merito computari. Nec propter hoc est hæreticus iudicandus. Quia erroribus Papæ hæretici minime credit. Nec forte crederet, si sciret errores eius. Quia ex hoc solummodo peccat, quia non vult, aut contemnit, vel non curat Papam esse hæreticum. Nullum etiam præstando auxilium, consilium, defensionem, receptationem, vel fauorem: nec forte actu ei obedit, licet forsitan sit obedire paratus: imo potest contingere quod ex alia causa quam ex causa hæresis, puta propter contentionem inter eum & Papam hæreticum de temporalibus vel ex causa alia ei renuit obedire, paratus eum totus viribus impugnare: nolens tamen scire quod sit hæreticus: nec volens permittere quod hæreticus publicetur.
units.tr: Disc. Begin with this first point. Magist. Yet it does not appear that such persons are heretics, strictly taking the word heretic. Nor are they properly supporters or defenders of the heretical Pope. For support and likewise defence seem to imply some positive external act. But such ignorant persons, merely because they are unwilling, or do not care or despise knowing that the Pope is a heretic, perform no external act. Therefore on this ground alone they are not to be judged supporters or defenders of the heretical Pope. It is said, then, that they are believers, not indeed explicitly in the errors of the Pope (since they do not know that he errs), but they are believers in the heretical Pope himself, culpably regarding him as Catholic. And in this way the name of believers seems to be taken in extra de hereticis, excommunicamus primo. But the name of believers is taken otherwise in the same chapter excommunicamus 2. That such persons, culpably regarding the Pope as Catholic when he is culpably a heretic, may be called believers, seems capable of proof. For all those who err culpably (and especially through adherence to the person of a heretical Pope) are either believers, or supporters, or defenders, or harbourers. For no more categories are found of those who by law are to be punished for the crime of adherence to the persons of heretics. But he who culpably regards the Pope, who is a heretic, as Catholic, is not on this ground alone a supporter or defender of the heretical Pope, as was said before. Nor is he on this account a harbourer of the heretical Pope. Therefore on this ground alone he is rightly counted among the believers. Nor is he on this account to be judged a heretic, because he does not at all believe the errors of the heretical Pope. Nor would he perhaps believe them, if he knew his errors. For he sins only in this, that he is unwilling, or despises, or does not care to know that the Pope is a heretic. He gives no help, counsel, defence, harbouring or favour, nor perhaps does he actually obey him, although he may be ready to obey him. Indeed it can happen that for some cause other than heresy, for instance because of a dispute between himself and the heretical Pope over temporal matters, or for some other reason, he refuses to obey him, being ready to assail him with all his strength, yet unwilling to know that he is a heretic, and unwilling to allow that he be published as a heretic.
