Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod absque omni utilitate bonorum & cum damno eorum & sine conversione & emendatione malorum non est impiis & infidelibus catholica veritas propalanda. & ita in hoc casu tacere licet; nec tacens consentit, quemadmodum inter Saracenos existens fidelis, inter quos non posset proficere, non intelligeretur eorum consentire erroribus, licet contra eos minime clamaret.
units.tr: The second, namely that if the condition were such that danger to the faith or to the faithful would follow, because the heretical Pope and his accomplices would be inflamed to outward persecution of the faithful, or to spreading the error more widely with danger to many, then the silent man would not sin mortally. This is proved by the text of Matthew 7: "Do not give what is holy to the dogs." From these words it is gathered that, without any benefit to the good, and with their harm, and without the conversion and amendment of the wicked, the Catholic truth is not to be proclaimed to the impious and unbelieving. And so in this case it is lawful to keep silent; nor does the silent man consent, just as a believer living among the Saracens, among whom he could not make progress, would not be understood to consent to their errors, even though he did not cry out against them.

units.la: DISCIP. Dic quomodo secundum sententiam istam Glossae, quae in contrarium sonare videntur, debent intelligi.
units.tr: DISCIP. Tell me how, according to this opinion, the Glosses, which seem to sound to the contrary, are to be understood.

units.la: MAGIST. Dicitur quod illae debent intelligi de negociis, in quibus vertitur proprium commodum vel incommodum temporale ipsius taciturnitatis. vbi autem ex taciturnitate ipsius potest provenire diminutio honoris diuini vel damnum spirituale proximorum: puta aversio a fide vel scandalum infirmorum per reclamationem aut contradictionem ipsius (licet non posset prohibere vel impedire sive retrahere Papam a sua intentione nefaria) posset tamen catholicos consolari & confirmare in fide, & ne crederent Papae haeretico praeseruare, reclamare tenetur. & ideo taciturnitas eius, per quam diuinus honor subtrahitur: & utilitas proximorum necessario impediretur, non est absque peccato mortali. quia ista taciturnitas tam amori Dei, quam fidei manifestae repugnat.
units.tr: MAGIST. It is said that they ought to be understood of matters in which the temporal advantage or disadvantage of the silent man himself is at stake. But where by his silence there may arise a diminution of the honour of God or a spiritual loss to his neighbours (for example, the turning away of others from the faith, or the scandal of the weak, through his protest or contradiction; even if he could not prohibit or prevent or turn the Pope from his wicked purpose), yet he could console and confirm Catholics in the faith and keep them from trusting the heretical Pope; he is bound to protest. And so his silence, by which the honour of God is withdrawn and the benefit of his neighbours would necessarily be hindered, is not without mortal sin, because such silence is contrary both to the love of God and to the open profession of the faith.

units.la: CAP. XXXII.
units.tr: CAP. XXXII.

units.la: In quo dicitur de consensu consilii & cooperatione.
units.tr: In which it is said concerning consent of counsel and cooperation.

units.la: DISCIP. Quia non est verisimile, quod Papa requireret Cardinales super aliqua assertione haereticali, quam diffinire vel determinare intenderet: & eosdem sustineret & non cogeret respondere. & ideo transeo ad consensum consilii. de quo dico an omnes consulendo consentientes, quod Papa quamcunque haeresim solenniter diffiniat & determinet, peccent mortaliter, & an sint fautores haereticae pravitatis.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Because it is not likely that the Pope would consult the Cardinals about some heretical assertion which he intended to define or determine, and would allow them to remain silent and not compel them to answer, I therefore pass on to the consent of counsel. Concerning this I ask whether all who consent by giving counsel, to the effect that the Pope may solemnly define and determine any heresy whatever, sin mortally, and whether they are supporters of heretical wickedness.

units.la: MAGIST. Ad hoc respondetur, quod omnes consentientes huiusmodi peccant mortaliter, nec possent per quamcunque ignorantiam excusari. Quam vero peccent mortaliter, videtur aperte posse probari. Nam de consulente negari non potest: quin aperte & expresse sit consentiens. consentiens autem peccat. Papa autem diffiniendo sive determinando assertionem, quae est haeretica, peccat mortaliter. ergo consulens, quod eam determinet, mortaliter peccat.
units.tr: MASTER. To this it is answered that all who consent in this way sin mortally, nor could they be excused by any ignorance whatever. That they sin mortally can clearly be proved. For it cannot be denied of the counsellor that he is openly and expressly consenting, and one who consents sins. But the Pope, in defining or determining an assertion which is heretical, sins mortally. Therefore the counsellor who advises that he define it sins mortally.

units.la: DISCIP. Quamuis mihi videtur probabile, quod consentientes consulendo diffinitioni haereticali Papae, si non possint per ignorantiam excusari, peccent mortaliter: videtur tamen quod ignorans assertionem Papae esse haereticam: per ignorantiam valeat excusari saltem a peccato mortali. nam si consulens Papae, quod assertionem haereticalem diffiniat, peccat mortaliter: peccatum suum est consimile peccato Papae. peccatum autem Papae est peccatum haeresis. ergo peccatum consulentis est peccatum haeresis. sed hoc non videtur, quia ignorans non ex ipso est haereticus quod ignorans. ergo cum iste sit talis ignorans, non videtur quod sit haereticus reputandus.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Although it seems probable to me that those who consent by counsel to the heretical definition of the Pope, if they cannot be excused by ignorance, sin mortally, yet it seems that one who is ignorant that the Pope's assertion is heretical can be excused, at least from mortal sin. For if the counsellor who advises the Pope to define a heretical assertion sins mortally, his sin is similar to the sin of the Pope. But the sin of the Pope is the sin of heresy. Therefore the sin of the counsellor is the sin of heresy. But this does not seem so, because one who is ignorant is not heretical on account of the very fact that he is ignorant. Therefore, since he is such an ignorant person, it does not seem that he should be regarded as a heretic.

units.la: MAG. Adhuc requiritur quod iste consulens ultra ignorantiam addat pertinaciam, velle scilicet pertinaciter adhaerere assertioni haereticali. & ideo sicut Papa diffiniens est pertinax, & ideo peccat mortaliter: ita consiliarius eius participans sic in crimine est pertinax: & ideo nullo modo potest per ignorantiam excusari de peccato mortali.
units.tr: MASTER. It is further required that this counsellor, beyond ignorance, add obstinacy, namely the will to cling obstinately to the heretical assertion. And so just as the Pope in defining is obstinate, and therefore sins mortally, so his participating counsellor is obstinate in the crime, and therefore can in no way be excused from mortal sin by ignorance.

units.la: DISCIP. Si non credit se in aliquo obuiare catholicae veritati. quare non potest per ignorantiam excusari: quemadmodum ille, qui opinatur assertionem haereticalem, excusatur: quia non credit se in aliquo obuiare catholicae veritati.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. If he does not believe that he is opposing Catholic truth in any way, why can he not be excused by ignorance, just as one who holds a heretical opinion is excused, because he does not believe he is opposing Catholic truth in any way?

units.la: MAG. Ideo iste non excusatur per quamcunque ignorantiam ad causam tam solennem, sicut debet esse papalis diffinitio, quia nullus debet procedere nec aliquis consulere debet, ut fiat, nisi sit certus certitudine sufficienti, quod talis diffinitio est consona veritati. Opinari tamen potest quis absque tali certitudine. & ideo unus peccat mortaliter, & alius minime.
units.tr: MASTER. This man is not excused by any ignorance concerning a matter so solemn as a papal definition must be, because no one ought to proceed, nor should anyone advise that it be done, unless he is certain with sufficient certainty that such a definition agrees with truth. One may, however, hold an opinion without such certainty. And so one sins mortally and another not at all.

units.la: DISCIP. Nunquid talis consiliarius Papae haeretici est fautor haereticae pravitatis. MAG. Tenetur quod talis consiliarius est aperte fautor haereticae pravitatis, quod probatur sic. consiliarius magis expresse consentit, quam ille qui tacet, licet prohibere possit illud quod fit. sed qui tacet, cum prohibere potest, censetur fautor. ergo multo magis consiliarius censendus est fautor. quare consiliarius Papae in diffinitione haereticali fautor pravitatis haereticae est censendus. Hic sunt duo probanda. Quorum primum est, quod magis fauet consiliarius, quam ille qui tacet, quamuis prohibere possit. Secundum est quod qui tacet cum prohibere potest, fauet. Primum probatur. quia magis fauet committens quam omittens, cum fauere magis videatur peccatum commissionis quam omissionis. sed qui tacet quamuis prohibere possit, magis videtur habere peccatum omissionis. consules autem peccatum commissionis committit. ergo magis proprie & magis directe fauet consiliarius Papae haeretici tali diffinitioni quam tacens. Secundum, scil. quod qui tacet cum prohibere potest, fauet: & ideo tacens qui potest prohibere reclamando vel contradicendo tali diffinitioni est fautor haereticae pravitatis, multipliciter videtur posse probari. Primo quidem per Anastasium ad Damasum Papam, quod allegatum est supra cap. 30. cum dicitur, qui potest obuiare & perturbare peruersos & non facit, nihil aliud quam fauere impietati eorum videtur. & eandem sententiam fere sub eisdem verbis ponit Innocentius Papa, ut legitur dist. 83. c. error. & Iohan. 8. ut legitur di. 86. cap. faciem, & Eleutherius Papa, ut habetur 2. quaest. 7. cap. negligere. Ex quibus verbis colligitur evidenter, quod qui potest obuiare diffinitioni haereticali Papae, & non obuiat, fauet haereticae pravitati.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Is such a counsellor of a heretical Pope not a supporter of heretical wickedness? MASTER. It is held that such a counsellor is clearly a supporter of heretical wickedness, which is proved thus. A counsellor consents more expressly than one who keeps silent, although he could prevent what is done. But one who keeps silent, when he is able to prevent it, is judged a supporter. Therefore much more is the counsellor to be judged a supporter. Wherefore the counsellor of the Pope, in a heretical definition, is to be judged a supporter of heretical wickedness. Here two things are to be proved. The first is that the counsellor supports more than the one who keeps silent, although he could prevent it. The second is that one who keeps silent, when he can prevent it, supports. The first is proved thus: one who commits supports more than one who omits, since supporting seems more a sin of commission than of omission. But one who keeps silent, although he could prevent, seems to have the sin of omission. But the counsellor commits the sin of commission. Therefore the counsellor of a heretical Pope supports such a definition more properly and more directly than the silent man. The second, namely that one who keeps silent when he can prevent supports, and therefore the silent man who can prevent such a definition by protesting or contradicting is a supporter of heretical wickedness, can be proved in many ways. First indeed by Anastasius to Pope Damasus, which was cited above in chapter 30, where it is said: he who can oppose and disturb the perverse and does not, seems to do nothing other than favour their impiety. And Pope Innocent sets forth almost the same sentiment in nearly the same words, as is read in dist. 83, c. error; and John 8, as is read in dist. 86, c. faciem; and Pope Eleutherius, as is found in 2 q. 7, c. negligere. From these words it is clearly gathered that whoever can oppose a heretical definition of the Pope and does not oppose it, favours heretical wickedness.

units.la: DISCIP. Verba praedicta quae possunt obuiare & c. negligere debent intelligi de praelato. Unde dicit Glossa 2. q. 7. c. negligere, quod illud capitulum, quod continet eandem sententiam cum verbis praedictis, debet intelligi de praelatis, ut 23. q. 4. duo ista nomina & q. vlt. praeterea. & ideo qui esset praelatus Papae: & non resisteret diffinitioni haereticali eius, si posset, fauret impietati eius. cardinales autem requisiti super diffinitione haereticali quam Papa intendebat facere sive taceant (cum possunt resistere) sive non taceant, non sunt praelati Papae. quare praedicta de ipsis non debent intelligi.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. The aforesaid words, "who can oppose" etc., "negligere", ought to be understood of a prelate. Hence the Gloss on 2 q. 7, c. negligere, says that the chapter which contains the same sentiment as the words above ought to be understood of prelates, as in 23 q. 4, "duo ista nomina", and q. ult., "praeterea". And so one who were a prelate of the Pope and did not resist his heretical definition, if he could, would favour his impiety. But the cardinals, consulted about a heretical definition which the Pope intended to make, whether they keep silent (when they can resist) or do not keep silent, are not prelates of the Pope. Therefore the aforesaid things ought not to be understood of them.

units.la: MAG. Quod verba praedicta intelligi debeant de tacentibus sive negligentibus obuiare diffinitioni haereticali Papae, Glossa ubi prius aperte insinuare videtur, tum quia dicit, vel intellige, (sc. illud negligere, cum possis perturbare) de atrocibus, & ut quisque tenetur. scilicet perturbare perversos. sed diffinire haereticam pravitatem est inter peruersitates atrocissimas merito computandum. ergo tali diffinitioni quilibet, qui potest, obuiare tenetur. & si non facit, fauet. tum quia Glossa ibidem subdit: vel dic, quod quilibet tenetur prohibere proximum a peccato committendo 11. q. 5. hoc videtur secus in commisso. si ergo Papa intendit contra fidem catholicam diffinire, quilibet qui potest eum prohibere, tenetur. & si non prohibet, sibi fauere convincitur. quod autem dicis de Glossa, quae dicit: quod illud capitulum neglegere, de praelatis debet intelligi: respondetur, quod Gloss. hoc dicit solummodo recitando. Unde dicit, haec verba alii intelligunt de praelatis.
units.tr: MASTER. That the aforesaid words ought to be understood of those who keep silent or neglect to oppose a heretical definition of the Pope, the Gloss earlier seems to hint plainly, both because it says, "or understand" (namely that neglecting, when you could disturb), of the atrocious and as each is bound, namely to disturb the perverse; but to define heretical wickedness is rightly counted among the most atrocious perversities. Therefore every one who is able is bound to oppose such a definition, and if he does not, he favours it. Also because the same Gloss adds: "or say that everyone is bound to prevent his neighbour from committing sin," 11 q. 5; "this seems otherwise in the case of one who has committed." So if the Pope intends to define something against the Catholic faith, everyone who can prevent him is bound; and if he does not prevent it, he is convicted of favouring him. As for what you say of the Gloss, which states that the chapter "negligere" ought to be understood of prelates, it is answered that the Gloss says this only by way of recitation. Hence it says that others understand these words of prelates.

units.la: Discip. Nunquid istorum opinio, quam hic recitat Gloss. potest saluari secundum praedicta?
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Can the opinion of these men, which the Gloss here recites, be saved in accordance with what has been said?

units.la: Magist. Respondetur quod verificari potest iuxta diffinitionem, quam ponit Gloss. 23. q. 4. cap. 1. vbi dicit sic: Aliter debent praelati corrigere delinquentes, alio modo socii. praelatus corrigit increpando, verberando, vt infra c. q. c. 400. similiter 2. q. 5. dominus Deus. Ex quibus verbis patet, quod duplex est correctio. Vna quae spectat ad praelatos: alia quae spectat ad socios & inferiores. & sicut est duplex correctio: ita est duplex obuiatio, & duplex perturbatio peruersorum. quia omnis correctio quandam obuiationem & perturbationem annexam habere videtur. qui enim corrigit alium manifestum, qui obuiat & aliquo modo corrigitur, perturbatur: qui vel correctus corrigitur de eo a peccato, quo errat & perturbatur de peccato commisso vel voluntate committendi, si non corrigitur tunc perturbatur de reprehensione corrigentis siue corripientis. Si igitur illa opinio, quam recitat Gloss. intelligat capitulum de obuiatione & perturbatione peruersorum, quae spectat ad praelatos: sic potest verificari, non de alia. requisiti autem a Papa volente aliquid contra fidem catholicam diffinire seu determinare, non debent obuiare, tanquam praelati, nisi possent aperte probare, quod Papa in sua intentione peruersa esset pertinax: sed debent obuiare tanquam veri & syncerii fidei zelatores, Papam scilicet consiliis, persuasionibus, & reprobationibus haeresis quam intendit a peccato quod proponit conuertendo & a diffinitione haeretica retrahendo, etiam si oportet cum perturbatione & indignatione Papae.
units.tr: MASTER. It is answered that it can be made to agree with the definition which the Gloss gives on 23 q. 4, c. 1, where it says thus: "Prelates ought to correct offenders in one way, companions in another. A prelate corrects by rebuking and beating, as below, c. q. c. 400; likewise 2 q. 5, Dominus Deus." From these words it is clear that correction is twofold: one which belongs to prelates, another which belongs to companions and inferiors. And just as correction is twofold, so is opposition twofold, and the disturbing of the perverse is twofold, because every correction seems to have a certain opposition and disturbance attached to it. For he who corrects another who is manifestly in error opposes him and is in some way corrected; he is disturbed, and the one corrected is corrected of the sin into which he has fallen, and is disturbed either about the sin committed or the will to commit it; if he is not corrected, then he is disturbed by the rebuke of the one correcting or reproving. If, therefore, that opinion which the Gloss recites understands the chapter of the opposition and disturbance of the perverse which belongs to prelates, then it can be made to agree, but not in any other sense. Those, however, who are consulted by the Pope when he wishes to define or determine something against the Catholic faith ought not to oppose as prelates, unless they could clearly prove that the Pope, in his perverse intention, is obstinate; but they ought to oppose as true and sincere zealots of the faith, namely by counsels, persuasions and rebukes of the heresy which he intends, turning the Pope from the sin which he proposes and withdrawing him from the heretical definition, even if it must be done with disturbance and indignation on the Pope's part.

units.la: Discip. Secundum ista si Papa publice requireret Cardinales vel alios super assertione haereticali, quam diffinit solenniter siue determinare intendit, ipsi publice deberent reprehendere & corripere de intentione sua peruersa, quod tamen auctoritate Innocentii tertii, quae ponitur extra de haereticis cap. cum ex iniuncto, repugnare videtur. Ait enim: Nec quisquam sua praesumptionis audacium illo defendat exemplo, quo asina legitur reprehendisse prophetam, vel quod dominus ait; quia ex vobis arguet me de peccato: cum aliud sit fratrem in se peccantem occulte corripere, quod quisque tenetur efficere secundum regulam euangelicam. in quo casu sane potest intelligi quod Balaam fuit correptus ab asina. & aliud est delinquentem corripere manifeste: quod utique nulli licet secundum euangelicam veritatem. nam qui etiam dicit fratri suo, fatue: reus est gehennae ignis. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod nulli subdito licet manifeste & publice corripere vel reprehendere superiorem suum praelatum: licet in occulto licite possit eum corripere. quare Cardinales & alii publice requisiti a Papa volente assertionem haereticalem solenniter diffinire, non debent ei publice contraire, nec corripere manifeste. His etiam Glossa super verbo quicunque, concordare videtur, cum dicit: ad hanc correctionem quilibet tenetur secundum quod hic dicit. & hoc intelligi de occulta correctione siue reprehensione, art. 23. quaest. 5. non putes: sed manifeste corripere pertinet ad praelatos vel ad eos qui habent potestatem aliquam in aliquos 23. quaest. 1. cap. duo ista & cap. forte. pater enim potest filium corripere: & praelatus subditum & manifeste & occulte. Unde Apostolus: argue, obsecra, increpa, & 45. dist. cap. 18. quaest. 1. qui autem. sed filius non potest publice reprehendere siue corripere patrem, nec subditus praelatum, vt hic requiritur in litera. & 21. dist. nolite. erubescit enim lex filios castigaturos parentes, in authenticis de nuptiis, si vero expectet, versus finem. & haec est canonica correctio secundum euangelicam veritatem ait. occulta ad omnes, manifesta ad praelatos vel ad alios aliquam potestatem habentes pertineat. ex quibus videtur, quod Papa a nullo debet manifeste & publice corripi seu reprehendi.
units.tr: Disciple. In that case, if the Pope publicly asked the cardinals or others about a heretical assertion that he intended to define or determine solemnly, they ought to publicly rebuke and reprove him for his perverse intention. Yet this seems to conflict with the authority of Innocent III, which is cited in extra de haereticis cap. cum ex iniuncto. For he says: Let no one defend his presumptuous audacity by that example, where we read that an ass rebuked the prophet, or by the Lord's words, "Which of you convicts me of sin?" For it is one thing to correct a brother who sins against you in private, which everyone is bound to do according to the gospel rule; in that case it can indeed be understood that Balaam was rebuked by the ass. It is another thing to rebuke an offender openly, which is certainly not permitted to anyone according to the gospel truth. For whoever says to his brother, "You fool," is liable to the fire of hell. From these words it is gathered that no subject may openly and publicly rebuke or reprove his superior or prelate, although he may lawfully correct him in private. Therefore the cardinals and others who are publicly asked by a Pope who wishes to define a heretical assertion solemnly ought not to oppose him publicly, nor rebuke him openly. The Gloss on the word "whoever" also seems to agree with this, when it says: "Everyone is bound to this correction, as this passage says." And this is to be understood of private correction or reproof; do not suppose otherwise, see 23 quaest. 5. But open rebuke belongs to prelates, or to those who have some power over others, see 23 quaest. 1, cap. duo ista and cap. forte. For a father may rebuke his son, and a prelate his subject, both openly and in private. Hence the Apostle: "Reprove, entreat, rebuke" (2 Tim. 4). But a son cannot publicly reprove or rebuke his father, nor a subject his prelate, as is required here in the text; see 21 dist. nolite. For the law is ashamed that children should chastise their parents, see the Authenticum de nuptiis, and if one looks further, toward the end. And this is the canonical correction according to the gospel truth: it says that private correction belongs to all, and open correction to prelates or to others who have some power. From these things it seems that the Pope ought not to be openly and publicly corrected or reproved by anyone.

units.la: Mag. Ad ista respondetur dupliciter. Vno modo, quod Innocentius & Glossa loquuntur de reprehensione seu correctione coactiua vel punitiua. ista enim solummodo pertinet ad praelatos vel alios potestatem habentes: non autem loquuntur de quacunque manifesta & publica correctione seu reprehensione. Constat enim, quod qui aliquem in iudicio accusat de crimine vel etiam in iudicio de crimine ipsum denuntiat, aliquo modo ipsum publice & manifeste reprehendit sibi crimen publice imponendo, & de eo fieri iustitiam postulando: & ita reprehendit eum & corripit. manifestum autem est, quod annunciatio, accusatio & denunciatio in iudicio ad alios spectat, quam ad praelatos eorum qui corripiuntur & reprehenduntur. & ita aliqua correctio & reprehensio manifesta & publica spectat ad alios quam ad praelatos. sed correctio & reprehensio coactiua pertinet solummodo ad praelatos, vel ad alios in alios potestatem habentes. & ideo quamuis Cardinales vel alii requisiti a Papa super aliqua assertione haeretica diffinienda antequam constiterit, quod Papa in suo proposito est pertinax, ipsum non debeat reprehendere seu corripere coactiue vel aliqualiter puniendo. debet tamen de necessitate salutis assertionem suam haereticalem reprobare, & ipsi efficaciter suadere, ne aliquo modo talem assertionem haereticam diffinire praesumat.
units.tr: Master. To these things a twofold answer is given. In one way, Innocent and the Gloss speak of reproof or correction that is coercive or punitive. For this pertains only to prelates or to others having power; they do not speak of any open and public correction or reproof whatever. For it is clear that whoever accuses someone of a crime in court, or even denounces him of a crime in court, in some way reproves him openly and publicly, publicly imputing a crime to him and demanding justice be done concerning it; and so he reproves and corrects him. Now it is manifest that the announcing, accusing and denouncing in court pertains to others than the prelates of those who are corrected and reproved. And so some open and public correction and reproof pertains to others than prelates. But coercive correction and reproof pertains only to prelates, or to others having power over others. And therefore, although the Cardinals or others summoned by the Pope concerning some heretical assertion to be defined, before it is established that the Pope is obstinate in his purpose, ought not to reprove or correct him coercively or punish him in any way, nevertheless they must of necessity of salvation reject his heretical assertion, and effectively persuade him not to presume in any way to define such a heretical assertion.

units.la: Aliter respondetur, quod praedictae responsioni non obuiat: quia Innocentius & Glossa loquuntur in aliis criminibus, quam in crimine haeresis prauitatis, quia subditi praelatum suum, vbi eum voluerunt in iudicio accusare, vel rite denunciare de crimine alio, quam de crimine haeresis, reprehendere seu corrigere manifeste non debent, quamuis possunt eum reprehenreprehendere in occulto. de crimine autem haeresis possunt & debent praelatum suum reprehendere & corripere manifeste, etiam extra iudicium; si crimen eius publicum & manifestum extiterit. quod patet per exemplum de beato Paulo, qui beatum Petrum in publico reprehendit, sicut lib. 5. cap. 2. probatum extitit. quod etiam expresse Clemens, ut legitur 2. quaest. 7. cap. sacerdotes, asserere videtur aperte, cum dicit: sacerdotes & alii Ecclesiae ministri omnesque plebes Episcopos suos diligere debent; & eorum praeceptis obedire; etiam si ipsi aliter (quod absit) agant, quam debeant, nisi in fide errauerint. cui Eusebius Papa eisdem causa & q. cap. oues, videtur concordare, cum dicit: oues, quae suo pastori commissae sunt, eum nec reprehendere nisi a fide exorbitauerit, nec vllatenus accusare possunt. Ex quibus verbis colligitur manifeste, quod si Papa a fide errauerit, licet cardinalibus & aliis ipsum corrigere & arguere & reprehendere manifeste. & ita verba Innocentii & Glossae superius allegata non debent intelligi; cum praelati crimine haereticae prauitatis sunt infecti.
units.tr: Otherwise it is answered that the foregoing answer is not contrary to this: for Innocent and the Gloss speak of other crimes than the crime of heretical depravity. For subjects ought not to openly reprove or correct their prelate when they wish to accuse him in court, or duly denounce him, of a crime other than heresy; although they may reprove him in private. But concerning the crime of heresy, they can and ought to reprove and correct their prelate openly, even outside court, if his crime has been public and manifest. This is clear from the example of the blessed Paul, who publicly reproved the blessed Peter, as was proved in Galatians 2 (book 5, chapter 2). Which Clement also seems to assert plainly, as is read 2 qu. 7, chapter "sacerdotes," when he says: "Priests and other ministers of the Church, and all the people, ought to love their bishops and obey their commands, even if they act otherwise than they ought (which God forbid), unless they have erred in the faith." With which Pope Eusebius seems to agree, in the same cause and question, chapter "oves," when he says: "The sheep committed to their shepherd can neither reprove him, unless he has strayed from the faith, nor accuse him in any way." From these words it is manifestly gathered that if the Pope has erred from the faith, it is lawful for the Cardinals and others to correct him, argue with him and reprove him openly. And so the words of Innocent and of the Gloss cited above ought not to be understood thus, since prelates are infected with the crime of heretical depravity.

units.la: DISCIP. Prosecuti sumus vnam probationem, qua patet, quod tacens quando potest prohibere diffinitionem haereticalem Papae est fautor prauitatis haereticae. nunc alias allegationes, si tibi occurrunt, adducas.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. We have pursued one proof, by which it is evident that one who keeps silent when he can prevent a heretical definition by the Pope is a supporter of heretical depravity. Now bring forward other arguments, if they occur to you.

units.la: MAG. Non minus peccat, nec minus est fautor haereticae prauitatis ille, qui tacet, cum potest prohibere diffinitionem haereticalem Papae, quam ille est fautor iniectionis manuum violentę, qui talem violentiam prohibere potest & non facit. sed qui potest prohibere talem violentiam & non prohibet est fautor iniectionis & eandem poenam incurrit cum illo. ergo qui tacet cum potest prohibere contradicendo, reclamando vel reprobando diffinitionem haereticalem Papae, est fautor haereticae prauitatis: quia est fautor haereticalis diffinitionis seu declarationis Papae. Maior licet euidens videatur, tamen probatur sic. Non minus tenentur requisiti super diffinitione haereticali facienda defendere catholicam veritatem, quam quicunque tenentur clericos defendere: imo multo fortius & efficacius aut animosius defendenda est veritas orthodoxa, quam quicunque clericus vel praelatus. ergo non minus peccant illi qui tacendo non defendunt fidem, quam ille qui clericum non defendit.
units.tr: MASTER. He who keeps silent when he can prevent a heretical definition by the Pope sins no less, and is no less a supporter of heretical depravity, than he is a supporter of the laying on of violent hands who can prevent such violence and does not. But he who can prevent such violence and does not prevent it is a supporter of the laying on of hands and incurs the same punishment as that man. Therefore he who keeps silent when he can prevent a heretical definition of the Pope by contradicting, protesting or rejecting it is a supporter of heretical depravity, because he is a supporter of the heretical definition or declaration of the Pope. The major premise, though it seems evident, is nevertheless proved thus. Those who are required to make a heretical definition are bound to defend Catholic truth no less than all who are bound to defend clerics; indeed orthodox truth must be defended much more strongly and effectively and boldly than any cleric or prelate. Therefore those who by keeping silent do not defend the faith sin no less than he who does not defend a cleric.

units.la: Minor probatur auctoritate Innocentii tertii, qui, ut habetur extra de sententia excom. cap. quantae, ait: non autem solos violentiae huius auctores aliquorum praesumptio extimet puniendos, & fauentes & consentientes pari poena plectendos catholica condemnat auctoritas, eos delinquentibus fauere interpretans qui cum possint manifesto facinori desinunt obuiare.
units.tr: The minor premise is proved by the authority of Innocent III, who, as is found in the Decretals, de sententia excommunicationis, chapter "quantae," says: "Catholic authority condemns not only the authors of such violence, but also decrees that those who favour and consent are to be punished with the same penalty, interpreting as favourers of wrongdoers those who, when they could oppose a manifest crime, cease to do so."

units.la: DISCIP. Glossa intendit, quod hoc debet intelligi de praelatis.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. The Gloss intends that this must be understood of prelates.

units.la: MAG. Alii dicunt sic: Glossa recitat ibi, quod de omnibus debet intelligi. sed quicquid sit de hoc, argumentum stare videtur. Nam nullus praelatus magis obligatur defendere clericum (praesertim sibi subditum) quam quilibet Christianus tenetur defendere fidem suam, cum potest. si ergo praelatus, qui clericum non defendit, interpretatur fautor violentiae talis: multo magis qui non defendit fidem suam, cum potest, contra diffinitionem haereticalem Papae, interpretandus est fautor diffinitionis huiusmodi.
units.tr: MASTER. Others say otherwise: the Gloss there records that it must be understood of all. But whatever be the case here, the argument seems to hold. For no prelate is more bound to defend a cleric (especially one subject to him) than any Christian is bound to defend his faith, when he can. If therefore a prelate who does not defend a cleric is to be interpreted as a favourer of such violence, much more is one who does not defend his faith, when he can, against a heretical definition of the Pope to be interpreted as a favourer of such a definition.

units.la: DISCIP. Si omnes rationes, quae in scripturis possunt fundari authenticis, inducerec ad probandum, quod talis tacens est fautor talis diffinitionis, & prolixe tractares, opus nimis prolixum efficeres. ideo absque formatione rationum aliquas auctoritates, ex quibus sumi valeant argumenta, ad conclusionem praefatam conceris allegare.
units.tr: STUDENT. If you were to bring forward every argument that can be founded on genuine Scripture to prove that the one who keeps silent is an accomplice of such a decree, and treat the matter at length, you would make the work far too long. So, without setting out the arguments in form, please cite some authorities from which arguments can be drawn for the aforesaid conclusion.

units.la: MAG. Ad hoc valere videtur auctoritas Hieron. qui, ut habetur dist. 86. cap. facientis, ait: faciente procul dubio culpam habet qui cum potest corrigere, negligit emendare. Item dist. 83. sic legitur: mortem languentibus probatur infligere qui hanc (cum possit) non excludit. Item Innocentius, ut allegatum est supra dist. 83. cap. error, ait: error cui non resistitur approbatur, & veritas cum minime defenditur opprimitur. Item Ambrosius, ut habetur dist. 86. cap. pasce, ait: quilquis enim pascendo hominem seruare poteris, si non paueris, occidisti. Item Leo Papa, ut habetur extra de haereticis cap. 3. ait: Qui alios cum potest ab errore non revocat, seipsum errare demonstrat. Item Iohan. 8. ut habetur 22. quaest. 8. cap. praeterea, ait: cum crimina, quae potest emendare, non corrigit, ipse committit. Item Alexander tertius, ut habetur extra de homicidio cap. sicut dignum, ait: qui potuit hominem liberare a morte, & non liberauit eum, occidit. ex quibus aliisque auctoritatibus quamplurimis consimilibus argumenta sumuntur ad probandum, quod quicunque reclamando, contradicendo, reprobando assertionem haereticalem Papae vel quocunque aliquo modo possunt cum retrahere, ne diffiniat haereticam prauitatem, si tacent, sunt fautores haereticae prauitatis.
units.tr: TEACHER. The authority of Jerome seems to serve this purpose. As it is found in dist. 86, cap. facientis, he says: "Without doubt, he who neglects to correct when he can is guilty of the fault." Likewise, dist. 83 reads: "He is held to inflict death on the sick who does not keep it away when he can." Likewise Innocent, as cited above in dist. 83, cap. error, says: "An error that is not resisted is approved, and when the truth is not at all defended, it is overwhelmed." Likewise Ambrose, as found in dist. 86, cap. pasce, says: "For whoever could save a man by feeding him, and does not feed him, has killed him." Likewise Pope Leo, as found in extra de haereticis cap. 3, says: "He who does not call back others from error when he can shows that he himself is in error." Likewise John 8, as found in 22 quaest. 8, cap. praeterea, says: "When he does not correct the crimes which he can amend, he himself commits them." Likewise Alexander III, as found in extra de homicidio cap. sicut dignum, says: "He who could free a man from death and did not free him, has killed him." From these and many other similar authorities, arguments are drawn to prove that whoever, by protesting, contradicting or condemning the heretical assertion of the Pope, or in any way they can, could turn him back from defining the heretical depravity, and yet keep silent, are accomplices of that heretical depravity.

units.la: DISCIP. Quamuis vna ratione apparenti nisus sis probare, quod consentiens Papae consulendo, quod haereticam diffiniat prauitatem, est fautor prauitatis eiusdem: adhuc tamen eandem conclusionem auctoritatibus vel si maluerit rationibus nitaris ostendere. & quia idem videtur iudicium de consulente non tacite, sed expresse & cooperante diffinitioni haereticali Papae quantum ad hoc, quod si vnus est fautor haereticae prauitatis, & alius (cum vterque expresse consentiat) sufficit mihi, quod probes consentientem tali diffinitioni haereticali esse fautorem diffinitionis eiusdem. & hoc vel rationibus vel auctoritatibus, vt tibi placuerit.
units.tr: STUDENT. Although you have tried to prove by one apparent argument that whoever agrees with the Pope in consulting on his defining a heretical depravity is an accomplice of that same depravity, nevertheless show the same conclusion by authorities or, if you prefer, by arguments. And since the same judgment seems to hold of one who consults not tacitly but expressly, and cooperates with the heretical definition of the Pope in this respect, it is enough for me that you prove that one who consents to such a heretical definition is an accomplice of that same definition, whether by arguments or by authorities, as you please.

units.la: MAGIST. Sunt nonnulli dicentes, quod quia raro & pauci existimant hactenus summum Pontificem, qui diffinitiones seu determinationes haereticales solenniter ediderit, paucae vel nullae auctoritates poterunt reperiri, quae de huiusmodi diffinitionibus Papae haereticalibus consentientibus eis loquantur expresse: multae tamen inveniuntur, quae quamuis de eis non loquantur nominatim, tamen in genere faciunt mentionem. & ideo videtur eis, quod in hac materia magis rationibus demonstrativis ex patrum auctoritatibus deductis, quam nudis auctoritatibus oporteat conclusionem propositam comprobare.
units.tr: TEACHER. There are some who say that, because until now the supreme Pontiff who has solemnly issued heretical definitions or determinations has been rare, and few have considered it, few or no authorities can be found that speak expressly of such heretical definitions of the Pope to which people consent. Yet many are found which, although they do not speak of them by name, nevertheless make mention of them in general. And so it seems to them that in this matter the proposed conclusion ought to be confirmed by demonstrative arguments drawn from the authority of the Fathers, rather than by bare authorities.

units.la: DISCIP. Placet quod rationes adducas: sed an sint demonstrativae, vel sophisticae, post hoc opus totum inquiram.
units.tr: STUDENT. I am content that you bring forward the arguments; but whether they are demonstrative or sophistical, I shall examine after the whole work.

units.la: MAG. Una ratione ad probandum: quod omnes consentientes sive cooperantes diffinitioni haereticali sunt fautores haereticae pravitatis, sis contentus ad praesens. est autem haec ratio. qui communicat alicui in crimine pravitatis haereticae, est fautor pravitatis eiusdem: quia communicans alicui in crimine favorem eidem (quantum ad idem crimen) impendit. sed consentiens diffinitioni haereticali Papae sive consulendo sive cooperando communicat eidem in crimine diffinitionis haereticalis. ergo est fautor pravitatis eius. Maior videtur manifesta, cum eadem poena plectatur criminosus & communicans ei in crimine. extra de sententia excommunicationis cap. super. & cap. super. Minor aperte probatur auctoritate beati Augustini, qui, ut habetur 23. quaest. 4. cap. a malis, ait: duobus modis te non maculat malus, si ei non consentias & redarguas, hoc est communicare, non consentire. Communicatur quippe quando facto eius consortium voluntatis vel approbationi adiungitur. neque ergo consentientes malis sitis ut approbetis: neque negligentes ut non arguatis. Ex quibus verbis clare colligitur, quod consentiens criminoso facto alicuius approbando vel volendo, & per consequens consulendo vel cooperando, communicat eidem. & ita consentiens diffinitioni haereticali Papae communicat eidem in crimine haereticae pravitatis. & hanc etiam minorem aperte insinuat beatus August. contra Donatistas, & ponitur causa & quaest. praedict. cap. si quis catholica, qui ait: communio malorum non maculat alium quem participatione factorum sed consensione factorum. Ex quibus verbis patet, quod qui consentit factis malorum in crimine, communicat eis:
units.tr: TEACHER. For now, let it suffice for you to have one argument proving that all who consent to or cooperate with a heretical definition are accomplices of the heretical depravity. The argument is this: whoever shares with another in the crime of heretical depravity is an accomplice of that same depravity, because one who shares in a crime gives favour to that same crime. But one who consents to a heretical definition of the Pope, whether by consulting or by cooperating, shares in the crime of the heretical definition. Therefore he is an accomplice of its depravity. The major premise seems plain, since the criminal and the one who shares in his crime are punished with the same penalty. Extra de sententia excommunicationis, cap. super and cap. super. The minor premise is plainly proved by the authority of blessed Augustine, who, as found in 23 quaest. 4, cap. a malis, says: A bad man does not stain you in two ways: if you do not consent to him and rebuke him. To share is to consent, not to rebuke. For one shares when partnership of will or approval is joined to his deed. Therefore neither consent to the wicked, lest you approve, nor neglect them, lest you fail to rebuke them. From these words it is clearly gathered that one who consents to the criminal deed of another, by approving or willing it, and consequently by consulting or cooperating, shares in it. And so one who consents to a heretical definition of the Pope shares in the crime of heretical depravity. Blessed Augustine also clearly suggests this minor premise against the Donatists, and it is set down in the aforesaid causa et quaest., cap. si quis catholica, where he says: The fellowship of the wicked does not stain another by participation in their deeds, but by consent to their deeds. From these words it is plain that whoever consents to the deeds of the wicked in their crime shares in them.

units.la: CAP. XXXIII. In quo tractatur, qua poena sunt plectendi consentientes diffinitioni Papae haereticali.
units.tr: CAP. XXXIII. On the punishment with which those who consent to a heretical definition of the Pope are to be punished.

units.la: DISCIP. Post praedicta dic, qua poena consentientes diffinitioni haereticali Papae sunt plectendi; & an debeant haeretici iudicari.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. After what has been said, tell me with what punishment those who consent to a heretical definition of the Pope are to be punished, and whether such persons ought to be judged heretics.

units.la: MAG. Dicitur quod poena haereticorum sunt plectendi. nam consentientes & facientes pari poena sunt plectendi. sed Papa determinans & diffiniens solenniter assertionem haereticalem est haereticus & poena haereticorum plectendus. ergo consentientes diffinitioni haereticali sunt poena haereticorum sunt plectendi. Maior sanctorum patrum auctoritatibus asseritur. ait enim Lucius Papa, ut habetur 17. q. 4. c. omnes: non solum qui faciunt rei iudicantur sed etiam qui facientibus consentiunt: per enim poena facientes & consentientes comprehendit. Item Nicolaus Papa, ut legitur 2. q. 1. c. notum: facientem & consentientem pari poena constringit. Item Alexander tertius, ut legitur extra de offic. delegat. cap. 1. ait: Agentes & consentientes pari poena scripturae testimonii puniuntur. Hoc etiam Gregor. dist. 89. c. Tanta, insinuat manifeste, ubi Gloss. super verbo, excommunicates, ait; non quod quandoque magis puniuntur consiliarii quam facientes. hoc etiam dicto Gelasii Papae, quod ponitur di. 86. cap. duo, aperte elicitur, cum ait: Innocentius Papa Archadium Imperatorem, quia consensit quod sanctum Iohannes Chrysostomus a sede sua pelleretur, excommunicavit. ubi dicit Glossa super verbo consensit, ait: consentientem maiori poena astringi quam facientem. cui concordat Glossa 24. quaest. 3. cap. qui aliorum, dicens: nota quod plus punitur consulens quam faciens. Ex quibus aliisque pluribus, probatur quod consentientes & facientes pari poena sunt plectendi, quod ex verbis beati Pauli Roman. 1. accipitur, ut videtur; cum ait: qui talia agunt digni sunt morte: non solum autem qui faciunt ea sed etiam qui consentiunt facientibus. ubi dicit Gloss. consentire est tacere cum possis arguere vel errorem adulando fovere. si autem adulando fovere est consentire: multo magis consulere & cooperari est consentire. & per consequens consentientes & cooperantes diffinitioni haereticali Papae pari poena sunt plectendi: & ita poena haereticorum feriri debent.
units.tr: MASTER. It is said that they are to be punished with the punishment of heretics. For those who consent and those who act are to be punished with the same penalty. But a Pope who solemnly determines and defines a heretical assertion is a heretic and to be punished with the punishment of heretics. Therefore those who consent to a heretical definition are to be punished with the punishment of heretics. The major premise is affirmed by the authority of the holy Fathers. Pope Lucius says, as is found in 17 q. 4 c. Omnes: "Not only are those who do the deed judged guilty, but also those who consent to the doers." For the penalty embraces both the doers and the consenters. Likewise Pope Nicholas, as is read in 2 q. 1 c. Notum: he binds the doer and the consenter with the same penalty. Likewise Alexander III, as is read in Extra, de officio delegati, c. 1: "Those who act and those who consent are punished with the same penalty as the bearers of false testimony." Gregory also shows this plainly in dist. 89 c. Tanta, where the Gloss, on the word excommunicentur, says: not that sometimes counsellors are punished more than the doers. This is also clearly drawn from the saying of Pope Gelasius, which is found in dist. 86 c. Duo, where he says: "Pope Innocent excommunicated the Emperor Arcadius, because he consented that St John Chrysostom should be driven from his see." There the Gloss on the word consensit says that the consenter is bound by a greater penalty than the doer. The Gloss on 24 q. 3 c. Qui aliorum agrees, saying: note that the one who advises is punished more than the one who acts. From these and many other authorities it is proved that those who consent and those who act are to be punished with the same penalty, which seems to be taken from the words of St Paul, Romans 1: "Those who do such things are worthy of death; not only those who do them, but also those who consent to those who do them." There the Gloss says that to consent is to keep silent when you could rebuke, or to foster an error by flattering it. If to foster by flattery is to consent, then much more is to advise and cooperate to consent. And consequently those who consent to and cooperate in the heretical definition of the Pope are to be punished with the same penalty, and so the punishment of heretics ought to be inflicted upon them.

units.la: DISCIP. Ista maior, consentientes & facientes pari poena sunt plectendi: non videtur vera de consentientibus consulendo tantummodo, quod Alexander tertius, ut habetur extra de homicidio cap. Sicut, affirmare videtur, cum dicit: qui vero se asserunt animum regis inflammasse ad odium, unde homicidium fuit secutum, dure & aspere, sed non severe sunt puniendi, sicut (supple) qui occidunt. ex quibus verbis videtur, quod inflammans & per consequentis consentiens consulendo non ita punitur, sicut faciens. quod Glossa, extra de officio delega. asserit manifeste, dicens: in secundo casu consilii minus punitur (quam supple, faciens) plus tanquam negligens. Glossae ergo, quae dicunt, quod consulens plus punitur quam faciens, tam Alexandri tertii quam Glossae ultimae allegatae repugnare videntur.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. That major premise, that those who consent and those who act are to be punished with the same penalty, does not seem true of those who consent merely by advising. Alexander III, as found in Extra, de homicidio, c. Sicut, seems to affirm this when he says: "Those who assert that they inflamed the king's mind to hatred, whence homicide followed, are to be punished harshly and roughly, but not severely, as (namely) those who kill." From these words it seems that one who inflames, and consequently one who consents by advising, is not punished as severely as the one who acts. The Gloss on Extra, de officio delegati asserts this plainly, saying: "In the second case of counsel, the one who advises is punished less (than the doer), more as one who is negligent." Therefore the Glosses which say that the one who advises is punished more than the doer seem to contradict both Alexander III and the last Gloss cited.

units.la: MAGIST. Respondetur, quod hoc regulare est, quod consulens & faciens poena consimili puniuntur, ut si unus est excommunicatus, alter est excommunicatus. & si unus est suspensus, & alter similiter. quandoque tamen quantum ad aliquam circumstantiam poenae consimilis gravius punitur consulens quam faciens: & quandoque econverso. & ideo quantum ad conclusionem propositam sufficienter ostenditur, quod consentiens constitutioni haereticali Papae poena haereticorum est plectendus.
units.tr: MASTER. The answer is that it is the rule that the one who advises and the one who acts are punished with a like penalty: if one is excommunicated, the other is excommunicated; and if one is suspended, the other likewise. Sometimes, however, with respect to some circumstance of a like penalty, the one who advises is punished more severely than the doer, and sometimes the reverse. And so, as regards the conclusion proposed, it is sufficiently shown that one who consents to a heretical constitution of the Pope is to be punished with the punishment of heretics.

units.la: CAP. XXXIV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXIV.

units.la: In quo probatur, quod predicti consentientes hæretici sunt censendi. vbi etiam plures mouentur quæstiones circa idem.
units.tr: In which it is proved that the aforesaid consenting persons are to be judged heretics. Where also several questions are raised about the same matter.

units.la: <bl>D</bl>Iscip. Dixisti secundum opinionem prædictam, quod consentientes diffinitioni hæreticali Papæ siue consulendo siue cooperando, non solum pœna hæreticorum sunt plectendi: sed etiam hæretici sunt censendi. ideo ad propositum, quod sunt hæretici, aliqua motiua non differas allegare.
units.tr: <bl>D</bl>Disciple. You have said, according to the opinion mentioned above, that those who consent to the heretical definition of the Pope, whether by advising or by cooperating, are to be punished not only with the penalty of heretics but are also to be counted as heretics. So, to the point that they are heretics, do not delay in setting out some reasons.

units.la: Magist. Quod omnes consentientes consulendo, inducendo, suadendo, suggerendo diffinitioni hæreticali Papæ sunt inter hæreticos computandi, multis modis videtur posse probari. Primo sic: qui simili modo cum hæretico est culpabilis iudicandus, crimine hæresis est irretitus. hæc videtur nota de se. sed omnes consentientes diffinitioni hæreticali Papæ sunt cum Papa hæretico simili modo culpabiles iudicandi. hoc ex verbis Isidori, quæ recitat & probat, vt habetur 11. quæst. 3. qui consentit, colligitur euidenter, cum dicit: alius pater ait, si quis alterius errori consentit, sciat se cum illo simili modo culpabilem iudicandum. ergo omnes consentientes, quod Papa assertionem, quæ est hæretica, diffiniat & determinet, sunt hæretici cum Papa iudicandi.
units.tr: Master. That all who consent to the heretical definition of the Pope, by advising, inducing, persuading or suggesting it, are to be reckoned among the heretics, can be proved in many ways. First, thus: whoever is to be judged guilty in the same way as a heretic is caught in the crime of heresy. This seems evident in itself. But all who consent to the heretical definition of the Pope are to be judged guilty in the same way as the heretical Pope. This is clearly gathered from the words of Isidore, which he recites and proves, as is found in 11. q. 3, "Qui consentit," when he says: "Another father says, if anyone consents to another's error, let him know that he is to be judged guilty in the same way as that man." Therefore all who consent that the Pope define and determine an assertion which is heretical are to be judged heretics together with the Pope.

units.la: Secundo sic: Qui alicui communicat in crimine, simili crimine est irretitus. sed consentientes, quod Papa diffiniat prauitatem hæreticam, communicat Papæ in crimine hæresis. ergo crimine hæresis inuoluitur.
units.tr: Second, thus: whoever shares in another's crime is caught in a like crime. But those who consent that the Pope define a heretical depravity share with the Pope in the crime of heresy. Therefore they are involved in the crime of heresy.

units.la: Tertio sic: omnes credentes pertinaciter erroribus hæreticorum sunt hæretici reputandi. omnes autem consentientes, quod Papa solenniter diffiniat hæreticam prauitatem, sunt credentes pertinaciter errori Papæ. ergo sunt inter hæreticos computandi. maior ex verbis Gregorii, quæ ponuntur extra de hæreticis, excommunicamus, secundo, patenter habetur, cum dicit, vt allegatum est supra. credentes autem eorum erroribus hæreticos similiter iudicamus. minor claret: quia qui consentit errori, iudicandus est quod illi errori adhæreat. Quod etiam sint pertinaciter credentes, patet ex hoc, quod non solum consentiunt errori, quem Papa diffinit, sed etiam consentiunt pertinaciæ suæ, qua solenniter diffinit errorem. ergo non solum communicant Papæ credendo errorem: sed etiam sibi communicant in pertinacia. ergo pertinaces & per consequens hæretici sunt censendi.
units.tr: Third, thus: all who obstinately believe the errors of heretics are to be regarded as heretics. But all who consent that the Pope solemnly define a heretical depravity are believers obstinately holding to the Pope's error. Therefore they are to be counted among the heretics. The major premise is plainly found in the words of Gregory, which are cited under the title "De haereticis, Excommunicamus," second, as was alleged above: "We likewise judge those who believe their errors to be heretics." The minor premise is clear, because whoever consents to an error is to be judged as clinging to that error. That they are also obstinate believers is shown by the fact that they consent not only to the error which the Pope defines but also to his obstinacy, by which he solemnly defines the error. Therefore they not only share with the Pope in believing the error, but also share with him in obstinacy. Therefore they are to be judged obstinate and consequently heretics.

units.la: Quarto: non minus est hæreticus reputandus, cuius consilio siue cooperatione crimen hæreticæ prauitatis committitur, quam ille est dicendus homicida, cuius consilio seu cooperatione homicidium perpetratur. sed ille, cuius consilio & cooperatione homicidium perpetratur, dicitur homicida. ergo omnes consulentes & cooperantes, quod Papa diffiniat assertionem, quæ est hæretica, committunt crimen hæreticæ prauitatis: & per consequens sunt inter hæreticos computandi siue numerandi. Maior non videtur probatione aliqualiter indigere. minor auctoritate Augustin. quæ ponitur in de pœnitentia dist. 1. cap. periculose, videtur aperte posse probari, cum dicit: periculose se decipiunt, qui existimant, eos tantum homicidas, qui manibus hominem occidunt, & non potius eos per quorum consilium, fraudem & exhortationes homines extinguuntur. nam Iudei nequaquam dominum proprio manibus interfecerunt. Scriptum est enim: Nobis non licet interficere quenquam. sed tamen illi mors domini imputatur: quia ipsi cum lingua interfecerunt dicentes: crucifige, crucifige eum. Ex quibus verbis patet, quod homicida censetur, qui consilio, exhortatione, & per consequens cooperatione hominem interfecit. cui Coelestinus tertius, vt legitur, extra de cleri. pugnantibus in duello. cap. hæreticum, concordare videtur, cum dicitur: homicidium tam dicto quam facto siue consilio aut defensione non est dubium perpetrari. hinc Glos. extra de homicidio. cap. licet, ait: nota quod homicidium committitur, facto, consilio, defensione. i. d. si quis non dicam. quod ex scriptura diuina videtur trahere fulcimentum: cum etiam secundum scripturam sacram ille dicatur occidere, cuius inuitu quis occidit, vt legitur 3. Reg. 21. vxor Regis Achab, non ipse Achab, iussit occidi Naboth Iezrahelitam, vt vineam suam traderet regi: & tamen dixit Helias Propheta ad eum, occidisti & possedisti. patet ergo quod aliter quam manu potest quis committere homicidium: quia consilio & etiam præcepto & cooperatione. ergo & eadem ratione perfidia hæresis potest consilio perpetrari.
units.tr: Fourth: whoever is responsible for the crime of heretical depravity by his counsel or cooperation is no less to be regarded as a heretic than the one who is called a murderer by whose counsel or cooperation a murder is committed. But he by whose counsel and cooperation a murder is committed is called a murderer. Therefore all who advise and cooperate that the Pope define an assertion which is heretical commit the crime of heretical depravity, and consequently are to be counted or numbered among the heretics. The major premise does not seem to need any proof. The minor premise can clearly be proved by the authority of Augustine, which is cited in De poenitentia, dist. 1, cap. "Periculose," where he says: "They deceive themselves dangerously who think that only those are murderers who kill a man with their hands, and not rather those by whose counsel, deceit and exhortations men are destroyed. For the Jews did not kill the Lord with their own hands. For it is written: It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death. Yet the death of the Lord is imputed to them, because they killed him with their tongue, saying: Crucify, crucify him." From these words it is plain that he is considered a murderer who has killed a man by counsel, exhortation, and consequently by cooperation. Celestine III, as is read in Extra, De clericis pugnantibus in duello, cap. "Haereticum," seems to agree with this, where it is said: "There is no doubt that a homicide is committed by word as by deed, whether by counsel or by defence." Hence the Gloss on Extra, De homicidio, cap. "Licet," says: "Note that homicide is committed by deed, by counsel, by defence," which seems to draw support from divine Scripture, since according to Scripture also he is said to kill at whose instigation someone kills, as is read in 3 Kings 21: the wife of King Ahab, not Ahab himself, ordered Naboth the Jezreelite to be killed so that he might hand over his vineyard to the king; and yet the prophet Elijah said to him: "You have killed and also taken possession." It is plain, then, that a man can commit homicide in ways other than with his hand: by counsel, and also by command and cooperation. Therefore, by the same reasoning, the treachery of heresy can be committed by counsel.

units.la: Discip. Nunquid secundum istos potest aliter dici hæreticus quam ille qui dicitur homicida, cuius consilio homicidium perpetratur.
units.tr: Disciple. Can one, according to these authorities, be called a heretic in any other way than as one is called a murderer by whose counsel a murder is committed?

units.la: Mag. Respondetur quod verius & magis proprie dicitur hæreticus ille, qui consentit diffinitioni Papæ hæreticali, quam ille dicitur homicida, cuius consilio homicidium perpetratur. nam ille qui solum consilio committit homicidium, non habet rationem completissimam homicidii: eo quod nequaquam manu interfecit: sed ille qui consentit diffinitioni hæreticali Papæ, nihil deficit de completissima ratione hæretici: quia ad completissimam rationem hæretici sufficit, quod quis pertinaciter adhæreat assertioni contrariæ catholicæ veritati. hæc autem ratio inuenitur ita in consentiente dictæ diffinitioni, sicut in Papa diffiniente, licet istam pertinaciam vnus ostendit vno modo, & alius alio modo: quia vnus diffinitiendo, & alius diffinitioni consentiendo. & ideo ita proprie est vnus reputandus hæreticus, sicut alius. non autem ita est de homicidio, quia licet quis dederit consilium de homine occidendo, non propter hoc homo vere realiter occiditur.
units.tr: Master. It is answered that he is more truly and more properly called a heretic who consents to the heretical definition of the Pope than he is called a murderer by whose counsel a murder is committed. For he who commits murder only by counsel does not have the complete character of murder, because he has by no means killed with his hand; but he who consents to the heretical definition of the Pope lacks nothing of the full character of a heretic, because for the full character of a heretic it is enough that someone obstinately clings to an assertion contrary to Catholic truth. This character is found in the consenter to the said definition just as in the Pope who defines it, although the one shows this obstinacy in one way and the other in another way: the one by defining, and the other by consenting to the definition. And therefore the one is to be regarded as a heretic just as properly as the other. It is not so with murder, because although someone has given counsel about killing a man, the man is not on that account truly and actually killed.

units.la: Discip. Puto quod pro opinione prædicta fortiora motiua quam sint præscripta non est facile inuenire: ideo ad præsens sufficiant. & dic an in aliquo casu consentientes dicta diffinitioni valeant excusari.
units.tr: Disciple. I think that stronger reasons than those set out above for this opinion are not easy to find; so let these suffice for the present. And tell me whether in any case those who consent to the said definition can be excused.

units.la: Mag. Respondetur, quod in nullo casu neque per ignorantiam neque per timorem mortis possunt excusari à peccato mortali, quod non per ignorantiam, patet per hoc, quod actui tam solenni sicut debet esse diffinitio summi Pontificis circa illa quæ spectant ad fidem nullus debet assentire: nisi sit certus certitudine sufficienti. de assertione autem hæreticali nullus potest esse certus, sicut nec potest esse certus de falso; tali diffinitioni nullus consentire debet.
units.tr: Master. It is answered that in no case can they be excused from mortal sin, neither through ignorance nor through fear of death. That they cannot be excused through ignorance is shown by this: that no one should assent to an act as solemn as a definition of the supreme Pontiff concerning matters that pertain to faith, unless he is certain with sufficient certainty. But no one can be certain of a heretical assertion, just as no one can be certain of what is false; no one ought to consent to such a definition.

units.la: Discip. Quid si credit se esse certum, quod talis diffinitio continet catholicam veritatem: licet in rei veritate doctrinæ catholicæ aduersetur?
units.tr: Disciple. What if he believes that he is certain that such a definition contains Catholic truth, although in the real truth it opposes Catholic doctrine?

units.la: Mag. Respondetur, quod non sufficit quod quis credat se esse certum, sicut ad excusandum Saracenos & Iudæos non sufficit quod credunt leges & sectas suas esse bonas, nec ad excusandum hæreticos sufficit quod credant se esse certos, quod non obtinant catholicæ veritati. quilibet ergo qui vult consentire diffinitioni Papæ debet esse certus, quod consonet catholicæ veritati: & non sufficit quod credat se esse certum: quia ignorantia iuris in hoc casu non excusat, licet forte attenuet.
units.tr: Master. It is answered that it is not enough that someone believes himself to be certain, just as it is not enough to excuse Saracens and Jews that they believe their laws and sects to be good; nor does it suffice to excuse heretics that they believe themselves certain that they do not hold Catholic truth. Anyone, therefore, who wishes to consent to the definition of the Pope must be certain that it agrees with Catholic truth; and it is not enough that he believes himself to be certain, because ignorance of the law does not excuse in this case, although perhaps it lessens the fault.

units.la: Discip. Quare non potest quis consentiens diffinitioni hæreticali excusari à peccato mortali per timorem mortis?
units.tr: Disciple. Why can one who consents to a heretical definition not be excused from mortal sin through fear of death?

units.la: Mag. Ad hoc respondetur, quod ideo minime excusatur, quia pro nullo metu debet quis peccatum mortale incurrere. de his extra que vi metuue causa fiunt. cap. sacris 32. quaest. 5. ita ne. quia, vt dicit Nicola, secundum quod legitur 31. quæst. 3. Lotharius: cum nec occisores corporis sint timendi contra iustitiam homines impellentes, Saluatore dicente Matth. 10. nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt: animam autem non possunt occidere.
units.tr: Master. To this it is answered that he is by no means excused, because for no fear ought anyone to incur mortal sin. Concerning these things see the Extra, "De his quae vi metusve causa fiunt," and C. 32, q. 5, "Ita ne." For, as Nicholas says, according to what is read in C. 31, q. 3, from Lothair: since men who compel others against justice are not to be feared, even though they are murderers of the body, the Saviour saying in Matthew 10: "Do not fear those who kill the body, but cannot kill the soul."

units.la: Discip. Nunquid per timorem mortis potest quis consentiens diffinitioni Papæ hæreticali excusari à perfidia hæreticæ prauitatis? Mag. Respondetur, quod timor mortis & forte grauium tormentorum excusaret consentientem à perfidia hæresis: sed timor perditionis bonorum & rerum & famæ seu cuiuscunq; rei temporalis minime excusaret, quin esset inter hæreticos computandus. Discip. Nunquid consentientes diffinitioni Papæ hæreticali omnibus pœnis (quibus Papa hæreticus) sunt plectendi.
units.tr: Disciple: Can someone who consents to a heretical definition of the Pope be excused from the perfidy of heretical wickedness out of fear of death? Master: It is answered that fear of death, and perhaps of severe torments, would excuse a person who consents from the perfidy of heresy. But fear of losing goods, property, reputation, or any other temporal thing would not excuse him, so that he would still be counted among the heretics. Disciple: Are those who consent to a heretical definition of the Pope liable to all the penalties to which a heretical Pope is liable?

units.la: Mag. Respondetur, quod vere & proprie sunt hæretici iudicandi. Discip. Nunquid cardinales consentientes tali diffinitioni sunt priuati potestate eligendi summum Pontificem. Mag. Dicitur quod sic: quia sunt ipso facto, quod consenserunt, cardinalatus dignitate de iure priuati.
units.tr: Master: It is answered that they are truly and properly to be judged heretics. Disciple: Are cardinals who consent to such a definition deprived of the power to elect the supreme Pontiff? Master: It is said that they are, because by the very fact that they consented, they have lost the dignity of the cardinalate by law.

units.la: Discip. Quid si omnes consentirent præter vnum, nunquid ille vnus habet potestatem eligendi? Mag. Respondetur q; sic: quia ius eligendi potest in vno solo remanere, vt notat Gloss. de postulatione, gratum. & di. 7. si forte. Discip. Quid si omnes electores consentirent diffinitioni tali? Mag. Dicunt quod in hoc casu potestas eligendi summum Pontificem devoluitur ad Romanos alios præter Cardinales vel ad omnes vel ad aliquos tantum. Discip. De hac materia te interrogabo sollicite in tractatu De gestis circa finem altercantium contra fidem catholicam. ideo ipsa dimissa dic, an aliquis consentiens diffinitioni hæreticali Papæ esset eligibilis in summum Pontificem. Mag. Respondetur quod non: quia nullus hæreticus est eligibilis in summum Pontificem. crimen enim hæresis electo in Papam potest opponi, vt notat Glossa extra de electione, licet. Discip. Dic, quid esset faciendum Cardinalibus & aliis requisitis à Papa hæretico, vt suæ diffinitioni hæreticali præbeant consensum. Mag. Respondetur, quod vel debent de necessitate salutis publice & manifeste contradicere, reclamare & pro viribus obuiare, vel si videatur eis expediens, possunt publice vel occulte fugiendo ad loca tutiora se conferre, vt fortius & efficacius perfidiæ Papæ hæretici resistere valerent.
units.tr: Disciple: What if all were to consent except one? Does that one have the power to elect? Master: It is answered that he does, because the right of electing can remain in one person alone, as the Gloss notes on "de postulatione, gratum," and Dist. 7, "si forte." Disciple: What if all the electors were to consent to such a definition? Master: They say that in this case the power of electing the supreme Pontiff passes to the Romans other than the cardinals, either to all of them or only to some. Disciple: I shall question you carefully about this matter in the treatise On the Deeds, near the end of the disputes against the Catholic faith. So, setting that aside, tell me whether anyone who consents to a heretical definition of the Pope could be eligible as supreme Pontiff. Master: It is answered that he could not, because no heretic is eligible as supreme Pontiff. For the crime of heresy can be objected against someone elected Pope, as the Gloss notes under "de electione, licet."

units.la: CAP. XXXV.
units.tr: CAP. XXXV.

units.la: Vsque ad 42. tractat de Episcopis & Prælatis Ecclesiæ fautoribus hæreticæ prauitatis, & pri- mo de diuulgantibus doctrinam Papæ hæretici. & ponuntur tres opi- niones secundum ordinem.
units.tr: Up to the 42nd, he treats of bishops and prelates who favour the heretical depravity of the Church, and first of those who publish the teaching of the heretical Pope. Three opinions are set out in order.

units.la: Discip. Quia probabiliter æstimo, quod si vnquam aliquis Papa fatuus temporali vallandus potentia, & qui plurimos exaltabit ad ecclesiasticas dignitates, rabie inficeretur hæretica: non solum tertiam partem stellarum, sed forte mille partes ecclesiæ militantis traheret cauda sua in abyssum prauitatis hæreticæ, vt iuxta sententiam beati Gregor. tolerabilius tanta mala si vnquam euenirent valeamus suscipere, si contra ipsa per prouidentia clipeum fuerimus pramuniti. post prædicta de consentientib. quod Papa assertionem hæreticalē solenniter & manifeste diffiniat, volo de Christianis diuersorum statuum & graduum, quomodo doctrinæ pestiferæ Papæ hæretici valeant fauere, interrogare q; plura. ppono inqrere sigillatim de Episcopis & Prælatis, do doctoribus. & magistris, de religiosis & regib. principib. & publicis potestatib. & de dignitatib. & vltimo de laicis & simplicib. nullam potestatem habentibus coactiuam.
units.tr: Student: Since I reckon it probable that if ever some foolish Pope, fortified by temporal power and promoting very many to ecclesiastical dignities, were to be infected with heresy, his tail would drag not merely a third part of the stars but perhaps a thousand parts of the militant Church into the abyss of heretical depravity, then, in accordance with the saying of the blessed Gregory, we may be able to bear such great evils more tolerably, should they ever occur, if we have been forearmed against them by foresight as with a shield. After the foregoing about those who consent, when the Pope solemnly and manifestly defines a heretical assertion, I wish to ask, also at length, how Christians of the various estates and ranks may be able to favour the pestilent teaching of a heretical Pope. I propose to inquire separately about bishops and prelates, about teachers and masters, about religious, about kings, princes and public powers, about dignitaries, and lastly about laymen and simple people who have no coercive power.

units.la: Incipiendo ergo ab Episcopis & Prælatis, quorum nomine Patriarchas & Archiepiscopos ac Abbates & alios maiores Prælatos comprehendo, Peto primo, vt discutias, an Episcopi & Prælati printi principes & diuulgantes per se vel per alios doctrinam erroneam Papae haeretici, sint fautores prauitatis haereticae reputandi.
units.tr: Beginning, then, with bishops and prelates, under which name I include patriarchs, archbishops, abbots and the other greater prelates, I ask first that you discuss whether bishops and prelates who are the first princes and who publish, either themselves or through others, the erroneous teaching of the heretical Pope, are to be reckoned favourers of heretical depravity.

units.la: MAGIST. Circa hoc possunt esse diuersae sententiae. vna quod scientes doctrinam Papae veritati catholicae obuiare: & eam per se vel per alios diuulgant & publicant, sunt fautores haeretica prauitatis & haeretici iudicandi. Si autem nesciunt eam veritati repugnare catholicae, non sunt fautores haereticae prauitatis, & haeretici iudicandi. Primum probatur sic. illi sunt fautores haereticae prauitatis, qui scienter haereticae prauitati consentiunt non solum tacendo, sed etiam diuulgando, & vt teneatur, doceatur, & etiam defendatur opem dando. tales autem sunt Episcopi & Praelati, qui doctrinam Papae haeretici praedictam diuulgant & publicant. ergo sunt fautores haereticae prauitatis.
units.tr: MASTER. On this there can be different opinions. One is that those who, knowing that the Pope's teaching opposes catholic truth, publish and make it public, either themselves or through others, are favourers of heretical depravity and are to be judged heretics. If, however, they do not know that it conflicts with catholic truth, they are not favourers of heretical depravity and are not to be judged heretics. The first is proved thus: those are favourers of heretical depravity who knowingly consent to heretical depravity, not only by keeping silent but also by publishing it, and by giving aid so that it is held, taught and even defended. Such, however, are the bishops and prelates who publish and make public the aforesaid teaching of the heretical Pope. Therefore they are favourers of heretical depravity.

units.la: DISCIP. Nunquid secundum istam opinionem tales censendi sunt haeretici? MAGIST. Respondetur quod sunt fautores haereticae prauitatis: quia in rei veritate prauitati haereticae fauent dando opem & operam, vt haeretica prauitas doceatur & teneatur: tamen non sunt haeretici, quia corde non credunt doctrinam, quam publicant esse veram. DISCIP. Quomodo probatur secundum.
units.tr: STUDENT. Are such men, according to this opinion, to be considered heretics? MASTER. It is answered that they are favourers of heretical depravity, because in the real truth they favour heretical depravity by giving aid and labour so that heretical depravity may be taught and held; yet they are not heretics, because in their hearts they do not believe the doctrine which they publish to be true. STUDENT. How is the second opinion proved?

units.la: MAGIST. Probatur hoc modo: omnes fautores haereticae prauitatis peccant mortaliter: quia fautoria haeresis cum puniatur grauii poena, puta poena excommunicationis, est peccatum mortale. qui autem ignorant doctrinam Papae haereticam esse, & eam publicant & diuulgant per se & per alios, non peccant mortaliter. ergo non sunt fautores haereticae prauitatis. maior videtur manifesta. & minor probatur sic. qui praeceptum superioris implet, quando tenetur, non peccat mortaliter. sed quando nescitur, an praeceptum superioris sit iustum vel licitum, obediendum est praecepto superioris, teste Augustin. contra Manicheos, qui, vt habetur 23. quaest. 1. cap. qui culpatur, ait, vir iustus si forte etiam sub rege & homine sacrilego militet, recte poterit illo iubente bellare, si vice pacis ordinem seruans: quod sibi iubetur vel non esse contra Dei praeceptum certum est; vel virum sit, certum non est: ita vt fortasse reum faciat regem iniquitas imperandi, innocentem autem militem ostendat ordo seruiendi. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod obediens praecepto superioris, quando non est certum praeceptum eius esse contra praeceptum Dei, non peccat. ergo qui publicat & diuulgat doctrinam Papae, quam nescit esse contra catholicam veritatem; non peccat. & per consequens non est fautor haereticae prauitatis.
units.tr: MASTER. It is proved in this way: all favourers of heretical depravity sin mortally, since favouring heresy, which is punished with a graver penalty, such as excommunication, is a mortal sin. But those who do not know that the Pope's doctrine is heretical, and who publish and spread it either themselves or through others, do not sin mortally. Therefore they are not favourers of heretical depravity. The major premise seems plain. The minor is proved thus: whoever fulfils the command of a superior, when bound to do so, does not sin mortally. But when it is not known whether a command of a superior is just or lawful, the command of the superior is to be obeyed, as Augustine teaches against the Manichaeans, and as is found in 23 q. 1 c. "Qui culpatur": a just man, he says, even if he serves under a king and a sacrilegious man, may rightly go to war at his command, if he keeps the order of peace; it is certain either that what he is ordered to do is not against God's precept, or else that it is not certain that it is a sin; so that perhaps the wickedness of the one who commands makes the king guilty, while the order of service shows the soldier to be innocent. From these words it is gathered that one who obeys a superior's command, when it is not certain that the command is against God's precept, does not sin. Therefore whoever publishes and spreads the Pope's teaching, which he does not know to be contrary to catholic truth, does not sin, and consequently is not a favourer of heretical depravity.

units.la: CAP. XXXVI.
units.tr: CAP. XXXVI.
