units.la: In quo ponitur opinio secunda contraria secundae parti seu conclusioni in capitulo praecedenti posita, & ibidem respondetur ad rationem factam cap. praecedenti pro secunda parte, quam ponit opinio.
units.tr: The second opinion, contrary to the second part or conclusion laid down in the previous chapter, is set out here, and the argument made in the previous chapter for that second part, which this opinion holds, is answered.

units.la: DISCIP. Aliam sententiam tracta. MAG. Alia sententia est, quod omnes Episcopi & Praelati publicantes & diuulgantes solenniter coram sibi subiectis totam tenendam doctrinam erroneam Papae haeretici, tanquam catholicam, sunt fautores haereticae prauitatis, siue sciant eam esse erroneam siue ignorent, haec per rationem pro prima parte superioris sententiae factam videtur aperte posse probari. Nam qui consentit dando opem vel operam, vt haereticalis doctrina tanquam catholica doceatur & teneatur, est fautor haereticae prauitatis. sic sunt Episcopi & Praelati, qui per se vel per alios doctrinam erroneam Papae haeretici tanquam catholicam publicant & diuulgant. ergo sunt approbati fautores haereticae prauitatis. minor euidens est. maior testimonio Pii Papae ostenditur, qui, vt legitur dist. 83. cap. quid enim prodest, ait: Quid enim prodest illi suo errore non pollui, qui consensum praestat erranti. q. d. nihil. ergo nihil prodest, vt excusetur a fautoria haeresis ille, qui consentit dando opem vel operam, vt error Papae tanquam catholicus diuulgetur. Secundo sic. non minus peccare videtur, qui non resistit errori, quam qui errorem diuulgat, & tanquam catholicum publicat. sed qui non resistit errori, censetur ipsum approbare, secundum quod per plures auctoritates, quarum aliquae sunt allegatae, aperte probatur. ergo multo fortius qui errorem publicat & diuulgat, tanquam catholicum, eundem approbare dinoscitur. qui autem errorem approbat, fautor erroris existit. ergo Episcopi & Praelati publicantes & diuulgantes doctrinam erroneam Papae haeretici, eiusdem doctrinae haereticalis sunt fautores.
units.tr: DISCIP. Tell me the other opinion. MAG. The other opinion holds that all bishops and prelates who solemnly publish and spread, before those subject to them, the whole erroneous doctrine of the heretical Pope as if it were Catholic, are promoters of heretical depravity, whether they know it to be erroneous or do not know it. This can apparently be clearly proved by the argument made for the first part of the earlier opinion. For whoever consents by giving aid or effort, so that heretical doctrine is taught and held as Catholic, is a promoter of heretical depravity. Such are the bishops and prelates who, either themselves or through others, publish and spread the erroneous doctrine of the heretical Pope as Catholic. Therefore they are approved promoters of heretical depravity. The minor premise is evident. The major is shown by the testimony of Pope Pius, who, as we read in Dist. 83, chapter "Quid enim prodest," says: For what does it profit him not to be defiled by his own error, who gives consent to one who errs? That is, nothing. Therefore nothing profits him, who gives consent by giving aid or effort so that the Pope's error is spread as Catholic, toward being excused from the promotion of heresy. Second, thus: he who does not resist an error seems to sin no less than he who spreads the error and publishes it as Catholic. But he who does not resist an error is judged to approve it, as is clearly proved by several authorities, some of which have been cited. Therefore much more does he who spreads and publishes an error as Catholic clearly approve it. But he who approves an error is a supporter of that error. Therefore the bishops and prelates who publish and spread the erroneous doctrine of the heretical Pope are supporters of that heretical doctrine.

units.la: Tertio sic. qui aliis offendicula erroris praeparat, fautor erroris est censendus. sed qui doctrinam Papae erroneam publicat & diuulgat, praeparat audientibus offendicula erroris. ergo fautor erroris est censendus. Quarto sic. ille, qui doctrinam nouam haereticalem Papae tanquam catholicam publicat & diuulgat, sequitur opiniones falsas & nouas. Sed qui consequitur opiniones falsas & nouas, non solum fautor haeresum, sed etiam haereticus est censendus, teste August. qui ait, vt legitur 24. q. 3. c. haereticus: Haereticus est, qui alicuius temporalis commodi & maxime vanagloriae principatus gratia, nouas vel falsas opiniones vel gignit vel sequitur. ergo Episcopi & Praelati, praesertim si vt aliquod commodum consequantur a Papa, & vitent incommodum, opiniones falsas & nouas Papae publicant & diuulgant, non solum fautores, sed etiam haeretici sunt censendi. Quinto sic: qui aliis est causa & occasio fauendi & adhaerendi pertinaciter haereticae prauitati, videtur esse fautor prauitatis eiusdem, & sibi imputari debet. sed Episcopi & Praelati publicantes & diuulgantes doctrinam erroneam Papae haeretici sunt aliis causa & occasio fauendi & pertinaciter adhaerendi eidem doctrinae strinæ erroneæ. ergo taliter publicates sunt fautores hæreticæ prauitatis: & si aliquando audientes eisdem fauerint & pertinaciter adhærere præsumpserint, publicantibus & diuulgantibus imputari debet. maior patet: quia ita punitur, qui causam præstat, sicut ipse faciens, sicut notat Glossa extra de homicidio c. suscepimus. quod etiam ex aliis sacris canonibus elicitur euidenter. quemadmodum enim qui causam damni vel occasionem dat, damnum dedisse videtur, extra de iniuriis de damno dato c. vlt. ita qui causam aut occasionem peccati dat, peccare videtur. qui ergo causam & occasionem fauedi & adhærendi doctrinæ erroneæ dat, peccat mortaliter. tale autem peccatum videtur ad fautoriam vel crimen hæresis debere reduci. ergo talis est fautor hæreticæ prauitatis reputandus.
units.tr: Third, thus: he who prepares stumbling blocks of error for others is to be judged a supporter of error. But he who publishes and spreads the Pope's erroneous doctrine prepares stumbling blocks of error for his hearers. Therefore he is to be judged a supporter of error. Fourth, thus: he who publishes and spreads the Pope's new heretical doctrine as Catholic follows false and new opinions. But he who follows false and new opinions is to be judged not only a supporter of heresies but also a heretic, as Augustine testifies, who says, as we read in C. 24, q. 3, chapter "Haereticus": A heretic is one who, for the sake of some temporal advantage, and especially the vainglory of primacy, either begets or follows new or false opinions. Therefore bishops and prelates, especially if they obtain some advantage from the Pope and avoid disadvantage, who publish and spread the Pope's false and new opinions, are to be judged not only supporters but also heretics. Fifth, thus: he who is the cause and occasion for others of favouring and stubbornly clinging to heretical depravity seems to be a supporter of that same depravity and must be charged with it. But bishops and prelates who publish and spread the erroneous doctrine of the heretical Pope are the cause and occasion for others to favour and stubbornly cling to that same erroneous heretical doctrine. Therefore those who publish it in this way are supporters of heretical depravity, and if their hearers have at some time favoured it and presumed to cling stubbornly to it, it must be charged to those who publish and spread it. The major is plain, because he who provides the cause is punished just as the one who acts, as the Gloss notes on Extra, De homicidio, chapter "Suscepimus." This is also clearly drawn from other sacred canons. For just as he who gives the cause or occasion of harm seems to have caused the harm (Extra, De iniuriis, De damno dato, chapter "Ultimo"), so he who gives the cause or occasion of sin seems to sin. Therefore he who gives the cause and occasion of favouring and clinging to erroneous doctrine sins mortally. Such a sin seems to be reducible to the crime of favouring or of heresy. Therefore such a person is to be reckoned a supporter of heretical depravity.

units.la: DISCIP. Videtur quod hæc ratio non procedat. nam secundum August. vt legitur 23. q. 5. c. de occidendis, sæpe bonum & licitum potest esse occasio mali, & tamen tale malum habenti aut facienti bonum ex quo proueniit imputari non debet. ergo quamuis ex prouulgatione & publicatione doctrinæ Papæ audientes faueant & adhæreant pertinaciter eidem doctrinæ erroneæ publicantibus imputari non debet. aliter enim sequeretur, quod nullus deberet aliquam doctrinam erroneam coram aliis ad improbandum legere, vel etiam recitare: quia ex tali recitatione posset contingere, quod aliqui audientes qui doctrinam huiusmodi nunquam ante audiuerant, fauere eidem inciperent, & pertinaciter adhærerent.
units.tr: DISCIP. It seems that this argument does not hold. For according to Augustine, as we read in C. 23, q. 5, chapter "De occidendis," what is good and lawful can often be the occasion of evil, and yet evil that arises from a good deed is not to be imputed to the one who does or has done the good. Therefore, although by the promulgation and publication of the Pope's doctrine the hearers favour it and stubbornly cling to it, this must not be imputed to those who publish it. Otherwise it would follow that no one ought to read out, or even recite, an erroneous doctrine before others in order to refute it, since from such a recitation it could happen that some hearers, who had never heard this doctrine before, would begin to favour it and cling to it stubbornly.

units.la: MAGIST. Ista ratio faciliter (vt nonnullis apparet) refellitur. nam sicut ex dictis maiorum elicitur: si quis dat operam rei licitæ ac diligentiam debitam adhibet, ei minime imputatur, si aliquid mali inde acciderit. & in hoc casu loquitur August. in prædicto capitulo dicens: absit vt ea quæ propter bonum & licitum facimus siper hæc præter nostram voluntatem quicquam mali accideret, nobis imputetur. Si vero aliquis dat operam rei illicitæ, & debitam diligentiam non adhibet, si aliquid mali acciderit, sibi merito imputandum est, extra de homicidio c. presbyterum. & c. continebatur, & ex pluribus aliis sacris canonibus elicitur euidenter. Cum igitur qui doctrinam Papæ hæretici erroneam tanquam catholicam publicat & diuulgat, det operam rei illicitæ, & diligentiam debitam nequaquam adhibeat: si ex tali publicatione vel diuulgatione aliquis fauerit vel pertinaciter adhærerit doctrinæ erroneæ Papæ hæretici, publicanti & diuulganti non immerito imputatur. secus autem de illo, qui publicat vel legit ipsam & improbat: quia non dat operam rei illicitæ. & ideo si aliqui audientes ex malitia propria eidem doctrinæ fauerint vel pertinaciter adhæserint, publicanti & diuulganti imputari non debet.
units.tr: MAGIST. This argument is easily refuted, as it seems to some. For, as is drawn from the sayings of the elders, if someone gives effort to a lawful thing and applies due diligence, nothing of the evil that happens from it is imputed to him. Augustine speaks in this sense in the chapter mentioned above, saying: Far be it that anything evil which happens to us, beyond our will, from things we do for a good and lawful end, should be imputed to us. But if someone gives effort to an unlawful thing and does not apply due diligence, then if any evil follows, it is rightly imputed to him (Extra, De homicidio, chapters "Presbyterum" and "Continebatur"), and this is clearly drawn from many other sacred canons. Since, then, he who publishes and spreads the erroneous doctrine of the heretical Pope as Catholic gives effort to an unlawful thing and by no means applies due diligence, if from such publication or dissemination anyone favours or stubbornly clings to the erroneous doctrine of the heretical Pope, it is not unjustly imputed to the one who publishes and spreads it. It is otherwise with one who publishes or reads it in order to refute it, for he does not give effort to an unlawful thing. And so, if some hearers favour or stubbornly cling to that doctrine out of their own malice, it must not be imputed to the one who publishes and spreads it.

units.la: DISCIP. Dic quomodo secundum istam sententiam ad rationem in contrarium factam in præcedenti capitulo respondetur.
units.tr: DISCIP. Tell me how, according to this opinion, the argument made to the contrary in the previous chapter is answered.

units.la: MAGIST. Ad istam respondetur, quod quando quis implet præceptum superioris, de quo non tenetur scire, antequam impleat, quod est contra præceptum Dei, non peccat implendo. si autem tenetur scire, quod est contra Dei præceptum, peccat implendo, licet nesciat hoc esse contra præceptum Dei. quia quantum ad id, quod quis tenetur scire, ignorantia non excusat. prælati autem & episcopi antequam publicent & diuulgent diffinitionem Papæ, tenentur scire an sit consona vel dissona catholicæ veritati: nec (antequam sciant) hanc diffinitionem Papæ aliqualiter debent publicare tanquam catholicam. circa enim publicationem authenticam & solennem eorum, quæ ad fidem spectant, est cautela diligentissima adhibenda: quia si erratur in fide, nullum bonum (imo etiam mors pro nomine Christi suscepta) potest proficere ad salutem, & ideo nullas circa causam cuiuscunque maiorem debet adhibere cautelam, quam circa ea quæ ad fidem spectant. cum ergo nullus episcopus vel prælatus debeat quemquam subditum suum de crimine damnare, antequam diligenter inquisierit veritatem: multo magis nullam doctrinam debet solenniter publicare (tanquam catholicam) antequam aperte cognouerit, quod est consona catholicæ veritati.
units.tr: MAGIST. To this it is answered that when someone carries out a command of a superior, about which he is not bound to know before he carries it out, that it is contrary to the command of God, he does not sin in carrying it out. But if he is bound to know that it is contrary to God's command, he sins in carrying it out, even though he does not know that it is contrary to God's command, because ignorance does not excuse in what a man is bound to know. But prelates and bishops, before they publish and spread the Pope's decision, are bound to know whether it agrees or disagrees with Catholic truth; nor (before they know this) ought they in any way to publish this decision of the Pope as Catholic. For in the authentic and solemn publication of matters which pertain to the faith the most careful caution must be applied, because if one errs in the faith, no good (indeed not even death undergone for the name of Christ) can profit toward salvation. Therefore they ought to apply no greater caution in any cause whatever than in matters which pertain to the faith. Since no bishop or prelate ought to condemn any of his subjects of a crime before he has diligently inquired into the truth, much more ought he not to publish solemnly any doctrine (as Catholic) before he has clearly known that it agrees with Catholic truth.

units.la: DIS. Ad episcopos vel prælatos examinare non pertinet doctrinam Papæ sibi sub bullis transmissam, sed tantummodo iuxta mandatum Papæ eam debent eorum subditis publicare.
units.tr: DIS. It does not pertain to bishops or prelates to examine the Pope's doctrine sent to them under bulls; they ought only, according to the Pope's command, to publish it to their subjects.

units.la: MAG. Videtur nonnullis, quod hic omnino à veritate recedis. nam secundum canones in rebus maioribus est maior inquisitio & examinatio facienda. 7. q. 2. c. vlt. episcopi & prælati recipientes mandatum Papæ super prouisionibus clericorum & aliis rebus multo minoribus, quam sit catholica fides, sibi bullas missas licite examinant diligenter. quod eis esse licitum Alexander tertius asserit manifeste, vt habetur extra de rescriptis c. si quando, qui ait: si quando aliqua fraternitati tuae dirigimus, quae animum tuum exasperare videntur, turbari non debes. & infra: qualitatem negotii, pro quo tibi scribitur, diligenter consideres, aut mandatum nostrum reuerenter adimpleas, aut per literas tuas, quare adimplere non possis, rationabilem causam pretendas. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod licet recipienti mandatum Papæ qualitatem negotii, pro quo scribitur, examinare & discutere diligenter. ergo multomagis si Papa scribit aliquid, quod tangit fidem, scripturam sacram examinare & discutere oportet diligenter. & si inueniatur in ea aliquid fidei obuians orthodoxæ, est nullatenus publicandum.
units.tr: MAG. Some think you here depart entirely from the truth. For according to the canons, in weightier matters a greater inquiry and examination must be made. 7. q. 2. c. vlt.: bishops and prelates who receive a mandate from the Pope concerning provisions of clergy and other matters far less important than the Catholic faith lawfully examine the bulls sent to them with care. That this is lawful for them Alexander the Third plainly asserts, as is found in Extra, de rescriptis, c. si quando, where he says: "If at any time we send to your brotherhood things which seem to vex your mind, you ought not to be disturbed. And below: consider carefully the nature of the business for which you are written to, and either faithfully carry out our mandate, or in your letter put forward a reasonable cause why you cannot carry it out." From these words it is gathered that, although the one receiving a papal mandate ought to examine and carefully weigh the nature of the business for which he is written to, much more, then, if the Pope writes something that touches the faith, ought one to examine and carefully weigh it by Holy Scripture. And if anything is found in it opposed to the orthodox faith, it is by no means to be published.

units.la: DIS. Forte episcopi & prælati non sunt in scriptura diuina excellenter instructi. quare ad eos profunde scripturam scrutari non spectat. & ideo non debent doctrinam Papæ discutere.
units.tr: DIS. Perhaps bishops and prelates are not excellently instructed in divine Scripture. Therefore it does not belong to them to search the Scripture deeply, and so they ought not to examine the doctrine of the Pope.

units.la: MAGIST. Dicunt nonnulli, quod hoc est principium periclitationis fidei Christianæ, constituere episcopos & prælatos scripturarum diuinarum ignaros. quia iuxta sententiam Saluatoris, si cæcus cæco ducatum præstet, ambo in foueam cadunt.
units.tr: MAGIST. Some say that this is the principle of endangering the Christian faith: to appoint bishops and prelates ignorant of the divine Scriptures, because according to the saying of the Saviour, "if the blind lead the blind, both fall into the pit."

units.la: DISCIP. De episcopis & prælatis non habentibus sacrarum literarum peritiam in trastatu De gestis circa fidem altercantium orthodoxam aliqua indagare studebo. Nunc vero quomodo per istam sententiam ad auctoritatem August. respondere contingat, expone.
units.tr: DISCIP. I shall endeavour to inquire into the matter of bishops and prelates who lack skill in the sacred letters, in the treatise On the deeds of those disputing about the orthodox faith. Now, however, explain how it comes about that this sentence answers the authority of Augustine.

units.la: MAGIST. Dicitur quod August. loquitur de militante sub rege sacrilego, quando non tenetur scire an praeceptum regis sit contra praeceptum Dei: & cum hoc nescit. Si vero miles ignorat praeceptum regis esse contra praeceptum Dei, & tamen tenetur scire, obediendo peccat. Nam si rex praeciperet militi, dicens, interfice istum, quia colit Deum, miles interficiendo peccaret, quia scire tenetur, quod nullus debet interfici propter hoc quod colit Deum.
units.tr: MAGIST. It is said that Augustine speaks of a soldier serving under a sacrilegious king, when he is not bound to know whether the king's command is against the command of God, and so he does not know it. But if the soldier is ignorant that the king's command is against the command of God, and yet is bound to know it, he sins by obeying. For if a king should order a soldier, saying, "kill that man, because he worships God," the soldier, by killing, would sin, because he is bound to know that no one ought to be killed on account of worshipping God.

units.la: CAP. XXXVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXVII.

units.la: In quo ponitur tertia opinio medians inter duas praecedentes et declarando.
units.tr: In which a third opinion is set out, midway between the two preceding ones, and explained.

units.la: DISCIP. Contingit ne aliter respondere ad interrogationem meam, supra c. 35. propositam? MAGIST. Vna est sententia, quae inter praedictas sententias aliquo modo media videtur: Quia distinguit de erronea doctrina Papae haeretici. Aut enim assertio est explicite condemnata, utpote quia sub propria forma est condemnata, vel quia est contraria alicui veritati explicite approbatae: qualis est omnis veritas in scriptura divina & determinationibus ecclesiae assertive contenta. Aut assertio Papae haeretici est solummodo implicite condemnata: qualis est omnis error, qui scripturae divinae vel determinationibus ecclesiae vniversalis repugnat, cuiusmodi sunt multae opiniones theologorum: qui circa ea, quae ad fidem spectant, contrarie opinantur. Quare constat, quod vna contrariarum illarum est erronea, & haeresis saltem implicite condemnata. Quia veritas contradictoria est saltem implicite approbata, eo quod omnis veritas catholica quantumcunque latens & multis incognita est per vniversalem ecclesiam in genere etiam implicite approbata. Si assertio Papae erronea est solum implicite condemnata, diuulgantes eam & publicantes tanquam catholicam obediendo mandato Papae, qui mandaret, quod talis assertio ab omnibus tanquam catholica teneatur, non sunt haeretici, nec fautores haereticae pravitatis, nec peccant mortaliter eam taliter publicando. Quemadmodum theologi non peccant mortaliter docendo & tenendo assertiones, quae in rei veritate sunt erroneae & haereticales, quas tamen non sciunt nec tenentur scire esse erroneas. Si vero assertio Papae erronea est explicite condemnata, quia est contradictoria alicuius assertionis, quae in scriptura divina vel determinatione ecclesiae sub forma propria continetur, vel patenter omnibus, sequitur ex assertione tali episcopi vel praelati, talem assertionem Papae solenniter diuulgantes tanquam catholicam sunt fautores reputandi haereticae pravitatis; quia nullam assertionem debent solenniter publicare, antequam constiterit eis quod non est haeretica explicite condemnata: & si hoc non possunt faciliter scire per seipsos, debent consulere peritos.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Can you answer my question, which I put to you above in chapter 35, in some other way? MASTER. There is one view which seems in some respect to lie between the opinions already mentioned. It distinguishes the erroneous teaching of a heretical Pope. Either the assertion is explicitly condemned, either because it is condemned in its own proper form or because it contradicts some truth that has been explicitly approved, such as every truth asserted in divine Scripture and in the determinations of the Church. Or the assertion of a heretical Pope is condemned only implicitly, as is every error that conflicts with divine Scripture or with the determinations of the universal Church, which is the case with many opinions of theologians who hold contrary views on matters that pertain to the faith. Hence it is plain that one of these contrary opinions is erroneous and at least implicitly condemned as heresy, since the contradictory truth is at least implicitly approved, because every catholic truth, however hidden and unknown to many, is approved in general by the universal Church, even implicitly. If the Pope's erroneous assertion is only implicitly condemned, then those who spread it and publish it as catholic, in obedience to a papal mandate that orders such an assertion to be held by all as catholic, are not heretics, nor supporters of heretical depravity, nor do they sin mortally in publishing it in this way. Just as theologians do not sin mortally by teaching and holding assertions that in truth are erroneous and heretical, which they do not know, and are not bound to know, to be erroneous. But if the Pope's erroneous assertion is explicitly condemned, because it contradicts some assertion that is contained in its own form in divine Scripture or in a determination of the Church, or that is plainly known to all, then it follows that bishops or prelates who solemnly publish such an assertion of the Pope as catholic must be regarded as supporters of heretical depravity. For they ought not to publish any assertion solemnly until it is clear to them that it is not explicitly condemned as heretical; and if they cannot easily know this by themselves, they ought to consult experts.

units.la: DISCIP. Quid si periti dicunt eis, quod talis assertio Papae non est explicite condemnata; sed est consona veritati.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. What if the experts tell them that such an assertion of the Pope is not explicitly condemned, but agrees with the truth?

units.la: MAGIST. Respondetur, quod non debet sufficere eis, quod periti hoc eis dicant solo verbo, sed debent petere ab eisdem peritis, ut eis evidenter ostendant, quod sit consona catholicae veritati. Quod si hoc facere periti non potuerint, debent supersedere & assertionem Papae erroneam explicite condemnatam nullatenus publicare. Quemadmodum episcopi & praelati, quando considerant, vel etiam dubitant, quod mandatum Papae est eis praeiudiciale, ipsum deserunt adimplere: & quod adimplere minime teneantur, multis & fortibus allegationibus probare nituntur. Ergo multo fortius si assertio Papae est consona catholicae veritati, mandatum Papae super tali publicatione facienda adimplere non debent: sed debent ostendere causas, quare tale mandatum implere non possunt. Si enim episcopi & praelati recipientes Papae mandatum (quod eorum honori vel commodo temporali obviare videtur) ipsum non implere tenentur, sed cum maxima diligentia allegare conantur, quod tale mandatum est praeiudiciale; & ideo adimplere non debent. Si vero recipiunt mandatum Papae super aliquo, quod ad fidem spectat, & non curant studiosissime per se & per alios inquagare, an tale mandatum derogat quocumque modo honori divino & fidei orthodoxae, sed statim absque omni deliberatione sufficienti praecipitanter assertionem erroneam tanquam catholicam publicant & diuulgant: ostendunt aperte, quod ea quae sua sunt quaerunt, non quae Iesu Christi. An enim per mandatum Papae ab eorum diuitiis vel honore aliquid depereat diligentissime inuestigant. Sed an per mandatum Papae eorum si des catholica destruatur, penitus non attendunt. & ideo si diligentiam debitam non adhibent, & publicant solenniter haereticam pravitatem, fautores haereticae pravitatis sunt censendi.
units.tr: MASTER. The answer is that it should not be enough for them that the experts merely say this to them in words; they ought to ask the same experts to show them clearly that it agrees with catholic truth. But if the experts cannot do this, they must hold back and in no way publish the Pope's assertion, which is explicitly condemned as erroneous. Just as bishops and prelates, when they consider, or even doubt, that a papal mandate is prejudicial to them, refuse to carry it out, and labour to prove by many strong arguments that they are not bound to carry it out. Therefore, much more strongly, if the Pope's assertion agrees with catholic truth, they ought not to carry out a papal mandate concerning its publication, but ought to show the reasons why they cannot carry out such a mandate. For if bishops and prelates, when they receive a papal mandate that seems to stand in the way of their honour or temporal advantage, are not bound to carry it out, but strive with the greatest care to argue that it is prejudicial and therefore must not be carried out, and yet when they receive a papal mandate on some matter that pertains to the faith, do not take the most careful pains, by themselves and through others, to inquire whether that mandate in any way detracts from the honour of God and the orthodox faith, but immediately, without any sufficient deliberation, rashly publish and spread an erroneous assertion as catholic, they show plainly that they seek what is their own, not what is of Jesus Christ. For they investigate most diligently whether anything is lost to their riches or honour through the papal mandate; but whether the catholic faith is destroyed by it, they do not consider at all. Therefore, if they do not apply the diligence that is due, and solemnly publish heretical depravity, they are to be counted as supporters of heretical depravity.

units.la: DISCIP. Non videtur licitum indagare, an sententia Papae super aliquo, quod tangit fidem, sit consona veritati, quia si hoc esset licitum, liceret episcopis & praelatis de sententia Papae super causa fidei disputare, quod non videtur verum; quia secundum Nicolaum Papam, ut legitur 17. q. 4. c. nemini: nulli licet de iudicio sedis apostolicae iudicare, & per consequens nemini licet de eiusdem iudicio disputare. Tum quia de illius sententia in causa fidei, ad quam causa fidei sunt vltimo deferendae, non est licitum disputare. Ille autem est Papa, ergo de sententia Papae disputare non licet. MAGIST. Ista friuola reputantur. Nam de sententiis iudicis & lite[illegible, ~6 letters] summi pontificis tota die licite disputatur: & cum sollicitudine maxima examinantur, discutiuntur & videntur. Quod enim de sententia Papæ licite disputetur etiam in dubium revoluendo, an sit iuste lata, probatur. nam de sententia, quæ potest retractari, & in melius commutari, teste Greg. qui vt habetur 35. q.9.c. apostolica, ait: Apostolicæ sedis sententia tanta super consilii moderatione temperatur, tanta patientia & maturitate decoquitur, tantaque deliberationis gravitate profertur, vt nec immutari necessarium ducat, nisi forte sic prolata sit, vt retractari possit vel immutari, si secundum tenorem premissæ conditionis exigat. Ex quibus verbis colligitur evidenter, quod apostolicæ sedis sententia retractari potest & etiam immutari. cui etiam Innocentius Papa, causa & q. prædicitis, capitulo veniam, concordare videtur, dicens: Veniam nunc ad maximum Fotinum, quasi ad quoddam thema, & quod mihi anxium est ac dissimulandum maiorum meorum (scilicet prædecessorum) revoluam (hoc est, revocabo sententias contra Fotinum) fuerat de illo quoquo pacto (id est aliqua fraude) vt ipsi etiam communem iniustis, aliquid utique gravius constitutum. verum quoniam id quod per rumorem falsum, vt asseritis, surreptum huic sedi & elicitum per insidias demonstratur, quia res ad salutem redit, venia tantum vobis hunc admittentibus post condemnationem more apostolico subrogamus, sanctisque vestris assentientibus vobisque tam bonis tamque caris non dare consensum omnibus duris rebus durius arbitramur. Ex quib. colligitur, quod sententia summi pontificis retractari potest. quod Nicolaus Papa, vt habetur sequenti c. sententiam, asserit dicens: sententiam Romanæ sedis non negamus posse in melius commutari, cum aut surreptum aliquid fuerit, aut ipsa pro consideratione ætatum aut temporum seu gravium necessitatum dispensatione, quædam ordinare decreverit. & infra: quod tamen observandum est quando illa (videlicet Romana ecclesia) discretissima consideratione hoc fieri diligenter prosperexerit. Ex quibus colligitur, quod sententia Romanæ sedis potest retractari & in melius commutari. & per consequens licet de tali sententia disputare, quomodo etiam super literis & scripturis summi pontificis tota die coram iudice disputatur & etiam litigatur, nullus, qui sequitur, causas ignorat. ergo licet super sententia Papæ disputare. DIS. Causa, quare super rescriptis in literis summi pontificis licite disputatur, est: quia literæ sæpe per rescriptionem & falsas suggestiones impetrantur; quandoque etiam Papa multis ex causis decipi potest. unde super talibus literis disputare licet. illa autem quæ emergunt contra fidem, & diffiniuntur per Papam, deliberatione maxima proferuntur, & super illis disputare non licet. MAGIST. Ex ista sententia putant nonnulli se per demonstrationem probare. Quod sententia Papæ super aliqua difficultate fidei lata est per peritos, ad quorum notitiam pervenerit cum maxima diligentia & studio examinanda, & super ea disputare licet. & si inventa fuerit disputando contraria veritati est penitus respuenda, & omnimode reprobanda. Primo probatur sic. vbi est eadem causa, eundem debet habere effectum. causa autem, quare literæ Papæ, quæcunque sint, inspiciendæ diligenter ac videndæ & examinandæ sunt, & quare de eis disputare licet, & quare eis obedire in casu nequaquam oportet; & quia Papa potest decipi. si enim Papa nullo modo posset decipi, prædicta non liceret. sed Papa ita bene potest decipi circa ea quæ sunt fidei, sicut circa quæcunque alia. aliter enim Papa hæreticari non posset, cuius oppositum supra libr. 5. auctoritatibus, rationibus & exemplis multipliciter est ostensum. ergo literæ Papæ, quæ super aliqua difficultate fidei emanare noscuntur, diligentissime sunt videndæ & examinandæ, & de iis disputare licet. & si a quocunque prælato vel subdito, discipulo vel magistro, fuerint deprehensæ a fide recedere orthodoxa, sunt penitus respuendæ & efficaciter reprobandæ.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. It does not seem lawful to inquire whether the Pope's opinion on some matter that touches the faith agrees with the truth. For if this were lawful, it would be lawful for bishops and prelates to dispute about the Pope's judgment on a matter of faith, which does not seem true. For according to Pope Nicholas, as we read in 17 q. 4 c. Nemini, no one is permitted to judge the judgment of the Apostolic See, and consequently no one is permitted to dispute about its judgment. Also, because it is not lawful to dispute about his decision in a matter of faith, to which matters of faith are finally to be referred. But that man is the Pope; therefore it is not lawful to dispute about the Pope's judgment. MASTER. These arguments are regarded as trifling. For the sentences of judges, and of the supreme pontiff in disputes, are lawfully disputed all day long, and are examined, discussed and scrutinised with the greatest care. That it is lawful to dispute about the Pope's judgment, even calling in doubt whether it was justly pronounced, is proved as follows. For concerning a judgment that can be retracted and changed for the better, Gregory says, as we have it in 35 q. 9 c. Apostolica: The sentence of the Apostolic See is tempered with such moderation of counsel, is ripened with such patience and maturity, and is pronounced with such gravity of deliberation, that it does not think it necessary to be changed, unless perhaps it has been so pronounced that it can be retracted or changed, if the tenor of the condition set out above requires it. From these words it is plainly gathered that the sentence of the Apostolic See can be retracted and also changed. Pope Innocent also seems to agree with this, in the case and question mentioned above, in the chapter Veniam, where he says: I shall now come to the greatest Photinus, as to a certain theme, and I shall revisit what is troubling and must be concealed by my elders (that is, my predecessors), that is, I shall revoke the sentences against Photinus. It had been decided in some way about him (that is, by some fraud) that something more severe should be imposed even on those who were wrongly... But since what is shown to have been obtained from this See by false rumour, as you assert, and drawn out by plots, is returning to salvation, we grant pardon to you, admitting him after condemnation in the apostolic manner, and with your holy assent, and we think it harsher than all harsh things not to give consent to you who are so good and so dear. From these words it is gathered that the sentence of the supreme pontiff can be retracted. Pope Nicholas also asserts this, as we have it in the following chapter, Sententiam, where he says: We do not deny that the sentence of the Roman See can be changed for the better, since either something has been obtained by stealth, or it has itself decreed some ordinance in consideration of ages and times or by dispensation of grave necessities. And below: This, however, is to be observed when that Church has carefully weighed that it is to be done with the most discreet consideration. From these words it is gathered that the sentence of the Roman See can be retracted and changed for the better; and consequently it is lawful to dispute about such a sentence, just as, in fact, disputes and even lawsuits about the letters and writings of the supreme pontiff go on all day in court, and no one who follows the cases is ignorant of them. Therefore it is lawful to dispute about the Pope's sentence. DISCIPLE. The reason why it is lawful to dispute about rescripts in the letters of the supreme pontiff is this: letters are often obtained by rescript and false suggestions; and sometimes the Pope himself can be deceived for many reasons. Hence it is lawful to dispute about such letters. But those matters which arise against the faith and are defined by the Pope are pronounced with the greatest deliberation, and it is not lawful to dispute about them. MASTER. From this argument some think they prove their point by demonstration: that a sentence of the Pope on some difficulty of faith, pronounced by experts, is to be examined with the greatest care and diligence by those who come to know of it, and that it is lawful to dispute about it; and if it is found, in disputing, to be contrary to the truth, it is to be wholly rejected and altogether condemned. First, it is proved thus: where the cause is the same, the effect must be the same. But the reason why the Pope's letters, whatever they are, must be carefully inspected, examined and scrutinised, and why it is lawful to dispute about them, and why in a case of this kind we are by no means bound to obey them, is that the Pope can be deceived. For if the Pope could in no way be deceived, the foregoing would not be lawful. But the Pope can be deceived as well about matters of faith as about anything else. For otherwise the Pope could not be made a heretic, which the opposite has been shown in many ways, by authorities, reasons and examples, above in book 5. Therefore the Pope's letters, which are known to have been issued on some difficulty of faith, must be most diligently seen and examined, and it is lawful to dispute about them. And if, by any prelate or subject, disciple or teacher, they are found to depart from the orthodox faith, they are to be wholly rejected and effectively condemned.

units.la: DISCIP. Quare ergo quotidie cernimus prælatos & alios de literis Papæ, quæ tangunt negotia tantum ecclesiastica, disputare, & omnes timent disputare de diffinitione Papæ super his quæ ad fidem pertinent orthodoxam?
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Why, then, do we see every day that prelates and others dispute the letters of the Pope that concern only ecclesiastical business, while everyone is afraid to dispute the Pope's definitions on matters that pertain to orthodox faith?

units.la: MAGIST. Causa multiplex assignati potest. vna tamen præcipua assignanda est ad præsens, quæ est defectus zeli catholicæ veritatis & amor terrenarum divitiarum & honorum. quia enim multi Christiani nihil asperum, nihil difficile, nullum periculum, nullam indignationem alicuius potentis, quem timent, volunt pro fide catholica sustinere, nec curant an fides proficiat aut deficiat. ideo nolunt disputare de diffinitionibus Papæ, quia eius indignationem timent incurrere. pro temporalibus autem divitiis & honoribus labores & pericula sunt parati sustinere. ideo ( quia ex disputatione de literis Papæ, quæ ipsorum tangunt negocia) sperant honores vel divitias adipisci, vel saltem damnum vel periculum temporale evitare in disputatione de huiusmodi literis summi pontificis non verentur. & similiter si de disputatione super sententia Papæ hæretica honorem vel commodum sperarent, de ipsa disputare nullatenus formidarent.
units.tr: MASTER. Many causes could be given, but for now one chief cause should be named: a lack of zeal for Catholic truth, and a love of earthly riches and honours. Many Christians do not want to endure anything harsh or difficult, any danger, or the anger of some powerful person whom they fear, for the sake of the Catholic faith, and they do not care whether the faith advances or declines. So they are unwilling to dispute the Pope's definitions, because they fear to incur his anger. But for temporal riches and honours they are ready to undergo labours and dangers. So, if they hope to gain honours or riches, or at least to avoid temporal loss or danger, by disputing letters of the Pope that touch their own affairs, they do not hesitate to dispute such letters of the supreme pontiff. Likewise, if they hoped for honour or advantage from disputing a heretical sentence of the Pope, they would not be in the least afraid to dispute it.

units.la: DISCIP. Dic quomodo respondetur ad secundam, per quam probant quod non licet alicui de sententia Papæ super fide catholica disputare.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Tell me how you answer the second argument, by which they prove that it is not lawful for anyone to dispute the Pope's sentence on Catholic faith.

units.la: MAGIST. Quod quamvis ad summum pontificem sunt causæ fidei deferendæ, quia tamen summus pontifex errare potest contra fidem, sententia eius super difficultate aliqua fidei Christianæ est studiosissime examinanda & diligentissime disputanda. & si per disputationem vel per aliquem modum fuerit deprehensa a veritate deviare catholica, est penitus condemnanda, & tanquam hæretica reputanda exemplo catholicorum, qui vt colligitur ex decretis, di. 19. c. secundum ecclesiam & §. quia ergo & c. Anastasius secundus, diffinitionem hæreticalem Anastasii hic sollicite inspexerunt, & an esset consona catholicæ veritati quæsierunt attente, sive dis-putansputando sive alio modo, quam cum inuenissent contrariam fidei orthodoxae tanquam haereticam respuerunt. & ita constat quod de diffinitione Papae antequam sciatur esse catholica, est licitum disputare.
units.tr: MASTER. Although causes of faith are to be referred to the supreme pontiff, nevertheless, since the supreme pontiff can err against the faith, his sentence on any difficulty of Christian faith must be most carefully examined and diligently disputed. If, whether by disputation or some other means, it is found to deviate from Catholic truth, it must be utterly condemned and regarded as heretical, following the example of Catholics. As may be gathered from the decrees (dist. 19, c. Secundum ecclesiam, and §. Quia ergo, and c. Anastasius secundus), they carefully examined the heretical definition of Anastasius, sought attentively whether it agreed with Catholic truth, whether by disputing or otherwise, and when they found it contrary to orthodox faith, they rejected it as heretical. Thus it is clear that it is lawful to dispute the Pope's definition before it is known to be Catholic.

units.la: DISCIP. Omnes catholici absque omni inquisitione debent supponere, quod diffinitio Papae super fide catholica sit consona fidei orthodoxae. & Gregorius dicit, vt allegatum est supra, apostolica sedis sententia praecipue super his quae spectant ad fidem, tanta semper concilii moderatione concipitur, tanta patientia & maturitate decoquitur, tantaque deliberationis consilii gravitate profertur, vt omnino recta sit credenda. ergo omnes debent praesumere sententiam Papae catholicam esse. quare eam examinare non debent; nec de ea disputare licet.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. All Catholics ought, without any inquiry, to assume that the Pope's definition on the Catholic faith agrees with orthodox faith. And Gregory says, as was cited above: "The sentence of the apostolic see, especially on those matters that concern the faith, is always conceived with such moderation of counsel, is ripened with such patience and maturity, and is delivered with such gravity of deliberation, that it is to be believed entirely right." Therefore everyone ought to presume that the Pope's sentence is Catholic. Hence they ought not to examine it, nor is it lawful to dispute it.

units.la: MAG. Ad hoc respondetur, quod Gregorius loquitur de modo, qui seruari debet circa sententiam apostolicae sedis: & etiam qui (vt frequenter) seruatus est. cum hoc tamen fiat, quod talis modus possit omitti circa sententiam Papae, quemadmodum Anastasius secundus talem modum circa sententiam suam non seruauit. Et ideo quamuis sententia Papae (maxime circa fidem) tanta consilii moderatione concipi debeat, tantaque maturitate patientiae decoqui, & tanta deliberationis gravitate proferri, vt antequam contrarium euidenter appareat, praesumi debeat consona veritati. quia tamen potest errare contra fidem, potest esse proprii sensus, & prudentiae ac sapientiae propriae nimis inniti, ac copiositatis, praecipitationis, praesumptionis & temeritatis vicio laborare, non est tam firmiter & tam certitudinaliter praesumendum prosententia Papae, quin debeat diligenter examinari, discuti & videri. & quando de ea (antequam non solum modo praesumptive, sed etiam euidenter constiterit quod a veritate non deviat) liceat disputare: quemadmodum de omnibus literis Papae praesumendum est, quod antequam constiterit contrarium, quod eis oporteat obedire, non tamen debet ista praesumptio esse violenta, vt non liceat literas Papae examinare & inuestigare sollicite an eis oporteat obedire. Omnes ergo sententiae quae contra fidem & bonos mores possunt emergere, examinandae sunt diligentissime & probandae iuxta illud Apo. omnia probate: quod de illis, quae dubia esse possunt, debet intelligi.
units.tr: MASTER. To this it is answered that Gregory speaks of the manner that ought to be observed with regard to the sentence of the apostolic see, and which (as is frequently the case) has been observed. Yet this manner may be omitted with regard to a papal sentence, just as Anastasius the Second did not observe such a manner with regard to his own sentence. And so, although a papal sentence (especially on faith) ought to be conceived with such moderation of counsel, ripened with such maturity of patience, and delivered with such gravity of deliberation, that it ought to be presumed to agree with truth until the contrary clearly appears, nevertheless, since it can err against the faith, can rest on his own opinion, lean too much on his own prudence and wisdom, and suffer from the vices of haste, rashness, presumption and temerity, it is not to be presumed so firmly and so certainly concerning the Pope's sentence that it need not be diligently examined, discussed and scrutinised. And it is lawful to dispute it, not only when it is presumptively but also when it is clearly established that it does not deviate from truth. Just as with all letters of the Pope it is to be presumed that one must obey them until the contrary is established, yet this presumption must not be so strong as to forbid us to examine and carefully investigate the letters of the Pope, to see whether we ought to obey them. Therefore all sentences that may arise against the faith and good morals are to be most diligently examined and tested, according to that saying of the Apostle: "Prove all things" (1 Thess. 5). This must be understood of those things that may be doubtful.

units.la: DISCIP. Contra praedicta, vna mihi adhuc occurrit obiectio. videtur enim, quod episcopi & praelati publicantes & diuulgantes doctrinam Papae haereticam non sint fautores haereticae prauitatis. imo etiam videtur, quod hoc possunt facere absque peccato mortali. nam minus est praedicare & diuulgare solummodo doctrinam haereticalem alterius, quam publica re & docere haeresim manifestam alienam vel propriam. Sed absque peccato mortali potest quis ex ignorantia vel simplicitate praedicare publice & docere haeresim manifestam, cuius contrarium in scripturis sacris reperitur expresse, quia quamuis publice quis praedicet vel doceat haeresim manifestam (si paratus est corrigi) non est haereticus, & per consequens non peccat mortaliter. ergo multo magis & fortius possunt praelati publicare doctrinam Papae haereticalem absque peccato mortali. & per consequens absque fautoria haereticae prauitatis.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Against what has been said, one objection still occurs to me. For it seems that bishops and prelates who publish and spread a heretical doctrine of the Pope are not supporters of heretical depravity. Indeed, it seems that they can do this even without mortal sin. For it is less to preach and spread merely the heretical doctrine of another than to publicly profess and teach a manifest heresy, whether of another or of one's own. But without mortal sin someone may, through ignorance or simplicity, publicly preach and teach a manifest heresy, the contrary of which is expressly found in Holy Scripture; for although someone publicly preaches or teaches a manifest heresy, if he is ready to be corrected, he is not a heretic and consequently does not sin mortally. Therefore much more and more strongly can prelates publish a heretical doctrine of the Pope without mortal sin, and consequently without being supporters of heretical depravity.

units.la: MAGIST. Ad hoc respondetur distinguendo: quia aut doctrina erronea Papae est per ipsum solenniter diffinita, & ab eo tanquam Papa determinata, aut ipse Papa assertionem erroneam solummodo praedicat & docet, aut tacet & solenniter non diffinit. Item, aut assertio haeretica Papae est talis, quod episcopi & praelati tenentur explicite credere contrariam veritatem: aut est talis, quod non tenentur explicite credere, sed solummodo implicite. Sintaque episcopi & praelati publicant & diuulgant solenniter per se vel per alios diffinitionem haereticalem Papae, sunt fautores expresse prauitatis haereticae. Si etiam publicant doctrinam Papae haereticalem, cuius contrariam veritatem tenentur credere explicite, peccant mortaliter, & sunt censendi fautores haereticae prauitatis. Si vero publicant aliquam diffinitionem haereticalem Papae seu aliquam assertionem haereticalem, quam absque diffinitione solenni pertinaciter tenet & asserit: & ipsi publicantes contrariam tenentur credere explicite, peccant mortaliter, & sunt censendi fautores haereticae prauitatis. Si vero non publicant aliquam diffinitionem haereticalem Papae, sed aliquam assertionem eius haereticalem, quam absque diffinitione solenni pertinaciter tenet & asserit: & ipsi non tenentur explicite credere contrariam veritatem, non sunt censendi fautores haereticae prauitatis, sed antea examinari debent sollicite, an ex ignorantia vel simplicitate vel pertinacia talem assertionem praedicant & diuulgant, & in hoc probantur publice praedicantes & docentes.
units.tr: MASTER. To this it is answered by distinguishing. Either the Pope's erroneous doctrine has been solemnly defined by him and determined by him as Pope, or the Pope merely preaches and teaches an erroneous assertion, or he is silent and does not solemnly define it. Again, either the Pope's heretical assertion is such that bishops and prelates are bound to believe the contrary truth explicitly, or it is such that they are not bound to believe it explicitly, but only implicitly. Therefore, if bishops and prelates solemnly publish and spread, either themselves or through others, a heretical definition of the Pope, they are plainly supporters of heretical depravity. If they also publish a heretical doctrine of the Pope, the contrary truth of which they are bound to believe explicitly, they sin mortally and are to be counted supporters of heretical depravity. If, however, they publish some heretical definition of the Pope, or some heretical assertion which he obstinately holds and asserts without a solemn definition, and they themselves are bound to believe the contrary explicitly, they sin mortally and are to be counted supporters of heretical depravity. But if they do not publish some heretical definition of the Pope, but some heretical assertion of his, which he obstinately holds and asserts without a solemn definition, and they are not bound to believe the contrary truth explicitly, they are not to be counted supporters of heretical depravity; rather, it must first be carefully examined whether they preach and spread such an assertion through ignorance, simplicity or obstinacy, and by this they are proved to be public preachers and teachers.

units.la: DISCIP. Quare qui diffinitionem Papae haereticalem publicant, sunt fautores haereticae prauitatis; & publice praedicantes haeresim manifestam, vel docentes non sunt censendi fautores haereticae prauitatis, nec etiam peccare mortaliter?
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Why, then, are those who publish a heretical definition of the Pope supporters of heretical depravity, while those who publicly preach or teach a manifest heresy are not to be counted supporters of heretical depravity, nor do they sin mortally?

units.la: MAGIST. Huius ratio assignatur talis. sicut maior deliberatio requiritur ad iuramentum, quam ad simplicem loquelam (& ideo grauius peccat periturus, quam qui simplici loquela mentitur) ita cum maiori deliberatione debet Papa solenniter diffinire quam absque tali diffinitione solenniter docere vel etiam publice praedicare, & grauius peccat, si assertionem contra fidem diffinit solenniter, quam si absque tali diffinitione aliquid contra fidem publice praedicat vel docet. Si enim publice diffinit aliquid contra fidem, habetur pro tenente vltimata deliberatione assertionem suam contra fidem. Sed si solummodo praedicat vel docet contra fidem, non habetur propter hoc pro tenente vltimata deliberatione assertionem suam. ideo post prædicationem publicam examinandus est, an sit paratus corrigi vel non. Si inueniatur paratus corrigi, non est hæreticus reputandus. Si autem non est paratus corrigi, pro hæretico est habendus. Sicut Papa grauius peccat aliquid solenniter diffiniendo contra fidem, quàm solummodo publicè prædicando vel docendo: sic grauius peccat qui solennem diffinitionem hæreticalem Papæ prædicat & diuulgat, quam qui eandem assertionem vel consimilem solum modo publicè docet vel prædicat. & ideo publicando diffinitionem hæreticalem Papæ est fautor hæreticæ prauitatis, sed non solummodo publicè prædicando. DIS. Quare non requiritur tanta deliberatio ad publicè docendum vel prædicandum, quanta requiritur ad aliquid solenniter diffiniendum? MAG. Actus publicè prædicandi & docendi est multo communior & pluribus conuenit, quam aliquid solenniter diffinire. Sicut simpliciter loquela est actus multo communior quam iuratio. & licut non requitur tanta deliberatio ad simplicem loquelam, sicut ad iuramentum (quia sæpe est loquendum & raro iurandum) ita non requiritur tanta deliberatio, cum quis publicè docet & prædicat: sicut cum Papa aliquid tanquam catholicum diffinit solenniter. & ideo quia iste actus diffiniendi solenniter determinando aliquid tanquam catholicum exercere non debet, nisi deliberatio vltimata præcedat. & in hoc casu est error inexcusabilis: quia ad hoc consilium nullus debet accedere, nisi sit sufficienter certus, qualiter non potest aliquis esse de falso. & propter consimilem rationem nullus debet prædicare solenniter diffinitionem Papæ tanquam catholicam circa ea quæ tangunt fidem, nisi sit certus, quod est consona veritati. & ideo excusabilis est, qui solenniter publicat diffinitionem hæreticalem Papæ tanquam catholicam. Secus est de illis, qui non sunt prælati, ad quos solennis publicatio non spectat. & ideo si legunt vel recitant coram aliis multis diffinitionem hæreticalem Papæ, quam nesciunt esse hæreticalem Papæ, non sunt ex hoc ipso fautores hæreticæ prauitatis reputandi.
units.tr: MASTER. The reason for this is assigned as follows. Just as greater deliberation is required for an oath than for a simple statement (and so one who perjures himself sins more gravely than one who lies in a simple statement), so the Pope must define solemnly with greater deliberation than he teaches or even publicly preaches without such a solemn definition, and he sins more gravely if he solemnly defines an assertion contrary to faith than if he publicly preaches or teaches something contrary to faith without such a definition. For if he publicly defines something contrary to faith, he is regarded as holding his assertion against faith after final deliberation. But if he merely preaches or teaches against faith, he is not on that account regarded as holding his assertion after final deliberation. Therefore, after public preaching, it must be examined whether he is ready to be corrected or not. If he is found ready to be corrected, he is not to be regarded as a heretic. But if he is not ready to be corrected, he is to be held as a heretic. Just as the Pope sins more gravely by solemnly defining something against faith than by merely preaching or teaching it publicly, so one who preaches and spreads a solemn heretical definition of the Pope sins more gravely than one who merely teaches or publicly preaches the same or a similar assertion. And so by publishing a heretical definition of the Pope one is a supporter of heretical depravity, but not merely by publicly preaching. DISCIPLE. Why is not as much deliberation required for publicly teaching or preaching as is required for solemnly defining something? MASTER. The act of publicly preaching and teaching is much more common and belongs to many more people than solemnly defining something. Just as simple speech is a much more common act than swearing, and just as not as much deliberation is required for simple speech as for an oath (because one must speak often but swear rarely), so not as much deliberation is required when someone publicly teaches and preaches as when the Pope solemnly defines something as Catholic. And since this act of defining solemnly, determining something as Catholic, ought not to be exercised unless final deliberation precedes it, in this case the error is inexcusable: for no one ought to undertake such counsel unless he is sufficiently certain that he cannot be wrong. And for a similar reason no one ought to preach solemnly a definition of the Pope as Catholic on matters that touch the faith, unless he is certain that it agrees with truth. Therefore one who solemnly publishes a heretical definition of the Pope as Catholic is excusable only in a limited sense... Otherwise it is with those who are not prelates, to whom solemn publication does not belong. And so, if they read or recite before many others a heretical definition of the Pope, which they do not know to be heretical, they are not on that account to be regarded as supporters of heretical depravity.

units.la: CAP. XXXVIII.
units.tr: CAP. XXXVIII.

units.la: In quo agitur de episcopis & ceteris prælatis permittentibus alios docere & prædicare assertionem Papæ hæreticam, vbi probatur multis auctoritatibus & rationibus, quod omnibus modis debent resistere, quia alias sunt fautores et grauiter peccant.
units.tr: In which it is discussed concerning bishops and other prelates who allow others to teach and preach the Pope's heretical assertion, where it is proved by many authorities and reasons that they must resist in every way, because otherwise they are supporters and sin grievously.

units.la: DISCIP. Postquam autem discreuisti de episcopis & prælatis diuulgantibus & prædicantib. solenniter doctrinam hæreticalem Papæ per se vel per alios, tracta de episcopis & prælatis, qui siue publicent solenniter doctrinam hæreticalem Papæ siue non sustinent & permittunt, quod doctrina Papæ erronea in suis dioecesibus & inter suos subditos publicetur & doceatur & teneatur. nec sequaces Papæ hæretici talia præsumentes corrigunt vel castigant. peto enim scire, an literati tales episcopos & prælatos reputant fautores hæreticæ prauitatis peccare mortaliter, & qua pœna sint plectendi. dic autem primo modo de culpa eorum. MAG. Quidam dicunt quod episcopi & prælati talia sustinentes aut sciunt aut scire tenentur, quod sequentes Papæ doctrinam erroneam contra fidem tenent & docent: aut nesciunt nec scire tenentur: quia forte sequaces Papæ hæretici ita occulte & secrete procedunt, quod eorum excessus ad noticiam prælatorum peruenire non possunt. Item aut assertio Papæ hæretici est condemnata explicite, aut tantum implicite. Si talis assertio est hæresis implicite tantummodo condemnata, prælati siue sciant sequaces Papæ docere & tenere doctrinam Papæ hæreticam, siue ignorent, non sunt propter hoc, quod non corrigunt taliter tenentes & docentes, fautores prauitatis hæreticæ reputandi; quemadmodum prælati & episcopi licet sciant theologos in suis dioecesibus (circa ea quæ ad fidem spectant) contraria opinari (& per consequens sciunt quod alteri tenent & docent errores) quia non est possibile quod vtraque contradictoriarum sit consona catholicæ veritati: tamen non tenentur eos corrigere, si neuter docet errorem explicite condemnatum. Si autem assertio Papæ est hæresis damnata explicite, quia videlicet vel sub propria forma est ab ecclesia condemnata, vel eius contradictoria est expresse & patenter in scriptura diuina reperta, vel est expresse in determinatione ecclesiæ aperta, vel est apud omnes catholicos tanquam catholica diuulgata; puta si Papa assereret pertinaciter, vel solenniter diffiniret Christum non fuisse vere passum, aut nullam animam in inferno puniri, vel Christum non elegisse Iudam in apostolum, vel in Christo non fuisse duas voluntates, aut aliquid huiusmodi, in hoc casu episcopi & prælati, qui scirent vel tenentur scire sequaces Papæ tenere pertinaciter & docere doctrinam talem Papæ hæretici, essent fautores hæreticæ prauitatis, si sequaces Papæ hæretici minime coherceret. Si autem nescirent, nec tenerentur scire, tales sequaces Papæ suos subditos taliter informare, necscirent eos esse tales, non essent fautores hæreticæ prauitatis.
units.tr: STUDENT. Since you have distinguished concerning bishops and prelates who solemnly publish and preach the heretical doctrine of the Pope, either themselves or through others, now treat of bishops and prelates who either solemnly publish the Pope's heretical doctrine or do not stop it and allow the Pope's erroneous doctrine to be published, taught and held in their dioceses and among their subjects, and who do not correct or punish the followers of the heretical Pope who presume such things. For I wish to know whether learned men regard such bishops and prelates as supporters of heretical depravity who sin mortally, and what punishment they should suffer. Speak first about their guilt. MASTER. Some say that bishops and prelates who tolerate such things either know, or are bound to know, that the followers of the Pope hold and teach his erroneous doctrine against the faith; or they do not know and are not bound to know, because perhaps the heretical followers of the Pope proceed so secretly and covertly that their excesses cannot come to the notice of the prelates. Again, either the Pope's heretical assertion has been condemned explicitly, or only implicitly. If such an assertion is a heresy condemned only implicitly, the prelates are not to be reckoned supporters of heretical depravity for not correcting those who hold and teach it, whether the prelates know that the followers of the Pope teach and hold his heretical doctrine or are ignorant of it. Likewise, although prelates and bishops may know that theologians in their dioceses hold opposing opinions on matters pertaining to the faith (and consequently know that one party holds and teaches error, since both contradictory propositions cannot be consistent with catholic truth), they are not bound to correct them, if neither side teaches an error explicitly condemned. But if the Pope's assertion is a heresy explicitly condemned, either because it has been condemned by the Church in its own form, or because its contradictory is expressly and plainly found in divine Scripture, or is clearly stated in a determination of the Church, or is commonly published among all catholics as catholic doctrine (for example, if the Pope were to assert obstinately, or define solemnly, that Christ did not truly suffer, or that no soul is punished in hell, or that Christ did not choose Judas as an apostle, or that there were not two wills in Christ, or anything of this kind), then in this case bishops and prelates who knew, or are bound to know, that the followers of the heretical Pope obstinately hold and teach such a doctrine of the Pope, would be supporters of heretical depravity if they did not restrain those followers. But if they did not know, and were not bound to know, that such followers of the Pope were teaching such things to their subjects, they would not be supporters of heretical depravity.

units.la: DIS. Tantummodo tractes prædictam materiam de episcopis & prælatis scientibus, vel qui tenentur scire sequaces Papæ esse in suis dioecesibus, qui docent doctrinam Papæ explicite condemnatam, quando scilicet est rumor & fama de talibus.
units.tr: STUDENT. Deal only with the aforesaid matter concerning bishops and prelates who know, or are bound to know, that there are followers of the Pope in their dioceses who teach the Pope's doctrine explicitly condemned, namely when there is a rumour and report of such people.

units.la: MAGIST. Dicitur quod in hoc casu episcopi sunt fautores hæreticæ prauitatis, si huiusmodi docentes & tenentes doctrinam Papæ hæretici non coherent. Quod enim episcopi in hoc casu damnabiliter peccent, multis sanctorum auctoritatibus videtur aperte posse probari. ait enim August. vt habetur dist. 83. & c. nemo: ita episcopus qui talia non corrigit magis dicendus est canis impudicus quam episcopus.
units.tr: MASTER. It is said that in this case bishops are supporters of heretical depravity if they do not restrain those who teach and hold the doctrine of the heretical Pope. For that bishops sin damnably in this case seems clearly provable by many authorities of the saints. For Augustine says, as found in dist. 83, and c. nemo: so a bishop who does not correct such things is to be called a shameless dog rather than a bishop.

units.la: DISCIP. Sicut ad episcopos non spectat corrigere Papam: ita nec sequaces Papae, & ideo licet sequaces Papae subditi episcoporum praedicent, doceant & teneant doctrinam Papae haereticI haereticalem, non sunt per episcopos cohercendi. MAG. Ista ratio putatur tam stulta, quod reprobatione non indiget: & tamen multiplicitet reprobatur. Primo sic: quia ex hac ratione sequeretur, quod quamuis aliqui praedicarent, docerent & tenerent fidem Christianam esse falsam, & Christum fuisse prophetam falsum: non essent per episcopos corrigendi, sed tolerandi. Quod autem hoc absurdum sequatur, patet aperte: quia possibile est, quod aliquis Papa futurus teneat & solenniter diffiniat fidem Christianam esse falsam, & Christum fuisse falsum prophetam: quia nescitur an Antichristus erit Papa futurus. Si ergo episcopi non debeant corrigere sequaces Papae haeretici, ipsi nō debent in hoc casu corrigere publice praedicantes & docentes fidem Christianam esse falsam, & Christum fuisse falsum prophetam, quod omnes auditores ecclesiae horrerent.
units.tr: STUDENT. Just as it is not for bishops to correct the Pope, so neither is it for the Pope's followers; and therefore, even if the Pope's followers, as subjects of the bishops, preach, teach and hold the Pope's heretical teaching, they are not to be restrained by the bishops. MASTER. This argument is thought to be so foolish that it needs no refutation, and yet it is refuted in many ways. First, thus: for by this argument it would follow that, even if some preached, taught and held that the Christian faith is false and that Christ was a false prophet, they would not be corrected by bishops but tolerated. That this absurdity follows is plain: for it is possible that some future Pope may hold and solemnly define that the Christian faith is false and that Christ was a false prophet, since it is not known whether Antichrist will be a future Pope. If therefore bishops ought not to correct the heretical followers of the Pope, then in this case they ought not to correct publicly those who preach and teach that the Christian faith is false and that Christ was a false prophet, which all hearers of the Church would abhor.

units.la: DIS. Si Papa haeretic' ita enormiter deviaret a fide, sequaces eius essent per episcopos cohercedi & corrigendi. sed si erraret in aliis, non essent sequaces eius per episcopos corrigendi. MAG. Ista responsio videtur nulla: quia ita episcopi tenentur corrigere vnam haeresim explicite damnatam, sicut aliam. omnem enim haeresim damnatam explicite debent episcopi extirpare de suis dioecesibus. & per consequens omnes haereticos docentes, praedicantes seu tenentes quamcunque haeresim damnatam explicite cohercere tenentur. quare sequaces Papae haeretici quamcunque haeresim damnatam explicite praedicantes, docentes, seu manifeste tenentes, sunt per episcopos castigandi, quia idem videtur esse de magnis & de his quae haereses parvae videntur. DIS. Improbasti vno modo responsionem meam ad auctoritatem beati August. improbabiliter. MAG. Quod sequaces Papae haeretici sint per episcopos corrigendi, ostenditur sic: propter prauitatem haereticam Papae nullus est a iurisdictione episcoporum exemptus. Sed praedicantes & docentes quamcunque haeresim damnatam explicite essent per episcopos castigandi, si Papa esset catholicus. ergo propter hoc, quod sunt sequaces Papae haeretici, non sunt a iurisdictione episcoporum exempti, & per consequens ita sunt per episcopos corrigendi, sicut si non essent sequaces Papae haeretici. Item sequaces Papae non sunt magis exempti a iurisdictione episcoporum, quam ipsemet Papa haereticus. Sed cum Papa haereticus sit omni dignitate priuatus (eo ipso quod fit haereticus) esset ratione delicti de iurisdictione episcopi, in cuius dioecesi moraretur, sicut supra multipliciter ostensum est. ergo sequaces Papae haeretici sunt per episcopos cohercendi. DIS. Quid si episcopus attentaret corrigere sequaces Papae haeretici, & ipsi ad Papam appellarent, nunquid episcopus appellationi tali deferre deberet. MAG. Respondetur quod tali appellationi esset minime deferendum: tum quia a correctione appellare non licet, nisi corrigens modum correctionis crederet: tum quia ad haereticum appellare non licet. & ita appellationi quae fit ad Papam haereticum est minime deferendum. DIS. Quid si tales appellarent ad concilium generale. MAGIST. Respondetur, quod cum tales tenerent haeresim damnatam explicite, non esset deferendum appellationi eorum.
units.tr: STUDENT. If the heretical Pope deviated so enormously from the faith, his followers would be restrained and corrected by bishops; but if he erred in other matters, his followers would not be corrected by bishops. MASTER. This answer seems worthless, for bishops are bound to correct one explicitly condemned heresy just as much as another. For bishops ought to root out from their dioceses every heresy explicitly condemned. And consequently they are bound to restrain all heretics who teach, preach or hold any heresy explicitly condemned. Therefore the heretical followers of the Pope who preach, teach or openly hold any heresy explicitly condemned are to be punished by bishops, since the same seems to hold for great heresies and for those which seem small. STUDENT. You have criticised my answer to the authority of the blessed Augustine in one way, and not persuasively. MASTER. That the heretical followers of the Pope are to be corrected by bishops is shown thus: on account of the heretical depravity of the Pope, no one is exempt from the jurisdiction of bishops. But those who preach and teach any heresy explicitly condemned would be punished by bishops if the Pope were catholic. Therefore, because they are followers of a heretical Pope, they are not exempt from the jurisdiction of bishops, and consequently they are to be corrected by bishops just as if they were not followers of a heretical Pope. Again, the followers of the Pope are no more exempt from the jurisdiction of bishops than the heretical Pope himself. But since a heretical Pope is deprived of all dignity (by the very fact that he becomes a heretic), he would, by reason of his crime, be under the jurisdiction of the bishop in whose diocese he dwelt, as has been shown in many ways above. Therefore the heretical followers of the Pope are to be restrained by bishops. STUDENT. What if a bishop attempted to correct the heretical followers of the Pope, and they appealed to the Pope; should the bishop yield to such an appeal? MASTER. It is answered that such an appeal is not to be yielded to at all: both because one may not appeal from a correction unless the corrector believes the mode of correction to be wrong, and because one may not appeal to a heretic. And so an appeal made to a heretical Pope is by no means to be yielded to. STUDENT. What if such people appealed to a general council? MASTER. It is answered that, since they hold a heresy explicitly condemned, their appeal is not to be yielded to.

units.la: DISCIP. Alias auctoritates vel rationes ad conclusionem principalem adducas. MAG. Quod episcopi, qui tales sequaces Papae haeretici negligūt castigare, damnabiliter peccent, & sunt fautores haereticae prauitatis, probatur per easdem auctoritates, quibus supra. c. 32. & 33. est ostensum, quod qui tacent, cum possunt crimen prauitatis haereticae corrigere, & qui consentiunt prauitati haereticae, sunt fautores haereticae prauitatis. quia quamuis auctoritates aliae & consimiles possent de subditis intelligi, tamen principalius intelligendae sunt de praelatis. praeter illas etiam sunt multae aliae ex quibus euidenter ostenditur, quod praelati qui negligunt sequaces Papae haeretici castigare damnabiliter peccant, & sunt merito inter fautores haereticae prauitatis computandi. Leo enim Papa vt habetur dist. 86. c. 1. ait: Inferiorum ordinum culpa ad nullos magis sunt referenda quam ad desides negligentesque correctores, qui multam saepe nutriunt pestilentiam, dum aut fieri orem dissimulant adhibere medicinam. ex quibus verbis infertur, quod culpae sequacium Papae haeretici docentium haereses damnatas explicite in dioecesibus episcoporum ipsis episcopis sunt imputandae, si sequaces Papae haeretici negligunt castigare: imo fautores prauitatis haereticae sunt censendi: quia illi, qui nutriunt prauitatem haereticam, sunt fautores prauitatis haereticae. tales autem episcopi (vt ex verbis colligitur) nutriunt prauitatem haereticam, quae est grauis pestilentia, dum austeram dissimulant adhibere medicinam. ergo merito fautores prauitatis haereticae sunt censendi.
units.tr: STUDENT. Bring forward other authorities or reasons for your main conclusion. MASTER. That bishops who neglect to punish such heretical followers of the Pope sin damnably and are supporters of heretical depravity is proved by the same authorities by which it was shown above, in chapters 32 and 33, that those who keep silent when they can correct the crime of heretical depravity, and those who consent to heretical depravity, are supporters of heretical depravity. For although other and similar authorities could be understood of subjects, nevertheless they are to be understood chiefly of prelates. Besides these there are also many others from which it is clearly shown that prelates who neglect to punish the heretical followers of the Pope sin damnably and are rightly counted among the supporters of heretical depravity. For Pope Leo, as found in dist. 86, c. 1, says: The fault of inferior orders is to be attributed to no one more than to idle and negligent correctors, who often nourish a great plague, while they dissemble, rather than apply the remedy. From these words it follows that the faults of the followers of the heretical Pope who teach heresies explicitly condemned in the dioceses of bishops are to be imputed to the bishops themselves, if they neglect to punish those followers; indeed they are to be judged supporters of heretical depravity, because those who nourish heretical depravity are supporters of it. Such bishops (as is gathered from the words) nourish heretical depravity, which is a grave pestilence, while they dissemble rather than apply a harsh remedy. Therefore they are rightly to be counted supporters of heretical depravity.

units.la: Item Greg. vt legitur dist. 43. Ephes. ait: Ephesis Paulus dixit, munda sunt manus mea a sanguine omnium vestrum, non enim subterfugi quo minus annunciarem vobis omne consilium Dei. mundus ergo a sanguine eorum non esset, si eis Dei consilium annunciare noluisset, quia eum increpare delinquentes noluerit, eos proculdubio tacendo pastor occidit. Ex quibus verbis dupliciter patet, quod episcopi, qui non corrigunt sequaces Papae haeretici, damnabiliter peccant. primo: quia ille damnabiliter peccat, qui non est mundus à sanguine subditorum. sed episcopi negligentes corgere subditos sequaces papæ hæretici à sanguine eorum non sunt mundi: quia consilium Dei hoc est dictu catholicam veritatem non eis annunciant. ergo non sunt mundi à sanguine eorum: & per consequens damnabiliter peccant. Item, ille damnabiliter peccat, qui alios occidit. sed episcopi qui non corrigunt eos tacendo occidunt, secundum sententiam beati Gregorii. ergo damnabiliter peccant. Item, pastores qui gregem sibi commissum non defendunt à lupis crudeliter inuadentibus, damnabiliter peccant. sed episcopi & prælati si non corrigunt & cohercent sequaces papæ hæretici manifestas hæreses prædicantes & docentes ac tenentes, & ad tenendum alios inducentes, non defendunt gregem dominicum à lupis sibi commissum, sed reste Esa. propheta sunt canes muti non volentes latrare. sunt etiam iuxta vocem dominicam mercenarii, non pastores: quia veniente lupo fugiunt, dum sequaces papæ hæretici atrociter per pravitatem hæreticam greges sibi commissos conantibus iugulare sub silentio se abscondunt. ergo damnabiliter peccant: & merito (si greges sibi commissi prauitate inficiantur hæretica) est eis tandem infectio imputanda. Item, illi sunt per episcopos cohercendi, cum quibus nec ipsi nec subditi communicare debent. sed nec ipsi episcopi, nec eorum subditi communicare debent cum hæreticis sequacibus papæ hæretici, 34. quæst. 3. c. illud. & c. clericus. & 6. cum quibus; quia excommunicati sunt, extr. de hæreticis, absoluendum, & c. excommunicamus. ergo sequaces papæ hæretici sunt per episcopos cohercendi.
units.tr: Likewise Gregory, as read in dist. 43, on Ephesians, says: "Paul said at Ephesus, 'I am clean from the blood of you all, for I did not shrink from declaring to you the whole counsel of God' [Acts 20:26–27]. He would not have been clean from their blood if he had refused to declare God's counsel to them, since by keeping silent when he would not rebuke the sinners, the minister undoubtedly kills them." From these words it is clear in two ways that bishops who do not correct the heretical followers of the Pope sin damnably. First, he who is not clean from the blood of his subjects sins damnably. But bishops who neglect to correct their subjects who are heretical followers of the Pope are not clean from their blood, because they do not declare to them God's counsel, that is, the Catholic truth. Therefore they are not clean from their blood, and consequently they sin damnably. Again, he who kills others sins damnably. But bishops who do not correct these people, by keeping silent, kill them, according to the judgment of blessed Gregory. Therefore they sin damnably. Again, ministers who do not defend the flock committed to them from wolves that attack it savagely sin damnably.
