But bishops and prelates, if they do not correct and restrain the heretical followers of the Pope, who preach, teach and hold manifest heresies and lead others to hold them, do not defend the Lord's flock committed to them from the wolves. Rightly, the prophet Isaiah calls them "dumb dogs unwilling to bark" [Isa. 56:10]. Also, according to the Lord's word, they are hired hands, not shepherds, because when the wolf comes they flee; while the heretical followers of the Pope fiercely try to slaughter the flocks committed to them by heretical perversity, they hide themselves in silence. Therefore they sin damnably, and if the flocks committed to them are infected with heretical perversity, the infection is rightly to be imputed to them in the end. Again, those people must be restrained by bishops with whom neither the bishops themselves nor their subjects ought to communicate. But neither the bishops themselves nor their subjects ought to communicate with the heretical followers of the Pope, as in 34 q. 3, c. Illud and c. Clericus, and 6, Cum quibus; because they are excommunicated, Extra, De haereticis, Absoluendum, and c. Excommunicamus. Therefore the heretical followers of the Pope are to be restrained by bishops.

units.la: Quinto, principaliter videtur posse probari eadem conclusio, sic. Putridæ carnes sunt à corpore resecandæ per illum qui corporis curam gerit: ne totum corpus penitus corrumpatur. & similiter ouis scabiosa & morbida repellenda est à caulis per illum qui curam caularum gerit ne totus grex inficiatur: teste Hieronym. qui, ut habetur. 24. quæst. 2. c. resecanda, ait: Resecanda sunt putrida carnes & oues scabiosa à caulis repellenda est, ne tota domus massa & corpus & pectora ardeat & corrumpatur & putrescat & intereat acrius. in Alexandria una scintilla fuit: sed quoniam non statim oppressa est, totum orbem eius flamma populata est. sed sequaces papæ hæretici sunt putridæ carnes reliquas partes corporis corrumpentes & sunt oues scabiosæ & morbidæ inficientes gregem, teste Hieronym. qui, ut legitur di. 45. capi. illud, ait: Sicut ex vna oue morbida vniuersus grex inficitur: sic etiam ex vno fornicante vel aliud quodcunque scelus committente (& per consequens vno hæretico doctrinam papæ hæretici publice prædicante) plebs vniuersa polluitur. ergo sequaces papæ hæretici tanquam putridæ carnes & oues scabiosæ sunt per episcopos à corpore resecandi, & à caulis fidelium repellendi.
units.tr: Fifthly, the same conclusion seems to be provable chiefly in this way. Rotten flesh must be cut away from the body by the one who has charge of the body, so that the whole body is not entirely corrupted; and likewise a scabby and diseased sheep must be driven away from the fold by the one who has charge of the folds, so that the whole flock is not infected. Jerome witnesses this, who, as is found in 24 q. 2, c. Resecanda, says: "Rotten flesh must be cut away, and a scabby sheep must be driven from the fold, lest the whole mass of the house, body and breast, burn, be corrupted, rot and perish more bitterly. In Alexandria there was one spark, but because it was not put out at once, its flame laid waste the whole world." But the heretical followers of the Pope are rotten flesh corrupting the remaining parts of the body, and they are scabby and diseased sheep infecting the flock, as Jerome witnesses, who, as is read in dist. 45, c. Illud, says: "Just as the whole flock is infected by one diseased sheep, so also through one fornicator, or one committing any other crime (and consequently through one heretic publicly preaching the doctrine of the heretical Pope), the whole people is polluted." Therefore the heretical followers of the Pope, as rotten flesh and scabby sheep, must be cut from the body by the bishops and driven from the folds of the faithful.

units.la: Sexto, episcopi & prælati voce prophetica iubentur ab omnibus malis spiritualiter recedere & exire, & eos omnino non tangere, teste Esa. qui. 52. c. recedite, ait: recedite, exite inde, pollutum nolite tangere. quod exponens beatus August. in lib. de verbis domini, & habetur 23. quæst. 4. cap. 1. ait: tolerandi sunt quidem mali pro pace, nec corporaliter ab eis recedendum est, sed spiritualiter. & idem, ut habetur causa & quæst. prædictis, c. ecce, inquit: dicit propheta, recedite & exite inde, ne immundum tetigeritis quoquomodo. ergo malos pro pace tolerabimus, à quibus exire & recedere iubemur, ne tangamus immundum: istam recessionem spiritualiter intelligimus. Ex quibus verbis patet aperte, quod prælati ab vniuersis malis spiritualiter tenentur recedere. cum igitur à sequacibus papæ hæretici spiritualiter non recedunt, nisi eos corrigendo & cohercendo, si possunt: ergo episcopi & prælati sequaces papæ hæretici debent corrigere & arcere. quod autem episcopi & prælati spiritualiter non recedant à talibus sequacibus, nisi cum eos (quando possunt) corrigunt & castigant, patet aperte per beatum August. qui, ut habetur. 23. quæst. 4. c. ecce, ait: spiritualiter autem exire est facere quod pertinet ad correctionem malorum quantum licet pro gratia cuiuslibet salua pace. & infra: hoc ergo est ore non parcere, immundum non tangere, voluntate non consentire. Item, ut habetur causa & quæstione prædictis, c. ecce, ait: clamamus nos & dicimus vobis, recedite, exite inde, & immundum ne tetigeritis, scilicet tactu cordis tantummodo, non corporis. quid est enim tangere immundum, nisi consentire peccatis? quid est enim exire inde, nisi facere quod pertinet ad correctionem, quod pro vniuscuiusque gratia atque persona salua pace fieri potest. & infra: quicquid inter nos malorum esse noscitis, quantum potestis, improbate ut corde recedatis, redarguite ut exeatis mente, & nolite consentire, immundum ne tangatis. Item idem August. ut habetur causa & quæst. eisdem. c. recedite, ait: quid est etiam exire inde, nisi facere quod pertinet ad correctionem malorum quantum pro vniuscuiusque gratia atque persona salua pace fieri potest, displicuit tibi quod quisque peccauerat: non tetigisti immundum, redarguisti, corripuisti, monuisti, adhibuisti etiam (si res exigit) congruam & qua veritatem non violet disciplinam, existi inde. & infra: hoc est exire inde, hoc est immundum non tangere, & voluntate non consentire, & ore non parcere. ex quibus verbis, ut videtur, colligitur euidenter, quod à malis quibuscunque & per consequens à sequacibus papæ hæretici prælati spiritualiter non recedunt, nisi faciant quod spectat ad correctionem eorum: nisi ore non parcant, nisi redarguant, nisi corripiant, nisi moneant, & quando possunt congruam adhibeant disciplinam. quare patenter infertur, quod sequaces papæ hæretici sunt per episcopos & prælatos arcendi.
units.tr: Sixthly, bishops and prelates are commanded by the prophetic voice to withdraw and depart spiritually from all evils, and not to touch them at all, as Isaiah witnesses in 52, c. Recedite, which says: "Depart, go out from there, touch nothing unclean" [Isa. 52:11]. Blessed Augustine, explaining this in his book De verbis Domini, and found in 23 q. 4, c. 1, says: "Evils indeed must be tolerated for the sake of peace, nor must one withdraw from them bodily, but spiritually." And the same, as is found in the aforesaid cause and question, c. Ecce, says: "The prophet says, Depart and go out from there, lest you touch the unclean in any way. Therefore we shall tolerate evil people for the sake of peace, from whom we are commanded to go out and withdraw, lest we touch the unclean; we understand this withdrawal spiritually." From these words it is clearly evident that prelates are bound to withdraw spiritually from all evils. Since therefore they do not withdraw spiritually from the heretical followers of the Pope, unless they correct and restrain them, if they can, therefore bishops and prelates ought to correct and keep off the heretical followers of the Pope. That bishops and prelates do not withdraw spiritually from such followers, unless they correct and rebuke them when they are able, is plainly shown by blessed Augustine, who, as is found in 23 q. 4, c. Ecce, says: "To go out spiritually is to do what pertains to the correction of evils, as far as it is permitted, for the grace of anyone, with peace preserved. And below: therefore not to spare with the mouth, not to touch the unclean, not to consent in the will, this is it." Again, as is found in the same cause and question, c. Ecce, he says: "We cry out and say to you, Depart, go out from there, and do not touch the unclean, that is, touch only with the heart, not with the body. For what is it to touch the unclean, except to consent to sins? And what is it to go out from there, except to do what pertains to correction, which can be done, with peace preserved, according to the grace and person of each." And below: "Whatever evils you know to be among us, as far as you can, reject them so that you withdraw in heart; rebuke them so that you go out in mind; and do not consent, do not touch the unclean." Again, the same Augustine, as is found in the same cause and question, c. Recedite, says: "What is it also to go out from there, except to do what pertains to the correction of evils, as far as can be done, with peace preserved, for the grace and person of each? You were displeased that someone had sinned; you did not touch the unclean, you rebuked, corrected, admonished, and also applied (if the matter requires it) a fitting discipline which does not violate the truth; you went out from there. And below: this is to go out from there, this is not to touch the unclean, and not to consent in the will, and not to spare with the mouth." From these words it seems to be clearly inferred that prelates do not withdraw spiritually from any evils, and consequently from the heretical followers of the Pope, unless they do what pertains to their correction: unless they do not spare with the mouth, unless they rebuke, unless they correct, unless they admonish, and when they can, apply fitting discipline. Hence it is plainly inferred that the heretical followers of the Pope are to be kept off by bishops and prelates.

units.la: DISCIP. Ex prædictis verbis Aug. colligitur, quod sequaces papæ hæretici, quando salua pace nequeunt cohercieri, sunt æquanimiter tolerandi. ergo non est semper necesse, ut episcopi & prælati eos corrigant & castigent. MAGIST. Ad hoc duplici ter respondetur. Primo, quia secus est de crimine hæresis, & de aliis minoribus, quia hæretici totam salutem nituntur extinguere. & ideo ipsis resistendum est etiam vsque ad mortem, quia in decretis 7. q. 1. c. aduersitas, §. hic tunc, vel §. cum vero, sic legitur: cum vero non prælatorum tantum sed totius ecclesiæ salus impugnatur (scilicet fides) necesse est vt ex aduerso ascendant, & in die belli seipsos vt murum opponant pro domo Dei, & animas suas pro quibus suis ponant, vt exemplo suæ passionis attendant, quos sermone doctrina diutius confirmare non valent. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod cum sequaces papæ hæretici totius ecclesiæ salutem quærunt destruere, fidemque impugnant, necesse est quod prælati se eis opponant etiam vsque ad mortem resistendo, & quantum vires suppetunt compescendo. Vnde cum hæreticis nullo modo in damnum fidei est pax habenda. proiftis enim dicit Christus Matth. 19. nolite arbitrari quia venerim pacem mittere in terram: non veni pacem mittere, sed gladium. & Luc. 12. Putatis quia pacem veni mittere in terram, non dico vobis, sed separationem. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod cum hæreticis non est pax habenda, vt propter eam prælati ab eorum correctione desistant. Aliter dicitur, quod vbi cernerent episcopi euidenter, quod de cohertione hæreticorum nullus fructus neque fidei neque fidelium proueniret, & grauis oriretur catholicorum turbatio, episcopi possent a correctione cessare ad tempus. quod intelligendum est non tantum respectu sequacium papæ hæretici, sed respectu quorumcunque hæreticorum. & ita æqualiter omnino coerceri debent sequaces papæ hæretici, sicut sequaces imperatoris hæretici vel alterius diuitis & potentis. vbi enim prælati viderent, quod ex cohertione sequacium imperatoris hæretici graue fidei periculum immineret, absque omni fructu possunt a correctione cessare. Ita est etiam sciendum, vt videtur, de sequacibus papæ hæretici vel imperatoris, vel propter aliquam aliam causam, quæ ita reputari potest in sequacibus imperatoris hæretici, sicut papæ. nec ratione imperii, nec ratione regni est cessandum a cohertione papæ hæretici, sed ratione periculi, vel propter aliquam aliam causam, quæ ita reperiri potest in sequacibus papæ hæretici vel imperatoris hæretici, ratione cuius licet quandoque abstinere.
units.tr: PUPIL. From the aforesaid words of Augustine it is inferred that the heretical followers of the Pope, when they cannot be restrained with peace preserved, are to be tolerated with equanimity. Therefore it is not always necessary that bishops and prelates correct and chastise them. MASTER. To this there is a twofold answer. First, because the matter is different with the crime of heresy than with other lesser ones, since heretics strive to extinguish all salvation. And therefore they must be resisted even unto death, because in the Decretum, 7 q. 1, c. Adversitas, §. Hic tunc or §. Cum vero, it is read thus: "But when the salvation not only of the prelates but of the whole Church is attacked (namely the faith), it is necessary that they rise up against the enemy, and on the day of battle set themselves as a wall for the house of God, and lay down their souls for those whom they cannot confirm by sermon and teaching for long, so that they may consider by the example of his suffering." From these words it is gathered that when the heretical followers of the Pope seek to destroy the salvation of the whole Church and attack the faith, it is necessary that the prelates oppose them, even unto death, resisting and restraining them as far as their strength allows. Hence, since peace must in no way be kept with heretics to the detriment of the faith, for Christ says in Matth. 19: "Do not think that I came to bring peace on earth; I did not come to bring peace, but a sword" [Matt. 10:34]; and in Luke 12: "Do you think that I came to bring peace on earth? I tell you, no, but division" [Luke 12:51]. From these words it is gathered that peace is not to be kept with heretics, so that for its sake prelates should desist from their correction. In another way it is said that where bishops clearly perceived that from the restraint of heretics no fruit would come either to the faith or to the faithful, and a grave disturbance of the Catholics would arise, the bishops could cease from correction for a time. This must be understood not only with respect to the heretical followers of the Pope, but with respect to any heretics whatever. And thus the heretical followers of the Pope must be restrained in exactly the same way as the heretical followers of the emperor or of some other rich and powerful man. For where prelates would see that from the restraint of the heretical followers of the emperor a grave danger to the faith threatened, without any fruit they could cease from correction. It is also to be known, as it seems, about the heretical followers of the Pope or of the emperor, or on account of some other cause, which can be reckoned in the heretical followers of the emperor just as in those of the Pope; not because of the empire, nor because of the kingdom, is one to cease from restraining the heretical followers of the Pope, but because of danger, or on account of some other cause which can be found in the heretical followers of the Pope or of the heretical emperor, on account of which it is sometimes permitted to refrain.

units.la: DISCIP. Prolixitatem quantum possumus euitemus, auctoritates tam scripturæ diuinæ quam sanctorum patrum, ex quibus possunt accipi argumenta ad probandum eandem conclusionem, allega, rationes ab eis non formando.
units.tr: STUDENT. Let us avoid prolixity as far as we can. Cite the authorities of divine Scripture and of the holy Fathers from which arguments may be drawn to prove the same conclusion, but do not spell out the arguments themselves.

units.la: MAGIST. Pro hac conclusione exhortari videtur Esa. 45. c. dicens: clama ne cesses, quasi tuba exalta vocem tuam & annuncia populo meo scelera eorum & domui Iacob peccata eorum. Item Hiere. 23. scribitur: vae pastoribus qui dispergunt & dilacerant gregem pascuæ meæ, dicit dominus. & post: vos dispersistis gregem meum & eiecistis eos & non visitastis eos. Item Ezech. 24. sic loquitur: vae pastoribus Israel, qui pascebant semetipsos, nonne greges a pastoribus pascuntur? lac comedebatis, & lanis operiebamini. & quod crassum erat occidebatis, gregem autem meum non pascebatis. quod infirmum fuit, non consolidastis. & quod ægrotum erat, non sanastis. quod fractum est non alligastis. & quod abiectum est non reduxistis, quod perierat non quæsistis, sed cum austeritate eis imperabatis, & cum potentia dispersa sunt oves meæ eo quod non esset pastor, & facta sunt in devorationem omnium bestiarum agri, sequacium scilicet papæ hæretici totam fidem devastantium orthodoxam. Item Threnorum secundo: prophetæ tui viderunt tibi falsa & stulta, nec aperiebant iniquitatem tuam, vt te ad pœnitentiam provocarent. Item prælati huiusmodi increpantur Ezech. 13. cum dicit dominus: non ascendistis ex aduerso, neque posuistis vos murum pro domo Israel, vt staretis in prælio in domo domini. & 33. c. sic habetur: Si speculator viderit gladium venientem, & non insonuerit buccinam, & populus non custodierit se, veneritque gladius, & tulerit de eis animam, ipse quidem in iniquitate sua captus est: sanguinem autem eius de manu speculatoris requiram. Item Exod. 22. maleficos non patieris viuere. Item Deutro. 13. Si surrexerit in medio tui propheta &c. quaere supra lib. 6. c. 99. Item ibidem: Si tibi voluerit persuadere frater tuus. quaere vbi prius. Item ibidem: Si audieris in vna vrbium tuarum, & cætera, quaere vbi supra. Item Deu. 16. cum reperti fuerint &c. quaere vbi prius. Hier. 3. dicit dominus dabo vobis pastores iuxta nomen meum & pascent vos doctrina & scientia. & Hiere. 6. Pascet vnusquisque eos qui sub manu sua sunt. item Mala. 2. labia sacerdotis custodiunt sententiam &c. Et Ezech. 3. Si dicente me ad impium morte morieris non annunciaueris ei, neque locutus fueris vt auertatur a via sua impia & viuat, ipse impius in iniquitate sua morietur, sanguinem autem eius de manu tua requiram. & ad Tit. 1. oportet episcopum sine crimine esse & primum amplectentem eum qui secundum doctrinam est fidelem sermonem, vt potens sit exhortari in doctrina sana & eos qui contradicunt arguere. & post: increpa illos dure, vt sani sint in fide. Item primo Corinth. 5. auferte malum ex vobis ipsis. Item infra ad Ti. 3. peccantes coram omnibus arguentur, vt ceteri timorem habeant. Item ad Gala. 2. cum autem venisset Cephas Antiochiam, in faciem ei restiti, quia reprehensibilis erat.
units.tr: MASTER. The conclusion seems to be urged by Isaiah 45: "Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins." Likewise Jeremiah 23: "Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture, saith the LORD." And after that: "Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and not visited them." Likewise Ezekiel 34: "Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks? Ye eat the fat, and ye clothe you with the wool, ye kill them that are fed: but ye feed not the flock. The diseased have ye not strengthened, neither have ye healed that which was sick, neither have ye bound up that which was broken, neither have ye brought again that which was driven away, neither have ye sought that which was lost; but with force and with cruelty have ye ruled them. And they were scattered, because there is no shepherd; and they became meat to all the beasts of the field" (that is, to the followers of the Papist heretic pope, who lay waste the whole orthodox faith). Likewise, Lamentations 2: "Thy prophets have seen vain and foolish things for thee, and they have not discovered thine iniquity, to turn away thy captivity." Likewise such prelates are rebuked in Ezekiel 13, where the Lord says: "Ye have not gone up into the gaps, neither made up the hedge for the house of Israel, to stand in the battle in the day of the LORD." And in chapter 33 it is written thus: "If the watchman see the sword come, and blow not the trumpet, and the people be not warned; if the sword come, and take any person from among them, he is taken away in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at the watchman's hand." Likewise Exodus 22: "Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live." Likewise Deuteronomy 13: "If there arise among you a prophet..." etc.; see above, book 6, chapter 99. Likewise in the same place: "If thy brother... entice thee secretly"; see the earlier passage. Likewise there: "If thou shalt hear say in one of thy cities..." etc.; see above. Deuteronomy 16: "When it is told thee..." etc.; see the earlier passage. Jeremiah 3: "The LORD saith, I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding." And Jeremiah 6: "Every one shall feed those that are under his hand." Likewise Malachi 2: "The priest's lips should keep knowledge..." etc. And Ezekiel 3: "When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life; the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thy hand." And to Titus 1: "A bishop must be blameless... holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince gainsayers." And after that: "Rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith." Likewise 1 Corinthians 5: "Put away from among yourselves that wicked person." Likewise below, to Timothy 3 [1 Tim. 5]: "Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear." Likewise Galatians 2: "But when Cephas was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed."

units.la: DISCIP. Sufficiant istæ auctoritates ex diuinis scripturis acceptæ: ideo aliquas auctoritates sanctorum patrum ad eandem conclusionem adducas. MAGIST. Huic Hieron. consentire videtur, cum dicit in prologo Bibliæ: sancta quippe rusticitas solum sibi prodest. & quantum ædificat ex vita merito ecclesiam Christi, tantum nocet si destruentibus non resistat. Item Innocentius 39. vt legitur extr. de simonia. c. licet Heli, ait: licet Heli summus sacerdos in se bonus exisseret, quia tamen filiorum suorum excessus efficaciter non corripuit & in se pariter & in ipsis animaduersionis diuinæ vindictam accipit, dum filius eius in bello peremptus est, & ipse corruens de sella fracta ceruicibus expirauit. ad corrigendos ergo excessus subditorum tanto diligentius debet prælatus assurgere, quanto damnabiliusque eorum offensas deferit incorrectas. Et illa vltima sententia sub eodem verbo ponitur ext. de accusationibus qualiter & quando. Item idem ext. de officio iudicis ordinarii. c. inrefragabili, in consilio generali ait: inrefragabili consticonstitutione sanctimus, ut ecclesiarum prælati ad corrigendum subditorum excessus, maxime clericorum & formandos mores prudenter ac diligenter intendant, ne sanguis eorum de suis manibus requiratur. vbi Gloss. dicit: durum verbum est illud prælatis negligentibus subditorum correctionem. Item Anacletus scribens cunctis, ut legitur. 83. di. capitulk nihil, ait: nihil illo pastore miserius, qui laporum gloriatur laudibus, quibus si placere voluerit atque ab hiis amari delegerit, erit & hinc omnibus magna pernicies. nullus igitur pastorum placere lupis & gregibus omium potest. Item papa Nicolaus, ut legitur di. 43. cap. dispensatio, ait: Dispensatio est nobis cælestis seminis iniuncta. vel si non sparserimus, vel si tacuerimus. quod cum electionis vas formidet, & clamat, quanto magis cuilibet exiguo metuendum est. metuendum est ergo, si non leue discrimen incumbit pontificibus siluisse quod congruit &c. Item Gregor. ut legitur di. 43. ait: sicut incauta locutio in errorem detrahit, ita indiscretum silentium eos qui erudiri poterant in errore derelinquit. sepe namque doctores rectores improuidis humanam amittere gloriam formidantes loqui libere recta pertimescant. cui concordat Hieronym. ut legitur di. 41. cap. sed illud, dicens: sed illud non ociose transcurrendum est, quod uno peccante ira Dei super omnem populum venit, hoc quoque accidit, quando sacerdotes qui populo præsunt erga delinquentes benignos videri volunt & illi verentes peccantium linguas ne forte de eis male loquantur sacerdotalis seueritatis immemores nolunt complere, quod scriptum est: peccantem coram omnibus argue. & infra: dum unus parcunt, universa ecclesia molliuntur interitum, que est ista misericordia, qua ista bonitas, uni proficere & omnes in discrimen adducere? Item Anacletus, ut legitur di. 43. c. scimus, ait: Scimus autem multos ob illud infestare doctores suos ut eos perdant & placita propria voluntatis adimpleant: non propterea tamen doctores inquantum vires suppetunt à recta æmulatione & bona intentione recedere debent, scientes quia beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter iustitiam. Item Leo papa, ut habetur. 24. quæst. 3. illud sane, ait: illud sane plurimum mihi displicere significo, quod interdictionis tuæ clerici quidam esse dicuntur, qui aduersariorum conueniant prauitati & vesania vasis misericordiæ vasa miscentur, quibus inuestigandis & seueritate congrua coercendis debet diligentia tua vigilanter insistere, ut hiis quibus prodesse non poterit correctio, non parcat abscissio. oportet & enim vos euangelici meminisse mandati, quod ab ipsa veritate præcipitur, ut si vos oculus aut pes aut dextra scandalisauerit manus, à compage corporis auferatur, quia melius sit hiis in seculo carere membris, quam cum ipsis in æterna supplicia ire. nam superfluo extra ecclesiam positis resistimus, si ab hiis qui intus sunt in eis quos decipiunt vulneramur, abiiciendæ prorsus pestifera haæ à sacerdotali vigore patientia est, quæ sibimet peccatis aliorum parcendo non parcit. Item Greg. in Registro, ut legitur extr. de regulis iuris. c. quamuis, ait: non potest esse pastorum excusatio, si lupus oues comedit, & pastor nescit. Item Cornelius, ut habetur di. 47. c. quo ad nos pertinet: Conscientia nostra conuenit semper darè operam, ne quis culpa nostra de ecclesia pereat.
units.tr: STUDENT. Let these authorities taken from divine Scripture suffice. Now cite some authorities of the holy Fathers for the same conclusion. MASTER. Jerome seems to agree with this when he says in the prologue to the Bible: "Holy rusticity profits only itself; and as far as it builds up the Church of Christ by the merit of its life, so far does it harm if it does not resist those who destroy." Likewise Innocent III, as is read in Extra, De simonia, c. Licet Heli, says: "Although Eli the high priest was good in himself, yet because he did not effectively correct the excesses of his sons, he received the vengeance of divine retribution both in himself and in them, when his son was slain in battle and he himself fell from his seat, broke his neck and expired." Therefore a prelate ought to rise up the more diligently to correct the excesses of his subjects, in proportion as he leaves their offences uncorrected to his greater condemnation. And that last sentence is placed under the same heading in Extra, De accusationibus, qualiter et quando. Likewise the same Innocent, in Extra, De officio iudicis ordinarii, c. Irrefragabili, says in a general council: "By an irrefutable constitution we decree that the prelates of the churches should attend prudently and diligently to correcting the excesses of their subjects, especially of the clergy, and to forming their morals, lest their blood be required at their hands." Where the Gloss says: "That is a harsh word for prelates who neglect the correction of their subjects." Likewise Anacletus, writing to everyone, as is read in Distinctio 83, chapter Nihil, says: "Nothing is more wretched than that shepherd who glories in the praises of the lax, and if he wishes to please them and chooses to be loved by them, he will be a great ruin to all. No shepherd can therefore please both the wolves and the flocks of all." Likewise Pope Nicholas, as is read in Distinctio 43, chapter Dispensatio, says: "The dispensation of the heavenly seed is enjoined upon us, whether we sow or whether we keep silent. Since the vessel of election trembles and cries out, how much more must every humble man fear! It is therefore to be feared, if a not slight peril lies upon the pontiffs, that they have kept silent when it was fitting to speak." Likewise Gregory, as is read in Distinctio 43, says: "Just as an incautious speech draws men into error, so an indiscreet silence leaves in error those who could have been taught. For teachers and rulers, fearing to lose human glory through lack of foresight, often dread to speak freely what is right." Jerome agrees with this, as is read in Distinctio 41, chapter Sed illud, saying: "But that must not be passed over idly: when one man sins, the wrath of God comes upon the whole people. This also happens when the priests who preside over the people wish to appear kind towards offenders, and, fearing the tongues of sinners lest they speak ill of them, forget priestly severity and refuse to fulfil what is written: 'Rebuke a sinner before all.'" And below: "While one spares, the whole Church is brought to ruin. What is this mercy, what is this kindness, that benefits one and brings all into peril?" Likewise Anacletus, as is read in Distinctio 43, chapter Scimus, says: "We know that many persecute their teachers in order to destroy them and to carry out their own selfish wishes. Yet teachers, so far as their strength allows, ought not therefore to depart from right zeal and good intention, knowing that they are blessed who suffer persecution for righteousness' sake." Likewise Pope Leo, as is read in 24 quaestio 3, chapter Illud sane, says: "I signify that I am very much displeased that some clergy under your interdict are said to join with the perversity of the adversaries, and that vessels of mercy are mixed with vessels of wrath. Your diligence ought to attend watchfully to investigating these men and restraining them with fitting severity, so that where correction cannot profit, cutting off may not spare. For you ought to remember the gospel command, which the Truth himself enjoins: if your eye or foot or hand offend you, it must be cut off from the body, because it is better to lack these members in this world than to go with them into eternal punishments. For we resist to no purpose those who stand outside the Church, if we are wounded by those who are within, by those whom they deceive. Such pestilential patience must be utterly cast off by priestly vigour, which, by sparing the sins of others, does not spare its own." Likewise Gregory, in his Register, as is read in Extra, De regulis iuris, c. Quamuis, says: "There can be no excuse for a shepherd if the wolf eats the sheep and the shepherd does not know it." Likewise Cornelius, as is found in Distinctio 47, chapter Quo ad nos pertinet: "Our conscience requires us always to take care that no one perish from the Church through our fault."

units.la: DISCIP. Plures allegasti auctoritates, ex quibus accipere nescio argumentum ad probandum, quod episcopi & prælati debent coherere sequaces pseudopapæ hæretici. quare da mihi vias, quibus auctoritates ad propositum valeam applicare.
units.tr: DISCIPULUS. You have cited many authorities, from which I cannot see the argument for proving that bishops and prelates ought to cohere with the followers of the heretical pseudo-pope. Therefore show me the ways by which I may apply the authorities to the point at issue.

units.la: MAGIST. Tribus propositionibus tanquam certis suppositis, satis potest conclusio suprascripta ex auctoritatibus allegatis inferri: quarum prima est hæc, quod non minus deberent episcopi & prælati corrigere hæreticos sibi subiectos, quam alios criminosos. Secunda est, quod omnes prælati & episcopi omnes sibi subditos hæreticos vel catholicos debent per se vel per alios non criminosos de veritate fidei informare, extra, de officio iudi. or. inter cetera, quod maxime veritatem habet, quando hæretici greges prælatorum à veritate niituntur auertere. Tertia est, quod sequaces papæ hæretici propter hoc à iurisdictione episcoporum & prælatorum minime sunt exempti, cum ipsemet papa hæreticus propter hoc, quod sit hæreticus, iudicio catholicorum reddatur subiectus.
units.tr: MAGISTER. Taking three propositions as certain premises, the aforesaid conclusion can sufficiently be inferred from the authorities cited. The first is this: bishops and prelates ought no less to correct heretics subject to them than other criminals. The second is that all prelates and bishops ought to inform all their subjects, heretical or Catholic, about the truth of the faith, either themselves or through others who are not criminals (see Extra, de officio iudicis ordinarii, "inter cetera"), which holds especially true when heretical flocks strive to turn the prelates' flocks away from the truth. The third is that the followers of the heretical pope are for this reason in no way exempt from the jurisdiction of bishops and prelates, since the pope himself, precisely because he is a heretic, is made subject to the judgment of Catholics.

units.la: CAP. XXXIX.
units.tr: CAP. XXXIX.

units.la: In quo determinatur, qua pœna sint plectendi episcopi & prælati, si subditos suos sequaces papæ hæretici non correxerint.
units.tr: In which it is determined by what punishment bishops and prelates are to be punished if they have not corrected their subjects who follow the heretical pope.

units.la: DISCIP. Nunc mihi apparet, quod ex omnibus auctoritatibus tam scripturæ diuinæ quam sanctorum patrum præscriptis scio sumere argumentum ad probandum, quod episcopi & prælati sequaces pseudopapæ hæretici cohercere tenentur, si possunt. ideo nunc dic, qua pœna si episcopi & prælati subditos suos sequaces papæ hæretici neglexerint cohercere, sint merito percellendi.
units.tr: STUDENT. Now it seems clear to me that from all the authorities, both of divine Scripture and of the holy Fathers, I can draw an argument to prove that bishops and prelates are bound to restrain the followers of the heretical pseudo-pope, if they are able. So now tell me by what punishment bishops and prelates should rightly be struck down if they have neglected to restrain their subjects who follow the heretical pope.

units.la: MAGIST. Respondetur, quod sint excommunicationis vinculo alligati, & ab officio suspendendi, & ab episcopali officio & ab omni alio deponendi. quod sint excommunicationis vinculo innodati, patet: cum sint fautores hæreticorum, quos non corrigunt & castigant, cum debent, & etiam hæreticæ prauitatis, quam de suis iurisdictionibus non extirpant. tales autem fautores sunt excommunicationis sententia innodati, extra, de sententia excommunicationis, noueris. & extra, de hereticis, excommunicamus. sunt etiam ab officio suspendendi, quia non minus ab officio est suspendendus, qui non impugnat hæreticos sequaces pseudopapæ hæretici, quam qui non impugnant fornicatores. sed qui non impugnat fornicatores, est ab officio suspendendus, teste Gregor. qui, vt legitur dist. 83. c. si quis, ait: Si quis episcopus fornicationem presbyterorum, diaconorum vel crimen incestus in parochia sua precio vel precibus interveniente concesserit, vel commissum auctoritate officii non impugnauerit, ab officio suspendatur. ergo episcopus, qui haereticos sequaces papae haeretici non impugnat, multo fortius est ab officio suspendendus. Quod vero episcopi, qui tales non coercent, sint ab episcopali officio deponendi, testatur concilium generale sub Innocentio 3. celebratum, in quo, vt habetur extra, de haereticis, c. excommunicamus, sic legitur: Si quis autem episcopus super expurgando de sua dioecesi haeretica prauitate fermento negligens fuerit vel remissus, cum illud certe indicium apparuerit, & ab episcopali officio deponatur, & in locum ipsius alter substituatur idoneus, qui velit & possit haereticam confundere prauitatem. Quibus verbis clare videtur asserere, quod episcopus negligens suam dioecesim de prauitate haeretica expurgare est penitus deponendus, quare cum sequaces papae haeretici a iurisdictione episcoporum nullatenus sint exempti, episcopus, qui eos non coercet, est omnino deponendus. DISC. Verba concilii generalis non sunt intelligenda de episcopo non cohercente sequaces papae haeretici, quia talis episcopus non est deponendus a papa, quia papa haereticus talem episcopum magis confirmaret: nec ab aliquo alio archiepiscopo vel primate vel patriarcha, quia nullus eorum potest episcopum ab episcopali officio deponere. MAGIST. Respondetur, quod episcopus qui negligit sequaces papae haeretici cohercere deponendus est a papa catholico, quandocunque fuerit canonice ad papatum assumptus. Unde accusandus est a catholicis coram papa catholico. & qui fuerit papa catholicus habet ipsum deponere. DISCIP. Quid facient interim subditi talis episcopi? MAGIST. Respondent quidam, quod subditi vitabunt ipsum tanquam haereticum, & expectabunt papam futurum catholicum, qui deponet eum. idem facient de tali episcopo quod facerent de episcopo, qui propter abnegationem spontaneam fidei vel propter occasionem alterius episcopi vel sacerdotis manifeste & publice incurreret excommunicationis sententiam.
units.tr: MASTER. The answer is that they are bound by the chain of excommunication, and are to be suspended from office, and deposed from the episcopal office and from every other office. That they are bound by the chain of excommunication is plain: since they are favourers of heretics, whom they do not correct and punish as they ought, and also of heretical depravity, which they do not root out from their jurisdictions. Such favourers are bound by the sentence of excommunication: Extra, de sententia excommunicationis, noueris, and extra, de hereticis, excommunicamus. They are also to be suspended from office, because one who does not oppose the heretical followers of the heretical pseudo-pope is no less to be suspended from office than one who does not oppose fornicators. But one who does not oppose fornicators is to be suspended from office, as Gregory witnesses, who, as we read in dist. 83. c. si quis, says: If any bishop, in his parish, has allowed the fornication of presbyters or deacons, or the crime of incest, through a bribe or at the intercession of others, or has not opposed a crime committed under the authority of his office, let him be suspended from office. Therefore a bishop who does not oppose the heretical followers of the heretical pope is much more strongly to be suspended from office. That bishops who do not restrain such men are to be deposed from the episcopal office is attested by the general council celebrated under Innocent III, in which, as it is found in extra, de haereticis, c. excommunicamus, it is read thus: If any bishop, negligent or remiss in cleansing his diocese of heretical depravity like leaven, is shown to have been so, let him certainly be deposed from the episcopal office, and let another suitable man, who is willing and able to confound heretical depravity, be substituted in his place. By these words it seems clearly to be asserted that a bishop who neglects to cleanse his diocese of heretical depravity is to be utterly deposed; therefore, since the followers of the heretical pope are in no way exempt from the jurisdiction of bishops, a bishop who does not restrain them is wholly to be deposed. STUDENT. The words of the general council are not to be understood of a bishop who does not restrain the followers of the heretical pope, because such a bishop is not to be deposed by the pope, since a heretical pope would rather confirm such a bishop; nor by any other archbishop, primate or patriarch, because none of them can depose a bishop from the episcopal office. MASTER. The answer is that a bishop who neglects to restrain the followers of the heretical pope is to be deposed by the Catholic pope, whenever he has been canonically raised to the papacy. Hence he is to be accused by Catholics before a Catholic pope, and the Catholic pope has the power to depose him. STUDENT. What, meanwhile, will the subjects of such a bishop do? MASTER. Some answer that the subjects will avoid him as a heretic and wait for a future Catholic pope, who will depose him. They will do with such a bishop what they would do with a bishop or priest who, by spontaneous denial of the faith, or on some other occasion, openly and publicly incurred the sentence of excommunication.

units.la: CAP. XL.
units.tr: CHAPTER XL.

units.la: In quo tractatur de modo inquirendi respersos prauitate haeretica, si papa haereticus efficiatur.
units.tr: In which is discussed the manner of inquiring into those tainted with heretical depravity, if the pope should become a heretic.

units.la: DISCIP. Dic breuiter & in summa, quid secundum priorem sententiam episcopis est agendum, si in suis dioecesibus sequaces papae haeretici doctrinam eius erroneam praedicarent, docerent & tanquam catholicam diuulgarent. MAG. Respondetur, quod si episcopo per famam constiterit, quod papa in haereticam inciderit prauitatem, dubitare debet, ne aliquis de grege suo perfidiam papae sequatur, quia pusillanimes & ambitiosi, quorum magnus, imo forte infinitus est numerus, errorem capitis vel vt placeant vel vt non displiceant de facili amplectuntur, iuxta illud Eccl. 10. secundum iudicem populi, sic & ministri eius. & qualis rector est ciuitatis, tales inhabitantes in ea. iuxta illud, quod scribitur. 6. q. 1. c. sunt plurimi, §. verum: Capite languescente facile reliqua corporis membra inficiuntur, sicut scriptum est. Omne caput languidum & omne cor moerens a planta pedis vsque ad verticem capi. &c. & ita papa labe haeretica maculato timendum est, ne populum labe consimili inficiat. quare cum episcopus officium gerit speculatoris, cuius est diligentissime circumspicere, ne hostes appropinquent, sollicite debet inquirere an fama de perfidia papae haeretici contineat veritatem: & qua haeresi est infectus: qua comperta scrutari per se & per alios debet attente, qualiter fidei obuient orthodoxae. quo facto consequenter inuestiget, an aliqui haeresim papae in gregem suum introducere moliantur, praesertim si fama est, quod aliqui in sua dioecesi doctrinam papae haeretici imitantur, docent, publicant & praedicant & diuulgant, tanquam catholicam, & tenendam, iuxta praeceptum Innocentii 3. qui, vt habetur ext. de haeretic. c. excommunicamus, ait: Addicimus insuper quod quilibet archiepiscopus vel episcopus per se aut per archidiaconum aut per alias idoneas & honestas personas bis aut semel saltem in anno parochiam propriam, in qua fama fuerit haereticos habitare, circumeat: & ibi tres vel plures boni testimonii viros & etiam si expedire videbitur totam viciniam iurare compellat. quod si quis ibidem haereticos sciuerit vel alios occulta conuenticula celebrantes seu a communi conuersatione fidelium, vita & moribus decedentes, eos episcopo studeant intimare. ipse autem episcopus ad prouinciam suam conuocet accusatos, qui nisi ab obiecto reatu se purgauerint, vel si post purgationem exhibitam in pristinam fuerint relapsi perfidiam, canonice puniantur. ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod si fama est, quod in aliqua dioecesi sint aliqui haeretici sequaces papae, episcopus debet eos cum diligentia debita inuestigare, & contra eos procedere secundum quod ordo iuris requirit. Si autem per se eos nequiuerit cohercere, auxilium inuocet brachii secularis. Si enim praelatus ecclesiae pro defensione pauperum postulare debet auxilium seculare, vt legitur 23. q. 3. c. Maximianus. & c. ab imperatoribus & q. 5. c. administratores: multomagis pro defensione fidei Christianae contra haereticos sequaces papae haeretici auxilium seculare debet cum instantia postulare, ad quod faciendum publicae potestatis debent iuramento ligari, sicut legitur extra, de haereticis, excommunicamus §. monentur. insuper cum episcopi sciuerint papam haeretica prauitate respersum circa reparationem errorum suorum per se vel per alios debent insistere diligenter: tenenturque veritatem modis quibus possunt congruentibus publicare, & quantum possunt manifestare & occulte auribus omnium inculcare, ac reges & principes aliosque seculi diuites & potentes sanctis exhortationibus & consiliis animare, vt causam fidei defendant vniuersaliter & potentes. omnia praedicta multis modis, vt habetur, possunt demonstratiue probari.
units.tr: Student: Tell me briefly and in summary what, according to your earlier opinion, the bishops must do if followers of a heretical pope were to preach, teach and publish his erroneous doctrine in their dioceses as though it were Catholic. Teacher: The answer is this. If it has been established to a bishop by report that the pope has fallen into heretical depravity, he ought to be concerned lest some of his flock follow the pope's perfidy. The timid and ambitious, who are a large and perhaps even an infinite number, readily embrace the error of the head, either to please or so as not to displease. So Ecclesiasticus 10 says: According to the judge of the people, so are his ministers; and what kind of ruler the city has, such are its inhabitants. Likewise, as is written in 6 q. 1, c. Sunt plurimi, §. Verum: When the head grows faint, the other members of the body are easily infected, as it is written: The whole head is sick and the whole heart faint, from the sole of the foot even to the crown of the head. And so, since a pope stained with the stain of heresy must be feared, lest he infect the people with a similar stain, a bishop who fulfils the office of a watchman, whose duty it is to look about most carefully lest enemies draw near, must diligently inquire whether the report of the pope's heretical perfidy contains the truth, and with what heresy he is infected. Once this is ascertained, he must examine carefully, himself and through others, how the orthodox faith may be defended against it. Having done this, he should next investigate whether any people are striving to introduce the pope's heresy into his flock, especially if it is reported that some in his diocese imitate, teach, publish, preach and spread the doctrine of the heretical pope as Catholic and to be held. This accords with the precept of Innocent III, who, as is found in ext. de haeretic. c. excommunicamus, says: We further decree that every archbishop or bishop, either in person or through an archdeacon or other suitable and honourable persons, shall go round his own parish, in which there is report that heretics dwell, once or twice a year at least; and there he shall compel three or more men of good reputation, and even, if it seems advisable, the whole neighbourhood, to swear. If anyone there knows of heretics, or of others holding secret conventicles or departing from the common life and morals of the faithful, let them take care to report them to the bishop. The bishop himself shall summon the accused to his synod, and unless they clear themselves of the charge laid against them, or if after clearing themselves they fall back into their former perfidy, they shall be punished according to the canons. From these words it is gathered that if there is report that in some diocese there are some heretics who follow the pope, the bishop must investigate them with due diligence and proceed against them according to the order of law. If he cannot restrain them himself, let him call upon the help of the secular arm. For if a prelate of the Church ought to seek secular aid in defence of the poor, as is read in 23 q. 3, c. Maximianus, and c. Ab imperatoribus, and 5 q. 5, c. Administratores, much more, in defence of the Christian faith against heretics who follow a heretical pope, ought he to seek secular aid with urgency. For this purpose the holders of public power must be bound by oath, as is read in extra, de haereticis, excommunicamus, §. Monentur. Moreover, since bishops know that the pope is tainted with heretical depravity, they must press diligently, themselves or through others, for his amendment of his errors. They are bound to make the truth known by whatever suitable means they can, to reveal it as far as they are able, and to impress it openly and secretly on the ears of all; and they must encourage kings, princes and the other rich and powerful of the world with holy exhortations and counsels, so that they may defend the cause of the faith both universally and powerfully. All these things, as is shown, can be proved demonstratively in many ways.

units.la: DISCIP. Tange breuiter aliqua media, quibus prescripta probari appareant. MAGIST. Argumenta ad probandum praedicta fundantur in quatuor propositionibus, quarum prima est haec: quod episcopi & praelati nullam causam debent magis defensare, quam fidem Christi. Secunda est, quod sine fide recta nullum est spirituale bonum proficiens ad salutem. & tertia est, quod episcopi & praelati pro salute gregis debent animam suam ponere. Quarta est, quod pro veritate usque ad mortem certare tenentur.
units.tr: Student: Touch briefly on some of the means by which what has been set out may be seen to be proved. Teacher: The arguments for proving the above rest on four propositions. The first is this: bishops and prelates ought to defend no cause more than the faith of Christ. The second is that without sound faith no spiritual good avails for salvation. The third is that bishops and prelates ought to lay down their souls for the salvation of the flock. The fourth is that they are bound to contend for the truth even unto death.

units.la: CAP. XLI.
units.tr: CAP. XLI.

units.la: In quo tractatur de episcopis & praelatis impugnatores papae haeretici molestantibus, quae poena sint plectendi.
units.tr: In which it is discussed what penalties are to be inflicted on bishops and prelates who harass the Papists' opponents, the heretics who attack the Pope.

units.la: DISCIP. Satis concipio, quomodo ex his possunt accipi argumenta ad probandum illa, quae in c. praecedenti sunt assERTA. Ideo illis omissis circa episcopos & praelatos tracta de illis, qui impugnatores papae haeretici & doctrinae suae erroneae molestarent, persequerentur, & graviter infestarent. MAGIST. De talibus tenetur a multis, quod sunt fautores haereticae prauitatis. si enim episcopi & praelati, qui tacent, & non corrigunt sequaces papae haeretici, sunt fautores prauitatis haereticae computandi: sunt etiam tales proditores catholicae veritatis & totius Christianitatis. nam si proditor est veritatis ille, qui non libere veritatem pronunciat, quam pronunciare oportet. II. q. 3. c. nolite, multo fortius proditor est veritatis & totius Christianitatis, qui persequitur vel molestat defensores catholicae veritatis & totius Christianitatis, quam papa haereticus reprobat & confundit, persequitur & impugnat. DISC. Quod episcopi & praelati non debent persequi quoquomodo impugnatores papae haeretici, videtur ex tractatis sup. libro 6. vbi de impugnantibus papam pro prauitate haeretica defendendis dependere videtur. Si enim impugnatores papae haeretici sunt a catholicis defendendi, non sunt ab eis aliqualiter impugnandi. quare nolo amplius hic probari, quod episcopi & praelati qui sciunt vel scire tenentur papam esse haereticum, impugnatores papae haeretici infestare non debent. Sed dic qua poena episcopi & praelati, qui impugnatores papae haeretici persequuntur & infestant, sunt merito feriendi. MAGIST. Sunt quidam dicentes, quod omnes tales poena fautorum haereticae prauitatis sunt plectendi, vltra quam poenam diuersi pro diuersis & specialibus modis persequendi & molestandi impugnatores papae haeretici sunt diuersis poenis & specialibus percellendi: quia pro diuersis iniuriis eis illatis sunt inferentes diuersimode puniendi. contingit enim eis iniuriari & in iudicio & extra iudicium multis modis: scilicet verbo & facto. verbo quidem cum diffamatione, detractione, contumeliis, derisione & maledictione. facto etiam tam in iudicio quam extra iudicium contingit eis multas iniurias inferri: quia possunt spoliari rebus suis, officiis & honoribus. & iterum possent incarcerari, detineri, mutilari, & occidi.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. I understand well enough how arguments may be drawn from these points to prove what was asserted in the previous chapter. So, leaving those aside, turn to bishops and prelates who harass, persecute and grievously molest those who attack the Pope as a heretic and his erroneous doctrine. MASTER. Many hold that such men are supporters of heretical depravity. For if bishops and prelates who keep silent and do not correct the followers of the heretical Pope are to be counted as supporters of heretical depravity, then such men are also betrayers of Catholic truth and of the whole of Christianity. For if he is a betrayer of the truth who does not freely proclaim the truth he ought to proclaim (II. q. 3. c. nolite), much more is he a betrayer of the truth and of the whole of Christianity who persecutes or molests the defenders of Catholic truth and of the whole of Christianity, whom the heretical Pope condemns, persecutes and attacks. DISCIPLE. It seems from what was treated above in book 6, where the defence of those who attack the Pope for heretical depravity seems to be discussed, that bishops and prelates ought not in any way to persecute the heretical Pope's opponents. For if the Pope's heretical opponents must be defended by Catholics, they must not be attacked by them in any way. Therefore I do not wish it to be proved here again that bishops and prelates who know, or are bound to know, that the Pope is a heretic, ought not to harass his opponents. But tell me by what penalty the bishops and prelates who persecute and harass the heretical Pope's opponents deserve to be struck. MASTER. Some say that all such men are to be punished with the penalty of supporters of heretical depravity; and beyond that penalty, those who persecute and molest the Pope's opponents in various particular ways are to be struck with various and special penalties, since for the various injuries they inflict they are to be punished in various ways. For injuries can be done to them in court and outside court in many ways, namely by word and by deed. By word, indeed, through defamation, detraction, insults, mockery and curses. By deed, too, both in court and outside it, many injuries may be inflicted on them: they may be stripped of their goods, offices and honours; and moreover they could be imprisoned, held in custody, maimed and killed.

units.la: DISCIP. Cerno quod multae iniuriae secundum istam opinionem possunt impugnatoribus papae haeretici per episcopos & praelatos inferri: de quibus tantum quatuor prosequere. Primo autem dic de spoliatione siue rerum siue officiorum. MAGIST. Respondetur, quod si episcopi & praelati impugnatores papae haeretici rebus vel officiis duxerint spoliandos, vltra poenam fautoriam haereticae prauitatis ad restitutionem rerum & officiorum sunt astricti: quia omne iniuste ablatum debet restitui. 10. q. 1. vnde & tales spoliatores illorum, qui impugnant papam haereticum, sunt raptores & praedones censendi, quia nisi res ablatas restituerint, si possunt, sunt ecclesiastica sepultura priuandi, ext. de raptoribus. c. super eo. DISCIP. Dic de diffamatione. MAG. Dicitur quod si episcopi & praelati quoquomodo, siue per se siue per alios siue legendo siue publicando processus papae haeretici defendendo contra impugnatores errorum suorum siue quocunque alio modo, diffamauerunt impugnatores eosdem vocando eos haereticos vel schismaticos vel crimen aliud quodcunque, quod non est probatum legitime, eis imponendo: de necessitate salutis tenentur famam restituere eorundem, dicendo publice, si publice diffamauerunt; vel occulte, si occulte falsum se dixisse. quia non minus tenetur quis restituere famam, quam iniuste abstulit alteri, quam rem temporalem aliquam ablatam iniuste, cum fama sit temporalibus preciosior. & ideo sicut nunquam est extra peccatum mortale, qui non restituerit rem alterius quam abstulit iniuste si potest, ita semper est in peccato mortali qui famam alterius abstulit vel denigrat iniuste & si non restituerit si potest. sed praelati diffamantes impugnatores papae haeretici, abstulerunt famam illorum iniuste. ergo eandem famam eis restituere de necessitate salutis sunt astricti.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. I see that according to this opinion many injuries can be inflicted on the heretical Pope's opponents by bishops and prelates. Of these, pursue only four. Speak first of plunder, whether of goods or of offices. MASTER. The answer is this: if bishops and prelates have seen fit to strip the heretical Pope's opponents of goods or offices, then beyond the penalty of supporting heretical depravity they are bound to restore the goods and offices, because whatever has been taken unjustly must be restored (10. q. 1). Hence those who plunder such men, who attack the heretical Pope, are to be judged robbers and pirates; and unless they restore the goods taken, if they are able to, they are to be deprived of ecclesiastical burial (Extra, de raptoribus, c. super eo). DISCIPLE. Now speak of defamation. MASTER. It is said that if bishops and prelates, in any way whatever, whether themselves or through others, whether by reading or publishing the proceedings in defence of the heretical Pope against those who oppose his errors, or by any other means, have defamed those same opponents by calling them heretics or schismatics or by imputing to them any other crime that has not been lawfully proved, then for the necessity of salvation they are bound to restore their reputation: by saying so publicly if they defamed them publicly, or privately if they defamed them privately, that they spoke falsely. For a man is no less bound to restore another's reputation which he has unjustly taken away than to restore some temporal thing unjustly taken, since reputation is more precious than temporal goods. Therefore, just as a man who does not restore another's property that he has unjustly taken, if he is able, is never free from mortal sin, so a man who unjustly takes away or blackens another's reputation, and does not restore it if he can, is always in mortal sin. But prelates who defame the Pope's heretical opponents have unjustly taken away their reputation. Therefore they are bound, for the necessity of salvation, to restore that same reputation to them.

units.la: DISCIP. Dic de violentia. MAGIST. Dicitur, quod si impugnatores papae haeretici sunt clerici vel religiosi, quicunque in eos manus iniecerit violentas capiendo, detinendo, incarcerando, vel quocunque alio modo, sententiam excommunicationis incurrunt: & ab eodem sunt absoluendi a quo absoluendi essent, si ex alia causa in eosdem iniecerint manus violentas. & propter idem quicunque sunt in potestate constituti & eisdem non defendunt, sententiam excommunicationis incurrunt, extra, de sententia excommunicationis, quamvis. DISC. Dic de morte.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Now speak of violence. MASTER. It is said that if the heretical Pope's opponents are clerics or religious, whoever lays violent hands on them, by seizing, detaining, imprisoning or in any other way, incurs the sentence of excommunication, and must be absolved by the same person by whom he would have to be absolved if he had laid violent hands on them for some other cause. For the same reason, whoever is set in authority and does not defend them incurs the sentence of excommunication: Extra, de sententia excommunicationis, quamvis. DISCIPLE. Now speak of death.

units.la: MAGIST. Dicitur quod quicunque episcopus vel alius sine fuerit legatus sive alio quocunque fungens officio impugnatorem papæ hæretici propter hoc curiæ tradiderit seculari, vel aliquid aliud fecerit vel mandauerit, aut ratum habuerit, ex quo sequitur mors alicuius impugnatoris papæ hæretici, irregularis efficitur, & omnem pœnam incurrit, quam incurreret si manibus propriis occidisset innocentem. hoc probatur sic. qui causam proximam dat homicidio, irregularis efficitur, teste Alexandro. 3. qui extra, de homicidio, de cætero, ait: de cætero nouerit quod diaconus, qui homicidio causam proximam dedisse videtur, non videtur ad sacerdotium promouendus. qui autem impugnatorem papæ hæretici tradit curiæ seculari, vel aliquid aliud facit vel mandat fieri, ex quo mors sequitur corporalis, dat causam proximam homicidio. ergo irregularis efficitur, & omnem pœnam incurrit, quam homicida incurreret. DISCIP. Per istam rationem omnis prælatus, qui quemcunque clericum hæreticum vel alium tradit curiæ seculari, irregularis efficitur: quia causam proximam dat homicidio. sed constat quod tales non efficiuntur irregulares. ergo ista ratio non procedit. MAGIST. Ad hoc in simili, Glossa ext. de homicidio c. continebatur, respondere videtur, vbi rationem assignat, quare vnus ex cuius ludo mors sequitur, irregularis efficitur, & alius ex cuius ludo etiam mors secuta est, irregularis non fit. unde obiiciens contra illud per id quod habetur in capitulo continebatur, super verbo rationem, ait: infra. c. proximo contra. ibi libere promouens ad ordines superiores, hic non sine licentia papæ. & idem casus videtur. quid ergo fines fecit diuersos? & respondens ait: solum hic dabat operam illicitæ rei ludendo cum laico: quod non licet. vel si etiam licitum fuisset, non adhibuit diligentiam, quam debuit, quia cum sciret ludi conditionem, non reliquit falcem à se. unde fuit in culpa: quare promoueri ad superiores non debet sine licentia papæ, vt hic dicit. in c. sequenti, ludebat cum clerico & licito ludo: & de illo cutello non sperabatur aliquid mortale, & ille potius ingessit se proiiciendo alium ad terram: & sic non fuit in culpa. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod si clerici dant operam rei licitæ, & debitam diligentiam adhiberent, quamuis ex facto eorum mors sequatur, irregularitatem nequaquam incurrunt. Si vero clericus dederit operam rei illicitæ, vel dando operam rei licitæ, diligentiam debitam non adhibuit: si ex opere suo mors sequatur, irregularis efficitur. Cum ergo episcopi & prælati tradendo impugnatores papæ hæretici curiæ seculari non dent operam rei licitæ: quia non licet eis quomodo libet molestare impugnantes hæreticam prauitatem: si mors secuta fuerit, irregularitatem incurrunt. episcopi autem & prælati tradendo hæreticos & quosdam alios malefactores curiæ seculari, non dant operam rei illicitæ: quia hoc incumbit eorum officio. & ideo si debitam diligentiam adhibent, non efficiuntur irregulares, quamuis mors sequatur.
units.tr: MASTER. It is said that whatever bishop or other man, whether a legate or one discharging any other office, has handed over to the secular court an opponent of the heretical Pope for that reason, or has done or commanded anything else, or has ratified it, from which the death of some opponent of the heretical Pope follows, becomes irregular and incurs the whole penalty he would have incurred had he killed an innocent man with his own hands. This is proved thus. Whoever gives the proximate cause of a homicide becomes irregular, as Alexander III says in Extra, de homicidio, de cetero: "Henceforth let it be known that a deacon who appears to have given the proximate cause of a homicide does not appear to be fit for promotion to the priesthood." But whoever hands an opponent of the heretical Pope over to the secular court, or does or commands something else to be done from which bodily death follows, gives the proximate cause of homicide. Therefore he becomes irregular and incurs the whole penalty that a homicide would incur. DISCIPLE. By this reasoning every prelate who hands over any heretical or other cleric to the secular court becomes irregular, since he gives the proximate cause of homicide. But it is plain that such men do not become irregular. Therefore this reasoning does not hold. MASTER. The Gloss on the chapter Continebatur in Extra, de homicidio, seems to answer this by a similar case, where it gives the reason why one from whose game a death follows becomes irregular, and another from whose game a death has also followed does not. Hence, objecting against that by what is found in the chapter Continebatur, on the word "reason", it says: "Below, in the chapter Proximo contra: there he freely promotes to higher orders, here not without the Pope's permission." And the case seems the same. Why then does it make different ends? And it answers: here he was merely engaged in an unlawful matter by playing with a layman, which is not allowed; or even if it had been lawful, he did not use the diligence he ought to have used, since, knowing the nature of the game, he did not put the sickle away from himself. Hence he was at fault, and so he must not be promoted to higher orders without the Pope's permission, as the text here says. In the following chapter he was playing with a cleric and a lawful game, and nothing deadly was expected from that knife; rather he himself rushed in, throwing the other to the ground; and so he was not at fault. From these words it is gathered that if clerics are engaged in a lawful matter and use due diligence, then even though death follows from their act they by no means incur irregularity. But if a cleric is engaged in an unlawful matter, or, engaged in a lawful one, fails to use due diligence, and death follows from his act, he becomes irregular. Therefore, since bishops and prelates, in handing opponents of the heretical Pope over to the secular court, are not engaged in a lawful matter, because it is not lawful for them in any way to molest those who attack heretical depravity, if death follows they incur irregularity. But bishops and prelates who hand heretics and certain other malefactors over to the secular court are not engaged in an unlawful matter, because this belongs to their office; and so, if they use due diligence, they do not become irregular, even though death follows.

units.la: CAP. XLII. In quo quaeritur de magistris & doctoribus docentibus doctrinam papæ hæretici, si sint fautores prauitatis hæretica.
units.tr: CHAPTER XLII. Concerning teachers and doctors who teach the doctrine of a heretical pope, and whether they are supporters of heretical depravity.

units.la: DISCIP. Nunc videamus de Doctoribus & Magistris, an docentes & tenentes doctrinam hæreticalem papæ hæretici sunt fautores hæreticæ prauitatis. MAG. Quos comprehendis sub nomine Doctorum & Magistrorum. DISCIP. Per Doctores & Magistros omnes habentes officium prædicandi vel legendi catholicam doctrinam. MAG. Ergo inter Doctores & Magistros reputas numerandos non solum magistros theologiæ: sed etiam omnes Lectores vel Bachalarios theologiæ, & etiam Decretistas, qui legunt libros decretorum & decretalium: in quibus multa, quæ ad doctrinam spectant catholicam, continentur: ac etiam Plebanos, & eos qui auctoritate papæ vel alterius prælati habent officium prædicandi? DISCIP. Ita est. omnes enim prædicti docere habent catholicam veritatem. quamobrem dicferas, an omnes prædicti si docuerint publice vel tenuerint doctrinam hæreticalem papæ hæretici, sint fautores hæreticæ prauitatis, vel etiam inter hæreticos computandi. MAG. Dicitur distinguendo: quia aut doctrina papæ erronea est talis, quod prædicti doctores & magistri tenentur explicite credere contrariam veritatem: Aut est talis quod eam credere explicite non tenentur. Item, aut prius sciuerunt papæ doctrinam esse hæreticam, erroneam, aut nescuerunt. Item, aut doctrina papæ erronea est per ipsum solenniter diffinita seu determinata, aut non est solenniter diffinita, sed est solummodo prædicata pertinaciter vel asserta. Si itaque doctrina papæ hæretica est talis, quod doctores & magistri tenentur explicite credere contrariam veritatem: quia videlicet est apud omnes catholicos diuulgata: vel si prius eä tanquam catholicam didicerunt, nec sunt obliti doctores & magistri docentes publice qualitercunque publice vel occulte doctrinam talem erroneam papæ hæretici, sunt fautores hæreticæ prauitatis & hæretici computandi; quia omnis docens vel tenens assertionem hæreticam, cuius contrariam veritatem tenetur explicite credere, est hæreticus iudicandus. Si autem doctrina papæ erronea est talis, quod doctores & magistri non tenentur explicite credere contrariam veritatem; nec est per papam solenniter diffinita seu determinata; docens eam aperte siue occulte non est ex hoc solo fautor hæreticæ prauitatis, nec hæreticus iudicandus; sed est sollicite & diligenter exanimandus, an paratus sit corrigi. & siquidem paratus est corrigi (ita quod nullo modo de pertinacia possit conuinci) non est reus censendus. Si vero non sit paratus corrigi; sed pertinaciter in doctrina papæ hæretici persistit, est fautor hæreticæ prauitatis, & hæreticus reputandus. Si autem magistri & doctores docerent publice doctrinam papæ erroneam, quam sciunt per ipsum solenniter diffinitam, & docent quod diffinitio huiusmodi papæ est tenenda, sunt fautores hæreticæ prauitatis, & hæretici reputandi, siue teneantur explicite credere veritatem contrariam, siue non teneantur explicite ipsam credere. Huius ratio assignatur: quia quicunque pertinaciter adhæret doctrinæ contra fidem, est hereticus reputandus. sed doctores & magistri docentes diffinitionem papæ erroneam esse tenendam, pertinaciter doctrinæ erroneæ diffinitæ adhærent. quia qui asserit quod irrevocabiliter & in omnem euentum est adhærendum doctrinæ erroneæ: ipse pertinaciter adhærere eidem doctrinæ censetur. quare est pertinax reputandus: & per consequens hæreticus est censendus. Item, non minus peccat doctor vel magister, qui publice docet diffinitionem papæ hæreticam esse tenendam: quam si consensisset, quod papa doctrinam huiusmodi solenniter diffiniret. sed si doctor consensisset, quod papa doctrinam huiusmodi solenniter diffiniret, fuisset fautor hæreticæ prauitatis. ergo docendo quod diffinitio eius erronea est tenenda, est fautor hæreticæ prauitatis reputandus.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Now let us consider teachers and doctors: whether those who teach and hold the heretical doctrine of a heretical pope are supporters of heretical depravity. MASTER. Whom do you include under the names of doctors and teachers? DISCIPLE. Everyone who has the office of preaching or lecturing on Catholic doctrine. MASTER. So you count among the doctors and teachers not only the masters of theology, but also all the lecturers and bachelors of theology, and even the canonists who read the books of the decrees and decretals, in which much that concerns Catholic doctrine is contained, and also parish priests and those who hold, by the authority of the pope or another prelate, the office of preaching? DISCIPLE. Yes, that is so, for all these are bound to teach Catholic truth. Therefore tell me whether all these, if they have publicly taught or held the heretical doctrine of a heretical pope, are supporters of heretical depravity, or are even to be counted among heretics. MASTER. The answer requires distinctions. For either the pope's error is of such a kind that these doctors and teachers are bound to believe the contrary truth explicitly, or it is of such a kind that they are not bound to believe it explicitly. Again, either they knew beforehand that the pope's doctrine was heretical and erroneous, or they did not know it. Again, either the pope's erroneous doctrine has been solemnly defined or determined by him, or it has not been solemnly defined but has only been pertinaciously preached or asserted. If, then, the pope's heretical doctrine is of such a kind that the doctors and teachers are bound to believe the contrary truth explicitly, because it is publicly known among all Catholics, or if they learned it earlier as Catholic and have not forgotten it, then doctors and teachers who publicly or privately, in any manner, teach such an erroneous doctrine of a heretical pope are to be counted supporters of heretical depravity and heretics; for everyone who teaches or holds a heretical assertion, the contrary truth of which he is bound to believe explicitly, is to be judged a heretic. But if the pope's erroneous doctrine is of such a kind that doctors and teachers are not bound to believe the contrary truth explicitly, and it has not been solemnly defined or determined by the pope, then one who teaches it openly or secretly is not for that reason alone a supporter of heretical depravity, nor to be judged a heretic; rather he must be carefully and diligently examined as to whether he is ready to be corrected. And if he is ready to be corrected (so that he cannot in any way be convicted of obstinacy), he is not to be considered guilty. But if he is not ready to be corrected, and persists obstinately in the doctrine of the heretical pope, he is a supporter of heretical depravity and is to be regarded as a heretic. If, however, teachers and doctors publicly teach the pope's erroneous doctrine, which they know has been solemnly defined by him, and they teach that such a definition of the pope is to be held, they are supporters of heretical depravity and to be regarded as heretics, whether or not they are bound to believe the contrary truth explicitly. The reason for this is given: whoever obstinately clings to a doctrine contrary to the faith is to be regarded as a heretic; but doctors and teachers who teach that the pope's erroneous definition is to be held are obstinately clinging to a defined erroneous doctrine, for he who asserts that an erroneous doctrine must be adhered to irrevocably and in every event is considered to cling to that doctrine obstinately; therefore he is to be regarded as obstinate, and consequently is to be considered a heretic. Again, a doctor or teacher who publicly teaches that the pope's heretical definition is to be held sins no less than if he had consented to the pope solemnly defining such a doctrine. But if a doctor had consented that the pope should solemnly define such a doctrine, he would have been a supporter of heretical depravity. Therefore, by teaching that his erroneous definition is to be held, he is to be regarded as a supporter of heretical depravity.

units.la: CAP. XLIII.
units.tr: CHAP. XLIII.

units.la: Docet, qualiter doctores catholici & prælati tenentur contra papam hæreticum ad bellum spirituale & corporale. & respondetur secundum auctoritates quasdam, quæ responsio deducitur ad tria inconvenientia, quæ consequenter in c. seq. & 45. pertractantur. & ad auctoritates c. 45. respondetur, & pro hac conclusione adducuntur 7, aliæ rationes infra c. 46.
units.tr: Teaches how Catholic teachers and prelates are bound to wage spiritual and bodily war against a heretical pope. A response is given on the basis of certain authorities, and this response leads to three difficulties, which are treated in the following chapters, 44 and 45. The authorities in chapter 45 are answered, and seven further arguments for this conclusion are adduced below, in chapter 46.

units.la: DISCIP. Quia dubito, quod si unquam aliquis papa potens, cui faveant reges & principes, erit hæreticus: spiritus mendax erit in ore omnium vel plurium prophetarum, i. doctorum, qui secundum beatum Greg. ut legitur di. 43. c. sit rector, per prophetas in sacro eloquio designantur: idcirco de doctoribus, qui forte erunt tempore papæ hæretici, plura interrogare propono, ad quæ tu breviter studeas respondere. disseras imprimis, an doctores & magistri, si papa fuerit hereticus, teneantur contra doctrinam eius erroneam prædicare & eam efficaciter reprobare.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. I doubt that if ever some powerful pope, supported by kings and princes, becomes a heretic, then the lying spirit will be in the mouth of all or most of the prophets, that is, the teachers, whom Gregory, as read in Dist. 43, c. Sit rector, says are designated in sacred speech by the prophets. I therefore propose to ask you several questions about the teachers who will perhaps exist in the time of a heretical pope, and I ask you to answer briefly. First, please explain whether teachers and masters, if the pope is a heretic, are bound to preach against his erroneous doctrine and to refute it effectively.

units.la: MAGIST. Respondetur, quod pro loco & tempore debitis circumstantiis observatis omnes doctores sive fuerint magistri sive in aliquo gradu docendi officium habentes exercere in theologica facultate, si fuerint habentes tantummodo officium prædicandi ad populum, de necessitate salutis tenerentur doctrinam papæ erroneam, præsertim si apud illos inter quos prædicta exercent officia, fuerit diuulgata, efficaciter reprobare, & contrariam veritatem simpliciter affirmare. hoc videtur pluribus modis probari. Primo quidem sic. In omni certamine corporali & spirituali laus præcipua bellatorum in hoc videtur consistere, quod suo duci indissolubiliter adhærendo hostes eius quanto fuerint fortiores & periculosiores & perniciosiores, tanto magis expugnare conantur. sed in catholicorum exercitu contra agmina hæreticorum primum locum vel saltem non infimum bellatorum doctores obtinere videntur, cum secundum Inno. tertium, ut habetur extr. de hæret. c. cum ex iniuncto, sit quasi præcipuus in ecclesia. & Honorius tertius, ut habetur extr. ne clerici vel monachi secularibus negociis se immisceant. c. super specula, prædicatores bellatores appellat: qui vero theologiæ studium cupimus ampliare, ut dilatato tentorii sui loco funiculos suos faciat longiores, ut sit fides catholica circumcincta muro inexpugnabili bellatorum, quibus resistere valeat ascendentibus ex aduerso, &c. vbi dicit Glos. super verbo Bellatorum. i. prædicatorum, qui possunt resistere hæreticis auctoritate diuina scriptura, qui contra nos surgunt ex aduerso & impugnant nos. ergo prædicatores & doctores quanto hæretici fuerint fortiores & periculosiores ac perniciosiores: tanto magis debent satagere, ut eis resistant, ac eos expugnent, eorum doctrinam auctoritatibus sacris & rationibus efficacibus reprobando. nullus autem hereticus potest esse periculosior aut perniciosior exercitui catholicorum quam papa hæreticus. nullus enim alius tantam poterit habere audaciam & sequelam tantam, quantam papa hæreticus. ergo contra ipsum debent prædicatores, doctores & magistri præcipue & potissime toto posse insurgere eum aperte & per insidias ac omnibus modis congruentibus impugnando.
units.tr: MASTER. The answer is this: with due regard for place, time and the other circumstances, all teachers, whether they are masters or hold the teaching office in any grade of theological faculty, and even those who have only the office of preaching to the people, are of necessity bound, for the sake of salvation, to refute effectively the erroneous doctrine of the pope, especially if it has been published among those among whom they exercise these offices, and to affirm the contrary truth plainly. This seems to be proved in several ways. First, in every contest, bodily or spiritual, the chief praise of soldiers seems to consist in this: that, cleaving inseparably to their leader, they try to overcome his enemies, the stronger, more dangerous and more destructive they are. But among the Catholic army, against the battle lines of the heretics, the teachers seem to hold the first place among the soldiers, or at least not the lowest, since, according to Innocent III (as is found in Extra, De haereticis, c. Cum ex iniuncto), they are as it were the chief in the Church. And Honorius III (as is found in Extra, Ne clerici vel monachi secularibus negotiis se immisceant, c. Super specula) calls preachers soldiers.
