Those who wish to extend the study of theology, so that by enlarging the place of their tent they may lengthen their cords, so that the Catholic faith may be surrounded by an impregnable wall of soldiers, by whom it may be able to resist those who come up against it, and so on, where the Gloss says on the word soldiers, that is, preachers, who can resist heretics by the authority of divine Scripture, those who rise against us and attack us. Therefore, the more powerful, dangerous and destructive the heretics are, the more preachers and teachers ought to labour to resist them and to overcome them, refuting their doctrine by sacred authorities and effective arguments. Now no heretic can be more dangerous or more destructive to the army of Catholics than a heretical pope. For no one else can have such great boldness and such a following as a heretical pope. Therefore preachers, teachers and masters ought above all and especially, with all their power, to rise up against him, attacking him openly, by stratagems, and by every suitable means.

units.la: DISCIP. Ista ratio non videtur probare intentum; quia non licet cuilibet bellatorum bellum indicere. quia secundum beatum August. ut legitur. 33. quæst. 1. cap. quid culpatur; suscipiendi bellum auctoritas atq; consilium penes principes est. vbi dicit Glos. nullus ergo bellator potest sine auctoritate principis. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod omnes bellatores parati debent esse ad prælium, quando princeps iubet. sine tamen auctoritate principis nulli bellare licet. ergo si papa fiat hereticus, indicetur; auctoritate tamen propria ipsum impugnare non debent. quamdiu enim ab ecclesia toleratur, doctores & magistri tacere debent.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. This argument does not seem to prove the point, because it is not lawful for any soldier to declare war. For according to Augustine, as read in C. 33, q. 1, c. Quid culpatur, the authority and counsel of undertaking war rest with the princes. Where the Gloss says: no soldier therefore can fight without the authority of the prince. From these words it is gathered that all soldiers ought to be ready for battle when the prince commands, yet without the authority of the prince it is lawful for no one to fight. Therefore, if the pope becomes a heretic, let him be declared so; yet they ought not to attack him on their own authority. For as long as he is tolerated by the Church, teachers and masters ought to be silent.

units.la: MAGIST. Ista responsio nonnullis friuola videtur, quantum ad tria, quæ videtur innuere. primum est quod contra papam hæreticum non eo ipso quo fit hereticus sed ex edicto principis bellum geritur spirituale. Secundum est quod papa hereticus quamdiu ab ecclesia toleratur est nullatenus expugnandus. Tertium est quod in nullo casu sine auctoritate principis licet alicui bellum generale siue particulare contra hostem suscipere. Ista enim tria quidam re‐ putant omnino falsa. Quod enim primum sit falsum ostenditur, quia contra papam haereticum tam a principe principum, scilicet a Domino nostro Iesu Christo, quam ab apostolis vicariis eius, est bellum indictum. quod enim Christus bellare spiritualiter contra papam si fiat haereticus aperte mandauerit, apparet per illud Matth. 10. cum dicit, non veni pacem mittere sed gladium. per gladium potestas bellandi datur intelligi. Christus ergo omnes catholicos in bello spirituali constitutos, praecipuum autem bellum catholicorum contra haereticos esse videtur.
units.tr: MASTER. This answer seems to many to be frivolous, as regards the three things it seems to imply. The first is that against a heretical pope, a spiritual war is waged not by the very fact that he becomes a heretic but by the edict of the prince. The second is that a heretical pope, as long as he is tolerated by the Church, is in no way to be attacked. The third is that in no case is it lawful for anyone to undertake war, general or particular, against an enemy without the authority of the prince. Some people consider these three things entirely false. That the first is false is shown by this: war has been declared against a heretical pope both by the Prince of princes, namely our Lord Jesus Christ, and by the apostles, his vicars. That Christ clearly commanded that spiritual war be waged against the pope if he becomes a heretic appears from that saying in Matthew 10, where he says: I came not to send peace but the sword. By the sword the power of waging war is understood to be given. Christ therefore seems to have set all Catholics in spiritual battle, and the chief war of Catholics to be against heretics.

units.la: Nullus autem haereticus perniciosior vel periculosior est papa haeretico ergo contra papam haereticum praecipue est bellandum spiritualiter: nec expectandum est edictum principis, quia iam edictum a Christo principe est egressum. hoc etiam edictum auctoritate Christi beatus Paulus scribens ad Ephesios promulgavit, dum ait sic: Accipite armaturam Dei ut possitis resistere in die malo. & post: calciati pedes in praeparatione evangelii pacis: in omnibus sumentes scutum fidei, in quo possitis omnia tela nequissimi ignea extinguere: & galeam salutis assumere & gladium spiritus, quod est verbum Dei. quod edictum licet omnibus quantum ad aliqua dirigatur, tamen quantum ad aliquid specialiter praedicatores & doctores videtur respicere. Dies enim mala, imo pessima erit, si unquam papa potens tegum, & principum munitus fauore in haereticam prauitatem incidet. putant enim nonnulli, & probabile est, quod talis erit tribulatio catholicorum, qualis non fuit ab initio Christianitatis usque modo: & tamen forte strages corporalis Christianorum pro fide nulla vel minima erit. multitudo enim Christianorum licet pro temporibus forsitan papae haeretici sit praelia innumera perpessura pro fide: tamen persecutionem nullam penitus sustinebit, quia absque coactione & violentia voluntate spontanea papae haeretico adhaerebit. & forte paucissimi eidem resistere conabuntur. & tamen omnes monet apostolus armaturam Dei accipere, ut in die mala papae haeretico possint resistere. praedicatores autem & doctores specialiter exhortatur, ut ad resistendum se praeparent, cum dicit: calciati pedes in praeparationem evangelii pacis. vbi dicit Gloss. id est ita ut sint parati ad praedicandum evangelium. & quomodo se debent praeparare, declarat, cum asserit: assumendum gladium spiritus, quod est verbum Dei. hoc enim ad praedicatores & magistros spectare dignoscitur: quorum est per verbum Dei tanquam gladium acutissimum omnes haereticos, specialiter papam haereticum, iugulare. & ita edictum de bello gerendo contra papam haereticum, quod a Christo exierat, cum dicit, non veni pacem mittere, sed gladium, hoc Paulus publice promulgat, cum gladium spiritus quod est verbum Dei & ad expugnandum haereticos asserit assumendum. unde & Gloss. ibi dicit: de hoc gladio dominus ait: non veni pacem mittere, sed gladium. de eodem etiam gladio loquuntur discipulus & magister. quare sequitur, quod edictum de bello gerendo contra haereticos & specialiter contra papam haereticum a Christo principe iam exiit.
units.tr: No heretic is more destructive or more dangerous than a heretical pope. Therefore against a heretical pope above all spiritual war must be waged, and one need not wait for an edict of the prince, since an edict has already gone out from Christ the Prince. Blessed Paul, writing to the Ephesians, also published this edict by the authority of Christ, when he says: Take up the armour of God, that you may be able to resist in the evil day. And afterwards: Having your feet shod in the preparation of the gospel of peace; in all things taking up the shield of faith, in which you may be able to quench all the fiery darts of the most wicked; and take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God. Although this edict is directed to all in some respects, yet in some particular respects it seems to concern preachers and teachers. For the day will be evil, indeed most evil, if ever a powerful pope, fortified by the favour of princes, falls into heretical depravity. For some people think, and it is probable, that the tribulation of Catholics will be such as has not been from the beginning of Christianity until now; and yet perhaps there will be no or very little bodily slaughter of Christians for the faith. For the multitude of Christians, though in the times of a heretical pope they may perhaps suffer countless battles for the faith, will nonetheless sustain no persecution at all, since without compulsion or violence they will cling to the heretical pope by their own free will. And perhaps very few will try to resist him. Yet the Apostle warns all to take up the armour of God, so that in the evil day they may be able to resist a heretical pope. He especially exhorts preachers and teachers to prepare themselves for resisting, when he says: having your feet shod in the preparation of the gospel of peace. Where the Gloss says: that is, so that they may be ready to preach the gospel. And how they ought to prepare themselves he declares when he asserts: the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, is to be taken up. For this is known to pertain to preachers and masters, whose task is to slay, through the word of God as a most sharp sword, all heretics, especially a heretical pope. And so the edict about waging war against a heretical pope, which had gone out from Christ when he said, I came not to send peace, but the sword, is publicly promulgated by Paul, when he asserts that the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, is to be taken up also for overcoming heretics. Hence the Gloss there also says: Of this sword the Lord says: I came not to send peace, but the sword. The disciple and the master also speak of the same sword. Therefore it follows that the edict about waging war against heretics, and especially against a heretical pope, has already gone out from Christ the Prince.

units.la: DISCIP. Absq; magna prosecutione alias auctoritates allega. ex quibus ostenditur, quod edictum de bello spirituali gerendo contra papam haereticum a principe iam exiit.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Without a long discussion, cite other authorities from which it is shown that the edict for waging spiritual war against the heretical pope has already gone out from the prince.

units.la: MAGIST. Hoc ex verbis Christi colligitur, cum dicit Matth. 16. Intuimini & cavete a fermento Pharisaeorum & Saducaeorum. quod apostoli primo intelligentes de panibus, postea per informationem Christi intellexerunt, quia non dixerat cavendum a fermento panum, sed a doctrina Pharisaeorum & Saducaeorum. & quare hoc? nisi quia est contraria catholicae veritati. ergo in doctrina papae haeretici fuerit contraria catholicae veritati, ab ea penitus est cavendum. hoc autem non facient praedicatores sine certamine spirituali. ergo edictum de bello gerendo contra papam haereticum in simili a Christo iam exiit. hoc etiam Christus insinuavit, cum dicit Matthaei 10. Ecce ego mitto vos sicut oves in medio luporum. estote ergo prudentes sicut serpentes: & simplices sicut columbae: ne scilicet doctrina papae haeretici vos seducat. Item Mar. 13. ait; videte ne quis vos seducat. Ex quibus verbis Christus omnes catholicos reddit cautos, ne doctrina erronea cuiuscunque sive papae sive alterius seducantur, & ut se contra eam expugnandam animosius accingant. Item beatus Petrus 1. canonica sua capitul. 5. ait; Vigilate, quia adversarius vester diabolus tanquam &c. usque fortes in fide. Si autem diabolo est per fidem resistendum, etiam papae haeretico, qui est de ducibus & principibus diaboli, oportet resistere orthodoxos.
units.tr: MASTER. This is gathered from the words of Christ, when he says in Matthew 16: "Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees." The apostles at first understood this of bread, but afterwards, through Christ's instruction, they understood that he had not said to beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees. And why this? Only because it is contrary to catholic truth. Therefore, if the teaching of the heretical pope is contrary to catholic truth, it must be avoided altogether. Preachers will not do this without spiritual conflict. Therefore the edict for waging war against the heretical pope has similarly already gone out from Christ. Christ also suggested this when he says in Matthew 10: "Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves." That is, lest the teaching of the heretical pope seduce you. Likewise, in Mark 13 he says: "Take heed that no man deceive you." From these words Christ makes all catholics cautious, lest they be seduced by erroneous teaching of anyone, whether pope or another, and so that they may gird themselves more boldly to overcome it. Likewise the blessed Peter, in chapter 5 of his first Catholic epistle, says: "Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about," down to "steadfast in the faith." If the devil must be resisted through faith, then the orthodox must also resist the heretical pope, who is among the leaders and princes of the devil.

units.la: DISCIP. Quamuis istae & aliae auctoritates quamplurimae innuere videantur, quod oportet orthodoxos contra papam haereticum bellum assumere; tamen non probat specialiter, quod praedicatores & doctores ac magistri debeant contra papam haereticum praedicare & docere ac doctrinam eius publice reprobare.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Although these and very many other authorities seem to suggest that the orthodox must take up war against the heretical pope, they do not specifically prove that preachers, teachers and masters ought to preach and teach against the heretical pope and publicly refute his doctrine.

units.la: MAGIST. Concedit ur, quod auctoritates superius allegatae & quamplures aliae generales sunt omnibus catholicis bellum spirituale contra papam haereticum indicentes. quia enim papa haereticus fidem impugnat, & una secundum apostolum est fides. ideo omnes catholici contra papam haereticum bellum debent assumere, tanquam pro causa communi quae est una omnium. veruntamen sicut in exercitu se ad bellum corporale praeparantes non omnes idem habent officium, nec omnes corporaliter praeliantur. clerici enim licet non debeant corporaliter bellare; possunt tamen isto proelio interesse, ut hortentur & consulant expedit adiutorem. multi et seruitores bellatorum ad proeliandum minime sunt apti, nec etiam omnes bellatores eodem modo hostem impugnant. equites enim & pedites diversimode hostes invadunt; sic in exercitu catholicorum contra papam haereticum non omnes habent idem officium. quidam namque nesciunt doctrinam papae erroneam per sacras scripturas efficaciter impugnare. & ideo non pertinet ad ipsos praedicando vel docendo per scripturarum testimonia reprobare. Alii vero officium praedicandi & docendi veritatem catholicam & expugnandi pravitatem haereticam susceperunt: & ideo ad illos tanquam praecipuos bellatores spectat doctrinam papae erroneam fortius expugnare. quare ex hoc ipso, quod omnibus orthodoxis videtur bellum contra papam haereticum praedicatoribus doctoribus specialiter injungi dignoscitur ut suum officium exercentes praedicando & docendo contra papam haereticum & doctrinam eius insurgant. Alii vero qui scripturas ignorant bellatores spiritualiter corporaliter defendere, nutrire & etiam eis favere in omnibus, quae ad eorum spectant officium, contra papam haereticum astringuntur. DISCIP. Adhuc restat praedicta obiectio. quia in omnibus auctoritatibus praeallegatis de papa haeretico nulla fit mentio. ergo si per auctoritates ostenditur, quod praedicatores & doctores debent doctrinam papae erroneam reprobare: & eadem ratione debent doctrinam erroneam cuiuscunque haeretici impugnare: ad hoc tamen minime sunt astricti. quia nullus praedicator aut doctor posset omnem doctrinam erroneam extirpare. MAGIST. Respondetur, quod quamvis in auctoritatibus allegatis mentio verbalis non fiat de papa haeretico: & ideo de omnibus haereticis, imo de omnibus malis debent intelligi: principalius tamen debent intelligi de papa haeretico pro eo, quod ipse esset magis nocivus, quam alii haeretici minores in potentia sive minoris potentiae & minorem sequelam habentes. si enim contra malos & seductores oportet bellum spirituale assumere: contra magis malos & qui levius ac citius possunt decipere orthodoxos est fortius resistendum, quia cum papa haereticus valeat plures facilius & citius seducere, quam alii haeretici minores, contra papam virilissime spiritualiter est resistendum & pugnandum.
units.tr: MASTER. It is granted that the authorities cited above, and many others of a general kind, call all catholics to spiritual war against the heretical pope. For since the heretical pope attacks the faith, and according to the apostle there is one faith, all catholics ought to take up war against the heretical pope as for a common cause, which is one for all. Yet, just as in an army those preparing for bodily war do not all have the same duty, nor do all fight with their bodies, so clerics, although they ought not to wage war bodily, may still take part in this battle, to exhort and counsel, as an assistant is needed. Many servants of the soldiers are not at all fit for fighting, nor do all soldiers attack the enemy in the same way: horsemen and foot soldiers assail the enemy in different ways. So in the army of catholics against the heretical pope, not all have the same office. Some indeed do not know how to attack the erroneous teaching of the pope effectively through the sacred Scriptures, and so it does not pertain to them to refute it by preaching or teaching from the testimonies of Scripture. Others, however, have undertaken the office of preaching and teaching catholic truth and of overcoming heretical wickedness, and so it belongs to them, as the chief fighters, to attack the erroneous teaching of the pope more vigorously. Hence, from the fact that war against the heretical pope is seen by all the orthodox to be enjoined especially on preachers and teachers, it is clear that they, exercising their office, should rise up against the heretical pope and his teaching by preaching and teaching. Others, however, who do not know the Scriptures, are bound to defend the warriors spiritually and bodily, to support them, and in all things that pertain to their office to favour them in their war against the heretical pope. DISCIPLE. The aforementioned objection still remains. For in all the authorities cited above there is no mention of the heretical pope. Therefore, if the authorities show that preachers and teachers ought to refute the erroneous teaching of the pope, then by the same reasoning they ought to attack the erroneous teaching of any heretic whatever; yet they are not at all bound to this, because no preacher or teacher could root out all erroneous teaching. MASTER. The answer is that although the cited authorities do not verbally mention the heretical pope, and so they must be understood of all heretics, indeed of all evils, they must nevertheless be understood principally of the heretical pope, because he is more harmful than other, lesser heretics, who have less power or a smaller following. For if spiritual war must be waged against wicked men and seducers, then against those who are more wicked and who can more easily and quickly deceive the orthodox, one must resist more strongly. Since the heretical pope can seduce many more easily and quickly than other lesser heretics, one must resist and fight against the pope most manfully in the spirit.

units.la: CAP. XLIV
units.tr: CAP. XLIV

units.la: In quo tractatur secundum inconveniens, quod sequeretur ex ratione data ad rationem factam c. praecedenti.
units.tr: In which is treated the second absurdity that would follow from the argument given against the argument made in the preceding chapter.

units.la: DISCIP. In responsione mea ad rationem principalem dixisti innui tria, quae quibusdam falsa videntur. Tractasti autem de primo illorum, nunc dissere de secundo. MAG. Secundum, quod tua responsio videbatur innuere, est, quod papa haereticus, quamdiu ab ecclesia toleratur, est nullatenus expugnandus. Quod videtur quibusdam esse falsum propter falsam implicationem. Quia si papa haereticus ab ecclesia toleratur, aut toleratur ab ecclesia catholica, aut ab ecclesia haeretica & schismatica. Si ab ecclesia haeretica & schismata, constat quod propter eius tolerantiam non est ab expugnatione papae haeretici desistendum. Si autem toleratur ab ecclesia catholica, hoc non potest contingere, nisi quia ecclesia catholica ignorat papam esse haereticum. Si enim sciret ipsum esse haereticum, eum nullatenus toleraret. Sed propter ignorantiam ecclesiae catholicae non est ab expugnatione papae haeretici cessandum, quando probari potest esse haereticus. Illi enim, qui sciunt papam esse haereticum, si possunt probare eum esse haereticum, debent hoc ecclesiae catholicae nunciare. Quae postquam quaesierit sollicite, & repererit papam haereticum, nullatenus contra veritatem tolerabit. Qui autem perfidiam papae haeretici ecclesiae catholicae nunciarent, debent ipsum, si docendi habent officium, efficaciter reprobare. ergo quamvis ab ecclesia catholica ignorante papa haereticus toleretur, non debet praedicatores & doctores scientes eum esse haereticum ab eius impugnatione cessare: & ita quamvis papa haereticus ab ecclesia catholica, hoc est, a multitudine Christiani populi toleretur, est a scientibus eum esse haereticum viriliter expugnandus.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. In my reply to the principal argument you said that three things were implied, which seem false to some. You have dealt with the first of them; now discuss the second. MASTER. The second thing your reply seemed to imply is that a heretical pope, so long as the Church tolerates him, must in no way be opposed. Some think this is false because of a false implication. For if a heretical pope is tolerated by the Church, he is tolerated either by the Catholic Church or by a heretical and schismatic Church. If by a heretical and schismatic Church, it is clear that because of its toleration we must not desist from attacking the heretical pope. But if he is tolerated by the Catholic Church, this can happen only because the Catholic Church does not know that the pope is a heretic. For if it knew him to be a heretic, it would in no way tolerate him. But because of the ignorance of the Catholic Church, we must not cease from attacking a heretical pope when it can be proved that he is a heretic. For those who know that the pope is a heretic, if they can prove him to be one, ought to announce this to the Catholic Church. When the Church has inquired diligently and found the pope to be a heretic, it will by no means tolerate him against the truth. Those who report the perfidy of a heretical pope to the Catholic Church ought, if they hold the office of teaching, to refute him effectively. Therefore, although a heretical pope may be tolerated by the Catholic Church while it is ignorant, the preachers and teachers who know him to be a heretic ought not to cease from opposing him. And so, although a heretical pope is tolerated by the Catholic Church, that is, by the multitude of the Christian people, he must be vigorously opposed by those who know him to be a heretic.

units.la: DISCIP. Hic essent duo probanda, quorum primum est, quod ab ecclesia catholica papa haereticus scienter nullatenus toleratur. Secundum est, quod illi qui scirent papam haereticum deberet hoc ecclesiae catholicae nunciare, quando possent hoc probare. unde ista duo coneris probare. MAG. Primum probatur sic. licet ecclesia catholica quantum ad ea quae facta sunt possit errare. unde & ecclesia universalis erravit, quantum ad ea quae facta sunt, quando mulierem venerabatur papa. & sic etiam posset errare, si quis non baptizatus, qui crederetur esse baptizatus, vel aliquis occulte haereticus eligeretur in papam, & ab ecclesia universali papa haberetur, tamen quantum ad ea quae iuris sunt divini ecclesia errare non potest. Sed si ecclesia universalis papam haereticum toleraret, erraret quantum ad ea quae iuris sunt divini, quia scienter haberet pro papa eum, qui iure divino esset papatu privatus, quod non esset sine errore iuris divini: quia reputare haereticum verum papam esset contra sacram scripturam: quia ex scriptura divina colligitur evidenter, quod papa haereticus non est verus papa, ut ostensum est in lib. 6. c. 68. ergo ecclesia catholica nunquam scienter papam haereticum toleravit.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Here two things would need proving: the first, that the Catholic Church never knowingly tolerates a heretical pope; the second, that those who know the pope to be a heretic ought to announce this to the Catholic Church when they are able to prove it. Therefore try to prove these two things. MASTER. The first is proved thus. The Catholic Church can err in matters of fact. Hence also the universal Church erred in matters of fact when the Pope venerated a woman. And so it could also err if someone who was not baptized, but was thought to be baptized, or some secretly heretical person, were elected pope and were held as pope by the universal Church. Yet the Church cannot err in matters that belong to divine law. But if the universal Church tolerated a heretical pope, it would err in matters of divine law, because it would knowingly hold as pope one who by divine law had been deprived of the papacy, and that could not be without error of divine law. For to regard a heretic as the true pope is contrary to Holy Scripture, since it is clearly gathered from divine Scripture that a heretical pope is not a true pope, as has been shown in book 6, chapter 68. Therefore the Catholic Church has never knowingly tolerated a heretical pope.

units.la: DISCIP. Ista ratio non procedit: quia ecclesia catholica tolerando papam haereticum non erraret, quantum ad ea quae sunt iuris divini, nisi papam haereticum reputaret verum papam. sed ecclesia catholica posset tolerare papam haereticum, licet non reputaret ipsum verum papam: quia multa toleratur, quae minime approbantur, teste Innoc. tertio, qui, ut habetur extr. de præben. c. iam dudum, ait: Cum multa per patientiam tolerentur, quæ si deducta fuerint ad iudicium exigente iustitia nostra debeant tolerari. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod multa tolerantur quæ minime approbantur. & ita absque errore potest ecclesia catholica papam hæreticum tolerare. MAG. Respondetur, quod sicut ecclesia universalis nunquam errabit quantum ad ea quæ sunt iuris diuini, ita nunquam usque ad finem seculi ecclesia universalis iustitia & charitate carebit, iuxta illud apostoli ad Ephe. 5. Dilexit Christus nos, (i. ecclesiam suam) & tradidit semetipsum pro ea, ut illam sanctificaret mundans lavacro aquæ in verbo vitæ, ut exhiberet ipse gloriosam ecclesiam non habentem maculam neque rugam aut huiusmodi: sed ut sit sancta & immaculata. non enim esset sancta & immaculata, neque in charitate & iustitia radicata, si scienter papam hæreticum toleraret. quare nunquam ecclesia universalis papam hæreticum tolerabit, si eum punire potest. & si eum punire non poterit, saltem ipsum specialiter verbaliter reprobabit. Ad cuius evidentiam dicitur esse sciendum, quod culpa ab ecclesia tolerari non debet, si potest eam punire. Tum, quia sunt mala quæ ab ecclesia tolerari non debent, si potest ea punire. Nam secundum Greg. habetur: quædam sunt culpæ in quibus relaxari debet vindicta, ita sunt quædam culpæ quæ minime sunt tolerandæ. Nam publicæ utilitatis interest, ne crimina remaneant impunita, extr. de sententia excommunicationis, ut fama huiusmodi autem culpæ sunt illæ quæ præcipue committuntur in Deum & in bonum commune. 23. q. 4. c. sicut. & c. sicut. perfidia autem hæresis in papa hæretico in Deum committitur & in præiudicium fidei, quæ communis est omnium. & ideo perfidiam hæresis in papa hæretico nunquam ecclesia universalis tolerabit: quia tolerando scienter prauitatem hæreticam in papa efficeretur ecclesia schismatica. quia ecclesia quæ schismatico scienter adhæret, schismatica est. ecclesia autem schismatica non est ecclesia catholica & universalis. ergo ecclesia universalis & catholica nunquam scienter perfidiam papæ hæretici tolerabit. quia eo ipso, quod est hæreticus, est etiam schismaticus. ideo non tolerabit ipsum habendo pro vero papa. licet forte multitudo Christianorum papam hæreticum tolerabit, & veri catholici persecutionem ab eo gravissimam sustinebunt: sed ipsum minime tolerabunt sibi tanquam vero papæ obediendo.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. This argument does not hold. The Catholic Church, by tolerating a heretical pope, would not err in matters of divine law unless it regarded the heretic as the true pope. But the Catholic Church could tolerate a heretical pope without regarding him as the true pope, because many things are tolerated that are not in the least approved, as Innocent III testifies, who, as is found in extr. de præben. c. iam dudum, says: Since many things are tolerated through patience which, if they were brought to judgment, our justice would require to be punished. From these words it is gathered that many things are tolerated which are not at all approved, and so the Catholic Church can tolerate a heretical pope without error. MASTER. The answer is that just as the universal Church will never err in matters of divine law, so the universal Church will never lack justice and charity until the end of the world, according to the saying of the Apostle to the Ephesians, chapter 5: Christ loved us (that is, his Church) and gave himself up for her, that he might sanctify her, cleansing her by the washing of water in the word of life, that he might present to himself a glorious Church, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she should be holy and without blemish. For she would not be holy and without blemish, nor rooted in charity and justice, if she knowingly tolerated a heretical pope. Therefore the universal Church will never tolerate a heretical pope if it is able to punish him; and if it cannot punish him, at least it will specially and verbally reprove him. For the clear understanding of this, it must be noted that a fault ought not to be tolerated by the Church if it is able to punish it. Since there are evils which ought not to be tolerated by the Church if it can punish them. For according to Gregory, there are faults in which vengeance ought to be relaxed; so there are faults which are in no way to be tolerated. For it is of public interest that crimes not remain unpunished, extr. de sententia excommunicationis, ut fama; and such faults are those which are committed chiefly against God and the common good, 23. q. 4. c. sicut. & c. sicut. But the perfidy of heresy in a heretical pope is committed against God and to the prejudice of the faith, which is common to all. And therefore the universal Church will never tolerate the perfidy of heresy in a heretical pope, because by knowingly tolerating heretical depravity in the pope, it would itself become schismatic, since a Church that knowingly adheres to a schismatic is itself schismatic. But a schismatic Church is not the catholic and universal Church. Therefore the universal and catholic Church will never knowingly tolerate the perfidy of a heretical pope, because by the very fact that he is a heretic he is also a schismatic. Therefore it will not tolerate him by holding him as the true pope. Perhaps the multitude of Christians will tolerate a heretical pope, and true Catholics will suffer from him very grievous persecution; but they will by no means tolerate him by obeying him as the true pope.

units.la: DISCIP. Recitasti quomodo probatur, quod ecclesia catholica nunquam scienter papam hæreticum tolerabit. nunc volire probare secundum; scilicet quod illi qui sciunt papam esse hæreticum, debent hoc ecclesiæ catholicæ nunciare.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. You have recited how it is proved that the Catholic Church will never knowingly tolerate a heretical pope. Now I wish you to prove the second point: namely, that those who know the pope to be a heretic ought to announce this to the Catholic Church.

units.la: MAGIST. Hoc videtur posse probari sic. hoc debent catholici aliis catholicis, nescientibus revelare seu nunciare, quod celatum vergeret in divini honoris diminutionem & fidelium commune & notabile detrimentum, si celaretur. sed sic est in proposito. ergo catholici scientes cum esse hæreticum, hoc debent aliis revelare, si possunt hoc ipsum reprobare.
units.tr: MASTER. This seems capable of being proved thus. Catholics ought to reveal or announce to other Catholics, who do not know it, whatever, if it were concealed, would tend to the diminution of divine honour and to the common and notable detriment of the faithful. But it is so in the present case. Therefore Catholics who know that the pope is a heretic ought to reveal this to others, if they are able to prove it.

units.la: CAP. XLV.
units.tr: CAP. XLV.

units.la: In quo tractatur tertium inconveniens, quod sequitur ex responsione data cap. 43.
units.tr: In which the third inconvenience that follows from the answer given in chapter 43 is treated.

units.la: DISCIP. Dissere de tertio, quod innuebat responsio mea ad rationem factam supra c. 43. vbi dixisti à quibusdam putari contrariam veritatem. MAGIST. Tertium, quod innuebat tua responsio, est, quod in nullo casu absque auctoritate principis nulli licet bellum sive generale sive particulare suscipere, hoc est absque auctoritate principis nulli licet alium occidere: quod non videtur verum. nam publicum latronem cuilibet licet absque auctoritate principis occidere: cum liceat unicuique sine iudice se vindicare. li. 1. & glo. notat 23. q. 3. c. fortitudo. & q. 5. c. cum homo. & ext. de immunitate ecclesiarum. c. inter alias. Item absque auctoritate principis seu iudicis licitum est cuilibet vim vi repellere, di. 1. ca. ius naturale. sed aliquando vis repelli non potest nisi inferendo occidatur. ergo in hoc casu licet absque auctoritate principis bellum saltem particulare suscipere. Item, non minus debet populus defendere patriam contra volentes ipsos occidere & patriam devastare: quam privata persona tenetur se & res proprias defensare, sed personæ privatæ licet se & res proprias absque auctoritate principis defensare & ne occidatur occidere. ergo multo magis toti populo in absentia principis, licet se contra hostes & ne occidantur bellum suscipere generale.
units.tr: STUDENT. Speak about the third point, which my reply to the argument made above in chapter 43 seemed to imply, where you said that some people think the contrary is true. TEACHER. The third point that your reply implied is this: in no case may anyone undertake war, whether general or particular, without the authority of the prince; that is, no one may kill another without the prince's authority. This does not seem true. For anyone may lawfully kill a public robber without the prince's authority, since each person may avenge himself without a judge. li. 1. & glo. notat 23. q. 3. c. fortitudo. & q. 5. c. cum homo. & ext. de immunitate ecclesiarum. c. inter alias. Likewise, without the authority of a prince or judge, anyone may lawfully repel force with force, di. 1. ca. ius naturale. But sometimes force cannot be repelled except by inflicting death. Therefore in this case it is lawful, even without the authority of the prince, to undertake at least a particular war. Again, the people ought to defend their country against those who wish to kill them and lay waste their land no less than a private person is bound to defend himself and his own property. But a private person may lawfully defend himself and his own property without the authority of the prince, and kill to avoid being killed. Therefore, much more, when the prince is absent, the whole people may lawfully undertake a general war against enemies, so that they are not killed.

units.la: DISC. Ad quid nituntur isti istud certum reprobare? MAG. Hoc ideo probant, ut ex contraria veritate eliciant argumentum ad probandum, quod licet prædicatoribus & doctoribus sive magistris absque mandato cuiuslibet prelati publice prædicare atque docere doctrinam papæ hæretici veritati catholicæ aduersari.
units.tr: STUDENT. Toward what end do these men strive to refute this certain point? TEACHER. They prove it so that from the contrary truth they may draw an argument to show that it is lawful for preachers and teachers, or masters, to preach and teach publicly, without the mandate of any prelate, that the doctrine of a heretical pope is opposed to catholic truth.

units.la: DISC. Quomodo? MAG. Hoc modo. bellum spirituale contra hostem spiritualem intentum cum non solum personam privatam, sed etiam totam communitatem fidelium spiritualiter per hæreticam prauitatem vult extinguere, non est magis illicitum, etiam absque auctoritate principis mortalis inferioris Deo, quam sit bellum corporale contra volentem personam privatam vel aliquem populum neci tradere corporaliter. sed licet absque auctoritate principis tam bellum particulare quam generale corporale sustinere. ergo multo magis licet prædicatoribus & doctoribus seu magistris absque auctoritate principis mortalis contra papam hæreticum cupientem totam multitudinem orthodoxorum spiritualiter hæretica prauitate occidere, bellum spirituale suscipere. ergo licet eis doctrinam papæ hæretici erroneam efficaciter reprobare, & publice expugnare. DISCIP. Quomodo ad auctoritates respondetur, quæ sonare videntur, quod absque auctoritate principis nulli licet bellum suscipere. MAG. Ad omnes datur unica responsio: quia omnes intelligendæ sunt, quando auctoritas principis potest convenienter haberi. Si autem principis auctoritas convenienter haberi non potest: vel propter eius absentiam vel propter eius imperitiam, seu propter eius maliciam: licet absque eius auctoritate ex iusta & rationabili causa bellum suscipere non solum particulare sed etiam generale. DISCIP. Ista responsio innuit, quod in pluribus casibus vel propter diversas conditiones principis liceat absque eius auctoritate bellum suscipere. Unde prædicta per exempla declara. MAGIST. Istud per unum exemplum videtur omnimode posse declarari. Ponatur enim, quod aliquis rex potens vel populus aliquam civitatem invadat iniuste, satagens omnes eius extinguere & civitatem funditus dissipare. Si in hoc casu princeps civitatis est ablens, ita quod cives eius auctoritatem & consilium non possent requirere: vel princeps est alienatus a sensu: vel alias infirmus, quod eis non potest consulere: vel etiam ipsemet princeps malitiose conatur tradere civitatem; civitati licet pro se defendenda bellum suscipere, principe minime annuente, imo ipso pro viribus resistente. Unde per multa exempla posset ostendi, quod populi plures & communitates sæpius depouerunt reges iuste & suos principes; & postea sibi principes elegerunt. Ex quo paret, quod etiam populus absque auctoritate principis potuit ex iusta causa & rationabili contra principem deponendum bellum promovere.
units.tr: STUDENT. How so? TEACHER. Like this. A spiritual war against a spiritual enemy, which seeks to destroy spiritually, through heretical depravity, not only a private person but the whole community of the faithful, is no more unlawful, even without the authority of a mortal prince, who is inferior to God, than a bodily war against one who wishes to hand over a private person or some people to bodily death. But it is lawful, without the authority of the prince, to wage both a particular and a general bodily war. Therefore, much more is it lawful for preachers, teachers, or masters, without the authority of a mortal prince, to undertake a spiritual war against a heretical pope who desires to kill the whole multitude of the orthodox spiritually by heretical depravity. Therefore it is lawful for them to effectively refute the erroneous doctrine of the heretical pope and to attack it publicly. STUDENT. How are the authorities that seem to say that no one may undertake war without the authority of the prince answered? TEACHER. All of them receive one answer: they are to be understood as applying whenever the authority of the prince can conveniently be had. But if the prince's authority cannot conveniently be had, whether because of his absence, his incompetence, or his malice, then it is lawful, for a just and reasonable cause, to undertake war without his authority, not only a particular war but also a general one. STUDENT. This answer implies that in many cases, because of the various conditions of the prince, it is lawful to undertake war without his authority. Therefore, explain these points by examples. TEACHER. This seems capable of being fully explained by one example. Suppose some powerful king or people unjustly invades a city, intending to destroy all its inhabitants and utterly lay waste the city. In this case, if the prince of the city is absent, so that the citizens cannot ask for his authority and counsel; or the prince is out of his mind, or otherwise too ill to advise them; or the prince himself maliciously tries to surrender the city, then the citizens may lawfully undertake war in defence of themselves, even though the prince does not consent and indeed resists them with all his strength. Many examples could show that peoples and communities have often justly deposed kings and their princes, and afterwards chosen princes for themselves. From this it is clear that even the people, without the authority of the prince, could, for a just cause and a reasonable reason, promote war to depose the prince.

units.la: CAP. XLVI.
units.tr: Chapter 46.

units.la: In quo probatur pluribus rationibus, quod prælatis, doctoribus & magistris licet bellum spirituale contra papam hæreticum movere, etiam sine licentia cuiuscunque superioris mortalis. & incipit in secunda ratione, quia prima posita est cap. 43.
units.tr: In which it is proved by several arguments that prelates, teachers and masters may lawfully wage a spiritual war against a heretical pope, even without the permission of any mortal superior. It begins with the second argument, since the first was set out in chapter 43.

units.la: DISCIP. Mihi videtur ostensum aperte, quod in pluribus casibus licet populo absque auctoritate principis bellum generale movere. ex quo concludi potest, ut apparet, quod licet prædicatoribus & doctoribus contra papam hæreticum absque auctoritate prælati cuiuscunque mortalis bellum spirituale suscipere eius doctrinam erroneam improbando. nihilominus tamen peto, ut ad eandem conclusionem aliquas alias rationes adducas. MAGIST. Quod non solum sit licitum, sed etiam prædicatores & doctores teneantur doctrinam papæ erroneam reprobare, non requisita auctoritate prælati mortalis, videtur posse probari. Secundo principaliter sic. Qui officium susceptum vel commissum negligit exercere, est merito arguendus. talis enim servus nequam, qui abscondit talentum sibi commissum, non immerito comparatur. facit enim contra præceptum apostoli scribentis. 2. ad Timoth. 4. ministerium tuum imple. sed ad officium prædicatorum & doctorum spectat veritatem catholicam affirmare; & pravitatem hæreticam confutare. quæ duo sunt opera sapientum, scilicet non mentiri; & de his quæ novit mentientem manifestare posse. ergo ad prædicatores & doctores spectat perfidiam papæ hæretici confutare.
units.tr: DISCIP. It seems to me clearly shown that in many cases the people may lawfully wage a general war without the authority of a prince. From this it can be concluded, as is evident, that preachers and teachers may lawfully take up a spiritual war against a heretical pope without the authority of any mortal prelate, by refuting his erroneous doctrine. Nevertheless I ask you to adduce some other arguments for the same conclusion. MAGIST. That this is not only lawful but that preachers and teachers are even bound to condemn the erroneous doctrine of the pope, without requiring the authority of a mortal prelate, seems capable of proof. Secondly, the main argument runs thus. One who neglects to exercise an office entrusted or committed to him deserves to be called to account. Such a wicked servant, who hides the talent committed to him, is not unfairly compared to him. For he acts against the command of the Apostle who writes: "Fulfil thy ministry" (2 Tim. 4). But it belongs to the office of preachers and teachers to affirm Catholic truth and to refute heretical depravity: these are the two works of the wise, namely not to lie, and to be able to make known to the liar what he knows. Therefore it belongs to preachers and teachers to refute the perfidy of the heretical pope.

units.la: DISCIP. Licet ad prædicatores & doctores pertineat pravitatem hæreticam confutare: non tamen spectat ad ipsos omnem hæresim confutare; quia nullus posset hoc facere. ergo per hanc rationem probari non potest quod ad eos spectat perfidiam papæ hæretici reprobare. MAGIST. Hæc responsio non sufficit, ut videtur multis. quia secundum beatum Greg. secundum qualitatem auditorem debet formari sermo doctorum. & videtur accepisse à beato Petro, qui, ut legitur 8. quæst. 1. c. oportet, ait; Oportet eum qui docet & instruit animas rudes esse talem ut pro ingenio dicendum semetipsum possit aptare, & verbi ordinem pro capacitate audientis dirigere. Sicenim oportet diligentem doctorem & prædicatorem secundum varietatem temporum doctrinam suam audientibus ministrare; aut quando ab hæreticis de aliquibus erroribus specialiter inuaduntur per doctrinam prædicatorum & doctorum contra eosdem errores specialiter muniantur. Si ergo papa hæreticus suæ perfidiæ plures fragit illaqueare, & viri infideles laborant transcendere; oportet prædicatores & doctores suæ perfidiæ specialiter obviare, & veritatem contrariam auditores salubriter informare.
units.tr: DISCIP. Although it belongs to preachers and teachers to refute heretical depravity, it does not belong to them to refute every heresy, since no one could do this. Therefore this argument cannot prove that it is their business to condemn the perfidy of the heretical pope. MAGIST. This answer does not seem sufficient to many. For according to the blessed Gregory, the teacher's speech ought to be shaped according to the quality of his hearers. And it seems to have been taken from the blessed Peter, who, as we read in Decretum 8, q. 1, c. "Oportet," says: "He who teaches and instructs rude souls must be such that he can adapt himself to their understanding and direct the order of his words to the capacity of the hearer." For so the diligent teacher and preacher must minister his doctrine to his hearers according to the variety of times; or, when they are attacked by heretics on some particular errors, they must be specially fortified against those same errors by the teaching of preachers and teachers. If therefore the heretical pope labours to ensnare many by his perfidy, and unbelieving men toil to surpass them, preachers and teachers must especially withstand his perfidy and wholesomely inform their hearers of the contrary truth.

units.la: DISC. Puto quod hanc rationem intelligam; ideo alias non differas allegare. MAGIST. Tertio principaliter videtur sic posse probari; cui ex officio incumbit peccanti resistere, si non resistit, peccanti consentit; & consimili modo cum eo iudicandus est culpabilis. hæc est enim ratio, quare sæpe taciturnitas & dissimulatio imputantur prælatis, quæ tamen subditis minime imputantur. quia ad prælatos & potestatem habentes spectat sæpe peccantibus obviare; quod tamen ad subditos minime spectat. Sed prædicatoribus & doctoribus ex officio suscepto incumbit perfidiæ papæ hæretici fidem corrumpere satagentis resistere. Ideo enim, ut dictum est, officium prædicatorum & doctorum debent suscipere, ut doceant catholicam veritatem, & confutent hæreticam prauitatem. ergo si non resistunt papæ hæretico, cum possunt, eius perfidiam reprobando, eidem consentiunt; & simili modo cum eo sunt culpabiles reputandi. Unde virtute illius medii omnes auctoritates, supra cap. 38. introductæ & aliæ quæ insinuare videntur, quod qui non resistit peccanti, cum potest, eidem consentire videtur, ad prædictam conclusionem possunt adduci.
units.tr: DISC. I think I understand this argument, so do not put off citing the others. MAGIST. Thirdly, the main argument seems capable of proof in this way: whoever is bound by his office to resist one who sins, if he does not resist, consents to the sinner, and in the same way is to be judged guilty along with him. For this is the reason why silence and dissimulation are often imputed to prelates, though they are by no means imputed to subjects: it belongs to prelates and those with power often to withstand sinners, which by no means belongs to subjects. But it is incumbent on preachers and teachers, by the office they have undertaken, to resist the heretical pope who strives to corrupt the faith. For, as has been said, they ought to undertake the office of preachers and teachers in order to teach Catholic truth and to refute heretical depravity. Therefore if they do not resist the heretical pope, when they can, by refuting his perfidy, they consent to him, and are to be reckoned guilty in the same way as he. Hence, by virtue of this middle term, all the authorities introduced above in chapter 38, and others that seem to suggest that one who does not resist a sinner when he can seems to consent to him, can be brought forward for the aforesaid conclusion.

units.la: Quarto principaliter sic arguitur; Omnis perfidia inimicorum fidei odio est habenda, teste psalpsalmista, qui dicit: Iniquos odio habui, & alibi ait: omnem viam iniquam odio habui. & rursus ait: nonne qui oderunt te Domine oderam, & super inimicos tuos tabescebam. perfecto odio oderam illos, inimici facti sunt mihi. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod omnis nequitia & malitia odio est habenda. & quod inimici Dei odio sunt habendi. quod etiam ipse Saluator testatur Luc. 14. Si quis venit ad me, & non odit patrem & uxorem & filios & fratres, non potest meus esse discipulus. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod hoc est in omni homine odiendum, quod est Deo contrarium. perfidia autem papae haeretici est Deo contraria. ergo odio est habenda. sed praedicatores & doctores odio non habent perfidiam papae haeretici, nisi ipsum debitis circumstantiis observatis detestentur, persequantur & improbare nituntur. ergo praedicatores ipsam oportet perfidiam papae haeretici reprobare. Maior videtur evidens. Minor aperte probatur. quia secundum beatum Gregorium: Probatio dilectionis exhibitio est operis, ita etiam probatio odii exhibitio est operis. & secundum eundem Greg. amor non est otiosus: sed multa operatur, si est. amor enim & odium sunt causae distinctae, distinctos effectus habentes. & ideo sicut ex amore, si est, multi sequuntur effectus: ita etiam ex odio plures effectus emanant. quare ex odio si est vere respectu perfidiae papae haeretici in praedicatoribus & doctoribus, opera exteriora sequuntur. Persecutio autem est effectus odii, & similiter reprobatio & detestatio exterior. quare si praedicatores & doctores vere odiunt perfidiam & malitiam papae haeretici, ipsam efficaciter persequuntur. quod August. ut habetur. 23. quaest. 4. c. duo ista, insinuare videtur dicens: duo ista nomina cum dicimus, homo peccator, non utique frustra dicuntur. quia peccator est corripe: & quia homo, miserere nec omnino liberabis hominem, nisi cum persecutus fueris peccatorem huic officio nominis inu gilet disciplina. & infra: ita nulli homini claudenda est misericordia, sicut nulli peccatori impunitas relaxanda. Ex quibus colligitur, quod quilibet ex necessitate tenetur quantum sibi licet pro gradu suo & officio corripere, & persequi peccatorem. ergo praedicatores debent omnium haereticorum doctrinam reprobare, imo omnem peccatorem persequi tenetur. ergo praedicatores & doctores oportet persequi congruenti modo sibi, scilicet reprobando perfidiam papae haeretici. DISCIP. Ex hac ratione haberetur, quod praedicatores & doctores deberent omnium haereticorum doctrinam erroneam reprobare, immo omnem peccatorem persequi tenerentur. quod eis impossibile esse dignoscitur. nullus autem ad impossibile obligatur. MAGIST. Ad hoc respondetur, quod sicut debemus diligere omnes proximos: & ideo papam tam haereticum quam catholicum tenemur diligere: non tamen omnibus possumus actu speciali beneficia exhibere: sed debemus esse parati repore necessitatis pro posse omni indigenti succurrere: ita omnes iniquos inquantum iniqui sunt odire tenemur, & secundum praeparationem cordis omnes persequi astricti sumus. illum tamen, qui deterior est & magis perniciosus populo Christiano, fortius, quia honorem Dei conatur minuere, omnes catholici fortius & melius persequi astringuntur. & ideo cum papa haereticus sit deterior & magis perniciosus populo Christiano, quam alii minus mali, illum singulariter persequi debent catholici universi. & ideo praedicatores & doctores singulariter contra papam haereticum debent suum officium exercere ipsum efficacissime & doctrinam suam erroneam reprobando. DISC. Si rationes alias cogitasti, allega. MAG. Quinto specialiter arguitur sic. Sicut oculi corporis mali, qui sibi & aliis partib. corporis minime vidét illa, quae sunt eis periculosiora & nociviora; puta foveas, laqueos, hostes, bestias, & alia quae possunt inferre corpori laesionem, inutiles reputantur: sic oculi corporis spiritualis, puta ecclesiae, qui sibi & ecclesiae nequaquam monstrat pericula etiam imminentia ecclesiae universae, inutiles sunt censendi. oculi autem ecclesiae sunt praedicatores & doctores, qui bona & mala, virtutes & vitia, peccata & utilia debent aliis & sibi videre & monstrare. maximum autem periculum imminet ecclesiae Dei, quando papa est haereticus. ergo si praedicatores & doctores vident, nec monstrant ecclesiae periculum, ex perfidia papae haeretici ecclesiae imminet orthodoxae, inutiles sunt censendi. Sexto sic. sicut ad testem pertinet in iudicio perhibere testimonium veritatis: sic ad praedicatores & doctores in suis sermonibus & locutionibus asserere veritatem ac veritati testimonium perhibere. imo praedicatores possent verisimiliter merito appellari testes veritatis. Unde quia a primo praedicaturi & docturi veritatem fuerunt testes veritatis poterant merito appellari, iuxta illud Redemptoris Act. 1. Eritis mihi testes, Hierusalem & in omni Iudaea &c. & ut legitur eodem capitulo, beatus Petrus dicit: oportet ergo ex hiis viris, qui nobiscum sunt congregati in omni tempore quo introivit & exiit inter nos Dominus noster Iesus incipiens a baptismate Iohannis usque ad diem qua assumptus est a nobis, testem resurrectionis eius nobiscum fieri unum ex istis. praedicatores ergo & doctores veritatis sunt testes veritatis. sed testes cum in iudicio examinantur, tenentur testimonium perhibere veritati. ergo praedicatores & doctores in sermonibus & lectionibus suis contra papam haereticum, testimonium veritatis perhibere tenentur. DISCIP. Ista ratio probare videtur, quod tunc solummodo praedicatores & doctores in suis sermonibus & lectionibus debeant contra papam haereticum afferre veritatem; quando ad hoc in suis sermonibus compelluntur. quemadmodum testes tunc solum perhibere testimonium veritati tenentur, quando ad hoc per suos superiores arcantur. MAGIST. Ista responsio vel obiectio nulla est, ut quibusdam apparet: nam non solum modo testes debent perhibere veritati testimonium, quando ad hoc a suo superiore compelluntur; imo saepe ad hoc ex conscientia sine omni coactione per superiorem astringuntur; quia sicut caritatis affectio, quam quilibet ad alium habere tenetur, suggerit unicuique, ut quod uni prodest, & alteri non nocet, illud nequaquam prohibeat; sic eadem caritatis affectio tio monet vnusquemque, vt quod alteri prodest, & sibi si faciat minime nocet, alteri faciat, iuxta regulam Saluatoris, qua vnusquisque iubetur alteri facere quod sibi vult fieri, quod nulli nocet nec corporaliter nec spiritualiter. sed saepe facere testimonium veritati etiam coram non superiore suo sibi non nocet & alteri multum prodest: quia liberat eum a damno vel periculo absque detrimento sui. ergo tunc quamuis testis non fuerit a superiori compulsus, tenetur perhibere testimonium veritati. ergo consimiliter praedicatores & doctores, quando possunt liberare auditores suos, ne incidant in perfidiam Papae haeretici, de necessitate salutis tenentur auditoribus suis veritatem contra Papam haereticum indicare. DISCIP. Tenet ne aliqui modernorum doctorum mutuo se reprobantium, quod testis aliquando non compulsus a superiore tenetur perhibere testimonium veritati. MAGIST. Thomas de Aquino videtur affirmare, secunda secundae, q. 70. articulo. 1. Sic ergo requiratur eius testimonium non auctoritate superioris, tunc distinguendum est: quia aliquando requiritur testimonium alicuius auctoritate superiorum, aliquando vero non requiritur testimonium subditi superiorum auctoritate. cum in hu, qua ad iustitiam pertinent, obedire tenentur, non est dubium quin teneatur testimonium ferre in his in quibus secundum ordinem iuris testimonium ab eo exigitur, puta in manifestis, in hiis in quibus infamia praecesserit. Si autem exigatur ab eo testimonium in aliis, puta in occultis, in quibus infamia non praecessit, non tenetur ad testificandum. Si vero requiratur eius testimonium non auctoritate superiorum, quibus subest, tunc distinguendum est: quia si testimonium requiratur ad liberandum hominem vel ab iniusta morte seu poena quacunque vel a falsa infamia vel etiam ab iniquo damno, tunc tenetur homo ad testificandum. & si eius testimonium non requiratur, tenetur facere quod in se est, vt veritatem annuncient alicui, qui ad hoc possit prodesse. dicitur enim in psalmista: Eripite pauperem, & egenum de manu peccatoris liberate. & Proverb. 24. erue eos qui ducuntur ad mortem. Et ad Rom. 7. dicitur: Digni sunt morte non solum qui faciunt, sed qui consentiunt facientibus. vbi Glo. dicit, quod consentire est tacere, cum possit redarguere. Ex quibus verbis patet, quod testis tenetur testimonium perhibere veritati quandoque, quamuis per superiorem minime compellatur. & per auctoritates quas ipse adducit ostenditur quod praedicatores & doctores in suis sermonibus & lectionibus tenentur si possint auditores suos (ne incidant in perfidiam Papae haeretici) praeservare; quia ad eundem spectat aliquem ab ingruenti siue imminenti periculo liberare, ad quem spectat alium a periculo in quod incidit si potest eripere.
units.tr: Fourthly, the argument runs thus. All the perfidy of the enemies of the faith is to be held in hatred, as the psalmist testifies, who says: I have hated the wicked, and elsewhere he says: I have hated every wicked way. And again he says: Do I not hate those who hate you, O Lord, and do I not pine away because of your enemies? I hate them with perfect hatred; they have become my enemies. From these words it is gathered that all wickedness and malice is to be held in hatred, and that the enemies of God are to be hated. The Saviour himself also testifies to this in Luke 14: If anyone comes to me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers, he cannot be my disciple. From these words it is gathered that in every man whatever is contrary to God is to be hated. But the perfidy of the heretical pope is contrary to God. Therefore it is to be held in hatred. But preachers and teachers do not hate the perfidy of the heretical pope unless, observing due circumstances, they detest it, pursue it and strive to reprove it. Therefore preachers must reprove the perfidy of the heretical pope. The major premise seems evident. The minor is plainly proved, because, according to the blessed Gregory, the proof of love is the showing of works, so too the proof of hatred is the showing of works. And according to the same Gregory, love is not idle, but if it is present it works much. For love and hatred are distinct causes, having distinct effects; and so, just as many effects follow from love when it is present, so also many effects flow from hatred. Hence, if in preachers and teachers there is real hatred toward the perfidy of the heretical pope, outward works follow. But persecution is an effect of hatred, and likewise outward reproof and detestation. Therefore if preachers and teachers truly hate the perfidy and malice of the heretical pope, they will pursue it effectively. Augustine seems to hint at this, as it is cited in 23 q. 4, c. Duo ista, where he says: When we say these two names, man and sinner, they are not used in vain. Because he is a sinner, rebuke him; and because he is a man, have mercy; and you will by no means free the man unless you have pursued the sinner, a discipline attending the office of this name. And below: just as mercy must be closed to no man, so impunity must be granted to no sinner. From these things it is gathered that everyone is under necessity, as far as he is permitted, according to his rank and office, to rebuke and pursue the sinner. Therefore preachers ought to reprove the doctrine of all heretics; indeed every sinner they are bound to pursue. Therefore preachers and teachers must pursue, in a manner suited to them, namely by reproving the perfidy of the heretical pope. STUDENT. From this argument it would follow that preachers and teachers should reprove the erroneous doctrine of all heretics, and indeed be bound to pursue every sinner. It is known that this is impossible for them, and no one is bound to the impossible. TEACHER. To this it is answered that just as we ought to love all our neighbours, and therefore are bound to love the pope, heretical as well as orthodox, yet we cannot actually confer special benefits on all; but we ought to be ready, in cases of need, to help every person in want as far as we are able; so we are bound to hate all the wicked insofar as they are wicked, and according to the disposition of the heart we are obliged to pursue all of them. Yet all Catholics are bound to pursue more strongly and more fully the one who is worse and more harmful to the Christian people, because he tries to diminish the honour of God. And so, since the heretical pope is worse and more harmful to the Christian people than other, less evil men, all Catholics together ought to pursue him in particular. And therefore preachers and teachers ought to exercise their office especially against the heretical pope, opposing him most effectively and reproving his erroneous doctrine. STUDENT. If you have thought of other arguments, state them. TEACHER. Fifthly, the argument is made in a special way thus. Just as the eyes of a body which are unhealthy, and which do not see for themselves or for the other parts of the body those things which are more dangerous and harmful to them, such as pits, snares, enemies, beasts and other things which can inflict injury on the body, are reckoned useless; so the eyes of the spiritual body, namely of the Church, which do not show to themselves and to the Church the dangers that threaten the whole Church, are to be judged useless. But the eyes of the Church are the preachers and teachers, who ought to see and show to others and to themselves what is good and what is evil, virtues and vices, sins and things useful. Now the greatest danger threatens the Church of God when the pope is heretical. Therefore, if preachers and teachers see the danger that threatens the orthodox Church from the perfidy of the heretical pope, and do not point it out, they are to be judged useless. Sixthly, thus. Just as it belongs to a witness in a court to bear witness to the truth, so it belongs to preachers and teachers in their sermons and lectures to assert the truth and bear witness to the truth. Indeed preachers could fairly and probably be called witnesses of the truth. Hence, since those who were first to preach and teach the truth were witnesses of the truth, they could rightly be called so, according to that saying of the Redeemer in Acts 1: You shall be witnesses to me, in Jerusalem and in all Judaea, etc. And as is read in the same chapter, the blessed Peter says: Therefore it is necessary that of these men who have been with us all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us, beginning from the baptism of John until the day on which he was taken up from us, one of them become a witness with us of his resurrection. Preachers and teachers of the truth, therefore, are witnesses of the truth. But witnesses, when they are examined in court, are bound to bear testimony to the truth. Therefore preachers and teachers are bound to bear witness to the truth in their sermons and lectures against the heretical pope. STUDENT. This argument seems to prove that preachers and teachers ought to set forth the truth in their sermons and lectures against the heretical pope only when they are compelled to do so in their sermons, just as witnesses are bound to bear testimony to the truth only when their superiors summon them to do so. TEACHER. This answer or objection is worthless, as it seems to some: for witnesses are not bound to bear testimony to the truth only when their superior compels them to do so; indeed, often they are bound to do so from conscience, without any compulsion from a superior. For just as the affection of charity, which everyone is bound to have toward another, suggests to each person that he should not forbid to another what benefits one and harms no other; so the same affection of charity admonishes each person that what benefits another, and does him in no way harm if he does it himself, he should do to another, according to the rule of the Saviour, by which each one is commanded to do to another what he wishes to be done to himself, which harms no one, neither in body nor in spirit. But often to bear testimony to the truth, even before one who is not one's superior, does no harm to oneself and greatly benefits another, because it frees him from loss or danger without any injury to oneself. Therefore, although the witness has not been compelled by his superior, he is bound to bear testimony to the truth. Likewise, then, preachers and teachers, when they can free their hearers from falling into the perfidy of the heretical pope, are bound, from necessity of salvation, to point out the truth to their hearers against the heretical pope. STUDENT. Some of the modern teachers, who refute one another, hold that a witness is sometimes bound to bear testimony to the truth even when he is not compelled by a superior. TEACHER. Thomas Aquinas seems to affirm this in Secunda Secundae, q. 70, art. 1. There he says: Thus, if his testimony is required not by the authority of a superior, a distinction must be made: for sometimes testimony is required by the authority of superiors, and sometimes testimony of a subject is not required by the authority of superiors. Since in those matters which pertain to justice they are bound to obey, there is no doubt that he is bound to give testimony in those matters in which, according to the order of law, testimony is demanded of him, for example in manifest matters, in those in which infamy has preceded. But if testimony is demanded of him in other matters, for example in hidden matters in which infamy has not preceded, he is not bound to testify. But if his testimony is required not by the authority of the superiors to whom he is subject, then a distinction must again be made: for if the testimony is required to free a man from unjust death or any punishment whatever, or from false infamy, or even from an unjust loss, then the man is bound to testify. And if his testimony is not required, he is bound to do what lies in him, so that he may announce the truth to someone who could profit from it. For it is said in the Psalmist: Rescue the poor and the needy, deliver them from the hand of the sinner. And in Proverbs 24: Deliver those who are being led to death. And in Romans 7 it is said: Those who do such things are worthy of death, and not only they, but also those who consent to those who do them. Where the Gloss says that to consent is to be silent when one could rebuke. From these words it is clear that a witness is sometimes bound to bear testimony to the truth, although he is in no way compelled by a superior. And from the authorities which he himself adduces it is shown that preachers and teachers, in their sermons and lectures, are bound, if they can, to preserve their hearers (lest they fall into the perfidy of the heretical pope); because it belongs to the same person to free someone from an impending or imminent danger, as it belongs to free another from a danger into which he has fallen, if he can rescue him.

units.la: DISC. Adhuc alias rationes ad conclusionem principalem allega. MAG. Septimo probatur eadem conclusio sic. Sicut aduocati patrocinium causae iuste pstare tenentur, ita praedicatores & doctores tenentur veritate catholicam docere & prauitate haereticam reprobare. Sed aduocatus catholicorum contra Papam haereticum patrocinium praestare tenetur: quia aduocatus patrocinium pretare tenetur causae pauperum. hoc enim opus est misericordiae, ad quod pro loco & tempore & aliis circumstantiis debitis obligatur. ergo multo magis debet aduocatus catholicorum contra Papam haereticum patrocinium & defensionem impendere, eo quod causa fidei est causae cuiuscunque pauperis praeferenda. ergo consimiliter praedicatores & doctores in suis sermonibus & lectionibus debent praestando patrocinium causae fidei Papam haereticum eiusque doctrinam erroneam confutare.
units.tr: DISC. Put forward some further arguments for the main conclusion. MAG. The same conclusion is proved seventhly as follows. Just as advocates are bound to give their support justly to a cause, so preachers and teachers are bound to teach Catholic truth and to refute heretical error. But the advocate of the Catholics is bound to give support against a heretical Pope, because an advocate is bound to give support to the cause of the poor. For this is a work of mercy, to which a person is obliged according to place, time and other due circumstances. Therefore the advocate of the Catholics ought much more to offer support and defence against a heretical Pope, since the cause of faith is to be preferred to the cause of any poor man. Likewise, then, preachers and teachers ought, in their sermons and lectures, to defend the cause of faith by refuting the heretical Pope and his erroneous doctrine.

units.la: DISC IP. Non videtur quod aduocatus semper teneatur, causis pauperum patrocinium impartiri. quia tunc oporteret ipsum omnia alia negotia & aliorum dimittere: & eadem ratione non semper tenentur praedicatores & doctores perfidiam Papae haereticam reprobare. MAG. Non attenduntur isti, quod semper aduocatus causis pauperum patrocinium teneatur impendere, nec quod semper omnes praedicatores & doctores haereticum Papam debeant in suis lectionibus & praedicationibus reprobare: sed intendunt, sicut aduocatus, quando non apparet, quod per alium modum quam per suum iuuamen potest causa pauperis subleuari, tunc de necessitate salutis tenetur patrocinium exhibere; ita praedicatores & doctores oportet viliter Papae haeretico obuiare, quando non apparent alii prompti, qui causam fidei velint & valeant contra Papam haereticum defendere.
units.tr: DISC. It does not seem that an advocate is always bound to give his support to the causes of the poor, for then he would have to abandon all his other business and that of others. And by the same reasoning, preachers and teachers are not always bound to refute the heretical perfidy of the Pope. MAG. These objectors do not consider that an advocate is not always bound to give support to the causes of the poor, nor that all preachers and teachers must always refute the heretical Pope in their lectures and sermons. Rather, they mean this: just as an advocate, when it does not appear that the cause of a poor man can be relieved by any means other than his own assistance, is then bound by necessity of salvation to give his support, so preachers and teachers must sternly oppose the heretical Pope when no others appear ready and able to defend the cause of faith against the heretical Pope.

units.la: DIS. Adhuc rationes alias, si occurrunt, allega. MAGIST. Octaua ratio est haec. Sicut ad accusatorem spectat crimen perniciosum reipublicae, quod potest probare iudici accusare; ita ad praedicatores & doctores spectat errores pernitiosos contra fidem catholicam insurgentes reprobare. sed sciens Papam esse haereticum & conantem a fide auertere orthodoxos; ipsum, si potest probare, accusare tenetur. ergo praedicatores & doctores scientes Papam haereticum laborare fidem corrumpere orthodoxam, doctrinam suam erroneam probare tenentur. Maior videtur aperta. Minor probatur auctoritate Gregorii, qui vt legitur 2. q. 7. c. sicut, ait: Sicut laudabilis discretumque est reuerentiam & honorem exhibere praedicatoribus: ita rectitudinis & Dei timoris est si qua in eis sunt quae indigent correctione nulla dissimulatione postponere, ne totum quod absit corpus morbus inuadat, si languor non fuerit curatus in capite. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod ad rectitudinem Deique timorem spectat accusare quemcunque praelatum, qui totum corpus conatur inficere. cum ergo Papa totum corpus ecclesiae haeretica prauitate molitur inficere, Papa haereticus est a scientibus & reprobare valentibus accusandus.
units.tr: DIS. Put forward other arguments too, if they occur to you. MAGIST. The eighth argument is this. Just as it is the business of an accuser to bring against a judge a crime that is harmful to the commonwealth, which he can prove, so it is the business of preachers and teachers to refute pernicious errors that rise up against the Catholic faith. But whoever knows that the Pope is a heretic and is trying to turn the orthodox away from the faith is bound to accuse him, if he can prove it. Therefore preachers and teachers who know that the Pope, a heretic, is labouring to corrupt the orthodox faith are bound to prove their doctrine erroneous. The major premise is plainly evident. The minor is proved by the authority of Gregory, who, as is read in 2 q. 7, c. sicut, says: "Just as it is praiseworthy and discreet to show reverence and honour to preachers, so it is a mark of uprightness and the fear of God not to pass over with any dissimulation whatever in them needs correction, lest, which God forbid, disease attack the whole body if the sickness is not cured in the head." From these words it is gathered that it belongs to uprightness and the fear of God to accuse any prelate whatever who tries to infect the whole body. Since, therefore, the Pope labours to infect the whole body of the Church with heretical depravity, the heretical Pope is to be accused by those who know and are able to refute him.

units.la: CAP. XXXXVII
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXXVII

units.la: In quo ostenditur, quod si pauci aut solus unus doctor theologus remaneat non consentiens doctrinæ Papæ hæretici, debet ei resistere toto posse, neque de victoria desperare.
units.tr: In which it is shown that if few, or only one, theologian and teacher remains who does not agree with the doctrine of the heretical Pope, he ought to resist with all his power and not despair of victory.

units.la: DISCIP. Pro assertione prædicta ad præsens nolo plures rationes audire: quia satis videtur probabile, quod prædicatores & doctores, si simul concordant, debeant unanimiter doctrinam Papæ erroneam reprobare. Sed nunquid si multitudo prædicatorum & doctorum seu magistrorum consenserit Papæ hæretico favere vel non resisterit, audebunt pauci doctrinæ erroneæ obviare? MAG. Sunt quidam dicentes, quod si pauci prædicatores & doctores in doctrina permanserint orthodoxa, & tota alia multitudo Papæ hæretico consensum & favorem præbuerit, illi pauci debent illi resistere modis congruis toto posse: imo si unus solus remaneret fixus in fide, deberet intrepide doctrinam erroneam Papæ hæretici improbare, exemplo Heliæ prophetæ, qui quamvis putaret se solum prophetam fidelem Dei fuisse relictum, a fide vera minime deviavit: sed hæreticos & apostatas, quando fuit opportunitas, constantissime confutavit. Et per consequens multo magis si aliquis prælatus cum paucis prædicatoribus & doctoribus sibi subiectis Papæ hæretico nullatenus consentiret, tota alia multitudine cum suis erroribus adhærente, illi prædicatores & doctores pauci unacum prælato suo debent doctrinæ Papæ erroneæ contraire, deberetque prælatus dicere cum Mattathia illud: 1. Machab. 2. Et si omnes regi Antiocho (hoc est Papæ hæretico) obediunt, ut discedant unusquisque a servitute legis patrum suorum, & consentiant mandatis eius, ego & filii mei & fratres mei obediemus legi patrum nostrorum. Propitius sit nobis Deus; non est nobis utile relinquere legem & iustitias Dei; non audiemus verba regis Antiochi (id est Papæ hæretici) nec sacrificabimus transgredientes legis nostræ mandata, & ut eamus altera via.
units.tr: DISCIPLE: For the assertion above, I do not for the present wish to hear many arguments, since it seems quite probable that preachers and teachers, if they agree together, ought unanimously to reject the Pope's erroneous doctrine. But what if a multitude of preachers, teachers and masters should consent to the heretical Pope or fail to resist him? Will the few dare to oppose the erroneous doctrine? TEACHER: Some say that if a few preachers and teachers have remained in orthodox doctrine, while all the rest of the multitude have given consent and favour to the heretical Pope, those few ought to resist him by fitting means with all their power. Indeed, even if only one remained fixed in the faith, he ought fearlessly to condemn the erroneous doctrine of the heretical Pope, after the example of the prophet Elijah, who, although he thought he alone of God's faithful prophets had been left, did not turn at all from the true faith, but most steadfastly refuted heretics and apostates whenever the opportunity arose. And consequently, much more so, if some prelate with a few preachers and teachers subject to him should in no way consent to the heretical Pope, while all the rest of the multitude clung to him with their errors, those few preachers and teachers, together with their prelate, ought to oppose the Pope's erroneous doctrine, and the prelate should say with Mattathias those words: 1 Macc. 2. And even if all obey King Antiochus (that is, the heretical Pope), so that each one departs from the service of the law of his fathers and consents to his commands, yet I and my sons and my brothers will obey the law of our fathers. God be merciful to us; it is not useful for us to leave the law and the righteousness of God. We will not listen to the words of King Antiochus (that is, of the heretical Pope), nor will we sacrifice, transgressing the commands of our law, and go another way.

units.la: DISCIP. Videtur quod si pauci resisterent toti residuo multitudinum Christianorum laborarent in vanum. Ergo hoc attemptare & prædicare nullo modo deberent.
units.tr: DISCIPLE: It seems that if a few resisted the whole remaining multitude of Christians, they would labour in vain. Therefore they ought in no way to attempt or preach this.

units.la: . MAGIST. Respondetur, quod pauci non deberent de victoria desperare: imo unus solus de victoria sperare deberet: quia ut habetur 1. Macha. 3. Non est differentia in conspectu Dei cæli liberare in multis & in paucis: quoniam non in multitudine exercitus victoria belli, sed de cœlo est fortitudo. 1. Reg. 14. sic habetur: Non est domino difficile salvare vel in multis vel in paucis. 2. Paral. 19. sic habetur: Domine non est apud te distantia, utrum in paucis auxilieris aut in multis.
