Ex quibus verbis patet, quod si pauci contra Papam hæreticum susciperent bellum (tota alia multitudine sibi adhærente) de victoria desperare non debent: quia bellum tale non est bellum eorum, sed bellum domini, qui est veritas, quæ super omnes vincit in veritate. Ergo habentes fiduciam pro eadem certent usque ad mortem, & Deus expugnabit pro eis inimicos eorum.
units.tr: TEACHER: It is answered that the few ought not to despair of victory; indeed, even one alone ought to hope for victory, because, as is found in 1 Macc. 3: There is no difference in the sight of God in heaven between delivering with many and delivering with few; for victory in battle does not lie in the multitude of an army, but strength is from heaven. 1 Kings 14 says: Nothing is difficult for the Lord, to save either with many or with few. 2 Paral. 19 says: Lord, with you there is no distinction whether you help with few or with many. From these words it is clear that if a few should take up war against the heretical Pope, with the whole other multitude adhering to him, they ought not to despair of victory, because such a war is not their war but the Lord's, who is truth, and who conquers all in truth. Therefore those who have confidence in it should contend unto death, and God will overthrow their enemies for them.

units.la: CAP. XXXXVIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER 48.

units.la: In quo docetur, quomodo se debeant habere in casu prædicto doctores & prædicatores, ne fiant fautores hæretica pravitatis.
units.tr: In which it is taught how teachers and preachers ought to conduct themselves in the aforesaid case, so that they do not become supporters of heretical depravity.

units.la: DISCIP. Auctoritates scriptæ mihi clare demonstrant, quod unus catholicus potest secure bellum contra Papam hæreticum cum tota sua cohorte suscipere: nec deberet de victoria aliqualiter desperare. Dubito autem, ut si unquam aliquis Papa futurus est hæreticus, pro multitudine Christianorum poterit dicere illud Salvatoris: Putas ne filius hominis veniens inveniet fidem super terram: quia reor quod paucissimi sibi resistent. Puto enim quod tunc adimplebitur prophetia beati Pauli dicentis 2. ad Timoth. 4. Erit enim tempus cum sanam doctrinam non sustinebunt: sed ad sua desideria coacervabunt sibi magistros prurientes auribus, & a veritate quidem auditum avertent, ad fabulas autem convertent: quia fabulas & errores Papæ hæretici multitudo præcipue magistrorum ambitiosorum & auaroru sequitur. Idcirco peto ut ostendas secundum aliquorum sententias, quid paucis in sacra pagina eruditis sive fuerint magistri sive discipuli esset agendum, si Papa efficeretur hæreticus, & quid omnes prædicatores & doctores haberent agere, nisi omnes veritati fidei adhærerent.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Scripture clearly shows me that a single Catholic may safely take up war against a heretical Pope, together with his whole company, and that he ought not to despair of victory in any way. I do wonder, however, whether, if any future Pope should become a heretic, the many Christians could say that saying of the Saviour: Do you think that the Son of Man, when he comes, will find faith on the earth? For I suppose that very few would resist him. I think that then the prophecy of the blessed Paul would be fulfilled, where he says in 2 Timothy 4: For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine, but will heap up for themselves teachers, having itching ears, and they will turn away their hearing from the truth and turn aside to fables. For the multitude, especially of ambitious and greedy teachers, follows the fables and errors of a heretical Pope. Therefore I ask you to show, according to the opinions of some, what should be done by the few who are learned in the sacred page, whether they be teachers or disciples, if the Pope were to become a heretic, and what all preachers and teachers would have to do, unless they all adhered to the truth of the faith.

units.la: MAG. Respondetur, quod si Papa de doctrina diffamaretur erronea, omnes prædicatores & doctores seu lectores vel magistri: imo etiam omnes literati quantum unusquisque ingenio & scientiæ concunerit, deberent doctrinam Papæ erroneam videre, studere, & examinare, & discutere diligenter, exemplo illorum, de quibus dicitur Act. 17. quotidie scrutantes scripturas, si hæc ita se haberent.
units.tr: MASTER. The answer is this: if the Pope were publicly reported to teach erroneous doctrine, all preachers, teachers, lecturers or masters, indeed all men of letters, each according to his talent and learning, ought to examine, study, and diligently scrutinise the erroneous doctrine of the Pope, following the example of those of whom it is said in Acts 17: examining the Scriptures daily, whether these things were so.

units.la: DIS. Hic dicitur de illis, qui scrutantur continue veritatem: non de scrutantibus doctrinas erroneas. MAGIST. Respondetur, quod ad eos spectat scrutari veritatem & errores contrarios & doctrinam, testante Salomone, qui Eccl. 1. ait: Dedique cor meum, ut scirem prudentiam atque doctrinam, erroresque & stultitiam. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod ita inquisitionem & discussionem di-
units.tr: DISC. This speaks of those who continually search out the truth, not of those who search out erroneous doctrines. MASTER. The answer is that it belongs to them to search out the truth and contrary errors and doctrine, as Solomon bears witness, who says in Ecclesiastes 1: I applied my heart to know wisdom and doctrine, and errors and folly. From these words it is gathered that the inquiry and discussion of errors against the faith is to be joined with that of the catholic truths, as in the same way

units.la: junc {s}aunt errores contra fidem: sicut catholicæ veritates, quia vt Sapiens testatur, Idem est index recti & obliqui, & eadem est scientia contrariorum. oportet ergo prædicatores & doctores errores Papæ hæretici examinare, studere & discutere diligenter, quia sic ad veritates plures, quas antea nesciebant, peruenient, teste Glo. accepta ab August. 1. Cor. 2. qui ait ab adversario mota quæstio discentiū existit occasio. DISCIP. Quid facient postquam doctrinam Papæ erroneam examinauerint diligenter? MAGIST. Responderetur, quod rationibus & scripturarum testimoniis contra eam quantum possunt debent se munire, ac illi qui scribendi gratiam receperunt, scribant & componant libros, tractatus, sermones, & epistolas, secundum quod videtur expedients ad reprobandum doctrinam Papæ erroneam. opera vero sua modis sibi possibilibus communicent & diuulgent, nominibus suis tacitis vel expressis, scilicet secundum quod expedire videtur.
units.tr: ...as the wise man testifies: The same is the judge of the straight and the crooked, and the same is the knowledge of contraries. It is therefore necessary for preachers and teachers to examine, study and diligently discuss the errors of the heretical Pope, because in this way they will arrive at many truths which they did not know before, as the Gloss, taken from Augustine on 1 Corinthians 2, witnesses, which says: a question raised by an adversary becomes an occasion for the learners. DISCIPLE. What will they do after they have diligently examined the erroneous doctrine of the Pope? MASTER. The answer is that they ought to arm themselves, as far as they can, against it with arguments and testimonies of Scripture; and those who have received the gift of writing should write and compose books, treatises, sermons and letters, as seems expedient for refuting the erroneous doctrine of the Pope. They should also communicate and publish their works by whatever means are possible for them, with their names either hidden or expressed, that is, as seems expedient.

units.la: Quædam enim opera ratione auctorum videntur libentius. & tunc erit vtile nomen auctorum exprimere. interdum autem multi odio habent auctores, & tunc illis nomen auctorum opetis expedit occultare, vt æmuli non quis dicat, sed quid dicatur, attendant. Illi vero, qui libros, tractatus & alia opera componendi gratiam minime habent, in scripturis authenticis, & etiam in operibus nouis, in quibus magis distincte doctrinam Papæ erroneam poterunt reprobare, se occupent studiose, vt cum tempus venerit oportunum, errores Papæ valeant efficaciter reprobare. Vndetam illi, qui noua opera contra prauitatem Papæ hæretici ediderunt, quàm alii prædicatores & doctores in lectionibus & sermonibus publicis ceterisque colloquiis, quando opportunitas loquendi assuerit, debent errores Papæ secundum gratiam eis datam efficaciter reprobare, & veritatem contrariam declarare, & quantum in eis est auribus omnium inculcare. Vnde nutu & verbo quid sentiant manifestent, dicantque vt more bellatorum qui hostes suos aperte & per insidias & omnibus modis licitis, quos excogitare valuerint, debellare nituntur: debent prædicatores & doctores seu magistri aperte & per insidias publice ac modis sibi conuenientibus perfidiam Papæ hæretici expugnare: nec aliter à culpa fautoriæ prauitatis hæreticæ sunt immunes. quia non caret scrupulo societatis occultæ, qui manifesto facinori desinit obuiare, extra de homicidio, si est. quod intelligendum est, cum quis potest manifesto facinori obuiare, & non apparet in promptu, quod per alium facinus manifestum valeat prohibere. & ideo si Papa hæreticus laborauerit inficere orthodoxos doctores & prædicatores regionum, ad quos doctrina pestifera Papæ hæretici peruenirer, ne illarum incolæ regionum auerterentur à fide, viliter obuiare deberent, nec carerent in hoc casu scrupulo societatis occultæ, nisi doctrinæ Papæ erroneæ obuiarent, si in regionibus illis non essent alii, qui doctrinæ Papæ erroneæ scirent, vellent, & possent resistere. & ita prædicatores & doctores in Francia commorantes tenentur doctrinam Papæ erroneam reprobare, priusquam doctrina eadem in Francia scperit publicari, vel probabiliter dubitatur, quod aliquos corrumperet in Francia, nisi resistatur eidem. Sic prædicatores & doctores Italiæ debent ab eadem doctrina mortifera præseruare Italiam, vt si in aliqua sui parte infecta fuerit, debent conari purgare eandem. & consimiliter de prædicatoribus & doctoribus aliarum regionum, in quibus morantur, est dicendum. Si vero in Francia vel in alia regione sunt aliqui prædicatores & doctores seu magistri, qui sufficienter eandem regionem à dicta doctrina præseruant vel expurgant, alii prædicatores & doctores vel magistri regionis eiusdem non tenentur de necessitate salutis doctrinæ illi obuiare, ex quo per alios ei sufficienter resistit: sed vbi alii deficerent, ipsi se ponere murum pro fide catholica contra Papam hæreticum deberent. alioquin in fautoriam inciderent prauitatis hæreticæ iuxta auctoritatem supersius allegatam, &c.
units.tr: For some works are more willingly received on account of their authors, and then it will be useful to name the authors. Sometimes, however, many hate the authors, and then it is expedient to conceal the authors' names, so that rivals may attend not to who says a thing but to what is said. Those, indeed, who have no gift for composing books, treatises and other works should devote themselves diligently to the authentic Scriptures, and also to new works in which they can more clearly refute the doctrine of the erroneous Pope, so that when the opportune time comes they may be able to refute the errors of the Pope effectively. Therefore those who have published new works against the depravity of the heretical Pope, like other preachers and teachers in lectures, public sermons and other conversations, whenever the opportunity to speak arises, ought to refute the errors of the Pope effectively, according to the grace given to them, to declare the contrary truth, and to impress it as far as they can on the ears of all. Let them make clear by nod and word what they think, and let them speak as warriors do, who strive to defeat their enemies openly, by ambush and by every lawful means they can devise. Preachers, teachers or masters should openly and by stratagem, publicly and by fitting means, assail the perfidy of the heretical Pope; otherwise they are not free from the guilt of favouring heretical depravity. For he who ceases to oppose a plain crime is not free from the taint of secret complicity, Extra, de homicidio, if it is. This must be understood to apply when someone can oppose a plain crime and it is not evident at hand that he could prevent the manifest crime through another. Therefore, if the heretical Pope should labour to infect the orthodox teachers and preachers of regions to which the pestilent doctrine of the heretical Pope might reach, then, lest the inhabitants of those regions be turned away from the faith, they ought to oppose it earnestly, and in this case they would not be free from the taint of secret complicity, unless they opposed the erroneous doctrine of the Pope when there were no others in those regions who knew, wished and were able to resist the erroneous doctrine of the Pope. And so preachers and teachers residing in France are bound to refute the erroneous doctrine of the Pope before the same doctrine is published in France, or it is probably feared that it would corrupt some in France unless it is resisted. Likewise, the preachers and teachers of Italy must protect Italy from this deadly doctrine, so that if any part of it has been infected they should strive to purge it. The same must be said of the preachers and teachers of the other regions in which they dwell. But if in France or another region there are some preachers, teachers or masters who sufficiently protect or purge that region from the said doctrine, the other preachers, teachers or masters of that same region are not bound of necessity to salvation to oppose that doctrine, since it is sufficiently resisted by others. But where others are lacking, they themselves ought to set themselves up as a wall for the Catholic faith against the heretical Pope; otherwise they would fall into the favouring of heretical depravity, according to the authority alleged above, etc.

units.la: DISCIP. Videtur quod illa auctoritas & consimiles non debent de quibuscunque intelligi, sed de illis tantum modo, qui sic supra alios potestatem habent. quales non sunt prædicatores & doctores, nisi fuerint prælati.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. It seems that that authority and similar ones ought not to be understood of everyone, but only of those who have power over others in this way; such are not preachers and teachers, unless they are prelates.

units.la: MAGIST. Dicunt quidam, quod hic errat aperte: quia auctoritas illa & consimiles debent intelligi non solum de prælatis: sed etiam de sociis & subditis, quod per decretalem supra allegatam, extra de homicidio, satis videtur aperte probari. conditor enim decretalis illius, scilicet Alexander tertius, loquitur de occisoribus beati Thomæ Cantuariensis, & de illis, qui associauerunt eos, quorum diuersi diuersimode culpabiles existiterunt. de quibus dicit in hæc verba: illis etiam qui non vt ferirent, sed vt persecutoribus opem ferrent, si forte per aliorum violentiam impediretur, paulo minori debent pœna multari, quia cum scriptum sit: Qui potuit hominem liberare à morte, & non liberauit eum, occidit. constat autem ab homicidii reatu immunes non esse qui occisoribus contra alios opem præstant, nec carent scrupulo societatis occultæ qui manifesto facinori desinit obuiare. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod Alexander tertius quasi duplicitér probare conatur, quod qui opem occisoribus præstare venerint, à reatu homicidii minime sunt immunes. Primo modo per illud, qui potuit hominem liberare, &c. Secundo per illud, nec carent scrupulo, &c. ergo vtrunque illorum dictorum, scilicet qui potuit hominem liberare, &c. nec caret scrupulo, &c. de his, qui opem occisoribus præstare venerint, debet intelligi. illi autem non erant prælati occisorum, nec superiores militibus, qui erant occisores: sed erant socii vel familiares subditi eorundem. ergo tales auctoritates, qui potuit hominem liberare, &c. nec caret scrupulo, &c. & consimiles, non solum de prælatis & superioribus. super alios potestate habentibus, sed et de omnibus debent intelligi. & verū est pro tempore necessitatis, cum non apparet alius in promptu, qui velit & valeat proximum a periculo liberare. Quod etiam auctoritates tales, quipotuit, &c. & nec caret, &c. de sociis & de omnib: debeant intelligi, probatur secundo sic. Non minus tenetur quilibet socius subditus vel praelatus subuenire necessitati spirituali proximi quam corporali. Sed quilibet tempore necessitatis ubi non apparet alius, qui proximo subueniat, tenetur opera misericordiae corporalia proximo (si poterit) impendere. ergo multomagis quilibet subditus & praelatus opera misericordiae spiritualia (si conuenienter poterit, cum non apparet alius qui subueniat) tenetur tempore necessitatis proximo exhibere. manifesto autem facinori obuiare, cum quis conuenienter poterit, & proximum tenetur (ne doctrina Papae haeretici insectatur erronea) praeseruare & regionem totam, vel pro parte doctrina erronea Papae infectam per sermones, informationes, exhortationes, & scripturas catholicas expurgare, & consimilia, quae sunt inter opera misericordiae spiritualia computanda. Ergo ad ista & consimilia tempore necessitatis, cum non apparet praelati, nec alii qui velint vel possint talia operari, quilibet siue socius siue subditus, qui conuenienter poterit, ita debet proximis de necessitate salutis impendere. Ex quibus colligitur, quod si praedicatores & doctores seu magistri siuein sermonibus & lectionib. publicis siue per informationes occultas possunt aliquos vel aliquas a doctrina Papae erronea retrahere & non faciunt: nec apparet alius, qui hoc faciat, sunt fautores haereticae prauitatis: nec carent scrupulo societatis occultae, ex quo possunt (& non apparet alius qui velit & possit) manifesto facinori desinunt obuiare.
units.tr: MASTER. Some say that here he is clearly mistaken, because that authority and similar ones must be understood not only of prelates but also of companions and subjects, which is quite plainly shown by the decretal alleged above, Extra, de homicidio. For the author of that decretal, namely Alexander III, speaks of the murderers of the blessed Thomas of Canterbury, and of those who joined them, of whom some were guilty in different ways. Of these he says in these words: Those too who came not to strike, but to bring help to the persecutors, if perhaps they were prevented by the violence of others, ought to be punished with a somewhat lesser penalty, because it is written: He who could have saved a man from death and did not save him, kills him. It is established that those who give help to murderers against others are not free from the guilt of homicide, nor are they free from the taint of secret complicity who cease to oppose a plain crime. From these words it is gathered that Alexander III tries to prove in a twofold way that those who came to give help to the murderers are by no means free from the guilt of homicide. In the first way, through He who could have saved a man, etc.; in the second, through nor is he free from the taint, etc. Therefore both of those sayings, namely he who could have saved a man, etc., and nor is he free from the taint, etc., must be understood of those who came to give help to the murderers. But those were not prelates of the slain, nor superiors of the soldiers who were the murderers; they were companions or household subjects of the same. Therefore such authorities, he who could have saved a man, etc., nor is he free from the taint, etc., and similar ones, must be understood not only of prelates and superiors who have power over others, but of everyone. And this is true for a time of necessity, when no other is evidently at hand who is willing and able to deliver the neighbour from danger. That such authorities, he who could, etc., and nor is he free, etc., must be understood of companions and of everyone, is proved secondly as follows. Every companion, subject or prelate is no less bound to help the spiritual necessity of his neighbour than the bodily. But everyone, in a time of necessity where no other appears who helps the neighbour, is bound to bestow the bodily works of mercy on his neighbour (if he is able). Therefore much more does every subject and prelate, in a time of necessity, bound to show the spiritual works of mercy to his neighbour (if he can suitably do so, since no other appears to help). To oppose a plain crime, when someone can do so suitably, and to preserve the neighbour (lest he be pursued by the erroneous doctrine of the Pope), and to purge the whole region, or the part of it infected with the erroneous doctrine of the Pope, by sermons, instructions, exhortations and Catholic writings, and similar things, are to be counted among the spiritual works of mercy. Therefore, in a time of necessity, when no prelate or others who are willing or able to perform such things appear, whoever, whether companion or subject, can do so suitably, ought in this way to bestow these things on his neighbour as necessary for salvation. From these things it is gathered that if preachers and teachers or masters, whether in sermons and public lectures or by secret instructions, can call back some men or women from the erroneous doctrine of the Pope and do not do so, and no other appears who does it, they are supporters of heretical depravity; they are not free from the taint of secret complicity, since they cease to oppose a manifest crime when they could (and no other appears who is willing and able to do so).

units.la: DIS. Quid si metu mortis tali facinori desinunt obuiare? MAGIST. Videtur quibusdam, quod si probabiliter crederent, quod si possunt aliquos a doctrina Papae erronea revocare, nec probabiliter reputarent, quod alio tempore si vinerent maiores possent facere fructum: peccarent mortaliter omittendo metu mortis alios a doctrina erronea revocare. verumtamen propter metum mortis excusarentur in tantum, quod sententiam excommunicationis nequaquam incurrerent. quemadmodum si quis inter Saracenos & infidelis alios constitutus metu mortis negaret Christum, & veneraretur Machometum, peccaret mortaliter; sed sententiam excommunicationis euaderet.
units.tr: DIS. What if, through fear of death, they fail to resist such a crime? MAGIST. Some think that if they believed with reasonable probability that they could recall some people from the Pope's erroneous doctrine, and did not reasonably judge that they might achieve more fruit at another time if they lived longer, they would sin mortally by omitting to recall others from the erroneous doctrine out of fear of death. Nevertheless, on account of fear of death they would be excused to such an extent that they would not incur the sentence of excommunication at all; just as if someone, placed among the Saracens and other unbelievers, denied Christ out of fear of death and worshipped Muhammad, he would sin mortally, yet would escape the sentence of excommunication.

units.la: CAP. XXXXIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXXIX.

units.la: In quo agitur de eis, qui impugnatores Papae haeretici persequerentur: aut quomodo libet infestarent, quid sit tenendum. vbi ponuntur quinque conclusiones.
units.tr: In which it is discussed who should be regarded as persecuting, or in any way harassing, those who attack the Pope as a heretic, and what must be held about them. Five conclusions are set out here.

units.la: DISCIP. Inquisiuimus de praedicatoribus, si teneantur doctrinam Papae erroneam reprobare. nunc dissere de illis praedicatoribus & doctoribus, qui impugnatores Papae haeretici improbarent vel sequerentur, aut quomodolibet infestarent. MAGIST. Circa hanc interrogationem videtur aliquibus distinguendum, quod improbare impugnatores Papae haeretici contingit dupliciter. Vno modo eorum assertiones per auctores & rationes solum modo conuincere satagendo. Alio modo personis eorum detrahendo vel in propria irrogando aut persecutionem quamlibet procurando, vel contra ipsos alios prouocando, seu eis per se vel per alios molestiam quamlibet inferendo. Item aut assertio Papae haeretici erronea est damnata explicite solummodo vel implicite. Item si est damnata, aut praedicatores aut doctores, qui non impugnant ipsum, possunt faciliter scire, quod assertio Papae est damnata explicite, aut non possunt faciliter scire. Item aut sciunt Papam a viris in sacra pagina eruditis de certis articulis fortiter impugnari, aut nesciunt. DISCIP. Quomodo potest contingere, quod aliqua assertio Papae erronea sit damnata explicite; & tamen praedicatores seu doctores hoc faciliter non possunt scire? MAGIST. Respondetur, quod hoc potest contingere propter ignorantiam praedicatorum & doctorum, & propter defectum librorum. multi enim sunt praedicatores & doctores tam simplices & tam paruam scripturarum habentes noticiam & peritiam, quod veritates quam plurimas sanctarum scripturarum ignorant, & de determinationibus ecclesiae parum vel nihil sciunt. multi eorum propter inopiam scripturarum, in quibus veritates catholicae plures explicite approbantur, & per consequens falsitates contrariae reprobantur & condemnantur, faciliter peruenire non possunt. vt dicunt, pauci, praeter Fratres Minores, habent decretalem Nicolai tertii, in qua explicite approbatur, quod abdicationes proprietatis omnium rerum Christus verbo docuit & exemplo confirmauit: & per consequens falsitas contradictionis explicite condemnata est. condemnationem etiam summorum pontificum, qui magistros quosdam Parisienses damnantes statum Mendicantium condemnauerunt, pauci habent, praeter Fratres praedicatores & Minores. & ita multi ad illas scripturas continentes damnationem talium haeresum facile peruenire non possunt. quidam autem a peritis longe distant; nec adest eis opportunitas consulendi peritos. quare si non sunt in scripturis excellenter instructi, non faciliter scire possunt tales haereses esse explicite condemnatas. DIS. De exemplis adductis in secundo tractatu De dogmatibus Iob. 22. loquuntur, per quae quamuis malitiose ab aemulis adducantur, intelligo quomodo aliqui praedicatores seu doctores de quibusdam haeresibus non possunt faciliter scire, an sint explicite condemnatæ. quamobrem enarra, qualiter per præscriptas distinctiones ad interrogationem propositam respondetur. MAG. Respondetur quinque conclusiones tenendo. Quarum prima est, quod prædicatores & doctores assertiones impugnantium Papam hæreticum de assertione, quæ non est damnata explicite, improbantes solo sermone intendendo, convincendo per rationes & auctoritates, quod assertiones eorum contrariæ assertioni Papæ hæretici non continent veritatem, non sunt censendi fautores hæreticæ prauitatis, nec ex hoc solo sunt reputandi peccare mortaliter. Hæc conclusio probatur per hoc, quod catholici possunt absque fautoria prauitatis hæreticæ & peccato mortali circa assertiones catholicas, quæ non sunt explicite approbatæ, nec explicite condemnatæ, contrarie opinari, & opiniones suas contrarias rationibus & auctoritatibus fulcire. ergo licet Papa hæreticus & impugnatores eius tenant opiniones contrarias, absque fautoria prauitatis hæreticæ & absque peccato mortali possunt prædicatores & doctores assertionem Papæ quæ in rei veritate est hæretica (licet hoc nesciant) conari probare assertionem contrariam improbare.
units.tr: STUDENT: We have asked about preachers, whether they are bound to reject the Pope's erroneous doctrine. Now discuss those preachers and teachers who condemn or follow those who attack the Pope as a heretic, or who in any way harass them. MASTER: On this question some think a distinction must be drawn. Condemning those who attack the Pope as a heretic can happen in two ways. In one way, one labours only to refute their assertions by authorities and arguments. In the other way, one disparages their persons, or inflicts injuries on them, or procures any persecution, or stirs up others against them, or in any way, personally or through others, causes them trouble. Again, the Pope's assertion may be condemned as erroneous either explicitly only or implicitly. Again, if it has been condemned, preachers or teachers who do not attack it may either easily know that the Pope's assertion has been condemned explicitly, or they may not easily know it. Again, they either know that the Pope is strongly attacked on certain articles by men learned in Sacred Scripture, or they do not know it. STUDENT: How can it happen that some erroneous assertion of the Pope has been explicitly condemned, and yet preachers or teachers cannot easily know this? MASTER: It can happen because of the ignorance of preachers and teachers and because of the lack of books. For there are many preachers and teachers, so simple and having so little knowledge and skill in the Scriptures, that they are ignorant of very many truths of Holy Scripture and know little or nothing of the determinations of the Church. Many of them, because of the scarcity of the Scriptures, in which many Catholic truths are explicitly approved, and consequently the contrary falsehoods are rejected and condemned, cannot easily come to them. As they say, few apart from the Friars Minor have the decretal of Nicholas III, in which it is explicitly approved that Christ taught by word and confirmed by example the renunciation of ownership of all things; and consequently the falsehood of the contrary is explicitly condemned. Few also have the condemnation by the supreme pontiffs who, condemning certain Parisian masters, condemned the state of the Mendicants, apart from the Friars Preachers and Minors. And so many cannot easily reach those writings containing the condemnation of such heresies. Some, moreover, are far from the learned, nor do they have the opportunity of consulting them. Therefore, if they are not excellently instructed in the Scriptures, they cannot easily know that such heresies have been explicitly condemned. STUDENT: The examples adduced in the second treatise On Dogmas, Job 22, speak of such things; although they are maliciously brought forward by rivals, I understand how some preachers or teachers cannot easily know whether certain heresies have been explicitly condemned. Therefore explain how, by the distinctions set out above, the question proposed is answered. MASTER: The answer holds five conclusions. The first is that preachers and teachers who, in rejecting or attacking the assertions of those who attack the Pope as a heretic, regarding an assertion not explicitly condemned, intend only by speech, by convincing with arguments and authorities, that their assertions contrary to the assertion of the heretical Pope do not contain truth, are not to be considered favourers of heretical depravity, nor for this alone are they to be judged to sin mortally. This conclusion is proved by the fact that Catholics may, without favouring heretical depravity and without mortal sin, hold opinions contrary to Catholic assertions that have not been explicitly approved or explicitly condemned, and support their contrary opinions with arguments and authorities. Therefore, although the heretical Pope and his opponents hold contrary opinions, without favouring heretical depravity and without mortal sin preachers and teachers may try to prove the contrary assertion and to reject the Pope's assertion, which in truth is heretical (though they do not know it).

units.la: DISCIP. Contra hanc probationem & conclusionem eius duæ obiectiones mihi occurrunt. Quarum prima est: quod si assertio Papæ non est damnata explicite tanquam hæretica: non erit propterea hæreticus iudicandus. ergo impugnantes Papam propterea asserendo eum esse hæreticum, sunt merito puniendi. Secunda obiectio est contra illud, quod dicitur & innuitur, quod licet prædicatores & doctores conantur auctoritatibus & rationibus improbare assertionem impugnantium assertionem Papæ hæreticam, non sunt censendi fautores hæreticæ prauitatis: hoc enim non videtur verum. nam nullus plus potest fauere hæreticæ prauitati, quam conando eam auctoritatibus & rationibus approbare, & ostendere eam veram esse. si ergo aliqui moliuntur rationibus & auctoritatibus probare contrariam assertionem Papæ hæretici, quæ est hæretica, esse saliam, videtur quod censendi sunt fautores hæreticæ prauitatis.
units.tr: STUDENT: Against this proof and its conclusion two objections occur to me. The first is this: if the Pope's assertion has not been explicitly condemned as heretical, he is not therefore to be judged a heretic. Therefore those who attack the Pope by asserting that he is a heretic deserve to be punished. The second objection is against what is said and implied, namely that although preachers and teachers try by authorities and arguments to refute the assertion of those who attack the Pope's heretical assertion, they are not to be considered favourers of heretical depravity. For this does not seem true. For no one can favour heretical depravity more than by striving to approve it by authorities and arguments and to show that it is true. If therefore some labour by arguments and authorities to prove that the contrary assertion of the heretical Pope, which is heretical, is false, it seems they must be considered favourers of heretical depravity.

units.la: MAG. Ad primam respondetur, quod licet assertio Papæ non sit damnata explicite; in casu tamen licitum est asserere & tenere Papam esse hæreticum. Ad cuius evidentiam dicitur esse sciendum, quod si assertio Papæ non est damnata explicite, aut Papa eam tenet solummodo opinando; & tunc licet scientibus in rei veritate eam esse hæreticam asserere, quod est hæretica; sed non licet eis dicere nec asserere Papam esse hæreticum; quia ex quo Papa solummodo opinando dicit eam, non est hæreticus reputandus. aut Papa talem hæresim non damnatam explicite non opinando, sed pertinaciter asserendo tenet, quæ est pertinacia. quia, sicut patet ex quarto huius diversimode potest de pertinacia deprehendi. & in hoc casu licet catholicis scientibus Papam hæresim damnatam solummodo implicite pertinaciter asserere & tenere, non tantummodo affirmare assertionem Papæ esse hæreticam, sed licet eis sentire, quod Papa est hæreticus. periculosum tamen hoc publice assererent: quia forte hoc reprobare non possent. & forsan extra concilium generale & in absentia catholici Papæ, quamuis esset verum, non debent hoc publice affirmare.
units.tr: MASTER: To the first objection the answer is that although the Pope's assertion has not been explicitly condemned, nevertheless in such a case it is lawful to assert and hold that the Pope is a heretic. To make this clear, it must be known that if the Pope's assertion has not been explicitly condemned, then either the Pope holds it only by opinion; and then it is lawful for those who know that it is in truth heretical to assert that it is heretical, but it is not lawful for them to say or assert that the Pope is a heretic, since, because the Pope says it only by opinion, he is not to be regarded as a heretic. Or the Pope does not hold such a heresy, not explicitly condemned, by mere opinion, but asserts and holds it obstinately, which is pertinacity. For, as is clear from the fourth [chapter] of this [work], pertinacity can be detected in various ways. And in this case, it is lawful for Catholics who know that the Pope obstinately asserts and holds a heresy condemned only implicitly, not only to affirm that the Pope's assertion is heretical, but also to think that the Pope is a heretic. Yet they would be acting dangerously if they asserted this publicly, because perhaps they would not be able to prove it. And perhaps outside a general council and in the absence of a Catholic Pope, although it might be true, they ought not to affirm this publicly.

units.la: Ad secundam obiectionem respondetur, quod ad fautoriam hæresis, quæ non est damnata, non sufficit, quod quis eandem rationibus & auctoritatibus munire conetur: sed ultra hoc requiritur, quod pertinaciter seu inique talem hæresim rationibus & auctoritatibus fulcire seu alias munire conetur: quemadmodum ad hæreticam prauitatem non sufficit, quod quis errando hæresi adhæreat; sed requiritur, quod pertinaciter adhæreat.
units.tr: To the second objection the answer is that to be a favourer of a heresy which has not been condemned, it is not enough that someone try to fortify it with arguments and authorities; beyond this it is required that he try to defend or otherwise fortify such a heresy with arguments and authorities obstinately or unjustly. Just as, for heretical depravity, it is not enough that someone adhere to a heresy through error; rather, it is required that he adhere to it obstinately.

units.la: DISCIP. Indica quæ sunt aliæ conclusiones, quas tenet prædicta opinio. MAGIST. Secunda conclusio est, quod prædicatores & doctores qui impugnatores doctrinæ hæretici Papæ quantum ad assertionem non damnatam explicite, non solum rationibus & auctoritatibus, sed etiam detrahendo & improperia irrogando, aut contra eos alios provocando, vel per se vel per alios molestiam quomodolibet inferendo impugnantibus, peccant mortaliter, & sunt fautores hæreticæ prauitatis. Quia qui propter bonum licitum infert alteri nocumentum notabile, peccat mortaliter. & si propter licitam impugnationem hæreticæ prauitatis infert alteri nocumentum, est fautor hæreticæ prauitatis. sed reputare assertionem Papæ hæreticam, licet non sit damnata explicite, est bonum & licitum. ergo prædicatores & doctores, qui propter impugnationem huiusmodi inferunt impugnantibus notabile nocumentum, peccant mortaliter: & sunt fautores hæreticæ prauitatis. hoc autem faciunt, qui eis detrahunt & etiam opprobria & contumelias irrogant, & contra eos alios provocant, vel per se vel per alios molestiam irrogant. ergo peccant mortaliter, & sunt fautores hæreticæ prauitatis. Tertia conclusio est: Quod illi prædicatores & doctores, qui impugnatores Papæ hæretici propter assertionem explicite damnatam, quam non possunt faciliter scire esse damnatam explicite propter imperitiam in scripturis authenticis, aut propter defectum librorum, aut propter aliam quamcunque causam, propter quam nesciunt Papam de hæresi impugnare; impugnant assertionem Papæ solummodo rationibus & auctoritatibus latagendo munire, & assertionem contrariam rationibus & auctoritatibus tantummodo improbare tacendo, non peccant mortaliter, nec sunt fautores hæreticæ prauitatis censendi. Quia absque peccato mortali potest quis (dummodo perinaciam non adiungat) opinando assertionem negare catholicam (etiam explicite approbatam) & contrariam assertionem hæreticam damnatam explicite opinari. si enim est aliquis non habens memoriam de historia libri Regum, qui absque pertinacia diceret & rationibus aliquibus confirmaret, quod Dauid non habuit plures simul vxores, nec peccaret mortaliter, nec esset fautor haereticae prauitatis. Sic dicūt aliqui, q; licet quidā, qui nunquā viderunt Decretalem Nicolai tertii (Exiit qui seminat) opinaren- tur, & suam opinionem auctoritatibus & rationibus confirmare studerent, quod Christus habuit aliquius rei proprietatem, quamuis hoc facerent imitando Papam haereticum, qui hoc diceret, non peccarent mortaliter, si dictam decretalem Exiit, faciliter habere non possent, nec scirent Papam propter assertionem praedictam à viris eruditis in sacra pagina impugnandum. quia opinari haeresim damnatam explicite nescienter potest quis absque peccato mortali & fautoria haereticae prauitatis, dummodo pertinacia nullatenus miscetur. Quarta conclusio est, quod praedicatores & doctores, qui impugnantes Papam haereticum pro assertione damnata explicite haeretica, quam possunt faciliter scire damnatam explicite, & propter quam sciunt Papam de haeresi impugnari, reprobant aut impugnant, peccant mortaliter, nec à fautoria prauitatis haereticae sunt immunes: quia tantum zelum debent habere de fide catholica, quod honori & fauori cuiuslibet mortalis praeferre tenentur: quia cum nunciatur eis Papam in certo articulo contra fidem catholicam errare, se de eadem assertione intromittere approbando vel reprobando proponunt, non debent negligere, sed quaerere diligenter, an assertio Papae sit condemnata. & ita si possent facile scire assertionem eandem esse damnatam explicite, seu illam veritatem esse explicite approbatam, nullatenus à peccato mortali & fautoria haereticae prauitatis excusatur, si impugnantes assertionem Papae erroneam improbare praesumant. Quinta conclusio est; Quia praedicatores & doctores impugnatores doctrinae erroneae Papae haeretici damnatam explicite sciant siue ignorent eam esse damnatam explicite propter impugnationem huiusmodi persequuntur eis detrahendo vel contumelias vel improperia irrogando, vel contra eos provocando, seu aliter per se vel per alios molestiam quomodolibet inferendo, peccant mortaliter, & sunt fautores haereticae prauitatis reputandi: gravius tamen peccant illi, qui sciunt doctrinam Papae esse erroneam, quam illi, qui ignorant.
units.tr: STUDENT: Point out what the other conclusions are, which the aforesaid opinion holds. MASTER: The second conclusion is that preachers and teachers who attack the doctrine of the heretical Pope, as to an assertion not explicitly condemned, not only by arguments and authorities, but also by disparaging and heaping insults, or by stirring up others against those attacking him, or by causing them any trouble whatever, whether personally or through others, sin mortally and are favourers of heretical depravity. For whoever for the sake of a lawful good inflicts a notable harm on another sins mortally; and if for the sake of a lawful attack on heretical depravity he inflicts harm on another, he is a favourer of heretical depravity. But to regard the Pope's assertion as heretical, although it has not been explicitly condemned, is good and lawful. Therefore preachers and teachers who, for the sake of such an attack, inflict a notable harm on those who attack him, sin mortally and are favourers of heretical depravity. Those, moreover, do this who disparage them and also heap disgrace and insults upon them, and stir up others against them, or inflict trouble either personally or through others. Therefore they sin mortally and are favourers of heretical depravity. The third conclusion is this: those preachers and teachers who attack the heretical Pope because of an explicitly condemned assertion, which they cannot easily know to be explicitly condemned, because of their inexperience in authentic Scripture, or because of the lack of books, or for any other cause on account of which they do not know that the Pope is to be attacked for heresy, and who labour only by arguments and authorities to fortify their own assertion and merely by silence to reject the contrary assertion by arguments and authorities, do not sin mortally, nor are they to be considered favourers of heretical depravity. For without mortal sin one may (provided that pertinacity is not added) hold by opinion the denial of a Catholic assertion (even one explicitly approved), and by opinion hold the contrary heretical assertion, which has been explicitly condemned. For if someone who does not remember the history of the Book of Kings were to say, without pertinacity, and confirm with some arguments, that David did not have several wives at once, he would not sin mortally, nor would he be a favourer of heretical depravity. So some say that although certain men, who had never seen the decretal of Nicholas III (Exiit qui seminat), held the opinion and tried to confirm their opinion by authorities and arguments that Christ had some ownership of a thing, yet, while imitating the heretical Pope who said this, they would not sin mortally, if they could not easily obtain the said decretal Exiit, and did not know that the Pope was to be attacked by learned men in Sacred Scripture for the aforesaid assertion. For one can unknowingly hold a heresy explicitly condemned without mortal sin and without favouring heretical depravity, provided that pertinacity is in no way mixed in. The fourth conclusion is this: preachers and teachers who attack or reject those attacking the heretical Pope for an assertion explicitly condemned as heretical, which they can easily know to be explicitly condemned, and because of which they know that the Pope is being attacked for heresy, sin mortally, and are not free from the favouring of heretical depravity. For they must have such zeal for the Catholic faith that they are bound to prefer it to the honour and favour of anyone at all. For when they are told that the Pope errs on a certain article against the Catholic faith, and they undertake to meddle in that same assertion by approving or rejecting it, they must not neglect this, but must diligently inquire whether the Pope's assertion has been condemned. And so, if they could easily know that the same assertion has been explicitly condemned, or that that truth has been explicitly approved, they are in no way excused from mortal sin and from favouring heretical depravity if they presume to attack the Pope's erroneous assertion. The fifth conclusion is this: preachers and teachers who attack the erroneous doctrine of the heretical Pope, whether they know or are ignorant that it has been explicitly condemned, and who on account of such an attack persecute those who attack him, by disparaging them, heaping insults or disgrace upon them, stirring up others against them, or otherwise causing them any trouble whatever, either personally or through others, sin mortally and are to be regarded as favourers of heretical depravity; yet those who know that the Pope's doctrine is erroneous sin more gravely than those who are ignorant of it.

units.la: DISCIP. Quare non possunt ignorantes per ignorantiam excusari? MAG. Respondetur, quod ignorantia iuris, quod semper quis scire tenetur, non excusat: hoc autem scire tenetur, quod impugnantes aliquam doctrinam tanquam erroneam non sunt aliqualiter molestandi, nisi certitudinaliter constet eos false vel inique impugnare doctrinam eandem. quare cum (si doctrina Papae sit erronea) non possit constare, quod impugnatores ipsius propter solam impugnationem eam false impugnant & inique (quia huiusmodi impugnatio est licita) non sunt propter impugnationem huiusmodi aliqualiter molestandi.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Why cannot those who are ignorant be excused on account of their ignorance? MASTER. It is answered that ignorance of law, which a person is always bound to know, does not excuse. Now a person is bound to know this: that those who attack some doctrine as erroneous are not to be harassed in any way, unless it is certain that they attack that same doctrine falsely or unjustly. Therefore, since (if the doctrine of the Pope is erroneous) it cannot be certain that its opponents attack it falsely and unjustly merely by attacking it (because such an attack is lawful), they are not to be harassed in any way on account of such an attack.

units.la: CAP. XXXXX.
units.tr: CAP. XXXXX.

units.la: In quo specialiter invehitur contra doctores doctrinam Papae erroneam defendentes: qua scilicet poena sint plectendi, & quibus vitiis inuoluti.
units.tr: In which he specially inveighs against the teachers who defend the erroneous doctrine of the Pope: what punishment they should suffer, and with what vices they are involved.

units.la: DISCIP. Puto quod ad probandum omnes conclusiones praedictas rationes & auctoritates quam plures (si cogitares) scires adducere, quas omnes causa brevitatis mitte, & dic breviter, quid faciendum esset de doctoribus & magistris, qui doctrinam Papae manifeste erroneam defendere aut excusare quomodolibet niterentur; doctrinas autem aliorum maxime pauperum disputabiles; imo veras & catholicas, licet doctrinis quorundam theologorum contrarias, damnare & pervertere, & ad malum sensum trahere conarentur? MAG. Respondetur, quod talium doctorum nequitia faciliter describi non potest: quia tales ab omni amore & zelo veritatis sunt penitus alieni, ostendentes aperte, quod nequaquam amore scientiae aut veritatis magistratum ascenderunt, sed propter gulam aut honorem, aut divitias obtinendas, in studio laboraverunt.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. I suppose that if you thought about it you could bring forward very many reasons and authorities to prove all the aforesaid conclusions; but omit them all for the sake of brevity, and tell me briefly what ought to be done about those teachers and masters who strive in any way to defend or excuse a doctrine of the Pope that is manifestly erroneous, and who try to condemn and pervert, and to draw into a bad sense, the doctrines of others, especially of poor men, which are open to dispute, nay, which are true and catholic, although they are contrary to the doctrines of some theologians. MASTER. It is answered that the wickedness of such teachers cannot easily be described, because such men are wholly alien to all love and zeal for the truth, showing plainly that they did not climb to the magistracy out of love of knowledge or truth, but labored at their studies to obtain gluttony, honour, or riches.

units.la: DIS. Quibus vitiis sunt tales censendi impliciti. MAGIST. Respondetur, quod tales sunt acceptatores personarum, talibus enim loquitur Esa. 5. c. dicens: Ve qui potentes estis ad bibendum vinum, & viri fortes ad miscendum ebrietatem, qui iustificatis impium pro muneribus (hoc est pro beneficiis gratiis & honoribus obtinendis) & iustitiam iusti auferris ab eo (veritatem suae doctrinae propriam pervertendo, & ad malum sensum ut placeant Papae haeretico inique trahendo) sunt potentes ad bibendum vinum; quia inter alios fines malos quos sperant per magisterium obtinere impletio ventris cibi & potus infimum locum minime tenent, ut de his vere sic dicatur illud apostoli Phil. 3. quorum Deus venter est: quia propter ventrem & honorem & propter alia terrena consequenda & incommoda deuitanda laborant in studio & discunt. unde & de quolibet tali doctore dicit Salomon Prouer. 38. Qui cognoscit faciem suam in iudicio, non habet, &c. Ille cognoscit faciem in iudicio, qui doctrinam manifeste erroneam non nititur excusare vel etiam defendere, quia à Papa est tradita & inuenta: doctrinam pauperis catholicam & excusabilem (ut Papae haeretico placeat contra veritatem dicentis) ad malum satagit trahere intellectum, qui probucella panis, id est, pro vno bono conuiuio, vbi confusionem non metuit temporalem, catholicam paratus est defendere veritatem.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. With what vices are such men to be considered entangled? MASTER. It is answered that they are respecters of persons. To such men Isaiah speaks in chapter 5, saying: Woe to you who are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mix strong drink, who justify the wicked for rewards (that is, for obtaining benefits, favours and honours) and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him (perverting the truth of his own doctrine, and unjustly drawing it to a bad sense so as to please the heretical Pope). They are mighty to drink wine; for among the other base ends they hope to attain through the teaching office, the filling of the belly with food and drink holds by no means the lowest place. So of them the saying of the Apostle in Phil. 3 is truly spoken: whose God is the belly; for they labour at their studies and learn for the sake of the belly and honour, and to obtain earthly advantages and avoid discomforts. Hence Solomon also says of every such teacher in Prov. 38: He who regards the face in judgment does not have, etc. He regards the face in judgment who does not strive to excuse or even defend a doctrine that is manifestly erroneous, because it was handed down and devised by the Pope; while he strives to draw the sense of a poor man's doctrine, which is catholic and excusable, to a bad meaning, so that the heretical Pope may be pleased, against the truth of the one who speaks; he who would not fear temporal confusion for the sake of a good dinner, a crust of bread, is ready to defend the catholic truth.

units.la: DISCIP. Ex his coniectuto, quod si vnquam aliquis Papa haereticus esset futurus manifestus, patebit aperte, qui doctores illius temporis zelo veritatis catholicae & propter haereticos conuincendos (si vnquam insurgent) in studio laborarunt: & qui propter terrena scientiae operam impenderunt. MAG. Nonnullis apparet, quod hic fallens. quia, teste Christo, multi ad tempus credunt & in tempore tentationis recedunt. sed forte nonnulli, si Papa esset haereticus, bono zelo in principio laborabunt, & cum vexatio tribulatio per Papam haereticum sustinenda, illi firmissime adhaerebunt. DIS. Quamuis tibi non apparebit, quod tempore futuro Papae haeretici (si fuerit) non possit sciri, qui propter zelum veritatis studio vacare coeperunt: tamen satis videbitur manifeste, qui erunt sinceri & fortes fidei zelatores. ideo redi ad materiam in isto capitulo disserendam, & enumera alia vicia, quibus doctores, de quibus hic est sermo, reputantur impliciti: nec cures alias probationes adducere. MAGIST. Doctores isti putantur fautores haereticae prauitatis ambitiosi, avari, adulatores, propter excusationem vel assertionem doctrinae erroneae Papae haereticî: propter perversionem autem aliarum doctrinarum putantur inuidi, malitiosi, innocentiae persecutores, detractores, diffamatores, calumniatores, falsorum criminum impositores. unde in Spiritum sanctum multipliciter peccare censentur. propter utrumque autem vitium falsi, mendaces, fallaces, seductores, & fraudulenti credentur.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. From this I conjecture that if ever any Pope were to be manifestly heretical, it will clearly appear which teachers of that time laboured at their studies from zeal for catholic truth and to refute heretics (if ever they should arise), and which spent their efforts on earthly learning. MASTER. It seems to some that this is a deceptive conclusion, because, as Christ witnesses, many believe for a time and in the time of temptation fall away. But perhaps some, if the Pope were a heretic, will at the beginning labour with good zeal, and when the vexation and tribulation to be endured through a heretical Pope comes, they will cling most firmly to it. DISCIPLE. Although it will not appear to you that in a future time it cannot be known, if there are heretical Popes, who began to devote themselves to study out of zeal for the truth, yet it will plainly be evident who will be the sincere and strong defenders of the faith. Therefore return to the matter to be discussed in this chapter, and enumerate the other vices with which the teachers of whom we speak here are considered entangled; and do not trouble to bring other proofs. MASTER. These teachers are thought to be ambitious, avaricious and flatterers, supporters of the heretical depravity, on account of excusing or asserting the erroneous doctrine of the heretical Pope; but on account of perverting other doctrines they are thought to be envious, malicious, persecutors of innocence, detractors, defamers, calumniators, and imposers of false charges. Hence they are judged to sin in many ways against the Holy Spirit. And on account of both vices they are believed to be false, lying, deceitful, seducers and fraudulent.

units.la: DIS. Qua poena essent tales plectendi? MAGIST. Respondetur, quod tales omnibus poenis, quae debentur vitiis superius enumeratis, essent merito percellendi. unde dicitur, quod sunt excommunicati, & ab omni officio deponendi, imo videtur quibusdam, quod essent curiae seculari tradendi, vel perpetuo carceri mancipandi.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. What punishment should such men suffer? MASTER. It is answered that such men should rightly be visited with all the punishments that are due to the vices listed above. Hence it is said that they are to be excommunicated and deposed from every office; indeed some think they should be handed over to the secular authority or condemned to perpetual imprisonment.

units.la: CAP. LI.
units.tr: CAP. LI.

units.la: In quo inquiritur de religiosis non resistentibus doctrinae Papae haeretici, vtrum sint fautores prauitatis haereticae, & qualiter in casu se habere debeant.
units.tr: Inquiry into religious who do not resist the doctrine of a heretical Pope: whether they are to be counted as supporters of heretical depravity, and how they ought to conduct themselves in such a case.

units.la: DISCIP. De praedictis posset longus tractatus fieri: sed quia cupio, quod finis cito isti tractatui imponatur, ideo ad religiosos censeo transferendum de quibus interrogo, an religiosi, qui Papae haeretico non resistunt, sint inter fautores haereticae prauitatis computandi. MAG. De religiosis distinguitur. quidam enim religiosi regulariter aliquos de fratribus suis ad studium theologiae admittunt, pluribus etiam officium praedicationis & confessionis committunt, multique ex diuersis causis per mundum discurrunt, & de loco ad locum saepius mouentur. magnam tamen communicationem habent inter se, quantumcunque sint per mundum dispersi. unde accidit, quod ea quae publice fiunt non solum in Curia Romana, sed etiam in studiis generalibus, & in aliis locis frequentabilibus facilius, certius, & distinctius cognoscuntur ab eis. Alii sunt religiosi, qui ex consuetudine in certis locis continue residentes sua loca non mutant, raroque exeunt claustra sua, nec aliquos de fratribus ad studia vel ad alia loca transmittunt, ac diuersis locis manentes parvam vel nullam inter se communicationem habere noscuntur. & ideo de his saepe, quae in curia Romana & in aliis locis frequentabilibus publice fiunt, multa ignorant, quae aliis minime sunt ignota. ergo Papa esset haereticus publicus, hoc est publice diffiniens assertionem, quae est haeresis explicite condemnata, vel publice praedicans aut docens assertionem contra veritatem apud omnes catholicos diuulgatam: puta si publice praedicaret, Christum non fuisse natum de virgine, vel resurrectionem non esse futuram; aut non esse infernum, nec aliquas animas cruciari in inferno: contra praedictos religiosos esset violenta praesumptio, quod minime ignorarent Papam esse haereticum: quia tales religiosi ea, quae publice fiunt in curia Romana, non ignorant, cum tot literas sibi mutuo scribunt de nouitatibus, quae contingunt, quod vix aliquid notabile fit in curia Romana, quin cito & in breui tempore in omnibus locis eorum per vniuersum orbem publice cognoscatur. & ideo si adhaeserint Papae haeretico, fautores sunt. cum eius perfidia fuerit publicata, praesumendum est, quod scienter adhaerent prauitati haereticae: & ideo fautores haereticae prauitatis sunt censendi, si dixerint vel tenuerint Papam esse catholicum & fidelem.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. A long treatise could be written on the matters just mentioned, but since I wish this discussion to be brought to an end quickly, I think we should turn to the religious, and I ask: are religious who do not resist a heretical Pope to be counted among the supporters of heretical depravity? MASTER. A distinction must be made concerning religious. Some religious, as a rule, admit some of their brothers to the study of theology, entrust many with the office of preaching and hearing confession, and many, for various reasons, travel through the world and are moved often from place to place. Nevertheless, they keep up a great deal of communication among themselves, however widely they are scattered throughout the world. Hence it happens that what is done publicly not only in the Roman Curia but also in the general schools and other frequented places becomes known to them more easily, more certainly and more clearly. Others are religious who, by custom, remain continually in fixed places, do not change their abode, rarely leave their cloisters, and send none of their brothers to the schools or to other places; living in scattered locations, they are known to have little or no communication with one another. And so they often remain ignorant of many things that are done publicly in the Roman Curia and in other frequented places, things that are by no means unknown to others. Therefore, if the Pope were a public heretic, that is, one who publicly defines an assertion that has been explicitly condemned as heresy, or who publicly preaches or teaches an assertion against the truth that is spread abroad among all Catholics, for instance if he publicly preached that Christ was not born of a virgin, or that there will be no resurrection, or that there is no hell and that no souls are tormented in hell, then it would be a strong presumption against the aforesaid religious that they could not possibly be ignorant that the Pope is a heretic. For such religious do not fail to know what is publicly done in the Roman Curia, since they write so many letters to one another about the novelties that occur that scarcely anything noteworthy happens in the Roman Curia without being quickly and in a short time made publicly known in all their places throughout the whole world. Therefore, if they adhere to a heretical Pope, they are supporters of him. Once his perfidy has been made public, it must be presumed that they adhere knowingly to heretical depravity; and so they are to be counted supporters of heretical depravity if they have said or held that the Pope is Catholic and faithful.

units.la: DISCIP. Quid si non dixerint Papam esse catholicum & fidelem, tamen sibi obediunt de eius fidelitate aliqualiter se intromittendo.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. What if they have not said that the Pope is Catholic and faithful, but nevertheless obey him, in some way involving themselves in his faithfulness?

units.la: MAGIST. Respondetur a quibusdam, quod in hoc casu, si non possunt perfidiam Papae ne transfundatur ad alios prohibere, non sunt censendi fautores haereticae prauitatis: sed sunt fautores haeretici putandi: quia ex quo perfidiam Papae haeretici prohibere non possunt, nec credentes erroribus suis corrigere, nec ne alii credant eius erroribus impedire, tacendo de eius perfidia non videntur culpam incurrere: sed obediendo sibi a culpa minime sunt immunes.
units.tr: MASTER. Some answer that in this case, if they cannot prevent the Pope's perfidy from spreading to others, they are not to be counted supporters of heretical depravity, but are to be regarded as supporters of the heretic; for since they cannot prohibit the perfidy of the heretical Pope, nor correct those who believe his errors, nor prevent others from believing his errors, they do not seem to incur fault by keeping silent about his perfidy; but by obeying him they are by no means free from blame.

units.la: DIS. Dic de aliis religiosis. MAG. De aliis dicitur, quod non est praesumptio tam violenta contra eos, qui sciant vel teneantur scire Papam haereticum esse. & ideo non sunt subito iudicandi fauere haereticae prauitati, vel quia peccent Papae haeretico obediendo, sed examinandi sunt sollicite, an sciant Papa esse haereticum: vel propter illa quae audierunt teneantur hoc scire. & secundo hoc vel culpabiles vel à culpa liberi sunt censendi. si enim ignorant Papam esse haereticum, & non laborant crassa ignorantia & supina obediendo Papae haeretico, ab omni culpa sunt immunes. Si vero sciunt Papam esse haereticum, quia vel ignorant vel quia nolunt scire, & laborant ignorantia crassa & supina obediendo Papae haeretico, peccant mortaliter, nec possunt aliter excusari. DISCIP. Quid spectat ad religiosos facere, si Papa haereticus fuerit? MAGIST. Respondetur, quod ad primos religiosos, si sint praedicatores vel confessores, aut lectores, quando praedicant vel legunt, aut confessiones audiunt, spectat debitis circumstantiis observatis, auditoribus suis perfidiam Papae haretici nunciare, ut caveant doctrinam pestiferam eius. Ad alios autem quando vadunt per mundum, ut (quando est opportunitas) illis, quibus loquuntur, non publice praedicando, sed loquela simplici perfidiam Papae haretici studeant nunciare. Ad alios autem religiosos, si sciuerunt Papam esse haereticum, hoc spectat, quod sibi tanquam Papae nullo modo obediant: & modis sibi congruentibus alios ab obedientia eiusdem revocare tenentur.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Tell me about the other religious. MASTER. Concerning the others it is said that it is not so strong a presumption against those who know, or are bound to know, that the Pope is a heretic. And so they are not to be judged hastily as favouring heretical depravity, either because they obey a heretical Pope, but they must be carefully examined as to whether they know the Pope to be a heretic, or whether, because of what they have heard, they are bound to know this. And, secondly, they are to be judged either culpable or free from fault according to this. For if they do not know the Pope to be a heretic, and do not labour under gross and supine ignorance while obeying a heretical Pope, they are wholly free from blame. But if they know the Pope to be a heretic, whether because they are ignorant or because they are unwilling to know, and they labour under gross and supine ignorance while obeying a heretical Pope, they sin mortally, nor can they be excused otherwise. DISCIPLE. What is incumbent on religious to do if the Pope should be a heretic? MASTER. It is answered that, as for the first sort of religious, if they are preachers, confessors or lecturers, then when they preach or lecture, or hear confessions, it is incumbent on them, with due circumstances observed, to announce to their hearers the perfidy of the heretical Pope, so that they may beware of his pestilential doctrine. As for the others, when they travel through the world, they should, when there is opportunity, strive to announce the perfidy of the heretical Pope to those to whom they speak, not by public preaching but by simple conversation. As for the other religious, if they knew the Pope to be a heretic, it is incumbent on them that they in no way obey him as Pope, and they are bound by suitable means to call others back from obedience to him.

units.la: CAP. LII.
units.tr: CHAP. LII.

units.la: In quo quaeritur, de regibus & principibus in suis provinciis & regnis admittentibus docere doctrinam Papae haretici: utrum tales fautores haereticae pravitatis sint censendi.
units.tr: In which it is asked concerning kings and princes who, in their provinces and kingdoms, allow the doctrine of the heretical Pope to be taught: whether such men are to be counted as supporters of heretical depravity.

units.la: DISCIP. Consequenter de regibus & aliis publicis potestatibus & communitatibus aliqua interrogare propono. Dicautem in primis, an reges, qui permitterent, & principes doctrinam Papae haretici in suis regnis & dominiis publicari & doceri, essent inter fautores haereticae pravitatis computandi. MAGIST. Videtur nonnullis de regibus & principibus distinguendum: quia aut sunt omnino illiterati, aut literati & noticiam sanctarum scripturarum habentes. si sunt in sacris literis eruditi, & doctrina Papae erronea est tam patenter haeretica, quod omnes catholici in sacris literis eruditi sciunt eam esse haereticam, reges & principes scientes per sacras literas doctrinam Papae esse erroneam, sunt fautores haereticae pravitatis: si eam sustinent in suis regnis & dominiis publicari & doceri; nisi ex causis probabilibus & verisimilibus aestimarent, quod si opponerent se publicae doctrinae Papae erroneae, nulla exaltatio fidei vel utilitas fidelium sequeretur. Sed catholici per talem oppositionem regum & principum corporaliter & spiritualiter turbarentur, & plures propter talem turbationem vel contradictionem auerterentur a fide, & ad perfidiam Papae haretici se transferrent. DISCIP. Ista opinio casum pene impossibilem & incredibilem videtur innuere. non enim videtur credibile, quod si aliquis rex doctrinam Papae haretici in suo regno publicari & doceri omnimode prohiberet, tum quia propter hoc plures averterentur a fide & ad doctrinam Papae erroneam se transferrent. tum etiam si rex aliquis Papam haereticum captiuaret, & neci corporaliter traderet; nec sibi nec suis magnum periculum immineret. vidimus enim his diebus, quod non solum reges & principes: sed etiam civitates & castra satis parvae potentiae summo pontifici praesumunt resistere, nec tamen multi eorum corporaliter humiliantur; quanto magis si rex potens & dives Papam captivaret haereticum, qui nec esset magni generis & nobilis, nec liberos relinqueret divites & potentes, periculum corporale nullatenus formidare deberet. unde & hoc omnino mihi videtur probabile, quod rex absque periculo temporali posset secure Papam haereticum captivare & eum corporaliter trucidare. sed an hoc facere ex conscientia tenetur, non est mihi clarum. de quo casu aliqualiter pertractatum est supra lib. 6. ideo revertere ad opinionem priorem, & narra quid teneant de regibus & principibus illiteratis. MAGIST. Dicitur quod reges illiterati, qui noticia scripturarum minime pollent, in plurimis excusantur, si permittant dictam doctrinam in suis regnis & dominiis publicari & doceri: quia propter scripturarum ignorantiam non tenentur statim prohibere doctrinam Papae haeretici: praesertim si eis a literatis viris minime intimatur, quod doctrina Papae sapit haereticam pravitatem; & doctrina Papae erronea est talis, quod est directe contra veritatem catholicam apud omnes catholicos divulgatam. dicunt igitur isti, quod si doctrina erronea Papae haeretici est contra veritatem catholicam apud omnes catholicos divulgatam; reges quantumcunque illiterati, si scienter sustinerent eam in suis regnis & dominiis publicari, docere & teneri: nisi probabiliter timeatur, quod ex prohibitione talis doctrinae nulla spiritualis utilitas sequeretur, & periculose catholici turbarentur, sunt inter fautores pravitatis haereticae computandi. Si vero doctrina Papae haeretici erronea non est contra veritatem catholicam apud omnes divulgatam: sed est contra veritatem catholicam, quam reges & principes credere explicite non tenentur, licet debeant eandem credere implicite, distinguitur. quia aut ad noticiam regum & principum per clamorem & rumorem vulgi publicum & manifestum pervenit, quod doctrina Papae a viris literatis in scripturis divinis, qui hactenus bonae opinionis sunt & famae, fortiter & efficaciter impugnatur. qui etiam petunt instanter, ut de Papa haeretico vel de se, si erraverint, fiat. fiat iustitiæ complementum, aut talis notitia ad reges & principes perueniat ex zelo fidei, quam omnibus bonis praeferre tenentur; tunc debent diligentissime facere examinare doctrinam Papæ per sapientes, si habeant in regnis suis vel per alios, si in regnis non sint sufficientes ad examinationem talem, & secundum vnam sententiam prohibere debent ne doctrina talis in regnis eorum & dominiis publicetur & doceatur, antequam fuerit sufficienter discussa & examinata, secundum veram aliam sententiam, antequam constiterit legitime regibus doctrinam Papæ esse erroneam, eam prohibere non debent. In secundo etiam casu reges & principes prohibere doctrinam Papæ erroneam non tenentur; quia neque per certitudinem, neque per famam constat eis doctrinam Papæ esse erroneam.
units.tr: DISCIPLE: Next, I propose to ask about kings and other public powers and communities. Tell me first whether kings who permitted the doctrine of the heretical Pope to be published and taught in their kingdoms and dominions should be counted among the supporters of heretical depravity. MASTER: Some think a distinction must be made between kings and princes, since they are either wholly unlettered or learned and acquainted with the holy Scriptures. If they are learned in the sacred letters, and the doctrine of the Pope is so plainly heretical that all Catholics learned in the sacred letters know it to be heretical, then kings and princes who know from the sacred letters that the doctrine of the Pope is erroneous, and who allow it to be published and taught in their kingdoms and dominions, are supporters of heretical depravity, unless they judged on probable and plausible grounds that, if they opposed the public teaching of the erroneous doctrine of the Pope, no advance of the faith or benefit to the faithful would follow. Rather, the Catholics would be disturbed in body and soul by such opposition by the kings and princes, and many would be turned away from the faith by such disturbance or contradiction and would pass over to the perfidy of the heretical Pope. DISCIPLE: This opinion seems to suggest a case that is almost impossible and incredible. For it does not seem credible that, if some king should utterly forbid the doctrine of the heretical Pope to be published and taught in his kingdom, then many would be turned away from the faith and pass over to the erroneous doctrine of the Pope because of it. Nor, even if some king were to take the heretical Pope captive and hand him over to death in body, would great danger threaten him or his. For we have seen in these days that not only kings and princes, but even cities and castles of quite modest power, presume to resist the supreme Pontiff, and yet many of them are not humbled in body. How much more, then, if a powerful and rich king should take captive a heretical Pope who was neither of great or noble family nor left behind rich and powerful children, ought he to fear no bodily danger at all? Hence this also seems to me entirely probable: that a king, without temporal danger, could safely take the heretical Pope captive and slaughter him in body. But whether he is bound in conscience to do this, is not clear to me. This case has been treated to some extent above, book 6, so let us return to the earlier opinion, and tell me what they hold about unlettered kings and princes. MASTER: It is said that unlettered kings, who have little knowledge of the Scriptures, are for the most part excused if they permit the said doctrine to be published and taught in their kingdoms and dominions, because on account of their ignorance of the Scriptures they are not immediately bound to forbid the doctrine of the heretical Pope, especially if learned men have not made it clear to them that the doctrine of the Pope savors of heretical depravity. And the erroneous doctrine of the Pope is of such a kind that it is directly contrary to the Catholic truth made known among all Catholics. These men therefore say that if the erroneous doctrine of the heretical Pope is contrary to the Catholic truth made known among all Catholics, then kings, however unlettered, who knowingly allow it to be published, taught and held in their kingdoms and dominions, are to be counted among the supporters of heretical depravity, unless it is probably feared that from the prohibition of such doctrine no spiritual benefit would follow and Catholics would be dangerously disturbed. But if the erroneous doctrine of the heretical Pope is not contrary to the Catholic truth made known among all, but is contrary to a Catholic truth which kings and princes are not bound to believe explicitly, although they ought to believe it implicitly, a distinction is drawn. For either it has come to the notice of kings and princes, by the public clamor and rumor of the common people, that the doctrine of the Pope is strongly and effectively attacked by learned men in the divine Scriptures, men who until now have been of good opinion and reputation, and who also urgently ask that let it be done against the heretical Pope, or against themselves if they have erred, so that the fulfilment of justice may follow; or such knowledge reaches kings and princes out of zeal for the faith, which they are bound to prefer to all good things. In that case they must have the doctrine of the Pope examined most diligently by wise men, if they have such men in their kingdoms, or, if they lack men sufficient for such an examination within their kingdoms, by others. And according to one opinion they ought to forbid that such doctrine be published and taught in their kingdoms and dominions before it has been sufficiently discussed and examined; but according to the other, true opinion, they ought not to forbid it until it has been lawfully established for the kings that the doctrine of the Pope is erroneous. In the second case also, kings and princes are not bound to forbid the erroneous doctrine of the Pope, because it is established for them neither by certainty nor by report that the doctrine of the Pope is erroneous.

units.la: CAP. LIII.
units.tr: CAP. LIII.

units.la: In quo ostenditur, quid agendum sit regibus potentiam Papæ non formidantibus, si perceperint à fide dignis doctrinam Papæ esse haereticam.
units.tr: In which it is shown what must be done by kings who do not fear the power of the Pope, if they have learned from trustworthy men that the Pope's doctrine is heretical.

units.la: DISCIP. Circa ista narrata peto, vt tria tantum modo probare conetris. Quorum primum est, quod si reges & principes, qui potentiam temporalem Papæ & suorum nequaquam metuerent, audierint Papam de doctrina erronea à viris in sacra pagina eruditis & qui semper antea bonæ opinionis & famæ fuerunt, fortiter impugnari, & ab eisdem peritis cum instantia petatur concilium generale, vt veritas fidei declaretur, tenerentur diligenter quaerere veritatem & efficaciter laborare, vt per concilium generale vel alium modum congruum veritas fidei ostendatur; quod tamen praedicatores seu doctores non possunt faciliter scire. Secundum est, quod reges & principes, si per quemcunque modum legitime constiterit eis doctrinam Papæ esse erroneam, tenentur (ne publicetur & doceatur in suis regnis & suis dominiis) prohibere, si propter talem prohibitionem non timent dispendium populi Christiani. Tertium est, quod si rex aliquis propter potentiam temporalem Papæ haereticI vel suorum sequacium probabiliter & ex causis vrgentibus formidaret, quod ex prohibitione doctrinae Papæ haeretici in suo regno nulla utilitas neque temporalis neque spiritualis fidelium sequeretur, sed magis catholici turbarentur, & plures auerterentur à fide, à tali prohibitione doctrinae Papæ erroneae cessare deberet. MAGIST. Primum & secundum simul videntur vna ratione posse probari, quae talis est. Ille ad quem spectat omnem prauitatem haereticam extirpare, & ne in terra sibi subiecta pullulet impedire, tenetur modo praedicto de doctrina Papæ erronea taliter impugnata, qua Papa haereticus omnes cupit inficere orthodoxos, diligenter inquirere, an sit consona vel dissona catholicae veritati. Si enim circa talem inquisitionem negligens appareret, propter negligentiam eius possent sibi subditi periculose corrumpi haeretica prauitate. Sed reges & principes Christiani debent omnem haereticam prauitatem extirpare, quantum in eis est, & ne in terris eis subiectis pullulet impedire. Ergo si audierint doctrinam Papæ haereticam, qua omnes cupit inficere orthodoxos, à viris peritis in sacra pagina impugnari, debent sollicite quaerere veritatem, an scilicet doctrina Papæ erronea sit consona vel dissona catholicae veritari. Maior istius rationis videtur evidens, & tamen probatur. Primo sic: cui conuenit potestas aliquid faciendi, omnia ad ipsum pertinere noscuntur, per quae illud conuenienter facere potest. Quemadmodum si aliqua causa alicui committitur super omnia, quae ad ipsam causam pertinere noscuntur, plenariam recepit potestatem; & sic concesso principali conceditur accessorium, extra de officio dele. c. propter & c. significasti & ta. prudenter. & c. suspicionis. Si ergo regibus & principibus competit haereticam prauitatem, ne in terris sibi subiectis pullulet, impedire, & hoc interdum facere non possunt, nisi diligenter inquirant, an doctrina Papæ, ad quam omnes intendit cogere Christianos, sit consona vel dissona veritari. Sequitur quod tunc saltem debent talem inquisitionem facere, quando eis per famam publicam nunciatur, quod doctrina Papæ, quam in terris eorum publicae proponit, à viris peritis in sacris literis impugnatur, qui toto posse laborant, vt veritas fidei declaretur. Secundo probatur eadem maior, sic.
