Sicut ad eundem spectat de personis diffamatis inquirere & de accusatis secundum iuris ordinem iudicare: ita ad eundem spectat de aliqua prauitate publice nunciati diligenter inquirere veritatem, ad quem spectat eandem prauitatem si aperte perpetrata fuerit extirpare. Sed ad reges & principes spectat prauitatem haereticam Papæ haeretici, si eam aperte cognouerint in suis regnis & dominiis pullulasse, penitus extirpare. Ergo ad eosdem spectat, si publice fuerit nunciatum, quod doctrina Papæ, quam in regnis eorum & dominiis plantare conatur, à viris eruditis tanquam haeretica impugnatur, diligenter inquirere veritatem. Tertio sic: Ad quem spectat periculis, quae nouiter emergunt, obuiare: spectat ad eundem de periculis, quae per famam publicam nunciantur, quaerere veritatem. Sicut ad quem spectat hostibus inuadentibus terram aliquam toto posse resistere: ad eundem spectat (si est publica fama, quod aliqui volunt eandem terram inuadere) diligenter inquirere veritatem. Igitur si fama est super haeresi debet diligenter inquirere, an contineat veritatem, vt ad resistendum sit minime imparatus, quia secundum beatum Greg. minus incule feriunt, quae praeuidentur. Vnde & quidam saluberrimum mum dans consilium; prospicet, qui venium hoc casus esse ferendos. Nam levius ladii, quicquid pro-ri. cum ergo, si doctrina Papae est erronea, non modicum periculum toti Christianitati immineat, ad quos spectat prauitatem haereticam extirpare: ad eosdem spectat de doctrina Papae, quae tanquam haeretica a viris in sacris literis eruditis fortiter impugnatur, postquam per famam publicam hoc eis constiterit, diligenter inquirere veritatem. Sic ergo probata est maior: minor, scilicet quod ad reges & principes spectat omnem prauitatem haereticam de eorum terris & dominiis extirpare, & ne pullulet impedire, probatur sic. Qui propter haereticos de terra sua fugere non tenetur, nec tamen debet communicare eisdem, nec eosdem quomodolibet receptare, tenentur eos de terra fugare, vel etiam captiuare, vel penitus extirpare. reges autem vel principes propter Papam haereticum vel sequaces eius non debet de terra sua recedere, nec debent communicare eisdem, nec eos quomodolibet recipere. ergo possunt eos de terra sua fugare, aut etiam captiuare, vel penitus extirpare. qui autem talem obtinet super haereticos potestatem, debere terram suam de omni prauitate haeretica expurgare dinoscitur: quia terra de haereticis expurgata dinoscitur iuste regulata. patet ergo, quod spectat ad reges & principes impedire, ne doctrina Papae erronea in eorum regnis & dominiis diuulgetur, aut quomodolibet teneatur. qui autem potest facinus prohibere, & non prohibet, cum tamen hoc ad ipsum pertineat, eidem facinori fauet. reges ergo & principes, qui sciunt doctrinam Papae esse haereticam, laborant ignorantia crassa & supina: quia nolunt scire doctrinam Papae esse erroneam, aut negligunt indagare. Si non prohibent eam in suis regnis & dominiis, sunt inter fautores prauitatis haereticae computandi.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Concerning these matters, I ask you to prove only three things. The first is that if kings and princes, who by no means fear the temporal power of the Pope and his followers, hear that the Pope's erroneous doctrine is being strongly attacked by men learned in Holy Scripture, men who have always been of good opinion and reputation before, and that these same experts earnestly demand a general council so that the truth of the faith may be declared, then they are bound to seek the truth diligently and to work hard so that the truth of the faith may be shown through a general council or some other suitable means. Yet preachers or teachers cannot easily know this. The second is that kings and princes, if it has been legitimately established to them by any means that the Pope's doctrine is erroneous, are bound to prohibit it from being published and taught in their kingdoms and dominions, provided that for such a prohibition they do not fear loss to the Christian people. The third is that if some king, because of the temporal power of the Pope or of his heretical followers, reasonably and for pressing reasons feared that no temporal or spiritual benefit to the faithful would follow from prohibiting the Pope's heretical doctrine in his kingdom, but that rather the Catholics would be troubled and more would be turned away from the faith, he ought to refrain from such a prohibition of the Pope's erroneous doctrine. MASTER. The first and second seem to be provable together by one argument, which is this. He to whom it belongs to root out all heretical depravity and to prevent it from sprouting in the land subject to him is bound, in the manner described, when the Pope's erroneous doctrine has been so strongly attacked, by which the heretical Pope seeks to infect all the orthodox, to inquire diligently whether it agrees or disagrees with Catholic truth. For if he appeared negligent in such an inquiry, through his negligence his subjects could be dangerously corrupted by heretical depravity. But Christian kings and princes ought to root out all heretical depravity, as far as lies in them, and to prevent it from sprouting in the lands subject to them. Therefore, if they hear that the Pope's heretical doctrine, by which he wishes to infect all the orthodox, is being attacked by men skilled in Holy Scripture, they ought earnestly to seek the truth, namely whether the Pope's erroneous doctrine agrees or disagrees with Catholic truth. The major premise of this argument seems evident, and yet it is proved. First, thus: to whomever the power to do something belongs, all those things are known to pertain to him through which he can properly do that thing. Just as, if a case is committed to someone over all matters that are known to pertain to that case, he receives full power; and thus, when the principal matter is granted, the accessory is granted too (Extra, De officio delegati, c. Propter, c. Significasti, and c. Prudenter; and c. Suspicionis). If therefore it belongs to kings and princes to prevent heretical depravity from sprouting in the lands subject to them, and they cannot sometimes do this unless they diligently inquire whether the Pope's doctrine, to which he intends to compel all Christians, agrees or disagrees with the truth, it follows that they must at least make such an inquiry when it is announced to them by public report that the Pope's doctrine, which he publicly proposes in their lands, is being attacked by men skilled in the sacred writings, who labour with all their strength that the truth of the faith may be declared. Second, the same major premise is proved thus. Just as it belongs to the same person to inquire into persons who are defamed and to judge the accused according to the order of law, so it belongs to the same person to diligently inquire into the truth of some depravity publicly reported, to whom it belongs to root out that same depravity if it has been openly committed. But it belongs to kings and princes to root out completely the heretical depravity of a heretical Pope, if they have openly recognised it sprouting in their kingdoms and dominions. Therefore it belongs to the same persons, if it is publicly announced that the Pope's doctrine, which he tries to plant in their kingdoms and dominions, is being attacked as heretical by learned men, to inquire diligently into the truth. Third, thus: it belongs to the one to whom it pertains to meet dangers that newly emerge, to the same person it belongs to seek the truth about dangers announced by public report. Just as it belongs to the one to whom it pertains to resist with all his strength enemies invading some land, so it belongs to the same person (if there is public report that some persons wish to invade that land) to inquire diligently into the truth. Therefore, if there is a report about heresy, he ought to inquire diligently whether it contains the truth, so that he may not be wholly unprepared to resist, because, as blessed Gregory says, things foreseen strike less harshly. Hence also someone giving most wholesome advice: let him who knows such cases must be borne provide for them, for whatever is foreseen wounds more lightly. Since therefore, if the Pope's doctrine is erroneous, no small danger hangs over the whole of Christendom, those to whom it belongs to root out heretical depravity must, after it has been established to them by public report that the Pope's doctrine is being strongly attacked as heretical by men learned in the sacred writings, diligently inquire into the truth. Thus the major premise has been proved. The minor, namely that it belongs to kings and princes to root out all heretical depravity from their lands and dominions and to prevent it from sprouting, is proved thus. He who is not bound to flee from his land because of heretics, yet ought not to have fellowship with them nor in any way receive them, is bound to drive them from the land, or even to imprison them, or to root them out completely. But kings or princes ought not to leave their land because of a heretical Pope or his followers, nor ought they to have fellowship with them, nor in any way receive them. Therefore they can drive them from their land, or even imprison them, or root them out completely. But he who holds such power over heretics is known to be bound to cleanse his land of all heretical depravity, for a land cleansed of heretics is known to be justly governed. It is clear therefore that it belongs to kings and princes to prevent the Pope's erroneous doctrine from being spread or in any way held in their kingdoms and dominions. But he who can prohibit a crime and does not, although this pertains to him, favours that same crime. Kings and princes therefore, who know the Pope's doctrine to be heretical, labour under gross and culpable ignorance, because they are unwilling to know that the Pope's doctrine is erroneous, or neglect to investigate it. If they do not prohibit it in their kingdoms and dominions, they must be counted among the supporters of heretical depravity.

units.la: CAP. LIV.
units.tr: CAP. LIV.

units.la: Vbi agitur de regibus & principibus potestatem Papae haeretici timentibus, aut quodcunque aliud incommodum temporale siue spirituale formidantibus, quid illis sit agendum, quod fuit tertium quaesitum capituli praecedentis.
units.tr: Here it is treated of kings and princes who fear the power of the heretical Pope, or dread any other temporal or spiritual inconvenience, and of what they ought to do. This was the third question of the preceding chapter.

units.la: DISCIP. Haec, vt puto, ab his quae tractata sunt libro 6. c. 99. dependent. ideo his omissis, quod sup. c. 51. promisisti, probare coneris. MAG. Tertium ibi promissum est, quod si rex aliquis propter temporalem potentiam Papae haeretici & suorum sequacium vel sibi fauentium probabiliter & ex causis vrgentibus formidaret, quod ex prohibitione doctrinae Papae haeretici in regno suo nulla vtilitas neque spiritualis neque temporalis fidelium sequeretur: sed magis catholici turbarentur, & plures auerterentur a fide, a tali prohibitione cessare deberent, & quod talis doctrina publicaretur & docereturin regno suo sustinere. quod videretur posse probari. Primo sic; Oportet regem, sicut & quemlibet alium sapientem, extremam dementiam declinare. Sed talis prohibitio esset extrema dementia, & frustra niti, & nihil nisi turbationem bonorum quaerere. quoniam frustra niti & nil nisi odium quaerere, extremae dementiae est, Hieron. attestante qui approbando sententiam cuiusdam ait in prologo Esdrae: frustra autem, vt ait quidam, niti, nec aliud se fatigando nisi odium quaerere, extrema dementia est. ergo rex, qui per prohibitionem huiusmodi nil nisi perturbationem fidelium quaereret, a tali deberet turbatione cessare.
units.tr: DISCIPULUS: I think these matters depend on what was treated in book 6, chapter 99. So, leaving those aside, you try to prove what you promised above in chapter 51. MAGISTER: The third thing promised there was this: if some king, because of the temporal power of the heretical Pope and his followers or supporters, feared with good reason and for pressing causes that no spiritual or temporal benefit would come to the faithful from forbidding the erroneous doctrine of the Pope in his kingdom, but that rather the Catholics would be disturbed and more would turn away from the faith, then he ought to refrain from such a prohibition, and tolerate that such a doctrine be published and taught in his kingdom. This seemed capable of proof. First, thus: a king, like any other wise man, ought to avoid extreme folly. But such a prohibition would be extreme folly, to strive in vain and to seek nothing but the disturbance of good people. For to strive in vain and to seek nothing but hatred is extreme folly, as Jerome bears witness, who, approving the opinion of a certain writer, says in the prologue to Ezra: "to strive in vain, as someone says, and to weary oneself seeking nothing but hatred, is extreme folly." Therefore a king who, by such a prohibition, sought nothing but the disturbance of the faithful, ought to cease from such disturbance. Second, thus: the prohibition of the erroneous doctrine of the Pope must be omitted no less, for the sake of avoiding disturbance of the faithful without any benefit to them or even to unbelievers, than correction must be omitted for the sake of avoiding schism. For schism is recognized as to be avoided because it is harmful to Christendom; but disturbance of the faithful, without any benefit to them, is likewise harmful to Christendom. Therefore, just as schism is to be avoided, so the disturbance of the faithful without benefit to them is wholly to be shunned. But for the sake of avoiding schism correction must be omitted, as Augustine teaches in his work against the letter of Parmenianus, as is read in 23 q. 4: "When any of the brethren and Christians established in the fellowship of the Church has been caught in some such sin that he deserves anathema, let this be done so that there is no persecution of the schism. And below: when someone's crime is known and appears detestable to all, let not the severity of discipline sleep, so that he has no defenders at all, or none of such a kind, through whom a schism could arise." From which it is gathered that, for the sake of avoiding schism, one must cease from the severity of correction and discipline. Likewise, therefore, for the sake of avoiding disturbance of the faithful, a king must for a time cease from prohibiting the erroneous doctrine of the Pope.

units.la: Secundo sic: Non minus omittenda est prohibitio doctrinae erroneae Papae, propter vitandam turbationem fidelium absque omni vtilitate eorum & etiam infidelium, quam sit omittenda correctio propter schisma vitandum; quia schisma vitandum dinoscitur, quia est Christianitati nocium; sed turbatio sic fidelium absque omni eorum vtilitate est Christiani ati nocita. ergo sicut schisma vitandum est; ita tubatio fidelium absque eorum vtilitate est penitus declinanda. Sed propter schisma vitandum est omittenda correctio, teste Augustin qui contra epistolam Parmeniani, vt legitur 23. q. 4. cum quisque, ait; Cum quisque fratrum & Christianorum in ecclesia societate constitutorum in aliquo tali peccato fuerit deprehensus, vt anathemate dignus habeatur, fiat hoc vt persecutio schismatis nullum est. & infra: quando cuiusquam crimen notum est & omnib. execrabile appareat, vt vel nullos prorsus vel non tales habeat defensores, per quos possit schisma contingere, non dormiat seueritas disciplinae. Ex quibus colligitur, quod propter schisma vitandum a seueritate correctionis & disciplinae oportet cessare. igitur & consimiliter propter turbationem fidelium declinandam oportet regem a prohibitione doctrinae Papae erroneae, ad tempus cessare.
units.tr: Secondly, thus: The prohibition of the Pope's erroneous doctrine must no less be set aside, in order to avoid disturbing the faithful, when it brings no benefit to them or even to unbelievers, than correction must be set aside in order to avoid schism. For schism is to be avoided because it is recognised as harmful to Christendom; but such disturbance of the faithful, bringing them no benefit, is also harmful to Christendom. Therefore, just as schism is to be avoided, so the disturbance of the faithful without benefit to them is to be wholly avoided. But correction must be set aside for the sake of avoiding schism, as Augustine teaches in his work against the letter of Parmenianus, as read at 23 q. 4: "When any one of the brothers and Christians established in the fellowship of the Church is caught in some such sin that he deserves anathema, let this be done so that there is no persecution of the schism. And below: when someone's crime is known and appears detestable to all, so that he has no defenders at all, or none of such a kind through whom schism could arise, let not the severity of discipline sleep." From these words it is concluded that, for the sake of avoiding schism, severity of correction and discipline must cease. Therefore, similarly, for the sake of avoiding disturbance of the faithful, the king ought for a time to cease from prohibiting the Pope's erroneous doctrine.

units.la: DISCIP. Dicitur forte, quod secus est, quando fides impugnatur, & quando alia peccata committuntur. licet enim a correctione aliorum excessuum sit cessandum propter schisma vitandum, tamen quando fides impugnatur, oportet illos, ad quos spectat, resistere; quia vt allegatum est, in decretis. 7. q. 1. c. aduersitas. §. cum vero, sic legitur: Cum vero non praedatorum tantum, sed totius ecclesiae salus quaeritur (fides impugnatur) necesse est vt ex aduerso ascendant, & in die belli seipsos vt murum opponant pro domo domini, animas suas ponant pro ouibus suis, vt exemplo sua passionis accendant, quos sermone doctrina diutius confirmare non valent. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod cum fides impugnatur, praelati non debent tacere aut dissimulare; sed resistere debent vsque ad sanguinem, ergo ratione consimili reges, quando impugnatur fides, visque ad mortem tenentur resistere. quia sicut praelatos oportet ecclesiam defendere sermone, doctrina, & vita bona, ac tandem si oportuerit passione: ita & reges per potentiam temporalem ecclesiam defendere tenentur. quare si Papa haereticus fidem impugnat, reges & principes dissimulare minime debent, imo sibi debent resistere viriliter & potenter etiam visque ad mortem, iuxta illud Sapientis; visque ad mortem certa pro iustitia. & eadem ratione certandum est magis visque ad mortem pro fide, quam pro quacunque humana iustitia aut patria vel subiectis aut re temporali quacunque.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. It may perhaps be said that the case is different when the faith is attacked, and when other sins are committed. For although correction of other excesses must cease for the sake of avoiding schism, nevertheless when the faith is attacked, those to whom it belongs must resist, because, as has been cited in the decretals, 7 q. 1, c. Adversitas, §. cum vero, it reads thus: "But when the safety not only of the plunderers but of the whole Church is sought (the faith is attacked), it is necessary that they go up against the enemy and, in the day of battle, set themselves as a wall before the house of the Lord, and lay down their souls for their sheep, so that by the example of their suffering they may kindle those whom they cannot longer strengthen by sermon and teaching." From these words it is gathered that when the faith is attacked, prelates ought not to be silent or to dissemble, but must resist even unto blood. Therefore, by a similar reasoning, when the faith is attacked, kings are bound to resist even unto death. For just as prelates must defend the Church by word, teaching and a good life, and at last by suffering if need be, so kings too are bound to defend the Church by temporal power. Wherefore, if a heretical Pope attacks the faith, kings and princes ought by no means to dissemble; rather they ought to resist him manfully and powerfully, even unto death, according to that saying of the Wise Man: "Even unto death, fight for righteousness." And for the same reason one must fight even more unto death for the faith than for any human justice, or for one's country, subjects, or any temporal thing whatever.

units.la: MAGIST. Respondetur quod rationem praedictam nequaquam intelligis, non enim intendit, quod nunquam spectat ad reges & principes etiam visque ad mortem pro fide certare catholica: sed vult, quod cum ex certatione nulla penitus speratur utilitas, sed de notabili & periculosa & perniciosa turbatione probabili dubitatur, abstinendum est ad tempus a tali certamine exemplo beatorum Petri & Pauli ac aliorum plurimorum sanctorum, qui interdum non tantummodo certantibus minime restiterunt, sed etiam fugerunt de loco certaminis. vbi autem reges & principes ex certamine tali & resistentia ac prohibitione doctrinae Papae erroneae fructum aliquem spiritualem sperarent, etiam visque ad mortem oportet eos, si velint veri catholici reputari, doctrinae Papae resistere & eam in suis regnis & dominiis prohibere. quemadmodum praelati, quando exemplo suae passionis possent subiectos accendere, quos sermone doctrinae confirmare nullatenus poterint, debent ascendere ex adverso & animas suas pro ouibus ponere. cum dicitur ergo, cum vero non praelatorum tantum, &c. Respondetur, quod quando fides impugnatur & ex passione speratur pro fide, quod catholici confirmabuntur in fide: tunc praelati debent mortem suscipere. si autem ex passione sua confirmationem fidelium non sperarent, sed timerent quod post mortem suam fideles infirmi in fide catholica fluctuarent, debent mortem fugiendo vel dissimulando vitare, & alio tempore, quo valerent fructum facere, expectare. cuius sententiae videtur esse beatus Greg. qui in libro dialogorum, vt habetur 7. q. 1. c. vbi, ait: Vbi omnino fructus de bonis deest, fit aliquando de malis labor superuacuus: maxime si e vicino causa suppetant, quae fructum valeant Deo ferre meliorem. Saepe agitur in animo perfectorum, quod silentio praetereundum non est: quia cum laborem suum sine fructu esse considerant, in loco alio ad laborem cum fructu migrant. Vnde iste quoque egregius praedicator, qui dissolui cupiebat & esse cum Christo, cui Christus est viuere & mori lucrum, quia certamina passionum ipse non solum appetiit, sed etiam ad toleranda haec etiam aliis accendit, Damasci per secutionem passus, vt potuisset euadere, murum, sportam funemque quaesiuit, seque latenter deponi voluit. Nunquid vero Paulum dicimus mortem timuisse, quam seipsum pro amore Iesu attestatur appetere? sed cum in eodem loco minorem sibi fructum adesse conspiceret, ad grauem laborem se alibi cum fructu seruauit. fortis etenim praelator Dei teneri intra claustra noluit, sed certaminis campum quaesiuit. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod fidei zelatoribus licet intentione fructum faciendi maiorem campum certaminis pro tempore declinare. quare reges & principes, si viderint quod prohibitio doctrinae Papae erroneae in regnis & terris sibi subiectis est ad honorem fidei & fidelibus fructuosa, doctrinam Papae erroneam, ne inficere valeat orthodoxos, debent prohibere, & pro tali prohibitione tuenda etiam arma mouere. Exemplo sincerissimi zelatoris Dei legis Iudae Machabei, qui suos confortans ad bellum pro lege diuina, vt habetur, 1. Machab. 3. ait: accingiminifilii potentes & estote parati in mane, vt pugnetis aduersus nationes, quae venerunt disperdere nos & sancta nostra. quoniam melius est mori in bello quam videre interitum gentis nostrae & sanctorum. Tamen si rex aliquis aperte videret, quod sine fructu fidelium & cum contumelia perniciosa esset prohibere doctrinam Papae erroneam, dissimulare deberet, & tempus aliud expectare, quo cum fructu maiori doctrinam eandem pestiferam prohibere & de suo regno penitus extirpare valeret. DISCIP. Rationem praedictam intelligo, licet casus praedictus, quem innuit, mihi penitus impossibilis videatur. Ideo alias rationes ad assertionem eandem adducas. MAGIST. Tertia ratio principalis haec est. Non minus dissimulanda vel tolerանda est ad tempus conueniens doctrina Papae erronea propter stragem corporalem & spiritualem vel etiam tantummodo spiritualem populorum & multorum, quam propter stragem corporalem multorum vitandam, siue propter alios excessus seueritatis, correctionis & iustitiae detrahendum. sed propter stragem multorum vitandam sunt alia flagitia minime punienda, teste Augustin. qui scribens ad Bonifacium, vt habetur. d. 50. c. vt constitueretur, ait: vbi per grauei [...] fissuras non buius aut illius hominis periculum sed plurimorum strages spiritualis iacet, detrahendum est aliquid seueritati vt maioribus malis sanandis catholica sincera permaneat fides. Vnde conclusiliter, vbi sine fructu plurimorum strages spiritualis iaceret, ita vt plurimi auerterentur a fide, si rex prohiberet doctrinam Papae haereticam. ergo a prohibitione huiusmodi est abstinendum. Quarto sic: Sicut rex praeceptis & statutis aut etiam, si oportuerit, materialibus armis debet doctrinam Papae erroneam extirpare: ita praedicatores & doctores ac magistri apertis rationibus & scripturarum testimoniis debent doctrinam Papae erroneam impugnare. sed praedicatores & doctores ac magistri non debent sine fructu & cum turbatione fidelium doctrinam Papae erroneam expugnare, ipsa veritate retinente, quae ait Math 7. Nolite sanctum dare canibus: nec mittatis margaritas ante porcos. ergo nec rex sine fructu & cum turbatione fidelium debet in regno suo doctrinam Papae erroneam prohibere. sed tempus in quo valeat cum fructu extirpare ipse expectare tenetur. Quinto sic: Quod non est ad gloriam Dei, est minime faciendum: quia nihil nisi ad gloriam Dei fieri debet teste apostolo, qui 1. ad Corinth. 10. ait: Omnia quae qua facitis in gloriam Dei facite. qui etiam ad Colo. 3. ait: Omnia quæcunque facitis in verbo aut in opere, omnia in nomine domini nostri Iesu Christi facite. Sed prohibitio doctrinæ Papæ erroneæ sine omni vUlitate & cum turbatione fidelium non esset ad gloriam Dei. ergo in hoc casu rex non debet in suo regno doctrinam erroneam prohibere.
units.tr: MASTER. The answer is that you by no means understand the aforesaid reasoning. For it does not intend that it never belongs to kings and princes to contend even unto death for the Catholic faith; rather it means that when no benefit at all can be hoped for from the contention, but a notable, dangerous and destructive disturbance is probable and to be feared, one must for a time abstain from such a contest, following the example of the blessed Peter and Paul and many other saints, who sometimes not only did not resist those contending, but even fled from the place of the contest. But where kings and princes could hope for some spiritual fruit from such a contest, and from resisting and forbidding the Pope's erroneous doctrine, then, even unto death, they ought, if they wish to be counted true Catholics, to resist the Pope's doctrine and forbid it in their kingdoms and dominions. Just as prelates, when by the example of their suffering they could kindle their subjects whom they can in no way strengthen by sermon and teaching, ought to go up against the enemy and lay down their souls for their sheep. When it is said, therefore, "but when the safety not only of the prelates," etc., the answer is that when the faith is attacked, and it is hoped from suffering for the faith that Catholics will be strengthened in the faith, then prelates ought to undergo death. But if they did not hope for the confirmation of the faithful from their own suffering, and feared that after their death the weak faithful would waver in the Catholic faith, they ought by fleeing or dissembling to avoid death, and to wait for another time in which they might bear fruit. To this opinion the blessed Gregory seems to belong, who, in the book of Dialogues, as found in 7 q. 1, c. Ubi, says: "Where no fruit at all is to be had from good things, sometimes labour upon evil things becomes superfluous; especially if causes near at hand are available which can bring to God a better fruit. Often in the minds of the perfect it is felt that something must not be passed over in silence; for when they perceive that their labour is without fruit in one place, they move on to labour with fruit in another. Hence that outstanding preacher also, who desired to be dissolved and to be with Christ, for whom to live is Christ and to die is gain, because he not only sought the contests of suffering but also kindled others to endure them, when he suffered persecution at Damascus, in order that he might escape, sought a wall, a basket and a rope, and wished to be let down secretly. Shall we then say that Paul feared death, which he himself testifies that he desired for the love of Jesus? But since he saw that in that same place there was less fruit for him, he reserved himself with fruit for another place for heavy labour. For a strong minister of God would not be kept within the cloister, but sought the field of contest." From these words it is gathered that zealots for the faith may, with intent of bearing greater fruit, for a time decline from the contest to a larger field. Wherefore kings and princes, if they see that the prohibition of the Pope's erroneous doctrine in the lands and territories subject to them is fruitful for the honour of the faith and for the faithful, ought to forbid the Pope's erroneous doctrine, lest it be able to infect the orthodox, and for the defence of such prohibition ought even to take up arms. Following the example of the most sincere zealot for the law of God, Judas Maccabeus, who, encouraging his men to fight for the divine law, as is found in 1 Maccabees 3, said: "Gird yourselves, you mighty sons, and be ready in the morning to fight against the nations that have come to destroy us and our holy things. For it is better to die in battle than to see the ruin of our nation and of the saints." Yet if some king should clearly see that to forbid the Pope's erroneous doctrine would be without fruit for the faithful and attended with pernicious contumely, he ought to dissemble and wait for another time, in which he could forbid the same pestilent doctrine with greater fruit and root it wholly out of his kingdom. DISCIPLE. I understand the aforesaid reasoning, although the case you indicate seems to me wholly impossible. Therefore bring forward other reasons for the same assertion. MASTER. The third principal reason is this. The erroneous doctrine of the Pope must be no less dissembled or tolerated for a suitable time, on account of bodily and spiritual slaughter, or even merely spiritual slaughter, of peoples and of many, than severity, correction and justice are to be relaxed on account of avoiding bodily slaughter of many, or other excesses. But, as Augustine teaches, other crimes are not to be punished for the sake of avoiding the slaughter of many; he, writing to Boniface, as found in d. 50, c. Ut constitueretur, says: "Where, through grave [...] fissures, not the danger of this or that man but a spiritual slaughter of many lies, something must be taken away from severity, so that the sincere Catholic faith may remain for the healing of greater evils." Hence it is concluded that where a spiritual slaughter of many would lie without fruit, so that many would turn away from the faith, if the king were to forbid the heretical doctrine of the Pope, therefore one must abstain from such a prohibition. Fourth, thus: just as the king ought to root out the Pope's erroneous doctrine by edicts and statutes, or even, if need be, by material arms, so preachers, teachers and masters ought to attack the Pope's erroneous doctrine by plain reasons and testimonies of the Scriptures. But preachers, teachers and masters ought not to overthrow the Pope's erroneous doctrine without fruit and with disturbance of the faithful, since the truth itself holds, which says in Matthew 7: "Do not give what is holy to dogs, nor cast your pearls before swine." Therefore neither ought the king in his kingdom, without fruit and with disturbance of the faithful, to forbid the Pope's erroneous doctrine. But he is bound to wait for the time in which he may be able to root it out with fruit. Fifth, thus: what is not to the glory of God must by no means be done, because nothing ought to be done except to the glory of God, as the Apostle teaches, who says in 1 Corinthians 10: "Whatever you do, do it to the glory of God." He also says in Colossians 3: "Whatever you do in word or in deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ." But the prohibition of the Pope's erroneous doctrine, without any benefit and with disturbance of the faithful, would not be to the glory of God. Therefore in this case the king ought not to forbid the erroneous doctrine in his kingdom.

units.la: CAP. LV.
units.tr: CAP. LV.

units.la: Quærit, quid agendum sit publicis potestatibus, regibus inferiores si cognoverint aliquid de doctrina Papæ hæretici.
units.tr: Asks what ought to be done by public powers, lower than kings, if they have learned something about the doctrine of a heretical Pope.

units.la: DISCIP. Quia reor, quod si vnquam aliquis Papa fieret hæreticus, omni regi Christianitatis (si sapienter & prudenter processerit) facile erit absque omni notabili periculo spirituali vel corporali de regno suo doctrinam Papæ erroneam extirpare. & ideo si rex aliquis sustineat doctrinam erroneam in regno suo in terris sibi subiectis doceri, publicari & teneri, hoc accidet aut propter defectum zeli ad catholicam fidem, aut propter defectum sagacitatis & prudentiæ, aut propter cupiditatem pecuniæ aut divitiarum extorquendi à Papa hæretico, aut propter corruptionem aliam quæ ab omni rege Christiano elongari deberet. & ita opinor quod casus quæ prædicta opinio innuit, nunquam euenerit. ideo circa eandem opinionem non amplius immoreris: sed ad publicas potestates & communitates te conuerte: & dic an publicæ potestates, regibus & principibus inferiores, & communitates, si sustinuerint sequaces Papæ hæretici doctrinam eius erroneam diuulgare, docere & tenere, debeant inter fautores hæreticorum & prauitatis hæreticæ computari. MAGIST. Publicæ potestates regibus & principibus inferiores, & communitates, quantum ad fidem catholicam defendendam & prauitatem hæreticam extirpandam, à regibus & principibus nequaquam differre videntur: nisi quo ad potestatem temporalem. quia minoris potentiæ sunt communitates, quam reges & principes. & ideo nonnullis apparet, quod per illa, quæ dicta sunt de regibus & principibus, patere potest, quid de aliis simplicibus potestatibus sit tenendum. si enim aliqua publica potestas vel communitas est tantæ potentiæ, quod cum fructu spirituali potest doctrinam Papæ erroneam prohibere, ad hoc tenetur de necessitate salutis. si vero est tam paruæ potentiæ temporalis, quod ex prohibitione doctrinæ illius sequeretur turbatio fidelium absque omni fructu spirituali eandem dogmatizari licite sustinebit, & ad tempus aliud expectabit. DISCIP. Quomodo scietur an aliqua potestas vel communitas sit tantæ potentiæ, quod cum fructu spirituali poterit doctrinam Papæ erroneam extirpare vel prohibere? MAG. Respondetur, quod nequaquam quæcunque persona vel communitas est tantæ potentiæ, quando pro rebus temporalibus vel pro honoribus obtinendis vel retinendis, vel pro quocunque damno vel incommodo temporali vitando auderet Papæ sive catholico sive hæretico rebellare, & si se sciret tantæ potentiæ reputari, quod auderet & posset pro fide defendenda doctrinam Papæ erroneam prohibere, ad hoc teneretur. quod si non fecerit, censeri debet zelum fidei catholicæ non habere. imo fautrix hæreticæ prauitatis est meritò iudicanda, ad quamlibet personam & communitatem super alios potestatem habentem spectat sibi subiectos, cum potest, à prauitate hæretica præseruare. quod hoc ostenditur. aut prælati sunt solliciti prauitatem hæreticam Papæ hæretici extirpare: aut sunt damnabiliter negligentes. si sint solliciti, & non possunt per se eas extirpare, brachium inuocent seculare. seculares autem prælatis, ecclesiæ requisiti tenentur fideliter adiuuare, vt prauitas hæretica confundatur. ergo in hoc casu tenentur doctrinam Papæ erroneam prohibere. si autem prælati in extirpando hæreses Papæ & sequacium eius sunt damnabiliter negligentes, in hoc casu debent seculares minime requisiti, si possunt cum fructu spirituali prauitatem hæreticam & hæreticos extirpare. ergo vbi veritas catholica ad hoc, vt defendatur & prauitas hæretica vt confundatur, requirit operam seculburium super alios potestatem habentium; ipsi (si possunt cum fructu spirituali) de necessitate salutis sunt astricti doctrinam Papæ erroneam prohibere, & totis viribus impedire, ne dogmatizetur, ne publicata inficiat orthodoxos.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Because I think that if ever any Pope became a heretic, it would be easy for any king of Christendom (if he proceeded wisely and prudently) to root out the Pope's erroneous doctrine from his kingdom, without any notable spiritual or bodily danger. And therefore, if some king should tolerate an erroneous doctrine being taught, published and held in his kingdom among lands subject to him, this would happen either through lack of zeal for the Catholic faith, or through lack of shrewdness and prudence, or through greed for money or riches to be extorted from the heretical Pope, or through some other corruption which ought to be far removed from every Christian king. And so I suppose that the cases which this opinion suggests never happen. Therefore do not linger any longer over this opinion, but turn yourself to the public powers and communities, and say whether public powers lower than kings and princes, and communities, if they have allowed followers of a heretical Pope to spread, teach and hold his erroneous doctrine, ought to be counted among the supporters of heretics and heretical wickedness. MASTER. Public powers lower than kings and princes, and communities, seem in no way to differ from kings and princes in defending the Catholic faith and rooting out heretical wickedness, except in temporal power. For communities are of less power than kings and princes. And so it appears to some that what has been said of kings and princes makes clear what is to be held concerning other lesser powers. For if some public power or community is of such power that it can with spiritual profit forbid the Pope's erroneous doctrine, it is bound to do so by necessity of salvation. But if it is of such small temporal power that forbidding that doctrine would bring about disturbance of the faithful without any spiritual profit, it will rightly tolerate that doctrine being taught and will wait for another time. DISCIPLE. How will it be known whether some power or community is of such power that it can with spiritual profit root out or forbid the Pope's erroneous doctrine? MASTER. It is answered that no person or community is of such power when, for obtaining or retaining temporal goods or honours, or for avoiding any temporal loss or inconvenience, it would dare to rebel against the Pope, whether Catholic or heretical; and if it knew itself to be reckoned of such power that it would dare and be able to forbid the Pope's erroneous doctrine in defence of the faith, it is bound to do so. If it does not do so, it ought to be judged as lacking zeal for the Catholic faith. Indeed, it is rightly to be judged a promoter of heretical wickedness, any person or community having power over others, when it can, which is bound to preserve those subject to it from heretical wickedness. This is shown thus: either prelates are anxious to root out the heretical wickedness of a heretical Pope, or they are culpably negligent. If they are anxious, and cannot root it out by themselves, let them call upon the secular arm. Secular rulers, moreover, when requested by the prelates and the Church, are bound to help faithfully, so that heretical wickedness may be overthrown. Therefore in this case they are bound to forbid the Pope's erroneous doctrine. But if the prelates are culpably negligent in rooting out the heresies of the Pope and his followers, in this case the secular rulers ought not to wait to be requested, if they can root out the heretical wickedness and heretics with spiritual profit. Therefore, where Catholic truth requires, in order that it may be defended and heretical wickedness overthrown, the work of secular rulers over others having power, those rulers (if they can with spiritual profit) are bound by necessity of salvation to forbid the Pope's erroneous doctrine, and with all their strength to prevent it from being taught and from infecting the orthodox once published.

units.la: CAP. LVI.
units.tr: CHAP. LVI.

units.la: Tractat de simplicibus, quid de illis sit agendum in casu.
units.tr: Treats of simple people who hold no power over others: what is to be done about them in such a case.

units.la: DISCIP. Licet circa istam rationem possunt multa dubia & obiectiones multæ moueri, quia tamen ad ea poterit per prædecentia faciliter responderi, pertransibo: & de simplicibus nullam super alios potestatem habentibus interrogo, an sint fautores hæreticorum & hæreticæ prauitatis, si doctrinæ Papæ erroneæ non resistunt. MAG. Ista interrogatio dupliciter potest intelligi. quia aut intelligitur de aliqua tota multitudine simplicium, nullam super alios potestatem habentium: aut intelligitur de quolibet simplici tali, si intelligitur primo modo. Dicitur, quod si est tanta multitudo, quod cum fructu spirituali potest doctrinam Papæ erroneam prohibere, censenda est fauere hæreticis & hæreticæ prauitatis, si non resistit. Hoc probatur primo sic. Non minus tenetur multitudo talis defendere fidem & resistere destruentibus eam, quam tenetur resistere inuadentibus iniquè & iniustè socium vel patriam. sed talis multitudo tenetur resistere inuadentibus iniquè vel iniustè socium vel patriam. 23. quæst. tertia c. fortitudo, ergo multo magis tenetur resistere (si potest) destruentibus fidem. quare si papa vult fidem destruere & hæreticam inducere prauitatem, multitudo, quæ potest sibi resistere, debet ei viriliter obuiare, & ne inficiat catholicos impedire. Secundo sic. ad quos spectat Christum defendere, ad eosdem spectat fidem eius defendere. sed ad multitudinem nequaquam super alios potestatem habentem pertinet defendere Christum, teste August. vt allegatum est supra. 23. q. 3. cap. ultim. vbi ait: ostendit propheta, nec illos immunes esse à scelere, qui permiserunt principibus Christum interficere, cum pra multitudine timerentur, & possent illos à facto & se à consensu liberare. ergo ad multitudinem spectat fidem Christi defendere: nec sunt immunes à scelere, si permittunt papæ, prælatis, regibus, & principibus & publicis potestatibus quibuscunque fidem subuere orthodoxam: si pre multitudine timentur, & possunt illos à facto & se à consensu liberare. quia sicut dicit Augustin. ibidem: Qui desinit obuiare cum potest peruersis, & non facit, consentire videtur. & ideo si multitudo Christianorum super alios potestatem nequaquam habentium posset resistere doctrinæ papæ erroneæ, & non faceret, consentiret eidem. similiter multitudo simplicium in vno regno vel in vno Ducatu vel in vna ciuitate posset prohibere tam sequaces papæ hæretici, quam dominum temporale ne publicarent vel facerent aut permitterent publicari doctrinam papæ erroneam, quam scirent esse erroneam, & non facerent, inter consentientes doctrinæ erroneæ papæ computari deberent. & causa secundum istos sæpe tacta est prius, quia videlicet nullius rei temporalis vel hominis mortalis cuiuscunque defensio magis spectat ad quemcunque hominem vel multitudinem Christianorum: quam defensio fidei orthodoxæ. & ideo si multitudo in quocunque casu contra regem proprium vel dominum temporale vel papam vel alium dominum quemcunque temporalem vel hominem deberet defendere, multomagis contra eundem debet defendere fidem, si potest. Constat autem, quod si papa vel rex aut dominus temporalis vellet omnes viros & mulieres parvulos & innocentes corporaliter trucidare, totam terram vastare, & ad solitudinem & ad desertum reducere, multitudo simplicium super alios potestatem nequaquam habentium deberet papæ, regi, & cuicunque domino temporali resistere. ergo si papa, reges, & principes, aut alii domini temporales vellent fidem destruere, & ad falsam sectam sibi subiectos inducere, multitudo tenetur eis resistere, cum posset: quia aliter consentiret eisdem. veruntamen si multitudo propter imperitiam nesciret doctrinam papæ esse erroneam, & ignorantia crassa & supina minime laboraret, excusaretur, quamuis doctrinæ papæ erroneæ nullatenus obuiaret. quemadmodum turba Iudæorum fuisset excusata de morte Christi, si ipsis nescientibus nec ignorantia crassa & supina laborantibus Christum principes occidissent. Si autem interrogatio tua intelligitur diuisim de simplicibus super alios potestatem nequaquam habentibus: sic dicitur, quod si vnus solus posset cum fructu dictæ doctrinæ resistere, & ad resistendum alios provocare, si non resisteret, esset fautor hæreticæ prauitatis. veruntamen sicut simplices non semper tenentur scire doctrinam papæ hæretici esse erroneam, quando prælati & alii maiores scire tenentur: quia non ita faciliter possunt scire, cum reges & principes ac quædam aliæ publicæ potestates possunt sæpe vocare peritos, & per eos cognoscere veritatem de doctrina papæ hæretici, quos simplices vocare non valent. ita in multis casibus simplices non tenentur dictæ doctrinæ resistere, quando principes & aliæ publicæ potestates tenentur obuiare.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Although many doubts and objections can be raised about this argument, I will pass over them, since they can easily be answered from what has come before. I ask only this about simple people who hold no power over others: are they supporters of heretics and of heretical depravity if they do not resist the erroneous teaching of the Pope? MASTER. This question can be understood in two ways: either it concerns some whole multitude of simple people who hold no power over others, or it concerns any single simple person of that kind. If it is understood in the first way, I say that if the multitude is so large that it can, with spiritual profit, forbid the Pope's erroneous teaching, it must be judged to favour the heretics and heretical depravity if it does not resist. This is proved first as follows. A multitude of this kind is bound no less to defend the faith and to resist those who destroy it than it is bound to resist those who unjustly and wrongfully attack a comrade or a country. But such a multitude is bound to resist those who unjustly or wrongfully attack a comrade or a country (23. qu. 3, c. Fortitudo). Therefore it is much more bound to resist (if it can) those who destroy the faith. Hence, if the Pope wishes to destroy the faith and bring in heretical depravity, a multitude able to resist him must confront him manfully and must prevent him from infecting Catholics. Second, as follows. Whatever belongs to someone to defend Christ, to the same belongs the defence of his faith. But it does not belong to a multitude holding no power over others to defend Christ, as Augustine testifies, as was cited above (23. qu. 3, last chapter), where he says: the prophet shows that those were not free of guilt who allowed the princes to kill Christ, since they feared the crowd, and could have freed themselves from the deed and from consent. Therefore it belongs to the multitude to defend the faith of Christ, and they are not free of guilt if they allow the Pope, prelates, kings, princes and any public powers whatever to subvert the orthodox faith, when they are afraid of those powers and could free themselves from the deed and from consent. For, as Augustine says in the same place: he who ceases to oppose the perverse when he can, and does not do so, seems to consent. Accordingly, if the multitude of Christians, holding no power over others, could resist the Pope's erroneous teaching and did not, it would consent to it. Similarly, a multitude of simple people in one kingdom, one duchy or one city could forbid both the Pope's heretical followers and the temporal lord to publish, or to do or allow to be published, the Pope's erroneous teaching which they know to be erroneous; if they did not, they ought to be counted among those who consent to the Pope's erroneous teaching. According to these writers, this point has often been made before, namely that the defence of no temporal thing or mortal man whatever belongs more to any man or multitude of Christians than the defence of the orthodox faith. Therefore, if in any case the multitude ought to defend itself against its own king, temporal lord, Pope, or any other temporal lord or man, it ought much more to defend the faith against them, if it can. It is clear that if the Pope, a king or a temporal lord wished to slaughter bodily all men, women, and innocent little ones, to lay waste the whole land and reduce it to solitude and desert, the multitude of simple people holding no power over others ought to resist the Pope, the king, and whatever temporal lord. Therefore, if the Pope, kings and princes, or other temporal lords wished to destroy the faith and lead those subject to them into a false sect, the multitude is bound to resist them, since it can; otherwise it would consent to them. Yet if the multitude, through lack of skill, did not know the Pope's teaching to be erroneous, and did not labour under gross and crass ignorance, it would be excused, although it did not in any way oppose the Pope's erroneous teaching; just as the crowd of Jews would have been excused for the death of Christ, if the princes had killed Christ without their knowledge and without their labouring under gross and crass ignorance. But if your question is understood separately, concerning simple people holding no power over others, I answer that if a single one could, with spiritual profit, resist that teaching and provoke others to resist, and did not, he would be a supporter of heretical depravity. Yet just as simple people are not always bound to know that the Pope's heretical teaching is erroneous, when prelates and other greater persons are bound to know it, because they cannot so easily know it (kings, princes and certain other public powers can often summon experts and through them learn the truth about the Pope's heretical teaching, which simple people cannot summon), so in many cases simple people are not bound to resist that teaching when princes and other public powers are bound to oppose it.

units.la: DISCIP. Hic essent multa quærenda, quæ breuitatis causa dimitto, & vnum tantum interrogo: an scilicet reges & principes ac publicæ potestates teneantur vocare peritos, & quomodo debent per eos quærere de doctrina prædicta.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Here many things would have to be asked, which I omit for brevity; I ask only one: are kings, princes and public powers bound to summon experts, and how ought they to inquire of them about the said teaching?

units.la: MAGIST. Respondetur, quod alii tenentur vocare peritos, quod ex prædictis dependere videtur. Sed quomodo per eos debent inquirere veritatem superius est minime discussum circa quod dicitur, quod publicæ potestates, quæ peritos vocauerunt, debent eis indicere iuramentum, vt dicant plenam & meram veritatem de doctrina papæ, quæ reputatur hæretica, eis fortiter comminando, quod si à veritate & conscientia deuiauerint in perpetuum confundentur, & firmiter promittendo, quod si plenam & veram veritatem dixerint, eos honoribus præmiabunt, & ab omni confusione ac impugnatione defensabunt.
units.tr: MASTER. The answer is that others are bound to summon experts, which seems to follow from what has been said. But how they ought to inquire of them the truth has not been fully discussed above. Regarding this, it is said that public powers which have summoned experts ought to require of them an oath to tell the full and pure truth about the Pope's teaching which is reckoned heretical, sternly threatening them that if they turn aside from the truth and their conscience they will be confounded for ever, and firmly promising that if they tell the full and true truth they will reward them with honours and defend them from all confusion and attack.

units.la: DISCIP. Dubito, quod si vnquam aliquis papa est hæreticus, multitudo peritorum firmiter ei adhærebit. Et ideo necesse erit, si rex aliquis vel alius potens velit ab eis quærere veritatem de doctrina papæ hæretici, oportet eos per iuramenta & per horribilissimas comminationes constringere. sed dic, quid faciendum est de peritis, si respondere recusant.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. I doubt that if ever any Pope is a heretic, a multitude of experts will firmly cling to him. Therefore, if some king or other powerful man wishes to ask them the truth about the Pope's heretical teaching, it will be necessary to bind them by oaths and most dreadful threats. But tell me, what should be done about the experts if they refuse to answer?

units.la: MAGIST. Ad hoc respondetur, quod in hoc casu sunt habendi suspecti de hæretica prauitate: nec vnquam eis magno negocio est credendum, quia sic habetur.
units.tr: MASTER. To this it is answered that in this case they are to be held suspect of heretical depravity, and one should never without great difficulty believe them, because it is written thus.

units.la: 20. q. 7. Non potest ergo homines esse fideles, qui extiterit Deo infideles.
units.tr: 20. qu. 7. A man therefore cannot be faithful who has proved unfaithful to God.

units.la: CAP. LVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER LVII.

units.la: Tractat de his qui sunt fautores, & qua poena sint plectendi.
units.tr: Treats of those who are favourers, and by what punishment they are to be punished.

units.la: DISCIP. Quamuis quamplurima adhuc circa fautores haereticae prauitatis essent discurienda: illis tamen pro nunc omissis (quae ad tractatum degestis circa fidem altercantium orthodoxam reseruo) ad fautores tantummodo haereticorum me transfero. de quibus discutias primo, qui sunt fautores haereticorum, qui quamuis de erroribus eorundem se nullatenus intromittunt, personis tamen eorum fauent, praebendo eis auxilium vel consilium aut qualemcunque fauorem, non vt errores suos diuulgent, doceant & defendant, vt ditiores & maiores vel contra alios potentiores fiant. MAGIST. De talibus fautoribus haereticorum dictum est supra c. 27. quantum pro nunc. DISCIP. Requiro hoc quantum ad hoc vt sciantur, qui sunt fautores haereticorum: & qua poena isti fautores haereticorum sunt plectendi. MAGIST. Poena taxatur explicite, extr. de haeretic. ca. excommunicamus. §. credentes. ibi enim loquitur de poena illorum, qui sunt fautores haereticorum, & non sunt fautores haereticae prauitatis.
units.tr: STUDENT: Although very many matters concerning the favourers of heretical depravity still remain to be discussed, I will set them aside for now (I reserve them for a treatise on the matters debated concerning the orthodox faith) and turn only to the favourers of heretics. Concerning these, first, I would like you to discuss who the favourers of heretics are. Although they in no way concern themselves with the errors of heretics, they nevertheless favour the persons of heretics, giving them aid, counsel, or some other kind of favour, not so that they may spread, teach and defend their errors, but so that the heretics may become richer and greater, or more powerful against others. MASTER: About such favourers of heretics, enough has been said for now above, chap. 27. STUDENT: I ask this so that it may be known who the favourers of heretics are, and by what punishment these favourers of heretics are to be punished. MASTER: The punishment is set out explicitly in extra, de haereticis, cap. excommunicamus, §. credentes. For there it speaks of the punishment of those who are favourers of heretics, and who are not favourers of heretical depravity.

units.la: CAP. LVIII.
units.tr: CAP. LVIII.

units.la: De communicantibus papae haretico: & quomodo sibi liceat communicare corporaliter.
units.tr: On those who communicate with a heretical pope, and how far it is lawful to communicate with him bodily.

units.la: DISCIP. Licet ex his, quae sunt in isto capitulo pertractata, via videtur aperta ad sciendum & cognoscendum tam qui sunt fautores haereticorum quam haereticae prauitatis: tamen circa utrosq; unam tantummodo difficultatem discutias, an scilicet communicantes & obedientes papae haretico vel cuicunque alii praelato haretico, sunt censendi fautores tam haereticorum quam haereticae prauitatis. MAGIST. Vnam interrogationem proponis, quae tamen duas includit: quarum una est de communicantibus papae haretico vel alii haretico: & alia est de obedientibus ei. DISCIP. Ex quo dicis, quod interrogatio mea duas includit; dic quomodo distinguuntur. MAGIST. Respondetur, quod distinguuntur sicut communicare & obedire. multi enim communicant alicui, qui nequaquam obediunt. & multi obediunt alicui seruando eius mandata antiqua vel noua sibi per literas intimata, qui tamen sibi nequaquam communicant. DISCIP. Dic ergo primo de communicantibus papae haretico. MAGIST. Contingit secundum quosdam communicare papae haretico multis modis. Vno modo corporaliter tantum, scilicet comedendo, bibendo, conuersando, loquendo: Alio modo ei in crimine quomodolibet consentiendo, ipsum videlicet quocunque modo, verbo vel scripto aut facto esse verum papam etiam & catholicum asserendo: qui primo modo tantum communicaret papae haretico, non esset propter hoc fautor tam haereticorum quam haereticae prauitatis. Quod enim non esset fautor haereticae prauitatis, probatur ex hoc, quod secundum apostolum. 1. Corinth. 6. Cum infidelibus absque fauore infidelitatis licet taliter communicare. ergo per talem communicationem cum haereticis non potest ostendi, quod communicans sit fautor haereticae prauitatis. Quod etiam non sit propter hoc fautor haereticorum, patet ex hoc, quod inimicus inimico suo non fauet: & tamen contingit inimicum & insidiatorem taliter communicare; teste Sapiente Ecclesia. 13. qui loquens de diuite pauperi iniuriam non faciente, sed pauperem consumente, ait: Si habes conuiuet tecum & euacuabit te, & ipse non dolebit super te. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod commune & communicare alicui potest esse absque omni fauore.
units.tr: STUDENT. Although what has been treated in this chapter seems to open a way to knowing and recognising both who are supporters of heretics and who of heretical depravity, there is still one difficulty to be discussed concerning both: namely, whether those who communicate with and obey a heretical pope, or any other heretical prelate, are to be counted supporters of heretics and of heretical depravity. TEACHER. You propose one question, but it contains two: one concerning those who communicate with a heretical pope or another heretic, and the other concerning those who obey him. STUDENT. Since you say my question contains two, explain how they are distinguished. TEACHER. They are distinguished as communicating and obeying are. Many communicate with someone without obeying him at all, and many obey someone by keeping his old or new commands sent to them in writing, yet do not communicate with him. STUDENT. Then tell me first about those who communicate with a heretical pope. TEACHER. According to some, one may communicate with a heretical pope in many ways. In one way, only bodily, that is, by eating, drinking, associating and speaking with him. In another way, by consenting to his crime in any manner whatever, that is, by asserting by word, writing or deed that he is in every way a true pope and a Catholic. Someone who communicated with a heretical pope only in the first way would not for that reason be a supporter of heretics or of heretical depravity. That he would not be a supporter of heretical depravity is proved from the Apostle, 1 Cor. 6: with unbelievers it is lawful to associate in this way without favouring their unbelief. Therefore by such communion with heretics it cannot be shown that the one communicating favours heretical depravity. That he would not for this reason be a supporter of heretics is clear from the fact that an enemy does not favour his enemy, and yet it happens that an enemy and a plotter associates in this way; as the wise Ecclesiasticus 13 testifies, speaking of a rich man who does no wrong to a poor man, but consumes him, he says: "If you have something, he will live with you and empty you out, and he will not grieve over you." From these words it is gathered that communion, and communicating with someone, can exist without any favour at all.

units.la: DISCIP. Satis apparet mihi, quod contingit alicui communicare absque fauore omni: imo ad detrimentum meius. sed nunquam contingit absque peccato communicare corporaliter tantum papae haeretico?
units.tr: STUDENT. It seems plain enough to me that one can communicate with someone without any favour at all, indeed to one's own loss. But can one never communicate bodily only with a heretical pope without sin?

units.la: MAGIST. Circa hoc possunt esse diuersae sententiae. vna, quod nullo modo licet cuicunque catholico communicare papae haretico. & haec sententia videtur posse probari ratione scripturae diuinae, quae omnes Christianos astringit. sed in scriptura diuina praecipitur, ne quis etiam corporaliter haereticis communicare praesumat. ergo nulli Christiano licet communicare etiam corporaliter papae haeretico. maior videtur nota. minor probatur auctoritate beati Iohannis, qui in canonica sua. 2. ait: Si quis venit ad vos & hanc doctrinam non affert: nolite eum recipere in domum, nec ave ei dixeritis. qui enim dicit illis ave: communicat operibus eius malignis.
units.tr: TEACHER. On this there can be different opinions. One is that it is in no way lawful for any Catholic to communicate with a heretical pope. This opinion seems capable of proof by the reasoning of divine Scripture, which binds all Christians. But divine Scripture commands that no one presume to communicate even bodily with heretics. Therefore it is lawful for no Christian to communicate even bodily with a heretical pope. The major premise seems well known. The minor is proved by the authority of the blessed John, who in his canonical epistle 2 says: "If anyone comes to you and does not bring this doctrine, do not receive him into the house, nor say 'hail' to him. For he who says 'hail' to him communicates in his evil works."

units.la: DISCIP. Haec auctoritas ad hanc conclusionem prolixe tractata est. sup. libro 6. c. 68. ideo si habes aliam auctoritatem, adducas. MAGIST. Hoc idem apostolus Paulus sentire videtur, qui ad Titum scribens ait: Haereticum hominem post primam & secundam correctionem devita. Ex quibus verbis patet, quod postquam constiterit papam esse haereticum, est ab omnibus catholicis euitandus. ergo non est sibi corporaliter communicandum. DISCIP. Haec etiam auctoritas adducta est ibidem. & ideo narra sententiam contrariam. MAGIST. Alia est sententia, quod in casu licet communicare corporaliter tantummodo papae haeretico. Ad cuius euidentiam dicitur esse sciendum, quod corporalis communio cum haereticis a iure diuino non prohibetur, sed tantummodo à iure humano: quod exemplo & auctoritate probatur. Exemplo quidam Iuliani apostatæ, qui fuit hæreticus: cui Christiani licite communicauerunt corporaliter, vt habetur. 11. quæst. 3. c. Iulianus: quod non fecissent, si talis communio à iure diuino fuisset prohibita, hoc etiam consimili modo exemplo & auctoritate Bonifacii martyris videtur aperte probari. idem enim martyr, vt legitur. 11. quæst. 3. c. antecessor, scribens Zachariæ papæ, ait: Antecessor prædecessoris vestri venerandæ memoriæ Greg. dum me indignum ordinauit & ad prædicandum verbum Dei Germanicu gentibus misit, sacramento me astrinxit, vt canonicis & iustis episcopis & presbyteris in verbo & facto & consensu astipulator & adiutor essem. hoc autem cum diuina gratia implere studui, falsos autem sacerdotes & hypocritas & seductores populorum vel corrigerem ad viam salutis, vel declinarem & abstinerem à communione ipsorum, quod ex parte seruans & ex parte custodire & implere non potui: sed spiritualiter impleui sacramentum, quia in consensum & consilium eorum non venit anima mea, corporaliter autem omnino abstinere ab eis non potui. Ex quibus verbis colligitur manifeste, quod iste martyr licite corporaliter communicauit hæreticis: quod tamen non fecisset, si talis communio cum hæreticis fuisset prohibita iure diuino.
units.tr: STUDENT. This authority has been treated at length in support of this conclusion, above in book 6, chapter 68. So if you have another authority, cite it. TEACHER. The Apostle Paul seems to hold the same view, writing to Titus: "Avoid a heretical man after the first and second admonition." From these words it is plain that once it has been established that the pope is a heretic, he is to be avoided by all Catholics. Therefore one must not communicate bodily with him. STUDENT. That authority too has been cited in the same place. So tell me the opposing opinion. TEACHER. The other opinion is that in such a case it is lawful to communicate bodily only with a heretical pope. To make this clear, it must be understood that bodily communion with heretics is not forbidden by divine law, but only by human law. This is proved by example and authority. By example: Julian the apostate, who was a heretic, with whom Christians communicated lawfully in the body, as is found in 11 q. 3, c. Iulianus. They would not have done so if such communion had been forbidden by divine law. In a similar way, this seems clearly proved by the example and authority of the martyr Boniface. For the same martyr, as is read in 11 q. 3, c. Antecessor, writing to Pope Zachary, says: "My predecessor of venerable memory, Gregory, when he ordained me though unworthy and sent me to preach the word of God to the German peoples, bound me by an oath that I should be a helper and supporter of canonical and just bishops and presbyters in word, deed and agreement. This I have striven to fulfil with divine grace. But false priests, hypocrites and seducers of the people, I was either to correct to the way of salvation or to avoid and abstain from their communion. This I have kept in part, and in part I have not been able to observe and fulfil; but spiritually I have fulfilled the oath, since my soul has not come into their consent and counsel. Yet bodily I could not altogether abstain from them." From these words it is clearly gathered that this martyr lawfully communicated bodily with heretics; which he would not have done had such communion with heretics been forbidden by divine law.

units.la: DISCIP. Ex his verbis non habetur, quod illi falsi sacerdotes, quibus communicauit Bonifacius, essent hæretici: quia nec de hæreticis sit hic mentio.
units.tr: STUDENT. These words do not show that those false priests with whom Boniface communicated were heretics, since there is no mention of heretics here.

units.la: MAGIST. Quod fuerint hæretici, testatur Zacharias, qui scribens eidem martyri (vt c. sequens ostendit) ait: prædecessor noster bonæ memoriæ Gregorius atque huius sanctæ sedis apostolicæ præsul, dum ad prædicandum verbum Dei euangelii tuam commisit firmitatem in Germaniæ partibus in gentibus illis paganis & verbo pollicitationis illam nouit ante esse communitatem, ita vt orthodoxos episcopos & presbyteros vel quoscunque reperire potuisses in verbo exhortationis perfectos amplum confirmares & cum communicares quod factum est. si quos vero seductores episcopos aut presbyteros aut à recto fidei tramite deviantes repperisses, nulla tibi cum eis esset communio, quod te Deo adiuvante vsque ad præsens spiritualiter obseruasse confessus es. vel si omnino propter principalem & humanum fauorem gentes Francorum, dum ad eos accessisses, corporaliter vero abstinere non valuisti cogente ecclesiarum Dei necessitate: & tamen in eorum consilio & communione consensu anima tua non est coinquinata. itaque propter hoc, quod cum eis conuersatus es, non consentiens iniquitati eorum, nullum tibi est detrimentum coram Deo. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod sacerdotes & episcopi, quibus communicauit Bonifacius martyr, fuerunt hæretici & pseudopresbyteri à recto fidei tramite deviantes, quibus tamen communicando nullam detrimentum apud Deum incurrit. ergo talis corporalis communio non est à iure diuino prohibita.
units.tr: TEACHER. That they were heretics is attested by Zachary, who, writing to the same martyr (as the following chapter shows), says: "Our predecessor of good memory, Gregory, prelate of this holy apostolic see, when he committed your firmness to preach the word of the gospel of God among the pagan peoples of Germany, knew beforehand that you would be in communion with the faithful in word of exhortation; so that you would strengthen the orthodox bishops and presbyters, or whoever you could find perfect in the word, and would communicate with them, which has been done. But if you found seducing bishops or presbyters, or those who strayed from the straight path of faith, you were to have no communion with them; and you have confessed that with God's help you have observed this spiritually up to the present. Or if, because of the principal and human favour of the Frankish peoples, when you came to them, you could not altogether abstain bodily, because of the necessity of the churches of God, yet your soul has not been defiled by their counsel and communion with consent. Therefore, since you have associated with them without consenting to their iniquity, there is no loss to you before God." From these words it is gathered that the priests and bishops with whom the martyr Boniface communicated were heretics and false presbyters who had strayed from the straight path of faith, yet by communicating with them he incurred no loss before God. Therefore such bodily communion is not forbidden by divine law.

units.la: DISCIP. Dic quomodo ex his concluditur, quod contingit communicare papæ hæretico absque peccato.
units.tr: STUDENT. Tell me how it follows from these points that one may communicate with a heretical pope without sin.

units.la: MAGIST. Hoc probatur sic. quod nec à iure naturali nec à iure diuino est prohibitum, & à iure humano in dispendium populi Christiani vel alicuius communitatis fidelium prohiberi non potest. quia ex quo lex humana pro communi vtilitate fieri debet, vt ex verbis Isidori, quæ ponuntur dist. 4. cap. erit autem, colligitur manifeste, nulla lex humana ligare potest in eo casu, in quo si seruaretur in communitatis dispendium redundaret. sed communicare papæ hæretico non est prohibitum à iure naturali nec à iure diuino, vt probatum est. ergo nulla lex humana prohibere potest communicare papæ hæretico, quando talis prohibitio in alicuius communitatis populi Christiani dispendium redundaret: si posset contingere casus, propter potentiam temporalem papæ hæretici, si catholici nollent sibi communicare, quod ex hoc sequeretur dispendium alicuius regni vel regionis: quia forte totam regionem subuerteret. ergo in tali casu vel consimili nulla lex humana potest prohibere communicare papæ hæretico, dicto modo.
units.tr: TEACHER. It is proved thus: what is forbidden neither by natural law nor by divine law, and cannot be forbidden by human law to the detriment of the Christian people or of any community of the faithful, is lawful. For, since human law ought to be made for the common good, as is clearly gathered from the words of Isidore given in dist. 4, c. Erit autem, no human law can bind in a case where, if it were observed, it would turn out to the detriment of the community. But communicating with a heretical pope is not forbidden by natural law or divine law, as has been proved. Therefore no human law can forbid communicating with a heretical pope when such a prohibition would turn out to the detriment of the Christian people or of some community of the faithful. It could happen that, because of the temporal power of a heretical pope, if Catholics refused to communicate with him, a loss would follow to some kingdom or region, since perhaps he would overthrow the whole region. Therefore in such a case, or a similar one, no human law can forbid communicating with a heretical pope in the way described.

units.la: CAP. LIX.
units.tr: CHAP. LIX.

units.la: Quæritur, quomodo liceat papæ hæretico spiritualiter communicare: & adducuntur quatuor rationes, quas soluuntur infra. c. 54.
units.tr: The question is how it is lawful to communicate spiritually with a heretical pope, and four reasons are adduced, which are answered below in chapter 54.

units.la: DISCIP. Videtur probabile, quod in hoc casu liceret communicare papæ hæretico, quemadmodum Bonifacius martyr, non obstante iuramento de non communicando hæreticis, corporaliter communicauit eisdem, & multi viri corporaliter communicauerunt Iuliano apostatæ, qui fuit hæreticus manifestus: ideo dic, an aliquo alio modo, quam corporaliter tantum, scilicet communicando sibi in diuinis; audiendo missam eius vel diuinum officium ab eo, aut ipsum facto, scripto vel verbo esse verum papam & catholicum asserendo, liceat cuicunque communicare papæ hæretico.
units.tr: STUDENT. It seems probable that in this case it would be lawful to communicate with a heretical pope, just as Boniface the martyr, notwithstanding his oath not to communicate with heretics, communicated bodily with them, and many men communicated bodily with Julian the Apostate, who was a manifest heretic. So tell me whether, in some other way than merely bodily, namely by communicating with him in divine things, by hearing his Mass or divine office, or by asserting by deed, writing or word that he is the true and catholic pope, it is lawful for anyone to communicate with a heretical pope.

units.la: MAGIST. Circa hoc possunt esse opiniones variæ & diuersæ. Quarum prima est, quod papæ hæretico licet communicare in diuino officio, & eum habendo pro papa quousque per sententiam generalis concilii fuerit condemnatus. hæc assertio videtur multis modis posse probari. Primo sic non detectoris conditionis est summus pontifex nouæ testamenti; quam fuerunt sacerdotes veteris testamenti. sed sacerdotes veteris testamenti in his quæ ad sacerdotale officium spectabant, non fuerunt vitandi propter prauitatem ante publicam damnationem eorum. ergo eadem ratione papa, qui est summus sacerdos nouæ legis, non est propter hæreticam prauitatem deuitandus in his, quæ ad papale spectat officium, antequam fuerit per generale concilium condemnatus. ergo licet communicare papæ hæretico in his, quæ pertinent ad papatus officium. Maior videtur aperta. Minor ostenditur.
units.tr: TEACHER. On this there may be various and differing opinions. The first is that it is lawful to communicate with a heretical pope in the divine office, and to regard him as pope until he has been condemned by the sentence of a general council. This assertion seems capable of being proved in many ways. First, the supreme pontiff of the New Testament is not of a lower condition than the priests of the Old Testament. But the priests of the Old Testament were not to be avoided, in those matters that pertained to the priestly office, on account of their wickedness before their public condemnation. Therefore, by the same reasoning, the pope, who is the supreme priest of the new law, is not to be avoided, on account of heretical wickedness, in those matters that pertain to the papal office, before he has been condemned by a general council. Therefore it is lawful to communicate with a heretical pope in those matters that belong to the papal office. The major premise is plain. The minor is shown as follows.

units.la: Nam sacerdotes veteris legis, qui prædicationi & doctrinæ Christi bequiter resistebant, fuerunt hæretici, eo quod contra fidem errabant & suo errori pertinaciter adhæserunt. & tamen Christus docuit, quod eis erat communicandum etiam in eis, quæ ad sacerdotale spectabant officium, cum dixit leproso Matth. 8. Vade & ostende te sacerdotibus, & offer munus quod præcepit Moyses in testimonium illis. Et Luc. 17. dicit Iesus leprosis: Ite, ostendite vos sacerdotibus. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod non obstante, quod illi sacerdotes fuerint hæretici, tamen Christus voluit quod leprosi communicarent eis in his etiam, quæ spectabant ad eorum officium. Hoc etiam Augustinus sentire videtur, qui loquens propheticis, qui populum suum propter idolatriam, & per consequens propter hæresim increpabant, ut habetur 23. quæst. 4. cap. 1. ait: Non enim prophetæ, qui hæc dicebant, populum suum dimiserunt: sed inter eos habitabant, quos increpabant, unum cum eis templum intrabant, eadem sacramenta celebrabant. Et idem, ut habetur causa & q. prædictis. Si quis, ait: communio malorum non maculat aliquem participatione sacramentorum: sed consensione factorum. Et ut legitur causa & q. prædictis. c. recedite, ait: Recedite & exinde exite, pollutum & immundum ne tetigeritis: sed contactu cordis, non corporis. Et infra: Clamavit Moyses ista, clamavit Esaias, clamavit Ieremias, clamavit Ezechias videntes dimiserunt populum Dei, & se ad gentes alias transfuderunt, quamvis multis modis & qua vehementer increpavit Ieremias peccatores & sceleratos seductores populi Dei. Inter eos erat tamen, & cum eis unum templum intrabat in eadem sceleratorum hominum congregatione vivebat. Ex quibus datur intelligi, quod prophetæ cum hæreticis & idolatris, quorum tunc erat numerus non modicus, in populo idem templum & eadem sacramenta tractabant. Ergo communicare hæreticis in divinis & in aliis, quæ ad sacerdotale spectant officium, non erat illicitum. Ergo nec modo est illicitum communicare papæ hæretico in his, quæ ad papale spectant officium: saltem antequam fuerit per sententiam generalis concilii condemnatus.
units.tr: For the priests of the old law, who stubbornly resisted the preaching and teaching of Christ, were heretics, since they erred against the faith and clung obstinately to their error. And yet Christ taught that they were to be communicated with even in those things that pertained to the priestly office, when he said to the leper in Matthew 8: "Go, show yourself to the priests, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony to them." And in Luke 17 Jesus says to the lepers: "Go, show yourselves to the priests." From these words it is gathered that, although those priests were heretics, Christ nevertheless willed that the lepers should communicate with them even in those things that pertained to their office. Augustine also seems to think this, who, speaking of the prophets who rebuked their people for idolatry, and consequently for heresy, as is found in 23 q. 4 c. 1, says: "For the prophets who said these things did not abandon their people, but lived among those whom they rebuked; they entered the temple together with them and celebrated the same sacraments." And again, as is found in the same cause and question: "If anyone says that the communion of evil men does not stain a person by participation in the sacraments, but by consent in their deeds." And as is read in the same cause and question, in the chapter "Recedite": "Depart and go out from there, and do not touch what is polluted and unclean, but touch it not with the heart, not with the body." And further on: "Moses cried out these things, Isaiah cried out, Jeremiah cried out, Hezekiah cried out; seeing this, they left the people of God and passed over to other nations, although Jeremiah rebuked the sinners and wicked seducers of the people of God in many ways and most vehemently. Yet he was among them, and he entered the temple with them and lived in the same congregation of wicked men."
