From these things it is given to understand that the prophets, together with heretics and idolaters, whose number was then not small, handled the same temple and the same sacraments among the people. Therefore to communicate with heretics in divine things, and in other things that pertain to the priestly office, was not unlawful. Therefore neither is it now unlawful to communicate with a heretical pope in those things that pertain to the papal office, at least before he has been condemned by the sentence of a general council.

units.la: Secundo, eadem assertio videtur posse probari: non est maius peccatum communicare hæreticis in divinis, quam procurare & laborare quod ecclesiæ hæreticorum reddantur hæreticis ad ritus suos colendos in eis. Sed hoc est licitum: quod probatur exemplo beati Iohann. papæ, in cuius Legenda sic legitur; hic vocatus est a Theodorico rege Ravennam, quem ipse rex rogans misit Constantinopolim cum legatione ad Iustinum papam imperatorem orthodoxum, quia eodem tempore Iustinus imperator, ut religiosus, summo ardoris amore religionis Christianæ voluit hæreticos exiliari. Nam summo fervore religionis Christianæ hoc consilio usus est, ut ecclesias Arrianorum catholicis conservaret: pro hac causa rex Theodoricus hoc audiens exarsit in iram, & voluit totam Italiam gladio extinguere. Eodem tempore Iohann. papa ægrotus infirmitate cum fletu ambulavit, & senatores & consules cum eo, scilicet Theodoricus, Imperiunus & Agapitus patricius, accipientes hoc in mandatis legationum, ut redderentur ecclesiæ hæreticis in partibus orientis, quod si non fecerint, omnem Italiam gladio perderent. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod licet ecclesias reddere hæreticis, & procurare quod reddantur eisdem. Ergo consimiliter licet communicare hæreticis in divinis; & per consequens licet communicare papæ hæretico in his, quæ ad papale officium spectant.
units.tr: Secondly, the same assertion seems capable of being proved: it is no greater sin to communicate with heretics in divine things than to procure and labour that churches of heretics be restored to heretics so that they may worship their rites in them. But this is lawful, as is proved by the example of blessed Pope John, in whose Legend it is read thus: "He was summoned by King Theodoric to Ravenna, whom the king himself, asking, sent to Constantinople with an embassy to Justin the pope and the orthodox emperor, because at the same time the Emperor Justin, as a religious man, with the greatest ardour of love for the Christian religion, wished to have the heretics exiled. For with the highest fervour for the Christian religion he used this plan, so that he might preserve the churches of the Arians for the Catholics. For this cause King Theodoric, hearing this, flared up in anger, and wished to extinguish all Italy with the sword. At the same time Pope John, sick with infirmity, walked with weeping, and the senators and consuls with him, namely Theodoric, Imperiunus and Agapitus the patrician, receiving this in the commissions of the embassies, that the churches should be restored to the heretics in the eastern parts; for if they did not do so, they would destroy all Italy with the sword." From these words it is gathered that it is lawful both to restore churches to heretics and to procure that they be restored to them. Therefore, in like manner, it is lawful to communicate with heretics in divine things; and consequently it is lawful to communicate with a heretical pope in those things that pertain to the papal office.

units.la: Tertio sic: quem debent fideles in aliquo officio tolerare, eidem possunt licite communicare, quantum ad ea quæ ad idem spectant officium; quia si non deberent ei communicare, deberent efficaciter laborare, ut eodem officio privaretur. Sed in aliquo casu saltem debent fideles papam hæreticum in papatus officio tolerare. Ergo in aliquo casu saltem licet eis communicare papæ hæretico, quantum ad ea quæ ad papatus spectant officium. Maior manifesta videtur, minor probatur; quia non minus tolerandus est papa hæreticus, quam doctrina hæretica ipsius, cum papa hæreticus non nisi propter doctrinam hæreticam debeat impugnari. Sed sicut ostensum est, in aliquo casu est doctrina papæ hæretica toleranda. Ergo etiam interdum est papa hæreticus tolerandus. Hoc etiam Augustinus sentire videtur, qui, ut legitur 23. quæst. 4. cap. 1. ait: tolerandi sunt mali quidem propter pacem. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod causa pacis conservandæ sint mali tolerandi, eadem autem causa eundem habet effectum. Et ubi est eadem ratio, ibi debet esse idem ius. Ergo si quidem mali causa pacis obtinendæ sunt tolerandi, sequitur quod papa hæreticus causa pacis conservandæ tolerari debet.
units.tr: Thirdly, thus: whomever the faithful must tolerate in some office, with them they may lawfully communicate in those things that pertain to the same office; for if they ought not to communicate with him, they ought to labour effectually that he be deprived of that office. But in some case at least the faithful must tolerate a heretical pope in the papal office. Therefore in some case at least it is lawful for them to communicate with a heretical pope in those things that pertain to the papal office. The major premise seems manifest; the minor is proved because a heretical pope is not to be tolerated any less than his heretical doctrine, since a heretical pope ought to be opposed only on account of his heretical doctrine. But, as has been shown, in some case the heretical doctrine of a pope is to be tolerated. Therefore also at times a heretical pope is to be tolerated. Augustine also seems to think this, who, as is read in 23 q. 4 c. 1, says: "The wicked indeed are to be tolerated for the sake of peace." From these words it is gathered that for the sake of preserving peace the wicked are to be tolerated, and the same cause has the same effect. And where the reason is the same, the right ought to be the same. Therefore, if indeed the wicked are to be tolerated for the sake of obtaining peace, it follows that a heretical pope ought to be tolerated for the sake of preserving peace.

units.la: Quarto: vitam Christi debent catholici imitari. Sed Christus in his, quæ ad religionem Christianam spectant, communicavit Iudæ, qui non solum proditor, sed etiam hæreticus exitebat, qui ei sacram communionem dedit, ut ait Augustinus in epistola ad Vincentium, & ponitur 23. quæst. 4. c. quam magnum. Ergo licet catholicis communicare hæreticis in his, quæ ad religionem Christianam spectant, & per consequens licet eis communicare papæ hæretico in his, quæ ad papatus spectant officium, antequam fuerit per sententiam generalis concilii condemnatus.
units.tr: Fourthly: Catholics ought to imitate the life of Christ. But Christ, in those things that pertain to the Christian religion, communicated with Judas, who was not only a traitor but also a heretic, and who gave him the sacred communion, as Augustine says in his letter to Vincentius, and it is set down in 23 q. 4 c. "Quam magnum." Therefore it is lawful for Catholics to communicate with heretics in those things that pertain to the Christian religion, and consequently it is lawful to communicate with a heretical pope in those things that pertain to the papal office, before he has been condemned by the sentence of a general council.

units.la: CAP. LX.
units.tr: CAP. LX.

units.la: In quo ostenditur, quod non licet cum papa manifesto hæretico spiritualiter communicare: quia tales aut sunt fautores, aut peccant mortaliter.
units.tr: In which it is shown that it is not lawful to communicate spiritually with a pope who is manifestly a heretic, because such people are either favourers of heresy or sin mortally.

units.la: DISCIP. Aliam sententiam circa interrogationem propositam audire desidero. MAGISTER. Alia sententia est, quæ de communicantibus papæ hæretico reputat distinguendum; quia aut communicantes papæ hæretico sciunt ipsum esse hæreticum, vel ignorant, aut laborant ignorantia affectata vel crassa vel supina, aut laborant ignorantia invincibili & non crassa & supina. Communicantes scienter papae haeretico in his, quae spectant ad paratus officium vel cuiuscunque ecclesiastici ministerii, excepta susceptione baptismatis in necessitatis articulo: aut quocunque alio modo, quam corporaliter tantum, puta communicando sibi verbo, facto vel scripto, habendo eum pro vero papa, protestando vel asserendo eum facto vel scripto aut verbo esse catholicum, sunt fautores haeretici & haereticae pravitatis: Et peccatum fautorum haereticorum & haereticae pravitatis incurrunt: nisi metu mortis vel forsitan gravium tormentorum sibi praedicto modo communicant. tunc enim non essent censendi fautores neque haereticorum neque pravitatis haereticae, quamvis peccarent mortaliter.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. I desire to hear another opinion on the question proposed. MASTER. There is another opinion, which holds that a distinction must be drawn concerning those who communicate with a heretical pope. For those who communicate with a heretical pope either know him to be a heretic or do not know it; and they either labour under affected, gross or supine ignorance, or under invincible ignorance that is neither gross nor supine. Those who knowingly communicate with a heretical pope in matters pertaining to the papal office, or to any ecclesiastical ministry, except in receiving baptism in a case of necessity; or in any way other than merely bodily, for instance by communicating with him in word, deed or writing, by regarding him as a true pope, or by declaring or asserting by deed, writing or word that he is Catholic, are favourers of heretics and of heretical depravity, and incur the sin of favourers of heretics and of heretical depravity; unless they communicate with him in the aforesaid manner for fear of death or perhaps of severe torments. For then they should not be counted as favourers either of heretics or of heretical depravity, although they would sin mortally.

units.la: DISCIP. Circa istam sententiam quatuor probanda mihi videntur. Quorum primum est quod non licet praedicto modo communicare papae haeretico. Secundum est, quod communicantes praedicto modo papae haeretico absque metu mortis & gravium tormentorum sunt fautores haereticorum & haereticae pravitatis. Tertium est, quod communicantes praedicto modo papae haeretico metu mortis & tormentorum non sunt fautores haereticorum vel haereticae pravitatis. Quartum est, quod taliter communicantes papae haeretico peccant mortaliter. Pro istis quatuor itaque allegare conare. Primo tamen (ut assertionem praedictam magis intelligam: & sic patebit mihi via ad cognoscendum, an aliquid contineat veritatis) enumera illos modos distincte, quibus isti dicunt non licere communicare scienter papae haeretico.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Concerning this opinion, four points seem to me to need proof. The first is that it is not lawful to communicate with a heretical pope in the aforesaid manner. The second is that those who communicate in the aforesaid manner with a heretical pope, without fear of death or of grave torments, are favourers of heretics and of heretical depravity. The third is that those who communicate in the aforesaid manner with a heretical pope from fear of death or torments are not favourers of heretics or of heretical depravity. The fourth is that those who communicate in this way with a heretical pope sin mortally. I shall therefore try to argue for these four. First, however (so that I may understand the assertion better, and so that a way may open for me to recognise whether it contains any truth), list distinctly the modes by which they say it is not lawful knowingly to communicate with a heretical pope.

units.la: MAGIST. Dicunt quod nulli catholico licet scienter a papa haeretico audire missam vel aliquod divinum officium: nec aliud suscipere sacramentum, excepto baptismo in necessitatis articulo: nec aliquam ecclesiasticam dignitatem: nec aliquod ecclesiasticum beneficium, puta, inquisitionem haereticae pravitatis, vel poenitentiariam, aut aliquid aliud: nec liceat catholico dicere vel scribere aliquod verbum, quo papa vel catholicus asseratur: nec sibi quamcunque reverentiam exhibere, qua quis aperte quod sit papa vel catholicus protestetur.
units.tr: MASTER. They say that no Catholic may knowingly hear mass from a heretical pope, or any divine office; nor receive any sacrament from him, except baptism in a case of necessity; nor any ecclesiastical dignity; nor any ecclesiastical benefice, such as a post in the inquisition of heretical depravity, or the office of penitentiary, or anything else of that kind; nor may a Catholic say or write any word by which the pope or a Catholic is affirmed; nor may he show him any reverence by which he would openly profess that he is pope or Catholic.

units.la: DISCIP. Puto quod assertionem praedictam quantum ad quatuor quae dixisti probanda intelligam. ideo primum istorum probare coneris.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. I think I understand the aforesaid assertion as far as the four points you have mentioned require proof. So please try to prove the first of them.

units.la: MAGIST. Quod non liceat communicare papae haeretico scienter modo praedicto, probatur sic. nulli haeretico licet communicare scienter modo praedicto. ergo nec papae haeretico licet communicare modo praedicto. Consequentia non solum patet per regulam scientiae topicalis, qua dicitur quod a superiori cum distributione ad inferius consequentia tenet. sed etiam patet ex hoc, quod papa haereticus nullo modo gaudet privilegio speciali ultra episcopos haereticos. & ita si aliis episcopis haereticis non licet communicare scienter modo praedicto, etiam papae haeretico non licet communicare scienter modo praedicto. antecedens autem auctoritatibus & exemplis ostenditur. In concilio enim Martini papae, ut legitur. 1. quaest. 1. c. non liceat, sic scribitur: Non liceat cum haereticis aut schismaticis orare. & in concilio Carthaginensi. 4. habetur. 24. quaest. 3. c. clericus, sic legitur: cum eis (scilicet cum haereticis & schismaticis) neque orandum neque psallendum. Item Innocentius papa, ut habetur 1. q. 1. c. constat, ait: constat multos vim passos esse atque iniquos attractos repugnantesque ab haereticis ordinatos. sed huiusmodi aliquis si post talem ordinationem non interfuit, cum illi confiteretur sacramenta, si communioni eorum participatum non est, si statim discedentibus illis pessimo consiliabulo eorum abrenunciaverit, & ad ecclesiam redit: iste talis potest habere colorem aliquem excusationis. caeterum qui post mensem aut amplius redierunt, cum se considerarent ab haereticis ordinatos, certe ab eis nihil receperunt: rei tamen sunt usurpatae dignitatis. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod non licet ab haereticis ordinari, nec communicare eis, cum conficiunt sacramentum; nec ab eis suscipere dignitatem. Item Leo papa, ut legitur. c. sequenti, restari videtur dicens: Omnis cuiuslibet ordinis clericus qui catholicam deserens unitatem haeretica vel schismatica communioni contagione se maculaverit, si ad ecclesiam redierit cum legitima satisfactione, & erroris sui damnatione, hoc in magno beneficio habeat, si adepta cum spe omnis promotionis in quo invenitur ordine permaneat. Ex quibus patet, quod nullus valet communicare haereticis, nisi peccati maculam contrahendo.
units.tr: MASTER. That it is not lawful to communicate knowingly with a heretical pope in the aforesaid manner is proved thus: no heretic may lawfully communicate knowingly in the aforesaid manner; therefore a heretical pope may not lawfully communicate in the aforesaid manner. The inference is clear not only from the rule of topical knowledge, by which it is said that a consequence holds from the superior with distribution to the inferior, but also from the fact that a heretical pope enjoys no special privilege whatever beyond heretical bishops. And so if it is not lawful to communicate knowingly in the aforesaid manner with other heretical bishops, neither is it lawful to communicate knowingly in the aforesaid manner with a heretical pope. The antecedent is shown by authorities and examples. In the council of Pope Martin, as we read in 1 q. 1 c. non liceat, it is written thus: "It is not lawful to pray with heretics or schismatics." And in the Council of Carthage IV, found in 24 q. 3 c. clericus, we read: "with them (namely heretics and schismatics) one must neither pray nor sing psalms." Likewise Pope Innocent, as found in 1 q. 1 c. constat, says: "It is established that many who were subjected to violence and led astray and unwilling were ordained by heretics. But if anyone of this kind was not present at such an ordination, and if he confessed to them and did not take part in their communion, and if he renounced their wicked conventicle as soon as they departed and returned to the Church, such a person may have some colour of excuse. But those who returned after a month or more, when they reflected that they had been ordained by heretics, certainly received nothing from them, yet they are guilty of having usurped a dignity." From these words it is gathered that one may not be ordained by heretics, nor communicate with them when they celebrate the sacrament, nor receive a dignity from them. Likewise Pope Leo, as we read in the following chapter, seems to restore the matter, saying: "Any clergyman of any order who, deserting the Catholic unity, has stained himself with the contagion of heretical or schismatic communion, if he returns to the Church with lawful satisfaction and condemnation of his error, let him count it a great benefit if he remains in the order in which he is found, with the hope of any promotion." From these things it is clear that no one can communicate with heretics without contracting the stain of sin.

units.la: Quod etiam non licet modo praedicto communicare haereticis, probatur exemplis. Primo quidem exemplo Ermigildi regis, qui etiam pro morte vitanda ab Arriano episcopo communionem accipere recusavit. de quo beatus Gregorius, ut habetur. 24. q. 1. c. ultimo, narrat in haec verba: superveniente autem festivitatis paschalis die, intempesta nocte silentio ad eum perfidus pater Arrianus episcopum misit, ut de eius manu sacrilega consecrationis communionem perciperet, atque per hoc ad patris gratiam redire mereretur. sed vir Deo deditus Arriano episcopo venienti exprobravit, ut debuit, eiusque a se perfidiam dignis increpationibus repulit, quia si exterius iacebat ligatus, apud se tamen in magno mentis culmine stabat securus. ad se itaque reversus episcopo Arriano pater infremuit: statimque suos apparitores misit, constantissimum qui confessorem Dei illic, ubi iacebat, occiderent. Aliud exemplum ponitur de Bonifacio martyre, de quo dictum est sup. qui licet corporaliter communicaret haereticis, eis tamen quantum ad divina vel etiam illa quae spectant ad religionem Christianam communicare nolebat. unde sic habetur 11. q. 3. c. antecessor, de seipso ait: corporaliter autem ab eis omnino (scilicet haereticis) abstinere non potui. dum enim venissem ad principem Francorum, cogente ecclesiarum necessitate, non tales ibi reperi, quales volui: sed tamen communionem corporis Christi non communicavi eis. Ex quibus auctoritatibus & exemplis aliisque innumeris videtur aperte probatum, quod non licet haeretico communicare, quantum ad illa, quae spectant ad religionem Christianam, excepta susceptione baptismi in casu, quis in necessitate liceat cum haereticis corporaliter conversari: a quibus ut docet Aug. est spiritualiter recedendum. Spiritualiter autem ab eis recedere est iniquitati eorum in nullo fauere, neque verbo, neque facto, neque scripto praetendere, quod pro catholicis, sint habendi. DISCIP. Ostendisti uno modo, quod non licet catholico communicare scienter papae haeretico, quantum ad ea quae ad religionem Christianam spectare noscuntur: nunc probaidem aliis modis, si quos alios cogitasti. MAGIST. Hoc idem secundo probatur sic: nulli excommunicato communicare licet, quantum ad ecclesiastica sacramenta & ea quae ad officium ecclesiasticum & iurisdictionem ecclesiasticam pertinere noscuntur: quia omnis excommunicatus omnibus huiusmodi actibus legitimis est priuatus. papa autem haereticus est excommunicatus excommunicatione maiori & papatu priuatus: sicut in praecedentibus, ut nonnullis apparet, est demonstratiue probatum. ergo nulli catholico licet praedicto modo scienter communicare papae haeretico. DISCIP. Licet supra lib. 6. cap. 72. 75. & 81. rationibus & exemplis ostenderis, quomodo probatur, quod papa eo ipso, quod fit haereticus, est papatu priuatus & excommunicatus absque congregatione noui concilii generalis: tamen peto, ut dicas nunc, an haec tenentes in iure canonico se fundare nitantur. MAGIST. Isti fundant se in decretis summorum pontificum, ut tamen mentem eorum, quam aliqualiter explicaui lib. 6. supra c. 75. perfecte intelligas, ac per hoc etiam (quamuis esset falsa) tradatur via ad intelligendum decreta summorum pontificum, quae sum allegaturus, debes scire quod de haeresi papae, sicut saepe tactum est, distinguunt. quia aut tenet haeresim damnatam implicite, aut damnatam explicite. Si tenet pertinaciter haeresim damnatam explicite, & est notorium: non est necesse generale concilium congregari: sed quilibet hoc sciens eum pro damnato & excommunicato debet habere. Quod etiam quilibet sciens (ne fides catholica subuertatur) tunc quando fuerit oportunum nescientibus reuelare tenetur. aliter enim se minime curare de fide probabit aperte. Si autem haeresis papae fuerit solummodo damnata implicite: quamuis papa pertinax in haeresi tali in rei veritate sit damnatus & excommunicatus, & papatu priuatus: non est tamen a catholicis ante damnationem explicitam haeresis suae pro damnato & excommunicato habendus; sed tolerandus est quamdiu vixerit, quousque per generale concilium condemnetur.
units.tr: That it is likewise not lawful to communicate with heretics in the aforesaid manner is proved by examples. First, by the example of King Hermenegild, who, even to avoid death, refused to receive communion from the Arian bishop. Blessed Gregory relates this in 24 q. 1 c. ultimo, in these words: "When the feast day of Easter drew near, in the dead of night the faithless Arian father sent a bishop to him in silence, so that he might receive communion from his sacrilegious hand, and thereby deserve to be restored to his father's favour. But the man devoted to God rebuked the Arian bishop as he came, as he ought to have done, and with worthy reproaches repulsed his perfidy; for although he lay bound outwardly, inwardly he stood secure on the high summit of his mind. Returning therefore to himself, the Arian father raged against the bishop, and at once sent his attendants, the most resolute of whom were to kill the confessor of God where he lay." Another example is given of Boniface the martyr, of whom it was said above, who, although he communicated bodily with heretics, nevertheless was unwilling to communicate with them in divine matters, or even in those things which pertain to the Christian religion. Hence it is written in 11 q. 3 c. antecessor, where he speaks of himself: "But I could not altogether abstain from them bodily. For when I came to the prince of the Franks, compelled by the necessity of the churches, I did not find there such men as I wished; yet I did not communicate with them in the communion of the body of Christ." From these authorities and examples, and from countless others, it seems clearly proved that it is not lawful to communicate with a heretic in those things which pertain to the Christian religion, except in receiving baptism in a case of necessity, when it is lawful to live bodily with heretics; from whom, as Augustine teaches, one must withdraw spiritually. To withdraw spiritually from them, however, is to favour their iniquity in no way, neither by word, deed nor writing, and to hold out nothing by which they may be regarded as Catholics. DISCIPLE. You have shown in one way that it is not lawful for a Catholic to communicate knowingly with a heretical pope in those matters which are known to pertain to the Christian religion. Now prove the same in other ways, if you have thought of any others. MASTER. The same is proved secondly thus: it is never lawful for an excommunicate person to communicate in ecclesiastical sacraments and in those matters which are known to pertain to ecclesiastical office and ecclesiastical jurisdiction, because every excommunicate is deprived of all such lawful acts. But a heretical pope is excommunicated by the greater excommunication and deprived of the papacy, as has been demonstratively proved in what precedes, as is evident to some. Therefore it is not lawful for any Catholic knowingly to communicate in the aforesaid manner with a heretical pope.

units.la: DISCIP. Occasione istorum verborum duae mihi interrogationes occurrunt. Quarum prima est. An papa per diffinitionem solennem vel alio modo manifesto ostendens se pertinaciter adhaerere haeresi damnatae duntaxat implicite: si postea generali concilio congregato eadem haeresis fuerit explicite condemnata; sit papa pro excessu praeterito deponendus, vel fuisse depositus declarandus, etiam si voluerit generali concilio assentire: vel eo generali concilio nullatenus resistente, sed suam haeresim reuocante, sit papa verus & catholicus reputandus. Secunda autem est, an papa pertinaciter tenens haeresim damnatam duntaxat implicite, & postea ante omnem actionem vel impugnationem ad catholicam rediens veritatem debeat seipsum depositum reputare: licet omnes catholici habeant eum pro vero papa. Ad istas duas interrogationes sine magna discussione respondeas.
units.tr: Student. Two questions occur to me on the occasion of these words. The first is this: if the pope, by a solemn definition or by some other clear sign, shows that he pertinaciously adheres to a heresy that was condemned only implicitly, and if that same heresy is afterwards condemned explicitly by an assembled general council, is the pope to be deposed for his past offence, or is he to be declared to have been already deposed, even if he is willing to assent to the general council? Or, if the general council offers no resistance and he retracts his heresy, is the pope to be regarded as true and Catholic? The second question is whether a pope who pertinaciously holds a heresy condemned only implicitly, and who afterwards, before any action or challenge, returns to Catholic truth, ought to consider himself deposed, although all Catholics regard him as the true pope. Answer these two questions without lengthy discussion.

units.la: MAGIST. Ad primam respondetur, quod papa si in concilio generali legitime convincatur pertinaciter adhaesisse cuicunque haeresi latenti qualitercunque scripturae diuinae vel doctrinae vniuersalis ecclesiae obuianti, etiam si de ea nunquam antea mentio expressa fuisset, quantumcunque in generali concilio paratus sit corrigi, pro depositio est habendus, nec potest licite papali fungi officio, nisi in summum pontificem nouiter eligatur. Cuius ratio assignatur, quia omnis haereticus siue occultus siue manifestus, siue pro haeresi damnata implicite vel explicite est damnatus priuatus & excommunicatus. cum ergo papa talis fuerit ante concilium haereticus, licet non constiterit ecclesiae, tunc fuit papatu priuatus, licet non haberetur pro priuato. ergo postquam constat ecclesiae quod fuit haereticus, ecclesia debet eum fuisse depositum reputare.
units.tr: Master. To the first it is answered that if a pope is lawfully convicted in a general council of having pertinaciously adhered to any hidden heresy, in whatever way it runs counter to divine Scripture or to the universal doctrine of the Church, even if it was never expressly mentioned before, and however ready he may be in the general council to be corrected, he is to be held deposed, and he cannot lawfully exercise the papal office unless he is newly elected as supreme pontiff. The reason given is that every heretic, whether hidden or manifest, and whether condemned implicitly or explicitly for a heresy, is deprived and excommunicated. Since, then, such a pope was a heretic before the council, although this had not been established to the Church, he was then deprived of the papacy, though he was not held to be deprived. Therefore, once it is established to the Church that he was a heretic, the Church ought to consider him to have been deposed.

units.la: DISCIP. Ista responsio videtur omnino falsa. quia secundum iura, quae saepe prius tacta sunt, errans contra fidem qui paratus est corrigi, non est haereticus reputandus. si ergo papa in concilio generali paratus est corrigi, non est haereticus reputandus: & per consequens pro damnato minime est habendus.
units.tr: Student. This answer seems wholly false, because according to the laws, which have often been cited before, one who errs against the faith but is ready to be corrected is not to be reckoned a heretic. If therefore the pope in a general council is ready to be corrected, he is not to be reckoned a heretic, and consequently is by no means to be held condemned.

units.la: MAGIST. Ista instantia videtur omnino falsa. nam licet secundum iura & testimonia sanctorum errans qui paratus est corrigi, tunc non sit inter haereticos computandus: multi tamen errantes contra fidem, possunt parati esse corrigi, qui prius parati corrigi non fuerunt, sed extiterunt penitus pertinaces. & ideo potest contingere, quod aliquis primo est haereticus, quia tunc non est paratus corrigi: & tamen cum coeperit esse corrigibilis, non est haereticus reputandus. Sic esset de papa, quia si primo quantumcunque latenter scripturae diuinae vel doctrinae vniuersalis ecclesiae aduersantem, & ideo non explicite, sed implicite tantummodo condemnatum solenniter diffinireret esse tenendum: tunc esset pertinax & haereticus iudicandus: si tamen postea in concilio generali vel alias paratus esset corrigi, tunc non esset haereticus, sed prius fuisset haereticus. non ergo per hoc, quod errans contra fidem paratus est corrigi, poterit ostendi quod prius non fuit haereticus: sed per hoc declaratur, quod tunc non est haereticus, quando paratus est corrigi.
units.tr: Master. This objection seems wholly false. For although, according to the laws and the testimonies of the saints, one who errs against the faith and is ready to be corrected is then not to be counted among heretics, nevertheless many who err against the faith may come to be ready to be corrected, though previously they were not ready but were utterly obstinate. So it can happen that someone is first a heretic, because then he is not ready to be corrected, and yet, once he has begun to be correctable, he is not to be reckoned a heretic. It would be the same with the pope: if at first, however hidden, he solemnly defined that something must be held which opposes divine Scripture or the universal doctrine of the Church, and so was condemned not explicitly but only implicitly, he would have to be judged pertinacious and a heretic. Yet if afterwards, in a general council or elsewhere, he were ready to be corrected, he would not then be a heretic, but he would have been one before. Therefore it cannot be shown from the fact that one who errs against the faith is ready to be corrected that he was not previously a heretic; rather it is declared that he is not a heretic at the time when he is ready to be corrected.

units.la: DISCIP. Dicad secundam interrogationem. MAG. Ad secundam consimiliter respondetur, quod papa pertinaciter tenens errorem contra fidem damnatum duntaxat implicite; si postea siue accusatur, siue diffamatur, siue in nullo penitus diffamatus cognoscat errorem suum, & sciat se errori contra fidem pertinaciter adhaesisse; debet seipsum depositum reputare & tenunrenunciare Papatui: quia dicit se scire à iure Diuino depositum: licet Ecclesia vniuersalis errans quantum ad id quod factum est & in facto consistit, reputauerit eum verum Papam. Quemadmodum Ecclesia vniuersalis erravit quantum ad id quod consistebat in facto, quando habuit mulierem pro Papa vero. Discip. Nunc allega illa decreta, in quibus fundant se dicentes deponendum Papam pertinaciter asserentem ac tenentem haeresim damnatam explicite, non est necesse generale concilium congregari. Magist. Ad hoc principaliter tria decreta adduci possunt: quae ponuntur 23. q. 1. Ast enim Gelasius Papa, vt habetur ibidem, c. Achatius, non est factus inventor novi erroris: sed veteris imitator. Atq; ideo non erat necessarium vt adversus eum nova scita prodirent: sed antiqua tantum modo renovarentur. Et infra: Quicunq; enim in haeresim semel damnatam labitur, eius damnatione seipsum involuit. Ex quibus verbis clare colligitur, vt videtur, quod si Papa erroris veteris imitator in haeresim, scilicet damnatam semel labitur, eadem damnatione involvitur. Nec est necesse, quod contra eum nova scita prodeant, id est nova statuta. Et per consequens non est necesse contra eum generale concilium novitèr congregari. Quia vt dicit Glos. ibidem: Hic est casus, in quo Papa in canonem latae sententiae incidit. Pro illo autem casu, in quo quis incidit in canonem latae sententiae, pro quo Ecclesia scit distincte speciale esse sententiam promulgatam, non est necesse concilium generale congregari novitèr. Discip. Secundum istam auctoritatem non videtur, quod sit necesse contra Papam, qui incidit in haeresim damnatam implicite novitèr concilium convocari: quia pro damnato non est necesse concilium convocari. Papa enim si incidit in haeresim damnatam implicite est damnatus. Quia, vt dicit Gelasius. Quicunq; in haeresim semel damnatam labitur, eius damnatione seipsum involvit. Non autem distinguit inter haeresim damnatam implicite & explicite. Ergo nec nos debemus distinguere: & per consequens si Papa incidit in haeresim damnatam implicite damnatus est. Ergo pro eius damnatione non est necesse generale concilium congregari. Magist. Ad hoc respondetur, sicut tactum est, quod pro damnato, quem constat Ecclesiae esse damnatum, non est necesse generale concilium convocari: sed pro damnato quem non constat Ecclesiae esse damnatum, necesse est in casu concilium convocari ad inquirendum & declarandum eum esse damnatum. Sic est de Papa, si labitur pertinaciter manifeste in haeresim damnatam tantum modo implicite, quem viri periti in diuinis scripturis cum instantia magna asserunt haereticum & haeresim pertinaciter affirmare. Quia tunc oportet concilium generale convenire non ad deponendum Papam, sed ad declarandum & pronunciandum Papam esse haereticum damnatum: quod accidit, si Papa incidit in haeresim damnatam explicite, non est necesse congregari concilium nec ad deponendum Papam haereticum nec ad declarandum esse damnatum. Discip. Aliud decretum allega. Magist. Aliud decretum eiusdem, qui, vt legitur ibidem c. maiores, sic ait: Maiores nostri diuina inspiratione cernentes necessarie praecaverunt, vt quod contra unamquamque haeresim coacta semel synodus pro fidei communione & veritate catholica atq; Apostolica promulgasset, non sinerent novis post hos retractationibus mutilari. Et infra: sed autore cuiuslibet infamia ac pariter errore damnato sufficere iudicauerunt, vt quisquis huiusmodi erroris aliquando communicator existeret, principali sententia damnationis eius esset obstructus. Sic Sabellium damnavit synodus: nec fuit necesse vt eius sectatores postea damnarentur. Sed pro tenore constitutionis antiquae, qui vel praesuitatis illius vel communionis existerint participes, vniversalis Ecclesia duxit esse refutandos. Sic Arrii, sic Eunomii Macedonii, & Nestorii synodus semel gesta condemnans vlterius ad nova concilia venire non finit. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, q; si Papa quicunq; vel alius pertinaciter adhaerere presumpserit erroridamnato, eadem damnatione involvitur: nec est necesse concilium novitèr convocari. Quod Felix Papa, vt ibidem dicitur, aperte testari videtur dicens: Achatius non fuit novi (vel proprii) inventor erroris, vt in eum nova scita prodirent: sed alieno facinori suam communionem miscuit. Itaq; necesse est vt in illam recideret ista lance sententiam, quam cum suis successoribus per conuenientiam synodalem susceperat autor erroris. Si igitur Papa labitur in damnatum errorem: non est necesse contra eum novitèr generale concilium congregari. Quod intelligendum est de omni errore damnato explicite, qualis est omnis error scripturae Diuinę vel doctrinae vniversalis Ecclesiae patenter omnibus intelligentibus contradicens pariter & aduersans. Unde si Papa sollenniter diffiniret, Abraham non habuisse plures vxores, aut Pharaonem non fuisse regem Ægypti, vel Ioab non fuisse filium Sannae, aut aliquid huiusmodi, quod ad salutem videtur impertinens, esset haereticus manifestus: nec esset necesse contra eum concilium generale congregare: sed statim quilibet sciens ipsum diffiniisse sollenniter vel alio modo pertinaciter tenuisse aliquod praedictorum vel aliquod consimile deberet eum pro depositio & pro damnato habere. Discip. Adducas alias rationes motiuas ad probandum, quod non licet communicare Papae haeretico modo expositio in principio huius capituli. Mag. Hoc probatur tertio sic. Illi, qui nihil habet potestatis aut iuris, non licet communicare modo illo. Papa autem haereticus nihil habet potestatis aut iuris, teste Cypriano, qui, vt legitur 24. q. 1. c. didicimus. Didicimus omnes omnino haereticos & schismaticos nihil habere potestatis aut iuris. Ergo Papae haeretico communicare non licet. Quarto probatur specialiter, q; non licet verbo, scripto, vel facto asserere, verum esse Papam, quia nulli licet mentiri neque verbo neq; scripto neq; facto. Sed qui credit eum esse haereticum, & tamen eum asserit verum Papam, mentitur: cum non sit verus Papa, sed depositus tam a iure Diuino quam a iure humano, scilicet conciliis generalibus, sicut probatum est prius. Quibus subest Papa in causa haeresis, prout superius est ostensum. Ergo nullo scienti Papam esse haereticum licet Papam vocare, nisi ratione alicuius adiectionis vel modi loquendi, vt per talem appellationem sane intelligentibus non intelligatur esse verus Papa. Licet enim vocare Papam haereticum, Papam talium, qui sibi faucerent & habent eum pro Papa. Si etiam aliquis confirmando modo loquendi aliorum vocarent eum Papam sine adiectione, non esset forte peccatum mortale.
units.tr: Student. Now state the second question. Master. To the second, similarly, it is answered that a pope who pertinaciously holds an error against the faith condemned only implicitly, if afterwards he is either accused, or defamed, or, though not defamed at all, recognises his error and knows that he has pertinaciously adhered to an error against the faith, ought to consider himself deposed and must renounce the papacy, because he knows from divine law that he is deposed; although the universal Church, erring as to what was done and consisting in fact, has regarded him as the true pope. Just as the universal Church erred as to what consisted in fact when it held a woman to be the true pope. Student. Now cite those decrees on which those who say that a pope who pertinaciously asserts and holds an explicitly condemned heresy must be deposed base themselves, and say that a general council need not be convened. Master. For this purpose three decrees can chiefly be adduced, which are set down in 23 q. 1. First, Pope Gelasius, as is found there in the chapter Achatius: "He was not the inventor of a new error but an imitator of an old one. And therefore it was not necessary that new decrees be issued against him, but only that the ancient ones be renewed." And below: "For whoever slips into a heresy once condemned has involved himself in its condemnation." From these words it is clearly gathered, as it seems, that if a pope, an imitator of an old error, slips into a heresy once condemned, he is involved in that same condemnation. Nor is it necessary that new decrees, that is new statutes, be issued against him. Consequently it is not necessary that a general council be newly convened against him. For, as the gloss there says: "This is a case in which the pope falls under a canon of latae sententiae." In the case of one who falls under a canon of latae sententiae, when the Church knows distinctly that a special sentence has been promulgated, it is not necessary that a general council be newly convened. Student. According to this authority it does not seem necessary that a council be convoked anew against a pope who has fallen into a heresy condemned only implicitly, because for one already condemned no council need be convened. For if the pope falls into a heresy condemned implicitly, he is condemned, since, as Gelasius says, "whoever slips into a heresy once condemned has involved himself in its condemnation." He does not, however, distinguish between a heresy condemned implicitly and one condemned explicitly. Therefore neither should we distinguish, and consequently if the pope falls into a heresy condemned implicitly, he is condemned. Therefore a general council need not be convened for his condemnation. Master. To this it is answered, as has been touched on, that for one condemned whose condemnation is certain to the Church, a general council need not be convened; but for one whose condemnation is not certain to the Church, a council must in such a case be convened to inquire into and declare that he is condemned. So it is with the pope, if he manifestly and pertinaciously slips into a heresy condemned only implicitly, which learned men in divine Scriptures with great insistence assert to be heretical, and which he pertinaciously affirms. For then a general council must assemble not to depose the pope but to declare and pronounce that the pope is a condemned heretic. Whereas if the pope falls into a heresy condemned explicitly, there is no need to convene a council either to depose the heretical pope or to declare him condemned. Student. Cite another decree. Master. Another decree of the same author, who, as is read there in the chapter Maiores, says: "Our elders, discerning by divine inspiration, wisely took precautions that what a synod once assembled had promulgated against each heresy, for the common faith and the catholic and apostolic truth, should not be mutilated by new retractations after them." And below: "But they judged that, once the author is infamous and the error likewise condemned, it should suffice that whoever at any time shared in this error should be bound by the principal sentence of condemnation. Thus the synod condemned Sabellius, and it was not necessary that his followers be condemned afterwards. But according to the tenor of the ancient constitution, the universal Church judged that those who had been participants in his perversity or communion should be refuted. So too the synod once held, condemning Arius, Eunomius, Macedonius and Nestorius, does not allow them to come any further to new councils." From these words it is gathered that if a pope, or anyone else, presumes pertinaciously to adhere to a condemned error, he is involved in that same condemnation, and it is not necessary that a council be newly convened. Pope Felix seems plainly to bear witness to this, as is said there, saying: "Acacius was not the inventor of a new (or his own) error, so that new decrees should be issued against him; but he joined his communion to another's crime. Therefore it is necessary that the sentence which the author of the error had received, together with his successors, through synodal agreement, should fall back upon him in that same balance." If therefore the pope slips into a condemned error, it is not necessary that a general council be newly convened against him. This is to be understood of every error condemned explicitly, such as every error that openly contradicts, and plainly opposes, the Scripture of God or the universal doctrine of the Church, to all who understand. Hence if the pope solemnly defined that Abraham did not have several wives, or that Pharaoh was not king of Egypt, or that Joab was not the son of Zeruiah, or anything of this kind which seems irrelevant to salvation, he would be a manifest heretic, and it would not be necessary to convene a general council against him. Rather, anyone who knew that he had solemnly defined, or otherwise pertinaciously held, any of the aforesaid or something similar, ought at once to hold him as deposed and as condemned. Student. Cite other reasons supporting the view that it is not lawful to communicate with a heretical pope in the manner set out at the beginning of this chapter. Master. This is proved thirdly thus. It is not lawful to communicate with one who has no power or right. But a heretical pope has no power or right, as Cyprian testifies, who, as is read in 24 q. 1, c. Didicimus, says: "We have learned that all heretics and schismatics absolutely have no power or right." Therefore it is not lawful to communicate with a heretical pope. Fourthly it is proved specifically that it is not lawful to assert by word, writing or deed that the pope is true, because it is lawful for no one to lie by word, writing or deed. But whoever believes him to be a heretic and yet asserts him to be the true pope, lies, since he is not the true pope but has been deposed both by divine law and by human law, namely by general councils, as was proved before. To these the pope is subject in a case of heresy, as was shown above. Therefore, to anyone who knows the pope to be a heretic, it is not lawful to call him pope, except by some addition or manner of speaking, so that by such an appellation he is not understood, by those who understand rightly, to be the true pope. For it is lawful to call the pope a heretic, or the pope of those who favour him and hold him as pope. If also someone, by the established manner of speaking of others, were to call him pope without addition, it would perhaps not be a mortal sin.

units.la: CAP. LXI.
units.tr: CHAPTER LXI.

units.la: In quo probantur tres conclusiones capitulo precedenti posita, scilicet secunda, tertia & quarta. Et ea que ibi est secunda, probatur hic primo.
units.tr: In which the three conclusions laid down in the preceding chapter are proved, namely the second, third and fourth. The second of them is proved here first.

units.la: Discipulus. In praeterito capitulo dixi, mihi visum fuisse quatuor esse probanda circa assertionem in principio eiusdem capituli recitatam, disseruisti de primo. Nunc autem breviter de tribus sequentibus inquiga. Magist. Primum illorum trium est, quod communicantes praedicto modo Papae sunt fautores haeretici & haereticae pravitatis. Quod videtur sic posse probari. Non minus sunt communicantes praedicto modo Papae haeretico fautores & suae haereticae pravitatis, quam illi qui sibi nunquam resistunt cum possint. Sed qui Papae haeretico non resistunt cum possint, sunt fautores haeretici & haereticae pravitatis, quemadmodum errare monstratur qui alios cum potest non revocat ab errore, extra, de haereticis, qui alios. Ergo communicantes Papae haeretico sunt fautores haeretici & haereticae pravitatis. Discip. Istud argumentum procedit de illis, ad quos spectat Papae haeretico resistere, & pro viribus obviare: non autem spectat ad omnes Papae haeretico resistere. Et ideo multi possunt absque fauore vel fautoria haereticorum & haereticae pravitatis non resistere, sed communicare eidem.
units.tr: Disciple. In the preceding chapter I said that I thought four things had to be proved concerning the assertion recited at the beginning of that chapter. You have discussed the first; now I ask you briefly about the three that follow. Master. The first of those three is that those who communicate with the Pope in the aforesaid manner are supporters of heresy and of heretical depravity. This seems to be provable as follows. Those who communicate with a heretical Pope in the aforesaid manner are no less supporters of heresy and of its depravity than those who never resist him although they are able to. But those who do not resist a heretical Pope although they are able to are supporters of heresy and of heretical depravity, just as one who does not recall others from error when he can is shown to be in error, Extra, On heretics, Qui alios. Therefore those who communicate with a heretical Pope are supporters of heresy and of heretical depravity. Disciple. That argument holds of those to whom it belongs to resist a heretical Pope and oppose him with their strength; but it does not belong to everyone to resist a heretical Pope. And so many people, without favouring or supporting heretics or heretical depravity, can fail to resist and yet communicate with him.

units.la: Magist. Istam responsionem nonnulli sicut insanissimam detestantur, affirmantes aperte, quod dicere quod possit esse aliquis catholicus, ad quem non pertineat pro loco & tempore si convenienter potest Papae haeretico obviare satagenti fidem corrumpere orthodoxam, sapit haeresim manifestam. Quia ex hoc sequitur evidenter, quod aliquis catholicus zelum fidei non tenetur habere: & quod ad aliquem catholicum defensio fidei modo sibi congruenti quando potest minime spectat. Quod infidelitatem sapere arbitrantur. Si enim quilibet modo sibi congruente (quando potest) socium, patriam, praelatum, Dominum temporalem, parentes, consanguineos, benefactores & amicos, pauperes, pupillos, viduas, & alias miserabiles personas, acres temporales communes, & proximorum suorum, quando viderit periculum iniquum & evidens imminere, tenetur, quantum sibi licet pro gradu & officio defensare: sapitque haeresim manifestam dicere, quod talis defensio ad quecunque non pertinet Christianum, quia hoc non est aliud quam dicere quod possit esse aliquis Christianus, qui proximos suos non teneatur diligere, qui indigentibus & in periculo constitutis cum non apparet alius, qui velit & possit subvenire, non debet subvenire, cum potest, qui proximo prodesse cum potest, nullatenus tenetur, & quad opera misericordiae quando potest nullatenus teneatur, quae omnia & consimilia scripturis Divinis & bonis moribus aperte repugnant. Multo magis debet quilibet modo sibi congruenti cum potest fide catholicam defendere: eo quod fides catholica, sine qua non est salus, universis mortalibus quantum ad vitam temporalem, & cunctis rebus temporalibus praeferenda est: quae magis quam vita temporalis aliena vel propria defendenda est. Non autem fides defenditur, nisi Papae haeretico cupienti ipsam destruere resistatur. Ergo quilibet catholicus cum potest tenetur Papae haeretico pro posse resistere; debitis tamen circumstantiis observatis: quia ad hunc articulum obligamur praecepto affirmativo, quod non obligat pro semper.
units.tr: Master. Some people utterly detest this answer as most insane, asserting openly that to say there can be a Catholic to whom it does not pertain, according to place and time, to oppose a heretical Pope striving to corrupt the orthodox faith, when he conveniently can, smacks of manifest heresy. For from this it evidently follows that a Catholic is not bound to have zeal for the faith, and that the defence of the faith in a manner suited to him does not at all belong to any Catholic when he can. They think this smacks of unbelief. For if anyone is bound, in a manner suited to him (when he can), to defend, as far as he is permitted by his rank and office, his companion, his country, his prelate, his temporal lord, his parents, his kinsmen, his benefactors and friends, the poor, orphans, widows, and other wretched persons, and the common temporal goods and those of his neighbours, when he sees an unjust and evident danger threatening them; then it smacks of manifest heresy to say that such defence does not pertain to any Christian. For this is nothing other than to say that there can be a Christian who is not bound to love his neighbours, who need not help the needy and those in danger when no one else appears who is willing and able to help, who is under no obligation to benefit his neighbour when he can, and who is in no way bound to perform works of mercy when he can. All these things, and things like them, openly contradict the Divine Scriptures and good morals. Much more, then, must each person, in whatever manner suits him, defend the Catholic faith when he can, since the Catholic faith, without which there is no salvation, is to be preferred to all temporal things for all mortals, as far as temporal life goes; it must be defended more than temporal life, whether another's or one's own. But the faith is not defended unless resistance is offered to a heretical Pope who desires to destroy it. Therefore every Catholic, when he can, is bound to resist a heretical Pope to the best of his power, the due circumstances being observed; for we are bound to this article by an affirmative precept, which does not bind at all times.

units.la: Quamvis autem ad omnes spectat resistere Papae haeretico, non tamen ad omnes spectat eodem modo resistere Papae haeretico: sed ad praelatos doctores & officium praedicationis habentes spectat resistere, eius errores publice reprobando, & auditores in veritate catholica instruendo & efficaciter confirmando. Ad praelatos autem specialiter spectat sequaces Papae haeretici (ne doctrinam eius erroneam teneant & divulgent aut asserant) prohibere, & poenis debitis coercere. Ad reges autem & principes & publicas potestates (si a catholicis fuerint requisiti, vel praelati in impugnando pravitatem haereticam fuerint negligentes damnabiliter) spectat per temporalem potentiam Papam haereticum & sequaces eius ne corrumpant catholicos impedire ipsos (si expediens fuerit) captiuando: & quousque rite fuerit ordinatum (quid sit de eis agendum) in firma custodia (ne inficere valeant orthodoxos & simplices) detinendo. Ad omnes autem simplices & alios quoscunque spectat alios impugnantes Papam haereticum & sequaces eiusdem tueri & defendere: ac omnibus praelatis regibus & principibus & aliis potestatibus publicis in his, qua rite agunt ad coertionem Papae haeretici obedire & resistere toto corde. Ad cunctos autem scientes Papam esse haereticum spectat ei in his quae ad religionem spectant Christianam nullatenus communicare. Ad hoc enim nos obligat praeceptum negativum, quod non solum semper, sed etiam obligat pro semper.
units.tr: Although it belongs to all to resist a heretical Pope, it does not belong to all to resist him in the same way. Rather, it belongs to prelates, teachers and those who hold the office of preaching to resist him, publicly condemning his errors and instructing and effectively confirming the hearers in Catholic truth. It belongs especially to prelates to forbid the followers of a heretical Pope (lest they hold, spread or assert his erroneous doctrine) and to restrain them with due penalties. It belongs to kings, princes and public authorities (if they have been asked by Catholics, or if the prelates have been culpably negligent in opposing heretical depravity) to hinder, by temporal power, a heretical Pope and his followers from corrupting Catholics, by imprisoning them (if it is expedient), and, until it has been properly decided what is to be done with them, to keep them in firm custody, lest they be able to infect the orthodox and simple. It belongs to all simple people and to any others whatever, who oppose the heretical Pope and his followers, to protect and defend them; and it belongs to all of them to obey and resist, with the whole heart, all prelates, kings, princes and other public authorities who act rightly in restraining a heretical Pope. It belongs to all who know that the Pope is a heretic to have no communion with him whatever in those matters which pertain to the Christian religion. For a negative precept binds us to this, which not only always binds but also binds at every moment.

units.la: Discip. Breviter proba tertium & quartum, quae posita sunt in capitulo precedenti. Magist. Tertium sic probatur. Qui negat Christum aut fidem Christianam metu mortis aut graviorum tormentorum, non est haereticus reputandus. Ergo a simili qui communicat Papae haeretico in his quae ad religionem Christianam vel Papale spectant officium, metu mortis aut graviorum tormentorum, non est fautor haeretici aut pravitatis haereticae reputandus. Quartum, scilicet quod communicantes Papae haeretico praedicto modo etiam metu mortis vel graviorum tormentorum peccant mortaliter, probatur sic. Quod est in detrimentum fidei Christianae, est peccatum mortale. Communicare autem Papae haeretico, praedicto modo, est detrimentum fidei Christianae: ergo est peccatum mortale.
units.tr: Disciple. Briefly prove the third and fourth points, which were laid down in the preceding chapter. Master. The third is proved thus. One who denies Christ or the Christian faith out of fear of death or of more severe torments is not to be reckoned a heretic. Therefore, by parity, one who communicates with a heretical Pope in those matters which pertain to the Christian religion or to the papal office, out of fear of death or of more severe torments, is not to be reckoned a supporter of a heretic or of heretical depravity. The fourth, namely that those who communicate with a heretical Pope in the aforesaid manner sin mortally even out of fear of death or of more severe torments, is proved thus. What is to the detriment of the Christian faith is a mortal sin. But to communicate with a heretical Pope in the aforesaid manner is to the detriment of the Christian faith. Therefore it is a mortal sin.

units.la: CAP. LXII. In quo quaeritur de eis, qui communicant Papae haeretico, ignorantes secundum utramque ignorantiam, scilicet crassam & invincibilem.
units.tr: CAP. LXII. Concerning those who communicate with the heretical Pope while ignorant in both kinds of ignorance, namely gross and invincible.

units.la: Discipulus. Tractavimus de communicantibus scienter Papae haeretico. Nunc videamus de communicantibus ignoranter eidem. Primo de laborantibus ignorantia crassa & supina, an scilicet sint censendi fautores haeretici & haereticae prauitatis: & de communicantibus Papae haeretico & de sequacibus eius. Magist. De ignorantibus ignorantia crassa & supina: & tamen communicantibus Papae haeretico & sequacibus eius dicitur, sicut de communicantibus eidem scienter: quod ignorantia talis non excusat peccatum: cum ipsa ignorantia sit damnabilis. Discip. Supra multa dicta sunt de ignorantia ista. Ideo nunc succincte dic, qui communicantes Papae haeretico ignoranter sunt censendi laborare ignorantia crassa & supina? Magist. Ex praedecentibus poteris hoc aperte colligere: quod illi, qui nolunt de haeresibus Papae haeretici informari: sed informare volentes persequuntur & molestant: & qui contemnunt scire Papam esse haereticum: & qui facile possunt scire: sunt ignorantes ignorantia crassa & supina. Discip. Dic de communicantibus haeretico Papae, qui ignorant ignorantia inuincibili & probabili. Magist. De illis dicitur, quod non peccant mortaliter, nec sunt fautores haereticorum: quia ignorantia talis eos excusat. Discip. Qui sunt censendi laborare ignorantia probabili? Magist. Illi qui nescirent Papam haereticum de haeresi diffamari: & qui non essent capaces informationis, qua ostenditur Papa esse haereticus, vel non possent faciliter neq; per se neq; per alios Papam scire esse haereticum: laborarent ignorantia probabili, & si communicarent eidem, excusarentur a peccato mortali.
units.tr: Disciple. We have treated of those who communicate knowingly with the heretical Pope. Now let us consider those who communicate with him in ignorance. First, concerning those labouring under gross and supine ignorance: whether they are to be judged supporters of the heretic and of heretical pravity; and concerning those who communicate with the heretical Pope and with his followers. Master. Concerning those ignorant with gross and supine ignorance, it is said of those who communicate with the heretical Pope and his followers, just as of those who communicate with him knowingly, that such ignorance does not excuse the sin, since the ignorance itself is damnable. Disciple. Many things have been said above about this ignorance. Therefore now briefly tell me: who are to be judged to labour under gross and supine ignorance while communicating ignorantly with the heretical Pope? Master. From what has been said before you may plainly gather this: those who are unwilling to be informed about the heresies of the heretical Pope, but persecute and harass those who want to inform them; those who scorn to know that the Pope is a heretic; and those who could easily know it: these are ignorant with gross and supine ignorance. Disciple. Tell me about those who communicate with the heretical Pope while ignorant with invincible and probable ignorance. Master. Of them it is said that they do not sin mortally, nor are they supporters of heretics, because such ignorance excuses them. Disciple. Who are to be judged to labour under probable ignorance? Master. Those who would not know that the Pope has been publicly reported as a heretic; and those who were not capable of the information by which it is shown that the Pope is a heretic, or who could not easily know, either themselves or through others, that the Pope is a heretic: they would labour under probable ignorance, and if they communicated with him, they would be excused from mortal sin.

units.la: CAP. LXIII. In quo agitur de obedientibus Papae haeretico.
units.tr: CHAPTER LXIII. In which it is treated of those who obey a heretical Pope.

units.la: Discipulus. De istis quaerere haberem multa: sed ea ad tractatum De gestu circa fidem altercantium orthodoxam reservo. Nunc autem dic breviter de obedientibus Papae haeretico, an scilicet sint fautores haeretici & haereticae prauitatis. Magist. Respondetur, quod obedire Papae haeretico contingit dupliciter. Uno modo in puris temporalibus & corporalibus: alio modo in spiritualibus vel in his quae ad Papatus spectant officium. Item, contingit obedire Papae haeretico scienter & ignoranter. Qui enim obediret Papae haeretico in temporalibus vel in puris corporalibus: & talis obedientia non esset in nocumentum Ecclesiae vel alterius personae: nec esset in scandalum, sed esset in salutationem corporalem obedientis & ad redimendum vexationem eius, non peccaret mortaliter. Si autem talis obedientia esset in nocumentum Ecclesiae & personae, vel in scandalum, obediens peccaret mortaliter, quia nullus propter mandatum vel praeceptum haeretici (praesertim qui non est Dominus in temporalibus eius, cui praecipit) debet aliquid facere in nocumentum vel scandalum alterius cuiuscunq;. Qui autem scienter obediret Papae haeretico in spiritualibus, puta recipiendo ab eo Ecclesiasticum beneficium, vel ordines, aut aliquid consimile, peccaret mortaliter, & fautor esset haeretici & haereticae prauitatis. De obedientibus Papae haeretico ignoranter, qui laborarent ignorantia crassa & supina, dicitur sicut de obedientibus scienter: quia talis ignorantia non excusat. De ignorantibus ignorantia invincibili dicitur: quod non peccant mortaliter, quia ignorantia eos excusat.
units.tr: Student. I would have many questions about these matters, but I am keeping them for the treatise On the conduct of those who dispute with the orthodox about the faith. For now, tell me briefly about those who obey a heretical Pope: whether they are, that is, supporters of heresy and of heretical depravity. Master. The answer is that obeying a heretical Pope happens in two ways. In one way, it is in purely temporal and bodily matters; in the other, it is in spiritual matters or in those that belong to the office of the Papacy. Again, one may obey a heretical Pope knowingly or unknowingly. Someone who obeyed a heretical Pope in temporal matters or in purely bodily ones, where such obedience would not harm the Church or any other person, nor give offence, but would serve the obedient man's bodily welfare and ransom him from trouble, would not sin mortally. If, however, such obedience would harm the Church or a person, or give offence, the obedient man would sin mortally, because no one ought to do anything, on the command or order of a heretic (especially one who is not lord of the temporal affairs of the person he commands), that harms or gives offence to anyone whatsoever. But whoever knowingly obeyed a heretical Pope in spiritual matters, for instance by receiving from him an ecclesiastical benefice, or orders, or something of the same kind, would sin mortally and would be a supporter of heresy and of heretical depravity. Of those who obey a heretical Pope unknowingly, and who labour under gross and listless ignorance, the same is said as of those who obey knowingly, because such ignorance does not excuse. Of those who are ignorant through invincible ignorance it is said that they do not sin mortally, because their ignorance excuses them.

units.la: CAP. LXIV. In quo solvuntur rationes cap. 59. adducta, quae videbantur contrariari tam dictis.
units.tr: CHAPTER 64. In which the arguments of chapter 59, which seemed to contradict the views stated, are resolved.

units.la: Discipulus. Circa interrogationem propositam supra c. huius septimi 59. audiui diuersas sententias, pro quibus fortiter allegasti. De allegationibus autem pro sententia tecum post completionem huius operis conferam diligenter. Nunc autem peto, ut quomodo respondetur ad allegationes pro prima sententia supra eodem c. 59. adductas non differas indagare. Magist. Ad primam illarum tripliciter respondetur. Uno modo, quod sacerdotes veteris legis ad quos Christus misit leprosos, ut communicarent eis in his quae spectabant ad sacerdotale officium, non erant haeretici. Quia Incarnatio Christi nondum fuerat divulgata. Et ideo licet explicite in Christum non crederent: non tamen erant haeretici iudicandi. Aliter dicitur, quod licet quidam sacerdotes illius temporis fuerunt haeretici (non quia non credebant explicite in Christum: sed quia praedicationi Christi pertinaciter resistebant) tamen praeter illos sacerdotes haereticos fuerunt quidam alii, qui Christo pertinaciter minime resistebant. Quorum aliqui in Christum explicite non credebant, nec etiam ei pertinaciter resistebant. Quidam forte explicite credebant in Christum, & erant forte occulti propter metum Iudaeorum. Unde & de sacerdotibus legitur Act. 6. quod multa turba sacerdotum obediebat fidei: quod contigit ante mortem Beati Stephani. Et ideo non est ita probabile dicere, quod aliqui sacerdotes, qui manifeste obedierunt fidei cito post mortem, quin crediderunt in Christum ante mortem eius, licet occulte. Erant ergo aliqui sacerdotes, qui non fuerunt haeretici: vel quia Christo nullatenus pertinaciter resistebant. citer resistebant: vel quia explicite credebant in eum. Ad quos potuit Christus leprosos transmittere, vt communicarent eis in his quae ad sacerdotale spectabant officium: licet non miserit eos ad sacerdotes, qui fuerunt prauitate haeretica irretiti. Aliter respondetur, quod sicut Papae haeretico licet communicare ignoranter, dummodo ignorantia non sit crassa & supina: ita tempore Christi fidelibus licuit communicare ignoranter sacerdotibus haereticis. Illi ergo leprosi, quos misit Christus ad sacerdotes haereticos, quia ignorabant eos esse haereticos, & non laborabant ignorantia crassa & supina, licite potuerunt communicare eisdem. Discip. Contra istam responsionem, mihi occurrit duplex obiectio. Prima est: quod Christus sciuit sacerdotes esse haereticos. Ergo ad eos non debuit mittere leprosos. Secunda est, quod ex quo Christus sciuit sacerdotes esse haereticos, hoc debuit declarare leprosis. Magist. Ad primam respondetur, quod quamuis Christus sciuerit sacerdotes esse haereticos: tamen potuit mittere leprosos ignorantes ad ipsos. Quia illis licuit, stante ignorantia, qua laborabant, communicare eisdem. Ad secundam respondetur, quod Christus non omnia omni tempore omnibus reuelauit: nec reuelare nisi quando voluit tenebatur. Et ideo quemadmodum non reuelauit Apostolis nequitiam Iudae: ita non reuelauit leprosis perfidiam sacerdotum. Et ideo licuit eis communicare eisdem. Discip. Quamuis licuisset leprosis communicare sacerdotibus haereticis ignoranter: non tamen licuit Christo praecipere vel consulere leprosis communicare eisdem. Quia cui non licet communicare alteri, non licet eidem dare consilium alii vt eidem communicet. Sicut cui non licet communicare excommunicato, ei non licet dare consilium alii vt excommunicato communicet. Si ergo Christo non licuit communicare sacerdotibus haereticis: non licuit Christo dare consilium vt eisdem sacerdotibus communicarent. Magist. Respondetur, quod ista instantia fundatur in medio falso. Hoc scilicet, cui non licet communicare alteri, non licet dare consilium alii vt eidem communicet. Exemplum habetur expressum in iure. 13. q. 2. c. quoniam multis. Ex quo capitulo colligitur expresse, quod multis non licet communicare quibusdam excommunicatis: quibus tamen licet consulere & dicere uxoribus excommunicatorum filiis suis & aliis quibusdam personis enumeratis ibidem, quod excommunicatis communicent. Sic si tu scis Papam esse haereticum manifestum, & quod probari potest haereticus, cui non licet communicare Papae haeretico, tibi non licet consulere credenti Papa non esse haereticum, & q non laborat ignorantia crassa & supina, vt eide communicet. Disc. Dic quomodo respondetur ad auctoritates Augustini, quibus videtur ostendi, q licet communicare haereticis in his, quae ad diuinum spectant officium. Mag. Ad auctoritates dupliciter respondetur. Primo, quia Aug. in omnibus illis auctoritatibus non loqtur de malis, qui erant haeretici: sed de aliis malis aliisq; criminibus irretitis, quibus licuit quantum ad sacramenta veteris legis communicare. Et a quibusdam recedendo non est corporaliter, sed spiritualiter. Aliter dicitur, quamuis non licuerit in veteri lege communicare haereticis & idolatris in perfidia sua manentibus: licuit tamen communicare eisdem correctis & ostendentibus se correctos. Illi autem haeretici & idolatrae eo ipso, q templum Dei ad brandum Deum & sacrificandum Deo & caetera faciendum, quae p lege Dei percipiebantur, eidem ostendebant facto se correctos: & ideo enim tempore licuit communicare eis: quia p tempore illo non debuerunt haeretici reputari. Disc. Secundum istam responsionem liceret in diuinis, haereticis communicare, q se ostenderent esse correctos. Mag. Respondetur, q alius modus recipiendi haereticos reuertentes ad fidem ordinatus est inter Christianos, q fuerit inter Iudaeos. Forte enim vt Iudaei reciperentur non aliud requirebatur, quando de eis non poterat fieri iustitia, nisi q facto vel verbo protestabantur se esse veros Dei cultores. Ad hoc aute, vt Christiani haeretici reuertentes ad fidem recipiantur ad communionem, quo ad Ecclesiastica sacramenta, hoc non sufficit: sed requiritur q in speciali abnegent errorem quem tenuerunt: & q a vinculo excommunicationis quo tenebantur, p Ecclesia absoluatur. Si autem fuerit platus, puta Papa, vel Episcopus, aut alia pditus dignitate, ad officium praelationis eius absq; electione noua nequaq; recipi debet: quia omnis haereticus tam in iure Diuino q in iure humano priuatus est omni Ecclesiastica dignitate. Aliter dicitur, quod in veteri lege non erat licitum interesse officio haereticorum. Licitum tamen erat permittere haeretico, officio & sacrificio fidelium interfuisse. Et ideo quamuis in noua lege esset licitum haereticos sustinere, audire diuinum officium a catholicis, nisi in contrarium esset per Ecclesiam ordinatum: nullo tamen modo licet catholicis officio haereticorum interesse: & ita missa Papae haeretici a nullo catholico debet audiri. Et eadem ratione in alio officio diuino sibi communicare non licet. Disc. Dic quomodo ad secundam rationem principalem respondetur. Mag. Respondetur, q sicut minora mala saepe permittenda sunt propter maiora vitanda: sic propter maiora mala vitanda, fas est petere missionem minorum malorum procurare & cetera impetrare: quia licet ipsa quae permittuntur sint mala & illicita: ipsa tamen permissio est licita. Et ideo permissionem malorum licet petere & etiam impetrare: licet commissio mali sit nullatenus impetranda. Et ideo beatus Ioh. Papa potuit licite impetrare, quod haeretici permitterentur in Ecclesiis catholicorum ritus suos celebrare, propter vitanda extinctionem Italiae: quae erat maius malum quam q haeretici in Ecclesiis permitterentur. Cum ergo dicitur, q beatus Iohannes impetrauit vel procurauit, quod Ecclesiae haereticis redderentur, dicitur q ibi verbum reddendi accipitur pro verbo permittendi. Quia eo ipso quod Ecclesiae permittebantur haereticis, ipsi erant parati eas accipere. Et ideo pro vitanda extinctione Italiae & gladio mali non fuit necesse plus impetrare, quam quod Ecclesiae permittantur haereticis. Et ideo beatus Iohannes solam permissionem huiusmodi impetrauit. Hoc autem fuit multo minus, quam in diuinis communicare haereticis. Sicut minus est permittere malum, quam committere malum. Ad tertiam rationem respondetur, quod non semper licet fidelibus alicui in aliquo officio communicare, quem debent in eodem ossiofficio tolerare. Quia sæpe tolerant, quia prohibere non possunt. Et ideo tolerantia talis est minime arguenda. Communicatio tamen cum eis esset omnino reprehensibilis iudicanda. Concedendum est ergo cum Augustino, quod tolerandi sunt mali pro pace; quando aliter pax absq; omni fructu spirituali penitus turbaretur. Non tamen pro pace communicandum est malis in his quæ sunt contra Deum. Quemadmodum ritus Iudæorum licite tolerantur: celebrare tamen cum eis ritus eorum catholicis minime licet. Sic etiam sancti toleraverunt idolatriam paganorum: quibus tamen in idolatria nullatenus communicare debebant. Ad quartam rationem respondetur, quod Iudas non legitur fuisse hæreticus, sed proditor. Unde etiam post proditionem dixit: peccavi tradens sanguinem iustum. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod Iudas post proditionem de Christo, quem iustum putavit, non erronee senserit: & ita non erat hæreticus. Vel si fuit hæreticus, non fuit hæreticus manifestus & publicus, sed occultus hæreticus. Occultus autem sive fuerit Papa, sive fuerit alius, non est in publico detestandus.
units.tr: Student. About the question put above in chapter 59 of this seventh part, I have heard various opinions, for which you argued strongly. I will compare the arguments for the opinion with you carefully after this work is finished. For now, I ask that you not delay in explaining how the arguments adduced in chapter 59 above for the first opinion are answered. Teacher. The first of those arguments is answered in three ways. First, the priests of the old law to whom Christ sent the lepers, so that they might take part with them in those things which pertained to the priestly office, were not heretics, because the incarnation of Christ had not yet been made known. So although they did not believe explicitly in Christ, they were not to be judged heretics. Second, it is said that although some priests of that time were heretics (not because they did not believe explicitly in Christ, but because they obstinately resisted the preaching of Christ), there were besides those heretical priests some others who did not obstinately resist Christ. Of these, some did not believe explicitly in Christ, nor did they obstinately resist him. Some perhaps believed explicitly in Christ and were perhaps secret believers for fear of the Jews. Hence we read in Acts 6 that a great crowd of priests obeyed the faith, which happened before the death of Blessed Stephen. And so it is not very probable to say that some priests, who openly obeyed the faith soon after his death, did not believe in Christ before his death, even if secretly. Therefore there were some priests who were not heretics, either because they did not obstinately resist Christ at all, or because they believed explicitly in him. To these Christ could send the lepers, so that they might take part with them in those things which pertained to the priestly office, although he did not send them to priests who were entangled in heretical wickedness. Third, it is answered that just as it is lawful to take part in the sacraments with a heretical Pope in ignorance, provided the ignorance is not gross and stupid, so in the time of Christ the faithful could take part with heretical priests in ignorance. Those lepers, then, whom Christ sent to the heretical priests, because they did not know that they were heretics and were not labouring under gross and stupid ignorance, could lawfully take part with them. Student. Against this answer, two objections occur to me. The first is that Christ knew the priests were heretics, so he ought not to have sent the lepers to them. The second is that, since Christ knew the priests were heretics, he ought to have declared this to the lepers. Teacher. To the first it is answered that although Christ knew the priests were heretics, he could still send the ignorant lepers to them, because it was lawful for them, while the ignorance they laboured under continued, to take part with them. To the second it is answered that Christ did not reveal everything to everyone at every time, nor was he bound to reveal anything except when he wished. And so, just as he did not reveal to the Apostles the wickedness of Judas, so he did not reveal to the lepers the perfidy of the priests. And so it was lawful for them to take part with them. Student. Although it would have been lawful for the lepers to take part in ignorance with heretical priests, it was not lawful for Christ to command or advise the lepers to take part with them. For whoever may not take part with another may not give advice to a third person that he should take part with him. Just as one who may not take part with an excommunicated person may not advise another to take part with the excommunicated person, so if it was not lawful for Christ to take part with heretical priests, it was not lawful for Christ to advise that the same priests should be taken part with. Teacher. It is answered that this objection is founded on a false premise, namely: whoever may not take part with another may not give advice to a third that he should take part with him. An example is expressly given in the law, 13 q. 2 c. Quoniam multis. From that chapter it is clearly inferred that it is not lawful for many to take part with certain excommunicated persons, yet it is lawful for them to advise the wives of excommunicated persons, their sons, and certain other persons listed there, that they should take part with the excommunicated. So if you know that the Pope is a manifest heretic, and that it can be proved that he is a heretic, and it is not lawful for you to take part with a heretical Pope, it is not lawful for you to advise one who believes the Pope is not a heretic, and who is not labouring under gross and stupid ignorance, that he should take part with him. Student. Tell me how the authorities of Augustine are answered, by which it seems to be shown that it is lawful to take part with heretics in those things which pertain to the divine office. Teacher. The authorities are answered in two ways. First, because in all those authorities Augustine does not speak of heretics, who were the wicked, but of others who were entangled in other wickedness and crimes, with whom it was lawful, as regards the sacraments of the old law, to take part. And he withdrew from some not bodily but spiritually. Second, it is said that although in the old law it was not lawful to take part with heretics and idolaters who remained in their perfidy, it was lawful to take part with the same persons once they had been corrected and showed themselves corrected.
