Those heretics and idolaters, by the very fact that they showed by their deeds that they had been corrected, by coming to the temple to bless God, to sacrifice to God, and to do the other things which were required by the law of God, were therefore at that time lawfully taken part with, because at that time they ought not to be regarded as heretics. Student. According to this answer, it would be lawful in divine matters to take part with heretics who showed themselves to be corrected. Teacher. It is answered that a different manner of receiving heretics returning to the faith has been established among Christians than among the Jews. For perhaps, in order that Jews be received, nothing more was required, when justice could not be done to them, than that they should declare by word or deed that they were true worshippers of God. But for Christian heretics returning to the faith to be received into communion, as regards the ecclesiastical sacraments, this is not enough. Rather it is required that they specifically renounce the error they held, and that they be absolved by the Church from the bond of excommunication by which they were held. If, however, a prelate, for instance a Pope or a Bishop, or another person deprived of dignity, is concerned, he must by no means be received back into the office of prelacy without a new election, because every heretic, both by divine law and by human law, is deprived of every ecclesiastical dignity. Another answer is that in the old law it was not permitted to take part in the office of heretics. It was, however, permitted to allow a heretic to be present at the office and sacrifice of the faithful. And so, although in the new law it is lawful to tolerate heretics and for Catholics to hear the divine office, unless the Church has ordained otherwise, yet in no way is it lawful for Catholics to take part in the office of heretics; and so the mass of a heretical Pope ought not to be heard by any Catholic. And for the same reason, it is not lawful to take communion with them in any other divine office. Student. Tell me how the second principal argument is answered. Teacher. It is answered that just as lesser evils often must be permitted in order to avoid greater ones, so, in order to avoid greater evils, it is permissible to ask for the permission of lesser evils, and to procure and obtain other things of that kind. For although the things that are permitted are evil and unlawful, the permission itself is lawful. And so it is lawful to ask for and even to obtain the permission of evils, although the commission of evil must in no way be obtained. And so Blessed Pope John could lawfully obtain that heretics be permitted to celebrate their rites in the churches of Catholics, in order to avoid the destruction of Italy, which was a greater evil than that heretics be permitted in the churches. When therefore it is said that Blessed John obtained or procured that the churches be given back to the heretics, it is said that the word "giving back" is taken there for the word "permitting." For by the very fact that the churches were permitted to the heretics, they were ready to receive them. And so, in order to avoid the destruction of Italy and the sword of evil, it was not necessary to obtain more than that the churches be permitted to the heretics. And so Blessed John obtained only such a permission. But this was far less than to take part with heretics in divine matters, just as it is less to permit an evil than to commit an evil. To the third argument it is answered that it is not always lawful for the faithful to take part with someone in an office in which they must tolerate him. For they often tolerate because they cannot prevent it, and so such toleration is by no means to be censured. Yet communion with them would be judged wholly reprehensible. It must therefore be conceded with Augustine that the wicked must be tolerated for the sake of peace, when otherwise peace would be wholly disturbed without any spiritual fruit. Yet for the sake of peace one must not take part with the wicked in those things which are against God. Just as the rites of the Jews are lawfully tolerated, yet it is by no means lawful for Catholics to celebrate their rites with them, so also the saints tolerated the idolatry of the pagans, yet they ought in no way to have taken part with them in idolatry. To the fourth argument it is answered that Judas is not read to have been a heretic, but a traitor. Hence also after the betrayal he said: I have sinned in betraying innocent blood. From these words it is gathered that Judas, after the betrayal, did not think erroneously about Christ, whom he considered just, and so he was not a heretic. Or if he was a heretic, he was not a manifest and public heretic, but a secret heretic. A secret heretic, however, whether he was a Pope or someone else, is not to be publicly detested.

units.la: CAP. LXV.
units.tr: CAP. LXV.

units.la: In quo agitur de defensoribus hæreticorum & hæreticæ pravitatis, & qui sint censendi esse tales.
units.tr: In which it is treated of the defenders of heretics and of heretical depravity, and who are to be counted as such.

units.la: DIscipulus. Quamvis adhuc de fautoribus hæreticorum & hæreticæ pravitatis essent inuestiganda quamplura, de quibus applicando ad determinatas personas in tractatu De gestis circa fidem altercantium orthodoxam sollicite indagabo: tamen omissis illis transeo ad defensionem hæreticorum & hæreticæ pravitatis. De quibus inprimis peto ut narres mihi, qui defensores hæreticorum & hæreticæ pravitatis sunt censendi. Magist. Respondetur quod cum defendere rem aliquam sit ab impugnatione tueri vel impugnatæ contra impugnantem opem ferre. Impugnatio autem tripliciter fieri potest, scilicet verbo, scripto & facto. Contingit defendere hæreticos & hæreticam pravitatem secundum quod hæretici & hæreticæ pravitas possent multipliciter impugnari. Hæreticus autem impugnari potest facto alicuius, qui conatur hæreticum captiuare aut detinere aut iudici præsentare vel ad iudicium trahere, ut de eo fiat iustitiæ complementum. Potest etiam impugnari verbo, & hoc multipliciter: vel in iudicio, cum rite & debite accusatur, vel extra iudicium, cum eius perfidia per prædicatores & doctores prælatos aut alios non ignaros nescientibus, ut caveant, nunciatur. Scripto etiam impugnari potest in iudicio, cum contra eum scribitur: vel etiam extra iudicium, cum eius perfidia rationibus & auctoritatibus demonstratur & ablentibus per Epistolas intimatur. Hæretica autem pravitas verbo & scripto poterit impugnari. Verbo quidem, cum in sermonibus aut locutionibus vel secretis colloquiis reprobatur. Scripto vero, cum ad reprobandum hæreticam pravitatem scripta à catholicis componuntur. Ex his verbis colligitur, quod contingit & hæreticos & hæreticam pravitatem multipliciter defendere. Et quot modis contingit hæreticos & pravitatem hæreticam impugnari, tot modis & forte pluribus defendi possent. Contingit ergo defendere hæreticos facto, impediendo videlicet ne capiantur aut detineantur, vel de his fiat iustitiæ complementum. Contingit etiam eos defendere verbo in iudicio & extra iudicium: allegando quod non sunt hæretici reprobandi vel reputandi. Scripto etiam contingit eos defendere libros & Epistolas componendo ad ostendendum & nunciandum, quod non sunt inter hæreticos computandi. Pravitatem etiam hæreticam contingit tripliciter defendere, scilicet verbo, facto, & scripto. Facto quidem duplicter ad præsens. Vno modo ipsos impugnatores ab impugnatione prohibendo. Alio modo impugnationes & allegationes eorum scriptas extinguendo sive comburendo, sive alio modo, vel malitiose detinendo & impediendo ne ad notitiam perveniant aliorum. Verbo etiam contingit pravitatem hæreticam defendere allegando, quod non sit inter hæreses computanda. Et eodem modo contingit scripto hæresim defendere. Disc. Secundum prædicta de defensoribus hæreticorum & hæreticæ pravitatis essent quamplurima indaganda: sed abbreviationis causa multa dimittam. Aliqua tamen quæram. Porro quia dubito, quod si vnquam aliquis Papa hæreticus perniciosior erit omnibus aliis hæreticis qui fuerunt vel erunt præter Antichristum magnum: si tamen idem Antichristus non erit Papa, interrogationes, quas faciam de defensoribus hæreticorum & hæreticæ pravitatis ad defensores Papæ hæretici & sequacium eius suarumque hæresum applicabo. Inprimis itaque dic qua pœna sint plectendi, qui de facto impediunt, ne de persona Papæ hæretici fiat iustitiæ complementum: tamen se de eius erroribus defendendis nullatenus intromittendo. Magist. Respondetur, quod tales impedientes & Papæ hæretico impedienti opem ferentes, ne de ipso fiat iustitiæ complementum, aut sciunt Papam esse hæreticum, aut ignorant. Et si ignorant, aut laborant ignorantia crassa & supina, quia nolunt aut contemnunt aut negligunt scire Papam esse hæreticum: vel laborant ignorantia probabili. Si sciunt Papam esse hæreticum vel ignorant & laborant ignorantia crassa & supina: & tamen eidem opem ferunt, ne fiat de eo iustitiæ complementum, & te de eius erroribus nullatenus intromittunt: imo asserunt forte manifeste eius errores esse contrarios catholicæ veritati, sunt defensores hæretici: sed non sunt directe defensores, nec approbatores hæreticæ pravitatis. Et ideo pœnam hæreticorum nequaquam incurrunt, sed in sententiam incidunt excommunicationis, & carere debent ecclesiastica sepultura, extra, de hæreticis, sicut etiam extra, de sententia excommunicationis, nouerunt. Aliæ etiam pœnæ eorum si in excommunicatione per annum persistunt, taxantur, extra, de hæreticis, excommunicamus, primo. Quædam etiam pœnæ eorum speciales taxantur, extra, de haereticis, si aduersus. Si autem ignorent Papam esse haereticum, & laborent ignorantia probabili, nullam poenam incurrunt. Discip. Nunquid scientes Papam esse haereticum, vel etiam ignorantes laborantes ignorantia crassa & supina, ad quos spectat & qui possunt facere de Papa haeretico iustitiae complementum, si negligunt, debent inter defensores Papae haeretici computari? Magist. Vna est opinio, quod sunt defensores Papae haeretici & poenam defensorum incurrunt: quemadmodum illi ad quos spectat ex officio defendere clericum verberatum, sunt fautores eiusdem violentiae & eandem poenam incurrunt, si possunt defendere & non faciunt, extra, de sententia excommunicationis, quam te. Alia est opinio, quod tales non sunt defensores Papae haeretici: quia defensio aliquem actum exteriorem importat. Tales autem nullum actum exteriorem ad dictam defensionem pertinentem exercent. Discip. Quid sentitur de illis, qui defendunt Papam haereticum verbo vel scripto, asserendo & dicendo quod non est haereticus reputandus? Magist. Hoc potest multis modis contingere. Vno modo, verbo vel scripto, asserendo & firmando quod errores ei impositos, quos in rei veritate pertinaciter tenet, non tenet neq; dicit neq; asserendo neq; opinando neq; recipiendo neq; aliquo modo: & quod errores impositos dicit tantum modo recitando. Alio modo, quod errores dicit & tenet tantum modo opinando & eos nullatenus pertinaciter asserendo. Alio modo, quod errores impositi Papae non sint inter haereticos computandi. Si primo modo, quia aut sciunt se dicere falsum: & tunc vel laborant ignorantia crassa & supina, vel probabili, si sciunt se dicere falsum, non tamen crimen incurrunt mendacii: sed etiam scienter defensores Papae haeretici sunt censendi; & poenam defensorum incurrunt. Si autem nō sciunt se dicere falsum, & laborant ignorantia crassa & supina, quia nolunt scire vel contemnunt aut negligunt scire, quamuis secundum aliquos a crimine mendacii valeant excusari: tamen a crimine defensionis Papae haeretici minime excusantur: & ideo in poenam incidunt defensorum. Si vero nesciunt se dicere falsum, & laborant ignorantia probabili: nec crimen mendacii, nec crimen defensionis haereticorum committunt: quia ab vtroq; crimine per ignorantiam probabilem excusantur. Consimiliter distinguitur de asserentibus Papam dicere aliquos errores impositos tantum modo opinando vel tantum modo recitando. Quia si sciunt vel credunt se dicere falsum, crimen mendacii & etiam crimen defensionis Papae haeretici manifeste committunt. Si vero nesciunt, & laborant ignorantia crassa & supina, sunt defensionis haereticae crimine inuoluti. Si vero laborent ignorantia probabili, de vtroq; crimine excusantur. Si autem dicunt, quod errores impositi Papae non sunt inter haereticos computandi, non solum sunt censendi defensores haeretici: sed etiam sunt defensores haereticae prauitatis: quod verum est, si errores Papae haeretici sunt explicite condemnati, & taliter defendentes Papam haereticum pertinaciter tenent, quod errores impositi non debent inter haereses reputari.
units.tr: DISCIPLE. Although many more things concerning the favourers of heretics and of heretical depravity remain to be investigated, which I will diligently look into when applying them to particular persons in the treatise On the deeds of those who dispute concerning the orthodox faith, I will nevertheless set those aside and pass on to the defence of heretics and of heretical depravity. On this point I first ask that you tell me who are to be counted as defenders of heretics and of heretical depravity. MASTER. It is answered that, since to defend a thing is to protect it from attack or to bring aid against the attacker, an attack can be made in three ways: by word, by writing, and by deed. Heretics and heretical depravity may be defended in several ways, insofar as heretics and heretical depravity may be assailed in several ways. A heretic may be assailed by the deed of someone who tries to seize or hold him, or to present him to a judge or bring him to trial, so that justice may be done upon him. He may also be assailed by word, and this in several ways: either in court, when he is accused duly and properly, or outside court, when his treachery is announced by preachers and by prelates or teachers or others who are not ignorant, to those who do not know of it, so that they may be on their guard. He may also be assailed by writing, in court when something is written against him, or even outside court, when his treachery is demonstrated by arguments and authorities and is made known by letters to those who are absent. Heretical depravity may be assailed by word and by writing. By word, when it is condemned in sermons, in speeches, or in private conversations. By writing, when Catholics compose writings to refute heretical depravity. From these words it follows that heretics and heretical depravity can be defended in many ways too. And as many ways as there are of assailing heretics and heretical depravity, so many, and perhaps more, ways of defending them could be found. Therefore one may defend heretics by deed, namely by preventing them from being seized or held, or from justice being done upon them. One may also defend them by word, in court and outside court, by alleging that they are not to be condemned or reckoned as heretics. One may defend them by writing too, by composing books and letters to show and declare that they are not to be counted among heretics. Heretical depravity itself may be defended in three ways: by word, by deed, and by writing. By deed, in two ways for the present purpose: in one way, by restraining the assailants themselves from attacking; in another way, by suppressing, burning, or otherwise destroying their written attacks and allegations, or by maliciously withholding them and preventing them from coming to the knowledge of others. Heretical depravity may also be defended by word, by alleging that it is not to be counted among heresies. And in the same way one may defend heresy by writing. DISCIPLE. In accordance with what you have said, very many things about the defenders of heretics and of heretical depravity would need to be investigated; but for the sake of brevity I will leave many aside. I will still ask some questions. Moreover, since I fear that if ever there is a Pope who is a heretic, he will be more pernicious than all other heretics who have been or will be, except the great Antichrist (unless that same Antichrist is himself the Pope), I will apply the questions I put about the defenders of heretics and of heretical depravity to the defenders of a heretical Pope and of his followers and heresies. First, then, tell me by what penalty those are to be punished who by deed prevent justice from being done upon the person of a heretical Pope, yet do not in any way meddle to defend his errors. MASTER. It is answered that such persons, who hinder and give aid to a Pope who is hindering, so that justice is not done upon him, either know that the Pope is a heretic or do not know it. If they do not know it, either they labour under gross and supine ignorance, because they are unwilling, or scorn, or neglect to know that the Pope is a heretic, or else they labour under probable ignorance. If they know that the Pope is a heretic, or they do not know it but labour under gross and supine ignorance, and yet they give him aid so that justice is not done upon him, and they do not in any way meddle with his errors, but indeed perhaps openly assert that his errors are contrary to Catholic truth, they are defenders of a heretic, though not direct defenders or approvers of heretical depravity. Therefore they do not incur the penalty of heretics at all, but fall into the sentence of excommunication, and ought to be denied ecclesiastical burial, as extra, on heretics, as also extra, on the sentence of excommunication, make known. Other penalties also are laid down for them if they persist in excommunication for a year, extra, on heretics, excommunicamus, primo. Certain special penalties for them are also prescribed, extra, on heretics, si aduersus. But if they do not know that the Pope is a heretic and labour under probable ignorance, they incur no penalty at all. DISCIPLE. Should those who know that the Pope is a heretic, or who do not know it but labour under gross and supine ignorance, to whom it belongs, and who are able to bring about justice upon a heretical Pope, if they neglect to do so, be counted among the defenders of a heretical Pope? MASTER. One opinion holds that they are defenders of a heretical Pope and incur the penalty of defenders, just as those whose office it is to defend a beaten cleric are accomplices of the same violence and incur the same penalty if they can defend him and do not, extra, on the sentence of excommunication, which you. Another opinion holds that such persons are not defenders of a heretical Pope, because defence implies some outward act, and such persons exercise no outward act pertaining to the said defence. DISCIPLE. What is held concerning those who defend a heretical Pope by word or in writing, asserting and saying that he is not to be regarded as a heretic? MASTER. This can happen in many ways. In one way, by word or in writing, asserting and affirming that the errors imputed to him, which in truth he obstinately holds, he neither holds, nor says, nor asserts, nor opines, nor receives, nor in any way holds, and that he merely recites the errors imputed to him. In another way, that he says and holds the errors only by opinion, and does not assert them stubbornly at all. In another way, that the errors imputed to the Pope are not to be counted among heresies. If in the first way: either they know that they are saying what is false, and then they labour under gross and supine ignorance, or probable ignorance; if they know they are saying what is false, they do not, however, incur the crime of lying, but they are also to be counted as knowing defenders of a heretical Pope, and incur the penalty of defenders. If, however, they do not know they are saying what is false, and labour under gross and supine ignorance, because they are unwilling to know, or scorn or neglect to know, although according to some they may be excused from the crime of lying, yet they are by no means excused from the crime of defending a heretical Pope, and so they fall into the penalty of defenders. But if they do not know they are saying what is false, and labour under probable ignorance, they commit neither the crime of lying nor the crime of defending heretics, because they are excused from both crimes by probable ignorance. In the same way a distinction is drawn concerning those who assert that the Pope says certain imputed errors only by opinion, or only by reciting them. For if they know or believe they are saying what is false, they clearly commit both the crime of lying and the crime of defending a heretical Pope. If, however, they do not know it and labour under gross and supine ignorance, they are involved in the crime of heretical defence. But if they labour under probable ignorance, they are excused of both crimes. If, however, they say that the errors imputed to the Pope are not to be counted among heresies, they are not only to be considered defenders of heretics, but are also defenders of heretical depravity; which is true, if the errors of a heretical Pope have been explicitly condemned, and those who so defend the Pope hold obstinately that the imputed errors ought not to be reckoned among heresies.

units.la: CAP. LXVI.
units.tr: CAP. LXVI.

units.la: In quo agitur de poena defensorum haereticae prauitatis.
units.tr: In which is treated the punishment of the defenders of heretical depravity.

units.la: Discipulus. Si pro singulis assertionibus supra scriptis satageres allegare: timeo, quod prolixitatem fastidiosam legentibus generares. Ideo ad defensores haereticae prauitatis accede. De quibus peto, vt dicas, qua poena sunt plectendi, qui sunt prauitatis haereticae defensores, siue defendant prauitatem haereticam prohibendo impugnatores prauitatis eiusdem, vt eam impugnent eis, scilicet pro impugnatione prauitatis haereticae, qua Papa haereticus maculatur, persecutionem & molestiam inferendo, siue allegationes eorum catholicas contra errores Papae haeretici comburendo, aut quouis modo impediendo malitiose ne ad notitiam perueniant aliorum. Magist. Istis modis videtur quibusdam, quod infectus haeretica prauitate defenditur. De qua defensione nonnulli tenent, quod huiusmodi Papae haeretici defensores non minus peccant quam Papa haereticus, quia nec sunt minori poena plectendi: imo dicunt, quod sunt haeretici reputandi. Quia sicut contingit facto mentiri secundum Ambrosium, vt habetur 23. q. 1. c. cauete, itaque contingit facto haeresi assentire & eam asserere. Et per consequens ex factis absque verbis potest quis ostendi esse haereticus manifestus. Praedicti igitur defensores haereticae prauitatis haeretici sunt censendi: & poena haereticorum sunt plectendi. Quod multis modis videtur posse probari. Haec enim Vrbanus Papa, vt 24. quaest. 3. cap. qui aliorum, sentire videtur, dicens: qui aliorum errorem defendit: multo amplius damnabilior est illis qui errant: quia non solum ille errat, sed etiam alii offendicula erroris praeparat & confirmat. Vnde quia Magister erroris est; non tamen haereticus dicendus est, sed etiam haeresiarcha dicendus est. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod defensores errorum sunt haeretici reputandi, & damnabiliores errantibus. Ergo & pari poena sunt plectendi. Discip. Ista auctoritas non videtur ad propositum: quia loquitur de defendentibus errores allegando pro eis siue verbo siue scripto. Quod patet p hoc, quod dicit, quod alii offendicula praeparat & confirmat: & per hoc quod dicit Magister erroris est. Ista enim ad allegandum pro erroribus pertinere videntur, & nequaquam spectant ad illos qui impugnatores errorum impediunt, persequuntur & molestant, & qui impugnatores destruunt vel impediunt, ne inter catholicos publicentur. Mag. Dicitur, quod instantia tua nulla est: quia licet auctoritas Vrbani praedicta de allegantibus ex pertinacia perroribus aliorum verbo vel scripto debet intelligi: debet nihilominus intelligi & de defensoribus de facto aliorum errorum, eo quod defensores facto errorum modis praescriptis grauius peccare videntur, quam solummodo pro erroribus allegantes. Defendentes enim facto modis praescriptis errores Papæ hæretici tam in Deum quam in proximum directe peccare noscuntur. Quia & veritatem catholicam manifestari impediunt: & ipsis impugnatoribus prauitatis hæreticæ grauiter iniuriantur, dum eorum personis molestiam inferunt: & in eorum infamiam aliquod ludibrium circa catholicas allegationes exercent. Qui autem pro erroribus aliorum solum verbo vel scripto pertinaciter allegare præsumunt, in Deum tantummodo peccare videntur. Et ideo si defensores (allegando solummodo pro erroribus) sunt damnabiliores illis, qui errant, multo magis illi qui in fauorem & defensionem errorum impugnatores eorum crudeliter persequuntur, & infamia eorum allegationes catholicas irreuerenter & probrose tractant, sunt damnationes his, qui errant, si solummodo stant in errore, & nihil plus faciunt. Cum vero dicitur, quod Vrbanus loquitur de illo, qui aliis offendicula errorum præparat & confirmat, & de illo qui est magister errorum: quæ duo non conueniunt nisi allegantibus pro errore. Respondetur, quod utrumque istorum potest aliquo modo persequentibus & destruentibus impugnatores errorum competere. Nam & remouens, prohibens aliquando causa vocatur. Potest etiam dici quodammodo magister errorum inquantum facto docet & monstrat quod errores sunt censendi. Disc. Alias allegationes ad eandem adducas assertionem. Magist. Hoc Isidorus, ut habetur ii. q. q. 3. cap. qui peccantibus, testari videtur, dicens: Qui peccantibus consenserit & defenderit alium delinquentem, maledictus erit apud Deum & homines, & corripietur increpatione seuerissima. Hoc etiam quidam sanctissimus pater ait: Si quis peccantem defendit, acrius quam ille qui peccauit coerceatur. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod qui Papam hæreticum pro crimine hæresis persequendo impugnatores & impugnationes defendit, acrius quam Papa hæreticus coerceri debet. Disc. Ista auctoritas non loquitur nisi de defensione delinquentis, non de defensore prauitatis hæreticæ, & ita ad propositum esse non videtur. Magist. Respondetur, quod cum loquitur de defendente deliquentem in genere, debet etiam intelligi de defendente Papam hæreticum. Et per consequens debet intelligi de defendente hæresim, quam tenet Papa: quia maius vel non minus peccatum est defendere iniquitatem alicuius, quam defendere facientem iniquitatem; cum ille qui facit, si non esset iniquitas, defendi deberet. Disc. Potest ne probari aliter, quod huiusmodi defensores hæresis, cui Papa hæreticus irretitur, sunt poena hæreticorum plectendi? Mag. Hoc videtur sic posse probari: consentientes eadem poena, qua agentes, sunt plectendi: quod videtur de consentientibus Papæ consensu defensionis vel etiam auctoritatis potissime debere intelligi. Quod Glossa extr. de ossi. & po. iudic. delect. c. i. testari videtur, dicens: in quarto casu defensionis seu auctoritatis magis peccant consentientes defendendo & auctoritatem præstando quam facientes, & magis sunt puniendi supra 24. q. 3. qui alterum ii. q. 3. qui consentit. Ergo defensores modis prædictis hæreticæ prauitatis poena hæreticorum sunt plectendi.
units.tr: Disciple. If you were to labour to cite authorities for each of the assertions written above, I fear you would weary your readers with tiresome length. So come to the defenders of heretical depravity. Concerning them I ask you to say by what punishment those are to be struck who are defenders of heretical depravity, whether they defend that depravity by forbidding its assailants to attack it, that is, by inflicting persecution and molestation on them for attacking the heretical depravity by which the heretical Pope is stained, or by burning their Catholic allegations against the errors of the heretical Pope, or by maliciously hindering them in any other way from coming to the knowledge of others. Master. In these ways it seems to some that one is infected with heretical depravity by defending it. Concerning such defence some hold that the defenders of a heretical Pope sin no less than the heretical Pope himself, since they are not to be punished with any lesser penalty; indeed they say that they are to be reckoned heretics. For just as, according to Ambrose, as is found in 23. q. 1. c. cauete, one may lie by deed, so one may by deed assent to heresy and assert it. And consequently, from deeds without words, a man may be shown to be a manifest heretic. Therefore the aforesaid defenders of heretical depravity are to be judged heretics, and are to be punished with the penalty of heretics. This can be proved in many ways. For Pope Urban, as 24. q. 3. c. qui aliorum, seems to think so, saying: "He who defends the error of others is far more damnable than those who err, because not only does he err himself, but he also prepares and confirms stumbling-blocks of error for others. Hence, since he is the teacher of error, he is not to be called a heretic only, but is to be called a heresiarch." From these words it is gathered that the defenders of errors are to be reckoned heretics, and more damnable than those who err. Therefore they are to be punished with the same penalty. Disciple. This authority does not seem to bear on the point, because it speaks of those who defend errors by alleging arguments for them, whether by word or in writing. This is clear from the fact that it says that "he prepares and confirms stumbling-blocks for others," and from the fact that it says "he is the teacher of error." For these seem to pertain to alleging arguments for errors, and in no way concern those who hinder, persecute and molest the assailants of errors, and who destroy or hinder the assailants, so that they are not published among Catholics. Master. It is said that your objection is no objection: for although the aforesaid authority of Urban must be understood of those who obstinately allege for the errors of others by word or in writing, it must nevertheless also be understood of those who defend the errors of others in deed, since defenders in deed of errors seem to sin more gravely by the aforesaid means than those who merely allege for errors. For those who defend the errors of the heretical Pope in deed, by the aforesaid means, are known to sin directly both against God and against neighbour. For they hinder the Catholic truth from being made manifest, they grievously wrong the very assailants of heretical depravity while they inflict molestation on their persons, and they exercise some mockery against Catholic allegations to their infamy. But those who presume obstinately to allege for the errors of others merely by word or writing seem to sin only against God. And therefore, if defenders (who allege merely for errors) are more damnable than those who err, much more are those who, in favour and defence of errors, cruelly persecute their assailants and, to their infamy, treat Catholic allegations irreverently and shamefully, more damnable than those who err, if they merely stand in error and do nothing more. When it is said that Urban speaks of him who prepares and confirms stumbling-blocks of error for others, and of him who is the teacher of errors, these two things belong only to those who allege for error. It is answered that both of these can in some way apply to those who persecute and destroy the assailants of errors. For one who removes or hinders is sometimes called a cause. One may also say that in a certain sense he is a teacher of error, inasmuch as by his deed he teaches and shows that the errors are to be judged such. Disc. Bring other allegations to the same assertion. Master. Isidore seems to bear witness to this, as is found in ii. q. 3. c. qui peccantibus, saying: "He who consents to sinners and defends another offender will be accursed before God and men, and will be rebuked with the most severe reproof. This also a certain most holy father says: If anyone defends a sinner, he is to be punished more sharply than he who sinned." From these words it is gathered that he who, by persecuting the assailants and assaults of the heretical Pope on the charge of heresy, defends him, ought to be punished more sharply than the heretical Pope. Disc. This authority speaks only of the defence of an offender, not of the defender of heretical depravity, and so does not seem to bear on the point. Master. It is answered that when it speaks of one who defends an offender in general, it must also be understood of one who defends the heretical Pope. And consequently it must be understood of one who defends the heresy which the Pope holds: for it is no lesser or equal sin to defend the iniquity of someone than to defend the one who commits iniquity, since he who commits it, if it were not an iniquity, ought to be defended. Disc. Can it be proved in another way that defenders of the heresy in which the heretical Pope is entangled are to be punished with the penalty of heretics? Master. This seems capable of being proved thus: those who consent are to be punished with the same penalty as those who act; which seems especially to be understood of those who consent to the Pope by consent of defence or even of authority. The Gloss on extr. de ossi. & po. iudic. delect. c. i. seems to bear witness to this, saying: "In the fourth case of defence or authority, those who consent by defending and lending authority sin more than those who act, and they are to be punished more, supra 24. q. 3. [qui alterum] and ii. q. 3. [qui consentit]." Therefore defenders of heretical depravity in the aforesaid ways are to be punished with the penalties of heretics.

units.la: Discipul. Audiui quorundam sententiam de his, qui factis defendunt hæreticam prauitatem. Nunc dic de illis, qui verbo vel scripto defenderunt doctrinam erroneam Papæ hæretici. Magist. De his breuiter dicitur, quod si doctrina Papæ erronea est talis, quod veritatem contrariam illi, qui doctrinam Papæ erroneam solum allegationibus verbo vel scripto nituntur defendere, credere tenentur explicite: tales defendentes sunt inter hæreticos computandi. Quia omnis qui negat veritatem, quam tenetur credere explicite, est inter hæreticos numerandus, & poena hæreticorum plectendus. Si vero doctrina Papæ erronea sit talis, quod allegantes pro ea non tenentur credere explicite contrariam veritatem, qui eam defendunt solummodo allegando verbis vel scriptis, non sunt hæretici computandi, nec poena hæreticorum plectendi: nisi quomodocunque appareat, quod suis allegationibus pertinaciter innituntur, qualiter autem debeant conuinci de pertinacia ex his quæ tractata sunt supra lib. 4. debet posse patere. Disc. Ex hac sententia mihi sequi videtur, quod allequi aliquantes verbo vel scripto pro doctrina Papæ erronea sunt censendi hæretici, & aliqui à prauitate hæretica sunt immunes. Magist. Concedatur quod hoc potest contingere secundum quod potest accidere, quod aliqui tenentur credere explicite veritatem contrariam doctrinæ Papæ erroneæ: & aliqui eam credere explicite non tenentur. Et secundum quod aliqui possunt suis allegationibus pertinaciter adhærere. Unde ad cognoscendum, qui allegantes verbo vel scripto pro doctrina Papæ hæretici sunt hæretici reputandi & qui non sunt inter hæreticos computandi, & numerandi, oportet diligentissime considerare, qui tenentur explicite credere veritatem contrariam, & qui ad hoc minime sunt astricti: qui sunt pertinaces, & qui de pertinacia conuinci non possunt. Disc. Nunquid illi, qui allegarent pro doctrina Papæ hæretici, & non cenerentur credere explicite veritatem contrariam, nec pertinaciter conuinci valerent, deberent defensores hæreticæ prauitatis nuncupari? Magist. Respondetur secundum quod nomen defensionis hæreticæ prauitatis in iure accipitur, non deberent defensores hæreticæ prauitatis appellari. Quia nomen defensionis sic acceptum semper pertinaciam includit. Disc. Si prædicta de defensoribus continentur veritatem, aperta est distinctio inter defensores hæreticorum & hæreticæ prauitatis. Sed an ista distinctio à canonicis sanctionibus accipi possit ignoro. Unde quid de hoc posset dici, expone. Magist. Quod ista distinctio ex canonicis statutis accipi posset, videtur tali modo posse probari. In quibusdam statutis canonicis defensores ab hæreticis distinguuntur. In quibusdam vero defensores hæretici appellantur. Ergo videtur quod vocabulum defensorum vel defendendi accipiatur prædicto modo æquiuoce. Antecedens, quoad utraque partem, probatur. Et primo quidem, quoad primam partem, sic probatur. Innoc. tertius in concilio generali, ut loquitur extr. de haret. c. excommunicamus, i. sic ait: Credentes præterea, praterea, defensores, receptatores & fautores haereticorum excommunicationi decreuimus subiacere, firmiter statuentes vt postquam quilibet talium fuerit excommunicatione notatus, si satisfacere contempserit infra annum & extunc ipso iure sit factus infamis: nec ad publica officia seu consilia, nec ad eligendos aliquos ad huiusmodi, nec ad testimonium admittatur. Sit etiam intestabilis &c. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod plures poenas, quas constat haereticos incurrere ipso facto, & statim defensores haereticorum non incurrunt, nisi satisfacere contemplerint infra annum. Nam bona haereticorum defensorum si satisfecerint infra annum, postquam fuerint excommunicatione notati, sunt minime confiscanda infra annum, vt ex verbis Innocentii allegatis & ex sequacibus colligi videtur aperte. Bona vero haereticorum confiscanda sunt vel confiscari possunt etiam si infra annum ad fidem redierint veracem, teste eodem Innocentio tertio, qui, vt legitur extra de haereticis c. vrgentes, ait: In terris vero episcopali nostra iurisdictioni subiectis bona haereticorum statuimus publicari. Et in aliis idem praecipimus fieri per potestates & principes seculares, quos ad illud exequendum, si forte negligentes extiterint, per censuram ecclesiasticam appellatione remota volumus & mandamus. Nec ad eos bona eorum vlterius reuertantur, nisi eisdem ad cor reuertentibus & abnegantibus haereticorum consortium misereri aliquis voluerit. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, quod vt Glossa dicit super verbo misereri haereticis ad cor reuertentibus & satisfacientibus siue infra annum de sola misericordia restituantur bona. Defendentibus autem non sunt bona infra annum auferenda. Ergo defensores, de quibus fit mentio in constitutione praedicta Excommunicamus, non sunt haeretici nec fautores haereticorum & haereticae prauitatis reputandi, sed defensores haereticorum tantummodo sunt censendi. Qui, sicut habetur extr. de haereticis sicut ait, & cap. si aduersus, & extra de sententia excommunicationis cap. nouerit, ab haereticis diffinitur. Secunda vero pars antecedentis rationis praedictae, scilicet quod quandoque defensores haeretici appellantur, probatur. Nam, sicut allegatum est supra 24. quaest. 3. qui aliorum, defensores errorum alienorum probantur esse non solum haeretici: sed etiam de haereticis: quia in hoc quod defendunt aliorum errores sunt magistri errorum. Item, quod aliqui defensores sint haeretici reputandi, testatur Innocent. extr. de verborum sig. cap. super quibusdam, dicens: Tua deuotio postulauit a nobis, qui sunt dicendi haeretici manifesti. Super quo duximus tibi respondendum, illos intelligendos esse manifestos haereticos, qui contra fidem catholicam publice dicunt aut profitentur seu defendunt errorem. Ex quibus verbis colligitur & datur intelligi, quod defensores eorum sunt inter haereticos reputandi. Quod secundum quosdam intelligendum est, siue facto siue verbo, siue scripto, defendant errores, quod secundum eos iuxta modum praeexpositum continet veritatem.
units.tr: Student: I have heard some people's opinion about those who defend heretical depravity by deeds. Now tell me about those who have defended, by word or in writing, the erroneous doctrine of a heretical Pope. Teacher: On these people it may be said briefly that if the Pope's erroneous doctrine is of such a kind that those who defend it only by arguments, in speech or in writing, are bound to believe explicitly the truth contrary to it, then such defenders are to be counted among heretics. For everyone who denies a truth that he is bound to believe explicitly is to be numbered among heretics and punished with the penalty of heretics. But if the Pope's erroneous doctrine is of such a kind that those who defend it merely by arguing in words or writing are not bound to believe explicitly the contrary truth, they are not to be counted as heretics, nor punished with the penalty of heretics, unless it somehow appears that they cling stubbornly to their arguments. How they must be convicted of obstinacy should be evident from what was discussed above in book 4. Student: From this opinion it seems to follow to me that some who argue in word or writing for the Pope's erroneous doctrine are to be judged heretics, while others are immune from heretical depravity. Teacher: Grant that this can happen, since it can be the case that some are bound to believe explicitly the truth contrary to the Pope's erroneous doctrine, while others are not bound to believe it explicitly, and since some can cling stubbornly to their arguments while others cannot. Therefore, to recognise which of those who argue in word or writing for the Pope's heretical doctrine are to be regarded and numbered as heretics, and which are not to be counted among heretics, we must very carefully consider who is bound to believe the contrary truth explicitly, and who is by no means so bound; who is obstinate, and who cannot be convicted of obstinacy. Student: Would not those who argued for the Pope's heretical doctrine, and who were not bound to believe the contrary truth explicitly, and could not be convicted of obstinacy, have to be called defenders of heretical depravity? Teacher: The answer is that, taking the name "defence of heretical depravity" as it is understood in law, they should not be called defenders of heretical depravity, because a defence so understood always includes obstinacy. Student: If what has been said about defenders is true, the distinction between defenders of heretics and defenders of heretical depravity is clear. But I do not know whether this distinction can be drawn from the canonical sanctions. So explain what can be said about this. Teacher: That this distinction could be drawn from the canonical statutes seems capable of being proved in this way. In some canonical statutes defenders are distinguished from heretics, while in others defenders are called heretics. Therefore it seems that the word "defender" or "defending" is taken equivocally in the way just described. The antecedent is proved for each part. First, the first part is proved thus. Innocent III, in a general council, as the decretal Excommunicamus (extra, De haereticis, c. 1) has it, speaks thus: "Moreover, we have decreed that believers, defenders, harbourers and supporters of heretics are subject to excommunication, firmly establishing that whoever of such people has been marked with excommunication, if he has despised making satisfaction within a year, is then by the very law made infamous, and is not admitted to public offices or councils, nor to the choosing of anyone for such things, nor to giving testimony. He is also to be intestable, etc." From these words it is gathered that the defenders of heretics do not incur the many penalties which it is agreed heretics incur by the very fact, and at once, unless they have despised making satisfaction within a year. For the goods of defenders of heretics, if they have made satisfaction within a year after being marked with excommunication, are not to be confiscated within the year, as is clearly gathered from the words of Innocent quoted above and from those that follow. But the goods of heretics are to be confiscated, or can be confiscated, even if they have returned within the year to the true faith; this is attested by the same Innocent III, who, as is read in the decretal Extra, De haereticis, c. Urgentes, says: "In lands subject to our episcopal jurisdiction we decree that the goods of heretics be made public. And in others we order the same to be done by secular powers and princes, whom, if perhaps they should be negligent in carrying this out, we wish and command to be compelled by ecclesiastical censure, appeal being set aside. Nor are their goods to return to them any further, unless someone wishes to show mercy to them when they have come to their senses and renounced fellowship with heretics." From these words it is gathered, as the Gloss says on the words misereri, that goods are restored by mercy alone to heretics who have come to their senses and made satisfaction, whether within the year or not. But goods are not to be taken away within the year from defenders. Therefore the defenders mentioned in the aforesaid constitution Excommunicamus are not to be regarded as heretics, nor as supporters of heretics and heretical depravity, but are to be considered only defenders of heretics. These, as is found in the decretal Extra, De haereticis, Sicut ait, and in cap. Si adversus, and in the decretal Extra, De sententia excommunicationis, cap. Noverit, are defined apart from heretics. The second part of the antecedent of the above argument, namely that defenders are sometimes called heretics, is proved as follows. For, as has been alleged above in 24. quaest. 3, Qui aliorum, defenders of other men's errors are shown to be not only heretics but also from among the heretics, because in defending the errors of others they are masters of errors. Likewise, that some defenders are to be regarded as heretics is attested by Innocent in the decretal Extra, De verborum significatione, cap. Super quibusdam, saying: "Your devotion has asked us who are to be called manifest heretics. On this matter we have thought fit to answer you that those are to be understood as manifest heretics who publicly say, profess or defend an error against the Catholic faith." From these words it is gathered, and it is given to be understood, that their defenders are to be reckoned among the heretics. According to some, this must be understood to mean that whether they defend errors by deed, by word, or in writing, they are heretics, provided that, according to the manner explained above, their defence contains the truth.

units.la: CAP. LXVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER LXVII.

units.la: In quo agitur de receptatoribus haereticorum, & quomodo a defensoribus &c. distinguuntur, circa quod plures per ordinem mouentur quaestiunculae. Vbi etiam nota de plenitudine potestatis.
units.tr: In which the harbourers of heretics are discussed, and how they are distinguished from believers, favourers and defenders, etc. Several small questions are raised about this in order. Note also here concerning the fullness of power.

units.la: Discip. De defensoribus haereticorum & haereticae prauitatis vsque ad tractatum de dogmatibus Iohannis 22. & tractatum De gestis circa fidem altercantium orthodoxam nola plura inquirere. Ideo ad receptatores transeo. De quibus verbis dic inprimis, quomodo a credentibus, fautoribus & defendentibus distinguuntur. Magist. Respondetur quod receptor & credens haereticis duo disparata videntur. Quia licet receptor possit esse credens, tamen potest etiam contingere, quod non sit credens: quia qui receptor est scienter haereticorum, non est credens, quia non credit eos esse catholicos, quos reputat haereticos: nec credit erroribus eorundem. Receptor vero haereticorum videtur esse fautor eorundem, quia qui recipit haereticos eis quodammodo fauet, cum etiam non impugnare haereticos quando quis debet eos impugnare, sit eis fauere. Omnis igitur receptor haereticorum est fautor eorum, sed non econuerso. Multi enim sunt fautores haereticorum, qui tamen non sunt receptores eorum. Receptor autem & defensor haereticorum disparata esse videntur. Nam quis potest esse defensor eorum, quamuis non sit receptor eorum: quia in eius dominio non morantur. Potest etiam quis esse receptor haereticorum, quamuis non sit defensor: quia scilicet eos a nulla impugnatione intendit defendere. Discip. Qui sunt receptores haereticorum? Magist. Respondetur, quod nomen receptoris secundum quod in iure accipitur, sonat in malum. Et ideo isti sunt receptores haereticorum qui cum possent haereticos de terra sua & dominio expellere, eos scienter vel ignoranter, ita tamen quod laborant ignorantia crassa & supina, permittunt in terra sua aut dominio absque custodia libere commorari. De istis loquitur Glossa extr. de haereticis excommunicamus 1. super verbo receptores, dicens: sine quibus haeretici diu manere non possunt. Discipul. Secundum praedicta si Papa haereticus manens in dominio alicuius regis vel principis, aut alicuius alterius, tanta fulciretur potentia, quod dominus temporalis non posset eum expellere, nec quomodolibet detinere: talis Dominus non esset censendus receptor. Magist. Hic respondetur, quod talem Dominum temporalem impotentia excusaret. Discip. Potest ne aliquid aliud excusare Dominum temporalem si non expellit Papam haereticum vel eius sequaces, de suo Dominio in terram non sibi subiectam? Magist. Respondetur, quod timor probabilis turbationis fidelium absque fructu spirituali potest excusare Dominum temporalem. Discip. Nunquid tenetur Dominus temporalis expellere Papam haereticum de suo dominio, si tantam habet potentiam temporalem, & non timet probabiliter turbatioturbationem fidelium absque fructu spirituali: quamuis ostendens non fuerit per prælatos ecclesiæ requisitus? Magist. De hoc tractatum est libro 6. cap. 99. & ultimo: vbi ostensum est, quod deficiente ecclesiastica potestate siue per impotentiam siue per damnabilem negligentiam, laici debent hæreticos coercere. Disc. Quid faciet Dominus temporalis, si scit Papam hæreticum manere in suo dominio, & non potest eum arctare? Magist. Requiret auxilium catholicorum. Si autem alii noluerint auxiliari ei, excusatus est. Disc. Quid faciet populus, vbi moratur Papa hæreticus, si Dominus temporalis, quamuis possit, nolit Papam hæreticum coercere? Magist. Respondetur, quod populus non obstante quod Dominus temporalis sit receptor Papæ hæretici, si potest absque dispendio spirituali, debet Papam coercere, vbi sciret Papam hæreticum. Puta vbi sciret, si Papa aliquid assereret contra veritatem apud omnes catholicos diuulgatam, vt puta si diceret Christum filium Prophetam, vel Christianam fidem esse falsam vel fictam: aut quod animæ reproborum in inferno minime cruciantur, vel aliquid huiusmodi, quod apud omnes catholicos tanquam catholicum diuulgatum existit: nec esset necesse, quod populus in hoc casu consuleret sapientes, nisi forte ad sciendum quomodo deberet procedere contra Papam hæreticum. Non enim propter persuasiones, allegationes vel verba quorumcunque sapientum vel insipientum deberet quoquomodo in dubium reuocare, an Papa esset in tali casu hæreticus reputandus, & tanquam hæreticus euitandus, ac etiam puniendus. Imo quicunque sapientes clerici vel laici, qui dicerent Papam in tali casu non debere a populo reputari hæreticum, essent a populo hæretici iudicandi. Disc. Quomodo potest populus absque auctoritate domini temporalis aliquid contra Papam hæreticum attentare, cum populus nullam habeat iurisdictionem omnino, sed in Dominum suum iurisdictionem transtulerit? Magist. Respondetur, quod quamuis in Imperatorem vel regem iurisdictionem transtulerit: iurisdictionem tamen, quam habet in fauorem fidei, quando Papa est hæreticus & remanet cum eis, & prælati & Domini temporales nolunt vel non possunt Papam coercere, à se transferre non potest; nec tali iurisdictioni potest renunciare: quia illa iurisdictio concessa est populo in fauorem fidei Christianæ.
units.tr: Disciple. Concerning the defenders of heretics and of heretical depravity, I need not inquire further, up to the treatise on the doctrines of John 22 and the treatise On the acts of those disputing about the orthodox faith. So I pass on to harbourers. About these words, tell me first how they are distinguished from believers, favourers and defenders. Master. The answer is that a harbourer of heretics and a believer in heretics seem to be two different things. For although a harbourer may be a believer, it can also happen that he is not a believer: one who knowingly harbours heretics is not a believer, since he does not believe that those whom he takes to be heretics are Catholics, nor does he believe their errors. A harbourer of heretics, however, seems to be a favourer of them, since whoever receives heretics in some way favours them, and not to oppose heretics when one ought to oppose them is to favour them. Every harbourer of heretics is therefore a favourer of them, but not conversely. For there are many favourers of heretics who are not their harbourers. A harbourer and a defender of heretics, however, seem to be different things. For someone may be a defender of heretics without harbouring them, since they do not remain in his domain. And someone may be a harbourer of heretics without being a defender, since he intends by this not to defend them from any attack. Disciple. Who are the harbourers of heretics? Master. The answer is that the term harbourer, as it is taken in law, has a bad sense. Those are harbourers of heretics who, though they could expel heretics from their land and domain, allow them to remain freely in their land or domain without guard, whether knowingly or ignorantly, provided that they labour under gross and culpable ignorance. The Gloss speaks of these people in Extra, On heretics, Excommunicamus 1, under the word harbourers, saying: without whom heretics cannot remain for long. Disciple. According to what has been said, if a heretical Pope, remaining in the domain of some king or prince or of someone else, were supported by such power that the temporal lord could not expel him or in any way detain him, such a lord would not be judged a harbourer. Master. Here the answer is that such a temporal lord would be excused by his powerlessness. Disciple. Can anything else excuse the temporal lord if he does not expel a heretical Pope or his followers from his domain into land not subject to him? Master. The answer is that a probable fear of disturbing the faithful, without spiritual fruit, can excuse the temporal lord. Disciple. Is the temporal lord bound to expel a heretical Pope from his domain if he has such temporal power and does not probably fear disturbing the faithful without spiritual fruit, even though he has not been asked to do so by the prelates of the Church? Master. This was treated in book 6, chapter 99 and the last, where it was shown that, when ecclesiastical power is lacking, whether through powerlessness or through blameworthy negligence, laymen ought to restrain heretics. Disciple. What will the temporal lord do if he knows that a heretical Pope remains in his domain and he cannot restrain him? Master. He will seek the help of Catholics. If others are unwilling to help him, he is excused. Disciple. What will the people do, where a heretical Pope lingers, if the temporal lord, although able, is unwilling to restrain the heretical Pope? Master. The answer is that the people, notwithstanding that the temporal lord is a harbourer of the heretical Pope, ought to restrain the Pope, if they can do so without spiritual loss, where they know him to be a heretic. Suppose they knew that the Pope asserted something against the truth that is publicly proclaimed among all Catholics, for example, if he said that Christ was not the Son of God and a Prophet, or that the Christian faith is false or feigned, or that the souls of the damned are not tormented at all in hell, or anything of this kind that is publicly known among all Catholics as Catholic teaching. In such a case there would be no need for the people to consult the wise, except perhaps to learn how they should proceed against the heretical Pope. For they ought not, on account of the persuasions, arguments or words of any wise or unwise persons whatever, to call into doubt in any way whether the Pope in such a case is to be regarded as a heretic and to be avoided as a heretic, and also punished. Indeed, any wise clerics or laymen who said that in such a case the Pope ought not to be regarded as a heretic by the people would be judged heretics by the people. Disciple. How can the people undertake anything against a heretical Pope without the authority of the temporal lord, since the people have no jurisdiction at all, but have transferred their jurisdiction to their lord? Master. The answer is that although they have transferred jurisdiction to the Emperor or king, the jurisdiction which they have in favour of the faith, when the Pope is a heretic and remains among them, and the prelates and temporal lords are unwilling or unable to restrain the Pope, they cannot transfer from themselves, nor can they renounce such jurisdiction, because that jurisdiction was granted to the people in favour of the Christian faith.

units.la: Disc. Quo iure habet populus iurisdictionem huiusmodi super Papam hæreticum? non iure diuino: quia de hoc in iure diuino nulla fit mentio. Nec etiam iure humano: quia etiam in iure humano de hoc nulla fit mentio. Nec iure naturali, quia a iure naturali nullus habet super alium potestatem. Natura enim omnes fecit æquales. Magist. Respondetur, quod quamuis in iure diuino nulla de iurisdictione huiusmodi fiat mentio vocalis, sententialiter tamen hoc ex iure diuino & naturali ac humano simul colligitur. Nam ex iure diuino concluditur quod Papa factus hæreticus est papatu priuatus. Ex iure autem humano habetur, quod Papæ hæretico non est communicandum modo prædicto. Quod etiam corporaliter seruari debet, quando absque perniciosa turbatione fidei seruari potest. Eo quod nulli hæretico est communicandum modo prædicto. Item ex iure humano habetur, quod si Papa vel Dominus temporalis alicuius populi fiat hæreticus, totus populus a iurisdictione tam Papæ quam Domini temporalis absoluitur, teste Gregorio tertio, qui vt habetur extra. de hæreticis c. vltim. ait: absolutos se esse nouerint a debito fidelitatis, homagii & totius obsequii, quicunque manifeste lapsis in haeresim aliquo pacto quacunque firmitate vallato tenebantur astricti. Ex iure autem naturali non quidem quod fuisset tempore naturæ institutæ, sed quod est pro tempore naturæ lapsæ, habetur quod populus propter perfidiam alicuius, qui non est superior eo, locum aut patriam relinquere non tenetur. Ex quibus concluditur, quod si Papa fiat hæreticus, & Dominus temporalis fuerit eidem, populus saltem iurisdictionem aliqualem obtinet super Papam hæreticum: quia ex quo Papa hæreticus iure diuino est papatu priuatus, non est superior populo, vbi moratur. Iure autem humano populus Papæ hæretico communicare non debet. Ergo debet Papam hæreticum deuitare. Iure autem naturali non tenetur propter Papam hæreticum patriam aut locum deserere aut relinquere. Ergo potest Papam hæreticum, ne eidem communicet, de loco suo expellere, vel cum in custodia detinere. Disc. Ista ratio non procedit, nisi Papa hæreticus se ingereret communioni populi. Ergo si non ingerit se communioni populi, populus nullam iurisdictionem habet super eum. Magist. Dicitur, quod sufficit quod per rationem prædictam probaretur populum in aliquo casu iurisdictionem aliquam, extendendo nomen iurisdictionis ad quamcunque potestatem expellendum vel etiam aliquem detinendum, super Papam hæreticum obtinere. Quia dicit, quod ex tali iurisdictione populi super Papam hæreticum multipliciter iurisdictionem contingit inferre. Disc. Causa breuitatis nolo, quod ex iurisdictione prædicta aliqua alia inferantur: sed dic secundum prædictam opinionem, si Papa hæreticus voluerit recedere, an populus debeat eum dimittere liberum abire, an eum teneatur in firma custodia detinere. Magist. Respondetur, quod populus tenetur eum in firma custodia detinere. Cuius ratio assignatur talis. Non minus debet vnaquæque persona & multitudo fidelium esse sollicita de salute spirituali proximorum quam corporali: secundum quod ex verbis beati Augustini, quæ ponuntur 23. q. 4. cap. ipsa pietas, quæ allegata sunt supra, colligitur euidenter. Sed si esset in populo aliquis, qui vallatus complicibus eundem populum & omnem alium catholicum corporaliter conaretur extinguere, populus non deberet liberum abire dimittere, sed ne alios populos Christianos occideret, detinere. Ergo si Papa hæreticus omnes catholicos spiritualiter per prauitatem hæreticam conatur necare, populus, cum quo moratur, non solum proprio periculo, sed etiam periculo aliorum fidelium, præcauendo ipsam detinere tenetur.
units.tr: Disciple. By what right does the people have such jurisdiction over a heretical Pope? Not by divine right, since no mention of this is made in divine law. Nor by human right either, since in human law too no mention of this is made. Nor by natural right, since by natural right no one has power over another. For nature made all men equal. Master. The answer is that although no such jurisdiction is expressly mentioned in divine law, it is nevertheless inferred from divine, natural and human law together in substance. For from divine law it follows that a Pope who has become a heretic is deprived of the papacy. From human law it is held that one must not communicate with a heretical Pope in the manner described above. This too must be observed in practice, when it can be observed without a pernicious disturbance of the faith, because one must not communicate with any heretic in the manner described. Likewise from human law it is held that if a Pope or the temporal lord of some people becomes a heretic, the whole people is absolved from the jurisdiction of both the Pope and the temporal lord, as Gregory III testifies, who, as is held in Extra, On heretics, last chapter, says: Let them know that they are absolved from the debt of fidelity, homage and all obedience, whoever were bound to those manifestly fallen into heresy by any pact, however firmly secured. From natural right, not indeed as it was at the time when nature was instituted, but as it is in the time of fallen nature, it is held that a people, on account of the perfidy of someone who is not superior to them, is not bound to abandon or leave its place or country. From these things it is concluded that if the Pope becomes a heretic and the temporal lord is of the same mind, the people at least obtains some jurisdiction over the heretical Pope, because, since the heretical Pope is deprived of the papacy by divine law, he is not superior to the people where he dwells. By human law, however, the people ought not to communicate with a heretical Pope. Therefore they ought to avoid the heretical Pope. By natural law they are not bound to desert or leave their country or place on account of a heretical Pope. Therefore they can expel the heretical Pope from their place, or keep him in custody, so as not to communicate with him. Disciple. This argument does not hold, unless the heretical Pope forces himself upon the fellowship of the people. Therefore, if he does not force himself upon the fellowship of the people, the people has no jurisdiction over him. Master. It is said that it is enough that the aforesaid argument proves that the people in some case obtains some jurisdiction over a heretical Pope, extending the name of jurisdiction to any power whatever of expelling or even detaining him. For he says that from such jurisdiction of the people over a heretical Pope many other consequences can be drawn in many ways. Disciple. For the sake of brevity I do not want other consequences to be drawn from the aforesaid jurisdiction; but tell me, according to the aforesaid opinion, if the heretical Pope wishes to withdraw, ought the people to let him go free, or is it bound to keep him in firm custody? Master. The answer is that the people is bound to keep him in firm custody. The reason assigned for this is as follows. Each individual person and the multitude of the faithful ought to be no less concerned for the spiritual salvation of their neighbours than for their bodily salvation, as is clearly inferred from the words of blessed Augustine, which are cited in 23, q. 4, chapter Ipsa pietas, quoted above. But if there were someone among the people who, backed by his accomplices, tried to destroy bodily the same people and every other Catholic, the people ought not to let him go free, but to detain him, so that he might not kill other Christian peoples. Therefore, if a heretical Pope seeks to destroy all Catholics spiritually through heretical depravity, the people among whom he dwells is bound to detain him, in order to guard against danger not only to itself but also to the danger of other faithful.

units.la: Discip. Nunquid si populus permittat Papam haereticum licite secum commorari, & suos dogmatizare errores, debet receptor haereticorum censeri, si potest Papam haereticum detinere? Magist. Respondetur quod sic. Quia ex quo spectat ad populum detinere Papam haereticum, quando Dominus temporalis & praelati circa coercionem Papae haeretici sunt damnabiliter negligentes, si populus eum non detinet, debet receptor Papae haeretici reputari. Discip. Nunquid quilibet de populo tali debet dici, quod sit receptor Papae haeretici? Magist. Respondetur quod omnes, qui damnabiliter negligunt Papam detinere, vel qui tali negligentiae consentiunt, sunt receptores Papae haeretici. Qui autem alios exhortantur, quantum licet eis pro gradu suo pariatque esse vna cum aliis Papam detinere, aut talem exhortationem metu mortis vel grauium tormentorum omittunt dolentes quod Papa haereticus minime detinetur, non sunt inter receptores Papae haereticos computandi. Discip. Nunquid tales, qui parati essent Papam haereticum detinere, tenentur recedere, ne communicent Papae haeretico? Magist. Respondetur quod si tales remanere in populo minime possunt, nisi communicant Papae haeretico propter potentiam Papae haeretici & suorum communicare possunt corporaliter Papae haeretico: scilicet loquendo, comedendo, bibendo, & corporaliter couuersando insimul. Necad vitandum talem communionem cum notabili damno suo tenentur recedere. Sed antequam communicent Papae haeretico aliter quam corporaliter tantum, puta in officio diuino, vel in his quae ad Papatus spectant officium, maxime quantum ad ea quae ordinis sunt, aut facto vel verbo profitendo eum esse Papam, debent de loco illo recedere. Quia taliter communicare Papae haeretico nullus potest absque peccato mortali. Quilibet autem ante debet omnia mala tolerare, quam peccare mortaliter.
units.tr: Disciple. If the people allow a heretical Pope to live lawfully among them and to spread his errors, are they to be counted as receivers of heretics, when they could hold the heretical Pope in custody? Master. The answer is yes. For it belongs to the people to hold a heretical Pope in custody, and when the temporal lord and the prelates are culpably negligent in restraining a heretical Pope, if the people do not hold him, they must be reckoned receivers of the heretical Pope. Disciple. Must every member of such a people be called a receiver of the heretical Pope? Master. The answer is that all who culpably neglect to hold the Pope, or who consent to such negligence, are receivers of the heretical Pope. But those who urge others, as far as they lawfully can according to their rank, and who are ready to hold the Pope together with the others, yet, through fear of death or of severe torments, refrain from such an exhortation while grieving that the heretical Pope is not held in custody, are not to be counted among the receivers of heretical Popes. Disciple. Must those who would be ready to hold the heretical Pope withdraw, so that they do not communicate with the heretical Pope? Master. The answer is that if such people cannot remain among the people without communicating with the heretical Pope, because of the power of the heretical Pope and his followers, they may communicate with the heretical Pope bodily, that is, by speaking, eating, drinking and living together in the body. In order to avoid such communion, they are bound to withdraw, even at considerable loss to themselves. But before they communicate with the heretical Pope in any way other than merely bodily, for example in the divine office, or in those matters which pertain to the office of the papacy, especially as regards things belonging to holy orders, or by professing by deed or word that he is Pope, they must leave that place. For no one can communicate with a heretical Pope in such a way without mortal sin. Yet anyone ought to endure all evils rather than sin mortally.

units.la: Discip. Prima pars istius sententiae decretalis Innocentii tertii, quae ponitur extra, de his quae vi metus ve causa fiunt cap. sacris, repugnare videtur. Ait enim: distinguimus vtrum aliquis, qui communicat excommunicatis inuitis, sit per coactionem astrictus, aut per metum inductus. In primo casu talem non credimus excommunicationem incurrere: cum magis pati quam agere conuincatur. In secundo licet metus culpam attenuet, quia cum quidam canones non eum prorsus excludunt, cum pro nullo metu quid peccatum mortale debeat incurrere, excommunicationis labe credimus inquinari. Ex quibus verbis colligitur, vt videtur, quod nullus metus etiam mortis excusat corporaliter communicantem excommunicato a peccato mortali. Cum ergo Papa haereticus, qui incidit in canonem sententiae promulgatae, vt notat Glossa 24. q. i. cap. 1. sit excommunicatus, sicut allegatum est supra, quicunque communicat Papae haeretico etiam corporaliter tantummodo, excommunicationis sententia inquinatur. Magist. Ad hoc respondetur, quod Innocentius tertius in decretali praedicta de communicatione corporali nullam facit penitus mentionem. Et ideo pro morte vitanda licitum est cuicunque excommunicato communicare corporaliter. Et similiter pro notabili damno vitando, licet excommunicato communicare corporaliter. Nec potest ecclesia de plenitudine potestatis artare quemcunque contra suam voluntatem in tali casu excommunicatum vitare. Et ideo Innocentius loquitur de communione non corporali: sed de aliqua alia, puta in crimine vel alio modo, quae absque constitutione humana noscitur interdicta.
units.tr: Disciple. The first part of this decretal sentence of Innocent III, which is placed in the Extra, De his quae vi metus ve causa fiunt, chapter Sacris, seems to conflict with what you have said. For it says: We distinguish whether someone who communicates with the excommunicated against his will is bound by compulsion or induced by fear. In the first case we do not believe he incurs excommunication, since he is shown to suffer rather than act. In the second case, although fear lessens the fault, since certain canons do not exclude him entirely, because one ought not to incur mortal sin for any fear, we believe he is stained with the taint of excommunication. From these words it seems to follow that no fear, not even fear of death, excuses one who communicates bodily with an excommunicated person from mortal sin. Therefore, since the heretical Pope, who falls under the canon of a published sentence, as the Gloss notes on 24, q. 1, c. 1, is excommunicated, as was said above, whoever communicates even merely bodily with a heretical Pope is stained by the sentence of excommunication. Master. To this it is answered that Innocent III, in the aforesaid decretal, makes no mention at all of bodily communion. And therefore, in order to avoid death, it is lawful for anyone to communicate bodily with an excommunicated person. Likewise, to avoid considerable loss, it is lawful to communicate bodily with an excommunicated person. Nor can the Church, by the fullness of power, bind anyone in such a case to shun an excommunicated person against his will. Therefore Innocent speaks of non-bodily communion, but of some other kind, for example in crime or in some other way, which is known to be forbidden without any human constitution.

units.la: Discip. Circa dictam responsionem duae difficultates mihi occurrunt. Prima est, quod videtur, quod ecclesia, quae etiam summum pontificem comprehendit, & penes quam plenitudo residet potestatis, potest praecipere cuilibet catholico, vt nullo metu mortis vel perditionis rerum excommunicato communicet. Alirer enim potestatis plenitudinem nequaquam haberet. Si autem ecclesia potest hoc praecipere: is, cui praecipitur, obedire tenetur. Secunda est: quia si ecclesia non potest aliquem obligare sub poena excommunicationis, ne etiam metu mortis corporaliter communicet excommunicato. Videtur etiam per eandem rationem, quod per eandem poenam non potest obligare fideles, ne aliter quam corporaliter excommunicato communicent. Magist. Ad primam respondetur, quod ecclesia non potest aliquem obligare sub poena excommunicationis, ne metu mortis vel perditionis rerum communicet cum excommunicato. Cuius ratio assignatur talis. Ad illa quae supererogationis sunt, vel excessiue grauia dignoscuntur, ad quae quis nec iure diuino nec iure naturali nec spontanea voluntate noscitur obligari: non potest ecclesia de plenitudine potestatis fideles artare. Haec enim est causa quare ecclesia non potest Christianos ad votum continentiae vel virginitatis artare. Quia, vt lex sacra dicit, virginitas suaderi potest, imperari non potest. Similiter ecclesia non potest cogere Christianos religionem Mendicantium, vt Minorum, intrare. Quia hoc supererogationis est, & causa, quare ad ea, quae supererogationis sunt, non potest ecclesia Christianos compellere, est, quia talia excessiue sunt grauia, ad quae Christiani lege diuina vel iure naturali minime obligantur. Quare ad ea praelati Christianos obligare non debent: ne sint de numero illorum, de quibus dicit Christus Matth. 13. Alligant enim grauia onera & importabilia & imponunt in humeros hominum: digito autem suo nolunt ea mouere. Ad ea ergo quae sunt excessiue difficilia & grauia, non potest ecclesia regulariter obligare fideles: licet ex causa & pro culpa ad talia possit aliquos obligare. Quemadmodum aliquibus pro culpa praecedenti matrimonium interdicit, & aliquos in monasteria etiam inuitos statuit retrudendos. Cum igitur mortem suscipere & res suas amittere, & grauia tormenta subire, & talia consilia sint inter excessiue grauia computanda, ecclesia per nullam constitutionem potest regulariter Christianos in aliquo casu (in quo ad huiusmodi nec per legem diuinam nec per legem naturae nec per voluntatem spontaneam obligantur) astringere, ad non communicandum corporaliter. ter excommunicato, Christiani autem nullo praedictorum modorum ad hoc tenentur vel artantur. Quia si ad hoc aliquo praedictorum modorum essent astricti, etiam de dispensatione Papae non possent aliqui communicare excommunicatis: quod constat esse falsum. Ergo ecclesia regulariter per aliquam constitutionem sub poena excommunicationis quomodolibet obligare non potest, ut nec mortis metu vel amissionis rerum corporaliter communicet excommunicatis. Cum vero dicit, quod ecclesia tunc non haberet plenitudinem potestatis. Respondent quidam, quod summe necessarium esset his diebus, quod per sapientes iuramentis & horribilibus comminationibus per reges & principes ad veritatem dicendam artatos declararetur, quae spectant ad plenitudinem potestatis, quam ecclesia noscitur obtinere. Dicunt n. quod aliqui literati (ut beneficia ecclesiastica consequantur) ita ampliant ecclesiasticae potestatis plenitudinem, quod omnem iurisdictionem laicalem: imo omne dominium & proprietatem laicorum in quibuscunque rebus temporalibus manifeste evacuant. Quod tamen scripturae divinae aperte repugnat: cum etiam infideles secundum scripturam sacram rerum temporalium habeant dominium & proprietatem. Nec tempore Apostolorum licuit ecclesiae dominos infideles rebus temporalibus spoliare. Disc. Quomodo evacuant aliqui omnem proprietatem & dominium laicorum? Magist. Respondetur, quod sunt quidam dicentes, quod omne illud spectat ad plenitudinem potestatis ecclesiae, quod non obviat legi divinae, neque legi naturali. Et in omnibus casibus omnes Christiani summo pontifici obedire tenentur. Quare cum non habere proprietatem temporalium & dominium nec legi divinae, nec legi naturae repugnat: in hoc tenetur omnes laici summo pontifici obedire. Quare summus pontifex potest ad libitum de temporalibus laicorum disponere: & per consequens non sunt censendi ad proprietatem laicorum & dominium pertinere.
units.tr: Disciple. Two difficulties occur to me concerning this answer. The first is this: it seems that the Church, which also comprehends the supreme pontiff, and in which the fullness of power resides, can command any Catholic that he communicate with an excommunicated person on no account, not even to avoid death or loss of goods. For otherwise it would not have the fullness of power. But if the Church can command this, the one who is commanded is bound to obey. The second is this: if the Church cannot bind anyone under penalty of excommunication not to communicate bodily with an excommunicated person even under fear of death, it seems by the same reasoning that it cannot bind the faithful, under the same penalty, not to communicate with an excommunicated person in any way other than bodily. Master. To the first it is answered that the Church cannot bind anyone under penalty of excommunication not to communicate with an excommunicated person through fear of death or loss of goods. The reason assigned for this is as follows. The Church cannot, by the fullness of power, bind the faithful to those things which are works of supererogation, or which are known to be excessively burdensome, and to which a person is not bound either by divine law, by natural law, or by his own free will. For this is why the Church cannot bind Christians to a vow of continence or virginity: as the sacred law says, virginity can be recommended but cannot be commanded. Likewise the Church cannot compel Christians to enter a mendicant order, such as that of the Friars Minor. For this is supererogatory, and the reason why the Church cannot compel Christians to things that are supererogatory is that such things are excessively burdensome, and Christians are in no way bound to them by divine law or natural law. Therefore prelates ought not to bind Christians to these things, lest they become among those of whom Christ says in Matthew 13: For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers. Therefore the Church cannot, as a general rule, bind the faithful to things that are excessively difficult and burdensome, although it can bind some to such things for cause and on account of a fault. Just as it forbids marriage to some on account of a previous fault, and ordains that some be shut up in monasteries even against their will. Since, then, to undergo death, to lose one's goods, and to endure severe torments, and such counsels, are to be counted among the excessively burdensome things, the Church cannot by any constitution generally bind Christians, in any case in which they are not bound to such things by divine law, by natural law, or by their own free will, to refrain from communicating bodily with the excommunicated. Christians, however, are not bound or compelled to this by any of the aforesaid means. For if they were bound to it by any of the aforesaid means, then not even by dispensation of the Pope could anyone communicate with the excommunicated, which is known to be false. Therefore the Church cannot, as a rule, bind under penalty of excommunication in any way, so that one does not communicate bodily with the excommunicated even through fear of death or loss of goods.
