As for the claim that the Church would then not have the fullness of power, some answer that it would be most necessary in these days that, by learned men, the matters which pertain to the fullness of power that the Church is known to hold should be declared, and kings and princes bound by oaths and dreadful threats to speak the truth. For they say that some scholars (in order to obtain ecclesiastical benefices) so enlarge the fullness of ecclesiastical power that they plainly annul all lay jurisdiction, indeed all lordship and ownership of laymen in whatever temporal things. Yet this openly conflicts with divine Scripture, since, according to sacred Scripture, even unbelievers hold lordship and ownership of temporal things. Nor in the time of the Apostles was it lawful for the Church to despoil unbelieving lords of temporal goods. Disciple. How do some annul all ownership and lordship of laymen? Master. The answer is that there are some who say that whatever does not conflict with divine law or natural law belongs to the fullness of the Church's power. And in all cases all Christians are bound to obey the supreme pontiff. Therefore, since not having ownership and lordship of temporal things conflicts with neither divine law nor natural law, in this matter all laymen are bound to obey the supreme pontiff. Hence the supreme pontiff can dispose of the temporal goods of laymen at will, and consequently they are not to be considered as belonging to laymen in ownership and lordship.

units.la: Disc. De hac materia te exquisite interrogabo in tractatu de dogmatibus Iohan. 22. quare nunc tantum modo dic, cur non obstante plenitudine potestatis ecclesiasticae ecclesia non potest obligare Christianos, ut etiam pro morte vitanda non communicent corporaliter excommunicatis. Magist. Respondetur breviter a nonnullis, quod hoc ad plenitudinem potestatis ecclesiasticae minime spectat. Quia sicut plenitudo potestatis ecclesiae ad res laicorum, ut libere faciant de eis quicquid sibi placuerit, minime se extendit: ita etiam plenitudo potestatis ecclesiasticae ad illa, quae supererogationis & gratia sunt, nullatenus se extendit, ut scilicet illa valeat imperare, licet persuadere possit. Disc. Hoc quod plenitudo potestatis ecclesiasticae ad gratia minime se extendit, c. Caroli, quod ponitur dist. 19. c. in memoriam, adversari videtur. Ibi enim sic legitur: Licet vix ferendum ab illa sancta sede imponatur iugum: tamen feramus & pro devotione toleremus. Quibus verbis manifeste asseritur, quod ad gratiam potestas summi pontificis se extendit, cum vix ferenda sunt inter gratia computanda. Magist. Respondetur, quod Carolus loquitur de his, quae spectant ad officium summi pontificis. De aliis autem nequaquam intelligit. Unde si Papa praeciperet regi vel comiti, quod daret nepoti suo aliquam civitatem vel castrum, imo duos florenos, sibi nullatenus obedire esset astrictus. Multo fortius si tale quid praeciperet pauperi, non teneretur sibi parere. Disc. Dic, quomodo respondetur ad secundam difficultatem, quam ego tetigi ante. Magist. Ad illam respondetur per praedicta, quod ubi aliquid a lege divina vel iure naturali noscitur esse prohibitum, ibi potest ecclesia gravissimam poenam transgredientibus infligere, & ad servandum praeceptum legis divinae & legis naturae catholicos obligare. Ubi autem non est, nisi praeceptum humanum, nisi ex causa rationabili non voluntaria non potest ad servandum idem praeceptum catholicos sub graui artare poena, quin saltem pro morte vitanda posset quis tale praeceptum praetergredi. In tali enim casu interpretatur legem humanam non esse servandam in illo intellectu, quem verba prima facie sonare videntur. Sic, sicut allegatum est supra, Bonifacius martyr iuramentum suum, quod praestitit de non communicando haereticis, interpretatus fuit: quam interpretationem Zacharias summus pontifex approbavit. Cum igitur communicare corporaliter excommunicatis non est prohibitum a lege divina, neque a lege naturae, per nullum praeceptum humanum possunt regulariter Christiani constringi, quin pro morte vitanda possint communicare excommunicatis. Sed pro causa & pro culpa aliqui & pro aliquo tempore omnes possunt astringi, ne cum aliquo excommunicato communicent & pro morte vitanda. Unde & tale quid posset accidere circa Papam haereticum, quod omnes Christiani possent astringi ne communicarent eidem, etiam pro morte vitanda. Sed hoc non est regulare de omnibus Christianis omni tempore respectu omnium excommunicatorum. Sed communicare excommunicato aliter quam corporaliter, puta in crimine, vel in his quae ad ecclesiasticum officium pertinent, quo excommunicatus fungi non potest, est prohibitum a lege divina. Ideo ibi potest ecclesia adiicere poenam excommunicationis, ut nullus Christianus taliter communicet excommunicato etiam pro morte vitanda.
units.tr: Student: I will question you closely on this matter in the treatise on the dogmas, in the section on John 22. For now, only tell me why, despite the fullness of ecclesiastical power, the Church cannot oblige Christians not even to avoid death by communicating physically with the excommunicated. Master: Some answer briefly that this does not belong at all to the fullness of ecclesiastical power. For just as the fullness of the Church's power does not extend at all to the property of laymen, so that they may freely do with it whatever pleases them, so too the fullness of ecclesiastical power does not extend in any way to those things that are works of supererogation and of grace, so that it could command them, though it may be able to persuade. Student: That the fullness of ecclesiastical power does not extend at all to grace seems to conflict with the chapter of Charles, which is placed at dist. 19, chapter "In memoriam." For there it is read thus: "Although the yoke imposed by that holy see can scarcely be borne, yet let us bear it and endure it out of devotion." By these words it is clearly asserted that the power of the supreme pontiff does extend to grace, since things that can scarcely be borne are to be counted as grace. Master: It is answered that Charles is speaking of those things that pertain to the office of the supreme pontiff. He does not understand it at all of other matters. Hence, if the Pope were to command a king or a count to give his nephew some town or castle, or even two florins, he would not be bound to obey him at all. Much more strongly, if he commanded such a thing of a poor man, he would not be obliged to obey him. Student: Tell me how you answer the second difficulty, which I touched on before. Master: To it we reply from what has been said, that where something is known to be forbidden by divine law or by natural right, there the Church can inflict the gravest punishment on transgressors and oblige Catholics to keep the precept of divine law and natural law. But where there is only a human precept, the Church cannot, except for a reasonable cause that is not voluntary, bind Catholics under grave penalty to keep that same precept, so that someone could not at least transgress such a precept to avoid death. For in such a case the human law is interpreted as not to be kept in the sense that its words seem at first sight to carry. Thus, as was alleged above, the martyr Boniface interpreted his oath, which he had sworn not to communicate with heretics; and Pope Zachary approved that interpretation. Since, therefore, communicating physically with the excommunicated is not forbidden by divine law or by the law of nature, Christians cannot as a rule be constrained by any human precept so as not to be able, to avoid death, to communicate with the excommunicated. But for some cause and some fault, some persons, and for some time, all may be bound not to communicate with any excommunicated person, even to avoid death. Hence something of this kind could also happen with regard to a heretical Pope, that all Christians might be bound not to communicate with him, even to avoid death. But this is not the general rule, for all Christians at all times with respect to all the excommunicated. However, to communicate with an excommunicated person in any way other than physically, for example in crime, or in those matters that pertain to ecclesiastical office, which an excommunicated person cannot perform, is forbidden by divine law. Therefore there the Church can add the penalty of excommunication, so that no Christian may in such a way communicate with an excommunicated person, even to avoid death.

units.la: CAP. LXVIII. Vbi demonstratur, quae poenae sint plectendi receptores papae haeretici, & sequacium eius.
units.tr: CAP. LXVIII. Where it is shown what penalties are to be inflicted on the receivers of the heretical pope and his followers.

units.la: Discipulus. Aliqua quae in praesenti recitasti, aliquibus forsan videbuntur obscura, quae in tractatu De gestis circa fidem altercantium orthodoxam te faciam explicare. Ideo illis omissis dic, quae poenae receptores Papae haeretici & sequacium eius sunt plectendi. Magist. Circa hoc possunt esse opiniones contrariae. Una quod poena haereticorum sunt plectendi: quia haeretici sunt censendi. Haec opinio videtur esse Glossae extra de haereticis cap. excommunicamus prime, §. credentes, quae supra super verbo receptores, ait: sine quibus haretici diu manere non possunt, ar. ff. de offic. praesid. congruit. & ff. de receptoribus lib. 1. Unde merito isti sunt puniendi: imo gravius delinquunt, quia aliorum errorem defendunt, 24. q. 3. qui aliorum. Et ideo simili poena cum haereticis puniuntur 11. q. 3. qui consentit. Ex quibus verbis datur intelligi, quod receptores haereticorum gravius delinquunt, quam haeretici, & simili poena puniendi sunt. Alia est opinio, quod illi qui solum sunt receptores haereticorum & non approbant eorum errores, licet timore vel cupiditate tracti, aut ex aliqua causa mala eos nolunt de terra sua fugare, nec etiam detinere, non sunt haeretici reputandi, nec sunt etiam quo ad omnia, poena haereticorum plectendi. Quia multi scientes inter haereticos & receptores haereticorum expresse distinguunt, & taxantes poenam receptoris haereticorum moderatiorem poenam infligunt, sicut patet extra de haereticis cap. excommunicamus §. credentes. Hoc autem ex eodem capitulo §. moneantur, colligitur euidenter, ubi legitur: Si vero Dominus temporalis requisitus & monitus ab ecclesia terram suam purgare ab haeretica foeditate neglexerit, per metropolitanum & caeteros comprovinciales episcopos excommunicationis periculo innodetur. Et si satisfacere contempserit infra annum, significetur hoc summo pontifici, ut extunc ipse vasallos ab eius fidelitate denunciet absolutos, & terram exponet catholicis occupandam, qui eam exterminatis haereticis absque ulla contradictione possideant. Ex quibus datur intelligi, quod Dominus temporalis, licet sit receptor haereticorum, utpote quia quamuis requisitus & monitus ab ecclesia terram suam non purgat ab haeretica pravitate: non est statim per eam omnium haereticorum poena plectendus: quia bona sua non sunt statim publicanda, nec terra sua est ab his catholicis statim occupanda: quam poenam haeretici ipso facto incurrunt: quia Papa haereticus etiam occultus de iure nihil possidet, dist. 8. quo iure.
units.tr: Disciple. Some of the things you have just recited may seem obscure to some people. I will ask you to explain them in the treatise On the Matters Disputed by Those Who Contend over the Orthodox Faith. So set those aside and tell me what penalties are to be inflicted on the receivers of a heretical pope and on his followers. Master. On this question there can be opposing opinions. One holds that the receivers of heretics are to be punished with the penalty of heretics, because they are to be counted as heretics. This opinion seems to be that of the Gloss on Extra, On Heretics, chapter Excommunicamus, first, §. credentes, which above, on the word "receivers," says: "without whom heretics cannot remain for long"; cf. ff. de offic. praesid., congruit, and ff. de receptoribus, lib. 1. Hence they rightly deserve punishment, and indeed they offend more gravely, because they defend the errors of others, 24 q. 3, qui aliorum. Therefore they are punished with the same penalty as heretics, 11 q. 3, qui consentit. From these words it is to be understood that receivers of heretics offend more gravely than heretics themselves, and are to be punished with a like penalty. The other opinion holds that those who are merely receivers of heretics, and do not approve their errors, but who, drawn by fear or greed, or for some other bad reason, are unwilling to drive heretics from their land or even to detain them, are not to be reckoned heretics, nor are they to be punished in every respect with the penalty of heretics. For many learned writers expressly distinguish between heretics and receivers of heretics, and in assessing the penalty they inflict a milder one on the receiver, as is evident in Extra, On Heretics, chapter Excommunicamus, §. credentes. This is clearly gathered from the same chapter, §. moneantur, where it is read: "If indeed the temporal lord, when required and warned by the Church to purge his land of heretical foulness, neglects to do so, he is to be bound by the danger of excommunication through the metropolitan and the other bishops of the province. And if he scorns to make amends within a year, this is to be reported to the supreme pontiff, so that he may then declare his vassals absolved from their allegiance to him and expose the land to be occupied by Catholics, who, once the heretics have been driven out, may possess it without any opposition." From these words it is to be understood that the temporal lord, although he is a receiver of heretics (inasmuch as, though required and warned by the Church, he does not purge his land of heretical wickedness), is not at once to be punished with the penalty of all heretics. His goods are not immediately to be confiscated, nor is his land at once to be occupied by Catholics. Heretics incur that penalty by the very fact of their heresy, because a heretical pope, even a hidden one, possesses nothing by right, dist. 8, quo iure.

units.la: Discip. Ista opinio secunda magis videtur mihi consona statutis sanctorum patrum: ideo quomodo ad Glossam, quae videtur esse in contrarium, respondetur declara. Magist. Dupliciter respondetur. Uno modo, quod Glossa non est autentica, & aperte veritati repugnat: ideo est neganda. Nec videtur inconveniens negare Glossas decretorum cum etiam iste textus decretorum aperte negetur, eo quod in textu assertiones erroneae inserantur, sicut patet 23. q. 4. Sed obiicitur, ubi narrat Gratianus, tempore Achab missi fuerunt duo quinquagenarii ad Heliam, qui dicerent, homo Dei, rex Israel vocat te. Quod tamen est haeresis explicite condemnata: quia contraria veritas est explicite approbata, quia quod hoc accidit tempore Othoziae, mortuo rege Achab, in scriptura divina invenitur expresse. Et ipse Gratianus, si dicto illi pertinaciter adhaesisset, fuisset haereticus manifestus. Quia autem ex sola ignorantia absque omni pertinacia dixit praedictam haeresim opinando, quod sibi ex hoc contigit, quia memoriam quarti libri Regum tunc actualiter non habebat. Unde super verbo Achab, dicit Glossa: confudit historiam. Non enim Achab misit illos quinquagenarios: sed rex Othoziás. Nec etiam illud contigit sub Othozia. Et ita patet, quod etiam Glossa negat textum libri decretorum. Glossa etiam in plerisque locis reprobat Gratianum, sicut patet 11. quaest. 3. euidenter itaque & 12. q. 1. cap. 1. in aliis locis pluribus. Et ideo dicunt, quod multo fortius licet negare Glossas, quae (ut dicunt) nonnunquam divinae scripturae repugnant: interdum etiam catholicas sanctiones allegant inepte. Quod (ut dicunt) ex hoc accidit, quod Glossatores in scripturis sacris & scientiis Philosophicis nequaquam periti fuerunt. Et ideo quam plura capitula iuris canonici ex scripturis divinis & originalibus sanctorum accepta nequaquam profunde & perfecte intelligere potuerunt. Aliter dicitur, quod Glossa praedicta non dicit receptores haereticorum gravius de iure quam haereticos aut consimiliter puniendos, sed transeundo de receptoribus haereticorum ad defensores haereticorum dicit eos gravius puniendos, & quod gravius deliquerunt. Quod bene intelligendum est de defensoribus haereticorum & continet veritatem.
units.tr: Disciple. This second opinion seems to me more consonant with the statutes of the holy Fathers. So explain how the Gloss, which seems to say the opposite, is to be answered. Master. There are two ways of answering. In one way: the Gloss is not authentic and openly contradicts the truth, so it must be denied. Nor does it seem unreasonable to deny the Glosses on the Decretum, since even this text of the Decretum is openly denied, because erroneous assertions have been inserted into the text, as is evident in 23 q. 4. But it is objected that where Gratian relates that in the time of Ahab two fifties were sent to Elijah, who said, "Man of God, the king of Israel calls you," this is an explicitly condemned heresy, because the contrary truth is explicitly affirmed: it is expressly found in divine Scripture that this happened in the time of Ahaziah, after King Ahab had died. Gratian himself, had he obstinately clung to that statement, would have been a manifest heretic. But because he said it through ignorance alone, without any obstinacy, this happened to him because at that time he did not actually have the fourth book of Kings in memory. Hence on the word "Ahab" the Gloss says: "he confused the history. For Ahab did not send those fifties; it was King Ahaziah. Nor did that happen under Ahaziah." And so it is clear that even the Gloss denies a text of the book of the Decretum. The Gloss also rebukes Gratian in many places, as is evident in 11 quaest. 3, euidenter itaque, and 12 q. 1, cap. 1, and in many other places. Therefore they say that it is much more permissible to deny the Glosses, which (as they say) sometimes contradict divine Scripture and at other times cite Catholic decrees foolishly. This (as they say) happens because the Glossators were by no means skilled in the Scriptures and the philosophical sciences. Hence very many chapters of canon law, drawn from divine Scriptures and the originals of the holy writers, they were quite unable to understand deeply and perfectly. Otherwise it is said that the aforesaid Gloss does not say that receivers of heretics are by law to be punished more gravely than heretics, or in the same way. Rather, passing from receivers of heretics to defenders of heretics, it says that the defenders are to be punished more gravely and that they offended more gravely. This is rightly to be understood of the defenders of heretics, and it contains the truth.

units.la: CAP. LXIX.
units.tr: Chapter 69.

units.la: In quo quaeritur, an omnes receptores, fautores, defensores doctrinae haereticae & Papa haretici eadem sint poena plectendi.
units.tr: In which it is asked whether all receivers, favourers and defenders of heretical teaching, and a heretical Pope, are to be punished with the same penalty.

units.la: Discipulus. Post inquisitionem distinctam, licet propter ampliationem materiae, breuem de credentibus, fautoribus, defensoribus, & receptoribus haereticorum, peto ut absque probationibus maximis causa prolixitatis vitandae dicas aliquam opinionem, an omnes credentes, & similiter si omnes fautores, & omnes defensores, & omnes receptatores Papae haeretici & aliorum haereticorum sint aequaliter reprehensibiles iudicandi. Magist. Respondetur, quod aliquos esse magis vel minus aut aequaliter reprehensibiles indicandos, dupliciter potest intelligi, scil. secundum duplex iudicium & humanum. Secundum iudicium divinum, illi sunt magis reprehensibiles iudicandi, qui ex maiori contemptu Dei vel ex maiori negligentia peccant in aliquo praedictorum. Hoc autem notum est soli Deo. Discip. Non intendebam quaerere, nisi qui essent reprehensibiles iudicandi secundum humanum iudicium: & hoc non simpliciter, sed quo ad aliquid, & quo ad quid. Nolo enim intricatas & secundum aliquos fantasticas quaestiones in hoc opere pertractari. Magist. Ad intentionem tuam dicunt nonnulli, quod secundum humanum iudicium credentium haereticis & haereticae pravitati graviter peccant literati quam illiterati. Quia literati caeteris paribus possunt facilius cognoscere veritatem. Item gravius peccant caeteris paribus Theologi, quam alii. & inter Theologos grauius peccant illi, qui magis nutriti fuerunt in contraria veritate. Si enim aliquis Papa vel alius dogmatizaret & asserere conaretur errores quorundam magistorum Parisiensium, scilicet a summis pontificibus condemnatos, qui statum Mendicantium, scil. Praedicatorum & Minorum erronee damnauerint, inter omnes credentes erroribus illis Papae vel alteri Praedicatores & Minores grauius delinquere noscerentur. Quia quanto aliquis magis cognoscit vel habet cognoscere veritatem status sui: tanto magis peccat, si veritatem negat eandem. Cum ergo ad praedicatores & Minores specialissime spectat cognoscere veritatem status sui, magis quam alii, cum sint in notitia status sui nutriti, si cupientes Papae placere, vel ex alia causa credunt erroribus, quibus status eorum damnatur, magis quam alii caeteris paribus peccare noscuntur. Et si illi errores in fidem impingant, non solum modo ordinum suorum, sed etiam proditores Christianitatis sunt censendi. Nec vnquam Christianitas de eis poterit confidere tempore tentationis. Si enim ille est proditor veritatis, qui non libere pronunciat veritatem, quam pronunciare oportet 2.q.3. notate: multo fortius est ille proditor veritatis, qui credit errori, quem antea reputauit errorem. In casu ergo praedicto & in omni consimili praedicatores & maiores vltra omnes peccarent credendo huiusmodi erroribus. Inter ipsos autem grauius peccant literati, siue sint magistri, siue discipuli. Saepe enim his diebus discipuli superant magistros in veritatis cognitione. Nam quia acceptatores personarum ad magisterium ambitiosos exaltant, plures magistri istis temporibus rursum indigent, vt doceantur quae sunt elementa exordii sermonum Dei, & facti sunt quibus lacte opus sit non solido cibo. Et ideo literatiores siue sint discipuli siue magistri grauius peccant credendo erroribus. Discip. Qui peccant grauius inter fautores Papae haeretici aut sequaces eius? Magist. Respondetur, quod reges & principes scienter fauentes Papae haeretico ratione potentiae temporalis, qua absq; periculo etiam temporali valent sibi resistere, grauius peccant qua alii. Nam alii, qui non tanta vallantur potentia, absque forti aliquali periculo Papae haeretico resistere non videntur: & ita timor periculi attenuaret peccatum eorum. Ex isto autem concluditur, quod quanto aliqui maiorem defensionem haberent, quam alii: tanto grauius peccarent Papae haeretico fauendo. Si enim aliquis rex vel princeps omnes resistentes Papae haeretico in dominio suo manentes defenderet vel minime impugnaret, multo grauius delinquerent, qui manentes in dominio illius regis vel principis Papae haeretico aliquo modo fauerent; quam alii commorantes in dominiis regum & principum, qui resistentes Papae haeretico nequaquam defenderent, sed persequerentur, vel persequi & molestari ab aliis minime prohiberent.
units.tr: Student. After the distinct inquiry, though the subject matter has grown, I ask briefly, and without the greatest proofs so as to avoid prolixity, that you state an opinion on whether all believers, and likewise all favourers, all defenders and all receivers of a heretical Pope and of other heretics, are to be judged equally blameworthy. Master. It may be understood in two ways that some are to be judged more or less blameworthy, or equally so: according to the divine judgment and according to the human judgment. According to the divine judgment, those are to be judged more blameworthy who sin in any of the aforesaid ways out of greater contempt of God or greater negligence. This, however, is known to God alone. Student. I did not intend to ask anything except who are to be judged blameworthy according to human judgment, and this not absolutely but in some respect and in what respect. For I do not want intricate questions, which some consider fanciful, to be treated in this work. Master. To your purpose, some say that according to human judgment, when believers sin against heretics and heretical depravity, the lettered sin more gravely than the unlettered. For the lettered, other things being equal, can more easily know the truth. Likewise, other things being equal, theologians sin more gravely than others, and among theologians those sin more gravely who were brought up more in the contrary truth. For if some Pope or other were to teach and try to assert the errors of certain Parisian masters, namely those condemned by the supreme pontiffs, who wrongly condemned the state of the Mendicants, that is of the Preachers and the Minorites, then among all believers the Preachers and Minorites would be known to sin more gravely than others in believing those errors held by the Pope or another. For the more someone knows, or ought to know, the truth of his own state, the more he sins if he denies that same truth. Since it especially belongs to the Preachers and Minorites, more than to others, to know the truth of their own state, and since they have been brought up in knowledge of their state, if they believe errors by which their state is condemned, either out of desire to please the Pope or for some other cause, they are known to sin more than others, other things being equal. And if those errors strike at the faith, they are to be judged not only traitors of their own orders but also traitors of Christianity. Nor will Christianity ever be able to rely on them in the time of trial. For if he is a traitor to the truth who does not freely proclaim the truth that ought to be proclaimed (see 2 q. 3, note), much more is he a traitor to the truth who believes an error he had previously recognised as an error. In the aforesaid case, then, and in every similar case, the Preachers and Minorites would sin beyond all others by believing such errors. Among themselves, moreover, those who are lettered sin more gravely, whether they are masters or disciples. For in these days disciples often surpass their masters in knowledge of the truth. For, because men ambitious for teaching offices exalt the favourers of persons, many masters nowadays again need to be taught what are the elements of the beginning of God's words, and they have become such as need milk and not solid food. And therefore the more learned, whether they are disciples or masters, sin more gravely in believing errors. Student. Who sin more gravely among the favourers of the heretical Pope or his followers? Master. It is answered that kings and princes who knowingly favour the heretical Pope sin more gravely than others, by reason of the temporal power by which they are able to resist him even without temporal danger. For others, who are not protected by such power, do not seem able to resist the heretical Pope without some considerable danger, and so the fear of danger lessens their sin. From this it follows that the more defence someone has than others, the more gravely he sins in favouring the heretical Pope. For if some king or prince were to defend, or at least not attack, all who resist the heretical Pope and remain in his dominion, then those who, remaining under the rule of that king or prince, favoured the heretical Pope in any way would sin much more gravely than others living under the dominions of kings and princes who, far from defending those resisting the heretical Pope, persecute them, or do not forbid others to persecute and harass them.

units.la: Discip. Mirum videtur, quod reges & principes in hoc casu grauius peccarent quam praelati, cum magis pertineat ad praelatos obuiare Papae haeretico quam ad reges & principes. M. Respondetur, quod quidam praelati inter principes ratione temporalis potentiae computantur. Et ideo illi praelati fauendo Papae haeretico peccarent grauissime. Quia peccatum aliorum aliquo modo attenuaret timor periculi temporalis. Cum vero dicis, quod ad praelatos temporales & magis magistros, quam reges & principes &c. Respondetur, quod ad omnes spectat obuiare Papae haeretico. Quia sicut notat Glossa extr. de haeret. vrgentis; quod in religionem diuinam committitur, in omnium fertur iniuriam & publicum crimen committi c. erunt & Manichaeos. Sic etiam, vt habetur dist. 1. ius publicum est in sacris & in sacerdotibus & magistratibus. Vbi dicit Glossa qui laedit sacerdotes vel res sacras, ab omnibus tanquam pro publico crimine potest accusari. Multo magis ius publicum in fide Christiana consistit, & multo fortius qui laedit & impingit in fidem catholicam, tanquam pro publico crimine, potest ab omnibus accusari. Quare omnes tenentur Papae haeretico tanquam publicum crimen committenti resistere. Ad reges igitur & principes spectat Papae haeretico obuiare. Et hoc etiam spectat ad praelatos, qui etiam inter principes nullatenus numerantur: sed quodammodo aliter: quia ad reges & principes spectat contra Papam haereticum exercere potentiam temporalem: nisi essent aliqui, qui vellent sponte ex instinctu diuino subire martyrium, quemadmodum legio Thebeorum ad martyrium sponte se obtulit, licet si voluisset armis materialibus restitisset. Ad praelatos autem, qui non sunt principes, spectat scripturarum sermonibus & sanctis exhortationibus secularis auxilii brachium inuocando Papae haeretico obuiare. Porro quia reges & principes essent extra timorem periculi, quamuis Papam haereticum impugnarent. Multi autem praelati absque periculo temporali Papam haereticum impugnare non possunt. Ideo reges & principes Papae haeretico fauendo grauius peccarent, quam praelati in periculo constituti. Et etiam religiosi ac priores & doctores, qui essent extra periculum: quamuis Papam haereticum non impugnarent, Papae haeretico fauendo grauius peccarent quam reges & principes: pro eo quod maiorem notitiam habent veritatis: & se ad opera spiritualia (inter quae impugnatio Papae haeretici non obtinet infimum locum,) se artius obligaucrunt.
units.tr: Student. It seems strange that in this case kings and princes would sin more gravely than prelates, since it belongs more to prelates than to kings and princes to oppose the heretical Pope. Master. It is answered that some prelates are counted among princes by reason of temporal power, and so those prelates would sin most gravely in favouring the heretical Pope, because the fear of temporal danger would in some measure lessen the sin of others. When you say that it belongs to temporal prelates, and more to masters than to kings and princes, etc., the answer is that it belongs to all to oppose the heretical Pope. For, as the Gloss notes on the extra decretal De haereticis, Urgentis: what is committed against the divine religion is directed against the injury of all and is committed as a public crime (see c. Erunt and Manichaeos). Likewise, as is found in dist. 1: the public law lies in sacred things, in priests and in magistrates. Where the Gloss says: whoever harms priests or sacred things can be accused by all as for a public crime. Much more does the public law consist in the Christian faith, and much more strongly, whoever harms and attacks the Catholic faith can be accused by all as for a public crime. Wherefore all are bound to resist the heretical Pope as one committing a public crime. It therefore belongs to kings and princes to oppose the heretical Pope. And this also belongs to prelates, who are in no way counted among princes, but in a certain way differently: for it belongs to kings and princes to exercise temporal power against the heretical Pope, unless there were some who of their own accord, moved by divine impulse, would undergo martyrdom, just as the Theban legion offered itself willingly to martyrdom, although if it had wished it could have resisted with material arms. But it belongs to prelates, who are not princes, to oppose the heretical Pope by the words of Scripture and holy exhortations, invoking the arm of secular help. Moreover, since kings and princes would be beyond the fear of danger even if they attacked the heretical Pope, while many prelates cannot attack the heretical Pope without temporal danger, therefore kings and princes would sin more gravely in favouring the heretical Pope than prelates who are placed in danger. And also religious men and priors and teachers who were beyond danger, although they did not attack the heretical Pope, would sin more gravely in favouring the heretical Pope than kings and princes, because they have greater knowledge of the truth and have bound themselves more tightly to spiritual works (among which the opposition to the heretical Pope does not hold the lowest place).

units.la: Discip. Nunquid sufficit regibus & principibus defendere impugnantes Papam haereticum? Magist. Respondetur quod non: quia si non potenter, cum poterint, impugnauerint Papam haeretico: sed solummodo defenderint impugnantes, non erunt calidi neq; frigidi, sed tepidi. Et ideo incipiet eos Deus euomere de ore suo. Et consimiliter esset iudicandum de regibus & principibus, si alios sequaces, viles & pauperes Papae haeretici acriter inuaderent: & ipsum Papam haereticum satagerent excusare. Tales enim nequaquam aduerterent illud Deut. 1. Paruum audietis vt magnum: nec accipietis cuiuslibet personam. Quia Dei iudicium est cor no accendere. Et quamuis in omnibus iudiciis potestatem habentibus sit damnabile, tamen in regibus & principibus multo damnabilius ignominiosius esse diuoscitur. Acceptio n. persone Papæ hæretici in regibus & principib', qui eius potentiæ temporale nullatenus ptimescunt, vel cōtemptui fidei Christianæ, aut stolidæ fatuitati, aut nimio defectui zeliad fidē Christianā, aut auaritiæ effrenatæ, vel pusillanimitati, aut stolidæ vanitati, vel alicui alio vitio, q; dignitati regiæ & eiā principū est, pbrosum, debet ascribi. Disc. Dic qui inferiores regib' & principib' graui' peccant fauendo Papæ hæretico: vtrū videl. plati vel doctores, clerici seculares vel religiosi? Mag. Resp. q; quo ad aliq d plati graui' peccāt q; doctores, quia n. plati curā simplicių suscepērūt, & eos nō diligēter informauerūt cōtra errores Papæ: q; tū ad hoc, graui' peccāt q; magistri, qui curā illorū minime gerūt. Illi autē qui sunt plati & doctores grauissime peccant. Ratione a. sciētiæ maioris qua ppollēt doctores vtra platos simplicis literaturæ graui' peccāt doctores q; plati huiusmodi. Religiosi a. cæteris parib.graui' peccāt fauendo Papæ hæretico, q; clerici seculares, inter quos illi peccarēt grauissime, quorū statū vel aliquid cōtingēs statū eorū Papa hæreticus erronee cōdēnaret. Disc. Qui peccāt grauius, fautores Papæ hæretici, vel credētes erroribus Papæ hæretici? Mag. Resp. q; si sint fautores aliqui Papæ hæretici, qui nō sunt credētes ei' errorib': credētes (eo q; sunt hæretici) graui' peccāt, q; fautores qui nō sunt credētes. Aliter dicitur, q; quia fautores peccant sciēter: & illi q; sunt credentes ignoratēr peccāt; fautores graui' peccāt q; credētes. Disc. Qui peccāt grauius, fautores vel defensores Papæ hæretici? Mag. Resp. quia omnis defensor hæreticorū est fautor eorū nō ecōuerso. Ideo qui sunt Papæ hæretici defensores, grauius peccāt, q; qui sunt tantūmō fautores. Disc. Qui peccāt graui' inter defensores Papæ hæretici? Mag. Resp. q; inter scienter defensores Papæ hæretici, graui' peccāt reges & principes ac potētes, qui potētiā Papæ hæretici nō formidāt. Inter defensores aūt ignorātēr Papæ hæretici qui laborāt ignorātia crassa & supina, dānabilior est in platis (& grauius peccāt) & in doctorib' & religiosis, q; in regib. & principibus, qui reb' secularib' ex officio sunt inteti. Disc. Dic de receptoribus. Papæ hæretici, q graui' peccār. Mag. Resp. q; to receptores Papæ hæretici muniūtur maiori potētia tēporali, & minus timent potentiā temporale Papæ hæretici, tanto grauius peccant. Et ideo grauius peccaret rex potētes, recipiēdo Papā hæreticū, q; Dux vel Baro, aut Castrū vel Ciuitas, nisi ex aliqua causa rex plus haberet timere potentiā temporale Papæ hæretici, quā alius minoris potentiæ temporalis. Et ex istis concluditur, q; cæteris parib' inter omnes reges & principes ille, qui maioris esset potentiæ, & quē plus timeret Papa hæreticus contra Deū & Christianitatē delinqueret, si Papam hæreticū minime impugnaret.
units.tr: Student. Is it enough for kings and princes merely to defend those who attack the heretical Pope? Master. It is answered that it is not, because if they do not attack the heretical Pope vigorously, when they could, but only defend those who attack him, they will not be cold or hot but lukewarm. And therefore God will begin to spew them out of his mouth. And the same judgment would be made of kings and princes if they fiercely assailed other followers of the heretical Pope who are base and poor, and strove to excuse the heretical Pope himself. For such men would by no means heed that saying of Deut. 1: You shall hear the small as well as the great; you shall not accept any person's face. For it is God's judgment not to kindle the heart. And although in all judgment-holding powers it is damnable, yet in kings and princes it is seen to be much more damnable and shameful. For respect of persons, shown to the heretical Pope by kings and princes who in no way fear his temporal power, or who through contempt for the Christian faith, or foolish stupidity, or excessive lack of zeal for the Christian faith, or unbridled avarice, or pusillanimity, or foolish vanity, or some other vice, which is disgraceful to the royal dignity and to that of princes, ought to be ascribed to them. Student. Tell me which of the inferiors to kings and princes sin more gravely in favouring the heretical Pope: that is, prelates or teachers, secular clergy or religious? Master. It is answered that in some respects prelates sin more gravely than teachers, because prelates have taken on the care of simple people and have not diligently instructed them against the errors of the Pope; but in this respect they sin more gravely than masters, who do not bear care for them. Yet those who are both prelates and teachers sin most gravely. By reason of greater learning, which teachers have over prelates of simple literacy, teachers sin more gravely than such prelates. Religious men, other things being equal, sin more gravely in favouring the heretical Pope than secular clergy, among whom those would sin most gravely whose state, or something touching their state, the heretical Pope wrongly condemned. Student. Who sins more gravely, the favourers of the heretical Pope or those who believe the errors of the heretical Pope? Master. It is answered that if there are some favourers of the heretical Pope who do not believe his errors, the believers (since they are heretics) sin more gravely than the favourers who do not believe. Otherwise it is said: because favourers sin knowingly, and those who believe sin in ignorance, the favourers sin more gravely than the believers. Student. Who sins more gravely, the favourers or the defenders of the heretical Pope? Master. It is answered that every defender of heretics is a favourer of them, but not conversely. Therefore those who defend the heretical Pope sin more gravely than those who are merely favourers. Student. Who sins more gravely among the defenders of the heretical Pope? Master. It is answered that among those who knowingly defend the heretical Pope, kings and princes and the powerful, who do not fear the power of the heretical Pope, sin most gravely. Among those who defend the heretical Pope in ignorance, who labour under gross and supine ignorance, prelates are more damnable (and sin more gravely), and teachers and religious men more than kings and princes, who are occupied with secular affairs by their office. Student. Tell me about the receivers of the heretical Pope: who sin more gravely? Master. It is answered that the more the receivers of the heretical Pope are protected by greater temporal power, and the less they fear the temporal power of the heretical Pope, the more gravely they sin. And therefore a powerful king who receives the heretical Pope would sin more gravely than a duke or baron, or a castle or city, unless for some cause the king had more reason to fear the temporal power of the heretical Pope than another of lesser temporal power. And from these things it follows that, other things being equal, among all kings and princes he who was of greatest power, and whom the heretical Pope feared most, would sin against God and Christianity if he did not attack the heretical Pope at all.

units.la: CAP. LXX. In quo quæritur, quare periculum immineret fidei catholicæ, si aliquando contingeret Papam fore hæreticum.
units.tr: CHAPTER 70. In which it is asked why the Catholic faith would be in danger if a Pope should ever happen to become a heretic.

units.la: Disc. De Papa hæretico, aut credentibus, fautoribus, defensoribus, receptoribus Papæ hæretici, vt modo mihi videtur, nonnulla dis'cussimus: nunc autē rogo, vt de grauitate periculi tempore Papæ hæretici, si vnq; aliquis Papa à fide deuiabit catholica, perscruteris, an scil. tempore Papæ hæretici graue imminebit periculum Christianis? Mag. Interrogatio tua, vt eā proponis, aliquid supponit, & aliquid quærit. Supponit n. q; aliquis erit Papa hæreticus. Quærit autē, quale tunc periculū Christianis instabit. Dic sto vero, quod supponit, fuerunt opiniones: quibusdam dicentibus, q; esset futurus Papa hæreticus. Aliis dicentibus, q; temerariū fuit & est dicere, q; erit Papa hæreticus, & temerariū est negare. Circa illud etiam, q; interrogatio tua quærit, sunt diuersæ opiniones. Vna est, q; si vnquā aliquis Papa fuerit hæreticus, non graue periculum fidelibus imminebit: quia cardinales, prælati & magistri statim sibi resistent. Aliqui etiā reges & principes, ac alii seculares potenter assistent. Et ideo statim perfidiam Papæ hæretici extirpabunt. Alia est opinio, quæ de futuris non reputat diuinandum. Tenentes enim opinionem illam dubitant, q; si vnquam erit Papa hæreticus, grauissimo periculo catholici exponentur. Ita quod timent, q; maius instabit periculū Christianis, si aliquis Papa diu victurus est hæreticus, q; si tota Christianitas à Sarracenis vel aliis infidelibus caperetur. Disc. Miror, q; aliquī de hoc valeant dubitare: quia si Sarraceni omnes regiones Christianorū per potentiā subiugarent, omnes Christianos extinguerent vel subdeterent seruituti. Papa a. hæreticus hoc minime attētaret. Et ita istorū opinio ratione carere videtur: de te tamen motiuū eorū audire desidero. Mag. Si affectas scire motiuū eorū, primo opinionē eorū intelligas. Disc. Puto q; intelligo. Mag. Nō apparet, quia tu videris intelligere de periculo corporali specialiter: ipsa intelligūt de periculo spirituali: quāuis etiā secundario intelligat de periculo corporali: qa dubitāt q; Papa hæreticus, nisi refrenetur timore catholicorū, cogitabit omnes Christianos extinguere vel cogere aliā sectā suscipere. Disc. Narra motiuū eorū intelligēdo de periculo spirituali. Mag. Motiuū eorum est tale. Quanto quis pluribus modis, quorum vnus non impedit alium, sed quilibet efficacior fit per quemlibet, nititur aliquē expugnare, tanto illū citius expugnabit, vel dubitandum est si citius superabit. Sed si Papa esset hæreticus, pluribus modis quam Saraceni (quibus tota Christianitas non posset corporaliter obuiare) conabitur populum Christianum expugnare, & spiritualiter iugulare. Modi autem impugnandi, quibus vteretur, essent æque efficaces vel efficaciores, quam modus impugnandi Sarracenorum. Vnusquisq; modus alium nequaquam impediet: sed quilibet quemlibet efficaciorem reddet. Ergo Papa, si esset hæreticus, citius quā Saraceni, populū Christianum superabit. Spiritualiter autem superari & in anima cruciari periculosius est & peius, q; morti succumbere corporaliter. Igitur grauius periculum imminebit vel imminere poterit populo Christiano, si Papa efficeretur hæreticus, q; si Saraceni totam terram Christianorum suæ subdererent ditioni. Disc. Qui sunt illi modi, quibus Papa, si esset hæreticus, catholicos & Christianos populos impugnaret? Mag. Respondetur, q; catholicos & sibi resistentes forte non minus acerbe, q; Saraceni, corporaliter procuraret inuadi: quia mandaret episcopis & inquisitoribus hæreticæ prauitatis, vt eos vbicunq; possent satagerent captiuare, & nisi à suo propòsito resiliarent, eos traderent curiæ seculari: qui, vt Papæ hæretico complacerent, & ab eo aliquod beneficiū obtinerent, tanquam belue crudelissimæ mandatum Papæ hæretici totis viribus conarentur effectui mancipare. Secundo, Papa si esset hæreticus, per scripturarum testimonia ad suum sensum retorta Christianos inuaderet, & multos traheret ad suam voluntatem: eo q; intelligentiam scripturarum nequaquam habentes ad verum intellectum venire nescirent. Tertio, impugnaret Christianos per speciem veritatis & religionis, cui non adhærere videretur multis stultum & insanum. Quarto, impugnaret catholicos per ecclesiasti- cam auctoritatem, cui non obedire putaretur à nonnullis inobedientiæ crimen incurrere. Disc. Probabile mihi videtur, quod istis modis & aliis Papa, si esset hæreticus, niteretur Christianos suis erroribus subiugare, vt eos spiritualiter ingulares. Sed Christiani sibi nequaquam acquiescerent: imo nec etiam tolerarent: sed statim de eo facerent iustiuæ complementū. Quare cum ipse esset vnus, cui omnes resisterent Christiani: Saraceni autem quamplurimi: nullo modo, tantū posset imminere periculum, si Papa efficeretur hæreticus, sicut si Saraceni sibi terram Christianorū subiicerent. Mag. Resp. q; si Christiani vellēt Papæ hæretico obuiare, non incumberet eis tantum periculum spiritualiter, sicut si Saraceni regiones Christianorū sibi subiicerent: Sed dubitant isti, q; multitudo Christianorū Papæ hæretico nullatenus obuiaret: imo suis erroribus inhæreret, ipsiq; sponte faueret. Disc. Vnde posset accidere, q; multitudo Christianorū Papæ hæretico adhærit? Mag. Dicitur, q; ex multis causis forte accideret, & aliqui adhærerent ex vna causa, alii ex alia. Disc. Enumera aliquas causas, ex quibus posset accidere. Magist. Dicitur, quod vna causa, ex qua aliqui Papæ hæretico adhærerent, est falsa & erronea æstimatio, quam habent nonnulli de Papa. Disc. Quæ est illa falsa & erronea æstimatio? Magist. Respondetur, quod est multiplex. Quidam enim putant, q; Papa peccare non potest: quemadmodum quidam imaginantur, q; in quodā loco antiquo legi in fauorem Sergii Papæ tradiderunt. Unde quidam (vt audiui) his temporibus publice dicunt, quod Papa est Deus in terris, non quidem sicut omnes sacerdotes dicuntur dii, qui tamen peccare possunt: sed sic, vt male facere nequaquam possit, & in terris omnia quæ vult possit. Quidam putant, quod Papa contra fidem errare non potest. Quidam putant, quod licet Papa peccare & errare contra fidem possit, de omnibus tamen quæ facit debemus supponere, quod sint bene facta: & de nullo quod facit licet nobis iudicare, quod sit male factum. Quidam putant, quod licet valeamus reputare aliqua facta Papæ esse mala, & male facta: tamen nulli licet Christiano Papam arguere vel iudicare, reprehendere aut aliquam contra eum iudicialiter ferre sententiam. Et ex his quatuor æstimationibus falsis de Papa, & ex qualibet earum accideret, quod Papa effecto hæretico ei Christiani aliqui adhærebunt. Discip. Primæ duæ æstimationes falsæ mihi videntur. De quarta autem tractatum est prius. Ideo dic secundum illos, in quo tertia æstimatio a veritate recedit. Magist. Dicitur quod quantum ad omnia quæ non possunt bono animo fieri, est contraria veritati. Quicquid enim Papa fecerit, quod non potest bono animo fieri, nec recta intentione, licet cuilibet hoc scienti iudicare de Papa, quod male facit & inique, & quod peccat mortaliter. Unde si viderem Papam fornicantem, simoniam committentem, vel mentientem in doctrina religionis, aut in proximi nocumentum, vel innocentem aliquem diffamantem, vel aliquid contra Deum præcipientem, aut aliquid huiusmodi, liceret mihi & deberem iudicare non quidem iudicialiter, sed certa credulitate, Papam peccare mortaliter. Discip. Secundum istam sententiam ita possem licite iudicare de Papa, quod male facit, sicut de quocunque alio Christianorum. Magist. Respondetur quod non: quia multa licent Papæ, quæ aliis illicita dignoscuntur. Et ideo de talibus si faciat ea Papa, non licet iudicare, quod Papa male faciat ea: de aliis hoc non licet. Patet hoc, quia sunt aliqua, quæ sunt illicita Papæ, quæ tamen aliis licent, & de talibus licet iudicare, quod Papa peccat: sed de aliis hoc minime licet. Discip. Videtur autem, quod isti parum reputant de persona Papæ: licet forte de officio Papæ multum æstiment. Magist. Isti reputant Papam hominem mortalem, peccabilem, innumeris periculis spiritualibus subiectum. Multos autem summos pontifices, qui fuerunt, reputant fuisse viros sceleratissimos, omni consusione dignos: & quia licet hoc asserere & sentire: & ita de quolibet summo pontifice licet hoc sentire in speciali, quandocunque facit aliquid, & constat eum facere, quod bono animo nequaquam facere potest. Unde assertionem, qua dicitur, quod debemus reputare bene factum quicquid fecerit, hæresim perniciosissimam & periculosissimam arbitrantur.
units.tr: Student. Concerning the Pope who is a heretic, or those who believe in, favour, defend or harbour a heretical Pope, I think we have discussed some matters, as it seems to me now. But I now ask you to examine the seriousness of the danger in the time of a heretical Pope, should any Pope ever depart from the Catholic faith. That is, would a grave danger then threaten Christians during the time of a heretical Pope? Master. Your question, as you put it, presupposes something and also asks something. It presupposes that some Pope will be a heretic. It asks what kind of danger would then threaten Christians. Tell me truly what it presupposes: there have been opinions, some saying that a Pope would be a heretic, others saying that it was and is rash to say that a Pope will be a heretic, and rash to deny it. There are also different opinions about what your question asks. One is that if any Pope were ever a heretic, no grave danger would threaten the faithful, because the cardinals, prelates and teachers would at once resist him. Some kings and princes, and other secular men, would also powerfully support them, and so they would at once root out the treachery of the heretical Pope. Another opinion holds that one should not presume to divine future events. For those who hold that opinion doubt that, if there ever were a heretical Pope, Catholics would be exposed to the gravest danger. They fear that a greater danger would threaten Christians if a Pope were to remain a heretic for a long time than if the whole of Christendom were captured by the Saracens or other unbelievers. Student. I am surprised that some can doubt this, because if the Saracens subdued all the regions of the Christians by force, they would destroy all Christians or reduce them to slavery. A heretical Pope would not attempt that. So their opinion seems to lack reason, but I would still like to hear from you what their motives are. Master. If you wish to know their motives, first understand their opinion. Student. I think I understand it. Master. It does not appear so, for you seem to understand it chiefly of bodily danger. They understand it of spiritual danger, although they also understand it secondarily of bodily danger, because they doubt that a heretical Pope, unless he were restrained by fear of Catholics, would plan to destroy all Christians or to force them to adopt another sect. Student. Tell me their motive, understanding it of spiritual danger. Master. Their motive is this. The more ways someone uses to overcome another, none of which hinders the others but each is made more effective by each of the others, the more quickly he will overcome him, or it must be doubted whether he will overcome him more quickly. But if the Pope were a heretic, he would try to overthrow the Christian people, and to slay them spiritually, in more ways than the Saracens (against whom the whole of Christendom could not resist bodily). The ways of attacking that he would use would be equally or more effective than the ways of the Saracens. Each way would in no way hinder another, but each would make every other more effective. Therefore a Pope, if he were a heretic, would overcome the Christian people more quickly than the Saracens. But to be overcome spiritually and tormented in the soul is more dangerous and worse than to succumb to death in the body. Therefore a greater danger would threaten, or could threaten, the Christian people if the Pope became a heretic than if the Saracens subjected the whole land of the Christians to their rule. Student. What are those ways by which a Pope, if he were a heretic, would attack the Catholic and Christian peoples? Master. It is answered that he would perhaps procure, no less bitterly than the Saracens, that Catholics and those who resisted him be attacked in body. For he would order bishops and inquisitors of heretical depravity to take pains to capture them wherever they could, and unless they withdrew from their purpose, to hand them over to the secular court. These men, to please the heretical Pope and to obtain some benefice from him, would strive with all their strength to carry out the Pope's command, like the most cruel beasts. Second, a heretical Pope would attack Christians by the testimonies of Scripture twisted to his own sense, and would draw many to his will, since those who have no understanding of Scripture would not know how to come to the true meaning. Third, he would attack Christians under the appearance of truth and religion, to which many would seem foolish and mad not to adhere. Fourth, he would attack Catholics by ecclesiastical authority, and some would think that by not obeying it they would incur the crime of disobedience. Student. It seems probable to me that by these and other means a Pope, if he were a heretic, would strive to bring Christians under his errors so as to slay them spiritually. But Christians would by no means agree with him, nor even tolerate him, but would at once carry out the just punishment upon him. Therefore, since he would be one man whom all Christians would resist, while the Saracens would be very many, in no way could as great a danger threaten, if the Pope became a heretic, as if the Saracens subjected the land of the Christians to themselves. Master. I answer that if Christians wished to resist the heretical Pope, they would not be threatened with as great a spiritual danger as if the Saracens subjected the regions of the Christians to themselves. But these men doubt that the multitude of Christians would by no means resist the heretical Pope, but would rather cling to his errors and willingly favour him. Student. How could it happen that the multitude of Christians would cling to a heretical Pope? Master. It is said that this could perhaps happen for many reasons, and some would adhere for one reason, others for another. Student. Enumerate some of the reasons by which it could happen. Master. It is said that one cause by which some would adhere to a heretical Pope is the false and erroneous estimation that some have of the Pope. Student. What is that false and erroneous estimation? Master. It is answered that it is manifold. For some think that the Pope cannot sin, just as some imagine, as they have handed down in favour of Pope Sergius, that they read something in an ancient place. Hence some (as I have heard) say publicly in these times that the Pope is God on earth, not indeed in the way that all priests are called gods, who nevertheless can sin, but in such a way that he cannot possibly do evil and can do everything on earth that he wishes. Some think that the Pope cannot err against the faith. Some think that although the Pope can sin and err against the faith, we must nonetheless suppose of everything he does that it is well done, and we may not judge of anything he does that it is badly done. Some think that although we may judge some of the Pope's deeds to be bad and badly done, yet it is not lawful for any Christian to accuse or judge the Pope, to rebuke him, or to pronounce any judicial sentence against him. And from these four false estimations of the Pope, and from each of them, it would follow that some Christians would adhere to him once he had become a heretic. Student. The first two false estimations seem to me to be false. But the fourth has been discussed before. So tell me, according to them, where the third estimation departs from the truth. Master. It is said that, as to all things which cannot be done with a good intention, it is contrary to the truth. For whatever the Pope does that cannot be done with a good intention or a right purpose, anyone who knows this may judge of the Pope that he acts badly and unjustly, and that he sins mortally. Hence if I saw the Pope committing fornication, committing simony, or lying in the teaching of religion, or to the harm of his neighbour, or defaming some innocent man, or commanding something against God, or anything of this kind, I would be allowed, and I ought to judge, not indeed judicially but with certain belief, that the Pope sins mortally. Student. According to this opinion I could lawfully judge the Pope, when he does wrong, in the same way as any other Christian. Master. It is answered that you could not, because many things are lawful for the Pope which are known to be unlawful for others. And so if the Pope does such things, one may not judge that he does wrong in them, but one may not do so in the case of others. This is clear, because there are some things which are unlawful for the Pope but which are lawful for others, and concerning such things one may judge that the Pope sins; but concerning others this is by no means lawful. Student. But it seems that these men think little of the person of the Pope, although perhaps they esteem the office of the Pope highly. Master. These men regard the Pope as a mortal man, liable to sin, and subject to countless spiritual dangers. But they think that many of the supreme pontiffs who have existed were most wicked men, worthy of all disgrace; and they say and hold that it is lawful to hold this, and so about any supreme pontiff it is lawful to hold this in particular whenever he does something, and it is evident that he does something which he cannot possibly do with a good intention. Hence they consider the assertion that we must regard as well done whatever he has done to be a most pernicious and dangerous heresy.

units.la: Discip. Sunt ne aliquæ aliæ æstimationes falsæ & erroneæ, quæ facerent multos Papæ hæretico adhærere? Magist. Respondetur quod sic. Putant enim quidam, quod coertio Papæ hæretici spectat solummodo ad concilium generale. Quidam autem putant, quod coertio Papæ hæretici spectat solummodo ad clericos, & nullo modo ad laicos: nisi fuerint per prælatos ecclesiæ requisiti. Quidam vero putant, quod coertio & similiter vitatio hæretici Papæ solummodo spectat ad cardinales. Quidam putant, quod solummodo spectat ad maiores prælatos ecclesiæ: puta ad patriarchas & episcopos. Quidam putant, quod simplices & laici de spiritualibus nihil facere debent, nisi quod fuerit eis per episcopos suos iniunctum. Et ideo de Papa hæretico se intromittere non debent, nisi quod eis præceperunt episcopi eorundem. Quidam dicunt, quod quamdiu Papa hæreticus toleratur a multitudine Christianorum, nullus debet eum aliqualiter impugnare. Quidam putant, quod multitudo est in omnibus sequenda. Et ideo ille pro Papa est habendus, quem multitudo Christianorum habet pro Papa. Ex his omnibus æstimationibus, & qualibet illarum, aliisque quam plurimis æstimationibus falsis & erroneis accideret: quod si Papa fieret hæreticus, quam plures ei firmiter adhærerent.
units.tr: Student: Are there some other false and erroneous opinions which would cause many people to cling to a heretical Pope? Master: The answer is yes. For some think that the restraint of a heretical Pope pertains only to a general council. Others think that the restraint of a heretical Pope pertains only to the clergy, and in no way to the laity, unless they have been called upon by the prelates of the Church. Still others think that the restraint and likewise the avoidance of a heretical Pope pertains only to the cardinals. Some think that it pertains only to the greater prelates of the Church, namely the patriarchs and bishops. Some think that ordinary people and laymen ought to do nothing in spiritual matters except what has been enjoined on them by their bishops, and therefore they ought not to meddle with a heretical Pope, except as their bishops have directed them. Some say that as long as a heretical Pope is tolerated by the multitude of Christians, no one ought in any way to attack him. Some think that the multitude is to be followed in all things, and therefore he is to be regarded as Pope whom the multitude of Christians regards as Pope. From all these opinions, and from any one of them, and from very many other false and erroneous opinions, it would come about that, if the Pope became a heretic, very many would cling firmly to him.

units.la: Discip. Dixisti unicam causam diuisam in plures, ex qua accideret, quod si Papa efficeretur hæreticus: & quod Christiani plures adhærerent eidem. Ideo nunc dic alias causas, ex quibus hoc accideret. Magist. Alia causa siue occasio secundum istos, quare multi Christiani Papæ hæretico adhærerent, est timor mundanus siue humanus, iunctus diffidentiæ, qua unus Christianus dissideret de alio. Et ista causa oritur ex defectu zeli ad catholicam fidem. Quia enim multi propter catholicam fidem nollent aliquod detrimentum corporis vel rerum incurrere, vel saltem non magnum. Et ideo nescientes, an alii Christiani nollent eis assistere contra Papam hæreticum, ab impugnatione Papæ hæretici omnino desisterent, & eidem cum aliis adhærerent, saltem quousque aliquis potens inciperet Papam hæreticum impugnare. Putant enim tenentes opinionem prædictam, quod si Papa esset hæreticus: & aliquis rex potens eum inuaderet cum toto posse: multi qui prius Papæ hæretico adhæserunt, eum fortissime impugnarent. Et hæc est una causa secundum istos, quare reges & principes & alii potestates, qui temporalem potentiam Papæ hæretici non timerent, gravius peccarent, quam alii, si Papæ hæretico favèrent. Quia eorum negligentia esset quam pluribus occasio Papæ hæretici adhærendi. Alia causa siue occasio, quare multi adhærerent Papæ hæretico, est cupiditas & ambitio. Cupiditas enim obtinendi diuitias & pecunias, ac beneficia ecclesiastica & honores à Papa hæretico, multos faceret eidem consentire.
units.tr: Student: You have named one cause, divided into several, from which it would come about that, if the Pope became a heretic, many Christians would cling to him. Now therefore name the other causes from which this would come about. Master: Another cause or occasion, according to these men, why many Christians would cling to a heretical Pope is worldly or human fear, joined with a distrust by which one Christian would distrust another. And this cause arises from a lack of zeal for the Catholic faith. For many, for the sake of the Catholic faith, would be unwilling to incur any loss of body or goods, or at least not a great one. And so, not knowing whether other Christians would be willing to stand by them against a heretical Pope, they would altogether desist from attacking the heretical Pope and would cling to him along with others, at least until some powerful man began to attack the heretical Pope. For those holding the aforesaid opinion think that if the Pope were a heretic, and some powerful king were to assail him with all his might, many who had previously clung to the heretical Pope would attack him most vigorously. And this is, according to these men, one reason why kings and princes and other powers, who did not fear the temporal power of a heretical Pope, would sin more gravely than others if they favoured a heretical Pope, because their negligence would give many an occasion to cling to a heretical Pope. Another cause or occasion why many would cling to a heretical Pope is covetousness and ambition. For the desire to obtain riches and money, and ecclesiastical benefices and honours from a heretical Pope, would make many consent to him.

units.la: CAP. LXXI.
units.tr: CHAPTER 71.

units.la: In quo inquiritur, qui sint reputandi idonei ad impugnationem Papae haeretici, & praerogativam unam quam debent tales habere declarat.
units.tr: In which it is asked who should be regarded as fit to oppose a heretical Pope, and it sets out the one special qualification such men must have.

units.la: DIscipulus. De impugnatione Papæ hæretici sæpe fecimus mentionem, de quibus vnum obscure vt pertractes, qui videlicet ad impugnandum Papam hæreticum sunt idonei reputandi. Magist. Ad hoc respondetur, quod omnes catholici discretionem habentes ad impugnandum Papam hæreticum, vno modo vel alio debent idonei reputari. Discipul. Ista responsio est tam generalis, quod ad mentem meam nequaquam vadit. Scio enim, quod cum Papa hæreticus sit omnium fidelium inimicus, omnes fideles rationes ventes ad impugnandum ipsum aliquomodo idonei sunt censendi: oportet tamen quod inter ipsos sint quidam, qui sint quasi duces, directores & capita aliorum de quibus interrogationem, quam proposui, intellexi. Magist. Respondetur quod virtutibus excellentes, in sacris literis eruditi, in arduis rebus experti, & potentia praediti temporali, vt sint duces & capita impugnantium Papam hæreticum, sunt censendi idonei. Contingit enim dupliciter Papam hæreticum impugnare, scil. corporaliter contra ipsum, si oportuerit, materialia arma movendo: & spiritualiter tam ipsum quam errores eius auctoritatibus & rationibus convincendo. Primo modo potentia praediti temporali debent idonei reputari ad Papam hæreticum impugnandum. Secundo modo in sacris literis eruditi sunt idonei, vt sint quasi duces & principales impugnatores Papæ haeretica prauitate maculati. Virtutum autem eminentia & rerum experientia opportunæ videntur vtrisque, vt sicut oportet & quando oportet Papam hæreticum & complices eius impugner. Discip. Adhuc ista responsio est magis generalis, quam vellem. Unde precor vt secundum aliquam sententiam aliquas praerogativas speciales assignes, quibus oportet principales impugnatores Papæ hæretici praeeminere ad hoc, quod idonei censeantur. Magist. Speciales praerogativæ tales sunt innumerae. Discip. Aliquas paucas tange. Magist. Dicunt quidam, quod ad hoc, quod quis impugnator Papæ hæretici idoneus censeatur, requiritur quod sit firmiter stabilitus in veritatibus contrariis Papæ hæretici erroribus, vt scilicet nulla ratione ab illis veritatibus possit avelli. Unde quantum ad veritates illas assertiones suas neq; correctioni Papæ, neq; correctioni concilii generalis, nec correctioni angelorum de caelo debet submittere: sed quemadmodum beatus Paulus scripsit Gal. 1. dicens: Sed licet nos aut angelus de caelo evangelizet vobis praeterquam quod evangelizavimus vobis, anathema sit. Ita quilibet impugnator idoneus Papæ hæretici, dicat in corde suo & proferat ore, cum fuerit opportunum: licet ego, aut Papa, aut concilium generale, aut tota congregatio Christianorum, aut tota multitudo angelorum de caelo, errores Papæ hæretici annunciare asserere vel affirmare præsumpserit, anathema sit. Ideo autem non debet impugnator idoneus Papæ hæretici assertiones suas, quantum ad veritates contrarias erroribus Papæ hæretici alicuius correctioni submittere: quia illas veritates non tanquam ab homine, sed tanquam a Deo, qui correctione non eget, traditas suscepit, amplectitur & veneratur. Et ex isto (vt dicunt) eliditur error quorundam dicentium, quod aliquis Christianus fidem suam debet supponere correctioni beatissimi Papæ. Quod probant per exemplum de beato Hieronymo, qui fidem suam didicerat in ecclesia, in qua nutritus fuit, correctioni & iudicio beatissimi Papæ. Sed hoc dicunt isti esse erroneum, imo haereticum manifeste. Quod exemplis & ratione probare conantur. Primo quidem exemplo beati Pauli, qui, vt legitur ad Gal. 2. cum reprehenderet Papam, scil. beatum Petrum, assertionem suam correctioni Papæ nequaquam submisit: imo voluit, quod Papa se suæ correctioni submitteret. Ideo enim reprehendit eum, vt de excessu commisso in praeiudicium evangelicæ veritatis corrigeret. Secundo probant hoc exemplo clericorum Romanorum, qui se a communione Anastasii Papæ secundi abegerunt. De quibus constat, quod assertionem suam correctioni Papæ nullatenus submiserunt.
units.tr: Disciple. We have often mentioned the opposing of a heretical Pope, and I ask you to explain one point obscurely stated: who should be regarded as fit to oppose a heretical Pope? Master. The answer is that all Catholics with judgement must in some way be regarded as fit to oppose a heretical Pope. Disciple. That answer is so general that it does not satisfy me. I know that since a heretical Pope is the enemy of all the faithful, all the faithful who are able to oppose him must be considered fit in some way. Yet there must be among them some who are, as it were, the leaders, directors and heads of the others, and it is this that I meant by my question. Master. It is answered that those who excel in virtue, are learned in the sacred writings, are experienced in difficult matters, and have temporal power, are to be considered fit to be the leaders and heads of those who oppose a heretical Pope. For a heretical Pope can be opposed in two ways: physically, by taking up material arms against him if necessary; and spiritually, by refuting him and his errors with authorities and arguments. In the first way, those who have temporal power must be regarded as fit to oppose a heretical Pope. In the second way, those learned in the sacred writings are fit to be, as it were, the leaders and chief opponents of the Pope stained by heretical depravity. Eminence in virtue and suitable experience of affairs seem to be needed by both, so that they may oppose the heretical Pope and his accomplices as is fitting and when it is fitting. Disciple. That answer is still more general than I would like. So I beg you, according to some opinion, to name some special qualifications by which the principal opponents of a heretical Pope ought to excel in order to be considered fit. Master. The special qualifications are innumerable. Disciple. Touch on a few. Master. Some say that, to be considered a fit opponent of a heretical Pope, a man must be firmly fixed in the truths contrary to the errors of the heretical Pope, so that by no reasoning can he be torn away from those truths. Hence, as regards those truths, he must submit his assertions neither to the correction of the Pope, nor to the correction of a general council, nor to the correction of angels from heaven. Rather, as blessed Paul wrote in Gal. 1, saying: "But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach to you anything other than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed." So every fit opponent of a heretical Pope should say in his heart, and declare with his mouth when it is fitting: "Even if I, or the Pope, or a general council, or the whole congregation of Christians, or the whole multitude of angels from heaven, presume to announce, assert or affirm the errors of the heretical Pope, let him be accursed." A fit opponent of the heretical Pope must not submit his assertions, insofar as they are truths contrary to the errors of the heretical Pope, to any correction, because he has received and embraces those truths not as coming from man, but as coming from God, who needs no correction, and he venerates them. And from this (as they say) is refuted the error of some who say that a Christian must submit his faith to the correction of the most blessed Pope. They prove this by the example of blessed Jerome, who had learned his faith in the Church in which he was brought up, and submitted it to the correction and judgement of the most blessed Pope. But these men say this is erroneous, indeed manifestly heretical. They try to prove this by examples and by reason. First, by the example of blessed Paul, who, as we read in Gal. 2, when he rebuked the Pope, namely blessed Peter, did not submit his assertion to the Pope's correction at all; rather he wished the Pope to submit himself to his correction. For he rebuked him so that he might correct the excess he had committed to the prejudice of evangelical truth. Second, they prove this by the example of the Roman clergy, who withdrew from communion with Pope Anastasius II. It is certain of them that they in no way submitted their assertion to the Pope's correction.

units.la: Disc. Forte diceretur istis, quod clerici illi assertionem suam non submiserunt correctioni Papæ haretici, qualis fuit Anastasius secundus: sed submiserunt correctioni futuri summi pontificis catholici. Magist. Hoc sufficit, quod Anastasium secundum reputaverunt haereticum propterhoc, quod assertioni eorum, quam acceperant a sanctis patribus, contradixit. Et propter eandem rationem quicunque futurus Papa postea contradixisset, eundem haereticum reputassent. Quare nullius hominis correctioni volebant assertionem suam submittere. Et ideo dicunt isti, quod Christianus assertione catholica Papæ correctioni non debet submittere. Quod etiam ratione probare nituntur. Nam veritatem infallibilem & immutabilem non debet quis illius correctioni submittere, qui falli potest & errare. Ergo tales veritates nullus debet correctioni Papæ submittere, unde minimam veritatem contemnam in scriptura divina non debet quicunque submittere correctioni Papæ: quia sicut certa discussione non indigent, ita & correctione non indigent. Quare etiam cum omnia asserta in scripturis divinis sint certa, nulla correctione egent. Quare nullius correctioni debent subiici. Cum vero dicitur, quod beatus Hieron. fidem suam, quam didicerat in ecclesia, suppositi correctioni Papæ beatissimi. Respondetur, quod hoc simpliciter est falsum: quod tamen ex verbis Hieron. male intellectis elicitur. Unde vt mente beati Hieron. cunctis aperia, ponantur verba eiusdem. Qui, vt habetur, 24. q. 1. c. hæc est fides, ait: hæc est fides, Papa beatissime, quam in catholica ecclesia didicimus, quamq; semper tenimus, in qua si minus perite aut parum caute forte aliquid positum est, emendari cupimus a te, qui Petri sedem tenes fidem. Si autem haec confessio nostra Apostolatus tui iudicio comprobetur, quicunque me culpare voluerit, se imperitum aut maleuolum vel etiam non catholicum, sed haereticum comprobabit. Ex quibus verbis concludunt quidam, quod beatus Hieron. fidem suam, quam in ecclesia didicerat, suppo-suit correctioni beatissimi Papae. Sed dicunt alii, quod ista verba beati Hieronymi minus bene intelligunt. Non enim intendit Hieronymus fidem suam, quam didicerat in ecclesia, correctioni beatissimi Papae supponere: quia si Papa illi fidei contradixisset, beatus Hieronymus haereticum ipsum reputasset. Didicit enim Hieron. in ecclesia, quod Christus fuit verus Deus & verus homo: cui si Papa obuiasset, pro haeretico pessimo Hieron. eum habuisset. Discip. Quid ergo suppo-suit beatus Hieronymus correctioni Papae? Magist. Respondetur, quod beatus Hieron. absolute nihil suppo-suit correctioni Papae, sed conditionaliter tantum: quod verba eius aperte declarant, cum dicit: in qua si minus perite, aut parum caute forte aliquid positum est, emendari cupimus a te &c. quae verba (sicut patet) sunt conditionalia. Discip. Saltem ex forma verborum apparet, quod Hieron. fidem suam, quam didicerat in ecclesia, conditionaliter suppo-suit correctioni Papae. Quia primo dicit: Haec est fides, Papa beatissime, quam in catholica ecclesia didicimus. Et post adiungit: in qua si minus &c. Magist. Respondetur, quod quamuis absque periculo Hieron. potuerit conditionaliter fidem suam supponere correctioni Papae: quia conditionalis nihil ponit. Unde & haec conditionalis vera est: si in euangelio aliquid falsum asseritur, corrigendum est: tamen beatus Hieron. in verbis praemissis non intendebat fidem suam supponere correctioni Papae: sed expositionem suam circa fidem intendebat conditionaliter supponere correctioni Papae, ut iste sit sensus verborum suorum: id est circa quam scilicet fidem exponendam & explanandam, si minus perite aut parum caute forte aliquid est positum, emendari cupimus a te &c. Quemadmodum si quis Postillator euangelii diceret: hoc est euangelium: in quo si aliquid minus bene dixi, paratus sum corrigere.
units.tr: Disciple. Perhaps it could be replied to these men that those clergy did not submit their assertion to the correction of a heretical Pope such as Anastasius II, but submitted it to the correction of a future Catholic supreme pontiff. Master. It is enough that they regarded Anastasius II as a heretic because he contradicted their assertion, which they had received from the holy Fathers. For the same reason, whoever later became Pope and contradicted them, they would have regarded as a heretic too. Hence they were unwilling to submit their assertion to the correction of any man. And so these men say that a Christian ought not to submit a Catholic assertion to the correction of the Pope. They also try to prove this by reason. For no one should submit an infallible and unchangeable truth to the correction of someone who can be deceived and err. Therefore no one should submit such truths to the correction of the Pope; so whoever should not despise even the smallest truth in the divine Scripture should not submit it to the Pope's correction, since, just as those truths need no careful examination, so they need no correction. Hence, since everything asserted in the divine Scriptures is certain, they need no correction, and so they must be subject to no one's correction. But when it is said that blessed Jerome submitted the faith he had learned in the Church to the correction of the most blessed Pope, the answer is that this is simply false, although it is drawn from words of Jerome that have been wrongly understood. So that the mind of blessed Jerome may be made plain to all, his own words are set down. He says, as we find in 24 q. 1 c. "Haec est fides": "This is the faith, most blessed Pope, which we learned in the Catholic Church and always hold; in which, if anything has been stated rather unskilfully or without enough care, we wish to be corrected by you, who hold the see of Peter. But if this our confession is approved by the judgement of your Apostleship, whoever wishes to blame me will prove himself unskilled, or ill-disposed, or not Catholic but heretical." From these words some conclude that blessed Jerome submitted to the correction of the most blessed Pope the faith he had learned in the Church. But others say that these words of blessed Jerome are poorly understood. For Jerome did not intend to submit to the correction of the most blessed Pope the faith he had learned in the Church, since if the Pope had contradicted that faith, blessed Jerome would have regarded him as a heretic. For Jerome had learned in the Church that Christ was true God and true man; had the Pope opposed this, Jerome would have held him to be a most wicked heretic. Disciple. What then did blessed Jerome submit to the Pope's correction? Master. The answer is that blessed Jerome submitted nothing to the Pope's correction absolutely, but only conditionally; his words make this plain when he says: "in which, if anything has been stated rather unskilfully or without enough care, we wish to be corrected by you," and so on, which words (as is clear) are conditional. Disciple.
