Secunda obiectio est illorum, quæ legë divinâ & doctrinâ sanctorum ignorat, nescientes distinguere fer scienter hæreticum & nescienter hæreticum: quæ tamen distinctio expresse colligitur ex verbis Augustini quæ recitantur, 6. q. 1. c. quarto. Dicunt ergo isti, quod esto quod iste nesciret se a fide catholica discrepare, ex quo tamen vere discrepat a fide recta, & pertinaciter discrepat, sicut ostensum est, supra, est hæreticus reputandus. quemadmodum Ariani, Sabelliani, Nestoriani & alii multi damnati hæretici, licet crediderunt se veram fidem Christi tenere, quia tamen in rei veritate non tenuerunt, & in suis erroribus pertinaces inventi fuerunt, vere fuerunt hæretici: quia quicunque pertinaciter adhæret minimo errori contra scripturam sacram seu doctrinam vniuersalis ecclesiæ est vere hæreticus. qualiter autem aliquis de pertinacia convinci debeat, ex præcedentibus dicunt isti patere. His visis superius tantum sunt pauca dicenda: quam quidem scripturam approbatam bullam nostram munitam. Hic notant aliqui duo. Primum est, quod in editione istius constitutionis cardinalium consensum non habuit, sed hoc videtur nonnullis ad populum parum valere. Secundo notat, quod sicut deductum est, ex hoc non solum de errore, sed etiam de pertinacia manifeste convincitur: quia ex hoc quod dictam constitutionem bulla sua munivit, probatur omnium errorum & singulorum contentorum in ipsa pertinax defensator: & ideo haereticus manifestus, etiam si nulla illarum haeresum unquam fuisset explicite condemnata, vel veritas contraria per Romanum pontificem explicite approbata. [Haereticorum doctrinam praedictam pestiferam] hic damnat doctrinam Romanae ecclesiae: cum doctrina appellantis non sit alia, quam doctrina Romanae ecclesiae, quam nunquam aliam defensavit, nec defendere intendebat.
units.tr: But two objections are raised against the foregoing. The first is that of Brother Geraldus Odo, which runs thus: kings, princes, prelates and a large multitude of other Christians hold him to be the true and catholic Pope; therefore he is not to be reckoned a heretic. The second is that of certain others, who say that he is not a heretic, since he believes that he in no way opposes the Catholic faith. To the first objection, these men reply that the said Brother Geraldus, as a heretic, labours to defend a heretic. For since this Geraldus is a manifest heretic, as shown by the second reason, which proves that the man attacked is a heretic, and as is plainly shown by the third, fifth and ninth, (1) because this Geraldus compels others to defend the attacked man's heretical constitutions obstinately; (2) because he compels others to abjure catholic truth; (3) because he knowingly attacks the determination of the universal Church; (4) because he most bitterly and cruelly persecutes and attacks the defenders of the Catholic faith. Moreover, they adduce several other reasons to prove that this Geraldus should be judged a heretic, some of which are briefly touched on here. The first is this: whoever, in favour of heretics, forbids the proof and reading of Catholic truths and Scriptures is a heretic, or at least a supporter of these heretics. Now this Geraldus does so, since in favour of the man attacked he forbade preaching that the souls of the saints see God in heaven, and at Paris he ordered that the determination of Pope Nicholas III should not be read. Therefore, etc. The second reason is this: whoever attacks a truth already recognised is worse than a heretic who does so in ignorance. But this man attacks the recognised truth about the poverty of Christ and the apostles, which he himself was accustomed to hold; therefore, etc. To this, perhaps, he will reply that he still holds it in his heart, as, it is said, he intimated to a certain Brother through his companion. But this answer does not excuse him at all; rather it accuses him of lying in matters of religious doctrine, and of duplicity and falsehood, as is evident from his own case. The third reason is this: whoever, in favour of heretics, labours to invent and hold new heresies is to be reckoned a heretic. Now this Geraldus, in favour of the man attacked, invents and holds new heresies, some of which are to be set down here. The first is that the Pope, when he enters canonically, cannot err in faith, nor has anyone been found who erred. The second error he holds is that an appeal cannot lawfully be made from the Pope. The third, that the Pope has no superior on earth in a matter of faith. The fourth, that true zeal for the faith never makes a man flee for the cause of the faith, except those who do not receive a stranger as a citizen, nor wish to hear him, but expel him from their city. The fifth, that the poverty of Blessed Francis and of his Rule is not founded on the poverty of Christ. The sixth, that the declarations of the supreme pontiffs upon the Rule of Blessed Francis are a ferment corrupting the first purity of the Rule. The seventh, that the declarations upon the Rule of Blessed Francis are heretical. The eighth, that the Rule of Blessed Francis, understood as declared by the supreme pontiffs, is to be reckoned unobservable. The ninth, that the Friars Minor may possess property in common. This Geraldus, in favour of the man attacked, invents and holds these and other errors which savour of manifest heresy; therefore he is to be judged a heretic. Thus, as they say, a heretic seeks to argue from a heretic. Yet his objection does not hold: first, because, as has been shown, the Church militant can err as to matters of fact; second, because not the whole multitude of Christians regards him as Catholic. Many kings and princes, indeed some prelates too, may perhaps be excused on account of ignorance. As for many rustics and other simple people there is no doubt that they are excused by ignorance. The second objection is that of those who, ignorant of divine law and the teaching of the saints, do not know how to distinguish between a heretic knowingly and a heretic unknowingly; yet that distinction is expressly drawn from the words of Augustine which are quoted in 6 q. 1 c. 4. These men therefore say that, even granting that he did not know he differed from the Catholic faith, since nonetheless he truly differs from the right faith and does so obstinately, as has been shown above, he is to be reckoned a heretic. Just as the Arians, Sabellians, Nestorians and many other condemned heretics, although they believed they held the true faith of Christ, because in the truth of the matter they did not hold it, and were found obstinate in their errors, were truly heretics: for whoever obstinately clings to the smallest error against holy Scripture or the doctrine of the universal Church is truly a heretic. How anyone ought to be convicted of obstinacy, these men say, is plain from what has gone before. Having considered these matters above, only a few things need be said here about that approved writing, fortified by our bull. Some note two things here. The first is that in the publication of that constitution the consent of the cardinals was not obtained, but this seems to some to count for little with the people. Secondly, they note that, as has been deduced, one is convicted by this not only of error but also of manifest obstinacy: for by the fact that he fortified the said constitution with his bull, he is proved to be a stubborn defender of all the errors and of each of the contents of it; and therefore he is a manifest heretic, even if none of those heresies had ever been explicitly condemned, or the contrary truth explicitly approved by the Roman pontiff. Here he condemns the aforesaid pestilent doctrine of heretics: the doctrine of the Roman Church, since the doctrine of the appellant is no other than the doctrine of the Roman Church, which he never defended otherwise, nor intended to defend.

units.la: Hoc Opus nonaginta dierum quamvis cursim & sermone nullatenus falerato, multo tamen copiosi labore, in quo me recitatorem assertionum contrariarum istius impugnati & impugnatorum suorum constituens nonnunquam etiam ipsorum impugnantium diversorum personas assumpsi: qui licet in principalibus assertionibus contra impugnatum conveniant, in quibusdam tamen incidentalibus contrarie opinantur. quare contrarietas, quae potest in praecedentibus inveniri, non uni, sed diversis debet imponi. Sane pro hoc opere ambae partes gratias mihi referre debebant. Nam impugnantium rationes scripturae mandavi, & quantum in me fuit omnibus publicavi, quod ipsos audio toto desiderio cordis affectare. impugnari vero exercitare volui intellectum, & sibi occasionem cogitandi, ac mentem suam circa omnia exprimendi praebere. quod vero de omnibus sentiam in quodam opere super omnes constitutiones istius ab aliis impugnatas, quantum patietur pro tempore isto ingenii penuria mei, divina gratia concedente, explicare curabo. quae autem in praemissis diminute, confuse vel obscure, prolata reperierint, non illis, quorum sententias volui recitare, sed brevitati temporis & ingenii mei tenuitati tanquam disertum lector ascribat. inter vera autem & falsa subtiliter iudicare conetur.
units.tr: This Work of Ninety Days, though written hastily and in no way in polished style, was nonetheless produced with much labour. In it I have set myself up as the reciter of the contrary assertions of this man attacked and of his attackers, and at times I have also assumed the persons of various of the attackers themselves. Although they agree on the principal assertions against the man attacked, they nevertheless differ on certain incidental matters; so the contrariety that can be found in the preceding pages ought to be attributed not to one party but to several. Indeed, both parties ought to thank me for this work. For I have set down the arguments of the attackers in writing, and as far as I could I have made known to all that I listen to them with the whole desire of my heart. But I wished to exercise the understanding against the attacked man, and to give the attackers occasion to think and to express their own opinion on all matters. As to what I myself think about all these things, I shall take care to set it out, as far as my present poverty of talent allows, by God's grace, in a certain work on all the constitutions attacked by others. As for whatever in the foregoing has been set forth meagrely, confusedly or obscurely, let the reader, being learned, ascribe that not to those whose opinions I chose to recite, but to the shortness of time and the slenderness of my ability. Let him try to judge carefully between the true and the false.

units.la: Explicitum est Opus nonaginta dierum, correspondens sexto tractatui Dialogi M. Guilhelmi de Ockam. Sequuntur libelli Fratris Michaelis de Cezena: in quibus gesta eius, de quibus idem Ockam in praedicto loco se tractaturum promiserat, plurima continentur, ut patebit eosdem diligenter lecturis.
units.tr: The Work of Ninety Days is finished; it corresponds to the sixth treatise of the Dialogue of Master William of Ockham. There follow the little books of Brother Michael of Cesena, in which many of his deeds are recorded, which the same Ockham promised in the place mentioned to treat; these will be plain to those who read them carefully.

units.la: MICHAELIS CAESENATIS, MAGISTRI GENERALIS IN ORDINE MINORUM,
units.tr: Michael of Cesena, Minister General of the Order of Friars Minor,

units.la: Anno Domini 1331.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1331.

units.la: TRACTATVS CONTRA ERRORES IOHANNIS XXII. PAPAE SUPER UTILI DOMINIO ECCLESIASTICORUM, & abdicatione bonorum temporalium in perfectione status Monachorum & Clericorum.
units.tr: TREATISE AGAINST THE ERRORS OF POPE JOHN XXII CONCERNING THE USEFUL DOMINION OF ECCLESIASTICS, AND THE RENUNCIATION OF TEMPORAL GOODS IN THE PERFECTION OF THE STATE OF MONKS AND CLERICS.

units.la: Litera recitatoria gestorum Fratris Michaelis de Cezena, edita, ut in fine earum patebit, subscriptione & suffragio Henrici de Thalheim, Francisci de Esculo, & Guilhelmi de Ockam, & aliorum ei adhaerentium, ex Monacho ad Capitulum Minorum in Parpiniano aut Avinione congregandum, Anno Domini M. CCCXXXI.
units.tr: Letter read out from the acts of Brother Michael of Cesena, published, as will appear at its end, with the signature and support of Henry of Thalheim, Francis of Ascoli, William of Ockham, and others adhering to them, sent from the Minister General to the Chapter of the Friars Minor to be gathered at Perpignan or Avignon, in the year of the Lord 1331.

units.la: NIuersis Fratribus Ordinis Minorum in proximo futuro festo Pentecostes in Parpiniano aut Avinione congregandis, Frater Michael Ordinis Fratrum Minorum Generalis Minister & servus, salutem. Literas plurium Magistrorum in sacra pagina aliorumq; notabilium Fratrum Ordinis beati Francisci tam Parisius quam de partibus aliis me noveritis recepisse, per quas me inducere videbantur, ut ad unitatem sanctae Romanae ecclesiae ac dicti Ordinis, a qua me dicebant aversum, accedere festinarem. Quibus literis explicando veritatem facti per ordinem duxi praesentibus sic breviter respondendum, videlicet quod cum anno Domini M.CCC.XXVIII. una cum Fratribus Raymundo Procuratore supradicti Ordinis, Petro de Prato tunc Ministro Provinciae sancti Francisci, & Laurentio tunc Baccalario, in conventu Avinionis essem in domini Iohannis praesentia constitutus, post multa ibidem dicta idem dominus Iohannes dixit & asseruit pluries literam sive determinationem, quam generale capitulum & Fratres dicti Ordinis olim Parisius congregati concorditer fecerant, fore haereticam. In qua litera firmiter asserebant & vniuersis Christi fidelibus intimabant in haec verba, videlicet: Dicimus quod dicere & afferre, quod Christus viam perfectionis ostendens & apostoli eandem viam perfectionis sequentes atque exemplum in alios volentes perfecte viuere derelinquentes nihil iuris, proprietatis & dominii seu iuris proprii in speciali vel in communi habuerunt, non esse haereticum: sed sanum, catholicum & fidele, maxime cum sancta Romana ecclesia catholica, quae a tramite apostolica traditionis numquam deuiasse aut errasse probatur, hoc expresse dicat affirmet & determinet manifeste, extra de verborum significatione, Exiit qui seminat. §. porro, sic inquiens: dicimus quod abdicatio proprietatis omnium rerum tam in speciali quam et in communi propter Deum meritoriae est & sancta, quae Christus viam perfectionis ostendens, versdixit, verbo domini & exemplo firmauit, quam & prius ecclesia fundatores (id est, Apostoli) prout ab ipso sancto (scil. Christo) hauserant in volentes perfecte viuere per doctrinae ac vitae ipsorum alueos deriuarunt. Quae quidem ecclesiae determinatio in 6. libro Decretalium per ipsam catholicam ecclesiam est inserta. Et per decretalem in Viennensi concilio promulgata: & in alio libro sub titulo De verb. sig. per universalem ecclesiam est approbata. Haec verba literae & determinationis, quam dictus Dominus Iohannes dixit & asseruit haereticam. Quae determinatio fuit etiam ab omnibus Magistris & Baccalaris in sacra pagina de Parisiis & de Anglia dicti Ordinis approbata, & vniuersis Christi fidelibus denunciata, sicut de praedicta determinatione capituli patet per literas Generalis Magistri ac omnium Magistrorum & Baccalariorum in sacra pagina in dicto generali capitulo praesentium, & quorundam Ministrorum provincialium dicti ordinis sigillis & subscriptionibus roborataš. Et de approbatione aliorum Magistrorum de Parisiis & de Anglia constat per alias ipsorum sigillis & subscriptionibus communitas. Quod autem dictus Dominus Iohannes pluries dixerit & asseruerit dictam literam sive determinationem generalis Capituli haereticam, patuit. Et patet per literas dictorum patrum Raymundi Petri & Laurentii subscriptione vallatas. Quod etiam reputauerit & firmiter tenuerit, tenet ac docet haereticum esse censendum asserere, Christum & Apostolos non habuisse aliquam iure proprietatis & dominii in speciali vel in communi. Et quod visus rerum visu consumptibilium non potest a proprietate & dominio separari. Et quicunque scienter verbo vel scripto contrarium asseruerit, tanquam rebellis & contumax haberetur, & alia plura contra sacram scripturam, per quae dictam determinationem ecclesiae & praedicti Capituli generalis, ac regulam & religionem sancti Francisci quantum in se est facit haereticam & schismaticam, ac destruit & confundit. Patet aperte per statuta per ipsum dominum Iohannem facta, & per mundum publice diuulgata, quorum primum incipit Ad conditorem: secundum, Cum inter nonnullos; tertium, Quia quorundam.
units.tr: To all the Brothers of the Order of Friars Minor who are to gather at Perpignan or Avignon at the coming feast of Pentecost, Brother Michael, Minister General and servant of the Order of Friars Minor, greetings. You will know that I have received letters from several masters in sacred theology and other notable brothers of the Order of blessed Francis, both from Paris and from other regions, which seemed to urge me to hasten to unity with the holy Roman Church and with the said Order, from which they said I had turned aside. In reply to these letters, and in order to explain the truth of the matter, I have thought it right to answer briefly in the present letter as follows. In the year of the Lord 1328, I was present at Avignon, in the presence of Lord John, together with Brothers Raymond, procurator of the aforesaid Order, Peter of Prato, then Minister of the Province of St Francis, and Lawrence, then bachelor. After many things had been said there, the same Lord John said and asserted several times that the letter or determination which the general chapter and the brothers of the said Order, formerly gathered at Paris, had unanimously made, was heretical. In that letter they firmly asserted, and made known to all the faithful of Christ, these words: We say that to say and assert that Christ, showing the way of perfection, and the apostles following that same way of perfection and wishing to live perfectly, renounced all right, ownership and dominion, whether personal or common, and possessed no right of property, is not heretical, but sound, catholic and faithful; especially since the holy Roman Catholic Church, which is shown never to have turned aside or erred from the path of apostolic tradition, expressly says, affirms and clearly determines this, in the decretal on the meaning of words, Exiit qui seminat, §. Porro, saying thus: We say that the renunciation of the ownership of all things, both personal and common, for the sake of God, is meritorious and holy, which Christ, showing the way of perfection, taught by word and confirmed by example, and which the Church's founders (that is, the Apostles) first drew from that holy one (namely Christ), and passed on to those who wished to live perfectly through the channels of their teaching and life. This determination of the Church has been inserted by the Catholic Church itself into the sixth book of the Decretals, and was promulgated by a decretal at the Council of Vienne, and it has been approved by the universal Church in another book under the title De verborum significatione. These are the words of the letter and determination which the said Lord John said and asserted to be heretical. This determination was also approved by all the masters and bachelors in sacred theology of Paris and of England of the said Order, and was announced to all the faithful of Christ, as appears from the determination of the chapter, by letters of the Minister General and of all the masters and bachelors in sacred theology present at the said general chapter, and strengthened by the seals and signatures of certain provincial ministers of the said Order. The approval of the other masters of Paris and England is established by their own seals and signatures, shared in common. That the said Lord John repeatedly said and asserted that this letter or determination of the general chapter was heretical has become clear, and it is evident from the letters of the said Fathers Raymond, Peter and Lawrence, fortified by their signatures. It is also the case that he considered, firmly held, holds and teaches that it must be judged heretical to assert that Christ and the apostles had no right or ownership, whether personal or common, and that the use of things consumed by use cannot be separated from ownership and dominion. And whoever knowingly asserted the contrary, by word or in writing, would be held as a rebel and obstinate; and he makes many other assertions against Sacred Scripture, by which he makes and declares the said determination of the Church and of the general chapter, and the rule and religion of St Francis, so far as in him lies, heretical and schismatic, and destroys and confounds them. This is plainly shown by the statutes made by the same Lord John and published throughout the world, the first of which begins Ad conditorem, the second Cum inter nonnullos, the third Quia quorundam.

units.la: Et attendens obrem attendens dictam assertionem praefati domini Ioannis manifeste aduersari sanctae catholicae & sanctae matris, ac professioni Ordinis saepe dicti. Et quod per eandem dictam determinationem ecclesiae & Capituli, quantum in se est, haereticabat, ac per consequens omnes illos, qui consenserunt in ipsam haereticos faciebat. Primo in eius praesentia constitutus in facie sibi restiti ad instar Pauli, qui Petro in facie restitit, cum gentes induceret ad iudaizandum & a veritate euangelii recedendum, sicut ipse testatur ad Gal. 2. c. & asserui dictam determinationem & literam Capituli generalis non esse haereticam, sed catholicam, & cum determinatione ecclesiae concordare. Et ipse me in sua curia statuit post dicta resistentiam, & arrestauit. Ego vero ex his, quae dixerat & fecerat contra me, ac ex aliis probabilibus coniecturis manifeste cognoscens, quod ipse Dominus intendebat me compellere ad abnegandum dictam determinationem Capituli generalis in Avinione adhuc existens zelo fidei catholicae & dictae religionis accensus & habito prius magno & maturo consilio, ab ipso domino Ioanne & a dicta eius assertione & arrestatione infra tempus legitimum meo nomine & omnium Fratrum mihi adhaerentium & adhaerere volentium, ac dicti Ordinis secundum quod tradunt canonicae sanctiones, ad sanctam Romanam ecclesiam catholicam & Apostolicam appellaui. Et sic ab ipsius domini Ioannis obedientia & communione recessi ad instar catholicorum & approbatorum virorum de clero Romano, qui ab obedientia & communione Anastasii Papae deuiantis a veritate fidei, quam etiam determinat, recesserunt, prout in canone 9. dist. Anastasius, legitur & habetur. Et ad instar sanctorum Anastasii, Eusebii, & aliorum, qui ab obedientia Liberii Papae: & Hilarii Pictauiensis episcopi, qui ab obedientia Leonis Papae, ex causa simili recesserunt. Et quia ipse Dominus Iohannes me & sequaces meos persequebatur ad mortem, sicut notorium & manifestum extitit; ideo iuxta consilium Christi dicentis: Si vos persecuti fuerint in vna ciuitate, fugite in aliam: ad ciuitatem Pisarum me transtuli. Et ibi vna cum Magistris in sacra pagina, & aliis notabilibus Fratribus dicti Ordinis mihi adhaerentibus dictam appellationem publicaui. Et etiam ab ipso Domino Iohanne de dictis gestis, & statutis per eum: ac ab omnibus aliis per eum factis contra me & mihi adhaerentes & dictum ordinem, iterum ad sanctam Romanam ecclesiam publice & solenniter appellaui: & dictam appellationem eidem Domino Iohanni transmisi. Licet autem secundum iura & canonicas sanctiones ad generale Concilium vniuersalis Ecclesiae, ad quam appellaueram, pertinet de huiusmodi appellatione & crimine haeresis cognoscere & diffinire: quia in his, quae ad fidem catholicam pertinent, Papa subest concilio, sicut patet per illud, quod legitur & notatur in praeallegato cap. Anastasius 9. distinct. & 15. distinctione cap. sicut sancti, in textu & Glossa: accusari & denunciari possit Papa de haeresi: nec possit statuere seu facere aliquid, per quod non valeat accusari. Quia ex tali statuto siue facto possit fides ecclesiae periclitari, sicut patet per illud, quod legitur & notatur 40. dist. cap. si Papa, in textu & Glossa: quod in his maius sit concilium quam Papa, sicut maior est orbis urbe 93. distinct. cap. legimus in textu & Glossa: & quod semel generale concilium, & synodus generalis statuit pro fidei veritate, Papa mutare non possit, cum in his subsit generali concilio 24. q. 1. maiores, & in dicto cap. sicut sancti, & 25. q. 1. cap. contra statuta & c. omne & cap. prima salus, & in eadem causa q. 2. c. si ea destruerem & c. amputato: imo si Papa a fide deuiat, minor est quocunq; catholico, sicut expresse notatur 24. q. 1. c. Achacius in Glossa, & c. Audivimus §. sin autem & §. item cum Dominus in fine. Et ideo per appellationem interpositam ab eo, ego & adhaerentes mihi, efficiemur ab omni potestate & iurisdictione ipsius Domini Iohannis exempti, vt patet per illud, quod legitur & notatur extra de appellatione c. propositum in textu & Glossa. Et is ad quem appellatum est, & non a quo, habet de appellatione cognoscere, extra de appellationibus c. vt debitus & c. cum spiritualis. Nec is, à quo appellatum est, posset in præiudicium appellantis, ipsa appellatione pendente; aliquid innouare, 2. q. 6. c. post appellationem §. appellatione & ff. Nil innouari appellatione pendente l. 1. Et maxime cum causa tangit illum à quo appellatum est, sicut tangebat dictum Dominum Iohannem, & contra eum & eius statuta tanquam hæretica appellaueram. Et in causa propria nullus potest iudicare vel ius sibi dicere, 24. q. 4. cap. inter querelas & q. 5. c. de occidendis & cap. ne quis in causa propria ius sibi dicat, per totum. Nec potest quis esse iudex & pars. 4. q. 4. c. 1. Tamen idem Dominus Iohannes recepta dicta appellatione per me interposita nominibus supradictis respondendo ad ipsam appellationem & diffiniendo & determinando de ipsa & contentis in ea pro libro voluntatis omni lege contempta penitus & subuersa composuit, fecit & publice promulgauit vnum statutum siue libellum, cuius initium est: Quia vir reprobus Michael de Cæsena. In quo libello siue statuto & priores errores pertinaciter defendit, & manifestius explicat, & alios errores ad primos accumulat, per quos quod est fidei, quod religionis, & quod morum destruit & confundit. Nam in eo inter cetera dogmatizat aperte infra scriptos errores.
units.tr: Considering this assertion of the aforesaid Lord John to be manifestly opposed to the holy Catholic Church, our holy mother, and to the profession of the Order often mentioned, and that by the same determination of the Church and of the Chapter, so far as in him lay, he made them heretical, and consequently made heretics of all those who had consented to it, I first, present in his presence, resisted him to his face, after the manner of Paul, who withstood Peter to his face when he led the Gentiles to Judaize and to depart from the truth of the gospel, as he himself testifies (Gal. 2), and I asserted that the said determination and the letter of the general chapter were not heretical, but catholic, and agreed with the determination of the Church. After this resistance, he placed me under arrest in his court. I, however, clearly recognising from what he had said and done against me, and from other probable conjectures, that the Lord himself intended to compel me to renounce the said determination of the general chapter, while I was still at Avignon, zealous for the Catholic faith and for the said religion, and after taking great and mature counsel beforehand, I appealed, in my name and in the names of all the brothers who adhered to me or wished to adhere, and of the said Order, according to what the canonical sanctions prescribe, from Lord John himself, from his assertion and arrest, within the legitimate time, to the holy Roman Catholic and Apostolic Church. Thus I withdrew from the obedience and communion of Lord John, in the manner of Catholics and approved men of the Roman clergy, who withdrew from the obedience and communion of Pope Anastasius, who had turned aside from the truth of the faith, which he also determined otherwise, as is read and found in Dist. 9, canon Anastasius. And in the manner of the saints Anastasius, Eusebius and others who withdrew from the obedience of Pope Liberius, and of Hilary, bishop of Poitiers, who withdrew from the obedience of Pope Leo, for a similar cause. And because the same Lord John persecuted me and my followers to death, as has become notorious and manifest, therefore, according to the counsel of Christ saying, If they persecute you in one city, flee into another, I transferred myself to the city of Pisa. There, together with masters in sacred theology and other notable brothers of the said Order adhering to me, I publicly proclaimed the said appeal. And again, from the same Lord John, and from the acts and statutes made by him, and from all the other things done by him against me and those adhering to me and the said Order, I appealed publicly and solemnly to the holy Roman Church, and I sent the said appeal to the same Lord John. Although, however, according to the laws and canonical sanctions, it belongs to a general council of the universal Church, to which I had appealed, to hear and decide such an appeal and the crime of heresy, because in matters that pertain to the Catholic faith the Pope is subject to a council, as is shown by what is read and noted in the aforesaid chapter Anastasius, Dist. 9, and in Dist. 15, chapter Sicut sancti, in the text and gloss: the Pope may be accused and denounced of heresy, nor can he make or enact anything by which he cannot be accused; because by such a statute or act the faith of the Church could be endangered, as is shown by what is read and noted in Dist. 40, chapter Si Papa, in the text and gloss: that in these matters a council is greater than the Pope, as the world is greater than the city (Dist. 93, chapter Legimus, in the text and gloss); and that the Pope cannot change what a general council or general synod has once decided for the truth of the faith, since in these matters he is subject to a general council (24 q. 1, Maiores, and in the said chapter Sicut sancti; 25 q. 1, chapters Contra statuta, Omne, and Prima salus; and in the same cause, q. 2, chapters Si ea destruerem and Amputato); indeed, if the Pope deviates from the faith, he is less than any Catholic, as is expressly noted in 24 q. 1, chapter Achacius, in the gloss, and chapter Audivimus, §. Sin autem, and §. Item cum Dominus at the end. Therefore, by the appeal lodged against him, I and those adhering to me are made free from all the power and jurisdiction of the same Lord John, as is shown by what is read and noted in the Decretals on appeals, chapter Propositum, in the text and gloss. And he to whom the appeal is made, and not he from whom it is made, has the right to hear the appeal (Decretals on appeals, chapters Ut debitus and Cum spiritualis). Nor may he from whom the appeal is made, while the appeal is pending, make any innovation to the prejudice of the appellant (2 q. 6, chapter Post appellationem, §. Appellatione; and Digest, Nil innovari appellatione pendente, l. 1), especially since the matter touches him from whom the appeal is made, as it touched the said Lord John, against whom and against whose statutes I had appealed as heretical. And in a case concerning himself no one may judge or pronounce law for himself (24 q. 4, chapter Inter querelas; q. 5, chapter De occidendis; and chapter Ne quis in causa propria ius sibi dicat, throughout). Nor can anyone be both judge and party (4 q. 4, chapter 1). Nevertheless, the same Lord John, having received the said appeal lodged by me in the above names, responding to the appeal itself and deciding and determining concerning it and the matters contained in it, at his own pleasure, setting aside and wholly subverting all law, composed, made and publicly promulgated a single statute or libel, which begins: Quia vir reprobus Michael de Cæsena. In this libel or statute he stubbornly defends the earlier errors, explains them more plainly, and piles other errors on top of the first ones, by which he destroys and confounds what belongs to the faith, to religion, and to morals. For in it, among other things, he openly teaches the following errors.

units.la: Primus est, quod Christus in quantum homo maior ab instanti suæ conceptionis, habuit ex Dei datione vniuersale dominium rerum omnium temporalium, sicut verus rex & Dominus in temporalibus.
units.tr: The first is that Christ, as man, from the moment of his conception was, by God's gift, the holder of universal dominion over all temporal things, as a true king and lord in temporal matters.

units.la: Secundus est, quod Christus in quantum homo maior per successum temporis acquisiuit sibi & habuit in speciali dominium proprium & immediatum vestimentorum, alimentorum, calciamentorum & loculorum, partim collatione fidelium, partim per emptionem.
units.tr: The second is that Christ, as man, over the course of time acquired for himself and held in particular, as his own and immediately, dominion over clothing, food, shoes and purse, partly by the gifts of the faithful and partly by purchase.

units.la: Tertius, quod Christus nunquam consuluit Apostolis, nec suis discipulis abdicationem proprietatis & dominii omnium rerum temporalium.
units.tr: The third is that Christ never counselled the Apostles or his disciples to renounce ownership and dominion of all temporal things.

units.la: Quartus quod Christus non dedit aliam legem viuendi Apostolis, quam discipulis, per discipulos intelligens quoscunq; fideles Christianos, sicut manifeste patet per eius exempla, in quibus inter discipulos numerat Ioseph ab Arimathia, qui erat diues in speciali, & Martham & Mariam, quæ secundum ipsum erant dominæ castri: & Lazarum ac Simonem Leprosum, & Dorcam, qui secundum eum habebant dominium temporalium in speciali.
units.tr: The fourth is that Christ did not give the Apostles a different rule of life from the disciples, understanding by disciples all faithful Christians, as is plain from his examples, in which he counts among the disciples Joseph of Arimathea, who was rich in particular, and Martha and Mary, who according to him were ladies of a castle, and Lazarus, Simon the Leper, and Dorcas, who according to him held temporal dominion in particular.

units.la: Quintus est, quod Christus non præcepit Apostolis simpliciter & absolute, ne possiderent aurum & argentum & pecuniam in zonis, & ne portarent calciamenta, sed solum pro tempore viæ, quando ibant ad prædicandum, & post reditum à prædicatione poterant talia libere habere & portare.
units.tr: The fifth is that Christ did not command the Apostles simply and absolutely not to possess gold, silver or money in their belts, nor to wear shoes, but only for the time of the journey when they went out to preach; after returning from preaching they could freely have and carry such things.

units.la: Sextus, quod Apostoli in speciali & sigillatim proprietatem & dominium vestimentorum, alimentorum, caligarum & gladiorum habuerunt etiam post missionem Spiritus sancti in eos factam. Et quod illa verba: Ecce nos reliquimus omnia &c. non sunt intelligenda quo ad abdicationem proprietatis & dominii, sed quo ad affectionem & curam.
units.tr: The sixth is that the Apostles, in particular and individually, had proprietorship and dominion over clothing, food, hose and swords, even after the Holy Spirit had been sent upon them. And those words, "Behold, we have left all things," etc., are not to be understood as referring to the renunciation of ownership and dominion, but to affection and care.

units.la: Septimus, quod Apostoli potuerunt habere in speciali & sigillatim dominia castrorum & villarum ac quorumcunque aliorum bonorum temporalium; quia, vt dicit, non reperitur, quod Christus aliam legem viuendi dederit Apostolis, quam quibuscunque aliis discipulis, vt dictum est.
units.tr: The seventh is that the Apostles could have in particular and individually dominion over castles, villages and any other temporal goods; because, he says, it is not found that Christ gave the Apostles a different rule of life from any other disciples, as has been said.

units.la: Octauus, quod Apostoli stante euangelica perfectione potuerunt habere in communi bona immobilia, vt agros & prædia; & quod talia in Iudæa non retinuerint, non fuit nisi ex eo quod præuidebant in spiritu se transituroc ad gentes.
units.tr: The eighth is that the Apostles, while evangelical perfection remained, could have immovable goods, such as fields and estates, in common; and that they did not keep such things in Judea was only because they foresaw in the Spirit that they would pass over to the Gentiles.

units.la: Nonus est, quod Apostoli nunquam emiserunt votum abdicationis proprietatis & dominii rerum temporalium.
units.tr: The ninth is that the Apostles never made a vow to renounce ownership and dominion of temporal things.

units.la: Decimus est, quod Apostoli potuerunt licite pro rebus temporalibus, sicut pro rebus propriis in iudicio contendere & litigare.
units.tr: The tenth is that the Apostles could lawfully contend and litigate in court over temporal things, just as over their own property.

units.la: Undecimus est, quod in prima multitudine credentium bona eis necessaria post distributionem bonorum ipsorum inter eos factam non erant ipsis communia quo ad dominium, sed solum ante distributionem: sed post ipsam distributionem quilibet efficiebatur in speciali proprietarius & Dominus portionis sibi assignatæ.
units.tr: The eleventh is that in the first multitude of believers, the goods necessary to them after the distribution of goods among them were not common to them as to dominion, but only before the distribution; after the distribution, each became the proprietor and lord in particular of the portion assigned to him.

units.la: Duodecimus est, quod votum religiosorum absque proprio viuere profitentium non extendit se ad illa, quibus necessario eget vita humana.
units.tr: The twelfth is that the vow of religious who profess to live without property does not extend to those things which human life necessarily requires.

units.la: Insuper ibidem dogmatizat quod illa benedictio data primis parentibus, quæ fuit: Crescite & multiplicamini &c. fuit data Adæ soli ante formationem Euæ, & plura alia erronea. Quem libellum respondionis, qui, vt dictum est: incipit: Quia vir reprobus, cum fui in ciuitate Mauacensi recepi. Et ipso examinato, visisque dictis erroribus contentis in eo, ab ipso & à contentis dogmatizatis in eo, ad sanctam Romanam ecclesiam publice & solenniter appellaui; & tam in ipsa appellatione, quam in aliis supradictis appellationibus me & mihi adhærentes & dicta nostra suppositi correctioni & emendationi ac protectioni & defensioni sanctæ Romanæ ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Moreover, in the same place he teaches that the blessing given to our first parents, which was, "Increase and multiply," etc., was given to Adam alone before the forming of Eve, and many other erroneous things. I received that book of reply, which, as said, begins "Because the reprobate man," in the city of Mauacensis. Having examined it and seen the errors contained in it, which he taught in it and from it, I appealed publicly and solemnly to the holy Roman Church, both from him and from the teachings in it; and in that appeal, as in the other appeals mentioned above, I placed myself, my adherents and our statements under the correction, emendation, protection and defence of the holy Roman Church.

units.la: Et sum semper protestatus in ipsis appellationibus me illam fidem tenere & seruare velle perpetuo, quam tenet & seruat sancta Romana ecclesia, quæ est omnium ecclesiarum mater & magistra, sicut constat per publica instrumenta confecta de appellationibus ante dictis.
units.tr: And in these appeals I have always declared that I wish to hold and keep perpetually that faith which the holy Roman Church holds and keeps, the mother and teacher of all churches, as is evident from the public instruments drawn up concerning the appeals mentioned above.

units.la: Cum igitur manifestum sit, quod ille qui ad sanctam matrem ecclesiam appellat, & ad eius auxilium refugit, ac eius iudicium instanter postulat & requirit, ac se eius correctioni, emendationi & iudicio totaliter subiicit: & regula beati Francisci expresse dicat, quod Fratres semper sint subditi & subiecti pedibus sanctæ Romanæ ecclesiæ, stabiles in catholica fide, paupertatem & humilitatem & sanctum euangelium domini nostri Iesu Christi, quod firmiter promiserunt, obseruent. Et ego, vt ex prædictis patet aperte, pro fide catholica, paupertate & euangelio, quod promisi firmiter obseruandum & defendendum, appellauerim & subiecerim me & dictum Ordinem correctioni, emendationi, protectioni & defensioni ipsius sanctæ Romanæ ecclesiæ: Cogor non modicum admirari, quomodo aut qua fronte aliqui dicunt me ab vnitate ecclesiæ & Ordinis recessisse. Et suadent, quod ad vnitatem & gremium sanctæ matris ecclesiæ, & dicti ordinis redeam vel accedam: cum ab ipsa vnitate ecclesiæ & dicti ordinis nunquam recesserim, nec recedere intendam; sed in vnitate ipsius sanctæ Romanæ ecclesiæ & ordinis dictam regulam firmiter tenentis & obseruantis, volo & intendo Domino assistente stare & perpetuo permanere. Nec obstat, quod aliqui dicere perhibentur, quod saltem ab vnitate dicti ordinis videor recessisse, ex eo quod congregatio Fratrum, quæ facta fuit Parisiis, anno Domini millesimo 300. 28. die mensis Iunii, me ab officio ministerii depositi & amouit ex auctoritate & potestate eis data, vt asserunt, per Capitulum regulæ beati Francisci, in quo dicitur in hæc verba: Et si aliquo tempore apparet vniuersitatis Ministrorum Prouincialium & Custodum prædictum Ministrum non esse sufficientem ad seruitium & communem vtilitatem Fratrum, teneantur prædicti Fratres, quibus electio data est, alium eligere in Custodem: quia hs nõ obstantibus gero me pro Generali Ministro. Et vere non obstat: quia constat, quod dictus dominus Iohannes post & contra primam appellationem me de facto absoluit, siue deposuit à dicto officio: quod iuris non possit, vt superius est probatum. Et quasi dictus Ordo Ministro Generali careret, fecit dominum Bertrandum de Turre Vicarium generalem dicti Ordinis. Et ipse Dominus Bertrandus auctoritate talis vicariatus mutauit terminum trienii secundum regulam constitutam per Capitulum generale Bononiæ celebratum: ac statuit, quod Fratres congregarentur Parisiis in feste Pentecostes tunc proxime futuro: & Ministros secundum formam regulæ & generalis concilii Viennensis per electionem institutos amouit pro maiori parte: & alios instituit non per electionem, sed motu proprio: & mandauit quod congregarentur Parisiis ad hunc effectum, vt dicto Ordini tanquam carenti Ministro per dictam depositionem siue amotionem de me factam prouiderent de Generali ministro. Et sic huiusmodi tales dicti Ministri cum quibusdam aliis in dicto festo Pentecostes se congregauerunt Parisiis; Et instrumentum publicum fecerunt fieri, in quo dicitur sic: Prædicti Ministri & Custodes asserentes Fratrem Michaelem fuisse iuste depositum, & alias pœnas incurrisse: nihilominus tamen ex abundanti & ad cautelam, & ad eius malitiam conuincendam, qua audet se erigere, vt abutatur dicto officio contra voluntatem & præceptum dicti domini Papæ, & etiam contra totius Ordinis voluntatem, qui eum reputat iuste depositum à prædicto domino nostro Papa, auctoritate regulæ & potestate ex eorum regula eis data ipsum deposuerunt, & amouerunt quantum in eis est ab officio memorato. Hæc verba dicti instrumenti siue depositionis prædictæ. Ex quibus clare patet, quod dictum Capitulum regulæ in dicto casu non vendicat sibi locum. Tum quia verba regulæ prædictæ loquuntur, quando Ministri veri & legitimi Ministrum generalem, quem habere se & reputant & habent pro vero Generali Ministro, vident insufficientem, ac in dicto casu dicti dicentes se Ministros expresse asseruerunt; quod habebant me pro deposito & amoto per ipsum dominum Iohannem. Vnde secundum eos non deposuerunt me tanquam insufficientem, sicut dictum Capitulum regulæ dicit, nec ad hoc se congregauerunt Parisiis: sed solum ad hunc effectum, vt elegerent alium Generalem Ministrum in locum mei secundum eos iuste depositi & amoti. Et secundum mandatum eis datum per ipsum dictum Bertrandum, & ab ipsis sponte assumptum, & ad cuius mandati executionem se congregauerunt, non habebant potestatem videndi vtrum forem sufficiens ad seruitium & communem vtilitatem Fratrum, sicut dicta regula requirit, sed habito me pro deposito & amoto alium debebant eligere in Generalem Ministrum. Et ideo dictum Capitulum regulæ in hoc casu sibi locum nullatenus vendicauit. Tum quia depositio & amotio per dominum Iohannem de me facta: & creatio dicti domini Bertrandi in Vicarium dicti Ordinis fuerunt factæ post & contra appellationem per me interpositam, & nullius fuerunt momenti, vt superius est probatum. Et ideo amotio antiquorum Ministrorum Prouincialium & creatio nouorum Ministrorum facta per dictum dominum Bertrandum, nullius fuit momenti, ex eo quod non erat Vicarius legitime institutus. Et ex eo, quod ipsa creatio fuit facta contra formam generalis concilii Viennensis, quod statuit Ministros Prouinciales debere per electionem Prouincialis Capituli institui, & decreuit quicquid contra fieret, irritum sit & inane. Vnde cum non fuerunt Ministri legitimi nec legitime instituti, dictum Capitulum regulæ, quod loquitur de veris & legitimis Ministris, qui habent videre vtrum existens Minister sit sufficiens, nullatenus vendicat sibi locum. Tum quia secundum iura & canonicas sanctiones, vbi principale non tenuit, scil. creatio Vicarii, mutatio termini triennii, & mandatum factum per dominum Bertrandum, quod se congregarent & congregatio ipsius auctoritate & mandato facta, per consequens quicquid secutum est ex ipsis vel ob ipla nullius fuit roboris vel momenti, vt iura dicunt. Tum ex aliis rationibus & allegationibus super his factis, & per diuersas partes Ordinis missis, quæ hic breuitatis causa omittuntur.
units.tr: Since it is plain that whoever appeals to holy mother Church and flees to her aid, and urgently asks and demands her judgment, and wholly submits himself to her correction, emendation and judgment; and since the rule of blessed Francis expressly says that the Brothers should always be subject and submissive at the feet of the holy Roman Church, steadfast in the Catholic faith, and should observe poverty, humility and the holy gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ, which they firmly promised; and since I, as is clearly evident from the above, for the sake of the Catholic faith, poverty and the gospel, which I promised firmly to observe and defend, have appealed and submitted myself and the said Order to the correction, emendation, protection and defence of that same holy Roman Church: I am compelled to marvel not a little how, or with what face, some say that I have withdrawn from the unity of the Church and of the Order. And they urge me to return and come back to the unity and bosom of holy mother Church and of the said Order; though I have never withdrawn from the unity of the Church or of the Order, nor do I intend to withdraw. Rather, in the unity of that holy Roman Church and of the Order which firmly holds and observes the said rule, I wish and intend, with the Lord assisting, to stand and remain forever. Nor does it count against me that some are said to claim that I seem at least to have withdrawn from the unity of the said Order, because the assembly of the Brothers held at Paris in the year of the Lord 1300, on the 28th day of June, deposed and removed me from the office of minister, by the authority and power which, they assert, were given to them by the chapter of the rule of blessed Francis, in which it is said in these words: And if at any time it appears to the whole body of the Provincial Ministers and Custodians that the said Minister is not sufficient for the service and common benefit of the Brothers, the said Brothers to whom the election has been given shall be bound to choose another as Custodian. Notwithstanding these things, I still hold myself to be Minister General. And indeed it does not count against me, because it is clear that the said lord John, after and against my first appeal, absolved me de facto from that office, or deposed me, which he could not lawfully do, as has been proved above. And as if the said Order lacked a Minister General, he made Lord Bertrand de Turre vicar general of the said Order. And this Lord Bertrand, by the authority of such a vicariate, changed the three-year term according to the rule established by the general chapter celebrated at Bologna; he decreed that the Brothers should gather at Paris at the next feast of Pentecost; and he removed most of the Ministers who had been instituted by election according to the form of the rule and of the general council of Vienne, and appointed others not by election but on his own motion; and he ordered them to gather at Paris for this purpose, so that they might provide the Order, as lacking a minister because of the said deposition or removal made of me, with a Minister General. And so these so-called Ministers, together with some others, gathered at Paris at that feast of Pentecost; and they had a public instrument made, in which it is said as follows: The aforesaid Ministers and Custodians, asserting that Brother Michael was justly deposed and had incurred other penalties, nevertheless, out of abundance and as a precaution, and to convict his malice, by which he dares to set himself up to abuse the said office against the will and command of the said lord Pope, and also against the will of the whole Order, which regards him as justly deposed by our said lord Pope, by the authority of the rule and the power given to them by their rule, have deposed and removed him, as far as in them lies, from the aforesaid office. These are the words of the said instrument or of that deposition. From these it is clearly evident that the said chapter of the rule does not claim a place in this case. For, first, the words of that rule speak of when true and lawful Ministers see that their Minister General, whom they themselves regard and hold as the true Minister General, is insufficient; but in this case the said men who called themselves Ministers expressly asserted that they held me to have been deposed and removed by the said lord John. Hence, according to them, they did not depose me as insufficient, as the said chapter of the rule says, nor did they gather at Paris for that purpose, but only in order to elect another Minister General in my place, as one justly deposed and removed according to them. And according to the mandate given to them by the said Bertrand, which they undertook of their own accord, and in execution of which they gathered, they did not have the power to see whether I was sufficient for the service and common benefit of the Brothers, as the said rule requires; rather, regarding me as deposed and removed, they were to elect another as Minister General. And therefore the said chapter of the rule in this case by no means claims a place for itself. Second, because the deposition and removal of me by Lord John, and the creation of the said Lord Bertrand as vicar of the said Order, were made after and against the appeal lodged by me, and were of no force, as has been proved above. And therefore the removal of the former Provincial Ministers and the creation of new Ministers made by the said Lord Bertrand was of no force, since he was not a lawfully instituted vicar. And because that creation was made against the form of the general council of Vienne, which established that Provincial Ministers must be instituted by election of the Provincial Chapter, and decreed that whatever was done contrary to this should be void and null. Hence, since they were neither lawful Ministers nor lawfully instituted, the said chapter of the rule, which speaks of true and lawful Ministers who have the power to see whether the existing Minister is sufficient, by no means claims a place for itself. Third, because according to laws and canonical sanctions, where the principal thing does not hold, namely the creation of the vicar, the change of the three-year term, and the mandate issued by Lord Bertrand that they should gather, and the gathering made by his authority and mandate, then consequently whatever followed from them or because of them was of no strength or force, as the laws say. Fourth, from other reasons and allegations concerning these matters, which have been sent by various parts of the Order, and which are omitted here for the sake of brevity.

units.la: Si vero potestis ostendere, quod prædicta per me superius allegata à veritate deuient, & quod prædicta statuta & gesta per præfatum dominum Iohannem cum veritate Euangelii & dictæ regulæ beati Francisci stare possit, quodque ipsi veritati nullatenus aduersantur, etiam veritatem regulæ quam voluistis, vultis tenere & inuiolabiliter obseruare, offero me paratum renunciare omnibus appellationibus per me interpositis ac officio Generalis Ministerii mihi impositο, quod (nouit Deus) inuite exerceo, nisi inquantum cogit necessitas defensionis fidei catholicæ & Ordinis sæpe dicti. Quod si non potestis, aut non vultis facere supradicta, saltem stantes & repugnantes pro ipsa veritate, & opponentes se murum pro domo Israel persequi desistatis. Licet autem indebite me putetis auersum, tamen mei officii non immemor suadeo & exhortor, ne regulam euangelicam cœlitus datam, per quam decenter velut specifice distincti estis, mutetis in aliquo: nec mutationi, quæ per aliquem fieri vellet, præbeatis assensum: quia quicunque hanc regulam secuti fuerint, pax super illos. Qui vero illam mutauerint, vel eius mutationi consenserint, Esaiæ vaticinio, vbi dicitur, Ve filii desertores &c. se nouerint subiacere. Ex parte Fratris Michaelis Generalis Ministri dicti Ordinis licet inuiti, de voluntate & assensu Fratrum Henrici de Thalhelm, Francisci de Esculo, Guilhelmi de Ockam in sacra pagina Magistrorum: Et Fratris Bonegratiæ, & aliorum Fratrum eis adhærentium. Data in Monacho in festo sancti Marci Euangelistæ. Anno Domini 1331. In quorum omnium testimonium, Ego dictus Frater Michael, una cum dictis Magistro Henrico, Francisco & Guilhelmo, sigilla imposuimus.
units.tr: But if you can show that the things I have alleged above depart from the truth, and that the aforesaid statutes and acts of the said Lord John can agree with the truth of the Gospel and of the said rule of blessed Francis, and in no way oppose that truth, then, if you wish to keep and inviolably observe the true rule you desired, I offer myself ready to renounce all appeals made by me and the office of General Minister imposed on me, which (God knows) I exercise unwillingly, except insofar as the necessity of defending the Catholic faith and of the aforesaid Order compels me. But if you cannot or will not do these things, at least stand and resist for that truth, and cease to persecute, opposing yourselves as a wall for the house of Israel. Although you may think I have been wrongly turned away, nevertheless, mindful of my office, I advise and exhort you not to change in any respect the evangelical rule given from heaven, by which you are becomingly and, as it were, specifically distinguished; nor should you give your assent to any change that someone would wish to make. For whoever have followed this rule, peace be upon them; but whoever have changed it, or consented to its change, let them know that they are subject to the prophecy of Isaiah, where it is said, "Woe to the rebellious sons," etc. Given on behalf of Brother Michael, General Minister of the said Order, though unwilling, with the consent and agreement of Brothers Henry of Thalheim, Francis of Ascoli, and William of Ockham, masters in sacred theology, and of Brother Bonagratia and the other brothers adhering to them. Given at Munich on the feast of Saint Mark the Evangelist, in the year of the Lord 1331. In witness of all of which, I, the said Brother Michael, together with the said Masters Henry, Francis and William, have affixed our seals.

units.la: LITTERÆ AD OMNES FRATRES ORDINIS MINORUM. IN QVIBVS OSTENDITVR, QVOMODO PER DVO STATVTA IOANNES PAPA 22. confirmauit & approbauit Regulam Fratrum Minorum esse Catholicam & Sanctam. Postea in reprobum sensum datus per quatuor Statuta hæretica damnauit eam. Quorum primum incipit Ad conditorem canonum. Secun- dum, Cum inter nonnullos. Tertium, Quia quorundam. Quartum, Quia vir reprobus, &c.
units.tr: LETTERS TO ALL THE BRETHREN OF THE ORDER OF MINORS, IN WHICH IT IS SHOWN HOW JOHN XXII, BY TWO DECREES, CONFIRMED AND APPROVED THE RULE OF THE FRIARS MINOR AS CATHOLIC AND HOLY; AND AFTERWARDS, BEING TURNED TO A REPROBATE SENSE, CONDEMNED IT BY FOUR HERETICAL DECREES. The first of these begins Ad conditorem canonum. The second, Cum inter nonnullos. The third, Quia quorundam. The fourth, Quia vir reprobus, etc.

units.la: NIuersis & singulis Ministris, Custodibus, Gardianis, Vicariis, cæterisq; Fratribus Ordinis Minorum fidem catholicam, sanctum euangelium & Regulam, quam voluerunt, firmiter tenentibus, & volentibus obseruare, Frater Michael eiusdem Ordinis Generalis Minister & seruus salutem & pacem in Domino sempiternam. Christianæ fidei fundamentum & fundator Dominus noster Iesus Christus, qui apparuit mundo, vt Diaboli dissolueret opera, in ecclesia sua catholica & Apostolica, duo genera saluandorum hominum stabiliuit. Primum eorum, qui per fidem rectam & mandatorum legis obseruantiam niituntur ad æternam beatitudinem peruenire. De quo in euangelio dicitur, Si vis ad vitam ingredi, serua mandata Dei. Secundum illorum, qui cupientes etiam in consiliis euangelicis vitam ipsius Domini nostri Iesu Christi, & Apostolorum eius insequi perfecte, quæ est sanctum euangelium obseruare viuendo in obedientia, sine proprio, & in castitate promittunt: de quo in ipso Euangelio dicit. Si vis perfectus esse vade & vende omnia quæ habes: & da pauperibus & veni, sequere me. Et sanctus Petrus in persona omnium Apostolorum insinuans se & Apostolos dictum perfectionis mandatum implesse respondit: Ecce nos reliquimus omnia & secuti sumus te. Quid ergo erit nobis? Quæ scilicet consilia sancta Romana & vniuersalis ecclesia in sacris canonibus, & præcipue extra de statu monachorum c. Cum ad monasterium, & 12. q. 1. c. dilectissimi & c. duo sunt & c. quia sua & c. scimus. & c. nolo & c. non dicatis & extra de verbo. signi. c. Exiit. Et in Regulis sanctorum Augustini, Benedicti & Francisci per vniuersalem ecclesiam approbatis & confirmatis, determinatis & diffinitis fore cuilibet religioni perfecte imitanti vitam Christi & Apostolorum annexam huic doctrinæ euangelicæ & sanctæ Romanæ ecclesiæ quicunq; contradictor extiterit, siue eam non crediderit, & fideliter confessus fuerit, absque dubio in æternum peribit, & ipso facto est excommunicatus atq; damnatus tanquam hæreticus per sententiam sacri concilii generalis vniuersalis ecclesiæ catholicæ, quia firmiter non credit, confitetur & tenet doctrinam, quam Christus viam vitæ demonstrando humano generi tribuit salutarem, quam sancta Romana ecclesia firmiter credit & fideliter confitetur, sicut patet in generali concilio vniuersalis ecclesiæ posito extra de summa trinitate & fide catholica cap. firmiter §. hoc sancta trinitas, & lib. 5. in eodem concilio generali in decretali quæ est pars dicti concilii generalis, posita sub titulo de haereticis, dicitur: Excommunicamus itaq; & anathematizamus omnem haeresim extollentem se aduersus hanc sanctam orthodoxam & catholicam fidem, quam superius expositimus, condemnantes vniuersos haereticos quibuscunque nominibus censeantur. Cum certum sit, quod illa salutaris doctrina & via vitæ, quam Christus humano generi tribuit & demonstrauit, quæ est firmiter credenda & fideliter confitenda, de qua dicitur in dicto §. Hæc sancta trinitas, est sacra doctrina in sancto euangelio à CHRISTO docta, & in noua testamento descripta, vt probatur 24. distinctione cap. qui episcopus. De qua non est licitum dubitare vel disceptare, vtrum verum sit & sanctum, quicquid in eá constitverit esse scriptum : sed quicquid in ea reperitur, incunctanter credendum est, vt dicitur 9 distinct. cap. 1. & c. quu nesciat. Et quæ in ipsam sacram doctrinam sancti Euangelii siue noui & veteris testamenti impingit in articulos fidei; Credo in Deum patrem : Credo in Iesum Christum filium eius: Credo in Spiritum sanctum, trinum & vnum Deum verum, à quo ipsa doctrina prolata est. Et in articulum; Vnam sanctam catholicam & apostolicam ecclesiam, quæ dictam doctrinam euangelii & dictorum sanctorum regulas approbauit, euidenter impingit. Et quicunque aliter euangelizat siue docet, quam euangelizatum est, anathema est, & à Deo & eius sancta catholica & apostolica ecclesia separatus, Apostolo testante ad Gal. 1. & dicente: licet nos aut angelus de cælo euangelizet vobis praterquam quod euangelizauimus vobis, anathema sit. Et quicunq; sacram scripturam aliter intelligit, quam sensus Spiritus sancti, à quo prolata est, flagitat, hæreticus est censendus, licet corpore ab ecclesia non recesserit, vt dicitur 24. q. 3. cap. hæref. Vnde & Papa contra doctrinam fidei catholicæ docens, siue statuens in sententiam excommunicationis, damnationis, & priuationis incidit ipso facto, & minor est quocunque catholico, sicut habetur & notatur 24. q. 1. in principio & in Glossa. Et in cap. Athacius, in textu & Gloss. & in §. Item cum Dominus & § si autem & §. his auctoritatibus & c. dicimus & 19. distinct. §. hoc autem & §. quia vero, in cap. Anastasius, in textu & Gloss. Et credentes, fautores & defensores eiusdem sunt ipso iure excommunicati & infames effecti: nec possunt aliquod officium legitimum exercere: nec ex testamento alterius aliquid capere, nec eligi, nec eligere ad officium vel dignitatem: nec ad testimonium aliquod nec ad hæreditatis alicuius successionem sunt aliquatenus admittendi: vt probatur in dicto cap. excommunicamus itaque §. credentes, & in sequenti c. excommunicamus & anathematizamus. Verum quia Saluator prædicit in euangelio circa finem seculi pseudoChristos & pseudoProphetas surgere, & multos seducere, & fideles suos in mundo multas habituros pressuras, sed tamen portas inferi (id est, hæreses) non præualituras. Proinde, vt ait Apostolus 1. ad Cor. 10. Oportet hæreses esse, vt qui probati fuerint, manifesti fiant. Oportet etiam vere catholicos & fideles cum propheta ex aduerso consurgere, & murum opponere pro domo Israel: & cum Apostolo per multas tribulationes intrare regnum Dei; quoniam non sunt condignæ passiones huius mundi ad futuram gloriam, quæ reuelabitur in nobis, vt hæc dicuntur 1. q. 3. cap. Saluator. Almus etiá Christi confessor, & vitæ ipsius præcipuus imitator sanctus Franciscus, ac eius stigmatibus notabiliter insignitus Spiritu sancto demonstrante prædixit regulam & religionem suam acerrime diffamandam. Et quod super eam venirent tentationes immensæ, & qui fuerint tunc probati, accipient coronam vitæ. Væ autem illis, qui de sola spe religionis confisi tepescent, nec resistent constanter tentationibus ad probationem electorum permissis. Sed quantiscunq; tentationibus fuerit dicta ipsius religio impulsa, salua semper Christi numine permanebit, vt habetur in dictis ipsius sancti.
units.tr: To all and each of the ministers, custodians, guardians, vicars, and the other brothers of the Order of Minors, who firmly hold the Catholic faith, the holy Gospel, and the Rule which they have chosen, and who are willing to observe it: Brother Michael, Minister General and servant of the same Order, wishes salvation and everlasting peace in the Lord. The foundation of the Christian faith, and its founder, our Lord Jesus Christ, who appeared in the world that he might destroy the works of the devil, established in his Catholic and Apostolic Church two kinds of men to be saved. The first are those who, by right faith and the observance of the commandments of the law, strive to attain eternal blessedness. Of these the Gospel says, If you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments of God. The second are those who, desiring to follow perfectly, even in the evangelical counsels, the life of our Lord Jesus Christ himself and of his Apostles, which is to observe the holy Gospel by living in obedience, without property, and in chastity, make promise. Of these the same Gospel says, If you wish to be perfect, go, sell all that you have, and give to the poor, and come, follow me. And holy Peter, speaking in the person of all the Apostles, indicating that he and the Apostles had fulfilled this command of perfection, replied: Behold, we have left all things and followed you. What then shall we have? These holy counsels the holy Roman and universal Church has set out, determined and defined in the sacred canons, and especially in the decretal Extra de statu monachorum, chapter Cum ad monasterium, and in 12 q. 1, chapters dilectissimi, duo sunt, quia sua, scimus, nolo, non dicatis, and in Extra de verbo significatione, chapter Exiit. And in the Rules of Saints Augustine, Benedict and Francis, which have been approved and confirmed by the universal Church, it has been determined and defined that a religious life which perfectly imitates the life of Christ and the Apostles is joined to this evangelical and holy doctrine of the holy Roman Church. Whoever shall be a contradictor of this, or shall not believe it, and shall have made a faithful confession, will without doubt perish forever; and by that very fact he is excommunicated and condemned as a heretic, by the sentence of the sacred general council of the universal Catholic Church, because he does not firmly believe, confess and hold the doctrine which Christ, by showing the way of life, has given to the human race for its salvation, which the holy Roman Church firmly believes and faithfully confesses. This is clear from the general council of the universal Church held Extra de summa trinitate et fide catholica, chapter firmiter, §. hoc sancta trinitas, and from the fifth book of the same general council, where a decretal, which is part of the said general council and placed under the title De haereticis, says: We therefore excommunicate and anathematize every heresy that raises itself against this holy, orthodox and Catholic faith which we have set out above, condemning all heretics, by whatever names they may be called. Since it is certain that that saving doctrine and way of life which Christ gave and showed to the human race, which must be firmly believed and faithfully confessed, of which the said §. Hæc sancta trinitas, speaks, is the sacred doctrine taught by Christ in the holy Gospel and written down in the New Testament, as is proved in 24 distinctio, chapter qui episcopus. It is not lawful to doubt or dispute about this doctrine, whether whatever has been written in it is true and holy; but whatever is found in it must be believed without hesitation, as is said in 9 distinctio, chapter 1, and chapter quum nesciat. And whatever strikes against the articles of faith in this sacred doctrine of the holy Gospel, or of the Old and New Testament, I believe in God the Father; I believe in Jesus Christ his Son; I believe in the Holy Spirit, the triune and one true God, from whom this doctrine was delivered, and against the article One holy, Catholic and Apostolic Church, which has approved the said doctrine of the Gospel and the rules of the said saints, plainly strikes against them. And whoever preaches or teaches otherwise than has been preached is anathema, and is separated from God and his holy Catholic and Apostolic Church, as the Apostle testifies to the Galatians, chapter 1, saying: Even if we, or an angel from heaven, should preach to you otherwise than we have preached to you, let him be anathema. And whoever understands Holy Scripture otherwise than the sense of the Holy Spirit by whom it was given is to be judged a heretic, even though he has not withdrawn from the Church in body, as is said in 24 q. 3, chapter haeresis. Hence also the Pope, if he teaches or decrees anything against the doctrine of the Catholic faith, falls by that very fact into sentence of excommunication, condemnation and deprivation, and is inferior to any Catholic whatever, as is held and noted in 24 q. 1, at the beginning and in the Gloss; and in the chapter Athanasius, in the text and Gloss, and in §. Item cum Dominus, and §. si autem, and §. his auctoritatibus, and chapter dicimus, and 19 distinctio, §. hoc autem, and §. quia vero, in the chapter Anastasius, in the text and Gloss. And those who believe, favour or defend the same are by law excommunicated and made infamous; nor can they exercise any lawful office, nor receive anything by another's will, nor be elected or elect to office or dignity, nor be admitted in any way to give testimony or to succeed to anyone's inheritance; as is proved in the said chapter excommunicamus itaque, §. credentes, and in the following chapter excommunicamus et anathematizamus. But since the Saviour foretold in the Gospel that near the end of the age false Christs and false prophets would arise and lead many astray, and that his faithful would have many distresses in the world, yet that the gates of hell (that is, heresies) would not prevail; therefore, as the Apostle says, 1 Corinthians 10: There must be heresies, so that those who are approved may be made manifest. It is also necessary that truly Catholic and faithful men, with the prophet, rise up on the other side and set up a wall for the house of Israel, and with the Apostle enter the kingdom of God through many tribulations; for the sufferings of this world are not worthy of the future glory which will be revealed in us. These things are said in 1 q. 3, chapter Salvator, as they are said there. Also holy Francis, the gentle confessor of Christ and his chief imitator, marked in a notable way with his stigmata, by the showing of the Holy Spirit foretold that his Rule and Order would be most bitterly defamed; and that immense temptations would come upon it, and that those who were then approved would receive the crown of life. But woe to those who, trusting only in the hope of the Order, grow lukewarm and do not stand firm against the temptations permitted for the testing of the elect. However many temptations this same Order is assailed by, it will always remain safe under the protection of Christ, as is contained in the sayings of the same saint.

units.la: Ideo factum est his diebus nouissimis, vt Iacob de Cadurco, dicit Iohannes Papa 22. qui prius antequam datus esset in reprobum sensum, pontificatus sui anno secundo approbauit & in iudiciis, & in scholis legi publice mandauit decretalem, quæ incipit: Exiui de paradiso, sicut patet in proœmio per ipsum facto super nouas constitutiones Clementis Papæ 5. In qua decretali Regula sancti Francisci, quæ est sanctum euangelium obseruare viuendo in obedientia sine proprio, & in castitate tanquam forma & regula vitæ cœlestis, & toti vniuersali ecclesiæ plurimum fructuosa, ac declaratio domini Nicolai Papæ tertii, & abdicatio proprietatis omnium rerum tam in speciali quam etiam in communi, tanquam abdicatio ad perfectionem ducens; & altissima paupertas solo Deo contenta approbatur & commendatur, ac dicta religio sancti Francisci pronunciatur sancta & muris regularis obseruantiæ firmiter vndiq; circumclusa. Et etiá idem dominus Iohannes de consilio Cardinalium suorum fecit aliam declarationem super dictam regulam, quæ incipit: Quorundam exigit: in qua pronunciauit decretalem Exiit qui seminat, salubriter editam, solidam, claram & lucidam, multaq; maturitate digestam, & dictam religionem sancti Francisci sanctam & de die in diem de virtute in virtutem ad perfectionem tendere terrena despiciendo & cœlestia complectendo. Et aliam ordinationem, quæ incipit Gloriosam: in qua pronunciauit dictum Ordinem Fratrum Minorum ab ipso suæ fundationis exordio dicti almi confessoris beati Francisci regulari traditione & Apostolicæ sedis confirmatione fore in vita & doctrina sanctam, & indissolubili quadam textura ecclesiæ catholicæ connexum, fide clarum, spe validum, caritate profusum, obedientia deuotum, velut singulare iubar sanctitatis exemplo vitæ ac doctrinæ verbo per vniuersum orbem claruisse & ecclesiasticæ doctrinæ multum vtilitatis & inclitæ alacritatis plurimum attulisse, & quosdam Fratres dicti ordinis in dictas declarationes suas iudicio suo impingentes tanquam hæreticos iudicauit, prout hæc omnia in dictis constitutionibus editis per dictum dominum Iohannem pontificatus sui anno secundo plenius & seriosius explicantur. Manifestum autem est, quod in sæpe dicta decretali Exiit qui seminat per ipsum dominum Iohannem in dictis suis constitutionibus, & præcipue in dicta sua declaratione, quæ incipit, Quorundam exigit, specialiter approbata diffinitur in hæc verba: dicimus, q abdicatio proprietatis omnium rerum tam in speciali quam etiá in communi propter Deum meritoria est & sancta, quam & Christus viam perfectionis ostendens verbo docuit & exemplo firmauit, quamq, primi fundatores militantis ecclesiæ prout ab ipso fonte hauserant, in volentes perfecte viuere, per doctrinæ ac vitæ ipsorum alueos deriuarunt. Hæc ibi. Ex quibus clare patet, quod etiá ipse Iohannes circa primordia sui pontificatus tenuit & docuit Christum & Apostolos eius proprietatem & dominium rerum omnium temporalium reliquisse siue à se penitus abdicasse. Sed ipse post modum in reprobum sensum datus, & à cupiditate diuitiarum huius seculi, quæ teste euangelio verbum Dei suffocant, excæcatus etiam sibiipsi & dictis suis constitutionibus contradicens & seipsum proprio iudicio condemnans, elapso anno 6 pontificatus sui fecit quatuor detestanda statuta haereticalia manifeste aduersantia fidei catholicae & dictae doctrinae euangelicae & Apostolicae & sanctae Romanae ecclesiae. Quae statuta per mundum publice diuulgauit, quorum primum incipit, Ad conditorem canonum, in cuius fine scriptum est: Datum Auinion. anno 7. Pontificatus nostri. Et secundum incipit: Cum inter nonnullos, datum anno 8. A qua constitutione Ad conditorem pro parte dicti Ordinis in praesentia eius domini Ioannis & Cardinalium suorum primo per Fratres Bonaiuhoram Procuratorem dicti Ordinis ad sanctam Romanam Ecclesiam catholicam extitit appellatum. Tertium incipit: Quia quorundam mentes, datu anno 9. Quartum statutum est, quo ipse Ioannes sui pectoris venenum manifestius explicat & euomit, incipit Quia vir reprobus Michael de Cesena, cuius signo scriptum est: Datum anno 14. pontificatus nostri. In quibus statutis siue libellis haereticalib' publice, notorie & pertinaciter dogmatizat, q; Christus & Apostoli in omnibus rebus temporalibus, quas scriptura eos habuisse testatur, tam in speciali q; etiam in communi proprietate & dominio habuerunt: & q; ale proprietatem & dominium rerum temporalium nullatenus abdicarunt, nec illa reliquerunt nec abdicatione huiusmodi docuerunt; & omnes asserentes oppositum esse censendos haereticos, & sicut haereticos condemnandos iudicat & diffinit. Et in dicto suo statuto siue libello, Quia vir reprobus, dogmatizare praesumit manifeste, q; Christus ingtum homo ab instanti suae conceptionis habuit ex Dei datione uniuersale dominium omnium temporalium huius mundi, & fuit Dominus & rex verus in temporalibus omnibus, & quod nihilominus habuit dominium multarum rerum temporalium non ab instanti suae conceptionis, sed postea successiue aliis modis, ut pote ex collatione fidelium vel emptione acquisitarum & quod illi dominio & regno nunquam renuntiauit, nec renuntiare potuit. Quia fecisset contra ordinationem patris, de qua dicitur Dan. 2. Suscitabit Deus caeli regnum q; non corrumpetur nec dissipabitur in aeternum & regnum eius alteri non tradetur & potestas eius aeterna, quae non auferetur. Et quod non carentia dominii fecit Christum pauperem; sed potius carentia perceptionis fructus & obuentionis rerum, quatenus erat Dominus: quia se ipsum fstructuum, quarum erat Dominus & rex, fructibus & prouentibus nisi in valde paucis non iuuabat. Et quod Apostoli etiam post missionem Spiritus sancti in rebus temporalibus eis concessis siue assignatis, habuerunt dominium tam in speciali q; etiam in communi. Et quilibet ipsorum Apostolorum rerum, q; eidem assignabatur in communitate credentium, de qua dicitur Act. 4. c. fuit procurator & dominus. Et quod ipsi Apostoli non emiserunt votum abdicationis proprietatis & dominii. Et quod votum viuendi sine proprio ad res, quas necessario requirit vita humana, minime se extendit. Et quod Christus nullo modo uiuedi in speciali imposuit Apostolis, nisi sicut ceteris discipulis, per discipulos intelliges non tantum septuaginta duos, sed etiam ceteros Christianos, qui Christum sequebantur, quod manifeste patet per eius verba, in quibus inter discipulos, de quibus ipse haereticus loquitur, computat Ioseph ab Arimathia & Lazarum & Marthām & Mariam Magdalenam & Dorcam, de quibus manifestum est, quod non fuerunt de septuaginta duobus, sed de turba conuersorum ad Christum: qui etiam in generali dicebatur discipuli Christiani, ut patet Act. 11. Et insuper dogmatizat, quod Christus & Apostoli incesserunt calciati. Haec est doctrina dicti haeretici in saepe dicto libello Quia vir reprobus, explicite dogmatizata. Et in supradicto libello siue statuto, Quia quorundam mentes, dicit quod Christus nō docuit nec exemplo firmauit non portare pecuniam. Et quod illud, quod dicitur in euangelio; Nolite portare pecuniam, nō fuit praeceptum, sed potestar recipiendi necessaria. Unde dicit, q; Apostolis licuit huiusmodi iniunctum siue dictum non seruare: Asserens quod Apostoli pecuniam portauerunt etiam post praedicta. Cum igitur sanctum euangelium, secundum Augustinum, sit vita & doctrina Christi, vt dicit in libro contra Faustum, & Christus Luc. 4. dicat; euangelizare pauperibus misit me: mea doctrina & vita informar. Et viuere sine proprio nihil aliud sit, nisi ea, quae ad vitam pertinent, non habere propria. Ex dictis assertionibus dicti haeretici concluditur manifeste, quod falsa & erronea ac haeretica fuit. Et est dicta regula & forma viuendi, quam beatus Franciscus tradidit suis Fratribus, & eum sequi volentibus, dicens: Regula & vita Fratrum Minorum haec est, scil. Domini nostri Iesu Christi sanctum euangelium obseruare, viuendo in obedientia sine proprio & in castitate. Et ita Fratres nihil sibi approprient, nec domum, nec locum, nec aliquam rem. Et in eadem regula: precipio firmiter Fratribus vniuersis, ne vllo modo denarios vel pecuniam recipiant per se vel per interpositam personam. Et alibi: quia necessitate cogentur, possunt portare calciamenta. Et in finem: sanctum euangelium Domini nostri Iesu Christi, quod firmiter promisimus obseruare; obseruemus. Quia secundum dictum haereticum talis vita siue forma viuendi non fuit vita Christi, nec in euangelio, siue a Christo docta: imo secundum dictum haereticum Christus verbo & exemplo docuit de proprio viuere, siue in rebus omnibus temporalibus proprietatem & dominium habere tam in speciali quam in communi, & pecuniam portare, & incedere calciatos: & secundum ipsum haereticum asserere quod Christus praedicta docuerit, contradicit sancto euangelio, siue vitae & doctrinae Christi & sancti euangelii.
