Ex dicta etiam assertione praedicti haeretici sequitur, quod vniuersalis ecclesia, quae dicta regula approbauit & confirmauit, sicut norma siue forma viuendi in euangelio a Christo docta, erraui in fide & doctrina Christi & sancti euangelii: & quod fallax erronea & haeretica fuit assertio ecclesiae catholicae, quam fecit in decretali praeallegata, quae incipit: Exiit qui seminat, cum dicit: hi sunt illius sanctae regulae professores, quae euangelico fundatur eloquio, vita Christi roboratur exemplo, fundatorum militantis ecclesiae Apostolorum eius sermonibus actibus confirmatur. Haec est apud Deum & patrem munda & immaculata religio, quae descendens a patre luminum per eius filium exeplariter & verbaliter Apostolis tradita, & demum beato Francisco & eum sequentibus inspirata. Et ita dicim, q; abdicationem proprietatis huiusmodi Christi via persecutionis verbo docuit exemplo firmauit. Et quod erraui in fide & doctrina euangelii totum concilium generale: imo tota Ecclesia, quæ ipsum concilium approbauit & recepit. In quo concilio quod incipit, Exiui de Paradyso, de dicta regula dicitur sic: Hæc est illa cælestis vitæ forma & regula, quam descripsit ille Christi confessor eximius sanctus Franciscus. Et sequitur etiam, quod sanctus Franciscus & alii sancti Fratres dicti Ordinis, qui in obseruantia & credulitate dictæ regulæ tanquam doctrinæ Euangelicæ vixerunt, & suos dies finierunt, in errore hæretico vixerunt & mortui sunt. Et per consequens in æternum damnari. Et quod vniuersalis Ecclesia errauit in canonizando dictum sanctum Franciscum & venerando eum ac venerari mandando tanquam sanctum. Et ita secundum hanc hæreticalem doctrinam vniuersalis Ecclesia errauit in fide multipliciter, si dictam regulam sancti Francisci tanquam formam in Euangelio & à Christo dicta approbando & confirmando, & dictas decretales, Exiit qui seminat, & Exiui, statuendo & in corpore iuris redigendo, & dictum sanctum canonizando: & per consequens huiusmodi doctrina euidenter impingit in articulû fidei, quo dicitur: Credo in sanctam Ecclesiam catholicam, sub quo continetur & includitur, quod ipsa Ecclesia in fide siue in vita & doctrina Christi & Apostolorum eius errare siue deficere non potest 19. dist. c. Ita Dominus 24. q. 1. c. A recta in textu & Gloss & c. pededa in fi. & c. hac est fides in fi. quia Christus rogauit pro ea, vt non deficiat fides eius. Lu. 12. & ext. de baptismo c. maior. in pr. in tex. & Glo.
units.tr: For this reason it has come about in these latest days that Jacob of Cahors, that is John XXII, who before he was given over to a reprobate mind, in the second year of his pontificate approved and ordered to be publicly read in the courts and in the schools the decretal that begins Exiui de paradiso, as appears in the preface which he himself made to the new constitutions of Clement V. In that decretal the Rule of Saint Francis, which is to observe the holy gospel by living in obedience, without property, and in chastity, as the form and rule of heavenly life, and very fruitful for the whole universal Church, is approved and commended, together with the declaration of Lord Nicholas III and the renunciation of all property, both particular and common, as a renunciation that leads to perfection; and the most exalted poverty, content with God alone, is approved and commended, and the said religion of Saint Francis is pronounced holy and firmly enclosed on every side by the walls of regular observance. Moreover, the same Lord John, with the advice of his Cardinals, made another declaration on the said rule, which begins Quorundam exigit: in which he pronounced the decretal Exiit qui seminat to be wholesomely issued, solid, clear and lucid, and digested with much maturity, and the said religion of Saint Francis holy, and from day to day, from virtue to virtue, tending towards perfection by despising earthly things and embracing heavenly ones. He also issued another ordinance, which begins Gloriosam: in which he pronounced that the said Order of Friars Minor, from the very beginning of its foundation by the blessed confessor Saint Francis, through the regular tradition and the confirmation of the Apostolic See, is holy in life and doctrine, and bound together by an indissoluble texture to the catholic Church, bright in faith, strong in hope, abundant in charity, devout in obedience, and that, like a singular ray of holiness, it has shone throughout the whole world by the example of its life and the word of its teaching, and has brought much usefulness and great eagerness to ecclesiastical doctrine; and he judged as heretics certain friars of the said Order who, by their own judgment, attacked his said declarations. All of this is explained more fully and seriously in the said constitutions issued by the said Lord John in the second year of his pontificate. It is clear, moreover, that in the often-mentioned decretal Exiit qui seminat, and especially in the said declaration that begins Quorundam exigit, the same Lord John, in those constitutions of his, specially approved and defined in these words: "We say that the renunciation of the ownership of all things, both particular and common, is meritorious and holy before God; Christ also, showing the way of perfection, taught it by word and confirmed it by example, and the first founders of the militant Church, as they had drawn it from the very source, derived it into the channels of their doctrine and life, for those who wished to live perfectly." Thus far that text. From these words it is plainly evident that John himself, at the beginning of his pontificate, held and taught that Christ and his Apostles left, or entirely renounced, the ownership and dominion of all temporal things. But he afterwards was given over to a reprobate mind, and blinded by the desire for the riches of this age, which, as the gospel witnesses, choke the word of God, and also contradicting his own constitutions and condemning himself by his own judgment, in the sixth year of his pontificate, having passed, he issued four detestable heretical statutes, plainly opposed to the catholic faith, to the said evangelical and apostolic doctrine, and to the holy Roman Church. He published these statutes throughout the world. The first of them begins Ad conditorem canonum, and at its end is written: Given at Avignon, in the seventh year of our pontificate. The second begins Cum inter nonnullos, given in the eighth year. From the constitution Ad conditorem, on behalf of the said Order, in the presence of the said Lord John and his Cardinals, an appeal was first made to the holy Roman catholic Church by Brother Bonaiuhora, procurator of the said Order. The third begins Quia quorundam mentes, given in the ninth year. The fourth statute, in which John himself more openly sets forth and pours out the poison of his breast, begins Quia vir reprobus Michael de Cesena, and at its end is written: Given in the fourteenth year of our pontificate. In these statutes or heretical pamphlets he publicly, notoriously and obstinately teaches as dogma that Christ and the Apostles had both particular and common property and dominion over all the temporal things which Scripture testifies they possessed; that they in no way renounced such property and dominion over temporal things, nor left them, nor taught by such renunciation; and he judges and defines that all who assert the opposite are to be considered heretics and condemned as heretics. And in his said statute or pamphlet Quia vir reprobus he presumes to teach plainly as dogma that Christ, as man, from the instant of his conception, by God's gift had universal dominion over all the temporal things of this world, and was the true Lord and king in all temporal things; and that nevertheless he had ownership of many temporal things not from the instant of his conception, but afterwards successively by other means, namely acquired by the gift of the faithful or by purchase; and that he never renounced that dominion and kingdom, nor could renounce it. For he would have acted against the ordinance of the Father, of which it is said in Dan. 2: God will raise up a kingdom of heaven which shall never be corrupted nor destroyed for ever, and its kingdom shall not be given to another, and its power is eternal, which shall not be taken away. And that Christ was made poor not by lack of ownership, but rather by lack of receiving the fruits and revenues of things, insofar as he was Lord; for, being himself Lord and king of the fruits, he did not help himself with the fruits and revenues except in very few cases. And that the Apostles, even after the mission of the Holy Spirit, in the temporal things granted or assigned to them, had dominion both in particular and in common; and each of the Apostles was procurator and lord of the things assigned to him in the community of believers, of which it is said in Acts 4. And that the Apostles themselves did not make a vow of renouncing property and dominion. And that the vow of living without property does not in the least extend to the things which human life necessarily requires. And that Christ in no way imposed on the Apostles the living without property in particular, except as on the other disciples; and by disciples he means not only the seventy-two, but also the other Christians who followed Christ, which is manifest from his words, in which, among the disciples of whom this heretic speaks, he counts Joseph of Arimathea, Lazarus, Martha, Mary Magdalene and Dorcas, of whom it is clear that they were not among the seventy-two, but from the crowd of those converted to Christ; who were also commonly called Christian disciples, as appears in Acts 11. And moreover he teaches as dogma that Christ and the Apostles went about shod. This is the doctrine of the said heretic, explicitly taught as dogma in the often-mentioned pamphlet Quia vir reprobus. And in the above-mentioned pamphlet or statute, Quia quorundam mentes, he says that Christ neither taught nor confirmed by example the not carrying of money; and that what is said in the gospel, Do not carry money, was not a precept but a permission to receive what is necessary. Hence he says that the Apostles were allowed not to observe what was enjoined or said in this way; asserting that the Apostles carried money even after the aforesaid. Since, therefore, the holy gospel, according to Augustine, is the life and doctrine of Christ, as he says in the book Against Faustus, and Christ says in Luke 4: He has sent me to preach the gospel to the poor: my doctrine and life are formed by it; and since to live without property is nothing other than not to have as one's own those things which pertain to life; from the said assertions of this heretic it is manifestly concluded that the said rule and form of living, which Saint Francis handed down to his Friars and to those willing to follow him, was false, erroneous and heretical. Saint Francis said: The rule and life of the Friars Minor is this, namely, to observe the holy gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ, living in obedience, without property, and in chastity. And so let the Friars appropriate nothing to themselves, neither house, nor place, nor any thing. And in the same rule: I firmly command all the Friars that in no way they receive pence or money, either themselves or through an intermediary person. And elsewhere: Because they are compelled by necessity, they may wear shoes. And at the end: The holy gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ, which we have firmly promised to observe; let us observe it. Since, according to the heretical saying, such a life or form of living was neither the life of Christ, nor taught in the gospel or by Christ; but rather, according to the heretical saying, Christ taught by word and example to live with property, to have ownership and dominion over all temporal things, both particular and common, to carry money, and to go about shod; and to assert, according to this heretic, that Christ taught these things, contradicts the holy gospel, and the life and doctrine of Christ and of the holy gospel. From the said assertion of the aforesaid heretic it also follows that the universal Church, which approved and confirmed the said rule as the norm or form of living taught in the gospel by Christ, has erred in the faith and doctrine of Christ and of the holy gospel; and that the assertion of the catholic Church, which it made in the decretal cited above, which begins Exiit qui seminat, is false, erroneous and heretical, when it says: These are the professors of that holy rule, which is founded on the evangelical word, strengthened by the example of the life of Christ, and confirmed by the words and deeds of his Apostles, the founders of the militant Church. This is the pure and immaculate religion before God and the Father, which, descending from the Father of lights through his Son, was handed down to the Apostles by example and word, and at last inspired in blessed Francis and in those who follow him. And so we say that Christ taught by word and confirmed by example the renunciation of such property, by the way of persecution. And that the whole general council, indeed the whole Church, which approved and received that same council, has erred in the faith and doctrine of the gospel. In that council, which begins Exiui de Paradyso, of the said rule it is said thus: This is that heavenly form and rule of life which that distinguished confessor of Christ, Saint Francis, described. And it also follows that Saint Francis and the other holy Friars of the said Order, who lived and finished their days in observance of, and belief in, the said rule as the doctrine of the gospel, lived and died in heretical error; and consequently are damned for eternity. And that the universal Church erred in canonizing the said Saint Francis, and in venerating him and commanding him to be venerated as a saint. And so, according to this heretical doctrine, the universal Church has erred in faith in many ways: in approving and confirming the rule of Saint Francis as a form taught in the gospel and by Christ, and in enacting the said decretals Exiit qui seminat and Exiui, and reducing them into the body of law, and in canonizing the said saint. And consequently this doctrine clearly strikes against the article of faith in which it is said: I believe in the holy catholic Church, under which it is contained and included that the Church itself cannot err or fail in faith, that is, in the life and doctrine of Christ and of his Apostles: 19 dist. c. Ita Dominus; 24 q. 1 c. A recta, in the text and gloss; c. pededa in fine; c. hac est fides in fine; because Christ prayed for her, that her faith might not fail: Luke 22; ext. de baptismo c. maior, in the beginning, in the text and gloss.

units.la: Et sicut etiam ex prædictis patet, quod omnes illi, qui dicto hæretico consenserunt & consentiunt in dictis erroribus & statutis, non sunt nec dici possunt Fratres regulæ nec Ordinis beati Francisci, sed sunt separati à dicto Ordine & regula, & ab vniuersali catholica & Apostolica Ecclesia, quæ dictâ regulam tanquam regulâ & doctrinam Christi & sancti Euangelii approbauit & confirmauit, & quæ dictû concilium ordinauit, & contenta in eo approbauit. Et ob hoc merito dicendi sunt & censendi hæretici, schismatici & apostatæ, & per consequens sunt priuati ipso iure & facto omnibus priuilegiis & gratiis, quæ & quas dicta Ecclesia catholica & Apostolica Fratribus Professoribus dictæ regulæ & religionis indulsit, & sunt infames, nec possunt eligere nec eligi ad aliquod officium, nec ad aliquam dignitatem, nec possunt prædicare, nec confessiones audire, nec absoluere, nec actus aliquos legitimos exercere, vt manifeste probatur in superius allegato c. de hereticis, Excommunicamus itaque, in prin. & in §. credentes.
units.tr: And just as is also clear from what has been said above, all those who have agreed to the said heretic, and still agree, to his errors and statutes, are not and cannot be called brothers of the rule or of the Order of blessed Francis. They are separated from the said Order and rule, and from the universal, catholic and apostolic Church, which approved and confirmed the said rule as the rule and doctrine of Christ and the holy Gospel, and which ordained the said council and approved what is contained in it. For this reason they are rightly to be called and regarded as heretics, schismatics and apostates. Consequently they are deprived, by law and in fact, of all the privileges and graces which the said catholic and apostolic Church granted to the friars professed in the said rule and religion. They are infamous, and they can neither elect nor be elected to any office or dignity, nor can they preach, hear confessions, absolve, or perform any lawful acts. This is plainly proved in the above-cited c. de hereticis, Excommunicamus itaque, in prin. & in §. credentes.

units.la: Confirmantur etiam prædicta ex eo, quod dictus Dominus Ioannes dixit frequenter siue pronuntiauit hæretica litera siue determinatione, quod Generalis Minister & omnes Magistri & Ministri generis Fratres dicti Ordinis, & totû capitulû Generale Parisiis congregatû fecerunt Anno Domini 1321. & vniuersis Christi fidelibus destinarunt. In qua litera concorditur & vnanimiter dixerunt & confessi sunt, quod dicere & asserere, quod Christus & Apostoli viâ perfectionis ostendentes nihil iure proprietatis & dominii seu iuris proprii in speciali vel in communi habuerunt, non est hæreticû, sed sanû catholicû & fidele, maxime cum sancta Romana Ecclesia hoc determinauerit in dicta decretali Exiit qui seminat §. porro. Qua litera & diffinitio fuit in autentica forma redacta, & sigillis & subscriptionibus Generalis Ministri & aliorû Magistrorû & Ministrorû dicti Ordinis roborata, & incipit, Vniuersis Christi fidelibus. Ergo dictus Dominus Iohannes frequenter dixerit siue pronuntiauerit dictâ litera & declarationem de Capitali Generalis hæretica patet per litera autenticam subscriptionibus & testimoniis Fratrû Raymundi procuratoris Ordinis, & Petri de Prato Prouinciæ sancti Francisci, & Laurentii Baccalarii Auinion. roborata. Quæ pronuntiatio facta fuit An. Dom. 1328. nona die mens. April. & in autentica formam redacta. Ex quo patet, quod etiâ secundû iudicium dicti Domini Iohannis omnes illi Fratres, qui interfuerunt dictæ literæ & determinationi factæ in dicto Capitulo Generali, & nunc habent dictâ Dominû Iohannem, pro vero & catholico Papa, & dicta gesta per eum comprobant, hæretici sunt censendi, quia constat quod ipse Dominus Iohannes anteq̃ foret in reprobû sensum datus, approbauit dicta decretale Exiit qui seminat, & pronuntiauit eâ solidâ, clarâ, salubriter editâ, lucidâ, multaq; maturitate digestâ: & dictâ religionem, quæ profitetur Euangelii doctrinâ perfectâ Christi vitâ consistere in abdicatione proprietatis & dominii omniû rerû temporaliû tâ in speciali & in communi facta, & de virtute in virtute ad perfectionem tendere, & fidê clarâ & in catholicâ Ecclesiâ indissolubili textura connexâ, sicut patet in dictis constitutionibus Domini Iohannis, quarû vna incipit: Quia quorundam exigit: & alia incipit, Gloriosam. Et etiâ pronuntiauit illos Fratres hæreticos censendos, quod tunc in ipsas suas constitutiones incidunt, quod hæreticas impingebat, sicut patet in literis ipsius Domini Iohannis, quod incipiunt super omnia desiderabilia cordis nostri. Cum ergo illi, quod assentiunt statutis prædictis quorum hæreticalibus edictis pro dictum Dominû Iohanne, postquam fuit in reprobû sensum datus, in quibus opposita & contraria eius dicit, asserit & pronuntiat impingunt in prædictas suas primas constitutiones, & eas per consequens fatentur fuisse erroneas & contra fidem. Sequitur, quod etiam secundum eius primû iudicium hæretici sunt censendi, cum illud quod aliquando fuit hæreticum dictum, semper hæreticum sit censendum. Insuper secundû iudicium vniuersalis Ecclesiæ catholicæ & Apostolicæ veritate infallibilem hæretici sunt censendi, quia veritatem fidei catholicæ & doctrinæ perfectionis Euangelicæ, quam sancta catholica & Apostolica Ecclesia tenet & firmiter confitetur, vt superius est probatum, abnegant, dictis statutis hæreticalibus aduersantibus ipsi fidei & Euangelio assentiendo & ipsorum statutorum & haresum contemnendo in eis conditorem & doctorem, verum & catholicum pontificem admittendo.
units.tr: The foregoing is also confirmed by the fact that the said Lord John often repeated, or proclaimed, the heretical letter or determination which the Minister General and all the Masters and Ministers of the Order, and the whole General Chapter gathered at Paris in the year of the Lord 1321, drew up and sent to all the faithful of Christ. In that letter they agreed and unanimously said and confessed that to say and assert that Christ and the Apostles, showing the way of perfection, had no right of ownership or dominion, nor any personal right, either individually or in common, is not heresy but sound, catholic and faithful doctrine, especially since the holy Roman Church had determined this in the said decretal Exiit qui seminat §. porro. This letter and definition was drawn up in authentic form and confirmed by the seals and signatures of the Minister General and the other Masters and Ministers of the said Order. It begins, Vniuersis Christi fidelibus. Therefore the said Lord John often said or proclaimed the said letter, and the declaration of the General Chapter is heretical. This is shown by the authentic letter, confirmed by the signatures and testimonies of Brother Raymond, procurator of the Order, Peter of Prato of the province of St Francis, and Laurence, Bachelor of Avignon. This proclamation was made in the year of the Lord 1328, on the ninth day of April, and was drawn up in authentic form. From this it is plain that, even by the second judgment of the said Lord John, all those friars who took part in the said letter and the determination made at the said General Chapter, and who now hold the said Lord John to be the true and catholic Pope, and who approve the deeds he has done, are to be regarded as heretics. For it is certain that the same Lord John, before he was given over to a reprobate mind, approved the said decretal Exiit qui seminat, and pronounced it solid, clear, wholesomely issued, lucid, and drawn up with much maturity. He also declared that the religion which professes that the perfect doctrine of the Gospel and the perfect life of Christ consist in the renunciation of all ownership and dominion over temporal goods, both individually and in common, and that it strives from virtue to virtue towards perfection, is bound together with a clear faith in an indissoluble fabric of the catholic Church. This is clear from the said constitutions of Lord John, one of which begins Quia quorundam exigit: and another Gloriosam. He also declared that those friars are to be considered heretics who fall into his own constitutions, since they assail heresy, as is clear from the letters of the same Lord John, which begin super omnia desiderabilia cordis nostri. Therefore, since those who assent to the aforesaid statutes, whose heretical edicts were issued by the said Lord John after he was given over to a reprobate mind, in which he states, asserts and pronounces the opposite and contrary, clash with those earlier constitutions of his, they thereby confess that those constitutions were erroneous and contrary to the faith. It follows that, even according to his first judgment, they are to be considered heretics, since what was once declared heretical must always be considered heretical. Moreover, by the second judgment of the universal catholic and apostolic Church, which is infallible in truth, they are to be considered heretics. For they deny the truth of the catholic faith and of the doctrine of evangelical perfection, which the holy catholic and apostolic Church holds and firmly confesses, as has been proved above. They do this by assenting to these heretical statutes, which are opposed to the faith itself and to the Gospel, and by despising in those statutes their author and teacher, while acknowledging him as a true and catholic pontiff.

units.la: Ex prædictis etiam ostenditur, quod dictus Iohannes & omnes Fratres eti in dictis suis erroribus sponte & scienter sequentes & defendentes, incidunt in plures hæreses per vniuersalem Ecclesiam catholicam & Apostolicam condemnatas. Et primo ostenditur, quod incidunt in damnatâ hæresim Vigilantii hæretici damnati, qui dicit & dogmatizauit illos melius facere & Christû & Apostolos sequi perfectius qui suarum possessionum & rerum proprietate & dominium retinent, & paulatim fructus & prouentus carum pauperibus diuidunt, quam illos qui suis possessionibus & rebus omnibus venundatis omnia simul pauperibus largiuntur. Quam hæresim sanctus Hieronymus Ecclesiæ sanctæ do&or reprobat in libro, quem edidit contra dictum Vigilantium hæreticum, sic dicens: Quod autem asserit Vigilantius, eos melius facere, qui vtuntur rebus suis & paulatim fructus possessionum suarum pauperibus dividunt, quam illos qui possessionibus venundatis semel omnia largiuntur, non à me, sed à Domino respondebitur: Si vis persectus esse, vade & vende omnia quæ habes & da pauperibus. Ad eum loquitur, qui vult esse perfectus, qui cum Apostolis patrem, naviculam & rete dimisit. Hæc Hieronymus. Quia secundum doctrinam in dictis statutis hæreticalibus per dictum Iohannem hæreticum dogmatizatam Christus nunquam exemplo nec verbo docuit abdicationem proprietatis & dominii rerum temporalium: sed totum oppositum, vt superius est ostensum. Et nullus est perfectus nec esse potest, nisi in quantum sequitur vitam & doctrinam Christi: qui fuit fundamentum & fundator ac doctor, forma & exemplar omnis perfectionis & omnium perfectorum, iuxta quod ipse dicit Matth. 10. Non est discipulus super magistrum nec servus super Dominum. Sufficit discipulo, quod sit sicut magister eius: & servo quod sit sicut Dominus eius. Et in Luca: Perfectus autem omnis erit, si sit sicut magister eius. Et sic patet secundum dictam doctrinam in dictis statutis eius hæreticalibus dogmatizatam, quod melius sequuntur Christum, & melius & perfectius per consequens fecerunt illi, qui sua retinent & in paucis de fructibus possessionum suarum se iuvant, quam illi qui proprietatem & dominium omnium rerum temporalium à se abdicant, sicut Vigilantius hæreticus asserebat.
units.tr: From what has been said it is also shown that the said John, and all the friars who follow and defend his errors, knowingly and willingly, fall into several heresies condemned by the universal catholic and apostolic Church. First, it is shown that they fall into the condemned heresy of the heretic Vigilantius, who taught and asserted that those act better and follow Christ and the Apostles more perfectly who keep ownership and dominion of their possessions and goods, and gradually divide their fruits and revenues among the poor, than those who sell all their possessions and give everything to the poor at once. St Jerome, doctor of the holy Church, rejects this heresy in the book he published against the said heretic Vigilantius, saying: As for Vigilantius's assertion that those act better who use their goods and gradually divide the fruits of their possessions among the poor, than those who sell their possessions and give everything away at once, it will be answered not by me but by the Lord: "If you wish to be perfect, go and sell all that you have and give to the poor." He speaks to the one who wishes to be perfect, who with the Apostles left father, little boat and net. Thus Jerome. Because, according to the doctrine taught in the said heretical statutes by the said heretic John, Christ never taught, by example or by word, the renunciation of ownership and dominion over temporal goods, but the very opposite, as has been shown above. No one is perfect, nor can be, except insofar as he follows the life and doctrine of Christ, who is the foundation, founder, teacher, form and pattern of all perfection and of all the perfect. This is in line with what he himself says in Matthew 10: The disciple is not above the master, nor the servant above his lord. It is enough for the disciple that he be as his master, and for the servant that he be as his lord. And in Luke: Everyone who is perfect will be as his master. Thus it is plain that, according to the said doctrine taught in his heretical statutes, those who keep their goods and help themselves with a little of the fruits of their possessions follow Christ better, and therefore act better and more perfectly, than those who renounce ownership and dominion of all temporal goods, as the heretic Vigilantius maintained.

units.la: Secundo ostenditur, quod ipse Iohannes & dictæ eius doctrinæ sequaces inciderunt in damnatam hæresim Iouinciani hæretici damnati, qui nullam differentiam faciens inter præcepta data omnibus Christianis & consilia data volentibus esse perfectis, dixit & dogmatizavit, quod quantum ad meritum nulla est differentia inter honestatem coniugalem & vidualem sive virginalem, & quod inter abstinentes & temperate epulantes nullum est discrimen. De qua hæresi habetur 24. q. vlt. in. c. Sexta hæreticorum (seu Quidam autem hæretici, versiculo Iouinianista. Quia si verum foret, quod dictus Iohannes hæreticus in dicto libello sive statuto suo, qui incipit: Quia vir reprobus, dogmatizat, cum dicit, quod Christus nullum modum viuendi specialem imposuit Apostolis, nisi sicut cæteris Christianis, sicut superius est deductum. Cum manifestissimum sit; quod Apostoli fuerunt perfectiores omnibus Christianis, & exemplar post Christum omnium perfectorum & maioris meriti, sicut manifeste probat Glossa Ord. super illud ad Romanos 8. Nos ipsi primitias spiritus habentes, dicens: nos Apostoli, qui maiores aliis sumus per hoc quod primitias spiritus habemus & cæteris abundantius. Hæc Glossa. Sequitur manifeste, quod status coniugalis & status habentium dominia & possessiones in merito & perfectione non differunt à statu religiosorum viuentium in castitate & sine proprio, sed eiusdem meriti sunt, sicut dictus Iouinianus hæreticus asseruit. Quam hæresim reprobant omnes Doctores Ecclesiæ catholicæ & sancti patres. Sed vna sola auctoritas Augustini ad præsens ratione brevitatis adducitur, qui in libro De bono coniugali, dicit sic: Bonum Susannam in coniugali castitate laudamus: sed tamen & bonum vidua Annæ ac multo magis Mariæ virginis anteponimus. Bonum erat quod faciebant, quæ de substantia sua Christo & eius Discipulis ministrabant: sed melius qui omnem substantiam dimiserunt, vt Christum Domini expeditiores sequerentur. Hæc Augustinus, p quę hæresis Iouiniani & Vigilantii & dicti Iohannis hæretici simul confunditur. Et per ea, quæ sanctus Hieronymus in libris, quos edidit contra dictos Iouinianum & Vigilantium allegantur. Quare hic brevitatis causa dimittuntur. Vnde & quantum generale concilium Ecclesiæ, scilicet Toletanum, diffinit: Meliorem esse vitam monachorum continentium quam secularium seruantium tantummodo præcepta. Et quod clerici possunt fieri monachi, quia ad meliorem vitam transeunt 20. q. 4. cap. 1. Et per Euangelium probatur, quod Christus Apostolis & viris volentibus esse perfectis, imposuit aliud modum specialem viuendi, quam cæteris Christianis, scilicet quod omnia temporalia reliquerent, dicens: Nolite possidere aurum nec argentum nec pecuniam &c. Et iterum: Si vis perfectus esse vade & vende omnia quae habes & da pauperibus. Vnde Hieronymus ad Ebidiam dicit: Si vis esse perfecta & flare in primo fastigio dignitatis, fac quod fecerunt Apostoli, vade & vende omnia quae habes & da pauperibus & sequere Salvatorem. Nudam solam, crucem nuda sequaris. Hæc Hieronymus. Item, in Euangelio dicitur sic: Sunt eunuchi, qui se castraverunt propter regnum cælorum. Et iterum: Qui vult venire post me, abneget semetipsum, tollat crucem suam, & sequatur me. Ex quibus verbis Euangelii per omnes Doctores catholicos & sanctos institutores religionum per catholicam Ecclesiam approbatarum triplex votum religiose viuentium & volentium Christum & Apostolos eius perfecte sequi: videlicet viuendi sine proprio & in castitate & in obedientia, elicitur & ab omnibus sanctis religiosis est emissum, vt vitam perfectionis Euangelicæ Apostolis & Apostolicis viris à Christi inositam inuiolabiliter observarent, sicut in omnibus regulis sanctorum per vniversalem catholicam Ecclesiam approbatis colligitur euidenter.
units.tr: Secondly, it is shown that the said John himself and his followers in this doctrine fall into the condemned heresy of the heretic Jovinian, who, making no distinction between the precepts given to all Christians and the counsels given to those who wish to be perfect, taught and asserted that in respect of merit there is no difference between marital honour and widowed or virginal honour, and that there is no distinction between those who abstain and those who feast temperately. This heresy is found in 24. q. vlt. in. c. Sexta hæreticorum (or Quidam autem hæretici, under the verse Iouinianista.) For if it were true that the said heretic John, in his said little book or statute which begins Quia vir reprobus, teaches that Christ imposed on the Apostles no special manner of living, other than what he imposed on other Christians, as has been deduced above, then the Apostles would be no more perfect than other Christians. But it is most manifest that the Apostles were more perfect than all Christians, and after Christ the pattern of all the perfect and of greater merit. The Ordinary Gloss clearly proves this on the words of Romans 8: We ourselves, having the firstfruits of the Spirit, saying: We Apostles, who are greater than others because we have the firstfruits of the Spirit, and in greater abundance than the rest. Thus the Gloss. It clearly follows that the married state and the state of those who hold dominions and possessions do not differ in merit and perfection from the state of religious who live in chastity and without property, but are of equal merit, as the said heretic Jovinian asserted. This heresy is condemned by all the doctors of the catholic Church and the holy Fathers. For brevity's sake, I adduce here only one authority, that of Augustine, who in his book On the Good of Marriage says: We praise Susanna's goodness in chaste marriage, yet we also put the goodness of the widow Anna, and much more of the virgin Mary, before it. What those women did was good, who ministered from their substance to Christ and his disciples; but better still were those who gave up all their substance so as to follow the Lord Christ more freely. Thus Augustine. In this passage the heresy of Jovinian, of Vigilantius and of the said heretic John is refuted together. The same is shown by what St Jerome says in the books he published against the said Jovinian and Vigilantius, which are cited there and are therefore omitted here for brevity. Hence also the general council of the Church, namely the Council of Toledo, defines: The life of continent monks is better than that of secular people who keep only the precepts. And that clerics may become monks, because they pass to a better life (20. q. 4. cap. 1.). The Gospel also proves that Christ imposed on the Apostles and on men who wish to be perfect a special manner of living different from that of other Christians, namely that they should leave all temporal goods, saying: Do not possess gold, nor silver, nor money, etc. And again: If you wish to be perfect, go and sell all that you have and give to the poor. Hence Jerome says to Ebidia: If you wish to be perfect and to stand at the highest rank of dignity, do what the Apostles did: go, sell all that you have, give to the poor, and follow the Saviour. Naked, follow the naked cross. Thus Jerome. Likewise, the Gospel says: There are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven. And again: Whoever wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me. From these words of the Gospel, as taught by all the catholic doctors and holy founders of religious orders approved by the catholic Church, a threefold vow of those who live religiously and wish to follow Christ and his Apostles perfectly is drawn out and taken by all the holy religious: namely, to live without property, in chastity, and in obedience. They take it so that they may inviolably observe the life of evangelical perfection instituted by Christ for the Apostles and apostolic men, as is evidently gathered from the rules of all the holy founders approved by the universal catholic Church.

units.la: Tertio ostenditur, quod dictus Iohannes & prædictæ eius doctrinæ sequaces incidunt in damnatam hæresim Naldensium, qui bonum & meritum obedientiæ semper, quod præstatur hominibus propter Deum, dimittentur & abnegant, soli Deo sive præceptis Dei obediendum esse pertinaciter asserentes. Quia si votum viuendi sine proprio non extendit se ad res, quas vita humana necessario requirit, vt dictus Iohannes hæreticus dogmatizat; & secundum eum in rebus omnibus vsu consumptibilibus non potest separari vsus à proprietate, ita quod quilibet, qui habet vsum taliun, habet per consequens proprietatem, vt ipse hæreticus in dicto statuto Ad conditorem, & in dicto libello, Quia vir reprobus, dogmatizat: Sequitur manifeste, quod religiosi in rebus omnibus vsu consumptibilibus sive ad vitam humanam necessariis eis in singulari concessis, datis vel oblatis, habent pro-
units.tr: Thirdly, it is shown that the said John and his aforementioned followers fall into the condemned heresy of the Waldensians, who consistently reject and deny the good and the merit of obedience that is rendered to men for God's sake, and who obstinately assert that obedience is due to God alone or to God's commands. For if the vow of living without property does not extend to the things that human life necessarily requires, as this heretic John teaches, and if, according to him, use cannot be separated from ownership in all things that are consumed by use, so that whoever has the use of such things consequently has ownership, as this same heretic teaches in the said statute Ad conditorem, and in the said pamphlet Quia vir reprobus, then it clearly follows that religious, in all things consumed by use that are necessary to human life, and which are granted, given or offered to them individually, have

units.la: priedominium ac liberam secundum eorum voluntatem dispositionem: & quod possint de eis tanquam de propriis rebus facere quicquid placet absq; voluntate superiorum siue prælatorum suorum cum (lege testante) quilibet in re propria sit legitimus moderator & arbiter, C. mandati. Lin re mandata. & infra de rerum diuisione. §. per traditionem. & C. de contrahend. emp. l. diuum. & 1. q. 1. ca. eas qui. Vbi dicitur: Omnis enim Dominus, quod habet, si vult, vendit. Et re propria ac potestate faciendi de ea quod placet, nullus prinandus est sine culpa, cum 16. dist. cap. sati perueršum, & 18. quæst. vltim. cap. inuentum. Et per consequens superiores siue prælati religiosorum non habent potestatem præcipiendi ipsis subditis suis, quod de talibus rebus aliter faciant, quam ipsis subditis videatur & placeat: nec ipsi subditi tenentur eis obedire in his, quod sint sine proprio. Et sic bonum obedientiæ, quod ponitur & prædicatur per religiosos suis superioribus, euacuatur. Similiter si verum est, quod dictus hæreticus dogmatizat, scilicet quod Christus nullum modum viuendi in speciali imposuit Apostolis, nisi sicut cæteris Christianis: cum Apostoli cæteris fuerint perfectiores & maioris meriti apud Deum: sequitur quod votum obedientiæ & viuere in obedientia in his, quæ supererogationis sunt ad perfectionem, data omnibus Christianis, non est maioris meriti, quam obedientia, quæ in præceptis continentur omnibus Christianis. Et sic per hanc hæreticalem doctrinam, quicquid est perfectionis in religiosis, scilicet viuere in obedientia sine proprio & in castitate, destruitur, & religiosi per obseruantiam suæ religionis nihil plus habent de merito, quam cæteri Christiani, qui præcepta omnibus data seruant. Et si hoc modo viuentibus in religione, vt dictum est, nullum meritum sanctitatis accrescit, profiteri viuere in obedientia sine proprio & in castitate, nihil aliud est quam penitus insanire, & omnes sancti qui talem professionem fecerunt & faciendam docuerunt, per consequens errauerunt.
units.tr: ownership and free disposal of them according to their own will. They may do with them, as with their own property, whatever pleases them, without the consent of their superiors or prelates, since (as the law states) everyone is the lawful manager and arbiter of his own property (C. Mandati, Lin re mandata; below, De rerum divisione, §. per traditionem; C. De contrahenda emptione, l. diuum; and 1 q. 1, cap. Eas qui). There it is said: For every lord, if he wishes, sells what he has. And no one may be deprived of his own property and of the power to do with it what pleases him without fault, cum 16 dist. cap. Sati perversum, and 18 quaest. ultim. cap. Inuentum. Consequently, the superiors or prelates of religious do not have the power to order their subjects to deal with such things otherwise than the subjects think fit and please; nor are the subjects bound to obey them in this, that they be without property. And so the good of obedience, which the religious profess and proclaim toward their superiors, is nullified. Likewise, if it is true, as the said heretic teaches, that Christ imposed no particular mode of living on the Apostles other than that imposed on other Christians, since the Apostles were more perfect than others and of greater merit before God, it follows that the vow of obedience, and living in obedience in those things which are beyond what is required for perfection and offered to all Christians, is not of greater merit than the obedience contained in the precepts that bind all Christians. And so, by this heretical doctrine, whatever perfection there is in religious, namely living in obedience without property and in chastity, is destroyed, and religious, by observing their rule, have no more merit than other Christians who keep the precepts given to all. And if, as has been said, no merit of holiness accrues to those living in religion in this way, then to profess living in obedience without property and in chastity is nothing other than sheer madness, and all the saints who made such a profession and taught that it should be made were consequently in error.

units.la: Insuper dictus Iohannes, & dictæ eius doctrinæ sectatores iudaizant, & erroribus Iudæorum & sectæ magni Antichristi viam præparant & fomentum. Quia, sicut iam in sæpedicto libello, qui incipit, Quia vir reprobus, ipsa dicta Danielis Prophetæ & aliorum Prophetarum loquentia de regno Christi spirituali & æterno, exponit & intelligit de temporali & mundano regno, probans per ipsa prophetarum dicta, quod Christus in quantum homo fuit verus rex & Dominus in temporalibus, & Iudæi similiter dicta prophetarum loquentia de regno Christi & Messiæ futuri intelligentes ad literam de regno temporali & mundano argunt ex ipsis dictis prophetarum, quod Christus, quem Christiani colunt, non fuit ille verus Christus & Messias, quem prophetæ venturum prædicant in scripturis. Quia certum est ex Euangelio, quod ipse regnum & dominia rerum temporalium & huiusmodi diuitias non habuit nec obtinuit: imo cum Iudæi eum regem vellent facere, recusauit & dominia & diuitias huius mundi docuit relinquendas. Unde ex tali falso intellectu scripturæ prophetarum Iudæi decepti expectant Christum & Messiam venturum, qui dominium & regnum huius mundi & diuitias obtineat. Et suscipient Antichristum, qui ad literam obtinebit vniuersale dominium & regnum totius mundi ac diuitias temporales & suis sequacibus largietur. Ex quo patet, [illegible, ~20 letters] dictum hæreticum exponentem & intelligentem dicta prophetarum, sicut expo[illegible, ~30 letters] Iudæi, de dominio & regno huius mundi, paratur via & fomentum ad sectam [illegible, ~40 letters] scilicet ad credendum, quod ille qui venturus est, & vniuersale dominium & regnum [illegible, ~25 letters] diuitias habiturus, & aliis largiturus, sicut ille verus Christus & Messias in Prophetis & [illegible, ~20 letters] sicut hoc plene probant in libello Magistrorum, de quo infra dicetur, qui incipit: [illegible, ~15 letters] vult salvus esse.
units.tr: Moreover, the said John and his followers of this doctrine Judaize, and they prepare the way and provide fuel for the errors of the Jews and for the sect of the great Antichrist. For, as in the aforementioned pamphlet which begins Quia vir reprobus, they expound and understand the very words of the prophet Daniel and of the other prophets, which speak of the spiritual and eternal kingdom of Christ, as referring to a temporal and worldly kingdom, proving from the prophets' own words that Christ, as man, was a true king and lord in temporal affairs. The Jews, likewise, understanding the prophetic words about the kingdom of the Christ and Messiah to come in the literal sense of a temporal and worldly kingdom, argue from those same prophetic words that the Christ whom Christians worship was not that true Christ and Messiah whom the prophets foretold in the Scriptures. For it is certain from the Gospel that he did not have or obtain a kingdom, lordship over temporal things, or such riches; indeed, when the Jews wished to make him king, he refused, and he taught that lordship and the riches of this world should be left behind. Hence, deceived by such a false understanding of the prophetic Scriptures, the Jews await a Christ and Messiah to come who will obtain dominion and kingdom over this world and its riches. And they will receive Antichrist, who will in the literal sense obtain universal dominion and kingdom over the whole world and temporal riches, and will bestow them on his followers. From this it is evident that [illegible], since this heretic expounds and understands the words of the prophets, as the Jews do, of the dominion and kingdom of this world, a way and fuel are prepared for the sect [illegible], namely for believing that he who is to come, and who will have universal dominion and kingdom [illegible] and riches, and will bestow them on others, is that true Christ and Messiah in the Prophets and [illegible], as they fully prove in the pamphlet of the Masters, which will be discussed below, which begins: [illegible] wants to be saved.

units.la: Item prædicta etiam doctrina dicti hæretici sequitur, quod fallax & deceptoria fuit doctrina [illegible, ~10 letters] dicentis: Regnum meum non est de hoc mundo, Iohan. 18. & Augustinus super Iohannem ipsa [illegible, ~10 letters] Euangelice pertractans dicit & probat manifeste, quod regnum Christi in quantum fuit homo degens in hac vita, non fuit regnum temporale, neque de rebus temporalibus huius mundi, sed spirituale. Quia vt ibi dicit Augustinus: Regnum Christi erant credentes in eum in quibus regnabat per fidem in eorum cordibus diffusam, ad quod Christi regnum peruenitur credendo. Hæc ibi dicit. Et idem ait Augustinus in sermone de Innocentibus: Praeterea regnum illum, qui venerat in mundum iudicari temporaliter, & non iudicare. Et qui prædicabat & docebat regnum terrenum contemnere & dimittere propter regnum cælorum, non debuit esse temporale & terrenum, ne aliud faciendo & aliud prædicando eius prædicatio contemptui haberetur.
units.tr: Likewise, it also follows from the said doctrine of this heretic that the doctrine of him who said, My kingdom is not of this world (John 18), was deceptive and false. And Augustine, treating these very words of the Gospel in his commentary on John, says and clearly proves that the kingdom of Christ, insofar as he lived as a man in this life, was not a temporal kingdom, nor one concerned with temporal things of this world, but a spiritual one. For, as Augustine says there: The kingdom of Christ is those who believe in him, in whose hearts he reigns through faith poured into them, and to this kingdom of Christ one comes by believing. Thus he says there. And Augustine says the same in his sermon on the Innocents: Moreover, he who had come into the world to be judged temporally and not to judge, and who preached and taught that the earthly kingdom should be despised and forsaken for the kingdom of heaven, ought not to have been temporal and earthly, lest by doing one thing and preaching another his preaching should be held in contempt.

units.la: Item, sequitur ex dicta doctrina dicti hæretici, quod fallax & deceptoria fuit doctrina Christi, quam legitur tradidisse Iudæis, Matth. 18. mandans eis, quod tributa redderent Cæsari, cum dicit: Reddite quæ sunt Cæsaris Cæsari, & quæ sunt Dei Deo. Ex quibus verbis Euangelii colligitur euidenter, quod Cæsar illo tempore, quo Christus prædicabat, erat verus rex & Dominus in temporalibus Iudæorum. Alias non fuissent ei reddenda tributa, si Christus in quantum homo fuit in temporalibus eorum rex & Dominus. Cum duo in solidum & immediati eiusdem regni temporales reges & dominii nullatenus esse possint. Et hoc plane probatur in dicto libello Magistrorum.
units.tr: Likewise, it follows from the said doctrine of this heretic that the teaching of Christ was deceptive and false, which we read he handed down to the Jews (Matt. 18), commanding them to render tribute to Caesar, when he says: Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's. From these words of the Gospel it is clearly gathered that Caesar, at the time when Christ was preaching, was the true king and lord in temporal affairs of the Jews. Otherwise, tribute would not have been due to him, if Christ as man was king and lord in their temporal affairs. For two temporal kings and lords of the same kingdom, each holding it entirely and immediately, cannot in any way exist. And this is plainly proved in the said pamphlet of the Masters.

units.la: Sequitur etiam ex dicta doctrina dicti hæretici, quod fallax & deceptoria fuit doctrina Christi, quam tradidit Apostolis & aliis volentibus eum perfecte sequi, dicens: Si vis perfectus esse, vade & vende omnia quæ habes & da pauperibus & veni & sequere me. Quæ verba pertractans beatus Bernhardus ad Fratres de Monte Dei, dicit de Christo sic: Cum dives esset pauper pro nobis factus est. Et qui voluntariam paupertatis dedit præceptum, ipse eiusdem in semetipso formam dignatus est demonstrare. Vt enim sciant Euangelici pauperes, quid eis faciendum sit, ipse etiam à fidelibus pasci voluit, & nonnunquam etiam ab infidelibus, vt eos vt eos fideles faceret vitae necessaria reciperet non recusauit. Haec Bernhardus loquens de pauperibus religiosis, qui vouent viuere sine proprio, quos exemplo Christi dicit debere de Eleemosynis sustentari. Unde & Christus dixit: Exemplum dedi vobis, vt quemadmodum ego feci, ita & vos faciatis. Quare si Christus inquantum homo habuit vniuersale dominium omnium rerum temporalium, & illud a se nunquam abdicarit, vt dictus haereticus dogmatizat, non fecit quod docuit. Sed illis Pharisaeis, quos ipse redarguit dicens: dicunt enim & non faciunt, similis fuit, quia aliis mandauit, si vellent esse perfecti, vt dominium omnium rerum temporalium a se abdicarent, & ipse sibi illud retinuerit & nunquam abdicarit.
units.tr: It also follows from the said doctrine of this heretic that the teaching of Christ, which he handed down to the Apostles and to others who wished to follow him perfectly, was deceptive and false, when he said: If you wish to be perfect, go and sell all that you have, and give to the poor, and come and follow me. Blessed Bernard, treating these words in his letter to the brethren of Mont-Dieu, speaks thus of Christ: Though he was rich, he became poor for our sake. And he who gave the command of voluntary poverty deigned himself to show its pattern in his own person. So that the evangelical poor may know what they ought to do, he also willed to be fed by the faithful, and sometimes even by unbelievers, and he did not refuse to receive the things necessary for life, so that he might make them faithful. Thus Bernard, speaking of religious poor who vow to live without property, whom he says by Christ's example ought to be sustained by alms. Hence Christ also said: I have given you an example, that as I have done, so you also should do. Therefore, if Christ as man had universal dominion over all temporal things and never renounced it, as this heretic teaches, he did not do what he taught. He would have been like those Pharisees whom he rebuked, saying: for they say and do not do; for he commanded others, if they wished to be perfect, to renounce from themselves dominion over all temporal things, while he kept it for himself and never renounced it.

units.la: Et falsum foret, quod ipse Christus in Euangelio dicit de seipso loquens: Filius hominis non habet vbi reclinet caput suum. Unde Hieronymus & Glossa Ord. in ipsis verbis dicit sic: Quid me propter lucra saeculi vis sequi, cum ita sim pauper, vt nec hospitiolum, quod meum sit, habeam, & tecto vtar alieno. Haec Hieronymus. Ex quibus clare patet, quod Christus non habuit hospitium aliquod quantum ad dominium, sed si habuisset dominium omnium rerum, habuisset vbi caput reclinasset.
units.tr: And it would be false, what Christ himself says in the Gospel speaking of himself: "The Son of man has nowhere to lay his head." Hence Jerome and the Glossa Ordinaria, on these very words, say thus: "Why do you wish to follow me for the sake of worldly gain, when I am so poor that I do not even have a little inn that is mine, and I use another's roof?" So Jerome. From these things it is clear that Christ had no lodging at all as regards ownership; but if he had possessed dominion over all things, he would have had somewhere to lay his head.

units.la: Ex eo etiam, quod dictus haereticus per auctoritatem praedictam Danielis dicentem: Suscitabit Deus caeli regnum, quod non corrumpetur nec dissipabitur in aeternum, nititur & intendit probare, quod Christus habuit regnum & dominium vniuersale totius mundi: Sequitur alia haeresis detestanda, scilicet quod regnum Christi terrenum & mundanum secundum eam non corrumpetur nec dissipabitur in aeternum. Alias probatio & inductio sua nulla foret. Et sic secundum istum errorem sequitur, quod mundus iste sit in perpetuum duraturus. Et per consequens, quod nunquam erit generalis resurrectio mortuorum. Qui error fidei catholicae articulis obuiat manifeste.
units.tr: Further, from the fact that the said heretic, by the aforementioned authority of Daniel saying, "God will raise up a kingdom of heaven which shall never be corrupted nor destroyed for ever," strives and intends to prove that Christ had a kingdom and universal dominion over the whole world, there follows another detestable heresy, namely that according to him the earthly and worldly kingdom of Christ shall never be corrupted nor destroyed. Otherwise his proof and argument would be worthless. And so, according to this error, it follows that this world will endure forever, and consequently that there will never be a general resurrection of the dead. This error manifestly opposes the articles of the Catholic faith.

units.la: Quamobrem ego praefato Iacobo, qui Papa appellatur, primo in eius praesentia constitutus in facie restitit, firmiter asserens dictam determinationem, quam dictum generale Capitulum & etiam in decretali Exiit qui seminat, fecerat de paupertate Christi & Apostolorum esse catholicam: & contradicens assertioni suae, cum ipsam determinationem generalis Capituli dicebat haereticam, ad instar Pauli, qui Petro restitit in faciem, cum gentes iudaizare & a veritate Euangelii recedere inducebat, ad Galat. 2. Ac deinde existens in curia Auinionis, ab ipso Iacobo ad sanctam catholicam & Apostolicam Ecclesiam meo nomine & dicti Ordinis & omnium Fratrum mihi adhaerentium & adhaerere volentium, solenniter appellaui. Et sic iuxta mandatum Apostoli ad Titum primo dicentis: Hominem haereticum post primam & secundam correctionem devita. & iuxta doctrinam Ecclesiae catholicae 24. q. 3. c. dicit Dominus, ab ipsius Iacobi haeretici pertinacis obedientia & communione recessi, cum Fratribus adhaerentibus mihi, & appellationi per me interpositae & iura ad loca tuta, vt possem ipsam appellationem publicare, prosequi & innouare; ad instar sanctorum & multorum de clero Romano, quae ab obedientia & communione Anastasii Papae deuiantis a fide catholica recesserunt; vt in superius allegato cap. 19. d. c. Anastasius. Et ad instar sanctorum Athanasii & Eusebii & aliorum sanctorum, qui ad obedientia & communione Liberii Papae deuiantis a fide catholica, & sancti Hilarii Pictauensis Episcopi, qui ab obedientia & communione Leonis Papae errantis in fide catholica recesserunt, prout in Chronicis & Sanctorum legendis legitur & habetur. Et cum fui in ciuitate Pisarum, dictam appellationem innouaui & solenniter publicaui. Quam etiam interposui contra statuta haereticalia publicata & facta per Iacobum saepe dictum, & ipsam appellationem eidem Iacobo in forma publica destinaui. Unde dato sine praeiudicio, cp non fuisset tunc certum, ipsum Iacobum fuisse haereticum manifestum, & tanquam haereticum manifestum fuisse ab omnibus catholicis euitandum, sicut erat, sed dubium diceretur: tamen in tali dubio generale concilium vniuersalis Ecclesiae catholicae, quod sancta Romana Ecclesiam, ad quam per me dictis nominibus appellatum extitit, repraesentat, habebat de huiusmodi appellatione & crimine haeresis cognoscere & diffinire, sicut habetur in dicto cap. Anastasius, in textu & Glossa, super verbo concilio & rj. dist. sicut sancti in textu & Glossa & 41. d. c. si Papa. Quia in his quae fidei sunt, maius est concilium quam Papa 93. di. c. legimus in textu & Glossa: Imo si Papa a fide deuiar, minor est quocunque catholico, vt habetur & notatur 24. q. 1. c. Achatium in Glossa & 1. §. si autem, circa finem. Et ideo in omnem casum manifestum est, quod ipse Iacobus post appellationem per me interpositam non potuit contra me aliquid innouare vel facere. Quia per appellationem eximitur appellans a potestate illius, a quo appellatur, vt patet per illud, quod legitur & notatur extra, de appellatione. c. propositum in textu & Glossa. Nec is a quo appellatum est, appellatione pendente potest in praeiudicium appellantis aliquid innouare 2. q. 6. c. post appellationem. §. appellatione ff. nil no. appellatione pendente l. 1. Et maxime cum causa tangit illum, a quo appellatum siue prouocatum est, sicut tangebat dictum Iacobum, contra quem tanquam haereticum appellabam: quia in causa propria nullus potest iudicare vel ius sibi dare 22. q. 4. cap. inter querelas & q. f. c. ad occidendum. & C. ne quis in causa propria iudicet vel ius sibi dicat per totum. & 4. q. 4. c. 1. cum similibus. Ex quibus clare patet, quod ille processus, quem de facto contra me & in praeiudicium mei & mihi adhaerentium & dicti Ordinis fecit post appellationem per me dicto nomine ab ipso, vt praedictum est, interpositam, absoluendo me ab officio Generalis Ministerii dicti Ordinis, & contra me excommunicationis sententiam fulminando, & instituendo Dominum Bertrandum de Turre Vicarium generale dicti Ordinis. Et quicquid factum fuit per ipsum Dominum Bertrandum mutando terminum triennii statutum a regula & Capitulo generali, & Ministros Prouinciales legitime & per electionem statutos absoluendo absque causae cognitione, & alios Ministros nouos proprio motu absque electione aliqua instituendo, & mandando quod tales sic perperam institui Parisiis conuenirent, & Ministrum alium Generalem eligerent, & omnis electio per tales facta & quicquid ex prædictis secutum fuit, nullius extitit firmitatis: sed omnia per eos facta fuerunt nulla & irrita, & nullius prorsus roboris & momenti: sicut hæc etiam plenius ostenduntur & probantur per octo rationes insertas in allegationibus Magistrorum super hoc factis. Ac per consequens patet, quod ipse Frater Bertrandus, quem elegerunt in Generalem Ministrum, nec est, ut dixi, Generalis Minister dicti Ordinis, & quicquid egit & fecit, tanquam Generalis Minister dicti Ordinis, nullius est momenti, & quod eidem non potest sine animæ dispendio quomodolibet obediri, & quod omnes qui sibi aut aliquibus institutis in officiis aliquibus per ipsum obediunt, sunt extra obedientiam regulæ & religionis institutæ per sanctum Franciscum, & omnibus gratiis & priuilegiis dictæ religionis per sanctam catholicam Ecclesiam concessis priuari. Et quod tam ipse Bertrandus, quam omnes illi in dicta congregatione, immo verius conspiratione facta Parisiis de mandato dicti hæretici consenserunt in gestis & factis per dictum hæreticum fuerunt & sunt excommunicati & apostatæ, & in ipso Bertrando & in suis sequacibus demonstratum adimpletur, quod Beatus Franciscus Spiritu Sancto demonstrante, ut supra dictum est, prophetauit dicens: Veilli qui de sola specie religionis confisi tepescent nec resistent tentationibus ad probationem electorum permissis. Cum ipse Frater Bertrandus scribat seu scribi faciat per omnes sequaces suos verba fallacia dicens, quod Dominus Papa reputat regulam & professionem nostram sanctam, & modum viuendi secundum se sumptum bonum. Qui tamen cum regulam & professionem per dicta statuta hæreticalia euidenter pronuntiat & asserit non esse regulam, nec vitam secundum Euangelium, sed contrariam vitæ & doctrinæ Christi & sancti Euangelii: imo euidenter pronuntiat hæreticum fore asserere, quod Christus & Apostoli non habuerunt proprietatem & dominium rerum temporalium in speciali & in communi, ut superius est ostensum. Et post prædicta dictus Bertrandus in suis scriptis contradicens sibiipsi subiungit, dicens: in hæc verba, quod Dominus Papa modum Fratrum viuendi reputat discrepare à mandatis regularibus & Papalibus. Et suadet quod aliud modum viuendi bonum inquirant. Si enim discrepat à mandatis regularibus & Papalibus: & ideo alium modum viuendi bonum suadet eligi: sequitur manifeste, quod præcedens modus hactenus à sanctis Patribus dicti Ordinis obseruatus non fuit bonus nec licitus, sed illicitus & erroneus. Et ut alium modum viuendi ab illo, quia sanctis Fratribus & Patribus dicti Ordinis est hactenus obseruatus, & per consequens aliam vitam & professionem eligant, mandat ipse Giraldus & sequaces sui, ut congregentur in Festo Pentecostes apud Parpinianum. Et hoc facit, ut dicit, de mandato prædicti Iohannis, quem Papam sanctissimum asserit. Et ad demonstrandum manifeste per professionem pseudo Fratrum sequentium dictum Iacobum hæreticum, quod dicta professio & status dicti Ordinis sunt hæreticales, fertur publice, quod ipse hæreticus vult & intendit omnino, quod illi, qui congregabuntur in dicto loco de Parpiniano, abiurent literam & determinationem prefati Generalis Capituli, quæ est eadem cum determinatione facta in decretali Exiit qui seminat. In qua professio & status dicti Ordinis sunt fundati: & per consequens se & professionem & statum prædicti Ordinis fuisse hæreticos fateantur. Et si aliquando contrarium dicent, tanquam relapsi seculari iudicio comburendi sine misericordia tradantur, per capitulum extra de hereticis, ad abolendam. Quos suppostit ex nunc per suas literas patentes iurisdictioni ordinariorum & inquisitorum hæreticæ prauitatis: ita quod non solum ad animarum mortem & damnationem, sed etiam ad corporalem mortem & perpetuam & irreparabilem confusionem suos sequaces adducit. Et sic patet, quod ipse Giraldus in sola specie religionis apparentia & verborum foliis, ut dicatur de Ordine sancti Francisci, licet in veritate non fuerit, gloriatur contra illud, quod legitur 1.q.1.Marchion. Liquet igitur quod illi soli Fratres, qui dictam veritatem Euangelii & professionem dictæ Regulæ, quam voluerunt ac determinationem Ecclesiæ catholicæ in decretali, Exiit, traditam fideliter & firmiter tenent, confitentur & seruant, & usque in finem seruare volunt, sunt veri Fratres Minores & filii Beati Francisci, & in statu & via salutis, & coronam vitæ æternæ Domino concedente suscipient, sicut de ipsis dictus sanctus Franciscus, ut prædictum est, prophetauit. Et quod ad ipsos solos spectat & pertinet officium audiendi confessiones, & prædicandi, & cætera alia faciendi, quæ per priuilegia sanctæ catholicæ Ecclesiæ Fratribus Ordinis & Regulæ Francisci sunt concessa. Prædictus quoque Iacobus hæreticus vltra prædictas hæreses superius specificatas, plures alias hæreses damnatas, notorias & manifestas in dictis suis statutis & libellis publice dogmatizat, quæ seriatim continentur & explicantur tam in Appellatione maiori per me aduersus dictum Iacobum & eius hæreses interiecta, quam in aliis libris allegationum compositis per appellantes Magistros in sacra pagina: quorum vnus incipit: De patre impio querantur filii. Alius incipit: Principales hæreses. Tertius incipit: Quicunque vult saluus esse. Et rationibus & auctoritatibus diuini iuris & sanctorum doctorum Ecclesiæ, ac diffinitionibus sacrorum conciliorum Ecclesiæ catholicæ comprimuntur: quæ omnia præsentibus explicare nimis foret prolixum. Quocirca ne aliquis sub colore ignorantiæ se excusabilem esse prætendat, vobis & cuilibet vestrum districte per obedientiam iniungo, quatenus præsentes litteras in vestris Conuentibus frequenter legi, & etiam exemplari in multis partibus faciatis, quodque exemplum ipsarum litterarum, originali penes vos retento, ad omnes partes, & omnia loca dicti Ordinis vobis subsubiecta curetis velociter destinare. Et quod etiam apud cæteras personas tam Ecclesiasticas quam seculares prædicta omnia, prout securius & melius per vos fieri poterit, publicetis. Ad hoc vt prædicta veritas, iuxta meum desiderium, ad communem omnium notitiam deducatur, & publice prædicetur, ne hæreses & errores præfati hæretici ab omnibus vere catholicis detestandi animas simplicium decipiant & inuoluant, & ad æternam damnationem perducant. Valete in Domino, & orate pro renelatione veritatis doctrinæ Euangelicæ, & Regulæ almi confessoris Beati Francisci, & pro me, & Fratribus sustinentibus persecutionem maximam pro defensione huiusmodi veritatis. In quorum omnium testimonium & fidem, præsentes literas fieri feci, & sigilli officii mei munimine roborari. Datum in Monacho, vicesima quarta die mensis Ianuarii, Anno Domini millesimo trecentesimo trigesimo tertio.
units.tr: Wherefore I, Brother Michael, first appeared before the aforesaid James, who is called Pope, in his presence, and withstood him to his face, firmly asserting that the determination which the said General Chapter made concerning the poverty of Christ and the Apostles, and also in the decretal Exiit qui seminat, is catholic. I contradicted his assertion, since he called the determination of the General Chapter heretical, in the manner of Paul, who withstood Peter to his face when he was leading the Gentiles to Judaize and turning them away from the truth of the Gospel, ad Galat. 2. Then, while I was at the papal court at Avignon, I solemnly appealed from James himself to the holy catholic and apostolic Church, in my own name, in the name of the said Order, and in the name of all the Brothers who adhered to me or wished to adhere to me. Thus, in accordance with the command of the Apostle to Titus, who says first, Avoid a heretic after the first and second admonition, and in accordance with the teaching of the catholic Church, 24 q. 3 c. dicit Dominus, I withdrew from the obedience and communion of this heretical and obstinate James, together with the Brothers adhering to me. I did so in order to publish, pursue and renew the appeal I had lodged, and I sought safe places to do it. I acted in the manner of the saints and of many of the Roman clergy, who withdrew from the obedience and communion of Pope Anastasius when he turned aside from the catholic faith, as stated in the cap. 19 d. c. Anastasius cited above. I acted also in the manner of the saints Athanasius and Eusebius and other saints, who withdrew from the obedience and communion of Pope Liberius when he turned aside from the catholic faith, and of the holy Hilary, bishop of Poitiers, who withdrew from the obedience and communion of Pope Leo when he erred in the catholic faith, as is read and found in the Chronicles and the Lives of the Saints. When I was in the city of Pisa, I renewed the said appeal and solemnly published it. I also lodged it against the heretical statutes published and made by the James so often mentioned, and I sent the appeal to James himself in public form. Accordingly, even granting, without prejudice, that it had not then been certain that this James was a manifest heretic, and that as a manifest heretic he was to be avoided by all catholics, as in fact he was, but that it might be called doubtful: nevertheless, in such a doubt the general council of the universal catholic Church, which the holy Roman Church represents, and to which the appeal was made by me under the said names, had the right to take cognizance of such an appeal and of the crime of heresy, and to decide them, as is found in the said cap. Anastasius, in text and gloss, under the word concilio, and in dist. 17 sicut sancti, in text and gloss, and 41 d. c. si Papa. For in matters that concern the faith, the council is greater than the Pope, 93 d. c. legimus, in text and gloss. Indeed, if the Pope turns aside from the faith, he is less than any catholic whatever, as is held and noted in 24 q. 1 c. Achatium, in the gloss, and in 1 §. si autem, near the end. And therefore, in every case, it is clear that this James, after the appeal lodged by me, could not do anything new against me. For by appeal the appellant is withdrawn from the power of the one from whom he appeals, as is plain from what is read and noted in extra, de appellatione, c. propositum, in text and gloss. Nor can the one from whom the appeal is made, while the appeal is pending, innovate anything to the prejudice of the appellant, 2 q. 6 c. post appellationem, §. appellatione; ff. nil innovetur appellatione pendente l. 1. This holds especially when the cause touches the very man from whom the appeal is made or to whom it is brought, as it touched the said James, against whom I was appealing as a heretic. For no one can judge in his own cause or give himself a right, 22 q. 4 cap. inter querelas; q. f. c. ad occidendum; C. ne quis in causa propria iudicet vel ius sibi dicat per totum; and 4 q. 4 c. 1, with similar passages. From these things it is clearly evident that the proceeding which he carried out against me, to my prejudice and to the prejudice of those adhering to me and of the said Order, after the appeal lodged by me in the said name, as has been said, was null: he absolved me from the office of General Minister of the said Order, fulminated the sentence of excommunication against me, and appointed Lord Bertrand de Turre as Vicar General of the said Order. Whatever was done by the said Lord Bertrand, by changing the three-year term established by the Rule and the General Chapter, by absolving the Provincial Ministers who had been lawfully appointed by election, without any hearing of the case, by installing other new Ministers on his own initiative without any election, and by ordering that those so wrongly installed should meet at Paris and elect another General Minister, and every election made by such men, and whatever followed from these things, had no force at all. All these things were null and void, of no strength or weight whatever, as is shown and proved more fully by the eight arguments inserted in the pleadings of the Masters made on this matter. Consequently it is plain that this Brother Bertrand, whom they elected as General Minister, is not, as I have said, General Minister of the said Order, that whatever he did or performed as General Minister of the said Order is of no moment, and that no one can in any way obey him without peril to the soul. Everyone who obeys him, or those whom he has installed in any offices, is outside the obedience of the Rule and of the religion instituted by St. Francis, and is deprived of all the graces and privileges of the said religion granted by the holy catholic Church. And that both this Bertrand and all those in that assembly, or rather conspiracy, held at Paris by order of the said heretic, who have agreed to the acts and deeds of the said heretic, are excommunicate and apostates. In Bertrand himself and in his followers is fulfilled what Blessed Francis, under the guidance of the Holy Spirit, as has been said above, prophesied when he said: Those who trust in the mere outward form of religion will grow lukewarm and will not resist the temptations permitted for the testing of the elect. For this Brother Bertrand writes, or causes all his followers to write, deceitful words, saying that the Lord Pope regards our Rule and profession as holy, and the manner of life taken according to itself as good. Yet when, by the said heretical statutes, he plainly pronounces and asserts that this Rule and profession is not the Rule, nor a life according to the Gospel, but contrary to the life and teaching of Christ and the holy Gospel, indeed he plainly pronounces that whoever asserts that Christ and the Apostles had no ownership or lordship over temporal goods, either individually or in common, is a heretic, as has been shown above. After these things, the said Bertrand, contradicting himself in his writings, adds, saying in these words: The Lord Pope judges that the manner of life of the Brothers differs from the regular and papal commands, and he advises that they seek another good manner of life. For if it differs from the regular and papal commands, and therefore he advises that another good manner of life be chosen, it clearly follows that the manner of life previously observed by the holy Brothers and Fathers of the said Order was not good or lawful, but unlawful and erroneous. And, so that they may choose another manner of life, different from the one hitherto observed by the holy Brothers and Fathers of the said Order, and consequently another life and profession, this Giraldus and his followers order that they gather at Parpignano on the Feast of Pentecost. He does this, as he says, by the command of the aforesaid John, whom he calls the most holy Pope. And, to show plainly through the profession of the pseudo-Brothers who follow the said James that the said profession and state of the said Order are heretical, it is publicly reported that this heretic wants and entirely intends that those who gather in the said place of Parpignano should abjure the letter and the determination of the aforesaid General Chapter, which is the same as the determination made in the decretal Exiit qui seminat, on which the profession and state of the said Order are founded. Consequently they would confess that they themselves, their profession and the state of the said Order were heretical. And if at any time they say the contrary, they are to be handed over, as relapsed, without mercy to the secular judgment for burning, by the chapter Extra de hereticis, Ad abolendam. From now on, by his open letters, he subjects them to the jurisdiction of the ordinaries and inquisitors of heretical depravity. Thus he leads his followers not only to the death and damnation of their souls, but also to bodily death and to perpetual and irreparable confusion. And so it is plain that Giraldus, relying only on the outward appearance of religion and on empty words, so that he may be called of the Order of St. Francis, though in truth he is not, glories against that which is read in 1 q. 1 Marchion. It is therefore clear that those Brothers alone who faithfully and firmly hold, confess and keep the said truth of the Gospel and the profession of the said Rule, which they have willed, and the determination of the catholic Church handed down in the decretal Exiit, and who wish to keep it to the end, are the true Brothers Minor and sons of Blessed Francis, and are in the state and way of salvation, and with the Lord granting it they will receive the crown of eternal life, as the said St. Francis, as has been said, prophesied concerning them. And the office of hearing confessions, preaching, and doing the other things that have been granted to the Brothers of the Order and Rule of Francis by the privileges of the holy catholic Church, belongs to them alone and pertains to them. Moreover, this heretic James, beyond the heresies specified above, publicly teaches many other condemned, notorious and manifest heresies in his said statutes and pamphlets. These are set out and explained in order, both in the greater appeal which I lodged against the said James and his heresies, and in the other books of pleadings composed by the appealing Masters in sacred Scripture. One of these begins: Let the sons complain of the impious father. Another begins: The principal heresies. The third begins: Whoever wishes to be saved. These heresies are repressed by the reasons and authorities of divine law, of the holy teachers of the Church, and by the decisions of the holy councils of the catholic Church. To explain all these things here would be too lengthy. Therefore, so that no one may pretend that he is excusable under the colour of ignorance, I order you, and each of you, strictly and under obedience, that you have these present letters frequently read in your convents, and that you also have copies made in many places. And that you take care to send a copy of these letters, while keeping the original with you, quickly to all the parts and all the places of the said Order subject to you. And that you also publish all the aforesaid matters among other persons, both ecclesiastical and secular, as securely and as well as you can. This is so that the aforesaid truth, according to my desire, may be brought to the common knowledge of all and be publicly preached, and that the heresies and errors of the aforesaid heretic, to be detested by all truly catholic people, may not deceive and ensnare the souls of simple people and lead them to eternal damnation. Farewell in the Lord, and pray for the revelation of the truth of the Evangelical doctrine and of the Rule of the kindly confessor Blessed Francis, and for me and the Brothers who are enduring the greatest persecution in defence of this truth. In witness and faith of all these things I have caused these present letters to be made and strengthened with the protection of the seal of my office. Given at Munich, on the twenty-fourth day of January, in the year of our Lord one thousand three hundred and thirty-three.

units.la: SEQVVNTVR LITERÆ DEPRECATORIÆ FRATRIS MICHAELIS DE CESE- NA OLIM MINISTRI GENERALIS FRATRVM MINORVM, ad Regem Romanorum & Principes Alemaniæ. In quibus re- citantur & improbantur duodecim errores ipsius iudicio collecti, ex consti- tutionibus Iohannis 22. iuxta quod in totidem partes diuidi possant.
units.tr: LETTERS OF ENTREATY OF BROTHER MICHAEL OF CESENA, FORMERLY MINISTER GENERAL OF THE FRIARS MINOR, TO THE KING OF THE ROMANS AND THE PRINCES OF GERMANY. In which twelve errors, gathered by his judgment from the constitutions of John XXII, are recited and refuted, according to the twelve parts into which they can be divided.

units.la: Serenissimo ac Christianissimo Principi, Ludovico Dei gratia Romanorum Monarchæ, pauperum patri, catholicæ fidei propugili & semper Augusto, cæterisq; Principibus, Baronibus & nobilibus secum in Parlamento existentibus: Frater Michael Ordinis Fratrum Minorum Generalis Minister & seruus licet indignus, cum Magistris & aliis Fratribus sibi in veritate adhærentibus, cum omni humilitate, devotione & subiectione ipsum seipsum. Quoniam, vt habetur 96. dist. Duo sunt, quibus principaliter hic mundus regitur: auctoritas sacra pontificum, & regalis potestas.
