units.tr: As to the fifth point, which concerns contracts entered into before a secular judge: he says that since suits over such contracts are personal by law, especially where there is a breach of oath or a broken faith, of which the Church alone has cognizance, no wrong is done. And even where there was no breach of oath or faith, cognizance may still belong to the Church by reason of the personal character of the suit. To prove this answer he cited the laws alleged above in the preceding articles.

units.la: Ad sextum, qui loquitur de conciliis prouincialibus & statutis synodalibus, dicit idem episcopus, quod pro sanctis & iustis tanquam sancti patres instituerunt ea teneri, & quod praelati nihil statuant ibi, quod temporalitatem tangat, nisi quatenus commissarum sibi animarum tangit salutem, & iura & libertates ecclesiarum esse seruandas, & hoc eis licitum esse facere, & ad hoc probandum induxit in autenticis, de sanct. episcoporum §. vt autem col. 9. in decretis 18. distinct. per totum.
units.tr: As to the sixth point, which concerns provincial councils and synodal statutes: the same bishop says that they are to be observed as holy and just, since the holy fathers established them, and that prelates decree nothing there that touches temporal affairs except insofar as it touches the salvation of the souls committed to them; that the rights and liberties of the churches must be preserved; and that it is lawful for them to do this. To prove this he cited Authenticis, de sanct. episcoporum, §. vt autem, col. 9, and in the Decretum, distinction 18, throughout.

units.la: Ad septimum, qui loquitur de contractibus recipiendis per notarios ecclesiasticos in terris seculariu, dicit quod tam de ratione naturali, quam de iure praescripto in terris Dominorum temporalium ecclesia habebat iurisdictionem suam spiritualem, sicut Dominus temporalis suam temporalem. Nulli infertur iniuria, si notarii tales recipiant contractus illorum, qui volunt se in foro ecclesiae obligare, & hoc est pro communi & publica utilitate, quia multi magis eligunt vinculum ecclesiae quam vinculum temporale, & ante dimitterent contractus facere, sine quibus viuere non possent, quam se supponerent curiae seculari, maxime de consuetudine notariorum est & fuit semper obseruatum, & ad hoc probandum allegauit idem Episcopus, extra de off. or. cum episcopus l. 6. ff. de off. pr. consulis l. 2.
units.tr: As to the seventh point, which concerns contracts received by ecclesiastical notaries in the lands of secular lords: he says that both by natural reason and by prescribed law, the Church has its spiritual jurisdiction in the lands of temporal lords, just as a temporal lord has his temporal jurisdiction. No one is wronged if such notaries receive the contracts of those who wish to bind themselves in the forum of the Church. This serves the common and public good, because many prefer the bond of the Church to a temporal bond, and would rather forgo making contracts, without which they could not live, than submit themselves to the secular court. Moreover, it is and always has been the custom of notaries to do this. To prove it the same bishop cited extra de off. or. cum episcopus, l. 6. ff. de off. pr., and consulis l. 2.

units.la: Ad octauum, qui loquitur de officialibus, qui crimina imponunt laicis, vt se redimant &c. dicit idem, quod nullus praelatus, si sciret talia facere suum officialem, aliqualiter sustineret, nisi esset de maleficiis, quorum cognitio ad ecclesiam pertinet & correctio de consuetudine vel de iure, & etiam in casibus, vbi recredentia fieri non deberet, & si quis esset, qui in speciali vellet conqueri super istis, erant parati, veritate prius inquisita, prout iustitia esset, facere emendam & apponere remedium opportunum.
units.tr: As to the eighth point, which concerns officials who impose crimes on laymen so that they may ransom themselves, etc.: the same bishop says that no prelate, if he knew that his official did such things, would tolerate it in any way, except in cases of wrongdoing, the cognizance and correction of which belong to the Church by custom or by law, and also in cases where a denunciation ought not to be made. And if anyone wished to complain of these matters in particular, they were ready, once the truth had first been inquired into, to make amends as justice required and to apply a suitable remedy.

units.la: Ad nonum, qui loquitur de officialibus, qui inquirunt super maleficiis & ab innocentibus volunt habere expensas & emendas: & expensas reddere nolunt, si succumbant in causa, dicit Episcopus quod si praelati scirent ista per officiales fieri, secundum quod in articulo proponuntur, nollent ista sustinere: sed vbi illi, contra quos proceditur, petunt copiam processuum sibi fieri, tenetur petens eam soluere, aut si super imposito sibi maleficio condamnetur, debet expensas restituere promotori. Si vero per iudicem absoluatur, & promotor malitiose & per fraudem hoc falsè suggesserit contra ipsum, debent ei expensae restitui, sed vbi mere ex officio proceditur, siue per famam publicam siue ad denuntiationem alicuius vel alias secundum quod licitum est de iure, iudex in hoc casu expensas cuiquam restituere non tenetur.
units.tr: As to the ninth point, which concerns officials who inquire into crimes and want to have the expenses and fines from innocent persons, and refuse to repay the expenses if they lose the case: the bishop says that if prelates knew that these things were done by officials in the way set out in the article, they would not tolerate them. But where those against whom proceedings are brought ask for a copy of the records to be given to them, the one asking must pay for it; or if he is condemned on the crime imputed to him, he must repay the expenses to the promoter. If, however, he is acquitted by the judge, and the promoter has maliciously and fraudulently made a false accusation against him, the expenses must be restored to him. But where proceedings are begun purely of office, whether on public report, or on the information of someone, or otherwise as the law permits, the judge in such a case is not bound to restore expenses to anyone.

units.la: Ad 10. qui loquitur de sententiis excommunicationis, quae dantur pro sola vna citatione, dicit idem episcopus, quod nullo modo sententia excommunicationis debet fieri, nisi citatio vel monitio praecesserit sufficienter. Sed saepe contingit, quod propter periculum animarum aut corporum, aut quia est causa fauorabilis, vel propter alias causas iustas, quae cōtinentur in iure, fit vna citatio peremptoria, quae valet tres, & tunc propter talem defectum poterit licite sententia excommunicationis ferri.
units.tr: As to the tenth point, which concerns sentences of excommunication given on the strength of a single citation: the same bishop says that a sentence of excommunication must in no way be pronounced unless a citation or warning has gone before, sufficiently. Yet it often happens that, on account of danger to souls or bodies, or because the cause is favourable, or for other just reasons contained in the law, a single peremptory citation is issued, which is valid for three. In such a case, because of this defect, a sentence of excommunication may lawfully be pronounced.

units.la: Ad 11. qui loquitur de obligationibus de nisi, dicit quod est secundum formam iuris, & pro communi utilitate statutum, nec sequitur ex hoc inconueniens, maxime quia in talibus nunquam fertur vel ferri debet sententia, nisi prius sufficientem terminum adhuc de consensu contrahentium assignatum, & ad hoc probandum induxit c. praeterea. de appell.
units.tr: As to the eleventh point, which concerns obligations "de nisi": he says that it is according to the form of law and established for the common good, and no inconvenience follows from it, especially since in such cases a sentence is never, or ought never to be, pronounced until a sufficient term has first been assigned, with the consent of the contracting parties. To prove this he cited c. praeterea, de appell.

units.la: Ad 12. qui loquitur de monitionibus, quae fiunt contra iudices seculares ad compellendum excommunicatos per captionem honorum &c. dixit praefatus Episcopus, quod cum ecclesia suo brachio spirituali contra tales procedendo fecit quod potuit, tunc habet recurrere ad brachium seculare, & hoc de iure diuino & humano conceditur. Et si propter malitiam vel negligentiam Dominus temporalis omittat factae sup hoc monitioni parere, & talem excommunicatum compellere, propter quod contingat debitorem amittere debitum, in quo excommunicatus tenebatur eidem, non est inconueniens, si sufficienti monitione praevia per sententiam excommunicationis, procedituir contra eum, & si de danis illatis nunc mereatur absolui, faciat satisfactionem competentem & condignam, in talibus enim de iure diuino & humano brachium temporale spirituali debet obedire, maxime vbi quis in excommunicatione persistit vltra annum, de quo in statuto beati Ludouici mentio fit expressa.
units.tr: As to the twelfth point, which concerns warnings issued against secular judges to compel the excommunicated, by seizure of goods, etc.: the aforesaid bishop said that since the Church, by proceeding against such people with its spiritual arm, has done what it could, it must then have recourse to the secular arm; and this is granted by divine and human law. And if, through malice or negligence, a temporal lord neglects to obey the warning given on this matter and to compel such an excommunicated person, so that the creditor loses the debt that the excommunicated person owed him, it is no inconvenience if, after a sufficient warning has been given, proceedings are taken against him by sentence of excommunication. And if he should now deserve to be absolved from the damages inflicted, he is to make adequate and proper satisfaction. For in such matters, by divine and human law, the temporal arm must obey the spiritual, especially where someone persists in excommunication for more than a year, which is expressly mentioned in the statute of blessed Louis.

units.la: Ad 13. qui loquitur de expensis, quas faciunt iudices seculares veniendo ad excusandum se coram iudicibus ecclesiasticis super compulsione excommunicatorum: dicit, quod postquam de iure & consuetudine tenentur in hoc iudices seculares iudici ecclesiastico obedire, debent cum expensis propriis ad excusandum se venire. Sed si talis monitio malitiose vel indebite ad suggestionem alicuius fuerit impetrata, talis suggerens ad restitutionem expensarum tenetur. Expensæ vero, quæ fuerunt in excommunicatione contra excommunicatum factæ, per prædictos iudices seculares excommunicatus ipse debet ad restitutionem compelli.
units.tr: As to the thirteenth point, which concerns the expenses that secular judges incur in coming to excuse themselves before ecclesiastical judges concerning the compulsion of the excommunicated: he says that since by law and custom secular judges are bound in this matter to obey the ecclesiastical judge, they must come at their own expense to excuse themselves. But if such a warning was obtained maliciously or without due cause at someone's suggestion, the one who made the suggestion is bound to make restitution of the expenses. The expenses incurred against the excommunicated person in the excommunication, however, are to be recovered from the excommunicated person himself by the said secular judges.

units.la: Ad 14. qui loquitur de appellationibus, quæ fiunt in curiis laicorum ad ecclesiasticos iudices, dicit idem episcopus, quod si in curia temporali prælatorum vel subditorum suorum fiat processus, aut detur iudicium temporale, & super huiusmodi processu aut iudicio appellatio ordinaria aut ratione falsi iudicii vel alias sequeretur, debet talis appellatio remitti ad examen sui iudicis temporalis, scilicet si laicus non per viam iurisdictionis ordinariæ: sed quia magis eligit ecclesiasticam curiam, quam temporalem, sicut de iure & consuetudine licitum eis extitit, tunc nullum inconveniens sequeretur, si officialis ad quem veniret talis cognitio, tanquam officialis & iudex ordinarius cognitionem haberet, & sic in Remensis, Laudunensis, ac in multis aliis regni Franciæ ecclesiis observatur, & probari posset per aliqua iura superius allegata.
units.tr: As to the fourteenth point, which concerns appeals made from lay courts to ecclesiastical judges: the same bishop says that if proceedings are carried out, or a temporal judgment given, in the temporal court of prelates or of their subjects, and an ordinary appeal, or an appeal on the ground of a false judgment or otherwise, follows upon such proceedings or judgment, such an appeal must be sent back for examination to the temporal judge, namely if the layman has not come by the ordinary course of jurisdiction, but because he prefers the ecclesiastical court to the temporal one, as it has been lawful for them by law and custom. Then no inconvenience would follow if the official to whom such cognizance came had it as official and ordinary judge. And so it is observed in the churches of Rheims, Laon and many other churches of the kingdom of France, and it could be proved by some of the laws alleged above.

units.la: Ad 15. qui loquitur de arrestis, quæ fiunt in villis, quæ vtuntur lege, dicit quod si talia fierent, sicut in articulo continetur, nisi de consuetudine aliqua ecclesiæ hoc haberent, quæ consuetudo est observanda, maxime vbi tale fieret sub aliquo conductu curiæ & sine fraude, & quod arrestatus non esset alicuius prælati clericus, nollent ea sustinere, ideo &c.
units.tr: As to the fifteenth point, which concerns arrests made in the towns that use the law: he says that if such arrests were made as the article describes, unless they had some custom of the church for this, which custom must be observed, especially where such an arrest were made under some safe-conduct of the court and without fraud, and the person arrested were not a cleric of some prelate, they would not be willing to tolerate them. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Ad 16. qui loquitur de illis, qui dicuntur præpositi clericorum, dicit quod tam de ratione quam de iure & consuetudine quilibet prælatus in quacunque parte suæ dioecesis potest habere officiales suos, & alias personas ad iurisdictionem ecclesiasticam exercendam, sive sit in citationibus, sive in captionibus personarum ecclesiasticarum, vel cognitione causarum, quæ ad forum ecclesiæ pertinent, & potest talibus illam, quæ sibi videtur, concedere potestatem, quare si tales iuxta commissionem sibi factam citationes faciant, aut personas ecclesiasticas capiant delinquentes, sive cognitionem causarum assumant, seu aliis quocunque modo ecclesiasticam iurisdictionem exercent, nulla sit iniuria. Quilibet enim Dominus temporalis vbicunque in terra sua potest habere gentes & iustitiarios suos, & eadem ratione & spiritualis iudex. Sed si tales commissarii abusi fuerint in aliquo, seu etiam abutantur, parati erunt prælati tales abusus corrigere, & apponere remedium opportunum, vel si alicubi sit talium commissariorum nimia multitudo, ipsi de sufficienti numero prouidebunt. Cæterum si tales commissarii iuxta potestatem sibi commissam arrestauerint in casu licito de iure bona mobilia clericorum, nullus laicus habet super hoc materiam conquerendi, nam bona mobilia sequuntur possidentem personam tam de consuetudine quam de iure, & hoc etiam in statutis regni Franciæ continetur.
units.tr: On 16, which speaks of those called provosts of the clergy, he says that by reason, by law and by custom alike, any prelate in any part of his diocese may have his own officials and other persons to exercise ecclesiastical jurisdiction, whether in issuing citations, in arresting ecclesiastical persons, or in hearing causes that belong to the Church's forum. He may grant such persons whatever power seems fit to him. So if such commissaries issue citations according to the commission given them, or arrest offending ecclesiastical persons, or take up the hearing of causes, or exercise ecclesiastical jurisdiction in any other way, no wrong is done. For any temporal lord may have his own agents and justices anywhere in his land, and by the same reasoning a spiritual judge may too. But if such commissaries have abused their power in any way, or still abuse it, the prelates will be ready to correct such abuses and apply a suitable remedy; or if in some place there is too great a number of such commissaries, they will provide a sufficient number. Moreover, if such commissaries, acting within the power committed to them, have in a lawful case arrested the movable goods of clerics, no layman has any ground for complaint on this point, for movable goods follow the person who possesses them, both by custom and by law, and this is also contained in the statutes of the kingdom of France.

units.la: Ad 17. & 18. est responsum, quia spiritualis iurisdictio clericorum & bonorum suorum mobilium in quacunque parte dioecesis pertinet ad prælatos. Et ad ista probanda inducit 4. Reg. 7. vbi dicitur quod Samuel iudex Israel ibat & circuibat Bethel, & Galgala, & Malphat, & adhuc etiam inducit extra de off. ordi. cum episcopus.
units.tr: On 17 and 18 the answer is given: the spiritual jurisdiction over clerics and their movable goods, in any part of the diocese, belongs to the prelates. To prove this he cites 4 Kings 7, where it is said that Samuel, judge of Israel, went about and circuited Bethel, Gilgal and Mizpah; and he also cites extra, de officio ordinarii, cum episcopus.

units.la: Ad 19. qui loquitur de assecuramento, quod petitur in curia ecclesiastica, dicit dictus episcopus, quod tam de iure quam de consuetudine clericus potest malefactorem suum vel illum, a quo verisimiliter dubitat sibi iniuriam irrogari, coram ecclesiastico iudice convenire, quia si per laicum committeretur maleficium in personam clerici, ecclesia tanquam de sacrilegio cognosceret super maleficio memorato, ergo faciliori ratione potest etiam prouidere dando assecuramenta, ne talia maleficia committantur, specialiter in ecclesiis, vbi hoc de consuetudine speciali habetur. Si autem hoc esset inter duos laicos, debet consuetudo seruari, quæ etiam in hoc concordat cum iure communi, per quod ecclesiastici iudices debent pacem apponere & peccata vitare, quia melius est peccanti ante temporis occurrere, quam culpam post vindictam vindicare. Et ad hoc probandum inducit iura superius allegata & extra de treuga & pace, per totum.
units.tr: On 19, which speaks of the security that is sought in the ecclesiastical court, the said bishop says that, both by law and by custom, a cleric may summon before an ecclesiastical judge a man who has wronged him, or one from whom he reasonably fears injury. For if a wrong were committed by a layman against the person of a cleric, the Church would take cognizance of the aforesaid wrong as a sacrilege. Therefore, by a still easier reasoning, it may also provide by granting securities, so that such wrongs are not committed, especially in churches where this is held by special custom. If, however, this were a matter between two laymen, the custom must be observed, and this too agrees with the common law, by which ecclesiastical judges ought to keep the peace and avoid sin, because it is better to forestall a sinner in time than to avenge the fault afterwards. To prove this he cites the laws quoted above and extra, de treuga et pace, throughout.

units.la: Ad 20. qui loquitur de inuentariis, quæ fiunt de bonis laicorum, dicit tam de iure sanctorum patrum, quam imperatorum & regum, quilibet prælatus in sua dioecesi est executor legitimus testamentorum, maxime elapso termino expresso in iure. Vnde si contigerit, quod executio testamenti venerit ad prælatum, non est inconveniens, si ex quo ad eum pertinet principale, pertineat accessorium siue sit in inuentariis, siue in aliis faciendis, specialiter in locis, vbi de consuetudine obseruatur, alias enim posset minime fieri executio testamenti, ad ista vero probanda inducit C. de sacro sanct. eccle. l. 1. & melius C. de episcopis & cle. l. nulli in autem de eccle. ti. §. si quis autem col. 9. extra de testamentis c. tua & c. nos quidem & c. Iohannes. C. de fide commissa autem amplius hac, cum aliis.
units.tr: On 20, which speaks of the inventories made of the goods of laymen, he says that by the law of the holy Fathers, and of emperors and kings alike, every prelate in his own diocese is the lawful executor of wills, especially once the term fixed by law has expired. Hence, if it happens that the execution of a will has come to the prelate, it is no objection that, since the principal matter belongs to him, the incidental matter also belongs to him, whether it be in making inventories or in other acts, especially in places where this is observed by custom; otherwise the execution of the will could hardly be carried out. To prove this he cites C. de sacrosanctis ecclesiis, l. 1, and more fully C. de episcopis et clericis, l. nulli, and in authenticum de ecclesiis, tit. §. si quis autem, col. 9; extra de testamentis, c. tua, c. nos quidem, and c. Iohannes. C. de fideicommissis, however, more on this, with others.

units.la: Ad 21. qui loquitur de hypothecariis actionibus, dicit idem episcopus, quod si hypothecaria procedat ex contractibus, vbi sit iuramenti vel fidei interpositio: & inde fiat directe petitio siue petitio super re obligata, talis petitio plus est personalis, quam realis: & in hoc casu nulla fiet iniuria. Quantum autem ad hypothecarias, quæ sunt reales, debet consuetudo seruari, quod si nulla fuerit consuetudo super hoc, dicebat dictus episcopus, ius scriptum esse in talibus sequendum. Et ad hoc probandum allegauit C. de præscript. 30. vel 40. annorum, l. cum notissimi, extra. de iureiurando si vero.
units.tr: On 21, which speaks of hypothecary actions, the same bishop says that if a hypothecary action arises from contracts in which an oath or pledge of faith is interposed, and a claim is then made directly, that is, a claim upon the obligated thing, such a claim is more personal than real, and in this case no wrong will be done. As for hypothecary actions that are real, custom must be observed; but if there is no custom on this point, the said bishop said that the written law is to be followed in such matters. To prove this he cited C. de praescriptione 30 vel 40 annorum, l. cum notissimi, and extra, de iureiurando, si vero.

units.la: Ad vicesimum secundum, qui loquitur de personis Hospitalium, dicit quod si tales personæ sint perpetuo donatæ Hospitali seu domorum eius, huiusmodi quidem factæ sunt de foro ecclesiæ elesiæ, & talium cognitio pertinet ad prælatos. De aliis vero, qui non essent talis conditionis, nisi ius, priuilegium, vel consuetudo aliud daret ecclesiis, prælatos de hoc se velle minime intromittere asse‑ rebat idem episcopus.
units.tr: On the twenty-second, which speaks of the persons of hospitals, he says that if such persons have been perpetually given to a hospital or to its houses, they were indeed made subject to the forum of the Church, and the cognizance of them belongs to the prelates. But as for others who were not of such a condition, the same bishop asserted that the prelates would by no means wish to meddle in this, unless law, privilege or custom gave otherwise to the churches.

units.la: Ad 23. qui loquitur de tonsuris dandis indignis: dicit quod quanto plures sunt digni in Dei seruitio constituti, tanto melius potest diuinum seruitium celebrari. Et bene cauebunt Domini Prælati Deo ducente, quod non conferent personis insufficientibus & indignis. Nullus enim Prælatus bonæ conscientiæ faceret ea, quæ in dicto articulo continentur, & vere super huiusmodi tonsuris conferendis, Domini temporales plures & inopportunas requestas prælatis facere consueuerunt.
units.tr: On 23, which speaks of conferring tonsures on the unworthy, he says that the more worthy men are placed in God's service, the better the divine service can be celebrated. And the lord prelates, God willing, will take good care not to confer them on insufficient and unworthy persons. For no prelate of good conscience would do what is contained in the said article; and indeed, temporal lords have often made many importunate requests of prelates for the conferring of such tonsures.

units.la: Ad 24. qui loquitur de viduis, pupillis & intestatis, dicit idem episcopus, quod de iure diuino & humano gardia talium personarum quantum ad violentias & saisinas pertinet ad ecclesiam: & sic de consuetudine obseruatur in ecclesiis Gallicanis quantum ad bona intestatorum & pupillorum: dicit quod in ecclesiis, vbi esset consuetudo super hoc specialis, debet eadem consuetudo seruari: vbi autem non esset, quantum tangit petitoriam cognitionem, ecclesia nolebat se intromittere, nisi hoc haberet ex priuilegio vel consuetudine speciali. Et ad hoc inducit 24. q. 3. c. si quis de potentibus, extra de foro compe. ex tenore & c. ex parte.
units.tr: On 24, which speaks of widows, orphans and those who die intestate, the same bishop says that by divine and human law the guardianship of such persons, so far as violent seizures and possessions are concerned, belongs to the Church; and so by custom it is observed in the Gallican churches as regards the goods of intestates and of orphans. He says that in churches where there is a special custom on this, the same custom must be observed; but where there is none, so far as it touches a petitory cognizance, the Church would not wish to meddle, unless it had this by privilege or special custom. To this he cites 24 q. 3, c. si quis de potentibus; extra de foro competenti, ex tenore, etc.; ex parte.

units.la: Ad 25. qui loquitur de impositionibus, quas officiales faciunt laicis super fide: dicit quod hoc est irrationabile, si alicui tale crimen imponeretur malitiose, prout in articulo continetur, sed vbi aliquis habetur suspectus super articulis fidei, ad ecclesiam in hoc casu debet cognitio pertinere: & per consequens propter inquestam & alios processus faciendos oportet iudicem ecclesiasticum de persona saisitum esse: & lata sententia contra eam expediri brachio seculari, quare in his nulla iniuria irrogatur, maxime in locis, vbi sic consuetudine obseruatur à tanto tempore, quod in contrarium hominum memoria non existit.
units.tr: On 25, which speaks of the accusations that officials make against laymen concerning the faith, he says that it is unreasonable if such a crime is imputed to anyone maliciously, as is contained in the article. But where someone is held suspect on articles of faith, cognizance ought in this case to belong to the Church; and consequently, because of the inquest and the other proceedings that must be carried out, the ecclesiastical judge must have taken hold of the person; and once sentence has been passed against him, he is to be handed over to the secular arm. Therefore in these matters no wrong is done, especially in places where it is observed by custom from such a long time that the memory of men does not run to anything to the contrary.

units.la: Ad 26. qui loquitur de officialibus currentibus: dicit quod prælati possunt habere in quacumque parte dioecesis tam de ratione quam de iure scripto & consuetudine officiales suos, secundum quod superius est ostensum, quare nulli fit iniuria.
units.tr: On 26, which speaks of the running officials, he says that prelates may have their officials in any part of the diocese, by reason, by written law and by custom, as has been shown above; therefore no one is wronged.

units.la: Ad 27. qui loquitur de pœnis pecuniariis, quas officiales in suis monitionibus apponunt: dicit quod licitum est eis tales pœnas apponere tam de consuetudine quam de iure: quia ex quo licet sententiam excommunicationis apponere, quæ est maior, licet apponere pœnam pecuniariam, quæ est minor. Item ex quo tali iudici ecclesiastico subditi existunt, & sic est eorum ordinarius, iudex ipse potest in tali casu eis apponere pecuniariam vel aliam secundum quod sibi videbitur expedire. Et ad hoc, ius diuinum & humanum concordant. Ad hoc probandum allegauit de pœnis c. licet de officio cum c. dilectus 23. q. 5. c. sinos 22. q. 4. c. quisquis, &, si quis mut. Deus etiam infligebat pœnas tales aliquando Leuit. 3. 4. & 5. c. Exod. 23. c. si quis furatus fuerit, ad hoc facit 23. q. 5. pro-dest.
units.tr: On 27, which speaks of the pecuniary penalties that officials attach to their monitions, he says that it is lawful for them to attach such penalties, both by custom and by law: since it is permitted to pronounce the sentence of excommunication, which is the greater, it is permitted to impose a pecuniary penalty, which is the lesser. Likewise, since such subjects are under an ecclesiastical judge, and he is thus their ordinary, the judge himself may in such a case impose on them a fine or other penalty as he thinks fit. Divine and human law agree on this. To prove it he cited de poenis, c. licet; de officio, cum c. dilectus; 23 q. 5, c. sinos; 22 q. 4, c. quisquis; and si quis mut. God too sometimes inflicted such penalties: Leviticus 3, 4 and 5; Exodus 23, "If anyone steals"; to this agrees 23 q. 5, prodest.

units.la: Ad 28. qui loquitur de laicis, qui vocantur ex officio ad ferendum testimonium, & non soluuntur eis expensæ: dicit quod tales quotiescunque vocantur ad ferendum testimonium, tenentur venire: alias non possunt excommunicari de iure: quia veritatem celare esset peccatum mortale, eis tamen debent expensæ tradi saluis consuetudinibus specialibus, vbi proceditur contra suspectos in fide, vel in aliis casibus specialibus, vel nisi aliquod ius consuetudo conferret.
units.tr: Regarding the 28th article, which speaks of laymen who are summoned ex officio to give testimony and are not paid their expenses: it says that such men, whenever they are summoned to give testimony, are bound to come, since otherwise they cannot by law be excommunicated, because to conceal the truth would be a mortal sin; yet their expenses ought to be paid to them, saving special customs, where proceedings are taken against those suspected in the faith, or in other special cases, or unless custom confers some right otherwise.

units.la: Ad 29. qui loquitur de rebus furatis clerico: dicit quod cum ad ecclesiam solum pertineat cognoscere de criminalibus, laici non possunt nec debent se intromittere de rebus furatis: quia ei pertinet accessorium, cui & principale, sic enim laici haberent indirecte cognitionem clericorum, & multi possent fingere notorium, quod non esset. Et ad hoc probandum inducit extra de dote post diuortium restitu. c. de prudentia, extra de regulis iuris. causa principalis li. 6. cum aliis.
units.tr: Regarding the 29th article, which speaks of goods stolen from a cleric: it says that since it belongs to the Church alone to take cognizance of criminal matters, laymen cannot and ought not to meddle with goods stolen, because what is accessory belongs to the one to whom the principal belongs; for in this way laymen would indirectly have cognizance of clerics, and many might feign a notorious matter which was not so. And to prove this he cites Extra, de dote post divortium restituenda, c. de prudentia; Extra, de regulis iuris, causa principalis; Liber VI, with others.

units.la: Ad 30. qui loquitur de clericis non coniugatis captis in habitu laicali: dicit quod tales propter quod non deferunt tonsuram vel habitum clericis congruentem, non amittunt priuilegium clericale, vnde si fit notorium iudici ecclesiastico talem esse clericum, vel fama fit publica super hoc, idem iudex sine cuiuscunque iniuria potest ad restitutionem talis clerici iustitiam compellere secularem, sed si dubium esset talem clericum esse vel non, & captus fuerit in habitu laicali, ad ecclesiam cognitio, & detentio ad iudicem secularem, secundum quod iura dicunt, extra de sentent. excom. si iudex laicus lib. 6. C. de fabric. l. si. c. de aquæduc. l. vlt.
units.tr: Regarding the 30th article, which speaks of unmarried clerics taken in lay dress: it says that such men, because they do not wear the tonsure or the dress befitting clerics, do not lose the clerical privilege; hence if it becomes notorious to the ecclesiastical judge that such a man is a cleric, or public report arises on this matter, the same judge may, without injury to anyone, compel the secular power to restore such a cleric to justice. But if it were doubtful whether such a man was a cleric or not, and he was taken in lay dress, then cognizance belongs to the Church, and detention to the secular judge, as the laws say: Extra, de sententia excommunicationis, si iudex laicus; Liber VI; C. de fabricensibus, l. si; C. de aquaeductu, l. ult.

units.la: Ad 31. qui loquitur de clericis captis per laicos, & redditis officialibus, quæ sine punitione expediuntur: dicit, quod male fieret, si maleficia eis imposita notoria essent, aut etiam probarentur, sed communiter accidit, quod cum laici accipiunt quendam clericum, licet non sit eis licitum de iure, postquam ipsum iudici ecclesiastico reddiderunt, cum de nullo maleficio dictum iudicem ecclesiasticum informabunt: propter quod cum causam rationalem detentionis non receperit iudex non possit eum in bona conscientia detinere.
units.tr: Regarding the 31st article, which speaks of clerics taken by laymen and handed over to officials, and dismissed without punishment: it says that it would be wrong if the crimes imputed to them were notorious or even proven; but it commonly happens that when laymen seize some cleric, although this is not lawful by law, once they have handed him over to the ecclesiastical judge, they inform the said judge of no crime at all; therefore, since the judge has received no reasonable cause for detention, he cannot in good conscience keep him in custody.

units.la: Ad 32. qui loquitur de monitionibus, quæ dantur contra spoliantes & iuramenta, quæ exiguntur: dicit idem episcopus, quod tales moniciones non conceduntur communiter per iudices ecclesiasticos, nisi super factis notoriis, vel in casu, vbi illi contra quos tales monitiones dantur, essent super aliquo crimine diffamati, vnde quotiens iudices memorati aut eorum commissarii talibus sic diffamatis iniungunt, quod satisfaciant aut veniant se per iuramentum suum coram eis super impositis sibi maleficiis purgaturi: & ipsi non obediunt iudicibus, aut eorum commissariis in praedictis, nec allegant causam rationabilem, quare ad hoc minime teneantur, tales sunt de iure conuicti, quare nulla fit iniuria, maxime quia causa spoliationis probata violata debet iuramento actoris super deperditis fides plena adhiberi.
units.tr: Regarding the 32nd article, which speaks of the warnings issued against despoilers and of the oaths that are demanded: the same bishop says that such warnings are not commonly granted by ecclesiastical judges except concerning notorious deeds, or in a case where those against whom such warnings are issued have been defamed of some crime. Hence, whenever the said judges or their commissaries enjoin on such men thus defamed that they make satisfaction, or come and clear themselves by their own oath before them concerning the crimes imputed to them, and they do not obey the judges or their commissaries in these matters, nor allege a reasonable cause why they are in no way bound to do so, such men are rightly convicted by law, so no injury is done; especially since, when the cause of despoliation has been proven, full faith ought to be given to the oath of the plaintiff concerning the losses.

units.la: Ad 33. qui loquitur de captionibus clericorum, dicit, sicut ad tricesimum superius iam dictum.
units.tr: Regarding the 33rd article, which speaks of the arrests of clerics: it says the same as was said above concerning the thirtieth.

units.la: Ad 34. qui loquitur de clericis malefacientibus, quos officiales praelatorum de facili expediunt pro poenis pecuniariis: dicit quod hoc esset irrationabile, vbi maleficium esset notorium vel manifestum, & tale vel tantum propter quod perpetua poena ei deberet imponi, si pro poena pecuniaria tale crimen transiret, sed nullum est inconueniens, si pro causa iusta dicti officiales poenam corporalem in pecuniariam conuertant: quia hoc etiam volunt iura tam canonica quam civilia.
units.tr: Regarding the 34th article, which speaks of clerics who do evil, whom the officials of the prelates readily dispatch with pecuniary penalties: it says that this would be unreasonable where the offence is notorious or manifest, and of such a kind that a perpetual penalty ought to be imposed on him if such a crime were passed over with a monetary fine; but there is no impropriety if, for a just cause, the said officials convert a corporal penalty into a pecuniary one, since both canon and civil law themselves wish this.

units.la: Ad 35. qui loquitur de clericis coniugatis, dicit quod si clericus coniugatus deferat tonsuram & vestes clericales, & in tali habitu capiatur per iudicem secularem: cum de iure & consuetudine notoriis tales clerici quantum ad delicta sunt de foro ecclesiae: officiales praedicti nullam faciunt iniuriam Dominis temporalibus, si compellant eos per sententias excommunicationis vel alias ad desistendum a cognitione talium delictorum, quia quocunque modo delinquatur, cognitio pertinet ad praelatos: & laici offendunt exactionem seu poenam etiam pecuniariam a talibus exigendo. De illis autem clericis non coniugatis dicit idem episcopus, quod in nullo casu cognitio eorum pertinet ad laicos, secundum quod iura declarant, salua consuetudine speciali in pluribus ecclesiis regni Franciae exante.
units.tr: Regarding the 35th article, which speaks of married clerics: it says that if a married cleric wears the tonsure and clerical garments, and is taken in such dress by the secular judge, then, since by law and custom such clerics, as far as offences are concerned, belong to the ecclesiastical forum, the aforesaid officials do no wrong to the temporal lords if they compel them, by sentences of excommunication or otherwise, to desist from taking cognizance of such offences; for whatever manner of offence is committed, cognizance belongs to the prelates, and laymen offend by demanding exactions or even pecuniary penalties from such men. Concerning those unmarried clerics, however, the same bishop says that in no case does cognizance of them belong to laymen, as the laws declare, saving a special custom long existing in many churches of the kingdom of France.

units.la: Ad 36. qui loquitur de assecuramentis laicorum & inhibitione quam faciunt officiales pendente citatione assecuramenti: dicit quod si tale fieret ad requestam laici contra laicum, maxime vbi ecclesia hoc haberet de consuetudine speciali, nulla fieret iniuria, si ecclesia prohiberet sub poena excommunicationis, nec pendente citatione facerent eum coram alio iudice conueniri: quia posset aliis magnum scandalum oriri.
units.tr: Regarding the 36th article, which speaks of the securities of laymen and of the prohibition which the officials make while the citation for security is pending: it says that if this were done at the request of a layman against a layman, especially where the Church had this by special custom, no injury would be done if the Church forbade, under penalty of excommunication, that, while the citation was pending, the man be sued before another judge; because great scandal could arise for others.

units.la: Ad 37. qui loquitur de citationibus, quae fiunt contra participantes cum excommunicatis: dicit quod non erat intentionis praelatorum, quod ea quae continentur in articulo, debet, prout sunt propositA, sustineri, nec credunt, quod officiales eo modo procedant, maxime quia aliqui praelatiin suis dioecesibus statuta ediderunt, per quae talia fieri prohibentur. Et alii, qui salubriter nondum fecerunt, erant super his parati pro tempore prouidere, cum bene debet de iure participatio cum excommunicatis absque tamen populi grauamine per iudices ecclesiasticos puniri & prohiberi, ideo &c.
units.tr: Regarding the 37th article, which speaks of citations issued against those who take part with the excommunicated: it says that it was not the intention of the prelates that the matters contained in the article, as they are proposed, should be upheld; nor do they believe that the officials proceed in that manner, especially since some prelates in their dioceses have issued statutes by which such things are forbidden. And others who have not yet done so wholesomely were prepared to provide for these matters in due time, since participation with the excommunicated ought rightly by law to be punished and forbidden by ecclesiastical judges, yet without burden to the people; therefore, etc.

units.la: Ad 38. qui loquitur de impositionibus, quas faciunt officiales laicis super vsurariis: dicit quod si in his officiales eorum alias, quam secundum formam iuris, procederent, vel pro exactione iniusta talibus exigenda, maxime vbi persona contra quam proceditur, non esset diffamata, nullus praelatus vellet quoquo modo talia sustinere. Et si quis in speciali vellet conqueri super istis, ipsi erunt parati, quod actum esset facere iuste & debite emendari.
units.tr: Regarding the 38th article, which speaks of the impositions which the officials make on laymen concerning usurers: it says that if their officials proceeded otherwise than according to the form of law, or demanded unjust exactions from such persons, especially where the person proceeded against was not defamed, no prelate would wish in any way to tolerate such things. And if anyone wished to complain about these matters in particular, they would be ready to see that what was done unjustly was made right and duly amended.

units.la: Ad 39. qui loquitur de adulteriis, quae laicis per officiales imponuntur: dicit quod nunquam talia faciunt, prout loquitur articulus memoratus, neque fieri debent talia, nisi super factis notoriis vel manifestis, aut vbi tales, contra quos proceditur, essent publice diffamati, seu in aliis casibus a iure permissit, & nihilominus parati erant praelati praecipere suis, quod alias in talibus nullo modo procedant.
units.tr: Regarding the 39th article, which speaks of adulteries which are imposed on laymen by the officials: it says that they never do such things, as the said article states, nor ought such things to be done, except concerning notorious or manifest deeds, or where those against whom proceedings are taken are publicly defamed, or in other cases permitted by law; and nevertheless the prelates were ready to order their men that otherwise they should in no way proceed in such matters.

units.la: Ad 40. qui loquitur de multitudine procuratorum & de abusionibus, quas faciunt, dicit quantum ad multitudinem quod quilibet praelatus in sua dioecesi debite prouidebit, quantum ad abusus dicit, quod nullo modo tales abusus fieri permittent: quin imo illi, qui abusi fuerunt, cum ad eorum notitiam peruenerit, iuste punient, secundum quod alias ad eorum quemlibet pertinebit.
units.tr: Regarding the 40th article, which speaks of the multitude of proctors and of the abuses which they commit: as to the multitude, it says that each prelate will duly provide in his own diocese; as to the abuses, it says that such abuses will by no means be permitted; indeed those who have abused their office, when it comes to their knowledge, will be justly punished, as it will belong to each of them to do in other matters.

units.la: Ad 41. qui loquitur de abusibus religiosorum in citationibus: dicit quod valde displicet praelatis, si religiosi praedicti faciunt aliquid indebitum vel iniustum, & quod libenter apponerent remedium in subditis suis quilibet, prout ad eum pertinebit.
units.tr: Regarding the 41st article, which speaks of the abuses of religious men in citations: it says that the prelates are much displeased if the said religious do anything undue or unjust, and that each of them would gladly apply a remedy among his subjects, as it will belong to him to do.

units.la: Ad 42. qui loquitur de vxoribus clericorum coniugatorum: dicit dictus episcopus, quod in locis, vbi de consuetudine speciali vxor clerici esset de foro ecclesiae, quia etiam ad hocius imperatoris concordat, nulla fieret iniuria, si cognitionem ipsarum mulierum ecclesia retinet, quantum ad cognitionem iniuriarum inter laicos, qua emendae iniuriarum petuntur per viam actionis personalis, vt in 3. articul. superius est responsum, & ad praemissa probanda inducit ff. de iuris dictio. iud. l. penult. C. de inter dictis l. vlt. §. ad inimici L. ca. qua C. de epis. & cler. l. i. ideo &c.
units.tr: Regarding the 42nd article, which speaks of the wives of married clerics: the said bishop says that in places where, by special custom, the wife of a cleric is under the ecclesiastical forum, since this also agrees with the law of the emperor, no injury would be done if the Church retains cognizance of those women as far as concerns injuries between laymen, for which amends for injuries are sought by way of personal action, as was answered above in the third article; and to prove the premises he cites Digest, de iurisdictione iudicium, l. penult.; C. de interdictis, l. ult., §. ad inimici; L. ca. qua, C. de episcopis et clericis, l. i.; therefore, etc.

units.la: Ad 43. qui loquitur de viduis trahentibus debitores suos ad curiam secularem: dicit, quod praelati non intendebant sustinere dictum articulum, prout iacet, nisi de consuetudine speciali aut priuilegio fuisset aliquibus ecclesiis ius illud acquisitum.
units.tr: On the 43rd article, which speaks of widows dragging their debtors before the secular court: the bishop says that the prelates did not intend to uphold the said article as it stands, unless by special custom or privilege that right had been acquired for some churches.

units.la: Ad 44. qui loquitur de appellationibus volagiis, dicit sicut in 14. articulo.
units.tr: On the 44th article, which speaks of frivolous appeals: he says the same as on the 14th article.

units.la: Ad 45. qui loquitur de capris in delicto clericis & laicis: dicit quod si sint laici, qui capiantur in tali delicto, tales appellationes, de quibus ibi fit mentio, non essent per ecclesiam admittendae, nisi de consuetudine vel de priuilegio aliquibus ecclesiis esset in hoc aliquod ius acquisitum. Sed si in delicto huiusmodi clericus caperetur per iustitiam secularem, quia de hoc ad nullum potest praeter ad ecclesiam captio pertinere, officiales possunt imo debent procedere contra iustitiam secularem, alias perderetur priuilegium ecclesiasticum, nec possunt etiam tales captiones fieri absque sententia excommunicationis a canone propter hoc incurrenda.
units.tr: On the 45th article, which speaks of the capture of clerics and laymen in crime: he says that if the persons caught in such a crime are laymen, those appeals mentioned there would not be admitted by the church, unless by custom or privilege some right in this had been acquired for some churches. But if a cleric were caught in such a crime by the secular justice, since the arrest can pertain to no one except the church, the officials can and indeed must proceed against the secular justice; otherwise the ecclesiastical privilege would be lost. Nor can such arrests be made without the sentence of excommunication incurred for this by the canon.

units.la: Ad 46. qui loquitur de impositionibus, quas officiales faciunt laicis super vsuris & arrestis corporum, dicit praefatus episcopus, quod si talia fierent, prout in articulo proponuntur, male fierent, & praelatis displiceret. Et si esset qui in speciali vellet eos informare super his, erant parati male acta facere corrigi & emendari, quantum ad eos pertineret. Sed vbi laicus esset super vsura diffamatus publice, officialis potest & debet ad inquisitionem contra talem procedere. Et si requisitus coram dicto officiali contumaciter neglexerit ad opposita respondere, potest officialis, donec sufficienter responderit, per arrestum corporis procedere contra ipsum. Sed post responsionem factam debet fieri recredentia corporis: nisi alia causa subsit rationalis, quare deberet vlterius detineri.
units.tr: On the 46th article, which speaks of the impositions that the officials lay on laymen regarding usury and arrests of the person: the said bishop says that if such things were done as the article sets out, they would be wrongly done, and the prelates would be displeased. And if anyone wished to inform them specially about these matters, they were ready to have their wrong acts corrected and amended, so far as it pertained to them. But where a layman is publicly defamed for usury, the official can and must proceed by inquisition against him. And if, when summoned before the said official, he obstinately neglects to answer the charges, the official may, until he has answered sufficiently, proceed against him by arrest of his person. But after the answer has been given, the person must be released, unless some reasonable cause exists why he should be detained further.

units.la: Ad 47. qui loquitur de captionibus clericorum in terris Baronum: dicit Dominus episcopus, de iure diuino & humano licitum est praelatis & eorum iudicibus capere clericos vbique, quia, secundum quod dictum est superius, non est dare locum, vbi non sit iurisdictio spiritualis, sicut temporalis, vnde talis captio clericorum, quae est spiritualis & de foro ecclesiastico potest & debet fieri per iudicem ecclesiasticum, & non per alium quemcunque. Et nisi ita fieret, quod capi possent clerici per iudices ecclesiasticos vbique, saepissime delicta clericorum remanerent impunita: cum per laicos non possint capi absque sententia excommunicationis a canone incurrenda propter hoc.
units.tr: On the 47th article, which speaks of the capture of clerics in the lands of barons: the lord bishop says that by divine and human law it is lawful for prelates and their judges to seize clerics everywhere, because, as was said above, there is no place where there is no spiritual jurisdiction, just as there is temporal. Hence such capture of clerics, which is spiritual and belongs to the ecclesiastical forum, can and must be made by an ecclesiastical judge, and not by any other whatever. And unless it were so, that clerics could be seized by ecclesiastical judges everywhere, the crimes of clerics would very often remain unpunished, since they cannot be seized by laymen without the sentence of excommunication incurred for this by the canon.

units.la: Ad 48. qui loquitur de laicis capientibus clericos, qui excommunicantur: dicit, quod nulli Domino vel iudici seculari licitum est in quocunque casu clericos capere, quare si tales capientes clericos declararentur per iudices ecclesiasticos sententiam excommunicationis incurrisse, nulla fit iniuria. Et contra illos specialiter dicebat Dominus Episcopus, grauius esse procedendum, qui clericos & presbyteros capiunt indifferenter malitiose ac in Dei & ecclesiae contumeliam & contemptum.
units.tr: On the 48th article, which speaks of laymen seizing clerics who are excommunicated: he says that it is lawful for no lord or secular judge, in any case whatever, to seize clerics; so if such persons who seize clerics are declared by ecclesiastical judges to have incurred the sentence of excommunication, no injury is done. And against those in particular the lord bishop said that proceedings should be more severe against those who seize clerics and presbyters indiscriminately, maliciously, and to the insult and contempt of God and the Church.

units.la: Ad 49. qui loquitur de tonsuris, quae conferuntur indignis: dicit quod si ita fieret, sicut in articulo continetur, non esset vtique sustinendum, nec aliquis praelatus vellet facere, quae proponuntur ibidem. Tamen in quacunque aetate potest praelatus personis literatis, omni fraude & impedimento canonico cessantibus, tonsuras conferre. Sed illi, qui hunc articulum fecerunt, deberent praelatum, qui talia facit, nominatim exprimere: & ipse de facto proprio responderet eidem. Et si qui forsan hoc fecissent (quod absit) non deberet imponi omnibus praelatis.
units.tr: On the 49th article, which speaks of tonsures conferred on the unworthy: he says that if things were done as the article contains, they would certainly not be tolerated, and no prelate would wish to do what is set out there. Yet at any age a prelate may confer tonsures on literate persons, when every fraud and canonical impediment has been removed. But those who drew up this article ought to name expressly the prelate who does such things, and he himself would answer for his own deed. And if any had perhaps done this (God forbid), it should not be imposed on all prelates.

units.la: Ad 50. qui loquitur de poenis pecuniariis, quae exiguntur ab excommunicatis: dicit quod cum sententia excommunicationis feratur propter peccatum mortale, oportet quod excommunicato, si petat absolui, iniungatur poenitentia & poena pro peccato, quia non remittitur peccatum, nisi Deo & ecclesiae fiat satisfactio condigna, vnde antequam absolui mereatur talis excommunicatus, debet satisfacere poena corporali aut pecuniaria. Et hoc in foro poenitentiae obseruatur specialiter, quia in quibusdam locis sunt emendae taxatae, & in aliis sunt emendae arbitrariae, ideo &c.
units.tr: On the 50th article, which speaks of pecuniary penalties exacted from the excommunicated: he says that since the sentence of excommunication is pronounced for mortal sin, it is necessary that the excommunicated person, if he asks to be absolved, be enjoined penance and punishment for the sin, because sin is not forgiven unless due satisfaction is made to God and the Church. Hence before such an excommunicate deserves to be absolved, he must make satisfaction by bodily or pecuniary punishment. And this is observed especially in the forum of repentance, because in some places there are fixed fines, and in others arbitrary fines, and so on.

units.la: Ad 51. qui loquitur de haereditagiis contentiosis positis ad manum laicorum propter debitum partium: dixit quod si duo ad inuicem contendentes essent laici, & fieret sine fraude, & non pro impediendo iurisdictionem ecclesiasticam, praelati non prosequerentur articulum supradictum, nisi de consuetudine vel priuilegio aliqua ecclesiae hoc haberent, & vbi essent ambo clerici, aut alter eorum, vt superius est responsum.
units.tr: On the 51st article, which speaks of contested inheritances placed in the hands of laymen on account of the debt of the parties: he said that if two contending parties were laymen, and it were done without fraud and not to impede ecclesiastical jurisdiction, the prelates would not pursue the aforesaid article, unless by custom or privilege some church had this right; and where both, or one of them, were clerics, the answer is as stated above.

units.la: Ad 52. qui loquitur de iniuriis & grauaminibus illatis gentibus regiis per officiales episcoporum: dicit dictus episcopus, quod praelati nullo modo permitterent, quod per officiales suos gentibus regiis damnum laborum vel expensarum, aut aliud incommodum inferretur. Nec est verisimile, quod sint vera, quae in dicto articulo proponuntur: quia semper praelati habent in suis agibilibus ad regios officiarios recursum, tamen si aliquis vellet in speciali aliquid super hoc declarare, parati erant praelati corrigere mala acta &c. & iniuriam passis emendam facere fieri.
units.tr: On the 52nd article, which speaks of injuries and burdens inflicted on the royal officials by the officials of the bishops: the said bishop says that the prelates would in no way permit their officials to inflict on royal officials loss of labour or expenses, or any other inconvenience. Nor is it likely that what is set out in the said article is true, since prelates always have recourse to the royal officers in their dealings; yet if anyone wished to declare something specific about this, the prelates were ready to correct their wrong acts, and to have amends made to those who suffered injury.

units.la: Ad 53. qui loquitur de haereditagiis clericorum positis propter debitum in manu iudicis seculari: dicit quod haereditagia clericorum sine causa rationabili aut malitiose, aut impediendo iurisdictionem ecclesiasticam ponuntur in manibus iudicis secularis, specialiter quando fit per violentiam & de facto sine causae cognitione aut alias in casu personalitatis: nulla fit iniuria Dominis temporalibus, si ecclesia super hoc se intromittat. Nam alias laici omnem iurisdictionem clericorum haberent, quia vbi non possent clericos compellere, ipsi procederent ad captionem bonorum: & sic quantum ad hoc periret priuilegium ecclesiasticum.
units.tr: On the 53rd article, which speaks of clerics' inheritances placed in the hands of a secular judge on account of debt: he says that the inheritances of clerics are placed in the hands of a secular judge without reasonable cause, either maliciously or to impede ecclesiastical jurisdiction, especially when this is done by violence and by force, without examination of the cause, or otherwise in a personal matter. No injury is done to the temporal lords if the Church interferes in this. For otherwise laymen would have all jurisdiction over clerics, since where they could not compel clerics, they would proceed to seize their goods; and thus, in this respect, the ecclesiastical privilege would perish.

units.la: Ad 54. qui loquitur de neganda sepultura vsurariis: dicit quod de iure, vsurario manifesto debet denegari ecclesiastica sepultura, quare nullam faciunt iniuriam officiales praedicti praelatorum talibus sepulturam denegando, maxime donec fuerit restitutum vel cautio data sufficiens derede restituendo illo, quod per tale pactum per eos fuerat acquisitum, sed si pro exactione duntaxat salsè imponerent alicui tale crimen, & propter hoc interdicerent ei ecclesiasticam sepulturam: prælati nullo modo ista fieri permitterent, si ad eorum notitiam peveniret, nec est inconveniens, vbi aliquis vlurarius manifestus decedit, si ecclesiæ tenentur satisfacere ratione peccati manifeste commissi.
units.tr: On the 54th article, which speaks of denying burial to usurers: he says that by law burial in consecrated ground ought to be denied to a manifest usurer; so the aforesaid officials of the prelates do no wrong in denying burial to such persons, especially until restitution has been made, or sufficient security given to make restitution to the heirs of what had been acquired by such a bargain. But if they falsely imposed such a crime on anyone merely for the sake of exaction, and on that account forbade him ecclesiastical burial, the prelates would in no way permit such things to be done, if they came to their knowledge. Nor is it unreasonable, when a manifest usurer dies, that the church should be bound to make satisfaction on account of a sin manifestly committed.

units.la: Ad 55. qui loquitur de reconciliatione cimiteriorum facienda: dicit dictus episcopus, quod prælati ad reconciliationem cimiteriorum faciendam cum expensis propriis non tenentur, & vltra hoc possunt emendam exigere ratione violentiæ in cimiterio commissæ, quare si decem libras exigunt vel vltra, quantum ascendunt eorum expensæ, non debet pro iniuria reputari. Sed ille, qui commisit violentiam, si habet vnde possit de prædictis satisfacere, nedum ad emendam, sed etiam ad expensarum restitutionem & satisfactionem tenetur.
units.tr: On the 55th article, which speaks of the reconciliation of cemeteries to be performed: the said bishop says that the prelates are not bound to perform the reconciliation of cemeteries at their own expense, and beyond this they may exact a fine on account of violence committed in the cemetery; so if they demand ten pounds or more, to the amount their expenses come to, it should not be reckoned as an injury. But he who committed the violence, if he has the means to make satisfaction for these things, is bound not only to the fine but also to the restitution and satisfaction of the expenses.

units.la: Ad 56. qui loquitur de priuilegiatis, quod possunt eligere iudices & abusus eorum &c. dicit quod si tales, quibus talia priuilegia sunt indulta, eisdem priuilegiis, vt proponitur in articulo, abutantur, prælati nollent eos excusare, imo eis displicerent, & non immerito, tales abusus.
units.tr: On the 56th article, which speaks of privileged persons, that they may choose judges, and their abuses, and so on: he says that if such persons, to whom such privileges have been granted, abuse those same privileges, as the article sets out, the prelates would not wish to excuse them; indeed such abuses would displease them, and not without reason.

units.la: Ad 57. qui loquitur, quando laicus citat clericum super causa hæreditatis coram iudice seculari: dicit quod super actione personali vel mixta aut super interdicto, quod in parte personale exstitit, clericus fuerit coram iudice seculari vocatus, non debet coram eo respondere, vbi autem actio esset mere realis, de iure deberet super hoc cuiuslibet ecclesiæ consuetudo seruari, & vbi consuetudo non esset, deberet ius scriptum in talibus imitari.
units.tr: On the 57th article, which speaks of when a layman summons a cleric before a secular judge in a case of inheritance: he says that in a personal or mixed action, or in an interdict which is in part personal, if the cleric has been summoned before a secular judge, he ought not to answer before him; but where the action is purely real, the custom of each church ought in law to be observed in this matter, and where there is no custom, written law ought to be followed in such cases.

units.la: Ad 58. qui loquitur de coniugatis clericis mercatoribus: dicit quod nisi talis actio vel petitio veniat ex maleficio vel delicto, prælati nollent in talium cognitione laicum turbare: nisi aliquibus ecclesiis ex consuetudine, priuilegio, seu compositione ius aliquod fuerit acquisitum.
units.tr: On 58, which speaks of married clerics who are merchants: he says that, unless such an action or claim arises from a crime or offence, the prelates would not wish to trouble a layman in the hearing of such cases, unless some right has been acquired by some churches through custom, privilege or agreement.

units.la: Ad 59. qui loquitur de interdicto apponendo in terra Domini Regis: dicit Dominus episcopus, quod priuilegia Domini Regis omnes prælati vellent integraliter seruare, nec vellent aliquid facere contra ea: supplicantes eidem Domino nostro Regi, quod placeret ei eisdem prælatis, dum erant ad inuicem, dicta priuilegia ostendere: ita quod super his possent certitudinaliter respondere.
units.tr: On 59, which speaks of an interdict to be imposed in the lands of the Lord King: the lord bishop says that all the prelates would wish to observe the king's privileges in full and would not wish to do anything contrary to them. They beg our same lord King that it would please him to show the said privileges to the same prelates, while they are together, so that they might be able to give a definite answer on these matters.

units.la: Ad 60. qui loquitur de Balliuis & Præpositis prælatorum, qui sunt clerici: dicit quod hoc licitum est prælatis tam de ratione quam de iure, & cedit ad vtilitatem iustitiæ: quia iura vel Iuristæ melius possunt iustitiam & sciunt tenere, quam laici, qui literas non nouerunt, hoc etiam eis sæpe ex necessitate incumbit, quia non inueniunt seculares ad hoc sufficientes, qui velint eorum officia assumere: aliquoties propter timorem Dominorum temporalium, & aliquotiens propter alias causas.
units.tr: On 60, which speaks of the bailiffs and provosts of the prelates, who are clerics: he says that this is lawful for the prelates, both in reason and in law, and it serves the advantage of justice, because lawyers can better uphold and know justice than laymen, who do not know letters. This also often falls upon them of necessity, because they do not find secular men sufficient for this who are willing to take up their offices: sometimes through fear of temporal lords, and sometimes for other reasons.

units.la: Ad 61. qui loquitur de monitionibus, quæ fiunt contra participantes cum excommunicatis in operibus faciendis: dicit hoc possunt & debent facere de iure: cum participare scienter cum excommunicato sit peccatum mortale, maxime post monitionem super hoc sibi factam, & hoc est vnus modus participandi, videlicet operari, & cum excommunicato negotiari.
units.tr: On 61, which speaks of warnings issued against those who take part with excommunicated persons in carrying out works: he says they can and ought to do this by law, since knowingly taking part with an excommunicated person is a mortal sin, especially after a warning has been given to them on this matter; and this is one way of taking part, namely to work and do business with an excommunicated person.

units.la: Ad 62. qui loquitur de illis, qui citantur propter participationem: dicit quod si talis citatio ad instantiam partis fuerit impetrata, & parsilla non possit contra tales citatos participationem probare: impetrator tenetur ad restitutionem expensarum huiusmodi citatorum, præter ea nunquam talis citatio conceditur, nisi talis citatus primo in generali, secundo in speciali fuerit monitus competenter, ne cum tali excommunicato scienter participare auderet, & cum hoc officiales nunquam contra tantam personarum multitudinem tales citationes concedunt, nisi videant ex hoc grande periculum animarum imminere, aut scandalum maximum exoriri, & vbi contra aliquos reperitur, quod sumpta monitione eis facta super hoc & contra mandatum ecclesiæ cum tali excommunicato participare curauerunt seu etiam præsumpserunt, bene tenentur de iure ad satisfactionem Deo & ecclesiæ, quos propter suam contumaciam offenderant, aut in poena pecuniaria, aut in poena corporali.
units.tr: On 62, which speaks of those who are summoned on account of taking part: he says that if such a summons has been obtained at the instance of a party, and that party cannot prove the participation against those so summoned, the one who obtained it is bound to restore the expenses of such summoned persons. Moreover, such a summons is never granted unless the person summoned has first been competently warned in general and secondly in particular, that he should not dare knowingly to take part with such an excommunicated person. And in addition, the officials never grant such summonses against so great a multitude of persons, unless they see that a great danger to souls is impending from this, or a very great scandal is arising. And where it is found against some that, after a warning given to them on this matter and against the command of the Church, they have taken care, or even presumed, to take part with such an excommunicated person, they are rightly bound by law to make satisfaction to God and the Church, whom they have offended by their obstinacy, either by a pecuniary penalty or by a corporal penalty.

units.la: Ad 63. qui loquitur de officialibus qui faciunt iurare aduocatos, ne dent consilium contra curiam, dicit episcopus, quod si hoc fieret, merito prælatis displiceret: cum deberent officiales vnicuique consilium præstare in curia sua litiganti, nec credunt quod aliquis Iudex spiritualis faceret hoc, quod continet articulus supradictus: nisi de familiari aut pensionario proprio, vel alio, qui teneretur eidem iudici ratione fidelitatis aut iuramenti præstare consueti pro aliquo honore aut alia iusta causa: adhuc tamen vbi litigans consilium non haberet, debet ei curia prouidere.
units.tr: On 63, which speaks of officials who make advocates swear that they will not give counsel against the court: the bishop says that if this were done, it would rightly displease the prelates, since the officials ought to give counsel to each litigant in their court, nor do they believe that any spiritual judge would do what the aforesaid article contains, except perhaps against a household servant or a paid dependant of his own, or another who is bound to the same judge by reason of fealty or of an oath customarily given for some honour or other just cause. Even so, where a litigant has no counsel, the court ought to provide for him.

units.la: Ad 64. & 65. qui loquuntur de executoribus & inuentariis bonorum testatoris & intestatoris dicit, quod tam de iure scripto quam de consuetudine speciali prælati sunt executores legitimi testamentorum, vnde si executio venerit ad prælatum: nulli facit iniuriam, bona inter hæredes distribuendo, & de eis inuentaria faciendo. Et hoc idem dicit de bonis intestatorum maxime in locis vbi sic de consuetudine extitit obseruatum à tanto tempore, quod in contrarium memoria non exstit.
units.tr: On 64 and 65, which speak of executors and inventories of the goods of testators and intestates, he says that the prelates are, both by written law and by special custom, the lawful executors of wills; so that if the execution comes to a prelate, he does no wrong by distributing the goods among the heirs and making inventories of them. And he says the same concerning the goods of intestates, especially in places where this has been observed by custom for so long a time that no memory exists to the contrary.

units.la: Ad vltimum, qui loquitur de approbationibus testamentorum, dicit idem episcopus, quod quando in præsentia alicuius notarii curiæ archidiaconi vel alterius minoris iudicis ordinarii ciuitatis aliquod conditur testamentū, quia multoties, tales notarii non sunt magnæ auctoritatis: vel si per aliquem notarium curiæ secularis recipiatur huiusmodi testamentum, habet consuetudo specialis plurium ecclesiarum regni Franciæ, & hoc etiam iura dicunt, quod donec talia testamenta coram iudice principali & ordinario illius diœcesis fuerint approbata vel publicata, non adhibetur ei fides, neque debet aliqualiter adhiberi. Et si alias hoc fieret, esset in maximum populi detrimentum: quia possent in talibus multæ falsitates committi. Quibus responsionibus sic factis per dictum episcopum fuit petitum ex parte Domini Regis, quod prædictæ responsiones, prout dictæ fuerunt & propositæ, verbotenus inscriptis redigerentur & traderentur. Super quibus petitis, prælati ad invicem diligenter habuerunt deliberationem, & tandem deliberauerunt inter se tradere loco responsionum prædictarum Domino regi scedulam infra scriptam in Gallico, licet sit in Latino translata, cuius tenor sequitur in hæc verba Latine.
units.tr: Lastly, on what speaks of the approval of wills: the same bishop says that when a will is drawn up in the presence of a notary of the archdeacon's court, or of another lesser ordinary judge of the city, since such notaries are often of no great authority; or if such a will is received by some notary of a secular court, a special custom of many churches of the kingdom of France holds, and the laws also say, that until such wills have been approved or published before the principal and ordinary judge of that diocese, no faith is to be given to them, nor ought it in any way to be given. And if otherwise it were done, it would be to the very great harm of the people, because many forgeries could be committed in such matters. When these answers had been given in this way by the said bishop, the lord King's side asked that the aforesaid answers should be written down and handed over word for word, just as they were spoken and put forward. On these requests the prelates carefully deliberated among themselves, and at last they resolved to hand over to the lord King, in place of the aforesaid answers, the schedule written below, in French, although it has been translated into Latin; its content follows, word for word, in Latin:

units.la: Supplicant Regiæ Maiestati prælati præsentes Parisiis, se aliquo iudicio minime submittendo, quod placeat ei iura, libertates, priuilegia canonica, consuetudines & saisinas, quæ & quas ecclesiæ Gallicanæ habent & habuerunt temporibus retroactis, eis defendere & seruare, specialiter super cognitionem actionum personalium & realium mixtarum, necnon & interdictorum maxime inter laicos. Item super cognitione clericorum, quando per laicos aliqua fit eis petitio, aut quando clerici super violentia in bonis illorum illata per laicos conqueritur. Item super cognitione contractuum initorum coram iudice seculari. Item quod non impediantur, quin eorum notarii contractus recipere valeant in quacunque parte suarum diœcesium. Item quod non impediantur super inuentariis faciendis de bonis defunctorum, quorum de iure vel consuetudine vel compositione executores existunt. Item quod non impediantur super cognitione hypothecarum, quam habent de iure vel consuetudine. Item quod non impediantur super cognitione viduarum & pupillorum, & super bonis intestatorum, quantum ad eos pertinet de consuetudine vel de iure. Item quod non impediantur in quacunque parte diœcesis suæ, quin possint habere suos officiales & eorum clericos capere, & ab ipsis clericis nec non à laicis emendas pecuniarias exigere debitas de consuetudine vel de iure. Item quod non impediantur super cognitione rerum futurarum à personis ecclesiasticis. Item quod tam super captione quam super cognitione clericorum non coniugatorum eorum iura & consuetudines obseruentur, & confirmentur eisdem, quia vobis manifeste ostenderunt, quod hæc debent fieri de iure diuino & humano. Item significant Regiæ Maiestati, quod super abusibus, quos aliqui conquerentes imponunt officialibus & gentibus suis, dicendo quod ipsi abutuntur eis imponendo crimina, vt redimant eos, & emendas ac expensas ab innocentibus exigendo, proferendoque sententias excommunicationis pro vna sola citatione non peremptoria præcedente, ac super eo quod propositum fuerit contra ipsos prælatos, quod ipsi conferebant tonsuras indignis, & dicti eorum officiales imponunt malitiosè laicis pro extorsione pecuniarum inde ab eis exigendarum, quod ipsi sunt circa fidem suspecti, quodque clericos super maleficiis accusatos & eis redditos per iudicem secularem dimittunt impunitos. Item quod labores & expensas multis irrationabiliter conferunt prætextu participationum cum excommunicatis. Item quod laicis malitiosè vsuras imponunt, vt redimant eos, & coniugatis tam viris quam mulieribus quod adulteria commiserunt. Item super abusibus, quos facere dicuntur procuratores eorum, & super abusibus quos religiosi faciunt in multis ciuitatibus. Item super iniuriis & grauaminibus, quos aliqui vt dicitur, faciunt ratione priuilegiorum eis indultorum. Item super eo, quod dicitur, quod litigantes in curia ecclesiastica contra officium non reperiunt aduocatos: nec non super omnibus aliis in quibus eorum officiales negligentes inuenirentur abusi fuisse vel conuicti tam in prædictis quam aliis: quæ si scirent, non permitterent vllo modo, ipsi sunt parati corrigere & facere corrigi & emendari pro futuris temporibus tam per statuta synodalia & prouincialia, quam per alia quæ poterunt bona remedia salubriter prouidere.
units.tr: The prelates present at Paris beg Your Royal Majesty, submitting themselves to no judgment whatsoever, that it may please you to defend and maintain for them the rights, liberties, canonical privileges, customs and seisins which the churches of Gaul have and have had in past times, especially concerning the hearing of personal, real and mixed actions, and also of interdicts, chiefly between laymen. Likewise concerning the hearing of clerics, when any claim is brought against them by laymen, or when clerics complain of violence done to their goods by laymen. Likewise concerning the hearing of contracts entered into before a secular judge. Likewise that they may not be hindered from having their notaries receive contracts in any part of their dioceses. Likewise that they may not be hindered in making inventories of the goods of the deceased, of whom they are executors by law, custom or agreement. Likewise that they may not be hindered in hearing cases of mortgages, which they have by law or custom. Likewise that they may not be hindered in hearing cases of widows and orphans, and in the goods of intestates, so far as these belong to them by custom or by law. Likewise that they may not be hindered, in any part of their diocese, from having their officials and their clerks arrest, and from exacting from these clerks, as well as from laymen, the pecuniary fines due by custom or by law. Likewise that they may not be hindered in hearing cases of future things from ecclesiastical persons. Likewise that, both as to the arrest and the hearing of unmarried clerics, their rights and customs may be observed and confirmed to them, because they have shown you plainly that these ought to be done by divine and human law. They also signify to Your Royal Majesty that, concerning the abuses which some complainants lay upon their officials and their people, saying that they abuse them by imposing crimes upon them so as to ransom them, and by exacting fines and expenses from the innocent, and by pronouncing sentences of excommunication after a single summons that was not peremptory; and concerning what has been put forward against the prelates themselves, namely that they confer tonsures on the unworthy, and that their said officials maliciously impose on laymen that they are suspect in the faith, in order to extort money from them; and that they dismiss unpunished clerics accused of crimes and handed back to them by the secular judge: and that they unreasonably impose labours and expenses under the pretext of taking part with excommunicated persons; and that they maliciously impose usury on laymen so as to ransom them, and charge married men and women with having committed adultery. Likewise concerning the abuses which their proctors are said to commit, and the abuses which the religious orders commit in many cities. Likewise concerning the injuries and grievances which some, as it is said, inflict by reason of privileges granted to them. Likewise concerning the claim that litigants in the ecclesiastical court, against the office, find no advocates; and likewise concerning all other matters in which their officials are found negligent or convicted of abuses, both in the aforesaid and in others, which, if they knew of them, they would by no means permit: they are ready to correct and to have corrected and amended these for future times, both by synodal and provincial statutes, and by other good remedies which they may be able to provide wholesomely.

units.la: Super aliis vero articulis supplicant dicti prælati, quatenus iura ecclesiæ, siue sint de iure aut per priuilegium seu compositionem vel consuetudinem acquisita, placeat Domino Regi seruare & defendere ac etiā confirmare, vbi autem in dictis articulis essent aliqua contraria ius, priuilegium, consuetudinem vel compositionem, ipsi prælati nollent ea aliqualiter sustinere.
units.tr: Concerning the other articles, the said prelates beg that the rights of the Church, whether acquired by law, privilege, agreement or custom, may please the Lord King to preserve, defend and also confirm. Where any of those articles contain anything contrary to right, privilege, custom or agreement, the prelates themselves would not in any way tolerate it.

units.la: Supplicantes eidem Domino Regi, vt pro Dei honore in statu, in quo sui boni prædecessores tenuerunt ecclesiam, ipse eam teneat & defendat, nec ei faciat aliquam nouitatem. Et placeat ei proclamationes & inhibitiones factas, scilicet quod nullus laicus trahat alium laicum coram iudice ecclesiastico reuocare: quia hoc esset omnia ecclesiarum iura tollere.
units.tr: They beg the same Lord King, for the honour of God, to hold and defend the Church in the state in which its good predecessors held it, and not to make any innovation in it. And may it please him to revoke the proclamations and prohibitions that have been issued, namely that no layman may summon another layman before an ecclesiastical judge, because this would take away all the rights of the Churches.
