For when Pilate boasted of the power he had over Christ, and said to him, Do you not know that I have power to crucify you, and to release you? as John relates, he answered, You would have no power over me unless it had been given you from above. The gloss explains this in two ways: in one way, from above, that is, from God, because there is no power except from God; in the other, from above, that is, from Caesar, who had appointed Pilate governor. Hence, on the words, If you release this man, you are not Caesar's friend, the gloss says: The Jews terrify Pilate with Caesar, whom he cannot despise as the author of his power. For God was the author of Caesar's power. According to this latter interpretation, God in these words greatly commends the Roman Empire. For he shows that Caesar's power excels the other worldly powers and holds them under Caesar. For what is it to be given power from above, except to be given it by him whose power surpasses the other worldly powers, containing and enclosing them beneath himself as inferior and lesser? Furthermore, the Lord not only honoured the Roman Empire, and still honours it, in this, that while the Roman Empire stands and endures, the man of sin, the son of perdition, will not come, as is read in the second epistle to the Thessalonians, chapter 2, where the Apostle says: He who now holds, let him hold until he is taken out of the way; and then that wicked one shall be revealed, whom the Lord will slay with the breath of his mouth. On these words of the Apostle the Gloss says that the Apostle, in the words, He who holds, let him hold, etc., designates the Roman Empire, which being destroyed, Antichrist will come; and then he signifies the Roman Emperor, who holds the Roman Empire or the world, successively from king to king, until he is taken out of the way. For to be taken out of the way is to be removed from the common view of men. Augustine, in the second book of The City of God, on these words of the Apostle, speaks thus: What the Apostle says, Only let him who now holds, hold until he is taken out of the way, is not absurdly believed to have been said of the Roman Empire, as if it were said: He who now rules, until he is removed from the midst, that is, taken away; and then that wicked one will be revealed, by whom no one doubts Antichrist is signified. It is a great honour for the Roman Empire that the Lord has deigned to privilege it above the rest in this, that Antichrist, the adversary of Christ and of his members, will not come unless the Roman Empire has first been wholly removed. But once the Roman Empire is removed there will be a tribulation so great and of such a kind, as is read in Matthew, as has not been from the beginning of the world until now. In those days iniquity and unbelief will so abound that, if it were possible, even the elect will be led into error. And the earlier times seem to have been times of peace compared with this most grievous and greatest tribulation. Hence the Psalmist: In his days righteousness will spring up, and abundance of peace, until the moon is taken away: that is, the Roman Empire, which is signified by the moon. Hence the Apostle writes to Timothy: But know this, that in the last days dangerous times will press upon us; and they will press upon us because before they were not so dangerous.

units.la: Nota, & durabit illa tribulatio tribus annis & dimidio, ut dicitur in Gloss. Matth. & Marc. & colligitur hoc ex Apocalypsi Ioannis, & Daniele. Sicut autem Christus Dominus & magister omnium in semetipso Romanum imperium honorauit: ita beatus Petrus, cui Dominus ecclesiam suam regendam commisit, honorari praecepit in epistola sua dicens, Deum timete, Regem honorate. Utinam Germani, ad quos mundi regnum est translatum, saperent & intelligerent, ac novissima providerent. Utinam saperent iustitiam, & Deum diligerent, & regem quem eis Deus loco iustitiae posuit, reverenter intenderent, & sicut Dei ministro honorem debitum exhiberent. Utinam exaltati per Romanum imperium, & dilatati, magnitudinem bonorum in eos collatorum intelligerent, & non essent ingrati. Utinam principes, praesertim hi ad quos pertinet ius & iustitia & potestas eligendi Regem Imperatorem primo, postmodum pericula quae venient sublato Romano Imperio, praeviderent. Dum enim sublatum fuerit Romanum imperium, tribulatio tanta erit in mundo, quod nisi dies illius tribulationis (ut dicitur in Matth. & Marco) fuissent breviati, non fieret salva omnis caro. Utinam Germani, ad quos & in quos Imperiale regnum translatum est, huius regis, quem Deus posuit in prodigium super terram, praeviderent, & sublationem eius pertimerent. Licet enim necesse sit ut veniant scandala, ut tamen illis per quos scandala sunt ventura.
units.tr: Note that this tribulation will last three years and a half, as is said in the Gloss on Matthew and Mark, and as is gathered from the Apocalypse of John and from Daniel. Just as Christ the Lord and Master of all honoured the Roman Empire in himself, so blessed Peter, to whom the Lord committed his Church to be governed, commanded in his epistle that it be honoured, saying, Fear God, honour the King. Would that the Germans, to whom the kingdom of the world has been transferred, were wise, understood, and foresaw the last things! Would that they were wise in justice, loved God, and reverently attended to the king whom God set in place of justice for them, and showed him the honour due to a minister of God! Would that they, exalted and enlarged through the Roman Empire, understood the greatness of the goods conferred upon them and were not ungrateful! Would that the princes, especially those to whom belongs the right, the justice and the power of electing the king and emperor, foresaw first, and afterwards, the dangers that will come when the Roman Empire is removed! For when the Roman Empire has been removed, there will be such tribulation in the world that, unless the days of that tribulation (as is said in Matthew and Mark) had been shortened, no flesh would be saved. Would that the Germans, to whom and in whom the imperial kingdom has been transferred, foresaw the removal of this king, whom God has set up as a wonder upon the earth, and feared it! For although it is necessary that offences come, yet woe to those through whom the offences will come.

units.la: CAP. II.
units.tr: CHAP. II.

units.la: Qui dicuntur Germani electores.
units.tr: Who are called the German electors.

units.la: ET attende quod Treuerensis, Colonensis & Moguntinensis, civitates & dioeceses, populi sunt Germani: & eorum Archiepiscopi debent Imperatorem eligere, adiuncto sibi Comite Palatino, a palatio quod est in civitate Treuerensi, quod olim fuit domus regni: a quo dicuntur Maiores domus, qui modo dicuntur Comites Palatini. Et hi dicuntur Germani, quia de eodem germine nati cum Romanis, videlicet de germanis, Aenea scilicet & Priamo iuniore. Dicuntur Germani, quasi Romanorum germine germinati. Illius enim imperator illam terram Romano subegit imperio, & eam Romanis habitantibus occupavit, & propter hoc debitus ordo requirebat, ut sicut Romani tanquam maiores sacerdotium, sic Germani tanquam minores regnum obtinerent: de eode enim fonte sive germine Regnum & Sacerdotium processerunt. Quod autem Saxoniae Dux & Brandeburgensis Marchio ad Regis seu Imperatoris electionem sunt vocandi, hoc est postmodum per quandam necessitatem introductum: quia ad tempus translationis Imperii de Graecis in Germanos, quae facta fuit sub Carolo rege magnifico, Saxones vel non erant, vel in fide nouelli erant, ac ut tanto commodius in fide & fidelitate retinerentur, ad electionem admissi sunt, cum essent quoq; potentes, & magnarum virium principes. Item nota, quod cum Antichristus venturus non sit, nisi prius Imperium destruatur: indubitanter omnes illi, qui ad hoc dant operam ut non sit imperiu, quantum ad hoc, sunt praecursores & nuncii Antichristi. Caveant ergo Romani & eorum Pontifices, nec peccatis & culpis suis exigentibus, iusto Dei iudicio sacerdotium ab ipsis auferatur. Caveant nihilominus praesules, & principes Germani, ne ipsi per ambitionem temporalis potestatis, iura sibi & possessiones Imperii vendicent & vsurpent: quia, sicut prius dictum est, necesse est ut veniant scandala, vae autem illis per quos scandala fiunt. Necesse est, quia tantus ardor dominandi & habendi cor eorum occaecauit, ut nec velint facere veritatem quam noverunt, nec ab aliis audire quam ignorant, sicut scriptum est: Oculos habent, & non videbunt: aures habent, & non audient, &c. Sunt quidam huius temporis clerici & laici, subditi & praelati, qui annales principum & gesta veterum ignorantes, Gallorum, Germanorum, & Francigenarum & Francorum originem & differentiam nescientes, spiritu indignationis inflati, huiusmodi vel in corde vel in ore faciant quaestionem: Qualiter summus Pontifex Romanum imperium per manus magnifici Caroli de Graecis transtulit in Germanos? populum tam rude, ineptum: qui cum seipsos neq; in ornatu vestium, nec in morum compositione regere sciant, quomodo regnum totius Ecclesiæ gubernabunt? Vel ideo vtique Imperium remanssse debuit apud Romanos: vel si transferendum fuit, tunc transferri potius debuit in Gallos: præsertim cum hoc tempore Carolus fuerit rex Francorum, & Galli sint homines qui omnibus consideratis sint cunctis hominibus præferendi. Ne igitur propter huiusmodi cogitantium suggestionem humana temeritas immutare præsumat statum sacri Imperii (quod non est dubium, sancti Spiritus ordinatione, secundum qualitatem ipsam & exigentiam meritorum humanorum gubernari & disponi) videatur expedient, vt quædam antiquitates ex multorum scriptis collectæ recitentur, ad demonstrandum quod non eventu vel casu fortuito, sed magis sanctorum principum actum est solertia, vt Romanum Imperium non apud Romanos remanere debuerit, vel transferri in Gallos, sed potius in Germanos. Vnde primo dicendum est de Gallis, postea de Germanis, Francis & Francigenis: & tandem quorundam regum nomina & gesta summarie & compendiose persequar, vt per hoc appareat veritas propositæ quæstionis.
units.tr: And note that the cities and dioceses of Trier, Cologne and Mainz are peoples of Germany, and their archbishops ought to elect the Emperor, together with the Count Palatine, from the palace in the city of Trier, which was once the house of the kingdom. From this they are called Maiores domus, who are now called Counts Palatine. These are called Germans because they were born of the same stock as the Romans, namely of the brothers Aeneas and the younger Priam. They are called Germans as if they had sprung from the stock of the Romans. For the emperor subdued that land to the Roman empire and occupied it with Roman inhabitants, and for this reason the due order required that, just as the Romans held the priesthood as the elder line, so the Germans, as the younger, should hold the kingdom, since kingdom and priesthood came forth from the same fountain or stock. As for the fact that the Duke of Saxony and the Margrave of Brandenburg are also to be summoned to the election of the King or Emperor, this was introduced afterwards by a certain necessity: at the time of the transfer of the empire from the Greeks to the Germans, which was made under the great King Charles, the Saxons either did not yet exist or were newly converted to the faith, and so that they might be kept more conveniently in the faith and in loyalty, they were admitted to the election, since they were also powerful and princes of great strength. Likewise note that, since Antichrist will not come unless the empire is first destroyed, undoubtedly all those who labour to bring it about that there is no empire, in so far as this is concerned, are forerunners and messengers of Antichrist. Let the Romans and their Pontiffs therefore beware, lest, their sins and faults demanding it, by the just judgment of God the priesthood be taken away from them. Let the prelates and princes of Germany beware nonetheless, lest through the ambition of temporal power they claim for themselves and usurp the rights and possessions of the Empire, because, as was said before, it is necessary that scandals come, but woe to those through whom scandals happen. It is necessary, because so great an ardour for ruling and possessing has blinded their hearts that they neither wish to do the truth which they know, nor to hear from others what they do not know, as it is written: They have eyes and will not see; they have ears and will not hear, etc. There are some clergy and laity of this time, subjects and prelates, who, ignorant of the annals of princes and the deeds of the ancients, not knowing the origin and difference of the Gauls, Germans, Francigenae and Franks, puffed up with a spirit of indignation, raise this question either in their heart or with their mouth: How did the supreme Pontiff transfer the Roman empire from the Greeks into the hands of the Germans, a people so rude and unfit, who cannot govern themselves either in the adornment of their clothing or in the composure of their manners, how will they govern the kingdom of the whole Church? Either the empire ought in any case to have remained with the Romans, or, if it had to be transferred, it ought rather to have been transferred to the Gauls, especially since at this time Charles was king of the Franks, and the Gauls are men who, all things considered, are to be preferred to all other men. Therefore, lest through the suggestion of those who think in this way human rashness presume to change the state of the holy Empire (which, without doubt, is ordered and disposed by the ordinance of the Holy Spirit, and governed according to the quality and demands of human merits themselves), it seems expedient that certain ancient records gathered from the writings of many be recited, to demonstrate that it was done not by chance or accident, but rather by the skill of holy princes, that the Roman empire ought not to remain with the Romans, nor be transferred to the Gauls, but rather to the Germans. Hence it must first be said about the Gauls, afterwards about the Germans, Franks and Francigenae; and finally I shall pursue, summarily and briefly, the names and deeds of certain kings, so that by this the truth of the question proposed may appear.

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: Diuisio Galliæ, & de Germanis, Francis ac Francigenis, & de habitu aut interpretatione eorundem.
units.tr: Division of Gaul, and of the Germans, Franks and Frenchmen, and of the character or interpretation of these same peoples.

units.la: SCiendum est, quod Gallia Europæ provincia, habens in Oriente Rhenum, magnum fluuium, in Meridie alpes Italiæ, in Occidente terminos Hispaniæ, & in Aquilone mare Britanniæ & Frisiæ. Et Gallia trifarie diuidatur, videlicet in Galliam Comatam (illi enim Galli quadam negligentia comam crescere permittebant) ipsa siquidem Gallia ornatui tegumentorum lineorum & lanearum multum intendebat. Et dicuntur Galli secundum quosdam, à nitore corporum: Γάλα enim Græce, Latine lac, & hanc expositionem vocabuli ego reprobare non debeo, tanquam ab antiquis traditam. Verum etiam est, quod respectu Hispanorum vel Maurorum, nitent corpore aliquantulum albiores: respectu vero circumiacentium provinciarum, videlicet Saxonum & Anglorum, nullatenus a nitore corporum dici possunt. Huiusmodi igitur dictis antiquorum videtur, quod non incongrue Galli dicuntur propter proprietates quas habent gallo communes: quæ sunt vtiq; triplices, videlicet malæ, bonæ, & optimæ. Proprietates itaq; galli mali sunt iste, supbus, clamosus, luxuriosus, inconstas, pronus ad lites, pronus ad pacem, vnde etiam Galli, qui has proprietates habent, pni sunt vel ad bella, vel ad pacem, & sunt de vili Gallicorum semine. Proprietates vero boni sunt istæ, pulchrer corpore, sed pulchrior plumatus quam deplumatus, vestitus quam nudus, audax, hilaris, amatiuus & liberalis: & ideo quorum Gallici has proprietates habent, de nobili Gallicorum prolapia processerunt, & bona consuetudo in eis se mutauit in meliorem. Forro hæ sunt proprietates galli optimi, circumspectus, vigilans, se primo ante alias excitans, gallinas, subditos suos bene regens, & fœcundans: granum ex palea eliciens, & illud proprie distribuens. Hæ sunt proprietates spirituales & mysticæ, quibus pollent præcæteris boni & idonei prælati. Et hæc de interpretatione Gallorum & Galliæ.
units.tr: It should be known that Gaul is a province of Europe, having the Rhine, a great river, to the east, the Alps of Italy to the south, the borders of Spain to the west, and the sea of Britain and Friesland to the north. Gaul is divided into three parts, namely Long-haired Gaul (for those Gauls, through a certain carelessness, let their hair grow long; indeed Gaul was much given to adorning itself with coverings of linen and wool). They are said by some to be called Gauls from the brightness of their bodies, for milk in Greek is [Γάλα], and I ought not to reject this explanation of the name, since it was handed down by the ancients. It is true that, compared with Spaniards or Moors, they are somewhat whiter in body; but compared with the neighbouring peoples, namely the Saxons and the English, they can by no means be called bright in body. Such, then, seems to be the meaning of the sayings of the ancients: that the Gauls are not inappropriately so named because of the qualities they share with the cock. These qualities are threefold: bad, good and best. The qualities of the bad cock are these: proud, noisy, lustful, inconstant, prone to quarrels, and prone to peace; whence also those Gauls who have these qualities are prone either to wars or to peace, and they are of the base stock of the Gauls. The qualities of the good cock are these: handsome in body, but handsomer when feathered than when plucked, clothed rather than naked, bold, cheerful, loving and generous; and therefore those Gauls who have these qualities have sprung from the noble stock of the Gauls, and their former custom has changed for the better. Furthermore, these are the qualities of the best cock: watchful, alert, the first to rouse himself before the others, who rules his hens and subjects well and makes them fruitful, who draws grain out of the chaff and distributes it properly. These are the spiritual and mystical qualities by which good and fit prelates excel above the rest. And so much concerning the interpretation of the Gauls and of Gaul.

units.la: CAP. IV.
units.tr: CAP. IV.

units.la: Qui primitus munitiones & castra ad Rhenum instituit.
units.tr: Who first established fortifications and camps on the Rhine.

units.la: PRimo sciendum est, quod post Troiæ destructionem Æneas & Priamus, magni Priami nepos, cum multis tyrannis & magno exercitu peragrantes Africam, peruenerunt ad Italiam: in qua Æneas cum suo populo regnum cœpit instituere. Sic vera habet historia. Priamus vero transiens in Galliam, Gallicos qui supra Rhenum morabantur de terminis suis expulit, & versus Occidentem retrocedere coegit: ibique munitiones & castra instituens, Troiam videlicet minorem, quæ nunc Xanthus dicitur, & Verona, Bonna nuncupatur, per diœcesim Coloniensem coniuges accepit cum suo exercitu, de mulieribus. Teutonicis, eo quod essent corpulentæ & habiles ad prolem fortiorem propagandam. Processerunt enim à Teutonia Gigantes, ex quo Teutonici nuncupati sunt. Et ex iis dictis mulieribus filios & filias genuerunt, ac ipsorum idioma didicerunt.
units.tr: First, it must be known that after the destruction of Troy, Aeneas and Priam, the grandson of the great Priam, wandering through Africa with many followers and a great army, came to Italy, where Aeneas with his people began to establish a kingdom. So runs the true history. But Priam, passing over into Gaul, drove the Gauls who dwelt beyond the Rhine from their borders and forced them to retreat towards the west. There he set up fortifications and camps, namely the lesser Troy, which is now called Xanten, and Verona, which is called Bonn, within the diocese of Cologne. He took wives for his army from the Teutonic women, because they were large of body and fit to bear stronger offspring. For giants came forth from Teutonia, from which the Teutons got their name. And by these women they begot sons and daughters, and learned their language.

units.la: CAP. V.
units.tr: CHAP. V.

units.la: De parte exercitus Priami.
units.tr: On the part of Priam's army.

units.la: TAndem reliquiæ exercitus Priami, cum Treuerensibus pacem firmauerunt, & amicitiam: ibi sedem regni illius provinciæ, id est Galliæ posuerunt. Est etiam Treuerensis ciuitas, omnium ciuitatum & regnorum totius Europæ antiquissima. Fundata erat octauo anno natiuitatis Abrahæ, à Trebeta filio Nini, qui Semiramidem nouercam fugiens, ne cum ipsa incestum cogeretur committere, illuc deuenit: ibique ciuitatem constituit, quam pro suo nomine Treuerim nominauit. Exercitus autem Æneæ, qui in Italia apud Latinos resederat, istos populos, videlicet exercitus Priami, qui Galliam occupauerant, lingua Latina Germani appellabat, eo quod illi & isti de tyrannorum germine processerant. Tandem cum hi Germani multiplicati essent, miserunt partem exercitus in Turingiam, vltra Rhenum: & ibidem regnum instituentes, multo tempore reges habuerunt, reges Crinitos: quorum vnus erat Basinus, de quo infra mentionem faciam. Et propter has causas successu temporis tota Teutonia, tanquam à digniori Germania est vocata.
units.tr: At last the remnants of Priam's army made peace and friendship with the Treverians and there established the seat of the kingdom of that province, that is, of Gaul. There is also the city of Trier, the most ancient of all the cities and kingdoms of the whole of Europe. It was founded in the eighth year after the birth of Abraham by Trebeta, son of Ninus, who, fleeing his stepmother Semiramis so that he would not be forced to commit incest with her, came there, founded a city there, and named it Trier after his own name. Meanwhile, the army of Aeneas, which had settled in Italy among the Latins, called those peoples, namely the army of Priam which had occupied Gaul, "Germans" in the Latin tongue, because both they and these had sprung from the seed of tyrants. Eventually, when these Germans had multiplied, they sent part of the army across the Rhine into Thuringia, and there, establishing a kingdom, they had kings for a long time, the kings called Criniti, of whom one was Basinus, about whom I shall speak below. And for these reasons, in the course of time the whole of Teutonia was called after Germania, as the more worthy.

units.la: CAP. VI. Quare dicuntur Germani.
units.tr: CHAP. VI. Why they are called Germans.

units.la: SAluis igitur descriptionibus quae dicunt, Germaniam Rhenum habere in meridie, & eam esse dictam Germaniam à germinando, cum tamen illis realis veritas quodammodo contradicere videatur.
units.tr: Therefore, setting aside the descriptions which say that Germany has the Rhine on its south side and that it is called Germany from germinating (sprouting), since real truth seems in some measure to contradict them.

units.la: CAP. VII. De primo regno Germania.
units.tr: CHAP. VII. On the first kingdom of Germany.

units.la: POstremo cum regnum Romanorum adeo esset dilatatum, vt fere totus mundus ei subderetur: venit Iulius cum Romanis illam sibi terram, videlicet primam Germaniam & totam Galliam subiiciens: & ibidem quam plura castra & civitates aedificans, totam Treuerensem, Coloniensem & Moguntinensem dioecesim Romanis habitatoribus occupauit, antiquam germanitatem inter Romanos & illos Germanos renouando.
units.tr: Finally, when the kingdom of the Romans had been so extended that almost the whole world was subject to it, Julius came with the Romans, subjugating to himself that land, namely First Germany and all of Gaul; and building there very many camps and cities, he occupied the whole diocese of Trier, Cologne and Mainz with Roman inhabitants, renewing the ancient kinship between the Romans and those Germans.

units.la: CAP. VIII. De pugna Germanorum contra Alanos.
units.tr: CHAP. VIII. On the battle of the Germans against the Alani.

units.la: POstea autem quidam populi qui Alani dicti sunt, se Romanis opponebant: vnde exiit edictum à Senatu & populo Romano, vt quicunque illos Alanos compesceren t, immunes & liberi à tributo decem annis essent. Quo audito, Germani tam propter dignitatem Romanorum, quam propter libertatem tuendam, Alanos cum exercitu copioso sunt aggressi, & ipsos Romano Imperio subdiderunt.
units.tr: Afterwards, certain peoples called Alani opposed the Romans, whereupon an edict went out from the Senate and the Roman people that whoever should restrain those Alani would be exempt and free from tribute for ten years. Hearing this, the Germans, both on account of the dignity of the Romans and to defend their liberty, attacked the Alani with a large army and subjected them to the Roman Empire.

units.la: CAP. IX. Quare Franci, & liberi Germani.
units.tr: CHAP. IX. Why the Franks, and the free Germans.

units.la: ABillo tempore praefati Germani liberi sunt vocati: & propter hoc vsque in praesentem diem populus ille procurationes, exactiones violentas, decimas vel tributa naturaliter dedignatur, quia per huiusmodi viles serui conditiones in aliquo suae libertati derogetur. Isti vero Franci, Germani, & Gallici Comati (quae omnia vnam gentem significant siue determinant) cum in tantum germinassent, quod terra illa illos commode capere non posset, miserunt partem militiae versus Orientem vltra Rhenum, qui vsque hodie Franci orientales cum Francis Germanis in idiomate Teutonico concordant: licet illi crassiori, & isti modo mitiori pronuncient, sed habitu vestium & aliis modis in moribus discordant.
units.tr: From that time the aforesaid Germans were called free, and for this reason that people, even to the present day, naturally disdains stewardships, violent exactions, tithes or taxes, because by such base conditions of slavery something would be taken away from its liberty. But those Franks, Germans and Gallic Comati (all of which terms signify or designate one nation), when they had so multiplied that that land could not comfortably hold them, sent part of the militia towards the East across the Rhine; these are the Eastern Franks, who even today agree with the German Franks in the Teutonic idiom, although the former pronounce it more coarsely and the latter more gently, but they differ in customs in the dress and other ways of life.

units.la: CAP. X. De Francis qui Gallici dicuntur.
units.tr: CHAP. X. On the Franks who are called Gallic.

units.la: ALiam vero partem militiae miserunt versus Occidentem, inter Sequanam & Ligerim, fluuios famosos: qui ibidem cum mulieribus Gallicis contrahentes, filios & filias genuerunt ex eisdem, & earum mores & linguam Gallicam didicerunt: & vsque modo Francigenae, quasi à Francis geniti: & eorum terra Francia nominatur, à Germanis siue Francis idiomate discordantes, sed exteriori habitu conformes.
units.tr: But they sent another part of the militia towards the West, between the Seine and the Loire, famous rivers; these, marrying Gallic women there, begot sons and daughters from them, and learned their customs and the Gallic language; and to this day they are the Francigenae, as if born of the Franks, and their land is called Francia, differing from the Germans or Franks in idiom, but conforming in outward dress.

units.la: CAP. XI. In quibus differant Franci Gallici à Francis Germanis.
units.tr: CHAP. XI. In what the Gallic Franks differ from the German Franks.

units.la: HOc excepto, quod Francigenae cultui vestium, & aliis moribus inuenilibus, sicut torneamentis & cantilenis & ornatui capillorum, tanquam iuniores, vacant & dant operam: Franci vero tanquam seniores, serio se exercent, & discordia plurimum occupantur, ex veteri Romanorum germanitate quodammodo.
units.tr: Apart from this, that the Francigenae, like younger men, devote themselves and give their efforts to the cultivation of dress and other youthful habits, such as tournaments, songs and the adornment of the hair; while the Franks, as their elders, apply themselves seriously and are much occupied with discord, in some measure from the ancient kinship with the Romans.

units.la: CAP. XII. De pluribus regnis Germaniæ.
units.tr: CAP. XII. On the several kingdoms of Germany.

units.la: INista igitur prouincia quæ Gallia dicitur, & modo à Germanis & Gallicis, Francis & Francigenis possidetur, quandoque vnum, quandoque plura fuerunt regna: aliquando similiter, aliquando successiue, sicut modo & diu fuit in Hispania, vbi licet plures sint reges, tamen vnum dicitur regnum Hispanorum. Et hæc diuersitas regnorum & regum in Gallia multas facit diuersitates & contrarietates. In scripturis gesta & antiquitates Gallicorum & Germanorum & Francorum descripserunt, indifferenter his populis hæc nomina imponentes.
units.tr: In this province which is called Gaul, and is now possessed by the Germans and the Gauls, the Franks and the Franconians, there have at one time been one kingdom and at another several; sometimes simultaneously, sometimes in succession, as is the case now and was for a long time in Spain, where, although there are several kings, the kingdom is nonetheless called one kingdom of the Spaniards. This diversity of kingdoms and kings in Gaul produces many diversities and contrarieties. In the writings, those who described the deeds and antiquities of the Gauls, the Germans and the Franks applied these names indiscriminately to these peoples.

units.la: CAP. XIII. De gentilibus Regibus Germanorum & Gallicorum.
units.tr: CAP. XIII. Concerning the Pagan Kings of the Germans and the Gauls.

units.la: PRæterea sciendum est, quod à Priamo supra dicto vsque ad Pharamundum, & à Pharamundo vsque ad Hildricum, omnes principes Gallicorum & reges Romanorum gentiles erant, & pagani.
units.tr: Furthermore, it should be known that from Priamus, mentioned above, down to Pharamond, and from Pharamond down to Hildericus, all the princes of the Gauls and the kings of the Romans were heathens and pagans.

units.la: Qui Hildricus rex Francorum, cum esset lubricus & luxuriosus, Francorum corrupit filias, & vxores violauit: propter quod eiicientes eum ex regno, quendam alium Egidium Valerianum nomine in regem elegerunt. Hildricus vero ad Basinum regem Turingiæ profugit, suum auunculum: ibique incestum faciens, Basini coniugem clam cognouit. Post 7. vero annos mortuus est Valerianus, & Franci Hildricum reuocauerunt: quem Basina secuta est, Basino derelicto. Et successu temporis concepit & peperit filium quem Clodoueum nominauit. Hunc Clodoueum sic de adulterio gentilium procreatum, beatus Remigius baptizauit. Et ab isto Clodoueo omnes reges Francorum Christiani, & ex successione hæreditaria vsque ad Hildricum vltro successerunt. In illo tempore reges frequenter habitabant in Gallia Togata, videlicet Parisiis, eo quod Gallia Belgica ad prædicationem sancti Martialis, discipuli sancti Petri, ad cultum Christianum iamdudum conuerla, reges non curaret, sed sub regibus suis maioribus regebatur.
units.tr: This Hildericus, king of the Franks, was wanton and lustful; he corrupted the daughters of the Franks and violated their wives. For this reason they drove him out of the kingdom and chose another, named Egidius Valerianus, as king. Hildericus, however, fled to Basinus, king of Thuringia, his uncle, and there, committing incest, had secret intercourse with Basinus' wife. But after seven years Valerianus died, and the Franks recalled Hildericus; Basina followed him, leaving Basinus behind. In time she conceived and bore a son, whom she named Clodoveus. This Clodoveus, born of such adultery among the heathens, was baptized by the blessed Remigius. From this Clodoveus all the kings of the Franks were Christians, and by hereditary succession they came to the throne down to Hildericus. At that time the kings often lived in Gallia Togata, namely at Paris, because Gallia Belgica, long since converted to the Christian worship through the preaching of Saint Martial, a disciple of Saint Peter, did not regard its kings, but was governed under its own greater rulers.

units.la: CAP. XIV. Pipinus Grossus.
units.tr: CAP. XIV. Pipinus Grossus.

units.la: SVb isto Hildrico Pipinus Grossus, secundus fuit post regem Maior domus regiæ, quæ nunc est Palatium tutissimum: à quo Palatio dicuntur nunc comites Palatini, qui olim Maiores domus dicebantur. Hic autem Hildricus rex erat popularis, habens mores regales, & quotidie trahebatur ad theatrum & spectaculum, in vehiculo cum bubalis, & super eodem apparatu vestium vtebatur. Pipinus autem maior domus per omnia vir militaris & strenuus, regnum solicite & regaliter gubernabat sub eodem Hildrico. Vnde factum est, vt ad procurationem dicti Pipini Grossi, Papa, Barones & fideles regis ab ipsius fidelitate absolueret: qui Hildrico destituto, Pipinum in regem elegerunt.
units.tr: Under this Hildric, Pipin the Fat was the second after the king as mayor of the royal household, which is now the most secure Palace; from that Palace the counts palatine, who were formerly called mayors of the household, are now so named. Now this King Hildric was a man of the people, with royal manners, and every day he was carried to the theatre and the show in a cart drawn by oxen, and he used the same display of garments. Pipin, however, the mayor of the household, was in every respect a man of war and of vigour, and governed the kingdom carefully and in royal fashion under this same Hildric. Hence it came about that, through the efforts of the said Pipin the Fat, the Pope, the barons and the king's faithful subjects absolved them from their allegiance to him; and Hildric being deposed, they chose Pipin as king.

units.la: CAP. XV. De Capitolio Coloniensi.
units.tr: CHAP. XV. On the Cologne Capitol.

units.la: PIpini vero Maioris domus principale domicilium erat in Colonia Agrippina, in loco vbi nunc est monasterium sanctæ Mariæ in Capitolio. Hoc siquidem Plectrudis dicti Pipini Grossi coniunx, fundauit in honorem genitricis Dei, ibique conuentum monialium congregauit, & ipsum locum multis diuitiis & ornatu sublimauit. Tandem præfatus Pipinus coniugem suam Plectrudem pro tempore deseruit, & ilico concubinæ Alpaidiadhæsit. Super quo dum beatus Lambertus Tungrensium & Traiectensium episcopus Pipinum argueret, Dudo dux Ardennæ, frater præfatæ Alpaidis, sanctum Dei Lambertum interfecit. Quo audito, rex Pipinus, videlicet quod Christi sacerdos pro suo peccato martyrium subiisset, rubore & verecundia confusus, reuersus est Coloniam ad Plectrudem coniugem suam, Alpaide grauida derelicta. Cum autem Alpais peperisset, cucurrit nuncius ad regem, vt sibi de natiuitate talis filii nunciaret. Sed inueniés Regem inter nobiles & cum sua coniuge sedentem, dixit: Viuat rex, quia Karil: subtili verborum tegumento innuens, quod Alpais sibi pulchrum filium peperisset. Est enim Karil lingua Germanica homo robustus, membra habens magna. Respondit rex: Bonum, Karil. Iste fuit primus Carolus Martellus dictus, qui expulsis legitimis filiis patrisui, Drogone & Grimoaldo, patri suo successit. Erat autem iste tyrannus, multas clero & Ecclesiæ iniurias & damna inferens: propter quod accidit, vt dum ipse moreretur, internuncius Papæ somniauit in vrbe, quod Carolus Martellus rex Francorum corpore & anima duceretur in infernum. Misit ergo papa nuncios ad episcopum Treuerensem, qui aperto monumento serpentem inuenerunt mirę magnitudinis, corpore non reperto. Iste Carolus genuit Pipinum Nanum, qui respectu partis & aui Nanus videbatur, sed alias in corpore mediocris.
units.tr: The principal residence of Pippin the Mayor of the Palace was in Colonia Agrippina, in the place where the monastery of St Mary in the Capitol now stands. Plectrudis, the wife of the said Pippin the Great, founded it in honour of the Mother of God, gathered there a convent of nuns, and raised the place to great distinction with many riches and ornaments. Eventually Pippin deserted his wife Plectrudis for a time and at once attached himself to the concubine Alpaida. When the holy Lambert, bishop of the Tongrians and the Tungrians of Maastricht, rebuked Pippin for this, Dodo, duke of the Ardennes and brother of Alpaida, killed the holy servant of God Lambert. When the king heard this, Pippin, ashamed and confused by the blush of shame that the priest of Christ had suffered martyrdom for his sin, returned to Cologne to his wife Plectrudis, leaving the pregnant Alpaida behind. When Alpaida gave birth, a messenger ran to the king to tell him of the birth of such a son. But finding the king sitting among the nobles with his wife, he said: "Long live the king, for Karil!" hinting in a subtle veil of words that Alpaida had borne him a handsome son. For Karil, in the German tongue, means a robust man with large limbs. The king replied: "Good, Karil." This was the first Charles, called Martel, who, after expelling the lawful sons of his father, Drogo and Grimoald, succeeded his father. This man was a tyrant who inflicted many injuries and losses on the clergy and the Church. As a result, while he was dying, a papal messenger dreamed in the city that Charles Martel, king of the Franks, was being led to hell in body and soul. The pope therefore sent messengers to the bishop of Trier, who, opening the tomb, found a serpent of wondrous size, the body not being found. This Charles begot Pippin the Short, who seemed a dwarf in comparison with the stature of his father and grandfather, but in other respects of middling size in body.

units.la: CAP. XVI. Pipinus Nanus.
units.tr: CAP. XVI. Pipinus Nanus.

units.la: PIpinus Nanus duxit in matrimonio Thetbergam, sororem Michaelis Imperatoris Romanorum. Erat autem diebus illis Romanum imperium apud Græcos. Ex qua Thetberga Pipinus genuit Carolum magnum. Iste Pipinus Romanos ab infestatione Longobardorum liberauit, & Romanam ecclesiam multis diuitiis & deuotis obsequiis sublimauit. Quo defuncto, Carolus Magnus eius filius, succedens ei in regno, vt quidam dicunt, anno ætatis suæ 18. accidit vt Papa iterato auxilium Græcorum & Imperatoris aduocaret contra regem Longobardorum, quia simultas erat illo tempore inter Romanos & ecclesiam. Et dum Græci falsa fide Romanis auxilium denegarent, tunc iterum recursum habebant ad Carolum Pipini filium, & Imperatoris Græcorum consanguineum, qui defectum supplebat auunculi, & Longobardiam cum exercitu copioso ingressus, ipsum regem cum vxore & filio captiuos in ipsam vrbem deduxit: propter quod primo proclamatus est in Patricium Romanorum.
units.tr: Pipinus Nanus married Thetberga, sister of Michael, Emperor of the Romans. At that time the Roman empire was held by the Greeks. From this Thetberga, Pipinus begot Charlemagne. This Pipinus freed the Romans from the attacks of the Lombards, and he exalted the Roman church with many riches and devoted services. When he died, his son Charlemagne succeeded him in the kingdom, at the age of eighteen, as some say. It happened that the Pope again called upon the help of the Greeks and the Emperor against the king of the Lombards, because at that time there was enmity between the Romans and the church. And since the Greeks, with false faith, denied help to the Romans, they then turned again to Charlemagne, son of Pipinus and a kinsman of the Greek Emperor, who made up for the lack of his uncle. He entered Lombardy with a large army and led the king himself, with his wife and son, captive into the city itself. For this reason he was first proclaimed Patrician of the Romans.

units.la: CAP. XVII. Translatio imperii ad Carolum.
units.tr: CAP. XVII. The transfer of the empire to Charles.

units.la: POst hæc Papa Græcis regnum abiudicans, ipsum Carolum in Romanorum Imperatorem (vt dicitur) renitentem consecrauit, anno sui regni 12. Imperauit autem annis 42. & ætatis suæ anno 72. mortuus, & humatus Aquisgrani, vbi sui sancti nominis memoria quolibet anno solenniter celebratur. Vnde quicunque desiderat scire istius sancti viri virtutum insignia, & qualiter in regno huius seculi societatem meruit angelorum, ad præfatum locum (Aquisgranum scilicet) transeat, ibi gestorum eius merita pro laude perlegens Deo omnipotenti referat, qui gloriosi nominis propugnatorem Carolum prodigiis & miraculis tam in morte quam in vita multipliciter honorauit. Verum qualiter dictum regnum Francorum diuisum fuerit in Lotharingiam, Franciam & Germaniam: & Lotharingicum regnum deuolutum fuerit ad Germaniam, & qualiter alter frater fratrem, & consanguineus consanguineum de suo regno exterminauit, & multa alia regna, & aliorum gesta tanquam impertinentia prætermitto: præcipue quia multi de hac materia diuersa & contraria scripserunt, quandoque gesta vnius Regis vel gentis ob amorem vel inuidiam, aut etiam ignorantiam aliis attribuentes. Quæ omnia discussioni legentium committo, nunc reuertens ad propositum principale.
units.tr: After this, the Pope, stripping the Greeks of the kingdom, consecrated Charles (as it is said) as Emperor of the Romans, though he resisted, in the twelfth year of his reign. He reigned for 42 years and died in his 72nd year, and was buried at Aachen, where the memory of his holy name is solemnly celebrated every year. Therefore, whoever wishes to know the outstanding virtues of this holy man, and how he merited a place in the company of angels in the kingdom of this world, let him go to the aforementioned place (Aachen, namely), and there, reading through the record of his deeds for their praise, let him give thanks to Almighty God, who in death and in life has many times honoured Charles, the champion of a glorious name, with prodigies and miracles. But how the said kingdom of the Franks was divided into Lotharingia, France and Germany, and how the Lotharingian kingdom passed to Germany, and how one brother drove out another brother, and kinsman drove out kinsman from his kingdom, and many other kingdoms and the deeds of others, I pass over as irrelevant: especially since many writers on this subject have written diverse and contrary accounts, sometimes attributing the deeds of one king or people to others out of love or envy, or even ignorance. I leave all these things to the judgement of the readers, and now return to my main purpose.

units.la: CAP. XVIII. Qualiter sanctus Carolus instituit & præcepit, vt Imperium Romanorum remaneret perpetuo apud electionem Principum Germanorum.
units.tr: CAP. XVIII. How Saint Charles instituted and ordained that the Roman Empire should remain forever with the election of the princes of Germany.

units.la: FActum est quod sanctus Carolus Magnus imperator de consensu & mandato Romani Pontificis ordinationem sibi diuinitus inspiratam instituit, & præcepit vt Imperium Romanorum apud electionem canonicam principum Germanorum in perpetuum remaneret, nec non etiam verum Sanctuarium Dei, id est, regnum ecclesiæ iure hæreditario possideret, considerans quod ipse de Græcorum, Romanorum & Germanorum germine directa linea processisset: & quod ipse pater suus Pipinus primo, & ipse Carolus secundo per Francorum, id est, Germanorum auxilium, Romanam vrbem & Ecclesiam Dei à Lombardorum infestatione liberasset.
units.tr: It was done that Saint Charles the Great, the emperor, with the consent and command of the Roman Pontiff, established an ordinance divinely inspired in him, and ordered that the Roman Empire should remain in perpetuity with the canonical election of the princes of Germany; and likewise that he should hold the true sanctuary of God, that is, the kingdom of the Church, by hereditary right, considering that he himself had descended in a direct line from the stock of the Greeks, Romans and Germans; and that his father Pepin first, and he himself, Charles, second, had freed the city of Rome and the Church of God from the attacks of the Lombards by the aid of the Franks, that is, the Germans.

units.la: CAP. XIX. Qui principes Electores.
units.tr: CAP. XIX. The Electoral Princes.

units.la: SVnt hi principes Germaniæ, Archiepiscopus Treuerensis, Archicancellarius Galliæ: Archiepiscopus Coloniensis, Archicancellarius Italiæ: Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis, qui est Archicancellarius Germaniæ: & omnes Palatini, à quo olim Maiores domus dicebantur, à qua dignitate progenitores Carolii originem traxerunt principalem. Porro quod ipse Carolus rex Francorum extiterit, & ab illis regnum ex successione ad eum fuerit deuolutum, deinde Imperium, fuisset indecens, quod ipse filios eorum hæredes dignitate regia penitus denudasset.
units.tr: These are the princes of Germany: the Archbishop of Trier, Archchancellor of Gaul; the Archbishop of Cologne, Archchancellor of Italy; the Archbishop of Mainz, who is Archchancellor of Germany; and all the Palatines, from whom the Mayors of the Palace were formerly called, and from whose dignity the ancestors of Charles drew their principal origin. Moreover, that Charles himself should have been king of the Franks, and that the kingdom should have passed to him by succession from them, and afterwards the Empire, would have been unseemly, if he had stripped their sons completely of the royal dignity as heirs.

units.la: CAP. XX. De institutione Regis.
units.tr: CAP. XX. On the Institution of the King.

units.la: STatuit igitur, vt Franciigenae cum quadam regni portione Francorum regem haberent, de regali semine iure haereditario successurum, qui in temporalibus superiorem non recognoscet: cui videlicet, tanquam Imperatoris posteritas, ad homagium vel aliud obsequium non teneretur.
units.tr: He therefore decreed that the Franks, together with a certain portion of the kingdom, should have a king of the French, who would succeed by hereditary right from royal seed and would acknowledge no superior in temporal matters; to whom, namely, as the posterity of the Emperor, they would not be bound to render homage or any other service.

units.la: CAP. XXI. Quomodo studium Parisios sit translatum.
units.tr: CAP. XXI. How the university was transferred to Paris.

units.la: HInc regi, & suo haeredi, recompensationis regni defalcati adiecit Studium Philosophiae & liberalium artium, quod ipse de urbe Roma in civitatem Parisiensem transplantauit. Et est notandum, quod debitus necessarius ordo requirebat, vt sicut Romani tanquam seniores Sacerdotio, sic Germani vel Franci tanquam iuniores Imperio, & ita Francigenae & Gallici perspicaciores scientiarum studio dirigentur, & vt fidem Catholicam, quam Romanorum constantia firmiter tenet, vitas & Germanorum magnanimitas imperialiter tenere praecipiebat: & eadem Gallicorum argutiam & facundiam ab omnibus esse tenendam firmissimis approbatet rationibus, & demonstraret. His siquidem tribus sc. Sacerdotio, Imperio & Studio, tanquam tribus virtutibus, videlicet naturali, vitali, & scientiali, catholica Ecclesia spiritualiter mirificatur, augmentatur & regitur. His itaque tribus tanquam fundamento, pariete & tecto, eadem ecclesia tanquam materialiter proficit.
units.tr: Hence he also added, to the king and his heir, by way of compensation for the diminished kingdom, the Study of Philosophy and the liberal arts, which he himself transplanted from the city of Rome to the city of Paris. And it should be noted that the due and necessary order required that, just as the Romans, as elders, were set over the priesthood, so the Germans or Franks, as juniors, were set over the empire, and thus the Frenchmen and Gauls, being keener in the pursuit of the sciences, would be directed by it; and that the Roman steadfastness firmly holds the Catholic faith, while the magnanimity of the Germans was to hold it imperially; and he would demonstrate, by the firmest reasons, that the subtlety and eloquence of the Gauls ought to be held by all. For by these three, namely the priesthood, the empire and the study, as by three virtues, the natural, the vital and the intellectual, the Catholic Church is spiritually made wonderful, increased and governed. Upon these three, as upon a foundation, a wall and a roof, the same Church is in a material way made to advance.

units.la: CAP. XXII. Quare Sacerdotium habeat unam sedem, Studium unum, & Imperium quatuor.
units.tr: CAP. XXII. Why the Priesthood has one seat, the Studium one, and the Empire four.

units.la: ET nota, quod sicut ecclesiae materiali unum fundamentum & unum tectum sufficit, sed vnus paries non sufficit: sic Sacerdotio vna sedes principalis, videlicet Roma: & Studio vnus locus, videlicet Parisius, sufficit. Sed imperii quatuor loca principalia sancti Spiritus ordinatione nouimus attributa, quae sunt, Aquisgranum, Arelatum, Mediolanum, & urbs Roma. Studeant igitur illi quorum interest, vt huiusmodi domus integra maneat, & intacta, ne (quod absit) partibus dissoluatur & fur ille Antichristus, vel sui praecursores intrent aliunde quam per ostium, & gregem ouium interficiant cum pastore.
units.tr: And note that, just as one foundation and one roof suffice for a material church, but one wall does not, so for the Priesthood one principal seat, namely Rome, and for the Studium one place, namely Paris, are sufficient. But we know that four principal places of the Empire have been assigned by the ordinance of the Holy Spirit: Aachen, Arles, Milan, and the city of Rome. Let those whose concern it is therefore take care that this kind of house remain whole and untouched, lest (which God forbid) it be broken apart into parts, and that thief Antichrist, or his forerunners, enter from elsewhere than by the door and slaughter the flock of sheep along with the shepherd.

units.la: CAP. XXIII. Quare dicantur reges Francorum.
units.tr: CAP. XXIII. Why the kings of the Franks are so called.

units.la: VErum a tempore praenotato, reges Francigenarum se fecerunt, & tanquam a digniori reges Francorum appellari voluerunt. Illi autem qui usque ad haec tempora reges Francorum dicebantur, non sunt dicti reges Francorum a Francis orientalibus, qui sunt homines grossi & incompositi: neque a Francigenis occidentalibus, qui sunt homines delicati & compositi: sed a Francis Germanis, qui in vestibus a Francigenis, & in moribus a Romanis non multum discordant. Sciendum est, quod & post discessum vel transitum sancti Caroli, multis temporibus Imperatores Romanorum de progenie tua, & de regno Francorum, & non aliunde per principes Alemaniae sunt electi. Et quod, licet in multis locis legatur, quod ille vel ille rex Francorum, vel Imperator Romanus talem vel talem filium suum substituit in imperio: huiusmodi totum intelligendum est, fuisse factum de electione Principum, & consensu. Postremo vero surrexerunt quidam reges Francorum, qui conuersi in spiritum perueritatis, praesumebant sacrum Imperium non secundum canonicam electionem, sed quasi haereditario possidere, & super eo pro successione contendere. Unde factum est, vt Imperatores tales a defensione reipub. Romanorum, & a protectione sanctae Ecclesiae torpescerent: & insuper ecclesias quas eorum progenitores fundauerant, & multis possessionibus & multis priuilegiis dotauerant, inuaderent & turbarent, a vestigiis patrum suorum penitus deuiantes.
units.tr: But from the time mentioned above, the kings of the Franks made themselves, and wished to be called, kings of the Franks, as though from the more worthy part. Those, however, who up to these times were called kings of the Franks were not so called from the eastern Franks, who are a coarse and unpolished people, nor from the western Franks, who are a refined and polished people, but from the German Franks, who do not differ much from the Franks in their dress or from the Romans in their manners. It must be known that, even after the departure or death of Saint Charles, for many years the emperors of the Romans were chosen from your lineage and from the kingdom of the Franks, and not from elsewhere, by the princes of Germany. And although in many places one reads that this or that king of the Franks, or Roman emperor, substituted this or that son of his in the empire, all such things must be understood to have been done by the election and consent of the princes. Lastly, however, there arose certain kings of the Franks who, turned to the spirit of perversity, presumed to hold the holy empire not according to canonical election but as if by hereditary right, and to contend over it for succession. Whence it came about that such emperors grew slack in the defence of the Roman commonwealth and in the protection of the holy Church; and moreover they invaded and disturbed the churches which their forefathers had founded and endowed with many possessions and many privileges, wholly departing from the footsteps of their fathers.

units.la: CAP. XXIV. Quare cessauerunt principes Alemaniae eligere Imperatorem de regno Francia.
units.tr: Chapter 24. Why the princes of Germany ceased to elect an Emperor from the kingdom of France.

units.la: PRopter quod principes Germaniae electores Imperii dedignantes, de domo illa nullum Imperatorem recipere vel eligere voluerunt: & sic de aliquo tempore vacabat imperium, licet (vt praedixi). dixi) rex Francorum faceret Imperatorem se vocare. Hæc Lombardi sentientes, qui olim à Carolo Magno regia dignitate iuste priuati fuerant, & Romanorum imperio confiscati, ad eam se erexerunt audaciam, ut sibi aliquos reges de facto eligerent: quos non solum reges, sed etiam Imperatores non timerent appellare. Propter quam insolentiam, Germani grauiter excitati super huiusmodi turbatione iuris sui, & deformatione sacri Imperii, generale concilium habuerunt cum principibus & nobilibus Saxoniæ, eo quod ipsi nobiles de Francorum gente essent orti. Rex enim Carolus, dum ipse gentem Saxonum prius gladio materiali quam spirituali ad fidem Christianam convertisset, & eos nulla arte vel potentia in cultu Christiano tenere posset, quin frequenter quasi fera bestia sui regis absentia ad gentilitatis redirent errorem: ipse de populo Francorum viros elegit catholicos, maiores, medios & minores, numero ducenta decem millia, & illos in Saxoniam transplantauit, distribuens eisdem possessiones & terras, prout uniuscuiusque status & conditio requirebat: & vice versa consimilem numerum de populo Saxonum duxit in Franciam inferiorem: cuilibet ibidem etiam de terris & possessionibus prouidebat, ut sic Franci in Saxonia fidem Christi colerent, & Saxones in Francia eandem colere cogerentur. Propter hanc itaque causam super statu Imperii Germani à Saxonibus, tanquam à suis fratribus consilium & auxilium requirebant. Consensu itaque vnanimi & voluntate concordi decretum extitit, vt ab illo die in antea principes Saxoniæ, videlicet ipse rex Carolus, dux Saxoniæ & comes, ad Imperatoris electionem cum principibus Germaniæ interesse tenerentur.
units.tr: For this reason the electors of the German empire, disdaining to receive or elect an emperor from that house, refused to do so, and for some time the empire stood vacant, although the king of the Franks (as I said above) styled himself Emperor. The Lombards, who had long before been justly stripped of royal dignity by Charlemagne and deprived of the Roman empire, took such boldness from this that they set up kings for themselves in fact, whom they did not fear to call not only kings but even emperors. Because of this insolence, the Germans, roused in earnest over such a violation of their right and such a disfiguring of the holy empire, held a general council with the princes and nobles of Saxony, since those nobles were sprung from the Frankish people. For King Charles had first converted the Saxon nation to the Christian faith more by the material sword than by the spiritual, and since he could not keep them in Christian worship by any skill or power, they often, like wild beasts, returned to the error of paganism whenever their king was absent. So he chose from the Frankish people Catholic men of every rank, greater, middling and lesser, two hundred and ten thousand in number, and transplanted them into Saxony, assigning to each possessions and lands in keeping with the standing and condition of each. In turn he brought a like number from the Saxon people into Lower Francia, and likewise provided each of them with lands and possessions there, so that the Franks in Saxony would cultivate the faith of Christ, and the Saxons in Francia would be compelled to cultivate the same. For this reason, therefore, the Germans sought counsel and help on the state of the German empire from the Saxons, as from their own brothers. By unanimous consent and harmonious will it was decreed that from that day forward the princes of Saxony, namely King Charles himself, the duke of Saxony and the count, were bound to take part with the princes of Germany in the election of the Emperor.

units.la: CAP. XXV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXV.

units.la: De electione Principis Othonis Saxoniæ, & quomodo Imperium peruenerit ad domum Ducum.
units.tr: On the election of the Prince Otto of Saxony, and how the Empire came to the house of the Dukes.

units.la: QVo facto processerunt ad electionem, & inuocato sancti Spiritus fauore, Dominum Ottonem ducem Saxoniæ in regem Romanorum, & futurum Imperatorem concorditer elegerunt. Qui quidem magnifice & imperiose Francorum regibus & Lombardis super Romano Imperio perpetuum silentium imposuit. Et quia de vacationibus & oneribus Romanum imperium, ecclesias & Pontificem Dei in Italia & Germania subleuauit, quia in multis scriptutis sufficienter exprimitur, non oportet hic narrare. Porro ab isto tempore, per annos plurimos de domo ducum Saxoniæ Imperatores eligi consueuerunt, propter prædicti Ottonis & quorundam suorum successorum strenuitatem & benignitatem, quam frequenter in fideles & sanctam Ecclesiam exercebant: tandem etiam ex illa propagatione Reges exierunt, qui propter ferocitatem & tyrannidem Romani Imperii indignos se fecerunt. Vnde factum est, vt domus Ducum Saxoniæ non solum Imperio, verum & ipso ducatu, & omni dignitate principatus per iustam principum sententiam priuaretur.
units.tr: This done, they proceeded to the election, and, invoking the favour of the Holy Spirit, unanimously chose Lord Otto, duke of Saxony, as king of the Romans and future Emperor. He indeed, with great authority and dominance, imposed perpetual silence on the kings of the Franks and the Lombards concerning the Roman Empire. As for how he relieved the Roman Empire, the churches and the Pontiff of God in Italy and Germany of their vacancies and burdens, since this is sufficiently set out in many writings, there is no need to narrate it here. Furthermore, from that time on, for many years emperors were customarily chosen from the house of the dukes of Saxony, on account of the vigour and kindness of the aforesaid Otto and some of his successors, which they often showed toward the faithful and the holy Church. At length, however, kings also sprang from that line who, by their ferocity and tyranny toward the Roman Empire, made themselves unworthy. Hence it came about that the house of the dukes of Saxony was deprived, by the just sentence of the princes, not only of the Empire but also of the duchy itself and of every dignity of princely rank.

units.la: CAP. XXVI.
units.tr: CAP. XXVI.

units.la: Quomodo Ducatus VVestphaliæ & Angariæ, ecclesiæ Coloniensi sit adiectus.
units.tr: How the duchies of Westphalia and Angria were added to the Church of Cologne.

units.la: ARchiepiscopus siquidem Coloniensis Philippus nomine, Saxoniam intrauit cum exercitu Germanorum fidelium suorum, tribus militibus militum electorum: exceptis armigeris, equitibus, & exercitu pedestri, cuius non erat numerus. Et hoc modo tribus annis continuis Henricum patrem Ottonis Imperatoris, de quo totaliter venerabilem mentionem facere oportet, qui vtiq; regem Angliæ potestatibus & viribus anteibat, impugnans penitus triumphauit, manu potenti ducatum VVestphaliæ ac ducatum Angariæ sibi auferens: quos ducatus ecclesia Coloniensis vsq; in præsentem diem possidet, & per Dei gratiam in perpetuum possidebit.
units.tr: For Philip, archbishop of Cologne, entered Saxony with an army of German loyalists, three knights of the electors' knights, besides squires, horsemen and a foot soldiery whose number could not be counted. In this way, for three continuous years, he fought against Henry, the father of the Emperor Otto (of whom we must make wholly honourable mention, who indeed surpassed the king of England in power and strength), and utterly triumphed over him; by a mighty hand he took from him the duchy of Westphalia and the duchy of Angria. These duchies the Church of Cologne possesses to the present day, and by the grace of God will possess forever.

units.la: CAP. XXVII.
units.tr: CAP. XXVII.

units.la: Quomodo Imperium peruenit ad domum Ducum Sueuiæ.
units.tr: How the Empire came to the house of the Dukes of Swabia.

units.la: TRanslato itaque Imperio serenissimi principis Ottonis 4. Imperatoris, culpis eorum exigentibus, Electores vota sua in Fridericum ducem Sueuiæ dederunt, post ipsum quosdam de suis successoribus & hæredibus in Reges eligentes. Sed vtrum dictus Fridericus prece, vel precio, vel vitio Electorum gratiam meruerit, nescio. Sed scio, quod Imperatores ab illo tempore parum, vel nihil operati sunt laude dignum, vel vituperio, de pleno consilio & auxilio principum Germanorum, imo per Sueuos & Bauaros ac vlteriores Alemanos Imperium laborare coepit. Gubernabant ita, vt deinceps non regnum Germaniæ, sed regnum Alemaniæ nuncuparetur: & ita sub Sueuorum Imperio potestas & authoritas imperialis augeri desiit, & vehementius decrescere incepit: cuius decrementi causam & occasionem ego telinquo Guelphis & Gebelinis disputandam.
units.tr: When the Empire of the most serene prince Otto the Fourth had thus passed away, through the faults of its holders, the Electors gave their votes to Frederick, Duke of Swabia, and afterwards chose some of his successors and heirs as kings. But whether this Frederick earned the favour of the Electors by entreaty, by money, or by some fault of theirs, I do not know. What I do know is that from that time the Emperors achieved little or nothing worthy of praise or of blame, and the Empire began to labour not with the full counsel and aid of the German princes, but through the Swabians and Bavarians and the further Alemanni. They governed in such a way that from then on the kingdom was called not the kingdom of Germany but the kingdom of Alemannia; and so under the rule of the Swabians the imperial power and authority ceased to grow and began to decline more and more sharply. The cause and occasion of this decline I leave to be debated by the Guelphs and the Ghibellines.

units.la: CAP. XXVIII. De Friderico ultimo.
units.tr: CHAP. XXVIII. Of Frederick the last.

units.la: VEruntamen qualis Fridericus ultimus fuerit, Propheta insinuat, vbi dicit: Denudasti gentem siue domum Imperii vsque ad fundamentum,&c. Dicunt etiam quidam à longis temporibus vaticinatum esse in Germania, quod de huiusmodi Friderico Germaniæ radix peccatrix erumperet Fridericus nomine, qui clerum in Germania & ipsam Romanam ecclesiam humiliabit vehementer. Dicunt praeterea quidam, aliud esse ibidem vulgare prophetatum: quod de Carilingis, id est, de stirpe regis Caroli, & de domo Regum quidam Franciæ Imperator suscitabitur Carolus nomine, qui erit princeps & monarcha totius Europæ, & reformabit Ecclesiam & Imperium, sed post illum nunquam alius imperabit. Qui huiusmodi vaticiniis & incertis prophetiis vult fidem adhibere, adhibeat. Ego contentus sum, quod creator praesidet suæ creaturæ, & quod iusto Dei & irreprehensibili agitur iudicio, vt secundum merita cleri & populi alii habeant aduocatum, alii nullum, sed pro rege tyrannum, ad vindictam reproborum, & ad exercitium electorum.
units.tr: Yet what kind of man Frederick the last was, the Prophet hints when he says: You have laid bare the nation, or house, of the Empire down to its foundation, etc. Some also say that from ancient times it has been prophesied in Germany that a sinful root would sprout from such a Frederick, a man named Frederick, who will greatly humble the clergy in Germany and the Roman Church itself. Some further say that another common prophecy is current there: that an emperor named Charles will be raised up from the Carolingians, that is, from the stock of King Charles and from the house of the kings of France, who will be the prince and monarch of all Europe, will reform the Church and the Empire, but after him no one else will ever rule. Whoever wishes to put faith in such prophecies and uncertain predictions may do so. I am content with this: that the Creator presides over his creation, and that things are governed by the just and blameless judgment of God, so that, according to the merits of clergy and people, some have a protector, others none, and instead of a king they have a tyrant, for the punishment of the reprobate and the discipline of the elect.

units.la: CAP. XXIX. Qualiter baculus sancti Petri missus est ad Alemaniam, ex inspiratione Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: CAP. XXIX. How the staff of St Peter was sent to Germany, by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: ISti praehabitis, velut ab alio inchoandum est exordio: veruntamen eodem nitendo fine, concludere narranda cum narratis. Cum itaque beatus Petrus apostolus, ad praedicandam Gallis sanctæ Trinitatis fidem, tres viros sanctissimos destinauerat, scilicet Eucharium, Valerianum, & Maternum: & cum hi tres in quandam Galliæ Belgicæ prouinciam, quæ dicitur Elsatia, peruenissent: accidit vt beatus Maternus, in villa quæ Legia dicitur, alias Olii, infirmatus moritur: cuius corpus Eucharius & Valerianus terræ commendantes, eadem qua venerant via, cum magna festinatione, ad vibem Romanam sunt reuersi. Et dum starent in praesentia sancti Petri, dicebant ei: Pater sancte, ecce noster collega Maternus mortuus est, & sepultus. Et quia vltro absque tuo mandato procedere non expedit, supplicamus vt alium loco suo nobis adiungas. Et respondit Petrus: Non est sic faciendum: sed hae facta sunt, vt manifestetur gloria Dei coram gentibus. Accipite hunc baculum meum, & cum sepultura ad locum peruenerit i, extrahite corpus de sepulchro: & supponentes sibi baculum, dicite illi: Materne, mandat tibi CHRISTVS IESVS, filius Dei viui, & seruus eius Petrus, vt surgas, & iniunctum tibi officium vna mobiscum exequaris. Sanctus igitur Valerius & Eucharius, accepto baculo & mandato Apostoli, ad Legiam, vbi Maternum sepelierant, & de sepultura sua quadragesima sunt reuersi: & facientes sicut praecepit eis Apostolus, dicebant: Materne, mandat tibi CHRISTVS, filius Dei viui, & seruus eius Petrus. Quo dicto, mox cadauer illud, quod in sepulchro quadraginta diebus iacuerat, spiritum recepit, & anima corpori se coniunxit, & recedit mors: surrexit, & ambulauit cum patribus suis sanus & incolumis. Hoc signo viso, fere totus illius prouinciae populus glorificabat Deum: & baptizatus fuit illo die, in nomine Domini nostri IESV CHRISTI, multitudo hominum copiosa.
units.tr: Having dealt with the matters above, we must begin this account in the same way, and by the same aim bring the narrative to a close along with what has been narrated. When the blessed apostle Peter had sent three most holy men to preach the faith of the holy Trinity to the Gauls, namely Eucharius, Valerian and Maternus, and these three had come into a certain province of Belgic Gaul called Alsace, it happened that the blessed Maternus fell ill in a village called Legia, also Olii, and died. Eucharius and Valerian committed his body to the earth and, by the same road by which they had come, returned in great haste to the city of Rome. And as they stood in the presence of St Peter, they said to him: "Holy Father, behold our colleague Maternus is dead and buried. And since it is not fitting to proceed on our own initiative without your command, we beg you to join another to us in his place." Peter answered: "That is not how it should be done; but these things have happened so that the glory of God may be made manifest before the nations. Take this staff of mine, and when you have come to the place of the burial, draw the body out of the tomb, and laying the staff upon it, say to him: 'Maternus, Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, and his servant Peter command you to rise, and to carry out with us the office enjoined upon you.'" So holy Valerian and Eucharius, taking the staff and the apostle's command, went to Legia, where they had buried Maternus, and returned from his tomb on the fortieth day; and doing as the apostle had instructed them, they said: "Maternus, Christ, Son of the living God, and his servant Peter command you." At these words that corpse, which had lain in the tomb for forty days, immediately received its spirit, the soul was joined again to the body, death departed, and he rose and walked with his fathers, sound and whole. When this sign was seen, almost the whole population of that province glorified God, and on that day a great multitude of people was baptized in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: CAP. XXX. Hic Valerianus & Eucharius decesserunt.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXX. Here Valerian and Eucharius died.

units.la: SAnctiigitur Eucharius & Valerianus ac Maternus, vbique virtutibus & signis ampliabant fidem CHRISTI, baptisantes gentes in nomine eius. Sed Eucharius & Valerianus infra duodecim annos decesserunt ab hoc seculo, regnantes cum CHRISTO. Maternus autem post diem resurrectionis suæ, vixit annis 31. & populum Treuerensem, Tungrensem & Colonien sem ad fidem CHRISTI conuertit. Fecit etiam ibidem hoc miraculum, quod in tribus his ciuitatibus, à se inuicem ad modum trianguli plus quam duas magnas diætas distantibus, vna die solenniter tres Missas celebrarit. Et cum etiam populum Treuerensem baptizaret, tanta simul multitudo confluxit, vt eos baptizare oporteret in riuulo qui ciuitatem influit: qui tunc Belgis dicebatur. Et dum oleum sanctum deficeret, missō cœlitus oleo, totus ille riuulus consecratus oleo sacro omnibus apparebat. Et propter hoc idem riuulus Oleuia, quasi olei via dicitur, qui olim Belgis dicebatur. Et ab hoc riuulo Galliae Belgica nomen habet, licet alii dicant aliter. Porro cum sanctus Maternus, post commissum sibi ossicium, in Colonia moraretur, signo ab angelo dato, corpus eius translatum est ad ciuitatem Treuerensem: & baculus beati Petri apostoli, cum quo resuscitatus fuerat, in partes duas est diuisus. Cuius pars inferior cum corpore Pontificis penes Treuerim, superior vero pars penes Coloniam, & qua decet reverentia, reseruatur. Et est causa, quare Romanus episcopus baculum non habet Pontificalem, quem vtique beatus Petrus in spiritu prophetico transmisit ad Germanos.
units.tr: Therefore the saints Eucharius, Valerian and Maternus everywhere spread the faith of Christ by their virtues and signs, baptizing the nations in his name. But Eucharius and Valerian departed from this world within twelve years, reigning with Christ. Maternus, however, lived thirty-one years after the day of his resurrection, and converted the people of Trier, Tongeren and Cologne to the faith of Christ. He also performed this miracle there: on a single day he solemnly celebrated three Masses in these three cities, which lay more than two long day's journeys apart, forming a triangle. And when he was baptizing the people of Trier, so great a crowd gathered at once that he had to baptize them in the stream that flows into the city, which was then called the Belgis. And when the holy oil ran short, oil was sent from heaven, and that whole stream appeared to everyone consecrated with holy oil. For this reason the same stream is called Oleuia, as if it were the way of oil, though it was once called the Belgis. From this stream Belgic Gaul also takes its name, although others say otherwise. Furthermore, when Saint Maternus, after the office entrusted to him, was staying in Cologne, by a sign given by an angel his body was translated to the city of Trier; and the staff of the blessed apostle Peter, with which he had been raised, was divided into two parts. The lower part is kept at Trier with the body of the bishop, and the upper part at Cologne, with due reverence. And this is the reason why the Roman bishop has no pontifical staff: the blessed Peter, in prophetic spirit, sent it over to the Germans.

units.la: CAP. XXXI.
units.tr: CAP. XXXI.

units.la: Allegoria, sive tropus huius historia.
units.tr: Allegory, or trope, of this history.

units.la: IN hac igitur historia quaedam sunt literaliter admiranda, & quaedam singulariter rememoranda. Quid autem dignius est miraculo, quam quod beatus Petrus in urbe remanens, per baculum suum, in Germania fratrem suum mortuum suscitauit? & multitudinem gentium huius beati ministerio ad fidem Christi convertit? Sed per Petrum Apostolorum principem & fundamentum ecclesiae, nil nisi Regale sacerdotium intelligimus: & per baculum pastoralem, per quem pastor sustentatur, ouis errans ad ouile reducitur, & lupus rapax repellitur, nisi sacrum Imperium, id est imperiale regimen, designatur per baculum: siquidem pastor sustentatur, dum Romanorum Imperator, terrena se induens potestate, summum Pontificem & pastorem ouium, sua reuerentia & honore subleuat & exaltat. Per baculum etiam ouis errans ad ouile reducitur, velut Maternus mortuus resuscitabatur, dum quicunque peruersi Christiani peruersis moribus vel schismaticis, aut aliis erroribus a Romana ecclesiae obedientia deuiantes, de mandato Apostolico, per Imperatorem materiali gladio ad vnitatem fidei revocantur. Per baculum, inimici Christiani nominis, auctoritate Romani Pontificis, per Romanum Imperatorem conterunter.
units.tr: In this history, then, some things are to be wondered at literally, and some things are to be remembered in a special sense. What is more worthy of a miracle than that the blessed Peter, remaining in the city, raised his dead brother in Germany by means of his staff, and by this blessed ministry converted a multitude of peoples to the faith of Christ? But by Peter, the prince of the Apostles and foundation of the Church, we understand nothing other than the royal priesthood; and by the pastoral staff, by which the shepherd is supported, the straying sheep is brought back to the fold, and the ravening wolf is driven off, the holy Empire is designated, that is, the imperial rule, by the staff. For the shepherd is supported when the Emperor of the Romans, clothing himself with earthly power, lifts up and exalts the supreme Pontiff and shepherd of the sheep with his reverence and honour. By the staff, too, the straying sheep is brought back to the fold, just as Maternus was raised from the dead, when whatever perverse Christians, straying from obedience to the Roman Church by perverse morals or schisms or other errors, are recalled to unity of faith by the Emperor with the material sword, at the Apostolic command. By the staff the enemies of the Christian name are crushed, by the authority of the Roman Pontiff, through the Roman Emperor.

units.la: Huncitaque baculum beatus Petrus Romanus & Antiochenus episcopus, per Eucharium & Valerianum transmisit in Galliam Belgicam, dum Romanus Pontifex magnifici Caroli Romanum imperium de Graecis transtulit ad Germanos. Huius igitur baculi partem inferiorem, sed longiorem, habet ecclesia Treuerensis: superiorem vero & breuiorem, ecclesia Coloniensis: quia licet ciuitas Treuerensis antiquitate sit longior, & praefulgeat quam Coloniensis, multo tamen inferior est potestate & merito. Colonia superiorem partem baculi tenet, quia non solum Coloniensis archiepiscopus Regem Romanorum eligit, sed etiam electum prae omnibus aliis principibus primo tenetur & debet eum consecrare: in hoc Romani Pontificis procurans officium, qui Regem electum canonice in Imperatorem consecrat Romanorum.
units.tr: This staff, then, the blessed Peter, bishop of Rome and of Antioch, sent into Belgic Gaul through Eucharius and Valerian, when the Roman Pontiff transferred the Roman empire from the Greeks to the Germans in the time of the illustrious Charles. Of this staff the lower part, but the longer, is held by the Church of Trier; the upper and shorter part by the Church of Cologne. For although the city of Trier is longer in antiquity and surpasses Cologne in splendour, it is nevertheless far inferior in power and merit. Cologne holds the upper part of the staff, because the archbishop of Cologne not only elects the King of the Romans, but also, before all other princes, is bound and obliged to consecrate the one elected; in this he discharges the office of the Roman Pontiff, who canonically consecrates the elected king as Emperor of the Romans.

units.la: CAP. XXXII.
units.tr: CAP. XXXII.

units.la: Quod ex praecogitata deliberatione & industria non debeat Regalis, vel Imperialis dignitas deleri.
units.tr: That the royal or imperial dignity ought not to be blotted out by deliberate planning and design.

units.la: EX praedictis igitur omnibus manifestum est, quod sicut ecclesia Romana est ecclesia Dei, sic vtique regnum Romanum est regnum Dei. De quo potest intelligi hoc, quod dicit Iesus discipulis suis: Vobis, inquiens, est datum nosse mysterium regni Dei: illis autem qui foris sunt (subaudi, vanitatibus seculi inuolutis) omnia fiunt in parabolis, vt videntes non videant, audientes non audiant, & intelligentes non intelligant. Si enim omnia quae mystice fiunt in hoc regno Dei, palam cunctis demonstrarentur: non solum carnales & superbi, quinimo ipsi potius veritatem verterent in derisum. Cum ergo, tantorum Romanorum Imperatorum, erga sanctam ecclesiam Romanam devotio & liberalitas non deberet ad memoriam reuocari, tunc absque regno esset Scriptura: ac sic ex praeexcogitata deliberatione vel industria, non redintegrata memoria, de Libro viuentium delerentur, & quare saltem semel in anno pro Rege vel regno Romanorum generalis oratio non fieret? cum etiam fieri consueuit pro Saracenis & Iudaeis, & hanc vtique ingratitudinem & iniuriam Rex regum suo tempore sibi factam reputaret.
units.tr: From all the foregoing, then, it is plain that just as the Roman Church is the Church of God, so the Roman kingdom is certainly the kingdom of God. This may be understood of what Jesus says to his disciples: "To you," he says, "it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God; but to those who are outside (understand, wrapped up in the vanities of the world) all things are done in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not hear, and understanding they may not understand." For if all the things that are mystically done in this kingdom of God were openly shown to everyone, not only the carnal and the proud, but rather they themselves would turn the truth into mockery. Since, then, the devotion and generosity of so many Roman emperors towards the holy Roman Church ought not to be recalled to memory, Scripture would be without a kingdom, and thus by premeditated deliberation or design, with memory not restored, they would be blotted out of the Book of the living. And why is a general prayer not made at least once a year for the King or the kingdom of the Romans? For it is customary to pray also for the Saracens and the Jews; and the King of kings would surely reckon this ingratitude and injury, done to him in his own time, as done to himself.

units.la: CAP. XXXIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXIII.

units.la: Quod Romanus Pontifex debet habere diligentiam de studio Parisiensi, & de Imperio, & de Sacerdotio.
units.tr: That the Roman Pontiff ought to take care of the study at Paris, and of the Empire, and of the Priesthood.
