Sed cum sonitu transiuit illa spes, & vt virgula fumi evanuit subito in seipsa. Cumula nunc, & sarcina fortiter tibi thesauros transitorios, quibus diu gaudere non potes. Nescis, quia scriptum est; Melius est nomen bonum, quam unguenta pretiosa multa? Dic mihi, quaeso, vbi remanserunt duodecim illae statuae aureae, quae bustum Magni Alexandri sustentabant. Vbi denique illae magnae sunt diuitiae praedicti Salomonis in cuius tempore argentum, sicut aes, & ferrum in Hierusalem habebatur? Et vbi remansit aes fusum, quod Marcus Crassus in tam magna copia recepit a templo memorato? Dic etiam mihi, rogo, vbi est illa statua grandis Nabuchodonosoris aurea tota, quam pene totus populus, vrgente Regis Imperio, adorabat? Vtinam possideres, & tunc forsan aliquid notatu dignum pro salute imperii efficere cogitares.
units.tr: ...names ought to agree with things. So use the title of Roman Prince in word only, as you have done until now. But King Ladislaus, the Third of that name among the kings who claim to be Roman kings, boasts not in writing but in deeds. You sleep, and he keeps watch. The Romans themselves, as is said, already call him Roman Emperor. Whose fault is this, if I may speak the truth, except yours through negligence? O how many thousands of florins has that King Ladislaus poured out before he could even reach Rome at all? What shame, and what disgrace here and everywhere, has arisen from your great idleness and folly, you who once believed yourself the magnificent liberator of the faithful of the Empire, even in these parts? But that hope passed away with a noise, and vanished suddenly like a wisp of smoke. Now heap up and carry, bravely, your fleeting treasures, which you cannot long enjoy. Do you not know that it is written: A good name is better than many precious ointments? Tell me, I ask you, where have those twelve golden statues gone, which held up the tomb of Alexander the Great? Where, finally, are the great riches of the aforesaid Solomon, in whose time silver was held in Jerusalem as common as bronze and iron? And where is the cast bronze which Marcus Crassus took in such great quantity from that temple I mentioned? Tell me too, I beg, where is that great golden statue of Nebuchadnezzar, all of gold, which nearly the whole people adored at the urging of the King's command? Would that you possessed it; then perhaps you would think of doing something worth noting for the safety of the Empire.

units.la: Haec & multa similia euanuerunt, aera refulgentia perierunt, & ad nihilum tractu temporis deuenerunt: tamen facta multorum magnificorum virorum memorabilia adhuc in magna copia conscripta videntur. Quid autem ad laudem carthulae faciat, tu ipse perpende. Quaeso esto vir de caetero sequendo eorundem tuorum praedecessorum commendanda vestigia, quorum hactenus apud mortales celebris memoria per tuam desidiam per orbem vndique offuscatur: cito etenim authores aliquod proverbium propter tam inexcusabilem tuam desidiam omnibus Alemannis imponent, sicut de aliis nationibus dicunt, vbi gratia non est militaris, certe neque virilis habitatio, in Cypro in qua fastus Gallicus, Syra mollities, Graecae blanditiae ac fraudes, quae vnam videlicet in insulam convenerunt. Heu timeo frustra laborare iuxta id, durum valde, grande aliquod debere, cui nolis: sitamen Romani nominis adeo pudet, consulo Romanam abiice dignitatem, non occupando illam inutiliter, prout fecisti hactenus in Catholicae fidei detrimentum. Vale feliciter, pronto opto. Scripta 1. die Maii.
units.tr: These things and many like them have vanished, the shining bronzes have perished, and have come to nothing in the course of time; yet the deeds of many magnificent and memorable men are still seen written down in great abundance. What it would add to the praise of your little paper, consider for yourself. I beg you, be from now on a man who follows the commendable footsteps of your own predecessors, whose celebrated memory among mortals has until now been dimmed throughout the world by your idleness. For soon the writers, on account of your utterly inexcusable idleness, will impose some proverb on all the Germans, just as they say of other nations where there is no military grace, and certainly no manly habitation: in Cyprus, where Gallic pride, Syrian softness, Greek flattery and deceits have come together in one island. Alas, I fear that you labour in vain, since it is very hard to owe something great to one who is unwilling. Yet if you are so ashamed of the Roman name, I advise you to cast off the Roman dignity, not holding it uselessly, as you have done until now to the detriment of the Catholic faith. Farewell and prosper, as I heartily wish. Written on the 1st day of May.

units.la: MAGISTRI IOAN- NIS CARLERII DE GERSON SACRARVM LITERARVM DOCTORIS RESOLUTISSIMI & Christianissimi, ac Cancel- larii Parisiensis
units.tr: The Works of Master John Charlier de Gerson, most learned and most Christian Doctor of Sacred Letters, and Chancellor of Paris

units.la: OPERA DE ECCLESIASTICA ET POLITICA POTESTATE.
units.tr: CONCERNING ECCLESIASTICAL AND POLITICAL POWER.

units.la: TRACTATVS IOANNIS DE GERSON CANCELLARII Parrhisiensis de potestate Ecclesiastica & de origine iuris & legum, editus Constantiae tempore Concilii generalis.
units.tr: THE TREATISE OF JOHN GERSON, CHANCELLOR OF PARIS, ON ECCLESIASTICAL POWER AND ON THE ORIGIN OF LAW AND LAWS, PUBLISHED AT CONSTANCE DURING THE TIME OF THE GENERAL COUNCIL.

units.la: ROEMIVM, quod expedit inquirere de ecclesiastica potestate.
units.tr: First, it is expedient to inquire into ecclesiastical power.

units.la: In prima consideratione describitur potestas ecclesiastica per causam quadruplicem.
units.tr: In the first consideration, ecclesiastical power is described by a fourfold cause.

units.la: In secunda distinguitur potestas ecclesiastica multis modis: & ostenditur, quod potestas ordinis est aequalis in omnibus sacerdotibus, quo ad consecrationem corporis Christi.
units.tr: In the second, ecclesiastical power is distinguished in many ways, and it is shown that the power of orders is equal in all priests as regards the consecration of the body of Christ.

units.la: In tertio ostenditur, quod potestas ordinis non est simpliciter aequalis in omnibus sacerdotibus & episcopis.
units.tr: In the third, it is shown that the power of orders is not simply equal in all priests and bishops.

units.la: In quarta ostenditur, quid sit potestas iurisdictionis in foro exteriori.
units.tr: In the fourth, it is shown what the power of jurisdiction in the outer forum is.

units.la: In quinta ostenditur, quid sit potestas iurisdictionis in foro interiori, & de duplici subiectione.
units.tr: In the fifth, it is shown what the power of jurisdiction in the inner forum is, and concerning the twofold subjection.

units.la: In sexta ponitur quatruplex distinctio vtilis & necessaria pro intellectu sequentium.
units.tr: In the sixth, a fourfold distinction is laid down, useful and necessary for understanding what follows.

units.la: In septima quid dicendum sit de ecclesiastica potestate, dum consideratur formaliter & absolute.
units.tr: In the seventh, what must be said of ecclesiastical power when it is considered formally and absolutely.

units.la: In octava quid dicendum sit de ecclesiastica potestate, prout consideratur respectiue & quodammodo materialiter seu subiectiue.
units.tr: In the eighth, what must be said of ecclesiastical power when it is considered relatively, and in a certain way materially or subjectively.

units.la: In nona quid dicendum sit de ecclesiastica potestate, dum consideratur quo ad vsum vel exercitium: & illic fundatur suprema plenitudo ecclesiasticae potestatis.
units.tr: In the ninth, what must be said of ecclesiastical power when it is considered as to its use or exercise; and there the supreme fullness of ecclesiastical power is grounded.

units.la: In decima ostenditur quod in Papa est plenitudo ecclesiasticæ potestatis & describitur.
units.tr: In the tenth, it is shown that the fullness of ecclesiastical power is in the Pope, and it is described.

units.la: In vndecima ostenditur qualiter plenitudo ecclesiasticæ potestatis sit in ecclesia vel generali concilio.
units.tr: In the eleventh, it is shown how the fullness of ecclesiastical power is in the Church or in a general council.

units.la: In duodecima ostenditur de plenitudine potestatis Papalis per respectum ad bona ecclesiasticorum & laicorum.
units.tr: In the twelfth, the fullness of papal power is shown with respect to the goods of clergy and laity.

units.la: In decima tertia fundatur omnis potestas à prima iustitia variis & multis membris.
units.tr: In the thirteenth, all power is grounded in primary justice, in various and many members.

units.la: Potestas ecclesiastica debet ab ecclesiasticis quid & qualis & quanta sit agnosci. Habet hoc itaq; fieri: vt & honoretur cognita, cum Deus dederit talem potestatem hominibus: & in suis terminis honorata seruetur, ne plus debito falsæ eam opiniones vel deprimant vel exultent. Quoniam primum est sacrilegæ impietatis. Alterum de adulatione pestifera suspectum est. Constat igitur, quod de potestate ecclesiastica disputare vel inquirere nedum licet, sed decet & expedit, tantummodo sit intentionis oculus simplex & rectus. Quid ni sic liceat cum de ipsius omnipotentis Dei potestate crebro fiat absque omni temeritate conquisitio. Hæc me consideratio mouit, vt de potestate ecclesiastica sub paucis considerationibus dissererem, quatenus materia, quæ quodammodo videtur infinita, sicut tractari solet ab aliquib. per auctoritates & allegationes, resolueretur ad paucos certos, & claros terminos, per descriptiones & diuisiones resolutiue procedendo, allegationum confusione dimissa, quales apud doctores inuenire non est difficile; Cæterum non vsurpo nunc in hoc opusculo vel aliis me dicturum aliquid, quod alibi non inueniatur, sciens illud Comici: Nullum est iam dictum quod non dictum sit prius. Satis est si ex bene inuentis & doctrinis aliorum ego meis verbis meo ordine fauum aliquem veritatis instar apum propria quadam arte compingam. Fiet autem initium quid nominis terminorum: quoniam hoc ignorato paralogizantur faciliter inquisitores veritatis. Erit vero finis de origine iuris & legum.
units.tr: Ecclesiastical power ought to be recognised by churchmen: what it is, of what kind, and how great. This can therefore be done so that, once it is known, it is honoured, since God has given such power to men; and, kept honoured within its own limits, it is not lowered or exalted by false opinions beyond what is owed. For the first is a sacrilegious impiety, and the second is suspected of pestilent flattery. It is clear, therefore, that to dispute or inquire about ecclesiastical power is not only permitted but proper and expedient, provided only that the eye of the intention be simple and upright. Why should it not be permitted, when inquiry is often made, without any rashness, into the power of almighty God himself? This consideration moved me to discuss ecclesiastical power briefly, in a few considerations, so that the matter, which in some way seems infinite and which some are accustomed to treat by authorities and citations, might be resolved into a few certain and clear points, proceeding resolutively by descriptions and divisions, the confusion of citations set aside, such as are not hard to find among the doctors. Yet I do not now claim in this little work, or in others, that I shall say anything that is not found elsewhere, knowing that saying of the comic poet: Nothing has now been said that has not been said before. It is enough if, from well-discovered matters and the teachings of others, I put together in my own words and in my own order some honeycomb of truth, in the manner of bees, by a certain art of my own. The beginning will be made with the meaning of the terms, since inquirers after truth are easily led into faulty reasoning if this is not known. The end will be concerning the origin of law and laws.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO I.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION I.

units.la: Potestas ecclesiastica est potestas, quæ à Christo supernaturaliter & specialiter collata est suis Apostolis & discipulis: ac eorum successoribus legitimis vsq; in finem seculi ad ædificationem ecclesiæ militantis secundum leges euangelicas pro consecutione felicitatis æternæ. Hæc descriptio data est per causam quadruplicem secundum quam distinguitur potestas ecclesiastica ab alia qualibet potestate. Potestas ibi ponitur pro genere. Est autem potestas facultas propinqua ad exeundum in actum. Propinqua, inquam: quia secundum facultatem remotam & obedientialem non est impossibile apud Deum omne verbum. Porro notatur causa efficiens principalis cum dicitur: à Christo supernaturaliter collata. Causa vero materialis vel subiectiua signatur cum subditur: suis Apostolis, &c. Causa formalis insinuatur, cum dicitur: secundum leges euangelicas, dant enim formam vtendi. Denique causa finalis concluditur. Ad ædificationem ecclesiæ militantis pro consecutione felicitatis æternæ. Additum est hoc aduerbium specialiter, ad exclusionem donorum supernaturalium; quæ omni viatori possunt esse communia: sicut sunt fides, spes, charitas, prophetia, timor, pietas & similia. Vnde & ecclesia contracte sumitur, dum loquimur hic de ecclesiastica potestate, pro illis videlicet, qui speciali quodam signaculo dedicati sunt ad diuinum seruitium; à clericatura quæ infimum tenet gradum, vsque ad supremum, quo Papa decoratur. Fallor si non sit hæc descriptio propria competens omni & soli ecclesiasticæ potestati: quoniam omnis alia potestas vel est naturaliter indita quo ad causam efficientem: vel est secundum leges naturales aut humanas regulata quo ad causam formalem: vel est ad finem naturalem immediate & principaliter ordinata: vel denique quo ad causam subiectiuam radicatur in habentibus eam secundum dona naturalia: etiam vbi supernaturalia non adessent: qualia sunt fides, spes & charitas.
units.tr: Ecclesiastical power is that power which was conferred supernaturally and specially by Christ on his Apostles and disciples, and on their lawful successors until the end of the age, for the building up of the Church militant according to the evangelical laws, for the attainment of eternal happiness. This description is given by a fourfold cause, by which ecclesiastical power is distinguished from any other power. Power is here put for the genus. Now power is a faculty near to passing into act. Near, I say, because according to a remote and obediential faculty, nothing is impossible with God. Next, the principal efficient cause is noted when it is said: conferred supernaturally by Christ. The material or subjective cause is indicated when it is added: on his Apostles, etc. The formal cause is suggested when it is said: according to the evangelical laws, for these give the form of exercising it. Finally, the final cause is concluded: for the building up of the Church militant, for the attainment of eternal happiness. The adverb specially has been added to exclude supernatural gifts, which can be common to every wayfarer, such as faith, hope, charity, prophecy, fear, piety and the like. Hence also the word Church is taken in a restricted sense, when we speak here of ecclesiastical power, namely for those who are dedicated to divine service by a special sign, from the clerical order, which holds the lowest rank, up to the highest, with which the Pope is adorned. I am mistaken if this description is not proper and suited to all and only ecclesiastical power; for every other power is either naturally implanted as to its efficient cause, or is regulated by natural or human laws as to its formal cause, or is ordered immediately and principally to a natural end, or finally, as to its subjective cause, is rooted in those who have it by natural gifts, even where supernatural gifts are absent, such as faith, hope and charity.

units.la: Vnde potestas secularis conuenit aliis, quam Christianis baptizatis. Potestas autem ecclesiastica de necessitate fundatur in dono supernaturali: sicut est character baptismalis de communi lege: qui character in viatoribus eos de ecclesia militante reddit, facit insuper idoneos & capaces ecclesiasticæ potestatis. Fatemur itaque quod charitas seu gratia gratum faciens valde decens est in suscepturis, vel iam habentibus ecclesiasticam potestatem: non tamen exigitur pro dando titulum, quasi sine ea nequeat in aliquo fundari vel subsistere potestas huiusmodi.
units.tr: Hence secular power belongs to others than baptized Christians. But ecclesiastical power is of necessity grounded in a supernatural gift, just as the baptismal character is by the common law; this character makes wayfarers members of the Church militant, and moreover makes them fit and capable of ecclesiastical power. We therefore admit that charity, or grace that makes one pleasing to God, is very fitting in those who are to receive, or already have, ecclesiastical power; yet it is not required for conferring the title, as though such power could not be grounded or subsist in anyone without it.

units.la: Hic enim fuit error verus Valdensium & pauperum de Lugduno, qui per Vvicleff & sequaces suos renouari quæsitus est, sed iuste damnatus. Cur ita? Ne Hierarchicus ordo potestatis ecclesiasticæ maneat instabilis, vagus & incertus: cum nemo sciat an amore vel odio dignus sit. Et minus hoc de gratia prædestinationis constet, quam ponunt radicem necessariam pro titulo vel iure cuiuslibet potestatis. Hac igitur: descriptione præsuppositâ pro intelligentia quid sit ecclesiastica potestas in genere, descendemus ad species. Pro quarum notitia multiplex animaduertenda est distinctio, vt differentiæ, quæ additæ generi constituunt speciem, innotescant.
units.tr: For this was the true error of the Waldensians and the Poor of Lyons, which was sought to be revived through Wycliffe and his followers, but was justly condemned. Why so? So that the hierarchical order of ecclesiastical power may not remain unstable, wandering and uncertain, since no one would know whether he were worthy of love or of hatred. And this is all the less certain of the grace of predestination, which they posit as the necessary root for the title or right of any power whatever. With this description presupposed, so that we may understand what ecclesiastical power is in general, we shall descend to its species. For the knowledge of these a manifold distinction must be noted, so that the differences which, added to the genus, constitute the species may become known.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO II.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO II.

units.la: Potestas ecclesiastica secernitur prima sui diuisione in potestatem ordinis & Potestatem iurisdictionis. Rursus potestas ordinis duplicem habet respectum. Vnus est super corpus Christi mystimysticum verum quo ad consecrationem eius. Alter est super corpus Christi mysticum seu membra eius. Et hoc dupliciter: vel quo ad ministrationem corporis Christi veri, vel quoad ministrationem, vel exhibitionem alterius sacramenti; sicut est ordo vel confirmatio, vel pœnitentialis absolutio.
units.tr: Ecclesiastical power is distinguished, by its first division, into the power of order and the power of jurisdiction. Again, the power of order has a twofold respect. One is over the true mystical body of Christ, with regard to its consecration. The other is over the mystical body of Christ, that is, its members. And this in two ways: either with regard to the administration of the true body of Christ, or with regard to the administration or exhibition of another sacrament, such as ordination or confirmation, or penitential absolution.

units.la: Potestas iurisdictionis duplex est: una in foro exteriori; altera in foro conscientiæ interiori.
units.tr: The power of jurisdiction is twofold: one is in the external forum, the other in the internal forum of conscience.

units.la: Rursus potestas iurisdictionis in foro exteriori dupliciter consideratur. Uno modo prout immediate à Christo tradita est secundum legem euangelicam. Alio modo prout superaddita est ex humana constitutione vel dono per principes seculares aut aliter. Subinde potestas iurisdictionis in foro interiori consurgit ex duplici radice. Uno modo ex parte hominis vltro se subiicientis tali potestati: sicut cum sponte confitens subiicit se presbytero; & ordinandus episcopo. Alius subiectionis modus consurgit ex authoritate superioris, hunc vel illum tali vel tali subiicientis: quod fieri potest non ad arbitrium illius qui subiicitur: & sic inter duplicem hanc subiectionem differentia magna patet.
units.tr: Again, the power of jurisdiction in the external forum is considered in two ways. In one way, as it is handed over immediately by Christ according to the evangelical law. In another way, as it is added on by human constitution, or granted by secular princes or in some other manner. Likewise, the power of jurisdiction in the internal forum arises from a twofold root. In one way, from the side of the man who voluntarily submits himself to such power: as when a penitent willingly submits himself to a priest, and an ordinand to a bishop. The other mode of subjection arises from the authority of a superior, who subjects this or that person to such or such a power; which can happen without the consent of the one who is subjected. And so the great difference between these two kinds of subjection is evident.

units.la: Et quoniam ad pauca aspicientes defacili enuntiant: & enunciantes seipsos vel dicta sua non resoluunt, sed confundunt: eorum doctrina redditur vel erronea vel inintelligibilis vel difficilis & perplexa. Doctrina vero sapientum facilis, teste Sapiente: quia resolute & ordinate per distinctiones tradent omnia separantes pretiosum à vili: & præcauentes ne lucem veritatis tenebrosa nubes erroris inuoluat, sed sit ignis sine fumo. Declarationem multiplicis huius distinctionis melius aliter dare non possumus, quam si sua cuilibet membro donetur descriptio vel specialis notificatio.
units.tr: And since those who look at only a few things readily make pronouncements, and in their pronouncements do not resolve their matters but confuse them, their teaching becomes either erroneous, or unintelligible, or difficult and perplexing. But the teaching of the wise is easy, as the Sage bears witness: because they will set out all things resolutely and in order, through distinctions, separating the precious from the worthless, and taking care that a dark cloud of error does not wrap up the light of truth, but that it be fire without smoke. We cannot give an explanation of this manifold distinction better than by giving each member its own description or special notification.

units.la: Dicamus igitur, quod potestas ordinis primo modo considerata, & potestas ecclesiastica respiciens principaliter & essentialiter consecrationem corporis Christi veri: qua scilicet potest habens eam consecrare corpus & sanguinem Christi virtute verborum sacramentalium.
units.tr: Let us say, therefore, that the power of order, considered in the first way, and the ecclesiastical power that looks principally and essentially to the consecration of the true body of Christ: namely, the power by which the one who has it can consecrate the body and blood of Christ by the virtue of the sacramental words.

units.la: Ponitur hic potestas ecclesiastica pro genere: quæ potestas quid & qualis sit immediate prædiximus: cuius descriptionem hic & in omnibus consequenter dicendis absque aliqua peritione supponimus, dum utemur hoc termino pro genere, potestas ecclesiastica. Additur hæc clausula: respiciens principaliter, &c. tanquam pro differentia specifica, distinguente eam à qualibet alia ecclesiastica potestate. Hæc potestas de lege communi inabdicabilis est, inauferibilis & illimitabilis in sua essentia: quoniam quisquis est sacerdos rite consecratus, si tentet cum intentione & cum forma & materia debitis consecrare: consecrat utique etiam si excommunicatus, si hæreticus, si quomodocunque degradatus exititerit, peccaret nihilominus in hoc casu; nec ad vtilitatem suam, sed damnationem hocageret.
units.tr: Here "ecclesiastical power" is taken as the genus: what this power is and what sort of thing it is we have just said directly; we presuppose its description here and in everything that follows without any further explanation, since we shall use this term, "ecclesiastical power", as the genus. The clause is added, "looking principally", etc., as a specific difference, distinguishing it from every other ecclesiastical power. This power, by the common law, cannot be renounced, cannot be taken away, and is unlimited in its essence. For whoever is a priest rightly consecrated, if he tries to consecrate with the intention, form and matter due, he does consecrate, even if he has become excommunicate, a heretic, or degraded in whatever way; yet in this case he would sin, and he would do this not for his own benefit but to his condemnation.

units.la: Iuxta quod vtiliter distingui solet: quod aliqua sunt de necessitate executionis huiusmodi potestatis dupliciter. Vna est necessitas solius præcepti, cuius transgressio grave peccatum est: sicut quod excommunicatus non consecret. Veruntamen hæc transgressio non impedit consecrationis effectum principalem, qui est transubstantiatio. Altera est necessitas consecrationis vel sacramenti: consistens in hoc, quod minister sit rite ordinatus habens intentionem consecrandi cum forma & materia debitis: quod si alterum defuerit, nihil efficitur & peccatur.
units.tr: On this point it is customarily and usefully distinguished that some things are necessary for the exercise of this kind of power in two ways. One is the necessity of precept alone, the transgression of which is a grave sin: as that an excommunicate should not consecrate. Yet this transgression does not hinder the principal effect of the consecration, which is transubstantiation. The other is the necessity of the consecration or sacrament, consisting in this: that the minister be rightly ordained, having the intention of consecrating, with the form and matter due; if any of these is lacking, nothing is effected and sin is committed.

units.la: Hanc potestatem tradunt doctores concorditer parem esse in omnibus, qui consecrati sunt sacerdotes, quæ potestas collata fuisse creditur in cœna, dum dixit Christus Apostolis: hoc facite in meam commemorationem: vbi doctores communiter sentiunt, quod Iudas illic fuit sacerdos constitutus: sicut prius electus in Apostolatum potestatem prædicandi & faciendi miracula susceperat.
units.tr: The teachers agree in holding that this power is equal in all who have been consecrated priests; and this power is believed to have been conferred at the Supper, when Christ said to the Apostles: "Do this in remembrance of me." Where the teachers commonly hold that Judas was then constituted a priest, just as, having been previously chosen to the apostleship, he had received the power of preaching and working miracles.

units.la: Et hic sumitur argumentum, quod potestas ecclesiastica non necessario fundatur in fide vel gratia, sed in charactere baptismali, quem de lege communi necessario præsupponit.
units.tr: And from this an argument is drawn: that ecclesiastical power is not necessarily founded on faith or grace, but on the baptismal character, which by the common law it necessarily presupposes.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO III.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION III.

units.la: Potestas ecclesiastica ordinis alio modo consecrata, prout respicit ministrationem corporis Christi fidelibus: & ministrationem sacramentorum ordinis & confirmationis: Consecrationem insuper virginum, abbatum & ecclesiarum, & institutionem ministrorum ecclesiæ, non est æqualiter in quolibet sacerdote. Cuius ratio est: quoniam simplex sacerdos iuxta communem doctorum sententiam non potest ordines conferre, neque sacramentum confirmationis dare, neque consecrare virgines, &c. etiam de facto sic, quod si tale aliquid tentet agere, nihil tamen efficitur: quia neque confirmat neque ordinat. Episcopus autem si volentem confirmari, si volentem præterea ad ordines promoueri, qui sit eorum susceptibilis (quod dicitur propter sexum muliebrem) tentauerit vel confirmare vel ordinare, ordinat vtique vel confirmat de facto: licet excommunicatus, licet irregularis, licet degradatus exititerit. Et in hoc par in omnibus episcopis ab infimo vsque ad supremum, qui Papa dicitur, potestas ordinis.
units.tr: The power of orders is consecrated in another way, insofar as it concerns the administration of the body of Christ to the faithful, the administration of the sacraments of orders and confirmation, and likewise the consecration of virgins and abbots and churches, and the institution of ministers of the Church. It is not equally present in every priest. The reason is this: according to the common opinion of the teachers, a simple priest cannot confer orders, nor give the sacrament of confirmation, nor consecrate virgins, and so on. This is also the case in fact, so that if he attempts any such thing, nothing is effected, because he neither confirms nor ordains. A bishop, however, if he attempts to confirm one who wishes to be confirmed, or to promote to orders one who wishes to be promoted (provided the person is capable of them, which is said to exclude women), actually ordains or confirms, even if he is excommunicate, irregular or deposed. In this respect the power of orders is equal in all bishops, from the lowest up to the highest, who is called the Pope.

units.la: Non autem in sacerdotibus minoribus est hæc potestas, vt dictum est: saltem in tali plenitudine seu perfectione, quod hoc possint. Licet concedatur cum maiori parte doctorum, quod supra sacerdotium simplex nulla est altera potestas ordinis, neque in episcopis, neque in Papa: sed alter est in episcopis & Papa: alter in simplicibus presbyteris: sicut exemplificant, quod eadem est humahumanitas in homine dum est puer, & eadem dum factus est vir: vir nihilominus generare potest sibi simile, puer nequaquam. Cum igitur fuerit inter Apostolos & discipulos talis distinctio, sicut inter episcopos & simplices curatos sacerdotes, sicut notat Isido. & Magister in 4. dist. 24 cap. 7. allegans cum, perspicua est veritas huius considerationis.
units.tr: This power, as has been said, is not found in lesser priests, at least not in such fullness or perfection that they could exercise it. Although it is granted with the majority of the teachers that above the simple priesthood there is no other power of orders, neither in bishops nor in the Pope, yet the power is different in bishops and the Pope and different in simple elders. They illustrate this: the humanity is the same in a man when he is a boy and when he has become a man; yet the man can beget something like himself, the boy by no means. Since, therefore, there was such a distinction between the Apostles and the disciples, as there is between bishops and simple parish priests, as Isidore notes, and the Master in the fourth book, distinction 24, chapter 7, citing him, the truth of this consideration is plain.

units.la: Si vero loqueremur de potestate iuris, iuxta quod dici solet: Illud possumus quod de iure possumus, certior adhuc est ista consideratio: quia nullus sacerdos rite ministrat aliquod sacramentum, seclusa necessitatis casu, nisi iurisdictionem habeat super illum, cui ministrat. Sed super hac redabitur consideratio sequens: satis sit interim aperuisse qualiter sit vel non sit aequalis potestas ordinis in omnibus presbyteris: quia quo ad consecrationem corporis Christi veri, eandem habent sacerdotes omnes potestatem. Quantum vero ad sacramentorum ministrationem: dispar est in episcopis & simplicibus presbyteris potestas seu facultas tam de iure quam de facto. Similiter in ministrorum ecclesiasticorum institutione: quae est potestas competens primis hierarchiis de primo ordine & secundo, non autem inferioribus: quemadmodum sunt curati, qui licet purgare, illuminare & perficere possint plebem suam, prout inferior angelorum hierarchia purgat, illuminat & perficit sub coelestem vel humanam hierarchiam: nihilominus haec potestas curatorum non extenditur ad hierarchatum specialem institutionem de instituto communi.
units.tr: If we were speaking of the power of right, according to the saying usually given: "We can do what we may do by right," this consideration is even more certain, because no priest rightly administers any sacrament, apart from a case of necessity, unless he has jurisdiction over the one to whom he administers it. But the following consideration will discuss this further. It is enough for now to have explained how the power of orders is or is not equal in all elders. As regards the consecration of the true body of Christ, all priests have the same power. As regards the administration of the sacraments, the power or faculty is unequal in bishops and simple elders, both by right and in fact. Similarly in the institution of ecclesiastical ministers, which is a power belonging to the first hierarchies of the first and second order, but not to the lower ones, such as parish priests. Although they can cleanse, enlighten and perfect their people, just as the lower hierarchy of angels cleanses, enlightens and perfects under the heavenly or human hierarchy, yet this power of parish priests does not extend to the special institution of the hierarchical office by common appointment.

units.la: Addamus quod & si primus hierarcha, summus pontifex, vel alii consequenter, suo modo possint pro rationabili causa vel necessitate dare suis inferioribus adiutores ad exercendum hierarchicos actus, qui sunt purgare, illuminare & perficere plebes sibi subditas: sicut invenitur de poenitentiariis & privilegiatis: hoc tamen sine manifesta ratione vel necessitate facere non debet, vel cum eorundem deiectione, irreverentia & vilipensione apud illos, quibus honori debent esse, & a quibus debitam sustentationem recipere pro suo statu & ministerio possunt. Quis enim tutorem dederit adulto, prudenti, providenti & potenti, se nolente?
units.tr: We may add that although the first hierarch, the highest pontiff, or others in due order, may in their own way, for a reasonable cause or necessity, give their inferiors helpers to exercise the hierarchical acts, which are to cleanse, enlighten and perfect the peoples subject to them (as is found with penitentiaries and privileged persons), yet they ought not to do this without a manifest reason or necessity, or to the disparagement, disrespect and contempt of those to whom they ought to be honoured, and from whom they can receive the proper maintenance for their status and ministry. For who would give a guardian to a grown man who is prudent, provident and powerful, against his will?

units.la: Nec tandem claudicare debet obligatio mutua episcoporum vel curatorum ad plebes suas. Claudicat autem, dum plebes eximuntur & libertantur (si ista libertas, non iniquitas est) dum eligere sibi possunt hierarchizantes eos in foro conscientiae vel in praedicatione aut sacramentorum aliorum ministratione. Praelati vero maiores vel minores remanent hac obligatione constricti, ut non liceat eis plebibus suis negare, quicquid in praedictis quaesiuerint, tanquam nedum Deo, sed eis rationem reddituri sint: etiam si pestilentiali, si epidimiali, si quavis alia abominabili contagione morbi laboraucrunt. Praeterea si tales vice pastorum dati, luporum accipiant officium: si seducant subditos, lacerent & devorent, nulla relinquitur eis obviandi vel promovendi potestas. Nisi forte dicatur, quod hi superiores habent pro iudicibus: sed aperta est responsio praelatorum de quibusdam, inimici nostri sunt iudices.
units.tr: Nor, finally, should the mutual obligation of bishops or parish priests to their peoples be defective. It is defective when the peoples are exempted and released (if that freedom is not iniquity), when they may choose for themselves those who priest over them in the forum of conscience, or in preaching, or in the administration of the other sacraments. The greater or lesser prelates, however, remain bound by this obligation, so that they may not refuse their peoples anything they have asked for in these matters, since they will have to render an account not only to God but also to them, even if they have laboured under a pestilential, epidemic or any other abominable contagion of disease. Moreover, if such men, given in place of ministers, take up the office of wolves, if they lead the subjects astray, tear and devour them, no power is left to them to oppose or promote anything. Unless perhaps it is said that these superiors have the people as judges; but the prelates' answer about certain people is plain: "Our enemies are the judges."

units.la: Attendat lector circa considerationem istam de episcopatu, si sit ordo vel sacerdotium: quod apud Theologos & Iuristas est concordia in re bene concipiendo, sed explicatio diversa est. Quia Iuristae vocant episcopatum esse ordinem, quoniam potest ultra sacerdotium. Theologi vero concedunt secundum scilicet quod episcopatus est potestas hierarchica supra sacerdotium: sed quia nihil addit potestatis supra corpus Christi verum: propterea non dicunt, quod sit novus ordo, sed bene nova potestas: & hoc redit in idem.
units.tr: In this consideration of the episcopate, let the reader consider whether it is an order or a priesthood. Among theologians and jurists there is agreement in the matter when it is rightly understood, but the explanation differs. For the jurists call the episcopate an order, because it can do more than the priesthood. The theologians, however, grant that the episcopate is a hierarchical power above the priesthood, but because it adds no power over the true body of Christ, they do not call it a new order but a new power; and this comes to the same thing.

units.la: Rursus attendat, quod de confirmatione dicit sanctus Thom. eam committi posse a papa simplici sacerdoti, propter beati Gregorii quoddam dictum: pluribus tamen hoc non placet, & dicunt illos, de quibus loquitur Gregor. non fuisse confirmatos: tolerati autem sunt sic manere, quia confirmatio non est necessitatis sacramentum. Denique datur ratio per doctores, cur mulier non sit susceptibilis cuiuscunque ordinis: quoniam subiectionis sexus est, non hierarchicae dominationis.
units.tr: Again, let the reader note that Saint Thomas says of confirmation that the Pope can commit it to a simple priest, on account of a certain saying of the blessed Gregory. Many, however, do not accept this, and they say that those of whom Gregory speaks had not been confirmed, but were tolerated in remaining so, because confirmation is not a sacrament of necessity. Finally, the teachers give the reason why a woman is not capable of any order whatever: because it belongs to the subjection of her sex, not to hierarchical dominion.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO IV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO IV.

units.la: Potestas ecclesiastica iurisdictionis in foro exteriori, est potestas ecclesiastica coercitiva, quae valet exerceri in alterum etiam inuitum ad dirigendum subditos in finem beatitudinis aeternae, velut in finem proximum & principaliter intentum. Addita est, fatemur, haec ultima clausula descriptionis ad expressionem magis quam necessitatem: quoniam haec includitur in hoc nomine posito pro genere, potestas ecclesiastica, sicut in descriptione sua notatum est.
units.tr: Ecclesiastical jurisdiction in the external forum is a coercive ecclesiastical power, which may be exercised even against another's will, to direct subjects toward the end of eternal blessedness as its proximate and principal aim. We admit that this last clause of the definition was added more for explanation than out of necessity, since it is already included in the term "ecclesiastical power," which stands for the genus, as noted in the definition itself.

units.la: Attendatur autem quod iurisdictio dicitur nomine generali, quasi iuris dictio, id est, potestas dicendiius: vel est iurisdictio quasi iuris dictutio, id est, promulgatio vel notificatio seu pronunciatio. Proprie vero dicitur iurisdictio facultas seu potestas propinqua dicendi vel sententiandi ius in alterum etiam inuitum. Et haec duplex est, temporalis & spiritualis. Temporalis exercetur secundum leges civiles ad finem quietae conversationis humanae pro hac vita. Spiritualis autem exercetur secundum leges Canonicas ad finem principalem aeternae beatitudinis consequendae.
units.tr: It should be noted, however, that jurisdiction is named in a general sense, as if it were iuris dictio, that is, the power of declaring the law; or it is iurisdictio, as if iuris dictutio, that is, the promulgation, notification or pronouncement of the law. Properly speaking, jurisdiction is the immediate faculty or power of declaring or pronouncing judgment in law against another, even against his will. This is twofold, temporal and spiritual. Temporal jurisdiction is exercised according to civil laws for the end of the peaceful conduct of human life in this world. Spiritual jurisdiction is exercised according to canon laws to attain the principal end of eternal blessedness.

units.la: Ceterum potestas haec iurisdictionis ecclesiasticae adeo vicina est iurisdictioni seculari & politiae: quod laicis, imo & mulieribus plerumque & in multis casibus communicari potest executio vel committi.
units.tr: Moreover, this power of ecclesiastical jurisdiction is so closely related to secular jurisdiction and civil government that its execution can be shared with laymen, indeed even with women, and in many cases can be entrusted to them.

units.la: Hanc potestatem contulit Christus Matth. 18. dum dixit Petro vice omnium: Si peccaverit in te frater tuus, vade & corripe eum, &c. Sequitur: quod si te non audierit, dic ecclesiae: quod si ecclesiam non audierit, sit tibi sicut ethnicus & publicanus.
units.tr: Christ conferred this power in Matthew 18, when he said to Peter on behalf of all: "If your brother sins against you, go and rebuke him," etc. It follows: "But if he does not listen to you, tell the church; and if he does not listen to the church, let him be to you as a heathen and a tax collector."

units.la: Quò in loco fundatur iuridica potestas excommunicandi vel interdicendi ab ecclesiasticis sacramentis & communione fidelium, rebelles & inobedientes ecclesiæ: sicut vsus est Apostolus: & idem hortatus est ad Titum 3. scribens: hæreticum hominem post primam & secundam correptionem devita. Et simile dixit 1. Corinth. 5. Si quis frater nominatur inter vos &c. Sequitur: Cum huiusmodi nec cibum sumere.
units.tr: In this passage is grounded the juridical power of excommunicating, or of barring from the ecclesiastical sacraments and the fellowship of the faithful, those who are rebellious and disobedient to the church, as the Apostle did; and he urged the same in Titus 3, writing: a heretical man, after the first and second admonition, avoid. He said something similar in 1 Corinthians 5: If anyone who is named a brother among you, etc. It follows: with such a person not even to eat.

units.la: Fundatur rursus absque omni calumnia ponibili in hoc textu plenitudo potestatis gladii spiritualis & executio eius in ecclesia super quemlibet Christianum, qui est frater noster, etiam si papa fuerit. Nec accipiendum est hic, dic ecclesiæ, id est, papæ. Quoniam Christus Petro loquebatur, qui non dixisset sibiipsi. Item quia subiunctum est pluraliter: Quacunque ligaveritis super terram &c.
units.tr: Again, without any plausible calumny, the fullness of the power of the spiritual sword and its exercise in the church over any Christian who is our brother, even if he be the pope, is grounded in this text. Nor is tell the church here to be understood as meaning the pope. For Christ was speaking to Peter, and he would not have said this to himself. Likewise, because what follows is in the plural: Whatever you bind on earth, etc.

units.la: Denique si non haberet ecclesia talem potestatem & executionem, frustra dixisset Christus: dic ecclesiæ: quia potuisset impune non audiri, contra illud quod sequitur: Si ecclesiam non audierit, sit tibi &c.
units.tr: Finally, if the church did not have such power and execution, Christ would have said tell the church in vain; for it could have gone unheeded with impunity, contrary to what follows: If he does not listen to the church, let him be to you, etc.

units.la: Fundatur etiam in hoc textu nedum potestas exercendi, sed potestas diffiniendi, determinandi, statuendi, decernendi, constituendi præcepta, leges & canones: procedendi denique contra non obedientes usque ad sententiam excommunicationis inclusive: imo secundum canones nunc institutos usque ad invocationem brachii secularis: quia dicitur in textu, quod si ecclesiam non audierit &c. Audire igitur debet ecclesiam quilibet frater noster, qui dicit ad Deum: Pater noster, sicut explicat alibi Christus: Qui vos audit, me audit.
units.tr: Furthermore, this text grounds not only the power of exercising discipline, but also the power of defining, determining, establishing, decreeing, and enacting precepts, laws and canons; and finally of proceeding against the disobedient, even to the sentence of excommunication inclusive; indeed, according to the canons now in force, even to the invoking of the secular arm; for the text says: but if he does not listen to the church, etc. Therefore every brother of ours, who says to God Our Father, ought to listen to the church, as Christ explains elsewhere: He who hears you hears me.

units.la: Confirmant hanc sententiam statuta & practicata in hoc sacro Constantiensi concilio: præsertim 6. Aprilis, anni 1415. in sessione publica. Cuius inter cætera sunt hæc decreta duo prima. Et primo declarat, quod ipsa in Spiritu sancto legitime congregata generale concilium faciens & ecclesiam catholicam militantem repræsentans, potestatem immediate à Christo habet, cui quilibet cuiuscunque status vel dignitatis, etiam si papalis existat, obedire tenetur in his, quæ pertinent ad fidem, & extirpationem dicti schismatis, ac generalem reformationem ecclesiæ Dei in capite & in membris.
units.tr: The statutes enacted and practised in this holy Council of Constance confirm this opinion, especially those of 6 April 1415, in the public session. Among other things, the first two decrees of that session are these. And first it declares that the council itself, lawfully assembled in the Holy Spirit, forming a general council and representing the militant Catholic Church, has its power immediately from Christ; and that everyone, of whatever state or dignity, even if he be papal, is bound to obey it in those matters which pertain to the faith, to the extirpation of the said schism, and to the general reformation of the Church of God in head and members.

units.la: Item declarat quod quicunque cuiuscunque status vel dignitatis, etiam si papalis existat, qui mandatis, statutis seu ordinationibus aut præceptis huius sanctæ synodi, & cuiuscunq; alterius concilii generalis legitime congregati super præmissis seu ad ea pertinentibus factis vel faciendis, obedire contumaciter contempserit, nisi resipuerit, condignæ pœnitentiæ subiiciatur, & debite puniatur, etiam ad alia iuris subsidia, si opus fuerit, recurrendo.
units.tr: It likewise declares that whoever, of whatever state or dignity, even if he be papal, stubbornly refuses to obey the mandates, statutes, ordinances or precepts of this holy synod, or of any other lawfully assembled general council, made or to be made concerning the foregoing matters or pertaining to them, unless he repents, shall be subjected to a fitting penance and duly punished, having recourse also to other aids of the law if need be.

units.la: Concluditur autem ex præmissis, quod si potestas prædicta sit ecclesiæ data: concilium generale repræsentans ecclesiam, habet illam, imo videtur quod ecclesia, ut sparsim considerata, non habet illam potestatem nisi in quodam materiali seu potentiali, sed congregatio sua & unitio, quæ fit in concilio generali, dat ei formam, sicut in aliis communitatibus exemplum dari potest. Et fundatur prædicta potestas ecclesiastica iurisdictionis in unitate vel unione tali, quemadmodum notasse videtur eleuatus Augustinus, quod claues ecclesiæ datæ sunt unitati.
units.tr: It follows from what has been said that if this power has been given to the church, then the general council, which represents the church, has it. Indeed it seems that the church, considered scattered, does not have that power except in a material or potential sense, but its gathering and unity, which takes place in a general council, gives it form, just as an example can be given in other communities. The aforesaid power of ecclesiastical jurisdiction is grounded in such unity or union, as the eminent Augustine seems to have noted, that the keys of the church were given to unity.

units.la: Veruntamen hoc non impedit, quin datæ sint Petro tanquam monarchæ legitimisque successoribus suis, principalius tamen ecclesiæ. Primo ratione indeuiabilitatis: quia portæ inferi non prævalebunt aduersus eam, nec deficiet fides eius: non sic de papa. Secundo ratione regulabilitatis: quoniam habet regulare vsum potestatis papalis: non sic econuerso. Tertio ratione multiplicitatis: quoniam ecclesia continet potestatem quamlibet ecclesiasticam, etiam papalem: non sic papa, præsertim in extensione. Quarto ratione obligabilitatis: quia ecclesia potest concedere leges obligantes & regulantes etiam ipsum papam tam quo ad personam, quam quoad vsus potestatis. Non sic econtra potest papa iudicare totam ecclesiam, vel vsum suæ potestatis limitare: imo si papa condat leges & canones, videtur obseruandum illud, quod sententialiter dicit Augustinus: Leges instituuntur, cum promulgantur: Firmantur autem, cum moribus utentium approbantur. Hocenim dicitur ad reprimendum præsumptionem quorundam summorum pontificum, vel eis adulantium, qui videntur voluisse debere seruari pro regula immutabili de papa respectu cuiuslibet prouinciæ vel totius ecclesiæ: Quod placuit principi, legis habet vigorem: quasi nullum superesset examen supremum.
units.tr: Nevertheless, this does not prevent the keys from having been given to Peter as monarch and to his lawful successors, yet principally to the church. First, by reason of indefectibility: because the gates of hell shall not prevail against her, nor shall her faith fail; this is not so with the pope. Second, by reason of regulability: because she has the power to regulate the exercise of papal power; the reverse is not so. Third, by reason of multiplicity: because the church contains every ecclesiastical power, including the papal; the pope does not contain the church's power, especially in its extent. Fourth, by reason of obligability: because the church can enact laws binding and regulating even the pope himself, both as to his person and as to the uses of his power. The pope cannot, conversely, judge the whole church or limit the use of his power. Indeed, if the pope enacts laws and canons, that saying of Augustine seems to be observed, which states the principle: Laws are established when they are promulgated; but they are confirmed when they are approved by the customs of those who use them. This is said to restrain the presumption of certain supreme pontiffs, or of those who flatter them, who seem to have wished that the pope's will with respect to any province or to the whole church should be kept as an unchangeable rule: What has pleased the prince has the force of law, as if no supreme judgment remained.

units.la: Addita est vero proinobedientium coertione pœnalis excommunicatio. Et sunt qui dicunt pœnam hanc esse vltimam, quam infligere posset ecclesiastica potestas iurisdictionis ex institutione Christi sola primaria: sic quod non extenditur ad incarcerationem, nec vt aliquis adiudicetur morti vel flagello corporali: sed facit hoc ecclesiasticus, dum facit ex concessione principum: quemadmodum multam ob eorum deuotionem iurisdictionis temporalis auctoritatem clerus accepit: quæ nihilominus iurisdictio vel censura dicitur spiritualis: sicut & ecclesiasticorum bona temporalia propter dedicationem & applicationem ad eos, qui ministrant ecclesiæ: sicut panes propositionis, primitiæ & decimæ: vasa insuper templi, vestes & similia dicebantur in lege veteri sacra, vel sancta: sic & noua lex hoc retinet.
units.tr: Excommunication as a penalty was added to restrain the disobedient. And there are those who say that this penalty is the last that ecclesiastical jurisdiction could inflict by the sole primary institution of Christ; so that it does not extend to imprisonment, nor to any sentence of death or bodily scourging. The churchman does this only by grant of princes, just as the clergy received the authority of temporal jurisdiction as a fine, out of the devotion of those princes; and this jurisdiction or censure is nonetheless called spiritual. So too the temporal goods of churchmen are called spiritual because of their dedication and application to those who minister to the church, as the bread of the Presence, the firstfruits and tithes, and likewise the vessels of the temple, its garments and similar things were called holy or sacred in the old law; so the new law retains this too.

units.la: Ac proinde consurgit, quod ecclesiastica censura, quam Christus contulit & promulgari voluit, vbi prius Mat. 18. consequenter post dotationem ecclesiæ in bonis temporalibus applicata est ad defensionem coercitionem volentium vendicare sibi, vel impedire temporalitatem huiusmodi, per excommunicationes videlicet & interdicta: quæ pœna vel censura videtur primitus instituta contra pertinaces, schismaticos & haereticos & alios incorrigibiles vitiosos. Cui legi tanquam diuinae & naturali papa subiicitur: sicut & frater est potens delinquere. Haec autem applicatio gladii spiritualis ad defensionem temporalium si confusionem magnam in ecclesia, si vilipensionem vel contemptum euangelicae huius censurae suae, quae est excommunicationis gladius extreme formidabilis, si denique laqueos animabus multorum magis quam salutem spiritualem induxerit vel inducat, experientiam testem voco. Itaque sicut temporalitas addita est ecclesiae pro dote sua, videri potest aliquibus, quod ad eius defensionem similiter addere suffecerat aduersus impetitores poenam vel censuram temporalem: vt est mulctatio pecuniaria, vel corporalis detentio, vel arrestatio bonorum proprietorum.
units.tr: It follows, then, that ecclesiastical censure, which Christ conferred and wished to be promulgated, first in Matthew 18, and afterwards, after the endowment of the church with temporal goods, was applied to the defence and restraint of those who wished to claim for themselves, or to hinder, such temporalities, namely by excommunications and interdicts. This penalty or censure seems to have been first instituted against the obstinate, schismatics, heretics and other incorrigible sinners. To this law, as divine and natural, the pope is subject, just as a brother is capable of sinning. I call experience as my witness that this application of the spiritual sword to the defence of temporal goods has caused, or does cause, great confusion in the church, and contempt or disregard of this evangelical censure of its own, which is the sword of excommunication, extremely formidable; and finally that it has drawn souls into snares rather than promoted their spiritual salvation. Thus, just as temporal goods were added to the church as its endowment, it may seem to some that, for its defence against assailants, it would have sufficed to add a temporal penalty or censure similarly: such as a pecuniary fine, or bodily detention, or the seizure of property.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO V.
units.tr: Consideration V.

units.la: POtestas ecclesiastica iurisdictionis in foro interiori, quae non est proprie coercitiva, sed magis spontanea quo ad subiicientes se eidem, est potestas ecclesiastica super corpus Christi mysticum illuminando & perficiendo ipsum per doctrinam & sacramentorum ministrationem, & purgando per baptismi & poenitentiae sacramenta.
units.tr: Ecclesiastical power of jurisdiction in the internal forum, which is not properly coercive but rather voluntary as regards those who submit to it, is the church's power over the mystical body of Christ, enlightening and perfecting it through teaching and the administration of the sacraments, and cleansing it through the sacraments of baptism and repentance.

units.la: Aduertendum est itaque, quod haec potestas iurisdictionis, quae radicaliter fundatur in potestate ordinis sacerdotalis & episcopalis, dum in sua generalitate consideratur, respicit multipliciter corpus Christi mysticum, quod est fidelium ecclesia: quos fideles oportet secundum tres actus hierarchicos regere, qui sunt secundum Dionysium purgare illuminare, & perficere. Purgare per infrictionem poenalem excommunicationis vel interdicti, si rebelles inueniantur: quod spectat ad iurisdictionem coercitivam, de qua praedictum est: quamuis haec purgatio fiat per baptismum & sacramentalem absolutionem non tamen coercitiue. Oportet insuper illuminare per praedicationem & doctrinam, oportet demum perficere per aliorum sacramentorum ministrationem.
units.tr: It must be noted, then, that this power of jurisdiction, which is radically grounded in the power of the priestly and episcopal order, when considered in its general scope, relates in several ways to the mystical body of Christ, which is the church of the faithful. The faithful must be governed according to three hierarchical acts, which, following Dionysius, are purging, illuminating and perfecting. They are purged by the penal infliction of excommunication or interdict if they are found rebellious; this belongs to the coercive jurisdiction spoken of above, although this purging is done through baptism and sacramental absolution and not coercively. They must further be enlightened through preaching and teaching, and finally they must be perfected through the administration of the other sacraments.

units.la: Porro talis ministratio sacramentorum non habet pro materia debita res solum insensibiles: prout est in consecratione corporis Christi, vbi pro materia debita requiritur & sufficit panis triticeus & vinum. Nec refert quo ad consecrationis necessitatem, si panis sit ipsius consecrantis vel alterius. Secus est in ministratione sacramentorum, vbi requiritur, quod persona, cui fit ministratio, sit ministranti subdita: praeterquam in baptismo, quod est necessitatis sacramentum non iterabile. Similiter in sacramento confirmationis & ordinis, quibus indelebilis character imprimitur: inde sufficit de necessitate sacramenti, non tamen praecepti, subiectio voluntaria suscipientis haec sacramenta ab illo, qui conferre potest illa: peccant tamen dans atque suscipiens, si non adsit subiectio per superiorem ordinata. Secus autem est in poenitentiae sacramento, vbi de necessitate sacramenti & praecepti requiritur praedicta duplex subiectio, iuxta communiorem doctorum sententiam, sic quod alicui non datur absolutio, etiam si dari tentetur, quia materia deficit, quae est peccator subditus. Subditus inquam nedum voluntaria subiectione, sed aliena superioris auctoritate. Hoc rite statuit primus legislator Christus: hoc ecclesia sic elucidauit & tradidit, ne confunderetur ecclesiasticum regimen: & ne hierarchicus ordo, quem tradit Dionysius talem esse vt infima reducantur ad suprema per media, turbaretur.
units.tr: Moreover, such administration of the sacraments does not take as its due matter merely insensible things, as in the consecration of the body of Christ, where wheaten bread and wine are required and suffice as due matter. Nor does it matter, as far as the necessity of the consecration goes, whether the bread belongs to the consecrator himself or to another. It is otherwise in the administration of the sacraments, where it is required that the person to whom the administration is made be subject to the minister; except in baptism, which is a sacrament of necessity and not to be repeated. Similarly in the sacraments of confirmation and order, in which an indelible character is imprinted, the voluntary submission of the recipient to the one who can confer them suffices for the necessity of the sacrament, though not for the precept. Yet giver and receiver both sin if the submission ordained by a superior is absent. It is otherwise with the sacrament of repentance, where, by the necessity both of the sacrament and of the precept, the aforesaid double submission is required, according to the more common opinion of the teachers, so that absolution is not given to anyone even if one attempts to give it, because the matter is lacking, namely a subject sinner. I say a subject, not only by voluntary submission but by the authority of a superior. Christ, the first lawgiver, established this rightly; the church has so explained and handed it down, lest the ecclesiastical government be confused and the hierarchical order, which Dionysius describes as such that the lowest are led back to the highest through the middle, be disturbed.

units.la: Videre est igitur quemadmodum potestas haec ecclesiastica iurisdictionem quandam exigit, cui conuenit, quod libera sit & spontanea vere & interpretatiue circa personam, in quam exercetur haec iurisdictio: aut saltem, quod non feratur in inuitum. Quis enim diceret, quod aliquis inuitus vel baptizatur vel confirmatur vel absoluitur in foro conscientiae, vel ordinatur: & ita de reliquis? Hinc est, quod papa, qui nulli personae particulari subest, vt coerceri iuridice possit in exteriori foro: subest tamen quo ad iurisdictionem hanc annexam ordini sacerdotali confessori suo & ordinatori suo, si antea sacerdos non fuerat: vnde & ab Hostiensi consecratur episcopo, qui minor est.
units.tr: It can be seen, then, how this ecclesiastical power requires a certain jurisdiction, to which it belongs that it be free and spontaneous, truly or interpretively, with respect to the person over whom this jurisdiction is exercised, or at least that it not be imposed on the unwilling. For who would say that anyone against his will is baptized, confirmed, absolved in the forum of conscience, or ordained, and so on for the rest? Hence it is that the pope, who is subject to no particular person so that he could be juridically coerced in the external forum, nevertheless is subject, as regards this jurisdiction annexed to the priestly order, to his confessor and his ordainer, if he had not previously been a priest; whence he is also consecrated a bishop by Hostiensis, who is the lesser.

units.la: Proficit autem supra modum talis distinctio duplicis iurisdictionis, coercitiuae scilicet & non coercitiuae: cuius ignorantia vel inaduertentia gignit confusionem apud aliquos infinitam. Nam cum vsus doctorum communis habeat dicere, quod potestas ordinis aequalis est in omnibus sacerdotibus & praelatis: accipiunt consequenter occasionem erroris, quod quilibet sacerdos possit quemlibet absoluere, possit praedicare non missus, possit eucharistiam ministrare. Inuenimus autem quod haec iurisdictionis potestas promissa est Apostolis ante passionem Christi Matth. 18. Amen dico vobis: Quaecunque ligaueritis super terram, erunt ligata & in caelis &c. Et promissa fuit Petro, Matth. 16. Tibi dabo claues regni caelorum. Sed post resurrectionem suam collata est Apostolis, quando insufflans in eos dixit: Accipite Spiritum sanctum quorum remiseritis peccata, remittuntur eis &c. Ioan. 21. Et ibidem vltimo dictum est Petro: Pasce oues meas.
units.tr: Moreover, such a distinction between a double jurisdiction, namely coercive and non-coercive, is beyond measure useful, and its ignorance or inattention breeds endless confusion among some. For since the common usage of the teachers is to say that the power of order is equal in all priests and prelates, they consequently take occasion for error: that any priest may absolve anyone, may preach without being sent, and may administer the Eucharist. We find, however, that this power of jurisdiction was promised to the apostles before Christ's passion: "Verily I say unto you, whatsoever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, etc." (Matt. 18). It was promised to Peter: "To you I will give the keys of the kingdom of heaven" (Matt. 16). But after his resurrection it was conferred on the apostles, when, breathing on them, he said: "Receive the Holy Spirit; whose sins you remit, they are remitted to them, etc." (John 21). And in the same place, at the end, it was said to Peter: "Feed my sheep."

units.la: Addita est seu potius confirmata potestas praedicandi cum potestate conferendi baptismum vel potius iam datae potestatis executio iussa est Matth. vltim. Euntes in mundum vniuersum, praedicate euangelium omni creaturae: baptizantes eos in nomine Patris & Filii & Spiritus sancti. Vnde licet in casu necessitatis quilibet viator baptizare possit: hoc tamen faciunt ex officio vel ecclesiastica potestate soli sacerdotes.
units.tr: The power of preaching, together with the power of conferring baptism, was added, or rather confirmed; or rather, the execution of the power already given was commanded: "Go into all the world, preach the gospel to every creature, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit" (Matt. last). Hence, although in a case of necessity any traveller may baptize, only priests do this by office or ecclesiastical power.

units.la: Huic autem potestati iurisdictionis, quae in latitudine sua considerata, nedum ad sacramentum poenitentiae, sed ad aliorum sacramentorum ministrationem & ad praedicationem extenditur: annexa est potestas, ius seu facultas accipiendi vitæ necessaria, Matth. 10. & Luc. 10. quod Apostolus confirmauit 1. Corint. 9. Quia dignus est operarius mercede sua.
units.tr: To this power of jurisdiction, which, considered in its breadth, extends not only to the sacrament of repentance but also to the administration of the other sacraments and to preaching, is annexed the power, right or faculty of receiving the necessities of life (Matt. 10 and Luke 10), which the Apostle confirmed in 1 Cor. 9: "For the labourer is worthy of his hire."

units.la: Consequenter fundatur in hac potestate sumendi vitæ necessaria, rationabilitas dotationis ecclesiasticæ loco decimarum & primitiarum legis antiquæ.
units.tr: Consequently, on this power of receiving the necessities of life is founded the reasonableness of ecclesiastical endowment in place of the tithes and firstfruits of the old law.

units.la: Denique potestas faciendi miracula etsi videatur annexa fuisse per Christum licentia prædicandi verbum Dei, quando misit discipulos ad prædicandum, & dixit eis: Infirmos curate, dæmonia eiicite &c. nihilominus videtur hæc potestas donum gratis datum, conuenire potens cuilibet ex fidelibus, prout ad ædificationem ecclesiæ iudicabit expediens Spiritus sanctus, qui distribuit singulis prout vult.
units.tr: Finally, although the power of working miracles seems to have been annexed by Christ to the licence of preaching the word of God, when he sent the disciples to preach and said to them, "Heal the sick, cast out devils, etc.", nevertheless this power seems to be a gift freely given, which can belong to any of the faithful as the Holy Spirit, who distributes to each as he wills, judges expedient for the building up of the church.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO VI.

units.la: POtestas ecclesiastica considerari potest & debet tripliciter. Vno modo formaliter in se & absolute sine respectu. Alio modo materialiter seu respectiue, prout applicatur ad hanc vel illam personam iure legitimo: quod communiter fit per consecrationem & electionem: quia, sicut dicit Apostolus: Nemo sibi assumit honorem, sed qui vocatur à Deo tanquam Aaron. Potestas hæc dicitur institutio ministrorum tam actiue quam passiue. Consideratur tertio modo quo ad exercitium vel executionem: quia frustra est potentia secundum Philosophum, si non habeat actum.
units.tr: Ecclesiastical power can and should be considered in three ways. In one way, formally, in itself and absolutely, without relation to anything. In another way, materially or relatively, as it is applied to this or that person by lawful right; this is commonly done through consecration and election, because, as the Apostle says: "No one takes this honour to himself, but he who is called by God, as Aaron was." This power is called the institution of ministers, both active and passive. It is considered in a third way with respect to its exercise or execution, because "power is in vain, according to the Philosopher, if it has no act."

units.la: Proficit hæc consideratio, quæ distinguit & resoluit modos loquendi varios, tam Theologorum quam Canonistarum de ecclesiastica potestate: cuius resolutionis ignorantia vel inadvertentia falli plerumque facit & fallere: quoniam aliter loquendum est de ecclesiastica potestate, dum in se consideratur formaliter & absolute: aliter, dum consideratur materialiter seu respectiue, aliter dum consideratur quo ad exercitii vsum vel executiue: sicut infra docebitur. Notemus præterea modos essendi in, quos in metaphysica posuit Aristot. quorum inadvertentia facit oberrare quosdam, dum inquiritur, in quo vel in quibus sit plenitudo ecclesiasticæ potestatis. Vnus modus essendi in, est sicut pars integralis in suo toto. Alius sicut totum integrale in suis partibus. Tertius sicut species in genere. Quartus sicut genus in specie. Quintus sicut forma in materia: quæ forma triplex est, essentialis, accidentalis & mathematicalis. Sextus, sicut effectus in sua causa efficiente, dirigente vel regente, vt regnum est in rege. Septimus sicut ordinata in finem sunt in suo fine: quemadmodum virtus in beatitudine. Octauus sicut locatum in loco.
units.tr: This consideration is useful, since it distinguishes and resolves the various modes of speaking about ecclesiastical power used by both theologians and canonists; ignorance or inadvertence of this resolution often causes and produces error. For ecclesiastical power must be spoken of one way when it is considered in itself, formally and absolutely; another way when it is considered materially or relatively; and yet another way when it is considered with respect to the use of its exercise, or executively, as will be taught below. Let us also note the modes of "being in," which Aristotle set out in his Metaphysics, and whose inadvertence causes some to go astray when they inquire in what, or in which things, the fullness of ecclesiastical power lies. One mode of "being in" is as an integral part in its whole. Another is as an integral whole in its parts. A third is as a species in a genus. A fourth is as a genus in a species. A fifth is as a form in matter; and this form is threefold: essential, accidental and mathematical. A sixth is as an effect in its efficient, directing or governing cause, as a kingdom is in a king. A seventh is as things ordered to an end are in their end, as virtue is in blessedness. An eighth is as a thing located is in a place.

units.la: Ex qua protinus distinctione manifestum est, quod secundum quadruplex genus causæ quadruplex reperitur & adaptatur modus essendi in, licet addantur & alii.
units.tr: From this distinction it is at once clear that, according to the fourfold kind of cause, a fourfold mode of "being in" is found and applies, although others may be added.

units.la: Subiungamus iterum distinctionem de vsu potestatis ecclesiasticæ. Est enim vsus aliquis licitus & ratus. Est vsus illicitus & ratus. Est vsus licitus & non ratus. Est vsus illicitus & irritus. Exemplum primi, dum sacerdos consecrat vel absoluit cum circumstantiis omnibus ad hoc requisitis de necessitate vel sacramenti vel præcepti. Exemplum secundi, dum sacerdos consecrat in peccato mortali, vel cum transgressione præcepti. Exemplum tertii: dum sacerdos quantum in se est bona fide & intentione credit absoluere confitentem sibi vtens in hoc bene clauibus: qui confitens, quia mentitur in confessione sua, vel obicem secreto ponit, nequaquam absoluitur. Exemplum quarti in casu priori, si sacerdos scienter quærit vti clauibus erga aliquem, cuius fictionem agnouerit, & qui neququam sibi subiectus est.
units.tr: Let us again add a distinction concerning the use of ecclesiastical power. There is a use that is lawful and valid; there is a use that is unlawful but valid; there is a use that is lawful but not valid; and there is a use that is unlawful and void. An example of the first: when a priest consecrates or absolves with all the circumstances required of necessity, either by the sacrament or by precept. An example of the second: when a priest consecrates in mortal sin, or with transgression of a precept. An example of the third: when a priest, in good faith and intention, as far as lies in him, believes he is absolving a penitent to whom he rightly uses the keys; yet the penitent, because he lies in his confession, or secretly places an obstacle, is by no means absolved. An example of the fourth, in the former case: if a priest knowingly seeks to use the keys over someone whose feigning he has recognised, and who is in no way subject to him.

units.la: Colligitur consequenter alia distinctio valens ad intelligentiam præmissorum & sequentium, dum quaeritur an potestas ecclesiastica sit æqualis in omnibus. Quia quæritur de potestate vel facti vel iuris. Facti sic: quod dum attentatur fieri fit siue bene siue male. Iuris vero dum bene fit, iuxta allegatum: Id possumus quod de iure possumus.
units.tr: Consequently another distinction follows, useful for understanding what has been said and what follows, when it is asked whether ecclesiastical power is equal in all cases. For there is a question of power in fact and of power in right. In fact, namely, when something is attempted, it is done either well or badly. In right, however, when it is done well, according to the saying: "We can do what we may do by right."

units.la: Redit autem hæc distinctio ad alteram prætactam de necessitate duplici in consecratione corporis Christi: quoniam altera est sacramenti, altera est præcepti. Et hæc similiter distinctio potest extendi ad ecclesiasticam potestatem super corpus Christi mysticum quo administrationem sacramentorum, quæ characterem imprimunt: sicut sunt baptismus, confirmatio & ordo: quoniam sicut in potestate ordinis super corpus Christi verum, sufficit aliquid de necessitate sacramenti, quod non sufficit de necessitate præcepti: quia peccat, qui contra vel præter ordinationem ecclesiæ consecrat. Sic inuenimus in potestate ecclesiastica super corpus Christi mysticum, præsertim quo administrationem trium sacramentorum, quæ dicta sunt.
units.tr: This distinction in turn goes back to the other one mentioned earlier, concerning the twofold necessity in the consecration of the body of Christ: for one necessity belongs to the sacrament, the other to precept. This same distinction can be extended to ecclesiastical power over the mystical body of Christ, namely to the administration of those sacraments which imprint a character, such as baptism, confirmation and orders. For just as in the power of orders over the true body of Christ, something sufficient by necessity of the sacrament does not suffice by necessity of precept, since he sins who consecrates contrary to or apart from the ordinance of the Church; so we find in ecclesiastical power over the mystical body of Christ, especially as regards the administration of the three sacraments just mentioned.

units.la: His distinctionibus & aliis quæ prædicta sunt attentis posset statim inuestigari, quid & in quo sit plenitudo ecclesiasticæ potestatis. Nihilominus antea iuxta priorem distinctionem trimebrem tres assignabimus consideraciones, septimam, octauam & nonam.
units.tr: Having considered these distinctions and the others already stated, one could at once investigate what, and in what, the fullness of ecclesiastical power consists. Nevertheless, following the earlier threefold distinction, we shall first assign three considerations: the seventh, the eighth and the ninth.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION VII.

units.la: POtestas ecclesiastica si consideretur in se formaliter & absolute, ipsa in se est inuariabilis: & eadem à principio nascentis ecclesiæ vsque in finem perseuerat.
units.tr: Ecclesiastical power, considered in itself formally and absolutely, is in itself invariable, and it has remained the same from the beginning of the nascent Church to its end.

units.la: Ecclesia si quidem sic consideratur in suis partibus essentialibus & permanentibus, quæ sunt Papatus, Cardinalatus, Patriarchatus, Archiepiscopatus, Episcopatus, sacerdotium habet integrari ex his omnibus: sic quod ablata penitus vna tali potestate, iam non maneret ecclesia prout à Christo seminaliter, & velut in quodam germine suo perfecte fuit instituta: ut si papatus per imaginationem praecindatur à reliquis potestatibus inferioribus, id quod superest non dicitur ecclesia. Propterea quaerere si papalis autoritas sit maior quam ecclesia: vel e contrario, redit in idem ac si peteretur: nonne totum est maius sua parte? vel pars minor suo toto?
units.tr: The Church, considered in its essential and permanent parts, which are the Papacy, the Cardinalate, the Patriarchate, the Archbishopric, the Bishopric and the priesthood, must be made up of all of these. So if any one such power were wholly removed, the Church would no longer remain as Christ instituted it, as a seed and as a perfect germ. Thus if the Papacy were cut off in imagination from the other, lower powers, what remained would not be called the Church. Therefore to ask whether papal authority is greater than the Church, or the reverse, comes to the same as asking: is not the whole greater than its part, and the part less than its whole?

units.la: Proinde sequitur, quod si generale concilium repraesentet universalem ecclesiam sufficienter & integre: necesse est ut includat autoritatem papalem, sive papa sit, sive desierit esse per mortem naturalem aut civilem. Sic dicimus de potestate Romanae ecclesiae vel sacri collegii. Sic de potestate episcopali: sic de sacerdotio, quod est potestas curatorum, qui sunt in ecclesia praelati minores.
units.tr: It follows that if a general council represents the universal Church sufficiently and fully, it must include papal authority, whether the pope is living or has ceased to be pope through natural or civil death. We say the same of the power of the Roman Church or of the sacred college. The same holds for episcopal power, and for the priesthood, which is the power of the parish priests, who are the lesser prelates in the Church.

units.la: Si vero vellet aliquis curiosus inquirere, qualiter habet fieri talis abstractio potestatis ecclesiasticae. Et si sit aliquod universale reale, specificum & quidditatiuum praeter omnem operationem intellectus: sicut inquiritur de animalitate & humanitate: remittimus ad Metaphysicam. Concedimus itaque quod abstrahentium non est mendacium, secundum Aristotel. licet negaverimus haec universalia realia: sicut nec mathematici mentiuntur, sive puncta sint realiter, sive non.
units.tr: If, however, some curious person wished to inquire how such an abstraction of ecclesiastical power is made, and whether there is some real, specific and quidditative universal beyond every operation of the intellect, as is asked of animality and humanity, we refer him to the Metaphysics. We therefore concede, with Aristotle, that "lying does not belong to those who abstract", although we deny these real universals, just as mathematicians do not lie, whether or not points exist in reality.
