units.tr: AGREEMENT THAT the fullness of ecclesiastical power lies in the supreme Pontiff and in the Church, though not altogether simply; and this under a threefold conclusion. Its explanation is evident from the treatise whose title is On Ecclesiastical Power, on the Origin of Right and of Laws.

units.la: Prima conclusio.
units.tr: First conclusion.

units.la: Plenitudo potestatis ecclesiasticae complectitur in se plenitudinem duplicis potestatis, scil. ordinis & iurisdictionis tam in foro interiori quam exteriori, quae circa quemlibet de ecclesia potest immediate & absq; limitatione exercéri claue non errante. Sed si errat, potest per solam ecclesiam synodaliter congregatam error iudicialiter corrigi: & ne fiat ulterius lex imponi, cui tenebitur habens huiusmodi potestatem reuerenter obedire sicut matri & sponsae Christi: & sicut regulae a Spiritu sancto directae.
units.tr: The fullness of ecclesiastical power comprises within itself the fullness of a twofold power, namely of order and of jurisdiction, both in the internal and the external forum, which can be exercised immediately and without limitation over anyone in the Church, provided the key does not err. But if it does err, the error can be corrected judicially by the Church alone, lawfully assembled in synod. And so that no further law be imposed, the one holding such power is bound to obey it reverently, as a mother and as the bride of Christ, and as rules directed by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Secunda conclusio.
units.tr: Second conclusion.

units.la: Plenitudo potestatis ecclesiasticae sic proprie sumpta non potest esse de lege ordinata, nisi in vnico summo pontifice formaliter & subiectiue. Alioquin ecclesiasticum regimen non esset monarchicum, & habere posset multiplex caput ex aequo, quod aperte est haereticum. Nec tamen plenitudo potestatis Papalis sic intelligenda est immediate super omnes Christianos, quod pro libito possit immediate iurisdictionem in omnes per se vel alios extraordinarios passim exercere. Sic enim praeiudicaret ordinariis, qui ius habent immediatius, imo immediatissimum super plebes eis commissas actu hierarchicos exercendi. Extenditur igitur plenitudo potestatis Papae super omnes inferiores, solum dum subest necessitas ex defectu ordinariorum inferiorum. Vel dum apparet euidens utilitas ecclesiae; quemadmodum dici potest de episcopis respectu plebanorum seu propriorum sacerdotum, quorum possunt supplere defectus.
units.tr: The fullness of ecclesiastical power, taken properly in this sense, cannot by law be ordained to reside in anyone but the one supreme Pontiff, formally and subjectively. Otherwise ecclesiastical government would not be monarchical, and could have several heads on an equal footing, which is openly heretical. Nor, however, is the fullness of papal power to be understood as extending immediately over all Christians, so that at his pleasure he could exercise jurisdiction immediately over all of them, either in person or through other extraordinary agents, wherever he liked. For that would prejudice the ordinaries, who have the right more immediately, indeed most immediately, to exercise hierarchical acts over the people committed to them. The fullness of the Pope's power therefore extends over all inferiors only while there is necessity because the inferior ordinaries are lacking, or when a clear benefit to the Church appears. This can be said in the same way of bishops with respect to parish priests or their own priests, whose deficiencies they can supply.

units.la: Tertia conclusio.
units.tr: Third conclusion.

units.la: Plenitudo potestatis ecclesiasticae dum ponitur in ecclesia synodaliter congregata cum plenitudine executionis huiusmodi potestatis sit variatio vel aequiuocatio de hoc quod est esse in, quia non eodem modo est plenitudo potestatis ecclesiasticae in Papa & in ecclesia. Fatendum est tamen, quod est vtrobique & principaliter in ecclesia suo modo, & hoc quadruplici respectu; scil. indeuiabilitatis ac indefectibilitatis extensionis, regulationis & generalis obligationis: cui subiicitur etiam ipse Papa tanquam imperatrici sponsae regis summi: qui potest condere canones, & diffinire, etiam si fuerit Papa praesens.
units.tr: The fullness of ecclesiastical power, when it is placed in the Church synodically assembled together with the fullness of the execution of this power, involves a variation or equivocation in the meaning of "being in", because the fullness of ecclesiastical power is not in the same way in the Pope and in the Church. Nevertheless it must be admitted that it is in both, and principally in the Church in its own way, and this in a fourfold respect: namely of indeviability and indefectibility, of extension, of regulation, and of general obligation. To this the Pope himself is also subject, as the empress-bride of the supreme King, who can enact canons and define matters, even when the Pope is present.

units.la: Faciunt auctoritates subsequentes pro utraq; parte secundae conclusionis cum prima & tertia. Dicit enim Bonauentura parte 6. c. 5 sui Breuiloquii ex dictis Augustini: Sic igitur baptismus potest esse extra ecclesiam: munus autem beatae vitae, non nisi intra ecclesiam reperitur: quae supra Petram fundata est, quae ligandi & soluendi claues accepit: hae est vna, quae tenet & possidet omnem sui sponsi & Domini potestatem: per quam coniugalem potestatem etiam de ancillis parere filios potest. Item Stephanus Papa sic scribit Gualberto Patriarchae: Nunc vero iterato tibi scripsimus, nolentes alicuius ecclesiae priuilegium infringere: licet Apostolica prarogatiua possumus de qualibet ecclesia clericum ordinare: Notentur decreta cum suis Glossis.
units.tr: The following authorities support both parts of the second conclusion, together with the first and the third. For Bonaventure says in part 6, chapter 5 of his Breviloquium, quoting Augustine: "Thus baptism can exist outside the Church, but the gift of blessed life is found only within the Church, which is founded upon the Rock and received the keys of binding and loosing. She alone holds and possesses all the power of her Bridegroom and Lord, by which, through her marital power, she can bear sons even from handmaids." Likewise Pope Stephen writes thus to the Patriarch Gualbert: "Now we have written to you again, not wishing to infringe the privilege of any church, although by Apostolic prerogative we can ordain a cleric from any church." Let the decrees be noted together with their Glosses.

units.la: Quod, etsi Papalis potestas extendatur ad omnes immediate, supple in casu necessitatis vel euidentis utilitatis, non tamen vult alicuius ecclesiae priuilegium infringere: supple, quia nec ita velle debet.
units.tr: This means that, even if papal power extends immediately to all, namely in a case of necessity or evident advantage, nevertheless he does not wish to infringe the privilege of any church; that is, because he ought not to wish it either.

units.la: Ut sit epilogus praemissorum.
units.tr: To sum up what has been set out above.

units.la: SERMO FACTVS PER EVN- DEM XXI. DIE IVLII, ANNO DOMINI MCCCCXV: SVPER PROCESSIONIBVS FACIENDIS PRO VIAGIO Regis Romanorum, ad Petrum de Luna. In quo ponuntur 12. conclusiones, seu regulæ practicæ in sacro gene- rali Constantinensi concilio.
units.tr: The Sermon Preached by the Same Man on 21 July, in the Year of the Lord 1415, on Processions to Be Held for the Journey of the King of the Romans, to Peter de Luna. In Which Are Set Out 12 Conclusions, or Practical Rules, of the Sacred General Council of Constance.

units.la: Prosperum iter faciet nobis Deus salutarium nostrorum. Ita loquitur Propheta in Psal. 67. Cuius initium est: Exurgat Deus & dissipentur inimici eius &c. Fiat ita quæsumus. Prosperum iter faciet nobis Deus salutarium nostrorum, auxiliante te beatissima Virgine, in qua est omnis gratia viæ & veritatis: quam imploremus & salutemus dicentes: Aue Maria.
units.tr: God will make our journey prosperous, the God of our salvation. So says the Prophet in Psalm 67, whose opening words are: "Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered," etc. So let it be, we pray. God will make our journey prosperous, the God of our salvation, with the help of you, the most blessed Virgin, in whom is all grace of the way and of the truth. Let us implore her and greet her, saying: Hail Mary.

units.la: Prosperum iter faciet nobis Deus salutarium nostrorum. Ita fieri credimus & speramus, ô Domine Deus salutarium nostrorum. Nec mirandum, si speramus & credimus, quoniam te donante assumus. Ecce ordinationi sanctissimæ super factæ, quam inspirasti, fit concentus iste celeberrimus & devotus ad orandum & deprecandum faciem tuam plenam gratiarum & dicendum: Domine salvum fac regem: iterum, suum in salutis tuæ prosperitate dispone.
units.tr: God will make our journey prosperous, the God of our salvation. So we believe and hope it will be done, O Lord God of our salvation. Nor is it to be wondered at that we hope and believe, since we are here by your gift. Behold, this most celebrated and devout chorus, made in accordance with the most holy ordinance which you inspired, comes together to pray and to beseech your face, full of graces, and to say: Lord, save the king. Again, dispose him in the prosperity of your salvation.

units.la: Sed quare nobis prosperum iter fieri petimus, viri Patres & Fratres reverendissimi, sapientes, illustres atque doctissimi, in omnium virtutum decore præclari. Nobis, inquam, prosperum iter quo pacto fieri petimus etiam qui loco manemus: nec moveri quoquam extra disponimus. Sed profecto videmur iter agere, dum facit iter nobis: hoc est ad utilitatem nostram, ad obsequium nostrum ad universalem ecclesiæ pacem, Serenissimus Romanorum Rex protector eiusdem ecclesiæ fidelissimus. Prosperum sit iter suum suppliciter & salubriter imploremus: quoniam in prosperitate sua salus nostra reponitur. Ita enim prosperum facies iter nobis, ô Deus salutarium nostrorum, si pedes eiusdem regis nostri in viam pacis direxeris: si concesseris eum redire cum exultatione portantem vberes vnionis perfectæ manipulos. Sic enim fas habebit ex sententia dicere cum Abrahæ servo, quod prosperum feceris iter suum: quod præterea fueris secum in omnibus ad quæ perrexit. Ambulet igitur ipse rex via regia per arma iustitiæ, à dextris & sinistris: te duce & te comite, qui es via, veritas & vita: te dicente ad eum: Intellectum tibi dabo & instruam te in via hac qua gradieris: firmabo super te oculos meos. Mandes Deus angelis tuis, ut custodiant eum in omnibus viis suis: portent eum in manibus suis protectionis, ut non offendat ad lapidem cuiuslibet obstaculi, vel obduratonis partis adversæ pedem suum. Sic enim prosperum iter facies, nedum tibi, sed nobis: & hoc ad utilitatem nostram tu Deus salutarium nostrorum.
units.tr: But why do we ask that our journey be made prosperous, most reverend fathers and brethren, wise, illustrious and most learned men, distinguished in the grace of all virtues? We ask, I say, that our journey be made prosperous, even though we remain in this place and have no plan to move anywhere outside it. Yet indeed we seem to be on a journey, since the journey is made for us: that is, for our benefit, for our service, and for the universal peace of the Church, of which the most serene King of the Romans is the most faithful protector. Let us humbly and profitably pray that his journey be prosperous, for our salvation is laid up in his prosperity. For thus, O God of our salvation, you will make our journey prosperous, if you direct the feet of this same king of ours into the way of peace; if you grant that he return with joy, bearing the full sheaves of perfect union. For then it will be right for us to say, in the words of Abraham's servant, that you have made his journey prosperous, and that you were with him in all the things to which he went. Let the king therefore walk the royal road, through the weapons of righteousness, on the right hand and on the left, with you as his leader and companion, who are the way, the truth and the life, and with you saying to him: I will give you understanding and instruct you in this way in which you shall walk: I will fix my eyes upon you. May God command his angels to keep him in all his ways, to bear him in the hands of their protection, so that he does not strike his foot against a stone of any obstacle, or against the hardness of the opposing side. For thus you will make the journey prosperous, not only for yourself but for us also; and this, you God of our salvation, for our benefit.

units.la: Potuerat sermo noster prolixius extendi: qui devotas pro regis itinere prospero fundendas orationes, commonefaceret atque suaderet. Sed inspicio vestrum devotionis ardorem: qui ut continuetur, vel in maiorem desiderium flammam erumpat, non eger flatu verborum meorum exiguo. Per se enim satis in meditatione vestra exardescit ignis piorum sanctorumq; desideriorum, ut iugiter leuatis sursum cordibus, ut tractis ex imo pectoris suspiriis atque gemitibus dicat unusquisque apud semetipsum: Prosperum iter faciet nobis Deus salutarium nostrorum. Faciet pro faciat. Nam apud Hebraeos (ut Nicolaus de Lyra debet) futurum indicatiui pro optitauo solet poni.
units.tr: Our sermon could have been extended at greater length, to remind and urge you to pour out devout prayers for the king's prosperous journey. But I see the warmth of your devotion, and that it may continue, or break out into a greater flame of desire, it does not need the small breath of my words. For in your meditation the fire of pious and holy desires already burns of itself enough, so that, with hearts constantly lifted up, and with sighs and groans drawn from the depth of the breast, each one may say to himself: God will make our journey prosperous, the God of our salvation. "Will make" for "may make," for among the Hebrews (as Nicholas of Lyra teaches) the future of the indicative is commonly used for the optative.

units.la: Diuertat nunc pauculum & pergat ad alia, non aliena sermo noster. Ecce quam offertur in ipsa meditatione mea iter quoddam non terrestre, quod agitur pedibus corporis: sed spirituale & cæleste iter æternitatis, quod peragratur pedibus mentis, qui sunt cognitio: pes sinister in intellectu, & volitio pes dexter in affectu. Hoc iter quale est, si quis interrogauerit? respondeat Propheta, id esse viam mandatorum Dei: quam nedum ambulasse, sed cucurrisse gloriabatur ipse cum ait: Viam mandatorum tuorum cucurri, cum dilatasti cor meum. Et rursus: In via testimoniorum tuorum delectatus sum, sicut in omnibus diuitiis. Et talia sunt in hanc sententiam absque numero. Etenim tu qui peregrinaris hic à Domino, si pergendo vis ad vitam ingredi, serua mandata. Hæc est enim via regia, hoc iter prosperum, hæc compendiosa semita quæ ducit ad vitam.
units.tr: Now let our sermon turn aside for a little, and proceed to other matters, not foreign to its purpose. Behold, in this very meditation of mine there is offered a certain journey, not earthly, which is made on the feet of the body, but a spiritual and heavenly journey of eternity, which is traversed on the feet of the mind, which are knowledge: the left foot being the understanding, and the right foot the will, which is the affection. What sort of journey this is, if someone should ask, let the Prophet answer: it is the way of God's commandments; and he boasted not only of having walked it but of having run it, when he said: I have run the way of your commandments, when you enlarged my heart. And again: I have delighted in the way of your testimonies, as in all riches. And there are countless such sayings to the same effect. For you, who are sojourning here away from the Lord, if you wish to enter into life by going forward, keep the commandments. For this is the royal road, this is the prosperous journey, this is the short path that leads to life.

units.la: At vero videre mihi videor consequenter in ipsa meditatione mea collectum esse sacrosanctum præsens concilium, ut viam istam præparet & dirigat, ut prosperum hoc iter nostrum faciat concedente Deo salutarium nostrorum. Nam væ mundo à scandalis: væ hostilibus insidiis, super quibus est illa Prophetæ conquestio: In via hac qua ambulabam abscondunt laqueum mihi. Et rursus: Iuxta iter scanda posuerunt mihi. Quis autem omnia iuxta iter mandatorum Dei posita superborum Dæmonum carnis & mundi scandala dinumeret? Quis omnes laqueorum nodos, artes & modos agnoscat? quis non Cum Antonio paucescens exclamauerit: Hos Domine laqueos omnes, hæc scandalorum retia quis euadet? At qui benedictus Deus salutarium nostrorum, qui prosperum nobis facit iter spirituale mandatorum suorum: dum voluntatem facultatemque contulit conueniendi seniores in vnum, conuocandi coetum, congregandi ecclesiam: vt viderent quid facto opus esset ad tollendum tot scandala posita in viis Sion, ita vt lugerent, eo quod non esset qui veniret ad solennitatem. Hinc offendebat scandalum schismaticæ diuisionis, hinc scandalum multiplex hæreticæ prauitatis, hinc multiplicata super numerum scandala, offensiones & retia cuiuslibet vitiositatis.
units.tr: But indeed it seems to me that, in the same meditation, I see the holy present council gathered, consequently, in order to prepare and direct this way, so that God, the God of our salvation, may grant that this our journey be prosperous. For woe to the world because of scandals, woe to hostile snares, concerning which there is that complaint of the Prophet: In the way in which I walked they have hidden a snare for me. And again: Beside the way they have set stumbling-blocks for me. But who could count up all the scandals of the proud demons, of the flesh and of the world, placed everywhere along the way of God's commandments? Who could recognise all the knots, arts and methods of the snares? Who would not cry out, like Anthony, growing pale: "Lord, who will escape all these snares, these nets of scandals?" But blessed be God, the God of our salvation, who makes for us the spiritual journey of his commandments prosperous, since he has granted the will and the power to bring the elders together into one, to summon the assembly, to gather the Church: so that they might see what had to be done to remove the many scandals placed in the ways of Zion, so that they might mourn, because there was no one coming to the solemn assembly. On the one hand there stood in the way the scandal of schismatic division; on the other the manifold scandal of heretical perversity; and beyond number, scandals, stumbling-blocks and snares of every kind of vice multiplied.

units.la: Obsidebat præcipue hoc iter spirituale monstrum horrendum, ingens, mole potens, superbia & filia eius improbissima dira dominandi libido, prohibuerat toto malignitatis spiritu & astu, ne celebraretur generale concilium: quod efficacissimum erat & pene unicum aduersus hæc omnia scandala remedium.
units.tr: Above all, this spiritual journey was beset by a horrible monster, huge and powerful in its bulk: pride, and its most wicked daughter, the dire lust of domination, which, with the whole spirit of malice and cunning, had prevented a general council from being held, though it was the most effective and almost the only remedy against all these scandals.

units.la: Exultet vero nunc omnis fidelium turba, nunc magnifice gratias referat Deo salutarium nostrorum, qui prosperum fecit iter mandatorum suorum, dum contulit celebrari sacrosanctum hoc generale concilium, sufficiens ad schismatum sedationem, ad hæresum extirpationem, & ad morum reformationem. Et hoc ex paucis in hoc eodem practicatis concilio, non tam declarare quam summatim narrare vel annotare curabo. Non accurato quidem, sed doctrinali quotidianoque sermone. Satis erit ita loqui, vt intelligar.
units.tr: Let now all the multitude of the faithful rejoice, and let them now gratefully give thanks to God, the God of our salvation, who has made prosperous the way of his commandments, in granting that this most holy general council should be held, sufficient for the calming of schisms, the uprooting of heresies, and the reformation of morals. And I shall take care not so much to declare as to narrate or note briefly, from among the few things done in this same council, these matters. Not in a careful style, but in an ordinary and everyday speech. It will be enough to speak so that I may be understood.

units.la: Considerans itaque mentalibus oculis præsens generale concilium & acta eius: inuenio quod ipsum ab itinere spirituali removit primo quadruplex scandalum obstans schismatis sedationi. Removit aliud quadruplex scandalum, nocens hæresum extirpationi. Removit alterum quadruplex contrarians morum reformationi, & ita contrarians, vt iam non esset prosperum, sed infaustum iter pacis, fidei & virtutis.
units.tr: Considering therefore with the eyes of the mind the present general council and its acts, I find that it first removed from the spiritual journey a fourfold scandal that stood in the way of the calming of the schism. It removed another fourfold scandal, harmful to the uprooting of heresies. It removed a third fourfold scandal, opposed to the reformation of morals, and opposed in such a way that the journey of peace, of faith and of virtue would no longer be prosperous, but unlucky.

units.la: Conformiter ad hanc triplicem quaternitatem scandalorum numeremus 12. conclusiones, regulas aut leges, quæ in hoc concilio vel explicite vel implicite stabilitæ sunt: quasi totidem directiones salutares, per quas prosperum iter fecit nobis Deus salutarium nostrorum, vt in hoc itinere sit vnitas ratione primi, sit veritas ratione secundi, sit bonitas respectu tertii. Sit super modus, species & ordo, sit denique mensura, numerus & pondus. Conformiter ad potentiam, sapientiam & bonitatem Patris & Filii & Spiritus sancti. Hoc modo prosperum iter facit nobis Deus, scil. vt sit iter planum, iter lucidum, iter pulchrum, dum iustitia ponit in via gressus suos: dum vestigia sua relinquit impressa, quasi certa totidem signa, ne obberremus vel exorbitemus nobis data.
units.tr: In accordance with this threefold quaternity of scandals, let us number the 12 conclusions, rules or laws which were established in this council, either explicitly or implicitly: as so many salutary directions, through which God, the God of our salvation, has made our journey prosperous, so that in this journey there may be unity by reason of the first, truth by reason of the second, and goodness with respect to the third. Let there be measure, form and order, and finally let there be measure, number and weight. In accordance with the power, wisdom and goodness of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. In this way God makes our journey prosperous, namely, that the way be level, the way be bright, the way be fair, while righteousness sets its steps in the way, while it leaves its footprints impressed, as so many certain signs, lest we wander astray or go beyond what has been given us.

units.la: Prima lex in via pacis.
units.tr: The first law on the way of peace.

units.la: ASignetur pro prima parte quæ est de via pacis prima lex, siue directio liberans iter nostrum a primo scandalo, quæ data est in sessione publica quinto Aprilis anni præsentis.
units.tr: For the first part, which concerns the way of peace, let the first law be set down, or the first direction, freeing our journey from the first stumbling-block; it was given in the public session of 5 April of the present year.

units.la: Concilium generale potestatem à Christo immediate habet: cui quilibet cuiuscunq; status vel dignitatis etiam si papalis existat, obedire tenetur in his, quæ pertinent ad fidem & extirpationem schismatis, ac generalem reformationem ecclesiæ Dei in capite & membris. Conscribenda prorsus esse mihi videretur in eminentioribus locis, vel insculpenda per omnes ecclesias saluberrima hæc determinatio, lex vel regula tanquam directio fundamentalis & velut infallibilis aduersus monstruosum horrendumq; offendiculum: quod hactenus positum erat per multos de ecclesia in itinere mandatorum Dei, determinantes ex textibus grossè, non ad regulam euangelicam & æternam acceptis: Papam non esse subiectum generali concilio, neq; iudicari posse per ipsum. Quod præterea generale concilium totum ab ipso robur immediatum sumebat. Nec poterat sine eo casu quocunq; vel convocari vel stabiliri. Quod nemo poterat ei dicere, cur ita facis? quoniam solutus erat legibus & supra ius. Et ita de plurimis, per quæ blanda, fallax & subdola adulatio fouebat libidinem dominandi, & tyrannidem ecclesiæ destructricem papatum seu eius vsum conuertebat, ita vt non pateret via reductionis seu pacis.
units.tr: A general council holds its power immediately from Christ, and everyone, of whatever status or dignity, even if he be papal, is bound to obey it in those matters which pertain to the faith, the extirpation of the schism, and the general reformation of the Church of God in head and members. It seems to me that this most salutary determination, law or rule, as a fundamental and as it were infallible direction against that monstrous and dreadful stumbling-block, ought to be written in the more prominent places, or engraved throughout all the churches. Until now this stumbling-block has been set in the path of God's commandments by many in the Church, who crudely determined from texts, not received according to the eternal gospel rule, that the Pope is not subject to a general council and cannot be judged by it. Moreover, a general council took its whole strength immediately from him; nor could it be convened or established in any case without him. No one could say to him, "Why do you act thus?" because he was loosed from the laws and above the law. And so with many other things, by which a flattering, deceitful and sly adulation fostered the lust for domination, and turned the papacy, the tyranny destructive of the Church, or its use, so that the way of reduction or peace lay open to no one.

units.la: Scripsit super hoc errore vel scandalo reuerendissimus pater & Dominus, Dominus Cardinalis Cameracensis præceptor meus inclitus dudum & nuper antequam fieret hæc constitutio, reputans esse perniciosissimum sic asserere: sicut & de multis dictis per quosdam nitentes suis iutibus positiuis annotauit. Nunc ex quo iam lex posita est, nec iam licet dubitare, probationes omittamus. Sed hæc probatio sufficeret, Si ecclesiam tuo audierit, sit tibi vt ethnicus & publicanus.
units.tr: The most reverend father and lord, Lord Cardinal of Cambrai, my illustrious teacher of long standing, wrote about this error or stumbling-block, both long ago and recently, before this constitution was made, judging it most pernicious so to assert; as he also noted concerning many statements made by some who strive to defend their positive rights. Now that the law has already been laid down, and it is no longer permitted to doubt, let us omit the proofs. Yet this proof would suffice: "If he refuses to hear the Church, let him be to you as a heathen and a tax collector" (Matt. 18).

units.la: Secunda directio, siue lex salutaris.
units.tr: The second direction, or salutary law.

units.la: Concilium generale potest eum, quem in reptirat summum pontificem, nedum consulere inducere, sed auctoritatiue compellere ad offerendum viam cessionis: vel ad cedendum papatui, etiam sine culpa sua, licet non sine causa. Qualis causa multiplex esse potest: quemadmodum in publicis sermonibus tactum fuit in hoc concilio.
units.tr: A general council may not only advise the one whom it judges to be the supreme pontiff, but also compel him by authority to offer a way of resignation, or to yield the papacy, even without his fault, though not without cause. Such a cause can be manifold, as was touched upon in the public sermons in this council.

units.la: Cccccc
units.tr: Cccccc

units.la: Hæc lex per hoc sacrum concilium determinatiue statuta est, & in Papa Ioanne 23. practicata: qui viam cessionis vrgente concilio, primum obtulit, deinde cessit. Tollitur ex hoc scandalum dicentium viam cessionis practicari non posse inuitis contendentibus de Papatu. Tollitur denique collusio seu tergiuersatio volentium inuito generali concilio, vel ecclesia perniciose Papatum detinere, nunc aut quomodolibet in futurum. Etenim si potest summus pontifex dare libellum repudii ecclesiæ sponsæ Christi, sicut egit Cœlestinus, & laudatur: cur non vice versa poterit sponsa Christi repudiare, non dicam sponsum suum, sed sponsi vicarium: præsertim vbi subest vel culpa vel causa.
units.tr: This law has been determinately established by this holy council and put into practice in Pope John XXIII, who, when the council urged the way of resignation, first offered it and then resigned. By this the scandal of those who say that the way of resignation cannot be carried out against the will of those contending for the papacy is removed. Finally, the collusion or evasion of those who, against the will of the general council or of the Church, wish to hold the papacy to its ruin, now or in any way in future, is removed. For if the supreme pontiff can give a bill of divorce to the Church, the bride of Christ, as Celestine did and is praised for it, why should not the bride of Christ, conversely, be able to repudiate, I do not say her husband, but the vicar of her husband, especially where either fault or cause is present?

units.la: Tertia directio.
units.tr: The third direction.

units.la: Concilium generale sic est supra Papam, quod eius bullas & processus vel ordinationes & statuta potest irritare vel annullare. Potest insuper translationem curiæ Romanæ à loco concilii impedire. Compellere rursus Papam stare cum concilio: & ita de similibus. Hoc determinatum est in publica sessione & multipliciter practicatum. Tollitur ex hoc scandalum, quo per indirectum quaeretur nunc aut alijs dissipare generale concilium.
units.tr: A general council is so far above the Pope that it can nullify or annul his bulls, processes, ordinances and statutes. Moreover, it can prevent the transfer of the Roman curia from the place of the council, and again compel the Pope to stand with the council, and so on with similar things. This has been determined in a public session and put into practice in many ways. By this the scandal is removed by which, indirectly, someone now or at another time might seek to dissolve the general council.

units.la: Quarta directio.
units.tr: The fourth direction.

units.la: Concilium generale sic est super omnes leges positiuas, vel à summis pontificibus vel à generalibus conciliis editas: quod eas potest interpretari, mutare vel tollere, pro quanto viderentur impedimentum vel scandalum esse ad iter ecclesiasticæ vnionis. Hoc practicauit præsens concilium tollendo poenas omnes & inhabilitationes &c. suspendendo insuper futuram summi pontificis electionem. Recipiendo denique ad cautelam & humili quadam condescensione prætensam confirmationem concilii à Domino Papa cum multis similibus: quæ & qualia iurium positiuorum rigor non admittit.
units.tr: A general council is so far above all positive laws, whether issued by supreme pontiffs or by general councils, that it can interpret, change or remove them, insofar as they might seem to be an obstacle or stumbling-block to the path of ecclesiastical union. The present council has practised this by removing all penalties and disqualifications, etc., by suspending moreover the future election of the supreme pontiff, and by receiving, as a precaution and through a certain humble condescension, the alleged confirmation of the council from the Lord Pope, along with many similar things, which the rigour of positive rights does not admit.

units.la: SECVNDA PARS PRINCIPALIS DE via veritatis.
units.tr: THE SECOND PRINCIPAL PART, CONCERNING THE WAY OF TRUTH.

units.la: EXposituimus in hac parte prima quatuor scandalorum genera, quibus obsistit præsens concilium, vt prosperum iter faceret nobis Deus salutarium nostrorum: ad dirigendos pedes nostros in viam pacis: & ad sedationem schismaticæ diuisionis. Transeamus pro secunda parte ad destructionem alterius quadruplicis scandali, quo videbatur impediri declaratio veritatis, & hæreticæ prauitatis destructio.
units.tr: In this first part we have set out four kinds of scandal which the present council opposes, so that God may grant us a prosperous journey toward our salvation, to direct our feet into the way of peace, and to calm the schismatic division. Let us pass on, in a second part, to the destruction of another fourfold scandal, by which the declaration of the truth and the overthrow of heretical depravity seemed to be hindered.

units.la: Prima directio salutaris in via catholicæ veritatis.
units.tr: The first saving direction on the way of Catholic truth.

units.la: Concilium generale potest & debet circa omnem personam cuiuscunque præeminentiæ vel status existat, absque fauore vel timore vel personarum acceptione iudicium in causa hæresis exercere. Patet ex tenore commissionis datæ reuerendissimis patribus Dominis quatuor Cardinalibus, & aliis de qualibet natione. Hoc insuper practicatum est circa inquisitionem factam de Papa Ioanne 23. & circa Ioannem Huss, qui quamuis esset status parui, habuit tamen fautores plurimos fortes, acres & potentes. Hoc autem est prosperum & efficax iter ad extirpationem errorum, dum nullis parcitur, sed constanter proceditur ad emendationem, vel si corrigi noluerint, ad punitionem & exterminationem errantium. Alioquin non satis destruuntur errores, si permittuntur liberi & impuniti, patentes & notorii verbis aut factis hæresum defensores. Si præterea prædicatoribus catholicæ veritatis non subest plena libertas elucidandi legem sanctam. Tollitur ex hoc præsenti concilio dictum Philosophi illius, qui leges comparabat telis aranearum: eo quod debiliores muscas retinent, transmittunt fortiores.
units.tr: A general council can and ought to exercise judgment in a case of heresy over any person, of whatever pre-eminence or rank, without favour, fear, or respect of persons. This is evident from the terms of the commission given to the most reverend fathers, the lords the four Cardinals, and others from every nation. Moreover, this has been done in the inquiry made into Pope John XXIII and in the case of John Huss, who, although he was of humble rank, nevertheless had very many supporters, strong, vigorous and powerful. This is indeed a prosperous and effective way to root out errors, when no one is spared but the process goes steadily on toward amendment or, if they will not be corrected, toward the punishment and extermination of those who err. Otherwise errors are not sufficiently destroyed if open and notorious defenders of heresies in word or deed are allowed to go free and unpunished. Furthermore, if the preachers of Catholic truth do not have full liberty to explain the holy law, [the way is blocked]. By this present council the saying of that philosopher is removed, who compared laws to spiders' webs, because they hold back the weaker flies and let the stronger ones pass through.

units.la: Secunda directio, siue sexta lex in ordine.
units.tr: The second direction, or sixth rule in order.

units.la: Concilium generale potest & debet assertiones hæreticas & erroneas in fide & moribus, quæ fuerunt & sunt in scandalum publicum, diligenter examinare, reprobare & damnare: etiam non facto prius vel simul processu aduersus assertores. Hoc pluries practicatum est in hoc concilio, vt de assertionibus quod communicandi erant laici sub utraq; specie. Et de ista assertione quilibet Christianus potest & debet &c. Deniq; tam rationes quam similitudines manifestas & exempla sanctorum probant idem, vt de falso numismate & famoso libello. Tollitur ex hoc scandalum vel tolli debet eorum qui pro bono accessorio quod in facto consistit, elucidationem veritatis vel impediunt vel procrastinant. Hoc autem procrastinare quid, nisi impedire est?
units.tr: A general council can and ought to examine carefully, reprove and condemn heretical and erroneous assertions in faith and morals, which have been and are a public scandal, even without a prior or simultaneous process against their authors. This has been done many times in this council, as with the assertions that the laity ought to receive communion in both kinds. And concerning this assertion every Christian can and ought, etc. Finally, reasons and clear likenesses and the examples of the saints prove the same, as with a counterfeit coin and a notorious libel. From this it is removed, or ought to be removed, the scandal of those who hinder or delay the clearing up of truth on account of some supposed side issue which lies in fact. But what is delaying such a thing except hindering it?

units.la: Tertia directio.
units.tr: The third direction.

units.la: Concilium generale potest damnare propositiones multas cum suis autoribus, licet habere Glossas aliquas vel expositiones vel sensus logicales veros possint. Hoc praticatum est in hoc concilio de multis articulis & Vicleff, & Ioannis Hus: quorum aliqui poterant vel de vi logicae vel grammaticae defensionem aliquam recipere: vt in articulis qui sunt indefinite traditi; vel qui loquuntur de possibilitate, prout posse logicum est, & non physicum. Vel qui possent ad aliquem sensum verum trahi, si seorsum ponerentur.
units.tr: A general council can condemn many propositions together with their authors, even though some of them may admit of glosses, or of explanations, or of true logical senses. This has been done in this council concerning many articles of Wycliffe and John Huss, some of which could receive some defence from the force of logic or grammar: as in articles which are put forward indefinitely, or which speak of possibility as it is a logical and not a physical possibility, or which could be drawn to some true sense if they were taken separately.

units.la: Sed concilium hoc solerter attendit: primo quia iuxta Hilarium, intelligentia dictorum ex causis est assumenda dicendi. Iterum illud Augustin. Liberis verbis vtuntur Philosophi, & in rebus ad intelligendum difficillimis offensionem parum aurium non pertimescunt. Nobis autem (scil. theologis) ad certam regulam loqui fas est. Illud denique vulgatum fundamentum in Aristot. quod sermones accipiendi sunt secundum materiam subiectam, vnde moralis sententia sumitur. Ea est enim diuinae formae substantia, vt quod nec in extrema dilabatur, nec in se extraneum aliquod ipsa suscipiat, sed sicut de ea Parmenides ait: Verti orbem mobilem retat, dum se immobilem ipsa conseruat. Quod si rationes quoq; non extra petitas, sed intra rei, quam tractabimus, ambitum collocatas agitauimus: nihil est quod admirere, cum Platone sanciente didiceras cognatos, de quibus loquimur; rebus oportere esse sermones 3. de consolatione vltima, prosa in sin. Similiter theologia suam propriam habet logicam & sensum literalem aliter quam speculatiuae scientiae. Haec directio vel lex praeseruauit hactenus praeclaram vniuersitatem Parrhysiensem, a pluribus erroribus, dum scholasticos suos semper ad certam regulam fidei loqui iussit & compulit. Vtinam in aliis studiis haec disciplina similiter teneatur. Mala libertas est male & erronee loqui posse.
units.tr: But the council has carefully considered this, first because, according to Hilary, the meaning of what is said must be gathered from the causes of the saying. Again, that saying of Augustine: Philosophers use free words, and in matters very difficult to understand they do not much fear offending ears. But for us (that is, for theologians) it is right to speak by a fixed rule. Finally, that commonly accepted foundation in Aristotle, that words are to be understood according to the subject matter, from which a moral judgement is drawn. For such is the substance of divine form, that it neither slips into anything extreme nor takes up anything foreign into itself; but, as Parmenides says of it: it keeps the moving sphere still, while itself remaining unmoved. And if we have also argued from reasons not sought from outside, but placed within the compass of the matter we are treating, there is nothing to wonder at, since you had learned, with Plato laying it down, that words ought to be fitted to the things which we are discussing, as in Boethius, De consolatione 3, prose at the end. Likewise, theology has its own logic and its literal sense, different from that of the speculative sciences. This direction or rule has so far preserved the famous University of Paris from many errors, since it has always ordered and compelled its scholars to speak according to a fixed rule of faith. Would that in other studies this discipline were kept in the same way. Freedom to speak badly and erroneously is an evil freedom.

units.la: Quarta directio siue octaua in ordine.
units.tr: The fourth direction, or eighth in order.

units.la: Concilium generale potest & debet damnare propositiones multas vel assertiones huiusmodi quamuis non possent ex solo & nudo textu expresso sacrae scripturae patenter reprobari: seclusis expositionibus doctorum vel vsu celebri ecclesiae & caeteris. Hoc praticatum est in hoc concilio in multis assertionibus Iohannis Vicleff, & Ioannis Hus: imo & de ista, quod est communicandum per laicos sub vtraq; specie panis & vini. Haec directio vel lex prosperum facit iterad haeresum & haereticorum exterminationem: quoniam haeretici, quos vidimus, defensionem suam vt plurimum accipiunt: quia nolunt haereses absolute reuocare, sed tantum conditionaliter: si videlicet ex rigore textus sacrae scripturae conuincantur errare dicentes, quod expositiones Doctorum, decreta, Decretales sint apocryphae, neque de illis curandum est. Haec autem praesumptio quam late pateat ad errores, nemo non intelligit.
units.tr: A general council can and ought to condemn many propositions or assertions of this kind, even though they could not be plainly refuted from the bare and express text of Holy Scripture alone, setting aside the expositions of the doctors, the widespread use of the Church, and other things. This has been done in this council in many assertions of John Wycliffe and John Huss, and indeed also in the one that the laity must receive communion under both kinds of bread and wine. This direction or rule makes the way prosperous for the extermination of heresies and heretics, since the heretics whom we have seen for the most part take up their defence in this way: they are unwilling to recant their heresies absolutely, but only conditionally, namely if they are convicted of error from the strict text of Holy Scripture, saying that the expositions of the doctors, the decrees and the Decretals are apocryphal, and that they need not be heeded. And how widely this presumption opens the way to errors no one fails to see.

units.la: TERTIA PARS PRINCIPALIS DE VIA morum, vel virtutum.
units.tr: THE THIRD PRINCIPAL PART, CONCERNING THE WAY OF MORALS, OR OF VIRTUES.

units.la: Declaratis vel narratis scandalis quatuor obuiantibus errorum extirpationi, loquamur pro tertia & vltima parte aliquid de remotione totidem scandalorum obstantium morum reformationi in capite & in membris, narrando quadruplicem legem vel directionem practicatam in hoc concilio, vt prosperum iter faciat nobis Deus salutarium nostrorum.
units.tr: Having declared and set out the four stumbling-blocks that stand in the way of rooting out errors, let us speak, for the third and last part, of the removal of the same number of obstacles that stand in the way of reforming morals, both in the head and in the members, by setting out the fourfold law or direction put into practice in this council, so that God may make our journey toward our salvation prosperous.

units.la: Prima directio salutaris in via morum virtutis.
units.tr: The first saving direction on the way of moral virtue.

units.la: Concilium generale sic est supra Papam in alium quemlibet de ecclesia, quod ipsum Papam potest deponere pro quocunque crimine, de quo notorie & incorrigibiliter scandalizatur ecclesia. Hoc est practicatum dudum de Papa Iohanne 12. & nunc de Ioanne. In cuius deiectione non inseritur, quod fuerit haereticus vel a fide deuius. Et sic ita actum est de cedro libani: quare non timebit humilis herba deserti? Accusatus tamen inter caetera fuit & conuictus, quod fuerat notorie simoniacus. Ex quo confunditur illa quorundam temeritas, qui Papam in collatione beneficiorum non posse committere simoniam, vel disputabant vel diffiniebant.
units.tr: A general council stands so far above the Pope, as above any other member of the Church, that it can depose the Pope himself for any crime by which the Church is notoriously and incorrigibly scandalized. This was practised long ago against Pope John XII, and now against John. In his deposition it was not alleged that he was a heretic or had departed from the faith. And so it was done: "Shall the humble herb of the desert not fear, since the cedar of Lebanon has been so treated?" He was, however, accused and convicted, among other things, of being notoriously simoniacal. From this it appears how rash is the view of some who have either argued or defined that the Pope cannot commit simony in conferring benefices.

units.la: Secunda directio, siue decima lex.
units.tr: The second direction, or tenth law.

units.la: Concilium generale quamuis non possit nec debeat plenitudinem potestatis Papalis commissam a Christo Petro & successoribus eius tollere vel minuere, sed de ea gratias agere Deo, qui contulit, eamq; reuereri debet & ampleqti. Potest nihilominus vsum potestatis illius certis legibus & statutis limitare in aedificationem ecclesiae. Hoc practicauit praesens concilium tum in multis, tum specialiter in hoc, quod legem praefixit in eligendo Papam futurum & suis electoribus: quod reuerendissimum patrem Dominum Angelum Corario, ob laudabilitatem suae cessionis spontaneae, nullus Papa futurus posset eum a collatis cardinalatu & potestate legati per hoc concilium deponere, nec re, nec eum super praeteritis quibuscunque factis quomodolibet impetere vel punire: iure quidem & indulgenti condescensione hoc factum est, ut exemplum posteris detur ultro cedendi, dum illud effiagitat ecclesiae vel pia velitas vel urgens necessitas.
units.tr: A general council, although it cannot and ought not to take away or diminish the fullness of papal power committed by Christ to Peter and his successors, but should give thanks to God who bestowed it, and should revere and embrace it, nevertheless can limit the exercise of that power by certain laws and statutes for the building up of the Church. The present council has practised this both in many matters and especially in this, that it laid down a law for the future Pope and his electors: that, on account of the praiseworthiness of his voluntary resignation, the most reverend father Lord Angelo Corraro should not be deposed by any future Pope from the cardinalate and the legateship conferred on him by this council, nor be assailed or punished in any way in person or property for any past acts whatever. This was done by right and by the indulgent condescension of the council, so that an example might be given to posterity of resigning freely, whenever either the piety of the Church or pressing necessity demands it.

units.la: Expedit autem nunc ante summi pontificis electionem ita fieri circa multa generalem statum ecclesiae concernentia: in quibus summi pontifices usum plenitudinis suae potestatis passim nimis verterunt in abusum: ut quia noluerunt generalia celebrare concilia: nec inferioribus praelatis ordinaria iura relinquere, quodque in statutis generalium conciliorum nunc cassando ea, nunc mutando, nunc ad libitum interpretando, nunc privilegia & exceptiones laigiendo, palam & absque manifesta ratione vel utilitate deuiarunt.
units.tr: It is, however, now expedient that this be done before the election of the supreme pontiff, in many matters concerning the general state of the Church. In these matters the supreme pontiffs have too often turned the exercise of the fullness of their power into abuse: by refusing to hold general councils, by not leaving ordinary rights to inferior prelates, and by going astray openly and without clear reason or advantage, now annulling the statutes of general councils, now changing them, now interpreting them at will, and now bestowing privileges and exemptions.

units.la: Unde sicut in usu dispensationum, concessione privilegiorum, innovatione decretalium non expedit usum potestatis papalis sic restringi, ut in omni casu tali fiat ad concilium generale recursus propter difficultatem & raritatem suae convocationis: qualis non erat in primitiva ecclesia, quando communi consensu dicente Hieronymo, fiebant omnia. Sic non expedit talem laxationem fieri, quae vim & robur generalium conciliorum in suis constitutionibus passim tollat & enervet.
units.tr: Hence, just as in the use of dispensations, the granting of privileges, and the renewal of decretals, it is not expedient that the exercise of papal power be so restricted that in every such case recourse must be had to a general council, on account of the difficulty and rarity of its convocation (which was not the case in the primitive Church, when, as Jerome says, with common consent, all things were done), so it is not expedient that such a relaxation be made as would everywhere take away and weaken the force and strength of general councils in their constitutions.

units.la: Considerari posset in hoc loco Aristot. traditio de triplici politia, regali scilicet & monarchica: in qua unus bene praeest, cui tyrannus opponitur. Altera est aristocratia, vbi dominantur pauci & boni: cui opponitur oligarchia. Tertiam ponit timocratiam, in qua populus bene dominatur, quae opposita habet democratiam.
units.tr: In this place one might consider the tradition of Aristotle concerning the threefold form of government: the kingly, namely, and monarchical, in which one rules well, to which tyranny is opposed; another is aristocracy, where a few good men rule, to which oligarchy is opposed; a third he sets down as timocracy, in which the people rule well, which has democracy as its opposite.

units.la: Esset autem inter istas politias illa melior quam aliqua singularis, quae ex regali & aristocratia componeretur, ut in regno Franciae: vbi rex instituit parlamentum, a quo iudicari non refugit. Esset vero omnium optima & salubberrima politia, quae triplicem hanc bonam complecteretur, regalem, aristocratiam & timocratiam.
units.tr: Among these forms of government, however, that one would be better than any single one which was compounded of the kingly and the aristocratic, as in the kingdom of France, where the king has instituted a parliament, from whose judgment he does not shrink. Indeed the best and most wholesome of all would be that form of government which embraced these three good elements: the kingly, the aristocratic, and the timocratic.

units.la: Est autem generale concilium politia talis composita habens suam directionem magis ex assistentia speciali Spiritus sancti & promissione Iesu Christi, quam ex natura, vel ex humana sola industria.
units.tr: Now a general council is a form of government so composed, having its direction rather from the special assistance of the Holy Spirit and the promise of Jesus Christ than from nature or from human industry alone.

units.la: Hinc est illud, quod praediximus, quod ipsum est salubberrima & efficacissima regula ad regimen totius ecclesiae tranquillum vel conseruandum vel reformandum vel inueniendum tanquam supremus & sufficiens legislator vniuersalis & potens. Praeterea legitimus & securus nec suspectus rationabiliter ab aliquibus Christianis: cum procedat omnium communi consensu vel assensu.
units.tr: Hence it is what we have said before: that it is the most wholesome and most efficacious rule, both for preserving and for reforming or finding out a tranquil government of the whole Church, as the supreme and sufficient universal and powerful lawgiver. Moreover, it is lawful and secure, and not reasonably suspected by any Christians, since it proceeds by the common consent or assent of all.

units.la: Quid autem est generale concilium? alij descriptum est & repeto, Concilium generale est congregatio legitima auctoritate facta ad aliquem locum ex omni statu hierarchico totius ecclesiae catholicae nulla fideli persona quae audire requirat exclusa, ad salubriter tractandum & ordinandum ea quae debitum regimen eiusdem ecclesiae in fide & moribus respiciunt. Deducit posset ex hac descriptione cum praecedentibus qualiter plenitudo potestatis papalis collata est a Christo in his, quae supra naturam sunt. In aliis etiam, quae leges naturalis, canonica & ciuilis sibi tribuunt, ut monarchae, supremo stat & concordatur cum potestate concilii quae dicta est: quoniam in concilio papalis potestas includitur: quamuis aliter sit haec potestas in Papa, aliter in concilio. Sicut aliter claues Petro traditae sunt, aliter ecclesiae. Unde concilium in multis, quae Papam respiciunt, habet auctoritatem conciliatiuam & dictatiuam: Papa exercitatiuam & executiuam. Non enim posset concilium per se ipsum vel absoluere in foro conscientiae: vel presbyteros ordinare: vel corpus Christi conficere: vel debellare manu armata infideles, & ita de multis: sed ad ipsum spectat circa haec huiusmodi consulere vel dictare: cuius dictamini qui repugnat, contumaciter repugnat Spiritui sancto, cuius est ipsum concilium in dictando vel consulendo dirigere. Exemplum in homine, vbi ratio potestatem habet dictatiuam & conciliatiuam, voluntas exercitium & executionem.
units.tr: But what is a general council? I have elsewhere described it, and I repeat: A general council is a lawful assembly, convened by authority, at some place, drawn from every hierarchical rank of the whole catholic Church, excluding no faithful person who desires to hear, for the purpose of wholesomely treating and ordering those matters which concern the due government of the same Church in faith and morals. From this description, together with what has gone before, it may be deduced how the fullness of papal power was conferred by Christ in those things which are above nature. In other matters also, which natural, canon and civil law assign to a monarch, the supreme power stands and agrees with the power of the council just described; for the papal power is included in the council, although this power is one way in the Pope and another way in the council. Just as the keys were delivered one way to Peter and another way to the Church. Hence the council, in many matters which concern the Pope, has authority that is advisory and directive, while the Pope has authority that is executive and carrying into effect. For the council could not itself, by its own action, absolve in the forum of conscience, ordain presbyters, consecrate the body of Christ, or wage war on unbelievers with armed hand, and so of many other things; but it belongs to the council to advise or direct concerning such matters, and whoever resists its direction resists the Holy Spirit obstinately, whose office it is to guide the council itself in directing or advising. An example is found in a man, where reason has the directive and advisory power, and the will the exercise and execution.

units.la: Tertia directio:
units.tr: The Third Direction:

units.la: Concilium generale potest de dissensionibus & guerris inter principes Christianos saeuientes in perniciem totius Christianitatis & perditionis hominum in anima & corpore auctoritate legitima cognoscere: prohibendo eis vias facti & ad suscipiendum vias iuris & rationis per censuras ecclesiasticas compellendo.
units.tr: A general council can, by lawful authority, take cognizance of dissensions and wars raging among Christian princes to the ruin of all Christendom and the destruction of men in soul and body: forbidding them recourse to force, and compelling them by ecclesiastical censures to accept the ways of law and reason.

units.la: Hoc practicare proposuit Serenissimus Rex Romanorum semper Augustus: qui priusquam recederet ab hoc concilio ad locum conuentionis cum rege Aragonum & Petro de Luna, orationem id deputatos habuit omni religiosa pietate & vera Christiana religione plenissimam: quam his auribus non sine pia compunctione laetus audiui. Narrauit illic propositum suum esse tendere post sedationem schismatis ad pacificationem regum Franciae & Angliae: maxime per auctoritatem huius concilii. Narrauit de pacificatione regis Poloniae cum Prutenis. Deinde de passagio Hierosolymitano, praecedente pacificatione regis Poloniae &c. Fundamentum seu regulam procurauit inducendo quamlibet partium, vt se generali concilio sacq; diffinitioni prorsus submitterent: cuius auctoritati ipsemet rex quemadmodum tunc & pluries antea sub attestatione diuini nominis protestatus esse debebat & volebat esse subiectus: & hoc in speculum & exemplar aeternum cuiuslibet principis catholici temporalis.
units.tr: His Serene Majesty, the King of the Romans, ever Augustus, proposed to put this into practice. Before he left this council for the place of meeting with the King of Aragon and Peter de Luna, he gave an address prepared for the assembled fathers, most full of all religious piety and true Christian religion, which I heard with these ears, not without holy compunction and joy. There he related that his purpose, after the healing of the schism, was to strive for the pacification of the kings of France and England, chiefly through the authority of this council. He related also the pacification of the King of Poland with the Prussians, and then the crossing to Jerusalem, the pacification of the King of Poland preceding it, and so on. He arranged a foundation or rule by bringing it about that each of the parties should submit themselves entirely to the holy definition of the general council, to whose authority the king himself, just as he had then and many times before declared under witness of the divine name, was bound and willed to be subject. And this he set forth as a mirror and eternal example for every temporal Catholic prince.

units.la: Quarta directio, siue lex duodecima & ultima.
units.tr: The fourth direction, or the twelfth and last law.

units.la: Concilium generale potest & debet constituere crebriorem generalium conciliorum celebrationem, quam retroactis temporibus fuerint celebrata: vt de decennio in decennium praefixa futuris summis pontificibus ista lege, quam transgredi non liceat. Fundatur in praemissis haec consideratio, & per argumentum ex oppositis: quoniam si tot & tam enormia discrimina prouenerunt Ecclesiae Dei, dum cessatum est a conciliis generalibus: quanta demum erit salutaris utilitas ex frequentiori celebratione perspicuum est. Quis itaq; nesciat, quod inde superiorum peccata minus vigebunt, dum minorem sibi sentient esse peccandi licentiam, vel impunitatis spem: dum scil. reddituros se rationem coram iudice suo generali concilio prospicient? Sunt quippe nonnulli, qui etsi Deum non timent, homines tamen reuerentur. Denique; si non sit assidue lex viua dirigens, regens & actuans leges mortuas ad effectum: ipsi non satis proficiunt. Vnde & Philosophus tradere satagens medium virtutis, non potuit illud efficacius inuenire, quam vt diceret, prout sapiens iudicabit.
units.tr: A general council can and ought to establish that general councils be celebrated more often than they have been in past times, so that, with a fixed interval of ten years, this law is laid down for future supreme pontiffs and may not be transgressed. This consideration is founded on what has been said above, and it is argued by way of the opposite: if so many and such grave dangers have arisen for the Church of God while general councils have ceased, then how great the saving benefit will be from more frequent celebration is clear. Who, then, does not know that from this the sins of superiors will flourish less, since they will feel they have less licence to sin or hope of impunity, when they foresee that they will have to render an account before their judge, the general council? For there are some who, even if they do not fear God, nevertheless show reverence to men. Finally, if there is not a living law that constantly directs, governs and gives effect to dead laws, they make little progress. Hence even the Philosopher, labouring to teach the mean of virtue, could find nothing more effective to say than that it is as the wise man shall judge.

units.la: Potuerant ex praemissis omnibus velut ex fundamentalibus quibusdam regulis, directionibus & signis in via mandatorum Dei leges elici particulariores, ad tollendum scandala impedientia prosperum iter pacis, fidei & virtutis ad sedationem schismatum quo ad primum; ad extirpationem errorum, quo ad secundum: & ad reformationem morum quo ad tertium: sed neq; tempus neq; locus sufficiunt: quia tetigerunt insuper multa ex eis prudentes & studiosi suis in scriptis: quia rursus debent huiusmodi leges & constitutiones particulares magis per mutuam collationem omnium de concilio agitari, tractari & diffiniri iuxta regionum aut patriarum varietatem. Quia deniq; decreta & decretales viderentur abundanter sufficere, si per legem viuam fieret efficax executio. Alioquin multiplicatio constitutionum huiusmodi etiam poenalium quandoq; plus onerat & aggrauat, quam subleuet aut proficiat.
units.tr: From all that has been said, as from certain fundamental rules, directions and signposts on the way of God's commandments, more particular laws could have been drawn out, to remove the scandals that hinder the prosperous course of peace, faith and virtue: for the first, to calm schisms; for the second, to root out errors; and for the third, to reform morals. But neither time nor place suffices, since prudent and diligent men have already touched upon many of these in their writings; and, again, laws and particular constitutions of this kind ought rather to be debated, treated and defined by the mutual deliberation of all members of the council, according to the variety of regions or nations. Finally, decrees and decretals would seem to suffice abundantly, if their execution were made effective through a living law. Otherwise, the multiplication of constitutions of this kind, even penal ones, often burdens and weighs down more than it relieves or benefits.

units.la: Faciamus tandem in oratione finem verbis, vt O, reuolet ad A, & dicamus obsecrantes: Prosperum iter faciat nobis Deus salutarium nostrorum. Iter nedum terrestre, sed spirituale & coeleste, iter aeternitatis ad Deum salutarium nostrorum: qui est Deus benedictus in secula: Amen.
units.tr: Let us at last end our address with words in the manner of "from O back to A," and let us say, beseeching: may God of our salvation make our journey prosperous. A journey not only earthly, but spiritual and heavenly, the journey of eternity to God our salvation, who is blessed God for ever: Amen.

units.la: LIBELLVS DE AVFERIBILITATE PAPAE AB ECCLESIA, IOANNIS DE GERSON CANCELLARII PARI- SIENSIS.
units.tr: THE BOOK ON THE REMOVABILITY OF THE POPE FROM THE CHURCH, BY JOHN GERSON, CHANCELLOR OF PARIS.

units.la: Venient autem dies, cum auferetur ab eis sponsus: Mar. 2. Circa quem textum pro materia nunc currente quaeritur: Si auferibilis sit sponsus Ecclesiae a filiis suis vel ab ea? Et ponantur hic consideraciones 20.
units.tr: "The days will come when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them" (Mark 2). On this text, as our present subject matter, the question is asked: whether the bridegroom of the Church can be taken away from his sons, or from her? And twenty considerations are laid down here.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO I.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION I.

units.la: Auferibilis non est sponsus Ecclesiae Christus homo ab ipsa tota Ecclesia, lege stante. Si quidem caput Ecclesiae Christus est, ad Ephes. 4. & ad Coloss. 1. & 2. Puto autem nemo concesserit, quod absque capite valeat permanere corpus aliquod verum vel mysticum: sed Ecclesiae corpus mysticum manere semper usque ad consummationem seculi necesse est, lege stante, Matth. vltim. & 24. Hoc ergo fiet per viuificum influxum capitis in ipsum. Pro quo facit parabola, qua Christus se viti comparat, discipulos palmitibus. Quod si quis dixerit oppositum dicens Ecclesiam incepisse ab Abel iusto secundum Gregor. quo tempore nondum Christus erat incarnatus. Respondet Ioannes in Apocal. qui dicit agnum fuisse occisum ab origine mundi, praeuisiue, scil. & acceptatiue a Deo, licet nondum corporaliter exhibitiue: quia nec ipsis antiquis erat salus nisi in fide: multum tamen implicita & generali mediatoris & capitis Ecclesiae Christi tunc futuri: quibus erat necessarium credere sanctum illud Symbolum, quod Deus est, & quod est remunerator in se credentium.
units.tr: Christ, as man, the bridegroom of the Church, cannot be taken away from the whole Church, the law standing. For Christ is the head of the Church (Eph. 4; Col. 1 and 2). Now no one, I think, will concede that any true or mystical body can remain without a head; but the mystical body of the Church must remain always, until the consummation of the age, the law standing (Matt. last chapter and 24). This therefore will happen through the life-giving influx of the head into the body. To this the parable belongs, in which Christ compares himself to the vine and his disciples to the branches. But if someone should say the contrary, namely that the Church began with the righteous Abel, according to Gregory, at a time when Christ was not yet incarnate: John in the Apocalypse answers him, who says that the Lamb was slain from the foundation of the world, foreseen, that is, and accepted by God, although not yet bodily exhibited; for not even the ancients had salvation except in faith, yet one that was very much implicit and general in the Mediator and Head of the Church, who was then to come; and it was necessary for them to believe that holy creed, that God is, and that he is the rewarder of those who believe in him.

units.la: Rursus deducitur, quod dictum est ex ipsa conditione matrimonialis vinculi inter Christum sponsum & Ecclesiam sponsam, sicut Ioan. in Apoc. Ecclesiam sub typo ciuitatis nouae Hierusalem vidit descendentem de coelo, sicut sponsam ornatam viro suo. Nam ad exemplar coelestis Ecclesiae terrena formata est. Quod autem Deus coniunxit, homo non separat: ita vt lege stante non posset aut debeat dari libellus repudii inter sponsum & sponsam coniunctos legitime. Quae autem coniunctio matrimonialis magis legitima quam Christi sit ad Ecclesiam confoederatio? Propterea dicit per Osee: Despensabo mihi in aeternum. Et per alterum Propheram: Si potest oblivisci mater, quod non miseretur filio uteri sui, ego tamen tui non obliviscar. Loquitur de Ecclesia sponsa sua. Nam relinquet homo patrem & matrem, & adhaerebit uxori suae: sic & Christus Ecclesiae: cum matrimonium carnale ideo sumat indissolubilitatem, quia sacramentum magnum est in Christo & Ecclesia: quia est illius matrimonii sacrum signum.
units.tr: Again, what has been said follows from the very condition of the matrimonial bond between Christ the bridegroom and the Church the bride, as John in the Apocalypse saw the Church under the type of the new city Jerusalem descending from heaven, like a bride adorned for her husband. For the earthly Church is formed after the pattern of the heavenly Church. "What God has joined together, man does not separate": so that, the law standing, a bill of divorce cannot, or ought not, be lawfully given between the spouses who are joined. And what matrimonial union is more lawful than the covenant of Christ with the Church? Therefore he says through Hosea: "I will betroth you to me for ever." And through the other prophet: "If a mother can forget that she has no pity on the son of her womb, yet I will not forget you." He speaks of the Church, his bride. For "a man shall leave father and mother and cleave to his wife"; so also Christ to the Church: since carnal marriage takes indissolubility for this reason, that it is a great sacrament in Christ and the Church, because it is the holy sign of that marriage.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO II.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION II.

units.la: AVeritabilis est absolute loquendo sponsus Ecclesiae Christus homo ab ipsa Ecclesia. Neque enim minus hoc est possibile, quam quod Christus desineret esse homo, sicut spontanea voluntate verbum caro factum: aut quod desineret esse nedum ecclesia ipsa, sed omnis generaliter creatura. Porro sicut non est absoluta & inauferibilis habitudo cuiuscunque creaturae ad alteram creaturam: neque tanquam finibilis ad suum finem, neque tanquam effectus ad suam causam. Sic non est hoc modo essentialis vel inauferibilis habitudo Ecclesiae ad Christi humanitatem, quam utique confitemur creaturam. Et ita staret absolute Christum hominem esse & Ecclesiam similiter esse: nec tamen ipsam a Christo ut homo est, vitales influxus suscipere.
units.tr: Speaking absolutely, Christ as man is capable of being taken away as bridegroom of the Church by the Church itself. For this is no less possible than that Christ should cease to be man, just as the Word was made flesh by his free will; or that the Church itself, and indeed every creature in general, should cease to be. Moreover, just as there is no absolute and non-removable relation of any creature to another creature, neither as the finite to its end nor as the effect to its cause, so there is not in this way an essential or non-removable relation of the Church to the humanity of Christ, which we surely confess to be a creature. And so it would stand absolutely that Christ is man and that the Church is likewise; yet the Church would not in that case receive vital influxes from Christ as he is man.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO III.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION III.

units.la: AVeritabilis est sponsus militantis Ecclesiae Christus a quolibet filiorum suorum hic in via: licet non ab omnibus collectiue, quamdiu permanebit militans Ecclesia & lege stante: sicut deinceps loqui proponimus. Perspicua est prima pars huius disiuncti: quoniam nullus est homo viuens, qui non videat mortem: & si hoc non sufficiat: quia dicit Apostolus, quod sive viuimus sive moriamur &c. aut perinde nunquam separamur a Christo. Constat tamen, quod sit separatio per mortem talem, qua definit esse quis viator & de ecclesia militante. Constat praeterea, quod quamdiu manebit hic aliquis in via, sicut potest proficere, ita deficere culpabiliter: & a Christo vera vite, ut palmes aridus & combustioni soli aptus separari, nisi tamen fuerit per confirmationem quodammodo positus extra statum, prout est viator.
units.tr: Christ, the bridegroom of the militant Church, can be taken away by any one of his sons here on the way, although not by all of them collectively, as long as the militant Church shall remain and the law stands, as we propose to speak hereafter. The first part of this disjunction is plain: since there is no living man who does not see death; and if this is not enough, because the Apostle says that "whether we live or die" etc., otherwise we are never separated from Christ. It is certain, however, that there is a separation through such a death, by which someone ceases to be a wayfarer and of the militant Church. It is further certain that, as long as anyone remains here on the way, he can as well make progress as fall away culpably, and be separated from Christ the true vine, like a dry branch fit for burning, unless indeed he has been in some way placed outside the state of a wayfarer through confirmation.

units.la: Altera pars disiuncti sequitur ex prima consideratione & eius deductione: quoniam & omnium collectio nihil aliud est quam ecclesiastici corporis indissolubilis compago: quemadmodum dici solet: totum nihil aliud est quam sua partes simul sumptae: sed haec compago manet in aeternum, lege stante.
units.tr: The other part of the disjunction follows from the first consideration and its deduction: for the collection of all is nothing other than the indissoluble framework of the ecclesiastical body; as is commonly said, "the whole is nothing other than its parts taken together"; but this framework remains for ever, the law standing.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO IV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO IV.

units.la: AVeritabilis non est sponsus ecclesiae Christus ab ipsa, quin influat quotidie tam per modum meriti & impetrationis, ut alii sancti & plus quod ipsi: quam etiam per modum dignatiae condespirationis & vivificationis per Spiritum sanctum suum, fidem, spem & charitatem cum caeteris donibus infundendo gratuitis, virtutis donorum & beatitudinum, & maxime sacramentorum. Itaque sicut non permanet corpus aliquod verum & viuens, nisi habuerit qualitatiuas dispositiones reddentes complexionem harmoniacam & decentem, per manutenentiam formae cum corpore organico secundum exigentiam ipsius ac formae actiuitatis & operationum suarum: cur aliunde venit mors: non aliter sentiendum est de corpore mystico ecclesiae. Ipse enim Spiritus sanctus, qui est Spiritus Christi, est etiam suo modo forma corporis Ecclesiae Christi: praebens ei vitam, vnitatem & motum. Et haec non permaneret cessantibus qualitatiuis dispositionibus praenominatis diffusis per totum corpus ecclesiae, & per membra varia, prout unicuique membro donatum est: & pro tanto opus habet ad aedificationem corporis vniuersi. Tradit hoc Apostolus clarissime scribens ad Ephes. 4. Solliciti, inquit, seruare vnitatem Spiritus in vinculo pacis: vnum corpus & vnus spiritus, sicut vocati estis in vna spe vocationis vestrae. Vnus Dominus, vna fides, unum baptisma, unus Deus & pater omnium. Sequitur: Vnicuique autem nostrum data est gratia secundum mensuram donationis Christi. Sequitur: Et ipse dedit quosdam quidem Apostolos &c. Quinetiam articuli quatuor principales Apostolici Symboli fundant illam consiterationem: Vnus est: Credo in Spiritum sanctum & vivificantem: quid vivificantem, nisi sanctam Ecclesiam? sicut protinus additur & vnam sanctam Ecclesiam Catholicam. Deinde sequitur: Sanctorum (hoc est sacramentorum) communionem. Ac deinde: remissionem peccatorum, intellige consequitur, & vitam aeternam.
units.tr: Christ, the true bridegroom of the Church, does not cease from flowing into her every day, both by way of merit and intercession, so that he gives more to other saints and to her than to himself, and also by way of a kindly co-operation and quickening through his Holy Spirit, pouring in faith, hope and charity together with the other gifts of grace, the virtues, the gifts and the beatitudes, and above all the sacraments. Therefore, just as no true and living body remains unless it has qualitative dispositions that render its complexion harmonious and fitting, through the preservation of its form in the organic body according to the requirement of that body and of the form's activity and operations (for death comes from elsewhere), so we must think no differently of the mystical body of the Church. For the Holy Spirit himself, who is the Spirit of Christ, is in his own way the form of the body of the Church of Christ, giving it life, unity and motion. And this would not remain if the aforesaid qualitative dispositions, spread through the whole body of the Church and through its various members, as each member has been given, ceased; and for this reason the body as a whole needs them for its building up. The Apostle teaches this very clearly, writing to the Ephesians 4: "Be eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace: one body and one Spirit, as you were called in one hope of your calling. One Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all." It follows: "But to each one of us grace has been given according to the measure of Christ's gift." It follows: "And he gave some indeed as apostles," etc. Moreover, the four principal articles of the Apostles' Creed establish that same consideration: "He is one. I believe in the Holy Spirit, who gives life": what is the life-giving, if not the holy Church? As is immediately added, "and one holy Catholic Church." Then follows "the communion of saints" (that is, of the sacraments). And then "the forgiveness of sins," understood as following from this, "and eternal life."

units.la: CONSIDERATIO V.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO V.

units.la: AVeritabilis non est ab Ecclesia militante sponsus Christus homo, quin semper influat in eandem Ecclesiam sponsam suam per membra varia, gradus hierarchicos, officiorum & administrationum & dignitatum & statuum ab ipso constitutorum, dum Ecclesiam fundauit primitus & aedificauit. Si enim permanebit Ecclesia usque ad consummationem seculi, permanebit ut perfecta. Dei enim perfecta sunt opera, non solum in inchoatione, sed magis in conseruatione & consummatione. Sed nemo dubitauerit, quin ablatio unius membri a corpore deformationem grandem & impersectionem inducat. Manebit ergo semper Ecclesia cum suorum integritate & perfectione membrorum. Scribit de his Apostolus 1. ad Corinth. 12. Diuisiones (inquit) gratiarum sunt: idem autem spiritus, & diuisiones ministrationum sunt, idem autem Dominus, & diuisiones operationum sunt idem autem Deus qui operatur omnia in omnibus. Vnicuique autem datur manifesto Spiritus ad utilitatem, alii quidem per spiritum datur sermo sapientiae: alii autem sermo scientiae secundum eundem spiritum, alteri fides in eodem spiritu, alii gratia sanitatum in uno spiritu, alii operatio virtutum, alii prophetia, alii discretio spirituum, alii genera linguarum. linguarum, alii interpretatio sermonum. Hac autem omnia operatur unus atq; idem spiritus, dividens singulis prout vult.
units.tr: Christ, the true man, the bridegroom of the militant Church, does not cease to flow always into that same Church, his bride, through the various members, the hierarchical grades, and the offices, administrations, dignities and states established by him, since he first founded and built the Church. For if the Church remains until the end of the age, it will remain as perfect; for the works of God are perfect not only at their beginning but much more in their preservation and completion. But no one will doubt that the removal of one member from the body brings great deformity and imperfection. The Church will therefore always remain with the integrity and perfection of its members. The Apostle writes about these things in 1 Corinthians 12: "There are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit; and there are varieties of ministries, but the same Lord; and there are varieties of workings, but it is the same God who works all things in all. To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good. To one is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge according to the same Spirit, to another faith in the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by the one Spirit, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another the discernment of spirits, to another various kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues. But all these things are worked by one and the same Spirit, who apportions to each one individually as he wills."

units.la: Concludamus ex his Pauli verbis, quod assiduus erit in Ecclesia vsus ministrationum & gratiarum gratis datarum, quas enumerat: & hoc quantum expediat eius decursui & ædificationi: sicut erunt sapientes, sic Prophetæ, sic discretores spirituum, quibus ex officio hierarchico commisso eis à Christo & Spiritu Sancto conveniunt tales actus: ita vt ab humana quavis auctoritate nequeant impediri, suspendi vel prohiberi: sicut nec status Papalis nec Apostolicus vel pastoralis. Fuerunt enim primitus velut in quodam seminario vivifico positi in Ecclesia per Christum: & postmodum crescente Ecclesia discretio talium magis innotuit: velut si stipes vineæ se in folia & flores & ramos explicuerit.
