units.tr: From these words of Paul we conclude that there will be a constant exercise in the Church of the ministries and the freely given gifts which he enumerates, and this as far as it serves its course and building up: just as there will be wise men, so prophets, so discerners of spirits, to whom, by the hierarchical office committed to them by Christ and the Holy Spirit, such acts belong, so that they cannot be hindered, suspended or prohibited by any human authority whatever; no more than the Papal, the apostolic or the pastoral state can be. For they were first placed in the Church by Christ, as it were in a life-giving seedbed; and afterwards, as the Church grew, the discernment of such people became better known, just as when the stock of a vine unfolds into leaves and flowers and branches.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO VI.

units.la: AVferibilis non est sponsus Ecclesiæ Christus ab Ecclesia taliter, quin semper habeat in se viuificum semen, quo potest p successiones generationis & generationis sese continuare in corpore toto & in membris præsertim officialibus: similiter & in filiis. Traducitur ad hoc illud Christi Matt. 24. Amen dico vobis, quia non præteribit generatio hac donec omnia fiant: loquens de generatione iustorum: quæ contrariatur illi, de qua dictum est: Amen dico vobis quod requiretur à generatione hac omnis sanguis ab Abel iusto. Itaque si Dominus in rerum mutabilium creatione singulis indidit semen rem secundum genus suum ad propagationis suæ generationem: Sicut in lege naturæ quam in lege Moysi status sacerdotalis durabat vel in primogenitis vel per successionem hæreditariam filiorum pro patribus suis: oportuit multo amplius legem gratiæ perfectissimam habere in semetipsa fœcunditatem pro sui continuatione legitima. Ad quod inducit Apostolus ad Romanos 9. textum Prophetæ Euangelici Esa. 1. Nisi Dominus exercituum reliquisset nobis semen, quasi Sodoma fuissemus, & quasi Gomorra similes essemus. Hoc autem quid aliud debet intelligi, quam vis insita spiritualis & ars quædam vivifica in vniuersum corpus Ecclesiæ: per quam hierarchicus ordo suus potest vsq; in finem subsistere.
units.tr: Christ, the bridegroom of the Church, cannot be removed from the Church in such a way that he does not always have within himself a life-giving seed, by which he can continue himself through successive generations in the whole body and especially in its officeholders, and likewise in their sons. To this applies that saying of Christ in Matthew 24: "Truly I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all these things are fulfilled," speaking of the generation of the righteous, which is opposed to that of which it was said: "Truly I say to you, that all the blood shed from the righteous Abel will be required of this generation." Therefore, if the Lord, in the creation of mutable things, implanted in each a seed to propagate its kind according to its genus, just as in the law of nature, and in the law of Moses, the priestly state endured either in the firstborn or by hereditary succession of sons after their fathers, it was fitting that the most perfect law of grace should have in itself much more fruitfulness for its lawful continuation. To this the Apostle, in Romans 9, leads with the text of the evangelical prophet Isaiah 1: "Unless the Lord of hosts had left us a seed, we would have been like Sodom, and we would have been like Gomorrah." But what else ought this to be understood as, than an implanted spiritual power and a certain life-giving art poured into the whole body of the Church, through which its hierarchical order can subsist until the end?

units.la: Et ex his protinus infertur, quod Ecclesia vel concilium eam representans potest instituere vel eligere, vel designare summum pontificem in sacra sede Petri. Potest insuper modum determinare vel limitare eum, vel taliter instituendi siue designandi: ita quod non spectat hoc ad solum pontificem summum: alioquin ipso mortuo vel nolente dare legem eligendi successorem, posset Ecclesia permanere iugiter sine summo pontifice: quod nequit fieri lege stante. Quod si quis dixerit: modos qui nunc obseruantur pro electione summi pontificis determinatos esse per summos pontifices. Placet: Si Ecclesia consensu suo vero vel interpretatiuo approbauit: aut in defectu qualem prædiximus fas haberet immutare. Et ita fas vt in contrarium nullus posset cuiuscunque pontificis auctoritas legem dare.
units.tr: And from these things it is immediately inferred that the Church, or a council representing it, can institute, elect or designate the supreme pontiff in the holy see of Peter. It can moreover determine or limit the manner of such institution or designation, so that this does not belong to the supreme pontiff alone; otherwise, if he died or were unwilling to give a law for choosing a successor, the Church could remain continually without a supreme pontiff, which cannot happen while the law stands. But if someone says that the methods now observed for the election of the supreme pontiff were determined by the supreme pontiffs, I grant it: if the Church approved them by its true or implied consent, or, in default, as we have said before, it would be lawful for it to change them. And so it would be lawful, since no authority of any pontiff whatever could give a law to the contrary.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO VII.

units.la: AVferibilis non est sponsus Ecclesiæ Christus ab ecclesia sponsa sua & filiis eius: sic quod remaneat ecclesia in sola muliere: imo nec in solis mulieribus omnibus, imo nec in laicis solum legestante & non facta diuinitus noua institutione. Da oppositum: Ecclesia deficere posset in suis gradibus & officiis hierarchicis: in suis etiam sacramentis vsq; in finem. Patet hoc præsupponendo, quod sacerdos à non sacerdote, & Episcopus à non Episcopo nequit institui: imo nec à tota multitudine laicorum aut mulierum simul congregata, si per casum mortui essent omnes sacerdotes. Additum est: non facta diuinitus institutione noua: quia Spiritu sancto dictante & operante noua præstari posset auctoritas, qualis nondum collata est: quemadmodum prius quam Deus instituisset sacerdotium novum, supremum & alios inferiores gradus hierarchicos in ecclesia non dubium quin hoc potuerit. Porro nulla communitas vel vniuersitas hominum mortalium simul congregata talem aliquem gradum nullo modo instituere potuisset cum potestate, qualis in quolibet reperitur, quæ supra naturam existens ipsam sibi præsupponit & substernit quodammodo, sicut forma materiam. Nec opinor quod aliquis Doctor Theologorum senserit in hoc contraire: quamuis verba quædam Epistolæ cuiusdam tractatus De concilio generali videri possunt aliqualiter hoc sonare, nisi benigno interprete foveantur.
units.tr: Christ, the bridegroom of the Church, cannot be taken away from his bride the Church and her children, so that the Church would remain in a single woman. Nor could it remain even in all women together, nor among laymen alone, with the law standing and without any new institution made by God. The opposite view holds that the Church could fail in its grades and hierarchical offices, and even in its sacraments, until the end of the world. This is shown by presupposing that a priest cannot be instituted by a non-priest, nor a bishop by a non-bishop, nor even by the whole multitude of laymen or women gathered together, if by some chance all the priests had died. The words without a new institution made by God are added because, with the Holy Spirit dictating and working, a new authority could be conferred that has not yet been bestowed, just as there is no doubt that before God instituted the new priesthood, God could have established the supreme and the other lower hierarchical grades in the Church. Moreover, no community or assembly of mortal men gathered together could in any way institute such a grade with the power that is found in any such grade, which, existing above nature, presupposes itself and in a sense underlies the matter, as form does. Nor do I think any doctor of theology has thought otherwise on this point, although certain words in a letter from a tract On a General Council may seem to sound somewhat like this, unless they are favoured by a kind interpreter.

units.la: Deducitur proinde quod nec Hieronymus, nec aliquis aliorum dicens Ecclesiam vel Apostolos sibi constituisse Petrum, vt supremus esset & princeps inter eos ad schisma tollendum: non intelligunt hoc nisi quod Ecclesia vel Apostoli declaraverunt ita esse constitutum à Christo: & hoc tenendum fidelibus tradiderunt. Et ita saluatur illa, quæ videtur super hac re inter Hieronymum & cæteros varietas.
units.tr: It follows, therefore, that neither Jerome, nor any of the others who say that the Church or the Apostles appointed Peter to be supreme and prince among them in order to end schism, understand this except in the sense that the Church or the Apostles declared that it had been so established by Christ, and handed it down to the faithful to be held. And so that apparent variance between Jerome and the others on this matter is resolved.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VIII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO VIII.

units.la: AVferibilis est aut mutabilis lege stante quælibet politia ciuilis, monarchica seu regalis, vt fiat Aristocratica: & non sic de Ecclesia, quæ in vno monarcha supremo per vniuersum fundata est à Christo.
units.tr: Any civil polity, whether monarchical or royal, can be taken away or changed into an aristocracy while the law stands. It is not so with the Church, which was founded by Christ throughout the whole world in one supreme monarch.

units.la: Posset deduci consideratio tam à priori quam à posteriori, deducendo variationes, quæ fuerunt in aliis politiis: quia nullam aliam politiam instituit Christus immutabiliter monarchicam, & quodam modo regalem, nisi Ecclesiam. Et oppositum sentientes de Ecclesia: quod scilicet fas est esse plures Papas, aut quod quilibet episcopus est in sua dioecesi Papa, vel pastor supremus æqualis Papæ Romano, errant in fide & unitate ecclesiæ contra articulum illum: & in unam sanctam &c. & si pertinaces maneant, iudicandi sunt hæretici, sicut Martinus de Padua & quidam aliorum.
units.tr: The consideration could be drawn both a priori and a posteriori, by tracing the changes that have occurred in other polities. For Christ instituted no other polity that is immutably monarchical and, in a certain manner, royal, except the Church. Those who think otherwise about the Church, namely that there may be several Popes, or that every bishop is a Pope in his own diocese, or a supreme pastor equal to the Roman Pope, err in faith and in the unity of the Church against that article, And in one holy etc. If they remain obstinate, they are to be judged heretics, as were Martin of Padua and some others.

units.la: Consonat ratio: quia sicut ad unam fidem & ad eadem sacramenta obligantur omnes viatores: sic oportet ut non esset schisma reductionem finalem fieri ad unum supremum. Secus ubi communitas regitur legibus solis naturalibus & traditionibus humanis: quæ pro varietate temporum & locorum laudabilius & utilius variantur, quam ut uno tenore ligent omnes: quemadmodum tradit Aristot. exemplificans de regula Lesbiæ.
units.tr: Reason agrees: just as all wayfarers are bound to one faith and to the same sacraments, so it is fitting that there should be no schism in the final reduction to one supreme head. It is otherwise where a community is governed by natural laws alone and by human traditions, which, according to the variety of times and places, are more commendably and usefully varied than bound by one uniform rule for all, as Aristotle teaches, giving the example of the Lesbian rule.

units.la: Quocirca dicamus ex incidenti consequenter, quod nec summus pontifex, nec aliquis alius debet conari, ut canones positi vel aliæ traditiones humanæ, observentur ubique per totam Ecclesiam, & per omnes invariabiliter nationes. Oppositum satagere dedit forte occasionem Græcis discedendi a Latinis. Dat præterea quotidie materiam multam litium scrupulorum graviun, dum æquali tenore quæritur observari lex humana: sive sit illa canonica, secularis vel civilis: quemadmodum custodiri divinam absque ulla variatione necesse est. Inde venit illa Christi quæstio Matth. 15. Irritum fecistis mandatum Dei propter traditiones vestras.
units.tr: Hence we may say, incidentally and by consequence, that neither the supreme pontiff nor anyone else ought to strive to have the canons or other human traditions observed everywhere throughout the Church and invariably by all nations. Striving for the opposite has perhaps given the Greeks occasion to separate from the Latins. Moreover, it daily provides much material for serious disputes and scruples, while human law is sought to be observed with an equal rigour, whether it be canonical, secular or civil, whereas the divine law must necessarily be kept without any variation. Hence comes that question of Christ in Matthew 15: You have made the commandment of God void because of your traditions.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XI.

units.la: Utilis est vicarius sponsus ecclesiæ per voluntariam eius cessionem aut renunciationem a Papatu. Fuerat enim olim dubitatio post renunciationem Cælestini: nunquid talis renunciatio iure subsisteret? Tum propter votum quo se Papa obligat ad ecclesiam. Tum propter desponsationem & matrimonium quoddam spirituale inter Papam & ecclesiam. Tum præterea quia Papa diuino iure statutus est in hoc gradu: & si quæ sunt aliæ rationes. Occasione cuius dubitationis facta est decretalis determinans affirmatiuam quod hoc licet. Et ita licet quod ex hac humili renunciatione cum cæteris patribus Cælestinus annumeratus est catalogo beatorum.
units.tr: The vicar, the bridegroom of the Church, is set aside usefully by her voluntary yielding or renunciation of the Papacy. For after the renunciation of Celestine there was once a doubt whether such a renunciation would stand in law: first, because of the vow by which the Pope binds himself to the Church; second, because of a betrothal and a certain spiritual marriage between the Pope and the Church; third, because the Pope is established by divine law in this rank; and whatever other reasons there may be. On the occasion of this doubt a decretal was issued determining in the affirmative that this is lawful. And so, because of this humble renunciation, Celestine was, along with other fathers, counted in the catalogue of the blessed.

units.la: Sunt autem casus aliqui etiam per Iuristas expressi, quando licitum est prælato, imo quandoque debitum cedere statui suo. Vnus est grande scandalum subditorum, quod non expectatur alio modo probabiliter terminandum quam per cessionem. Alius casus est, dum occupatio seu retentio prælaturæ patenter vergit in detrimentum salutis propriæ: Nam quid prodest homini, si universum mundum lucretur, anima vero sua detrimentum patiatur? aut quam dabit homo pro anima sua commutationem? Alius casus est, ubi manifeste talis retentio impediret maius bonum vel in prælato vel in subditis.
units.tr: There are, moreover, some cases also expressed by the jurists in which it is lawful, and sometimes even obligatory, for a prelate to yield his office. One is when there is a great scandal among the subjects, which cannot reasonably be expected to be ended in any other way than by resignation. Another case is when the holding or retention of the prelacy clearly tends to the detriment of one's own salvation: For what does it profit a man if he gain the whole world and suffer the loss of his soul? Or what will a man give in exchange for his soul? Another case is when such retention would plainly hinder a greater good, either in the prelate or in the subjects.

units.la: Multiplices essent casus in particulari secundum illud triplex genus. Sed breuitati nostræ satis sint ista pro nunc. Per quæ dissoluitur prima ratio, quæ fiebat de voto: quod non obligat, dum vergit in detrimentum salutis, vel exitum deteriorem. Alteram rationem soluit dissimilitudo, quæ est inter matrimonium carnale & spirituale, licet conueniant in multis. Dissimilitudo est quantum ad hoc, quod in spirituali non est sacramentum: ex quo consurgat indissolubilis nexus ex institutione divina. Quemadmodum de carnali est expressa lex: Quod Deus coniunxit, homo non separet: & sacramentum hoc magnum est. Dico autem in Christo & Ecclesia: inquit Apostolus. Ac perinde soluitur ratio tertia: quia proprie solus Christus est sponsus Ecclesiæ. Alii sunt tantummodo vicarii, quos per humanam designationem vel electionem voluit institui: quamuis officium sit divinum, & sola auctoritate divina primitus ordinatum.
units.tr: The cases in particular would be many, according to that threefold kind. But for our brevity these will suffice for now. By these the first reason is dissolved, which was raised concerning the vow: that it does not bind when it tends to the detriment of salvation or to a worse outcome. The dissimilarity between carnal and spiritual marriage, though they agree in many respects, dissolves the second reason: the dissimilarity is that in the spiritual marriage there is no sacrament, from which an indissoluble bond arises by divine institution. Concerning carnal marriage there is an express law: What God has joined together, let not man put asunder; and this is a great sacrament. But I speak concerning Christ and the Church, says the Apostle. In the same way the third reason is dissolved, because properly Christ alone is the bridegroom of the Church. Others are only vicars, whom he willed to be instituted by human designation or election, although the office is divine and was originally ordained by divine authority alone.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO X.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION X.

units.la: Utilis est in casibus dubiis vicarius sponsus Ecclesiæ ab ipsa Ecclesia: & hoc per eam, vel per concilium generale repræsentans eam: vel per aliquos ad hoc per eam institutos: sive consentiat ipse vicarius, vel non consentiat suæ cessioni.
units.tr: In doubtful cases a vicar of the Bridegroom of the Church is useful, chosen by the Church herself: either by her directly, or through a general council representing her, or through certain persons appointed by her for this purpose; and this holds whether the vicar himself consents to his resignation or does not.

units.la: Sumitur inprimis argumentum pro hac consideratione ex veritate præcedentis. Nam si vicarius sponsus potest resignare sponte ipsi ecclesiæ dando ei libellum repudii. Cum sponsus & sponsa non debeant quoad hoc impari iure censeri: potetit similiter repudiare sponsum talem ipsa Ecclesia sponsa, dum par ratio vel potior adducitur pro ipsa contra sponsum: vel quia prostituere quærit eam quantum in se est, vel tyrannide sua trahat, laniando eam, vel placitando bona sua dissipando, vel quia abuti conatur ea in perniciem filiorum. Nullum quippe statum, nullum gradum dignitatis, nullum ministrationis genus dedit Deus nisi in ædificationem suam & utilitatem communem. Patet ad Eph. 4. & ad Cor. 6. Dedit vtiq; ad pacem eius, cuius finem posuit pacem secundum prius. Et hanc operatur dilectio: propter quod finis legis ab Apostolo ponitur dilectio: in qua etiam fundauit Christus officium pastorale, Si diligis me, (inquit Christus Petro) pasce oues meas, Ioan. vlt. Sed quis non videat casus multos esse possibiles: quorum aliqui nunc tacti sunt, in quibus Ecclesia non ædificaretur, sed destrueretur: non uniretur, sed dissiparetur: non pasceretur, sed depasceretur: si non cederet voluntarius, vel ejiceretur inuitus hic, qui in vicarium sponsum Ecclesiæ rite & canonice fuerat ordinatus. Nec sit cuiquam illud admirationi, quod dicimus quasi contantiantes illi iussioni: Nolite tangere Christos meos: quomodo etiam vnus sugulari personæ fas esset in casu violentia attentata per Papam verum contra castitatem suam vel vitam repellere, cum appositione inculpatæ tutelæ: & ita licite stabit quod tangat Papam violenter, vel in mare deiiciat. Cur similiter in casu non liceat idem toti Ecclesiæ pro defensione sua & violentia attentata cauta repressione?
units.tr: The first argument for this consideration is drawn from the truth of the preceding one. For if a vicar of the Bridegroom can resign of his own accord, giving the Church herself a bill of divorce, then, since the Bridegroom and the Bride ought not to be judged under unequal law in this matter, the Church as Bride could likewise repudiate such a Bridegroom, since an equal or even stronger reason is brought forward on her side against the Bridegroom: either because he seeks, as far as he can, to make her a harlot, or because he tears her apart by his tyranny, or because he squanders her goods to satisfy his own pleasures, or because he tries to misuse her to the ruin of her children. For God has given no state, no rank of dignity, no kind of ministry, except for the building up of his Church and the common good. This is plain from Eph. 4. and 1 Cor. 6. God gave them, in any case, for her peace, and the end he set for them was peace in the first place; and love produces this peace, which is why the Apostle names love as the end of the law. On this love Christ also founded the pastoral office: If you love me, Christ said to Peter, feed my sheep, John last chapter. But who does not see that there are many possible cases in which the Church would not be built up but destroyed, not united but scattered, not fed but devoured, if this man, who had been duly and canonically ordained as the vicar of the Bridegroom of the Church, did not yield willingly or were not cast out against his will? Nor should anyone be surprised that we say this as though resisting that command: Touch not my anointed. Just as a single private person may, in a case where violence is attempted by the Pope against his chastity or his life, lawfully repel it, with the addition of blameless defence, so it will be lawful for him to lay hands on the Pope violently or to throw him into the sea. Why, then, in a similar case, should it not be lawful for the whole Church to employ, in defence of herself against violence attempted upon her, a careful restraint?

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION XI.

units.la: AVferibilis est in casu vicarius Ecclesiæ per concilium generale, eo non consentiente, vel inuito celebratum.
units.tr: In a case of necessity, the vicar of the Church may be removed by a general council held without his consent or even against his will.

units.la: Fateamur prius, quod regulariter concilium generale non est celebrandum de iure etiam diuino non vocante vel approbante Papa, si est vnicus: nec aduersus eum allegatio legitima. Sed regulæ generales bene suscipiunt exceptiones, sicut in Grammaticalibus, ita & in moralibus: præsertim vbi casus particulares incidunt modis variabilibus infinitis: ad quas exceptiones ordinata est lex superior interpres aliarum, quam Aristot. vocat ἐπιεικείαν, 5. Ethicorum. Et alia diuinior, quam γνώμη appellat in 6. Ethicorum. Hæc autem lex semper habet locum in interpretatione legum aliarum particularium, vbi deficere cernitur ratio & finis institutionis ipsarum. Finis autem legum omnium nedum humanarum, sed diuinarum est dilectio, quæ vnitatem operatur. Sit ergo casus, vbi legis alicuius obseruatio dissiparet vnitatem & obesset publicæ saluti. Quis ratione vtens, diceret eam tenere oportere? Nimirum nec sibiipsi quisquam vellet hoc fieri: quanto minus tota communitas rationabiliter hoc fugiet.
units.tr: Let us first concede that, as a rule, a general council is not to be convened by divine law without the summons or approval of the Pope, if he is the only one. Nor is there any lawful appeal against him. But general rules admit exceptions, as in grammar, so also in morals, especially where particular cases arise in endlessly varying ways. For these exceptions there is a higher law, the interpreter of the others, which Aristotle calls equity [ἐπιεικείαν] in the fifth book of the Ethics, and another, more divine, which he calls judgement [γνώμη] in the sixth book of the Ethics. This law always applies in interpreting other particular laws, when the reason and purpose of their institution are seen to fail. The purpose of all laws, not only human but divine, is love, which produces unity. Suppose, then, a case where observance of some law would break up the unity and harm the public welfare. Who, using reason, would say that it ought to be kept? Certainly no one would wish this done to himself, and much less would the whole community reasonably shun it.

units.la: Quod si quis interrogaret, qua auctoritate fulcietur, vel vtetur huiusmodi concilium ἀκέφαλον, vt videtur, sine Papa? Respondendum quod auctoritate Christi capitis sui & indefectibilis sposi: auctoritate præterea legum suarum tam diuinæ quam naturalis: quæ hanc licentiam vel necessitati vel manifestę charitati vel religiosæ pietati concedunt. Pro quo facit textus Marc. 2. de excusatione discipulorum vellentium spicas in sabbato per legem necessitatis confirmatam: exemplo Dauid, qui comedit panes propositionis.
units.tr: If anyone should ask by what authority such a council, headless [ἀκέφαλον] as it seems, without the Pope, would be supported and would act, the answer is: by the authority of Christ, its head and indefectible spouse, and also by the authority of his laws, both divine and natural, which grant this liberty either to necessity, or to manifest charity, or to religious piety. In support of this stands the text of Mark 2 concerning the excuse of the disciples who wished to pluck ears of corn on the sabbath, a case confirmed by the law of necessity, with the example of David, who ate the showbread.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION XII.

units.la: AVferibilis est in casu vicarius sponsus Ecclesiæ per Ecclesiam vel generale concilium, nedum conciliatiue, aut dicatiue vel denunciatiue, sed auctoritatiue iudicialiter atq; iuridice.
units.tr: In this case the Church, or a general council, may remove the vicar and bridegroom of the Church, not merely by conciliar action, declaration or denunciation, but authoritatively, judicially and juridically.

units.la: Præsupponamus, quod iurisdictio idem est quod iuris dictio seu potestas: vel iurisdictio est facultas propinqua dicendi ius. Et solet restringi ad coactiuam iurisdictionem, quæ fertur vel dicitur in alterum etiam inuitum. Sequitur protinus ex hac descriptione considerationis veritas, quomodo Ecclesia seu concilium habet in casu facultatem propinquam vel auctoritatem seu potestatem dicendi ius; etiam in alterum, qui in Papam fuit rite susceptus & electus. Nolumus tamen impugnare, quin summus pontifex habeat potestatem regitiuam & auctoritatiuam respectu omnium hominum, quantum Christus voluit & cognouit expedien sibi dare pro exercendo eam. Non pio se tantummodo, sed magis ad vtilitatem Ecclesiæ, qualem auctoritatem Ecclesiæ non habet totum Ecclesiæ residuum, nisi vnitiue quodam modo vel electiue. Et ex ista diuisione verum est, quod claues datæ sunt nedum vni, sed vnitati. Ex hoc tamen non habetur, quod Ecclesia tota vel concilium absente Papa, præsertim suo demerito non possit auctoritatiuam iurisdictionem exercere: sicut lex quædam diuina & indeuiabilis ad reducendum ipsum vel corrigendum vel compescendum, ne noceat ipse, nedum Ecclesiæ, sed sibimet tanquam freneticus: vel vt pessima malarum passionum ebrietate seductus. Sicut enim tradit Aristotel. 5. Polit. quod ad communitatem totam spectat principis vel correctio vel totalis destitutio, si inemedabilis perseueret. Et hæc potestas inauferibilis vel inabdicabilis est à communitate libera, quæ de rebus suis facere potest ad libitum: nec per appropriationem vel aliquam legem potest suspendi: quanto magis hoc habebit Ecclesia.
units.tr: Let us presuppose that jurisdiction is the same as the declaring of law (iuris dictio), or power; or that jurisdiction is a near faculty of declaring law. It is usually restricted to coercive jurisdiction, which is exercised over another even against his will. From this description of the consideration there follows at once the truth that the Church or a council has, in this case, a near faculty or authority or power of declaring law, even over the one who was duly received and elected as Pope. We do not wish, however, to deny that the supreme pontiff has ruling and authoritative power over all men, as far as Christ willed it and knew it fitting to give him for its exercise. This is for the benefit of the Church and not for his own sake alone. The rest of the Church does not have such authority, except in some unitive or electoral manner. From this distinction it is true that the keys were given not to one person only, but to unity. It does not follow from this, however, that the whole Church or a council, in the Pope's absence, cannot exercise authoritative jurisdiction, especially when the fault is his own. There is a certain divine and unavoidable law for calling him back, correcting him or restraining him, lest he harm not only the Church but himself, like a madman, or like one led astray by the drunkenness of wicked passions. For Aristotle teaches in the fifth book of the Politics that the correction of a ruler, or his total deposition if he persists incorrigibly, belongs to the whole community. This power cannot be taken away or renounced by a free community, which may do with its own affairs as it pleases, nor can it be suspended by any appropriation or law. How much more, then, will the Church have it?

units.la: Iudaizabat olim Petrus per dissimulationem, Paulus ei resistit in faciem, ad Galat. 2. Introducebat Petrus rem nouam in Ecclesia Dei ad Centurionem gentilem intrauit, Actuum 10. subortum est murmur in Ecclesia: ita vt compulsus sit Petrus insequi, quam tradidit scriptis: vt scilicet paratus esset coram tota Ecclesia rationem reddere de eâ, quæ in ipso erat fide & spe: alioquin non sibi credidisset Ecclesia. Quanto fortius & rationabilibus possunt duo contendentes diffamati apud bonos & graues de schismate, de periurio, de hæresis suspitione compelli, rationem reddere, si se cognouerint innocentes. Sic Simachus, sic beatus Marcellus, sic ipse Gregorius, sic alii plures iudicium subiere concilii nequaquam ex humili condescensione, sicut fingunt aliqui, sed ex debito & obligatione: quorum multos, quia concilium non reperit conuictos de crimine, reliquit causam eorum examine iudicis Dei terminandam.
units.tr: Peter once Judaized through dissimulation, and Paul resisted him to his face (Gal. 2). When Peter introduced something new into the Church of God by entering the house of a gentile centurion (Acts 10), a murmur arose in the Church, so that Peter was compelled to render an account of what he had written, namely that he should be ready to give account before the whole Church of the faith and hope that was in him; otherwise the Church would not have trusted him. How much more strongly and reasonably may two contending men, defamed among good and grave people with schism, perjury or suspicion of heresy, be compelled to give an account, if they know themselves to be innocent. Thus Symmachus, thus blessed Marcellus, thus Gregory himself and many others submitted to the judgment of a council. They did so not from humble condescension, as some pretend, but from duty and obligation. Many of them, because the council did not find them convicted of crime, left their cause to be decided by the examination of the judge of God.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XIII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XIII.

units.la: AVferibilis non est vicarius sponsus Ecclesiæ per Ecclesiam aut concilium generale quo ad ea quæ sunt ordinis sacri cuiuscunque, quin semper remaneat vel sacerdos vel Episcopus, si in talem fuerit aliquando consecratus. Similiter etiam de Papatu si diceret ordinem à sacerdotio vel Episcopatu distinctum.
units.tr: The vicar of the Bridegroom of the Church cannot be removed by the Church or by a general council, as far as those things belonging to sacred orders are concerned, so that he would not always remain either a priest or a bishop, if he had at some time been consecrated as one. The same holds for the papacy, if someone were to say that it is an order distinct from the priesthood or the episcopate.

units.la: Dudum tempore beati Cypriani martyrisin Affrica, dum sanctus Cornelius Papatum Romæ gerebat, fuit error multorum etiam magnorum, quod schismatici & hæretici, excommunicati & simoniaci deiiciebantur ab omni gradu & dignitate & ordine: ita quod non remanebant sacerdotes, nec Episcopi retinebant Episcopalem gradum, nec Diaconi diaconatum: & ita de similibus. Imo vsque ad hoc deuenturn est, vt diceretur ab eis, quod tales nullo modo valebant baptizare, sed baptizabantur hi quos baptizauerunt. Similiter nec consecrabant, ne ordinabant, quin totum postea dicerent iterandum. Introducebant pro seipsis multos passus scripturatu, ut illud: Maledicam benedictionibus vestris &c. Affirmabant denique quod tales Spiritum sanctum dare non poterant, quem utique non habebant. Notata sunt haec in Decreto causa prima: & in quarto Sententiarum dist. 25. & dist. 14. ubi Magister non tenetur: licet loquatur magis recitative quam determinative.
units.tr: Long ago, in the time of the blessed martyr Cyprian in Africa, while Saint Cornelius held the papacy at Rome, many, even great men, held the error that schismatics, heretics, the excommunicated and the simoniacal were deprived of every grade, dignity and order, so that they were no longer priests, bishops did not keep the episcopal rank, deacons did not keep the diaconate, and so on for similar cases. Indeed it went so far that they said such men could not baptize at all, and that those whom they had baptized were baptized again. Likewise they did not consecrate or ordain, and they said that everything they had done must afterwards be done again. They adduced many passages of Scripture for their own purposes, such as I will curse your blessings, etc. Finally they affirmed that such men could not give the Holy Spirit, which of course they did not have. These matters are noted in the Decretum, cause 1, and in the fourth book of the Sentences, distinction 25 and distinction 14, where the Master is not committed, although he speaks rather by way of report than by way of determination.

units.la: Illustrissimus vero Doctor Augustinus post Cyprianum materiam hanc declaravit conformiter ad concilia generalia ante eum & post celebrata. Et hunc insecuti sunt Doctores Theologi dicentes, quod ea quae sunt ordinis stabilia sunt & indelebilia: propterea dicunt hi imprimi characterem, quem appellant indelebilem, & non iterabilem.
units.tr: But the most illustrious Doctor Augustine, after Cyprian, clarified this matter in agreement with the general councils held before and after him. And the theologians who followed him have said that those things which belong to orders are stable and indelible. For this reason they say that a character is imprinted, which they call indelible and not repeatable.

units.la: Attamen pro concordantia diversarum sententiarum in hac parte proficit duplex distinctio: Episcopus itaque haereticus & degradatus ab ecclesia aut intendit dare & facere conformiter ad intentionem ecclesiae vel baptizat vel consecrat vel ordinat vel confirmat: materiam insuper & formam debitas observat. Aut deficit in aliquo istorum: Intentione, scil. corrupta & erronea vel in materia vel in forma. Secundum hanc distinctionem procedunt multae auctoritates sanctorum: quorum aliqui dicentes, quod sacerdotes haeretici nihil agant: intelligunt de his qui secundo modo deficiunt, quales erant plurimi haereticorum: ut Ariani & errantes in ipsa substantia sacramentorum. Alii dicentes oppositum, sicut Augustinus & ecclesia de prioribus intelligunt.
units.tr: Nevertheless, a twofold distinction helps to reconcile the different opinions on this point. A heretical bishop, deposed from the Church, either intends to give or do what agrees with the intention of the Church, when he baptizes, consecrates, ordains or confirms, and moreover observes the proper matter and form; or he fails in one of these: his intention is corrupt and erroneous, either as to the matter or as to the form. According to this distinction, many authorities of the saints proceed. Some of them, saying that heretical priests do nothing, understand this of those who fail in the second way, which was the case with very many heretics, such as the Arians and those who erred about the very substance of the sacraments. Others, saying the opposite, as Augustine and the Church do, understand it of the former.

units.la: Rursus alia est distinctio de efficacia sacramentorum collatorum ab indignis sacerdotibus & haereticis. Nam quod talia sunt efficacia potest intelligi vel quoad utilitatem, vel quoad veritatem. Si primo modo illa dicuntur esse nulla: quia neque prosunt facientibus neque scienter recipientibus, sed obsunt potius. Si secundo modo, sic consecrationes haereticorum sacerdotum efficaciam habere & veritatem fatendum est.
units.tr: Again there is another distinction concerning the efficacy of sacraments conferred by unworthy priests and heretics. For that such sacraments are effective may be understood either as to their usefulness or as to their truth. If they are called null in the first sense, that is because they neither profit those who administer them nor those who receive them knowingly, but rather harm them. If they are taken in the second sense, then it must be admitted that the consecrations of heretical priests have efficacy and truth.

units.la: Tandem ex hac consideratione cum suis probationibus, quae latiori deductione ponuntur ab auctoritatibus: sequitur quod durante praesenti schismate non oportet dubitare, quin utrobique fuerint consecrati: & sint veri episcopi, & sacerdotes per mutuam successionem usque in praesens.
units.tr: Finally, from this consideration, together with its proofs, which the authorities set out at greater length, it follows that, while the present schism lasts, there is no need to doubt that consecrations were performed on both sides, and that there are true bishops and priests, by a mutual succession, down to the present day.

units.la: Necesse difficultas in collatione sacramentorum, nisi de sacramento poenitentiae, in quo iurisdictio quaedam requiritur, quam non habent haeretici & schismatici vel excommunicati sacerdotes. Sed haec difficultas redundat similiter in illos, qui ante schisma fuerunt ordinati: & secundum aestimationem illorum qui iudicarent hanc vel illam partem esse schismaticam: & ex consequenti non habere sacerdotes nisi excommunicatos & suspensos. Et ita unum est & forte scandalosum gloriari, quod Presbyterales vel Episcopales ordinatio suspecta fuerit ante schisma praesens, potius quam hoc tempore. Si per hoc velint huiusmodi gloriantes vocare se veros esse sacerdotes & episcopos, quam posteriores. Si velint praeterea dicere, sicut aliqui dixerunt & scripserunt temporibus istis: quod veradditionally sacramenta & veri sacerdotes & veri episcopi & verum corpus Christi & verus baptismus, cum similibus non sint in hac parte obedientiae vel in illa.
units.tr: The difficulty concerns the conferring of sacraments only in the case of the sacrament of penance, in which a certain jurisdiction is required, which heretical, schismatic or excommunicated priests do not have. But this difficulty similarly falls on those who were ordained before the schism, and, by the judgement of those who would say that this or that side is schismatic, it follows that there are no priests except excommunicated and suspended ones. Therefore it is both a vain and perhaps a scandalous boast that the presbyteral or episcopal ordination was suspect before the present schism rather than in this time, if such boasters mean by this to call themselves true priests and bishops rather than those who came later. Still more, if they wish to say, as some have said and written in these times, that there are true sacraments, true priests, true bishops, a true body of Christ and true baptism, these things are not, in this respect, a matter of obedience or disobedience.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XIV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XIV.

units.la: A Verferibilis est vicarius sponsus ecclesiae per ipsam ecclesiam aut generale concilium quo ad executionem licitam eorum omnium, quae potestatem ordinis respiciunt; id est, quod non licite agit. Data quippe est Papalis potestas ipsi Ecclesiae: & sua est, sicut est ipsius Papae: quamuis alio & alio modo. Sua est inquam & Papae ad aedificationem Ecclesiae, non ad destructionem. Potest ergo usus talis potestatis tolli vel suspendi per ecclesiam ab eo, qui vellet uti manifeste in perditionem Ecclesiae aut membrorum suorum tali dignitate. Unde & si potestas ordinis sit immediate a Deo, sit etiam indelebilis: tamen usus ipsius multum dependet ab Ecclesia & a rectoribus suis, qui vices eius exequuntur.
units.tr: The vicar of the Bridegroom of the Church can be removed by the Church itself or by a general council as far as the lawful exercise of all those powers that concern the power of orders is concerned; that is, when he acts unlawfully. For the papal power has indeed been given to the Church itself, and it belongs to the Church just as it belongs to the Pope, although in different ways. It belongs, I say, to the Church and to the Pope for the building up of the Church, not for its destruction. The use of such power can therefore be taken away or suspended by the Church from one who would clearly wish to use such a dignity to the ruin of the Church or of its members. Hence, even if the power of orders comes immediately from God and is indelible, the use of it nonetheless depends greatly on the Church and on its rulers, who carry out its office.

units.la: Et hic fundabilis est possibilitas subtractionis vel suspensionis obedientiae ab aliquo in Papam rite electo. Nam quod obedientia tali praestetur, est praeceptum affirmativum, quod non obligat pro semper nec in perniciem ecclesiae. Si viderit ergo Ecclesia quod praestare nunc obedientiam Papae in administratione ordinum, sacramentorum & similium, fieret ecclesiae perniciosum; & Papae instrumentum malitiae: cur non suspendere potest huiusmodi obedientiam quousque; nullum in obediendo cadat periculum? Haec autem subtractio obedientiae magis adhuc fundabilis est in his, quae sunt temporalis administrationis.
units.tr: And here is the ground for the possibility of withdrawing or suspending obedience from someone who has been duly elected Pope. For the rendering of such obedience is an affirmative precept, which does not bind at all times, nor to the ruin of the Church. If, then, the Church sees that to render obedience to the Pope now, in the administration of orders, sacraments and similar matters, would be harmful to the Church and an instrument of the Pope's malice, why should it not be able to suspend such obedience until no danger arises from obeying? Moreover, this withdrawal of obedience is still more justifiable in matters of temporal administration.

units.la: Sed utrum haec obedientiae subtractio vel suspensio valeat per alium quam ecclesiam vel generale concilium? Forte videretur respondendum negative: praesertim si fiat sermo de subtractione generali & auctoritatiua, & quae ligat omnes de ecclesia in hoc statu.
units.tr: But might this withdrawal or suspension of obedience be valid when carried out by someone other than the Church or a general council? It might seem that the answer should be negative, especially if we are speaking of a general and authoritative withdrawal, one that binds all in the Church in this state.

units.la: Secus est de subtractione particulari quoad hos vel illos, quae non fertur, auctoritative, sed vel doctrinaliter & insinuative, vel necessitatis quadam inductione.
units.tr: It is otherwise with a particular withdrawal as regards these or those persons, which is not issued authoritatively, but either by way of doctrine and hint, or by a kind of inducement arising from necessity.

units.la: Iubebit (exempli gratia) summus pontifex coram Theologis expertis, quod fideles credant Spiritum sanctum non procedere a patre & filio: dicimus quod Theologorum erit doctrinaliter resistere & dicere quod sibi non obediatur.
units.tr: Suppose (for example) that the supreme pontiff, before expert theologians, orders the faithful to believe that the Holy Spirit does not proceed from the Father and the Son. We say that it will be the task of the theologians to resist by teaching, and to say that he is not to be obeyed.

units.la: Iubebit alter summus pontifex, quod vastetur regnum Franciae igne & gladio: dicimus quod regis erit resistere & iubere, quod ei non obediatur, sed resistatur: hoc enim fas est agere cuicunque, im quem vim illicitam vellet inferre etiam verus Papa.
units.tr: Suppose another supreme pontiff orders the kingdom of France to be laid waste with fire and sword. We say that it will be the task of the king to resist, and to order that he is not to be obeyed but resisted. For this is lawful for anyone at all against whom a true Pope himself might wish to inflict unlawful force.

units.la: Nota Non est pax iubebit ipse idem, quod vnio ad pacem ecclesiæ non quæratur viis conuenientibus & congruis, aut etiam per eum iuratis, aut quod ecclesia nequaquam congregetur ne forte ipsum eiiciat. Dicimus quod omnium catholicorum erit resistere & non obedire.
units.tr: Note: the same man commands that union for the peace of the Church is not to be sought by suitable and fitting means, or even by means sworn by him, or that the Church is by no means to be gathered, lest perhaps he cast it out. We say it will be the duty of all Catholics to resist and not to obey.

units.la: Quod si sit aliquis qui totam præsidentiam suam & papalem dignitatem conuertere velit in instrumentum nequitiæ & destructionis alicuius partis ecclesiæ in temporalibus vel spiritualibus: nec pateat sufficiens remedium aliud: nisi subducendo se ab obedientia talis potestatis sequentis & seipsa abutentis: & hoc ad tempus, vel quousque ecclesia vel concilium prouiderit, hoc fas erit: dum tamen illud agere pia quædam impellat necessitas, non libido seu cupiditas assumendi improbe velamen malitiæ libertatem.
units.tr: But if there is someone who wishes to turn his whole presidency and papal dignity into an instrument of wickedness and of the destruction of some part of the Church, in temporal or spiritual matters, and no other sufficient remedy is open, except to withdraw oneself from obedience to such a power, which abuses itself, then this will be lawful, for the time being, or until the Church or a council provides otherwise, provided that a certain pious necessity compels it, and not lust or greed for assuming under the cover of such a withdrawal the freedom of wickedness.

units.la: Fatemur enim duo illa nullo modo debere fieri nisi manifestis causis vrgentibus: ne in toto corpore ecclesiæ deterior & generalior scissura fiat & inducatur: dum particularia membra consuescunt non obedire: sicut notat Aristot. in polit. pessimum esse consuescere non obedire principi siue regi: quanto magis erronea & damnanda est assertio, quod licet vnicuique subditorum, mox vt aliquis est tyrannus ipsum viis omnibus fraudulentis & dolosis sine quauis autoritate vel declaratione iudiciaria morti tradere: præsertim si addat hæc assertio, quod tyrannus ille omnis est, qui non præest ad vtilitatem subditorum: sed de hac re alibi, de qua viderint assertores.
units.tr: For we admit that those two things must in no way be done except for manifest and urgent causes, lest a worse and more general schism be made and brought about in the whole body of the Church, while particular members grow accustomed to disobedience. As Aristotle notes in the Politics, it is the worst thing to grow accustomed to disobeying a prince or king. How much more erroneous and condemnable is the assertion that it is lawful for each of the subjects, as soon as someone is a tyrant, to put him to death by any fraudulent and deceitful means, without any authority or judicial declaration, especially if this assertion adds that every man is a tyrant who does not rule for the advantage of his subjects. But on this matter, let the advocates of that view see to it elsewhere.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XV.

units.la: AVferibilis est vicarius sponsus ecclesiæ per ecclesiam aut generale concilium perpetuo vel ad tempus: quo ad ea omnia, quæ sunt iurisdictionis. Satis indirecte deductio considerationis istius patet ex præcedenti. Nam possunt ab aliquo rite in papam electo tolli tam de iure quam de facto subditi: in quos debet iurisdictionem exercere. Et ita per indirectum iurisdictio non subsistet.
units.tr: The vicarious bridegroom of the Church may be removed by the Church or a general council, either permanently or for a time, so far as concerns all that belongs to jurisdiction. The deduction of this consideration is sufficiently clear, indirectly, from the preceding one. For jurisdiction could be taken away from the pope, once rightly elected, by someone, both in law and in fact, over the subjects over whom he ought to exercise it. And so, indirectly, jurisdiction would not remain.

units.la: Verum vero directe & absolute possit omnis potestas iurisdictionis a papa rite electo remoueri, posset esse duplex imaginatio quo ad aliquas iurisdictiones: qualis est iurisdictio respiciens sacramentalem absolutionem: quæ alterius est rationis, quam aliæ respicientes forum exterius. Hanc enim iurisdictionem habet confessor papæ super ipsum: cui tamen non posset communicari iurisdictio in foro exteriori supra papam, vt quod eum posset excommunicare. Hanc insuper iurisdictionem habet in casu necessitatis omnis sacerdos apud peccatorem sibi volentem confiteri.
units.tr: But if it were to be granted directly and absolutely that every power of jurisdiction could be removed from a pope rightly elected, there could be a twofold view concerning certain jurisdictions. One is the jurisdiction concerning sacramental absolution, which is of a different kind from the others that concern the external forum. For the pope's confessor has this jurisdiction over him, though jurisdiction in the external forum over the pope could not be communicated to him, so that he could excommunicate him. Moreover, every priest has this jurisdiction in cases of necessity over a sinner who wishes to confess to him.

units.la: Dicerent ergo aliqui de hac spirituali iurisdictione, sicut de potestate ordinis, quod licet inauferibilis sit in se & in sua essentia: tamen est suus vsus impedibilis modis prætactis. Sicut etiam impeditur schismatici & hæretici præcisi ab ecclesia: ne quisquam eis nisi in casu necessitatis debeat confiteri.
units.tr: Some would therefore say of this spiritual jurisdiction, as of the power of orders, that although it cannot be taken away in itself and in its essence, its exercise can be impeded by the means mentioned above. Just as the use of it is also impeded in the case of schismatics and heretics who have been cut off from the Church, so that no one ought to confess to them except in a case of necessity.

units.la: Dicerent alii, quod talis iurisdictio non solum impeditur in suo vsu, sed etiam tollitur ministerio ecclesiæ & prælati superioris: dum degradatur hæreticus aliquis prælatus vel sacerdos: & hoc quia condescendit Deus tollere ab illo sacerdote potestatem diuinitus sibi collatam per ministerium, talis tanquam per causam sine qua, non sicut imaginantur doctores multi de potentia collata sacramentis respectu gratiæ, quam figurant, non enim attingit illa virtus actiua sacramentorum substantiam gratiæ: sed tamen sunt causa, sine qua non talis gratia nequaquam crearetur. Sicut præterea dicimus de infusione animæ in embrionem dispositum: & magis ad proprium de recessu animæ a corpore per inductionem disconuenientem qualitatum: præsertim si imaginemur, quod anima sicut creabatur prius, ita nunc annihilaretur consequenter ad has dispositiones vel ad alias. Vel exemplificemus de annihilatione gratiæ per peccatum mortale.
units.tr: Others would say that such jurisdiction is not only impeded in its exercise but is also taken away through the ministry of the Church and of a superior prelate, when some heretical prelate or priest is deposed. And this is because God condescends to take away from that priest the power divinely conferred on him through the ministry; such a power is taken as a cause without which the effect does not follow, not as many teachers imagine concerning the power conferred on sacraments with respect to the grace which they signify. For that active power of the sacraments does not reach the substance of grace, yet they are a cause without which such grace would never be created. Likewise we say the same of the infusion of the soul into a disposed embryo, and more properly of the departure of the soul from the body through the induction of unfitting qualities, especially if we imagine that the soul, which was created earlier, is then annihilated as a consequence of these dispositions or others. Or let us illustrate it by the annihilation of grace through mortal sin.

units.la: Aduertamus tamen in hac materia, quod oportet nos concedere consequenter ad præmissa & ad factum Cœlestini, qui cessit papatui, quod papatus non dicat ordinem super sacerdotium vel episcopatum. Quod insuper non dicat iurisdictionem inabdicabilem humana voluntate supra episcopatum. Alioquin tunc temporis remansissent duo habentes papalem dignitatem: aut talem quæ suisset superior ad episcopalem vel archiepiscopalem. Oportet vt videtur consequenter dicere, quod mortuo vel cedente Bonifacio, qui in locum Cœlestini successit, ipse Cœlestinus potuerat assumi in papatum sine noua alicuius ordinis vel potestatis iuridicæ essentialis & inabdicabilis collatione, quemadmodum dicimus de episcopali dignitate in his, qui fuerunt degradati vel deiecti: qui iterum possunt restitui nulla consecratione noua facta.
units.tr: We should note, however, in this matter, that, in accordance with what has been said and with the fact of Celestine, who resigned the papacy, we must concede that the papacy does not confer an order above the priesthood or the episcopate. Nor does it confer a jurisdiction over the episcopate that cannot be relinquished by human will. Otherwise at that time there would have remained two holders of the papal dignity, or one of a kind that would have been superior to the episcopal or archiepiscopal dignity. It seems we must consequently say that, when Boniface, who succeeded Celestine in his place, died or resigned, Celestine himself could have been raised to the papacy without any new conferral of an order or of an essential and irrevocable juridical power, just as we say of the episcopal dignity in the case of those who have been degraded or deposed, who can be restored again without any new consecration being performed.

units.la: Hæ autem considerationes proficiunt studiosis ad cognoscendum magis & magis quid dicat vel importet, & quid non, papalis dignitas: & qualiter potest exercere iudicium ecclesia circa papam. Notetur Bonauentura in dist. 25. quarti: vbi quæritur si episcopatus sit ordo supra sacerdotium: & ponit quod neque episcopatus neque papatus dicit plenitudinem aliquam vel dignitatem in ordinem, & ordine nouum nullum addit.
units.tr: These considerations, moreover, help students to understand more and more what the papal dignity says or implies, and what it does not, and in what manner the Church can exercise judgment over the pope. Note Bonaventure on Distinction 25 of the fourth book, where he asks whether the episcopate is an order above the priesthood; and he holds that neither the episcopate nor the papacy expresses any fullness or dignity in the order, and adds no new order at all.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XVI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XVI.

units.la: AVferibilis est vicarius sponsus ecclesiæ per ecclesiam aut generale concilium, vt dictum est: & dum hoc euenit, probabile est, quod magis fiat destitutiue & iuridice: quam solum declaratiue seu dictatiue seu consiliatiue.
units.tr: The bridegroom's vicar of the Church may be removed by the Church or by a general council, as was said above. When this happens, it is probably done by deposition and judicial act, rather than merely by declaration, pronouncement or counsel.

units.la: ● Fuerunt duæ opiniones, vt alias tangebatur de institutione papæ. Vna ponit, quod papa dum labitur in hæresim, iam damnatus est: & eo facto per Deum depositus, & perdidit iure diuino papalem dignitatem: siue hæc hæresis sit secreta, vt ampliant aliqui, siue sit manifesta, vt placet aliis loqui restrictius.
units.tr: There were two opinions, as was mentioned elsewhere, about the appointment of a pope. One holds that when a pope falls into heresy, he is already condemned, and by that very fact deposed by God and loses the papal dignity by divine right, whether this heresy is secret, as some extend it, or manifest, as others prefer to say more narrowly.

units.la: Credunt alii, quod nullus rite in papam electus redditur per aliquod crimen eo facto depositus: licet bene fit deponendus, & manet talis rite electus semper papa usque ad sententiam depositionis latam contra eum per ecclesiam vel generale concilium: aut nisi cesserit sponte sua, quemadmodum in aliis episcopatibus & dignitatibus minoribus dicunt esse certum, ita quod resolutio sinalis huius opinionis, quam nunc dicimus probabilem, stat in hoc, quod sicut nullus efficitur papa, ligate stante, & nisi fieret noua revelatio vel miraculosa institutio: nullus inquam talis rite efficitur papa, nisi per legitimam electionem dominorum Cardinalium aut aliorum, quibus haec potestas collata fuerit per ecclesiam aut per generale concilium: sic nullus talis rite electus definitur esse papa, nisi per destitutionem legitimam factam ab ecclesia vel concilio vel aliis, quibus voluerit conferre ecclesia vel concilium huiusmodi potestatem, qualis nondum collata esse reperitur.
units.tr: Others believe that a man who has been rightly elected pope is not, by any crime, deprived of office by that very fact. He is indeed rightly to be deposed, and such a rightly elected man remains pope until a sentence of deposition is pronounced against him by the Church or a general council, or unless he resigns of his own accord. They say this is certain in other bishoprics and lesser dignities. So the final resolution of this opinion, which we now call probable, rests on this: just as no one becomes pope while the bond stands (unless a new revelation or a miraculous institution occurs), so no one, I say, is rightly made pope except by the lawful election of the lord Cardinals or of others to whom this power has been committed by the Church or a general council. Likewise, no one rightly elected is judged to have ceased to be pope except by a lawful deposition made by the Church, a council, or others to whom the Church or council may grant such power, which has not yet been found to be conferred.

units.la: Probabilitas huius opinionis fundata est alias in alio opusculo. Et nunc breviter repetamus dicentes aliqua. Primo quod status hierarchicus in ecclesia debet esse certus & constans, da oppositum. Iam ecclesia non fuisset sufficienter instituta: quia subditi remanerent semper exposti discrimini peccati mortalis in obediendo vel non obediendo suis superioribus: cum non posset eis constare sufficienter, quando superiores ius perdidissent in praesidendo, vel ipsum retinerent.
units.tr: The probability of this opinion has been grounded elsewhere in another little work, and now let us briefly repeat it, stating a few points. First, the hierarchical order in the Church ought to be certain and constant; the contrary would be absurd. For then the Church would not have been sufficiently instituted, since its subjects would always remain exposed to the danger of mortal sin, whether they obeyed or disobeyed their superiors, because it could not be sufficiently known to them when superiors had lost the right to preside, or still retained it.

units.la: Ac proinde dicimus consequenter: quod titulus ecclesiasticæ dignitatis vel autoritatis non est fundatus in sola sanctitate: quemadmodum dixerunt haeretici, qui nominabantur Pauperes de Lugduno, & alii similes: sicut deducit Bonauentura, in dist. 25. quarti. alioquin nihil esset certum in actibus hierarchicis: Sicut nemo scit an odio vel amore dignus sit.
units.tr: Accordingly, we consequently say that the title of ecclesiastical dignity or authority is not founded on holiness alone, as the heretics called the Poor of Lyons and others like them have said. Bonaventure, in dist. 25 of book four, also draws this out. Otherwise nothing would be certain in hierarchical acts, since no one knows whether he is worthy of hatred or of love.

units.la: Ex eadem radice patet, quod per praescientiam vel reprobationem aeternam non datur vel aufertur praecise titulus ecclesiasticæ dignitatis. Nam Iudas praescitus fuit Apostolus: & multi praedestinati carent tali dignitate. Sequitur amplius, quod titulus ecclesiasticæ dignitatis non est fundatus in donis gratuitis latentibus in anima: quia forte per revelationem: & praesertim si sint dona, quæ statim habita statim perdi possunt: quod dicitur propter characteres indelebiles postquam semel habiti sunt, & de quibus praesuppositia fide potest haberi sufficiens certitudo, dum aliquis rite suscipit sacramenta imprimentia tales characteres.
units.tr: From the same root it is clear that the title of ecclesiastical dignity is not given or taken away simply by foreknowledge or by eternal reprobation. For Judas was foreknown as an apostle, and many who are predestined lack such a dignity. It follows further that the title of ecclesiastical dignity is not founded on gratuitous gifts lying hidden in the soul, since these may be revealed only by chance. This especially applies to gifts which, once possessed, can be lost at once. I say this because of the indelible characters, once they have been received, and about which, given prior faith, sufficient certainty can be had whenever someone rightly receives the sacraments that imprint such characters.

units.la: Addamus rursus, quod sicut iniustus homo sine charitate & in peccato mortali potest iuste dominari temporaliter, & esse rex vel princeps iusto titulo. Sic etiam potest esse episcopus vel sacerdos. Et hoc sequitur ex prioribus contra imaginationem aliquorum nostris temporibus in Anglia & alibi: qui posuerunt omne dominium & omnem dignitatem fundari in iustitia charitatis & quod sine ea nihil potest esse iustum neque iuste fieri neque possideri: quod utique repugnat assertionibus sacrae scripturae in locis plurimis, in quibus idololatræ & pessimi homines & reprobi appellantur Reges: vt Saul, Cyrus & Aacham. Vnde & Christus docuit, quod Pharisaeis & reprobis daretur obedientia in doctrina eorum, dum ait: Supra cathedram Moysis sederunt scribae & Pharisaei, quae dicunt, facite &c.
units.tr: Let us add again that just as an unjust man, without charity and in mortal sin, can rightly rule temporally and be king or prince by a just title, so too he can be a bishop or priest. This follows from what has been said earlier, against the notion of some in our times in England and elsewhere, who held that all lordship and all dignity are founded on the justice of charity, and that without it nothing can be just, nor justly done, nor possessed. This certainly contradicts the statements of Holy Scripture in many places, where idolaters, the very worst men and the reprobate are called kings, such as Saul, Cyrus and Ahab. Hence also Christ taught that obedience was to be given to the Pharisees and the reprobate in their teaching, when he said: "The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat; whatever they say, do ye," etc.

units.la: Dicamus consequenter quod dignitates ecclesiasticæ non fundantur in fide interiori, neque in spe sancta, neque in charitate: patet ex eisdem fundamentis.
units.tr: Let us then consequently say that ecclesiastical dignities are not founded on inward faith, nor on holy hope, nor on charity. This is plain from the same foundations.

units.la: Ac proinde sequitur ulterius, quod deficiente fide in aliquo praelato, non est consequens vt mox perdiderit pastoralem dignitatem: quia nec fides est, nec necessarium eius fundamentum.
units.tr: Accordingly it follows further that if faith is lacking in some prelate, it does not follow that he at once loses his pastoral dignity, since faith is neither that dignity nor its necessary foundation.

units.la: Patet amplius, quod canones sacrae scripturae ac summorum pontificum dicentes haereticos esse vitandos tanquam ethnicos & anathematizatos: verum dicunt, dum constat eos tales esse: & maxime per sententiam iudiciariam, aut propriam confessionem, aut facti euidentiam. Nihilominus quod tales sint eo facto depositi a dignitatibus: & quod eas perdiderint sine destitutione, non habetur ex eisdem canonibus. Aut si aliqui canones videantur hoc sonare de notoriis & manifestis haereticis, qui sunt eo facto depositi: intelligi potest, quod contra tales non requiritur processus iuridicus ordinatus ad degradandum eos per sententiam diffinitiuam: sicut in occultis & non confessatis oporteret.
units.tr: It is clearer still that the canons of Holy Scripture and of the supreme pontiffs, which say that heretics are to be avoided as pagans and accursed, speak truly when it is established that they are such, and especially by a judicial sentence, by their own confession, or by the plain evidence of the fact. Nevertheless, the canons do not teach that such men are by that very fact deposed from their dignities, and that they have lost them without deposition. Or if some canons seem to say this of notorious and manifest heretics, who are deposed by that very fact, it can be understood that against such men no ordered judicial process is required to degrade them by a definitive sentence, as would be necessary in the case of hidden heretics who have not confessed.

units.la: Dicamus ergo concludentes probabiliter, quod sicut humana electio dat ius & titulum ad papalem dignitatem, si homo sit capax huius lectionis atque dignitatis: & si sit viator baptizatus, sic per humanam destitutionem perdit illam praesidentiam & non aliter, eo inuito, siue sit haereticus siue sit schismaticus.
units.tr: So let us conclude with probability: just as human election gives the right and title to the papal dignity, if the man is capable of this election and dignity and is a baptized wayfarer, so by human deposition he loses that presidency, and not otherwise, against his will, whether he is a heretic or a schismatic.

units.la: Et dum opponitur quod haereticus non potest esse membrum ecclesiæ: quanto minus potest esse caput eius vel vicarius suus, aut sponsus, multa in hanc sententiam.
units.tr: And when it is objected that a heretic cannot be a member of the Church, and so much less can he be its head or its vicar or bridegroom, many arguments are offered to this effect.

units.la: Respondetur quod haec ratio vel similis si bene perpendatur, omnino fuit illa, quae fundauit omnes errores, de quibus praetactum est, quod solus iustus iuste damnatur, vel est sacerdos vel consecrat: & ita de similibus.
units.tr: It is answered that this argument, or one like it, if weighed carefully, is entirely the one which founded all the errors previously mentioned, namely that only the just man is justly condemned, or that only the just man is a priest or consecrates, and so on for similar claims.

units.la: Notemus ergo sine processu longiori, quod multae sunt connexiones membrorum in corpore mystico ecclesiæ: sicut diuersæ sunt in eodem corpore vnitates. Vna est enim vnitas charitatis: & ita soli habentes charitatem dicuntur vere membra ecclesiæ. Alii quantumcunque fideles sunt, vel vt præcisa vel vt arida & emortua membra, imo sunt proditores Domini sui, nec de familia eius hoc modo dici possunt, nec sunt digni pane quo vescun-tur.
units.tr: Let us therefore note, without a longer discussion, that there are many connections of members in the mystical body of the Church, just as there are different unities in the same body. There is one unity of charity, and so only those who have charity are truly said to be members of the Church. Others, however faithful they may be, whether as cut-off or as withered and dead members, are even traitors to their Lord; they cannot be called members of his household in this way, nor are they worthy of the bread on which they feed.

units.la: Alia est vnitas in donis naturæ, sicut omnes homines connectuntur in intellectu & ratione. Alia est vnitas in simili participatione sacramentorum: & præsertim in vnitate baptismatis, in quo character imprimitur, in qua vnitate connectuntur omnes, qui baptisma rite susceperunt: etiam vbi fidem actualem vel habitualem perdidissent. Et hæc vnio videtur absolute sufficere ad hoc, quod aliquis rite in papam electus maneat caput ecclesiæ quousque fuerit per sententiam diffinitivam depositus.
units.tr: There is another unity in the gifts of nature, as all men are connected in understanding and reason. There is another unity in the like participation of the sacraments, and especially in the unity of baptism, in which the character is imprinted, and in which unity all are joined who have rightly received baptism, even where they have lost actual or habitual faith. And this union seems absolutely sufficient for a man rightly elected pope to remain head of the Church until he is deposed by a definitive sentence.

units.la: Nolo tamen propterea dicere, quod semper sit obediendum tali hæretico: vel non sibi resistendum, aut quod sit appellatione papalis dignitatis honorandus: quoniam in casu, sicut iam factum est, posset papa verus manens papa licite etiam ligari vel incarcerari vel in mari demergi: quanto magis posset obedientia sibi vel reverentialis nominatio denegari?
units.tr: I do not, however, wish to say on that account that such a heretic must always be obeyed, or that he must not be resisted, or that he should be honoured with the name of papal dignity. For in such a case, as has already happened, a true pope remaining pope could lawfully be bound, imprisoned, or drowned in the sea. How much more, then, could obedience or the title of reverence be refused to him?

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XVII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XVII.

units.la: AVsferibilis non est vicarius sponsus ecclesiæ rite prius electus, quin posset creare veros sacerdotes & episcopos, & alia facere, quæ ordinem suum respiciunt in tali plenitudine receptum: absque hoc quod iterari debeant ea quæ fecisset: quia valida sunt iure diuino: quamuis peccabit ipse cum partibus suis, si hoc attentaverit.
units.tr: The vicar, the bridegroom of the Church, once rightly elected, cannot be removed. He can create true priests and bishops and do the other things that belong to his order, which he has received in its full extent, without what he has done needing to be repeated, since it is valid by divine right. He himself, however, with those who side with him, will sin if he attempts this.

units.la: Consimiliter ea quæ iurisdictionem puram respiciunt, illa possunt dici valida, quæ egerit talis, quamdiu toleratur ab ecclesia: & hoc iure seu approbatione totius ecclesiæ vel præcedentium pontificum & conciliorum generalium institutione: præsertim nisi aliunde ex culpa subditorum talia reddita fuerint inualida: quia participant in crimine.
units.tr: Likewise, acts that concern pure jurisdiction can be called valid when such a man performs them, for as long as the Church tolerates them. This holds by right, or by the approval of the whole Church, or by the institution of preceding popes and general councils. This is especially so unless, on some other ground, such acts have been made invalid through the fault of subjects, because they share in the crime.

units.la: Respondet hæc consideratio multis dubitationibus, quæ potuerunt oriri durante hoc pestifero schismate tam in collationibus ordinum quam in dependentibus & collationibus beneficiorum & similibus: vbi facilius se expedit opinio, quam probabili modo posuimus in præcedenti consideratione circa obiecta. Multum prodest insuper eadem consideratio ad celeriorem & expeditiorem terminationem schismatis per viam cessionis, omissa qualibet discussione facienda.
units.tr: This consideration resolves many doubts that could have arisen during this pestilential schism, both about the conferring of orders and about dependent matters, and about the conferring of benefices and the like. Here the opinion is more easily settled than in the probable manner we set out about the objections in the preceding consideration. Moreover, this same consideration greatly helps toward a quicker and more expeditious end to the schism by way of resignation, without any lengthy discussion.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XVIII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XVIII.

units.la: AVsferibilis est vicarius sponsus ecclesiæ tanquam hæreticus aut schismaticus: etiam vbi in casu ipse non est veraciter & mentaliter talis.
units.tr: The vicar, the bridegroom of the Church, can be removed as a heretic or a schismatic, even where, in the case at hand, he is not truly and inwardly such.

units.la: Assignemus summatim casus aliquos circa personas alias, qui similiter possunt in papam cadere, duos inuenimus in iuribus expressos.
units.tr: Let us briefly list some cases concerning other persons that could likewise befall a pope. We find two expressed in the law.

units.la: Vnus est dum aliquis sustinet excommunicationem vltra annum: & citatur super materia fidei, nec respondet.
units.tr: The first is when someone persists under excommunication for more than a year, and is summoned on a matter of faith and does not answer.

units.la: Alius dum citatus coram iudice renuit præstare iuramentum. Talis aliquis poterit manere semper verus fidelis: attamen ipse tanquam hæreticus iuris præsumptione damnabitur.
units.tr: The second is when someone, summoned before a judge, refuses to take an oath. Such a person may always remain a true believer, yet he will be condemned as a heretic by the presumption of law.

units.la: Tertius assignatur casus, si timore mortis vel alia passione motus quis vocaliter negat ea quæ sunt fidei: nec possit aut velit sufficienter se purgare.
units.tr: A third case is assigned: when someone, moved by fear of death or some other passion, verbally denies the things that belong to the faith, and cannot or will not sufficiently clear himself.

units.la: Quartus casus, vbi per actus hæreticales aut idolatricos habebitur præsumptio vehemens contra aliquem: & talis nec poterit aut velit sufficienter se purgare. Dicuntur autem actus hæreticales vel idolatrici, qui sunt contrarii vel oppositi actibus, quibus solet fieri professio fidei & religionis Christianæ & cultus diuini: sicut est genuflexio coram sacramento altaris, & ingressus templi, & similia. Et in hoc multum valet vsus hominum, sic talia accipientium. Unde si quis exhibet talia in honorem Machometi vel idolorum, aut si oppositis factis detestaretur sacramentum altaris, & templi Dei & sacras imagines, & similia faceret: haberi deberet de hæresi & idololatria suspectus: & hoc vel vehementer vel graviter vel leviter, secundum quod plures causæ suspitionem aggravantes, & pauciores releuantes concurrerent. Et hic esset longus sermo de modo accusationis talium coram inquisitore: quando scilicet & quando non veniunt iudicialiter in materia fidei vel idololatriæ pertractandi.
units.tr: A fourth case: where a strong presumption arises against someone from heretical or idolatrous acts, and such a person cannot or will not sufficiently clear himself. Heretical or idolatrous acts are those contrary or opposed to the acts by which the profession of the Christian faith, religion and divine worship is usually made, such as kneeling before the sacrament of the altar, entering a church, and the like. In this matter the custom of men, who so understand such acts, carries great weight. Hence, if someone performs such acts in honour of Muhammad or of idols, or if by contrary deeds he should despise the sacrament of the altar, the temple of God and the holy images, and do similar things, he ought to be held suspect of heresy and idolatry. He would be suspect either strongly, gravely or lightly, according as more or fewer circumstances aggravating or relieving the suspicion concur. And here there would be a long discussion of the manner of accusing such persons before an inquisitor: when, namely, and when they do not come to be dealt with judicially in matters of faith or idolatry.

units.la: Casus quintus inuenitur, vbi quis per falsos testes accusatur atque conuincitur fuisse relapsus in hæreses iam damnatas. Ille plane damnabitur & iuste damnabitur per ecclesiam, quæ non iudicat de occultis, sed de allegatis & probatis per sententiam.
units.tr: A fifth case is found where someone is accused by false witnesses and convicted of having relapsed into heresies already condemned. He will plainly be condemned, and justly condemned, by the Church, which does not judge hidden things but what is alleged and proved by sentence.

units.la: Sextus casus incidens cum quarto: vbi quis etiam leui suspitione notatus de fide, vocatus fuerit ad iudicium, & venire neglexerit sen contempserit, aut forte non potuerit, de qua tamen impotentia fidem facere non valebit. Cum enim summus pontifex iuxta probata prius possit tam doctrinaliter quam iudicialiter denunciari, deferri & acculari coram concilio generali in materia fidei & cultus diuini, non repugnat casus istos & similes in ipso posse reperiri, qui circumdatus est infirmitate, sicut dicit Apostolus experientiæ voce loquens.
units.tr: A sixth case, which falls under the fourth: where someone, even if noted with a slight suspicion regarding the faith, has been called to judgment and has neglected or scorned to come, or perhaps was unable to, though he will not be able to prove that inability by faith. For since the supreme pontiff, according to what was proved earlier, can be denounced, referred and accused, both doctrinally and judicially, before a general council in matters of faith and the worship of God, it does not contradict these and similar cases being found in him as well, who is compassed with infirmity, as the Apostle says, speaking in the voice of experience.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XIX.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XIX.

units.la: AVferibilis est vicarius sponsus ecclesiæ per ecclesiam etiam sine culpa sua, quamuis non sine causa.
units.tr: The vicar of the Bridegroom of the Church may be removed by the Church, even without fault on his part, though not without cause.

units.la: Tangamus similiter casus aliquos. Vbi coram tota ecclesia vel concilio generali proponetur & probaretur per testes, quod papa qui forte est detentus inter Saracenos iam obiit, & cum ecclesia iam non posset commode diutius remanere sine papa: videtur omnino quod in hoc casu concilium poterit creare nouum papam: & cum non possint esse duo simul, videtur quod primus ent destitutus per concilium. Posset etiam destitui, vbi constaret de vita, si de eo ablata esset spes omnis redeundi.
units.tr: Let us touch upon some similar cases. Where it is put before the whole Church or a general council, and proved by witnesses, that the pope, who perhaps is held among the Saracens, has already died, and the Church cannot conveniently remain any longer without a pope: it seems altogether that in this case a council may create a new pope; and since two cannot be at the same time, it seems that the first would be deposed by the council.
