He could also be deposed, where it was certain that he was alive, if all hope of his returning had been taken away from him.

units.la: Alter casus est, vbi quis rite electus in papam efficeretur adeo inutilis propter indispositionem corporalem, ac propter carentiam perpetuam vsus rationis: quod per concilium iam per eum congregatum dum sanæ mentis erat, expediret aliter prouideri de summo pontifice.
units.tr: Another case is where someone duly elected pope became so unfit, because of bodily infirmity and a perpetual lack of the use of reason, that the council already gathered by him while he was of sound mind should provide otherwise for the supreme pontiff.

units.la: Alter casus est, vbi post electionem canonicam alicuius in papam per Cardinales, ipsi Cardinales omnes morerentur, priusquam possent electionem suam canonicam publicare, constat quod ecclesia non tenetur hunc recipere pro papa: & ita posset ad electionem alterius procedere.
units.tr: Another case is where, after the canonical election of someone as pope by the Cardinals, all the Cardinals themselves die before they can publish their canonical election. It is agreed that the Church is not bound to receive this man as pope, and so it could proceed to the election of another.

units.la: Alter casus similis stat cum priori, vbi nullo modo Cardinales etiam viuentes possent facere fidem sufficientem de electione canonica facta circa vnum: qualis casus videtur esse & fuisse in schismate præsenti, si bene perpendatur. Et ideo circumstantia eius multum iustificat processus habitos contra illos contendentes & aduersus Cardinales.
units.tr: Another case, similar to the previous one, arises where even the Cardinals who are living could in no way make sufficient proof of a canonical election made concerning one man. This seems to be, and to have been, the case in the present schism, if it is weighed carefully. And therefore its circumstances greatly justify the proceedings taken against those contending and against the Cardinals.

units.la: Alter casus propter communem errorem aut æstimationem subditorum aut ipsorum malitiam generalem: de quibus non est præsumendum, quod vnquam debeant obedientiam præstare tali, qui fuit in papam rite electus: tamen alteri nouiter eligendo parati sunt: vt forte si Græci vellent ad vnitatem ecclesiæ redire, dummodo tolleretur papa iam existens, & nouus rite canonice crearetur. Confirmat hoc imaginatio casus illius iuxta positionem Innocentii & aliorum Iuristarum: qui dicunt hominem expresse professum in religione posse vxorem ducere pro salutatione magnæ gentis aut ad fidem conuersione. Cur non similiter pro aliquo tanto bono posset rite electus per ecclesiam aut concilium generale destitui bono zelo & integra charitate?
units.tr: Another case arises from a common error or esteem among the subjects, or from the general malice of the subjects themselves; of whom it is not to be presumed that they will ever owe obedience to one who was duly elected pope; yet they are ready for another newly to be elected: as perhaps if the Greeks were willing to return to the unity of the Church, provided that the pope now existing were removed and a new one were duly and canonically created. The imagining of this case is confirmed by the position of Innocent and other jurists, who say that a man who has expressly professed in a religious order may take a wife for the salvation of a great people or for the conversion of a nation to the faith. Why, then, for some such great good, could one duly elected by the Church or a general council not be deposed, out of good zeal and entire charity?

units.la: Casus alter sextus esset, vbi per iuramentum & votum aliquis in papam rite electus, seipsum ad cessionem obligasset; sed differret hoc adimplere, in scandalum populorum putantium ex tali facto papæ, quod neque iuramentis suis obligantur, neque votis, qualem casum habere videmur in manibus.
units.tr: A sixth case would be where someone duly elected pope had bound himself by oath and vow to resign, but deferred fulfilling this, to the scandal of peoples who think that from such a fact the pope is not bound by his oaths or his vows; which case we seem to have before us.

units.la: Denique etsi casus notati in hac & præcedenti consideratione vix aut nunquam visi fuerint: nihilominus expediens est tangere ad inquisitionem solidiorem veritatis, & ad confutationem illorum, qui in iuribus suis scriptis omnia particulatim & sufficienter arbitrantur esse decisa.
units.tr: Finally, even if the cases noted in this and the preceding consideration have hardly or never been seen, nevertheless it is expedient to touch upon them for a more solid inquiry into the truth, and for the refutation of those who in their writings on rights judge that everything has been decided in detail and sufficiently.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XX.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XX.

units.la: AVferibilis non est vsque ad consummationem seculi vicarius sponsus ecclesiæ, quin aliquis certus & vnicus præficiatur: & hoc lege stante & præsuppositá mundi duratione longissima.
units.tr: The Bridegroom of the Church, who cannot be taken away, does not leave her without some certain and single vicar set over her until the end of the age. This holds while the law stands and the world is presupposed to last a very long time.

units.la: Detur oppositum: tunc ecclesia maneret imperfecta vsque ad consummationem seculi, nec suorum gauderet integritate membrorum, & præsertim membri principalis.
units.tr: Suppose the contrary: then the Church would remain imperfect until the end of the age, and would not enjoy the integrity of its members, and especially not of its principal member.

units.la: Quocirca concludamus sub quadruplici corollario moraliter conformiter ad prædicta & ad alias considerationes alibi notatas super eadem materia.
units.tr: Therefore let us conclude with a fourfold corollary, morally in agreement with what has been said above and with the other considerations noted elsewhere on the same matter.

units.la: Et dicamus primo, quod hi repugnant ordinationi Christi & Spiritui sancto rebelles sunt, qui præsentis schismatis terminationem impediunt modis talibus, quos sciunt aut scire debent, ad pacem protinus reducendam esse, vel inutiles vel nociuos: vt si quæratur fieri pax per reductionem vnius obedientiæ ad alteram, vel per vim armatam, vel per dispositionem iuris, quæ non sunt probabiliter & salubriter expectanda. Nec sufficit dicere: habemus papam Christum: sufficit vt credamus in eum, nam talis vnio ad Christum etsi sit necessaria, non tamen vsque quaque sufficit, vt in ea stemus non procurando quantum in nobis est vnionem alteram ad vnum vicarium suum in terris, de quo constat ecclesiæ.
units.tr: First, let us say that those who hinder the ending of the present schism, by means which they know, or ought to know, are useless or harmful for restoring peace at once, are rebels against the ordinance of Christ and the Holy Spirit. This applies when peace is sought by reducing one obedience to the other, by armed force, or by a legal settlement, none of which can reasonably and beneficially be expected. Nor is it enough to say, "We have Christ as pope; it is enough that we believe in him." Such union with Christ, though necessary, is not always sufficient for us to rest in it without seeking, as far as lies in us, the other union, with one vicar of his on earth, whose identity is known to the Church.

units.la: Addimus consequenter pro secundo corollario: quod hi fallunt & falluntur qui propter assectionem qualemcunque commodi vel honoris, vel amicitiæ circa alterum contendentium, tenderent impedire suam cessionem pro impletione iuramentorum & votorum suorum & pacis datione, si nollent suam deiectionem vbi hoc agere renuerent, imo prorsus quanto magis aliquis fuerit amicus, tanto amplius debet hoc quærere vt eorum spiritus saluus fiat: & vt pateat omnibus, quia non zelo malo zelati sunt eos aliquando, sed zelo charitatis: licet forte vel error vel deceptio in iudicio particularium agendorum interuenire potuerit.
units.tr: Second, let us add that those err and are deceived who, out of some affection for profit, honour or friendship toward one of the contenders, would try to prevent his resignation, which is needed to fulfil his oaths and vows and to give peace. They would do so even if they did not want his deposition in case he refused to do this. Indeed, the more a man is a friend, the more he ought to seek this, so that their souls may be saved; and so that it may be plain to all that they have sometimes been zealous not with bad zeal but with the zeal of charity, even though error or deception may perhaps have entered into their judgement of particular actions to be taken.

units.la: Dicamus præterea pro tertio corollario, quod hi nutu Dei & Spiritus sancti (sicut credendum est) inspiratione tracti fuerunt, qui ad conuocationem sacri concilii Pisis celebrandi dederunt operam, & promptitudinem præstiterunt, præstant & præstabunt. Ille orando, ille exhortando, hic protegendo, ille comparando: & ita de singulis. Impeditores si qui essent numerosi numerandi sunt inter illos, de quibus nunc tetigimus: qui rei sunt detrimentorum omnium tam temporalium quam spiritualium ex hoc schismate horrendo nascentium, qualia vix sufficerit tractatus grandis vel summatim enarrare. Nam quomodo paratus esset audire ecclesiam, qui suam congregationem vel nollet damnabiliter, vel damnabilius impediret? Hanc convocationem pro finali sciuto sua protectionis ad Deum, quaesivit in morte rex Franciae Carolus quintus. Ad hanc esse debet finalis resolutio omnium, qui de schismate nolunt increpari apud Deum, imo ad hoc rendit neutralitas accepta, si bene capiatur.
units.tr: Third, let us say that those were moved by the will of God and the inspiration of the Holy Spirit (as we must believe) who have given effort, showed readiness, show it now, and will show it, toward the calling of the holy council to be held at Pisa. One prays, another exhorts, another protects, another provides, and so on for each. If there were any obstructers, they must be counted among those we have just mentioned, who are guilty of all the losses, temporal and spiritual, arising from this dreadful schism. A large treatise would scarcely suffice to describe them in summary. For how could a man be ready to hear the Church who either refuses, damnably, or hinders, more damnably still, his own congregation? King Charles V of France sought this convocation at his death, as the final shield of his protection. To this must be directed the final resolution of all who do not wish to be called to account before God for the schism. Indeed, the neutrality adopted tends to this, if it is rightly understood.

units.la: Dicamus ad extremum pro quarto corollario, quod hi qui factum concilium Pisanum constituerant, sufficientem habebant authoritatem deiiciendi duos contendentes aut suos complices, si noluerint parere dictatis per hoc concilium in cessione faciendā realiter & de facto & scito & aliis requisitis. Poterunt que procedere ad electionem unius tertii Vicarii, qui tertius & indubitatus ab ecclesia poterit & debebit reputari, etiam ubi non omnes obedire vellent sic electo: quod tamen non est indebite praesumendum.
units.tr: Fourth and last, let us say that those who constituted the Council of Pisa had sufficient authority to depose the two contenders or their accomplices, if they were unwilling to obey the decrees of this council, namely to make the resignation really and in fact, knowingly, and with the other requisites. They could then proceed to the election of a third vicar, who could and should be regarded by the Church as a third and undoubted vicar, even where not all were willing to obey the one so elected. This, however, is not to be presumed without due cause.

units.la: Ecce ergo viginti considerationes quodam ordine geometrico se sequentes. Quae iunctis adhuc sedecim, in quarum qualiber initium est unitas ecclesiastica, additis quoque aliis quatuor dum Tarascone praedicatis, redduntur 40. Considerationes. Et haec quaelibet possunt afferre studiosioribus cognitionis materiam, sit eorum iudicium qui viderint.
units.tr: Behold, then, twenty considerations following one another in a certain geometrical order. With sixteen more joined to them, each of which begins from ecclesiastical unity, and with four others added from the sermon preached at Tarascon, they make forty considerations. Each of these can furnish matter for knowledge to the more studious; let the judgement rest with those who have examined them.

units.la: Postulemus tandem, ut inauferibilis sponsus ecclesiae Christus vicarium certum & unicum nobis instituat, ad gloriam nominis sui & nostram omnium salutem, praestante eodem, qui est benedictus in secula seculorum: Amen.
units.tr: Finally, let us ask that Christ, the indefectible Bridegroom of the Church, appoint for us a certain and single vicar, to the glory of his name and the salvation of us all, through the help of him who is blessed for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: Sedecim considerationes, quarum hic mentionem fecit, paulo post subsequentur. Quatuor alia in sermone Tarascone praedicato: qui incipit: Apparuit gratia Dei &c. etiam subiungentur.
units.tr: The sixteen considerations which he mentioned here will follow shortly after. The four others, from the sermon preached at Tarascon which begins "The grace of God has appeared," etc., will also be appended.

units.la: SENTENTIA MAGI- STRI IOHANNIS DE GERSON, DE MODO HABENDI SE TEMPORE SCHISMATIS.
units.tr: The Opinion of Master John Gerson, on How to Conduct Oneself in Time of Schism.

units.la: Ad tollendam quorundam in praesenti schismate pertinaciam, improbitatemque nimiam, specialiter in patria Flandrensi, si pro meritis aut falsis assertionibus suis certissima & perniciosissima schismata formant & fraternam violant charitatem, dum homines ab obedientia debita suorum superiorum auertunt: dum postremo pro instabili sua opinione & humana traditione legem Dei sanctam & stabilem deserere, contemnere & violare compellunt: Dignum duxi quaedam fundamentalia per me posita saluo semper in omnibus superiorum ac sapientiorum iudicio, nunc sub aliquarum conclusionum compendio ponere.
units.tr: To curb the obstinacy and excessive wickedness of some in the present schism, especially in the land of Flanders, who, on account of their merits or their false assertions, create most certain and most pernicious schisms, violate fraternal charity by turning men away from the obedience they owe their superiors, and finally compel men, for the sake of their unstable opinion and human tradition, to abandon, despise and violate the holy and stable law of God: I have thought it worthwhile to set out, in the form of a summary of conclusions, some basic points that I have laid down, always saving the judgement of superiors and of wiser men in all things.

units.la: 1. Quocunque de papatu contendentium demonstrato non est haereticum dicere, A. non est papa.
units.tr: 1. Whichever party of the contenders over the papacy is pointed to, it is not heretical to say: A. is not pope.

units.la: 2. In casu praedicto stat aliquos esse, apud quos istud pertinaciter asserere, A. non est papa, saperet haeresim.
units.tr: 2. In the case just stated, to assert stubbornly that A. is not pope would savour of heresy for those to whom it is asserted.

units.la: 3. In schismate praesenti tam dubio temerarium, iniuriosum, & scandalosum est asserere omnes tenentes istam partem vel alteram vel omnes neutrales etiam absolutos esse universaliter extra statum salutis vel excommunicatos vel rationabiliter de schismate suspectos.
units.tr: 3. In the present schism, which is so doubtful, it is rash, injurious and scandalous to assert universally that all who hold either this side or the other, or all neutrals, even those who are absolved, are outside the state of salvation, or excommunicated, or reasonably suspected of schism.

units.la: 4. In schismate praesenti licitum, imo cautum est praestantibus obedientiam isti vel illi, eam sub conditione tacita vel expressa tribuere.
units.tr: 4. In the present schism it is lawful, indeed prudent, for those who render obedience to this or that man to give it under a tacit or express condition.

units.la: 5. Quacunque parte demonstrata temerarium & scandalosum, & sapiens haeresim est asserere: sacramenta ecclesiae suam efficaciam non habere, aut sacerdotes non esse consecratos, pueros non esse baptizatos, sacramentum altaris non esse confectum, & similia.
units.tr: 5. Whichever party is pointed to, it is rash, scandalous, and savours of heresy to assert that the sacraments of the Church have no efficacy, or that priests are not consecrated, that children are not baptized, that the sacrament of the altar is not made, and the like.

units.la: 6. In schismate praesenti temerarium & scandalosum est asserere, quacunque parte demonstrata, quod non licet audire missas eorum vel sacramentis non communicare: praesertim attenta diversitate locorum, temporum atque personarum.
units.tr: 6. In the present schism it is rash and scandalous to assert, whichever party is pointed to, that it is not lawful to hear their masses or to communicate in their sacraments, especially given the diversity of places, times and persons.

units.la: 7. Possibile est aliquos verae parti assentientes esse veraciter schismaticos & aliquos falsae parti modo praedicto assentientes, schismaticos non existere.
units.tr: 7. It is possible that some who assent to the true party are truly schismatics, and that some who assent in the manner described to the false party are not schismatics.

units.la: 8. Salubrius, iustius & tutius est quaerere unitatem ecclesiae insistendo circa contendentes de papatu: & hoc per viam cessionis utriusque vel subtractionis obedientiae, vel alterius licitae coactionis, quam subditos per excommunicationis censuram vel aliter vexare seu turbare: aut quod una pars Christianitatis ab alterius communione pertinaciter separetur.
units.tr: 8. It is more wholesome, more just and safer to seek the unity of the Church by dealing with the contenders over the papacy, and this by way of the resignation of both, or the withdrawal of obedience, or some other lawful constraint, rather than to harass or disturb the subjects by the censure of excommunication or in some other way, or to let one part of Christendom be obstinately separated from the communion of the other.

units.la: Ratio primæ conclusionis hæc est: quoniam nulla propositio, ad cuius verificationem exigitur veritas unius propositionis contingentis & ad fidem impertinentis est de necessitate aut integritate fidei. Nam sicut propositio copulativa, cuius una pars est contingens, est tota contingens cuius una pars est falsa aut impossibilis, est tota falsa aut impossibilis: sic in proposito. Constat autem quod ad verificationem illius, A. est Papa, exigitur non solum una, sed multæ contingentes puræ esse veræ: ut quod electio sit rite celebrata, & ab illis qui habebant potestatem, & consimiles multæ. Ex simili ratione colligitur quod quocunque sacerdote demonstrato, ista non est hæretica, iste non est sacerdos: & consequenter sequitur quod nec ista: hoc non est corpus Christi in altari &c.
units.tr: The reason for the first conclusion is this: no proposition whose verification requires the truth of one contingent proposition that is irrelevant to the faith is a matter of necessity or of the integrity of the faith. For just as a conjunctive proposition, one part of which is contingent, is wholly contingent, and one part of which is false or impossible, is wholly false or impossible, so it is in this case. Now it is clear that to verify A. is pope requires not only one but many purely contingent things to be true, such as that the election was duly celebrated and by those who had the power, and many similar things. By a similar argument it follows that, whichever priest is pointed to, this is not heretical: this man is not a priest; and consequently it follows that neither is this: this is not the body of Christ on the altar, and so on.

units.la: Ratio secundæ propositionis: quoniam propositio dicitur sapere hæresim, quando ex ipsa coassumptis aliquibus veris, quæ rationabiliter negari non possunt, sequitur error in fide: sed possibile est aliquos homines per revelationem vel aliter sic certificatos esse, quod omnia rite facta sunt in electione & consecratione eius in papam A. quod rationabiliter dubitare tunc non possunt. Si negant A. esse vel fuisse papam, incidunt in errorem illum, quod rite electus & consecratus in papam non est, nec unquam fuit papa: & quod non succedit Petro: & similia, quæ sunt hæretica.
units.tr: The reason for the second proposition: a proposition is said to savour of heresy when, from it together with some truths that cannot reasonably be denied, an error in the faith follows. But it is possible that some men, by revelation or otherwise, are so certain that everything was duly done in the election and consecration of A. as pope that they cannot then reasonably doubt it. If they deny that A. is or was pope, they fall into that error, namely that he was not duly elected and consecrated as pope, and never was pope, and that he does not succeed Peter, and similar errors, which are heretical.

units.la: Ratio tertiæ conclusionis: quia multi sunt ex utraque parte & neutrales, quibus non est materia ista clarifica, quin rationabiliter possint negare vel dubitare istam propositionem quocunque contendentium demonstrato: A. est aut fuit rite electus. A. non est schismaticus aut hæreticus: & consimiles, ad quas sequitur: A. non est papa. Assumptum docet experientia, & tot doctorum diversæ aduersæque sententiæ. Et constat multos esse simplices, qui ad talia dubia inquisitionem non tenentur alios sequi: nec moventur favore vel odio seu quæstu ad non consentiendum huic parti vel illi: & parati sunt obedire veritati sufficienter agnitæ: nec sunt pertinaces: igitur nec excommunicati, nec de schismate rationabiliter suspecti. Tota ratio fundatur in hoc, quod nunquam fuit tam rationabilis vehemens causa dubitationis in aliquo schismate, sicut in isto. Cuius signum evidens est varietas opinionum doctorum, & inter doctissimos & probatissimos ex utraque parte: quinetiam suppletis eis, quæ facti sunt concessis adhuc restarent quæstiones iuris ad utrumlibet disputabiles, quæ omnia incertitudinem rationabilem generant in hoc schismate: & ab errore pernicioso plures excusant. Potest igitur illud dici rationabiliter dubitabile, quod plurimi & maxime sapientes dubitabile reputant & præ-licant.
units.tr: The reason for the third conclusion: there are many on both sides, and neutrals, for whom this matter is not so clear that they could not reasonably deny or doubt this proposition, whichever of the contenders is pointed to: A. is or was duly elected; A. is not a schismatic or a heretic, and similar propositions, from which it follows: A. is not pope. Experience teaches the assumption, and so do the diverse and opposed opinions of so many learned men. It is clear that there are many simple people who are not bound, in such doubtful matters, to inquire or to follow others, and who are not moved by favour, hatred or gain to refuse assent to this party or that; they are ready to obey the truth sufficiently recognised, and they are not obstinate. Therefore they are neither excommunicated nor reasonably suspected of schism. The whole argument rests on this: there has never been in any schism so reasonable and powerful a cause for doubt as in this one. A clear sign of this is the variety of opinions among the learned, and among the most learned and most approved on both sides; moreover, even if the facts were granted, questions of law would remain open to dispute on either side, and all of these produce a reasonable uncertainty in this schism and excuse many from a pernicious error. That can therefore reasonably be called doubtful which very many, and especially the wise, regard and proclaim as doubtful.

units.la: Ratio quartæ conclusionis colligitur ex præcedenti; & per simile de adoratione hostiæ in altari, dum occurrit aliqua dubitatio, quod presbyter celebrans non compleuerit omnia rite ad consecrationem requisita, sufficit enim adorare sub conditione implicita: imo semper debet subiungi conditio implicita, ista videlicet vel similis: si omnia rite facta sint secundum institutionem Christi & ecclesiæ. Cur igitur in casu præsentis schismatis tam dubio, & quod non tam proprie tangit statum salutis & fidei, non poterit aut debebit apponi conditio ista vel consimilis: si talis fuerit canonice electus & consecratus, & non sit hæreticus aut schismatice depravatus.
units.tr: The reason for the fourth conclusion follows from the preceding one, and by analogy from the adoration of the host on the altar. When some doubt arises whether the celebrating priest has not completed all the things required by the rite for consecration, it is enough to adore under an implicit condition; indeed, an implicit condition should always be added, namely this or a similar one: if all things have been done rightly according to the institution of Christ and the Church. Why then, in the case of the present schism, which is so doubtful and does not so directly touch the state of salvation and the faith, could this condition or a similar one not be, or not be required to be, attached: if such a man has been canonically elected and consecrated, and is not a heretic or corruptly schismatic?

units.la: Ratio quintæ conclusionis manifesta est aduertenti: quoniam neque schisma neque hæreses neque aliud quodcunque vitium obstat in ministro, quin sacramentorum collatio habeat suam efficaciam: dummodo conferentes intendant id facere, quod Christus & ecclesia instituerunt: & recipiens illud recipere, sicut rationabiliter præsumi debet de omnibus.
units.tr: The reason for the fifth conclusion is plain to anyone who considers it: neither schism, nor heresy, nor any other vice in the minister prevents the conferral of the sacraments from having its efficacy, provided that those who confer them intend to do what Christ and the Church instituted, and that the recipient receives it as it should be presumed reasonably of all.

units.la: Ratio sextæ conclusionis manifestatur ex præcedentibus: quoniam nihil debet rationabiliter a talibus impedire excommunicatio lata, si non adsit pertinacia. Nunquam excommunicatio intenditur ferri, nisi in pertinaces, qui non sunt parati audire ecclesiam. Alioquin frustra ferretur excommunicatio, imo damnabiliter & in ecclesiæ destructionem. Non autem data est potestas ministris ecclesiæ quibuscunque ad destructionem, sed ad ædificationem secundum Apostolum: quemadmodum medicina datur prout conferre possit sanitati, & sanitas rationi. Sic finis excommunicationis est subditorum emendatio: quæ si clare per excommunicationem videatur aut videri debeat non sequi emendatio: vel fructus damnabilis in oppositio conferri videatur, secundum Aug. in parabola de zizaniis. Matt. 13. cum ibidem notatis. Rursus ista conclusio aperte trahitur ex tertia & quarta conclusionibus. Si enim multi ex utraque parte sunt in statu salutis, & non pertinaces: imo parati stare & mori in veritate agnita sufficienter: aut qui sub conditione etiam falsæ partis assentiunt: quæ conditio etiam eoldem ab errore damnabili reddit excusatos: constat quod tales non debuerunt nec potuerunt rationabiliter excommunicari: & per consequens nec eorum communicationem prohibemus.
units.tr: The reason for the sixth conclusion is shown from what precedes: excommunication pronounced should not reasonably hinder such people, if there is no obstinacy. Excommunication is never intended to be pronounced except against the obstinate, who are not ready to hear the Church. Otherwise excommunication would be pronounced in vain, indeed damnably and to the destruction of the Church. But the ministers of the Church have not been given power for destruction, but for edification, according to the Apostle, just as medicine is given so that it may serve health, and health reason. Thus the purpose of excommunication is the amendment of subjects; if it is clear, or ought to be clear, through excommunication that amendment will not follow, or if a damnable fruit seems to result in the opposite, then, according to Augustine in the parable of the tares, Matt. 13, with the notes given there. Again, this conclusion is plainly drawn from the third and fourth conclusions. For if many on both sides are in the state of salvation, and are not obstinate, indeed are ready to stand and die in the truth sufficiently recognised, or if those who assent under a condition even to the false party, a condition which also excuses them from damnable error, it is clear that such people neither ought nor could reasonably be excommunicated, and consequently we do not forbid their communion either.

units.la: Si dicatur, quod etiam excommunicatio iniuste lata timenda est. Hæc propositio male intelligitur a plerisque, & scrupulos varios & periculosos ingerit. Tamen, quantum ad præsens sufficit, respondetur: quod si lator non reputetur iudex, eadem executione qua hoc fit, potest consequenter excommunicatio non tenere. Et quia multi tenentes unam partem, debent rationabiliter tenere, quod alii sint in statu salutis non pertinaces: & parati stare iuri agnito: imo qui forte suo papæ assentiunt sub conditione, possunt ex hoc communicationem eis impendere. Non enim debent suo papæ tale crimen imponere, quod volunt homines non pertinaces excommunicare, vel eos qui tenent antipapam: sub conditione tamen rationabiliter apposita, si & in quantum fuerit rite electus, & non aliter a communione ecclesiastica canonica segregare.
units.tr: If it be said that even an unjustly pronounced excommunication is to be feared: this proposition is badly understood by most people, and it brings in various and dangerous scruples. Yet, as far as the present purpose requires, the answer is this: if the one who pronounces it is not regarded as a judge, the excommunication can consequently have no force, by the same process by which it is pronounced. And since many who hold one party ought reasonably to hold that others are in the state of salvation, not obstinate, and ready to stand by the law as recognised; indeed, those who perhaps assent to their pope under a condition may on this account offer them communion. For they ought not to impute to their pope such a crime that they wish to excommunicate men who are not obstinate, or those who hold the antipope; rather, under the condition reasonably attached, if and insofar as he was duly elected, they should not separate them from canonical ecclesiastical communion.

units.la: Ratio septimæ conclusionis est: quia stat aliquem veræ parti assentientem & pertinacem esse: quod vel propter quæstum, vel propter vanam gloriam, vel aliam causam non habet animum paratum ad obediendum veritati agnitæ: si per ecclesiam vel aliter reperiretur eundem errare: vel etiam dum in tanto dubio inuoluto pro sua assertione sustinenda, separaret se à membris veris & viuis ipsius ecclesiæ. Casus sunt multi de parte opposita, vt dictum est. Non est enim schisma tantum in separatione membrorum à capite, sed etiam in separatione pertinaci membrorum ab inuicem. Ex quo consequetur habetur, quod temerarium & periculosum est pertinaciter vnam partem vel alteram impugnare: & ab eiusdem communione eam detestando declinare. Altera pars conclusionis patet ex tertia conclusione.
units.tr: The reason for the seventh conclusion is this: it may be that someone who assents to the true party is nevertheless obstinate, because on account of profit, vainglory, or some other cause he does not have a mind ready to obey the truth once recognised, should it be found, through the Church or otherwise, that he is in error; or even while, in so great and entangled a doubt, he separates himself, in defence of his own assertion, from the true and living members of the Church itself. There are many cases on the opposite side, as has been said. For a schism lies not only in the separation of members from the head, but also in the obstinate separation of members from one another. From this it follows that it is rash and dangerous to attack obstinately one party or the other, and to shun its fellowship by detesting it. The other part of the conclusion is clear from the third conclusion.

units.la: Ratio octauæ conclusionis perspicua est ex præcedentibus, quoniam vbi radix & origo talis vel principalis ipsius schismatis consistit, ibi eradicatio fieri debet, aut antidotum summi pro vnitatis adeptione. Ipsi enim sunt qui peccauerunt: alii autem qui oues sunt, quid meruerunt? Ipsi sunt propter quos tempestas orta est in mari. Dederunt denique & dant scandalum, propter quod ad illud remouendum de necessitate salutis obligantur. Non negandum tamen est, quod quilibet pro parte sua obligatur secundum donum à Deo sibi præstitum quærere quæ ad pacem sunt: hic orando, ille monendo, alter docendo. Vltima pars, quod non expedit vnam partem generaliter vitare alteram, & facere scissuram in principalioribus actibus religionis Christianæ, & fraternam charitatem violare, patet ex præcedentibus, & principaliter ex quinta conclusione & sexta.
units.tr: The reason for the eighth conclusion is plain from what has gone before: where the root and origin of the schism, or its chief source, lies, there the cure must be applied, or the remedy of the highest authority must be used to attain unity. For it is they who have sinned; but the others, who are sheep, what have they deserved? It is on their account that the storm has arisen at sea. Finally, they have given and still give scandal, and for the removal of this they are bound by necessity of salvation. Yet it must not be denied that each person, according to the gift bestowed on him by God, is bound in his own part to seek the things that make for peace: one by praying, another by admonishing, another by teaching. The last part, that it is not expedient for one party generally to avoid the other, and to make a rent in the principal acts of the Christian religion, and to violate fraternal charity, is clear from what precedes, and chiefly from the fifth and sixth conclusions.

units.la: Verum est enim, quod singularitas in opinione propria contumaciter alios condemnans, incomparabiliter videtur esse periculosior & detetior, quam communicatio fraternalis per charitatem: quæ est compago membrorum ecclesiæ sub intentione semper recta & firma de obediendo ecclesiæ. Etenim qui aliter agit pro incerto vero, ille se exponit certæ violationi fraternæ charitatis.
units.tr: For it is true that singularity in one's own opinion, obstinately condemning others, seems incomparably more perilous and more detestable than fraternal communion through charity, which is the bond of the members of the Church, held always under a right and firm intention of obeying the Church. For whoever acts otherwise, for an uncertain truth, exposes himself to a certain violation of fraternal charity.

units.la: Nec oportet allegare iura super periculis & maledictionibus eorum, qui non obediunt præceptis & institutionibus summi Pontificis & sententiis. Habet enim locum talium allegatio apud illos, qui nulla possunt rationabili causa excusari, quin sciant vel scire debeant talem vel talem esse suum superiorem. Si vero est ignorantia probabilis, sicut est in præsenti schismate apud multos de vtraque obedientia, & apud neutros, non reputantur talibus sententiis alligati. Ex omnibus prædictis videntur posse elici quædam documenta.
units.tr: Nor is it necessary to allege the laws concerning the dangers and curses of those who do not obey the precepts and ordinances of the supreme Pontiff and his sentences. Such an allegation applies to those who cannot be excused by any reasonable cause from knowing, or from being bound to know, that this or that man is their superior. But if the ignorance is probable, as it is in the present schism among many who adhere to either obedience, and among those who adhere to neither, they are not regarded as bound by such sentences. From all the foregoing, certain lessons seem able to be drawn.

units.la: Primum est quod in præsenti schismate potest apud plurimos applicari rationabiliter documentum Ambrosii ad Augustinum de ieiunando vel non ieiunando sabbata secundum diuersitatem temporum, locorum & personarum. Potest sine periculo schismatis aut damnationis, nunc illi, nunc isti modis istis obedire: & nunc cum illis, nunc cum aliis communionem præstare. Et hoc totum dicitur propter probabilem ignorantiam iuris istius vel illius partis. Et supposito quod ab initio schismatis forte tentanda fuisset alia via, ad sciendum si per excommunicationes aut prædicationes vel aliter, omnes ad vnam obedientiam trahi potuissent. Attamen cognitio per experientiam, quod talia nihil proficerent: imo nocuerunt, quod de die in diem maior inuolutio sequitur, videtur faciendum, vt dictum est.
units.tr: The first is that in the present schism, the lesson of Ambrose to Augustine concerning fasting or not fasting on the Sabbath, according to the diversity of times, places and persons, can reasonably be applied to very many. Without danger of schism or damnation, one may now obey this party, now that, in these ways, and now have communion with these, now with those. And all this is said on account of the probable ignorance of the law of this or that party. And even granting that at the beginning of the schism some other way perhaps ought to have been tried, to learn whether by excommunications, or preachings, or otherwise, all might have been drawn to one obedience, yet experience has shown that such things would profit nothing: indeed they have done harm, since from day to day a greater entanglement follows; so it seems that the course stated should be followed.

units.la: Secundum documentum, quod inter omnes eiusdem obedientiæ expedit adhærere sententiis latis à suo superiore credito: alioquin non esset vinculum charitatis.
units.tr: The second lesson: among all those of the same obedience it is expedient to adhere to the sentences pronounced by their believed superior; otherwise there would be no bond of charity.

units.la: Tertium documentum est de casibus reseruatis Papæ, de dispensationibus & aliis in foro conscientiæ vel publico possunt homines secundum credulitatem suæ partis, & ipsos quietare pro facto tenendo id, quod eorum superior creditus fecerit. Neutrales autem videntur habere sufficientem recursum ad ordinarios, apud quos secundum eorum opinionem communiter loquendo, est potestas devoluta. Ver.
units.tr: The third lesson concerns the cases reserved to the Pope, and dispensations and other matters, both in the forum of conscience and in public, which people may, according to the belief of their own party, accept and quiet themselves about, holding as done that which their believed superior has done. Neutrals, however, seem to have sufficient recourse to the ordinaries, to whom, speaking commonly according to their opinion, the power has devolved. Vale.

units.la: Fac pacem Christe, de qua tractatus iste Disputat, atque pia mediatrix esto Maria. Pastor & ecclesia Deus en grex nunc balat ad te, Ergo causa tui nunc miserere sui.
units.tr: Make peace, Christ, the subject of which this treatise disputes, and be the pious mediatrix Mary. Shepherd and Church, God, behold the flock now bleats to you; therefore, for your own cause, now have mercy on your own.

units.la: TRACTATVS DOMINI THEOFORI, QVI ASCRIBITVR IOANNI DE GERSON:
units.tr: TRACTATE OF LORD THEOFORUS, WHICH IS ATTRIBUTED TO JOHN DE GERSON:

units.la: QVALIS FVERIT STATVS ECCLESIAE IN VETERI ET Nouo Testamento: Et qualiter ecclesia fuerit erecta temporibus praedictis, Et quot schismata, & quot intrusiones fuerunt in ecclesia Romana: Et qualiter in schismatibus praeteritis fuerit actum secundum veras chronicas.
units.tr: What the state of the Church was in the Old and New Testaments; and how the Church was established in the aforementioned times; and how many schisms and how many intrusions there were in the Roman Church; and how things were done in past schisms according to the true chronicles.

units.la: Postquam superior status & effectus praesentis schismatis, acta & agenda in universali ecclesia, & specialiter in Roma, secundum veros prophetas digesta & notata sunt. Propleniori notitia praedictorum acuitur stilus, vt secundum veras Chronicas & approbatas: & specialiter Antistitis nostri reuerendi Archiepiscopi Eusontini verissimi antiquitatum relatoris, & Fratris Ptolomei de Luca venerabilis chronistae status & acta praeterita in dicta ecclesia lucidius cognoscantur, & sciantur a lectoribus. Inuenimus enim ego Theoforus & socius meus charissimus Frater Eusebius in praedictis & aliis Chronicis, vt infra dicitur fideliter referendo, quae Eusontinus & Ptolomaeus gesta & acta Romanae ecclesiae denotarunt, a natiuitate Christi vsque ad annum Domini 1316. a quo tempore citra nullum schisma fuit in ecclesia Dei, vsque ad istud nouissimum tempus Petri de Luna & Angeli Corario.
units.tr: After the earlier state and outcome of the present schism, and the acts and matters to be dealt with in the universal Church, and especially in Rome, have been set out and noted according to the true prophets, the pen is sharpened with a fuller knowledge of these things, so that, according to the true and approved chronicles, and especially those of our reverend bishop, the Archbishop of Eusonte, a most accurate reporter of antiquities, and of the venerable chronicler Brother Ptolemy of Lucca, the past state and acts of the said Church may be more clearly known and understood by the readers. For I, Theoforus, and my dearest companion Brother Eusebius, have found in these and other chronicles (as is faithfully reported below) what Eusonte and Ptolemy recorded as the deeds and acts of the Roman Church, from the birth of Christ to the year of the Lord 1316. From that time until this most recent time of Peter de Luna and Angelo Corario, there has been no schism in the Church of God.

units.la: Ex quarum Chronicarum lectione clare reperimus, quod ecclesia tam in Veteri Testamento quam in Nouo exigentibus peccatis & malitia Sathanae multas tribulationes passa est. Tamen ab omni tribulatione ipsam semper Deus liberauit, cum ipsi humiliter & contrito corde ad Deum conuersi sunt veniam petentes & maiorem quietem. Aliqua in Nouo Testamento habuit ecclesia Dei a destructione Frederici Imperatoris Secundi vsque ad tempora bonae memoriae domini Gregorii Papae Vndecimi, quae quies & abundantia diuitiarum reduxerunt ecclesiam in peccata & vitia: propter quae ecclesia patitur praesens schisma; & multa discrimina & maiora patietur.
units.tr: From reading these chronicles we clearly find that the Church, both in the Old Testament and in the New, has suffered many tribulations because of sins and the malice of Satan. Yet God has always delivered it from every tribulation, whenever the people turned to God with humble and contrite hearts, seeking pardon and greater peace. In the New Testament the Church of God enjoyed some quiet from the destruction of the Emperor Frederick II until the times of the good memory of Pope Gregory XI. That quiet and abundance of riches led the Church back into sins and vices, and because of these the Church now suffers the present schism; and it will suffer many greater dangers.

units.la: In Veteri autem Testamento ecclesia multas tribulationes passa est. Primo decem plagas, dum fuit in terra Aegypti. Item in tempore habitae passionis terrae promissionis vsque ad templi aedificationem II. persecutiones passa est ecclesia. Item post templi aedificationem suscitauit durissimam iacturam & schisma: quod fuit inter Roboam & Hieroboam. Item suscitauit transmigrationem totius sacerdotii & destructionem templi in Babyloniam per patrem Nabuchodonosor. Item passa est tempore Nabuchodonosor: quo tempore multi fuerunt pseudo Pontifices maximi & schismata: clerus magnam persecutionem passus: & fuit vltima in Veteri Testamento. Cui persecutioni praesens & persecutio Frederici Tertii, & magni vltimi Antichristi futuri similes erunt secundum Abbatem Ioachim libro de vltimis tribulationibus.
units.tr: In the Old Testament, however, the Church suffered many tribulations. First, the ten plagues, while it was in the land of Egypt. Likewise, during the time from its suffering in the land of promise until the building of the temple, the Church suffered two persecutions. Again, after the building of the temple, it endured the most severe loss and schism, which was between Rehoboam and Jeroboam. Again, it endured the transmigration of the whole priesthood and the destruction of the temple into Babylon under the father Nebuchadnezzar. It suffered again in the time of Nebuchadnezzar, when there were many false supreme pontiffs and schisms, and the clergy suffered a great persecution; and this was the last in the Old Testament. The present persecution, and that of Frederick III, will be like that persecution, and like the persecution of the great Antichrist who is to come, according to Abbot Joachim in his book On the Last Tribulations.

units.la: In Nouo autem Testamento ecclesia etiam varias & diuersas persecutiones passa est exigentibus peccatis & opere naturae humanae hostis. In primitiua enim ecclesia summi Pontifices, Apostoli, praelati & alius clerus, opprobria, damna & iniurias & mortis diuersa martyria passi sunt. Item cessantibus martyriis & crescente dicta ecclesia a Constantino Magno & ab aliis principibus a populo Christiano inceperunt haereses Menandri primi haretici, Arrii, & aliorum haereticorum, maxima scandala generantes in ecclesia Dei.
units.tr: In the New Testament, the Church has also suffered various and diverse persecutions, because of sins and the work of the enemy of human nature. In the primitive Church, the supreme pontiffs, the apostles, the prelates and the other clergy suffered reproach, losses, injuries and diverse kinds of martyrdom and death. Then, when the martyrdoms ceased and the said Church grew under Constantine the Great and other princes of the Christian people, the heresies of Menander, the first heretic, of Arius, and of other heretics began, producing the greatest scandals in the Church of God.

units.la: Postquam autem in ecclesia multiplicata sunt dominia in temporalibus & spiritualibus, inceperunt intrusiones & schismata in Romana ecclesia: propter quae dominia & potestates continue fuerunt odia & rancores inter summos Pontifices, Imperatores Romanos & dominos temporales. Quae schismata fuerunt viginti cum praesenti, & intrusiones 41.
units.tr: But after dominions multiplied in the Church, both temporal and spiritual, intrusions and schisms began in the Roman Church. Because of these dominions and powers there were continual hatreds and rancours between the supreme pontiffs, the Roman emperors and the temporal lords. There have been twenty such schisms, including the present one, and forty-one intrusions.

units.la: Quorum primum schisma incepit anno natiuitatis Domini 244. inter primum Cornelium & Nouatianum. Secundum schisma fuit anno 353. inter Tiberium & Felicem. Tertium anno 374. inter Damasum primum & Visinum. Quartum schisma fuit anno 437. inter Bonifacium primum & Eulalium presbyterum. Quintum anno Domini 516. inter Symachum primum & Laurentium. Sextum anno 723. inter Bonifacium & Dioscorum.
units.tr: The first of these schisms began in the year of the Lord's birth 244, between Cornelius I and Novatian. The second schism was in the year 353, between Liberius and Felix. The third in the year 374, between Damasus I and Ursinus. The fourth schism was in the year 437, between Boniface I and Eulalius the presbyter. The fifth in the year of the Lord 516, between Symmachus I and Laurentius. The sixth in the year 723, between Boniface and Dioscorus.

units.la: Septimum 743. inter Stephanum Tertium sanctum virum, & Constantinum Secundum: quod schisma, si bene videatur quasi per omnia simile est instanti schismati: & plus assimilatur praesenti schismati, quam alia praeterita.
units.tr: The seventh, in 743, between Stephen III, a holy man, and Constantine II. If this schism is looked at carefully, it is in all respects almost like the present schism, and it resembles the present schism more than the other past schisms do.

units.la: Octauum schisma fuit anno 848. inter Eugenium secundum & Sisinum.
units.tr: The eighth schism was in the year 848, between Eugene II and Sisinnius.

units.la: Nonum fuit 930. inter Leonem V. & Christophorum presbyterum.
units.tr: The ninth was in 930, between Leo V and Christopher the presbyter.

units.la: Decimum fuit anno 862. inter Ioannem secundum nobilem Romanum & Leonem VIII.
units.tr: The tenth was in the year 862, between John II, a Roman noble, and Leo VIII.

units.la: Vndecimum fuit 864. inter Gregorium V. & Ioannem episcopum Placentinum.
units.tr: The eleventh was in 864, between Gregory V and John, bishop of Piacenza.

units.la: Duodecimum 999. inter Benedictum IX. & Leonem praedictum.
units.tr: The twelfth, in 999, between Benedict IX and the aforementioned Leo.

units.la: Decimum tertium 1036. tempore Benedicti VIII. qui a Romanis eiicitur & alius intruditur postea Benedictus restituitur.
units.tr: The thirteenth, in 1036, in the time of Benedict VIII, who was driven out by the Romans, and another was then intruded; afterwards Benedict was restored.

units.la: Decimum quartum schisma fuit anno 1052. tempore Benedicti: qui cum iam sedisset multis annis, aliique sunt electi, expulso Benedicto.
units.tr: The fourteenth schism was in the year 1052, in the time of Benedict, who had already sat for many years, and others were elected after Benedict was expelled.

units.la: Decimum quintum fuit 1078. inter Alexandrum II. & Codullum episcopum Permensem.
units.tr: The fifteenth was in 1078, between Alexander II and Cadalus, bishop of Parma.

units.la: Decimum sextum fuit 1085. inter Gregorium & Episcopum Permensem.
units.tr: The sixteenth was in 1085, between Gregory and the bishop of Parma.

units.la: Decimum septimum schisma fuit 1100. inter Pascalem secundum & tres praelatos, qui nomen & officium occupauerunt fauore haeretici Imperatoris.
units.tr: The seventeenth schism was in 1100, between Paschal II and three prelates, who seized the name and office by the favour of the heretical emperor.

units.la: Decimum octauum fuit 1111. inter Gelasium II. & Britodinum Hispanum.
units.tr: The eighteenth was in 1111, between Gelasius II and Burdinus of Spain.

units.la: Decimum nonum fuit 1131. inter Innocentium II. & Petrum Leonis.
units.tr: The nineteenth was in 1131, between Innocent II and Peter Leonis.

units.la: Vicesimum anno 1149. inter Alexandrum III. & quatuor schismaticos.
units.tr: The twentieth, in the year 1149, between Alexander III and four schismatics.

units.la: Vicesimum primum schisma fuit tempore Ludouici de Bauaria: qui Ludouicus veniente & regnante Ioanne XXII. qui Ioannes assumptus fuit ad Papatum Anno Domini 1319. fecit fieri antipapam fratrem Petrum de Carbario Ordinis Minorum, a quo coronam imperii recepit. Tamen facta doctorum antipapae & antiImperatoris annullata sunt infra annos.
units.tr: The twenty-first schism was in the time of Louis of Bavaria, who, during the reign of John XXII (who was raised to the papacy in the year of the Lord 1319), had the friar Peter of Corvara of the Order of Friars Minor made an antipope, and from him received the crown of the empire. Yet the acts of this antipope and anti-emperor were annulled within a few years.

units.la: Vicesimum secundum schisma praesens est & melius coloratum aliquo alio prophetatum a Spiritu sancto pro punitione cleri & reformatione ecclesiae. Circa quorum intrusionem schismatum confectionem processuum ordinationem, oblationem & finem ex flore supradictorum notum est.
units.tr: The twenty-second schism is the present one, and it is better disguised than any other, foretold by the Holy Spirit for the punishment of the clergy and the reform of the Church. Concerning the intrusion, the making of these schisms, the conduct of the proceedings, their presentation and their end, what is known is taken from the flower of the aforementioned accounts.

units.la: Et potest notari singulariter, quod omnia & singula schismata & intrusiones praedicta confecta fota & nutrita semper fuerunt opere ingenio & inuidia pessimorum sacerdotum & cleri Dei: sibi semper fauentibus & auxiliantibus imperatoribus & populo Romano: excepto Carolo magno & tribus Ottonibus primis de Saxonia, qui ecclesiam multum afflictam semper erexerunt.
units.tr: It may be noted particularly that all and each of the aforesaid schisms and intrusions were always made, contrived and fostered by the work, cunning and envy of the worst priests and clergy of God, who were always favoured and aided by the emperors and the Roman people. The exceptions were Charlemagne and the three first Ottos of Saxony, who always raised up the Church when it was sorely afflicted.

units.la: Item notamus quod in omni schismate semper ille vicit & obtinuit, qui habuit ius siue primo siue secundo electus fuisset. Et semper antipapis & sequacibus male successit.
units.tr: Likewise we note that in every schism, the one who prevailed and held the office was always the one who had the right, whether he was elected first or second. And it always turned out badly for the antipopes and their followers.

units.la: Item in omni schismate iste Papa visus est habere ius & obtinuit, qui electus fuit a maiori parte electorum & habentium vocem in electione Papatus.
units.tr: Likewise, in every schism, that pope was seen to have the right and held the office who was elected by the greater part of the electors and of those who had a voice in the election of the papacy.

units.la: Item notamus, quod de conuersione magni Constantini circa & postquam Roma & maxima pars fidem Christi agnouit, quod Imperatores Romani vel populus Romanus 25. veros summos Pontifices expulerunt de Roma: & ipsos diuersis poenitentiis afflixerunt iniuste: quorum summorum Pontificum nomina sunt haec: Iulius I. Simachus, Siluerius I. Vigilius I. Martinus I. Leo III. Eugenius II. Ioannes VIII. Leo V. vel VI. Ioannes X. Benedictus VIII. Iannes XIV. Ioannes XVI. Gregorius V. Benedictus IX. Gregorius VII. Victor III. Pascalis II. Alexander III. Bonifacius VI.
units.tr: Likewise we note that, from the conversion of the great Constantine, when Rome and the greater part of it acknowledged the faith of Christ, the Roman emperors or the Roman people expelled from Rome twenty-five true supreme pontiffs, and unjustly afflicted them with various penalties. The names of these supreme pontiffs are: Julius I, Symmachus, Silverius I, Vigilius I, Martin I, Leo III, Eugene II, John VIII, Leo V or VI, John X, Benedict VIII, John XIV, John XVI, Gregory V, Benedict IX, Gregory VII, Victor III, Paschal II, Alexander III, and Boniface VI.

units.la: Item notatum fuit, quod Reges Franciae, qui pro tempore fuerunt, nunquam in aliquo dictorum schismatum adhaeserunt schismatico, sed semper veris Pontificibus, imo quod plus est, Reges Franciae octo summos Pontifices de sede expulsos posuerunt & reduxerunt in Romam in sedem propriam: quorum summorum Pontificum sunt haec nomina, Vigilius vel Eugenius, Leo, Zacharias, Stephanus, Calixtus, Innocentius, Alexander Tertius & Paschalis.
units.tr: It has also been noted that the kings of France, who reigned in their time, never adhered to any schismatic in any of the said schisms, but always to the true pontiffs. Moreover, what is more, the kings of France set eight supreme pontiffs who had been expelled from their see back in Rome, in their own see. The names of these supreme pontiffs are: Vigilius or Eugene, Leo, Zacharias, Stephen, Callixtus, Innocent, Alexander III and Paschal.

units.la: Item singulariter notatum est: quod quandocunque ecclesia in schismate vel alio modo vacillauit, semper ecclesia erecta fuit per aliquos principes seculares: vt per Carolum M. Ottones de Saxonia, Reges Franciae, commune Pisis seu Pisanos, & diuersos alios. Nunquam enim ecclesia relapsa vel vacillans suis operibus vel viribus se erexit.
units.tr: Likewise it has been noted in particular: whenever the Church has wavered in a schism or otherwise, it has always been set upright again by some secular princes, as by Charlemagne, the Otto of Saxony, the kings of France, the commune of Pisa or the Pisans, and various others. For the Church, when it has fallen back or wavered, has never raised itself up by its own works or strength.

units.la: Item singulariter est notatum, quod nunquam in schismate per ecclesiam concilium generale fuit vocatum. Sed illi qui fuerunt in schismatibus veri Pontifices vocauerunt concilia particularia in diuersis locis, prout videbatur sibi expedire. Tamen non reperio aliquod schisma sine concilio aliquo fuisse ablatum.
units.tr: Likewise it has been particularly noted that in no schism was a general council ever summoned by the Church. But those who were the true popes in the schisms summoned councils of particular scope in various places, as seemed expedient to them. Yet I find that no schism was ended without some council.

units.la: Item reperio quod tempore Gregorii Sexti & Clementis Secundi: quo tempore erat schisma in ecclesia quando Henricus Imperator conuocauit & congregauit concilium generale, non vocatis Papa nec Cardinalibus, qui erant discordes: & quod ibi ordinatum fuit, valuit & seruatum fuit in ecclesia, non obstante absentia Papae & Cardinalium.
units.tr: Likewise I find that in the time of Gregory VI and Clement II, when there was a schism in the Church, the Emperor Henry called and gathered a general council, without summoning the pope or the cardinals, who were at odds; and what was decreed there was valid and was kept in the Church, notwithstanding the absence of the pope and the cardinals.

units.la: Item notatum est, quod aliqui in sede Apostolica & tenentes pacem iuste suis temporibus regnauerunt sine schismate: quorum nomina sunt haec: Ioannes X. Ioannes XVII. Siluester II. Damasus, & Victor II.
units.tr: Likewise it has been noted that some who held the Apostolic See and kept the peace, ruling justly in their own times, reigned without schism. Their names are these: John X, John XVII, Sylvester II, Damasus, and Victor II.

units.la: Item notandum est, quod Leo Papa IV. dubitans, ne eius electio esset bona, renunciauit Papatui: tamen Cardinales videntes eius bonitatem reelegerunt ipsum. Et idem contigit Honorio Secundo, natione Bononiensi.
units.tr: Likewise it is to be noted that Pope Leo IV, doubting whether his election had been valid, resigned the papacy; yet the cardinals, seeing his goodness, re-elected him. The same happened to Honorius II, a native of Bologna.

units.la: Schismata supradicta fideliter extracta sunt a supradictis chronicis: quae patent omnibus volentibus eas audire.
units.tr: The schisms mentioned above have been faithfully extracted from the chronicles cited above, which are open to all who wish to consult them.

units.la: TRACTATVS QVI VULGO ASCRIBITVR IOANNI DE GER- SON, DE VNITATE ecclesiastica.
units.tr: A Treatise Commonly Attributed to John Gerson, On Ecclesiastical Unity.

units.la: VNITATIS ecclesiasticae tractatoribus, vnus ex zelatoribus eiusdem patriam feliciter inuenire. Etsi alligatum corpus vinculis occupationum tenetur, ne pergat ad sacrum concilium, Piis Deo auspice celebrandum: nihilominus verbum Dei (sicut dicit Apostolus) non est alligatum. Propterea decreuit spiritus promptus, & pacis auidissimus verbum aliquod Dei literulis insertum quaqua versum spargere, qua infirma nequit ire caro. Non quidem ad determinandum (absit haec temeritas) sed ad examinandum & dandum sapientibus occasionem & offerendum in tabernaculo Dei cum hominibus, id quod ex talento qualisque scientiae commissum est.
units.tr: To the writers on ecclesiastical unity, one of its zealous advocates wishes a happy outcome. Although the body is held by the chains of business and cannot go to the sacred council to be celebrated at Pisa, by God's favour, nevertheless the word of God (as the Apostle says) is not bound. Therefore a ready spirit, most eager for peace, has resolved to scatter in every direction some word of God set down in small letters, to places where weak flesh cannot go. Not indeed to determine (far be such rashness) but to examine, to give the wise an occasion, and to offer in the tabernacle of God among men what has been entrusted to him, the talent of whatever knowledge he has.

units.la: Vnitas quippe ecclesiastica ad vnum certum Christi vicarium stantibus terminis, in quibus est ecclesia, Anno Domini 440. 29. Ianuarii non est retardanda propter allegationes quasdam ex iuribus positiuis sumptas contra celebrationem concilii generalis: aut viam cessionis, vt quod concilium non potest celebrari sine authoritate Papae. Quia spoliatus ante omnia debet restitui. Quia recusandi sunt tanquam inimici, qui subtraxerunt se ab obedientia. Et allegari potest iustus metus: Quia Papae nemo dicere potest: cur ita facis? praesertim si non sit expresse errans contra articulos fidei, cum a nemine valeat iudicari: & nemini sit subiectus: nec possit effici schismaticus. Quia periculosum est pastori deserere gregem suum cedendo. Rursus quod quilibet fecit debitum suum pro ecclesiastica vnione, nec est in culpa. Denique quod inquirendum est de iustitia verae partis, sine cuius cognitione non possunt hi qui errauerunt poenitere: & si qua sunt similia.
units.tr: The unity of the Church under one certain vicar of Christ, while the terms stand on which the Church depends, in the year of the Lord 440, on 29 January, should not be delayed by certain objections drawn from positive law against the celebration of a general council, or by the way of resignation, namely that a council cannot be celebrated without the authority of the Pope. For the one despoiled must first of all be restored. Those who withdrew from obedience are to be rejected as enemies. A just fear may also be alleged, since no one can say to the Pope, "Why do you act thus?", especially if he is not expressly erring against the articles of faith, since he cannot be judged by anyone, is subject to no one, and cannot be made a schismatic. It is dangerous for a shepherd to desert his flock by ceding. Again, whoever did his duty for ecclesiastical union is not at fault. Finally, what must be inquired into is the justice of the true party, without knowledge of which those who have erred cannot repent; and whatever else is of this kind.

units.la: Ponunt igitur aduersus istas considerationes, 12. generales: quorum explicatio specialis sufficit studiosis ista reuellere.
units.tr: They therefore set against these considerations twelve general ones, whose detailed explanation is enough for diligent readers to refute them.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO I.
units.tr: FIRST CONSIDERATION.

units.la: VNitas ecclesiae generalis sicut impedita est per diuisiones filiorum suorum tanquam membrorum putrescentium & contra Deum peccantium, nam peccata nostra iuxta verbum philosophicum diuiserunt inter nos & Deum. Sic per vnionem oppositam, scilicet per reconciliationem cuiuslibet ad Deum corrigendo prauos mores, humiliando se & orando, rursus debet haec vnitas impetrari: alioquin manente causa schismatis qualis de sua cessatione poterit spes haberi? nisi tantum in pura gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui immeritis & ingratis conferre solet magna: nihilominus coadiutores eius esse nos oportet: nunc praecipue quando pacis inimicus saeuiet acrius, quanto reditus pacis propinquior apparet: immittet quandoq; si poterit validissimum ad continuationem schismatis impedimentum, diuisiones scilicet inter eos, qui prosecuturi sunt vnionem ministerio superbiae, cupiditatis aut inuidiae.
units.tr: The unity of the Church in general is hindered by the divisions of her sons, who are like rotting members sinning against God, for our sins, according to the philosophical saying, have divided between us and God. So this unity must again be obtained by the opposite kind of union, namely by each man's reconciliation to God: correcting bad morals, humbling oneself and praying. Otherwise, while the cause of the schism remains, what hope could there be of its ceasing? Only in the pure grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is accustomed to bestow great things on the undeserving and the ungrateful. Even so, we ought to be his co-workers, especially now, when the enemy of peace will rage more fiercely the nearer the return of peace appears. He will sooner or later, if he can, bring in the most powerful hindrance to the continuance of the schism, namely divisions among those who are about to pursue the union, through the service of pride, greed or envy.

units.la: Secunda Consideratio contra primam allegationem.
units.tr: Second Consideration, against the first objection.

units.la: Vnitas ecclesiae essentialis semper manet ad Christum sponsum suum. Nam caput ecclesiae Christus, in quo sumus omnes vnum secundum Apostolum, etsi non habet vicarium, dum scilicet mortuus est corporaliter & ciuiliter: vel quia non est probabiliter expectandum, quod vnquam sibi vel successoribus suis obedientia praestetur a Christianis: tunc ecclesia tam diuino quam naturali in re, cui nullum obuiat ius positiuum rite intellectum, potest ad procurandum sibi vicarium vnum & certum, semel congregare ad concilium generale repraesentans eam: & hoc non solum authoritate dominorum Cardinalium, sed etiam adiutorio & auxilio cuiuscunque principis vel alterius Christiani. Non enim habet corpus ecclesiae mysticum a Christo perfectissime stabilitum minus ius & robur ad procurationem suae vnionis, quam corpus aliud ciuile, mysticum vel naturale verum, neque enim est de immediato ac immutabili iure diuino vel naturali, quod ecclesia se non possit congregare & vnire & sine Papa aut sine aliquo particulari statu vel collegio, vbi in casu cadere potest mors vel error.
units.tr: The essential unity of the Church always remains with Christ, her bridegroom. For Christ is the head of the Church, in whom we are all one, according to the Apostle. Although he has no vicar, since he is dead bodily and in civil terms, or because it cannot reasonably be expected that obedience will ever be rendered to him or his successors by Christians, the Church, in a matter that is both divine and natural and to which no positive law rightly understood stands in the way, can gather itself once into a general council, representing her, in order to secure for herself one certain vicar. She may do this not only by the authority of the lord Cardinals, but also with the help and aid of any prince or other Christian. For the mystical body of the Church, most perfectly established by Christ, has no less right and strength to procure its union than any other civil, mystical or true natural body. Indeed, it is not by immediate and unchangeable divine or natural law that the Church cannot gather and unite itself without the Pope, or without some particular state or college, where death or error may befall.

units.la: Tertia Consideratio contra secundam allegationem.
units.tr: Third Consideration, against the second objection.

units.la: Vnitas ecclesiae ad vnum certum vicarium Christi, qui quodammodo accidentalis atque mutabilis est, non debet impediri minime vel differri propter contentionem duorum de Papatu, aut fautorum suorum, si quaerant sic manere per allegationes iurium positiuorum: & iustificationes varias, & conquestiones quod sunt spoliati: & quod debent ante omnia restitui, vel aliunde. Sed videtur rur expedients, quod ea quae retro sunt obliuiscentes isti de concilio, in anteriora sicut Apostolus loquitur, se extendant: vt iuxta narrationem ab Augustino commemoratam, plus quaeratur quomodo liberabitur ecclesia ab hac schismatis touea profundissima, quam qualiter & a quibus in eam est prolapsa.
units.tr: The unity of the Church under one certain vicar of Christ, who is in some measure accidental and changeable, ought not in the least to be impeded or deferred because of the dispute between two claimants to the Papacy, or their supporters, if they seek to maintain their position by objections drawn from positive law, by various justifications, by complaints that they have been despoiled, and by the claim that they must first be restored, or on any other ground. But it seems more useful that those men, forgetting what lies behind them, should stretch forward to what lies ahead, as the Apostle puts it. So, following the account recorded by Augustine, more care should be taken to inquire how the Church may be freed from this most deep pit of schism, than how and by whom she fell into it.

units.la: Quarta Consideratio contra sextam allegationem.
units.tr: Fourth Consideration, against the sixth allegation.

units.la: Vnitas ecclesiae ad vnum certum Christi vicarium sic amanda est, vt pro sua adeptione possint rationabiliter plurima mala singularium personarum dimitti, nunc vel in posterum sine poena. Et quaedam vera singularia iura possunt differri: sic quod fiat cessatio voluntaria de eis, vel etiam coacta per auctoritatem concilii. Hoc nimirum dictat naturae lex, vt pars quaelibet pro suo toto saluando se det & exponat. Quia si quis contendentium iustificare se seu iniuste secum agi contenderit, dicatur ei: tu te tuaque omnia debes ecclesiae: tu qui pastorem te nominas, quantumcunque sis innocens, debes pro ea vel saluanda, vel vnienda, vel non graviter scandalizanda paratus esse ponere vitam propriam: quanto magis quamlibet dignitatem quaerendo quae sunt Iesu Christi: & hoc non secundum dictamen proprium vel carnale, sed publicum & incorruptum spirituale, prout concilium, quod utique sapiens est, iudicabit. Neque prorsus hoc agendo deseres gregem: sed pasces, vnies & manere diceberis.
units.tr: The unity of the Church under one certain vicar of Christ must be so loved that, in order to obtain it, many wrongs done to particular persons may reasonably be set aside, both now and in future, without penalty. Certain true particular rights may also be deferred, so that they are voluntarily given up by those concerned, or even surrendered under compulsion by the authority of the Council. Natural law certainly dictates this: every part should give and expose itself for the saving of its whole. For if one of the contenders should claim to be justified, or to be treated unjustly, let it be said to him: you and all that you have belong to the Church. You who call yourself a minister must be ready to lay down your own life, however innocent you are, for her preservation, her unity, or to avoid grave scandal to her; how much more, then, should you seek no dignity at all in preference to the things of Jesus Christ. And this is to be done not according to your own or carnal judgment, but according to the public and incorrupt judgment of the spirit, as the Council, which is certainly wise, shall decide. By acting in this way you will not desert the flock at all; rather you will feed it, unite it, and be said to remain.

units.la: Quinta Consideratio.
units.tr: Fifth Consideration.

units.la: Vnitas ecclesiae ad vnum Christi vicarium non habet necesse, quod nunc procuretur seruando terminos literales, aut ceremoniales iurium positiuorum, aut processuum ordinariorum, in euocationibus, accusationibus, dilationibus aut similibus: sed summarie & de bona grossaque aequitate potest procedere concilium istud generale. In quo residebit sufficiens authoritas iudicialis vtendi ἀπεικέᾳ, id est, interpretandi omnia iura positiva, & ad finem celeriorem & salubriorem habendae vniones eadem adaptandi, aut si opus fuerit relinquendi. Quod enim pro ecclesiastica pace & salute institutum est, si rite & non tyrannica malignitate fuerit institutum, non debet contra eam militare, ne potestas data videatur constitutionibus humanis in destructionem ecclesiae, non in eius aedificationem. Authoritas vero doctrinaliter vtendi ἀπεικέᾳ, residet principaliter apud peritos in Theologia, quae est architectoria respectu aliarum. Et consequenter apud peritos in scientia iuris canonici & civilis, prout ex principiis iuris diuini & naturalis habeant accipere fundamenta.
units.tr: The unity of the Church under one vicar of Christ does not require that it now be pursued by observing the literal and ceremonial terms of positive laws, or the ordinary procedures in summonses, accusations, delays, or the like. Rather, this general Council may proceed summarily and by good and broad equity. In it there will reside sufficient judicial authority to use epieikeia, that is, to interpret all positive laws and to adapt them, or if necessary to set them aside, so as to bring about unions more quickly and beneficially. For what has been instituted for the peace and salvation of the Church, if it was rightly instituted and not by tyrannical malice, ought not to work against her, lest the power given to human constitutions seem to be used for the destruction of the Church and not for her building up. The authority to use epieikeia in matters of doctrine resides principally with those skilled in Theology, which is the architectonic science with respect to the others; and consequently with those expert in canon and civil law, insofar as they must take their foundations from the principles of divine and natural law.

units.la: Sexta Consideratio contra quartam allegationem.
units.tr: Sixth Consideration, against the fourth allegation.

units.la: Vnitas ecclesiae ad vnum certum Christi vicarium, videtur per concilium nunc celebrandum sic procuranda: quod primo detur securitas tam per principes quam per alios quoscunque pro duobus contendentibus, si voluerint comparere procedendo ad implendum iuramenta sua atque vota. Quod si noluerint considere, quaeratur ab eis cessio per procuratores legitimos. Quod si vtrumque contempserint, procedatur contemptis ambobus contendentibus ad electionem vnius per communem assensum totius concilii roborantis & approbantis illud, quod duo de collegio dominorum Cardinalium aut eorum pars maior & sanior constituerint aut fecerint. Quod si voluerint aliqui pertinaciter adhaerere alteri contendentium: nec insequi sententiam concilii, quod non est leuiter praesumendum, viderint ipsi de salute sua: quia concilium istud & sequaces eius se apud Deum & homines a schismatis imputatione liberauerit.
units.tr: The unity of the Church under one certain vicar of Christ seems to be promoted, as the Council now to be held should do it, in this way: first, security should be given, both by the princes and by all others, to the two contenders, if they are willing to appear and proceed to fulfil their oaths and vows. But if they are unwilling to submit, let a cession be sought from them through lawful proctors. If they despise both of these, let the process go forward, both contenders being set aside, to the election of one by the common assent of the whole Council, confirming and approving what the two of the college of the lord Cardinals, or the greater and sounder part of them, have determined or done. But if any should obstinately cling to one of the contenders and not follow the sentence of the Council (which is not lightly to be presumed), let them look to their own salvation; for this Council and its followers will have freed themselves before God and men from the charge of schism.

units.la: Septima Consideratio contra tertiam allegationem.
units.tr: Seventh Consideration, against the third allegation.

units.la: Vnitas ecclesiae ad vnum certum Christi vicarium sic priuilegiata & sancta est: vt eam syncero zelo quaerentes, nullo modo debent reputari a contendentibus sui aduersarii, sed amicissimi in Christo, dum cessionem ipsorum voluntariam quaerunt: vel eis nolentibus cedere petunt deiectionem, quatenus vt spiritus eorum saluus fiat, nec ecclesia diutius perturbetur. Agunt quippe tam rem ipsorum contendentium, quam id quod quilibet Christianus agere debet. Imo iussionem Dei habent in tam desperato & inueterato matris communis morbo. Haec est radix inuiolanda & sufficiens piae necessitatis & necessariae pietatis: in qua Christianissimus rex Francorum, vere innocentissimus, nec quaerens quae sua sunt, nec quempiam odio habens, fundauit hactenus omnem agibilium varietatem laudabilem circa pacis reductionem, sicut litera sua patens indicat: cuius initium est post salutationem Pax ecclesiastica, &c. Praeclaram itaque attulit excusationem Cicero in Philippicis, dum inconstans inamicitia Caesaris & varius fuisse culparetur: cuius est haec sententia, quia verba non habeo: Caesarem, ait, nunquam dilexi nisi pro quanto diligere visus est rempublicam. Dum ergo mutauit amorem ad eandem rempublicam, factus tyrannus: ego consequenter aduersus eum amicitiam commutaui.
units.tr: The unity of the Church under one certain vicar of Christ is so privileged and holy that those who seek it with sincere zeal must in no way be regarded by the contenders as their adversaries, but as their dearest friends in Christ, while they seek their voluntary cession or, if they are unwilling to yield, ask for their deposition, so that their souls may be saved and the Church be no longer troubled. For they act both in the interest of the contenders themselves and in what every Christian ought to do. Indeed, they have God's command for so desperate and long-standing a disease of their common mother. This is the inviolable root and sufficient ground of pious necessity and necessary piety, on which the most Christian King of the French, truly most innocent, seeking neither his own things nor hating anyone, has hitherto founded every praiseworthy course of action concerning the restoration of peace, as his open letter shows, whose beginning after the greeting is "Ecclesiastical peace," etc. Cicero, in the Philippics, offered a fine excuse when his inconsistent unfriendliness and changeableness toward Caesar were blamed; his statement is this, "I have no words: I never loved Caesar except insofar as he seemed to love the commonwealth. Since he changed his love for the same commonwealth, becoming a tyrant, I in turn changed my friendship toward him."

units.la: Consideratio octaua contra tertiam allegationem.
units.tr: Eighth Consideration, against the third allegation.

units.la: Vnitas ecclesiae ad vnum certum Christi vicarium non debet impediri propter restitutionem obedientiarum ambobus contendentibus tanquam spoliati sint prius faciendam. Nam quod iniustus detentor vel praedo spoliatus sit restituendus, est magis ex institutione positiua & iudiciaria, non pure naturali vel diuina. Propterea tenet in solis casibus expressis, nec in praeiupræiudicium iuris diuini, & naturalis, & boni communis est aliquatenus obseruanda. Neque enim restitutio debet fieri (exempli gratia) hæreticis, neque schismaticis manifestis, neque furiosis, & ebriisin sui perniciem, neque intrusis in Papatum, neque perentibus vxorem non desponsabilem, aut affinem in gradu prohibito iure diuino, ueque petenti beneficium quod tenere non potuit, alio iam existente legitimo possessore, neque postremo volenti rebus detentis abutii in contumeliâ creatoris, aut in ecclesiæ perniciem, aut in hominis liberi seruitutem, aut contra castitatem alicuius & vitam: & si qua sunt similia. Multas autem exceptiones huiusmodi contra contendentium quemlibet interuenire videre facile est.
units.tr: The unity of the Church under one certain vicar of Christ must not be hindered on account of the restitution of obediences to both contenders, as though they had first to be restored as despoiled persons.
