For that a despoiled person be restored by an unjust holder or robber is derived more from positive and judicial institution than from what is purely natural or divine. Therefore it holds only in the expressly stated cases, and is not to be observed in any way to the prejudice of divine, natural and common good law. For restitution ought not to be made (for example) to heretics, to manifest schismatics, to madmen and drunkards to their own ruin, to intruders into the Papacy, to those who seek a wife who is not marriageable, or who is related within a degree prohibited by divine law, nor to one who asks for a benefice which he could not hold, another lawful possessor already existing, nor finally to one who wishes to abuse the things he holds to the dishonour of the Creator, to the ruin of the Church, to the enslavement of a free man, or against someone's chastity and life; and whatever else is similar. It is easy to see that many exceptions of this kind arise against each of the contenders.

units.la: Consideratio nona contra octauam allegationem.
units.tr: Ninth consideration, against the eighth allegation.

units.la: Vnitas ecclesiæ ad vnum certum Christi vicarium videtur melius procuranda, si neque ante concilium, neque in concilio, neque postmodum quærantur fieri iustificationes vel iniustificationes eorum, quæ hincinde facta sunt: vt de intrusione huius vel illius in Papatum : de processibus primo fulminatis in alterutrum: de violatione iuramentorum & votorum : de subtractione aut neutralitate: vel libertatis ecclesiarum particularium reductione: de imputatione schismatum vel hæresum: de adhæsione reprobanda vel laudanda alterius partis obedientiæ: de sententiis excommunicationum aut aliarum pœnarum.
units.tr: The unity of the Church under one certain vicar of Christ would seem better secured if, neither before the council, nor in the council, nor afterwards, people sought to make justifications or unjustifications of those things that have been done on either side: such as the intrusion of this or that man into the papacy; the processes first thundered against each other; the violation of oaths and vows; withdrawal or neutrality; the reduction of the liberty of particular churches; the imputation of schisms or heresies; the approval or disapproval of adherence to one or other obedience; and sentences of excommunication or other penalties.

units.la: Cessent quippe talia, & iuxta rationes pro via cessionis & practicam eius alias pluries ostensam procedatur auferendo processus factos & iustificando vel ratificando aut etiam tollerando præterita, prout rerum qualitas patitur, aut plurima ad statum quo prius erant ante schisma præsens absque alia discussione reponendo: prouidendo rursus ambobus contendentibus de sufficienti securitate & statu post cessionem, si eam per se vel procuratores legitimos vltro facere etiam sero voluerint: quæ cessio eis per concilium pro purgatione omnium prius impositorum tanquam sufficiens reputetur valitura.
units.tr: Let such things cease, and, according to the reasons already given for the way of cession and the practice of it shown on many other occasions, let us proceed by annulling the processes that have been made, and by justifying, ratifying or even tolerating what has gone before, as the nature of the matters allows, or by restoring most things to the state they were in before the present schism, without any further discussion. Let provision also be made for both contending parties, with sufficient security and a secure standing after the cession, if they are willing, even late, to make it themselves or through lawful proxies of their own accord. This cession should be held by the council, as sufficient for the purging of all the charges previously laid, to be valid.

units.la: Consideratio decima contra septimam & quintam allegationem.
units.tr: Tenth consideration, against the seventh and fifth allegations.

units.la: Vnitas ecclesiæ ad vnum certum Christi vicarium tanto zelo quærenda est, vt vix possit sobria esse, & non temeraria reputatio alicuius Christiani, quod sufficienter ad hoc dubiû peregerit: quanto minus hoc quispiam audere debet asserere iuramento: præsertim vbi hominum maxima multitudo reputat contrarium, hoc enim quid aliud est quam pertinaciter & incorrigibiliter talem in erratis persistere?
units.tr: The unity of the Church under one certain vicar of Christ is to be sought with such zeal that scarcely any Christian could be sober, and not rash, in judging that he has sufficiently settled this doubt; how much less ought anyone to dare to assert it on oath, especially where the greatest multitude of men thinks the contrary? For what else is this than to persist obstinately and incorrigibly in error?

units.la: Rursus occurrere possunt casus multi, in quibus pro adeptione pacis publicæ aut iustæ defensionis, sicut vim vi repellendo, liceret à rite electo in Papam subtrahere obedientiam. Liceret in neutralitate manere: liceret ipsum corporaliter incarcerare: liceret ei administrationem omnem publicam interdicere: liceret per appellationem aut simile remedium sibi resistere, fieretque sic ei obedientia vera potius quam contradictio vel resistentia. Liceret præmissas sententias suas quascunque non timere, nec timendas asserere, sed lacerare eas & in caput suum retorquere. Liceret præterea accusare eum de schismate vel hæresi, tam doctrinaliter in locis publicis per Theologos & sapientes, quam secrete in correctione fraterna: cum subiicitur tanquam peccator in foro pœnitentiæ & iuridice coram tota ecclesia: cui similiter subiectus est tanquam deuiabilis in deuiabili. Liceret concilium generale eo inuito celebrare. Liceret tandem ipsum ad cessionem compellare vel renitentem deiicere ab omni honore & gradu: imo & vita priuare.
units.tr: Again, many cases can arise in which, in order to obtain public peace or just defence, it would be lawful, just as force is repelled by force, to withdraw obedience from one who has been duly elected as Pope. It would be lawful to remain neutral; lawful to imprison him bodily; lawful to forbid him all public administration; lawful to resist him by appeal or a similar remedy, and so obedience would be rendered to him in truth rather than contradiction or resistance. It would be lawful not to fear any sentences whatever that he might pronounce, nor to assert that they are to be feared, but to tear them up and turn them back upon his own head. It would moreover be lawful to accuse him of schism or heresy, both doctrinally in public places by theologians and wise men, and secretly in fraternal correction, when he is subjected as a sinner in the forum of penance, and judicially before the whole Church, to which he is likewise subject as one who may err, within the sphere of error. It would be lawful to hold a general council even though he is unwilling. It would be lawful, finally, to compel him to cession, or, if he resists, to depose him from every honour and rank, and even to deprive him of life.

units.la: Hæc omnia denique taliter licere possunt sub tali iure diuino & naturali: quod aduersus hanc veritatem nulla lex vel constitutio puri hominis cuiuscunque sine noua authorizatione Dei fieri debet, quin erroris intolerabilis damnanda sit. An vero prædicti casus in schismate præsenti concurrerint discutiendo nequaquam assumimus, cum distinctiones particularium casuum omitti debere magis æstimemus.
units.tr: All these things, finally, may be lawful under such divine and natural law, that no law or constitution of any mere man whatever, made without fresh authorization from God, ought to be made against this truth, unless it is to be condemned as intolerable error. Whether the aforesaid cases have indeed occurred in the present schism we do not undertake to discuss at all, since we judge that the distinctions of particular cases ought to be omitted.

units.la: Consideratio vndecima contra octauam allegationem.
units.tr: Eleventh consideration, against the eighth allegation.

units.la: Vnitas ecclesiæ ad vnum certum Christi vicarium non requirit, vt errantes præsertim in dubio probabili circa obedientiam veri Papæ pœnitere non possint: nec esse in statu salutis, nisi expressè & absolute confiteantur errratum suum: cum sæpe in talibus pœnitentia vel absolutio conditionata sufficiat. Sed nec oportet omnes inculpare de schismate, qui in tanta iuris papalis dubietate consurgente ex factis dubiis & variis, certam vero Papæ non præstiterunt obedientiam. Sicut nempe verus Papa potuit in schismatis culpam labi, si pertinax fuerit in recusando eam, quæ pacem vniuersalem habebant reducere: & vt concilium generale, vel promptitudinem animi ad viam cessionis iuratæ & voti complementum. Sic excusari poterunt multi aduersantes ei, si fuerit hoc zelo vnionis habendæ: si fuerit ex dubio probabilis ignorantiæ: dum tamen paratos semper ecclesiam exhibuerint semetipsos, & obedire cognitæ veritati.
units.tr: The unity of the Church under one certain vicar of Christ does not require that those who err, especially in a probable doubt about the obedience owed to the true Pope, be unable to repent, nor that they be in no state of salvation unless they expressly and absolutely confess their error, since in such matters repentance or conditional absolution often suffices. Nor is it right to blame all for the schism who, amid so great a doubt of papal law arising from doubtful and various facts, did not render certain obedience to the Pope. Just as the true Pope himself could have fallen into the guilt of schism, if he were obstinate in refusing what would have restored universal peace, such as a general council, or readiness of mind for the way of sworn cession and the fulfilment of a vow. So many who opposed him may be excused, if this was done from zeal for achieving unity, or from a doubt of probable ignorance, provided that they have always shown themselves ready to hear the Church and to obey the truth once known.

units.la: Consideratio duodecima.
units.tr: Twelfth consideration.

units.la: Vnitas ecclesiæ ad vnum certum Christi vicarium sicut inchoanda impetrandaque est per orationes deuotas, & morum correctionem: sic in eius reformatione à summo vsque deorsum per omnem suorum membrorum principalium vel non principalium iunctuarm, debet, cum facta fuerit, studium vehementissimum & continuũ adhiberi, ne iusto Dei iudicio deterius quid contingat si post concessam Dei misericordiam vnionis salutarem recidiuatio prior fiat. Qualia vero in ecclesiastica politia veniant reformanda, poterunt docere tam libri experientiæ, quam multiplices chartulæ iam super hoc editæ & relationes ecclesiasticorum in concilio fide dignæ. Denique, si contigerit forsitan generale concilium retardari propter principum vel aliorum in diuersis patriis diuisiones vel aliunde, sic quod multi notabiles vel nequeant vel noluerint comparere: nec mittere sed differre: & domini Cardinales vtrobiq; sentiant probabili coniectura, quod tales multi & magni de vtraq; parte non obediunt suæ electioni: videretur expediens in hoc casu, quod ipsi Cardinales comparentes in concilio inuenirent saltem modum tollendi perpetuitatem in hoc schismate, prouidendo quod post decessum amborum contendentium: & si non citius pax haberetur, quia melius esset sero quam nunquam: & hoc iuxta modum, qui in alio concilio Franciæ fuit conclusus, vt per suos Ambasiatores quæreretur & prosequeretur apud ambos contendentes & sua collegia de non eligendo, scil. quempiam in casu mortis huius & illius, cum cæteris clausulis ad hoc opportunis.
units.tr: The unity of the Church under one certain vicar of Christ, just as it must be begun and obtained through devout prayers and the correction of morals, so, once it has been brought about, must be maintained with the most vehement and continual zeal, from the top down through every principal and non-principal joint of its members, lest, by the just judgment of God, something worse happen, if after God's merciful grant of a saving union a former relapse should occur. What things in the ecclesiastical polity need reforming can be taught both by the books of experience and by the many pamphlets already published on this matter, and by the reports of churchmen worthy of belief in council. Finally, if perhaps it should happen that the general council is delayed on account of divisions among princes or others in the various countries, or for some other reason, so that many notable persons either cannot or will not appear, and do not send representatives but postpone; and if the lord Cardinals on both sides perceive by probable conjecture that such many and great men on either side do not obey their election, it would seem expedient in this case that the Cardinals themselves, attending the council, should at least find a way of removing the perpetuity of this schism, providing that, after the death of both contending parties, and if peace is not had sooner (since it would be better late than never), it be done in the manner that was concluded at another council in France, namely that by their ambassadors it be sought and pursued with both contending parties and their colleges not to elect anyone in the event of the death of this one or that one, together with the other clauses suited to this purpose.

units.la: PARS SECVNDA. SEQVVNTVR QVATVOR CON- SIDERATIONES, AD FVLCIMENTVM ET declarationem præmissorum.
units.tr: PART TWO. FOUR CONSIDERATIONS FOLLOW, TO SUPPORT AND EXPLAIN THE FOREGOING.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO PRIMA.
units.tr: FIRST CONSIDERATION.

units.la: VNitas ecclesiæ ligatur quadruplici lege: diuina scilicet vel euangelica, naturali, canonica & ciuili. Quarum duas extremas regulare necesse est per primas secundum ἐπιεικείαν, id est bonam æquitatem. Hoc itaque ex traditionibus earundem legum vltimarum conuincitur: quarum annotationes aliquas pro minus eruditis & literatis placet adducere.
units.tr: The unity of the Church is bound by a fourfold law: divine or evangelical, natural, canonical and civil. Of these, the two outermost must necessarily be regulated by the first, according to equity [ἐπιεικείαν], that is, good fairness. This is proved from the traditions of those last two laws, and I think it fitting to set out some notes from them for the less learned and literate.

units.la: Prima annotatio: Non debet reprehensibile iudicari: sed secundum varietatem temporum statuta quandoque variantur humana: præsertim cum vrgens necessitas vel euidens vtilitas id exposcit, quoniam ipse Deus ex his, quæ in Veteri Testamento statuerat, nonnulla mutauit in Nouo. Hæc Innocentius Tertius in concilio generali: & habentur in decretali, Non debet, de consanguinitate & affinitate, in antiquis.
units.tr: First note: A thing should not be judged blameworthy merely because human statutes are sometimes varied according to the changing times, especially when pressing necessity or clear utility demands it, since God himself changed some of the things he had laid down in the Old Testament in the New. Innocent III said this in a general council, and it is found in the decretal Non debet, de consanguinitate et affinitate, in antiquis.

units.la: Secunda annotatio: Quoniam nulla iuris sanctio quantumcunque perpenso digesta concilio ad humanæ naturæ varietatem & machinationes eius inopinabiles sufficit: nec ad decisionem lucidum suæ nodosæ ambiguitatis attingit: eo præsertim, quod nihil adeo certum clarumque statuitur, quin ex causis emergentibus, quibus iura iam prædicta mederi non possunt, in dubium reuocetur, &c. Hæc Ioan. XXII. in proœmio Clementi.
units.tr: Second note: No legal enactment, however carefully drawn up by a council, is adequate to the varied nature of human beings and their unforeseeable schemes, nor does it reach a clear decision on its knotty ambiguity. This is especially so because nothing is established so firmly and clearly that it cannot be called back into doubt by emerging circumstances which the aforesaid laws cannot remedy, and so on. John XXII said this in the preface to the Clementines.

units.la: Tertia annotatio: Non possunt omnes casus seu iuris articuli legibus comprehendi: sed cum aliquo casu sententia legum manifesta est, is qui iurisdictioni præest ad similia procedere, atque ius ita dicere debet. Hæc habentur in L. non possunt. ff. de legibus.
units.tr: Third note: Not all cases or articles of law can be embraced by laws. But when the sense of a law is clear in one case, the one who presides over jurisdiction ought to proceed in similar cases and so declare the law. This is found in L. non possunt, ff. de legibus.

units.la: Quarta annotatio: Certum est, quod is committit in legem, qui legis verba complectens, contra legis nititur voluntatem, hoc habetur in regula iuris Certum in 6. Contra facit qui id facit quod lex prohibet. In fraudem legis facit, qui saluis verbis legis sententiam eius circumuenit. Hæc habentur in L. contra legem ff. de legibus.
units.tr: Fourth note: It is certain that he commits an offence against the law who, while keeping to the words of the law, strives against its will; this is found in the rule of law Certum in the Sixth Book. He acts against the law who does what the law forbids. He acts in fraud of the law who, with the words of the law left intact, gets around its sense. This is found in L. contra legem, ff. de legibus.

units.la: Quinta annotatio: Nulla iuris ratio aut æquitatis benignitas patitur, vt quæ sa ubritet pro vtilitate hominum introducuntur, ea nos interpretatione duriore contra ipsorum commoda perducamus ad seueritatem. Hæc habentur in l. nulla ff. de legibus. Cum quo concordat regula iuris canonici in 6. Quod ob gratiam alicuius conceditur, non est in eius dispendium retorquendum. Item Ipsa leges cupiunt, vt iure regantur.
units.tr: Fifth note: No principle of law or kindness of equity allows us to take things introduced for the good of men and, by a harsher interpretation, turn them to severity against their own advantage. This is found in l. nulla, ff. de legibus. In agreement with this is the rule of canon law in the Sixth Book: What is granted for someone's favour is not to be turned to his loss. Likewise: The laws themselves wish to be governed by law.

units.la: Item ait Scipio Nasica: Consul dum iuris ordinem sequitur; id agit vt cum legibus suis Romanum corruat imperium. Ideo iuris ordo est in casu, vt scilicet iuris ordo non seruetur.
units.tr: Scipio Nasica also said: When the consul follows the order of law, he brings it about that the Roman empire falls along with its laws. Therefore the order of law applies in a case where the order of law is not to be observed.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO II.
units.tr: SECOND CONSIDERATION.

units.la: Vnitas ecclesiæ ad vnum certum Christi vicarium nequit modo procurari commode sine recursu ad ἐπιεικείαν, seu bonam æquitatem: quæ interpretatur literam iurium positiuorum secundum intentionem legislatorum radicatam in legibus æternis ac immutabilibus diuinæ legis, per quam legum conditores iusta decernunt, atque secundum dictamen legis naturalis. Hic autem processus antonomatice & summe iudicandus erit iuridicus, si innitetur legibus & iuribus & canonibus, proprie & vero nomine sic vocandus.
units.tr: The unity of the Church cannot now be conveniently secured under one certain vicar of Christ without recourse to equity [ἐπιεικείαν], or good fairness, which interprets the letter of positive laws according to the intention of the lawgivers. That intention is rooted in the eternal and unchangeable laws of the divine law, by which lawgivers decree what is just, and in accordance with the dictate of natural law. This process will rightly be judged juridical par excellence and in the highest degree if it rests on laws, rights and canons, and is properly so called.

units.la: Veritas considerationis legitur clarissime in libro experientiæ prudentes & circumspectos, nec proteruos, nec male affectatos: dum considerant materiam præsentis schismatis cum circumstantiis omnibus, quales nunquam visæ sunt concurrisse in aliquo casu lege positiua memo-rato.
units.tr: The truth of this consideration is read most clearly in the book of experience by prudent and circumspect men, neither headstrong nor ill-disposed, when they weigh the matter of the present schism with all its circumstances, such as have never been seen to coincide in any case mentioned in positive law.

units.la: Quid igitur mirandum, si non habetur in eisdem traditionibus positiuis modus ad remediandum expressus? quemadmodum multi vigebant morbi prius quam leges nunc conditæ latæ essent, quibus non erat expresse prouisum: & cum leges huiusmodi factæ sunt, constat quod non poterunt infinitati casuum possibilium prouidere. Sunt autem ipsius iuris diuini & naturalis regulæ tales immobiles & æternæ, vt exempli gratia, Principia iuris diuini & naturalis: Obedire oportet Deo magis quam hominibus. Dedit Deus potestatem hominibus in ædificationem, non in destructionem ecclesiæ. Nihil possumus contra veritatem. Plenitudo legis atque finis eius est dilectio. Dilectio est causa vnionis atque pacis. Dilectio non quærit quæ sua sunt. Finis omnis potestatis & Hierarchia ecclesiastica est dilectio, pax & vnio. Finis imposuit necessitatem his, quæ ad finem sunt, id est secundum exigentiam finis cætera debent moderari. Necessitas non habet legem. Felix necessitas quæ ad meliora compellit. Bonus pastor ponit animam suam pro ouibus suis vniendis & saluandis. Inimici hominis domestici eius, id est carnales sensus. Spiritualis homo omnia diiudicat. Medium virtutis accipiendum est, vt sapiens iudicabit. Vim vi repellere. Fas est vnicuique se tueri & rem suam defendere contra vim iniustam. Qui suo iure vtitur, nemini facit iniuriam. Deteriora sunt animarum quam corporalium vel rerum exteriorum detrimenta. Depositum non est reddendum in depositarii vel reipublicæ detrimentum. Salubrius panis aut vestis aut gladius abusiuus subtrahitur, quam donatur. Vnicuique mandauit Deus de proximo suo: diliges, inquit, proximum tuum sicut teipsum. Quod pro charitate institutum est, contra charitatem militare non debet. Si pes tuus aut manus (& ita de capite) scandalizat te, proiice abs te. Qui ecclesiam non audierit, sit sicut ethnicus & publicanus. Tolleranda sunt zizania, ne simul eradicetur & triticum. Communis error facit ius. Non periurabis. Reddes altissimo vota tua. Omne iuramentum & votum quod sine detrimento salutis potest custodiri, seruandum est. Cuius est condere vel doctrinaliter vel iudicialiter, eius est similiter interpretari. Intelligentia dictorum ex causis assumenda est dicendi: & similia multa.
units.tr: What wonder, then, if no mode of remedy is expressed in those positive traditions? Many diseases were already prevalent before the laws now in force were enacted, and no express provision had been made for them. And when such laws are made, it is clear that they cannot provide for the infinite number of possible cases. But the rules of divine and natural law are immovable and eternal, such as, for example, the principles of divine and natural law: We ought to obey God rather than men. God gave men power for building up, not for destroying, the Church. We can do nothing against the truth. The fullness of the law and its end is love. Love is the cause of union and peace. Love does not seek its own. The end of all power and of ecclesiastical hierarchy is love, peace and unity. The end imposed necessity on the things that are toward the end; that is, other things ought to be governed according to the demands of the end. Necessity has no law. Happy necessity, which compels toward better things. The good shepherd lays down his life for the uniting and saving of his sheep. A man's enemies are those of his own household, that is, the carnal senses. The spiritual man judges all things. The mean of virtue is to be taken, as the wise will judge. To repel force with force. It is lawful for everyone to defend himself and his property against unjust force. He who uses his right does wrong to no one. The losses of souls are worse than losses of bodies or of external goods. A deposit is not to be returned to the detriment of the depositary or of the commonwealth. It is more wholesome that bread, clothing or a sword be taken away when it is abused than that it be given. God commanded each one concerning his neighbour: You shall love, he says, your neighbour as yourself. What has been instituted for charity ought not to fight against charity. If your foot or your hand (and likewise your head) causes you to stumble, cast it from you. Let him who does not hear the Church be to you as a heathen and a publican. Tares must be tolerated, lest the wheat be uprooted along with them. Common error makes law. You shall not forswear yourself. Pay your vows to the Most High. Every oath and vow which can be kept without loss of salvation is to be observed. Whoever has the right to establish something by teaching or by judgment has the same right to interpret it. The understanding of statements is to be drawn from the causes for which they were spoken; and many similar things.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO III.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION III.

units.la: Vnitas ecclesiæ ad vnum certum Christi vicarium dum procuratur per ἑνωσιν seu bonam æquitatem non exigit in sic equitatis amantibus seu legum positiuarum interpretibus, quod habeant euidentiam mathematicam seu demonstratiuam, sed saltem si certitudinem moralem seu ciuilem & politicam attulerint.
units.tr: The unity of the Church under the one certain vicar of Christ, when it is sought through equity [ἐπιείκεια], or good fairness, does not require of those who love equity, or who interpret positive laws, that they have mathematical or demonstrative evidence. It is enough that they bring moral, civil and political certainty.

units.la: Considerat quippe bonus ἑνωσιας circumstantias omnes particulares: quales non potuit legislator præuidere nec exprimere: quibus attentis aspicit finem, qui sequeretur si rigorem litteralis expressionis obseruaret: qui dum videt ex hac obseruatione læsuram fore ex legibus diuinis vel æternis, contra intentionem debitam legislatorum dictat vel doctrinaliter vel authoritatiue: quod lex scripta sic vel sic, applicanda est seu descenda: secundum imaginationem Philosophi de regula Lesbia, quæ erat plumbea, & non ferrea, id est flexibilis, non immutabilis.
units.tr: A good judge of equity considers all the particular circumstances, which the lawgiver could not foresee or express. Having weighed these, he looks to the outcome that would follow if the rigour of the literal wording were kept. Seeing that such observance would harm the divine or eternal laws, he rules, either by teaching or by authority and against the due intention of the lawgivers, that the written law is to be applied or adjusted in this or that way. This is after the image of the Philosopher's Lesbian rule, which was of lead and not of iron, that is, flexible and not immovable.

units.la: Constat autem, quod de circumstantiis moralibus non potest haberi certitudo, nisi moralis secundum Philosophi sententiam in Ethic. Exempli gratia: Tyrannus persequitur rempublicam cautelis dolosis, sicut lupus rapax: nihilominus ipse teget se vestimentis ouium, quæ sunt tam verba quam facta apparenter sanctissima, in quibus est frequenter æquiuocatio vel hypocrisis. Ago, inquiet, ista pro republica ago pro salute populi, pro quibus paratus sum etiam mori: nec dicentibus oppositum quomodolibet fides detur. Ita mentietur tyrannus, & multos ex simplicibus seducet. Prudentes vera & iudicis, quorum est ἑνωσιας, vti legentur in operibus suis oppositum secundum artem Christi: Ex operibus eorum cognoscetis eos. Vult dicere consideratio, quod prudentibus ipsis credendum est, etiam si nescīuerint rationes euidentes & incalumniabiles adducere: alioquin periret confestim omnis politia. Denique aptæ sunt hoc loco parabolicæ narrationes de lupo & oue, quam lupus diuersis fraudibus nunc ostendendo similitudinem & amicitiam, nunc falsam imponendo calumniam, quærebat fallere vt vororet. Propter quod monuit Christus: Attendite a falsis prophetis.
units.tr: It is agreed, however, that about moral circumstances no certainty can be had except moral certainty, according to the Philosopher's opinion in the Ethics. For example: a tyrant attacks the commonwealth with deceitful precautions, like a ravening wolf. Nevertheless he covers himself with sheep's clothing, in words and deeds that appear most holy, in which there is often equivocation or hypocrisy. "I act," he will say, "for the commonwealth, I act for the safety of the people, and I am ready even to die for them." Nor should anyone who says the opposite be believed in any way. So the tyrant will lie and seduce many of the simple. Prudent and judicious men, whose task is equity, will be found in their works to act otherwise, according to the art of Christ: By their works you shall know them. The consideration means that the prudent themselves must be believed, even if they do not know how to bring evident and unassailable reasons; otherwise all government would perish at once. Finally, the parables of the wolf and the sheep are apt here, in which the wolf, now showing likeness and friendship through various frauds, now bringing a false accusation, sought to deceive in order to devour. For this reason Christ warned: "Beware of false prophets."

units.la: CONSIDERATIO IV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION IV.

units.la: Vnitas ecclesiæ ad vnum certum Christi vicarium nunc per concilium Pisanum Domino concedente procuranda debet solidius inniti sententiis & deliberationibus huiusmodi concilii & sapientum in eorum tenturorum, etiam si non offerant rationes euidentes, quam allegationibus vel assertionibus vel accusationibus aut iustificationibus vel contendentium de Papatu vel saluorum suorum.
units.tr: The unity of the Church under the one certain vicar of Christ, which is now to be sought through the Council of Pisa, God granting it, ought to rest more firmly on the judgments and deliberations of such a council and of wise men, even if they do not offer evident reasons, than on the allegations, assertions, accusations or justifications of those contending about the Papacy or about their own safety.

units.la: Deducitur faciliter consideratio ex hoc, quod medium virtutis accipiendum est, vt sapiens iudicabit: vt spiritualis qui omnia diiudicat dicet, non vt carnalis homo, qui non sapit quae Dei sunt, sibi fingit. Quis enim dubitauerit, quando plures causae concurrere habeant pro omnibus de concilio, vt eis fides detur, qui laborant ad vnionem dandam, quam pro aliis contendentibus ad suam praesidentiam talem qualem occupandam. Amor quippe nimius & carnalis ad seipsum & ad suos nonne fallere solet, & in errores impios traducere etiam vsq; ad imitationem Luciferi, vt adorari velint sicut dii: neq; reputent se subditos esse cuiquam, sicut filii Belial sine iugo: nec sibi posse dici: cur ita facis? qui nec Deum timent, nec hominem reuerentur: cum tamen humiliores esse debeant, & ad seruiendū promptiores ex praelationis munere quanto se obligatiores esse conspiciunt in reddenda ratione. Postremo tamē hoc summopere cauēdum est iudicibus, ne vlus πneuματικος passim & absq; manifesta ratione fiat, transmutando legem scriptam: alioquin tolleretur protinus a legibus sua stabilitas: quibus nutantibus totam rempublicam disciplinam innitentem eis collabi, & ex consequenti rempublicam corruere vel conturbari necesse est. Inde contigit apud Romanos ista seueritas etiam in nece propriorum filiorum, ne labefacerent optimam rei publicae disciplinam.
units.tr: The consideration follows easily from this: the middle course must be taken, as the wise will judge, as the spiritual man who judges all things will say, and not as the carnal man, who does not savour the things of God, imagines for himself. For who would doubt, when several reasons favour all of the council, that faith should be given to those who labour to bring about union, rather than to the others who strive to seize its presidency, whatever its kind? Excessive and carnal love of oneself and of one's own is wont to deceive, and to lead into impious errors, even to the imitation of Lucifer, so that men wish to be adored as gods. They think they are subject to no one, like the sons of Belial without a yoke, and nothing can be said to them such as: why do you act so? They fear neither God nor respect man, although they ought to be humbler and readier to serve, given the office of prelacy; the more they see themselves bound to give an account, the more they should be so. Finally, however, judges must guard most carefully against any pneumatic man [πνευματικός] acting here and there, without manifest reason, changing the written law. Otherwise its stability would be removed at once from the laws, and with them wavering, the whole commonwealth resting on discipline would necessarily collapse, and consequently the commonwealth would fall or be thrown into confusion. Hence among the Romans came that severity, even in the killing of their own sons, lest they weaken the best discipline of the commonwealth.

units.la: Quatuor considerationes quae ad robur praedictorum faciunt, reperiuntur postea in oratione: Apparuit gratia.
units.tr: The four considerations which strengthen the foregoing are found afterwards in the oration: Grace has appeared.

units.la: TRACTATVS EIVSDEM, DE STATIBVS ECCLESIASTICIS.
units.tr: A TREATISE OF THE SAME AUTHOR, ON ECCLESIASTICAL STATES.

units.la: Aux quam omnes obseruare conuenit cum omnibus, tamen maxime circa ministerium religionis Christianae, nunquam solicitius subsistit, quam si veritate & iustitia tanquam sororibus fulciatur. Nam si non in vera iustitia & iusta veritate reddatur vnicuique quod suum est, nonne schisma protinus irrumpens pacem exturbabit? Audiamus idcirco sub breuium consideratione numero quid status summorum Pontificum, quid praelatorum, quid curatorum, quid mendicantium possit quilibet de suo ministerio veraciter offerre: ne transgressio finium propriorum seu dilatatio nimia separet iustitiam ab osculo felici pacis: proinde lites foedas, vt assolet, introducat.
units.tr: Although everyone ought to observe justice toward everyone, it is especially in the ministry of the Christian religion that things stand most securely when they are supported by truth and justice as by sisters. For if each person is not given what is his in true justice and just truth, will not schism, breaking in at once, drive out peace? Let us therefore hear, in a brief survey, what anyone may truthfully set forth, point by point, about the status of the supreme Pontiffs, of the prelates, of the parish priests, and of the mendicant friars. Let us do so lest overstepping one's own bounds, or excessive expansion, separate justice from the happy kiss of peace and so, as is usual, bring in shameful quarrels.

units.la: PARS PRIMA. SEX CONSIDERATIONES SVPER STATV SVMMI PONTIFICIS.
units.tr: PART ONE. SIX CONSIDERATIONS ON THE STATUS OF THE SUPREME PONTIFF.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO I.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION I.

units.la: Status Papalis institutus est a Christo supernaturaliter & immediate tanquam primatum habens monarchicum & regalem in ecclesiastica Hierarchia: secundum quem statum vnicum & supremum ecclesia militans dicitur vna sub Christo: quem statum quisquis impugnare vel diminuere, vel alicui ecclesiastico statui particulari coaequare praesumit: si hoc pertinaciter faciat, haereticus est, schismaticus, impius atq; sacrilegus. Cadit enim in haeresim totiens expresse damnatam a principio nascentis ecclesiae vsque hodie: tam per institutionem Christi de principatu Petri super alios Apostolos, quam per traditionem totius ecclesiae in sacris eloquiis suis & generalibus conciliis.
units.tr: The papal status was instituted by Christ, supernaturally and immediately, as having a monarchical and royal primacy in the ecclesiastical hierarchy. According to this one and supreme status the militant Church is said to be one under Christ. Whoever presumes to attack or diminish this status, or to make it equal to any particular ecclesiastical status, if he does so obstinately, is a heretic, a schismatic, impious and sacrilegious. For he falls into a heresy that has been expressly condemned so often from the beginning of the nascent Church down to today, both by Christ's institution of the primacy of Peter over the other Apostles, and by the tradition of the whole Church in its sacred utterances and general councils.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO II.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION II.

units.la: Status Papalis licet non omnino vacet seu deficiat per mortem Papae naturalem vel ciuilem, nec per consequens ecclesia desinit esse vna: nihilominus eniti debent Christiani sub poena schismatis, quod in hoc statu constituatur & praesideat assidue vnicus & certus summus Pontifex, quantum fieri potest pro loco & tempore: sic quod non est licitum scienter impedire, quod minus sit vnus talis supremus Pontifex in ecclesia, in quo sit ecclesiasticae potestatis plenitudo: & quod non sint plures in quo tanquam ecclesiasticum regimen desinere posset esse monarchicum, & in aliam politiae speciem, vt in aristocraticam aut timocraticam verteretur: quamuis Papatus has politiarum species non excludat, sed assumat: quemadmodum de sacro dominorum Cardinalium collegio & de generali concilio videre est.
units.tr: Although the papal status is not wholly vacant or defective through the natural or civil death of the Pope, and the Church consequently does not cease to be one, nevertheless Christians ought to strive, under penalty of schism, that in this status there be constituted and continually preside one certain supreme Pontiff, as far as is possible according to place and time. Thus it is not lawful knowingly to hinder the existence in the Church of one such supreme Pontiff, in whom is the fullness of ecclesiastical power, and that there should not be several, by which the ecclesiastical government would cease to be monarchical and turn into another form of polity, such as aristocratic or timocratic. Yet Papacy does not exclude these forms of polity but takes them up, as may be seen in the sacred college of the lord Cardinals and in a general council.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO III.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION III.

units.la: Status Papalis non eximit Papam a legibus pure diuinis, quae vel in euangeliis vel generalibus conciliis positae sunt. Et ex hoc consequenter patet, quod Papa subiicitur legi illi de correctione fraterna: Si peccauerit in te frater tuus, &c. sic quod potest fraternaliter corripi dum peccat. Etsi tandem nollet audire ecclesiam, quam generale concilium repraesentat, debet haberi sicut ethnicus & publicanus. Et ita potest hoc modo per concilium vel iudicari vel coerceri, vel pro excommunicato haberi.
units.tr: The papal status does not exempt the Pope from laws that are purely divine, which are laid down either in the Gospels or in general councils. And from this it follows that the Pope is subject to that law of fraternal correction: "If your brother sins against you, etc." So he may be corrected in a brotherly way while he sins. And if at last he will not hear the Church, which a general council represents, he ought to be held as a heathen and a tax collector. And so in this way he can be either judged or restrained by a council, or be held as excommunicate.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO IV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION IV.

units.la: Status Papalis non eximit Papam à iuribus, quæ sunt pure de dictamine naturali: quemadmodum sunt principia iuris naturalis. Propterea cum lex naturalis dicat, quod bonum commune tanquam aliquid diuinum præferendum est particulari bono: deducitur ex hoc, quod ad bonum totius ecclesiæ, quam concilium generale repræsentat: reducendum est bonum personale Papæ, sic quod in præiudicium boni communis particulare bonum Papæ seu commodum vel status, retentio vel dilatatio prævalere non debet: cum secundum exigentiam finis cætera debeant moderari: finis autem Papatus est vtilitas ecclesiæ.
units.tr: The papal status does not exempt the Pope from rights that rest purely on natural reason, such as the principles of natural law. Therefore, since natural law says that the common good, as something divine, is to be preferred to a particular good, it follows that the personal good of the Pope must be referred to the good of the whole Church, which a general council represents. Thus, to the prejudice of the common good, the particular good, convenience or status of the Pope, whether its retention or its extension, ought not to prevail, since everything else ought to be regulated according to the demands of the end; and the end of the Papacy is the usefulness of the Church.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO V.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION V.

units.la: Status Papalis quamuis eximat Papam à legibus pure positiuis, canonicis vel ciuilibus, sic quod secundum eas coerceri punitiue non potest, vt præcise tales sunt: nihilominus Papa non deberaut potest leges positiuas, præsertim per concilium generale, ad quod sufficienter spectat discernere vel dictare, si Papa palam conuertat potestatem suam in destructionem ecclesiæ, non in ædificationem.
units.tr: Although the papal status exempts the Pope from laws that are purely positive, canonical or civil, so that he cannot be punitively restrained by them insofar as they are precisely such, nevertheless the Pope ought not, and cannot, revoke or change positive laws, especially through a general council, to which it properly belongs to discern or dictate, if the Pope openly turns his power to the destruction of the Church and not to its building up.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION VI.

units.la: Status Papalis obligat Papam tanto amplius, quanto maior est in ecclesia, subiicere se legibus diuinis, naturalibus & canonicis ad vtilitatem ecclesiæ. Propterea cum magis videant oculi quam oculus, videtur quod non sine grandi discrimine salutis Papa possit deliberationes vel instituta generalium conciliorum contemnere: vt non secundum communem, sed propriam deliberationem contendat in ecclesiastico regimine præsidere. Propterea bene dictum est, quod Papa non potest generalem statum ecclesiæ immutare vel tollere.
units.tr: The papal status binds the Pope all the more, the greater his place in the Church, to subject himself to divine, natural and canonical laws for the usefulness of the Church. Therefore, since the eyes see more than a single eye, it seems that the Pope cannot, without great danger to salvation, despise the deliberations or decrees of general councils, so as to preside over the ecclesiastical government by his own deliberation rather than by the common one. Hence it has been rightly said that the Pope cannot change or remove the general status of the Church.

units.la: PARS SECVNDA. SEX CONSIDERATIONES DE STATV SVMMI PONTIFICIS, ET DOMINORVM sanctæ Romanæ ecclesiæ Cardinalium.
units.tr: PART TWO. SIX CONSIDERATIONS ON THE STATUS OF THE SUPREME PONTIFF AND OF THE LORDS CARDINALS OF THE HOLY ROMAN CHURCH.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO I.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION I.

units.la: Status summi Pontificis ac sacri collegii dominorum Cardinalium sibi collateralium est in ecclesiastica Hierarchia subcœlesti, immediatè à Christo: nec humana institutione seu præsumptione potest destitui. Cui statui qui pertinaciter derogat, censendus est iuxta sacros canones hæreticus atque sacrilegus.
units.tr: The status of the supreme Pontiff and of the sacred college of the Lord Cardinals associated with him is part of the ecclesiastical hierarchy on earth, and it comes immediately from Christ. It cannot be removed by human institution or presumption. Whoever obstinately detracts from this status is to be judged, according to the sacred canons, a heretic and a sacrilegious person.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO II.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION II.

units.la: Status prædictus dotandus est vel fouendus pro debita & honesta sustentatione temporalium, sine quibus in hac vita misera, spiritualia diu non subsistunt: quemadmodum alter status quicunq; ecclesiasticus inferior seu subditus dotatus est, vel dotandus iuxta sui qualitatem.
units.tr: The aforesaid status ought to be endowed or supported with the temporal goods needed for its due and honourable maintenance, for without these, spiritual things cannot long subsist in this wretched life. In the same way, every other ecclesiastical status, whether inferior or subordinate, is or ought to be endowed according to its rank.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO III.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION III.

units.la: Status prædictus non ideo perdit iura sibi conuenientia, quæ poluit propositio duplex præcedens: si forte fuerint abusus aliqui personales, olim vel nunc inuenti. Alioquin sic argueretur aduersus omnem statum, nedum ecclesiasticum, sed temporalem: quod dissipandus est, deserendus & perdendus: quoniam in multis offendimus omnes.
units.tr: The aforesaid status does not therefore lose the rights that belong to it, which the preceding twofold proposition might seem to suggest, if perhaps some personal abuses have been found, either formerly or now. Otherwise one could argue in the same way against every status, not only ecclesiastical but also temporal: that it must be scattered, abandoned and destroyed, since we all offend in many things.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO IV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION IV.

units.la: Status prædictus potuit & potest in subuentionibus temporalis & honestæ sustentationis prescribere de certo modo, vel quota subuentionis: sicut prælati vel curati inferiores respectu subuentionis factæ per subditos in oblationibus, decimis & similibus: etiam vbi status prædictus aliounde dotatus esset ex patrimonialibus bonis vel aliis, quemadmodum in prælatis dicimus & curatis.
units.tr: The aforesaid status could and can prescribe, for the support of its temporal and honourable maintenance, a certain manner or proportion of support, just as bishops and inferior parish priests do with respect to the support provided by their subjects in offerings, tithes and similar payments; this holds even where the aforesaid status is endowed from elsewhere, from patrimonial goods or others, as we say of prelates and parish priests.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO V.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION V.

units.la: Status prædictus dum recipit & quærit subuentiones consuetas, in oblationibus, decimis, vel annatis & similibus, non debet eo ipso de simoniaca prauitate notari: nisi forte vitium aliud in executionis modo concurrerit: quod vitium corrigi debet, non obinde status minui, destrui, culpari, vel iuribus aliunde debitis defraudari. Sicut ab infirmo morbus tollendus est, non subiectum vel corpus destruendum. Oppositum vero pertinaciter imponens, notando generaliter de Simoniaca prauitate totum statum illum, temerarius esset, nec ferendus.
units.tr: The aforesaid status, while it receives and seeks the customary contributions in offerings, tithes, annates and similar payments, ought not for that reason alone to be branded with the taint of simony, unless perhaps some other fault has entered into the manner of carrying this out. That fault ought to be corrected; the status should not thereby be diminished, destroyed, blamed, or defrauded of rights due to it from elsewhere. Just as the disease is to be removed from the sick man, not the subject or body destroyed, so too. To assert the contrary obstinately, by generally branding that whole status with simoniacal depravity, would be rash and not to be tolerated.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION VI.

units.la: Status prædictus potest & debet rationabiliter resistere per viam appellationis, aut alias, si aduersus prædicta voluerit aliquis de facto procedere: præsertim dum personæ de illo statu subiiciunt se: & statum suum debitæ regulationi sanctæ matris ecclesiæ, si forsan aliqua fuerunt in eis reformanda, & hoc agendo, nedum non scandalizant actiue vel peccant, sed merentur tanquam defensores iniurium, non solum suorum personalium, vel ecclesiæ particularis Romanæ, sed vniuersalis ecclesiæ & ad vtilitatem honestatemque totius reipublicæ Christianæ, quæ consistit in suo decore membrorum maxime principalium.
units.tr: The aforesaid status can and ought reasonably to resist, by way of appeal or otherwise, if anyone wishes to proceed against these matters by force; especially since the persons of that status submit themselves and their status to the proper regulation of our holy mother the Church, if perhaps some things in them need reform. In so doing they not only do not give scandal actively or sin, but they deserve to be regarded as defenders of wrongs done, not only to themselves personally or to the particular Roman church, but to the universal Church, and for the advantage and honour of the whole Christian commonwealth, which rests on the honour of its chief members.

units.la: PARS TERTIA. DE STATV PRÆLATORVM.
units.tr: PART THREE. ON THE STATUS OF THE PRELATES.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO I.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION I.

units.la: STATVS prælationis episcopalis in ecclesia sic est de primaria & immediata ac supernaturali institutione Christi, quod naturali vel humana solum authoritate non potuit institui: sicut potuit status dominationis temporalis regiæ vel imperialis humanitus & naturaliter ordinari.
units.tr: The status of episcopal prelacy in the Church is so much of primary and immediate and supernatural institution by Christ that it could not have been instituted by natural or human authority alone, as the status of temporal, royal or imperial dominion could be ordained by human and natural means.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO II.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION II.

units.la: Status prælationis episcopalis in ecclesia quo ad sui collationem primariam fuit immediate à Christo datus primis Apostolis, sicut status papalis Petro: licet postmodum talis collatio vel acquisitio fieri potuerit & facta sit in successoribus per homines: sicut Matthias factus est Apostolus per electionem vel sortem: & successores etiam Petri fiunt nunc per humanam electionem dominorum Cardinalium: qui modus potuit & potest variari, vt infra ponetur.
units.tr: The status of episcopal prelacy in the Church, as regards its primary conferral, was given immediately by Christ to the first Apostles, just as the papal status was given to Peter. Yet afterwards such conferral or acquisition could be, and has been, made in their successors through men, just as Matthias was made an Apostle by election or by lot; and the successors of Peter are now made by the human election of the lord Cardinals. This mode could be, and can be, varied, as will be set out below.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO III.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION III.

units.la: Status prælationis episcopalis habuit in Apostolis & in successoribus vsum vel exercitium suæ potestatis sub Papa Petro, & successoribus eius tanquam sub habente vel habentibus plenitudinem fontalem episcopalis authoritatis. Vnde & quo ad talia minores prælati, sc. curati, subsunt episcopis, & quibus vsus suæ potestatis quandoque limitatur vel arcetur: & sicà Papa posse fieri circa prælatos maiores ex certis & rationabilibus causis non est ambigendum.
units.tr: The status of episcopal prelacy had, in the Apostles and in their successors, the use or exercise of its power under Pope Peter, and under his successors, as under the one or ones who hold the fontal fullness of episcopal authority. Hence, as regards such matters, the lesser prelates, namely the parish priests, are subject to the bishops, and the use of their power is sometimes limited or restrained; and it is not to be doubted that the Pope can do this with respect to the greater prelates, for certain and reasonable causes.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO IV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION IV.

units.la: Status episcopalis non ita subest statui Papali, quod illum possit Papa annullare: sicut nec status Papalis posset humanitus destitui. Nihilominus idem status episcopalis quo ad acquisitionem isti personæ & quo ad exercitium, subest rationabili Papæ voluntati ad vtilitatem ecclesiæ, vt dictum est. Hæc autem rationabilitas videtur attendenda seu regulanda maxime per determinationes conciliorum generalium, præsertim iam factas de consensu & authoritate summorum Pontificum.
units.tr: The episcopal status is not so subject to the papal status that the Pope could annul it, just as the papal status itself could not be removed by human means. Nevertheless, this same episcopal status, both as to the acquisition of this person and as to its exercise, is subject to the reasonable will of the Pope for the good of the Church, as has been said. This reasonableness seems to be weighed or regulated chiefly by the determinations of general councils, especially those already made with the consent and authority of the supreme Pontiffs.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO V.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION V.

units.la: Status episcopalis quo ad sui acquisitionem isti personæ & quo ad exercitium, non ita subest theræ voluntati Papæ, quod pro libito posset sine iniuria & peccato circa huiusmodi acquisitionem & destitutionem, ampliationem & restrictionem operari: quoniam data est ei potestas, dicente Apostolo, non ad destructionem, sed ad edificationem.
units.tr: The episcopal status, both as to the acquisition of this person and as to its exercise, is not so subject to the mere will of the Pope that he could, at pleasure and without wrong and sin, act in such acquisition and removal, in enlarging or restricting it; since, as the Apostle says, power has been given to him, not for destruction but for building up.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION VI.

units.la: Status episcopalis habet ex se & Christi institutione primaria potestatem conficiendi corpus Christi & ministrandi sacramenta ecclesiastica omnia: ius insuper prædicandi: ius stipendia temporalia sumendi: ius excommunicandi: ius prælatos minores, sc. curatos, instituendi: ius ecclesias consecrandi: ius beneficium ecclesiasticum vel stipendium temporale conferendi, vel facere conferri ministrantibus sub se spiritualia: ius indulgentias dandi. Et ita de reliquis multis, quæ summo Pontifici competunt, vt in fonte.
units.tr: The episcopal status has, from itself and by Christ's primary institution, the power of consecrating the body of Christ and of administering all the ecclesiastical sacraments; moreover the right of preaching; the right of receiving temporal stipends; the right of excommunicating; the right of instituting lesser prelates, namely parish priests; the right of consecrating churches; the right of conferring ecclesiastical benefices or temporal stipends, or of causing them to be conferred on those who minister spiritual things under him; the right of granting indulgences. And so with many others, which belong to the supreme Pontiff as to their source.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION VII.

units.la: Status episcopalis quo ad sui vsum vel exercitium non ita subest puræ voluntati Papæ, sicut status priuilegiatorum Mendicantium vel aliorum, quibus essentiali ordine & Hierarchico statu prædicta iura episcopalia non competunt. Potest idcirco Papa sub talibus priuilegiis & priuilegiatis absq; iniuria vel peccato immutationes operari restringendo vel tollendo: non sic passim in prælatis vel curatis.
units.tr: The episcopal status, as regards its use or exercise, is not so subject to the pure will of the Pope as is the status of privileged Mendicants or of others, to whom the aforesaid episcopal rights do not belong by essential order and hierarchical status. The Pope may therefore, under such privileges and privileged persons, make changes without wrong or sin, by restricting or removing them; but not so generally in the case of prelates or parish priests.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VIII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION VIII.

units.la: Status episcopalis licet esse possit in aliquo sine plebe & sine vsu vel exercitio hoc fieri non conuenit: quia vanum & monstruosum in ecclesia videretur: quoniam frustra est potestas, cui non subest operatio.
units.tr: The episcopal status may exist in some case without a flock, but it is not fitting that this be so without use or exercise; for it would seem vain and monstrous in the Church, since power is in vain to which no operation is subject.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO IX.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION IX.

units.la: Status episcopalis si nimis arceretur in suis iuribus essentialibus quo ad restrictionem vsus vel exercitii passim communiter per Papam absq; vtilitate maiori ecclesiæ: siue hoc esset in exemptionibus subditorum ab eo, siue in relaxatione casuum in foro pœnitentiæ: seu in restrictione stipendiorum temporalium: seu in reseruatione beneficiorum ecclesiasticorum subeo: seu per inductionem onerosam priuilegiatorum: aut modis similibus. Ille inquam status episcopalis posset rationabiliter deferre querelam, nedum ad Papam & generale concilium, quod est conuenientissimum medium: sed ad principes orthodoxos implorando iuuamen opportunum,
units.tr: If the episcopal status were too greatly restricted in its essential rights, through the general and common restriction of its use or exercise by the Pope, without greater advantage to the Church, whether this were done by the exemption of subjects from it, or by the relaxation of cases in the forum of penance, or by the restriction of temporal stipends, or by the reservation of ecclesiastical benefices to the bishop, or by the burdensome induction of privileged persons, or by similar means: that episcopal status, I say, could reasonably lodge a complaint, not only with the Pope and a general council, which is the most suitable remedy, but also by imploring fitting aid from orthodox princes.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO X.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION X.

units.la: Status episcopalis sicut non acquiritur in aliquo per solum titulum fidei, vel charitatis, ita non deperditur per solam haeresim, vel peccatum mortale, non intervenien te humana institutione, vel diuina revelatione: alioquin status ecclesiae Hierarchicus prorsus esset incertus, cum suo usu vel exercitio: quod non est conueniens dicere de politia a supremo legislatore constituta.
units.tr: The episcopal status is not acquired in anyone by the mere title of faith or charity, and so it is not lost by heresy alone or by mortal sin, unless human institution or divine revelation intervenes; otherwise the hierarchical status of the Church, together with its use or exercise, would be wholly uncertain, which is not fitting to say of a polity established by the supreme Lawgiver.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION XI.

units.la: Status episcopalis sicut potest diuersis temporibus & institutionibus modis variis acquiri & similiter auferri: sic & status Papalis in casu per ordinationes Papales, aut per concilium generale, sicut & factum est, aliquando potest immutari.
units.tr: Just as the episcopal status can at different times and by different institutions be acquired in various ways, and likewise taken away, so too the papal status can, in certain cases, by papal ordinances or by a general council, as has also happened, sometimes be changed.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XII.
units.tr: Consideration XII.

units.la: Status episcopalis potest ab aliquo propter suam malitiam auferri, licet reiteretur occupans: sic & status Papalis, ut videtur in casu, praesertim per concilium generale potest auferri: cum status Papalis datus sit ecclesiasticae communitati: quae in hoc habet quid diuinum tanquam commune bonum, ad quod Papalis authoritas conseruandum fuit instituta.
units.tr: An episcopal office may be taken away from a man by someone because of his wickedness, even if he who holds it is reinstated; so too the papal office, as seems likely in this case, may be taken away especially by a general council, since the papal office has been given to the ecclesiastical community, which holds in this a divine good as a common possession, and for the preservation of which the papal authority was instituted.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XIII.
units.tr: Consideration XIII.

units.la: Status episcopalis habet rationabiliter monarchiam supremum, scilicet Papam ratione vnitatis fidei & sacramentorum, sed hoc non ita perspicuum est esse debere ex institutione Christi: & pro vtilitate vniuersalis ecclesiae respectu dispensationis bonorum temporalium, & iurisdictionum coercionum tentiosarum seu coercituarum: quae diuersis legibus seu decretalibus, aut statutis pro diuersitate locorum & temporum regi debent: sicut & alia mere temporalia, regalia, & imperialia. Hinc bene dictum est quod qualibet prouincia in sensu suo abundat.
units.tr: The episcopal office reasonably holds a supreme monarchy, namely the Pope, on account of the unity of faith and of the sacraments; but it is not so clear that this ought to be so by the institution of Christ. And for the benefit of the universal Church, with respect to the disposal of temporal goods and of jurisdictions, of contentious or coercive powers, which ought to be governed by diverse laws, decretals or statutes according to the diversity of places and times, as are other purely temporal, royal and imperial matters. Hence it has been well said that every province abounds in its own sense.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XIV.
units.tr: Consideration XIV.

units.la: Status praelationis si fiat limitatio sui vsus in beneficiis conferendis, vel in exemptionibus: non debet rationabiliter conqueri, dum hoc manifeste fit propter studium literarum, praesertim sacrae doctrinae, quod per talia promouetur: & dum hoc potenter fit ad reprimendos abusus notorie prouenientes: siue hoc sit ex importunitate dominorum temporalium, vel ex propria pusillanimitate, vel alia quauis corrupta affectione.
units.tr: If a prelate's office limits its use in conferring benefices or in exemptions, it should not reasonably complain, since this is manifestly done for the sake of learning, especially sacred teaching, which such measures promote; and since it is done effectively to check abuses that are notoriously arising, whether this comes from the importunity of temporal lords, or from the prelate's own timidity, or from any other corrupt affection.

units.la: Sed in hoc capere medium conueniens non aliter videtur posse determinari, quam iuxta Aristotel. sententiam, scilicet vt sapiens iudicabit. Nihil autem videtur in hoc sapientius, quam generale concilium rite & libere celebratum.
units.tr: But in this matter, the suitable middle course does not seem able to be determined otherwise than according to the opinion of Aristotle, namely that the wise man will judge. Yet nothing in this seems wiser than a general council duly and freely held.

units.la: PARS QVARTA. DE STATV CVRATORVM.
units.tr: PART FOUR. ON THE STATE OF PARISH PRIESTS.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO I.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION I.

units.la: Status curatorum succedit statui discipulorum Christi, quo ad legem nouam: & figuratus est in antiqua lege per Leuitas: ac proinde status curatorum est de institutione Christi & Apostolorum suorum a principio fundationis ecclesiae: quae institutio per declarationes summorum Pontificum & synodorum tam generalium quam specialium magis ac magis innotuit.
units.tr: The state of parish priests succeeds the state of Christ's disciples, as regards the new law, and it was prefigured in the old law by the Levites. Accordingly, the state of parish priests has its origin in the institution of Christ and of his Apostles from the beginning of the foundation of the Church; and this institution has become better and better known through the declarations of the supreme Pontiffs and of synods, both general and particular.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO II.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION II.

units.la: Status curatorum est de essentiali ac intrinseca ecclesiae Hierarchia, sicut status praelatorum: quamuis inferior sit, & pro sua perfectione variabilis. Quo ratione curati simplices non aeque proprie dicuntur sponsi, sicut episcopi: liberiusque permittuntur cedere vel renunciare curis suis.
units.tr: The state of parish priests belongs to the essential and intrinsic hierarchy of the Church, as does the state of prelates, although it is lower and variable according to its perfection. For this reason parish priests are not called spouses in the same proper sense as bishops are; and they are allowed more freely to give up or resign their cares.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO III.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION III.

units.la: Status curatorum institutus est ad regimen animarum dirigendarum in finem virtutum per communionem sacramentorum & peccatorum remissionem, & promotionem ad virtutes.
units.tr: The state of parish priests was instituted to rule souls, to direct them to the end of the virtues, through communion in the sacraments, the remission of sins, and the advancement in virtues.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO IV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION IV.

units.la: Status curatorum annexam habet obligationem docendi & publicandi verbum Dei suis parochianis: saltem quodam generali tenore legis euangelicae quo ad credenda & agenda secundum statum suae simplicitatis: sicut maioribus praelatis convenit ex obligatione scientiae reddere rationem particularium de ea, quae in eis est, fide & spe: apud omnes tam qui deforis sunt, quam qui intus, fideles scilicet & infideles, haec enim obligatio consequitur ad obligationem priorem, quae est de spirituali regimine subditorum.
units.tr: The state of parish priests carries with it the obligation of teaching and proclaiming the Word of God to their parishioners, at least by the general tenor of the evangelical law concerning what is to be believed and done, according to the condition of their simple state. Just as it befits the greater prelates, by the obligation of knowledge, to render an account of the particular faith and hope that is in them to all, both those outside and those inside, that is, the faithful and the unfaithful, so this obligation follows from the prior obligation, which concerns the spiritual government of subjects.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO V.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION V.

units.la: Status curatorum est status perfectionis, non solum acquirendae, sed etiam exercendae: cum sibi competat tam obligatio quam auctoritas reducendi animas ad Deum, secundum hierarchicos actus, qui purgare, illuminare, perficere nominantur.
units.tr: The state of parish priests is a state of perfection, not only to be acquired but also to be exercised, since both the obligation and the authority belong to it to lead souls back to God, according to the hierarchical acts which are called purging, enlightening, and perfecting.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION VI.

units.la: Status curatorum superior est hierarchicae ecclesiae ad statum simplicium religiosorum: sicut divinus Dionysius & Hieron. in praecedentis consideratione determinant ratione.
units.tr: The state of parish priests is superior, within the hierarchical Church, to the state of simple religious, as Dionysius the Areopagite and Jerome determine by reasoning in the preceding consideration.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION VII.

units.la: Status curatorum ecclesias parochiales sibi deputatas habet in tali libertate, quod nulli alteri sacerdoti fas est ipsis invitis aut sine eorum licentia praedicare in eadem: praesertim dum praedicare voluerint ipsi: sed nec confessiones illic audire, nec sacramenta ministrare: salva semper auctoritate vel rationabili ordinatione superiorum praelatorum.
units.tr: The state of parish priests has the parish churches assigned to them in such freedom that no other priest may lawfully preach in them against their will or without their permission, especially while they themselves wish to preach; nor may any other hear confessions there or administer the sacraments, always saving the authority or the reasonable ordinance of the superior prelates.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VIII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION VIII.

units.la: Status curatorum habet ius & titulum recipiendi decimas & oblationes & funeralia: aut alia emolumenta loco illorum pro sustentatione sufficienti status sui. Et hoc fit tam de iure divino quam naturali praesupposito domino. Determinatio autem huius vel illius quotae, vel commutatio in aliam subventionem, habet fieri solo iure positivo.
units.tr: The state of parish priests has the right and title to receive tithes, offerings, and funeral fees, or other emoluments in place of these, for the sufficient support of their state. This holds by divine and natural law, the lord being presupposed. The determination, however, of this or that proportion, or its change into some other form of support, must rest solely on positive law.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO IX.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION IX.

units.la: Status curatorum sicut habet de sibi subditis quibus cogitare in ministratione sacramentorum, ut sancte suscipiantur: sic decet maxime ut quilibet parochianus se prius ostendat suo curato generaliter vel specialiter in foro conscientiae, quam eadem sacramenta suscipiat. Potest insuper edictum generale vel speciale suis parochianis super hoc per curatos, ne aliter se ingerant, promulgari.
units.tr: Just as the state of parish priests has charge of those subject to them, to take care in the administration of the sacraments that they are received worthily, so it is especially fitting that each parishioner should first show himself to his priest, generally or specifically, in the forum of conscience, before he receives those sacraments. Moreover, a general or special edict may be promulgated by the priests to their parishioners on this matter, that they should not otherwise thrust themselves forward.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO X.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION X.

units.la: Status curatorum securius & iustius eligitur quantum est de se & caeteris paribus, pro confessione sacramentali faciendā a parochianis quam alius status: praesertim qui non est superior secundum institutionem ecclesiae hierarchicam: patet quia mutua & correlativa est obligatio parochianorum ad curatos: unde vicissim magis obligantur. Collusiones praeterea hinc inde possibiles fieri magis ex hoc evitantur. Denique remedia spiritualia celerius & consultius in casibus multis exhibentur. Potest nihilominus apud privilegiatos quandoque ratio potior inveniri.
units.tr: The state of parish priests is, as far as it is in itself and other things being equal, chosen more safely and more justly for sacramental confession to be made by parishioners than any other state, especially one that is not superior according to the hierarchical institution of the Church. This is evident, because the obligation of the parishioners to the priests is mutual and correlative; hence in turn they are more bound. Moreover, collusions that may arise on either side are thereby more easily avoided. Finally, spiritual remedies are applied more quickly and more wisely in many cases. Nevertheless, among the privileged a stronger reason can sometimes be found.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION XI.

units.la: Status curatorum sanctus & salubris non debet inculpari vel infamari per quoscunque, si in eo quandoque sint personae minus idoneae ad debitum regimen animarum: alioquin nullus esset status in ecclesia militante, qui culpari non deberet: sicut nullus absque macula quorundam de vllo statu visus est diu stare.
units.tr: The state of parish priests, being holy and wholesome, ought not to be blamed or defamed by anyone if, in it, at times there are persons less fit for the proper government of souls; otherwise there would be no state in the militant Church that ought not to be blamed, since no state has long been seen to stand without the stain of some of its members.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION XII.

units.la: Status curatorum potest sufficienter regere suos parochianos, si polleat bona charitate & simplici morum honestate, etiam ubi litteratura magna deesset. Propterea non leviter se eis praeponere debent alieni, quamvis inveniantur magis litterati.
units.tr: The state of parish priests can sufficiently govern its parishioners if it possesses good charity and simple uprightness of life, even where great learning is lacking. Therefore outsiders ought not lightly to be set over them, although they may be found to be more learned.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XIII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION XIII.

units.la: Status curatorum potest cum facili studio habere ea & scire, quae ad parochiam suam regendam sufficiunt, maiora maioribus prudenter remittendo. Hoc autem si agnoscere neglexerint, debet apud eos correctio episcopalis maxime vigilare, ut astringantur severius tenorem habere in scriptis eorum, quae scire debent in punctis regiminis, tam institutiones synodales positivas, quam caeteras.
units.tr: The state of parish priests can, with little effort, have and know those things which suffice for governing their parish, prudently leaving the greater matters to the greater men. If they have neglected to recognise this, episcopal correction ought especially to watch over them, so that they are more strictly bound to keep in writing what they ought to know on the points of government, both the positive synodal regulations and the others.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XIV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XIV.

units.la: Status curatorum potest obventiones ordinatas licenter exigere: veruntamen tali modo & tempore, quod simoniaca pravitas vel eius suspicio nequaquam incurratur: ut quod propter negationem temporalium, spiritualium interim ministratio non negetur, nec interveniat quaestuosa mercatio.
units.tr: The state of parish priests may lawfully demand the ordinary dues; yet it must be done in such a manner and at such a time that the taint of simony, or even the suspicion of it, is in no way incurred: so that spiritual ministration is not refused on account of the withholding of temporal things, and no profit-seeking bargaining comes in.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XV.

units.la: Status curatorum debet cum bona gratia suscipere statum priuilegiatorum tanquam coadiutores missos habentes à superioribus licentiam prædicandi, & confessiones audiendi, si non appareat rationabilis causa aliquem talem repellendi: vtpote si detractor, si collusor, si corruptor, si quaefluosus, si seductor appareat. Aut parochianorum multi inde veniunt in contemptum curatorum. Aut si tunc curatus per seipsum id agere circa parochianos suos, quod agendum sit, satis potuerit: quia videretur præferendus, nisi legitima fieret exceptio contra eum.
units.tr: The state of parish priests ought to receive with good grace the state of the privileged, as assistants sent in, who have licence from their superiors to preach and to hear confessions, unless some reasonable cause appears for rejecting such a person; for example, if he appears to be a slanderer, a colluder, a corrupter, a profiteer, or a seducer. Otherwise many of the parishioners will come to hold the parish priests in contempt. Or, if the parish priest is himself able to do adequately whatever needs to be done for his parishioners, he would seem to be the one to be preferred, unless a lawful objection were raised against him.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XVI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XVI.

units.la: Status curatorum vix potest à parochianis sine peccato sic contemni, quod eorum licentia neque in generali, neq; in speciali prius quaeratur, dum alibi confiteri, aut missas vel sermones audire tempore diuini seruitii, diebus dominicis & festiuis voluerint. Quae licentia si sine causa rationabili denegetur, sufficit excusare frequenter eos, qui alibi confitentur, licentia non obtenta, sed petita.
units.tr: The state of parish priests can scarcely be so despised by the parishioners without sin that their permission is not first sought, either in general or in particular, when they wish to confess elsewhere, or to hear Mass or sermons at the time of divine service on Sundays and feast days. If this permission is refused without a reasonable cause, it is enough to excuse those who frequently confess elsewhere without having obtained permission, but having asked for it.

units.la: PARS QVINTA. DECEM CONSIDERATIONES QVAE PONVNTVR PRO STATV PRIVILEGIATORVM
units.tr: PART FIVE. TEN CONSIDERATIONS PUT FORWARD CONCERNING THE STATUS OF THE PRIVILEGED

units.la: CONSIDERATIO PRIMA.
units.tr: FIRST CONSIDERATION.

units.la: Status priuilegiatorum ad Prædicandum, & confessiones audiendum, statutus est post primariam ecclesiæ institutionem, rationabiliter ordinatus ad subleuamen eorum, qui hierarchicos in ecclesia status habent: præsertim post talem & tantam in temporalibus ditationem, quæ secum attulit multam occupationem.
units.tr: The status of the privileged, to preach and to hear confessions, was established after the first institution of the Church, reasonably ordained to relieve those who hold the hierarchical status in the Church, especially after such a great increase of temporal wealth, which brought with it much occupation.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO II.
units.tr: SECOND CONSIDERATION.

units.la: Status priuilegiatorum debet cum bona charitate licentia sua uti: Non ad quæstum, non ad æmulationem, non ad ambitionem, non denique in præiudicium temporale vel spirituale curatorum: sed in stando clam & palam apud parochianos, quatenus honorem debitum ac sustentationem suis reddant curatis: alioquin faciunt quod sibi fieri nollent, meritoque repelluntur hi, de quibus aliter constiterit, & excommunicationem à canone nonnunquam incurrunt.
units.tr: Those of the privileged status ought to use their licence with good charity: not for gain, not out of rivalry, not out of ambition, and not finally to the temporal or spiritual prejudice of the parish priests; but in acting openly and in private among the parishioners, insofar as they render due honour and support to their own parish priests. Otherwise they do what they would not want done to themselves, and those about whom it is otherwise established are rightly repulsed, and sometimes incur excommunication under the canon.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO III.
units.tr: THIRD CONSIDERATION.

units.la: Status priuilegiatorum & omnium generaliter religiosorum prohibetur sub pœna excommunicationis latæ sententiæ, ne sacramentum eucharistiæ ministrent & matrimonium solennizent.
units.tr: The privileged status, and all religious in general, are forbidden, under penalty of excommunication latae sententiae, to administer the sacrament of the Eucharist and to solemnize marriage.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO IV.
units.tr: FOURTH CONSIDERATION.

units.la: Status priuilegiatorum habet, quod in suis locis & publicis prædicare possunt: dum prælatus non prædicat, nec prædicationem instituit. Similiter hoc possunt in ecclesiis parochialibus de licentia curatorum.
units.tr: The privileged status has this: that they may preach in their own places and in public, provided the prelate is not preaching nor has arranged a sermon. Likewise they may do this in the parish churches with the licence of the parish priests.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO V.
units.tr: FIFTH CONSIDERATION.

units.la: Status priuilegiatorum hoc habet, vt idonei præsentati sufficienter per superiores suos ad prælatum dioecesanum valeant in locis suis confessiones audire dioecesanorum & eos absoluere cum tali potestate: & in casibus talibus quemadmodum curati parochiales ordinarie funguntur & non ampliori: nisi de speciali gratia prælati maior eis fuerit elargita potestas.
units.tr: The privileged status has this: that suitable persons, sufficiently presented by their superiors to the diocesan prelate, may in their own places hear the confessions of the diocesan people and absolve them with such power; and in such cases they function as parish priests ordinarily do, and no more, unless a greater power has been granted to them by the special grace of the prelate.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VI.
units.tr: SIXTH CONSIDERATION.
