units.la: Status priuilegiatorum habet hoc: vt quamuis sacramentum pœnitentiæ possit pluries super eadem peccata suum effectum sortiri, saltem quo ad augmentum gratiæ: cum sit sacramentum iterabile: & licet meritorie eadem peccata pluribus confiteri: nec sit repugnantia, quin adhuc possit tempus obligari: nihilominus confessi priuilegiatis non tenentur inuiti eadem peccata amplius confiteri plus quam si suis curatis eadem confessi fuissent, quantum est ex parte efficaciæ sacramenti. Hoc per Ioannem 22. fuit declaratum: & vsus communis hoc obtinuit.
units.tr: The privileged status has this: that although the sacrament of penance can take effect many times over the same sins, at least as regards the increase of grace, since it is a sacrament that can be repeated, and although it is meritorious to confess the same sins to several people, nor is there any incompatibility in the matter of still being able to bind a time, nevertheless those who have confessed to the privileged are not bound, against their will, to confess the same sins again any more than if they had confessed them to their own parish priests, so far as the efficacy of the sacrament is concerned. This was declared by John 22, and common usage has upheld it.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VII.
units.tr: SEVENTH CONSIDERATION.

units.la: Status priuilegiatorum hoc habet, vt à confessis sibi non debeant curati nouam extorquere confessionem de eisdem peccatis, præsertim si secreta sint: nec debent prohibere parochianos, cum talia voluerint eis confiteri. Fas sit curatis, imo tutum inquirere à parochianis suis quando & qualiter, à quibus confessionem receperint. Quibus veritatem respondere si quis parochianus negauerit, vix in statu salutis esse credi posset. Ipsique in hoc casu petenti eucharistiæ sacramentum rationabiliter denegaretur, dicendo: nescio si confessus sis ab habente potestatem: & an in hoc te decipias, vel alter te.
units.tr: The privileged status has this: that parish priests ought not to extort from those who have confessed to them a fresh confession of the same sins, especially if they were secret; nor ought they to forbid parishioners when they wish to confess such things to them. It is lawful for parish priests, indeed safe, to inquire of their parishioners when and in what manner they have received confession, and from whom. If any parishioner should deny telling the truth in reply, he could scarcely be believed to be in a state of salvation. And in this case the sacrament of the Eucharist would reasonably be refused to him if he asks for it, with the words: "I do not know whether you have confessed to one who has the power, and whether you are deceiving yourself in this, or the other man is deceiving you."

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VIII.
units.tr: EIGHTH CONSIDERATION.

units.la: Status priuilegiatorum hoc habet, dum de peccatis publicis absoluunt parochianos, vt ipsi debeant facere fidem de absolutione & absoluendi potestate: si super hoc à curatis parochialibus fuerint requisiti; sub poena denegandi rationabiliter talibus, cum se dicunt absolutos, eucharistiæ sacramentum.
units.tr: The privileged status has this: when they absolve parishioners of public sins, they ought to give proof of the absolution and of the power to absolve, if they are asked about this by the parish priests; under penalty of reasonably denying the sacrament of the Eucharist to such people, when they say they have been absolved.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO IX.
units.tr: NINTH CONSIDERATION.

units.la: Status priuilegiatorum hoc habet, vt non debeant inducere voto vel promisso alios ad eligendum sepulturam in ecclesiis & locis suis: vel ad persistendum in iam electa ibidem: & hoc sub poena excommunicationis latæ sententiæ. Debent præterea reddere quartam partem legatorum seu funeralium curato parochiali ipsius defuncti: quæ pars canonica nominatur.
units.tr: The privileged status has this: they ought not to induce others, by vow or promise, to choose burial in their churches and places, or to persist in a burial already chosen there; and this under penalty of excommunication latae sententiae. Moreover, they ought to pay a fourth part of the legacies or funeral dues to the parish priest of the deceased person himself; this is called the canonical portion.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO X.
units.tr: TENTH CONSIDERATION.

units.la: Status priuilegiatorum ad prædicandum debet secundum qualitatem auditorum formare sermonem, ne coram laicis & subditis detegantur vitia clericorum atque Dominorum. Hoc enim esset non extirpare vitia, sed nutrire rebellionem, scilicet murmurationis & contemptus apud audientes. Fiat insuper prædicatio principaliter de punctis nostræ religionis in fide, spe & charitate cum cæteris virtutibus. Sed & præsertim confessiones mulierum & iuuenum non nisi locis patentibus & publicis audire: nec conuenticula in cameris & angulis agere præsummant, ab omni specie mala abstinentes se.
units.tr: The privileged status, in preaching, ought to shape the sermon according to the quality of the hearers, so that the faults of clerics and of lords are not exposed before laymen and subjects. For this would not be to root out vices but to nourish rebellion, namely murmuring and contempt among the hearers. Let the preaching moreover be given chiefly on the points of our religion in faith, hope and charity, with the other virtues. And especially let them hear the confessions of women and young people only in open and public places, and let them not presume to hold private meetings in rooms and corners, abstaining from every evil appearance.

units.la: PARS SEXTA. DE VTROQVE STATV SIMVL.
units.tr: PART SIX. CONCERNING BOTH STATES TOGETHER.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO I.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION I.

units.la: Tatus vterque, curatorum scilicet & priuilegiatorum, inuigilet cognoscere casus reseruatos prælatis, ne seducantur & seducant, si transgrediantur limites suæ potestatis; quamuis expediret pauciores casus præsertim occultos reseruari, vt sunt peccata illa carnis, quæ frequentissime commissa vix confitentur: præsertim per mulieres & adolescentulos.
units.tr: Let both states, that is the parish priests and the privileged clergy, take care to learn the cases reserved to the prelates, so that they neither be led astray nor lead others astray, should they overstep the limits of their power; although it would be expedient for fewer cases to be reserved, especially secret ones, such as those sins of the flesh which, though very often committed, are scarcely confessed, particularly by women and young people.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO II.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION II.

units.la: Status vterque studeat alter alterius onera portare sine contentione & æmulatione de rebus prædicatis vel aliis: ne si inuicem more cornicum se mordeant, consumantur. Né præterea surgat fœda opinio ecclesiasticorum apud laicos: & vituperetur ministerium verbi Dei. Nonne Deus quæso abunde dives est pro omnibus? Nonne pacis est Deus, non diuisionis? Denique quid prodest Pharisaica contentio de statu præeminentia, quin sanctius est dare operam, vt quis perfectus inueniatur, quam si iacens in imis de perfectione status glorietur. Attento præsertim, quod consiliorum ecclesiasticorum obseruatio non potest ita concludi sub regulis quibuscunque, quin necesse sit recurrere sæpissime ad glossam sapientissimi Augustini tractam ex operibus Christi: videlicet quod talia dantur in obseruanda animi præparatione, & non semper operis exhibitione.
units.tr: Let each state strive to bear the burdens of the other without quarrelling and rivalry, whether over the matters just mentioned or others, lest, if they bite one another like crows, they be consumed. Furthermore, let no disgraceful opinion of churchmen arise among the laity, and let the ministry of the Word of God not be held in contempt. Is not God, I ask, abundantly rich for all? Is not God the God of peace, not of division? In short, what good does a Pharisaical contest over the pre-eminence of a state do? Would it not be holier to labour that someone be found perfect, than for a man lying in the lowest place to boast of the perfection of his state? This is especially so, since the observance of the ecclesiastical counsels cannot be concluded under any rules, so that it is necessary to recur very often to the gloss of the most wise Augustine, drawn from the works of Christ: namely, that such things are given with regard to the preparation of the mind, and not always to the outward performance of the work.

units.la: Quæ animi præparatio potest apud omnem statum & personam Christianæ religionis, si vult, inueniri.
units.tr: This preparation of the mind can be found, if one wishes, in every state and person of the Christian religion.

units.la: TRACTATVS EIVSDEM CANCELLARII PARISIENSIS DE MODO VIVENDI OMNIVM FIDELIUM.
units.tr: TRACTATE OF THE SAME CHANCELLOR OF PARIS, CONCERNING THE WAY OF LIFE OF ALL THE FAITHFUL.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO PRIMA.
units.tr: FIRST CONSIDERATION.

units.la: Ad Nobiles.
units.tr: To the Nobles.

units.la: REgula prima, quæ spectat ad nobiles, potentes & scabinos: ne pauperes videlicet per potentiam suam opprimant, & à subditis suis opprimi permittant. Malos vsus in villis suis destruant. Causas pauperum, viduarum & orphanorum libenter audiant: & cito iuste iudicent. Munera pro iudicio faciendo vel festinando aut retardando non accipiant. Nil à subditis suis extorqueant.
units.tr: The first rule, which applies to nobles, powerful men and magistrates (scabini): namely, that they should not oppress the poor through their power, nor allow their subjects to be oppressed. They should destroy bad customs in their villages. They should gladly hear the causes of the poor, widows and orphans, and judge them quickly and justly. They should not accept gifts for judging, or for hastening or delaying judgment. They should extort nothing from their subjects.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO II.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION II.

units.la: Ad Milites.
units.tr: To Soldiers.

units.la: Regula ad Milites tangitur Lucæ 3. Neminem concutiatis, scilicet in persona per potentiam indebite. Nemini calumniam faciatis in rebus, quam per militiam facere possetis. Et contenti estote stipendiis vestris, id est, de redditibus vestris multis temporibus: accipiendo vero ad defendendam patriam 2. Macch. 15. Accipe gladium sanctum munus &c. Rom. 13. Non sine causa gladium portat.
units.tr: The rule for soldiers is touched on in Luke 3. Do violence to no one, that is, do not unjustly harm anyone through power. Do not accuse anyone falsely in matters of property, which you might do by means of your military service. And be content with your wages, that is, with your pay from your estates over many seasons; but take up the sword in defence of the fatherland, 2 Macc. 15: Take this holy sword as a gift, etc. Rom. 13: He does not bear the sword in vain.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO III.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION III.

units.la: Ad Simplices.
units.tr: To Simple People.

units.la: Regula simplicium quo ad ecclesiam: vt ieiuni ad missam veniant. In missa non loquantur nec circumspiciant. Ante missam orare debent, vt gratiam Dei recipiant. In missa memoriam passionis Christi habeant. Ante euangelium sancti Ioannis non exeant. Sermones libenter & diligenter audiant: & referre post missam gratias Deo satagant.
units.tr: The rule for simple people, as regards the church: that they come to Mass fasting. In Mass they should not talk or look about. Before Mass they ought to pray, that they may receive the grace of God. During Mass they should keep in mind the passion of Christ. They should not leave before the Gospel of St John. They should gladly and diligently hear the sermons, and take care to give thanks to God after Mass.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO IV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION IV.

units.la: Ad Episcopos & Prælatos.
units.tr: To Bishops and Prelates.

units.la: Regula episcoporum & prælatorum satis patet ad Titum 1. Oportet episcopum sine crimine esse sicut Dei dispensatorem. Et Matth. 20. Quì maior est vestrum, sit vester minister 2. Corinth. 6. Hortamur vos &c. Est autem officium episcopi, malos corrigere & arguere bonos & pusillanimes pacificare. Quia, sicut Dominus Petro in persona cuiuslibet prælati ait: Pasce oues meas &c. 1. Thessal. 5. Fratres corripite inquietos: consolamini pusillanimes, De istis 2. ad Timo. 4. Prædica verbum: insta opportune, importune: obsecra, argue, increpa in omni patientia & doctrina. Et ad Galat. 6. Si præoccupatus fuerit homo in aliquo delicto &c.
units.tr: The rule for bishops and prelates is quite plain from Titus 1: A bishop must be blameless, as God's steward. And Matt. 20: Whoever is greatest among you, let him be your minister. 2 Cor. 6: We exhort you, etc. The office of a bishop, however, is to correct the wicked, to reprove the good, and to calm the fainthearted. For, as the Lord said to Peter in the person of every prelate: Feed my sheep, etc. 1 Thess. 5: Admonish the unruly, comfort the fainthearted. To these things 2 Tim. 4 also applies: Preach the word; be urgent in season and out of season; rebuke, reprove and exhort with all patience and teaching. And Gal. 6: If a man is overtaken in any fault, etc.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO V.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION V.

units.la: Ad Clericos.
units.tr: To Clergy.

units.la: Regula clericorum est habere doctrinam sanam, vitam sanctam, famam odoriferam. Hebr. 5. Sacerdotes habent hostias pro delictis suis offerre. Et Aug. in Regula sua: Sit vobis cor unum & anima una in Domino. Psal. Sacerdotes tui induantur iustitia. Col. 4. Induite vos sicut electi Dei viscera misericordiæ & pietatis habentes.
units.tr: The rule for clergy is to have sound doctrine, a holy life and a fragrant reputation. Heb. 5: Priests have to offer sacrifices for their own sins. And Augustine in his Rule: Let your hearts and souls be one in the Lord. Psalm: Let your priests be clothed with righteousness. Col. 4: Put on, as God's elect, bowels of mercy and kindness.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION VI.

units.la: Ad Religiosos.
units.tr: To Religious.

units.la: Regula religiosorum est viuere in obedientia, castitate & paupertate. Et devote orare & contemplari, & carnem mortificare contra vitia & concupiscentias. Unde Augustinus in Regula monachorum: In omnibus & super omnia ametur & honorificetur Deus. Et Hugo de sancto Vict. de claustro animæ: Summa religionis regula in hoc dependet vt prælati custodiant subditos suos: subditi prælatis benigne obediant: devoti sint senes: iuuenes vero laboriosi. Sit honestas in habitu: mediocritas in victu. Sint in claustro assidui: & ad iniuriam rari. Non sint ciuiles, sed claustrales. Sint intenti Psalmis, non causis. Non sit rumor in claustro, sed dilectio. In capitulo non lites, sed confessio. In choro sit sacra simplicitas, & circa altare reverentia honestas.
units.tr: The rule for religious is to live in obedience, chastity and poverty; to pray devoutly and contemplate, and to mortify the flesh against vices and lusts. Hence Augustine in the Rule for monks: In all things and above all things let God be loved and honoured. And Hugh of St Victor, in On the Cloister of the Soul: The sum of the rule of religion depends on this: that prelates protect their subjects, that subjects obey their prelates kindly; let the elders be devout and the young be industrious. Let there be decency in dress and moderation in food. Let them be constant in the cloister and rarely outside it. Let them be cloistered, not worldly. Let them attend to the Psalms, not to lawsuits. Let there be no gossip in the cloister, but love. In chapter let there be no quarrels, but confession. In the choir let there be holy simplicity, and around the altar reverent decency.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION VII.

units.la: Ad Diuites.
units.tr: To the Rich.

units.la: Regula diuitum: ne aliquid iniustum acquirant: ne propter diuitias suas pauperes vicinos despiciant. Pauperes sustineant. Operariis suis bene & cito persoluant. Adulatores neque adulatrices in mensa recipiant. Diligenter & libenter ad concordiam vicinorum suorum laborent.
units.tr: The rule for the rich: that they acquire nothing unjustly; that they not look down on their poor neighbours because of their riches; that they support the poor; that they pay their workers well and promptly; that they not receive flatterers, male or female, at their table; and that they labour diligently and gladly for the harmony of their neighbours.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO VIII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION VIII.

units.la: Ad Pauperes.
units.tr: To the Poor.

units.la: Regula pauperum: vt diuitibus libenter & fideliter seruiant: nec diuitibus propter diuitias suas inuideant, nec propter paupertatem adulatione vel detractione peccent. Nec impatienter, sed gratanter paupertatem sustineant: nec iniuste ditari cupiant: nec ecclesias propter diuites vitent. Nihil furti a familia suorum vicinorum, nec ab aliis retineant.
units.tr: The rule for the poor: that they serve the rich gladly and faithfully; that they not envy the rich for their riches, nor sin, either by flattery or by slander, on account of their poverty. They should bear poverty not impatiently but with thanksgiving, nor desire to be enriched unjustly, nor avoid the churches on account of the rich. They should keep nothing stolen from the households of their neighbours, nor from anyone else.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO IX.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION IX.

units.la: Ad Virgines.
units.tr: To Virgins.

units.la: Regula virginum: Non sint loquaces, sed simplices corde & habitu. Ad virginitatem matris Christi cogitent, & eam diligant. Choreas vitent. Inter iuuenes non sedeant: nec se ab eis palpari permittant: non ament aliquem illicito amore. Adulatores neque adulatrices recipiant nec audiant. Orationes libenter dicant. Sordida verba & inhonesta fugiant.
units.tr: The rule for virgins: they should not be talkative, but simple in heart and in dress. They should think of the virginity of the mother of Christ and love it. They should avoid dances. They should not sit among young men, nor allow themselves to be fondled by them; they should not love anyone with an unlawful love. They should not receive or listen to flatterers, male or female. They should gladly say prayers. They should flee foul and indecent words.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO X.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION X.

units.la: Ad Viduas.
units.tr: To Widows.

units.la: Regula viduarum est, vt continentiam diligant: & in vestibus humiliter se habeant: & orationibus libenter insistant. Homines suspectos in hospitio suo non recipiant. De consilio proborum se gubernent & viuant. Sanctam Annam & Elisabet viduas cogitent. Familiam castam habeant. Parum per vicos currant.
units.tr: The rule for widows is that they love continence, behave humbly in their clothing, and devote themselves gladly to prayers. They should not receive suspect persons into their house. They should govern and live by the counsel of upright people. They should think of the holy widows Anna and Elizabeth. They should have a chaste household. They should seldom run about the villages.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XI.

units.la: Ad Nuptas.
units.tr: To Wives.

units.la: Regula nuptarum est Thimo. honorare superiores: diligere maritum: regere familiam: diligenter gubernare domum, & seipsam honestam & irreprehensibilem ostendere siue exhibere.
units.tr: The rule for wives is set out in 1 Tim.: to honour their superiors, to love their husband, to rule the household, to manage the home diligently, and to show and present themselves as honest and blameless.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XII.

units.la: Ad Mulieres.
units.tr: To Women.

units.la: Regula mulierum est: quod non se indecenter ornatas ostendant. Aures, collum, guttur & caput tegant. Humiliter in ecclesia & vbique se habeant: nec alias mulieres per superbiam suam imitentur.
units.tr: The rule for women is that they should not display themselves with indecent adornment. They should cover their ears, neck, throat and head. They should conduct themselves humbly in church and everywhere, and not imitate other women in their pride.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XIII.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XIII.

units.la: Ad Maritos & Vxores.
units.tr: To Husbands and Wives.

units.la: Regula virorum ad mulieres & econuerso ponitur ad Ephes. 5. Viri diligite vxores vestras, sicut & Christus dilexit ecclesiam suam. Vxor autem timeat virum suum, 1. Pet. 3. Viri cohabitantes secundum conscientiam quasi infirmiori vasculo muliebri impartientes honorem.
units.tr: The rule for husbands towards wives, and conversely, is given in Ephes. 5: Husbands, love your wives, as Christ also loved his church. And let the wife fear her husband. 1 Pet. 3: Husbands, dwelling with your wives according to knowledge, giving honour to the female as to the weaker vessel.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XIV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XIV.

units.la: Parentum ad Filios.
units.tr: Of Parents to Children.

units.la: Regula parentum ad filios, Ephes. 6. Et vos patres nolite provocare ad iracundiam filios vestros: sed educate eos in disciplina & correptione 2. Corinth. 12. Non debent filii thesaurizare parentibus: sed parentes filiis.
units.tr: The rule for parents towards children is in Ephes. 6: And you fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the discipline and correction of the Lord. 2 Cor. 12: Children ought not to lay up treasure for their parents, but parents for their children.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XV.

units.la: Filiorum ad parentes.
units.tr: Of Children to Parents.

units.la: Regula filiorum ad parentes est: quod parentes honorent, & eis in bonis obediant: nec eis sua furentur. Ante eos non respondeant: a maledictionibus omnino sibi caveant. Cum parentibus aliquando ad ecclesiam vadant libenter: in negotiis parentum suorum fideliter laborent.
units.tr: The rule for children towards parents is that they honour their parents and obey them in good things, and not steal their goods. They should not answer back before them, and should guard themselves entirely against curses. They should gladly go to church with their parents at times, and labour faithfully in their parents' affairs.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XVI.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XVI.

units.la: Dominorum ad seruos.
units.tr: Of Masters to Servants.

units.la: Regula Dominorum ad seruos Ephes. 6. Vos Domini eadem facite illis remittentes minas & soluite: Domini quod iustum est & aequum seruis praestate: scientes quod vos Dominum in coelis habetis. Eccl. 7. Ne ladas seruum tuum in veritate operantem. Seruus sensatus sit tibi dilectus quasi anima tua: non defraudes illum libertate: neque inopem derelinquas illum.
units.tr: The rule for masters towards servants is in Ephes. 6: And you masters, do the same to them, forbearing threatening, and give to your servants what is just and equal, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven. Eccl. 7: Do not wrong your servant who works faithfully. Let a sensible servant be dear to you as your own soul; do not defraud him of liberty, nor leave him in want.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XVII. Seruorum ad Dominos.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION XVII. Of Servants towards their Masters.

units.la: Regula seruorum ad Dominos. Col. 3. Serui obedite Dominis carnalibus: non ad oculum seruientes quasi hominibus placentes: sed in simplicitate cordis timentes Deum: scientes quod a Domino accipietis retributionem hereditatis. 1. Pet. 2. Serui subditi estote in omni timore Dominis vestris, non tantum bonis &c.
units.tr: The rule for servants towards their masters. Col. 3. Servants, obey your masters according to the flesh, not serving with eye-service as men-pleasers, but in singleness of heart fearing God; knowing that from the Lord you shall receive the reward of the inheritance. 1. Pet. 2. Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle, etc.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XVIII. Ad Familiam.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION XVIII. To the Household.

units.la: Regula ad familiam: Ne fraudem Dominis suis in seruiendo, negligendo faciant: Fideles sint in rebus suis custodiendis. Nihil ab eis auferant occulte: nec alios facere permittant. Nuncium malum non faciant vxori vel filiis Domini sui. De male respondendo caueant. Malos rumores sugiant, vnde in domum malum oriri possit: sed discordias etiam reportare vitent. Missi cito reuertantur. Mercedem suam in superbia vestium non expendant. Ita viuant in humilitate vt labor eorum sit eis in remissionem peccatorum suorum.
units.tr: The rule for the household: they must not defraud their masters by neglect in serving; let them be faithful in looking after their masters' goods. They must not take anything from them in secret, nor allow others to do so. They must not carry bad news to the wife or children of their master. They should take care in how they answer back. They should shun evil gossip, from which evil might arise in the house, and they should avoid bringing back quarrels as well. Those who are sent should return quickly. They should not spend their wages on showy clothing. Let them live in such humility that their labour may be to them a remission of their sins.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XIX. Ad Mercatores.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION XIX. To Merchants.

units.la: Regula mercatorum est: vt non in die Dominica mercentur. Nec periurent. Ab illicito sibi caueant lucro: nec ad diem vendant vel charius propter dilationem. Vt debitum suum tempore promisso soluant. Nec scientes mentiantur. Æquam stateram habeant, æqua pondera & æquam mensuram.
units.tr: The rule for merchants is this: that they do not trade on the Lord's Day. Nor should they swear falsely. They should guard against unlawful gain, nor sell on credit or at a higher price on account of delayed payment. They should pay their debts at the promised time. Nor should they lie knowingly. They should keep honest scales, honest weights and an honest measure.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XX. Ad Tabernatores.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XX. To Tavern-Keepers.

units.la: Regula tabernatorum est: Ne permittant ludere ad taxillos in tabula sua, neq; in taberna sua. Deum blasphemare non permittant, nec meretrices recipiant de nocte. Plenam mensuram dent omnibus. Vinum cum aqua ad vendendum non misceant: nec aliqua pocula vel fercula aliquo modo ad vendendum defraudent.
units.tr: The rule for tavern-keepers is this: they must not allow dice games to be played at their table or in their tavern. They must not permit blasphemy of God, nor take in prostitutes at night. They are to give full measure to everyone. They must not mix wine with water for sale, nor cheat in any way in the sale of cups or dishes.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XXI. Ad Hospites.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION XXI. To Innkeepers.

units.la: Regula ad hospites est: quod malos in hospitio suo non permittant vel scienter recipiant: nec hospitibus suis furentur auenam vel fœnum. Nec sustineant quod hospites scienter fornicentur in hospitio suo. Iustam, bonam, rationabilem computationem cum hospitibus suis faciant.
units.tr: The rule for innkeepers is this: they should not allow bad people to lodge in their house, nor knowingly receive them. They must not steal oats or hay from their guests. Nor should they tolerate guests committing fornication knowingly in their house. They should make a just, good and reasonable reckoning with their guests.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XXII. Ad Senes.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XXII. Concerning the Elders.

units.la: Regula ad senes est: In ecclesia libenter iaceant. Iuuentibus bonum exemplum præbeant. De maledicendo siue malefaciendo ipsos reprehendant. Turpia verba non habeant: nec laudent malitias coram iuuenibus. Mulierculas a bono non retrahant: nec iuuenes laudent in superbiis suis.
units.tr: The rule for the elders is: they should be willing to lie down in the church (that is, to be humble and submit themselves). They should set a good example for the young. They should rebuke them for slandering or doing evil. They should not use obscene words, nor praise wickedness in the presence of the young. They should not draw the women away from what is good, nor praise the young men in their pride.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO XXIII. Ad Omnes.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO XXIII. To All.

units.la: REgula ad omnes est, vt excommunicatos vitent. Non se inebrient. Pauperes pro posse suo sustineant. Sacerdotes & religiosos & ecclesiam vbique honorent. Et deuote ab eis doctrinam audiant. Festa bene custodiant. Decimas rite soluant. Detractionem caueant. Ab adulatione, a blasphemia, a mendacio, a periurio, ab assiduo iuramento, a turpibus verbis, & maxime a luxuriosis verbis se abstineant: quia circumstantes & audientes ab eis inflammantur. Præcepta ecclesiæ teneant: pœnitentias sibi iniunctas diligenter impleant. Alter alterum ad bonum opus inuiter, & de malo reprehendat. Dent libenter eleemosynas: quia sicut aqua extinguit ignem: ita eleemosyna extinguit peccatum. Missas, sermones & confessiones libenter colant & frequentent. Ablata restituant: quia non dimittitur peccatum, nisi restituatur ablatum: vt dicit Aug. in vespere, id est, in fine vitæ tormenta inferni & gaudia Paradisi cogitent. Regula omnium ponitur Matth. 28. Baptizantes omnes gentes in nomine Patris & Filii & Spiritus sancti: vt secundum illud Ioan. 1. Omnes crederent per illum 1. Pet. 3. In fide autem omnes vnanimes. In oratione estote compatientes: fraternitatis amatores, misericordes, modesti, humiles: non reddentes malum pro malo, neque maledictum pro maledicto: sed e contrario benedicentes &c. Eccles. vltim. Deum time & mandata eius observa. hoc est omnis homo &c. vnde Gal. 6. Qui hanc regulam secuti fuerint, pax super illos & misericordia.
units.tr: The rule for everyone is this: they should avoid the excommunicated, not get drunk, support the poor as far as they are able, and honour priests, religious and the Church everywhere, and devoutly hear her teaching. They should keep the feast days well, pay their tithes duly, and beware of slander, flattery, blasphemy, lying, perjury, constant swearing, and foul words, and above all of lewd speech, since those who stand by and hear it are inflamed by it. They should keep the precepts of the Church and carefully perform the penances laid on them. Let each urge the other to good works and rebuke him for evil. They should give alms willingly, for as water quenches fire, so alms quench sin. They should gladly attend and frequent Masses, sermons and confessions. They should make restitution of what they have taken, because "sin is not forgiven unless what was taken is restored," as Augustine says. In the evening, that is, at the end of life, let them think on the torments of hell and the joys of Paradise. The rule of all is given in Matt. 28: "Baptizing all nations in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit," so that, according to John 1, "all might believe through him"; and 1 Pet. 3: "But in faith, all of one mind." In prayer, be sympathetic, lovers of the brotherhood, merciful, modest and humble, not rendering evil for evil, nor curse for curse, but on the contrary blessing, etc. (Eccles. last chapter): "Fear God and keep his commandments," that is, the whole duty of man, etc. Hence Gal. 6: "As many as walk according to this rule, peace be upon them and mercy."

units.la: cordia.
units.tr: mercy.

units.la: SERMO EIVSDEM DOCTORIS DE TRIBVLATIONIBVS EX DEFECTVOSO ECCLESIASTICORVM REGIMINE, ADHVC ECCLESIAE PROVENTURIS: & de signis earundem, ex sententia pronunciatus de conceptione gloriosæ virginis Mariæ, in concilio Constantiensi.
units.tr: THE SAME DOCTOR'S SERMON ON THE TRIBULATIONS TO COME FOR THE CHURCH FROM THE DEFECTIVE GOVERNMENT OF ITS CLERGY, AND ON THE SIGNS OF THEM, DELIVERED ON THE CONCEPTION OF THE GLORIOUS VIRGIN MARY, BY SENTENCE OF THE COUNCIL OF CONSTANCE.

units.la: Dominus dabit vobis signum: Ecce virgo concipiet & pariet filium. Esai. septim. recitatum &c.
units.tr: The Lord himself will give you a sign: Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son. Isaiah 7, quoted etc.

units.la: Nunc quoad secundum, Reuerendi patres & Domini, restat ostendere quomodo signum omnipotentiæ & summæ clementiæ factum sit signum contradictionis & ruinæ. Contradixit enim Achaz petere signum, quod per Prophetam, scil. Esaiam a Domino sibi erat præceptum: Non petam, inquit, & non tentabo Dominum. Hoc quidem addidit: & non tentabo Dominum i forma quidem pietatis, sed non virtutis. Colebat Achaz idolum, quod deserere noluit: & ideo ne Dominus exaltaretur & idolum vilipenderetur, signum petere recusauit. Et propter hoc, teste beato Hieron. in Gloss. in grauem ruinam incidit: quia totaliter à Domino derelictus fuit.
units.tr: Now as to the second part, reverend fathers and lords, it remains to show how the sign of almighty power and supreme mercy became a sign of contradiction and ruin. Ahaz contradicted the request for a sign, which the Lord had commanded him through the prophet Isaiah: I will not ask, he said, and I will not tempt the Lord. He added, and I will not tempt the Lord, in the form of piety but not of virtue. Ahaz worshipped an idol, which he was unwilling to abandon; so, lest the Lord be exalted and the idol be despised, he refused to ask for a sign. And for this, as blessed Jerome testifies in the Gloss, he fell into grievous ruin, because he was utterly forsaken by the Lord.

units.la: Verum quia ipsius Achaz contradictio signi aduentum longe præcessit. Consideremus illud, quod iustus Simeon & timoratus post signi ortum prophetauerit: Ecce, inquit, positus est hic in ruinam multorum in Israel, & in signum cui contradicetur. Ad Virginem vero: Tuam, inquit, ipsius animam pertransibit gladius, Luc. 2. Quod vtiq; orto signo Herodes impleuit: quia mox pueri animam quæsiuit. Postmodum contradixerunt Iudæi, contradixerunt persecutores, contradixerunt hæretici: quorum aliqui Virginem non de substantia carnis Christum edidisse dogmatizabant. Alii filium non peperisse, sed reperisse sibilabant. Alii vero cognitam blasphemabant. Alii Dei matrem audire non sustinentes, magnum illud nomen θεοτόκον impiissime sugillabant. Sed cunctas hæreses in suis auctoritatibus sola Virgo in ruinam detrusit, quando Archangeli signum nuncianris credidit. Sed præter hos magis contradicunt alii, scil. moderni Ecclesiastici, qui nedum signo contradicunt, sed gladio Virginis animam crudeliter transfigunt. Per virginem noto Ecclesiam, cuius typum gerit virgo Maria: quam trahunt in ruinam per mala exempla. Neq; enim hæreticorum atq; persecutorum contradictio tantam Ecclesiæ intulit ruinam: quin ipsa semper in sobolem creseret nimiam: imo quanto maiorem contradictionem sustinuit, tanto plures suæ virginitatis defensores peperit. Tales pergebant intrepidi in eius aditorium, galeam bonorum exemplorum imponebant capiti, & accingebant gladium spiritus, quod est verbum Dei. Porro si quandoq; hic videbatur calcari in sanguine, tamen viuebat, & eo amplius crescebat ex Dei virtute: Domino de eo loquente sub nomine Hierusalem Ezech. In die qua nata es, inquit, vidi te conculcari in sanguine tuo, & dixi tibi: In sanguine tuo viue. Et loquitur de tempore martyrum. Sequitur: Et multiplicata es quasi germen agri, & grandis effecta es: emundaui sanguinem tuum, scilicet cessante persecutione. Grandis quidem effecta erat multitudine credentium, grandis speciositate virtutum: grandis copiositate temporalium, eodem Propheta subsequenter dicente: Dedi, inquit, coronam decoris in capite tuo, & ornata es auro & argento. Decora facta es nimis vehementer & profecisti in regnum. & egressum est nomen tuum in gentes propter speciem tuam, quia perfecta eras in decore meo quem posueram super te. Magis videtur historia hæc quam Prophetia de prosperitate Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: But since Ahaz's contradiction came long before the sign appeared, let us consider what the just and devout Simeon prophesied after the sign's birth: Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and for a sign which shall be contradicted. And to the Virgin: a sword shall pierce your own soul, Luke 2. This Herod fulfilled as soon as the sign was born, since he at once sought the child's life. Afterwards the Jews contradicted, persecutors contradicted, heretics contradicted; some of them taught that the Virgin did not bring forth Christ from the substance of flesh; others hissed that she did not bear a son but found one; others blasphemed that she had been known by a man; and others, unable to bear the name Mother of God, most impiously reviled that great name θεοτόκος [theotokos]. But the Virgin alone, when she believed the announced sign of the archangel, overthrew all the heresies by their own authorities. Yet beyond these there are others who contradict more, namely the modern churchmen, who not only contradict the sign but cruelly pierce the Virgin's soul with the sword. By the virgin I mean the Church, whose type the Virgin Mary bears, and whom they drag into ruin by bad examples. For the contradiction of heretics and persecutors did not bring such great ruin upon the Church; rather she always grew into a very numerous offspring. Indeed, the greater the contradiction she endured, the more defenders of her virginity she bore. Such defenders went fearlessly to her court, put the helmet of good examples on their heads, and girded on the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God. Moreover, if at times she seemed to be trodden down in blood, she nevertheless lived, and grew all the more by God's power, the Lord speaking of her under the name of Jerusalem in Ezekiel: On the day you were born, I saw you trodden in your blood, and I said to you: Live in your blood. And he speaks of the time of the martyrs. It follows: And you were multiplied like the plant of the field, and became great; I have cleansed your blood, namely when persecution ceased. She indeed became great in the multitude of believers, great in the splendour of her virtues, great in temporal abundance, as the same prophet says afterwards: I put a crown of beauty on your head, and you were adorned with gold and silver. You became exceedingly beautiful, and you prospered into a kingdom. Your name went out among the nations because of your beauty, for you were perfect in my comeliness which I had placed upon you. This is history rather than prophecy, concerning the prosperity of the Church.

units.la: Sed quid Reuerendi Patres & Domini de moderno tempore idem Propheta subiungit, audiamus: Et habens, inquit, fiduciam in pulchritudine tua, scilicet in temporalium abundantia & seculari potentia, fornicata es in nomine meo, loquitur similitudinarie de fornicatione: sicut mulier præbens venale quod natura fecit non venale, dicitur fornicari. Sic etiam dicitur fornicari secundum Doctores præbens venale prece, pretio vel inordinato fauore, quod gratis erat dandum pro virtute.
units.tr: But let us hear what the same prophet adds about the present time, reverend fathers and lords: And trusting in your beauty, namely in the abundance of temporal things and secular power, you played the harlot in my name. He speaks figuratively of fornication: as a woman who offers for sale what nature made not for sale is said to play the harlot, so, according to the doctors, one is said to "fornicate" who offers for sale, by prayer, price or disordered favour, what ought to be given freely for virtue.

units.la: Sequitur: Et post omnes abominationes tuas non es recordata dierum adolescentiæ tuæ, scilicet de tempore martyrum & sanctorum patrum, sed in cunctis plateis ad omne caput vie ædificasti signa prostitutionis tuæ & abominabilem fecisti decorem tuum. Tunc sequitur punitio & grauis ruina: Ecce ego, inquit, dabo te in manus odientium te, & destruent lupanar tuum, & demolientur prostibulum tuum, id est, locum in quo exercebatur iniustitia & symonia: & denudabunt te vestimentis tuis, & auferent vasa gloriae tuae, & relinquent te plenam ignominia. Hæc dicit Dominus omnipotens. Ezech. 16. Sed forsan aliqui blandientes sibi putant hæc sic dicta de futuro, quod non sint timenda, aut quod venire debeant de propinquo. Et ideo quamvis non sit nostrum nosse tempora vel momenta, quæ pater posuit in sua potestate, tamen propono ex dictis doctorum & sacra scriptura aliqua contradictionis & ruinæ signa adducere: ex quibus possumus propinquitatem suspicare vel coniicere.
units.tr: It follows: And after all your abominations you did not remember the days of your youth, namely the time of the martyrs and holy fathers, but in all the squares, at every corner of the road, you built your signs of prostitution, and made your beauty abominable. Then follows punishment and grievous ruin: Behold, I will give you into the hands of those who hate you, and they will destroy your brothel and pull down your harlot's house, that is, the place where injustice and simony were practised; and they will strip you of your garments, take away the vessels of your glory, and leave you full of shame. Thus says the Lord God Almighty, Ezekiel 16. But perhaps some, flattering themselves, think that these things are said of the future in such a way that they need not be feared, or that they must come from a near time. And therefore, although it is not ours to know the times or moments which the Father has placed in his own power, nevertheless I propose to adduce from the sayings of the doctors and from Holy Scripture some signs of contradiction and ruin, from which we may suspect or conjecture that the time is near.

units.la: Primum signum est rebellionis & inobedientiæ. Et hoc sumitur ex verbis Apostoli 2. ad Thessal. 2. Et nisi venerit discessio primum &c. Quod Beatus Hieronym. ii. q. ad inquisitionem Algasiæ exponit de Romani Imperii desolatione: inter quam & Ecclesiæ persecutiones præuias Antichristo: quarum una forsitan erit prima temporalium ablatio, nullum ponit medium. Quædam Glossa dicit, quod erit discessio aliarum ecclesiarum ab ipsa Romana Ecclesia. Magister super verbo præmisso has simul coniungit: Completa, inquit, hac accessione ad Romanum Imperium & Ecclesiæ obedientiam: aderit discessio ab utroque imperio. Accessionem novimus fuisse ante huius schismatis ortum, postmodum completa videtur fuisse discessio. Et primo ab imperio temporali. Hoc satis euidenter apparuit: quia vix ciuitas, Baro aut miles ante huius gloriosæ Virginis assumptionem Romano Imperio obedire cœpit. Et si aliqui videbantur obedire, hoc erat vel in sanguinis propinquitate, vel præsidentis proprii dominii potestate.
units.tr: The first sign is rebellion and disobedience. This is taken from the words of the Apostle, 2 Thessalonians 2: Unless the falling away comes first, etc. Blessed Jerome, in his second question, in answer to Algasia's inquiry, explains this of the desolation of the Roman Empire, and between this and the persecutions of the Church preceding Antichrist he places no intermediate step; one of these, perhaps, will be the first removal of temporal things. A certain Gloss says that it will be the departure of other churches from the Roman Church itself. The Master, on the preceding word, joins these together: When this accession to the Roman Empire and obedience to the Church is complete, there will be a departure from both empires. We know that the accession took place before the rise of this schism; afterwards the departure seems to have been completed, and first from the temporal empire. This appeared quite plainly, for hardly any city, baron or soldier began to obey the Roman Empire before the assumption of this glorious Virgin. And if some seemed to obey, this was either from bonds of blood-kinship or from the power of their own lordship.

units.la: Discessio à Romana Ecclesia videtur in ecclesia completa. Nam si primo vel secundo electus in exordio schismatis fuerit pontifex vere: tunc ab utroq; vel successoribus recessus videtur completus. Nam ad tantam ambiguitatem vniuersalis Ecclesia deuenit, quod ignorat apud quam partem vera Sedes Romana erat, nisi forsan Deus alicui reuelasset: aut Salomonis iudicium de puero diuidendo, & vera & falsa matre hoc persuaderet.
units.tr: The departure from the Roman Church seems to have been completed within the Church itself. For if the pope elected first or second at the beginning of the schism was truly pope, then the withdrawal from both, or from their successors, seems complete. For the universal Church has come to such great uncertainty that it does not know on which side the true Roman See lay, unless God had perhaps revealed it to someone, or unless Solomon's judgment about dividing the child, between the true and the false mother, were to persuade it of this.

units.la: Secundum signum desolationis est inuerecundia. Et hoc sumitur ex illo: quia efficitur moribus peior quam fuit Synagoga, cum imminebat eius ruina. Vnde secundum Beatum Hieronym. triplex erat peccatum Pharisæorum, qui & dicebantur clerici Iudæorum, scilicet auaritia: quia columbas in templo vendi permittebant. Solum labiis Deum honorabant, & tanquam hypocritæ docebant quæ non faciebant. Sed nunquid id peius est sacrilegium ecclesiastica beneficia & spiritualia potestates pretio aut inordinato fauore distribuere, quam columbas in templo vendi permittere? An ne minus malum sit solum labiis Deum honorare, aliosque per hoc ad devotionem inducere quam locum ministerii, solum spe quæstus suscipere: & cessare ob superbiam à laude Dei, & silere? Et de talibus Esai. 56. Canes muti non valentes latrare. Canes impudentissimi nescientes saturitatem. Venient dies super vos &c. Demum nunquid minus nociuunt videtur Ecclesiæ propriam malitiam hypocrisis pallio cooperire, & velut æs sonans & cymbalum tinniens per alios prædicationis officium docere: quam inuerecunde prauis moribus & exemplis subditos secum in ruinam trahere? Æstimo enim quod nemo boni iudicii contrarium diceret: sed illud Hierem. 3. potius completum concederet: Iustificauit animam suam auersatrix Israel, id est, synagoga comparatione prevaricationis Iudæ. Ibi Origenes, De nobis, inquit, hac intelligit. Ezech. 16. Dominus loquens ecclesiæ: Soror tua Samaria, (id est synagoga,) dimidium peccatorum tuorum non peccauit: sed vicisti eam sceleribus tuis. Sequitur ruina: Ergo & tu porta confusionem tuam Et infra 23. postquam diffuse descripsit malitiam & destructionem synagogæ, adiecit dicens de Ecclesia: Plus insanauit libidine, & fornicationem suam prebuit impudenter diuitibus & magistratibus ad se venientibus indutâ veste varia. Et bene, inquit, induta veste varia insaniuit libidine, id est, cupiditate diuitiarum & concupiscentia delitiarum. Erat namq; futurum, ut prælati ecclesiarum non vererentur ecclesiæ primitiuæ venerandam pudicitiam pretio ac precibus & impiis actibus infamare. Ita ut impletum sit quod sequitur: Confracta sunt mamma pubertatis tuæ.
units.tr: The second sign of desolation is shamelessness. This is taken from the fact that she becomes worse in morals than the Synagogue was when its ruin was at hand. Hence, according to blessed Jerome, the sin of the Pharisees, who were also called the clergy of the Jews, was threefold: avarice, since they allowed doves to be sold in the temple; they honoured God only with their lips, and as hypocrites taught what they did not practise. But is it not a worse sacrilege to distribute ecclesiastical benefices and spiritual powers for a price or out of disordered favour than to allow doves to be sold in the temple? Or is it less evil to honour God only with the lips, and thereby lead others to devotion, than to take up a place of ministry only in hope of gain, and out of pride to cease from praising God and to keep silent? Concerning such men, Isaiah 56: Dumb dogs unable to bark; shameless dogs not knowing satiety. Days will come upon you, etc. Finally, does it not seem that they harm the Church less who cover their own malice with the cloak of hypocrisy, and teach through others the office of preaching, like sounding brass and a tinkling cymbal, than those who shamelessly drag their subjects with them into ruin by wicked morals and examples? For I judge that no one of sound judgment would say otherwise; rather he would concede that that saying of Jeremiah 3 has been fulfilled: Faithless Israel has justified her soul, that is, the Synagogue, in comparison with the prevarication of Judah. There Origen says: He understands this of us. Ezekiel 16, the Lord speaking to the Church: Your sister Samaria (that is, the Synagogue) did not sin half of your sins, but you surpassed her by your crimes. Ruin follows: Therefore you also bear your confusion. And below, in chapter 23, after describing at length the wickedness and destruction of the Synagogue, he added, speaking of the Church: She went mad more and more with lust, and shamelessly offered her fornication to the rich and to the magistrates who came to her, clothed in a varied garment. And rightly, he says, clothed in a varied garment she went mad with lust, that is, with the desire for riches and the craving for luxuries. For it was going to happen that the prelates of the churches would not be ashamed to defame the venerable chastity of the primitive Church with price, with prayers and with impious deeds, so that what follows would be fulfilled: The breasts of your youth were broken.

units.la: Subiungit tunc ruinam reperendo causam eius: Recessit anima mea ab ea, sicut recesserat à sorore eius, (id est synagoga,) quia scelus tuum & fornicationes tuæ fecerunt hæc tibi: loquitur de fornicatione superius expressa, id est simonia.
units.tr: Then he adds the ruin, giving its cause: My soul departed from her, as it had departed from her sister (that is, the synagogue), because your wickedness and your whoredoms have done these things unto you. He speaks of the whoredom expressed above, that is, simony.

units.la: Tertium signum sumitur ex personarum dispositione, & est immoderata inæqualitas, qua alius & sæpe dignior esurit. Alius & frequenter indignior præ multitudine & magnitudine beneficiorum ebrius est. Nam sicut in bona harmonia requiritur vocum inæqualitas proportionabilis, tamen moderata: quæ si nimia fuerit tollitur melodia. Ita secundum Philosophum propter ciuium disparitatem, & præsertim indignorum exaltationem, dignorumq; depressionem, obruitur politia, in qua sunt plures mediocres, est diututior. Sed non puto, quod vnquam fuerit aliquarum gentium politia, in qua esset tanta sacerdotum differentia: vt hi quidem essent maiores principibus huius seculi, licet indoctiores. Alii eiusdem gradus & ordinis: licet doctiores & sapientiores, deteriores vulgo. Communitas enim talis apud eum Philosophum vocatur oligarchia. Præterea videmus in corpore humano (cui Apostolus in pluribus suarum Epistolarum passibus ecclesiam comparat) quod si nutrimentum fluit ad vnum membrum, ita vt enormiter ingrossetur: & alia nimia attenuatione dematerentur, non potest viuere. Sic in corpore Ecclesiæ si superiores fiant ita grauies attractione substantiæ, quod inferiores vix possunt præ inopia se sustinere: hoc est signum iam propinquæ ruinæ. De talibus enim ait Dominus Amos 4. Vacca pingues in Hierusalem qui calumniam faciunt egenis: & confringitis pauperes. Ecce dies venient super vos. Et infra sext. Va qui opulenti estis in Sion, id est in Ecclesia.
units.tr: The third sign is taken from the arrangement of persons, and it is an immoderate inequality, by which one man, often the more worthy, goes hungry, while another, often the less worthy, is drunk with the multitude and magnitude of benefices. For just as in good harmony a proportionate inequality of voices is required, yet a moderate one, and if it is too great the melody is destroyed, so, according to the Philosopher, a polity in which there are many middling people endures longer, while it is overthrown by the disparity of citizens, especially by the elevation of the unworthy and the depression of the worthy. But I do not think there has ever been a polity of any nation in which there was such a great difference among priests: that some should be greater than the princes of this age, though less learned, while others of the same grade and order, though more learned and wiser, should be worse than the common people. For such a community is called an oligarchy by that Philosopher. Moreover, we see in the human body (to which the Apostle compares the Church in many passages of his Epistles) that if nourishment flows to one member so that it grows enormously, and the others are starved by excessive thinning, the body cannot live. So in the body of the Church, if the superiors become so heavy with the drawing off of substance that the inferiors can scarcely sustain themselves for want, this is a sign of ruin already near. For the Lord says of such men in Amos 4: Ye kine of Bashan, that are in the mountain of Samaria, which oppress the poor, which crush the needy; behold, the days shall come upon you. And below, in chapter 6: Woe to them that are at ease in Zion, that is, in the Church.

units.la: Quartum signum est fastus & superbia prælatorum, & aliorum ecclesiasticorum. Quamuis enim ex naturali prudentia & morali Philosophia similiter & Theologia conceditur, quod ecclesiastici debent habere, vnde possint honestius viuere quam populares, & prælati quam subditi.
units.tr: The fourth sign is the haughtiness and pride of prelates and of other churchmen. For although natural prudence, moral philosophy, and likewise theology grant that churchmen ought to have what allows them to live more honourably than laymen, and prelates more honourably than their subjects,

units.la: Ex hoc tamen non admittitur familiæ & equorum & vestium superflua pompa, quæ raro absq; superbia potest duci & salua iustitia sustineri: & plerumq; non sine iniuriis & delictis gubernari. Nam tantus fastus in Dei Ecclesia potissime temporibus istis non tam paucos mouet ad reuerentiam, quâ multos ad indignationem: & plures inuitat ad prædam, qui se reputarent forsan Deo sacrificium offerre, si possent quosdam diuites Ecclesiasticos spoliare. Tales fastuosos notat Dominus Amos 6. Optimates capita populorum ingredientes pompatice domum Israel. Quibus in signum ruinæ in eodem capitulo de dicit Esai. vigesim. octau. Væ corona superbiæ: pedibus conculcabitur. Quod abbas Ioachim exponit vę magnis prælatis, qui propter eorum superbiam procurant vt fiant in Ecclesia Dei schismata.
units.tr: yet from this is not admitted the superfluous pomp of household, horses, and clothing, which can rarely be displayed without pride, and can scarcely be maintained with justice intact, and generally cannot be governed without wrongs and offences. For such great haughtiness in the Church of God, especially in these times, moves not so many to reverence as it moves many to indignation, and invites more to plunder, who would perhaps think they were offering a sacrifice to God if they could despoil some wealthy churchmen. The Lord marks such proud men in Amos 6: The chief of the nations, into whom the house of Israel entered with pomp. As a sign of ruin, Isaiah says in chapter 28 of the same book: Woe to the crown of pride; it shall be trodden under foot. Abbot Joachim explains this as woe to the great prelates who, on account of their pride, bring it about that schisms arise in the Church of God.

units.la: Quintum signum sumitur ex tyrannide præsidentium: quæ cum sit violenta, durare in æternum non potest. Vnde proprietas tyranni est quærere non bonum publicum subditorum, sed vtile proprium. Tales sunt pastores, qui non pascunt gregem Domini, sed semetipsos: quibus dicit væ Ezechiel. 34. Gaudent de malefactis eorum quos pecunialiter possunt condemnare. Nec quærit quis quantum deliquerit: sed quantum quis soluere possit. Quibus Dominus dicit Mich. 3. Audite Duces domus Israel. Vos odio habetis bonum & diligitis malum: qui violenter tollitis pelles eorum desuper eis. Qui comederunt carnes populi mei & pellem eorum desuper excoriauerunt. Ideo dicit Dominus Ezech. 34. Cessare eos faciam vt non vltra pascant gregem meum: liberabo eum de ore eorum & non erit eis vltra in escam.
units.tr: The fifth sign is taken from the tyranny of those who preside, which, since it is violent, cannot endure forever. Hence it is the property of a tyrant to seek not the public good of his subjects but his own advantage. Such are the ministers who do not feed the flock of the Lord but themselves, to whom Ezekiel 34 says woe: They rejoice in the evils of those whom they can condemn for money. Nor does one ask how much a man has offended, but how much he is able to pay. To such the Lord says in Micah 3: Hear, ye heads of Jacob, and princes of the house of Israel; who hate the good, and love the evil; who pluck off their skin from off them, and their flesh from off their bones; who also eat the flesh of my people, and flay their skin from off them. Therefore the Lord says in Ezekiel 34: I will cause them to cease from feeding the flock; neither shall the shepherds feed themselves any more; for I will deliver my flock from their mouth, that they may no more be meat for them.

units.la: Sextum signum est; quod conturbatio principum & commotio populorum, quam in multis partibus experimur irrecuperabiliter destruere ecclesiam & destruxisse: ita vt impleatur illud Hierem. quart. Contritio super contritionem vocata est repente: vastata sunt tabernacula mea, Ezech. 7. Adducam pessimos de gentibus & possidebunt domos eorum, & quiescere faciam superbiam potentium, & possidebunt sanctuaria eorum. Conturbatio super conturbationem veniet, & auditus super auditum. Et ista videmus impleta in Græcia, in Vngaria, in inclyto olim Bohemiæ regno, & plurimis vicinis regionibus.
units.tr: The sixth sign is the disturbance of princes and the commotion of peoples, which we experience in many parts, destroying the Church beyond recovery and having destroyed it, so that what is written in Jeremiah 4 is fulfilled: Destruction upon destruction is cried; for the whole land is spoiled; suddenly are my tents spoiled, and my curtains in a moment. Ezekiel 7: I will bring the worst of the heathen, and they shall possess their houses; I will also make the pomp of the strong to cease, and their holy places shall be defiled. Destruction cometh; they shall seek peace, and there shall be none. Mischief upon mischief shall come, and rumour shall be upon rumour. And we see these things fulfilled in Greece, in Hungary, in the once famous kingdom of Bohemia, and in very many neighbouring regions.

units.la: Septimum signum est recusatio correctionis; si forte de principibus Ecclesiæ intelligatur, quod scriptum est Zachar. septim. Noluerunt attendere, & cor suum posuerunt vt adamantem, ne audirent verba quæ misit Dominus in spiritu suo per manus Prophetarum suorum. Et Esai. trigesim. Filii mendaces noluerunt audire verbum Dei qui dicunt: Nolite inspicere nobis qua recta sunt. Loquimini nobis placentia, quia nolunt intelligere vt bene agant. De quibus Amos 7. Odio habuerunt in porta corripientem, & loquentem perfecte abominati sunt. Tales salutaria monita & sacram scripturam reputant fabulas: & in ea meditantes iudicant fantasticos. Contra quorum Ecclesiam Dominus Oseæ quart. Quia tu scientiam repulisti, repellam te ne sacerdotio fungaris mihi. Et oblitus es legis Dei tui, obliuiscar & ego filiorum tuorum, & secundum multitudinem eorum sic peccauerunt mihi, gloriam eorum in ignominiam commutabo. Et erit sicut populus sic sacerdos. Et Ezech. septim. Lex peribit a sacerdote, & consilium a senioribus.
units.tr: The seventh sign is the refusal of correction, if perhaps it is understood of the princes of the Church, as is written in Zechariah 7: They refused to hearken, and pulled away the shoulder, and stopped their ears, that they should not hear. Yea, they made their hearts as an adamant stone, lest they should hear the law, and the words which the Lord of hosts hath sent in his spirit by the former prophets. And Isaiah 30: This is a rebellious people, lying children, children that will not hear the law of the Lord; which say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits. Of whom Amos 7 says: They hated him that rebuked in the gate, and they abhorred him that spake uprightly. Such men regard salutary warnings and Holy Scripture as fables, and those who meditate on it they judge to be fanatics. Against their Church the Lord says in Hosea 4: Because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me; seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children. As they were increased, so they sinned against me; therefore will I change their glory into shame. And it shall be, like people, like priest. And Ezekiel 7: The law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders.

units.la: Octauum signum est novitas opinionum. Ex hoc enim surgunt hæreses, schismata orta defenduntur, & defensa radicantur: radicata vt experimur fidem & Ecclesiam destruunt. Modernò enim tempore vnusquisq; interpretari & trahere non veretur sacram scripturam, iura, sanctorumque patrum instituta ad libitum suæ voluntatis: prout amor, odium, inuidia, spes promotionis aut vindicta eum inclinat. Aliqui eorum leuiter nimis alios hæreticos dicunt; quos tamen nondum hæreticare noluerunt. Alii verecundia ducti quandoq; forsan errores defendunt: ne leui opinione vulgi videantur inquinati. Hi inuicem, vt ait Apostolus, languent circa quæstiones & pugnas verborum: ex quibus oriuntur inuidiæ, contentiones, blasphemiæ, suspiciones malæ. 1. Tim. 6. & 2. Tim. 4. Erit, inquit, tempus cum sanam doctrinam non suscipient, sed ad sua desideria coacervabunt sibi magistros prurientes auribus, & a veritate quidem auditum auertent, & ad fabulas conuertentur. Fabulæ & non sanæ doctrinæ sunt, quæ in persuasibilibus humanæ sapientiæ verbis, vel in sublimitate sermonum, aut secundum zelum & contentionem aut inanem gloriam: non in revelatione Spiritus sancti, sed secundum traditionem hominum consistunt. A quibus quatuor nos cautos reddit, vt non circumferamur, inquit, omni vento doctrinæ, & nequitia hominum in astutia & circumuentione errorum.
units.tr: The eighth sign is the novelty of opinions. For from this heresies arise, schisms that have begun are defended, and what is defended takes root; once rooted, as we experience, they destroy the faith and the Church. For in our time each man does not hesitate to interpret and twist Holy Scripture, the laws, and the institutions of the holy Fathers at his own pleasure, as love, hatred, envy, hope of promotion, or revenge inclines him. Some of them too lightly call others heretics, though they have not yet been willing to brand them as heretics. Others, restrained by shame, perhaps sometimes defend errors, lest they seem tainted by the light opinion of the crowd. These, as the Apostle says, languish among themselves about questions and strife of words, from which come envy, contentions, blasphemies, and evil suspicions. 1 Tim. 6 and 2 Tim. 4: There will come a time, he says, when they will not endure sound doctrine, but will heap up for themselves teachers, having itching ears; and they will turn away their hearing from the truth and turn aside unto fables. Fables, and not sound doctrine, are those things which consist in the persuasive words of human wisdom, or in the loftiness of speeches, or in zeal and contention, or in vain glory, not in the revelation of the Holy Spirit, but according to the tradition of men. From these he makes us wary, that we be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive.

units.la: Præter hæc sunt alia signa, videlicet recessus iustitiæ. Hæc fuit causa destructionis Romanorum: prout deducit Augustinus lib. de ciui. Dei. Destructio studiorum: quam comitatur penuria sapientum: & hanc sequebatur destructio Græcorum. Pigritia puerorum ac ignorantium ad prauitatem: & hæc erit destructio Latinorum.
units.tr: Besides these there are other signs, namely the withdrawal of justice. This was the cause of the destruction of the Romans, as Augustine deduces in the book On the City of God. The destruction of learning, which is accompanied by a lack of wise men; and the destruction of the Greeks followed this. The laziness of boys and of the ignorant toward wickedness; and this will be the destruction of the Latins.

units.la: Plura alia sunt scripta in Prophetis de deiectione sacerdotalis honoris: ex quibus & prædictis sapiens potest concludere tuitam temporalium Ecclesiæ de propinquo imminere. Et forsan iuxta illud Esa. 30. Subito dum non sperabitur veniet contritio. Quia Prouerb. 1. scribitur: Despexisti omne consilium meum, & omnes increpationes meas neglexisti. Ego autem in interitu vestro ridebo, cum irruerit super vos repentina calamitas, quando veniet super vos tribulatio & angustia. Nec debemus reputare hoc impossibile: quia nostris temporibus vidimus aliqua, quæ nuper erant incredibilia. Et timendum est maiora esse in posterioribus. Imo verisimile puto, quod a multis annis non fuerunt tot malevoli; tanti cordæ rebelles & animo accensi contra ecclesiam, sicut his diebus. Videtur enim quod Dominus conuertit cor eorum, vt odirent populū eius: & dolos facerent in seruos eius, sicut in sacerdotes: Psal. 104. Quos in longum compescere nequaquam valebimus, nisi signis virtutum manifestis ad benevolentiam eos inclinauerimus. Nec multum proderit, vel forsan ad modicum durabit vnio, nisi essent praemissa signa, quae etiam fuerunt causa schismatis, & sequatur notabilis & magna morum reformatio.
units.tr: Many other things are written in the Prophets about the overthrow of priestly honour, from which, and from those already mentioned, a wise man can conclude that the ruin of the temporal affairs of the Church is imminent. And perhaps this accords with Isaiah 30: Suddenly, when it is not expected, the destruction will come. For it is written in Proverbs 1: You have despised all my counsel, and have neglected all my reproofs. I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh; when your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish come upon you. Nor ought we to regard this as impossible, because in our times we have seen some things which lately were incredible. And we must fear that greater things are to come in the future. Indeed I think it likely that for many years there have not been so many malicious men, such rebellious hearts and minds so inflamed against the Church, as in these days. For the Lord seems to have turned their heart to hate his people, and to deal craftily with his servants, as with the priests: Psalm 105. We shall by no means be able to restrain them for long, unless we incline them to goodwill by manifest signs of virtue. Nor will the union profit much, or perhaps endure for a little while, unless the signs mentioned above, which were also the cause of the schism, are removed, and a notable and great reformation of morals follows.

units.la: Ad hoc enim Reuerendi Patres & Domini, Deus omnipotens miro quodam modo cunctis prius inaestimabili vos adunauit, quia aduersos, tanta multitudine in vnum congregauit. Ad vos totus mundus tanquam naufragantes ad portum: respicit hoc ipsa ecclesia, innarrabilibus lachrymis & gemitibus à quolibet vestrum quaerendo requirit. Iohan. 29. Quis mihi tribuat vt sim sicut fui in diebus adolescentiae meae, quoniam omnipotens erat mecum. Tunc enim omnipotens erat secum: quia in prisci patribus nullum apparuit contradictionis signum.
units.tr: For this reason, Reverend Fathers and Lords, Almighty God has united you in a wonderful way, in a manner beyond all estimation, since he has gathered into one body so great a multitude of you who were once opposed to one another. To you the whole world looks as sailors shipwrecked look to a harbour; the Church herself looks to you, and with unspeakable tears and groans she asks of each of you. John 29: "Who will grant me that I may be as I was in the days of my youth, when the Almighty was with me?" For then the Almighty was with him, because among the ancient fathers no sign of contradiction appeared.

units.la: Praeflatur etiam dies adolescentiae suae: vt moribus & doctrinis sanctorum patrum decorata, possit (vt ait beatus Augustinus in Sermone super Cantica) exemplo virginis credendo verbum diuinum concipere, & praedicando parere, rebelles quoque & contradicentes vigore suae adolescentiae in ruinam detrudere. Hoc significauit virga Aaron, quando Dominus praecepit Moysi Numer. 17. Defer, inquit, virgam Aaron in tabernaculum, vt seruetur in signum rebellium filiorum Israel. Virga Aaron florida & fructifera: quamuis non sarculo culta nec humefacta, virginem concipientem & parientem, quamuis virum non cognoscentem, signat: quae posita erat in signum rebellium, id est, contradicentium & ruinam. Et hoc Propheta nunciauit domui Dauid, vbi thema: Numquid parum vobis est molestos esse hominibus, id est, contradicentes: quia molesti estis & Deo meo? propter hoc dabit Dominus ipse vobis signum.
units.tr: He also foretells the days of her youth, so that she, adorned with the morals and teachings of the holy fathers, may (as blessed Augustine says in his Sermon on the Song of Songs) by the example of the Virgin conceive the divine word by believing and bring it forth by preaching, and by the vigour of her youth cast down into ruin those who rebel and contradict. The rod of Aaron signified this, when the Lord commanded Moses (Numbers 17): "Bring the rod of Aaron back into the tabernacle, that it may be kept as a sign against the rebellious sons of Israel." The rod of Aaron, flourishing and fruitful, though not tended by a hoe nor moistened, signifies the virgin conceiving and bearing, although she knows no man; and it was placed as a sign against the rebellious, that is, the contradicting, and for their ruin. And the Prophet announced this to the house of David, the text being: "Is it too little for you to be troublesome to men, that is, to contradict them? Because you are troublesome to my God too, the Lord himself will therefore give you a sign."

units.la: PARS SECVNDA. DECLARATIO COMPENDIOSA DEFECTVVM VIRORVM ECCLESIASTICORVM.
units.tr: PART TWO. A BRIEF DECLARATION OF THE FAILINGS OF CHURCH MEN.

units.la: Orte dicitur mihi: Ecclesia fundata est supra firmam petram, flauerunt venti, inundauerunt flumina, non est passa ruinam, quomodo tu dicis, reformatione indiget? Aut dic in quibus. Sed si in nullis eius partibus heterogeneis, id est, in eius statibus, vel in nullis partibus materialibus siue fluentibus, id est, singularibus suppositis hodie correctione & emendatione Ecclesia indiget, quaeso vbi sunt tunc praecedentium patrum sanctae & rationabiles constitutiones innumerae, in eorum conciliis vel epistolis Papalibus traditae: quarum obseruantia nunc oblita nedum expediuit olim, sed & magis modo fidelibus saluberrima esset & opportuna? Et vt de pluribus taceam & grandioribus:
units.tr: Someone may say to me: "The Church is founded on a firm rock. Winds blew and rivers flooded, yet she has not suffered ruin. How can you say she needs reformation? Name the respects in which she does." But if the Church today needs correction and amendment in none of her heterogeneous parts, that is, in her estates, and in none of her material or fluid parts, that is, in her individual members, then where are the countless holy and reasonable constitutions of the earlier Fathers, handed down in their councils and papal letters? Their observance, now forgotten, would not only have been useful in the past, but would even now be most salutary and timely for the faithful. To pass over many others and the weightier ones:

units.la: 1. Primo, vbi est quod Episcopus bonus & probatus opere & doctrina eligatur, non puer, non homo carnalis spiritualium ignarus?
units.tr: 1. First, where is the rule that a bishop be chosen who is good and approved in work and teaching, not a boy, not a carnal man ignorant of spiritual things?

units.la: 2. Vbi est quod clerici in duabus ciuitatibus & ecclesiis praebendas vel prelationes non habeant?
units.tr: 2. Where is the rule that clergy do not hold prebends or offices in two cities or churches?

units.la: 3. Quod pro sepultura, confessione, ordinatione, promotione, nullo praetextu vbicunque; aliquid exigitur aut detur.
units.tr: 3. That nothing be demanded or given, on any pretext whatever, for burial, confession, ordination or promotion.

units.la: 4. Quod nullus principum laicorum capellanum habeat, nisi ab Episcopo datum in casu ab Episcopo deponendum vel corrigendum.
units.tr: 4. That no lay prince have a chaplain unless he was given by the bishop and can be removed or corrected by the bishop.

units.la: 5. Quod nullus Episcopus aut sacerdos munetibus, precibus ac fauoribus personarum acceptionibus promoueatur.
units.tr: 5. That no bishop or priest be advanced by bribes, entreaties or the favour of persons.

units.la: 6. Vbi est quod Episcopi extra dioecesim non morentur?
units.tr: 6. Where is the rule that bishops not stay outside their diocese?

units.la: 7. Quod non plures quam sufficiant ordinentur?
units.tr: 7. That not more than are sufficient be ordained?

units.la: 8. Quod Episcopi & sacerdotes spectaculis & ludis non intersint, nec delectentur.
units.tr: 8. That bishops and priests not attend or take pleasure in spectacles and games.

units.la: 9. Quod sacerdotes nihil foenoris aut rustici ministerii exerceant: nec mercatores, venatores aut negociatores sint.
units.tr: 9. That priests engage in no usury or rustic trade, nor be merchants, hunters or traders.

units.la: 10. Quod negocia causarum festiuis diebus & in Ecclesiis non tractentur.
units.tr: 10. That business matters not be transacted on feast days or in churches.

units.la: 11. Vbi est hodie, ne rectores ecclesiarum instrenui sint rebus, & in ecclesiasticis remissi: aut plus propria quam ecclesiastica iura procurent?
units.tr: 11. Where is the rule today that the rulers of churches not be slack in temporal affairs and remiss in ecclesiastical ones, or pursue their own rights more than the Church's rights?

units.la: 12. Quod non liceat Dominis & praelatis obseruationibus superstitiosis gentilium attendere: nec diuino consulere, aut stellarum cursus respicere in agendis.
units.tr: 12. That lords and prelates may not observe the superstitious observances of the heathen, nor consult diviners, nor watch the courses of the stars in their undertakings.

units.la: 13. Vbi sunt Synodi prouinciales secundum patrum constitutiones semel vel bis in anno celebrandae.
units.tr: 13. Where are the provincial synods, which by the constitutions of the Fathers ought to be held once or twice a year?

units.la: 14. Vbi quod non licet quemcunq; clericum vel Episcopum die Dominico absentem esse, sed missarum solemniis interesse ieiunum.
units.tr: 14. Where is the rule that no cleric or bishop may be absent on the Lord's day, but must attend the solemn celebration of the Mass fasting?

units.la: 15. Quod clerici ad matutinum seu vespertinum officium non venientes deponantur, nisi Episcopo vel decano satisfaciant.
units.tr: 15. That clerics who do not come to the morning or evening office be deposed, unless they make satisfaction to the bishop or dean.

units.la: 16. Quod non liceat clericis ante tertiam horam prandere.
units.tr: 16. That clerics may not dine before the third hour.

units.la: 17. Quod nullus sacerdotum a quinquagesima vsq; pascha carnes comedat.
units.tr: 17. That no priest eat meat from Quinquagesima until Easter.

units.la: 18. Quod sacerdotes aduentum Christi ieiunent.
units.tr: 18. That priests fast during Advent.

units.la: 19. Quod clerici à subiectione non cessent.
units.tr: 19. That clerics not cease from subjection.

units.la: 20. Vbi est hodie, ne quicquam pro gradibus, pro dignitatibus, pro diuinis sacramentis accipiatur.
units.tr: 20. Where is the rule today that nothing be received for degrees, for dignities, or for the divine sacraments?

units.la: 21. Ne prælati monasteriis vel Ecclesiis consanguineos suos vel eis fauentes præficiant.
units.tr: 21. That prelates not set their kinsmen or their favourites over monasteries or churches.

units.la: 22. Quod non ordinentur, qui Psalmorum, canticorum seu hymnorum ignari sunt.
units.tr: 22. That those ignorant of the Psalms, canticles or hymns not be ordained.

units.la: 23. Quod scripturis diuinis studeant Episcopi & sacerdotes, maxime monachi & religiosi, scientis litigiosis & practicis omissis.
units.tr: 23. That bishops and priests, and especially monks and religious, devote themselves to the divine Scriptures, leaving aside the litigious and practical sciences.

units.la: 24. Vbi quod oppressores pauperum, potentes & tyrannos Episcopi arguant & corripiant.
units.tr: 24. Where is the rule that bishops rebuke and correct oppressors of the poor, the powerful and tyrants?

units.la: 25. Vbi quod per annos singulos Episcopi parochias suas circumeant cum effectu.
units.tr: 25. Where is the rule that bishops go round their parishes every year, and do so effectively?

units.la: 26. Vt ad mensam Episcopi scripturæ diuinæ legantur.
units.tr: 26. That the divine Scriptures be read at the bishop's table.

units.la: 27. Quod Episcopus angarias & impositiones, vel huiusmodi grauamina subiectis non imponant.
units.tr: 27. That bishops not impose forced labour, levies or similar burdens on their subjects.

units.la: 28. Quod clericus scurrilis & verbis turpibus plenus ab officio retrahatur.
units.tr: 28. That a cleric who is buffoonish and full of foul words be removed from office.

units.la: 29. Vbi est nunc clericorum singularis decor continentiæ in gestu, in vestitu, victu & risu?
units.tr: 29. Where now is the distinctive decency of clerical continence in bearing, dress, food and laughter?

units.la: 30. Vbi ne clerici comam barbam ve nutriant, aut calciamenta & vestimenta aliter quam religionem deceret, habeant.
units.tr: 30. Where is the rule that clerics not grow hair or beards, or have shoes and clothing other than befits religion?

units.la: 31. Vbi quod stipendia clericorum iuxta merita distribuantur personarum.
units.tr: 31. Where is the rule that the stipends of clerics be distributed according to the merits of persons?

units.la: 32. Quod clerici nuptialia vitent conuiuia.
units.tr: 32. That clerics avoid wedding feasts.

units.la: 33. Quod clerici tabernas non ingrediantur: necin eis dominetur crapula & ebrietas.
units.tr: 33. That clerics not enter taverns, and that drunkenness and gluttony not rule among them.

units.la: 34. Vbi est illud Carthaginensis concilii quarti, vt Episcopus vilem supellectilem, & mensam ac victum pauperem habeat: & dignitatis suæ auctoritatem fide & vitæ meritis quærat?
units.tr: 34. Where is the rule of the Fourth Council of Carthage, that a bishop have cheap furniture, a plain table and simple food, and seek the authority of his office through faith and the merits of his life?

units.la: 35. Quod Episcopus pro rebus transitoriis non leuiter litiget.
units.tr: 35. That a bishop not litigate lightly over transitory things.

units.la: 36. Quod Episcopus de loco ignobili ad nobilem per ambitionem aut auaritiam non transeat.
units.tr: 36. That a bishop not move from a humble place to a more distinguished one through ambition or avarice.

units.la: 37. Quod studendum est clericis, vt dissidentes Fratres magis ad pacem quam ad iudicium cohortentur.
units.tr: 37. That clerics take care to urge quarrelling brothers toward peace rather than toward judgment.

units.la: 38. Quod clerici per plateas & fora discurrere non debent.
units.tr: 38. That clerics ought not to run about the streets and marketplaces.
