units.la: 39. Quod clericus quemlibet verbo erudiat: & ne pauperes grauentur (vt Paulus) artificio victum quærat.
units.tr: 39. That a cleric instruct anyone by word, and, so as not to burden the poor, earn his living by a craft, as Paul did.

units.la: 40. Quod clericus artificio vel agricultura sibi victum absque sui officii detrimento præparet.
units.tr: 40. That a cleric provide his living by a craft or by farming, without detriment to his office.

units.la: 41. Vbi est, quod clerici in aliena ciuitate sine causa legitima non morentur extra prebendas vel Ecclesias suas?
units.tr: 41. Where is the rule that clerics not stay in another city without lawful cause, outside their prebends or churches?

units.la: 42. Quod ab his, qui sacramentis diuinis inseruiunt, singularis castitas custodiatur.
units.tr: 42. That those who serve the divine sacraments keep a singular chastity.

units.la: 43. Quod clerici actus seculariům vel procurationes non suscipiant.
units.tr: 43. That clerics not take up secular business or agency.

units.la: 44. Quod laici clericos actores vel rectores sibi non constituant.
units.tr: 44. That laymen not appoint clerics as their stewards or governors.

units.la: 45. Vbi est hodie illud Calcedonensis concilii: Monachi tantummodo intenti sint ieiuniis & orationibus, in locis vbi renunciauerint seculo: nec Ecclesiasticis vel secularibus negociis propria monasteria deserendo insistant? Et maxime quid opus est monachos euocari: cum infiniti seculares hodie studeant in facultatibus litium, iuris scil. & legum.
units.tr: 45. Where is today the rule of the Council of Chalcedon: Let monks be intent only on fasting and prayer, in the places where they have renounced the world, and not engage in ecclesiastical or secular business by deserting their own monasteries? And why need monks be summoned at all, when today countless laymen devote themselves to the resources of lawsuits, namely of law and legal procedure?

units.la: 46. Vbi est quod non liceat Episcopo à sua Ecclesia plus tribus hebdomadis abesse?
units.tr: 46. Where is the rule that a bishop may not be away from his Church for more than three weeks?

units.la: 47. Vbi quod clerici allegatores, venatores &c. communione priuentur?
units.tr: 47. Where is the rule that clerics who are advocates, hunters and so on be deprived of communion?

units.la: 48. Quod officia Ecclesiastica pecunia non obtineantur: vt nihil pro ordinatione, vel pallio, vel pastillo detur aut accipiatur. Cap. 5. Epistolæ tertiæ Gregor. Papæ: Nunquid vult modo verbum illud esse verum, scil. Beati Hieronymi (quod qui clericorum audierit, ambæ eius aures tinniant.) Veteres, inquit, scrutans scripturas, inuenire non possunt scidisse Ecclesiam & de domo Dei populos seduxisse, praeter eos qui sacerdotes à Deo positi fuerant & Prophetæ. Et Chrysostomus super illud Matth. vigesim. primi. Et intrauit Iesus templum: sicut, dixit: de templo omne bonum egreditur: & ita de templo omne malum procedit.
units.tr: 48. That ecclesiastical offices not be obtained for money, so that nothing is given or received for ordination, for the pallium, or for a lozenge. Chapter 5 of the third letter of Pope Gregory: Does that saying of Blessed Jerome now hold true, namely (that whoever hears the clergy, both his ears ring)? The ancients, searching the Scriptures, inquire, could not find that the Church was torn or that peoples were led away from the house of God, except by those whom God had placed as priests and prophets. And Chrysostom, on that verse of Matthew 21: "And Jesus entered the temple": as he said, all good comes out of the temple, and so all evil proceeds from the temple.

units.la: Si enim sacerdotium integrum fuerit, tota Ecclesia floret: si autem corruptum fuerit, omnium fides & virtus marcida est: sicut cum videris arborem pallentibus foliis, intelligis quia vitium habet in radice: siccum videris populum indisciplinatum, sine dubio cognosce quia sacerdotium eius non est sanum. Vbi est forte propter hoc devotio & obedientia inferiorum, defensio militum, pax principum Christianorum? ad finem vt inter se concordes impugnent (schismaticos & infideles) recuperando regiones, quas iam Christianis abstulerunt & peruerterunt. Sed nunquid hodie omnes sacerdotes Domini & prælati in antedictis & post dicendis culpabiles sunt malis? Absit. Reliquit enim Dominus sibi in Israel septem millia virorum, quorum genua non sunt curuata ante Baal. 3. Reg. 19. cap. &c.
units.tr: For if the priesthood is whole, the whole Church flourishes; but if it is corrupted, the faith and virtue of all wither. Just as when you see a tree with pale leaves, you understand that it has a fault at the root, so when you see a people undisciplined and dry, know without doubt that its priesthood is not sound. Is it perhaps for this reason that the devotion and obedience of inferiors, the defence of soldiers and the peace of Christian princes have gone missing, so that they fight among themselves (schismatics and infidels) and fail to recover the regions which they have already taken from Christians and overthrown? But are all the priests of the Lord and the prelates today guilty of the evils mentioned above and to be mentioned below? Far from it. For the Lord has left himself seven thousand men in Israel whose knees have not bowed before Baal. 1 Kings 19 and following.

units.la: 49. Iterum ad quid expedit aut quid vtilitatis Ecclesiæ confert tam magnifica principum gloria: & tam superflua prælatorum & cardinalium pompa: vt quasi (le homines esse nescire faciant?) Et quæ vtique abominatio, quod vnus tenet ducenta, alter trecenta beneficia Ecclesiastica? Non ne inde cultus diuinus diminuitur, Ecclesiæ depauperantur: valentibus viris & doctoribus priuantur: fidelibus mala exempla dantur.
units.tr: 49. Again, to what purpose, or what use to the Church, is such magnificent princely glory, and such superfluous pomp of prelates and cardinals, that (as it were, they make men forget that they are men?) And what abomination is it that one holds two hundred, another three hundred ecclesiastical benefices? Does not divine worship thereby diminish, and the Church grow poor, and the strong men and teachers go without, and bad examples given to the faithful?

units.la: 50. Quid sibi voluit, quod cardinales solum de vna natione, vel quasi de vna patria fiebant: inter quos de singulis vel notabilibus linguis aliqui esse deberent: nunquid apud Christum est differentia Graeci & Latini & Alemani, Hispani & Vngari &c.
units.tr: 50. What did it mean that cardinals were made only from one nation, or almost from one country, when some of them ought to have come from each of the principal languages? Is there a difference with Christ between Greek and Latin, German, Spaniard and Hungarian, and so on?

units.la: Quid est quod hodie vnus vrinam mediocriter doctus, tenet quatuor, quinq; vel sex vel octo beneficia: quorum vno est non dignus, quibus octo sustentari possent, doctrinis, orationibus & diuinis laudibus insistentes? Attendite an potius hodie equi, canes aues & superflua ecclesiasticorum familia patrimonium ecclesiae comedere debeant, quam pauperes Christi? vel quam ad diuini cultus ampliationem & pro infidelium conuersione: aut in huiusmodi pietatis operibus, modis congruis expendendum sit.
units.tr: Why is it that today one man, only moderately learned, holds four, five, six or eight benefices, of which he is not worthy even one, when eight could support men devoted to teaching, prayer and divine praise? Consider whether horses, dogs, birds and the superfluous household of the clergy ought today to consume the patrimony of the Church rather than the poor of Christ, or rather than being spent, in suitable ways, on enlarging divine worship, on the conversion of unbelievers, or on works of this kind of piety.

units.la: Quot hodie loca diuini cultus, vt monasteria & venerabilium martyrum Ecclesiae Romae & alibi, ob praedicta & ex praelatorum incuria desertae sunt & destructae?
units.tr: How many places of divine worship, such as monasteries and churches of the venerable martyrs at Rome and elsewhere, have been deserted and destroyed today because of the aforesaid evils and the negligence of prelates?

units.la: Iudicate etiam, si iustum quandoque sit, vel exactiones ab episcopis, clerico imponi vt colectoribus soluatur.
units.tr: Judge also whether it is ever just that exactions should be imposed by bishops on the clergy, to be paid to collectors.

units.la: Quid est etiam, quod hodie omnes medium Christianitatis pinguibus abundans beneficiis tanquam centrum quietis ambiunt, derelictis partibus ecclesiae in circuitu; vbi impii ambulant inuisitatis, & a Doctoribus immittendis & promouendis vacuis & incultis? Vbi fides est debilis, virtus imperfecta: schismatici abundant, infideles impugnant: vtriq; opus esset in lege Christi expertioribus praelatis & doctoribus, magistris atq; probiori & abundantiori militari potestate.
units.tr: Why is it also that everyone today seeks the middle of Christendom, abounding in rich benefices, as the centre of quiet, leaving the outlying parts of the Church, where the wicked walk unseen, and are unvisited and uncultivated by teachers who should be sent and promoted? Where faith is weak and virtue imperfect, schismatics abound and unbelievers attack. Both need, under the law of Christ, prelates and teachers more experienced, masters, and a more upright and more abundant power of the sword.

units.la: Quid est, quod gladius ecclesiae, scilicet excommunicatio, in sui contemptum modo tam leuiter extrahitur, & pro modica re, vt pro debitis vel huiusmodi tam crudeliter in pauperes extenditur.
units.tr: Why is the sword of the Church, that is excommunication, drawn so lightly now, to its own contempt, and for a trivial matter, and extended so cruelly against the poor for debts or things of that kind?

units.la: Quid est, quod vna causa super modica re durat tam multis annis: quare litium prolixitas pauperum spoliatrix, conuenienti modo non rescinditur?
units.tr: Why does one cause, over a trifling matter, last for so many years? Why is the prolixity of lawsuits, which despoils the poor, not cut short in a suitable manner?

units.la: Quare conuersis Iudaeis de eorum bonis misericorditer non datur vitae necessitas, potius quam egestate compulsi apostatent; & Christianos impietatis arguant.
units.tr: Why, when Jews are converted, is no provision made out of their goods, in mercy, for the necessities of life, so that they do not apostatise, compelled by poverty, and accuse Christians of impiety?

units.la: Etiam quare non ordinatur Iudaeos inter Christianos morari non debere, nisi vel Christianis seruiendo, vel agros colendo, vel in mechanicis laborando acquirant victum suum: & non vlurando eis in peccatum & Christianis in spolium.
units.tr: Likewise, why is it not ordained that Jews should not be allowed to dwell among Christians unless they earn their living by serving Christians, cultivating fields, or working at trades, and not by usury, which leads to sin for them and to plunder for Christians?

units.la: Quid etiam sibi vult, quod quarundam ecclesiasticarum cathedralium canonici, calceis iotrati, vestibus accurtati, abiecto habitu clericali & assumpto militari, in armis & hastiludiis se exercent. Episcopiq; cappa, superpellicio libroq; depositis arma sumunt: in campis armati pugnant, vt principes seculares.
units.tr: What also does it mean that the canons of certain cathedral churches, with their shoes laced up, their garments shortened, their clerical habit laid aside and a military one assumed, exercise themselves in arms and tournaments? And that bishops, having put aside cope, surplice and book, take up weapons, and fight armed in the fields like secular princes?

units.la: Quid est, quod nonnulli praelati iurisdictionem spiritualem & temporalem quibusdam potentibus tyrannis & auaris pro certa summa locant, in grauamen Ecclesiae, subuersionem iustitiae & oppressionem pauperum.
units.tr: Why is it that some prelates let out spiritual and temporal jurisdiction for a fixed sum to certain powerful tyrants and greedy men, to the burden of the Church, the subversion of justice and the oppression of the poor?

units.la: Quid est, quod hodie episcopi, abbates, monachi sunt plus officiales fisci quam Christi, totis nisibus militantes mundo in curiis principum & secularium iudiciorum seu Parlamentorum.
units.tr: Why is it that today bishops, abbots and monks are more officials of the treasury than of Christ, striving with all their effort in the service of the world, at the courts of princes and in secular tribunals or parliaments?

units.la: Ecce quid sibi vult etiam, quod modo potius omnes Episcopi, praelati & parochiales sacerdotes per Papam constituuntur, quam eligantur personae nota & aptiores de patria: vt non praeferantur ecclesiis homines extranei in moribus & linguis & consuetudinibus.
units.tr: Behold also what it means that now all bishops, prelates and parish priests are appointed by the Pope, rather than persons well known and better suited being chosen from the country, so that men foreign in morals, languages and customs are not preferred to the churches.

units.la: Quid est, quod hodie potentum & nobilium pueri ecclesiasticis dignitatibus praeferuntur: & clerici famosi in vita & doctrina eis subiiciuntur.
units.tr: Why is it that today the sons of the powerful and nobles are preferred to ecclesiastical dignities, and famous clergy, in life and teaching, are made subject to them?

units.la: Quid est, quod nunc spiritualium penitus ignaris, qui a pueto mundanae & litigiosae scientiae vt legum, quarum studium sacerdotibus est prohibitum, vacauerunt, regimen ecclesiae potius committitur? Nunquid ecclesia per mundum gubernanda, & non potius contra morem mundi eo quod scriptum est: Nolite conformari huic seculo, & caetera multa.
units.tr: Why is the government of the Church now committed rather to men utterly ignorant of spiritual things, who from boyhood have devoted themselves to worldly and litigious learning, such as the law, the study of which is forbidden to priests? Ought the Church not to be governed by the world, but rather against the custom of the world, since it is written: Be not conformed to this world, and many other things?

units.la: Rursus oculos aperite, & inquirite, si quae hodie claustra monialium facta sunt quasi prostibula meretricum. Si quae consecrata canonicorum monasteria fiant quasi fora & diuersoria. Si quae cathedrales ecclesiae factae sunt sicut speluncae raptorum & latronum.
units.tr: Again, open your eyes and inquire whether any convents of nuns have today become like brothels of harlots; whether any consecrated monasteries of canons have become like markets and inns; whether any cathedral churches have been made like dens of robbers and thieves.

units.la: Scrutamini si alicubi sacerdotes in consuetudinem duxerunt sub praetextu ancillarum habere concubinas.
units.tr: Search whether anywhere priests have made it a custom, under the pretext of maidservants, to keep concubines.

units.la: Iudicate si tanta imaginum & picturarum in ecclesiis varietas expediat: & an plures simplices nonnunquam ad idolatriam peruertant.
units.tr: Judge whether so great a variety of images and paintings in churches is expedient, and whether they sometimes lead many simple people into idolatry.

units.la: Videte si tanta religionum numerositas & varietas conueniat.
units.tr: See whether so great a number and variety of religious orders is fitting.

units.la: Examinate si religiones militares faciunt debitum: habeant in honore sacerdotium: seruent mores, fidem, regulas & canones patrum.
units.tr: Examine whether the military orders do their duty: whether they hold the priesthood in honour, keep the morals, faith, rules and canons of the Fathers.

units.la: Discutite si expediat quorundam tam large exemptio & priuilegiatio atque ordinariorum coercione fit commoda subductio.
units.tr: Consider whether it is expedient that the exemption and privileging of some should be so wide, and whether withdrawal from the control of the ordinaries is a beneficial thing.

units.la: Si conueniat Vrbanum quintum Brigittam de Suetia, Ducem Britanniae Carolum: non obstante nimia sanctorum multitudine canonizari.
units.tr: Whether it is fitting that Urban V canonized Bridget of Sweden and Charles, Duke of Brittany, notwithstanding the excessive multitude of saints.

units.la: Si decent quorundam nouorum sanctorum festa solennius peragi, quam praecipuorum Apostolorum.
units.tr: Whether it is becoming that the feasts of certain new saints should be celebrated more solemnly than those of the principal Apostles.

units.la: Si iustum sit priores sanctorum solennes ecclesias deseri & destrui, redditibus à collectoribus vel cardinalibus levatis: & quandoq; post ad eorum memoriam vel quasi gloriam capellulas novas aedificari.
units.tr: Whether it is just that the former solemn churches of the saints should be deserted and destroyed, their revenues taken up by collectors or cardinals, and afterwards new little chapels built in their memory or, as it were, for their glory.

units.la: Rursum pensate, si æquum est fatuos praesse & sapientes subesse: iuvenes dominari, senes famulari: ignaros ardua discutere, scientes loqui non audiri: equorum famulos in promotionibus praeponi, eloquiorum Dei discipulos postponi.
units.tr: Again weigh whether it is fair for fools to rule and the wise to be subject, young men to lord it and old men to serve; for the ignorant to discuss lofty matters and those who know how to speak not to be heard; for the servants of horses to be placed before in promotions, and the disciples of the words of God to be put behind.

units.la: Perquirite si quae scripturae apocryphae aut hymni aut orationes successu temporis studio vel ignorantia in detrimentum fidei introductae sint. Et corrigite opinionum discordias, utpote de conceptione virginis gloriosae & consimilium. Sedate iniquas leges: consuetudines pravas emendate. Nonne in Saxonia reperiuntur iniustae leges à Theologis impugnatae. Et quae Christianorum consuetudo damnabilior esse potest ea, qua iam clerici & laici & principes ubiq; insaniunt, sanctissima natalis nocte celebrantes ludo taxillorum, non contemplatione coelestium mysteriorum? Nonne in Livonia consuetudo invaluit, ut nulli rusticorum sacramentum eucharistiae detur? Nonne ibidem reperitur, quod vir duas uxores vivas habeat, & mulier plures maritos? Quid plura? Ab episcopis ad concilium generale venientibus de qualibet provincia: de omnibus inquirite abusuis consuetudinibus & perniciosis ritibus, quacunque occasione in ecclesiis & hominum statibus regionum diversarum introductis, ut super deviationibus praemissis & consimilibus, omnes ecclesiae status vel in generali concilio reformetis, aut in conciliis provincialibus reformari mandetis: ut de auctoritate vestra reparetur ecclesia: & purgetur domus Dei ab immunditiis, vitiis & erroribus universis. Hoc autem ut diligenter fieret, sancti priores patres ordinaverunt: & ordinationes eorum posteriores semper in conciliis confirmaverunt, ut scil. bis in anno in qualibet provincia celebranda esset synodus. Unde in canonibus Terraconensis Concilii c. 8. ita dicitur: Propter ecclesiasticas causas & altercationum solutiones placuit per singulas provincias bis in anno concilia fieri, convocante Metropolitano omnes episcopos provinciales: ita ut ad concilium procedant omnes presbyteri vel diaconi, vel hi qui laesos se existimant, ut in concilio causae examinatae adiustum iudicium perducantur. Haec ibi. Secundumq; capitulum Carthaginensis Concilii tertii dicit similiter: Placuit ut propter causas ecclesiasticas quae ad provinciae plebem saepe intentatae sunt: singulis annis concilium provinciale convocetur. Rursus capitulum septimum Toletani Concilii sexti: Quamvis, inquit, priora neququam siluerunt de tanto facinore Concilia: ratio dictabat ut ea quae frequenti praevaricatione iterantur, frequenti sententia condemnentur. Quamuis, ut scribitur in eodem concilio, sape pullulantia pravitatis germina, sanctorum sapissime Patrum iusta noverimus severitate damnata, tamen quia crebro conspiciuntur denuo vigere radicibus: iustitiae acriori vigore radicitus ea amputari sancimus. Caeterum capitulum tertium quarti Concilii Toletani ita loquitur: Nulla pene disciplina mores ab ecclesia Christi magis expellit, quam negligentia sacerdotum, qui contemptu canonibus ad corrigendos ecclesiasticos mores synodos facere negligunt. Ob hoc a nobis definitum est, ut quia iuxta antiquorum patrum decreta, bis in anno difficultas temporis fieri concilium non sinit, saltem semel a nobis celebretur; ita tamen ut si fidei causa est: aut quaelibet alia ecclesia communis, generalis totius Hispaniae & Galliae synodus convocetur. Si vero de ecclesiae communi utilitate tractabitur, speciale erit concilium, prout uniuscuiusq; provinciae Metropolitanus elegerit peragendum. Haec ibi. Ex quibus omnibus arguit à simili, quod etiam propter defectum conciliorum generalium totius ecclesiae, quae sola audet intrepide corrigere omnes ea mala quae universalem tangunt ecclesiam, manentia diu incorrecta crescunt, & inventa sunt de malo in peius, donec tandem iniqua sub infectione consuetudinis reputentur licita.
units.tr: Inquire whether any apocryphal writings, hymns or prayers have, with the passing of time, been introduced to the detriment of faith, through zeal or ignorance; and correct the discords of opinion, such as those concerning the conception of the glorious Virgin and the like. Quiet unjust laws; amend wicked customs. Are not unjust laws found in Saxony, which the theologians have attacked? And what Christian custom can be more deserving of condemnation than that by which clergy, laity and princes everywhere now go mad, celebrating the most holy night of the Nativity with games of dice rather than contemplating the heavenly mysteries? Has it not become customary in Livonia that the sacrament of the Eucharist is given to none of the country people? Is it not found in the same place that a man has two living wives, and a woman several husbands? What more? From the bishops coming to a general council from every province, inquire into all the abusive customs and pernicious rites introduced in the churches and among the conditions of men in various regions, on whatever occasion; so that, concerning the aforesaid and similar deviations, you may reform all the states of the Church either in a general council, or order them to be reformed in provincial councils, so that by your authority the Church may be restored and the house of God purged of all uncleanness, vices and errors. And so that this might be done diligently, the holy earlier Fathers ordained, and their later ordinances were always confirmed in councils, that a synod should be held twice a year in every province. Hence the canons of the Council of Tarragona, c. 8, speak thus: For ecclesiastical causes and the settling of disputes, it has pleased that councils be held twice a year in each province, the metropolitan summoning all the provincial bishops, so that all presbyters or deacons, or those who think themselves wronged, come to the council, so that the causes may be examined there and brought to a just judgement. So far there. The second chapter of the Third Council of Carthage says similarly: It has pleased that, for ecclesiastical causes which are often raised against the people of the province, a provincial council be convoked every year. Again, the seventh chapter of the Sixth Council of Toledo: Although, it says, the earlier councils were not without reason silent about so great a crime, reason dictated that those things which are repeated by frequent transgression should be condemned by frequent sentence. And although, as is written in the same council, we have often known the shoots of wickedness that sprout, condemned by the just severity of the holy Fathers, yet because they are constantly seen to grow again from their roots, we decree that they be cut off from the root with sharper vigour of justice. Moreover, the third chapter of the Fourth Council of Toledo speaks thus: Scarcely any discipline drives morals more out of the Church of Christ than the negligence of priests, who, in contempt of the canons, neglect to hold synods for correcting ecclesiastical morals. For this reason it has been decided by us that, since according to the decrees of the ancient Fathers the difficulty of the times does not allow a council to be held twice a year, it shall be held by us at least once; yet so that, if it concerns the cause of the faith, or some other common matter of the Church, a general synod of all Spain and Gaul be convoked. If indeed it is to treat of the common utility of the Church, it shall be a special council, to be held as the metropolitan of each province shall choose. So far there. From all these things he argues by analogy that, also on account of the lack of general councils of the whole Church, which alone dares fearlessly to correct all those evils which touch the universal Church, evils that remain uncorrected for a long time grow, and have been found to go from bad to worse, until at last iniquitous things, under the infection of custom, are regarded as lawful.

units.la: His itaq; peractis, ut in illo sit nostrum explicuisse, à quo nobis fuit inchoasse, inuisibilis omnium creatoris principis pacis imploro opem suffragiis ut meis verborum energia tenuibus hortamentis vim tribuat effectus peroptatam, fragilitatemq; humanae veritatis illustret fulgoribus, ut intentioni pietatis se non opponat pertinacem, ne divinae severitatis ultio postmodum corripiat contradictores, & non ut recto rationis libramine amplectentes, viam consilii pacis misericordia profluens, pax perpetua & gloria suscipiat sempiterna. Clemens Vrbano litem quia moverat, ergo Explicis errantem codex vasurus in orbem, Consilii placeat, nominetur Epistola Pacis: Si facit anterior torpor vel devius error, Ut taceant linguae, mundum transite libelle. Schisma necat tale pote concilium generale. Clama, non metue montes transfire per altos. Per sylvas & aquas, valles, lacerasque miricas. Non defers merces, sed veri portitor es tu. Et si displiceas veri quia nuncius, ex quo Assem vix valet esse tuum, quid si lacerarиc: Finit Epistola pacis
units.tr: Having finished these things, so that what I began may be brought to its conclusion, I implore the aid of the invisible Creator of all things, the Prince of Peace, with my prayers, that the power of my words may lend force to my slight exhortations and bring about the much-desired effect. May he illuminate the frailty of human truth with his brightness, so that it does not stand obstinately against the intention of piety, lest the vengeance of divine severity afterwards seize those who contradict it. May those who embrace it not on the balance of right reason, but who accept the way of the counsel of peace flowing from mercy, receive everlasting peace and glory. Clement, because he had stirred up a quarrel with Urban, therefore the book, about to go out into the world, explaining the erring one: may it please to be named the Epistle of Peace. If a former sluggishness or a devious error makes it so, let the tongues be silent and the little book pass over the world. A general council can end such a schism. Cry out, do not fear to cross the high mountains, through the woods and waters, the valleys and the rough brambles. You do not carry wares, but you are the bearer of truth. And if you are displeasing because you are the messenger of truth, for which scarcely an as is worth being yours, what if it should be torn? Here ends the Epistle of Peace.

units.la: DE EODEM SCHISMATE, ALIVS TRACTATVS EIVSDEM.
units.tr: On the same schism, another treatise by the same author.

units.la: IN inquisitione veritatis tangentis proximum schisma & statum eius, oportet non esse monoculum: sic quod tantum vno oculo ad rem ipsam attendamus: quod fit dum illa tantummodo, quae pro parte nostra faciunt, aspicimus; & aduersas rationes videre negligimus. Et quia multi, vt suppono, offerent oculis videre volentium rationes, quae faciunt pro sua opinione in materia, quae nunc ventilatur, scilicet de subtractione obedientiae a Domino nostro in toto vel in parte: decreui quadam similiter in aspectu adducere in oppositum facientia.
units.tr: In inquiring into the truth about the present schism and its state, one must not be one-eyed, looking at the matter with only one eye. That happens when we look only at what supports our side and neglect to see the opposing arguments. Since many, as I suppose, will put before the eyes of those who wish to see the arguments that support their opinion on the question now being debated, namely whether obedience to our Lord [the Pope] should be withdrawn wholly or in part, I have decided to set out in the same way some considerations on the opposite side.

units.la: Primo notetur, quae & qualis persona, & cuius fama & status nunc tractatur: & quibus priuilegiis, qua dignitate & superioritate dotatus est. Idcirco summe cauendum est, ne quid temere aut inconsiderate aut praecipitanter fiat.
units.tr: First, let it be noted who and what kind of person is now under discussion, what his reputation and status are, and with what privileges, dignity and superiority he is endowed. Therefore the greatest caution must be taken that nothing be done rashly, inconsiderately or hastily.

units.la: Secundo notetur, quod obtulit semper & publice in primo consistorio, quod videlicet habebat promptitudinem animi ad mortem pro eius sustinendam, antequam non fiet vnio ecclesiae.
units.tr: Second, let it be noted that he has always offered openly, and in the first consistory, that he was ready in mind to die for its sake, rather than the union of the Church should fail to be achieved.

units.la: Tertio notetur, quod cessio sua si nunc fieret, non esset conueniens; sed pessima: nisi prius ab aduersa parte alia sentiremus. Et ita non debet accusari de periurio, si non cesserit vel cedat praesentialiter. Si dicatur, quod nec hoc petitur, sed quod reddat se voluntarium & promptum ad cessionem. Primo videatur, si iuramentum hoc importat, quod vocaliter nunc istud offerat. Secundo aduertatur si illa oblatio de promptitudine ad mortem, satis hoc importat quod etiam paratus est cedere antequam non fieret pax. Tertio videatur, si possit habere colorem sufficientem ad excusationem suam, quod vocaliter pro nunc non offert cessionem; antequam sciatur voluntas eorum de aduersa parte: quia aestimat forsan & non sine apparentia, quod aduersarii magis fortificarentur vel indurarentur. Et dicerent interpretantes istam oblationem in malum, quod diffidit de iure suo: & hoc non sine colore.
units.tr: Third, let it be noted that his cession, if it were made now, would not be fitting but very harmful, unless we first knew the mind of the other side. Therefore he ought not to be accused of perjury if he has not ceded, or does not cede, in person now. If it be said that this is not even what is sought, but that he should make himself willing and ready for cession, let us first see whether the oath imports that he should now offer it aloud. Second, let it be considered whether that offer of readiness to die sufficiently implies that he is also prepared to cede before peace should fail to be made. Third, let it be seen whether he could have a sufficient colour for his excuse, in that for the present he does not offer cession aloud, until the will of those on the opposing side is known; for he perhaps judges, and not without appearance, that the adversaries would be strengthened or hardened. And those who interpret that offer in a bad sense would say that he distrusts his own right, and this not without some colour.

units.la: Quarto principaliter notetur: quod per bullam in responsione tertia offert simpliciter & absolute, quod vult tenere iuramentum in forma. Quomodo igitur poterit argui de periurio? Si dicatur, quod intelligi taliter iuramentum quam Cardinales & alii: non obstat: quia nondum vidimus nec venimus ad hoc quod cessio debeat compleri, quoniam viderimus de responsionibus aliorum alterius obedientiae. Et si tunc Papa velit subterfugere & glossare, & ita pacem per hoc impedire: locum habebit interpretatio, & suae interpretationis si mala sit impugnatio.
units.tr: Fourth, it should principally be noted that by the bull, in his third response, he offers simply and absolutely that he wishes to keep the oath in its form. How then can he be charged with perjury? If it be said that the Cardinals and others understand the oath in another way, that is no obstacle, for we have not yet seen, nor come to the point, at which the cession must be carried out, since we shall see the responses of others of the other obedience. And if then the Pope should wish to escape and gloss the matter, and so impede peace, interpretation will have its place, and his interpretation may be impugned if it is bad.

units.la: Quinto notetur, quod per nuncium Apostolicum, qui nouissime venit, fecit multa offerre Domino Regi & aliis super declaratione voluntatis suae: & difficile esset iudicare eum, nisi talia scirentur, quae tamen non est necesse reuelare vniuersitati vel omnibus: praesertim vbi negotia non tractantur ita secrete, quin faciliter sciri possint.
units.tr: Fifth, let it be noted that through the Apostolic nuncio who came most recently, he caused many things to be offered to the lord King and to others concerning the declaration of his will. It would be difficult to judge him without knowing such things; yet it is not necessary to reveal them to the university or to everyone, especially where affairs are not handled so secretly that they cannot easily be known.

units.la: Sexto notetur quod in quarta quaestione inter illa quae ponuntur, supponitur quod Papa fuerit protestatus de non recedendo a viis suis: quod multi omnino falsum aestimant: imo potius offert omnem viam rationabilem.
units.tr: Sixth, let it be noted that in the fourth question, among those things put forward, it is assumed that the Pope has protested that he will not depart from his ways. Many consider this wholly false; rather, on the contrary, he offers every reasonable way.

units.la: Septimo notetur quod via cessionis est inefficax & insufficiens, si alii de alia obedientia nolint illam recipere. Et ideo mirum videretur, quod ad talem viam, quae ex hypothesi possibili esset inefficax, aliquis obligaretur. Si dicatur quod saltem Papa tenetur secundum praeparationem animi acceptare istam viam. Non video qualiter istud possit negari, quia etiam tenetur acceptare isto modo mortem. Sed quod non habeat istam promptitudinem, non potest sciri, cum sit in mente. Nec videtur quod teneatur explicare voce vel signis exterioribus pro nunc, propter aliqua tacta circa tertium notatum, quia nec etiam hoc iurauit. Et forte expediens est silere usque ad tempus renunciationis, propter ambitiones illorum, qui tenderent ad Papatum diuersis viis, cautelis & modis, & possent impedire factum totum.
units.tr: Seventh, let it be noted that the way of cession is ineffective and insufficient if those of the other obedience are unwilling to accept it. Therefore it would seem strange that anyone should be bound to such a way, which, on a possible hypothesis, would be ineffective. If it be said that at least the Pope is bound, according to his readiness of mind, to accept this way, I do not see how that can be denied, since he is also bound to accept death in this manner. But whether he has this readiness cannot be known, since it lies in the mind. Nor does it seem that he is bound to explain it by voice or outward signs for the present, on account of certain matters touched on under the third point noted, since he has not sworn this either. And perhaps it is expedient to keep silent until the time of renunciation, because of the ambitions of those who would strive for the papacy by diverse ways, devices and means, and could impede the whole deed.

units.la: Octauo notetur, quod possibilis est alia via conueniens & bona, & quae ab aduersariis forte acceptabitur, & in hoc casu qui clarus est, Papa sufficienter se absoluet apud Deum & homines, si illam viam acceperit, per quam fiet pax. Nam supposito, quod cessio de se esset via melior, tamen potest fieri sufficiens per accidens. Item non semper melius bonum cadit sub obligatione, quin sufficiat minus bonum acceptare. Duobus enim propositis bonis, maiori & minori stat quod ad nullum obliger. Stat etiam quod ad minus obliger & non ad maius, & stat quod ad vtrumq; obliger sub distinctione. Et in casu isto est quaestio apud Doctores: an teneat acceptare maius bonum. Et non est dubia ista quaestio, si maius bonum sit mihi difficilius, sed si caeteris paribus, & stante aequa facilitate. In casu isto si dimittam maius bonum, dicunt aliqui quod pecco propter contemptum, apud alios oppositum est multum probabile. Vnde propter experiendam libertatem meam vel aliquod tale: possum vt videtur licite maius bonum deserere minori acceptato. Tunc applicetur in casu nostro: & constat, quod Papa dicere poterit de ista via & alia minus bona: quod cætera non sunt paria.
units.tr: Eighth, let it be noted that another suitable and good way is possible, which perhaps will be acceptable to the adversaries. In this case, which is clear, the Pope will sufficiently absolve himself before God and men if he takes that way by which peace will be made. For, supposing that cession were in itself the better way, it can nevertheless be made sufficient accidentally. Likewise the greater good does not always fall under obligation, so that it is not enough to accept the lesser good. For of two goods proposed, the greater and the lesser, it is possible that one is bound to neither; it is possible that one is bound to the lesser and not to the greater; and it is possible that one is bound to each, under a distinction. In this case there is a question among the Doctors: whether one is bound to accept the greater good. This question is not doubtful if the greater good is more difficult for me, but if other things are equal and the ease is the same. In this case, if I give up the greater good, some say that I sin through contempt; among others the opposite is very probable. Hence, for the sake of exercising my liberty or something of that kind, I may, it seems, lawfully forsake the greater good for the lesser one accepted. Let this then be applied to our case; and it is clear that the Pope will be able to say of this way, and of another less good way, that the other things are not equal.

units.la: Nono notetur quod Papa non potest teneri ad cessionem secluso iuramento, nisi istæ tres conditiones ponantur. Primo quod per cessionem habeatur unio. Secundo quod aliter non posset humanitus haberi. Tertio quod malum illud, propter quod fit cessio facienda, sit mortiferum animabus: & quod per cessionem non augeatur. Nunc bene attendamus, si rebus adhuc stantibus ut stant, præsertim apud aduersarios nostros, quorum opiniones ignoramus, posset dici apparenter aliquam trium conditionum deesse nunc in cessione.
units.tr: Ninth, let it be noted that the Pope cannot be held to cession, setting aside the oath, unless these three conditions are posited. First, that union be obtained through the cession. Second, that otherwise it could not be obtained by human means. Third, that the evil on account of which the cession is to be made be mortal to souls, and that it not be increased by the cession. Now let us well consider whether, with things still standing as they stand, especially among our adversaries, whose opinions we do not know, it could be said with some appearance that one of the three conditions is now lacking in the cession.

units.la: Decimo notetur, quod etiam de parte nostra Rex Arragonum, & præsertim eius populus, non sunt adhuc determinati ad istam viam cessionis: imo dicunt multi vidisse multas literas, quibus oppositum clare perpenditur. Et ipsis sic perdurantibus, constat quod cessio non esset via totaliter sufficiens: imo multi formidant, ne iam sit formatus unus rancor & quoddam seminarium discordiæ inter illos Hispanos & Arragonenses, ex una parte contra Gallos, & interpretantur quod in odium eorum volunt Papam deponere, quia de patria.
units.tr: Tenth, let it be noted that also on our side the King of Aragon, and especially his people, are not yet determined upon this way of cession. Indeed many say they have seen many letters in which the opposite is clearly weighed. And with things thus persisting, it is evident that cession would not be a wholly sufficient way. Indeed many fear that already one rancour and a certain seedbed of discord has been formed between those Spaniards and the Aragonese on one side and the French on the other, and they interpret it as meaning that they wish to depose the Pope out of hatred of them, because he is of their own country.

units.la: Undecimo notetur qualiter per determinationem istarum quæstionum, si nunc fierent, posset poni schisma in fide inter Universitatem Parisiensem, & Papam nostrum & sibi adhærentes ex una parte. Eundem & alias Universitates alterius obedientiæ, quæ sunt æmulæ eius, & in quibus sunt clerici, & viget Universitas.
units.tr: Eleventh, let it be noted how, through the determination of these questions, if they were now made, a schism in faith could be set up between the University of Paris, our Pope and those adhering to him on the one side, and the same and other universities of the other obedience, which are rivals of it and in which there are clergy, and where the university flourishes.

units.la: Duodecimo notetur modus qui tenetur de schedulis, & modo vocum seu opinionum vel deliberationum: quia in illis quæ fiunt per modum universitatis, facultas Theologiæ, ad quam spectat principalissime illud negotium, non habet nisi quartam vocem, & facultas medicinæ tantam.
units.tr: Twelfth, let it be noted the manner held concerning the ballots, and the manner of voices, or opinions, or deliberations. For in those things which are done by way of the university, the faculty of theology, to which that business chiefly belongs, has only a fourth vote, and the faculty of medicine as much.

units.la: Tertio decimo notetur, quomodo potest requiri salua conscientia, quod à Papa, qui non est iudicatus schismaticus aut hæreticus, posset remoueri obedientia circa ea quæ ad eum semper spectare confessa sunt. Et aduertere debent talia agentes super pœnis expressis, & de peccato ad Deum: notatur q 4. none: cum ibi allegatis. Si dicatur, quod Papa ostendit se schismaticum, hoc non est clarum per præcedentia. Item non est talis iudicatus ab habentibus potestatem: & non est in potestate libera cuiuslibet sic iudicare de Papa, & ab eius obedientia remouere, aut contemnere sententias suas, vel iurisdictionem diminuere. Et videatur si tales sint suspecti de schismate contra Papam. Item notent p. incipes, quid tales facerent contra eos, si impune audirent &c. & quam fidelitatem seruarent: quia sic d cerepossent, quod essent tyranni.
units.tr: Thirteenth, let it be noted how it can be required, consistent with conscience, that obedience be withdrawn from the Pope, who has not been judged a schismatic or heretic, in those matters which have always been confessed to belong to him. Those who act in such matters should note the express penalties and the sin before God; this is noted in "q. 4, none", with the citations there. If it be said that the Pope shows himself to be a schismatic, this is not clear from what has gone before. Likewise he has not been so judged by those who have the power to do so; and it is not in the free power of any individual to judge the Pope in this way and remove him from obedience, or to despise his sentences, or to diminish his jurisdiction. Let it be seen whether such persons are themselves suspected of schism against the Pope. Likewise let princes note what such persons would do against them if they heard them with impunity, and what fidelity they would keep; for thus they might be said to be tyrants.

units.la: Quartodecimo notetur si expediret simpliciter ecclesiæ quod prælati darent beneficia: & si melius distribuerentur attento statu eorum & familiarium &c. Et an studiosi in Universitatibus haberent beneficia. Et an mali prælati fierent peiores: quia magis honorarentur, & eis adularetur in pec-catis.
units.tr: Fourteenthly, it should be considered whether it would simply be expedient for the Church that prelates should grant benefices, and whether they would be better distributed, given the condition of the prelates and their households. Also whether students in the universities should hold benefices, and whether bad prelates would become worse because they would be more honoured and flattered in their sins.

units.la: Quintodecimo notetur quod si expediat principes incitare ad remouendum vel diminuendum iurisdictionem vel redditus ecclesiæ, sue ratione sue alterius autoritate: & si bona melius distribuerentur: & felicite hoc facerent. Et si totus clerus finaliter infra breue tempus perderetur & affligeretur, maioribus primo destructis & afflictis.
units.tr: Fifteenthly, it should be considered whether it is expedient to incite princes to remove or diminish the jurisdiction or revenues of the Church, whether on their own initiative or by another's authority; whether goods would be better distributed; and whether they would succeed in doing this. And whether the whole clergy would in the end be lost and afflicted within a short time, the greater ones being destroyed and afflicted first.

units.la: Decimosexto notetur circa iuramentum Papæ. Si factum ante Papatum liget eum postquam est assumptus. Item si posset secum dispensare. Item si iudicet quod vergat in detrimentum salutis & totius ecclesiæ obseruatio iuramenti. Item si interpretatio spectet ad eum. Item si magna pars clericorum, specialiter Doctorum utriusque iuris diuini & humani sit secum, quod obseruari illa iuramenti esset in detrimentum salutis &c. an excusetur. Item, ut iam dictum est, offert quod ut observare: & quod laboretur interim apud alios. Item si habuerit causam male suspicandi in materia ista & caute respondendi, attenta variatione circa cum & Clementem, & moribus quorundam Cardinalium, & quod sibi negabatur modus practicandi viam cessionis.
units.tr: Sixteenthly, it should be noted concerning the Pope's oath: whether an oath made before the papacy binds him after he has been raised to it; also whether he can dispense himself from it; also whether he judges that keeping the oath would tend to the detriment of salvation and of the whole Church; also whether its interpretation belongs to him; also whether a large part of the clergy, especially teachers of both divine and human law, is on his side, holding that keeping that oath would be to the detriment of salvation, and whether he is thereby excused. Also, as has already been said, he offers that he is ready to observe it, and that meanwhile efforts are being made with others. Also whether he had cause to suspect ill in this matter and to answer cautiously, given the change of attitude regarding Clement, the conduct of certain cardinals, and the fact that he was denied the means of pursuing the way of cession.

units.la: Decimoseptimo notetur, quod in prima responsione sua, in qua aliqui dicunt eum reprobasse simpliciter modum cessionis, non potest hoc expressè haberi: quia illud, quod ponit de scandalo & pernicie &c. refert ad modum exequendi illam viam, si esset ineptus: & ideo illud petebat modum exequendi. Et circa hoc mirantur aliqui, quomodo hoc sibi potuit rationabiliter denegari, cum maxime hoc tangat eum: & sit caput &c.
units.tr: Seventeenthly, it should be noted that in his first reply, in which some say he simply rejected the manner of cession, this cannot be expressly held. What he says about scandal and ruin and so on refers to the manner of carrying out that way, should it prove unsuitable; and therefore he was asking for the manner of carrying it out. Some are surprised at this, asking how it could reasonably have been refused him, since it touches him most of all and he is the head, and so on.

units.la: Decimooctauo notetur & aduertat universitas, quomodo aliqui de suppositis improbant simpliciter & de plano vias, quas ipsa reputauit utiles, bonas & convenientes, & per quarum quamlibet posset haberi pax, & rationes ad hoc dedit: & se obtulit in literis patentibus quamlibet illarum contra quemlibet sustinere. Et videatur si circumstantiæ sic sunt immutatæ vel ex persona vel tempore, quod omnes viæ aliæ præter cessionem sint factæ ineptæ & insufficientes, imo quod illarum coloratores aut opinatores digni sint punitione vel infamatione, & præsertim quia in impugnatione dictarum viarum aliarum sunt rationes ab aliquibus, qui pro omni tempore militant contra eos, si quid virtutis habeant, & si sit in honorem Universitatis ipsa viderit.
units.tr: Eighteenthly, let the university note and take heed how some of those under it plainly and flatly disapprove the ways which it judged useful, good and suitable, and by any one of which peace could be obtained; it gave reasons for this and offered itself, in open letters, to defend any one of them against anyone. And it should be considered whether the circumstances, whether of persons or of time, have so changed that all the other ways apart from cession have been rendered unsuitable and insufficient; indeed, whether the advocates or proposers of them deserve punishment or infamy. This is especially so because, in attacking those other ways, there are arguments from some who fight on against them at all times, if they have any force; and let the university see whether it is for its own honour.

units.la: Decimonono notetur specialiter probatio concilii generalis: tamen necessario fiendum quidam bene apparet persuadebat: propter electionem noui Papæ. Hæc est radix in sententia breui. Quia magna pars catholicorum est neutra: sic quod credit quod neuter sit Papa: aut in dubio suspensam se tenet. Isti vero consequenter habent credere aut dubitare de Cardinalibus utriusque partis: quod non possint etiam similiter eligere nouum Papam: quia si neuter sit Papa: maxima pars eorum nec habet nec habere potest potestatem creandi nouum Papam: nec alii quicunq; a cardinalibus nisi per concilium generale. Supposito quod omnes catholici particulariter consentirent in aliquos certos pro eligendo nouo Papa, si non fieret collegialiter, nihil esset: alioquin Vrbanus intrusus habuisset maximam apparentiam. Si dicatur quod Cardinales soli antiqui creabunt nouum. Primo dubium est apud multos, an perdiderunt potestatem eligendi. Item si alii Cardinales omnes sunt veri Cardinales, si antiqui, non habebunt nisi partiales voces. Alii enim habent potestatem in electione Papae sicut ipsi: ideo non esset secundum istam rationem plena pacificatio omnium sine concilio generali.
units.tr: Nineteenthly, the proof of a general council should be noted in particular. Yet it seemed to some, and they persuaded it fairly well, that it was necessary, on account of the election of a new Pope. This is the root of the short opinion. For a great part of the Catholics are neutral, so that they believe neither is Pope, or else hold themselves in suspense and doubt. These, consequently, must believe or doubt of the cardinals of both parties that they likewise cannot elect a new Pope; for if neither is Pope, the greatest part of them neither has nor can have the power of creating a new Pope, nor can any others, except by a general council. Suppose all Catholics agreed particularly on certain persons to elect as the new Pope; if it were not done collegially, it would be nothing. Otherwise the intruded Urban would have the greatest appearance of right. If it is said that the old cardinals alone will create a new Pope, then first, it is doubtful to many whether they have lost the power of electing. Again, if the other cardinals are all true cardinals, the old ones will have only partisan votes, for the others have power in the election of the Pope just as they do. Therefore, according to this reasoning, there would be no full pacification of all without a general council.

units.la: Vicesimo notetur: Si Papa incipiat persequi alios: quia videtur inter cætera, quod illi qui sunt pro se, ab eis persequuntur, & quædam talia: & vtatur excommunicationibus, vtrum illæ erunt timendæ vel non. Si remoueat beneficia: vtrum reperientur alii qui capiant. Si illi excommunicentur & non curent: vtrum præsumendum sit simile, quod alii non curabunt: & quod debent conuiuere & communicare cum eis sicut ante. Et quod erit remedium in celebrare volente & in articulo mortis: an erit aliquis sic negligens propriam salutem: aut temerarius quod non formidet sententiam illius quem tenet aut tenere debet Papam: saltem qui non est iudicatus non esse talis. Et quod erit etiam in vita remedium vel releuamen.
units.tr: Twentiethly, it should be noted: if the Pope begins to persecute others (for it seems, among other things, that those who take his side are persecuted by them, and such things), and uses excommunications, whether these will be feared or not. If he removes benefices, whether others will be found to take them. If those excommunicated do not care, whether one should presume that others likewise will not care, and that they ought to live and communicate with them as before. And what the remedy will be for one who wishes to celebrate, and at the point of death: will there be anyone so negligent of his own salvation, or so rash, that he does not fear the sentence of the one whom he holds, or ought to hold, as Pope, at least one who has not been judged not to be such? And what remedy or relief there will be even in life.

units.la: ITEM ALIUS TRACTA- TUS DE EODEM.
units.tr: ANOTHER TREATISE ON THE SAME SUBJECT.

units.la: Præsupposito quod Papa possit fieri hæreticus & schismaticus: Eo etiam quod de his criminibus posset accusari, si de his esset vehementer infamatus & suspectus. Quorum vtrumq; quidam negare voluerunt. Quæritur vtrum rebus stantibus vt nunc turbatis in ecclesia, sit expediens accusare iudicialiter Dominum Benedictum nouissime in Papam electum, super huiusmodi criminibus hæresis & schismatis.
units.tr: Presupposing that the Pope can become a heretic and a schismatic, and that he could be accused of these crimes if he were strongly defamed and suspected of them (some wished to deny both), the question is whether, with the Church now in its present troubled state, it is expedient to bring a judicial accusation against Lord Benedict, lately elected Pope, for the crimes of heresy and schism.

units.la: Primo quod sic: quia non debent fideles se exponere discrimini. Amans enim periculum peribit in illo, inquit Sapiens: Sed obedire homini schismatico vel hæretico, vt vero Papæ, esset discrimen peccati mortalis, vt videtur. Et non obedire eidem; si sit verus Papa & non schismaticus, est similiter discrimen: ideo in casu dubio, sicut est modo apud multos, debet inquiri & sciri veritas. Et videtur fundari posse ista ratio in regula magistrali theologiæ: quod dubitans de aliquo actu an sit peccatum mortale, & faciens illum actum: debet esse certus quod peccat mortaliter. Cuius ratio assignatur illa quæ dicta est: quia exponit se discrimini. Quod autem nunc sit dubium apud multos; an Benedictus sit schismaticus & hæreticus vel non: patet ad oculum de multis, qui sibi obediunt, & alii non etiam de sua obedientia, etiam de eodem regno, imo & in eadem vniuersitate vel collegio. Tollendum est igitur illud dubium à cordibus hominum: ne obediendo exponant se discrimini ratione dubitationis antedictæ. Notetur ig. distinctione Anastasius, qui communicauit Fortino & Archacio.
units.tr: First, that it is: because the faithful ought not to expose themselves to danger. "He who loves danger will perish in it," says the Wise Man (Amans enim periculum peribit in illo). Yet to obey a schismatic or heretic as if he were the true Pope would be, it seems, a danger of mortal sin; and not to obey him, if he is the true Pope and not a schismatic, is likewise a danger. Therefore, in a doubtful case, such as now exists for many, the truth must be sought and known. This reasoning seems to be grounded in the master's rule of theology: whoever doubts whether an action is a mortal sin, and yet performs it, must be certain that he sins mortally. The reason given for this is the one already stated, namely that he exposes himself to danger. That there is now doubt among many whether Benedict is a schismatic and heretic or not is plain to see from many who obey him and others who do not, even within the same kingdom, indeed within the same university or college. This doubt must therefore be removed from men's hearts, so that they do not expose themselves to danger by obeying while in the doubt just mentioned. Let it be noted at the ig. distinction concerning Anastasius, who communicated with Fortinus and Acacius.

units.la: Secundo sic: Non minus necesse est vel expediens scire an subtractio sit continuanda, quam fuit expediens cognoscere an esset facienda. Sed expediens fuit secundum, vt nunc supponitur; igitur & primum. Antecedens pro prima parte fundatum videtur in sufficienti similitudine. Addito etiam quod post subtractionem multa facta sunt, & aliqua oblata per Benedictum, propter quæ multi varie sentiunt de subtractione continuanda vel non continuanda. Dicentibus aliis; quia Benedictus satis offert, & cessant causæ subtractionis. Aliis in oppositum asserentibus quod nec cessant, imo nec cessare possunt, vt vnquam possit in Papatu ius habere: propterea necessaria est, vt videtur, iuridica discussio.
units.tr: Second, as follows: it is no less necessary or expedient to know whether the withdrawal of obedience is to be continued than it was expedient to know whether it should be undertaken at all. But the second was expedient, as is now supposed; therefore the first is too. The antecedent for the first part seems well founded on a sufficient analogy. Add to this that since the withdrawal much has been done, and some things offered by Benedict, on account of which many think differently about whether the withdrawal should be continued. Some say that Benedict offers enough and the grounds for withdrawal have ceased; others assert the contrary, that they have not ceased and indeed cannot cease, so that he could ever have a right to the papacy. Therefore, it seems, a juridical discussion is necessary.

units.la: Tertio sic: Charitas obligat & mandat curare de proximis & eorum salute & reductione ad cognitionem veritatis. Si ergo sumus certi sufficienter, quod Benedicto nullo modo est obediendum sub poena schismatis, quia schismaticus est: nos ex hoc debemus procurare, quod alia Regna vel singularia suppositia, eidem nullatenus obediant, & hoc fieri non potest absque discussione iuridica, vt videtur. Nam si non vocarentur alii, ipsi de facili contemnerent quicquid ageremus. Si autem adhuc dubitamus: redit argumentum primum, quod exponimus nos discrimini continuando subtractionem ab illo. Cui autem sit obediendum, dubitamus.
units.tr: Third, as follows: charity obliges us and commands us to take care of our neighbours, of their salvation and of their restoration to knowledge of the truth. If, then, we are sufficiently certain that Benedict must in no way be obeyed under penalty of schism, because he is a schismatic, we ought for this reason to see to it that other kingdoms or individual states do not obey him at all; and this cannot be done, it seems, without a juridical discussion. For if others were not summoned, they would easily scorn whatever we did. But if we are still in doubt, the first argument returns: that we expose ourselves to danger by continuing the withdrawal from him. And to whom we ought to be obedient, we are in doubt.

units.la: Quarto sic: Aut causa præcisa fuit necessario via cessionis, sicut multi tenent dicentes: quod sic fuit pronunciatum per Cancellarium Franciæ ex deliberatione concilii prælatorum: nec aliter prælati iudicauerunt: aut fuerunt cum hoc aliæ causæ. Si primum: constat, vt dicitur, quod offert ipse Benedictus, & Dominus Alexander obtulit eandem viam cessionis & largius quam petebatur. Si secundum: dicatur quod fuerunt aliæ causæ: quæritur an cessent: & si sic, idem quod prius. Si non cessant: ipse ergo Benedictus continuat peccatum suum in grande scandalum totius ecclesiæ. Scita debet confestim fieri processus contra cum ad eius destitutionem totalem realiter & de facto: quatenus possit ecclesiae melius de pastore prouideri. Similiter tales causae quia non notificatae sunt apud omnes, nec certae, illae debent manifestari, ne ex ignorantia faciant sibi restitutionem aliqui: per quorum auxilium ipse posset multipliciter grauare ecclesiam, & praecipue suos cardinales & alios sibi inobedientes, quos odit & persequitur (vt multi aestimant) odio capitali: sicut ex minis eius & processibus (vt fama fert) contra eos inchoatis iudicatur: imo per hoc posset destituere omnes Cardinales veteres & nouos creare, exaltare fautores suos, & alios iustitiae zelatores crudeliter impugnare. His autem inconuenientibus quis non videat expedien esse remedium apponere? Hoc autem fieri non potest, vt videtur, absque iuridica inuestigatione causarum omnium & motiuorum tam iuris quam facti, super rationabilitate subtractionis & eiusdem continuationis.
units.tr: Fourth, as follows: either the matter could necessarily be settled by way of resignation alone, as many hold, saying that this was pronounced by the Chancellor of France on the deliberation of the council of prelates, and that the prelates judged in no other way; or other causes were involved as well. If the first, it is agreed, as is said, that Benedict himself offers resignation, and Lord Alexander offered the same way of resignation, and more fully than was asked. If the second, let it be said that there were other causes; the question is whether they have ceased, and if so, the same as before. If they have not ceased, then Benedict himself continues his sin to the great scandal of the whole Church. Proceedings should be begun at once against him for his total deposition in reality and in fact, so that the Church may be better provided with a minister. Likewise, since such causes have not been made known to all, nor are certain, they ought to be disclosed, lest some through ignorance make restitution to him, through whose help he could harm the Church in many ways, and especially his cardinals and others who are disobedient to him, whom he hates and persecutes with deadly hatred (as many judge), as is inferred from his threats and the proceedings (as rumour has it) begun against them. Indeed, through this he could depose all the old cardinals, create new ones, exalt his supporters, and cruelly attack the zealots of justice. Who does not see that a remedy ought to be applied to these inconveniences? But this cannot, it seems, be done without a juridical investigation of all the causes and motives, both of law and of fact, concerning the reasonableness of the withdrawal and of its continuation.

units.la: Addunt aliqui, quod omnia quae promisit existens in carcere super cessione, refutabit dum erit liber: & allegabit timorem cadentem in constantem virum. Alii dicunt, quod hoc non impedit; alioquin obligatus esset nunc ad impossibile: quia nihil potest agere nisi in carcere, dum semper in illo est. Non est tamen alibi conseruandus, nec in regno, nec extra, vt aliorum est assertio.
units.tr: Some add that whatever he promised about resignation while in prison he will retract once he is free, and he will plead the fear that falls upon a constant man. Others say that this does not prevent it; otherwise he would now be bound to the impossible, since he can act only in prison, as he is always in it. Yet he is not to be kept elsewhere, neither in the kingdom nor outside it, as is the assertion of others.

units.la: Ad oppositum arguitur sic: Discussio iuridica debet coram iudice competenti fieri, & audita parte. Sed nulla persona vel etiam communitas, nisi ecclesia, aut Concilium generale repraesentans ecclesiam, debet esse iudex competens Papae: imo nec ipsum potest iudicare, vt quidam Iuristae dicere volunt: sed pronunc oppositum supponitur. Concluditur ergo quod ista accusatio, discussio & declaratio fieri debebit coram concilio generali totius ecclesiae, saltem istius obedientiae. Tunc vltra arguitur: Si non est expediens celebrare huiusmodi concilium pro hac causa principaliter non est expediens discussionem fieri. Sed non est expediens celebrare huiusmodi Concilium generale pro hac causa: igitur &c. Supposita maiore probatur minor multipliciter. Primo ex parte conuocantis. Secundo ex parte conuocatorum. Tertio ex parte medii in tractando. Quarto ex parte finis in obediendo.
units.tr: To the contrary it is argued as follows: a juridical discussion must be conducted before a competent judge, and with the other party heard. But no person, nor even a community, except the Church or a general council representing the Church, ought to be a competent judge of the Pope; indeed, some jurists wish to say that he cannot even be judged by them. Yet the opposite is here supposed. It follows, therefore, that this accusation, discussion and declaration must be made before a general council of the whole Church, or at least of this obedience. Further it is argued: if it is not expedient to call such a council principally for this cause, it is not expedient for the discussion to be held. But it is not expedient to call such a general council for this cause; therefore etc. Granting the major, the minor is proved in many ways: first from the side of the convener, second from the side of those convened, third from the side of the means of proceeding, fourth from the side of the end in obeying.

units.la: Primo sic ex parte conuocantis: nulla congregatio habet vim concilii generalis, nisi fiat in forma iuris: vel saltem non erit verisimile vel necesse quod omnes obediant sententiae talis congregationis, quae non erit in forma iuris conuocata: & ita erit totum quod ibi agetur dubium, fluctuans & inualidum. Concilium autem generale non potest conuocari in forma iuris, nisi auctoritate summi pontificis: dist. 17. cum ibi allegatis. Et praesertim si sit aliquis talis reputatus in ecclesia: & si non pertinaciter refutauerit celebrare concilium: dum super hoc rationabiliter fuerit requisitus. Istas duas exceptiones reputarent aliqui Iuristarum etiam superfluas: quia tenent regulam in suis terminis generaliter esse veram, tamen ita dicimus in proposito. Supponimus insuper quod Benedictus nondum depositus est de Papatu, quia nec fuit iuridice accusatus, nec auditus, & per consequens non conuictus. Nam etsi haereticus & schismaticus sit iure deponendus, & apud Deum sic meretur, non est tamen depositus de facto ante sententiam: [?]. Notae: & Glossa super hoc verbo: Exempla sunt multa in similibus materiis, de episcopis, aut inferioribus principibus aut praelatis. Quod si quis dixerit non esse expectandam sententiam a iudice latam, dum feratur a iure, dum notorium factum est. Istud dicere est confundere omnem ordinationem politiae, & contra omnem ecclesiae regulam. Nam quilibet ad libitum dicere poterit de non notorio, quod est notorium, & sic quilibet erit iudex in causa sua, sicut ad propositum praesens possemus applicare. Nam multa dicuntur a multis esse notoria crimina contra Benedictum, quae alii vel negant, vel approbant.
units.tr: First, as follows, from the side of the convener: no assembly has the force of a general council unless it is held in due legal form; or at least it will be neither likely nor necessary that all obey the sentence of such an assembly if it has not been convened in legal form; and so whatever is done there will be doubtful, unsettled and invalid. A general council, however, cannot be convened in legal form except by the authority of the supreme pontiff (dist. 17, with the authorities cited there). This holds especially if there is someone reputed such in the Church, and if he does not stubbornly refuse to call a council when he has been reasonably asked to do so. Some jurists think these two exceptions superfluous, since they hold the rule to be true in general terms as stated; yet we speak thus in the present case. We further suppose that Benedict has not yet been deposed from the papacy, since he has not been juridically accused or heard, and consequently not convicted. For although a heretic and schismatic is to be deposed by law, and so deserves it before God, he is nevertheless not deposed in fact before sentence [?]. Note the gloss on this word: there are many examples in similar matters, concerning bishops, or lower princes or prelates. But if someone says that the sentence of a judge need not be awaited, since the matter is carried on by law, once the fact is notorious: to say this is to confound all order of polity and to go against every rule of the Church. For anyone could at will call something notorious which is not notorious, and so each man would be judge in his own cause, as we could apply to the present purpose. For many people say that many crimes against Benedict are notorious, which others either deny or approve.

units.la: Deinde dicentes quod Papa haereticus minor est quocunque catholico, & iurisdictioni ecclesiae subest, intelligunt quod ab aliis potest vt inferior iudicari, sed ante iudicium debet semper reputari maior. Non enim insequimur errorem quorundam dicentium, iniustum non posse iuste dominari. Iura ad haec non allego, quia totus textus libri Conciliorum ab Isidoro plenus est, quod Concilium nullum robur habet, nec potest conuocari, nisi auctoritate Papae, & quod etiam ante omnia spoliatus debet restitui. In prologo vocat istas duas regulas duas claues & duos gladios sufficientes &c. Et est casus in terminis de Symacho Papa, qui licet accusatus esset de haeresi, conuocauit concilium, & ante omnia restitutus est. Postmodum se purgauit. Reperitur etiam quod clerus Romanus, scilicet Cardinales, puniti sunt, eo quod a Papa discesserant.
units.tr: Then, those who say that a heretical Pope is inferior to any Catholic and subject to the jurisdiction of the Church mean that others may judge him as an inferior, but before judgment he must always be regarded as superior. For we do not follow the error of some who say that an unjust man cannot rule justly. I do not cite laws for these points, because the whole text of the book of Councils, from Isidore onward, is full of the principles that a Council has no force and cannot be convoked except by the authority of the Pope, and that a person who has been despoiled must be restored before anything else. In the prologue he calls these two rules two keys and two swords, sufficient, and so on. And there is a case in point concerning Pope Symmachus, who, although accused of heresy, convoked a council and was restored before anything else. Afterwards he cleared himself. It is also found that the Roman clergy, namely the Cardinals, were punished because they had withdrawn from the Pope.

units.la: His suppositis arguamus vltra, quomodo Dominus Benedictus conuocabit concilium stans in carcere & spoliatus, vt dicitur. Qualiter etiam illi, qui non restituunt obedientiam iam subtractam sibi parebunt? Qualiter etiam ipsemet in causa sua audietur, vt iuris est, si non relaxetur, siue detur libertati, saltem in concilio? Qualiter praeterea poterit multos a concilio abiicere, vel petere remoueri tanquam inimicos sibi, specialiter proprios fratres Dominos Cardinales? Et an causam habeat super hoc rationabilem, videte quid praesumendum.
units.tr: Given these premises, let us argue further. How will Lord Benedict convoke a council when he is standing in prison and despoiled, as is said? How will those who do not restore the obedience already withdrawn from them obey? How will he himself be heard in his own cause, as the law requires, if he is not released or given his liberty, at least for the council? Moreover, how will he be able to cast many out of the council, or ask that they be removed as his enemies, especially his own brothers, the Lord Cardinals? And whether he has a reasonable cause for this, consider what is to be presumed.

units.la: Secundo sic arguitur ex parte conuocandorum, quod si verum sit Proverbium, Vbi multitudo, ibi confusio, praecipue hic habet veritatem, quando non est vnio sub aliquo capite, neque sub eadem regula siue lege. Sed conuocandi de diuersis regnis, imo de eodem regno non conuenient in iudicio & opinione super eode capite, p rrale & omnimodo obedient.s, vt verisimiliter supponitur. Et hoc est, quia non conueniunt sub eadem regula siue lege, quæ est de subtractionis rationabilitate dicentibus aliis subtractionem benefactam & continuandam fore, aliis non sic, sed & malefacta fuit. Et si bene facta, tamen rebus immutatis nunc est mutanda, & ita murmur erit inter eos, & quis compescet illud? Denique nondum scimus an alii principes volent conuenire nobiscum, praesertim ad hoc tractandum si praesciuerint. Necesse tamen est vt praesciant, nec praesumendum est quin ante omnia hoc scire flagitent, dum proponetur eis istud concilium. Quod si ab eis veritas celetur & mendacijs seduci quærantur, quam indecorum hoc esset, imo periculosissimum & scandalosissimum nescit nemo. Quod dicatur eis nos velle tractare, an Benedictus sit verus Papa vel schismaticus, & quod certum putant, in dubium revocare, verisimilius est quod respondebunt se certos esse, nec velle hoc discutere, sicut obedientia partis intrusi nunc vsque respondet. Ecce igitur quam difficile sit vel impossibile conuocandos in vnam viam coniungere pro discussione negotii quod loquimur.
units.tr: Secondly, the argument is made on the side of those to be convoked. If the proverb "where there is a multitude, there is confusion" is true, it holds especially here, where there is no unity under one head and no single rule or law. But those to be convoked, from different kingdoms, or indeed from the same kingdom, will not agree in judgment and opinion on this same head, and will not be wholly obedient, as is probably supposed. This is because they do not share one rule or law: some say that the withdrawal of obedience was rightly done and must be continued, others say it was not so, but was wrongly done. And even if it was rightly done, yet with circumstances changed it must now be altered, and so there will be murmuring among them, and who will quell it? Finally, we do not yet know whether the other princes will want to meet with us, especially to treat this matter, if they have foreseen it. Yet it is necessary that they foresee it, and it must not be presumed that they will not first demand to know this when the council is proposed to them. But if the truth is hidden from them and they are sought to be seduced by lies, how unseemly this would be, indeed most dangerous and scandalous, no one fails to see. If it is said to them that we wish to treat whether Benedict is a true Pope or a schismatic, and to call into doubt what they think certain, it is more likely that they will answer that they are certain and do not wish to discuss it, just as the obedience of the intruding party has answered until now. Behold, then, how difficult, or rather impossible, it is to bring those to be convoked into one path for the discussion of the matter we are speaking of.

units.la: Tertio sic arguitur ex parte mediorum in tractando. Praesupponamus itaq; illud, quod non est verisimile, quod omnes vnanimi assensu de ista obedientia velint conuenire ad concilium, pertractando hanc materiam, etsi non solam, tamen praecipue & principaliter istam. Constat quod Benedictus & sui pro se audientur in sui defensione. Propterea videndum est ante omnia, si ea quae opponuntur contra ipsum vel opponentur sint talia quæ debeant facere fidem omnibus etiam sibi obedientibus & fauentibus, quia si non sint talia & taliter evidentia, non solum frustra, imo confusibiliter ea proponemus nos, qui subtractionis continuationem defendimus, & ponemus nos in periculo moti schismatis, & condemnationis opprobriosæ. Addito hoc, quod fauor & amor multum impediunt iudicia hominum & iustorum: licet hoc non credant vel videant. Cum ergo maior pars in concilio erit de eis qui subtractionem aut saltem subtractionis continuationem reprobent: non restat nisi vt condemnemur. Nec valet hoc dicere, quod Dominus non permittet errare concilium: quoniam in eis quæ sunt facti aut iuris positiui, & breuiter in omnibus aliis praeterquam in materiis quæ sunt pure de fide: ecclesia fallit & fa'litur seruata charitate. Patet cum compellit aliquem habitare cum non sua. Istæ vero propositiones: Subtractio fuit bene facta vel male facta: non sunt propositiones pure de fide: sed præsupponunt alias iniurias, quæ sunt pure de facto. Rursus ad idem si Benedictus accusetur de aliquibus, quis dubitat quin accusabit fratres suos & alios aduersarios, de pluribus & de forte maioribus & magis coloratis & fundatis, tam in materia fidei quam in materia schismatis. Exempli gratia: Accusabit Cardinales de rebellione ad eum & conspiratione & crimine machinationum dolosarum: aut de aliis criminibus, vt simonia & similibus. Item habet quaedam scripta aliquorum, in quibus sunt haereses manifestæ, dum credunt eundem impugnare, vt quod soli cardinales sint successores Apostolorum. Quod ecclesia tota non posset creare Papam, nisi per medium Cardinalium, nec vnquam potuit. Quod res expresse prohibita à Deo, si iuretur, debet seruari in reuerentiam iuramenti. Quod leptè occidens propriam filiam meruit. Quod Deus potest obligari. Item de aliis: Quod possunt esse plures summi pontifices. Quod decreta & decretales plus nocuerunt ecclesiæ quam profuerunt. Quod clauses datæ sunt vnitati, non vni. Quod omnis obediens vel procurans obedientiam ad ipsum Benedictum stantibus terminis, in quibus summus, est schismaticus: per consequens pertinax. Quod probabile est stante dubio probabili & notorio: de aliquibus contendentibus de Papatu dicere, quod alteri est obediendum: est error in fide & moribus. Nam cum casus præsentis schismatis sit in tali dubio probabili & notorio, si vnquam fuit vel erit tale dubium: omnes qui obedierunt vsque nunc vel obediunt vni parti vel alteri errant in fide & moribus. Item quod in eodem dubio quilibet contendens tenetur cedere iuri, si quod habet, & similia. Item quod à Papa licet appellare: & quod licite appellatum est in hac materia. Cuius tamen oppositum determinauit nuper totum Concilium Cardinalium, vt dicitur. Item forte accusabuntur multi de multis criminibus, tam in fide quam in moribus, quæ debent puniri morte: & merentur secundum leges & decreta perpetratores talium exhaeredari pro se & suis posteris: & ita videre facile est quod horrenda scissura fieret. Ita tamen debere fieri in contractando materias antedictas videtur verisimilius. Nam si Benedictus accusetur ad mortem & sui fautores: nonne credibile est attento suo quod alios similiter accusabit ad mortem si poterit. Praesertim si fautores aliquos habeat eorum, quos accusare voluerit inimicos odiosos: imo & forte accusabit praelatos regni de sententiis excommunicationis multis, & nominatim, quia consenserunt contra iura vt dicet, & contra ecclesiasticam libertatem, subsidia pro Dominis temporalibus absque causa manifestæ necessitatis &c. Praelati econtra volent se tueri. Volent etiam dare beneficia ad nutum, sicut modo, & hoc forte Benedictus non volet neque sui cardinales. Item forte retorquebit omnia contra praedecessorem suum Clementem & sui fautores, qui contra ipsum allegabuntur: saltem quo ad ipsa quae concernunt modos diversos machinandi pro impedimento vnionis, non dico quod iuste, sed nec etiam quod iniuste, parcat omnibus Deus.
