units.tr: But if anyone at last doubts likewise concerning the other princes, that they will not approve this middle way, we confess that this is not altogether certain, except in the sense that in moral matters certainty is to be taken from those things which for the most part happen according to probable and plausible conjectures. If in all respects the aforesaid way asks nothing difficult, burdensome or dishonourable, the question is why princes and prelates should disapprove it, especially in order to obtain so great a good as the reunion of this whole obedience. For what would be grievous about it? That all past matters be indulged and not investigated; that Lord Benedict have good counsellors, not suspect to any party, according to whose judgment he may act in what he is about to do; that he be immune from avenging his own or others' injuries and commit this to God, or else remit them for the universal good of the Church and of peace. We say the same concerning all subjects whatsoever towards Lord Benedict. Assuredly none of these things is difficult, except perhaps for those to whom humility, charity and ecclesiastical unity are burdensome, namely those who rejoice in disturbances and seek their own things, not those of Jesus Christ; or those who trust too much in their opinions with a cauterising animosity. Or if anyone contends that these things are difficult, let him, I beg, consider whether there are more difficulties and circuitous routes in other ways; or let him put forward some way free of all difficulty, and we will embrace it with glad minds. But if he will not do even this, or, as we rather believe, cannot, then since something must be done, let him go along with us in this opinion and consider which course holds more loss for the Church: either to remain as we are, indeed to fall daily into great lapses, and to see Lord Benedict imprisoned, the Cardinals stripped of their honours, and the princes disposed to dangerous contention; or to prepare ourselves, by this first and total reunion of this obedience, so that we may be able to treat other matters quickly and usefully. And how this may be done has already been answered in part, as (if anyone should ask) it will be inquired into more diligently by the wiser men and found more easily.

units.la: DECRETA IN SESSIONE PVBLICA CONCILII GENERALIS CONSTANTI- ENSIS, DIE SABBATI 9. OCTOBRIS, ANNO M. CCCC. XVII. ET primo Proœmium super futuris conciliis celebrandis: & provisione aduersus futura schismata.
units.tr: DECREES IN THE PUBLIC SESSION OF THE ECUMENICAL COUNCIL OF CONSTANCE, ON SATURDAY 9 OCTOBER, IN THE YEAR 1417. AND FIRST, a Preface concerning future councils to be held, and provision against future schisms.

units.la: Requens generalium conciliorum celebratio agri Dominici præcipua cultura est: quæ vepres, spinas & tribulos hæresum, errorum & schismatum extirpat, excessus corrigit, deformata reformat, & vineam Domini ad frugem vberrimæ fertilitatis adducit. Illorum vero neglectus præmissa disseminat atque fouet. Hæc præteritorum temporum recordatio, & præsentium consideratio ante oculos nostros ponunt. Ea propter hoc edicto perpetuo sancimus, decernimus atq; ordinamus: vt amodo generalia concilia celebrentur. Ita quod primum à fine huius concilii in quinquennium immediate sequens. Secundum vero à fine illius mediate sequentis concilii in septennium & deinceps in decennium perpetuo celebretur: in locis quæ summus pontifex per mensem ante finem cuiuslibet concilii approbante & consentiente concilio, vel in eius defectum ipsum concilium deputare & assignare tenebatur: vt sic per quandam continuationem semper aut concilium videat, aut per terminì prouidentiam expectetur. Quem terminum liceat summo pontifici de Fratrum suorum sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ Cardinalium consilio, ob emergentes forte casus abbreuiare: sed nullatenus prorogetur. Locum autem pro futuro concilio celebrando deputatum absq; euidenti necessitate non mutet: sed si forte casus aliquis occurrerit, quo necessarium videretur ipsum locum mutari: puto obsidionis, guerrarum, pestis, aut similis, tunc liceat summo pontifici de prædictorum Fratrum aut duarum partium ipsorum consensu atque subscriptione alium locum prius deputato loco viciniorem & aptum, sub eadem tamen natione, subrogare: nisi idem vel simile impedimentum per totam illam nationem vigeret: tunc ad aliquem alium locum viciniorem alterius nationis aptum huiusmodi concilium poterit conuocari: ad quem prælati & alii qui ad concilium solent conuocari, accedere tenentur, acsi à principio locus ille fuisset deputatus. Quam tamen loci mutationem vel termini breuiationem teneatur dictus summus pontifex legitime & semel per annum ante præfixum terminum publicare & intimare, vt ad ipsum concilium celebrandum prædicti possint statuto termino conuenire.
units.tr: The frequent celebration of general councils is the chief cultivation of the Lord's field. It uproots the brambles, thorns and thistles of heresies, errors and schisms, corrects excesses, reforms what has been deformed, and brings the Lord's vineyard to the fruit of the most abundant fertility. Neglect of councils, on the other hand, spreads and nourishes the aforesaid evils. The memory of past times and the consideration of the present set these things before our eyes. For this reason, by this perpetual edict, we decree, determine and ordain that general councils shall henceforth be held: the first in the five years immediately following the close of this council, the second, at the close of that next council, in seven years, and thereafter every ten years, in perpetuity. They shall be held in the places which the supreme pontiff is bound to appoint and assign, a month before the close of each council, with the approval and consent of the council, or, if it fails to do so, the council itself shall do so. In this way, by a certain continuity, a council shall always either be sitting or be awaited through the foresight of the set term. The supreme pontiff may, with the advice of his brothers, the cardinals of the holy Roman Church, shorten this term should chance events arise, but it shall never be extended. He shall not change the place appointed for a future council without clear necessity. But if some circumstance arises that seems to make a change of place necessary, such as a siege, war, plague or the like, then the supreme pontiff may, with the consent and signature of the said brothers or of two parts of them, substitute another place, nearer to the appointed one and suitable, but within the same nation. If the same or a similar hindrance prevails throughout that whole nation, the council may then be summoned to some other suitable place nearer in another nation, and the prelates and others who are customarily summoned to a council are bound to attend it just as if that place had been appointed from the beginning. The said supreme pontiff must, however, publish and announce such a change of place or shortening of the term lawfully and once a year before the fixed term, so that those concerned may assemble at the appointed time to hold the council.

units.la: Si vero quod absit, in futurum schisma oriri contingeret: ita quod duo vel plures pro summis pontificibus se gererent: à die quo ipsi duo vel plures insignia pontificatus publice assumpserint seu administrare coeperint: intelligatur ipso iure terminus concilii tunc forte vltra annum pendens ad annum proximum breuiatus: ad quos omnes prælati & cæteri qui ad concilium ire tenentur sub pœnis iuris & aliis per concilium imponendis absq; alia vocatione conueniant. Nec non imperator cæteriq; reges & principes plonaliter vel per solennes nuncios tanq; ad commune inducedu extinguendum: dum, per viscera misericordiæ Iesu Christi exnunc exorati concurrant. Et quilibet ipsorum pro Romano Pontifice se gerens infra mensem à die qua scientiam habere potuit alium vel alios assumpsisse papatus insignia vel in papatu administrasse, teneatur sub interminatione maledictionis æternæ & amissionis iuris, si quod forte sibi quæsitum esset à Papatu, quam ipso facto incurrat: & vltra hoc ad quaslibet dignitates actiue & passiue sit inhabilis: concilium ipsum ad terminum anni prædictum loco prius deputato celebrandum indicere & publicare, & per suas literas competitori vel competitoribus, ipsum vel ipsos provocando ad causam, vel cæteris prælatis ac principibus quantum in eo fuerit intimare: nec non termino præfixo sub pœnis prædictis ad locum concilii personaliter se transferre, nec inde discedere, donec per concilium causa schismatis plenarie fit finita. Hoc adiuncto, quod nullus eorum contendentium de papatu, in ipso concilio vt Papa præsideat. Quinimo vt tanto liberius & citius ecclesia vnico & indubitato pastore gaudeat, sint ipsi omnes de papatu contendentes, postquam ipsum concilium inceptum fuerit, auctoritate huius sanctæ synodi ipso iure ab omni administratione suspensi, nec eis aut eorum alteri, donec causa ipsa per concilium terminata fuerit, quomodolibet à quoquam sub pœna fautoriæ schismatis obediatur.
units.tr: But if, which God forbid, a schism should arise in the future, so that two or more men act as supreme pontiffs, then from the day on which those two or more publicly assume or begin to exercise the insignia of the pontificate, the term of the council, if it then lies more than a year ahead, is by law itself shortened to the next year. All prelates and others who are bound to attend the council shall assemble, without any further summons, under the penalties of law and such others as the council may impose. Likewise the emperor, the other kings and princes shall assemble, either in person or through solemn envoys, as a common means of extinguishing the schism, since they are now entreated, by the bowels of mercy of Jesus Christ, to come together. And any man who acts as Roman Pontiff shall, within a month from the day on which he could have known that another or others had assumed the insignia of the papacy or administered the papacy, be bound, under threat of eternal damnation and loss of any right he may have acquired to the papacy, which he incurs by that very fact, and, beyond this, be incapable of any dignity, active or passive, to summon and publish the council for the aforesaid year, at the place previously appointed, and to notify it by his letters to his rival or rivals, calling them to the cause, and to the other prelates and princes as far as in him lies. He must also, under the aforesaid penalties, personally betake himself to the place of the council by the fixed term and not depart from it until the schism has been fully ended by the council. This is added: that none of those contending for the papacy shall preside as Pope in the council itself. Indeed, so that the Church may rejoice all the more freely and quickly in one undoubted pastor, all those contending for the papacy, once the council has begun, shall by the authority of this holy synod be suspended by law itself from all administration, and no one shall in any way obey them, or either of them, under penalty of favouring the schism, until the cause has been ended by the council.

units.la: Quod si forte electionem Romani Pontificis per metum, qui caderet in constantem virum seu impressionem de cætero fieri contingat, ipsam nullius decernimus efficaciæ vel momenti, nec posse per sequentem consensum etiam metu prædicto cessante ratificari vel approbari. Non tamen liceat Cardinalibus ad aliam electionem procedere, nisi ille sic electus forte renunciet vel decedat, donec per generale concilium de electione illa fuerit iudicatum, & si procedant, nulla sit electio ipso iure. Sintque sic secundo eligentes & electus si se papatui ingessit, omni dignitate, honore & statu etiam cardinalatus & pontificali ipso iure priuati, inhabiles de cætero ad eandem, ac etiam ad papalem. Nec aliquis eidem secundo electo vt Papæ sub pœna fautoriæ schismatis obediat quoquo modo. Et eo casu concilium de electione Papæ prouideat illa vice. Sed liceat, imo & teneantur electores omnes, aut saltem maior pars ipsorum, quam cito sine periculo personarum possunt, etiam si periculum omnium bonorum immineret, se transferre ad locum tutum, & metum prædictum allegare coram notariis publicis & notabilibus personis in multitudine populi in loco insigni: ita tamen quod allegantes metum huiusmodi, habeant in ipsius metus allegatione exprimere speciem & qualitatem dicti metus, & iurare solenniter, quod metus taliter allegatus est verus: & quod credunt se ipsum posse probare, & quod per malitiam vel calumniam huiusmodi metum non proponunt. Nec vltra proximum futurum concilium vllo modo possit differre allegatio dicti metus. Teneantur insuper postquam se transtulerint & metum allegauerint, modo prædicto prouocare sic electum ad concilium: quod concilium si vltra annum pendeat à die prouocationis huiusmodi, intelligatur ad annum, vt supra ipso iure terminus breuiatus: & nihilominus teneatur electus ipse sub pœnis prædictis, & cardinales prouocantes sub pœna amissionis cardinalatus & omnium beneficiorum suorum, quam ipso facto incurrant, infra mensem à die prouocationis concilium ipsum, vt supra dicitur, indicere & publicare, & quam citius poterit intimare: cardinales ipsi cæteriq; electores ad locum concilii tempore conuenienti personaliter se transferre & vsq; ad finem causæ expectare. Teneantur quoq; prælati & cæteri, vt supra, ad conuocationem cardinalium tantum si forte sit electus conuocare, cessaret accedere. Quod etiam sic electus in concilio ipso non præsideat: quinimo sit à termino initiandi concilii ipso iure ab omni administratione papatus suspensus: nec sibi à quoquam sub pœna fautoriæ schismatis quomodolibet obediatur.
units.tr: But if it should happen in future that the election of a Roman Pontiff is made through fear, such as might fall upon a constant man, or through pressure, we decree that it is of no effect or validity, and that it cannot be ratified or approved by a later consent, even when the aforesaid fear has ceased. Yet the cardinals may not proceed to another election unless the man so elected happens to resign or die, until a general council has judged that election. If they do proceed, the election is void by law itself. The second electors and the elected man, if he has thrust himself upon the papacy, shall be deprived by law itself of every dignity, honour and status, including the cardinalate and pontifical office, and shall henceforth be incapable of that office, and of the papal office too. No one shall obey this second elected man as Pope in any way, under penalty of favouring the schism. In that case the council shall provide for the election of the Pope for that occasion. But all the electors, or at least the greater part of them, may, and indeed are bound to, transfer themselves as soon as they can without danger to their persons, even if danger to all goods threatens, to a safe place, and there, before public notaries and notable persons, in the presence of a crowd of people in a prominent place, to allege the aforesaid fear. Those who allege such fear must in their allegation state the kind and quality of the fear, and swear solemnly that the fear so alleged is true, that they believe they can prove it, and that they do not put it forward out of malice or calumny. Nor may the allegation of this fear be deferred in any way beyond the next council. Moreover, after they have transferred themselves and alleged the fear in the manner described, they are bound to summon the man so elected to the council. If the council is more than a year away from the day of this summons, the term shall, as above, be shortened by law to a year. Nevertheless the elected man himself is bound, under the aforesaid penalties, and the summoning cardinals, under penalty of loss of the cardinalate and of all their benefices, which they incur by that very fact, are bound within a month from the day of the summons to announce and publish the council, as stated above, and to notify it as quickly as they can. The cardinals and the other electors are to betake themselves in person to the place of the council at a suitable time and to await the end of the cause. The prelates and others are bound, as above, to attend only the summons of the cardinals, should the elected man happen to summon them and should they fail to attend. Likewise the man so elected shall not preside in the council itself. Indeed, from the beginning of the council he shall be suspended by law itself from all administration of the papacy, and no one shall in any way obey him under penalty of favouring the schism.

units.la: Quod si infra annum ante diem indicti concilii contingant supradicti casus: videlicet quod plures se gerant pro Papa: vel quod vnus per metum seu impressionem eligatur, censeatur ipso iure tam gerentes se pro Papa, quam electus per metum seu impressionem, & cardinales ad dictum concilium prouocati: teneanturq; in isto concilio comparere, personaliter causam exponere, & iudicium concilii expectare.
units.tr: But if the aforesaid cases occur within a year before the day appointed for the council, that is, if several men act as Pope, or if one is elected through fear or pressure, then both those acting as Pope and the man elected through fear or pressure, as well as the cardinals summoned to the said council, are judged by law itself to be summoned to that council. They shall be bound to appear at this council, to set out their cause in person, and to await the judgment of the council.

units.la: Quod si dictis casibus occurrentibus contingat forte casus aliquis quo necessarium sit locum concilii mutare vel obsidionis vel guerræ vel pestis vel similis: teneantur nihilominus tam omnes supradicti quam omnes prælati, cæteriq; qui ad concilium ire tenentur ad locum proximiorem, vt præmittitur, qui sit habilis ad concilium conuenire, possitq; maior pars prælatorum, qui infra mensem ad locum certum declinauerint illum sibi & aliis pro loco concilii deputare: ad quem cæteri conuenire teneantur, ac si à principio fuisset deputatus.
units.tr: But if, in those cases occurring, it happens that some case arises in which it is necessary to change the place of the council, whether because of siege, war, plague or something similar, then all the above-mentioned persons, as well as all prelates and the others who are bound to attend the council, are nevertheless bound to go to the nearest place, as is laid down above, which is suitable for the council to assemble; and if the greater part of the prelates have come within a month to a certain place, they may appoint it for themselves and others as the place of the council, and the rest are bound to assemble there, just as if it had been appointed from the beginning.

units.la: Concilium autem, vt præfertur, conuocatum & congregatum de huiusmodi schismatis causa cognoscens, & in contumaciam electorum seu gerentium se pro Papa vel cardinalium, si forte venire neglexerint, litem dirimat, causamq; diffiniat, ac culpabiles in schismate procurando seu nutriendo, vel in administrando aut obediendo vel administrantibus fauendo, seu contra interdictum superius eligendo, vel calumniosos in allegando metum, etiam vltra prædictas pœnas cuiuscunq; gradus, status seu præeminentiæ existant, ecclesiasticæ vel mundanæ sic puniat, vt vindictæ rigor transeat cæteris in exemplum.
units.tr: The council, convoked and gathered as stated above, shall take cognizance of the cause of this schism, and, in case the electors or those who style themselves Pope, or the cardinals, have neglected to come, shall settle the dispute and decide the cause; and it shall punish, whether ecclesiastically or civilly, those guilty of promoting or fostering the schism, or of administering or obeying in it, or of favouring those who administer, or of electing contrary to the prohibition stated above, or those who falsely allege fear, even beyond the penalties mentioned above, whatever their rank, status or pre-eminence may be, so that the severity of punishment may pass to others as an example.

units.la: Vt autem metus seu impressionis molestia in electione Papæ eo formidolosius euitetur, quo toti Christianitati lamentabilius eorum incussio seu factio perpetret vltra prædicta, specialiter duximus statuendum: quod si quis huiusmodi metum vel impressionem aut volentiam electoribus ipsis vel alicui eorum in electione Papæ intulerit seu fecerit aut fieri procuauerit, vel factum ratum habuerit: aut in hoc concilium dederit vel fauorem: facientemve scienter receptauerit vel defensauerit: sit: aut negligens in executione poenarum inferius memoratarum extiterit, cuiuscunq; status, gradus vel praeminentiae fuerit: etiam si imperiali, regali, pontificali, aut alia quavis Ecclesiastica aut seculari praefulgeat dignitate: illas poenas ipso facto incurrat, quae in constitutione Felicis recordationis Bonifacii Papae octavi, quae incipit, Felicis, continentur, illis effectualiter puniatur. Ciuitas vero etiam si quod absit vrbs Romana fuerit, vel alia quaevis vniuersitas, quae talia facienti consilium vel auxilium dederit aut fauorem: vel infra mensem saltem taliter delinquentem: prout tanti facinoris enormitas exegerit, & facultas ei affuerit, non duxerit puniendum: eo ipso subiaceat Ecclesiastico interdicto. Et nihilominus praeter dictam vrbem, pontificali & supra eo ipso sit priuata dignitate, non obstantibus priuilegiis quibuscunque.
units.tr: Moreover, so that the trouble of fear or undue pressure in the election of the Pope may be avoided all the more dreadfully, the more lamentable is the effect of their infliction or contrivance upon the whole of Christendom beyond the aforesaid penalties, we have especially decided to enact: that if anyone has inflicted or caused, or procured to be caused, such fear or pressure or violence upon the electors themselves or any of them in the election of the Pope, or has ratified the deed, or has given his favour to this council, or has knowingly received or defended one who does so, or has been negligent in carrying out the penalties mentioned below, whatever his status, rank or pre-eminence, even if he shines with imperial, royal, pontifical or any other ecclesiastical or secular dignity, he shall incur ipso facto the penalties contained in the constitution of Pope Boniface VIII of happy memory, which begins "Felicis", and shall be effectually punished by them. But a city, even if it be (which God forbid) the city of Rome, or any other community, which has given counsel, aid or favour to one so acting, or which, within a month at least, has not thought fit to punish such an offender in a manner befitting the enormity of so great a crime, and so far as its means allowed, shall by that very fact be subject to ecclesiastical interdict; and, besides the said city, it shall by that very fact be deprived of its pontifical and other dignity, notwithstanding any privileges whatever.

units.la: Volumus insuper quod in fine cuiuslibet concilii generalis hoc decretum publicetur solenniter, nec non quandocunq; & vbicunq; Romani Pontificis electio imminebit facienda, ante ingressum conclavis legatur, & publice intimetur.
units.tr: We further wish that at the close of every general council this decree be published solemnly, and also that, whenever and wherever the election of a Roman Pontiff is about to take place, it be read and publicly announced before the entry into the conclave.

units.la: SERMO EIVSDEM CANCELLARII FACTVS IN DIE CIRCVMCISIONIS DOMINI, CORAM PAPA APVD TARA- SCONAM.
units.tr: THE SERMON OF THE SAME CHANCELLOR, PREACHED ON THE DAY OF THE CIRCUMCISION OF THE LORD, BEFORE THE POPE AT TARASCON.

units.la: Apparuit gratia Dei & Saluatoris nostri omnibus hominibus, erudiens nos, vt abnegantes impietatem & seculária desideria, sobrie & iuste ac pie viuamus in hoc seculo: & reliqua quae nunc audiuit ex epistola Pauli vestra deuotio.
units.tr: The grace of God and our Saviour has appeared to all men, teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly desires, we should live soberly, righteously and godly in this world; and the rest, which your devotion has just heard from the epistle of Paul.

units.la: Quoniam apparuit gratia Dei & Saluatoris nostri, adeamus cum fiducia thronum gratiae eius, vt misericordiam eius consequamur, & gratiam auxilio opportuno. Nam quia finis noster super nos, & nos debilitati confractique iacemus in imo, & limo configimur: confundatur Pelagiana haeresis, quae gratiam Dei pro subleuatione necessaria abnegare praesumit.
units.tr: Since the grace of God and our Saviour has appeared, let us come with confidence to his throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy and find grace to help in time of need. For our end hangs over us, and we lie weakened and broken in the depths, stuck fast in the mire. Let the Pelagian heresy be confounded, which presumes to deny that the grace of God is needed for our raising up.

units.la: Rursus qui de gratia Dei sermo habendus est, & de nomine Iesu, quem nemo potest dicere nisi in Spiritu sancto, vt ipse Iesus secundum nomen suum sit nobis Iesus: vt praetemptos condemnatos in curia iustitiae, gratiae nos curia suscipiat, dum interim sedet in throno suae gratiae, priusquam legitimum tempus comparendi praeroreat, appellamus ad curiam & thronum gratiae: illic nos praesentemus in confessionibus, vbi soror nostra mater est eiusdem gratiae & aduocata nostra, quae plane despicere nos non poterit. Caro enim & sanguis noster est, & curiae suae iura defendet iura gratiae. Sed quis est iste thronus gratiae? Ille proculdubio pater hodie circumcisus, cuius vocatum est nomen Iesus, vt per Iesum gratia fieret, sicut lex per Moysen data est, vt saluaretur mundus per ipsum quem vidimus plenum gratia, imo gratiarum. Deus meus misericordia mea, inquit Propheta. Et quid misericordia, nisi gratia? Sed dicet hoc aliquis timidior: Ego apertos habens oculos cordis in lumine fidei & lucerna Euangelicae veritatis hodiernae: intueor in hoc puero seueritatem diuinae iustitiae seueram sed: quae etiam proprio Filio Dei non pepercit, quin eum nuditati & frigori & duro vulneri cum tenellus circumciditur, exponeret. Et tu mihi apud ipsum puerum inuenire thronum gratiae repromittis. Si in viridi hoc fecit Deus: si innocentissimo filio non pepercit, in quid fiet: peccatoribus seruis qualiter ignoscet? Quin etiam mater eius mater benedicta: oculis peccatores inspiciet, qui tota hodierni doloris sui causa sunt: qui totam suae granditatis anxietatis materiam praebuerunt, dum propter eos vnigenitum dilectissimum ex acri vulnere cruentum, ex nuditate & frigore vagientem cognoscit & dolentem? At vero quisquis hoc dixerit: sciat nil tale timendum: satisfactum est iustitiae, satiata est, non puniet bis in idipsum eam, qui gratiam huius pueri flagellati meruit: qui factus est a Deo nobis iustitia atque redemptio: in quo etsi iustitia appareat in eius attritione propter peccata nostra: supereminenter gratia Dei apparet gratia Dei: qui vt seruum redimeret, tradiderit filium quasi peccatorem puniendum.
units.tr: Again, we must speak of the grace of God and of the name of Jesus, which no one can say except in the Holy Spirit, so that Jesus himself, according to his name, may be Jesus to us. So that the court of grace may receive us, who have been condemned in advance in the court of justice, we appeal to the court and throne of grace while it sits upon the throne of its grace, before the lawful time of appearing arrives. There let us present ourselves in confessions, where our sister is the mother of that same grace and our advocate, who will certainly not be able to despise us. For she is our flesh and blood, and she will defend the rights of grace as the rights of her own court. But who is this throne of grace? Undoubtedly it is that child, circumcised today, whose name was called Jesus, so that grace might come through Jesus, just as the law was given through Moses, so that the world might be saved through him whom we have seen full of grace, or rather of graces. "My God, my mercy," says the prophet. And what is mercy but grace? But someone more timid will say: "I, with the eyes of my heart opened in the light of faith and the lamp of today's gospel truth, see in this child the severity of divine justice, severe yet: which did not spare even its own Son of God, but exposed him to nakedness, cold and a cruel wound, when he, still tender, was circumcised. And you promise me that in this same child I will find a throne of grace. If God did this to a green tree, if he did not spare the most innocent Son, what will he do? How will he forgive sinful servants?" Yet his mother, the blessed mother, will look upon sinners with her eyes, those who are the whole cause of her sorrow today, who have supplied the whole matter of her anxiety and distress, since she sees and grieves that her dearest only-begotten Son, bloodied by the sharp wound, crying out in nakedness and cold, is suffering because of them. But whoever says this should know that nothing of the kind is to be feared: satisfaction has been made to justice, it is satisfied, it will not punish twice for the same thing. It is grace that has earned the favour of this scourged child, who was made by God our righteousness and redemption. In him, although justice appears in his being crushed for our sins, yet the grace of God appears supremely as the grace of God, who, to redeem a servant, delivered up his son to be punished as though he were a sinner.

units.la: Sed & tu Virgo dignissima, non abhorre peccatores: sine quibus nunquam fores tali dignae filio: qui licet exigenitus est, attamen nobis natus, nobis datus. Adimus ergo cum fiducia te & filium tuum. In quibus talis apparuit gratia Dei, vt tu mater Dei fieres inueniendo gratiam apud Deum, & ipse homo filius Dei diceretur, ita vt non dubitauerit Augustus asserere nullam in rebus per tempus ortis maiorem ista esse gratia, dum verbum caro factum est. De quo verbo locuturus, der ipse nobis gratuita benignitate verbum efficax & fructuosum meritis & precibus tuis Virgo gloriosa, quae ab angelo vocata es gratia plena, antonomatice & diuina salutatione, quam repetimus dicentes: Ave &c.
units.tr: But you too, most worthy Virgin, do not shrink from sinners, for without them you would never have been worthy to be the mother of such a Son. Though he was begotten of the Father before all ages, yet he was born for us and given to us. We therefore approach you and your Son with confidence. In them such grace of God has appeared that you became the mother of God by finding grace before God, and he himself, a man, was called the Son of God; so that Augustus did not hesitate to affirm that among all things that have come into being in time there is none greater than this grace, when the Word was made flesh. Concerning this Word we are about to speak. May he himself, by his free kindness, make the Word effective and fruitful, through your merits and prayers, glorious Virgin, who were called by the angel full of grace, by the name above all names and by the divine salutation, which we repeat, saying: "Hail," etc.

units.la: Apparuit gratia Dei & Saluatoris nostri, & reliqua: Exhilaresce tu qui perieras, miserande homo, erige aures, audi & gratias age, quoniam apparuit gratia Dei, datum certe optimum & donum persectum: quoniam gratia Dei vita aeterna, & si Dominus dat gratiam, dabit & gloriam. Non igitur inuanum hanc Dei gratiam accipias: non per ingratitudinem in huius anni principio encenium tam insigne paruipendas. Et attendas vigilanter: quia non dixit Apostolus: Apparuit sapientia Dei, apparuit iustitia Dei, apparuit potentia. Illas quippe magis eximiescebat homo reus proditor & damnatus quam desserebat. Quoniam sapientia accusabat, & non habebat locum negatio, nec valebat excusatio Adam ... &c. Si voluerit mecum contendere (dicebat Iob afflictus) non potero respondere unum pro mille. Iustitia accusatum condemnabat, & non inueniebatur appellatio: quia audisti vocem uxoris tuae &c. Propterea idem Iob verebatur omnia opera sua, sciens quod non parceret delinquenti. Hinc quoque est Prophetica supplicatio: Non intres in iudicium cum seruo tuo Domine: quia non iustificabitur in conspectu tuo omnis viuens. Potentia denique accusatum & condemnatum puniebat, & non erat euasio: A facie manus tuae, (id est potentiae) ego defeci, plorabat Psalmista. Et rursus: Quis nouit potestatem irae tuae, & pra timore tuo iram tuam dinumerare? Et, nemo est qui de manu tua possit eruere. Non ergo quaerebamus sapientiam accusantem, non iustitiam condemnantem, non potentiam executioni sententiam demandantem atque saeuientem. Vbi saeuientem? Saeuientem nunc in coelo contra apostatas angelos, nunc in Paradyso contra parentes primos: nunc in turri Babel per confusionem linguarum, nunc in terra per diluuium aquarum multarum: nunc in Pentapoli peccatrice per subuersionem peruersorum, tandem in inferis per inclusionem omnium. Sed solam gratiam miserantem & absoluentem petebamus: qua salui effemus, non ex operibus iustitiae quae fecimus nos. Et haec hodie nobis apparuit, dum celauit Deus potentiam in infirmitate, sapientiam in infantia, iustitiam in pietate & circumcisionis satisfactione. Tanquam imposuerit Deus silentium eis, & dederit audientiam totam misericordiae. Ita superatis omnibus datur triumphus gratiae. Et haec apparuit hodie nobis valde necessaria. Nam quid ageret, quo se verteret homo condemnatus in curia iustitiae, si nemini datus esset locus appellationis ad curiam gratiae, si non superaret misericordia iudicium?
units.tr: The grace of God and our Saviour has appeared, and the rest. Rejoice, you who were lost, wretched man: lift up your ears, hear, and give thanks, since the grace of God has appeared, a truly excellent gift and a perfect present. For the grace of God is eternal life, and "if the Lord gives grace, he will also give glory." Therefore do not receive this grace of God in vain, nor by ingratitude make light of so remarkable a festival at the beginning of this year. And pay close attention: the Apostle did not say, "The wisdom of God has appeared, the justice of God has appeared, the power has appeared." For man, guilty, a traitor and condemned, would have dreaded those rather than desired them. For wisdom accused him, and denial had no place, nor could excuse avail: Adam ... etc. If he will contend with me (said Job in his affliction), I cannot answer him one in a thousand. Justice condemned the accused, and no appeal was found: because you have listened to the voice of your wife, etc. For this reason Job also feared all his works, knowing that God would not spare the offender. Hence also the prophetic entreaty: Do not enter into judgement with your servant, O Lord: for in your sight no one living shall be justified. Finally, power punished the accused and condemned, and there was no escape: From the face of your hand (that is, of power) I have fainted, the psalmist lamented. And again: Who knows the power of your anger, and can number your wrath for fear of you? And: there is no one who can deliver out of your hand. We were therefore not seeking wisdom to accuse, justice to condemn, or power to hand over sentence for execution and to rage. Where would it rage? Raging now in heaven against the apostate angels, now in Paradise against our first parents, now in the tower of Babel by the confusion of tongues, now on earth by the flood of many waters, now in the sinful Pentapolis by the overthrow of the wicked, and at last in the underworld by the confinement of all. But we sought only grace that pities and absolves, by which we might be saved, not by works of righteousness that we have done ourselves. And this has appeared to us today, when God hid his power in weakness, his wisdom in infancy, his justice in mercy and in the satisfaction of circumcision. As if God had imposed silence on those powers and granted a complete hearing to mercy. So, all being overcome, the triumph is given to grace. And this has appeared to us today as most necessary. For what would man condemned in the court of justice do, where would he turn, if no place of appeal to the court of grace were given to anyone, if mercy did not overcome judgement?

units.la: Dicamus iterum quod prius sempiterna Dei virtus atque diuinitas (teste Apostolo) ex eis quae facta sunt intellecta conspiciebatur: sicut antea dixerat sapiens, quod ex magnitudine speciei & creaturae potest visibiliter earum creator agnosci. Sed & sapientiam eius ex operibus agnouit, quae exclamans dixit: Quam magnificata sunt opera tua Domine: omnia in sapientia fecisti. Poterat quidem Dei beneuolentia vtcunque agnosci in rerum dignantissima conseruatione & directione in fines: sicut potentia ex creatione, & sapientia ex gubernatione videbatur. Quapropter forte gratiam appellat sapiens nutricem omnium. Sed ex reparatione lapsi, ex recreatione deperditi, ex iustificatione impii maxime apparuit gratia Dei. Nam quae gratia maior, quae liberalior vel dici vel existimari potuerat, quam vt tantum daret Deus homini, vt pauper fieret? quis hoc crederet, si non conscius secretorum Dei Paulus asseret: quia pro nobis egenus factus est, vt illius inopia diuites essemus? Gratia insuper qualis mirabilior, quam vt taliter compateretur homini misero Deus, quod miser fieret, opprobrium & abiectio plebis. Ista nonne sunt viscera misericordiae Dei nostri, in quibus visitauit nos oriens ex alto. In quibus apparuit gratia Dei & Saluatoris nostri hodie circumcisi.
units.tr: Let us say again what was said before: the eternal power and divinity of God (as the Apostle testifies) was seen, being understood through the things that have been made; just as the wise man had said earlier, that from the greatness and beauty of creatures the Creator can be known by sight. But he also recognised his wisdom from his works, crying out: How great are your works, O Lord: you have made all things in wisdom. Indeed, God's kindness could in some measure be recognised in the most gracious preservation of things and their direction to their ends, just as power appeared in creation and wisdom in governance. Therefore perhaps the wise man calls grace the nurse of all. But the grace of God appeared most of all in the restoration of the fallen, the recreation of the lost, and the justification of the ungodly. For what greater or more generous grace could be spoken of or imagined than that God should give so much to man that he himself would become poor? Who would believe this, if Paul, who knew the secrets of God, did not assert that for our sake he became poor, so that through his poverty we might become rich? Moreover, what grace could be more wonderful than that God should so take pity on wretched man as to become wretched himself, the reproach and abjection of the people? Are these not the bowels of mercy of our God, in which the dayspring from on high has visited us? In these the grace of God and our Saviour has appeared today, in his circumcision.

units.la: Amplius vero domina natura (vt humano more loquamur) quamuis in suo creaturarum speculo pulcherrimo, in libro capacissimo, in carmine sonoro & harmonico monstraret potentiam Dei efficientem, & sapientiam exemplantem, & bonitatem cunctaa finientem: primum ex vnitate: secundum ex veritate: tertium ex bonitate creaturarum. Rursus primum ex earum modo: secundum ex specie: tertium ex ordine. Similiter ex creaturarum mensura potentiam, ex eatum numero sapientiam ex pondere trahente in suos fines bonitatem, vt quodcirculo intelligibili ex ipso creante, & per ipsum exemplantem, & in ipso finiente sint omnia nihilominus mundus hanc sapientiam Dei potentiam & bonitatem cognoscere habens, non glorificauit Deum neque gratias egit: sed vilueranr sibi omnia, & obscuratum factum est insipiens cor eorum defecerunt scrutantes scrutinio. Quamobrem ordinauit Deus facere opus nouae gratiae supra ram, vt esset gratia domina regnaque naturae. Nam gratia eius & misericordia super omnia opera eius. Quae gratia licet superborum oculos sua luminosi rate caecauerit: illuminauerit mentes humilium, sicut exultans Iesus in spiritu: Confiteor, inquit, tibi pater caeli & terra, quoniam abscondisti haec sapientibus & prudentibus: & reuelasti ea paruulis. Ita pater, quoniam sic placitum est apud te. Placitum non meritum: vt non glorietur ante eum stulta praesumptio omniscarnis, quae in sapientia Deum non cognouit. Ideo placuit per stultitiam praedicationis nouae gratiae saluos facere credentes. Hoc autem opus gratiae apparuit manifeste in eo, quod verbum caro factum est: vbi totum opus gratia, totum sibi datur. Nil aut paucum habet natura, neque ex radice superiorum astrorum & constellationum, sicut impietas quotundam finxit. Neque ex actione inferioris elementorum, sed tamen quo ad modum, qui subiius fuit. Vbi praeterea patitur misericors & miserator Dominus, vt saluetur & regnet praeuaricator homo reus.
units.tr: Moreover, Lady Nature (to speak in human fashion) displayed God's efficient power, his exemplary wisdom and his goodness, which brings all things to their end, in her most beautiful mirror of creatures, in her most capacious book, and in her resonant and harmonious song. She showed his unity, his truth and the goodness of creatures; again, their mode, their species and their order; similarly, from the measure of creatures his power, from their number his wisdom, and from their weight his goodness drawing all things to their ends. Thus in an intelligible circle all things proceed from him who creates them, are formed through him, and are brought to their end in him. Nevertheless the world, though it had the means to know this wisdom, power and goodness of God, did not glorify God or give thanks to him, but became vain in its own thoughts, and their foolish heart was darkened; those who searched failed in their searching. Therefore God determined to work a new work of grace above nature, so that grace should be the mistress and queen of nature. For "his grace and mercy are over all his works." This grace, although its dazzling brightness blinds the eyes of the proud, enlightens the minds of the humble, as Jesus exulting in the Spirit said: "I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and prudent and revealed them to little ones. Yes, Father, for so it was pleasing in your sight." It was a matter of God's pleasure, not of merit, so that no foolish presumption of any flesh might glory before him, since in wisdom it did not know God. Therefore it pleased God through the foolishness of the preaching of the new grace to save those who believe. This work of grace appeared plainly in this, that "the Word was made flesh"; in which the whole work is grace and the whole is given to us. Nature contributes nothing, or little, neither from the influence of the higher stars and constellations, as the impiety of certain men has imagined, nor from the action of the lower elements; yet in the manner in which he was made subject, nature has its part. Here moreover the merciful and compassionate Lord permits a guilty transgressor man to be saved and to reign.

units.la: Apparuit ergo benignitas & humanitas Saluatoris nostri Dei, vt alibi gaudet Apostolus. Apparuit inquam mystice haec humanitas, vt signum magnum in coelo coelorum Deo. Nam sibi hypostatica vnione coniuncta est, & haec quasi mulier amicta sole iustitiae, quia plena gratiae luminosae, minosæ, & luna totius mutabilitatis naturæ sub pedibus eius, ratione auctoritatis imperiosæ, & corona stellarum duodecim, quæ sunt duodecim prærogatiuæ singulares in capite eius ex dominationis sublimitate. Nam & benigna humanitas Dei Saluatoris nostri vniuersum mundum spiritualium æternarumque creaturarum purgat, illuminat & perficit, superior eis in ordine hierarchico stabilita, ut sol quidam æternitatis. Imperium quoque possidet super vniuersum materiale atq; corporeum, vt ex miraculorum operatione monstratum est. Duodecim postremo prærogatiuis quasi totidem sideribus coronata refulget: quatuor in comparatione ad diuinitatem, totidem in comparatione animæ ad carnem, & rursus totidem in comparatione ad totam rerum vniuersitatem. Considera humanitatem huius pueri hodie circumcisi in ordine ad diuinitatem, & inuenies quod in ea tanquam in opere præclarissimo super aliud omne creatum relucent quatuor attributa: quæ sunt Dei potentia, Dei sapientia, Dei iustitia, & supereminenter Dei gratia: quæ circulo quodam spirituali infimum summo iungit, pacem operans in terris & in cœlo. Considera animam in ordine ad carnem, & inuenies carnem ab ea quadruplici dote decorari, agilitate, subtilitate, impassibilitate & claritate. Et quod in via non ita fiebat, hoc erat speciale dispensationis diuinæ miraculum. Deinde si consideraueris humanitatem huius pueri in ordine ad creaturam vniuersam, videbis eam tanquam instrumentum diuinitatis habere omnem potestatem in cœlo & in terra, in mari & in omnibus abyssis: beatos illuminat & perficit in cœlo: viatores iustificat in terra: alios non plene iustificatos dimittit hic vel alibi in mari purgationis. Alios obstinatos damnat & deturbat in abyssum damnationis.
units.tr: The kindness and humanity of our Saviour God therefore appeared, as the Apostle rejoices elsewhere. This humanity appeared, I say, mystically, as a great sign in heaven, a sign to God. For it is joined to him in hypostatic union, and it is like a woman clothed with the sun of righteousness, because it is full of luminous grace, and the moon of all mutable nature is under its feet by reason of its commanding authority, and it is crowned with a crown of twelve stars, which are its twelve singular prerogatives, from the height of its dominion. For the kindly humanity of our Saviour God cleanses, enlightens and perfects the whole world of spiritual and eternal creatures, being set above them in hierarchical order, as a kind of sun of eternity. It also possesses dominion over the whole material and corporeal world, as has been shown by the working of miracles. Finally, it shines crowned with twelve prerogatives, as with so many stars: four in relation to the divinity, as many in relation of the soul to the flesh, and again as many in relation to the whole universe of things. Consider the humanity of this child circumcised today in relation to the divinity, and you will find that in it, as in a most excellent work, shine forth above every other created thing four attributes: the power of God, the wisdom of God, the justice of God, and above all the grace of God; these by a certain spiritual circle join the lowest to the highest, working peace on earth and in heaven. Consider the soul in relation to the flesh, and you will find the flesh adorned by the soul with a fourfold gift: agility, subtlety, impassibility and clarity. And what did not happen thus on the way was a special miracle of the divine dispensation. Then, if you consider the humanity of this child in relation to the whole creation, you will see it, as the instrument of the divinity, having all power in heaven and on earth, in the sea and in all the abysses: it enlightens and perfects the blessed in heaven; it justifies the wayfarers on earth; it leaves others not fully justified here or elsewhere in the sea of purgation; it condemns and casts down the obstinate into the abyss of damnation.

units.la: At vero quia multus est hic sermo & ad interpretandum difficilis, & oratio nostra ad alios properans expediri desiderat: coartemus eam infra limites præsentis celebritatis, & duobus quasi gradibus itinere breuiato decurrat. Et dicamus quod apparuit gratia Domini primo in humili subiectione sua ad legem circumcisionis. Postquam impleti sunt dies octo ut circumcideretur puer, inquit Euangelista. Apparuit secundo in populi redemptione secundum nomen saluationis: vocatum est nomen eius Iesus: quod vocatum est ab angelo priusquam in utero conciperetur. Caussam reddit Angelus apud Matthæum: Quoniam saluum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum. Hoc modo Euangelium cum Epistola sociantes: vtrumq; per alterum deducamus sub duobus tantum gratiæ Dei signis: quæ sunt humanitas seu humilitas primum signum, & secundum benignitas seu charitas. Vnum in circumcisione; in nominatione alterum: vt verum sit quod apparuit humanitas in primo mysterio, benignitas in secundo, & gratia in vtroq; Dei Saluatoris nostri. Itaq; quis fidelium non perspicum habeat & compertum gratiam Dei hodie apparuisse, dum attendit quod ipse legis conditor durose legis vinculo quasi seruus astringit, & fit sub lege velut iufans, velut impotens & peccatis obnoxius. Ad quid ista? Nimirum vt ingratitudo nequam præsumptionis humanæ confunderetur & erudiretur: quæ in tantam prorupit audaciam, magis vero amentiam, vt diuinitatis maiestatem appeteret: volens esse sicut Deus, sciens bonum & malum: propterea Deus medicamentum contrarium humilitatis opposuit, descendens a summo suæ maiestatis ad ima vilissima nostræ humanitatis. Sic aduersus auaritiam primi hominis ipse summam libertatem. Sic aduersus gulam eius ipse summam frugalitatem. Sic aduersus ingratitudinem nimiam ipse gratiam ostendit infinitam: erudiens nos facto certissimo, vt abnegantes impietatem malam hospitem, & sodalem perfidiam, & secularia desideria quæ mergunt in interitum: sobrie, iuste & pie viuamus in hoc seculo. Sobrie quo ad nos. Iuste quo ad proximos. Pie quo ad Deum & sanctos. Humiliemus igitur animas nostras legi imitantes hunc puerum, & circumcidamus per disciplinæ cultrum vitiorum superfluitatem a nobis & sensibus nostris. Circumcidatur cor a præsumptionis præputio, ne plus sapiat quam oportet: nec prudentiæ propriæ innitatur. Circumcidatur ipsum ab omni carnalitatis excessu, vt sine sordibus & colluuie voluptatis sit purum & mundum. Circumcidantur oculi ne videant vanitatem: os & lingua, ne loquantur mendacium: aures ne audiant detractionem: tactus & gustus ab omni lubricitate: totum corpus a rebellione contra animam contumacia. Vt sobrie viuamus in nobismetipsis: viuamus & iuste apud proximos, reddentes vnicuique quod suum est: cui vectigal, vectigal, cui honorem, honorem. Viuamus tandem pie, Deo adhærentes per fidem & spem & per charitatem: circumcidentes omnem errorem & superstitionem per fidem, omnem desperationem & præsumptionem per spem, omne odium & cupiditatem in per charitatem. Sit in nobis fides vera & viua secundum vim & rationabilem ex recognitione immensæ sapientiæ: sit spes certa secundum vim irascibilem ex professione summæ eius potentiæ. Sit charitas feruida ex consideratione summæ beneuolentiæ & gratiæ: quæ apparuit hodie in circumcisionis humilitatione. Hoc modo sobrie intra nos, iuste iuxta nos, & pie supra nos viuemus in hoc seculo. Væ tibi pessima: væ tibi nequam ingratitudo cordis humani, cordis incircumcisi & certe inuitani, dum ad tantam gratiam notissimam Dei tui non corrigeris, non emolliris, non flecteris. Humilis est ipse, qui est Deus benedictus in secula, & tu ceruicem erigis, & tu superbis, terra & cinis. Tu sordida pellis inflaris & tenderis. Tu inquam inflaris & tenderis sordida pellis, saccus stercorum & vermium. Humilis est ipse legislator tuus obleruans legem tuam, & tu quotidie legis suæ iugum suaue & leue contumaciter excutis & confringis. Humilis postremo inuenitur pius erga te misericors & benignus, & tu plenus impietate errores fingis, & sequeris supersuperstitiones: de eo quoq; vel superbe praesumis vel desperas superbius. Ad ipsum deniq; nullo pietatis, nullo dilectionis affectu moueris. Pudebat fortassis inlequi humilem hominem: vsque quo pudebit humilem Christum imitari? Vide stupendum & horresce, flagellatur in circumcisione Leo de tribu Iuda, vt humilietur canis mortuus, filius hominis putredo & vermis. Circumciditur in carne puer Iesus, vt absq; praeputio nos in corde & sensibus maneamus: vt cum Abraham nos filium vnigenitum cum tota familia & vernaculis, hoc est spiritum nostrum cum affectionibus & cognitionibus vniuersis circumcidere disciplinae cultro nequaquam omittamus: sed tollamus opprobrium Aegypti, si neq; perire de populo, neq; foedus Dei irritum efficere voluerimus.
units.tr: But since this discourse is long and difficult to interpret, and since our speech, hastening to others, desires to be brief, let us confine it within the limits of the present festival, and let it run its course briefly, as by two steps. Let us say that the grace of the Lord appeared first in his humble submission to the law of circumcision. "When eight days were fulfilled that the child should be circumcised," says the Evangelist. Second, it appeared in the redemption of the people according to the name of salvation: "his name was called Jesus, which was named by the angel before he was conceived in the womb." The angel gives the reason in Matthew: "For he shall save his people from their sins." Joining the Gospel with the Epistle in this way, let us draw each through the other under just two signs of the grace of God: humanity or humility is the first sign, and kindness or charity the second. The one is in the circumcision, the other in the naming; so that it is true that humanity appeared in the first mystery, kindness in the second, and grace in both, of God our Saviour. Therefore, which of the faithful does not clearly perceive and know that the grace of God has appeared today, while he considers that the very author of the law is bound under the law like a servant, and becomes subject to the law like an infant, weak and liable to sins? To what end? Assuredly so that the wicked ingratitude of human presumption might be confounded and instructed, which has broken out into such audacity, or rather madness, as to aim at the majesty of the divinity, wishing to be like God, knowing good and evil. Therefore God set against it the contrary remedy of humility, descending from the height of his majesty to the lowest and most base depths of our humanity. So against the avarice of the first man he himself showed the highest liberty; so against his gluttony he himself showed the highest frugality; so against excessive ingratitude he himself showed infinite grace, teaching us by a most certain deed that, renouncing impiety, the evil guest, and the companion of faithlessness, and worldly desires which drown men in destruction, we should live soberly, justly and piously in this present age: soberly with regard to ourselves, justly with regard to our neighbours, piously with regard to God and the saints. Let us therefore humble our souls, imitating this child in the law, and let us circumcise by the knife of discipline the superfluity of vices from ourselves and from our senses. Let the heart be circumcised from the foreskin of presumption, that it may not be wiser than it ought to be, nor lean on its own prudence. Let it be circumcised from every excess of the flesh, that it may be pure and clean, without the filth and pollution of pleasure. Let the eyes be circumcised, that they may not see vanity; the mouth and tongue, that they may not speak falsehood; the ears, that they may not hear detraction; touch and taste from all wantonness; the whole body from rebellious obstinacy against the soul. So that we may live soberly within ourselves, and live justly among our neighbours, rendering to each what is his own: "tribute to whom tribute is due, honour to whom honour." Let us finally live piously, cleaving to God through faith, hope and charity, circumcising every error and superstition by faith, every despair and presumption by hope, every hatred and cupidity by charity. Let there be in us a true and living faith, according to the power of reason, from the recognition of immense wisdom; let there be a certain hope, according to the irascible power, from the profession of his supreme power; let there be a fervent charity from the consideration of his supreme goodwill and grace, which appeared today in the humility of the circumcision. In this way we shall live soberly within ourselves, justly beside ourselves, and piously above ourselves in this age. Woe to you, most wicked one! Woe to you, evil ingratitude of the human heart, uncircumcised and truly unwilling, while you are not corrected, not softened, not bent by so great and so well-known grace of your God! He is humble, who is God blessed for ever, and you raise your neck and you are proud, dust and ashes! You, a filthy skin, are puffed up and stretched out. You, I say, are puffed up and stretched out, a filthy skin, a sack of dung and worms. Your lawgiver is humble, observing your law, and you daily stubbornly shake off and break the sweet and light yoke of his law. Finally he is found humble, merciful and kind towards you, and you, full of impiety, invent errors and follow superstitions; of him too you presume either proudly or despair more proudly. Finally, you are moved by no affection of piety or love towards him. Perhaps it shames you to imitate a humble man; how long will it shame you to imitate humble Christ? See the wonder and tremble: in the circumcision the Lion of the tribe of Judah is scourged, that the dead dog may be humbled, the son of man, a rot and a worm. The child Jesus is circumcised in the flesh, so that we may remain without foreskin in heart and senses; so that, with Abraham, we should by no means omit to circumcise with the knife of discipline our only son with the whole household and servants, that is, our spirit with all its affections and all its knowledge; and let us take away the reproach of Egypt, if we are unwilling either to perish from the people or to make the covenant of God void.

units.la: Omnes quidem hoc agere conuenit, clerum praecipue: sicut ipse prae caeteris in Domini sortem electus est. Exultet igitur cum tremore humili, & gratias agat, & appareat in eo gratia Dei & Salvatoris nostri. Sed heu clerus hodie, quem pro maiori gratia gratiae vicissitudinem rependere dignum fuerat, plus aliis repletur ingratitudine, & praeputium sibi fecit impietatibus & secularibus desideriis: neque sobrie neque iuste neque pie viuens in hoc seculo. Ita pergebam in meditatione mea satyram in clerum declamare. Neq; enim in tam vberi indignationis materia deesse verba potuerant. Dum ecce studiositas speculatrix importunitate quadam sua grandem quaestionum speculatiuarum syluam apponere videbatur, vt plus sibi quam aedificationi deseruirem.
units.tr: Everyone ought to do this, and the clergy above all, since he himself has been chosen by lot of the Lord above the others. Let him therefore rejoice with humble trembling, give thanks, and let the grace of God and of our Saviour appear in him. But alas, the clergy today, who ought to repay the grace they have received with a greater return of grace, are filled with more ingratitude than others. They have made a foreskin for themselves through impieties and worldly desires, living neither soberly, nor justly, nor piously in this world. So I was going on in my meditation, declaiming a satire against the clergy, for in such an abundant matter of indignation words could not be lacking. Then, look, my inquisitive mind, with a kind of importunity, seemed to lay before me a great forest of speculative questions, so that I would serve myself more than edification.

units.la: Dic, inquit, si Christus circumcisus est, an circumcisus resurrexerit in gloria dispergentibus factus? Ita me pie tenere respondi ad honorem eorum, ex quibus Christus fuit secundum carnem: qui est Deus benedictus, & ad peruersorum confusionem.
units.tr: "Tell me," it said, "if Christ was circumcised, did he rise again in glory circumcised, or was he made one of those who scatter?" I answered piously, so as to honour those from whom Christ came according to the flesh, who is God blessed forever, and to confound the perverse.

units.la: Dic particulam illam carnis virginea, vt multi ferunt, dimisit in terris. Et talis de effuso tunc sanguine quaestio est? Respondi quasdam partes esse de integritate humanae naturae & necessitate, sine quibus non subsisteret. Quasdam de congruitate, sine quibus neque perfecte neque decenter existeret. Quasdam de superfluitate. Primae duae resumptae sunt, sicut in aliis resurgentibus fiet: no oportet hoc de reliquis. Si quis igitur contenderit, particulam illam cum sanguine fuisse de integritate humanitatis primo vel secundo modo, illa resumpta sunt: & vel in terra non manent, vel multiplicata sunt. Erat ne igitur pars illa carnis vel sanguinis per communicationem idiomatum Deus, & si Deus, vtrum homo? Huius responsionem, tanquam egentem longissima & subtilissima perscrutatione, praetero. Et consequenter illam, si sit adoranda adoratione latriae. Perge ad alia: quia melius est hic nihil; quam pauca dicere.
units.tr: "Tell me about that particle of flesh and blood which, as many report, he left on earth from the virgin's womb. Is such a question about the blood shed at that time?" I answered that some parts belong to the integrity and necessity of human nature, without which it would not subsist; some to fitness, without which it would neither exist perfectly nor becomingly; and some to superfluity. The first two were taken up again, as will happen in others who rise; the rest need not be. If anyone therefore contends that that particle with the blood belonged to the integrity of humanity in the first or second way, those parts were taken up again, and either do not remain on earth or have been multiplied. Was that part of the flesh or blood, then, God through the communication of properties, and if God, was it also man? I pass over its answer, as something that needs the most lengthy and subtle investigation. And consequently whether it is to be adored with the adoration of latria. Move on to other things, since it is better to say nothing here than to say little.

units.la: Dic ad quid proderat circumcisio? Respondeo: proderat originale peccatum delendo & dando gratiam: sed non aperiebat ianuam Paradysi. Dic quale dabatur pro foeminis remedium? Responsio, fides propria, si adultae erant, vel parentum pro paruulis. An alienigenas obligabat? Responsio, non. Cur ante diem octauam non impendebatur? Responsio, propter teneritudinem, & ad resurrectionis mysterium. Quid de filiis Israel in deserto non circumcisis? Pie teneo fuisse cum eis a Deo reuelante Moysi dispensatum. Dic si per cognationem spiritualem circumcidens circumcisio iungebatur? Puto cognationem hanc magis humana constitutione, quam naturali vel diuino iure inuentam. Quod si quis aliter sentiat propter gratiam quae confertur: dicat consequenter sicut de baptismo. Dic an circumcisus simulque baptizatus insignebatur duplici charactere & si in eo gratia duplex augebatur? Ita, si capax erat vtriusque: & dum circumcisio curebat vtiliter.
units.tr: "Tell me, what was the use of circumcision?" I answer: it was of use in blotting out original sin and in giving grace, but it did not open the gate of Paradise. "Tell me, what remedy was given for women?" The answer: their own faith, if they were adults, or that of their parents on behalf of infants. "Did it bind foreigners?" The answer: no. "Why was it not administered before the eighth day?" The answer: on account of the tenderness of the infant, and for the mystery of the resurrection. "What about the sons of Israel who were not circumcised in the wilderness?" I hold piously that God dispensed this with them through a revelation to Moses. "Tell me, if circumcision was joined by a spiritual kinship with the one circumcising?" I think that this kinship was established more by human ordinance than found by natural or divine right. But if anyone thinks otherwise because of the grace that is conferred, let him say the same consequently as about baptism. "Tell me, was the one circumcised and at the same time baptized marked with a double character, and was a double grace increased in him?" Yes, if he was capable of both; and while circumcision lasted, it was of use.

units.la: Dic cur circumcisio, quae data in foedus aeternum, cessauit: quid dico cessauit: imo facta est mortifera, adeo vt Paulus denunciet: Si circumcidimini, Christus nihil vobis prodest. Dico quod proprie non cessauit, sed transiit in baptismum, cuius erat figura: quid igitur mirandum, si re exhibita, figura cesserit? Sed auget quaestionis admirationem, cur propter conseruationem circumcisionis & aliarum legalium Paulus restitit Petro in facie: cum tamen ipse quoldam circumciderit. Igitur quo pacto reprehendit ipse quod agebat: & praesertim superiorem in auctoritate, apostolatu seniorem, in gratia confirmatum die Pentecostes: qualiter inculpat Paulus eum, & narrat non recte ambulasse ad veritatem Euangelii? Responsio: distinguenda sunt tempora, & concordabuntur scripturae. Tempus circumcisionis tripliciter cucurrit. Currebat primo vtiliter vsque ad baptismum. Secundo permissiue apud Iudaeos, vsque ad publicationem Euangelii pleniorem, vt mater synagoga honestas haberet exequias. Sed nunc apud gentes, & post apud omnes pestifera fuit eius obseruatio.
units.tr: "Tell me why circumcision, which was given as an everlasting covenant, has ceased. What am I saying, has ceased? Rather it has become deadly, so that Paul declares: 'If you are circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing.'" I say that it did not properly cease, but passed over into baptism, of which it was the figure. What is there to wonder at, then, if the figure has ceased when the thing itself has been revealed? But what increases the wonder of the question is why Paul resisted Peter to his face for the sake of keeping circumcision and other legal observances, when yet he himself circumcised certain people. How then did he rebuke what he himself was doing? And especially Peter, superior in authority, older in apostleship, confirmed in grace on the day of Pentecost; how does Paul blame him in this way, and say that he did not walk uprightly according to the truth of the Gospel? The answer: the times must be distinguished, and the Scriptures will agree. The time of circumcision ran in three phases. First it ran usefully until baptism. Second, it was permitted among the Jews, until the fuller publication of the Gospel, so that the mother synagogue might have an honourable funeral. But now among the Gentiles, and afterwards among all, its observance has been deadly.

units.la: Propterea Petrus & Paulus licite quosdam circumciderunt ex Iudaeis tempore illo medio. Sed quia facta Petri circa Iudaeos, gentiles scandalizabant, quasi sic deberent circumcidi: Paulus doctor gentium auertit Petrum de re huiusmodi, qui tota sibi humilitate paruit, & ita neuter peccauit, saltem mortaliter. Sed dic: si Petrus non errabat in fide, qualiter sibi dixit Paulus, cur ita facis? Certe ex auctoritate legis diuinae iubenris fraternam correctionem: cui legi nemo non subiectus est. Quid si Petrus versa vice Paulo restitisset in faciem nolens acquiescere: an Paulus se ab eo subtrahere, an non obedire, an ad Ecclesiae concilium appellare potuerat? Si concilium in hoc superius erat vel Petro, vel econtra? si Paulus restitit Petro, vt eius Cardinalis existens, vel vt aequalem se deputans, & nihil a Petro auctoritatis, sicut nec Euangelium suum recipiens? Quid si de facto in Paulum excommunicationis sententias promulgasset: an eas Paulus timuisset? Quid si Petrus perstitisset in hoc errore, nunquid eo facto Papatum perdiderat? quod si non: nunquid tamen deponendus erat, & per quos & quomodo? An concilium sine eo potuisset in hoc casu celebrari? Quid si Petrus vi armata errorem suum defendere voluisset, nunquid ipso etiam manente Papa vim vitare posset repellere, aut verbis aut carceribus, aut ipsa denique morte? Hieronymus praeterea & Augustinus doctores eximii cum discordent in hac materia, nunquid alter eorum dicendus est haereticus? Ille Paulum dispensatione mentitum, hic Petrum iuste reprehensum fuisse defendit.
units.tr: Therefore Peter and Paul lawfully circumcised certain Jews in that intermediate time. But because Peter's actions towards the Jews gave offence to the Gentiles, as though they ought to be circumcised in this way, Paul, the teacher of the Gentiles, turned Peter away from such a practice. Peter obeyed him with complete humility, and so neither sinned, at least not mortally. But tell me: if Peter was not erring in the faith, how did Paul say to him, "Why do you so?" Surely on the authority of the divine law, which enjoins fraternal correction, to which no one is not subject. What if, in turn, Peter had resisted Paul to his face, unwilling to yield? Could Paul have withdrawn from him, or refused to obey, or appealed to the council of the Church? If the council was superior in this matter, was it superior to Peter or the reverse? If Paul resisted Peter as being his cardinal, or as counting himself equal, and receiving nothing of authority from Peter, just as he did not receive his Gospel from him? What if Peter had in fact pronounced sentences of excommunication against Paul: would Paul have feared them? What if Peter had persisted in this error: had he by that fact lost the papacy? But if not, was he nonetheless to be deposed, and by whom and how? Could a council have been held in this case without him? What if Peter had wished to defend his error by armed force: even with the Pope still remaining, could he have warded off violence by repelling it with words, with prisons, or finally with death itself? Moreover, since Jerome and Augustine, outstanding teachers, disagree on this matter, is one of them to be called a heretic? The former defends that Paul lied by way of dispensation; the latter, that Peter was justly rebuked.

units.la: Porro cur in concilio de cessatione circumcisionis Petrus summus Pontifex non tulit sententiam, sed Iacobus. Innuebam studiositati ut taceret, & non poneret in cogitationem suum. Tunc exclamans dixit: Nunquid non expedit de talibus inquirere, ut sciat quilibet magnus cum pusillo qualitatem suae potentiae, suae subiectionis, sui cordis: quae sibi competit iure divino, naturali vel humano? alioquin error facile surreperet, & confusionis horrore cuncta foedarentur. Quid est igitur quod innuis mihi, quasi non liceat de potestate Petri disputare? Nonne de omnipotentia Dei quotidie perquirimus? Sed tamen vis ut ista nunc praeteream, revertamur ad puerum Iesum.
units.tr: Further, why in the council on the cessation of circumcision did Peter, the supreme Pontiff, not pronounce sentence, but James did? I gestured to my inquisitive mind to be silent and not to put its own opinion forward. Then, crying out, it said: "Is it not expedient to inquire about such things, so that every great man, along with the small, may know the quality of his power, of his subjection, and of his heart, which belongs to him by divine, natural or human right? Otherwise error would easily creep in, and everything would be befouled by the horror of confusion. What then is it that you are hinting at to me, as if it were not permitted to dispute about the power of Peter? Do we not every day inquire about the omnipotence of God? But since you wish me now to pass over these matters, let us return to the boy Jesus."

units.la: Dic si puerum istum circumcisionis dolor attigit, cum utique gaudio magno fuisset? Sic & forte tantus, quantus in passione tunc praesuisa. Dic si cor eius motibus oppositis dilatatione & constrictione simul movebatur? Responsio, non oportet: quia gaudium superioris portionis non redundabat in corpus. Dic si vere compatiebatur ei mater sua conscia tanti gaudii, tantique mysterii non ignara? Responsio, compatiebatur: & iam pertransibat gladius animam eius, ut non eximeretur ab illa regula: quod per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum Dei. Et hoc horrendum pro peccatoribus, quia aut hic erunt in labore hominum per poenitentiam, aut in societate daemonum per damnationem.
units.tr: "Tell me, if the pain of circumcision touched that boy, when surely it was full of great joy? And perhaps it was as great as the suffering that he then foresaw in the passion. Tell me, if his heart was moved at once by opposite movements, of dilation and constriction?" The answer: it need not be so, because the joy of the higher portion did not overflow into the body. "Tell me, did his mother truly suffer with him, being aware of so great a joy and not ignorant of so great a mystery?" The answer: she did suffer with him, and already the sword was passing through her soul, so that she was not exempt from that rule: through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of God. And this is dreadful for sinners, because they will either be here in the toil of men through repentance, or in the company of demons through damnation.

units.la: Caeterum dic, cur hoc potissimum die Christus circumcidi voluerit, cum superstitiones impiae in his Ianuarii Cal. plus vigebant? Responsio, ut eas deserendas ostenderet. Cur nondum cessaverunt neque in clero neque in populo, tam super encaeniis & aliis observationibus vanis & variis, quam super ritibus improbis per ecclesias, quos appellant ludos Fatuorum, sicut vere fatuitates sunt, imo insaniae sacrilegae, impiae & blasphemae, quas inter ecclesiasticos impune fieri stupor est? Nunquid apponi deberet provisio? Ita deberet: sed pluries audisti, quia quaestio per debet, solvitur per non facit. Prouideat gratia Dei Saluatoris nostri, & summi Pontificis diligentia.
units.tr: Moreover, tell me, why Christ wished to be circumcised on this particular day, when the impious superstitions were most in vigour on the Kalends of January? The answer: so as to show that they must be abandoned. Why have they not yet ceased, neither among the clergy nor among the people, both regarding the encaenia and other vain and various observances, and regarding the wicked rites in the churches, which they call the Feast of Fools, as they truly are foolishness, indeed sacrilegious, impious and blasphemous madness, which it is astonishing is done with impunity among churchmen? Ought provision to be made against it? It ought to be; but you have often heard that a question is resolved by "it ought," and not by "it does." Let the grace of God our Saviour and the diligence of the supreme Pontiff provide for it.

units.la: Quaestiones huiusmodi multiplicare magis & magis satagebat importune nimis studiositas speculatrix in meditatione mea. Cui ego: Noli precor mihi molesta esse, locum & tempus aliud expecta. Non est iste disputationis speculativae actus, sed aedificationis practicae. Tu interim secedas aliorsum, ut de gratia Dei & signis eius certo pergat itinere sermo noster, praesertim ad signum secundum, quod esse posuimus benignitatem salutricem, sicut notatur in nominis impositione. Si tamen prius ex eis, quae circa primum signum diximus, quod est humanitas seu humilitas, considerationem moralem quadruplicem notauero secundum quatuor affectus gratiae Dei: qui sunt abnegare impietatem & saecularia desideria. Sed & sobrie & iuste & pie viuere in hoc saeculo. Quanquam male suasa pestis adulatio perstrepat, & susurrans loqui prohibeat, asserens quod vetere proverbio, veritas odium parit. Et quod
units.tr: This overly eager inquirer, who kept pressing me during my meditation, was trying more and more to multiply questions of this kind. To her I said: Please do not trouble me; wait for another place and time. This is not an act of speculative disputation but of practical edification. In the meantime, withdraw elsewhere, so that our sermon may proceed on a sure course concerning the grace of God and its signs, especially the second sign, which we have said is saving kindness, as the naming indicates. If, however, I first set out a fourfold moral consideration drawn from what we said about the first sign, which is humanity or humility, according to the four effects of the grace of God, these are: to renounce impiety and worldly desires, and to live soberly, justly and piously in this present age. Although the pestilent flattery, ill-advised as it is, chatters on and, whispering, forbids me to speak, asserting by the old proverb that truth breeds hatred. And that

units.la: Non opus est teneras mordaci radere verbo
units.tr: There is no need to scrape tender ears with a biting word

units.la: Auriculas.
units.tr: Ears.

units.la: Sed plus roboris affert Apostolus in fine epistolae, stimulans quemlibet praedicatorem in persona Titi: Haec loquere & exhortare & argue cum omni imperio. Nemo te contemnat.
units.tr: But the Apostle brings greater strength at the end of his epistle, spurring every preacher in the person of Titus: Speak these things, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no one despise you.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO I.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION I.

units.la: A Dapparentem gratiam Dei in circumcisione humilis pueri Iesu, princeps & praelatus quilibet, etsi dicatur solutus legibus, pati debet legem, quam ipse tulerit, tum pro subditorum exemplo, & pro reverentia praestanda Deo, ut appareat gratia Dei in eo, & non impietas aut saecularia desideria videantur dominari. Poterant hic ut gentilium exemplis proprias in se leges, quamuis durissimas servantium: quorum Valerius meminit. Sed abunde satis est ad exemplum summus legislator Christus & Pontifex supremus: qui ob hoc legem propriam non soluere, sed in semet implere voluit, ut eius actio esset in hoc principum praelatorumque instructio. Vbi nihilominus notandum occurrit contra eos, qui tanta obstinatione legibus mortuis humanis adhaerent, legem viuam fundatam in lege aeterna & in aequitate, seu penitus vel ignorantes vel spernentes: quod lex perficitur & impletur, dum vel in finem meliorem, vel salubrioribus mediis ordinatur: qui finis est charitas secundum Apostolum: alioquin Christus legem antiquam non implesset, quam soluisset. Et hoc documentum non mediocriter spectat ad schisma praesens: cuius seditionem inuenire non sufficerent leges humanae iam conditae, nisi superior lex diuina viua & architectonica consulatur. Quod quia forte non satis actum est usque in praesens, obtigit quod ait Dominus in Esa. Timuerunt me mandato hominum & doctrinis. Ideo ecce ego addam, ut admirationem faciam populo huic miraculo grandi & stupendo. Peribit enim sapientia a sapientibus eius, & intellectus prudentium eius abscondetur. Ex quo loco sumpsit Iesus illud improperium contra Pharisaeos quod irritum faciebant mandatum Dei propter suas traditiones. Audirent utinam istaque auribus suis hi, qui legem euangelicam, legem diuinam cum professoribus suis deserentes, humanis inuentionibus incumbunt toti, adeo ut ad superiorem legem illam oculos attollere vel non valeant ex ruditate, vel nolint ex iniquitate, vel negligant ex inerti segnitie. Cum tamen vbi leges humanæ non sufficiunt (prout in schismate præsenti compertum videtur) vt ad legis diuinæ radicem & interpretationem consultatio referatur, & secundum eam constitutio formetur necesse est. Quid autem mali, quid periculi, quid confusionis attulerit contemptus sacræ Scripturæ vtique sufficientis pro regimine ecclesiæ (alioquin Christus fuisset legislator imperfectus) interrogetur experientia: consideretur clerus, cui desponsari debuerat sapientia, quæ desursum est pacifica & pudica, an ipse fornicatus est cum adultera illa meretricula sapientia terrena, animalis & diabolica? Status insuper ecclesiæ nonne factus est totus quasi brutalis & monstruosus? vbi cœlum deorsum, hoc est scilicet id quod spirituale est, & terra sursum spiritus seruiens & caro dominans: principale accessorium & accessorium principale, vsque ad hoc, vt quidam delirare non dubitent, quod per inuentiones humanas etiam melius quam per legem diuinam euangelicam regeneretur, quasi minus sit anima quam corpus, & spiritualis quam carnalis fructus. Hæc assertio per meam fidem blasphemia est, nedum falsa. Euangelica quippe doctrina per suos professores dilatauit ecclesiam vsque in cœlum, quam filii Agar exquirentes sapientiam, quæ de terra est, detruserunt vsque in cænum. Et quod non ex toto corruerit, est ex gratia Dei & Saluatoris nostri.
