Videas inquam acute, quam nihil sit omne, illud quod mundus affert gloriæ, iocunditatis, potentiæ, quam vana, quam lubrica & sepulto somniósque similliima: imo quam anxia & amaritudinibus respersa, tristissima sint omnia, ... omnes morimur, & quasi aqua fluentes dilabimur super terram: hodie rex, cras Papa moritur. Eheu fugaces, Posthume, labuntur anni: deflet Horatius & Tragicus: Properat cursu vita citato, volucrique die rota precipitis volvitur anni. Et Naso: Volat irreparabile tempus, & nihil est annis velocius. Et est omnium horribilissimum quod dicitur: quia in puncto ad inferna descendunt, & Ite maledicti in ignem aeternum. Caeterum quid quaeso usque est tam altum aut pretiosum, pro quo vel adipiscendo vel retinendo generosus animus & divinorum conscius, se perdere & alios turbare dignum ducat? Viderat hoc ex alto, qui tam sapienter exclamavit: Vanitas vanitatum & omnia vanitas. Quam sententiam si saperent, imo ut saperent, deberent omnes in potestatibus constituti secundum Chrysostomum consilium scriptum habere in ianuis suis, in penetralibus, in frontibus, & maxime in cordibus suis. Amplius si filii huius seculi tam avida sollicitudine curant peritura: adeo ut cum eis perire non formident, obsurdescentes ad illam increpationem propheticam: Filii hominum usquequo graui corde, &c. Filios igitur lucis, imo te patrem huiusmodi filiorum, quantam apponere decet curam, quot labores, quas vigilias, ubi de rebus aeternis agitur, ubi verum & vnice expauescendum pro animabus tractatur damnationis periculum? Non est ista lis de pauperr regno, ut apud Statium ponitur: neque de lana caprina, ut Satyricus ait, de vita & morte perpetuis res versatur, agitatus & quaeritur. Quod si pastoralis praesidentiae delectet aliquem honor volatilis & nomen inane, terreat eum districtum iudicis examen in reddenda de ouium salute & numero ratione. Agnoscat quoniam positus est non in destructionem, sed aedificationem, non ad otium, sed laborem: & ut per eum iuxta verbum maximi regis Artaxerxis seclusio abusu potentiae, subditi optata cunctis mortalibus pace perfruantur, quoniam hic est finis omnis potentatus tam secularis quam spiritualis.
units.tr: But so that you may be stirred all the more to act, often raise up the lofty light of your mind, lifting yourself above yourself. There, looking down on the earth beneath, look constantly and keenly before the eyes of your mind, in the light of faith, in the height of hope, in the breadth of charity, with him who says: I have considered the days of old, etc. You should clearly see, I say, how nothing is all that the world offers of glory, pleasure and power: how vain, how slippery, how like a dream of sleep; indeed how anxious and sprinkled with bitterness, how full of sadness are all things. We all die, and like water flowing away we slip over the earth: today a king, tomorrow a Pope dies. Alas, Posthumus, the fleeting years slip away: Horace laments it, and the tragic poet: Life hastens with swift course, and the wheel of the year rolls headlong on the flying day. And Naso: Time flies irretrievably, and nothing is swifter than the years. And the most dreadful thing of all is what is said: that in a moment they go down to hell, and Depart, you cursed, into everlasting fire. Moreover, what, I ask, is so lofty or precious that a noble mind, aware of divine things, would think it worth destroying itself and disturbing others to obtain or keep it? He who cried out so wisely from on high saw this: Vanity of vanities, all is vanity. If they were wise, or rather that they might become wise, all those set in power ought, according to the counsel of Chrysostom, to have that saying written on their doors, in their inner chambers, on their foreheads, and above all in their hearts. Furthermore, if the sons of this age care for perishable things with such eager anxiety that they do not fear to perish with them, and grow deaf to that prophetic rebuke: Sons of men, how long will you be heavy of heart? etc. How much care, then, should be given to the sons of light, and to you, father of such sons, how many labours and watches, when eternal things are at stake, when the danger of damnation is to be truly and solely dreaded for souls? This is not a dispute over a poor kingdom, as it is put in Statius; nor over goat's wool, as the satirist says. The matter concerns eternal life and death; it is debated and sought with urgency. But if the fleeting honour of pastoral presidency and its empty name delight anyone, let the strict examination of the Judge terrify him when he must render account of the salvation and the number of the sheep. Let him recognise that he has been placed not for destruction but for building up, not for leisure but for labour; and that through him, in the words of the greatest king Artaxerxes, with the abuse of power shut out, the subjects may enjoy the peace desired by all mortals, since this is the end of every power, as much secular as spiritual.

units.la: Sed ad te convertor, Pater sancte. Finge precor in ipsa sublimitate meditationis tuae sponsam ecclesiam talibus vtentem querulis plangoribus. Eheu quis consolabitur anxiam? & quis desolatae, quis plaga crudeli percussae medebitur? Inter has angustias, quae me circumuallarunt vndique, quale dabitur effugium? quis mei miserebitur? Ego illa sponsa regis aeterni, quam olim vidit vnus ex filiis meis nouam descendentem de coelo, quasi sponsam ornatam viro suo. Ego lota in sanguine agni immaculati, ego tot sudoribus & sanguinibus martyrum innumerabilium stabilita, violis confessorum, liliis virginum coronata. Ego tanta deuotione principum vsque ad inuidiam dotata, ornata, diues facta. Nunc heu velut misella & ancilla deiicior, despicior. Filios enutriui & exaltaui, ipsi autem spreuerunt me, & facti sunt hostes in capite. Pacem insuper iucundissimum in coelo & in terra bonum, qua me dotauerat sponsus meus nascens, praedicans, moriens, resurgens & regnans: conuerterunt in schisma perniciosissimum, quod iam quinque lustris me per omnes artus miseris modis depascitur & absumit. Pro mea olim defensione certamen erat vsque ad mortem, & modo nihil aliud agi vel quaeri videtur a multis, quam vt corruam, & miserabili labefactione deficiam, & hostibus meis ludibrium fiam. Ecce versa sunt omnia fere in contrarium prioris meae institutionis, disciplinae & decoris, ornata ornamenta: dum pro corona humilitatis puluis, foedus vanitatis, & pro croceis spiritualitatis stercora sola temporalitatis amplexantur, & erigitur super me sapientia animalis & terrena & diabolica, repudiata ea quae deorsum est pacifica & quieta. Si his tecum ecclesia planctibus loqueretur, P. B. noui miserationem animi tui, quae ab utero egressa est tecum, continere non posses, quin erumperent lachrymae ab oculis tuis, quin ad succurrendum inflammaretur totus zelus tuus iam succensus, & diceret ex intimo cordis suspirio: Domine super hac desolatione ante te omne desiderium meum, & gemitus meus a te non est absconditus. Succurre, fer opem, ut quid natus sum videre mala gentis meae? Rapidos rector comprime fluctus, & quo coelum regis immensum, firma stabiles foedere terras, & dispersiones Israel congrega.
units.tr: But I turn to you, holy Father. Imagine, I beg you, in the very height of your meditation, the spouse, the Church, using such plaintive laments. Alas, who will console the anxious one? And for the forsaken one, who will heal the wound struck by cruel blows? Amid these straits, which have surrounded me on every side, what escape will be given? Who will have pity on me? I am that bride of the eternal King, whom once one of my sons saw newly descending from heaven, like a bride adorned for her husband. I was washed in the blood of the spotless Lamb; I was established by the sweat and blood of countless martyrs, crowned with the violets of confessors and the lilies of virgins. I was endowed and enriched by the great devotion of princes, to the point of envy. Now, alas, like a poor little maidservant, I am cast down and despised. I nourished and exalted sons, but they have despised me and become enemies at my own head. Moreover, peace, the most delightful good in heaven and on earth, with which my bridegroom endowed me at my birth, in his preaching, his death, his resurrection and his reign, they have turned into the most pernicious schism, which for twenty-five years now has been devouring and consuming me in every limb, in wretched ways. Once there was a struggle to the death in my defence, and now, it seems, many do nothing else and seek nothing else than that I should fall, fail in miserable collapse, and become a laughing-stock to my enemies. Behold, almost everything is turned to the contrary of my former institution, discipline and beauty: my adorned ornaments are turned about. For the crown of humility they take dust, for the saffron of spirituality they embrace only the dung of worldliness, and animal, earthly and diabolical wisdom is raised up over me, while that which is from above, peaceable and quiet, is rejected. If the Church were to speak to you with these laments, Blessed Father (I know the compassion of your heart, which has been with you from the womb), you could not hold back. Tears would burst from your eyes, your whole zeal, already kindled, would be inflamed to help, and from the depths of your heart you would sigh: Lord, all my desire is before you in this desolation, and my groaning is not hidden from you. Help, bring aid: why was I born to see the evils of my people? Ruler, restrain the rushing waves, and you who by covenant firmly establish the immense heaven of the King and the lands, gather together the dispersed of Israel.

units.la: Sed quid ago? quorsum rapior? quid Mineruam (ut dicitur) impudens doceo? Praemeditata sunt namque apud tuam considerationem assidue & acriter talia salutis monita: nihilominus patere P. B. patere obsecro, commonefacere te & orare pro parte deuotissimae filiae tuae ut facias quod facis. Nam equum etiam sponte velocem calcar adiuuat. Fac ut calcata saeculi pompa & iniquis adulationibus eius, ut nullum retrahentibus uncis vitiosarum passionum, non ira, non odio, non spe, non gaudio fallacibus (melioribus namque hospitibus digna est sanctitas tua) abiecta rursus adulatorum peste, omnia ad gratiam, nihil ad veritatem loquentium & claudentium ianuam veritati, ac scrupulos varios (ut soli diligere videantur) ingerentium: de quorum vno dixit Comicus: Hic profecto ex stultis insanos facit. Et qui sunt stulti? vtrique vane gloriosi, prudentes in oculis suis, prudentiae suae innitentes.
units.tr: But what am I doing? Where am I being carried? Why do I, shamelessly, teach Minerva, as the saying goes? Such warnings for your salvation have indeed been constantly and earnestly weighed by you. Nevertheless, Most Blessed Father, I beg you to bear with me while I remind you and plead on behalf of your most devoted daughter that you do what you are already doing. For even a horse that is willing and swift is helped by the spur. Let your holiness trample down the pomp of the world and its wicked flatteries, and cast off the plague of flatterers, who hook us with the barbs of vicious passions: not anger, not hatred, not hope, not joy, which deceive. For your holiness is worthy of better guests. Let there be no speakers who say everything for favour and nothing for truth, who shut the door on truth, and who throw various scruples in your way, as if they alone seemed to love you. Of one of them the comic poet said: "Surely this man makes madmen out of fools." And who are the fools? Those who are vainly proud on both sides, wise in their own eyes, and relying on their own prudence.

units.la: His inquam procul pulsis, tu totus cum pacificis, qui non oderunt pacem, cogites ea quae ad pacem sunt Hierusalem: totus inuigiles implere id quod pro matre ecclesia petit a te filia vtriusque, velut altera columba Noe, ferens ramum paciferae oliuae per nos humiles nuncios clamitans pia sollicitudine: Benedic haereditati tuae: vt nobis contingat illud prophetae: Dominus benedicet populo suo in pace. Sed quomodo & quibus viis benedices populo tuo in pace? Si pergat aliquis particularius inquirere? iubet hic humilis & devota S. T. filia quiescere, ne suos patres, te videlicet & regem Franciae Christianissimum, aut legatos ab eodem praeuenire arrogantius videatur. Simul quia publicam & celebrem audientiam super hac pacis materia, si & dum tempus fuerit beneplaciti tui supplicat, & sperat obtinere, exhortatura latius & forte particularius, ut benedices ecclesiasticae haereditatis tuae. Et tantundem dictum sit de primo legationis nostrae articulo.
units.tr: With these, I say, driven far away, may you, together with the peacemakers who do not hate peace, think on the things that belong to the peace of Jerusalem. May you watch with all your care to fulfil what your daughter, the daughter of both of you, asks of you for her mother, the Church. Like a second dove of Noah, she sends us humble messengers bearing the olive branch of peace, and cries out with pious anxiety: Bless your inheritance, so that it may come to pass for us what the prophet says: The Lord will bless his people with peace. But how, and by what ways, will you bless your people in peace? If anyone should go on to inquire more particularly, this humble and devoted daughter of yours bids him be quiet, lest it seem too presumptuous to anticipate your fathers, namely yourself and the most Christian King of France, or the envoys sent by him. At the same time, she begs, and hopes to obtain, that when the time comes, if it pleases you, there may be a public and well-attended hearing on this matter of peace, at which she will speak more fully and perhaps more particularly, so that you may bless the inheritance of the Church. And let as much be said about the first article of our embassy.

units.la: Superest alter & postremus nostrae legationis articulus: cuius ideo longe breuior erit expeexpeditio quam prioris: quia licet necessarius existat, eum tamen neque tantæ dignitatis, neque paris difficultatis existimo. Hic supplicamus, vt benedicas hæreditati tuæ partiali, & quodammodo peculiari, segregando pluuiam voluntariam huic hæreditati tuæ. Et quoniam infirmata est præ tenuitate & multis incommodis, tu perfice eam, quam tua tuorumque prædecessorum dextera plantauit. Præueniisti nos, Pater beatissime, in benedictionibus dulcedinis, heri in osculo pacis, pridem in odore bonæ famæ mansuetudinis & liberalitatis tuæ, vt hanc à te benedictionem petere, hancque spe certa præsumere auderemus. Denique iam præuentos subsequeris, dum aures tuæ, scilicet benevolas, orationi nostræ præbet tua pastoralis sollicitudo, recogitans (vt arbitror) quoniam filia tua primogenita est studiorum; cuius primogenituræ ratione competit benedictio de rore cœli desuper, & de pinguedine terræ, hoc est in spiritualí & temporali prouisione.
units.tr: There remains the second and final article of our embassy. Its treatment will therefore be much shorter than that of the first, because although it is necessary, I do not think it is of equal dignity or equal difficulty. Here we beg you to bless your partial inheritance, and in a certain way its peculiar part, by separating a voluntary rain for this inheritance of yours. And since it has been weakened by its slenderness and many inconveniences, bring to completion what your right hand and that of your predecessors planted. You have gone before us, Most Blessed Father, with blessings of sweetness: yesterday with the kiss of peace, and before that with the fragrance of the good report of your gentleness and generosity. So we dare to ask this blessing from you, and to presume it with sure hope. Finally, you follow those already gone before, while your pastoral solicitude gives your kindly ears to our prayer, reflecting (as I think) that your firstborn daughter is the daughter of studies. By the right of her firstborn status, the blessing of the dew of heaven from above and of the fatness of the earth belongs to her, that is, in spiritual and temporal provision.

units.la: Rursus quia exemplo Axæ filiæ Caleph suspirat sedens super asinam, calcans scilicet omnem brutalitatem, petens benedictionem à te patre suo, vis eam à liberalitate paternitatis tuæ irriguum inferius & irriguum superius expectare? Dic igitur verbum Boos & Ruth: Benedicta es filia Domino, quicquid dixeris mihi hoc faciam tibi. Et ita fac, pater beatissime, vt sit ante te odor filiæ tuæ, sicut odor agri pleni cui benedixit Dominus. Et bene agER plenus est filia tua Parisiensi Vniuersitas, imo nihil errauero, si eam appellauero paradisum voluptatis, in quo est lignum scientiæ boni & mali, & fons scientiæ in quatuor facultatum flumina condiuisus, irrigans vniuersam superficiem terræ. Tu huius professor es, tu pastor & cultor, vt operaris & custodias illam tanquâ agriculturam viuam, vt Aristoteles loquitur in politi. Vbi sub mysterio nihil deest eorum, quæ egregius poeta Virgilius in Georgicis, & Palladius in de agricultura, de hæreditate agraria conscripserunt, distinguentes agrum quadruplicem, qualem figuraliter in hæreditate tua secundum quadruplicem facultatem reperimus. Vnus ager est apricus & florifer pro apibus, figurans sub quadam appropriatione facultatem Theologiæ. Alius est pascualis pro ouibus & domesticis animantibus, figurans facultatem decretorum. Alter frugifer pro hominum vita, figurans facultatem medicinæ. Quartus vitifer & pomifer in omnigenere suo, figurans typice artium facultatem.
units.tr: Again, since she sighs after the example of Achsah, the daughter of Caleb, sitting upon an ass, trampling indeed all brutishness, and asks a blessing from you, her father, do you wish her to await from your paternal generosity an irrigated lower field and an irrigated upper field? Speak, then, the word of Boaz and Ruth: Blessed are you, daughter, by the Lord; whatever you say to me, I will do for you. And so act, Most Blessed Father, that before you there may be the fragrance of your daughter, like the smell of a field full of which the Lord has blessed. And indeed your daughter, the Parisian University, acts well in being full. Nay, I would not be wrong if I called her the paradise of delight, in which is the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, and the fountain of knowledge, divided into the four rivers of the faculties, watering the whole surface of the earth. You are her professor; you are her shepherd and tiller, so that you may work and guard her as a living field, as Aristotle says in the Politics. There, in this mystery, nothing is lacking of what the excellent poet Virgil in the Georgics and Palladius in his book on agriculture have written about an agrarian inheritance, distinguishing a fourfold field. Such a field we find figuratively in your inheritance, according to its fourfold faculty. One field is sunny and flowery for bees, figuring, under a certain appropriation, the faculty of theology. Another is pasture for sheep and domestic animals, figuring the faculty of decrees. Another is fruitful for human life, figuring the faculty of medicine. The fourth bears vines and fruit of every kind, figuring typically the faculty of the arts.

units.la: Tuum est igitur hæreditatem tuam hanc benedicere, colere & augere, vt fructum suum det in tempore suo. Ecce ipsi Theologi velut apes intellectuales peruolitant in hæreditate tua, flores sacrorum eloquiorum de rore cœli roscidos compingunt mel in cellulas & fauos, vt sit cera in illuminationem intelligentiæ, & mel in oblectationem affectiuę. Hanc hæreditatis tuæ portionem spectans, dicere habes ex sententia illud Ecclesiastici: Hæreditas mea super mel & fauum. Nam eloquia Domini dulciora super mel & fauum. Et, præceptum Domini lucidum illuminans oculos, in intellectu. Venerat in mentem laudes huiusmodi tum augere, tum suo modo deducere, de reliquis hæreditatis tuæ partibus, hoc est facultatibus, quo magis animaretur sanctitas tua sibi benedicere: sed negligentius istud ago breuitati studens & sciens nihil laudum harum te latere. Dicam vero te concedente id, quod nuper meditatione mea, dum solus essem, & non solus, solus quidem corpore, non solus cogitatione versabatur. Itaque posita erat ante mentis oculos sedes tua præclarissima: & thronus sicut sol & luna perfecta, astitit regina illa virtutum dilectio à dextris tuis vestitu sapientiæ deaurato, circumdata varietate virtutum. Nam ita iussit rex optimus maximus Christus, vt sedem Papalem dilectio stabiliret, dum ait Petro interrogato ter, & ter respondente quod diligeret eum: pasce oues meas: pasce agnos meos. Quæ dilectio vna est in quadam trinitate virtutum, in misericordia & veritate, quæ custodiunt regem omnem duabus manibus hinc & inde portantes thronum eius, & in præclarissima virtutum iustitia, & neque Hesperus neque Lucifer ita admirabilis. Has sub compendio numerauit propheta reginas, eas paci consocians: Misericordia, inquit, & veritas obuiauerunt sibi, iustitia & pax osculatæ sunt. Quarum officium alibi descripsit: Propter veritatem (inquit de Christo, cuius vicarius es) mansuetudinem & iustitiam, & deducet te mirabiliter dextera tua.
units.tr: It is therefore yours to bless, cultivate and increase this inheritance of yours, so that it may give its fruit in its season. Behold, the theologians themselves, like intellectual bees, fly about in your inheritance, gathering the flowers of the sacred oracles, dewy with the dew of heaven, and building honey into cells and combs, so that there is wax for the illumination of understanding and honey for the delight of the affections. Looking to this portion of your inheritance, you may fittingly say that saying of Ecclesiasticus: My inheritance is above honey and the honeycomb. For the words of the Lord are sweeter than honey and the honeycomb. And the commandment of the Lord is bright, enlightening the eyes. It had come into my mind to increase and in my own way to set out such praises of the remaining parts of your inheritance, that is, of the faculties, so that your holiness might be more stirred to bless it. But I am doing this more carelessly, aiming at brevity and knowing that none of these praises is hidden from you. I will, however, with your permission, say what lately turned in my meditation while I was alone and not alone: alone indeed in body, but not alone in thought. So there was set before the eyes of my mind your most splendid seat, and the throne, like the sun and the perfect moon. There stood that queen of the virtues, love, at your right hand, clothed in the golden garment of wisdom and surrounded by a variety of virtues. For thus the best and greatest King, Christ, ordered that love should establish the Papal seat, when he said to Peter, who was asked three times and three times answered that he loved him: Feed my sheep; feed my lambs. This love is one in a certain trinity of virtues, in mercy and truth, which guard the king, carrying his throne on both sides with two hands, and in the most splendid justice of the virtues, than which neither Hesperus nor Lucifer is more admirable. The prophet numbered these queens briefly, joining them with peace: Mercy and truth have met each other; justice and peace have kissed. Of their office he wrote elsewhere: For the sake of truth, meekness and justice; and your right hand will lead you wonderfully.

units.la: Hæc præclara dilectio seu charitas vna in hac trinitate virtutum, sicut Apostolus insinuauit ad Cor. scribens: parabat orare pro filia tua Parisiensi Vniuersitate, vt ei modo quo diximus, benedicere tanquam hæreditati tuæ. Nam vbi adesset vel quando rogaret dilectio, si inter patrem deest & filiam. Nihilominus affuit & Sathan à sinistris, ita mihi monstrabat meditatio mea. Aderat & infelix proles sua, æmulatio liuida, per quam mors intrat in orbem terrarum, monstrum heu horrendum, informe, ingens. Cui quot insunt in dilectione virtutes, tot insunt vitia, crudelitas, falsitas, iniquitas. Crudelitas contra misericordiam, contra veritatem falsitas, & iniquitas contra iustitiam. Agnoui ex descriptione Nasonis quænam illa esset: Pallor in ore sedet, macies in corpore toto, Nusquam recta acies, liuent rubigine dentes, Pectora felle virent, lingua èst suffusa veneno, Risus abest, nisi quem visi fecere dolores. Nec fruitur somno, vigilantibus excita curis, &c. Obstupui visu subito gelidusque cucurrit. Ossa tremor ——
units.tr: This excellent love, or charity, one in this trinity of virtues, as the Apostle hinted when writing to the Corinthians, was preparing to pray for your daughter, the Parisian University, that in the way we have described she might be blessed as your inheritance. For where would love be, or when would it ask, if there were no father and daughter between them? Nevertheless, Satan too was present at the left hand, as my meditation showed me. There was also his unhappy offspring, livid emulation, through which death enters the world, a horrible, shapeless, huge monster. As there are virtues in love, so there are vices in it: cruelty, falsehood and iniquity. Cruelty is against mercy, falsehood against truth, and iniquity against justice. I recognised from Ovid's description what that thing was: Pallor sits in the face, leanness in the whole body; the gaze is never straight; the teeth are livid with rust; the breast is green with gall; the tongue is suffused with poison; laughter is absent, except what pains have made to show. Nor does she enjoy sleep, roused by anxious cares, etc. I was stunned at the sudden sight, and a cold shiver ran through my bones ——

units.la: Dum ecce terrifico boatu rabida ora laxans, & dentibus frendens: Eheus Pater sanctecaue benedixeris hæreditati huic tuæ: quæ facta est tibi sicut leo in sylua: odi propterea eam & maledic. Cane benedixeris ei in collatione gratiarum. Nam & tarde venerunt, & in multis à tua sententia defecerunt. Abiice eos positos à te, calcibus protere, & impera vt discedant maledicti.
units.tr: While, behold, with a terrifying roar, she opened her raging mouth and gnashed her teeth: "Alas, holy Father, bless this your inheritance, which has become to you like a lion in the forest; therefore I hate it and curse it. Bless it in the bestowal of graces. For they came late, and in many things they have fallen away from your judgment. Cast them off, set aside from you, trample them under foot, and command that these accursed ones depart."

units.la: Ita parabat portentum hoc horrificum magno conatu, contumeliosa nefandaque mendacia contra filiam tuam delatrare: dum tu Pater beatissime, hoc indignabunde ferens, toruum e latere vultum paulisper in hanc aemulationem impiam, mendacem & nequam visus es declinare, & vt confestim abscederet imperare. Abi hinc in malam horam & in crucem tuam pestis horrida, satrix discordiae, mater nequitiae. Vide ne vltra mutire vel apparere praesumpseris. Attende ne filiam criminari studueris apud patrem, cui etiam pro magno peccato satis esset modicum supplicii. Falleris si te recipi vel audiri existimas, vbi in conspectu meo parterna dilectio verax & iusta pro eis decreuit orationem assumere. Dic tu dilectio hac increpatione deterrita aemulatio tristis abscessit, & dilectio sic orsa est. Facis Pater sanctissime id quod te decet, te patrem erga filiam, & talem filiam: te vicarium illius qui accusatorem fratrum deturbauit in stagnum ignis ardentis, qui iussit Pontificem agere in spiritu lenitatis: quoniam & ipse circundatus est infirmitate, qui postremo propter decem iustos toti Pentapoli peccatrici pepercisset. Praeterea me dilectionem iussit assistere à dextris tuis: quae natura patiens sum, benigna sum, non aemulor, non ago perperam. Age igitur, pater beatissime, age quod agis, ne vlla te vnquam accusatrix aemulatio à meo consortio diuulserit. Non audiatur precor aduersum me crudelis haec & maligna aemulatio. Absit vt ponat hanc maculam in gloria tua spreuisse haereditatem tuam: abiecisse à te & pedibus tuis supplices tuos cultores quoque in vinea Domini Sabaoth: & coadiutores tuos vacuos absque vtili prouisione ingloriosque remisisse, vbi tanta est prouisionis tenuitas de bonis ecclesiasticis, vt vix pauci ex magistris & doctoribus etiam in Theologia, sine aliquo quaestu valeant habere alimenta & quibus tegantur, & hic septemdecim annus agitur. Haec est haereditas tua peculiaris & electa & praeclarissima studiorum, velit nolit aemulatio, vbi generatio praeterit & generatio aduenit, sed ipsa terra tua in aeternum stat. Tu supremus pastor & custos inopiae suae prouidere, irrigare arida, ruinosa reparare, non conquassare positum es, hoc misericordia petit titulo filiationis, hoc veritas titulo studii veritatis, hoc iustitia titulo militiae & laboris.
units.tr: So this monstrous thing prepared itself with great effort, barking out insulting and wicked lies against your daughter. But you, most blessed Father, bore it with indignation: you were seen to turn a grim look sideways for a moment from this impious, lying and worthless rivalry, and to command it to leave at once. "Go hence to an evil hour, and to your cross, you dreadful plague, sower of discord, mother of wickedness. See that you do not presume to mutter or appear any more. Take care that you do not try to slander the daughter before the father, to whom even for a great fault a small punishment would be enough. You are mistaken if you think you will be received or heard, when in my sight parental love, true and just, has decided to take up the case for them." At this rebuke the sad rivalry withdrew, and love began to speak: "You do, most holy Father, what befits you: you as a father towards a daughter such as this, and you as the vicar of him who threw the accuser of the brethren into the lake of burning fire, who bade the Pontiff act in a spirit of gentleness, since he himself is surrounded by weakness, and who at last, for the sake of ten righteous men, spared the whole sinful Pentapolis. Besides, love has bidden me stand at your right hand. I am patient by nature, I am kind, I do not envy, I do not act perversely. Come then, most blessed Father, do what you are doing, and let no accusing rivalry ever tear me from my fellowship with you. I pray that this cruel and malicious rivalry is not heard against me. Far be it that you should place this stain on your glory, that you despised your inheritance, cast off from you and at your feet your suppliant worshippers as well, in the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts, and sent away your co-workers empty, without useful provision and without honour, when the provision from ecclesiastical goods is so meagre that scarcely a few of the masters and teachers, even in theology, can have sustenance and clothing without some gain; and this has gone on now for seventeen years. This is your peculiar, chosen and most illustrious inheritance of studies, whether rivalry wills it or not, where one generation passes and another comes, but your land itself stands for ever. You, the supreme pastor and guardian, are set to provide for its poverty, to water what is dry, to repair what is ruined, not to shatter what is standing. Mercy asks this under the title of sonship, truth under the title of devotion to truth, and justice under the title of warfare and labour."

units.la: Porro tarditas huiusmodi postulationis benedictionis tuae per rotuli praesentationem nunc & non antea, non tarditatem meretur exauditionis, vt accusat aemulatio, sed celeritatem: quatenus sint nouissimi primi, quia bono intentionis fine fiebat dilatio, magno sicut arbitrantur zelo prosecutionis vnionis ecclesiasticae mouebantur, nec soli mouebantur, reges & regna cum suo clero pariter sentiebant.
units.tr: Moreover, the delay in such a petition for your blessing, made now and not before by presenting the roll, deserves not the slowness of an answer, as rivalry charges, but speed; so that the last may be first. The delay was made with a good purpose of intention, and, as they believe, they were moved by a great zeal for pursuing the union of the Church; nor were they alone moved: kings and kingdoms, with their clergy, felt the same.

units.la: Nunc post experimenta plurima quid inculpandum, si mutatis rebus mutauerunt sententiam. Esto rursus fuisset in aliquibus dissidens eorum sententia à tua. Nonne potuit hoc fieri sine mei laesione? quia sine obstinatione. Nonne Paulus & Barnabas tales viri sic contenderunt vt discederent ab inuicem? Et Paulus Petro restitit in facie. Et princeps Persarum bonus secundum Gregorium restitit Michaeli, & vtrobique illaesa me matre omnium charitate. Aduenit ecce supplex & humilis devota filia tua, P. B. absque vlla difficultate praecellentissima studiorum, & suo nunc aduentu dat palam intelligi, quod nulla diffidentia iuris tui & aduersarii falso fingebant, nulla indignatione peruersa suum differebat accessum ad petendum sibi benedici per praesentationem roruli more solito: qualiter nunc praesentat reuerenter in approbationem iustitiae tuae, & in egregiam laudem mansuetudinis tuae. Neque enim peteret benedictionem gratiarum ab eo, quem non crederet iuridicum largitorem: neque ab eo, quem benigno exaudito, rem non speraret. Vnde in capite rotuli ita scriptum est: Fiduciam accepit B. P. nunc rotulum istum supplicationum generalium & specialium, praesentandum apud S. V. celsitudinem humilis & devota I. S. V. filia Parrisiensis Vniuersitas, plus in paterna benevolentissima libertatis vestra gratia, quam in meritis propriis post Deum spem reponens, plus insuper studens ex hoc rotulo in- seruire commodis ecclesiae quam auara cupiditati, vt denique obedientiam sinceram ac filialem dicta filia erga S. V. sublimitatem non tantummodo verborum aut literarum assertione sed factorum soliditate monstraret. Haec ibi.
units.tr: Now, after very many trials, what is there to blame, if, with things changed, they changed their opinion? Suppose again that in some matters their opinion differed from yours: could this not happen without harm to me, since it was without obstinacy? Did not Paul and Barnabas, such men, so contend that they parted from one another? And Paul withstood Peter to his face. And the good prince of the Persians, according to Gregory, withstood Michael, and on both sides the charity of the mother of all remained unharmed. Behold, your devoted daughter, the University of Paris, most excellent in studies, comes as a suppliant and humble petitioner, without any difficulty; and by her present coming she makes it plain that no distrust of your right, such as the adversary falsely feigned, and no perverse indignation delayed her approach to ask for your blessing by presenting the roll in the usual way. She now presents it reverently, in acknowledgement of your justice and in fine praise of your gentleness. For she would not seek a blessing of grace from one whom she did not believe to be a just giver, nor would she hope for a thing from one who, when kind, would not hear her. Hence at the head of the roll it is written thus: The Blessed Father has received the confidence of this roll of general and special supplications, to be presented before your Holiness by your humble and devoted daughter, the University of Paris, placing its hope, after God, more in the most benevolent grace of your paternal freedom than in its own merits, and studying moreover to serve the advantages of the Church from this roll rather than to serve greedy cupidity; so that finally the said daughter might show her sincere and filial obedience towards the sublimity of your Holiness, not only by assertion of words or letters but by the solidity of deeds. So far there.

units.la: Hinc igitur Pater sancte per me dilectionem matrem omnium beneviuentium exoratus: perque virtutes meas inclytas misericordiam, veritatem & iustitiam, propter quas deducere habet te mirabiliter dextera tua, & si quid vnquam de te bene meruimus apud Deum, apud homines iustificando te, exaltando te, liberando te: & per spem futuri praemii si nobis persequeranter inhaeseris, oramus, petimus, obsecramus vt benedicas huic haereditati tuae, huic filiae tuae, alumnae nostrae, concedendo talem in gratiis suis signationem, aut certe vberiorem, qualem petunt & ab initio dedisses anno primo. Nam hic est annus benignitatis tuae, annus nouenarius, terpario te in se ducto coronatus. Benedices huic coronae anni, huic anno coronato benignitatis tuae, & campi tuae replebuntur vbertate.
units.tr: Therefore, Holy Father, entreated by me, love, the mother of all who live well, and through my illustrious virtues of mercy, truth and justice, for which your right hand is wont to lead you wonderfully, and if we have ever deserved anything well of you before God and before men, by justifying you, exalting you, freeing you, and by the hope of future reward if we have persevered in clinging to you, we pray, ask and beseech that you bless this your inheritance, this your daughter, our foster child, by granting in your graces such a sign, or certainly a fuller one, as they seek, and as you would have given from the beginning in the first year. For this is the year of your kindness, the nine-year period, crowned by a threefold leading of yourself into it. Bless this crown of the year, this year crowned with your kindness, and your fields will be filled with fruitfulness.

units.la: Hanc de te tuaque affluentissima libertate spem conceperunt, hanc conceptam multipliciter modum & magnis iudiciis roboratam auctamque senserunt etiam heri. Tu autem spem nunc in rem ipsam conuertito: tui quippe sunt, sed tu eos maiori tibi vinculo constrinxeris, tu postremo non mediocriter illustraueris gloriam tuam & famam tuam, quae sicut non est ambitiose quaerenda, ita non est negligenda crudeliter. Et vbinam gentium poterit famae celebritas vel scriptis vel viuis vocibus ampliori dilatatione vulgari, quam vbi confluunt & refluunt ex omni fere natione, quae sub ccelo est, viri literis omnibus & studiis eruditi, ita vt in obscuro esse nequeat, si grate, si benigne responderis, si benedixeris huic haereditati tuae, quemadmodum tu benedices, speramus & obsecramus: fiat fiat.
units.tr: This hope they conceived of you and of your most abundant liberality; this, once conceived, they felt, in many ways and strengthened and increased by great judgments, even yesterday. But now turn the hope into the thing itself: they are indeed yours, but you have bound them to you with a stronger chain; and finally you will not a little brighten your glory and your fame, which, as it is not to be sought ambitiously, so it is not to be cruelly neglected. And where among the nations could the renown of fame be spread more widely, by writings or by living voices, than where men learned in all letters and studies flow in and out from almost every nation under heaven? So that it cannot remain in obscurity, if you answer graciously and kindly, if you bless this your inheritance, as you will bless it, we hope and beseech. So be it, so be it.

units.la: Animaduertis, P. B. redeo enim & ad tuam sanctitatem & ad meam paruitatem, animaduertis qualiter transfiguraui sub nomine paternalis dilectionis supplicationem pro humili & devota S. T. filia, & id quidem aptissima videor fecisse ratione. Suam quippe sedem vbi collocaret dilectio, vbi peroraret, si inter patrem & filiam sacratissima dilectionis nomina apud ipsos etiam barbaros honoranda defuerit. At vero neque volo neque aequum iudico quicquam adiicere, quanquam aliqua dicenda supersint. Vereor enim ne iam multiloquium nostrum minus sit fauoris habiturum, dum occupationes tuae celsitudinis aliorsum te vocant & trahant. Quia postremo super isto & priore articulo audientias aliquas obtinere clam & palam supplicamus & speramus, vt non frustra spem hanc concepe- rimus de benignissima S. T. spiritum, pater sanctissime. Sic benedicat te Dominus ex Sion, vt sis re & nomine Benedictus. Sic videas bona Hierusalem militantis sponsae tuae, & triumphantis illius quae deorsum est mater nostra, omnibus diebus vitae nostrae praesentis & futurae. Sic praeterea videas filios filiorum tuorum in spirituali propagine, & tandem quod est omne bonum & benedictionis consummatio, & consummationis finis, videas pacem super Israel, & nos tecum hic inchoatiue per gratiam, & beato complemento per gloriam in futuro, praestante eo, qui est benedictus in secula seculorum, Amen.
units.tr: You notice, Blessed Father (for I return both to your Holiness and to my own littleness), you notice how I have transfigured under the name of paternal love the supplication for your humble and devoted daughter, and indeed I seem to have done this with the most fitting reason. For where should love place its seat, where should it plead, if among father and daughter the most sacred names of love, to be honoured even by barbarians, were lacking? Yet I neither wish nor think it right to add anything, although some things remain to be said. For I fear that our long speech may now have less favour, since your high occupations call and draw you elsewhere. Lastly, we beg and hope to obtain some hearings, privately and publicly, concerning this matter and the former article, so that we have not conceived this hope in vain from your most kindly spirit, most holy Father. May the Lord bless you out of Zion, so that you are blessed in deed and in name. May you see the good things of Jerusalem, your militant spouse, and of that triumphant one which is below, our mother, all the days of our life, present and future. May you see moreover the sons of your sons in spiritual posterity; and at last, which is all good and the completion of blessing and the end of completion, may you see peace upon Israel, and we with you here inchoately through grace, and in blessed fulfilment through glory in the future, he granting it who is blessed for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: PROPOSITIO FACTA AB EODEM DOMINO CAN- CELLARIO CORAM ANGLICIS, RARISIIS euntibus ad sacrum concilium Pisis, & hoc ex par- te Vniuersitatis Parisiensis,
units.tr: PROPOSITION MADE BY THE SAME LORD CHANCELLOR BEFORE THE ENGLISH, AS THEY PASSED THROUGH PARIS ON THEIR WAY TO THE HOLY COUNCIL AT PISA, AND THIS ON BEHALF OF THE UNIVERSITY OF PARIS,

units.la: ANNO DOMINI M. CCCC. VIII.
units.tr: IN THE YEAR OF THE LORD 1408.

units.la: Congratulatur vestrae deuotioni, vestro zelo feruenti, vestrae laboriosae, sed laudabilissimae legationi: Congratulatur & applaudit, o reuerendissimi & praeclarissimi Patres, o doctissimi & sapientes viri & fratres in Christi dilectione charissimi. Congratulatur inquam & congaudet amatrix & admiratrix & cultrix bonorum omnium Parisiensis Vniuersitas. Itaque non aemulatur nec gaudet super iniquitate, congaudet autem veritati. Quidni congaudeat igitur super veritate, quam vt soletis amplectimini, & complexam retinetis, & retentam ad effectum deducere totis studiorum neruis conamini. Est autem modo congratulationis nostrae spiritualis thema satis accommodum verbum Ozeae propheticum Ozeae 1. Congregabuntur filii Israel & filii Iuda pariter. Itaque libet exclamare: Ecce quam bonum & quam iucundum habitare fratres in vnum, conuenire sed & congregare ad concilium. Nam in concilio fratrum & congregatione magna opera Domini. Et hoc est concilium sacrum & venerandum, ad quod legati pergitis, quod Pisis Deo duce & authore celebrabitur: vtinam felici (prout optandum & sperandum est) aduentu. Ait quippe veritas, quod omne regnum in se diuisum desolabitur, & econtrario vnitum in se regnum manet. Quod vidit Salustius: Concordia, inquit, parua res crescunt, discordia maxima dilabuntur. Cur ergo non bene sperabitur, dum adunatur ecclesia, dum conuocatur coetus, dum conueniunt seniores? Videte de verbo hoc, praesertim cum teneamus certissimam Christi promissionem dicentis: Vbi duo vel tres, &c. Audiuimus praeterea laetanter & gaudenter, quod congregabuntur, &c.
units.tr: I congratulate your devotion, your fervent zeal, and your laborious but most praiseworthy embassy. I congratulate and applaud you, most reverend and most distinguished Fathers, most learned and wise men, and brothers most dear in the love of Christ. I say, I congratulate, and the University of Paris, lover, admirer and cultivator of all that is good, rejoices with you. It does not envy or rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth. Why, then, should it not rejoice in the truth, which you embrace as is your custom, hold fast once embraced, and strive with all the sinews of your study to bring to effect? The theme for our spiritual congratulation is fittingly taken from the prophetic word of Hosea, Hos. 1: The children of Israel and the children of Judah shall be gathered together. So let us cry out: Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity, to meet and also to gather in council. For in the council of the brethren and the great assembly are the works of the Lord. This is the holy and venerable council to which you, the envoys, are journeying, and which will be held at Pisa, God leading and authoring it; would that its arrival be happy, as is to be wished and hoped. Truth itself says that every kingdom divided against itself shall be laid waste, and on the contrary a kingdom united in itself endures. Sallust saw this: By concord, he says, small things grow; by discord, the greatest things fall apart. Why, then, should we not hope well, while the Church is gathered, while the assembly is summoned, while the elders come together? Consider this word, especially since we hold the most certain promise of Christ, who says: Where two or three, etc. Moreover, we have heard with joy and gladness that they shall be gathered, etc.

units.la: At vero ne prolixior vel euagatior sermo taedio sit vel oneri, coartemus si placet totam dicendorum materiam, rotamque deductionem thematis ad quatuor sententias sumptas ex themate, ex verbis ipsi protinus appositas, & videamus quid in illis loquitur Deus, quia loquetur pacem in plebem suam. Postquam enim dixit Dominus per Ozeae: Congregabuntur filii Israel & filii Iuda pariter pro prima sententia, mox subiunxit, & ponent sibi caput vnum, ecce secundam sententiam. Et ascendent de terra, ecce tertiam, quia magnus dies Israel, ecce quartam. Incipientes ergo prosequamur, & inuenimus puto causas quatuor sufficientes, quare congregabuntur filii Israel & filii Iuda pariter. Ipsi enim qui sunt populus vnus Dei: foeda nunc diuisione proh nefas dispersi sunt, velut olim in figura sub Roboath & Hieroboam contigisse meminit Scriptura tert. Regum decim. sept. Et est tanquam materialis aliqua ratio, & confusa huiusmodi concilii celebrandi. Inuenimus praeterea causam finalem luculenter expressam in altera sententia. Et ponent, inquit, sibimet caput vnum. Denique tangitur causa dispositiua, & velut efficiens celebrationis huius concilii, dum dicitur in altera sententia, quod quòd ascendent de terra, & quid terra mystice, nisi terrenus affectus? Quid igitur ascendere de terra, nisi de terrenis affectibus, quibus oppressi sunt hactenus multi, ad spirituales & divinas affectiones se potenter erigere, & erigendo salubriter ascendere, tanquam audiret quisque de excelso clamantem Deum: Exurge qui dormis. Et rursus: Surgite postquam sederitis.
units.tr: But so that a longer or more rambling discourse may not become tedious or burdensome, let us, if you please, confine the whole matter to be discussed, and the unfolding of the theme, to four sentences taken from the theme, placed immediately beside its words, and let us see what God says in them, since he will speak peace to his people. For after the Lord had said through Hosea, The children of Israel and the children of Judah shall be gathered together, as the first sentence, he immediately added, and they shall set themselves one head, behold the second sentence. And they shall come up out of the land, behold the third, for great is the day of Israel, behold the fourth. Beginning, then, let us proceed, and I think we find four sufficient causes why the children of Israel and the children of Judah shall be gathered together. For they who are the one people of God have been scattered by a shameful division, alas, as Scripture recalls once happened in figure under Rehoboam and Jeroboam, 3 Kings 12 (in the Vulgate, 3 Kings 12 and following). This is something like the material and, as it were, confused reason for celebrating such a council. Further, we find the final cause clearly expressed in the second sentence: and they shall set themselves, he says, one head. Lastly, the disposing cause, and as it were the efficient cause, of the celebration of this council is touched upon in the second sentence, where it is said they shall come up out of the land. And what is the land mystically, if not earthly affection? What, then, is it to come up out of the land, except out of earthly affections, by which many have hitherto been oppressed, to raise themselves powerfully to spiritual and divine affections, and by rising to ascend healthfully, as if each one heard God crying from on high: Awake, you who sleep. And again: Arise after you have sat down.

units.la: Habemus praeterea causam quodammodo formalem, & ad huius celebrationem concilii vivifice praeparantem; quae forma est semen Dei viuum & efficax semen Spiritus sancti, habens virtutem formatiuam & reformatiuam totius vnitatis, totius ecclesiae corporis, in vna fide & spe & charitate sub vno Deo & Domino per omnem iunauram, secundum deductionem Apostoli ad Ephes. quart. Quod notatur in hoc verbo Israel, quod interpretatum sonat idem quod semen Dei vel semmit Deus. Er quale semen istud? Plane illud de quo alibi propheticus sermo dicit: Nisi Dominus exercituum reliquisset nobis semen, quasi Sodoma fuissemus, & quasi Gomorra similes essemus: Esai. prim. Gratiasti. bi Deus Israel, quoniam accessit nunc dies magnus Israel, magnus scilicet dies seminis Dei, quod habet in se artem & virtutem viuificam, qua mysticum corpus ecclesiae se viuificare potest & vnire salubriter, in cuius efficacia & virtute congregabuntur filii Israel & Iuda pariter. Bene haec iactafunt fundamenta, sicut ex Cicerone sumit Lactantius. Haec autem fundamenta sunt perfectibilitas ecclesiae per congregationem, vt causa materialis, ordinabilitas ecclesiae vt ad vnius capitis positionem, vt causa finalis: intelligibilitas in aequitate amanda, seu interpretando, vt efficiens, insita foecunditas in se conuersando, vt formalis dispositiua.
units.tr: Moreover, we have a cause that is in a way formal, and which prepares life-givingly for the celebration of this council. This form is the living seed of God and the effective seed of the Holy Spirit, having the forming and reforming power of the whole unity and of the whole body of the Church, in one faith, hope and charity, under one God and Lord, through every joint, according to the teaching of the Apostle, Eph. 4. This is noted in the word Israel, which, interpreted, means the same as the seed of God or God sows. And what kind of seed is it? Plainly that of which the prophetic word speaks elsewhere: Unless the Lord of hosts had left us a seed, we would have been like Sodom, and like Gomorrah we would have been made, Isa. 1. Thanks be to you, God of Israel, since now the great day of Israel has come, the great day, that is, of the seed of God, which has in itself an art and a life-giving power, by which the mystical body of the Church can quicken itself and unite itself healthfully, and in whose efficacy and power the children of Israel and of Judah shall be gathered together. These foundations have been well laid, as Lactantius takes them from Cicero. And these foundations are: the perfectibility of the Church through the gathering, as the material cause; the orderability of the Church toward the setting of one head, as the final cause; intelligibility, in loving equity, or in interpreting, as the efficient cause; and the inherent fruitfulness, in turning itself toward itself, as the formal disposing cause.

units.la: Superaedificemus fabricam quadrangularem quatuor considerationum principalium, ad erectionem aedificii praesentis congregationis ampliorem: Et dicamus pro prima consideratione iuxta primam causam in verbo notatam.
units.tr: Let us build up a fourfold structure of four principal considerations, to raise a larger edifice of the present assembly; and let us speak, for the first consideration, according to the first cause noted in the word.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO I.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO I.

units.la: CONgregatio filiorum Israel & Iuda pariter quaeritur ab ecclesia, quemadmodum materia quaerit formam, & imperfectum perfectionem, & mulier virum siue sponsa sponsum. Tractat diuinus Dionysius, & post eum Boetius & Augustinus, quibus experientia suffragatur, quod res quaelibet non minus diligit aut appetit congregationem sui ipsius, quam propriam entitatem, nimirum quia ens & vnum conuertuntur: Hinc est ille dolor, illa concussio, ille vehemens horror in corpore vero, dum membratim quaeritur diuidi vel dispergi. Sic nemo dubitauerit, quin ecclesia diuisionem suam refugiat & horreat, cum sit corpus mysticum, secundum deductionem Apostoli ad Ephes. 4. & 1. Corinth. 12. & ad Roman. 12. & alibi saepissime. Est etiam terribilis vt castrorum acies ordinata. Acies vero quis nesciat separationem maximum afferre detrimentum. Est insuper ecclesia ciuitas, de qua gloriosa dicta sunt, est regnum Dei, est Hierarchia subcoelestis, & ita de multis similitudinibus, secundum quas conuincitur diuisionem et atque separationem schismaticam esse penitus odiosam. Potuerat hoc loco fieri sermo prolixior, deducens perfectionem ecclesiastici corporis stare principaliter in vnitate tanquam in consummatione omnis boni. Fallor itaque si non optabundus propheta postulat hoc, imprecans pacem super Israel, sciens quoniam posuit author eius Deus fines suos pacem. Vide si non hinc ortum est illud Christi ad ipsam Hierusalem, quae figuram tenet ecclesiae: Hierusalem Hierusalem quoties volui congregare filios tuos sicut gallina congregat pullos suos, & noluisti. Ad hoc quippe mortuus est Iesus, vt filios suos dispersos in vnum congregaret, tanquam lapis angularis faciens vtraq; vnum. Et ecce hea fera pessima, monstrum horrendum ingens, monstrum biceps portentum iam 31. annos habens, schisma pestiferum pulcherrimam hanc & perfectam pacem quantum in se fuit lacerauit, dissipauit, & in exilii longinquam regionem trusit. Sed veniat o vtinam pax iuxta votum Esaiae: Veniat & requiescat in cubiculo suo, quod est ecclesia: quatenus expulso disconuenienti schismate, forma pacis conueniens inducatur. Nam qualis est ista deformitas, qualis imperfectio, videre corpus mille partibus miseris modis laceratum, dissipatum & dispersum? Cuius lacerationi nulla hactenus profuerunt efficaciter humana remedia, quin potius schisma hoc horrendum velut insanabilis cancer aegrescit medendo, vt de Trano loquitur Virgilius. Ipsum denique tanquam fabulosa hydra redit ex succisione sua foecundius. Hinc scandala populorum sine numero aduersus fidem nostram, religionem nostram, mores sanctos: aduersus spem quoque futurae beatitudinis, contemptum seculi, sanctitatem immobilem iurisiurandi, voti sacramentorum virtutem, obedientiam ad Deum, & ad omnem disciplinam. Quare? Quia saeuissima dominandi libido, mater infausta schismatis huius pestiferi confundit haec omnia: fasque nefasque velut hianti voragine mergit, sorbet & obruit. Quid potro de paganorum infidelium quefabuler probro & irrisione aduersus catholicos? Demum tota illa flebilis Hieremiae lamentatio, si ad calamitatem ecclesiae praesentem defletatur, nescio si satis illam vt dignum est expressat, dum ait: Quomodo sedet sola ciuitas plena populo, &c. Nequit prorsus aequari verbis, quantum res ipsa videatur indigna, pro qua reformanda celeriter expeditissimum est quod congregentur filii Israel & filii Iuda pariter.
units.tr: The congregation of the sons of Israel and Judah is sought by the Church together, just as matter seeks form, the imperfect seeks perfection, and the woman seeks the man, or the bride the bridegroom. Dionysius treats this, and after him Boethius and Augustine, and experience supports them, that every thing loves and desires the gathering of itself no less than its own being, namely because being and one are convertible. Hence comes that pain, that shaking, that violent horror in a living body when it is sought to be divided or scattered limb from limb. So no one will doubt that the Church shrinks from and dreads its own division, since it is the mystical body, according to the teaching of the Apostle in Ephes. 4, 1 Corinth. 12, and Roman. 12, and very often elsewhere. It is also terrible, like an army drawn up in battle line. Who does not know that separation in an army brings the greatest harm? Moreover, the Church is a city, of which glorious things have been said; it is the kingdom of God, it is the heavenly hierarchy below, and so on through many similitudes, by which it is shown that division and schismatic separation are utterly hateful. Here I could have spoken at greater length, showing that the perfection of the ecclesiastical body rests chiefly in unity, as in the completion of every good. I am mistaken, then, if the prophet, longing for it, does not ask this when he prays for peace upon Israel, knowing that his author, God, has set peace as his boundary. See whether from this came that saying of Christ to Jerusalem itself, which holds the figure of the Church: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, how often would I have gathered your children as a hen gathers her chicks, and you would not. For Jesus died precisely to gather into one his scattered children, making both one like the cornerstone. And behold, this wild beast, most wicked, a huge monster, a two-headed portent, now in its thirty-first year, this pestilent schism, has as far as it could torn apart, scattered and dissipated this most beautiful and perfect peace, and thrust it off into a distant land of exile. But may peace come, O that it would, according to the wish of Isaiah: Let it come and rest in its chamber, which is the Church, so that the unsuitable schism being driven out, a fitting form of peace may be brought in. For what kind of deformity and imperfection is it to see a body torn in a thousand parts in wretched ways, scattered and dispersed? No human remedy has yet effectively helped its laceration; rather this dreadful schism, like an incurable cancer, grows worse by being treated, as Virgil says of Tranus. Finally, like the fabled hydra, it grows back more fruitfully from its cutting. Hence come countless scandals of peoples against our faith, our religion, our holy manners; against the hope too of future blessedness, contempt of the world, the unchanging sanctity of an oath, the power of vows and sacraments, obedience to God and to every discipline. Why? Because the most savage lust of dominion, the unhappy mother of this pestilent schism, confounds all these things: it sinks right and wrong alike into a gaping chasm, swallows them and overwhelms them. Why should I speak of the reproach and mockery of unbelieving pagans against Catholics? Lastly, that whole tearful lamentation of Jeremiah, if it is applied to the present calamity of the Church, I do not know whether it expresses it sufficiently as it deserves, when he says: How the city sits solitary, full of people, etc. It cannot be matched in words, how unworthy the thing itself appears; for the reform of which, it is most readily arranged that the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah be gathered together.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO II.
units.tr: CONSIDERATIO II.

units.la: PRo causa secunda. Congregatio filiorum Israel & Iuda pariter quaerenda exequendaque est, vt ponant sibimet caput vnum. Iste est finis, haec intentio imminentis sacri concilii Pisis celebranlebrandi, ad quod vos cum caeteris religiosa & filiali ad matrem ecclesiam pietate pergitis & peruenia-tis oro feliciter. Non ignoratis scio o doctissimi & sapientes viri, quod caput ecclesiae primarium & principale semper vnum est, inuariabile & permanens, sicut testatur Apostolus: Caput, inquit ecclesiae Christus. Christus autem manet in aeternum (vt idem ait) sempiternum habens sacerdotium & Papatum. Itaque salutifer Christe caput nostrum es, a quo fluunt in ecclesia sensus omnes & motus viuifici spirituales ac gratuiti: ac proinde nunquam ecclesia tua esse potest acephala, neque te sponso suo viduata. Nihilominus tu quondam ascensurus ad patrem reliquisti sibi vicarium super terram tanquam caput aliquod secundarium, fluens & refluens in stabili loco tui sacerdotii & Papatus essentialis indefectibilis & manentis usque ad consummationem seculi, quando euacuabis omnem dominationem, principatum & potestatem, & reddideris regnum Deo Patri. Nuncautem proh dolor & viri patres & fratres, nunc scandalizantur aduersus hoc caput primarium duo contendentes, dum simul illud quod fieri nefas est repraesentare volunt, vel vices gerere, vel in suum locum succedere. Sic in impiam succedimus maledictionem hanc, quod facti sunt eius hostes ecclesiae in capite. Oportebat quidem ad vnitatem Papalis sacerdotii vnicum sacerdotem & certum vicarium Christi super terram assumi succedentem Petro, non Pharisaica contentione dicere, sicut olim conquestus est Apostolus: Ego sum Gregorii, ego sum Benedicti. Sanctius quoque filiaque ad matrem charitati, conuenientius est est relinquere Papalem dignitatem & Petri sedem vni tertio sub pace possidendam, sub quo congregati essent filii Israel & filii Iuda vnus populus Dei, quam foedissima seditione partiretur obedientia, & spargeretur grex, quasi non esset vnum ouile & vnus pastor.
units.tr: As to the second cause: the congregation of the sons of Israel and Judah together is to be sought and carried out, so that they may set for themselves one head. This is the end, this the purpose, of the sacred council about to be held at Pisa, to which you are going with religious and filial devotion to our mother the Church, and I pray that you arrive safely. You are not unaware, I know, most learned and wise men, that the primary and principal head of the Church is always one, unchangeable and permanent, as the Apostle bears witness: Christ, he says, is the head of the Church. But Christ remains forever (as the same writer says), having an everlasting priesthood and Papacy. Therefore, O saving Christ, you are our head, from whom all the spiritual, life-giving and gracious senses and motions flow into the Church; and so your Church can never be headless, nor widowed of you, its bridegroom. Nevertheless, when you were about to ascend to the Father, you left to it a vicar upon earth, as a kind of secondary head, flowing and returning in the stable place of your priesthood and of your essential, indefectible Papacy, abiding until the end of the age, when you will abolish every dominion, principality and power, and hand over the kingdom to God the Father. But now, alas, brothers and fathers, two men are contending, and are scandalized against this primary head, while they wish at the same time to represent what is impious to do: either to act in its place, or to succeed into its position. Thus we succeed into that impious curse, that they have become enemies of the Church in its head. It was indeed fitting, for the unity of the Papal priesthood, that a single priest and a certain vicar of Christ upon earth be taken up as successor to Peter, not saying, in Pharisaic contention, as the Apostle once complained: I am of Gregory, I am of Benedict. It is also holier and more befitting for a child's love toward its mother to leave the Papal dignity and the see of Peter to be possessed in peace by one third person, under whom the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah might be gathered as one people of God, rather than that obedience be divided by the most foul sedition and the flock scattered, as though there were not one fold and one shepherd.

units.la: Quasi rursus indecens esset quod congregarentur filii Israel & filii Iuda pariter. Meditabar haec nuper in abscondito scrutinio cordis mei priusquam proferretur: dum ecce animalis homo non sapiens quae Dei sunt, sed ea quae de terra sunt loquens, numeratus quippe est inter filios Agar, de quibus dicit Scriptura, quod exquisierunt sapientiam quae de terra est. Coniungitur quippe ipsi sapientiae terrenae, animali & diabolicae, non ei quae desursum est, praeterea obscuratum habet intellectum. Ipse inquam animalis homo, vt impatiens, hebes & praeceps, & quo pacto, inquit, opus est congregatione filiorum Israel & Iuda: quasi resiuncta sit super iure precium: quasi praeterea liceat vel expediat nunc concilium generale nouum celebrari. Non itaque licet, cum non possit concilium generale sine Papa celebrari, & nisi primitus ante omnia spoliatus ab obedientia sua restituatur eidem. Quomodo praeterea decens esset ea quae certa sunt & tam per longissimos temporis tractus in consuetudinem versa, rursus in discussionem tanquam dubia reuocari. Et quod vera & iusta pars exponat se discrimini condemnationis. Nam euentus iudiciorum varii sunt, qui falluntur & fallunt. Denique quid expedit contraniti voluntati diuinae, suaeque prouidentiae? quae iusto iudicio permittit haereses fieri, & dicit esse necesse vt veniant scandala. Qui etiam ait: Nolite arbitrari quod venerim pacem mittere in terram, sed gladium. Qui demum olim prohibuit fieri congregationem filiorum Israel & Iuda pariter: asserens diuisionem ab eo factam esse. Multa maioraque parabat animalis homo delatrare aduersus celebrationem concilii, asserens quod nec licebat, nec dicebat, nec expediebat illud fieri, dum exhorrui fateor, nihilominus aio ad eum: Obmutesce importune & stulte, aut expecta donec consideration um caeptarum numerus impleatur. Audies forte ea, quae contradictionibus tuis imponere possint silentium. Extorsi velut ab inuito dilationem, vt tertia & quarta consideratio nes liberiori sermone complerentur.
units.tr: Again, as if it were unseemly that the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah should be gathered together! I was pondering these things lately in the hidden searching of my heart before they were brought forth, when behold, an animal man, not wise in the things of God but speaking the things that are of the earth, one counted indeed among the sons of Hagar, of whom Scripture says that they sought the wisdom that is of the earth. He is joined indeed to earthly, animal and diabolical wisdom, not to that which is from above, and moreover has an obscured understanding. This same animal man, impatient, dull and headlong, says: "In what way is there need of a gathering of the sons of Israel and Judah?" as though the question of right had been settled, and as though it were allowed or expedient now to hold a new general council. It is therefore not lawful, since a general council cannot be held without the Pope, and unless he is first of all restored to the obedience that was taken from him. Moreover, how fitting would it be for things that are certain, and that have passed into custom over such long stretches of time, to be called back again into question as if they were doubtful? And for the true and just party to expose itself to the danger of condemnation? For the outcomes of judgments are various, and men are deceived and deceive. Finally, what is the use of resisting the will of God and his providence, which by a just judgment permits heresies to arise, and says that it must be that scandals come? He also says: Do not think that I came to send peace on earth, but a sword. He who once forbade the gathering of the sons of Israel and Judah together, declaring that the division had been made by him. The animal man was preparing many greater things to bark against the celebration of the council, asserting that it was neither lawful, nor said, nor expedient to do it. Although I confess I shuddered, I nevertheless said to him: Be silent, foolish and importunate man, or wait until the number of the begun considerations is complete. Perhaps you will hear things that can impose silence on your objections. I wrested a postponement from him, as though from an unwilling man, so that the third and fourth considerations might be completed with freer speech.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO III.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION III.

units.la: Congregatio filiorum Israel & Iuda pariter habet fieri tanquam a causa dispositiua, quae remouet prohibens, dum ipsi ascendunt de terra, hoc est secundum moralem intellectum, dum de terrenis affectibus ascendunt ad coelestes, & fiunt de animalibus spirituales, dumque litera dimissa quae occidit, ipsi spiritum qui viuificat, ampleCtuntur: hoc tamen obseruato, ne quid nimis: ne dum nimis obseruari quaeritur spiritus, obruatur simul caro cum spiritu. Vnde quaesto tamdiu viri patres tardata est fieri congregatio concilii generalis & sacri: nisi quod tamdiu non fuerunt audito spirituales viri, quales (si Apostolo creditur) diiudicant de omnibus? Ecce quid praeclara Vniuersitas Oxoniensis, vnde sibi meruit congratulari, pridem ad hoc concilium petendum determinauit se & misit in Francia: scio qui praesens interfui dum proponeretur haec conclusio compendii sub hoc themate Ioelis, id est: Vocate coetum, coadunate senes. Sed pridem antea Parisiensis vniuersitas ab exordio nascentis diuisionis deliberauit solenniter & concordi sententia conclusionem hanc petendam & prosequendam esse, quam ex parte sui proposuit reuerendus pater ac praeceptor meus praecipuus dominus nunc Cameracensis, coram Ludouico Duce Andegauensi, tunc Regenti in Francia.
units.tr: The assembly of the sons of Israel and Judah likewise is to be understood as taking place by way of a disposing cause, which removes the hindrance, when they ascend out of the land. That is, in the moral sense, it happens when they rise from earthly affections to heavenly ones and become spiritual instead of animal, and, the letter that kills having been put aside, they embrace the Spirit who gives life. Yet this must be observed: nothing in excess, lest, while the Spirit is sought too eagerly, the flesh be crushed along with the Spirit. Hence the fathers have delayed for so long the convening of a general and holy council, except that for so long spiritual men were not heard, such as (if we believe the Apostle) judge all things. See what the famous University of Oxford, whereby it earned itself congratulation, lately determined to seek this council, and sent to France. I know this, for I was present when this conclusion was put forward as a summary under this theme of Joel, namely: Call an assembly, gather the elders. But long before, the University of Paris, from the beginning of the rising division, solemnly and with one accord resolved that this conclusion should be sought and pursued; and on its behalf the reverend father and my chief teacher, the now Bishop of Cambrai, set it forth before Louis, Duke of Anjou, then regent in France.

units.la: Circa quod tempus scripsit pro eadem conclusione clarissimae memoriae Magister Henricus de Hassia magister in Theologia Parisiensis, & Vicecancellarius sub magistro Ioanne de Calore tunc Cancellario Parisiensi. Scripsit insuper dominus Praepositus Vormacensis magnus & deuotus & Licenciatus in artibus Parisiensis. Scripserunt quoque alii, sicut ex eorum tractatibus adhuc constat. Amplius vero scripsit post multos annos Vniuersitas Parisiensis epistolam grandem continentem tres vias, inter quas concilium generale numeratum est. Ecce quot viri spirituales & eruditi, non innitentes soli terrae, ascendentes de terrenis affectibus. & in liberum atque purum aether lucidissimae veritatis, desideriorumque splendidorum sese attollentes, quaesiuerunt olim multo studio concorditer, quod congregentur filii Israel & filii Iuda pariter. Et haec est non parua congratulationis materia, quod in vnam conuentum est sententiam per duas vniuersitates toto orbe celeberrimas, & ipsis non nisi fides dari debet, cum illic sint viri spirituales & sapientes, secundum qualia iudicia medium virtutis accipere iubet Philosophus. Illic praeterea sunt idonei conditores legum doctrinaliter & instructiue, quibus similis interpretatio per Ἑρμηνείαν debita est. Illic sunt, qui mentiri nesciunt, de quibus nouerunt, & mentientes redarguere possunt, dum a vero fallum, a licito illicitum sciunt secernere. Cum ergo conueniunt congregatio multiplex sapientum in celebrationem huius concilii generalis tanquam in rem expedientem, vt in prima causa dicebatur. In re praeterea decentem sicut visum est in secunda. Nam quid decentius, quam vt vnum corpus habeat caput vnum. Postremo superest ostendere rem hanc esse per se licitam atque legitimam, quod in quarta & vltima consideratione videbimus, quae talis est.
units.tr: About this time the most famous Master Henry of Hesse, Master of Theology at Paris and Vice-Chancellor under Master John of Chalon, then Chancellor of Paris, wrote in support of this same conclusion. Moreover, the lord Provost of Worms, a great and devout man and licentiate in arts of Paris, wrote as well. Others also wrote, as their treatises still show. Later, after many years, the University of Paris wrote a large letter setting out three ways, among which a general council is counted. Here are so many spiritual and learned men, not resting on the earth alone, rising from earthly affections into the free and pure air of most clear truth, and lifting themselves up to splendid desires, who long ago with great zeal agreed in seeking that the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah be gathered together. This is no small cause for rejoicing: that two universities, most renowned throughout the whole world, have come together in one judgment. Faith should be given to them alone, since there are spiritual and wise men there, who, according to such judgments, the Philosopher bids us to take the mean of virtue. There are also men fit to frame laws, learned and instructive, to whom a like interpretation [Ἑρμηνείαν] is owed. There are those who do not know how to lie about what they know, and who can refute liars, since they know how to separate the false from the true and the unlawful from the lawful. Therefore, since a multitude of wise men agree to bring about this general council, it is a matter of expediency, as was said in the first cause. It is also a matter of fitness, as was seen in the second. For what is more fitting than that one body should have one head? Lastly, it remains to show that this matter is in itself lawful and legitimate, which we shall see in the fourth and final consideration, which is as follows.

units.la: CONSIDERATIO IV.
units.tr: CONSIDERATION IV.

units.la: CONgregatio filiorum Israel & Iuda pariter sumit suam efficaciam & virtutem a diuino semine, quod per ecclesiasticum corpus tanquam sanguis viuificus diffusum est, & radicaliter seu inseparabiliter insertum. Ponamus pro solido fundamento praesentis considerationis & aliorum tam dictorum quam dicendorum textum Apostoli ad Ephes. quart. Solliciti seruare vnitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis vnum corpus & vnus spiritus, sicut vocati estis in vna spe vocationis vestrae, vnus Dominus, vna fides, vnum baptisma, vnus Deus & pater omnium, qui super omnes & super omnia in omnibus. Sequitur: Et ipse dedit quosdam quidem Apostolos, quosdam autem prophetas, alios vero Euangelistas, alios autem pastores & doctores ad consummationem sanctorum, in opus ministerii in aedificationem corporis Christi, donec occurramus omnes in vnitatem fidei & agnitionis filii Dei in virum perfectum, in mensura aetatis plenitudinis Christi. Sequitur: Veritatem autem facientes in charitate, crescamus in illo per omnia qui est caput Christus, ex quo totum corpus compactum & connexum per omnem iuncturam subministrationis secundum operationem in mensuram vniuscuiusque membri, augmentum corporis facit in aedificationem sui in charitate. Eliciamus ex his paucissimis, sed sententiosissimis Apostoli verbis aliquas veritates.
units.tr: The congregation of the sons of Israel and Judah likewise draws its efficacy and power from the divine seed, which has been poured through the ecclesiastical body as a life-giving blood, and inserted into it at the root, or inseparably. Let us take as the solid foundation of this consideration, and of the others both already set out and yet to come, the text of the Apostle to the Ephesians, chapter 4: Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. There is one body and one Spirit, as you are called in one hope of your calling; one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all. It follows: And he gave some apostles, and some prophets, and some evangelists, and some pastors and teachers, for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ, until we all come in the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ. It follows: But speaking the truth in love, let us grow up in him in all things, which is the head, even Christ: from whom the whole body fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplieth, according to the effectual working in the measure of every part, maketh increase of the body unto the edifying of itself in love. From these very few but very pithy words of the Apostle let us draw out some truths.

units.la: Prima: Congregatio ecclesiastica ad vnum caput Christum facit, & conglutinatur per vinculum amarosum Spiritus mediatibus qualitatiuis dispositionibus reddentibus in corpore mystico complexionale viuificam & decentem. Haec autem dona sunt virtutes Theologicae, fides, spes & charitas, sacramenta ecclesiastica, sunt diuersae diuisiones gratiarum, prout vnicuique concessum est. Hoc est semen in quo conueniunt ambae obedientiae, quale non abstulisset schisma pestiferum, si de pace reformanda nihil actum esset, prout alias scripsit ipsis Romanis Parisiensis Vniuersitas.
units.tr: The first: the ecclesiastical congregation is made one under Christ as its one head, and is bound together by the bond of the Spirit, through qualitative dispositions which render the mystical body a living and becoming whole. These gifts are the theological virtues, faith, hope and charity, and the ecclesiastical sacraments; they are "diversities of gifts, according as it has been given to each one." This is the seed in which both obediences agree. A pestilent schism would not have taken this away, had nothing been done about reforming the peace, as the University of Paris has written elsewhere to the Romans themselves.

units.la: Secunda: Congregatio ecclesiastica ad vnum caput Christum copiosior est atque fecundior, quam fuit congregatio synagogae. Non enim habuit synagoga talem in sacramentis & aliis multis commutationem adiunctionis sicut ecclesia. Nam extra eam stabat salus, quemadmodum saluatus Iob ostendit.
units.tr: The second: the ecclesiastical congregation under Christ as its one head is more abundant and more fruitful than the congregation of the synagogue was. For the synagogue did not have such a variety of additions in the sacraments and many other things as the Church has. For outside the Church there was salvation, as Job, who was saved, showed.

units.la: Tertia: Congregatio ecclesiastica ad vnum caput secundarium multiplicior est & maior, quam sit congregatio ciuilis sub vno rectore vel imperatore vel rege. Connexio quippe talis politiae ciuilitatis fit per leges & dona naturae principaliter, & in illis constituit suam vnitatem. Ecclesia vero vt politia & ordinata habet hanc vnitatem, & vltra hanc habet alteram supernaturalem & diuinam, quae dicta est. Et ita sequitur consequenter, quod ecclesiastica pluribus legibus regitur, quam altera politia.
units.tr: The third: the ecclesiastical congregation under one secondary head is more numerous and greater than a civil congregation under one ruler, emperor or king.
