Haec Apostolus ad Ephes. 4. Et in hanc sententiam multa ad Coloss. 1. & 2. 1. Cor. 12. & ad Rom. 12. posita sunt. Haec autem comparatio veri corporis ad mysticum, multum luminis affert inquisitoribus veritatis, nedum apud Philosophos, sicut Aristotelem & Plutarchum, sed apud Theologos; Paulum praecipue. Diffunduntur vero sicut praemisimus 12. considerationes ex hoc symboli & Apostoli doctrinali luce, quasi totidem radii veritatis splendidissimi.
units.tr: Let us add another light, agreeing with this light, from the apostolic word: Being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace: one body and one Spirit, as you were called in one hope of your calling; one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is above all, through all and in all of us. It continues: And he gave some indeed as apostles, some as prophets, others as evangelists, others as pastors and teachers, for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the building up of the body of Christ, until we all come in the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ. It continues: But speaking the truth in love, let us grow up in all things into him who is the head, Christ; from whom the whole body, fitted and joined together through every joint of supply, according to the working in due measure of each part, makes the increase of the body to the building up of itself in love. The Apostle says this in Ephes. 4. Many things to the same effect are set down in Coloss. 1 and 2, 1 Cor. 12, and Rom. 12. This comparison of the true body to the mystical body brings much light to seekers of truth, not only among philosophers such as Aristotle and Plutarch, but among theologians, Paul above all. Twelve considerations, as we premised, are diffused from this doctrinal light of the creed and the Apostle, like so many most splendid rays of truth.

units.la: I. Ecclesiastica vnitas ad vnum caput Christum fit, & agglutinatur per amorosum Spiritus sancti vinculum, mediantibus diuinis charismatibus, tanquam qualitatiuis dispositionibus reddentibus in corpore mystico complexionalem harmoniam viuificam & decentem ad opera vitae spiritualiter sufficienter exercenda.
units.tr: I. Ecclesiastical unity is brought about with the one head, Christ, and is joined together by the loving bond of the Holy Spirit, through divine gifts, as qualitative dispositions which give to the mystical body a vivifying and fitting harmony of composition, sufficient for carrying on the works of spiritual life.

units.la: II. Ecclesiastica vnitas ad vnum caput secundarium, quod dicitur summus pontifex Christi vicarius foecundior est, multiplicior, copiosiot & maior, quam fuerit congregatio synagogae: & quam sit congregatio ciuilis sub vno, rectore rege vel Imperatore.
units.tr: II. Ecclesiastical unity with the one secondary head, which is called the supreme pontiff, Christ's vicar, is more fruitful, more multiplied, more abundant and greater than was the congregation of the synagogue, and than is a civil congregation under one ruling king or emperor.

units.la: III. Ecclesia habet potestatem seu facultatem ex viuifico germine sibi insito per Spiritum sanctum, quod seipsam potest continuare in integritate & vnitate membrorum suorum, tam essentialium seu formalium, quam materialium atque fluentium.
units.tr: III. The Church has the power or faculty, from the life-giving seed implanted in it by the Holy Spirit, of continuing itself in the integrity and unity of its members, both essential or formal and material and flowing.

units.la: IV. Ecclesia habet sponsum indefectibilem Christum, sic quod lege stante, nec Christus potest ipsi sponsae suae ecclesiae dare libellum repudii: nec econuerso.
units.tr: IV. The Church has an indefectible spouse, Christ, so that, while the law stands, Christ cannot give a bill of divorce to his spouse, the Church, nor, conversely, can she to him.

units.la: V. Ecclesia non ita ligatur matrimoniali vinculo ad vicarium indefectibilem sponsi sui, quin mutuo se possint absoluere & dare libellum repudii.
units.tr: V. The Church is not so bound by the matrimonial bond to the indefectible vicar of her spouse that they cannot mutually release each other and give a bill of divorce.

units.la: VI. Ecclesia vel generale concilium eam representans est regula a Spiritu sancto directa, tradita a Christo, vt quilibet cuiuscunque status, etiam Papalis, existat, eam audire ac eidem obedire teneatur, alioquin habendus est vt ethnicus & publicanus. Patet ex immutabili lege diuina Matth. 18. promulgata. Concilium generale sic describi potest: Concilium generale est aggregatio legitima autoritate facta ad aliquem locum, ex omni statu hierarchico totius ecclesiae catholicae, nulla fidelis persona quae audiri requirat, exclusa, ad salubriter tractandum & ordinandum ea quae debitum regimen eiusdem ecclesiae in fide & moribus respiciunt.
units.tr: VI. The Church, or a general council representing it, is a rule directed by the Holy Spirit and handed down by Christ, so that whoever, of whatever state, even papal, exists, is bound to hear it and obey it; otherwise he is to be held as a heathen and a tax collector. This is evident from the immutable divine law promulgated in Matth. 18. A general council may be described thus: "A general council is a lawful assembly, made by lawful authority to some place, from every hierarchical rank of the whole catholic Church, no faithful person who requires a hearing being excluded, for the salutary treatment and ordering of those matters which concern the due governance of the same Church in faith and morals."

units.la: VII. Ecclesia vel generale concilium, dum dictat aliqua regimen ecclesiae concernentia, Papa non sic est supra iura etiam positiva, quod possit pro libito dissoluere talia dictata per ecclesiam eo modo & intentione, quibus dictata conclusaque sunt.
units.tr: VII. The Church, or a general council, when it decrees anything concerning the government of the Church, does not place the Pope so far above even positive laws that he may dissolve at will such decrees made by the Church in the manner and with the intention in which they were decreed and concluded.

units.la: VIII. Ecclesia vel generale concilium quamuis non possit tollere plenitudinem potestatis Papalis a Christo supernaturaliter & misericorditer collatae: potest tamen vsum eius limitare sub certis regulis ac legibus in aedificationem ecclesiae, propter quam Papalis autoritas & alterius hominis collata est. Et in hoc est totius ecclesiasticae reformationis stabile fundamentum.
units.tr: VIII. The Church, or a general council, cannot take away the fullness of papal power, which Christ supernaturally and graciously conferred. It can, however, limit the use of that power under certain rules and laws, for the building up of the Church, for the sake of which papal authority was given to a man at all. In this lies the firm foundation of all ecclesiastical reformation.

units.la: IX. Ecclesia vel generale concilium potuit & potest congregari sine expresso consensu vel mandato Papae etiam rite electi, & viuentis in multis casibus. Vnus inter caeteros est, quia accusatus & euocatus sit vt audiat ecclesiam iuxta euangelicam allegatam, cui legi subiectus est: & ipse renuit contumaciter ecclesiam conuocare. Alius casus vbi materiae grandes concernentes regimen ecclesiae, veniunt terminandae per generale concilium, & Papa renuit contumaciter illud euocare. Alius etiam dictatum sit per generale concilium, quod debeat tali vel tali tempore conuocari. Alter casus est, vbi probabilis est dubitatio super contendentia plurium de Papatu.
units.tr: IX. The Church, or a general council, could and can be convened, in many cases, without the express consent or command of the Pope, even one lawfully elected and living. One such case is when he has been accused and summoned to hear the Church, according to the gospel rule cited above, to which law he is subject, and he obstinately refuses to convene the Church. Another case is when great matters concerning the government of the Church are to be settled by a general council, and the Pope obstinately refuses to call it. Another is when a general council has decreed that it must be convened at such and such a time. A further case is when there is a probable doubt about the contested claims of several men to the papacy.

units.la: X. Ecclesia seu generale concilium, si viam aliquam conclusterit seu dictauerit acceptandam esse a Papa pro terminatione schismatis, ipse tenetur illa acceptare, & ita secundum praeparationem animi tenetur ad concessionem, & dum vltro offert eam & praeuenit, ipse redditur multipliciter commendandus.
units.tr: X. If the Church or a general council has determined or decreed that some way is to be accepted by the Pope for ending the schism, he is bound to accept it. He is thus bound to consent, in accordance with the readiness of his mind; and if he offers it of his own accord and anticipates the council, he is deservedly to be commended in many ways.

units.la: XI. Ecclesia seu generale concilium praecipue debet intendere cum prosecutione vnius perfectae ad extirpationem errorum, & emendationem errantium sine personarum acceptione. Similiter ad hoc, quod hierarchicus ordo ecclesiasticus praelatorum & curatorum multipliciter turbatus reformetur ad similitudinem diuinae coelestis hierarchiae: & conformiter ad regulas primitus institutas.
units.tr: XI. The Church, or a general council, ought above all to aim, with the pursuit of one perfect aim, at the uprooting of errors and the correction of those in error, without regard to persons. Likewise, the ecclesiastical hierarchy of prelates and parish priests, which has been greatly disturbed, ought to be reformed after the likeness of the divine heavenly hierarchy and in conformity with the rules originally instituted.

units.la: XII. Ecclesia non habet efficacius medium ad generalem sui ipsius reformationem, quam sistatur generalium conciliorum continuatio, celebrationem prouincialium non omittendo. Explicit.
units.tr: XII. The Church has no more effective means for its general reformation than that the holding of general councils be continued without interruption, provided that provincial councils are not neglected. Here ends the text.

units.la: Et attendat benignus lector quod prolator huius sermonis Ioannes Cancellarius Parrhisiensis, pressus nimia temporis angustia, probationes dictatas non appositi ad has considerationes, sed prout in mentem & linguam ex recordatione praeteritorum opusculorum praesertim tempore concilii. Eilii Pisani, dum absens abeo legebat Parrhisiis, inserens, materiam hanc quam in tractatulo quodam sub 20. considerationum numero scriptam reposuit. Cuius initium est: Venient autem dies, cum auferetur ab eis sponsus: ubi prædictæ considerationes & in propositione una coram Legatis Angliæ pergentibus ad Concilium Pisanum tunc Parrhysiis habita, prolixiori solidiorique manifestatæ sunt argumentatione, qui tractatus & propositio prodierunt in publicum, ut habeat qui voluerit, fas est.
units.tr: And let the kind reader note that the speaker of this sermon, John the Chancellor of Paris, pressed by the great shortness of time, did not set down the proofs in these considerations as they were prepared, but as they came to mind and to his tongue from his recollection of earlier writings, especially from the time of the Council of Pisa, when, while absent, he read them at Paris. He inserted this matter, which he had written in a little treatise under the number of twenty considerations, beginning: Venient autem dies, cum auferetur ab eis sponsus. There these considerations were set out at greater length and with firmer argument, in a proposal delivered before the English envoys then travelling to the Council of Pisa and held at Paris. That treatise and proposal have been published, and whoever wishes may have them.

units.la: AMplius vero iuxta legationis onus impositum pet Christianissimū Regem Francorū ac Vniuersitatem præclarissimam Parrhisiensem propositerat idē Cancellarius post verbū de ecclesiastica vnitate subiungere de errorum extirpatione: sed impeditus tunc partim amicorum suasione, partim temporis artatione, vt in prolixitate non inesset fastidium silentio præteriit, quorum aliqua summarim hic subiuncta sunt.
units.tr: Moreover, in accordance with the charge laid upon the embassy by the most Christian King of the Franks and the most famous University of Paris, the same Chancellor had intended, after his words on ecclesiastical unity, to add something on the uprooting of errors. But, hindered then partly by the advice of friends and partly by the shortness of time, he passed over it in silence so that the length should not cause weariness. Some points of it are subjoined here in summary.

units.la: Glorificationem Dei, patres Apostolici, patres gloriosi, posuimus esse fine huius concilii sanctorū, quatenus pleni sint cœlum & terra, ô Deus magne & terribilis, gloria tua: quatenus non iam ambulent in errorum circumitu impii super terram, sed agnoscant quoniam magna est gloria (dicente sapiente) sequi te Dominum per semitas legis tuæ pacificas, quoniam pax multa diligentibus legem tuam, & non est illis scandalum, & quia si creditur eidem sapienti, nihil dulcius quam respicere in mandatis Dei. Sed væ mundo à scandalis, væ tibi mala voluntas, & ideo mala, quoniam arrogantia superbia gloriam propriam quærens anteponis eam diuinæ, nolens subiici legi suæ, neq; captiuare omnem intellectum in obsequium fidei. Hinc hæreses & errores impii, hinc scandalorum turbationes horridæ, hinc ordine violato plurima fœdaq; confusio: hinc tandem in hominibus & ex consequenti per omnia, quæ propter homines fecit Deus, suboritur frequenter non gloria Dei, non pax hominibus, sed terra quædam alteratio mortificans & abiiciens viuificantem gratiæ spiritum: & cadauerosam monstrosorum defectuum, non tam formam quam deformitatem inducens. Deplorat hanc peruersissimam rerum vicissitudinem Christianissimus Francorum rex, cum ecclesia tota regni sui miseretur, dolet, compatitur; & ab hoc sacrosancto concilio legitimas prouisiones efflagitat. Nō confundatur precor ab expectatione sua: nolite careat piissimis desideriorum suorum affectionibus, sed & patrem sequitur sua proles, regem videlicet filia sua Parrhisiensi Vniversitas: nec tamen sequitur, sed præit humilitate salua, quandoque consiliis, nunc exhortationibus, aliquando doctrinis sciens quod veritas custodit regem, sciens præterea se positam Apostoli iussu, ut potens sit exhortari in doctrina sana: & eos qui contradicunt arguere, quæ posuit Aristot. opera duo sapientis. Denique parata est tanquam posita in lucem ecclesiæ ad satisfactionem omni poscenti rationem, de ea quæ in ipsa est fide & spe, ut in omnibus & per omnia glorificetur Deus.
units.tr: We have set the glorification of God as the aim of this holy council, Fathers Apostolic, glorious Fathers, that the heavens and the earth may be full of it: O great and terrible God, Thy glory. So that the wicked no longer walk about in the circuit of errors upon the earth, but acknowledge that great is the glory (as the wise man says) of following Thee, the Lord, along the peaceful paths of Thy law, since there is great peace for those who love Thy law, and for them there is no stumbling-block; and because, if we believe that same wise man, nothing is sweeter than to look upon the commandments of God. But woe to the world because of offences, woe to you, ill will, and therefore evil, since in your arrogance and pride you seek your own glory and set it above the divine, unwilling to be subject to His law, nor to bring every intellect captive to the obedience of faith. Hence come heresies and impious errors, hence the dreadful disturbances of scandals, hence, with order violated, very great and foul confusion. Hence at last, in men, and consequently in all things which God made for the sake of men, there frequently arises not the glory of God, not peace for men, but a certain corruption of the earth which deadens and casts out the quickening spirit of grace, and which brings in a carcass-like and monstrous deformity, not so much a form as a disfigurement. The most Christian King of the Franks laments this most perverse change of affairs; he grieves for and sympathises with the whole Church of his kingdom, and from this most holy council he asks for lawful provision. Let him not, I pray, be confounded in his expectation. Let him not lack the most pious affection of his desires. And his child follows the father: the University of Paris, his daughter, follows the king, yet not as a follower, but goes before him in humility, sometimes by counsels, now by exhortations, at other times by teaching, knowing that truth guards the king, and knowing moreover that she has been set, by the Apostle's command, that she may be able to exhort in sound doctrine and to convict those who contradict. These are the words of Aristotle, the two works of a wise man. Finally, she is ready, as a light set before the Church, to give an account to everyone who asks for the reason of the faith and hope that is in her, so that in all things and through all things God may be glorified.

units.la: Insurrexerunt ecce post aliqua tempora plurimæ doctrinæ peregrinæ, variæ, pestiferæ & damnatæ, obtenebrantes ecclesiam per multa Christianitatis membra, per regna, per provincias, per regiones insignes. Processum est ad expellendas huiusmodi doctrinarum tenebras: nunc luce disputationis doctrinalis per doctores & universitates: nunc libello iudicialis reprobationis per diœcesanos & inquisitores hæreticæ prauitatis in Anglia, in Scotia, in Praga, in Francia. Nondum: tamen vel illuminari vel emendari sufficienter inspeximus cæcam & stultam imbibitatem assertorum sectatoriumque suorum, quin error assidue sicut cancer serpat & alicubi palam quasi nudato ense per nationes & populos imprudenter erumpat. Propterea necesse est per splendidissimam & inobfuscabilem huius sacri concilii lucem prouida celeritate de remediis instituti, ut qui spreuerunt prælatos & doctores diuisim positos tanquam lucernas in domo Dei reuereantur eos, conspiciant & obediant, dum in vnam hanc ecclesiæ domum collecti, dabunt autoritatis suæ robur & pondus, ibunt in splendore fulgurati s hastæ reprobationis iudicialis, qualem nemo qui Christianus videri vult, audebit contemnere.
units.tr: Behold, after some time there have arisen many strange, various, pestilent and condemned doctrines, darkening the Church in many members of Christendom, in kingdoms, in provinces, in notable regions. Efforts have been made to drive out the darkness of such doctrines: now by the light of doctrinal disputation through doctors and universities; now by a written judicial condemnation through diocesan bishops and inquisitors of heretical depravity in England, in Scotland, in Prague, in France. Yet we have not seen the blind and foolish obstinacy of their assertors and followers sufficiently enlightened or corrected; the error keeps creeping on constantly, like a cancer, and here and there breaks out rashly, almost with a bared sword, among nations and peoples. Therefore it is necessary that remedies be provided with swift foresight by the most splendid and unclouded light of this holy council, so that those who have despised prelates and teachers set apart as lamps in the house of God may reverence them, look to them and obey them, while, gathered together into this one house of the Church, they give strength and weight to their authority. The lightning-bolt of judicial condemnation will go forth in splendour, and no one who wishes to be considered a Christian will dare to scorn such a condemnation.

units.la: Esto contemnat, ipse tamen de conteptu suo fulgurationem concremationemq; subiicit, vt iustu est. Et quoniā charitas sicut incipit à se & à suis dilectionis exhibitione, sic in correctionis & emendationis procuratione priore habere locum debet, ne subeat illud improperii prouerbium Medice cura teipsum. Et illud de Apostoli sententia: Qui prædicas non furandū, furaris, nō occidendū, occidis: non periurandū, deieras & ita de reliquis. Hinc Christianissimus Rex noster suaq; per adoptionē dignatiua t hanissima filia Parrhysi. Vniuersitas voluerunt hactenus à regno & à suis peruerla quorumlibet eorum zizania mox vt erumpere seu germinare sentiebantur, diligenter opprimi relecariq;, nunc falce doctrinæ, nunc securi pastoralis sententiæ, ita tamen vt non simul eradicetur & triticum. Sunt plurima rei, loquimur, documenta è quibus vnum quod nouitate actitateq; præcellit, censuimus in medium deducere. Ecce patentes regis nostri literas, quas audire libeat: legi debebat hæc litera patens, cuius initium est post intitulationem: Regia maiestas nostra, dehinc subiungendum erat:
units.tr: Let him scorn it if he will; yet he himself, for his contempt, will bring upon himself lightning and burning, as is just. And since charity, as it begins with itself and with the showing of love to its own, so in the care of correction and amendment ought to have the first place, lest that reproachful proverb come upon us: Physician, heal yourself. And that saying of the Apostle: You who preach that one should not steal, do you steal? You who say one should not kill, do you kill? You who say one should not swear falsely, do you swear falsely? And so on for the rest. Hence our most Christian King and his daughter, the Parisian University, most worthy by adoption, have hitherto wished that whatever tares of perverse men from the kingdom or from their own ranks were felt to be sprouting or springing up should be diligently suppressed and rooted out at once: now with the sickle of doctrine, now with the axe of pastoral sentence. Yet they have so acted that the wheat is not uprooted along with the tares. There are many proofs of this, as we speak, from which we have thought fit to bring forward one which surpasses the rest in novelty and in activity. Behold the open letters of our king, which it is pleasing to hear. This open letter was to be read; its beginning, after the title, is: Our royal majesty; and then what follows was to be added:

units.la: Audiuit sacrosanctum hoc concilium iustorum, quatenus in Christianissimo Rege nostro feruneat zelus, ad ea quæ fidei sunt absque omni personarum acceptione, absq; respectu propriæ etiam carnis & sanguinis. Terreat ipse Deus magnus & terribilis, qui glorificatur in concilio iustorum, qui salubriter & potenter intonat: Ambulate dum lucem habetis: subdit monitionis causam, ne tenebræ vos comprehendant. Et quales ero densiores, fugibiliores, horribilioresque tenebrę quam errorum & hæresum circa prima præceptorum moralium principia, vt sunt: Non periurabis: Non occides, Non id fidiaberis.
units.tr: This holy Council has heard how zeal burns in our most Christian King, zeal for the things of faith, without regard to any person and without regard even to his own flesh and blood. May God, great and terrible, who is glorified in the council of the just, and who thunders salutarily and powerfully, terrify you: Walk while you have the light; he adds the reason for his warning, lest the darkness overtake you. How much thicker, more fleeing and more horrible is the darkness of error and heresy concerning the first principles of the moral precepts, such as: You shall not swear falsely; You shall not kill; You shall not steal.

units.la: Terreat ipsos ecclesiasticos pastores & Doctores positos in lucem aliorum, si non ad exemplar tam insigne atque perlucidum Christianissimi Regis nostri, non eos illuminet, accendat & inflammet zelus domus Dei. Vox dicentis: Clama, ne cesses, & annuncia populo meo peccata sua. Si non ut eos procedere constanti celeritate ad effugationem errorum tenebrosorum, & ad illuminationem errantium. Neq; enim potest integra salubritate sine secundo primum fieri: quoniam dum impune pertinacia manet in errantibus, conualescant & saeuiant errores necesse est.
units.tr: May it also terrify the ecclesiastical ministers and teachers, who are set in the light of others, if not by the example, so remarkable and clear, of our most Christian King, then at least the zeal of the house of God may enlighten, kindle and inflame them. The voice of him who says: "Cry aloud, do not cease, and declare to my people their sins" should move them. If they do not proceed with steady speed to drive away the dark errors and to enlighten those who are in error, then it cannot be that the first thing is done with full benefit without the second. For while obstinacy in those in error remains unpunished, their errors must of necessity grow strong and rage.

units.la: Sed in ipsa meditatione mea videtur occurrere animalis homo, non sapiens quae Dei sunt, Deum non invocans. Illic praeterea trepidat timore, ubi non est timor: magnus est inquit susurratione tremula, magnus creditur & terribilis, quem tangunt & norant errores huiusmodi, princeps est. Scimus autem quid sapiens enunciet: Indignatio principis mors, & vir prudens placabit eam, quid quaeso si saeuiat, si seditiones concitet, si bella moveat, si secum plurimos hos terroribus, hos promissis in errorem suum trahat, ita ut si fieri potest, moveantur etiam electi? Vide sedulo ac iterum iterumque recogita (ait animalis homo) ne fortassis obinde praestetur tam desiderantissimae iam iamque in ianuis existenti, paci ecclesiae grandis obex vel totalis diruptio. Atvero nihil hic tale timendum, o strenuissimi pugiles fidei, o potentissimi regum diuinarum defensores. Nihil inquam tale timendum timentibus Deum, & obedientibus iussioni quae dixit: Nolite terreri ab eis, qui corpus occidunt, animam vero occidere non possunt. Ita dico vobis, hunc timete, timeatur Deus creat. Homo tamen Deum (suadet Augustinus) & minuentem inundum uniuersum ridebis. Tollatur haec ... pigri formidatio dicentis, leo est in via, deuorandus sum, quia profecto magna & unica securitas timere Deum. Cuius haec iussio est: Usque ad mortem certa pro iustitia. Et iterum: Similia. Potueramus rem hanc in longius deducere, pro quanto fidei ... fiderationes, quasi totidem radii morales luminosi; veritatis.
units.tr: But in my own meditation there seems to present itself the natural man, who does not perceive the things of God and does not call upon God. He trembles with fear where there is no fear; "The prince is great," he says in a trembling whisper, "he is believed great and terrible, and those who are touched and marked by such errors belong to him." We know, however, what the wise man declares: The wrath of a king is death, but a prudent man will appease it. What, I ask, if he rages, if he stirs up sedition, if he moves war, if he draws many with him into his error by terrors and promises, so that, if it were possible, even the elect would be moved? "See carefully, and think again and again," says the natural man, "lest perhaps by this there be offered to the peace of the Church, which is now at the very doors and so greatly desired, a great obstacle or total ruin." But truly nothing of this kind is to be feared here, O most valiant champions of the faith, O most powerful defenders of the divine kings. I say, nothing of this kind is to be feared by those who fear God and obey the command which says: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body, but cannot kill the soul. I tell you this: fear him, let God be feared. Let the fear of the lazy man be taken away, who says: "There is a lion in the way, I shall be devoured," for surely great and sole security is the fear of God. His command is this: Unto death, be certain for justice. And again: Likewise. We could have drawn this matter out at greater length, as far as faith ... these, like so many luminous moral rays of truth.

units.la: I. Prouidendum est haereticali deuiationi daemoniperturbationi ... nus celeriter & efficaciter quam schismati super contendentia ... fide quam in secundario capite fundata est.
units.tr: I. Provision must be made to meet the heretical deviation and the disturbance ... quickly and effectively, as well as the schism contending over ... faith, which is founded on the second head.

units.la: II. Prouidendum est constantius per hoc sacrum concilium ad extirpationem ... dationem errantium, quanto qui errant plures sunt potentiores & maiores. Quod si quis dixerit bella suscitabunt, diffamat eos ninis, neque ei leviter credi debet.
units.tr: II. Provision must be made by this holy Council more steadily for the extirpation ... of those in error, in proportion as those who err are more numerous, more powerful and greater. If anyone says that they will stir up wars, he slanders them; nor ought such a man to be lightly believed.

units.la: III. Prouidendum est ad emendationem errantium per eos, qui se dicunt ... lantiori sollicitudine quam per extraneos, ceteris paribus.
units.tr: III. Provision must be made for the amendment of those in error through those who call themselves ... with a greater care than through outsiders, other things being equal.

units.la: IV. Praestantes scienter impedimentum, ne errantes resipiscant & corde credant ad iustitiam, & ore faciant confessionem ad salutem, habendi sunt hostes capitales errantium & salutis eorum.
units.tr: IV. Those who knowingly hinder the errant from coming to repentance, and from believing in the heart unto righteousness and making confession with the mouth unto salvation, are to be regarded as capital enemies of the errant and of their salvation.

units.la: V. Praestantes scienter impedimentum, ne tollantur errores, & errantes corrigantur, reddituri sunt rationem de damnis omnibus tam spiritualibus quam temporalibus, quae obinde pervenerunt aut veniant.
units.tr: V. Those who knowingly hinder the removal of errors and the correction of those in error will have to give account for all the damages, both spiritual and temporal, which have come or will come from this.

units.la: VI. Omissio seu dissimulatio praestantium impedimentum nedum positiue, sed priuatiue vel omissiue, directe vel indirecte, per cautelas humanas ne tollantur errores, causat suspicionem de fautoria haereticae pravitatis, quandoque leuem, quandoque vehementem, quandoque conuincentem iuxta varietatem obligationum.
units.tr: VI. The omission or dissimulation of those who hinder, not only positively but also privatively or by omission, directly or indirectly, through human precautions, that errors be not removed, causes suspicion of favouring heretical depravity: sometimes slight, sometimes grave, sometimes convicting, according to the variety of obligations.

units.la: VII. Inexcusabilior & aliquando perniciosior est error in principiis legis naturalis, sicut sunt praecepta Decalogi secundum planum & visitatum intellectum verborum apud omnes utentes ratione, quam sit error in articulis fidei, qui sunt supra naturae facultatem, & in agibilibus quam speculabilibus.
units.tr: VII. An error concerning the principles of the natural law, such as the precepts of the Decalogue according to the plain and customary sense of the words among all who use reason, is more inexcusable and sometimes more pernicious than an error concerning the articles of faith, which lie above the power of nature, and more in matters of action than in matters of speculation.

units.la: VIII. Conditionalis protestatio vel confessio non sufficit ad purgationem legitimam super publicatione vel defensione vel annotatione errorum, quorum oppositas veritates tenetur errans explicita fide tenere.
units.tr: VIII. A conditional protestation or confession is not sufficient for legitimate purgation concerning the publication, defence or annotation of errors, the opposite truths of which the erring person is bound to hold by explicit faith.

units.la: IX. Diffamatus publice & notorie super publicatione aut defensione errorum contrariorum rectae fidei & moribus, tenetur seipsum purgare si potest coram iudice legitimo, etiam nemine eum personaliter accusante. Tenetur enim seruare famam propriam, & ab aliis scandala praestita remouere.
units.tr: IX. One who is publicly and notoriously defamed for the publication or defence of errors contrary to the right faith and morals is bound to clear himself, if he can, before a lawful judge, even though no one accuses him personally. For he is bound to preserve his own good name and to remove from others the scandals he has caused.

units.la: X. Pax regnorum per Christianitatem vix potest efficacius & diuinius procurari, quam per legitimam extirpationem errorum & correctionem errantium.
units.tr: X. The peace of kingdoms throughout Christendom can scarcely be secured more effectively or more divinely than through the lawful extirpation of errors and the correction of those in error.

units.la: XI. Quaerere prouisionem super extirpatione errorum & correptione errantium non est impedire persecutionis vnionem ecclesiae, sed est eam iuuare & accelerare multis attentis: ita vt verum sit, quod oportet vnum facere, & aliud non omittere.
units.tr: XI. To seek provision for the extirpation of errors and the correction of those in error is not to hinder the union of the Church against persecution, but rather to help and hasten it, with many things considered: so that it is true that one must do the one thing and not omit the other.

units.la: TRACTA-
units.tr: TRACTA-

units.la: TRACTATVS MAGISTRI IOHANNIS DE GERSON: QVOMODO ET AN LICEAT IN CAVSIS FIDEI A SVMMO PONTIFICE appellare, seu eius iudicium declinare.
units.tr: Treatise of Master John Gerson: How, and Whether, It Is Lawful in Matters of Faith to Appeal from the Supreme Pontiff, or to Decline His Judgment.

units.la: VAeritur, vtrum haec assertio sit catholica, tam iure diuinitus promulgato quam etiam humano: quibus sacrorum canonum autoritas innititur: Nulli fas est a supremo iudice, videlicet Apostolica sede seu Romano pontifice, Iesu Christi vicario in terris appellare: aut illius iudicium in causis fidei, quae tanquam maiores ad ipsum & sedem Apostolicam deferenda sunt, declinare? Arguitur quod sic, autoritate sanctissimi Domini Martini Papae quinti in sua constitutione ad perpetuam rei memoriam facta, & promulgata in consistorio generali celebrato Constantiae 6. idus Martii pontificatus sui anno primo: vbi reperitur haec assertio, sicut dicitur & videtur in canonum litera manifeste fundari.
units.tr: The question is whether this assertion is Catholic, according to both the law promulgated by God and human law, on which the authority of the sacred canons rests: No one may lawfully appeal from the supreme judge, namely the Apostolic See or the Roman Pontiff, Vicar of Jesus Christ on earth, nor decline his judgment in matters of faith, which must be referred to him and to the Apostolic See as to the greater authority? It is argued that it is so, on the authority of the most holy lord Martin V, Pope, in his constitution made and promulgated for a perpetual memorial at the general consistory held at Constance on 6 March in the first year of his pontificate. There this assertion is found, and it is said and seen to be manifestly grounded in the letter of the canons.

units.la: ARguitur in oppositum primo autoritate determinationis siue constitutionis generalis Concilii Constantiensis. Quae determinatio multipliciter facta est & practicata, & specialiter in sessione publica celebrata die 6. Aprilis, Anno M. CCCCXV. quae sic habet inter cetera: Et primo declarat quod sancta synodus in Spiritu sancto legitime congregata generale concilium faciens & ecclesiam catholicam militantem repraesentans, potestatem a Christo immediate habet, cui quilibet cuiuscunque status vel dignitatis, etiamsi Papalis existat, obedire tenetur in his, quae pertinent ad fidem & extirpationem dicti schismatis, ac generalem reformationem ecclesiae Dei in capite & in membris. Item declarat, quod quicunque, cuiuscunque status vel dignitatis, etiamsi Papalis existat, qui mandatis, statutis seu ordinationibus huius aut praeceptis sanctae synodi & cuiuscunque alterius concilii generalis legitime congregati, super praemissis seu ad ea pertinentibus, facienda vel faciendis obedire contumaciter contempserit, nisi resipuerit, condigna poenitentia subiiciatur, & debite puniatur: etiam ad alia iuris subsidia si opus fuerit recurrendo.
units.tr: On the contrary, it is argued first from the authority of the decree or general constitution of the Council of Constance. This decree was made and put into practice in many ways, and especially in the public session held on 6 April 1415, which says among other things: First, it declares that the holy synod, lawfully assembled in the Holy Spirit, forming a general council and representing the militant Catholic Church, has its power immediately from Christ; and everyone of whatever state or dignity, even if he be Papal, is bound to obey it in those matters which pertain to the faith, to the extirpation of the said schism, and to the general reformation of the Church of God in head and in members. Likewise it declares that whoever, of whatever state or dignity, even if Papal, shall stubbornly refuse to obey the mandates, statutes or ordinances of this holy synod or of any other lawfully assembled general council, concerning or pertaining to the aforesaid matters, unless he repents, shall be subjected to a fitting penance and duly punished, even by having recourse to the other remedies of law if need be.

units.la: Deinceps arguitur rationibus ducentibus ad inconvenientia manifesta contra ius diuinum pariter & humanum:
units.tr: Next it is argued by reasons leading to manifest inconveniences against divine and human law alike:

units.la: SEqueretur enim primo, quod Papa non subiiceretur legi diuinae vel euangelicae: quae generaliter absque omni exceptione promulgata est a Christo Matth. 18. dum loqueretur ad personam Petri, sicut tradit ecclesia, & circumstantia textus satis indicat: Si peccauerit in te frater tuus &c. Sequitur, die ecclesiae: quod si ecclesiam non audierit, sit tibi sicut ethnicus & publicanus &c. Hoc autem consequens est erroneum manifeste: quoniam Papa est frater noster: alioquin non deberet dicere, Pater noster, si non simus fratres ipse & nos: sed haberet dicere, pater meus vel pater mi: sed nec cardinales nec episcopos fratres appellare deberet. Denique constat, quod est proximus noster & ex consequenti frater: non obstante, quod pater sit. Est insuper Papa peccabilis: quoniam circumdatus est infirmitate, sicut notatur ad Hebr. 5.
units.tr: For it would follow, first, that the Pope would not be subject to the divine or evangelical law, which was promulgated by Christ without any exception in general terms, Matt. 18., when he spoke to Peter as a person, as the Church teaches, and the context of the text sufficiently indicates: If your brother sins against you, etc. It follows: Tell it to the Church; but if he refuses to hear the Church, let him be to you as a heathen and a tax collector, etc. But this consequence is plainly false, since the Pope is our brother. Otherwise he ought not to say Our Father, if he and we were not brothers; he would have to say "my father" or "my father" only. Nor would he be bound to call cardinals and bishops brothers. Finally, it is clear that he is our neighbour and therefore our brother, even though he is a father. Moreover, the Pope is capable of sin, since he is surrounded by weakness, as is noted Heb. 5.

units.la: Sequeretur secundo, quod Paulus egisset contra ius diuinum & humanum, dum restitit Petro in faciem, hoc est publice & coram ecclesiae congregatione, sicut habetur ad Gal. 2. Haec enim resistentia non fuit minor provocatio Pauli contra Petrum, quam fuisset appellatio ad ecclesiam: immo fuit aequivalenter appellatio. Vnde etsi Petrus desistere noluisset, fuisset ab ecclesia condemnandus. Constat autem, quod Petrus erat summus pontifex, & secundum Doctores confirmatus in fide & gratia post pentecosten. Propterea dicunt, quod Petrus non errabat in fide, nec haereticabat: sed tantummodo nimis dissimulanter se habebat circa obseruationem legalium. Dicebat ideo Paulus, quod non recte ambulabat ad veritatem euangelii, & quod reprehensibilis erat. Ex quibus palam elicitur, quod summus pontifex, qui succedit Petro in apostolatu, reprehendi potest publice per Doctorem theologum, qui in officio praedicationis succedit Paulo, etiam vbi non haereticaret vel erraret in fide. Et hoc similiter elicitur generalius & inconcussibilius ex autoritate proxime allegata: Si peccauerit in te frater tuus: quemadmodum pluries in sacro Constantiensi Concilio latissime deductum est in sermonibus publicis & multiplicibus scripturis, quorum copiae sunt apud multos.
units.tr: It would follow, secondly, that Paul acted against divine and human law when he withstood Peter to his face, that is, publicly and before the assembly of the Church, as is recorded Gal. 2. For that resistance was no lesser challenge of Paul against Peter than an appeal to the Church would have been; indeed it was in effect an appeal. Hence, if Peter had been unwilling to desist, he would have been condemned by the Church. Yet it is certain that Peter was the supreme pontiff, and, according to the Doctors, confirmed in faith and grace after Pentecost. Therefore they say that Peter did not err in faith nor was he a heretic, but only behaved too evasively in observing the legal rites. Paul therefore said that he was not walking uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, and that he was blameworthy. From these things it is plainly drawn that the supreme pontiff, who succeeds Peter in the apostolate, can be publicly rebuked by a theologian teacher, who in the office of preaching succeeds Paul, even where he is not heretical or in error in faith. This is likewise drawn, more generally and more unshakeably, from the authority just cited: If your brother sins against you, as has often been set out at length in the holy Council of Constance, in public sermons and in many writings, of which there are plenty in the hands of many.

units.la: Sequeretur tertio, quod Papa, qui est membrum corporis ecclesiae, sicut homines alii, si scandalizaret totum corpus, ipse non esset rescindendus, vt totum corpus sanum fieret: contra doctrinam Christi euangelicam fundatam in similitudine iuris naturalis Matth. 18. cum Glossis & determinationibus Doctorum in materia de scandalo se fundantium in hac lege diuina & naturali.
units.tr: It would follow, thirdly, that the Pope, who is a member of the body of the Church as other men are, if he gave scandal to the whole body, would not be cut off, so that the whole body might be made sound. This is contrary to the evangelical teaching of Christ, grounded in the likeness of natural law, Matt. 18., together with the glosses and determinations of the Doctors on the matter of scandal, which rest on this divine and natural law.

units.la: Sequeretur quarto, quod Petrus summus pontifex non debuisset compelli reddere rationem ab Apostolis & fratribus, qui erant in Iudaea, quia visitauerat Cornelium gentilem, cuius tamen oppositum dicitur expresse Act. 11. cum adisset Petrus Hierosolymam, scil. vbi erat ecclesia, disceptabant aduersus illum, qui erant ex circumcisione dicentes: quare introisti ad viros praeputium habentes & manducasti cum illis? Et statim subiungitur obedientiae Petri responsio, dans in hoc successoribus suis formam debitae humilitatis: expressit epistolae suae primae c. 3. Paratī, inquit, semper ad satisfactionem omni poscenti vos rationem de ea quae in vobis est fide & spe. Quod si in destructione fidei tumus aliquis pontifex volens superbire nollet hoc facere, constat quod a fratribus aeque posset accusari, sicut & Petrus.
units.tr: It would follow, fourthly, that Peter, the supreme pontiff, should not have been compelled to give an account by the Apostles and brethren who were in Judea, because he had visited the Gentile Cornelius. Yet the opposite is stated expressly, Acts 11., where, when Peter had gone up to Jerusalem, that is, to where the Church was, those who were of the circumcision contended with him, saying: Why did you go in to men uncircumcised and eat with them? And immediately Peter's reply of obedience is added, giving in this his successors a pattern of due humility. He expressed it in his first epistle, chapter 3: Being ready always, he says, to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the faith and hope that are in you. But if some pontiff, in order to destroy the faith, were to be arrogant and refuse to do this, it is certain that he could be accused by the brethren just as Peter was.

units.la: Sequeretur quinto, quod aliquis iniuriato per Papam sicut potest euenire, tam in corpore quàm in membris, imo & in fama, circa ea quæ fidei sunt, non pateret in casu dabili aliqua defensio vel grauaminis subleuatio, quod est contra ius naturale, cui ius diuinum non repugnat. Patet tamen consequentia dato casu tali vel simili. Sit Petrus, qui prædicet coram Papa & multitudine populi copiosa, quod Christus fuit verus propheta, iubeat tunc Papa quod detrudatur in carcerem, eo quòd prædicat istam veritatem. Sentiat Petrus, quòd si appellet ad concilium generale submittendo se eidem, quod populus protegeret eum, nec scandalizabitur in doctrina eius, sed manebit in recta fide, quod Christus fuerit verus propheta: si autem non appellauerit, populus reputabit quod Papa verum dicat & bene faciat, & ita deserat fidem cum prædicato suo. Quæritur in casu, si Petrus dicere poterit, concilium appello? quemadmodum Paulus timens à seditiosis occidi, clamauit: Cæsarem appello. Hanc autem materiam latissime & studiosissime prosecutus est & fundauit Ockam in Dialogo suo, cuius solius auctoritati non oportet inniti, quamuis fuerit egregius theologus, sed innitendum est rationibus suis, pro quanto robur & auctoritatem accipiunt à sacra scriptura: cuius contemptus cum suis professoribus saepe duxit & ducet in errores.
units.tr: It would follow, fifthly, that if someone were wronged by the Pope, as may happen both in body and in members, and even in reputation, in matters concerning the faith, then in such a case no defence and no relief from the grievance would be open to him, which is contrary to natural law, to which divine law is not opposed. Yet the consequence holds given such a case or a similar one. Let there be Peter, who preaches before the Pope and a large crowd of people that Christ was a true prophet, and let the Pope then order him to be thrown into prison because he preaches this truth. Peter perceives that if he appeals to a general council, submitting himself to it, the people would protect him, and he would not be led into scandal by its teaching but would remain in the right faith that Christ was a true prophet. But if he did not appeal, the people would judge that the Pope speaks truly and does well, and so would abandon the faith together with his preaching. The question arises in this case: could Peter say, "I appeal to the council," as Paul, fearing to be killed by the seditious, cried out, I appeal to Caesar? This matter has been pursued and grounded most fully and most diligently by Ockham in his Dialogue. Yet one ought not to rest on his authority alone, however outstanding a theologian he was; one must rest on his reasons, insofar as they receive strength and authority from Holy Scripture. Contempt for this Scripture, together with its professors, has often led, and will lead, into error.

units.la: Sequeretur sexto, quod in nullo casu Papa posset iudicari vel deponi per generale concilium, quantumcunque criminosus esset vel scandalosus ecclesiæ. Patet consequentia, quoniam ex opposito sequitur oppositum. Si enim Papa potest iudicari vel deponi per generale concilium: ipse poterit denunciari per aliquem vel aliquos coram concilio præsenti vel futuro, Qui si velit grauamen inferre talibus denunciare volentibus: nonne poterunt ipsi se ponere extra manus suas vel potestate, ne de facto grauet eos & opprimat iniuste. Hoc autem facere est vere & æquiualenter ab eodem appellare. Et hoc practicatum est in concilio Pisano per utrumque collegiorum duarum obedientiarum, scil. Gregorii & Benedicti sic in suis obedientiis nuncupatorum. Hoc etiam practicatum est per quosque Reges & principes, qui se subtraxerunt ab obedientia illorum, quos isti vel illi iudicabant esse summos pontifices, quæ tamen subtractiones approbatæ sunt per sacrum Constantiense Concilium; quædam expresse, quædam implicite vel æquiualenter.
units.tr: It would follow, sixthly, that in no case could the Pope be judged or deposed by a general council, however criminal or scandalous he might be to the Church. The consequence is clear, since the opposite follows from the opposite. For if the Pope can be judged or deposed by a general council, then he could be denounced by someone or some people before a present or future council. If he were willing to inflict harm on those who wished to denounce him, could they not place themselves outside his hands and power, lest he in fact burden and unjustly oppress them? But to do this is truly and equivalently to appeal from him. This was indeed put into practice at the Council of Pisa by both colleges of the two obediences, namely those of Gregory and of Benedict, as they were called within their obediences. It was also put into practice by various kings and princes, who withdrew from obedience to those whom this or that party judged to be the supreme pontiffs. These withdrawals were approved by the holy Council of Constance, some expressly, some implicitly or equivalently.

units.la: Sequeretur septimo & magis ad hominem: quod Concilium generale non esset supra Papam, vel iudex Papæ legitimus: cuius oppositum determinauit & practicauit sacrum Constan. Concil. Non n. processum est ad inchoandū depositionē Ioannis, quousque fuisset articulus iste declaratus: sicut apparet ex actis eiusdem concilii: quoniā aliqui videbantur super hoc hæsitare. Constat a quo ab omni homine, qui habet legitimū superiorē iudicē, siue sit vnus homo siue vna communitas, potest si rationabilis & vrgens imminear causa, fieri appellatio ad eundem iudicem. Et si dicatur, prout aliqui fingere volunt, quod concilium non est supra Papam, nisi quando est hæreticus seu deuius à fide, in quo casu non est mirū inquiūt, si concilii sit supra talē Papā, quia desiit esse Papa, & est inferior omni homine: & ita niuntur etiam inuadere illā ineuasibilē Christi legem: Si peccauerit in te frater tuus &c. Hoc breuiter ad psens respondetur. Primo quia Ioannes nō est accusatus vel cōuictus de hæretica prauitate: & tamē concilii vocauit & iudicauit ipsum tanquam suū subditū. Vnde & in toto processu vsq; post sententiā diffinitiuā suæ depositionis, reputatus est ab eodē concilio verus Papa. Amplius, nō est verū quòd Papa eo facto, quo cadit in hæresim, plertim latenter, sit depositus à Papatu: sicut nec est verū de aliis episcopis, quēadmodū ista materia declarata est alibi latius, reducendo hac opinione ad multiplex inconueniens, sicut ad incertitudinē ecclesiasticæ politiæ & susceptionis sacramentorū: & ad fauorabilitate damnatæ doctrinæ Ioannis Wicleff, quæ principaliter innitebatur tali fundamento, quòd nullus existens in peccato mortali erat Papa vel episcopus, nec consecrabat &c. Et qui bene ponderat causas reprobationis huius doctrinæ Wicleff in hac parte: illæ vel similes causæ concludunt, quòd peccatū hæresis licet reddat vnum platū dignū depositione iuncta ptinacia, nō tamē reddit eū depositū eo facto, sed requiritur humana depositio. Sicut n. nulla sanctitas quantūcunq; magna constituit aliquē in statu Papali vel episcopali, nisi per electionē humanā de lege cōmuni, contra opinionē Waldensiū: ita nulla iniquitas remouet aliquē ab episcopali gradu vel Papali de cōmuni lege, si non interueniat humana depositio. Amplius tertio quo ad hoc arguitur, quod concilium sit iudex Papæ non hæretici, imo sancti, assignando casus multos, in quibus aliquis episcopus verus Papa poterit per multos testes diffamari de hæretica prauitate seu fautoria hæresis, aut per vehementes coniecturas ex operibus & conuersatione diffamatur apud multos & graues populos, quòd non recte ambulat ad veritatem euangelii: aut quod lapsus est in hæresim iam damnatā, aut quòd nouā velit confingere. Constat quòd existente generali concilio vel proxime futuro, poterit idē Papa iudicialiter compelli, vt purget se, quemadmodū exemplificatū est de Petro. Quod si nollet hoc facere, sicut facere noluit Marcellinus sine accusatione sua de idololatria: nonne concilii posset consequenter ad depositionis suæ sententiā procedere? Et si dicatur quod nō, ex quo nō est hæreticus. Respond. quòd apud iudicū ecclesiæ, vbi circa ea quæ facti sunt, fallere potest & falli, simile est iudiciū de his quæ nō apparet & quæ nō sunt. Et p hoc eliditur manifeste friuola responsio dicentiū Papā nō subiici correctioni fraternæ aut iudiciali iussæ à Christo vbi prius: Si pecca
units.tr: It would follow, seventhly and more pointedly against the man himself, that a general council would not be above the Pope, nor a lawful judge of the Pope. The holy Council of Constance determined and practised the opposite of this. For proceedings to depose John did not begin until this article had been declared, as appears from the acts of the same council, since some seemed to hesitate over it. It is agreed that from any man who has a lawful superior judge, whether he be a single man or a community, an appeal may be made to that same judge when a reasonable and pressing cause arises. But if it is said, as some like to pretend, that the council is not above the Pope unless he is a heretic or has departed from the faith, and that in that case it is no wonder if the council is above such a Pope, since he has ceased to be Pope and is inferior to every man, then they are also trying to override that unassailable law of Christ: "If your brother sins against you," and so on. This is briefly answered as follows. First, John was not accused of, or convicted of, heretical depravity, and yet the council summoned and judged him as its own subject. Hence, throughout the whole process, right up to the final sentence of his deposition, the same council regarded him as the true Pope. Furthermore, it is not true that the Pope is deposed from the papacy by the very fact that he falls into heresy, and that most often in secret; nor is it true of other bishops. This matter has been explained more fully elsewhere, where this opinion is shown to lead to many absurdities, such as uncertainty in ecclesiastical government and in the reception of the sacraments, and to the support of the condemned doctrine of John Wycliffe, which rested chiefly on this foundation: that no one who is in mortal sin is a Pope or a bishop, nor can he consecrate, and so on. Whoever weighs carefully the reasons for the condemnation of Wycliffe's doctrine on this point will see that these or similar reasons prove that the sin of heresy, although it makes a man worthy of deposition when joined with obstinacy, does not by that very fact depose him; a human deposition is required. For just as no holiness, however great, places anyone in the papal or episcopal office except by human election according to the common law (contrary to the opinion of the Waldensians), so no wickedness removes anyone from the episcopal or papal rank by common law, unless a human deposition intervenes. Thirdly, it is argued on this point that the council is the judge of a Pope who is not a heretic but holy. It cites many cases in which a bishop who is a true Pope may be defamed before many witnesses for heretical depravity or for favouring heresy; or he may be defamed before many serious people by strong conjectures drawn from his works and conduct, to the effect that he does not walk rightly according to the truth of the gospel; or that he has fallen into a heresy already condemned, or that he wishes to devise a new one. It is clear that, when a general council is in session or about to meet, the same Pope may be compelled judicially to clear himself, as was shown in the case of Peter. But if he were unwilling to do this, as Marcellinus was unwilling to clear himself without accusation of idolatry, could not the council then proceed consequently to a sentence of deposition? And if it is said that it could not, since he is not a heretic, the answer is that before a judge of the Church, where he can err and be deceived about matters of fact, the judgment concerns things that do not appear and things that do not exist, which is much the same. By this the frivolous answer of those who say that the Pope is not subject to fraternal or judicial correction, which Christ ordered earlier, is plainly refuted: "If he sins..."

units.la: Sequeretur octauo & ad hominē multiplex inconueniens, in ciuitate fuisse quæ adpdictæ assertioni, nullatenus existimandi sunt concedere velle. Et primum est adhuc Papa, sicut prius, & ita quòd sanctissimus Dominus noster Papa: quod ideo Dominus noster & suū collegiū sunt p sacrū Const Conc. inuiolabiliter obseruare; Cuius tamen oppositum dixit, quòd Imperator nō est cōfirmatus in Imperiū: quòd grauiter peccauerunt... Domini Domino nostro summo pontifici tanquam Papæ. Denique Petrus de Luna fuisset iniuste & perperam accusatus in concilio de materia haeresis praecipue & principaliter. Quoniam in quadam constitutione, quae de verbo ad verbum ponitur in actis concilii, ipse conatus fuit determinare, quod nunquam licitum est aut fuit facere subtractionem ab eo, neque ab alio vero Papa: fundans se in hoc, quod Papa non habeat superius iudicium in terris, nec potest ab aliquo iudicari. Haec autem iudicata fuit haereticalis constitutio, & ita de plurimis inconvenientibus diceretur.
units.tr: It would follow, eighthly and against the man himself, that there are many absurdities, and that those who are in the state to which the aforesaid assertion refers should by no means be thought willing to concede them. The first is that he is still Pope, as before, and so our most holy Lord the Pope; and that for this reason our Lord and his college are to be inviolably observed by the holy Council of Constance. Yet the opposite was said: that the Emperor was not confirmed in the empire, and that they had grievously sinned ... the Lords to our Lord the supreme pontiff, as Pope. Finally, Peter de Luna would have been unjustly and wrongly accused in the council, chiefly and principally on the matter of heresy. For in a certain decree, which is set out word for word in the acts of the council, he himself tried to determine that it had never been lawful, nor was it ever lawful, to withdraw obedience from him or from any other true Pope, grounding himself on the claim that the Pope has no superior judgment on earth and cannot be judged by anyone. But that decree was judged to be heretical; and so the same could be said of many absurdities.

units.la: Postremo dimissis illis, quae sunt in facto circa iustificationem vel iniustificationem appellationis dominorum Polonorum: nam multa hinc & inde diversa, imo adversa & contraria videntur asseri, circa quae theologicum negotium non versatur, nisi pro quanto sub regulis generalibus & authenticis daretur ars, sicut & data est convincendi aliquem de pertinacia & fautoria haereticae pravitatis. Conuertatur tandem inquisitio particulatae quaestionis circa ultimam particulam suam, quae sic habet: quod nulli fas est &c. illius (videlicet Apostolicae sedis seu Romani pontificis) iudicium in causis fidei, quae tanquam maiores ad ipsum & sedem Apostolicam deferenda sunt, declinare.
units.tr: Finally, setting aside those matters which concern the fact of the justification or non-justification of the appeal of the Polish lords (for many things are asserted on either side, indeed adverse and contrary things, and these do not belong to theological business, except in so far as an art might be given under general and authentic rules, just as an art is given for convicting someone of obstinacy and favouring heretical depravity), let us at last turn the inquiry to the particular question concerning its last clause, which reads thus: that no one is permitted to decline the judgment of him (namely of the Apostolic See or of the Roman pontiff) in causes of faith, which, as being greater, are to be referred to him and to the Apostolic See.

units.la: Sunt aliqui, sicut dicitur, qui minus istam particulam reputant sustinibilem quam praecedentem: qualificantes eam quod est palam haereticalis, & totius ecclesiasticae hierarchiae circa fidei defensionem seu conservationem finalem & resolutivam subvertit. Nituntur autem fundare dictum suum in aliquibus propositionibus, quas reputant catholicas veritates.
units.tr: There are some, as it is said, who regard this clause as less tolerable than the preceding one. They characterise it as openly heretical, and as subverting the whole ecclesiastical hierarchy with regard to the defence of the faith and its final and decisive preservation. They try to base their claim on certain propositions which they consider Catholic truths.

units.la: Prima Propositio.
units.tr: First Proposition.

units.la: IN causis fidei iudicium inniti debet infallibili regulae, sic quod ultimus & supremus iudex, cuius sententiae necessario standum est tanquam verae catholicae, non sit a fide deviabilis; alioquin statret in casu; quod homines obligarentur assentire contra fidem.
units.tr: In matters of faith, judgment ought to rest on an infallible rule, so that the ultimate and supreme judge, whose sentence must necessarily be followed as true and Catholic, cannot deviate from the faith. Otherwise it would follow in such a case that men were bound to assent against the faith.

units.la: Secunda propositio. In causis fidei non habetur in terra iudex infallibilis, vel qui non sit deviabilis a fide de lege communi; praeter ipsam ecclesiam universalem, vel concilium generale eam sufficienter repraesentans.
units.tr: Second proposition. In matters of faith there is no infallible judge on earth, or one who cannot deviate from the faith by common law, apart from the universal Church itself or a general council sufficiently representing it.

units.la: Tertia propositio. In causis fidei nullus particularis homo per suam determinationem potest de propositione non haeretica facere haereticam, sicut nec de catholica non catholicam, ita nec Papa nec episcopus proprie & vere loquendo possunt propositionem aliquam haereticare. Possunt tamen propositionem aliquam, quae videtur aliquibus non haeretica, declarare quod sit haeretica, & hoc iudicialiter, sicut Doctores scholastice hoc faciunt, vel doctrinaliter. Et hoc appellatur facere articulum, diversimode tamen, quia Papae determinatio poenalis extendit se ad omnes fideles: sed episcopalis tantummodo ad subditos suos, ut precise est episcopalis.
units.tr: Third proposition. In matters of faith no particular man can, by his own determination, make a non-heretical proposition heretical, any more than he can make a Catholic one non-Catholic. So neither the Pope nor a bishop, speaking properly and truly, can make any proposition heretical. They can, however, declare that some proposition which seems to some people not heretical is heretical, and they can do this judicially, as the scholastic doctors do, or doctrinally. This is called making an article, though in different ways: the Pope's penal determination extends to all the faithful, but an episcopal one extends only to his subjects, insofar as it is precisely episcopal.

units.la: Quarta propositio. In causis fidei nulla determinatio iudicialis episcopi, imo nec Papae solius praecise, ut est episcopi vel Papae, ligat fideles ad credendum, quod ita sit de veritate fidei; sicut praetendit sua declaratio, quoniam tam Papa, quam episcopus deviabiles sunt a fide: obligat tamen subditos sub poena excommunicationis talis determinatio, quod non dogmatizent oppositum talis determinationis; nisi appareat manifesta ratio repugnandi vel per sacram scripturam, vel per revelationem, vel per ecclesiae seu generalis concilii determinationem.
units.tr: Fourth proposition. In matters of faith, no judicial determination of a bishop, nor even of the Pope alone precisely as bishop or Pope, binds the faithful to believe, as a truth of faith, that it is so, as its declaration claims, since both Pope and bishop can deviate from the faith. Yet such a determination does bind subjects, under penalty of excommunication, not to teach the opposite of the determination, unless a manifest reason for opposing it appears, either from Holy Scripture, or from revelation, or from the determination of the Church or of a general council.

units.la: Quinta propositio. In causis fidei sicut potest declinari iudicium episcopi, si appareat deviius a fide, & requiri iudicium Papae: sic de Papa respectu generalis concilii suo modo dici potest. Et haec est ad formam responsiva sequens ex praemissis: iuncto quod apud summum pontificem & eius sedem Romanam potest esse quandoque, raritas peritorum in sacris literis; & in vera fide probatorum magis, quam apud quoldam ex ipsis, qui generalia habent studia sacrae scripturae & aliarum facultatum.
units.tr: Fifth proposition. In matters of faith, just as the judgment of a bishop may be declined if he appears to deviate from the faith, and the judgment of the Pope sought, so the same can be said of the Pope with respect to a general council, in its own way. This is the answer in form that follows from the premises, given that at the supreme pontiff and his Roman see there can at times be a scarcity of experts in Holy Letters, and of men more proven in the true faith, than among some of those who hold general studies of Holy Scripture and of the other faculties.

units.la: Sexta propositio. In causis fidei illa causa dicitur maior esse, non quae est de re maiori, sicut de trinitate & unitate personarum: sed quae difficilis est & ambigua ad determinandum iuxta textum scripturae Exodi 18. Deut. 17. & 2. Paral. 19. In quibus fundantur canones dicentes, quod causae maiores fidei sunt ad sedem Apostolicam referendae.
units.tr: Sixth proposition. In matters of faith, that cause is called greater which is not concerned with a greater matter, such as the Trinity and the unity of the persons, but which is difficult and ambiguous to determine, according to the text of Scripture in Exodus 18, Deuteronomy 17, and 2 Chronicles 19. On these texts are founded the canons which say that the greater causes of faith are to be referred to the Apostolic See.

units.la: Septima propositio. In causis fidei poterit una causa dici maior apud aliquem episcopum vel dioecesim: quae apud alium episcopum vel dioecesim non reputabitur esse maior, vel ad superiorem sicut ad Papam remittenda: quia scil. apud talem episcopum vel dioecesim propter abundantiam theologorum causa talis non reputabitur difficilis vel ambigua; sed per sacram scripturam iam damnata vel approbata.
units.tr: Seventh proposition. In matters of faith, one cause may be considered greater before one bishop or diocese, and yet before another bishop or diocese it will not be regarded as greater, nor need it be remitted to a superior such as the Pope. For before such a bishop or diocese, on account of the abundance of theologians, such a cause will not be regarded as difficult or ambiguous, but as already condemned or approved by Holy Scripture.

units.la: Octava propositio. In causis fidei non minus aliquando occurrendum est sive per episcopum, sive per summum pontificem, sive per generale concilium; dum cernuntur oriri scandala & errores crudeles & impii contra pacificum conventum Christiani populi, qui maxime consistit in observatione mandatorum Dei de servando iuramento, & de non interficiendo homines authoritate propria, & de non praestando ad usuram, vel de non rapiendo, vel de non adulterando: quam dum insurgunt errores contra aliquos de articulis fidei qui numerati sunt in symbolo.
units.tr: Eighth proposition. In matters of faith, action must sometimes be taken no less by a bishop, or by the supreme pontiff, or by a general council, whenever scandals and cruel and impious errors are seen to arise against the peaceful agreement of the Christian people. That agreement consists chiefly in the observance of God's commandments: keeping oaths, not killing men on one's own authority, not lending at usury, not stealing, and not committing adultery. Errors rise up against some of the articles of faith which are enumerated in the Creed.

units.la: Formant igitur rationem suam, qui praedictam particulam impugnant iuxta propositiones praemissas, praesertim iuxta quinq; primas. Fas est in casibus concernentibus causas fidei declinare illius iudicium, qui reperiretur deuius à fide, vel eis, quae fidei sunt, cum suis consiliariis vehementer suspectus, per aperta signa nimiae dissimulationis vel acceptionis personarum, vel aliunde multis modis: sed (loquendo semper cum reverentia) staret aliquem summum pontificem cum suo collegio sic posse deficere circa ea, quae fidei sunt, quemadmodum Petrus & alii Apostoli defecerunt in passione: imo quod minus videretur, sicut Petrus deficiebat, nec recte ambulabat ad veritatem evangelii, & reprehensibilis erat, dum Paulus sibi restitit in faciem: ac perinde declinabat eius iudicium: ergo fas est interdum summi pontificis iudicium in causis fidei declinare.
units.tr: Those who attack the aforesaid part therefore frame their argument from the premises above, especially the first five. It is lawful, in cases concerning matters of faith, to decline the judgment of one who is found to deviate from the faith, or who is strongly suspected, with his counsellors, in matters of faith, through open signs of excessive dissimulation or of acceptance of persons, or in many other ways. But (always speaking with reverence) it may stand that some supreme pontiff, with his college, could so fail in matters of faith as Peter and the other apostles failed at the Passion. Indeed, what would seem even less, Peter was faltering and not walking uprightly toward the truth of the gospel, and was open to reproof when Paul withstood him to his face; and so Paul declined his judgment. Therefore it is sometimes lawful to decline the judgment of the supreme pontiff in matters of faith.

units.la: Haec autem dicta sunt vel argumentata magis ad veritatis inquisitionem, quam ad aliquius, praesertim sanctissimi Domini Martini Papae reprehensionem: attento quod constitutio sua quantum ad illa quae fundatur in facto, non iacet sub theologica reprehensione: & quantum ad alia quae ius concernunt, sicut est praedicta pars excepta. Dicerent benevoli sui, quod non obstantibus allegationibus in oppositum illam potest suscipere rationabilem & veram interpretationem: sicut recipiunt constitutiones positivae decretis insertae, quibus innititur. Sic intelligendo, quod non est fas appellare à Papa, vel eius iudicium in causis fidei declinare: non quidem pro omni casu: sed quando facit id, quod in se est, & quando non apparet deuius à fide, sed ambulat recte ad veritatem evangelii sine personarum acceptione: quemadmodum in proemio & narratione suae constitutionis dicit esse faciendum per summum pontificem: & quod ita fecit, affirmat. Nam constitutiones & leges secundum Aristot. feruntur vniuersaliter: quamvis in aliquo casu dabili pati possunt instantiam.
units.tr: These things, however, have been said or argued more for the inquiry after truth than for the reproof of anyone, especially of the most holy lord Pope Martin. For his constitution, insofar as it rests on fact, does not lie under theological reproof, and insofar as it concerns law, the aforesaid part excepted, it does not either. His well-wishers would say that, notwithstanding the allegations to the contrary, it can receive a reasonable and true interpretation, just as positive constitutions receive the decrees inserted into them on which they rest. Understanding it thus: that it is not lawful to appeal from the Pope, or to decline his judgment, in matters of faith, not indeed in every case, but when he does what lies in him to do, and when he does not appear to deviate from the faith, but walks rightly toward the truth of the gospel without acceptance of persons. This is what he says in the preface and narration of his constitution ought to be done by the supreme pontiff, and he affirms that he has so done. For constitutions and laws, according to Aristotle, are framed universally, although in some conceivable case they may admit of an exception.

units.la: Porro Dominus noster tollere poterit efficaciter suspitionem sinistram, quae contra sanctitatem suam fieri posset, si dicta sua factis compensat, hoc est, si sponte, nullo inquirente, damnet doctrinam illam pestiferam & crudelem contra Polonos cum similibus aliis, cum tali celeritate & rigore, qualem fidei materia urgens in scandalum & perniciem reipublicae postulat & requirit, protinus abiecta quavis acceptione personarum.
units.tr: Moreover, our Lord will be able effectively to remove the sinister suspicion which could arise against his holiness, if he matches his words with deeds. That is, if he spontaneously, with no one inquiring, condemns that pestilential and cruel doctrine against the Poles, together with other similar ones, with that speed and rigour which the pressing matter of faith demands and requires, to the scandal and ruin of the commonwealth, casting off at once any acceptance of persons.

units.la: Finit tractatus magistri Iohan. de Gerson sacrae paginae Professoris eximii: quomodo & an liceat in causis fidei à summo pontifice appellare, seu eius iudicium declinare.
units.tr: Here ends the treatise of Master John de Gerson, distinguished professor of sacred page: how and whether it is lawful in matters of faith to appeal from the supreme pontiff, or to decline his judgment.

units.la: LIBELLVS EIVSDEM DO- CTORIS ARTICVLORVM THEOLOGICORVM ET SCHOLASTICE COMPOSITORVM CONTRA PETRVM DE LVNA, ad convincendum eum fuisse & esse notorie haereticum: & pertina- citer errasse & errare contra catholicam & evangelicam veritatem, super potestate & autoritate ecclesiae. Et continet duos tracta- tus. In primo ponuntur generales articuli. In secundo spe- ciales, & subsumpti specialiter ex generalibus.
units.tr: A LITTLE BOOK BY THE SAME DOCTOR, OF THEOLOGICAL ARTICLES COMPOSED IN THE SCHOLASTIC MANNER AGAINST PETER DE LUNA, to convince him that he was and is notoriously a heretic, and has stubbornly erred and continues to err against the Catholic and evangelical truth, concerning the power and authority of the Church. And it contains two treatises. In the first, general articles are set out; in the second, special articles, and drawn specifically from the general ones.

units.la: Primus Articulus.
units.tr: Primus Articulus.

units.la: ET primo constat, quod iste est articulus fidei quod est una sancta catholica & Apostolica ecclesia.
units.tr: And first it is established that this is an article of faith: that there is one holy, catholic and apostolic Church.

units.la: Secundus articulus. Item quod haec unitas ecclesiae non sic dependet à persona Papae essentialiter, quin posset manere una, & maneret de facto, quando nullus est Papa in ecclesia.
units.tr: Second article. Likewise, this unity of the Church does not so depend essentially on the person of the Pope that it could not remain one, and it does in fact remain one when there is no Pope in the Church.

units.la: Tertius articulus. Item quamvis unitas ecclesiastica essentialis sit ad primarium caput Christum, nihilominus unitas altera accidentalis vel secundaria consistit in obedientia ad unum summum pontificem, qui est caput secundarium in ecclesia cum Christo. Sic videlicet, quod quilibet catholicus debet habere promptitudinem seu praeparationem animi ad obediendum vni summo pontifici, dum constiterit sibi aut constare debuerit, quod sit Papa aliquis legitime electus. Et ultra secundo requiritur, quod non ponat scienter impedimentum commissiue vel omissiue, ne praeficiatur ecclesiae Dei unus Papa certus & legitime electus. Ideo non condemnatus est inter caeteras causas Ioannes Huss, quia dicebat, quod ecclesia Dei usque ad consummationem seculi poterat aeque bene regi per sacerdotes dispersos per mundum absque uno capite, sicut cum tali capite. Unde sicut dicunt Theologi, sacramentum confirmationis est sacramentum necessitatis, non quidem simpliciter, cum sine illo staret salus, sed sic quod obligatur quilibet ad non contemnendum suscepti-onem huius sacramenti tempore & loco opportunis, ita proportionabiliter de unione vel adhaesione ad unicum Papam potest intelligi, sicut etiam dici solet apud theologos, quod praeceptum affirmativum, quale est de habendo Papam, obligat ad semper, non pro semper.
units.tr: Third article. Likewise, although the essential ecclesiastical unity is to its primary head, Christ, nevertheless another, accidental or secondary unity consists in obedience to one supreme pontiff, who is the secondary head in the Church together with Christ. That is, every Catholic ought to have a readiness and preparation of mind to obey one supreme pontiff, as long as it is or ought to be evident to him that there is a Pope who has been lawfully elected. And, secondly, it is further required that he not knowingly place an impediment, by commission or omission, to the appointment over the Church of God of one certain and lawfully elected Pope. For this reason John Hus was not condemned among the other charges, because he said that the Church of God could be governed until the end of the world just as well by priests scattered throughout the world without one head as with such a head. Hence, as the theologians say, the sacrament of confirmation is a sacrament of necessity, not indeed absolutely, since salvation would stand without it, but in such a way that everyone is bound not to despise the reception of this sacrament at the proper time and place. In the same proportion, union with or adherence to the one Pope can be understood, just as it is customarily said among the theologians that an affirmative precept, such as that of having a Pope, binds always, but not for always.

units.la: Quartus art. Item culpabilis in priori articulo primo modo vel secundo, vere dicitur fautor & nutritor schismatis, imo & schismaticus, si iungat pertinaciter, id est, si non velit corrigi, quis staret ex hoc solo non esset haereticus, si faceret hoc non ex errore intellectus, sed ex depravatione affectus, quamvis apud ecclesiam habendus esset ille vel haereticus, vel de haeresi vehementer suspectus.
units.tr: Fourth article. Likewise, one who is guilty in the preceding article in the first or second way is truly called a supporter and nurturer of schism, indeed a schismatic, if he persists obstinately, that is, if he is unwilling to be corrected. Yet by this alone he would not be a heretic, if he did this not from an error of the understanding but from a depravity of the will, although in the eyes of the Church he should be regarded either as a heretic or as strongly suspected of heresy.

units.la: Quintus artic. Item ecclesia sic instituta est à Christo pfecto legislatore, quae potest se continuare, & de facto continuabit in unitate usque ad consummationem seculi, & hoc intelligendo nedum de primaria & &c essentiali vnione, quæ est ad Christum: sed de accidentali & secundaria ad summum pontificem: sic quod potest & poterit sibi instituere caput vnum secundarium, quod dicitur Papa. Et quicunq; impedit scienter, committiue vel omissiue talem vnitatem Ecclesiæ, agit contra articulum iam dictum: vnam sanctam catholicam &c. Etiam vbi videretur stare cum prima vnitate ad Christum.
