Inde patet q; aliquis exponens Papa legitime electus potest effici schismaticus, si det impedimentum scienter committiue vel omissiue, quod tota Ecclesia non obediat vno summo pontifici: dum exempli gratia Papa non potest reducere maiorem partem Christianitatis ad obediendum vni capiti, nisi cesserit, & alter constituatur: ipse vero hoc pertinaciter renuit facere, aut in aliquo multiplici casu tali. Simile diceretur de obedientibus vero Papæ, quod possunt esse schismatici, & alii qui non obediunt, sed parati sunt obedire modo prædicto, & apponunt diligentiam suam quod vniatur Ecclesia, sunt immunes à schismate.
units.tr: Fifth article. Likewise, the Church has been so instituted by Christ, the perfect lawgiver, that it can continue itself, and in fact will continue in unity until the end of the world; and this is to be understood not only of the primary and essential union, which is to Christ, but also of the accidental and secondary union to the supreme pontiff, so that it can and will be able to institute for itself one secondary head, who is called the Pope. And whoever knowingly impedes such unity of the Church, by commission or omission, acts against the article already stated: one holy catholic Church, etc. This holds even where he seems to remain consistent with the first unity to Christ. From this it is clear that a Pope, supposing he has been lawfully elected, can become a schismatic if he knowingly places an impediment, by commission or omission, to the whole Church obeying one supreme pontiff; for example, if the Pope cannot bring the greater part of Christendom to obey one head unless he resigns and another is appointed, and yet he obstinately refuses to do so, or in any similar case of this kind. The same would be said of the obedient followers of the Pope: they can be schismatics; and others who do not obey, but are ready to obey in the aforesaid manner and apply their diligence that the Church be united, are free from schism.

units.la: Sextus art. Item, si probetur de aliquo, q; circa prmissa sit hæreticus: hoc est iuxta verba Arg. q; fingat sibi novū errorē, vel antiquū sequatur, gloriæ siue principatus sui causa: pbabitur consequenter manifestissime, q; talis est nedū fautor schismatis, sed vere schismaticus. Et ideo sufficiat in sequentibus coartare sermonem ad hæresim, quoniam ex isto sufficienter concludetur schisma.
units.tr: Sixth article. Likewise, if it is proved of anyone that concerning the foregoing he is a heretic, that is, according to the words of the argument, that he invents for himself a new error or follows an old one for the sake of his glory or principate, it will consequently be most manifestly proved that such a man is not only a supporter of schism but truly a schismatic. And therefore it will suffice in what follows to confine the discussion to heresy, since from that the schism will be sufficiently concluded.

units.la: Septimus art. Item, quod dum nullus est Papa, vel dum lapsus est in hæresim manifestam & iam damnatam, vel dum consentire non potest, quod ecclesia congregetur: quia scil. effectus est amens & insanus incurabiliter, vel incarceratus est taliter, q; haberi non potest accessus ad eū, et à si necessitas vel evidens utilitas imminet, potest se congregare sine Papa. Et idem dicendum est, vbi Papa sufficienter summatus & requisitus pro congregando Ecclesiam ad vniendū eam in fide & moribus, vel ad constituendum sibi Papam certum, noller contumaciter eam convocare. Iste art. sequitur ex prioribus, & ex negatione eius sequeretur, quod Ecclesia non fuisset à Christo perfecte instituta pro sui conservatione & vnitate legitima in membris suis in fide & moribus & ad vnum caput secundarium, verum & certum, quod apertissime est contra Apostolum ad Eph 4. & alibi multis locis, & Osee 1.
units.tr: Seventh article. Likewise, while there is no Pope, or when a man has fallen into manifest heresy already condemned, or when he cannot consent that the Church be assembled, because he has been made insane and incurably mad, or has been imprisoned in such a way that access to him cannot be had, and if necessity or evident advantage threatens, the Church can assemble without the Pope. And the same must be said where the Pope, having been sufficiently summoned and requested to convoke the Church for uniting it in faith and morals, or for appointing for itself a certain and true Pope, obstinately refuses to convoke it. This article follows from the preceding ones, and from its denial it would follow that the Church had not been perfectly instituted by Christ for its own preservation and its lawful unity in its members in faith and morals, and for one secondary head, true and certain; which is most openly contrary to the Apostle in Eph. 4. and in many other places, and to Hos. 1.

units.la: Octauus art. Item, Ecclesia dicitur catholica, i.e. vniversalis & apostolica: quoniam omnis homo generaliter obligatur adhærere firmiter illis veritatibus, quas eadē Ecclesia tenet, docet & prædicat. Quæ veritates sunt sufficienter in sacra scriptura contentæ, præsertim in Euangelio, vel ex contentis in sacra scriptura sufficienter & clare deducuntur: vel p apostolorum doctrinam successiue deductæ sunt de generatione in generationem vsq; ad nos per observationem legitimam. Vnde dicitur Ecclesia Apostolica: quoniam in doctrina Apostolorum fundata est tam verbis quam scriptis.
units.tr: Eighth article. Likewise, the Church is called catholic, that is, universal, and apostolic, because every man is generally bound to adhere firmly to those truths which this same Church holds, teaches and preaches. These truths are sufficiently contained in Holy Scripture, especially in the Gospel, or are sufficiently and clearly deduced from what is contained in Holy Scripture; or they have been successively derived through the teaching of the apostles from generation to generation down to us by lawful observance. Hence it is called the apostolic Church, since it is founded on the teaching of the apostles, both in word and in writing.

units.la: Nonus art. Item, dum est data in Euangelio per Christum aliqua regula generalis observanda: illa obligat omnem hominem habentem vsum rationis, nisi de exceptione alicuius hominis constiterit per eandem legem Euangelicam, & non solum per humanam traditionem vel exceptionem: quoniam inferioris lex derogare non potest superioris auctoritati.
units.tr: Ninth article. Likewise, when some general rule to be observed has been given in the Gospel by Christ, that rule binds every man who has the use of reason, unless the exception of some person is established by that same evangelical law, and not merely by human tradition or exception; for a lower law cannot derogate from the authority of a higher one.

units.la: Decimus art. Item, quod hæc est lex Euangelica generaliter promulgata Matt. 8. Si peccauerit in te Frater tuus: vade & corripe eum inter te & ipsum solum, si te audierit, lucratus es Fratrem tuum, si te non audierit, adhibe tecum vnum vel duos testes, vt in ore duorum vel trium testium stet omne verbum, quod si eos non audierit, dic Ecclesiæ, si autem Ecclesiam non audierit, sit tibi sicut ethnicus & publicanus. Sequitur continuo: Amen dico vobis: quaecunq; alligaueritis super terram &c. vbi fundatur potestas supernaturalis Ecclesiæ vltra naturalem.
units.tr: Tenth article. Likewise, this is the evangelical law generally promulgated in Matt. 8.: "If thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and rebuke him between thee and him alone. If he shall hear thee, thou shalt gain thy brother. But if he will not hear thee, take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may stand. And if he will not hear them, tell the Church. And if he will not hear the Church, let him be to thee as the heathen and the publican." It follows immediately: "Amen I say to you, whatsoever you shall bind upon earth," etc., where the supernatural power of the Church beyond the natural is founded.

units.la: Vndecimus articul. Item, quod ad prædictum articulum ex aliis sacræ scripturæ passibus possent induci variæ leges, quæ sunt de iure proprie diuino & expresse, imo & iure proprie naturali præsuppositio diuino, vt de abiiciendo partem corporis scandalizantem totum corpus, siue sit pes, siue manus, siue oculus, Matth. 18. Et ita de reliquis. Sed sufficit ad deducendum propositum hæc vnica lex prædicta: Si peccauerit. Et forte diceret hic aliquis, quod quicquid sit de membris abiiciendis aut rescindendis: caput tamen non potest abiici vita manente. Respondeo quod similitudo corporis veri & mystici, non est vsquequaq; eadem: quoniam sine capite naturali corpus non potest viuere, sed sine capite secundario corpus mysticum potest habere vitam: sicut in casu nostro patet de Papa, quo remoto vel abscisso stat vnitas & vita in corpore mystico Ecclesiæ: & hoc in virtute capitis essentialis & primi, quod est Christus.
units.tr: Eleventh article. Likewise, for the aforesaid article, various laws could be brought forward from other passages of Holy Scripture, which are of divine right properly and expressly, and indeed of natural right presupposing the divine, such as that of cutting off a part of the body that causes scandal to the whole body, whether it be a foot, a hand or an eye, Matt. 18.; and so with the rest. But for deducing the present proposition this one law suffices: "If he shall trespass." And perhaps someone might say here that whatever may be the case concerning the members to be cut off or removed, the head, however, cannot be removed while life remains. I answer that the likeness of the true and mystical body is not in every respect the same: for without a natural head the body cannot live, but without a secondary head the mystical body can have life; as in our case is evident concerning the Pope, whose removal or cutting off leaves unity and life standing in the mystical body of the Church, and this by virtue of the essential and first head, which is Christ.

units.la: Duodecimus art. Item, sicut summus pontifex quantumcunq; legitime fuerit electus est filius Ecclesiæ: sic dici potest & debet Frater vniuscuisq; hominis de Ecclesia. Vnde & ad hoc significandum dedit nobis Christus hanc formam orandi: Pater noster &c. Si vnum ergo habemus patrem in cœlis, si vnam matrem Ecclesiam in terris: constat quod omnes mutuo sumus fratres. Et oppositum sentire vel dicere de Papa, esset apertissima dementia.
units.tr: Twelfth article. Likewise, however lawfully the supreme pontiff has been elected, he is a son of the Church, and in the same way each man can and should be called the brother of every other person in the Church. For this reason Christ also gave us this form of prayer: "Our Father," etc. If we have one Father in heaven and one mother, the Church, on earth, it is clear that we are all brothers to one another. To think or say otherwise of the Pope would be the plainest madness.

units.la: Tredecimus art. Item, q; Papa quantumcunq; legitime electus, potest peccare: q; non est impeccabilis ex assumptione papalis dignitatis. Oppositum dicere, nisi constaret de aliquo per diuinam revelationem, esset intolerabiliter superbire, & contra testimonium experientiæ præsentis & præteritæ.
units.tr: Thirteenth article. Likewise, a Pope, however lawfully elected, can sin, since he is not free from sin by assuming the papal dignity. To say the opposite, unless someone were certain of it by divine revelation, would be intolerable arrogance and contrary to the evidence of present and past experience.

units.la: Decimus quartus art. Item, prædicta lex: Si peccauerit: quamuis data fuerit pro regimine totius Ecclesiæ & filiorum suorum: nihilominus appropriate data est personæ Petri, quia erat suturus summus pastor, sicut promissum fuerat Matth. 16. & executioni demandatum: Ioannu vigesim. primi.
units.tr: Fourteenth article. Likewise, the aforesaid law, "If he sins," although it was given for the governance of the whole Church and its sons, was nevertheless given in particular to the person of Peter, because he was to be the supreme minister, as had been promised in Matthew 16 and entrusted to be carried out in John 21.

units.la: Decimus quintus art. Item, quod Christus in prædicta lege: Si pec. &c. non accipiebat Ecclesiam, quando dixit, dic Ecclesiæ, pro ipso Petro vel pro successoribus suis summis pontificibus, patet; quia Petrus non dixisset sibiipsi, quando Frater suus noluisset obedire monitioni suæ seu fraternæ correctioni. Intelligebat ergo de Ecclesia, quæ est congregatio fidelium: præsertim quando Frater, qui peccabat & nolebat corrigi, fuisset talis, quod non habuisset prælatum supra se, sicut est Papa i qui tamen subiectus est legi prædictæ, sicut ipse est frater peccabilis.
units.tr: Fifteenth article. Likewise, it is plain that in the aforesaid law, "If he sins," etc., Christ did not mean the Church when he said "tell it to the Church," meaning Peter himself or his successors, the supreme pontiffs. For Peter would not have said this to himself when his brother refused to obey his warning or his brotherly correction. He therefore meant the Church, which is the congregation of the faithful, especially when the brother who sinned and refused to be corrected was of such a kind that he had no superior over him, as the Pope is. Yet he is subject to the aforesaid law, being himself a sinning brother.

units.la: Decimus sextus art. Item Christus dicendo in prædicta lege: quod si Ecclesiam non audierit, sit tibi sicut ethnicus & publicanus: docet manifeste, quod Ecclesia habet auctoritatem iudiciariam: alioquin si non audiretur, non esset contumacia vel peccatum. Et patet aliunde per illud: Qui vos audit me audit &c. Et iterum: Quaecunque alligaveritis super terram &c. Sic subiungitur statim post prædictam legem: Si peccaverit.
units.tr: Sixteenth article. Likewise, in the aforesaid law Christ, saying that "if he refuses to hear the Church, let him be to you as a heathen and a tax collector," clearly teaches that the Church has judicial authority. Otherwise, if it were not heard, there would be no contumacy or sin. This is also plain from elsewhere, from "He who hears you hears me," etc., and again, "Whatever you bind on earth," etc. Thus it is added immediately after the aforesaid law: "If he sins."

units.la: Decimus septimus art. Item, quod omnis, qui potest & debet licite punire iudicialiter, potest etiam licite evocari ad iudicium, etiam per appellationem aut provocationem aut citationem, prout visum fuerit expediens iudici vel illis, qui ad iudicium accusare volunt Fratrem delinquentem, præsertim vbi non apparet protunc modus convenientior procedendi contra reum & peccatorem Fratrem.
units.tr: Seventeenth article. Likewise, whoever can and ought lawfully to punish by judicial process can also lawfully be summoned to judgment, whether by appeal, by complaint, or by citation, as the judge, or those who wish to accuse the offending brother, shall see fit, especially where at that time no more suitable way of proceeding against the guilty and sinning brother appears.

units.la: Decimus octavus art. Item, quod nulla constitutio humana potuit aut potest præiudicare legi prædictæ: Si peccaverit &c. cum sit de iure divino, & de iure proprie naturali, præsupposito divino.
units.tr: Eighteenth article. Likewise, no human constitution has been able or can prejudice the aforesaid law, "If he sins," etc., since it is of divine right and, properly speaking, of natural right, presupposing the divine.

units.la: Decimus nonus art. Item, quod constitutiones, quæ dicunt quod Papa potest deponi, si labitur in haeresim, non sunt censendæ constitutiones pure humanæ vel positiveæ aliquorum summorum pontificum vel alterius: Patet: quia tunc non ligarent Papam, quia par in parem non habet imperium.
units.tr: Nineteenth article. Likewise, the constitutions which say that the Pope can be deposed if he falls into heresy are not to be judged mere human or positive constitutions of some supreme pontiffs or of anyone else. This is plain, because they would not then bind the Pope, since an equal has no authority over an equal.

units.la: Vicesimus art. Item, quod fundantur hæ constitutiones principaliter in prædicta lege: Si pecc. &c. Et in aliis iuribus conformibus, sicut prætactum est articulo 11.
units.tr: Twentieth article. Likewise, these constitutions are founded chiefly on the aforesaid law, "If he sins," etc., and on other laws that agree with it, as was said in article 11.

units.la: Vicesimus primus art. Item, quod sicut hæc constitutio Christi: Si pecc. &c. non specificat vel restringit de solo peccato haeresis, sed & generaliter de quolibet peccati genere, quod potest deduci in publicum. Sic quodlibet peccatum Papæ publicum seu notorium potest denunciari Ecclesiæ, si fraternaliter monitus Papa nolit audire monentem, neq; testes inductos, nisi daretur ex lege propria divina, quod aliquod peccatum Christus istic excluserit, quod utiq; fieri non poterit.
units.tr: Twenty-first article. Likewise, just as this constitution of Christ, "If he sins," etc., does not specify or restrict itself to the sin of heresy alone, but applies generally to every kind of sin that can be brought into the open, so any public or notorious sin of the Pope can be reported to the Church, if the Pope, when fraternally admonished, refuses to hear the one admonishing him, or the witnesses brought forward. This would hold unless it were granted from some proper divine law that Christ excluded some sin there, which surely cannot be the case.

units.la: Vicesimus secundus art. Item, quicunq; cuiuscunq; status fuerit, qui scripserit vel asseruerit, quod Papa non possit pro crimine accusari coram Ecclesia, quam pro haeresi, ille negandus est simpliciter tanquam contradicens textui Euangelico, vel reuerenter glossandus est, si non appareat, quod fuerit in hac assertione pertinax, & si in aliis bene sensit. Simile dicitur de scripturis, quæ sonare videntur, quod Papa non habet superiorem iudicem in terris, & quod ab eo nunquam licuit neq; licet appellare, & ita de similibus: quæ si excludunt auctoritatem generalis concilii, sunt haereses manifestæ. Sed non est leuiter præsumendum, quod alii doctores sic senserint generaliter absq; omni exceptione possibili occasione vel colore.
units.tr: Twenty-second article. Likewise, whoever, of whatever status, has written or asserted that the Pope cannot be accused before the Church of a crime other than heresy, must be simply rejected as contradicting the Gospel text, or else must be respectfully explained away, if it does not appear that he was obstinate in this assertion and if otherwise he meant well. The same applies to Scriptures which seem to sound as if the Pope has no superior judge on earth, and that from him it was never lawful, nor is it lawful, to appeal, and to similar statements. If these exclude the authority of a general council, they are manifest heresies. But it is not to be lightly presumed that other teachers have held such a view in general, without any possible exception, occasion or pretext.

units.la: Vicesimus tertius art. Item, quod Glossa quæ dicit, quod pro alio crimine quam pro haeresi potest Papa accusari vel deponi, non habet auctoritatem vel robur tanquam ab uno Glossatore vel homine, sed à Christo immediate & expresse: alioquin non faceret fidem, sicut prædictum est in altero articulo, quod par in parem, & unus inferior in superiorem non habet iudicium.
units.tr: Twenty-third article. Likewise, the Gloss which says that the Pope can be accused or deposed for a crime other than heresy has no authority or force as coming from a single Glossator or man, but only from Christ immediately and expressly. Otherwise it would not carry weight, as was said in another article, since an equal has no judgment over an equal, and an inferior has none over a superior.

units.la: Vicesimus quartus art. Item, quod de iure divino & naturali est propria defensio sui ipsius, dum laedit, dum tamen hoc faciat per media non prohibita in lege divina & naturali.
units.tr: Twenty-fourth article. Likewise, by divine and natural right there is a proper defence of oneself when one is injured, provided that this is done by means not forbidden in divine and natural law.

units.la: Vicesimus quintus art. Item, quod stare potest in facto, quod aliquis molestatus à Papa etiam vero & legitimo, non possit habere sufficientem defensionem, nisi provocet vel appellet à Papa ad iudicium Ecclesiæ, & nisi subtrahat se ab eo, sic quod eius mandatis non obediat: quæ mandata vel obedientia tollerent laesò iustam defensionem sui ipsis vel suorum, vt esset tuitio propriæ matris vel patris aut patriæ suæ, imo & totius catholicæ veritatis aut vnitatis Ecclesiæ: sicut appartit in subtractionibus multis legitime factis tempore nostro & per prius.
units.tr: Twenty-fifth article. Likewise, it may be the case in fact that someone troubled by the Pope, even by a true and lawful Pope, cannot have a sufficient defence unless he appeals or calls on the Church's judgment against the Pope, and unless he withdraws from him, so that he does not obey his commands. Those commands or obedience would take away from the injured party the just defence of himself or his own, which would be the protection of his own mother or father or country, indeed of the whole Catholic truth or unity of the Church. This is evident from the many lawful withdrawals made in our time and before.

units.la: Vicesimus sextus art. Item, sicut alias prædicatum est coram hoc sacro concilio potest haberi multiplex occasio, & quasi us color, ad hoc quod possit & debeat per Ecclesiam seu concilium generale vice sua dari libellus repudii vero Papæ; quandoq, sine culpa Papæ; licet non sine causa: quandoq; cum culpa Papæ, etiam alia quam sit haeresis, & numerati sunt colores vel occasiones 10. quem admodum viceuerla summus pontifex potest dare libellum repudii Ecclesiæ, sicut patuit in Caelestino cedente. Vxor autem & vir non videntur hic ad imparia iudicari.
units.tr: Twenty-sixth article. Likewise, as was said elsewhere before this holy council, there can be many occasions, and as it were pretexts, by which the Church or a general council may, in its own place, give a bill of divorce to the Pope. Sometimes this happens without fault on the Pope's part, though not without cause; sometimes it happens with fault on the Pope's part, even for something other than heresy. Ten such pretexts or occasions have been counted. And, conversely, the supreme pontiff can give a bill of divorce to the Church, as was seen in the case of Celestine when he resigned. Yet husband and wife are not here to be judged as unequals.

units.la: Vicesimus septimus art. Item, quod prædicti omnes & singuli articuli sunt per hoc sacrum concilium Constantiense solenniter & iudicialiter declarati & multipliciter practicati tam in eiectione olim Ioannis 23. quam in constitutionibus & decretis factis super auctoritate generalis concilii, præsertim 6. Aprilis Anno 1415. Et nouissime in decreto facto, quod praesens constitutio Petri de Luna non praeiudicat subtractioni factæ sibi in Aragonia &c.
units.tr: Twenty-seventh article. Likewise, all and each of the aforesaid articles have been solemnly and judicially declared by this holy Council of Constance, and applied in many ways, both in the deposition of John XXIII and in the constitutions and decrees made concerning the authority of a general council, especially those of 6 April in the year 1415. And most recently in the decree made that the present constitution does not prejudice the withdrawal made against Peter de Luna in Aragon, etc.

units.la: Vicesimus octavus art. Item, quod docens vel asserens nunc oppositum alicuius articulorum praemissorum, cadit in haeresim iam damnatam, & asserit expresse contra legem Euangelicam: Si peccaverit &c. Et contra articulum istum: Vnam sanctam catholicam & contra determinata expresse per hoc sacrum concilium, sicut prætactum est.
units.tr: Twenty-eighth article. Likewise, whoever now teaches or asserts the opposite of any of the articles set out above falls into a heresy already condemned, and asserts expressly against the Gospel law, "If he sins," etc. He also acts against the article "One holy catholic" and against the matters expressly determined by this holy council, as was said before.

units.la: Vicesimus nonus art. Item, quod prælatus Ecclesiasticus etiam Papa determinans iudicialiter, aut per modum constitutionis perpetuæ & poenalis oppositum præmissorum articulorum, non potuit aut potest à pertinacia quomodolibet excusari: tum quia demonstrat, quod non quærit tota sollicitudine veritatem, dum eam scienter impugnat, & ad impugnandum omnes alios inducit, quantum in se est per excommunicationes & alias poenas grauissimas, tum rursus in casu præsenti, quia non ostendit se paratum corrigi, dum regulam sui correctricem negat & impugnat, scil. auctoritatem Ecclesiæ vel generalis concilii vice sua.
units.tr: Twenty-ninth article. Likewise, an ecclesiastical prelate, even the Pope, who judicially determines, or by way of a perpetual and penal constitution, the opposite of the aforesaid articles, could not have been, and cannot be, excused from obstinacy in any way. First, because he shows that he does not seek the truth with his whole care, while knowingly attacking it and, as far as he is able, leading all others to attack it, through excommunications and other most grievous penalties. Second, in the present case, because he does not show himself ready to be corrected, while he denies and attacks the rule that corrects him, namely the authority of the Church or of a general council in its own place.

units.la: Tricesimus art. Item, quod nullæ protestationes factæ in oppositum relevant talem assertorem vel determinatorem quatenus debeat in errore suo pertinax iudicari: quia cum talibus protestationibus generalibus de volendo stare in fide Ecclesiæ &c. stat de facto particularis erroris assertio: sicut posset latius deduci tam per rationes quam per exempla priorum hæreticorum, & etiam modernorum, dum factum repugnat protestationi.
units.tr: Thirtieth article. Likewise, that no protestations made to the contrary avail to free such an asserter or determiner from being judged pertinacious in his error, since with such general protestations of wishing to stand in the faith of the Church, and so on, there stands in fact the assertion of a particular error. This could be argued at greater length, both by reasons and by the examples of earlier heretics and also of recent ones, since the deed contradicts the protestation.

units.la: SECVNDVS LIBER EIVSDEM DOCTORIS ARTICVLORVM SPECIALIVM SVBSVMPTORVM SPE- CIALITER EX GENERALIBUS ARTICULIS SUPER POTESTATE & AUCTORITATE ECCLESIÆ, CONTRA PETRUM DE LUNA, AD CONVINCENDUM EUM UT PRIUS.
units.tr: The Second Book of the same Doctor, on special articles drawn specifically from the general articles concerning the power and authority of the Church, against Peter de Luna, to convict him as before.

units.la: ET primo notandum est: quod Petrus de Luna dudum fecit quandam prætensam constitutionem, & eam pluries solenniter publicauit & publicari fecit: imo & practicauit quantum in se fuit, tam contra Christianissimum Regem Franciæ ante concilium Pisanum, quam nouissime contra Illustrissimum Regem Arragoniæ, & generaliter contra omnes, qui sunt in hoc Constantiensi concilio, sicut patet ex sua responsione ad citationem. Quæ prætensa constitutio incipit: In dierum successu crescente malitia &c. Datum Maßiliæ 14. Cal. Iun. Anno 13. pontificatus nostri: ita quod sunt decem anni vel circiter.
units.tr: First, it should be noted that Peter de Luna some time ago issued a certain alleged constitution, and solemnly published it many times and had it published. Indeed, he also put it into practice as far as he could, both against the most Christian King of France before the Council of Pisa and most recently against the most illustrious King of Aragon, and generally against all who are in this Council of Constance, as is clear from his reply to the citation. That alleged constitution begins: "As malice grows with the passing of days," etc. Given at Marseilles, 14 days before the Kalends of June, in the 13th year of our pontificate. So it is ten years or thereabouts.

units.la: Secundus art. Item, quod in prætensa constitutione ponitur in forma talis clausula inter cæteras: Omnes &c. qui à nobis vel successoribus nostris Romanis Pontificibus canonice intrantibus appellare præsumperint, seu à nostra seu ipsorum successorum nostrorum Romanorum Pontificum canonice intrantium obedientia recesserint, ac se subtraxerint, vel in præmissa subtractione aut appellatione perseuerauerint seu persisterint, seu eis in præmissis impedimentum seu appellationibus, subtractionibus vel provocationibus scienter per se vel per alium vel alios quavis occasione seu quaesito colore dederint auxilium, consilium vel favorem & qui pertinaciter asseruerint illos qui præmissa committunt per nostras sententias non ligari, cuiuscunq; status, gradus, dignitatis existant vel conditionis, etiam si cardinalatus, patriarchali, Archiepiscopali, Episcopali, imperiali, regali, vel alias quavis Ecclesiastica vel mundana prafulgent dignitate, ex nunc auctoritate Apostolica excommunicationis sententiam promulgamus, à quà nullus praeterquam à Romanis pontificibus, nisi dum taxat in mortis articulo poterit beneficium absolutionis obtinere &c. Et adduntur poenæ dispositionis &c.
units.tr: Second article. Likewise, the alleged constitution contains, among other clauses, one in this form: "All who presume to appeal from us or from our successors, the Roman Pontiffs canonically entering office, or who withdraw from our obedience or that of their successors, the Roman Pontiffs canonically entering office, and who persist in that withdrawal or appeal, or knowingly give aid, counsel or favour to those who make appeals, withdrawals or provocations in these matters, whether in person or through another or others, on any pretext or under any colour; and who obstinately assert that those who commit the aforesaid acts are not bound by our sentences, of whatever state, rank, dignity or condition they may be, even if they shine with the dignity of cardinal, patriarch, archbishop, bishop, imperial, royal, or any other ecclesiastical or worldly dignity: from now on, by apostolic authority, we promulgate the sentence of excommunication, from which no one except the Roman pontiffs, and then only at the point of death, may obtain the benefit of absolution," etc. Penalties of the same disposition are added, etc.

units.la: Tertius art. Item, quod dicta clausula, sicut patet ex forma sua, est generaliter absq; omni exceptione posita de Petro de Luna, quam de quocunq; legitimo successore suo: siue labitur aliquis eorum in haeresim, siue in aliud peccatum quodlibet quantumcunq; enorme, quia dicit, quavis occasione seu quaesito colore &c. Et quia si voluisset aliquam exceptionem fuisse, illam explicasset. Sed quia videbat exceptionem redundare potuisse contra seipsum, propterea nullam apposuit vel apponendam iudicauit.
units.tr: Third article. Likewise, as is clear from its wording, the said clause is general and admits no exception concerning Peter de Luna, or any legitimate successor of his, whether one of them falls into heresy or into any other sin, however grave, because it says "on any pretext or under any colour," etc. And if he had wished any exception to be made, he would have stated it. But because he saw that an exception might rebound upon himself, he made none, nor did he judge that one should be made.

units.la: Quartus art. Item, quod Petrus de Luna in suis responsionibus datis ad citationem contra eum facta, dat aperte intelligi, quod vult practicare dicta pretensam constitutionem, & tenet firmiter, quod habuit & habet robur & vim suam contra omnes & singulos, qui sunt in hoc sacro Constantiensi concilio: quia sic dicit in forma. Protestandum tamen, quod per quemcunq; facta vel facienda, dicta seu dicenda, sub quacunq; forma non intendit dictam congregationem aut eius pretensam citationem comprobare: nec ipsam citationem quomodolibet exaudire, aut ei quemcunq; seu qualemcunq; vigorem tanquam à notorie nullam potestatem habentibus emanatam quoquomodo tribuere seu praestare: imo ipsam & alia quaecunq; facta seu facienda, ordinata seu ordinanda contra ipsum & Romanam Ecclesiam, cum sint de facto praesumpta per eos, pronunciauit, decreuit & declarauit, pronunciat, decernit & declarat cassa, nulla & irrito ipso iure, ut de his etiam est solenniter protestatus.
units.tr: Fourth article. Likewise, Peter de Luna, in his replies to the citation issued against him, plainly makes it understood that he wishes to put the said alleged constitution into practice, and firmly holds that it has and had its force and power against all and each of those who are in this holy Council of Constance. For he says in form: "It must however be protested that, whatever is done or is to be done, said or to be said, in whatever form, by anyone, he does not intend to confirm the said assembly or its alleged citation, nor to heed that citation in any way, nor to grant or lend it any force whatever, as having proceeded from those who manifestly have no power. Rather, he has pronounced, decreed and declared, and now pronounces, decrees and declares, that it, and all other things done or to be done, ordered or to be ordered against him and the Roman Church, since they have been presumptuously undertaken by them, are void, null and invalid by law itself, as he has also solemnly protested concerning these things."

units.la: Postremo cum prætensa citatione contineatur, quod convenientes in vnum canonice convocati, & repræsentantes ipsam vniuersalem Ecclesiam, decreuerunt &c. Respondet idem Dominus Papa, quod prædicti congregati in Constantia non sunt generalis synodus, nec vniuersalem Ecclesiam repræsentant, cum sint excommunicati & omnibus Ecclesiasticis dignitatibus, gradibus & auctoritatibus & iurisdictione priuati, & per consequens nullas partes iudicii potuerunt assumere nec possunt: sicut nec etiam iurisdictionem aliquam exercere, præcipue cum minor in maiorem, & permaxime in Papam, quem nec iuris auctoritas, nec rationis debitum, nec alicuius obligationis necessitas ad hoc artant, actum imperiosum exercere non posset. Ecce temeritatem & pertinaciam aduersus hoc sacrum concilium, & aduersus omnes indifferenter, qui sibi non obediunt. Unde & reputat solam Ecclesiam esse apud se, & solum concilium generale, & quod cathedra sua est archa Noe, sicut dixit verbo, dans intelligi quod nullus extra hanc archam saluabitur. Et ita de plurimis.
units.tr: Lastly, since the alleged citation states that those canonically convoked and gathered together, representing the universal Church itself, have decreed etc., the same Lord Pope replies that the aforesaid men assembled at Constance are not a general synod and do not represent the universal Church, since they are excommunicated and deprived of all ecclesiastical dignities, ranks, authorities and jurisdiction. Consequently they could not, and cannot, take any part in a judgment, just as they cannot exercise any jurisdiction, especially since a lesser person cannot exercise an imperious act over a greater, and most of all over the Pope, whom neither the authority of law, nor the due of reason, nor the necessity of any obligation compels to this. Behold the rashness and obstinacy against this holy council, and against all indifferently who do not obey him. Hence he also considers that the Church is with him alone, and the general council is with him alone, and that his chair is the ark of Noah, as he has said in words, giving to understand that no one will be saved outside this ark. And so on for very many points.

units.la: Quintus art. Item, quod hæc prætensa constitutio de directo & expresse repugnat omnibus singulis prioribus articulis, qui elucidant hanc legem Euangelicam: Si peccauerit &c. Et qui fundatur in hac lege cum suis similibus: & hoc notorium est ex terminis.
units.tr: Fifth article. Likewise, this alleged constitution directly and expressly contradicts all the preceding articles, which expound this Gospel law, "If he sins," etc., and which is founded on this law together with its like. This is notorious from its very terms.

units.la: Sextus art. Item, quod Petrus de Luna non excusatur vel releuatur ab haeresi praedicta & pertinacia per generales protestationes, quas facit: quae sic habentur in forma. Dicit ac etiam profitetur, quod in veritate fidei & unitate catholica Ecclesiae semper fuit & est, semperque se fuisse & permansisse firmiter credit; nec ab illis vnquam modo aliquo deuiauit, sicut nec deuiare intendit, nec fauorem schismatis vel haeresi aliquo modo dedit, sicut nec dare intendit, imo semper tenuit & tenet, firmiterque credidit & credit, quod sancta Romana & Catholica Ecclesia tenuit & tenet, profitetur & docet: nec aliquid a praedictis decreuit dicere, scribere, docere, tenere seu credere intendit in posterum, gratia eidem diuina assistente: nihilque pertinaciter seu incorrigibiliter dixisse seu dicere voluit, nec intendit. Sed omnia praeterita, praesentia & futura quacunque dicta & dicenda, facta & facienda, scripta & scribenda, credita & credenda, docta & docenda subiicit subiectaque, esse voluit correctioni & determinationi catholicae Ecclesiae Sacrosanctae. Et si contra praemissa vel aliquod praemissorum dixerit, scripserit aut fecerit quouis modo, quod non credit, paratus est semper stare correctioni dictae sanctae matris Ecclesiae, in cuius vnitate viuere intendit, atque mori, sicut catholicus & fidelis, & facere & complere ea ad quae astringitur in praemissis & quolibet praemissorum. Constat enim quod cum his protestationibus remaneret particularis error suus non purgatus.
units.tr: Sixth article. Likewise, Peter de Luna is neither excused nor relieved of the aforesaid heresy and obstinacy by the general protestations which he makes, which are found in this form: He says and also professes that in the truth of the faith and the catholic unity of the Church he always was and is, and firmly believes that he has always been and has remained so; nor has he ever in any way strayed from these, nor does he intend to stray, nor has he in any way given favour to schism or heresy, nor does he intend to give it; but he has always held and holds, and has firmly believed and believes, that the holy Roman and Catholic Church held and holds, professes and teaches. Nor does he intend to decide in future to say, write, teach, hold or believe anything contrary to the aforesaid, with divine grace assisting him. Nor has he wished or intended to say anything obstinately or incorrigibly. But he has subjected, and wishes to subject, all things past, present and future, whatever has been or will be said, done, written, believed or taught, to the correction and determination of the holy Catholic Church. And if he has said, written or done anything in any way contrary to the foregoing or any part of it, which he does not believe, he is always ready to abide by the correction of the said holy mother Church, in whose unity he intends to live and die, as a Catholic and faithful man, and to perform and fulfil those things to which he is bound in the foregoing and in each of them. For it is evident that with these protestations his particular error remained unpurged.

units.la: Septimus art. Item, si nunc praedictus Petrus de Luna vellet a praedicta haeresi sua reuerti & redire ad gremium Ecclesiae: ipsa posset non claudere sibi gremium, dando indulgentiam de scelere: sed non deberet ipsum impunitum relinquere, vel in papatu praetenso retinere, etiam vbi fuisset aliunde Papa legitimus.
units.tr: Seventh article. Likewise, if the aforesaid Peter de Luna now wished to turn back from his heresy and return to the bosom of the Church, the Church could not close its bosom to him, granting indulgence for his crime. But it ought not leave him unpunished, nor retain him in the pretended papacy, even if there were otherwise a legitimate Pope.

units.la: Octauus art. Item, quod si mittat nuncios suos, videtur quod in primis & ante omnia proponendi sunt ipsis praecedentes articuli, vt respondeant sigillatim ad quemlibet: quoniam per hoc fiet abbreviatio aliorum processuum iuridicorum, qui versarentur in his quae sunt facti: quoniam per praedictos articulos potest veraciter vno verbo dici ipsi Petro de Luna: Ex ore tuo te iudico serue nequam: imo videtur quod nuncii si mittantur, erunt interrogandi super praemissis nedum pro nomine seu vice Petri de Luna, sed etiam pro seipsis, vt videtur, quid sentiant super eisdem articulis: vt si male habeant & ipsi male iuxta demeritum & errorem, si bene condemnabitur eorum magister ex eorum confessione catholica & vera.
units.tr: Eighth article. Likewise, if he sends his messengers, it seems that the preceding articles should first and above all be put to them, so that they may answer each one separately. For by this means the other juridical processes, which would concern matters of fact, will be shortened; since by the aforesaid articles one can truthfully say to Peter de Luna in a word: "Out of your own mouth I judge you, wicked servant." Indeed, it seems that if messengers are sent, they will have to be questioned on the foregoing not only in the name or on behalf of Peter de Luna, but also for themselves, namely what they think about the same articles. So that if they are in the wrong, they too will be condemned according to their demerit and error; if they are right, their master will be condemned by their own Catholic and true confession.

units.la: Articulatio praetacta constitutionis Petri de Luna potest fieri contra ipsum sub propositionibus sequentibus cum probatione summaria, & aliarum quarundam additione conclusionum.
units.tr: The aforesaid article of Peter de Luna's constitution can be framed against him under the following propositions, with a summary proof and the addition of some further conclusions.

units.la: Haec constitutio Petri de Luna est haereticalis, quae incipit: In die &c. Haec constitutio cum suis circumstantiis reddit Petrum de Luna proprie haereticum, schismaticum, temerarium, scandalosum atque sacrilegum.
units.tr: This constitution of Peter de Luna is heretical; it begins: In die etc. This constitution, with its circumstances, makes Peter de Luna properly a heretic, a schismatic, rash, scandalous and sacrilegious.

units.la: PRobatur prima conclusio sic: Constitutio illa est haeretica lis, quae directe & expresse praeiudicat & contrariatur legi Euangelicae de correctione fraterna & de correctione iudiciali per authoritatem Ecclesiae, si fraterna non satisfecerit, quae habetur Matth. decim. octau: Si peccauerit in te frater tuus &c. Sed haec constitutio Petri de Luna est huiusmodi: igitur est haeretica lis. Deducitur maior per descriptionem haeresis, quod est dogma peruersum fidei catholicae contrarium. Constat autem quod Euangelium est fides orthodoxa obiectiue, sicut dicitur in Symbolo: Haec est fides catholica &c. Sed minor, in qua stat difficultas, deducitur sic: Lex praedicta de correctione fraterna & iudiciali, aut comprehendit Petrum de Luna & suos successores, quos reputat summos pontifices futuros legitime, vel non comprehendit. Non potest dici secundum: quoniam lex fertur generaliter de omni fratre, dum peccauerit tali peccato, quod potest deduci in publicum. Constat autem quod quilibet Christianus est frater noster, etiam si fuerit Papa: quia propter hoc non definit dicere Pater noster. Si ergo est pater noster, nos pariter sumus fratres. Si vero detur primum, sicut dari necesse est: quod scilicet Papa comprehenditur sub lege hac Euangelica & immutabili, quae consonat etiam iuri proprie naturali: Sequitur ergo, quod si peccauerit in nos etiam frater noster, debet fraternaliter primo corripi, iuxta regulam generaliter ita positam: quod si noluerit audire, adhibendi sunt testes, quod si audire noluerit, denunciandus est Ecclesiae; quam si contempserit, habendus est tanquam ethnicus & publicanus, id est, excommunicatus, & extra Ecclesiam positus. Sequitur ergo consequenter, quod Ecclesia est iudex Papae, dum peccauerit peccato publico & Ecclesiae denunciato. Et potest Ecclesia talem Papam excommunicare & eiicere a consortio multiplici occasione, & multiplici quaesito colore. Constat autem, quod ab inferiori ad superiorem legitimum potest fieri appellatio seu prouocatio, seu deductio in causam: seu iudicialis citatio & euocatio, nunc ad denunciationem alterius, nunc ex puro iudicis officio. Sed manifestum est, quod haec constitutio tollit omnia ista media, dum fert generalem excommunicationis sententiam, & poenas depositionis in omnes, qui quacunque occasione vel quocunque quaesito colore praesumpserint a persona Petri de Luna, vel a quocunque successore seu appellare seu prouocare, vel ab obedientia se subtrahere &c. quod utique repugnat & contradicit manifestissime huic legi Euangelicae, prout modo deductum est.
units.tr: The first conclusion is proved as follows. That constitution is heretical which directly and expressly prejudices and contradicts the evangelical law concerning fraternal correction and judicial correction by the authority of the Church, if the brother has not given satisfaction; this is found in Matthew 18: If your brother sins against you etc. But this constitution of Peter de Luna is of that kind; therefore it is heretical. The major premise follows from the description of heresy, which is a perverse doctrine contrary to the Catholic faith. It is certain that the Gospel is the orthodox faith objectively, as is said in the Creed: This is the Catholic faith etc. The minor premise, where the difficulty lies, follows thus. The aforesaid law of fraternal and judicial correction either includes Peter de Luna and his successors, whom he regards as lawful future popes, or it does not. The second cannot be said, since the law is laid down generally concerning every brother who sins in such a way that the sin can be brought into public view. It is certain that every Christian is our brother, even if he is the Pope; for this reason he does not cease to say Our Father. If, then, he is our Father, we are likewise brethren. But if the first holds, as it must, namely that the Pope is included under this evangelical and unchangeable law, which also agrees with the law of nature properly so called, it follows that if our brother the Pope sins against us, he must first be corrected fraternally, according to the rule laid down in general terms: "If he will not hear you, take with you witnesses; if he will not hear them, tell it to the Church; and if he refuses to hear the Church, let him be to you as a heathen and a publican," that is, excommunicated and placed outside the Church. It therefore follows consequently that the Church is judge of the Pope when he sins by a public sin that has been reported to the Church. And the Church can excommunicate such a Pope and cast him out of fellowship on many occasions and under many pretexts. It is certain that an appeal, or a provocation, or a bringing into a cause, or a judicial summons and calling forth, can be made from a lower to a higher lawful authority, sometimes on the denunciation of another, sometimes by the pure office of the judge. But it is evident that this constitution removes all these means, since it imposes a general sentence of excommunication and penalties of deposition on all who, on whatever occasion or under whatever pretext, presume to appeal or provoke from the person of Peter de Luna or from any successor, or to withdraw from obedience, and so on; which plainly contradicts and opposes this evangelical law, as has now been shown.

units.la: PRobatur secunda conclusio faciliter ex praecedenti. Ille enim proprie dicitur haereticus, qui pertinaciter asserit, imo determinat haeresim: sed Petrus de Luna pertinaciter ita facit. Est enim pertinax, qui non est paratus corrigi, & qui non quaerit cauta sollicitudine veritatem, sed impugnat, & ad impugnandum omnes inducit sub poenis terribilibus, quantum in ipso est. Sic est in proposito: proposito: addendo maxime, q hic impugnatur regula veritatis de directo, per quam errans frater habet corrigi. Quae regula est authoritas & potestas iudicialis ipsius Ecclesiae vel concilii generalis vice sua. Unde tollit quantum in ipso est omnia media, per quae debet errans ad viam & regulam reduci veritatis. Possent addi circumstantiae quasi sine numero, quae probant hanc pertinaciam in Petro de Luna respectu constitutionis huiusmodi, & aliorum errorum multiplicium & scandalosissimorum, sed haec pro nunc sufficiunt, attento quod tam erga Regem Franciae, quam erga Regem Aragoniae voluit practicare constitutionem istam haereticalem atq; pestiferam: imo & in omnes existentes in hoc concilio, sicut patet in responsione sua ad citationem.
units.tr: The second conclusion is easily proved from the preceding. He is properly called a heretic who pertinaciously asserts, indeed determines, a heresy. But Peter de Luna does exactly this pertinaciously. For he is pertinacious who is not ready to be corrected, and who does not seek the truth with careful diligence, but attacks it, and, as far as he is able, brings everyone to attack it under terrible penalties. So it is in the present case, especially adding that here the rule of truth is assailed directly, by which an erring brother ought to be corrected. That rule is the judicial authority and power of the Church itself, or of a general council in its place. Hence he removes, as far as in him lies, all the means by which an erring person ought to be brought back to the way and rule of truth. Countless further circumstances could be added which prove this pertinacity in Peter de Luna with respect to such a constitution and to his many other errors, most scandalous; but these suffice for now, considering that he wished to put this heretical and pestilential constitution into practice both against the King of France and against the King of Aragon, indeed against all who are present in this council, as is clear from his reply to the summons.

units.la: Probatur tertia conclusio considerando materiam, circa quam est haeresis praedicta: quae de necessitate infert peccatum schismatis: quoniam tendit ad impossibilitandum reunionem Ecclesiae sub uno certo pastore supremo: quia tollit medium convenientissimum, imo necessarium, scil. authoritatem iudicialem Ecclesiae seu concilii generalis vice sua, dum prohibet Ecclesiam congregari &c. & dum removet omnem Papam a subiectione authoritatis iudicialis Ecclesiae.
units.tr: The third conclusion is proved by considering the matter concerning which the aforesaid heresy arises, which of necessity brings in the sin of schism, since it tends to make impossible the reunion of the Church under one certain supreme minister. For it removes the most suitable, indeed necessary, means, namely the judicial authority of the Church or of a general council in its place, while it forbids the Church to be assembled, and while it removes every Pope from subjection to the judicial authority of the Church.

units.la: Confirmantur omnia praedicta per constitutiones huius sacri concilii factas & publicatas plu-ries. Confirmantur etiam per subtractiones licitas illorum principum, qui se subtraxerunt. Oportet enim concedere praemissas tres conclusiones: vel dicere quod hoc concilium generale erravit faciendo quaestiones tales, & in approbando novissime subtractionem dominorum Arragonensium, absit autem hoc a nobis ita delirare.
units.tr: All the foregoing is confirmed by the decrees of this holy council, made and published many times. It is also confirmed by the lawful withdrawals of those princes who withdrew. For one must either concede the three conclusions premised, or say that this general council erred in raising such questions and in lately approving the withdrawal of the lords of Aragon; but far be it from us to rave thus.

units.la: Et si dicatur, quod multa iura canonica, multae constitutiones Papales, & aliae videntur sonare pro constitutione Petri de Luna. Respondetur, quod illa iura sunt reverenter glossanda & interpretanda conformiter ad inuariabilem legem Christi. Aut si vult aliquis illa tenere in suis terminis proterue & rigide, nos eum omni libertate talia scripta negabimus esse vera, & per consequens nec iura canonica: quoniam nullum ius esse censendum est, quod divinae legi conuincitur contraire. Addatur & hic clausula constitutionis, quae ponitur supra articulo 2. In secundis articulis. Omnes &c. qui a nobis &c. supra.
units.tr: And if it is said that many canon laws, many papal constitutions and other texts seem to sound in favour of Peter de Luna's constitution, the answer is that those laws are to be glossed and interpreted reverently, in conformity with the unchangeable law of Christ. Or if anyone wishes to hold them in their terms stubbornly and rigidly, we shall with full freedom deny that such writings are true, and consequently that they are canon laws; for no law is to be counted as law which is shown to contradict the divine law. Let the clause of the constitution be added here as well, which is set out above in the second article, among the second articles: "All etc. who from us etc." above.

units.la: EXCERPTA DE ARTICULIS CONTRA PETRUM DE LUNA, IN PROCESSU PRODUCTIS.
units.tr: Excerpts from the Articles against Peter de Luna, Produced in the Trial

units.la: Primo in tractatu, quem fecit aut fieri fecit, & ab aliis factum approbavit & ratum habuit, intitulato De schismate, ponit hanc conclusionem sequentem & ponitur conclusio sequens: Nulli convenit potestati nec divinae nec humanae, quod quid sit intra unum locum & extra eundem. Dictamq; conclusionem pertinaciter asseruit & sustinuit, quae haeretica est contra sacram scripturam & divinam potentiam est, cum Deus sit intra & extra eundem locum, & hoc est notorium.
units.tr: First, in a treatise which he wrote, or caused to be written, and which he approved and ratified when made by others, entitled On the Schism, he puts forward and holds the following conclusion: "No power, neither divine nor human, can be within one place and outside the same place at once." He obstinately asserted and maintained this conclusion. It is heretical against Holy Scripture and against the divine power, since God is both within and outside the same place; and this is notorious.

units.la: Item quod dixit, scripsit vel scribi fecit, & asseruit idem Dominus vocatus, ut praemittitur, Benedictus, quod si iuisset ad Pisanum concilium vel misisset ad illud ad cedendum Papatui, ut aliqui sibi consuluerunt & consulebant, iam non essent claves in Ecclesia, nisi Deus incarnatus fuisset, & claves de novo dedisset, & hoc est notorium.
units.tr: Likewise, the same man, called Benedict as stated above, said, wrote or caused to be written, and asserted that if he had gone to the Council of Pisa, or had sent to it in order to cede the Papacy, as some advised him and were advising him, then there would no longer be keys in the Church, unless God had become incarnate again and given the keys anew; and this is notorious.

units.la: Item, in tractatu, quem fecit aut fieri fecit & factum approbavit, & ratum habuit contra Pisanum concilium, qui incipit: Quia nonnulli, in quarta parte, via tertia. C. subsequenter: & alibi in dicto tractatu dixit, asseruit & pertinaciter sustinuit: quod stante dubio huius schismatis, illi qui non possunt certificari de veritate & iustitia alterius contendentium de Papatu primo electorum obediendo Papae Benedicto 23. scil. sibi quo ad Deum in conscientia, sunt & essent securi. Et hoc est notorium.
units.tr: Likewise, in a treatise which he wrote or caused to be written and approved as made, and which he ratified against the Council of Pisa, beginning "Because some...", in the fourth part, third way, subsequently ...; and elsewhere in the said treatise he said, asserted and obstinately maintained that, while the doubt of this schism stands, those who cannot be assured of the truth and justice of either of the contending parties concerning the Papacy are and would be safe before God in conscience if they first obey Pope Benedict XIII, that is, himself, as the elected pope. And this is notorious.

units.la: Item, dicunt & proponunt dicti persecutores & ministri, quod idem Petrus vocatus, ut praemittitur, Benedictus post praemissum per eos praetensum Perpinianum concilium, dixit & asseruit pertinaciter & constanter, quod si totus mundus diceret sibi, quod cederet Papatui, & sibi videretur quod non sequeretur inde unio Ecclesiae, aut videretur sibi quod ipse non deberet cedere, ipse non cederet, & si totus mundus diceret sibi, quod non cederet, & sibi videretur quod deberet cedere: ipse cederet. Per hoc suum iudicium, imo potius errorem pertinaciter praeferendo omni humano & Ecclesiae universalis iudicio: quod manifeste probat pertinaciam in errore.
units.tr: Likewise, the said persecutors and ministers allege and propose that the same Peter, called Benedict as stated above, after the Council of Perpignan which they claim was convened, said and asserted obstinately and constantly that if the whole world told him to cede the Papacy, and it seemed to him that no union of the Church would follow from it, or it seemed to him that he ought not to cede, he would not cede; and if the whole world told him not to cede, and it seemed to him that he ought to cede, he would cede. By this, his own judgment, or rather his error, he obstinately preferred to every human judgment and to the judgment of the universal Church; which clearly proves obstinacy in error.

units.la: Item, quod Christus & Papa sunt unum caput Ecclesiae, posuit in quodam tractatu contra decem propositiones stabilientes concilium Pisanum.
units.tr: Likewise, he put forward in a certain treatise against the ten propositions establishing the Council of Pisa that Christ and the Pope are one head of the Church.

units.la: Item, quod concilium generale nullo modo & in nullo casu potest celebrari sine Papa, etiam dum Papa mortuus est. Et ita necessario dicendum esset, quod in Constantia post adunationem totius obedientiarum & regionum, nullum est aut fuit generale concilium. Cuius oppositum tanquam catholicum determinatum est & practicatum in hoc sacro concilio. Et quod ab hoc errore dato sequeretur manifeste, quod Ecclesia non fuisset sufficienter & perseueranter pro sui conseruatione institura à Christo. Quia deniq; non apparet modus condemnandi vel eiiciendi Papam schismaticum, incorrigibilem & haereticum contradicentem pertinaciter Ecclesiae.
units.tr: Likewise, he maintained that a general council can in no way and in no case be celebrated without the Pope, even when the Pope is dead. And so it would necessarily have to be said that at Constance, after the union of all the obediences and regions, there is or was no general council. The opposite of this has been determined and practised as Catholic in this holy council. It would also clearly follow from this false opinion that the Church had not been instituted by Christ sufficiently and lastingly for its own preservation. For finally, no way appears of condemning or removing a schismatic, incorrigible and heretical Pope who obstinately resists the Church.

units.la: Ponuntur consequenter ad probata de praedictis & aliis articulis tres conclusiones sequentes. Haec assertio Petri de Luna quod concilium generale non potest in aliquo casu congregari sine Papa, est haeresis nunc expresse damnata. Haec assertio Petri de Luna quod si credidisset aliquibus tempore concilii Pisani, clauses hodie non essent in Ecclesia, est manifeste haeretica, praesupposita duratione legis Dei vsq; ad consummationem mundi. Haec assertio Petri de Luna quod Christus & Papa sunt vnum caput Ecclesiae, est haereticalis, nisi reducatur ad aliquem sensum sanum satis improprium.
units.tr: Following from the matters proved about these and the other articles, three conclusions are laid down. This assertion of Peter de Luna, that a general council cannot in any case be convened without the Pope, is a heresy now expressly condemned. This assertion of Peter de Luna, that if he had believed certain people at the time of the Council of Pisa, there would not be keys in the Church today, is manifestly heretical, on the presupposition that the law of God endures until the consummation of the world. This assertion of Peter de Luna, that Christ and the Pope are one head of the Church, is heretical in appearance, unless it is reduced to some sound, though rather improper, sense.

units.la: Aduertendum est postremo, quod super materia haeresis fundatae sunt principaliter conclusiones praedictae in assertionibus Petri de Luna. Primo, quoniam & voces & scripturae significant manifestius conceptum mentis iuxta dictum Christi: Ex verbis tuis iustificaberis &c. Cui consonat dictum Aristo. quod voces sunt signa earum quae in mente sunt passionum. Secundo, quia conuincere hominem haereticum esse, ex solis operibus sine vocibus difficilimum est: attento quod haeresis principaliter consistit in intellectu. Propter quod tertio dicitur, quod licet ex praedictis articulis contra Petrum de Luna & sufficienter in facto probatis posset & debeat sufficienter concludi contra eundem Petrum de Luna, quod ipse est notorie periurus, notorie schismaticus, notorie scandalizans vniuersalem Ecclesiam sanctam Dei, & per consequens de haeretica prauitate vehementer notandus & suspectus; praesertim circa hunc articulum: Vnam sanctam &c. Et circa praeceptum hoc: Non periurabis &c. Ac perinde per huiusmodi suspitionem vehementem & scandalum notorium datum in materia schismatis & periurii & incorrigibilitatem sit ab omni officio papatus vero vel praetenso rationabiliter & iudicialiter deponendus: prout multi solemniter ex iuribus allegarunt & probauerunt: nihilominus ex solis eisdem productis & probatis non videtur sufficienter concludi, quod sit haereticus proprie dictus, nisi confundatur ex propriis assertionibus, suis, constitutionibus & responsionibus datis tam verbo quam scripto. Quamobrem studiosius scriptum est vel articulatum circa huiusmodi assertiones: attento praecipue, quod nonnulli reuocant in dubium, an Papa deponi possit, vel habeat iudicem superiorem in quocunque crimine, nisi sit a fide deuius, vel haereticus proprie dictus.
units.tr: Lastly, it must be noted that the aforesaid conclusions drawn from the assertions of Peter de Luna are based chiefly on the matter of heresy. First, because both words and writings signify more plainly the concept of the mind, according to the saying of Christ: By your words you shall be justified etc. To this agrees the saying of Aristotle: words are signs of the affections that are in the mind. Second, because it is very difficult to prove from deeds alone, without words, that a man is a heretic, since heresy consists principally in the intellect. For this reason, third, it is said that although from the aforesaid articles against Peter de Luna, which are sufficiently proved in fact, it can and should be sufficiently concluded against the same Peter de Luna that he is notoriously perjured, notoriously schismatic, and notoriously scandalizing the holy universal Church of God, and consequently that he is to be strongly marked and suspected of heretical depravity, especially concerning this article "One holy [Church]" etc., and concerning this precept "You shall not swear falsely" etc. Accordingly, on account of such strong suspicion and notorious scandal given in the matter of schism and perjury, and his incorrigibility, he is to be reasonably and judicially deposed from every office of the papacy, whether true or claimed, as many have solemnly argued and proved from the laws. Nevertheless, from these same produced and proved matters alone it does not seem sufficiently concluded that he is a heretic properly so called, unless he is convicted out of his own assertions, his constitutions, and the replies given both by word and in writing. Wherefore the matter has been examined and articulated more carefully concerning such assertions, especially since some call into doubt whether the Pope can be deposed, or has a superior judge in any crime, unless he has departed from the faith or is a heretic properly so called.

units.la: DECRETA SACRAE FACVLTATIS THEOLOGIAE PARISIENSIS, DE POTESTATE ECCLESIASTICA, ET PRIMATV ROMANI PONTIFICIS, contra Sectarios huius se- culi.
units.tr: DECREES OF THE SACRED FACULTY OF THEOLOGY OF PARIS, CONCERNING ECCLESIASTICAL POWER AND THE PRIMACY OF THE ROMAN PONTIFF, against the sectaries of this age.

units.la: IN nomine Domini, Amen: Per hoc praesens publicum instrumentum, cunctis pateat euidenter, & sit notum, quod anno eiusdem Domini millesimo CCCCmo XXIXo, more Gallicano, indictione octaua, mensis Martii die tricesima & penultima, pontificatus sanctissimi in Christo patris, & Domini nostri, Domini Martini diuina prouidentia Papae, V. Anno XIIIo. In congregatione venerabilium & circumspectorum virorum Dominorum & Magistrorum sacrae Theologiae Facultatis studii Parisiensis, in sancto Mathurino multum solenniter congregatorum, & more solito dictae Facultatis Theologiae congregationem ibidem celebrantium: de mandato venerabilis & circumspecti viri Magistri Petri de Dierreyo dictae Facultatis Decani, tam regentium quam non regentium, & religiosorum ac secularium, ad infra scripta ibidem vocatorum, speciliter propter hoc personaliter constitutus praefatus Dominus Decanus dicens & proponens, quod frater Ioannes Sarrazin ordinis fratrum Praedicatorum, Licentiatus in Theologia, post vesperias suas, fuerat delatus apud ipsum, & consequenter apud dictam Facultatem, tanquam dixisset ea quae sequuntur, sicut etiam scripta exhibita de propria manu sonate videbantur, formam quae sequitur continentia.
units.tr: In the name of the Lord, Amen. Let it be plain and known to all by this present public instrument that in the year of the same Lord 1429, according to the Gallican reckoning, in the eighth indiction, on the thirtieth and penultimate day of March, in the thirteenth year of the pontificate of the most holy father in Christ and our Lord, Lord Martin, by divine providence Pope V, there was a gathering of the venerable and circumspect men, the Lords and Masters of the Sacred Faculty of Theology of the University of Paris, solemnly assembled at St Mathurin and holding there, as usual, the congregation of the said Faculty of Theology. By the mandate of the venerable and circumspect Master Pierre de Dierreyo, Dean of the said Faculty, regents and non-regents, religious and secular alike, summoned there to the matters written below, the aforesaid Lord Dean, personally present for this purpose, said and set forth that brother Jean Sarrazin of the Order of Preachers, Licentiate in Theology, after his vespers, had been reported to him and consequently to the said Faculty as having said the things that follow; the written statements shown, which seemed to be in his own hand, contained the form that follows.

units.la: Primo, omnes potestates iurisdictionis Ecclesiae, aliae a Papali potestate, sunt ab ipso Papa quantum ad institutionem, & collationem.
units.tr: First, all powers of jurisdiction in the Church, other than the Papal power, derive from the Pope himself, as to their institution and conferral.

units.la: Secundo, huiusmodi potestates non sunt de iure diuino, nec immediate instituta a Deo.
units.tr: Second, such powers are not of divine right, nor instituted immediately by God.

units.la: Tertio, non inuenitur Christum tales potestates, scil. alias a Papali, expressisse, sed tantum premam, cui commisit Ecclesiae fundationem.
units.tr: Third, it is not found that Christ expressed such powers, that is, other than the Papal power, but only the chief, to whom he committed the foundation of the Church.

units.la: Quarto, quandocunq; in aliquo Concilio aliqua instituuntur tota auctoritas dans vigorem statutis, in solo lumine residet Pontificio.
units.tr: Fourth, whenever some matters are instituted in any Council, the whole authority giving force to the decrees resides in the Pontiff's light alone.

units.la: Quinto, extra Euangelii non habetur expresse alicui Apostolorum, nisi Petro auctoritatem iurisdictionis fuisse collatam.
units.tr: Fifth, outside the Gospel, it is not expressly found that the authority of jurisdiction was conferred on any of the Apostles except Peter.

units.la: Sexto, dicere inferiorum Prælatorum potestatem iurisdictionis, siue sint Episcopi, siue Curati, esse immediate à Deo, sicut potestatem Papæ, veritati quodammodo repugnat.
units.tr: Sixth, to say that the power of jurisdiction of inferior prelates, whether they be bishops or parish priests, is immediately from God, just as the power of the Pope is, is in some way opposed to the truth.

units.la: Septimo, sicut nullus flos, & nulla pullulatio, nec etiam omnes flores & pullulationes, simul possunt aliquid in arborem, quia hæc omnia sunt propter arborem instituta, & ab arbore deriuata: sic omnes aliæ potestates, nihil de iure possunt contra summum sacerdotium. Infra dicitur, quod spiritualis potestas est summus Pontifex, vt recitatur Hugonem de sancto Victore dixisse, secundo de Sacramentis: ex quo potest videri, quod hic per summum Pontificium, summus Pontifex intelligatur.
units.tr: Seventh, just as no flower and no sprouting, nor indeed all flowers and sproutings together, can make anything into a tree, because all of these were instituted on account of the tree and derive from the tree, so all other powers can do nothing by right against the supreme priesthood. Below it is said that the spiritual power is the supreme Pontiff, as is reported to have been said by Hugh of St Victor in the second book On the Sacraments; from which it can be seen that here by the supreme Pontificate the supreme Pontiff is meant.

units.la: Octauo, summus Pontifex canonicam Simoniam à iure positiuo prohibitam, non potest committere.
units.tr: Eighth, the supreme Pontiff cannot commit canonical simony, which is forbidden by positive law.

units.la: Quæ propositiones seu dicta, pluries per deputatos eiusdem Facultatis diligenter examinata, iudicabamus esse reparanda: præsertim cum Dominus Rector, & multi de Vniuersitate, talem reparationem requisissent in præsentia dictæ Facultatis. Tandem præfatus Dominus Decanus, ex matura & diligenti ac concordi deliberatione Magistrorum dictæ Facultatis, tam regentium quam non regentium, & tam secularium quam religiosorum, præhabita: concludit, quod prædictus frater Iohannes Sarrazin, ordinis fratrum Prædicatorum, qui tunc & alias auditus fuit ad longum, & cuius intentio scita fuit, & qui etiam se submiserat dictæ facultati Theologiæ, diceret in dicta congregatione, & deinde in aula fratris Girardi de Salinis ordinis fratrum Minorum, post primam quæstionem expectatoriam, sub hac forma.
units.tr: These propositions or statements, examined carefully many times by the deputies of the same Faculty, we judged to need correction, especially since the Rector and many of the University had required such a correction in the presence of the said Faculty. At last the aforesaid Lord Dean, after mature and careful deliberation and common agreement of the Masters of the said Faculty, regents and non-regents, secular and religious alike, having been obtained beforehand, concluded that the aforesaid brother Jean Sarrazin, of the Order of Preachers, who had then and at other times been heard at length, whose intention was known, and who had also submitted himself to the said Faculty of Theology, should say in the said congregation, and afterwards in the hall of brother Girard de Salinis of the Order of Friars Minor, after the first expected question, in this form.

units.la: Ex vesperiis meis quidam fuerunt scandalizati sicut mihi significatum est per matrem meam facultatem Theologiæ, tanquam intellexerint, quod voluerim inter alia, detrahere potestati & Ecclesiæ, & prælatorum aliorum à summo Pontifice, tam maiorum quam minorum, & quorundam aliorum Ecclesiasticorum: & specialiter occasione quarundam propositionum per me in eisdem vesperiis meis dictarum: Volens propterea quantum in me est, tollere omne scandalum, & esse filius obedientiæ & pacis, & assertor veritatis, dico nunc ex ordinatione eiusdem matris meæ facultatis Theologiæ, cuius ordinationi, dispositioni, & omnimodæ determinationi me submisi, & submitto, ac etiam vltronea voluntate viri, tales quæ sequuntur.
units.tr: Following my vespers, some were scandalised, as my mother the Faculty of Theology has informed me, since they understood that I had wished, among other things, to detract from the power and the Church, and from the other prelates under the supreme Pontiff, both greater and lesser, and from certain other ecclesiastics; and especially on account of certain propositions which I had stated in those vespers of mine. Wishing therefore, as far as in me lies, to remove all scandal, and to be a son of obedience and peace and an asserter of the truth, I now say, at the direction of this same mother of mine, the Faculty of Theology, to whose direction, disposition and full determination I have submitted and do submit myself, and also of my own free will, the following things.

units.la: Prima, omnes potestates iurisdictionis Ecclesiæ, aliæ à Papali potestate, sunt ab ipso Christo, quantum ad institutionem & collationem primariam: à Papa autem & ab Ecclesia, quantum ad limitationem, & dispensationem ministerialem.
units.tr: First, all powers of jurisdiction in the Church, other than the Papal power, derive from Christ himself as to their primary institution and conferral; but from the Pope and from the Church as to their limitation and ministerial dispensation.

units.la: Secunda, huiusmodi potestates sunt de iure diuino, & immediate institutæ à Deo.
units.tr: Second, such powers are of divine right and instituted immediately by God.

units.la: Tertia, inuenitur in sacra scriptura Christum Ecclesiam fundasse, & potestates alias à Papali expresse ordinasse.
units.tr: Third, it is found in holy Scripture that Christ founded the Church and expressly ordained other powers besides the Papal power.

units.la: Quarta Veritas, quandocunque in aliquo Concilio aliqua instituuntur, tota auctoritas dans vigorem statutis, residet non in solo summo Pontifice, sed principaliter in Spiritu Sancto, & Ecclesia Catholica.
units.tr: Fourth, the truth is that whenever some matters are instituted in any Council, the whole authority giving force to the decrees resides not in the supreme Pontiff alone but principally in the Holy Spirit and the Catholic Church.

units.la: Quinta, ex textu Euangelii & doctrina Apostolorum habetur expresse, Apostolis & discipulis à Christo missis, auctoritatem iurisdictionis fuisse collatam.
units.tr: Fifth, it is expressly held from the text of the Gospel and the teaching of the Apostles that the authority of jurisdiction was conferred on the Apostles and disciples sent by Christ.

units.la: Sexta, dicere inferiorum prælatorum potestatem iurisdictionis, siue sint Episcopi, siue sint curati, esse immediate à Deo, Euangelicæ & Apostolicæ consonat veritati.
units.tr: Sixth, to say that the power of jurisdiction of inferior prelates, whether they be bishops or parish priests, is immediately from God, agrees with the Gospel and Apostolic truth.

units.la: Septima, aliqua potestas Ecclesiæ, de iure potest aliquid, & in certis casibus, contra summum Pontificem.
units.tr: Seventh, some power of the Church may by right do something, and in certain cases, against the supreme Pontiff.

units.la: Octaua veritas, quicunque parus viator, habens vsum rationis, cuiuscunque dignitatis, auctoritatis, aut præeminentiæ, etiamsi Papalis, existat, Simoniam potest committere.
units.tr: Eighth truth: whoever is a mortal wayfarer, having the use of reason, of whatever dignity, authority or pre-eminence, even if Papal, may commit simony.

units.la: Denique, si aliqua protulerim vel scripserim, quæ videantur prædictis contraria, vel quæaliter scripta sint, nolo in eis stare, sed volo & supplico haberi pro non dictis vel scriptis, & alia quæcunque, quæ viderentur præbere occasionem scandali vel erroris.
units.tr: Finally, if I have uttered or written anything which seems contrary to the foregoing, or which is written in any other way, I do not wish to stand by it, but I wish and beg that it be held as unsaid and unwritten, and likewise anything else which might seem to give occasion for scandal or error.

units.la: Qui quidem frater Ioannes Sarrazin, modo & forma prædictis, omnia & singula fecit, dixit & protulit. Primo, videlicet in dicta congregatione in Capitulo sancti Mathurini Parisiis, vt præfertur, celebrata, præsentibus ibidem venerabilibus & circumspectis viris, Domino Decano prænominato, ac magistris Ioanne de Trecis, Guillermo de Bomillon, Guillermo de Sello, Emerico de Brusseriis, Rollando Barguenal, Gillermo Boutitot, Ioanne de Vernonne, Remondo de Altoponte, Philippo Bauet, Dionysio de Sabreuois, Ioanne le Gallois, Girardo Gerron, Martino Billery, Ioanne Pulchripatris: Ioanne de Gondeuiller, Thoma Monachi, Rogerio de Gaillon, Ioanne Soqueri, Guillermo Adelie, Ioanne Tripier, Ioanne Grauestain, Gofredo Coclearis, Michaele Langlois, Georgio de Vallesponsa, Roberto de Porta, & Ioanne de Quesneyo, Magistris in Theologia, tam secularibus quam religiosis, ac Ioanne Vacheau principali bidello eiusdem Facultatis. Item eisdem anno, indictione, mense, die, & pontificatu prædictis, dictus frater Ioannes Sarrazin dictas propositiones legit & reparauit modo & forma supradictis, in aula reuerendi patris Domini Episcopi Parisiensis, post primam quæstionem magisterii fratris Girardi de Salinis supradicti, præsentibus dicto reuerendo in Christo Patre, Domino Episcopo Parisiensi, ac venerabilibus ac circumspectis viris Magistris Petro de Diereyo Decano eiusdem Facultatis, Guillermo Eurardy Rectore Vniuersitatis Parisien. Hugone Maioris vicegerentis Cancellarii Ecclesiæ Parisien. Guillermo de Sella, Ioanne Pulchri patris, Rogerio de Gaillon, Ioanne Soqueti, Gofredo Coclearis Magistris in Theologia, Laurentio Callor, Petro de la Hafardiere, Guillermo Hugueti, & Guillermo Candelli, Magistris in artibus, cum pluribus aliis tam Magistris, quam Doctoribus, Icholaribus, Baccalariis, & secularibus ibidem existentibus: de & supra quibus praemissis omnibus & singulis, dicti Domini Decanus & Rector, & quilibet ipsorum petierunt & petiit a me notario publico sibi fieri & confici publicum instrumentum, vnum vel plura. Acta fuerunt haec anno, indictione, mense, die, pontificatu, & locis praedictis, praesentibus praenominatis testibus ad praemissa vocatis specialiter, & rogatis. Et ego Laurentius Pontrelli presbyter Curatus Parochialis Ecclesiae de Annouilla, Rothomagensis dioecesis, publicus Apostolica & Imperiali auctoritatibus notarius, praemissis omnibus & singulis, dum sic, vt superius scripta sunt, fierent, & agerentur, vna cum praenominatis testibus praesens fui, eaque sic fieri vidi, & audiui: Idcirco huic praesenti publico instrumento aliena manu fideliter scripto, me aliis occupato negotiis, signum meum publicum appositi consuetum, hic me propria manu subscribendo, requisitus & rogatus, in testimonium veritatis praemissorum.
units.tr: Which brother Jean Sarrazin, in the manner and form stated above, did, said and uttered all and each of these things.
