First, namely, in the said congregation held in the chapter of St Mathurin at Paris, as stated, in the presence there of the venerable and circumspect men, the aforesaid Lord Dean, and the Masters Jean de Troyes, Guillaume de Bomillon, Guillaume de Sella, Aymeric de Brussières, Roland Barguenal, Guillaume Boutitot, Jean de Vernon, Raymond de Haute-Pont, Philippe Bauet, Denis de Sabreuois, Jean le Gallois, Girard Gerron, Martin Billery, Jean Pulchripatris, Jean de Gondeuiller, Thomas Monachi, Roger de Gaillon, Jean Soquer, Guillaume Adelie, Jean Tripier, Jean Grauestain, Geoffroy Coclearis, Michel Langlois, Georges de Vallesponsa, Robert de Porta, and Jean de Quesnoy, Masters in Theology, both secular and religious, and Jean Vacheau, principal beadle of the same Faculty. Likewise, in the same year, indiction, month, day and pontificate as above, the said brother Jean Sarrazin read and corrected the said propositions in the manner and form stated above, in the hall of the reverend father, the Lord Bishop of Paris, after the first question of the mastership of the aforesaid brother Girard de Salinis, in the presence of the said reverend father in Christ, the Lord Bishop of Paris, and the venerable and circumspect men, Masters Pierre de Dierreyo, Dean of the same Faculty, Guillaume Eurardy, Rector of the University of Paris, Hugues Maioris, vice-chancellor of the Church of Paris, Guillaume de Sella, Jean Pulchripatris, Roger de Gaillon, Jean Soqueti, Geoffroy Coclearis, Masters in Theology, Laurent Callor, Pierre de la Hafardiere, Guillaume Hugueti, and Guillaume Candelli, Masters in the arts, together with many others, both Masters and Doctors, scholars, bachelors and laymen present there. Concerning and upon all and each of the aforesaid matters, the said Lord Dean and Rector, and each of them, asked and requested of me, the notary public, that one or more public instruments be made and drawn up for them. These things were done in the year, indiction, month, day, pontificate and places aforesaid, the aforenamed witnesses being specially summoned and asked to be present for the matters stated. And I, Laurent Pontrelli, priest, parish curate of the church of Annouilla, of the diocese of Rouen, public notary by apostolic and imperial authority, was present when all and each of the aforesaid matters were done and transacted as written above, together with the aforenamed witnesses, and I saw and heard that they were so done. Therefore, being occupied with other business, I have, at the request and asking of the parties, written this present public instrument faithfully by another hand, and have affixed my customary public sign, subscribing here with my own hand, in witness of the truth of the aforesaid matters.

units.la: Signatum Pontrelli.
units.tr: Signed at Pontrelli.

units.la: Hoc decretum confirmatur etiam sex sequentibus conclusionibus articulorum eiusdem facultatis Parisiensis contra Lutherum: quibus constat Christum Dominum immediate contulisse infallibilem auctoritatem decernendi, & excommunicandi, toti Ecclesiae collectiue sumptae, vt per vnum exerceretur: summa vero totius iurisdictionis Ecclesiasticae, in facultate excommunicandi consistit, vt omnes Theologi norunt.
units.tr: This decree is also confirmed by the six following conclusions of the articles of the same Faculty of Paris against Luther; from which it is established that Christ the Lord immediately conferred on the whole Church, taken collectively, the infallible authority of decreeing and excommunicating, to be exercised through one person; and the sum of all ecclesiastical jurisdiction consists in the power of excommunicating, as all theologians know.

units.la: Articulus XVIII.
units.tr: Article XVIII.

units.la: Tenetur & quilibet Christianus firmiter credere vnam esse in terris vniuersalem Ecclesiam visibilem, quae in fide & moribus errare non potest: cui omnes fideles, in his quae sunt fidei & morum, obedire astringuntur.
units.tr: Every Christian is also bound to believe firmly that there is one universal visible Church on earth, which cannot err in faith or morals, and to which all the faithful are bound to render obedience in those matters which pertain to faith and morals.

units.la: XIX.
units.tr: XIX.

units.la: Quod si quid in scripturis sacris controuersiae aut dubii oriatur, ad praefatam Ecclesiam definire & determinare spectat.
units.tr: If any controversy or doubt arises in the sacred Scriptures, it belongs to the aforesaid Church to define and determine it.

units.la: XX.
units.tr: XX.

units.la: Est & certum, multa esse credenda, quae non sunt expresse & speciatim tradita in scripturis sacris: quae tamen per traditionem Ecclesiae sunt necessario recipienda.
units.tr: It is also certain that many things are to be believed which are not expressly and specifically handed down in the sacred Scriptures, and which nevertheless must necessarily be received through the tradition of the Church.

units.la: XXI.
units.tr: XXI.

units.la: Eodem veritatis firmamento recipiendum, potestatem excommunicandi esse de iure diuino immediate a Christo Ecclesiae concessam: & ob id magnopere timendas esse censuras Ecclesiasticas.
units.tr: With the same firmness of truth it must be received that the power of excommunication was granted by divine right immediately to the Church by Christ; and that for this reason ecclesiastical censures are greatly to be feared.

units.la: XXII.
units.tr: XXII.

units.la: Certum est Concilium generale legitime congregatam vniuersalem repraesentans Ecclesiam, in fidei & morum determinationibus errare non posse.
units.tr: It is certain that a general Council, lawfully assembled and representing the universal Church, cannot err in its determinations of faith and morals.

units.la: XXIII.
units.tr: XXIII.

units.la: Nec minus certum, vnum esse de iure diuino, in Ecclesia Christi militante summum Pontificem: cui omnes Christiani parere tenentur: qui quidem potestatem habet & indulgentias conferendi.
units.tr: No less certain is it that by divine right there is one supreme Pontiff in the militant Church of Christ, to whom all Christians are bound to submit; and who indeed has the power of granting indulgences.

units.la: Hic operae pretium est notare, in more positum esse, vt omnes Baccalaurei Facultatis Theologiae Parisiensis, tam seculares quam regulares, solenniter iurent in praedictos articulos, eosque propria syngrapha obsignent: atque insuper in omnium disputationum aut actorum suorum exordio, palam & publice profitentur, se sacrorum Conciliorum definitionibus, nec non decretis sacratissimae facultatis Theologiae Parisiensis, iugiter adhaesuros: quarum protestationum eximium extat monimentum in tabulario Facultatis, anno M. D. VIII. factum, & a Guidone Rigaudeau, ac Ioanne Crozon Notariis publicis obsignatum.
units.tr: It is worth noting here that it is the custom that all Bachelors of the Faculty of Theology of Paris, both secular and regular, solemnly swear to the aforesaid articles and confirm them with their own signed bond; and moreover, at the beginning of all their disputations or acts, they openly and publicly profess that they will constantly adhere to the definitions of the sacred Councils and likewise to the decrees of the most sacred Faculty of Theology of Paris. An outstanding record of these protestations survives in the archive of the Faculty, made in the year 1508 and sealed by Guido Rigaudeau and John Crozon, public notaries.

units.la: PAVLI DECRETO- RVM DOCTORIS, ANGLI AVREVM SPECV- LVM PAPAE, EIVS CVRIAE, PRAELATORVM, ET aliorum Spiritualium, super plenitudine potestatis Papalis scriptum ante ducentos annos.
units.tr: Paul, Doctor of the Decretals, an Englishman: The Golden Mirror of the Pope, His Curia, the Prelates, and Other Spiritual Persons, concerning the Fullness of Papal Power, written two hundred years ago.

units.la: Venerendissimis in Christo Patribus & Dominis, Dominis sacrosanctæ Romanæ ac Vniuersalis Ecclesiæ Cardinalibus, nec non aliarum Ecclesiarum Patriarchis, Metropolitanis, Archiepiscopis, Episcopis, Abbatibus, Prælatisque, ac etiam Curiæ Romanæ officialibus vniuersis, totiq; clericali coetui per vniuersum constitutis: Paulus minimus, & vtinam inter discipulos veros Iesu Christi, planctum pro affectu, & dolorem, heu corde anxius qua voce intonare ipse debeam. Quis hominum non attendit tantam pestem, mortificantem animas, in populo Christiano grauissime saeuientem? En schismata, en hæreses & errores vbilibet infiniti. Vere durissima plaga Domini descendit in Israel, quam in se experitur his temporibus nostra ætas. Sed heu vile aurum in tātū cathenauit modo mentem Moysi, quod nedum placare non curat indignantem animum, sed mala malis accumulans machinatur quotidie ad deteriora prouocare. Mira supra omne modum res agitur, vt inde exemplar omnis mali progrediatur, vnde processerat sanctitatis omnis norma, & vnde tota Christi ecclesia Deo ædificante constructa sumpsit exordiū, inde patitur iam ruinam, illic iugum suaue Domini abiicitur, frangitur lex diuina, iuraq; canonica pro salute humana per ora sanctorum Spiritus sancti dictata, respuuntur penitus, & quasi inania reputantur. Sicq; tota Romana curia à plāta pedis vsq; ad verticē capitis, patenter excæcata erroribus, ipsa errorum sqorū veneno inebriauit omnes fere mundi partes, ac si immensam creatoris omnipotentia Papa ad suū libitum posset limitare. Omnes quidem intus murmurant, nullus clamat. Et quoniā in extremis iam malorū laborantes summus positi, in quos cuncti errores huius seculi deuenerunt: qua ergo ratione silere valeo, & non potius obmutescentibus aliis tam præsidibus quam doctoribus, fortius exclamare? Nam etiam principes catholici seculares mutuis dissensionibus occupati, tantam corruptionē sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ non aduertunt. Vos tamen, qui pastores estis positi, & officii apostolici successores, cur tā longum periculosumq; negligentiæ somnū agitis, & non celerius concurritis: obmutescitis, & non clamatis? Eia & eia, ô patres & Domini, nunq; ne ob perditionis ignominiam, gens sancta & regale sacerdotiū voce estis prophetica nuncupati? Salte iam ad hanc vocem meā pusillam, iam desides confluite. Quoniā securis est iam posita ad radicē arboris. Et exaltatis in altum vocibus, exclamate: quia non nisi in multitudine clamantiū, fugam hostes receperunt. Et ruina suo pondere nocuior, non nisi per multitudinem subleuatur. Vt igitur ego ipse viribus exiguus, militaturus sub vexillo Domini, & indutus fortitudine Iesu Christi, vestrę vniversitati occurrendo viā aperiam, & aciem aduersus inimicos Domini pugnæ ponam: Tria tanta mala germinantia, prolequenda à persequenda, p præsenti aggredior: quæ iuxta posse conabor machina triplici, sc. auctoritate sacræ scripturæ, ratione naturali, & iure canonico, dirigente Domino conterere, euellere, & radicitus extirpare. Primo sc. errores grauissimos curiæ Romanæ detegam, circa puisiones beneficiorū, & indulgentiarū concessiones, detestasq; eliminando cū simoniacis, & eorum participibus condemnabo. Secundo, scripta minus catholice scribentiū quædam quæ tantæ destructioni ecclesiasticæ causam præstasse videbantur aut occasionē, tanq; hæretica, clarissime reprobabo: & ibi fundamentū eueruabo illius destructionis de symoniacis, q a phibitis, & de phibitis, q a symoniacis, quę multas etiā cōmuniter peritos videtur ponere in errorē. Tertio, totā Romanam curiā erroneam, & in statu damnationis laborantē, ex verissimis fundamentis declarabo, nec non omnes, q à iure cōmuni per exorbitātes gratias, beneficia ecclesiastica sunt adepti, Papæ plenitudine potestatis pertractando. Et secundū hoc tres erunt partes, quas Lectori suadeo toto studio perlegere. Quoniā, quia ea quæ Dei sunt nesciunt, à Deo etiam nesciuntur, ad Cor. 14. Siquis ignorat, ignorabitur. Si quæ vero in consueta fortasse reperiat, non tamen spero à veritate deuiare, ardentius ponderet sollicitus animus, & nō de facili respuat: quemadmodū non intelligentium, imo veriùs detrahentium, dicit mordax lingua: correctione tamen melius sentientiū, cū humilitate postulo, in spiritu lenitatis. Nec plixitatem charitas legentis arguat, quam vtiq; expetebat infirmitas per vniuersum ægrotantis. Et vt tractandi materia legenti reddatur suauior, & elucidationem recipiat clariorē, singo per dialogū, Petrum & Paulū inuicem disputantes. Insuper hoc prouiso, quod quæcunq; iura allegauero propter melius veritatem dicendorum experiri cupientem, virgulam seu lineam tubeam vbilibet sub quotis seu allegatis protraham, vt legentem non impediat: quas lector cum signo huiusmodi rubeo, vt taliter designatas, pro suo libito faciliter poterit persaltare. Et sic praesens Capitulum tam exercitatis in iure canonico, quam non exercitatis, aptus patebit omnib. ad legendum: quem ad gazophylacium Domini offero in charitate viduae, duo minuta offerentis.
units.tr: To the most venerable fathers and lords in Christ, the Cardinals of the holy Roman and universal Church, and likewise the Patriarchs, Metropolitans, Archbishops, Bishops, Abbots and Prelates of the other churches, and also all the officials of the Roman Curia, and the whole clerical assembly throughout the world: Paul, the least of men, and would God among the true disciples of Jesus Christ, with a heart anxious with grief and sorrow, must I raise a lament, alas, with what voice I can. Who among men does not notice so great a plague, deadening souls and raging most grievously among the Christian people? Behold schisms, behold heresies and errors without number everywhere. Truly the most severe stroke of the Lord has fallen upon Israel, and our age experiences it in these times. But alas, vile gold has so enchained the mind of Moses that it not only takes no care to appease the indignant spirit, but, heaping evils upon evils, it plots daily to provoke worse. A strange thing beyond all measure is going on: the pattern of all evil is advancing from the very place from which the standard of all holiness proceeded, and from which the whole Church of Christ, built by God's hand, took its beginning. From there it now suffers ruin; there the sweet yoke of the Lord is cast off, the divine law is broken, and the canonical laws, dictated for the salvation of men by the mouths of the saints through the Holy Spirit, are utterly rejected and reckoned as empty things. Thus the whole Roman Curia, from the sole of the foot to the crown of the head, plainly blinded by errors, has itself drunk up with the poison of its errors almost all the parts of the world, as though the Pope could limit the immense omnipotence of the Creator at his pleasure. All indeed murmur inwardly, but no one cries out. And since those who labour in the extremities of evils, that is, the highest rulers, have fallen into all the errors of this age, by what reasoning can I keep silent, and not rather cry out more loudly, while the other leaders as well as the teachers are struck dumb? For even the Catholic secular princes, occupied with their mutual dissensions, do not notice so great a corruption of our holy mother the Church. But you, who have been set as ministers and are successors of the apostolic office, why do you sleep so long and so dangerous a sleep of negligence, and do not run together more quickly? Are you struck dumb and do not cry out? Come, come, O fathers and lords, were you never named, by the reproach of perdition, a holy people and a royal priesthood with prophetic voice? Now at last, at this my little voice, come together, you who have been idle. For the axe is already laid to the root of the tree. And raise your voices on high and cry out, for enemies have taken to flight only before a multitude of those crying out; and a ruin, more harmful by its own weight, is raised up only by a multitude. Therefore, that I, though weak in my own strength, may serve under the banner of the Lord, clothed with the strength of Jesus Christ, and may open a way by meeting your whole assembly, and set my battle line against the enemies of the Lord: I now take up three great evils that are sprouting, to be set forth and pursued. With God directing, I will attempt to crush, pluck up and root out these with a threefold machine, namely the authority of Holy Scripture, natural reason, and canon law. First, I will lay bare the most grievous errors of the Roman Curia concerning the provisions of benefices and the granting of indulgences, and I will condemn them, detesting them along with the simoniacs and their partners. Second, I will clearly reprove as heretical certain writings of less than Catholic authors, which seemed to have given the cause or occasion for so great a destruction of the Church, namely the doctrine that the things forbidden come from the simoniacs, and that the simoniacs come from the forbidden things, a doctrine which seems to lead many of the commonly experienced into error, and there I will overturn the foundation of that destruction. Third, I will declare from the most true foundations that the whole Roman Curia is erroneous and labours in a state of damnation, and I will also treat of all who have obtained ecclesiastical benefices contrary to the common law through exorbitant graces, by the fullness of the Pope's power. And accordingly there will be three parts, which I urge the reader to read through with all diligence. For those who do not know the things of God are themselves unknown to God, 1 Cor. 14: "If anyone is ignorant, he will be ignored." If he finds some things perhaps at odds with the customary view, let him not hope to stray from the truth, but let the anxious mind weigh them more eagerly, and not reject them lightly, just as a biting tongue speaks of those who do not understand, or rather of those who slander; yet I ask, with humility and in a spirit of gentleness, for correction from those who think better. Nor let the charity of the reader find fault with the length, which indeed the weakness of one sick throughout the whole body demanded. And so that the matter may be rendered more pleasant to the reader and receive a clearer elucidation, I feign a dialogue with Peter and Paul disputing with one another. Moreover, I make this proviso: whatever laws I have cited, for the sake of setting out the truth more clearly, I will draw a small red stroke or line under the citations wherever they occur, so that it does not hinder the reader; and the reader, who has marked them with such a red sign, may easily skip over them at his pleasure. And thus the present chapter will lie open to all, to read, those trained in canon law as well as those not trained. I offer it to the treasury of the Lord in the charity of the widow, the two small coins of the giver.

units.la: Quantum ad primum, haec pars prima pertractabit naturam titulorum ecclesiasticorum, & quomodo q; plurimi sunt involuti prouisionibus simoniacis: & continebit decem capitula. In capitulo primo ponitur definitio tituli, & eius declaratio. In secundo capitulo, titulorum ecclesiasticorum ordo, vbi incidenter quaedam vtilia pertractantur, & differentia inter dignitates personarum & officia assignatur: insuper inter canonicatus & praebenda. In capitulo tertio declarantur tria, quae requiruntur ad hoc, vt titulus canonice acquiratur: & vnum eorum prosequitur. In capitulo quarto damnatur el. ctionum Papam facta reseruatio, occasione cuius male prouidetur ecclesiis, & decipiuntur electi. In quinto capitulo diuersi errores Romanae curiae circa prouisiones & assecurationes beneficiorum & indulgentiarum, &c. deteguntur. In capitulo sexto ponuntur quatuor regulae, quibus cognoscitur, quando prouisio tituli est simoniaca, aut canonica: & declaratur, quomodo in prouisione simoniaca non datur titulus. In capitulo septimo declaratur multipliciter veritas secundae & tertiae regularum. In capitulo octauo declaratur multipliciter veritas quartae regulae: & datur ratio, quare non transfertur titulus, si datur simoniace: & tamen si solum recipitur simoniace, tenet. In capitulo nono declaratur, quomodo saluari non potest, qui beneficium per symoniam obtinuit, sed illud dimittat secundo, de suspensione symoniaci in beneficio, & ipsius irregularitate. In capitulo decimo declaratur, quomodo officiales & vicarii episcoporum intrantium per symoniam, & intrantium familiares, sunt participes simoniae: & omnes alii qui eis participant in his quae spectant ad titulum per symoniam acquisitum, sunt in statu damnationis, vt puta recipientes ab eis beneficia, &c.
units.tr: As to the first, this first part will treat of the nature of ecclesiastical titles, and how very many are entangled in simoniacal provisions; and it will contain ten chapters. In the first chapter the definition of a title is set out and explained. In the second chapter, the order of ecclesiastical titles, where certain useful matters are incidentally treated, and the difference between dignities of persons and offices is assigned; moreover, between canonries and prebends. In the third chapter three things are declared which are required for a title to be canonically acquired, and one of them is pursued further. In the fourth chapter, the reservation made by the Pope on elections is condemned, the occasion of which is that churches are badly provided for and the elect are deceived. In the fifth chapter various errors of the Roman Curia concerning the provisions and assurances of benefices and indulgences, etc., are exposed. In the sixth chapter four rules are laid down by which it is known when the provision of a title is simoniacal or canonical, and it is declared how in a simoniacal provision no title is given. In the seventh chapter the truth of the second and third rules is declared in many ways. In the eighth chapter the truth of the fourth rule is declared in many ways, and the reason is given why a title is not transferred if it is given simoniacally; and yet, if it is only received simoniacally, it holds. In the ninth chapter it is declared how one cannot be saved who has obtained a benefice through simony, but must give it up; and secondly, concerning the suspension of the simoniac in his benefice, and his irregularity. In the tenth chapter it is declared how the officials and vicars of bishops who enter by simony, and the household servants of those who enter, are partakers of simony; and all others who share with them in those things which pertain to a title acquired through simony, are in a state of damnation, for example those who receive benefices from them, etc.

units.la: DIALOGVS PETRI ET PAVLI, DE INSO-LENTIIS ET ERRORIBVS ROMANAE CVRIAE.
units.tr: DIALOGUE OF PETER AND PAUL, CONCERNING THE INSOLENCE AND ERRORS OF THE ROMAN CURIA.

units.la: CAP. I.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: In quo ponitur definitio tituli, & etiam ipsius declaratio.
units.tr: In which the definition of a title is set out, together with its explanation.

units.la: PET. Nunc restat tibi, vt quid de natura titulorum beneficialium est sciendum, in medium edisseras, scilicet quid sit titulus, & vnde habeat originem, &c. vt de corruptione Christianitatis latius appareat, quae inde creuit, & quam non nisi solius Dei virtus sufficit reformare.
units.tr: PET. Now it remains for you to set out before us what must be known about the nature of benefice titles, namely what a title is and where it has its origin, etc., so that the corruption of Christianity that has grown from this may appear more fully, and which only the power of God is sufficient to reform.

units.la: Vt tibi ad praemissa congrue respondere valeam, expedit aequiuocationem termini praenotare. Et multipliciter capitur titulus in iure. Aliquando tatum valet, sicut signum rei appositum: vt vexillum, vel aliud soli principi permissum, de quo in textu & Glo. 16. q. 6. consuetudo. Secundo modo dicitur titulus, omnis causa acquirendi dominium: vt titulus pro emptorio, pro donato, &c. vt dicimus, q; praescriptio in aliquib. requirit bonam fidem, & iustum titulum, in capitulo, Si diligenti, de praescriptis, &c. & cap. 1. lib. 6. Et de his duobus modis non est ad propositum. Tertio modo dicitur ecclesia: vt titulus sancti Petri. Et sic secundum Bernhar. qui hoc notat de cler. c. dudum 2. & in Gl. intitulari dicitur 80. di. episcopi, quod singuli clerici per singulos titulos sunt ponendi, id est, ecclesias. Vnde dicitur in Ordinationibus clericorum, quando vocatur, dicitur talis ad titulum talis plebis. Quarto modo dicit, q; titulus tantum valet, quantum clericatus, vel canonicatus, & sic dicitur quis intitulari, id est, incanonicari, vel incleriari, & sic dicitur 70. di. ab episcopo, quod nullus debet ordinari sine titulo. Glibidem: id est, sine ecclesia, vel beneficio. Sed haec dicta sunt improprie.
units.tr: Since the word is ambiguous, it is useful to note this beforehand, for titulus is taken in several ways in law. Sometimes it means merely a sign attached to a thing, such as a banner, or something else permitted only to the prince, on which see textu & Glo. 16. q. 6. consuetudo. In a second sense titulus means any cause of acquiring ownership, as a title by purchase, by gift, and so on; as we say that prescription in some cases requires good faith and a just title, in the chapter Si diligenti, de praescriptis, &c. & cap. 1. lib. 6. These two senses are not to the point. In a third sense it means a church, as in titulus sancti Petri. So, according to Bernhard, who notes this in de cler. c. dudum 2., and in the gloss, the word intitulari is used in 80. di. episcopi, where it says that individual clerics are to be placed under individual tituli, that is, churches. Hence in the ordination of clerics, when someone is called, it is said that he is called ad titulum talis plebis. In a fourth sense it says that a title is worth as much as clerical or canonical status, and so one is said to be intitulari, that is, made a canon or made a cleric; and thus it is said in 70. di. ab episcopo that no one ought to be ordained without a title. The gloss in the same place says: id est, sine ecclesia, vel beneficio. But these things have been said improperly.

units.la: PET. Ergo dic proprie, definiendo quid sit titulus.
units.tr: PET. Then tell us properly, by defining what a title is.

units.la: PAVL. Ad tuum propositum potest sic describi: Titulus ecclesiasticus est, ius spirituale ex electione, confirmatione, institutione, collatione, vel receptione canonica consentienti proueniens, ad praesidendum alicui ecclesiae, monasterio, vel capellae: seu ad aliquod diuinum officium tantum, aut diuinum officium vel aliud ministerium ecclesiastícum, circa aliquod vel in aliquo eorum exercenda. In hac descriptione, ius spirituale ponitur pro genere, & exprimit causam formalem diffiniti, hoc aggregatum quod sequitur, distinctiue captum, scilicet ex electione, confirmatione, &c. loco differentiarum constitutuarum speciem. Et exprimit causam efficientem, q; adiungitur in descriptione, ibi consentienti, exprimitur subiectum, seu causa materialis: q; ideo ponitur, qa ad hoc vt quaeratur alicui titulus, necesse est vt consentiat, vt in c. quam sic de cler. &c. si tibi absenti. de praeben. lib. 6. Quod autem adiicitur, Ad praesidendum alicui ecclesiae, &c. causa finalis denotatur, seu obiectu formale, circa q; tale ius versatur. Et intelligue illud, ad praesidendum, cum effectu, scilicet cum debitis diuinis officiis, & aliis seruitiis requisitis ad impendendum in prebendis. Et quia quidam sunt tituli tantum ad diuinum officium exercendum destinati, quos vocamus beneficia simplicia: aliq vero non tantum ad diuinum officium, sed etiam cum hoc ad talia seruitia impendenda, siue circa curam & salutem animarum, siue aliarum rerum ecclesiasticarum, & talia dicuntur dignitates personatus, & officia: ad quod vtrumque denotandum, ponitur in descriptione vltima particula. Et iste est finis, propter quem dantur, & sunt inuenti tituli ecclesiastici. Ex quo sequitur, quod qui non potest illa exercere, propter quae inuenti sunt tituli, non est capax beneficii: & per consequens, nec titulus etiam per Papam licite potest sibi conferri, nisi necessitas aut tanta vtilitas reipublicae suadeat, quae sua pietate aequiparetur illi fini, propter quem titulus est inuentus. Ex quo infero, pro prima sagitta in errantes, quod pueri, qui non sunt apti ad diuina officia peragenda, scilicet horas canonicas, ad quas quilibet beneficiatus ratione tituli tenetur, etiam non existens in sacris, ex precepto ecclesiæ 91. di. c. 1. & se. 92. di. c. fi. de cele. miss. dolentes. & secundum omnes communiter doctores (præter Pe. & Ab. qui dixerunt, per alia talia posse fieri, in quo communiter reprobantur) nō sunt capaces de iure communi, in titulo beneficio. ū ecclesiasticorum, quantumcunq; simpliciū. De hoc est casus in c. super ordinata. de præben. Vbi tamen Bernh. in Gl. in v. pueri, vult contrariū, dicens, ex. qui dicit, q pueri nō sunt idonei, & c. intelligitur, id est, infantes ante septennium: post septe vero annos possunt habere simplicia beneficia. Idem tenet post eum Io. An. in c. si eo tempore. de rescrip. & c. ex eo. de elec. li. 6. Et multi scribentes post eos, communiter tali ratione: Quia, ex quo tales possunt ordinari ad minores ordines, & per consequens ordinati possunt deseruire ecclesiis: ergo possunt etiam ad stipendia ecclesiastica intitulari, arg. in c. cum sec. apost. de præben. Salua reuerentia eorum, non aduerterunt, quod magna est differentia inter ea, quæ spectant ad ordinem, & ad titulum. Quia spectatia ad minores ordines, ut portare cereas, vrceolum, canes expellere de ecclesia, &c. illa sunt ordinis, & possunt bene facere pueri: non autem illa contra, quæ spectant ad titulum, ut supra. Et si quandoq; pueri infra 14. annos sciunt talia, quæ titulus exigit, communiter tamen nesciunt: iura autē debent adaptari ad ea quæ communiter accidunt, de despon. impub. literas, non ad ea quæ raro veniant. Et ideo stylus curiæ obseruat, cum mandatur ptouideri de quantumcunq; simplici beneficio, scribitur, Si talis scit legere, & construere, & cantare, &c. Quia propter officium datur beneficium, de rescript. Quia per ambitiosa lib. 6.
units.tr: PAVL. For your purpose it can be described thus: A church title is a spiritual right arising from election, confirmation, institution, collation, or canonical reception with consent, for presiding over some church, monastery or chapel, or for some divine office alone, or for a divine office or other ecclesiastical ministry to be exercised about some or in some of these. In this description, a spiritual right is put for the genus and expresses the formal cause of the thing defined; the aggregate that follows, taken distinctively, namely by election, confirmation, etc., stands in place of the differences that constitute the species. It also expresses the efficient cause, and what is added in the description, with consent, expresses the subject or material cause, which is included because, for a title to be granted to someone, his consent is necessary, as in c. quam sic de cler. &c. si tibi absenti. de praeben. lib. 6. What is added, for presiding over some church, etc., denotes the final cause, or the formal object with which such a right is concerned. And understand that phrase for presiding as including its effect, namely with the due divine offices and the other services required to be rendered for the prebends. And since some titles are destined only for performing the divine office, which we call simple benefices, while others are destined not only for the divine office but also for discharging such services, whether concerning the care and salvation of souls or other ecclesiastical affairs, and such are called dignities, personages and offices, the last particle of the description is included to denote both. This is the end for which ecclesiastical titles are given and were devised. From this it follows that one who cannot perform those things for which titles were devised is not capable of a benefice; and consequently a title cannot lawfully be conferred on him even by the Pope, unless necessity or so great a benefit to the commonwealth urges it, which by its piety equals that end for which the title was devised. From this I infer, as the first arrow against the erring, that boys, who are not fit to perform the divine offices, namely the canonical hours, which every beneficed man is bound by his title to recite, even though he is not in holy orders, by precept of the Church (91. di. c. 1. & 92. di. c. fin. de cele. miss. dolentes), and according to all the doctors commonly (except Pe. and Ab., who said that these things could be done by other such persons, a view commonly rejected), are not capable by common law of a title in an ecclesiastical benefice, however simple. There is a case on this in c. super ordinata. de praeben. Where, however, Bernhard in the gloss on the word pueri holds the contrary, saying: when it says that boys are not suitable, etc., it is to be understood of infants before seven years; after seven years indeed they can hold simple benefices. After him John Andreae holds the same, in c. si eo tempore. de rescrip. and c. ex eo. de elec. lib. 6. And many writing after them commonly reason thus: since such persons can be ordained to the minor orders, and consequently ordained persons can serve the churches, therefore they can also be given ecclesiastical stipends, arguing from c. cum sec. apost. de praeben. With all respect to them, they have not noticed that there is a great difference between what pertains to order and what pertains to title. For the things pertaining to the minor orders, such as carrying wax candles, the ewer, driving dogs out of the church, and so on, belong to order, and boys can do them well; but not those things which pertain to the title, as above. And even if boys under fourteen sometimes know what the title requires, yet commonly they do not; and laws ought to be adapted to what commonly happens, de despon. impub. literas, not to what rarely occurs. And therefore the style of the Curia observes that when it is ordered to provide for any, however simple, benefice, it is written: If such a one knows how to read, construe and sing, etc. Because the benefice is given for the office, de rescript. Because by ambitious [means], lib. 6.

units.la: PET. Quare ponis in descriptione tituli illam clausulam, Ex electione proueniens: cum tamen ex electione nullum ius quæritur in beneficio: & per consequens nec titulus, quamuis ius ad rem tribuitur? Hæc autem multum differunt, ut de concess. præben. c. vlt. lib. 6.
units.tr: PET. Why do you put into the description of a title the clause arising from election, since no right is acquired in a benefice by election, and consequently no title, although a right to the thing is granted? These, however, differ greatly, as in de concess. praeben. c. vlt. lib. 6.

units.la: PAVL. De iure Canonico, electio Romani pontificis etiam a duabus partibus Cardinalium facta, dat statim titulum 23. di. in nomine Domini. De elec. c. licet. Consuetudo tamen Romanorū pontificum, quæ potius solito vsu q iure roboratur, est, quod ante consecrationem & coronationē non scribunt pontificatum in datis, ut refert Io. An. Super datis lib. 6. super verb. Pontificatus. Nam dicit expresse tex. in dicto c. licet: illa absq; vlla exceptione ab vniuersali ecclesia Romanus pontifex habeatur, &c. De aliorum autem inferiorum electionibus est secus: quamuis alii statim post electionem, iure concedente, recipiunt administrationem, in tribus casibus, quorum primus in c. nihil de electis. Secundum est eodem titulo, c. indemnitatibus § si vero & § caterum lib. 6. Tertius in Imperatore, secundum Hug. & Ioh. 93. dist. legimus. Non tamen talis administratio dat titulum. In confirmatione vero etiam datur titulus; nam in electione initiatur spirituale coniugium, quemadmodum sponsalia de futuro: in confirmatione ratum, in consecratione intelligitur consummatum, De translat. præla. Hæc autem accumulatiue ponuntur, institutio, collatio, receptio, in descriptione prædicta. Quia, quamuis vnum sæpe recipitur pro alio, diuersa tamen sunt: vt no. in c. cum in illis. De præben. lib. 6. Et quodlibet illorum dicit titulū ecclesiastici beneficii. Nam instituere, est ius canonicum in ecclesia vel ecclesiastico beneficio tribuere, vt no. in Glos. 2. in c. auctoritate de institutis. Et habet fieri à patrono in præsentatione præcedente, vt de iure pat. c. consultationibus, cum similibus. Collatio autem est, quam facit prælatus iure proprio, sine aliquius facto, vt in c. Si tibi absenti & c. Statutum de præben. cum concor. Prouisio autem est genus ad illa, secundum alios est species. Recipere vero in canonicum & fratrem, quandoq; titulum tribuit, vt no. c. illorum, de præben. in Glo. vlt. & in c. capitulum ecclesiæ sanctæ crucis de rescript. Et subditur hæc dictio, Canonica, in descriptione præmissa, quæ determinat omnia precedentia: quoniam si institutio, collatio, &c. canonica: id est, si non esset facta secundum canones approbatos, & regulas traditas per sanctos patres, non acquireretur aliquis titulus, vt inferius apparebit: sed talis esset fur & latro, vt dicit Saluator in euangelio Iohan. 10. Qui non intrat per ostium, &c. & iura multa consonantia.
units.tr: PAVL. By canon law, the election of the Roman pontiff, even when made by only two parts of the Cardinals, immediately gives a title (23. di. in nomine Domini. De elec. c. licet.). The custom of the Roman pontiffs, however, which is strengthened more by settled practice than by law, is that before consecration and coronation they do not write pontificate in their dates, as John Andreae reports Super datis lib. 6. under the word Pontificatus. For the text in the said chapter licet expressly says that the Roman pontiff is held by the universal Church without any exception, etc. As for the elections of lesser persons, it is otherwise; although others immediately after election, by law, receive administration in three cases, of which the first is in c. nihil de electis. The second is under the same title, c. indemnitatibus § si vero & § caterum lib. 6. The third is in the Emperor, according to Hugh and John, 93. dist. legimus. Such administration, however, does not give a title. In confirmation, however, a title is also given; for in election the spiritual marriage is begun, as betrothal is for the future; in confirmation it is ratified, and in consecration it is understood as consummated, De translat. praela. These things are set down cumulatively in the above description: institution, collation, reception. For although one is often taken for another, they are nevertheless different, as is noted in c. cum in illis. De praeben. lib. 6. And each of them confers a title to an ecclesiastical benefice. For to institute is to confer a canonical right in a church or ecclesiastical benefice, as is noted in Gloss 2 in c. auctoritate de institutis. It must be done by the patron in a preceding presentation, as in de iure pat. c. consultationibus, and similar texts. Collation, however, is what a prelate does by his own right, without anyone else's act, as in c. Si tibi absenti & c. Statutum de praeben. with the concordance. Provision is a genus to these, according to others a species. To receive as canon and brother sometimes confers a title, as noted in c. illorum, de praeben. in the last gloss, and in c. capitulum ecclesiae sanctae crucis de rescript. And the word canonical is added in the above description, which determines all that precedes; for if institution, collation, etc. were not canonical, that is, not made according to the approved canons and rules handed down by the holy fathers, no title would be acquired, as will appear below; such a one would be a thief and a robber, as the Saviour says in the Gospel, John 10. He who does not enter by the door, etc., and many laws agree with this.

units.la: CAP. II.
units.tr: CAP. II.

units.la: De ordine titulorum.
units.tr: On the order of titles.

units.la: PET. Nunc de ordine titulorum te expedias, veluti promisisti.
units.tr: PET. Now, as you promised, settle the order of the titles.

units.la: PAVL. Hic est aduertendum, quod quemadmodum est in cœlesti hierarchia, quod sub potestatibus, quæ indistincte præsunt, ponuntur principatus, quæ singulis prouinciis distribuuntur: & sub his angeli, qui singulis hominibus ad custodiam deputantur, vt patet in 2. Sententiarum, dist. 9. ita etiam est in prælatione Ecclesiæ militantis, vt apud aliquem esset prælatio indistincte in omnes: & sub hoc essent alii, qui in diuersas prouincias diuersam reciperent potestatem: Consequenter sub his alii, ad singula officia deputati. In hac prælatione, quamuis Saluator noster gloriosissimus, prædicatorem post se alios prætulit, tamen Romanam ecclesiam quasi matrem omnium ecclesiarum esse voluit: ex eo, quia Petri & Pauli præsentia ipsam decorauit, qui eam ambo sub eodem tyranno, suo gloriosissimo sanguine decorantes, consecrantes tam sua præsentia quam venerando prætulerunt triumpho, vt legitur 22. di. Sancta & de elect. fundamenta lib. 6. Et ideo successores Petri, quamuis omnes indistincte exercent auctoritatem potestatem: tamen propter corporalem præsentiam, qua non possunt esse vbique, super dispositione Romanam ecclesiam in titulum sunt sortiti, & Romani pontifices appellantur. Secunda vero sedes post Romam, est Alexandrina, beati Petri nomine, in qua beatus Marcus Euangelista, beati Petri discipulus, fuit primus episcopus: & per beatum Petrum illuc missus, qui ipsum in episcopum ordinauit: vt habetur ex Chronica, de Consecrat. & 65. di. §. porro & 22. di. sacro-sancta. sancta 24. q. 1. cum beatissimum. Tertia vero sedes apud Antiochiam, eiusdem B. Petri apostoli honorabilis: quae illic, postquam Romam venisset, 11 annis (ut dicunt Chronica) rexit: & deinde recedens, Ignatium episcopum constituit, & illic primum nomen Christianorum exortum est. Primo. n. omnes fideles dicti fuerant Fratres, vel discipuli, sicut legitur Actuum 21. Sed postea Apostoli fecerunt concilium Antiochenum, didi sunt Christiani, ut dicit Gl. c. Sacrosancta, supra allegata. Et hac auctoritate, Alexandrina ecclesia secundo loco censetur habere a prima. Sed postea in concilio Constantinopolitano, quando Achatius haereticus, praetendens se patriarcha Constantinopolitanum, pro eo quod excommunicaverat & depositerat patriarcham Alexandrinum & Antiochenum, fuit depositus a Gelasio Papa, ut dicit Glossa, 1. c. qua traditione 22. di. & tunc ecclesia Constantinopolitana, quae non fuit de principalioribus sedibus, secundum locum obtinuit a sede Apostolica, tertium Alexandrina, quartum Hierosolymitana: ut in c. vlt. 22. di. in qua Hierosolymitana primus archiepiscopus B. Iacobus Alphaei, qui & Iustus dicebatur, & secundum carnem frater Domini nuncupatus est, a Petro & Iacobo Zebedaei & Iohanne apostolis, est ordinatus, 66. dist. porro.
units.tr: PAUL. Here it must be noted that just as in the heavenly hierarchy the principalities, which are distributed to single provinces, are placed under the powers that preside indiscriminately, and under these the angels who are assigned to guard individual men, as is clear in 2. Sententiarum, dist. 9., so also in the prelacy of the Church militant there is a prelacy over all indiscriminately, and under it others who receive a distinct power for different provinces, and under these again others appointed to particular offices. In this prelacy, although our most glorious Saviour placed other preachers above himself, he nevertheless wished the Roman church to be, as it were, the mother of all churches. This was because the presence of Peter and Paul adorned it, for both of them, adorning and consecrating it with their most glorious blood under the same tyrant, honoured it with their presence and with their venerable triumph, as is read in 22. di. Sancta & de elect. fundamenta lib. 6. And therefore the successors of Peter, although all alike exercise authority and power, nevertheless, on account of the bodily presence which they cannot have everywhere, have obtained the Roman church as their title for the management of affairs, and are called Roman pontiffs. The second see after Rome is Alexandria, which bears the name of blessed Peter, and in which blessed Mark the Evangelist, disciple of blessed Peter, was the first bishop, sent there by blessed Peter, who ordained him bishop, as is found in de Consecrat. & 65. di. §. porro & 22. di. sacro-sancta. sancta 24. q. 1. cum beatissimum. The third see is at Antioch, honourable for the same blessed Peter the apostle. He ruled there, as the Chronica say, for eleven years after coming to Rome; and then, withdrawing, he appointed Ignatius bishop, and there the name of Christians first arose. For at first all the faithful had been called Fratres, vel discipuli, as is read in Acts 21. But later the apostles held the council of Antioch, and they were called Christiani, as the Gloss says on the chapter Sacrosancta cited above. By this authority the Alexandrian church is reckoned to hold second place after the first. But afterwards, at the council of Constantinople, when Acacius the heretic, pretending to be patriarch of Constantinople, had excommunicated and deposed the patriarchs of Alexandria and Antioch, he was deposed by Pope Gelasius, as the Gloss says on qua traditione 22. di. Then the church of Constantinople, which was not among the principal sees, obtained second place from the apostolic see, Alexandria third, and Jerusalem fourth, as in c. vlt. 22. di., where the first archbishop of Jerusalem, blessed James the son of Alphaeus, who was also called Just and was named the brother of the Lord according to the flesh, was ordained by the apostles Peter, James the son of Zebedee, and John, 66. dist. porro.

units.la: PET. Ante quam tractatum diuertas ad alia, videtur omnino, quod non Romana, sed potius Hierosolymitana, caput esse debeat ecclesiarum: quia ultimum locum inter principaliores sedes habere asseris, cum ipsa Hierusalem civitas per praesentiam Salvatoris nostri, & per effusionem sui gloriosissimi sanguinis, quae ibi in ara crucis salutis nostrae victima obtulit, sit consecrata, & non immerito dignior aliis est censenda.
units.tr: PET. Before you turn to other matters, it seems altogether that Jerusalem, and not Rome, ought to be the head of the churches. You say it holds the last place among the principal sees, yet the city of Jerusalem itself was consecrated by the presence of our Saviour and by the effusion of his most glorious blood, which was offered there on the altar of the cross as the victim of our salvation, so that it is not unreasonably to be judged worthier than the others.

units.la: PAVL. Si locus appellaretur ecclesia, probabiliter affirmates, quod Hierosolymitana esset dignior quam Romana. Verum qua non locum, sed congregationem fidelium ecclesia appellamus, non illa vtiq; erit dignior, propter defectum fidei Christianae. Non enim gentem propter locum, sed locum propter gentem Dominus elegit: ut legitur 2. Machab 5. Electio vero Dei gentem sanctificat, ac dignificat, ex quibus aedificatur ecclesia, non aliquis locus terrenus. Vnde potest videri quato Dei mysterio actu sit, ut Petrum non Hierosolymis dimiserit successorem, ubi Christus examinatione suae fidei puiderat in proximo affutura: sed in Romanis partibus, ubi eam praeuiderat ampliandam, & infinitorum martyrum sanguine consecrandam. Cum enim persecutione crebrescente Romae, B. Petrus de Roma fugere voluisset, iux praeceptum magistri, Matt. 10. Cum vos persequentur in civitate ista, fugite in aliam, &c. occurrit ei Christus extra portam civitatis, cui Petrus stupefactus, dixit: Domine, quo vadis? Cui tu Christus respondit, Vado Romam iterum crucifigi, & statim ab oculis eius disparuit. Petrus ex hoc dicto se intelligens tanquam alterum Christum, qua eius in terris ibi vicarius, ibi crucifigi debere, reuersus est, & ibi ad finem vitae remansit: Qui fil. sint le. p venerabilem. Nusquam enim Christi vicarius plus ecclesiae aedificandae conferre potuit, quam in urbe Romana: quia tunc, & diu post, quasi totius orbis dominium tenuit. Et sic congruentissime, quod alibi non ficret, ab eodem fonte pro spiritualib. causis ac temporalibus in orbe duplex riuulus regiminis emanaret: & ut regna Romano imperio subiecta, eo citius fidem Christi suscipierent, quo suam dominationem eandem fidem cernerent recepisse: sic insuper praedicatores fidei Christianae eo fide liberius & securius praedicaret, quo forent imperiali potentia communiti, &c. Vnde Paulus ob hoc dixit ad Festum, sicut legitur Actuum 25. Ad tribunal Caesaris sto, ubi me oportet iudicari, & sic euasit mortem corporalem.
units.tr: PAUL. If a place were called the church, one could fairly affirm that Jerusalem was worthier than Rome. But since we call the church not a place but the gathering of the faithful, Jerusalem will certainly not be worthier, on account of the lack of Christian faith. For the Lord chose not a people for the sake of the place, but the place for the sake of the people, as is read in 2 Maccabees 5. Indeed God's election sanctifies and dignifies the people out of whom the church is built, not some earthly place. Hence one can see what a mystery of God it was that Peter did not leave a successor at Jerusalem, where Christ had already foreseen that his faith would soon be tested, but in the Roman regions, where he had foreseen that the church would be extended and consecrated by the blood of countless martyrs. For when persecution grew fiercer at Rome, blessed Peter wished to flee from Rome, following the precept of his Master in Matthew 10: Cum vos persequentur in civitate ista, fugite in aliam, etc. Christ met him outside the city gate, and Peter, astonished, said: Domine, quo vadis? To which Christ answered: Vado Romam iterum crucifigi, and at once vanished from his eyes. Peter, understanding from this saying that as Christ's vicar on earth he ought to be crucified there, as another Christ, returned, and remained there until the end of his life: Qui fil. sint le. p venerabilem. For nowhere could Christ's vicar contribute more to building up the church than in the city of Rome, because then and long afterwards it held, as it were, dominion over the whole world. And so most fittingly, as would not happen elsewhere, a double stream of government, for spiritual and for temporal affairs, flowed out into the world from the same source; and the kingdoms subject to the Roman empire received the faith of Christ the more quickly, seeing that their own dominion had received the same faith; and likewise the preachers of the Christian faith preached it the more freely and securely, since they were supported by imperial power, etc. Hence Paul said to Festus, as is read in Acts 25: Ad tribunal Caesaris sto, ubi me oportet iudicari, and so escaped bodily death.

units.la: PET. Iam video aperte, quod Romana ecclesia aliarum omnium rationabiliter esse debeat mater & magistra. Progredere vlterius ad alios titulos explanandos.
units.tr: PET. Now I clearly see that the Roman church ought rightly to be the mother and teacher of all the others. Go on to explain the other titles.

units.la: PAVL. Praedicti tituli sunt principaliu ledii patriarchalii: Aquilegiensis vero, & Gradensis, nomen primatis seu patriarchae sibi acquisierunt, qui tamen sunt secundum aliquos Metropolitani, put etiam sunt Cantuariensis & Bitinensis archiepiscopi. Etiā dicuntur aliquando primates & Metropolitani, vt 22. di. a mensura civitatum, in quib. sunt cathedrae episcopales, & dicitur ab archos graece, quod est princeps latine, quasi princeps episcoporum, & ipsi, ac etiam episcopi, qui vices apostolorum gerunt, non nisi in civitatib. & locis insignib. intitulatur 60. d. c. 1. & c. episcopos. Inde est, quod in Iure canonico non dicitur civitas, nisi ibi sit episcopalis, aut alterius superioris titulus, seu ecclesia cathedralis. Postea alii sunt inferioris tituli ecclesiarum parochialium, & alii ta in ecclesiis cathedralibus quae cōuentionalib. &c. ad diuersa officia, ministeria ecclesiastica, vltra diuinum officium exercendo institutiv, ut sunt, ad quae exercenda tempore Apostolorum fuerunt electi septe discipuli, Stephanus, &c. quando erant eis omnia communia, iuxta illud dictum ab Apostolis, Actuum 6. Non est aequum nobis, relinquere verbum Dei, & ministrare mensae. Considerate igitur fratres ex vobis viros boni testimonii septe plenos Spiritu sancto, & sapientia, quos constituamus super hoc opus. Sed proh dolor, modernis temporib. Apostoli p contrarium dereliquerunt verbum Dei, & ministrant mensae. Hinc est etiā, quod multiplicatis reditib. ecclesiae, & postquam ad proprietatem deuenimus dictorum ossiciorum, nomina quasi ad sola temporalia commoda translata videtur: & non officia, sed beneficia nuncupantur, ex eo quod vnusquisq; communiter quaerit quae sua sunt, non quae Iesu Christi, & amplius temporalia obtinenda, quae diuina ministeria exercenda. Et quoad istos titulos, tā quoad iplorum ordine, quae officia tenenda, est diuersarum ecclesiarum consuetudo. Nā etiam aliquae ecclesiae plures habent huiusmodi titulos, quae aliae, de iure communi. Archidiaconus, qui est quasi oculus episcopi, est primus. Postea archipresbyter & in aliquibus ecclesiis dicitur Decanus, postmodum primicerius, & apud aliquas ecclesias dicitur scholasticus: deinde thesaurarius, &c. 30. di. perlectis. PET. Dixisti supra, quod tales tituli dicuntur dignitates, personatus, & officia: quae est differentia inter ista? PAVL. Vnum saepe recipitur pro alio, tamen differentia consuevit assignari. Nam dignitas habet administrationem rerum temporalium, cum iurisdictione, vel nomine dignitatis, habet praelationem in ecclesia, in choro, & aliis: licet non habeat administrationem temporalium, vel iurisdictionem, vel quae de consuetudine habetur, pro dignitate. Personatus aut praerogativa habet in choro, capitulo, possessionibus, optionibus, vocib. plus quam canonici: sed non tantum, quantum dignitatem habentes. In Anglia personatus vocatur ecclesia parochialis. Officium cognoscimus ex administratione rerum, sive praerogativa in choro, vel capitulo, vltra alios sui ordinis. Vel habet onus, sive praerotiuam honoris, vel quia sic habet ecclesiæ consuetudo pro simplici officio. Canonicatus autem, siue canonia, est ius spirituale, principaliter ad exercendum diuinum officium in ecclesia, propter quod continue peragendum dati sunt fructus à fidelibus, qui secundum aliquos dicuntur Prebenda, quia præbentur agentibus diuina officia, & secundum Bernh. in c. cum M. Ferrariensis de const. laicus potest habere prębendam, sed non canoniam, quod est ius spirituale, non cadens in laicum. Sed salua reuerentia, aliud est fructus præbendæ, aliud præbenda, sc. ius percipiendi fructus, quod est spirituale, vt in c. dilecto. de præbend. & essentialiter idem est quod canonia: quia eodem iure quo teneor ad officium, debeo facere omnia accessoria ad hoc spectantia, & sine quibus principale non potest fieri, sicut sustentationis fructus percipere, pastorem eligere, pro bono communi consulere. Et ita canonia & præbenda non differunt essentialiter, sed respectu diuini officii, quod est principale, dicitur canonia: respectu fructuum, quod est accessorium ad diuinum officium, dicitur præbenda. Et hoc idem ius, sci. canonia & præbenda, est titulus. Et tale ius, siue titulus, visitato vocabulo dicitur beneficium: & ita accipit denominationem ab accessorio, & non principali, vt prius dixi. Quia homines communiter ordine præpostero magis quærunt temporalia commoda, quam spiritualia. Et ita quilibet titulus est canonia, capiendo canoniam generaliter, id est ius canonicum, siue spirituale. Alio modo canonia in communi usu loquendi, & specialiter est titulus distinctus in ecclesia, contra dignitatem personarum & officium. Et dicitur visitato vocabulo Canonicatus, & licet cancellaria & stylus curiæ habet, quod scribitur in literis gratiæ, (c. sibi dictos canonicatum & præbendam assignantes, &c.) tanquam essent diuersa, non tamen nisi in illum finem scribitur, vt vterque effectus, sc. spiritualis & temporalis siue accessorius, actualiter suo iure respondeat, &c.
units.tr: PAUL. The aforementioned titles belong to the principal patriarchal sees. The bishops of Aquileia and Grado have won for themselves the name of primate or patriarch, though according to some they are metropolitans, just as the archbishops of Canterbury and Bitinensis are. Sometimes they are also called primates and metropolitans, as in 22. di., from the size of the cities in which there are episcopal sees. The word comes from the Greek archos [ἄρχος], which in Latin means "prince," as if they were princes of the bishops. Bishops themselves, who bear the place of the apostles, are likewise entitled only in cities and notable places, 60. d. c. 1. & c. episcopos. Hence in canon law a place is not called a city unless it has a bishop, or some other higher title, or a cathedral church. Next there are the titles of the parish churches, and others in the cathedral churches, which are appointed for various offices and ecclesiastical ministries, beyond the performance of the divine office. For the performance of these, seven disciples, Stephen and the others, were chosen in the time of the apostles, when all things were held in common, according to the saying of the apostles in Acts 6. It is not fitting that we should leave the word of God and serve tables. Therefore, brethren, look out among you seven men of good report, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business. But alas, in modern times the apostles, on the contrary, have left the word of God and serve tables. Hence it is also that, as the revenues of the church have multiplied, and as we have come to the ownership of these offices, their names seem to have been transferred to mere temporal advantages; and they are called not offices but benefices, because everyone commonly seeks what is his own, not what is Jesus Christ's, and seeks more to obtain temporal gains than to exercise the divine ministries. As for these titles, both the order in which they are held and the offices to be held under them vary according to the custom of different churches. For some churches have more such titles than others, by common law. The archdeacon, who is as it were the bishop's eye, is first. After him comes the archpriest, and in some churches the dean; then the primicerius, and in some churches the scholasticus; then the thesaurarius, and so on, 30. di. perlectis. PET. You said above that such titles are called dignities, personates, and offices. What is the difference between these? PAUL. One is often taken for another, yet a difference is usually assigned. For a dignity has the administration of temporal goods, together with jurisdiction, or by the name of dignity it has precedence in the church, in the choir, and elsewhere, even if it has no administration of temporal goods or jurisdiction, or whatever is held by custom as a dignity. A personate, or prerogative, has more in the choir, the chapter, possessions, options, and votes than the canons do, but not as much as those who hold dignities. In England a parish church is called a personate. We know an office from the administration of goods, or from a prerogative in the choir or chapter beyond the others of its order; or it carries a burden, or the honour of a prerogative, or because church custom so holds it as a simple office. A canonry, however, or canonia, is a spiritual right, chiefly for performing the divine office in the church, for the sake of which fruits are given by the faithful to be continually discharged; according to some these are called a prebend, because they are furnished to those who perform the divine offices. And according to Bernh. in c. cum M. Ferrariensis de const., a layman can hold a prebend but not a canonry, which is a spiritual right and does not fall to a layman. But with due respect, the fruit of the prebend is one thing, the prebend another, namely the right to receive the fruits, which is spiritual, as in c. dilecto. de praebend. In essence the prebend is the same as the canonry, because by the same right by which I am bound to the office, I must do all the things pertaining to it and without which the principal thing cannot be done, such as receiving the fruits for support, choosing a minister, and taking counsel for the common good. So the canonry and the prebend do not differ in essence, but with respect to the divine office, which is the principal thing, it is called a canonry; with respect to the fruits, which are accessory to the divine office, it is called a prebend. And this same right, namely canonry and prebend, is a title. Such a right, or title, is commonly called a benefice, and so it takes its name from the accessory and not the principal, as I said before, because men commonly, in a backward order, seek temporal advantages more than spiritual ones. Thus any title is a canonry, taking canonry in the general sense, that is, canon law or spiritual right. In another sense, in common usage, a canonry is specifically a distinct title in the church, set against dignity, person, and office, and in ordinary usage it is called a canonicate. And although the chancery and the style of the court have it that in letters of grace it is written (c. sibi dictos canonicatum & praebendam assignantes, etc.) as if they were different things, it is nevertheless written only to this end, so that both effects, namely the spiritual and the temporal or accessory, may actually answer to their right, etc.

units.la: CAP. III. In quo declarantur tria, quæ requiruntur ad hoc, vt titulus acquiratur, & tertium eorum prosequitur.
units.tr: CAP. III. In which three things are declared that are required for a title to be acquired, and the third of them is pursued.

units.la: PET. Declara, si placet, particularius de institutione, seu prouisione canonica, de qua dicit tua definitio, vt quæram intelligere, quando quis iuste aut iniuste agens, contra salutem quærit, seu obtinet ecclesiasticum beneficium.
units.tr: PET. Please explain more particularly the canonical institution or provision of which your definition speaks, so that I may understand when someone, acting justly or unjustly, seeks or obtains an ecclesiastical benefice against his salvation.

units.la: PAVL. Aliud est iniuste quærere, aliud iniuste quæsitum retinere. Nam multi iniuste quærunt beneficia ecclesiastica, quæ tamen quæsita iuste tenent. Alii autem econuerso iuste & canonice quærunt, sed quæsita quandoque iniuste detinent. Alii iniuste quærunt, ac etiam iniuste quæsitum, cum periculo salutis detinent. Alii vero sunt iuste & canonice quærentes, & canonice quæsita retinentes. Sed isti quarti, maxime hoc tempore nulli sunt, aut rari.
units.tr: PAUL. It is one thing to seek unjustly, another to retain unjustly what has been sought. For many seek ecclesiastical benefices unjustly, yet hold what they have sought rightly. Others, conversely, seek justly and canonically, but sometimes hold what they have obtained unjustly. Others seek unjustly and also hold what was unjustly obtained, at risk to their salvation. Others, indeed, seek justly and canonically, and retain what was canonically obtained. But these fourth sort are now, especially in this age, none or rare.

units.la: PET. Imo, sicut te aliqualiter intelligo, promoti in curia Romana his temporibus, docente fama publica, vel potius infamia, tales quarti sunt quasi nulli. Sed rogo prosequere viterius, quoniam offert se salubris materia ad tractandum.
units.tr: PET. Indeed, as I understand you in some measure, those promoted at the Roman court in these times, as public report, or rather infamy, teaches, are almost none of this fourth sort. But please go on further, since a wholesome subject presents itself for treatment.

units.la: PAVL. Diligenter debes animaduertere, quod ad assecutionem canonicam alicuius tituli, siue beneficii ecclesiastici, requiruntur principaliter tria. Quædam debent antecedere, quædam mediare, quædam vero sequi. Antecedentia sunt, sicut personæ promouendæ postulatio, electio, præsentatio, vel debita examinatio, &c. Mediantia sunt, institutio, collatio, prouisio, receptio, vt in descriptione præmissa. Sequentia sunt, inuestitura, & in possessionem realis inductio, quæ secundum dist. post Hostiensem & alios canonistas, super regul. beneficiu, de reg. iur. li. 6. differunt. Quia institutio, est iuris alicuius beneficii verbalis collatio: inuestitura vero, institutionis, seu collationis confirmatio: Missio in possessionem, est præcedentium, sc. collationis & inuestiturę, executio. Per institutionem tribuitur ius proprietatis: per inuestituram, declaratur & confirmatur illius iuris collatio, vt in c. Cum ex iniuncto. de haret. Per inductionem in possessionem, tribuitur ius possessionis, & actualis administrationis: vt c. ad hoc & c. vt nostrum, de offic. archi. Et vt euidentius hoc clarescat, aduerte. Facta n. institutione verbali ad ipsius declarationem & confirmationem, iure vel consuetudine inducta est quædam solennitas: quæ quandoq; fit per annulum, aliquando per librum, quandoq; per birreti impositionem, &c. vt in auctoritate, de instit. Gl. 2. de his quæ fiunt à ma. per ca. ex ore. c. fi. quo facto, illius iuris spiritualis taliter acquisiti, datur q. possessio, vt cū assignatur canonicatus, possessio fit, assignação stallu in choro, & voce in capitulo, & sic de aliis: quia talia proprie possideri non possunt, vt in c. fi. s. cū ecclesia. de causa poss. & proprie. Sed quasi possidetur. Habita vero possessione, in illis effectibus spiritualibus, non per hoc est possessio acquisita in corporalibus pertinentiis ad titulum: sicut sunt, villæ, prædia, decimæ, & alia corporalia, quia sunt diuersa. Sed necessaria est primo realis conductio in possessionem corporalem, quā facit gratiarum Apostolicatū subexecutor, vel archidiaconus in ecclesiis cathedralib. de offic. archi. ad hoc. & c. vt nostrū 25. di. perlectis. Demum omniū corporaliū (sepatatorū ab iuuice apprehensio corporalis, prout notari consueuit post Innoc. c. in litteris de restit. spo. &c. q. etiā cōfirmatus vel prouisus auctoritate propria pōt adhibere, sinō est cōtradictor, secundū Io. An. in c. transmisf. de elect. Inuestitura tñ, est absentis institutio: sed institutio, est præsētis, secundū aliquos doctores, q. hoc not. in dicto c. ex ore. & de cōcef. præben. proposuit.
units.tr: PAUL. You must carefully observe that three things are chiefly required for the canonical acquisition of any title or ecclesiastical benefice. Some must precede, some must intervene, and some must follow. The preceding things are, for example, the petition of the person to be promoted, election, presentation, or due examination, etc. The intervening things are institution, collation, provision, and reception, as in the description given above. The following things are investiture and the actual induction into possession, which, according to the distinction drawn by Hostiensis and other canonists after the rule beneficium, de reg. iur. lib. 6, differ. For institution is the verbal conferral of the right of some benefice; investiture is the confirmation of the institution or collation; missio in possessionem is the execution of the preceding things, namely collation and investiture. Through institution the right of ownership is granted; through investiture the conferral of that right is declared and confirmed, as in c. Cum ex iniuncto, de haer. Through induction into possession the right of possession and actual administration is granted, as in c. ad hoc and c. ut nostrum, de offic. archid. And that this may be made clearer, note the following. After the verbal institution, for its declaration and confirmation, a certain solemnity has been introduced by law or custom: sometimes it is done by a ring, sometimes by a book, sometimes by the imposition of a biretta, etc., as in auctoritate, de instit., gloss 2, de his quae fiunt a maiore per c. ex ore, c. fin. When this is done, possession is given of such spiritual right thus acquired, as when a canonry is assigned: possession is taken by the assignment of a stall in the choir and a voice in the chapter, and so on for other things, since such things cannot properly be possessed, as in c. fin. § cum ecclesia, de causa poss. et prop., but are as it were possessed. Yet once possession is had in those spiritual effects, possession is not thereby acquired in the corporal appurtenances belonging to the title, such as farms, estates, tithes, and other corporal things, because they are distinct. But first a real induction into corporal possession is necessary, which is made by the subexecutor of the Apostolic grace or by the archdeacon in cathedral churches, de offic. archid., ad hoc, and c. ut nostrum, 25 dist., perlectis. Finally, the corporal apprehension of all corporal things (separated from the spiritual) is a thing commonly noted after Innocent, c. in litteris de restit. spol., etc., which even one who has been confirmed or provided may do on his own authority, unless there is an opponent, according to John Andreae on c. transmissa, de elect. Investiture, however, is the institution of one who is absent; but institution is of one who is present, according to some doctors, which is noted in the said c. ex ore and de concess. praeb., and has been proposed there.

units.la: PET. Nūc breuiter dic de his quæ canonica debet tituli prouisione antecedere, quid vnūquodq; sit: &an ad hoc, vt sit prouisio canonica, psonæ puisæ valor, vt electio canonica, necessaria, requiratur.
units.tr: PET. Now briefly tell me what each of the things which must precede a canonical provision of a title is, and whether, for a provision to be canonical, the value of the person provided, as with a canonical election, is required.

units.la: PAVL. Breuibus verbis multa quæris, nam iura noua & antiqua longioribus titulis diffusa, prolixique processus doctorum scribentium, vix poterant explicari.
units.tr: PAUL. You ask much in few words, for the new and old laws, spread out in longer titles, and the lengthy processes of writing doctors, could scarcely be explained.

units.la: PET. Non te occupare desidero, vt plenam de his doctrinā tradere debeas: sed vt tempus restet, ad alia saltem, de secundo modo, quo breuiari potteris, percurres.
units.tr: PET. I do not wish to burden you, so that you should deliver a full doctrine on these matters; but, so that there is time left, at least run through the other things, concerning the second way, by which you may be able to shorten the matter.

units.la: CAP. IV.
units.tr: CAP. IV.

units.la: In quo damnatur electionum reseruatio, occasione cuius male prouidetur ecclesiis, & decipiuntur electi.
units.tr: In which the reservation of elections is condemned, the occasion through which the churches are badly provided for and the elect are deceived.

units.la: PET. Videtur nec postulatio, nec electio hodie locum habere, imo vix personarum examinatio, ad minora beneficia, pro forma taliter qualiter obseruatur. Nam electionibus praelatorum videtur esse derogatum per regulas Cancellariae, quas Romani Pontifices in sua promotione pro se referuant, in quantum eis uti volunt, quod reiectis plurium ecclesiarum electionibus in Romana curia hodie practicatur. Ex quo videtur, quod ad hoc, ut canonica fiat prouisio, non oportet, ut capitularis electio antecedat.
units.tr: PET. It seems that neither postulation nor election has a place today, indeed hardly any examination of persons, for minor benefices, which are observed only as a matter of form and in some fashion. For the elections of prelates seem to have been overridden by the rules of the Chancery, which the Roman Pontiffs reserve to themselves at their promotion, so far as they wish to use them. In this way, with the elections of many churches set aside, the practice now prevails at the Roman court. From this it seems that, for a canonical provision to be made, it is not necessary for a chapter's election to come first.

units.la: PAVL. Errore graui deciperis. Ad omnem enim iustitiae actum duo debent concurrere, scilicet rectae rationis iudicium, quo discernitur, an hoc fieri expediat, vel non, exigitur pariter auctoritas, siue potestas faciendi. Non enim dare vel facere possumus, nisi ad hoc potestatem habeamus. Nec iudicium dici potest, nisi vim coactiuam habeat: eo quod iudicium tantum ad unum determinatur. Haec quidem determinatio in speculatiuis fit per veritatem primorum principiorum, quibus resisti non potest: & in rebus practicis per vim imperatiuam, in iudicante existentem. Et ad hoc, secundum beatum Thomam super quarto sententiarum, distinctio 18. sunt duo claues vicario Christi, & cuilibet praelato ecclesiae traditae, quae non distinguuntur in essentia auctoritatis, qua utrumque ex officio suo sibi competit: sed comparatio ad actus, quorum unus alium supponit, sicut voluntas praesupponit iudicium rationis. Quomodo ergo dictos reseruatores iustificare poteris, cum Papa ad suum libitum non potest ad aliud, vel aliter facere in spiritualibus, quam exigunt dictae claues? Alioqui clauis errando nec claudere potest, nec aperire, ut dicunt Glossantes. Quicquid enim aliter faceret, quam rectae rationis iudicium exposceret, non virtute clauium hoc fieret, sed potestate propria: & per consequens, non valeret, sed quaedam umbra taliter appareret in opere, & nulla veritas in effectu. Quid namque fore potuit illa vis, ad reseruandum praelatorum electiones, &c. rationis iudicium determinans, & non potius ad errandum: quae scilicet causae reseruandi, & non verius graviter oberrandi. Arbitrium itaque Papae nudum proprie non sufficit. Non enim sola voluntas Papae regere debet claues ecclesiae: sed potius econuerso, ad hoc sunt sibi traditae, ut secundum ipsas deber dirigi, & alios regulare.
units.tr: PAUL. You are deceived by a serious error. For two things must concur in every act of justice: the judgment of right reason, by which it is discerned whether a thing is expedient or not, and likewise authority, or the power of doing it. For we cannot give or do anything unless we have the power to do so. Nor can it be called judgment unless it has coercive force, since judgment is determined to one outcome only. This determination, in speculative matters, comes through the truth of first principles, which cannot be resisted; and in practical matters, through the commanding force that exists in the one who judges. And on this point, according to blessed Thomas on the fourth book of the Sentences, distinction 18, there are two keys given to the vicar of Christ, and to every prelate of the Church; these are not distinguished in the essence of the authority by which each of them belongs to him by his office, but in relation to acts, one of which presupposes another, as the will presupposes the judgment of reason. How then can you justify those reservers, since the Pope cannot, at his pleasure, act in spiritual matters otherwise or to another end than these keys require? Otherwise, as the glossators say, a key that errs can neither lock nor unlock. For whatever he did otherwise than right reason demanded would be done not by virtue of the keys but by his own private power; and consequently it would not be valid, but a certain shadow would appear in the work, and no truth in the effect. For what force of reason, determining the reservation of prelates' elections, etc., could there have been? Its causes of reserving would be, not truer, but rather grave errors. Therefore the bare will of the Pope does not strictly suffice. For the will of the Pope alone ought not to govern the keys of the Church; rather, on the contrary, they have been handed to him so that he should be directed by them and regulate others by them.

units.la: PET. Audiuia Curiensibus mihi dici, quod reseruationes huiusmodi pro honore curiae facit Papa. Idem certi praedecessores sui fecerunt: non tamen in tantum practicabant, sicut nunc dictus honor conuersus est in errorem.
units.tr: PET. I have been told by people from the Curia that the Pope makes reservations of this kind for the honour of the court. His predecessors did the same; yet they did not practise it to such an extent, so that the said honour has now been turned into error.

units.la: PAVL. Mirabile regentium Christi ecclesiam iudicium, ad eligendum potius honorem curiae, quam salutem totius Germaniae, & Italiae, &c. Quis namque modus vnquam aptior inueniri potuit ad prouidendum ecclesiis, & conuenientibus de pastore, aliisque beneficiis conferendis, quam is, qui tot centenis annis diligentissima sanctorum patrum prouidentia masticatus, & iure canonico declaratus est? Et quid sceleratius, magisque erroneum, quam eo contempto, scandalose & inutiliter prouidere taliter qualiter ecclesiis, ac per hoc ecclesiam Christi peruertere, & quamplurimas simplicium animas Christi fidelium sic damnare? Dic quaeso, unde sibi haec potestas, clauibus ecclesiae prorsus contraria? Nonne approbati canones late improbant, & expresse, Papam mutare non posse, vel eius contrarium facere, quod per praedecessores suos rationabiliter statutum est, absque causa euidenti & vrgenti? 25.q.4. per totum. de consang. & affin. non debet. Quia si voluntarie violat canones, Spiritum sanctum dicitur blasphemare, cuius institutu ac dono sunt editi. eo cap. & q. violatores. Quae potuit esse causa, vrgens necessitas, aut reipublicae aequa vel maior utilitas, sublimitas, decreta generalis concilii immutandi, formasque electionum, &c. per huiusmodi reseruationes respuere studiose vtique discurrenti ingenio, causasque singulas percunctanti non apparet, quam quod fiat capitularis electio, iuxta formas generali concilio approbatas, vt in cap. quia propter de elect. Et certus sum, Papam aliter facere non posse sine causa, vt dictum est.
units.tr: PAUL. What a wonderful judgment for those who rule Christ's Church, to choose the honour of the court rather than the salvation of all Germany and Italy, etc.! For what method could ever have been found more suitable for providing churches with a fitting minister and conferring other benefices, than the one which has been chewed over and confirmed by the most diligent providence of the holy Fathers over so many centuries and declared by canon law? And what is more wicked, and more erroneous, than to disregard it, and to provide, in whatever way, for the churches in a scandalous and useless manner, and thereby to overthrow the Church of Christ and condemn so many simple souls of Christ's faithful? Tell me, I beg you, where does this power come from, which is utterly contrary to the keys of the Church? Do not the approved canons widely and expressly forbid the Pope to change, or to do the contrary of, what has been reasonably established by his predecessors, without a clear and urgent cause? 25 q. 4 throughout; de consang. & affin. non debet. For if he knowingly violates the canons, he is said to blaspheme the Holy Spirit, by whose institution and gift they were issued; eo cap. & q. violatores. What cause could there be, what urgent necessity, or what equal or greater advantage of the commonwealth, that would justify changing the decrees of a general council, and the forms of elections, etc., and rejecting them studiously through such reservations? To a mind that examines the matter with diligence and inquires into each cause, there appears no reason except that the chapter's election should take place according to the forms approved by a general council, as in cap. quia propter de elect. And I am certain that the Pope cannot act otherwise without a cause, as has been said.

units.la: PET. Hoc vtique pro causa huius a magnis intellexi, quoniam quandoque duo, interdum tres vel quatuor electi fuerunt in eadem ecclesia, & inde nonnunquam suscitata fuerunt odia, litesque graues, cum multo ecclesiarum incommodo atque damno. Expediebat igitur talis reseruatio Romano Pontifici, ad talibus obuiandum.
units.tr: PET.
