Sigismund, one of the Dukes of Austria, two months later, which is the time set by the new constitutions, has acted against this, and therefore he is guilty of treason and heresy. But we have been taught that the great Council of Constance decreed that a general council has its power immediately from Christ over the Pope in those matters which are recognised as belonging to faith, reformation and peace; which the sacred Council of Basel also renewed, and which Popes Eugenius and Nicholas acknowledged. Whence, then, has Pope Pius usurped the authority to shut the hand of his superior, namely the general council, to which he himself is bound to obey? Nor let anyone wonder if an appeal is made to a council that has not yet been assembled, since the authority of the Church, which is immortal, remains firm; and the Church, now dispersed throughout the whole world, will then be in that very council lawfully assembled. That it is not known when it will be assembled is no hindrance to appealing to it there. For this much is known: according to the decrees of the great Council of Constance, councils are to be held from decade to decade in perpetual times, and now the time of the obligation has come, the day has arrived. If the execution is hindered or deferred through someone's fault, let the blame fall on that person as a penalty, for he who forbids a judgment to be made is convicted of distrusting his own justice.

units.la: Transgrediamur nunc ad circumstantias citationis, & quidem coram se mandat Papa comparere, qui legationis sacra violauit, tunc Senis agens, nunc Romæ manens. Quam securitatem nobis aut nostris polliceri potest, qui publici iuris fidem fecit irritam, & per prædecessores suos aliquando dictum est, fauore Roberti Regis Siciliæ, contra Henricum Imperatorem, non teneri ipsum sese in manibus inimici credere, etiam sub fide salui conductus. Papa vero iam quidem nos diffidauit, & antea legatum nostrum iusto metu perculsum persequutus est, fugientem, cui si tertio credamus, nosmetipsos decepisse videbimur, quippe qui fallenti fidem accommodat si rursum sallatur, iam seipsum fefellit. Nunc descendamus ad causam. Ait Papa, Nouum processum inchoamus aduersus Sigismundum, tanquam sanæ fidei non recipientem articulum quem per hæc symboli Apostolici verba, fidelium exprimit vnusquisque: Credo in vnam sanctam catholicam & Apostolicam Ecclesiam. Nos profecto didicimus à patre nostro, Credo in Deum Patrem omnipotentem creatorem cœli & terræ, & in Iesum Christum filium eius vnicum, Dominum nostrum, & in Spiritum sanctum; non autem in ecclesiam, neque hoc habet symbolum Apostolorum, vt credamus in Dei creaturam.
units.tr: Let us now pass to the circumstances of the citation. The Pope commands us to appear before him, he who has violated the sacred character of the envoy, acting then at Siena, now remaining at Rome. What safe-conduct can he promise us or ours, he who has made void the faith of public law? It has once been said by his predecessors that, in the favour of Robert, King of Sicily, against Emperor Henry, one was not bound to entrust himself to the hands of an enemy, even under the faith of a safe-conduct. The Pope has already distrusted us, and earlier he pursued our envoy, struck with just fear, as he fled. If we trust him a third time, we shall seem to have deceived ourselves, since he who gives faith to a deceiver, if he is deceived again, has deceived himself. Now let us come to the matter. The Pope says: We begin a new process against Sigismund, as one who does not accept the article that everyone of the faithful expresses by these words of the Apostles' Creed: I believe in one holy catholic and apostolic Church. We have indeed learned from our father: I believe in God the Father almighty, Creator of heaven and earth, and in Jesus Christ his only Son, our Lord, and in the Holy Spirit; but not in the Church, nor does the Apostles' Creed have this, that we should believe in a creature of God.

units.la: Hoc nempe symbolum, quod Apostoli, quod milites Christi ad bellum diuinum profecturi, quod cum idolatris, quod cum omni gentilitate gesturi erant, concordi animo & vno spiritu assumpserunt, cuius armati clypeo, cuneos hostium penetrarunt, hæc verba continet; Credo in Spiritum sanctum, sanctam ecclesiam catholicam; non autem, in ecclesiam. In qua fide perstamus cum Apostolis, postquam adoleuimus, & ad cultum diuinum, prout ecclesiæ sanctæ catholicæ doctrinis instítutus est, animaduertimus, ex symbolo Niceni concilii didicimus credere in vnum Deum Patrem omnipotentem, factorem cœli & terræ, visibilium omnium & inuisibilium, & in vnum Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum filium Dei vnigenitum. Et infra; & in Spiritum sanctum Dominum & viuificantem. Et infra: & vnam sanctam catholicam & Apostolicam ecclesiam; non autem, in ecclesiam. Quia & factura Dei est factoris omnium visibilium & inuisibilium. Pergit propterea dicens: Nunc ergo canonibus & censuris eius obedire tenetur. Scimus quod canonum statuta ab omnibus sunt custodienda, & honesta præcepta superiorum à subditis reuerenter suscipienda: At non ita, vt iubeamur credere in ecclesiam, aut vllam Dei creaturam seu facturam, sed nec vt credamus, nos rite neque iuste, sed nec vllo modo putemus excommunicatos, qui nec auditi quidem sumus, quin etiam nec vim, vel iniuriam vllam intulerimus Cardinali, cuius iniurias crudelesque factiones à nobis & subditis nostris, naturæ gentium iure propulsamus, quod nemo nobis prohibere potest, nec à nobis auferre: quia natura nobis instinxit, & nobiscum natum est, ipsaque pietatis & æquitatis naturalis ratio, nullius exteri iuris aut institutionis indigna firmauit.
units.tr: That creed, indeed, which the Apostles, the soldiers of Christ about to set out on the divine war, which they were to wage against the idolaters and against all paganism, took up with one mind and one spirit, and with whose shield armed they broke through the ranks of the enemy, contains these words: I believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy catholic Church; not in the Church. In this faith we persist with the Apostles, now that we have grown up, and we have noticed, as we were instructed in the worship of God according to the doctrines of the holy catholic Church, that from the creed of the Council of Nicaea we learned to believe in one God the Father almighty, maker of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible, and in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God. And further down: and in the Holy Spirit, the Lord and giver of life. And further: and in one holy catholic and apostolic Church; not in the Church. For the Church too is the work of God, the maker of all things visible and invisible. He goes on therefore to say: Now therefore he is bound to obey its canons and censures. We know that the statutes of the canons are to be observed by all, and that the honourable precepts of superiors are to be received reverently by subjects. But we are not so commanded to believe in the Church, or in any creature or work of God; nor are we to think that we have been rightly or justly excommunicated, we who have not even been heard; nor have we inflicted any violence or injury at all on the Cardinal, whose injuries and cruel factions we repel from ourselves and our subjects by the law of nature and of nations, which no one can forbid us or take from us, because nature has instilled it in us and it was born with us, and natural reason itself, of piety and equity, has established it as worthy of no outside law or institution.

units.la: Hoc quippe ius solidum iniuriæ propulsandæ nascitur, non fingitur. Et idcirco apud omnes gentes & nationes æque colitur & obseruatur. Ex quo & bella tum publica tum etiam priuata iustificantur, nonnunquam vero consecrantur & sanctificantur, & pro ipsis æternæ vitæ præmia conceduntur.
units.tr: This right of repelling injury is solid and arises from nature; it is not invented. For this reason it is observed and honoured equally among all peoples and nations. From it wars, both public and private, are justified, and sometimes even consecrated and sanctified, and eternal rewards are granted for them.

units.la: Quid ergo aliud videtur egisse Papa, aut quid aliud quæri videtur Cardinalis, quam quod nos homicidia in nostros admissa, turbationes metallariarum per ipsum nobis illatas non voluimus sustinere, neque expectare donec ipse alienigenas, qui in comitatu Goritiæ siue militabant siue grassabantur, in suas fortias introduxisset, quippe qui treugas annuales inire recusauit. Nonne satis ostendit, qualis animus sibi esset? maxime autem imminente sibi occasione tam optata, & opportunitate tam sperata, Comitis de Posingen, Iohannis de Rein de VVirtvvis & aliorum, qui comitatum Boritiæ in confiniis principatus nostri situm popularentur, castra, terras & fortias eius subigendo. At quis tam hebetis sensus, tam obtusi cordis, qui suam negligens opportunitatem, atque impendentem sibi necessitatem, belligerandi opportunitatem concedat a duerfario, cum scilic. quasi dubius, medius Mars errat in armis? In his quae violentiae Martis committuntur propter periculi gravitatem, turpe est dicere; Non putaram. O quantum cachinum excitasset sacerdos ille, si nos oscitantes aut dormientes praevenisset.
units.tr: What else, then, does the Pope seem to have done, or what else does the Cardinal seem to be seeking, than that we did not wish to endure the murders committed against our people and the disturbances in the mines brought upon us by him, nor to wait until he had introduced foreigners, who were either serving or raiding in the county of Görz, into his fortresses, since he refused to make annual truces? Does this not sufficiently show what his disposition was? Especially when the so longed-for occasion and the so hoped-for opportunity was at hand: by subduing the castles, lands and fortresses of Count of Poyssingen, John of Rhein of Wirtwis and others, who were laying waste the county of Görz, situated on the borders of our principality. But what sense is so dull, what heart so blunt, as to neglect its own opportunity and the necessity hanging over it, and to grant the enemy the chance of making war, since, as it were, "the Mars of the middle way wanders in arms"? In those matters which are done by the violence of Mars, on account of the gravity of the danger, it is shameful to say, "I did not think so." Oh, how much laughter that priest would have raised, had he got ahead of us while we were yawning or sleeping!

units.la: Nos vero subito restitimus factionibus suis, & parua manu, impetus & incursiones alienigenarum cohibuimus, ut absque ulla caede pacem restitueremus. Laudine vel vituperio dentur haec opera, omnium bonorum virorum sit arbitrium. Sequitur in hoc erroneo citatorio; Citamus Sigismundum ut compareat de fide catholica, praesertim de praetacto articulo vnitatis ecclesiae, & quae ad ipsum ex sanctorum doctorum doctrina sequuntur, respondeat. Iam satis respondimus, nos credere vnam sanctam catholicam & Apostolicam Ecclesiam; non autem in illam, ne latriam soli Deo debitam creaturae & facturae impendamus. Quod vero subiicit; & quae ad ipsum ex sanctorum patrum doctrina sequuntur. O copiosum verbum, & infinitam habens indaginem. O ridiculosum, a seculari principe requirere, quae doctores & scholastici viri disceptant, pro quibus eis insignia & praeclari scientiarum tituli decernuntur. Satis est nobis, expresse credere, quae Apostoli crediderunt, quaeque Patres Niceni Concilii declarauerunt; caetera sub generali fide sanctae matris Ecclesiae credere, eiusque fidem vna tenere, imitantes Apostoli doctrinam, ne scilicet plus sapere velimus quam oportet. O quot Sancti iam triumphant in coelis, qui sanguinem suum pro Christi nomine fuerunt, qui illas doctorum scientias nunquam audierunt neque cogitarunt, profecto maxima pars coeli, illorum scilicet qui a seculo migrauerunt, eorum est qui caritate arserunt; scripturarum autem arcana minime inuestigarunt.
units.tr: We, indeed, promptly resisted their factions and, with a small force, checked the attacks and incursions of the foreigners, so as to restore peace without any slaughter. Whether these deeds are to be given praise or blame is for the judgment of all good men. The erroneous summons continues: "We summon Sigismund to appear and answer concerning the Catholic faith, especially concerning the aforesaid article of the unity of the Church, and what follows from it from the teaching of the holy doctors." Already we have answered sufficiently that we believe in one holy catholic and apostolic Church; yet we do not believe in it, lest we give to a creature and a thing made the worship (latria) due to God alone. As for what he adds: "and what follows from the teaching of the holy Fathers" — oh, what a copious word, with an infinite field of inquiry! Oh, how ridiculous it is to require of a secular prince what doctors and scholastic men dispute about, for which honours and illustrious titles of learning are conferred on them! It is enough for us to believe expressly what the Apostles believed, and what the Fathers of the Nicene Council declared; the rest we believe under the general faith of our holy mother the Church, holding her faith as one, imitating the doctrine of the Apostles, namely so that we may not wish to be wiser than we ought. Oh, how many saints already triumph in heaven, who shed their blood for the name of Christ, who never heard or thought of those learned doctrines! Surely the greatest part of heaven, namely those who have departed from this age, are those who burned with charity; they did not search out the secrets of the Scriptures at all.

units.la: Ideo propheta non ex hoc beatos ait eos, qui scrutantur testimonia Domini, quod & superbi faciunt & impugnatores & qui contra talia nituntur, approbant ut reprobant; sed ita demum beatos ait si in toto corde Deum exquirant. Hunc sincero corde libet exquirere, absque Scripturarum profunditate, quae nostrum superat sensum. Nostrum est, patriam nostram tutare alacriter, quod seruando, iuuando, rite ac fideliter adaugendo, sub fide Christi & Apostolorum eius, etiam in Niceno Concilio declarata, quam expresse credimus & explicite, caetera quae ad fidem pertinent, cum ecclesia tenemus, speramus aeternae retributionis praemia promoueri. Sed neque contentus mansit, nos modo praemisso citasse, quin etiam ad consiliarios atque omnes omnino subditos nostros digressus est dicens: Similiter etiam, & infra: aliosque omnes ipsius Sigismundi consiliarios, domesticos, oppidanos, & infra: omnes etiam ipsius Sigismundi subditos Curiensis, Tridentinensis, & Brixinensis dioecesēon, qui ecclesiasticas censuras vilipendunt, &c. Certe nemo vilipendit censuras, quia nullae adhuc rite emanarunt, sed pro libito Cardinalis conuitia multa, contumeliae, iniuriae & calumniae in nos dictae & factae sunt, contra nos & nostros inauditos, quae potius expiandae forent quam exaggerandae, ut praedixi-mus, & iure cautum est, quae poena debetur illis, qui censuras efflant, irrite abutentes concessa sibi potestate. Est tamen in hoc ineptia illius praesumptionis expugnanda & euacuanda, quod omnes subditos examinari cupit, sup articulo fidei, & quae ex sanctorum doctrina sequuntur ad illum, nā hoc est de fide vulgo disputare, quod lege vetitum est. Siquidem id publice fit, quod ducentis millibus marium, foeminarium & puerorum agitur. Quid dicet agricola, interrogatus, quid sit ecclesia, aut in quo sustentetur Papa errante: & an Graecus sit pars Ecclesiae, vel Iudaeus, vel alius Christianus habitans in extremis terrae? In quo differat verum caput ecclesiae a ministeriali? Quam auctoritatem dederit scripturis, & qualem receperit ab illis? Tantum certe studium fuit maioribus nostris, arcana scripturarum custodiendi, ne vulgo tractarentur, ut maxime reprehenderent, qui Bibliam ex lingua Latina in Teutonicā traduxerunt. Nunc vero Cardinalis ille rusticos vult interrogare, de his, quae ex sanctorum doctrina sequuntur ad ipsum fidei articulum. Hanc disceptationem scholasticis permittamus; Agricolis & vinitoribus arua colenda & pastinanda sunt, quibus satis est symborum Apostolorum recitare; discussionem vero vnionis collectiuae mysticae, aut quot modis plures sint vnum, non est disputatio laicorum. Sed si placet Cardinali rusticam gentem ex sententiis doctorum expolire, poterit (si velit) erigere scholas quo diebus feriatis confluant, ita scilic. ne cultum aruorum omittant. Sed nō sic docuit beatissimus Papa Gregorius in Pastoralibus, ut tacenda pro loco & persona, passim proferantur, & sine delectu, quod est ante porcos mittere margaritas, scilicet arcana scripturarum vulgo tractare. Si Papa putaret nos minus doctum in fide, & hoc ex sincero corde manaret, facile hoc resciscere posset ex summis viris ac principibus, qui nobiscum versantur, absque contumeliis, quibus se contra nos oblectat. Si de subditis nostris ecclesiasticis vel secularibus, aliqua talis disputatio esset, si certe sinceritas in ipso esset, id facile resciscere absque tot personarum commotione. Postulauit autem impossibilia, ut occasionem sibi confingeret saeuiendi. Quis oro gentilium seu idololatrarum in Christianos tantam mouit persecutionem, ut tot Christianorum animas, vna sententia condemnaret, quot ille Papa iam euocauit, ut occasionem condemnationis inueniret? quippe qui legationis sanctae prophanauit. Profecto quid de sua clementia vel crudelitate sentiendum sit, satis abundeque monstrauit. Nos vero, apud illum compareamus nostri ve subditi Clerici siue Laici, & illi fidem habeamus, qui nos audire contempsit, absit a nobis haec insania, sed fidem nostra tum scilic. Apostolorum, tum etiam Patrum Niceni Concilii apud omnes principes palam faciemus, ut nemo de sinceritate fidei nostrae valeat haesitare. Clerum, & sacra loca praecipua veneratione prosequimur; temporalia eorum sincera protectione custodimus, nec vllus episcoporum aut praelatorum, qui sub temporali ditione Papae consistit, personae aut rerum tanta libertate potitur. Haec certe non possunt esse haeresis aut fidei suspecta indicia, sed bonorum morum exemplaria inevitabilia. Idcirco ab illis suis iniuriis, conuitiis & contumeliis, ab illa erronea citatione, & illa iniuriosa comminatione appellamus & prouocamus pro nobis & subditis nostris, ecclesiasticis & saecularibus, salua tamen nullitate ipsius, & permanentibus erroribus eius tam in fide quam in iure, quibus per hoc nullatenus assentimus, sed Christi fidem & Apostolorum eius in Nicena etiam Synodo declaratam profitemur, etiam si Papa & Cardinalis Cusa aliter sentirent. Est enim fides ipsa vniuersalis & omnium communis, quae non solum ad clericos, verum etiam ad laicos, & omnes omnino pertinet Christianos.
units.tr: Therefore the prophet did not call them blessed for this, that they search the testimonies of the Lord, which proud men also do, and opponents, and those who strive against such things, approving and disapproving; but he calls them blessed only if they seek God with the whole heart. This we are pleased to seek with a sincere heart, without the depth of the Scriptures, which exceeds our understanding. It is our duty to defend our fatherland zealously, which by preserving, helping, and rightly and faithfully increasing it, under the faith of Christ and his Apostles, declared also in the Nicene Council, which we believe expressly and explicitly, and, with the Church, hold the rest of what pertains to the faith, we hope will be advanced to the rewards of eternal recompense. But he was not content to have summoned us in the aforesaid manner; he has even turned to our counsellors and to all our subjects without exception, saying: "Likewise also, and below: the other counsellors of Sigismund himself, his household, townsmen, and below: also all the subjects of Sigismund himself of the dioceses of Chur, Trent and Brixen, who despise ecclesiastical censures," etc. Certainly no one despises censures, since none has yet been validly issued; but at the Cardinal's pleasure, many reproaches, insults, injuries and calumnies have been uttered and committed against us and ours, who have not been heard. These things ought rather to be atoned for than magnified, as I have said, and the law has provided what penalty is owed to those who issue censures, abusing with futility the power granted to them. Yet in this matter the folly of that presumption must be assailed and overturned, that he wishes all subjects to be examined on an article of faith and on what follows to it from the doctrine of the saints; for this is to dispute about the faith in the common manner, which is forbidden by law. For that is done publicly which is carried on among two hundred thousand men, women and children. What will a farmer answer when asked what the Church is, or on what the erring Pope is sustained; and whether the Greek is a part of the Church, or the Jew, or any other Christian dwelling at the ends of the earth? In what does the true head of the Church differ from the ministerial one? What authority did it give to the Scriptures, and what kind of authority did it receive from them? Certainly our forebears had such zeal for guarding the secrets of the Scriptures, lest they be handled by the common people, that they most severely reproached those who translated the Bible from the Latin language into German. But now that Cardinal wishes to question the rustics about those things which follow from the teaching of the saints concerning this very article of faith. Let us leave this disputation to the scholars; farmers and vinedressers must cultivate and dig their fields, for whom it is enough to recite the Creed of the Apostles; but the discussion of the mystical collective unity, or in how many ways several are one, is not a disputation for laymen. But if it pleases the Cardinal to polish the rustic people with the opinions of the doctors, he may (if he wishes) set up schools to which they may flock on holidays, so that, of course, they do not neglect the cultivation of the fields. But the most blessed Pope Gregory did not teach in his Pastoralia that things which ought to be kept silent, depending on place and person, should be put forward everywhere and without discrimination, which is to cast pearls before swine: namely, to handle the secrets of the Scriptures before the common people. If the Pope thought that we were less learned in the faith, and if this sprang from a sincere heart, he could easily learn this from the chief men and princes who dwell with us, without the insults with which he delights himself against us. If there were any such dispute about our ecclesiastical or secular subjects, and if there were truly sincerity in him, he could easily learn it without so much disturbance of persons. But he has demanded impossible things, so that he might contrive for himself an occasion to rage. Who, I pray, of the Gentiles or idolaters has stirred up such a persecution against the Christians, that by one sentence he would condemn as many Christian souls as that Pope has already summoned, so that he might find an occasion for condemnation? He, indeed, has profaned the holy legation. Truly, what is to be thought of his clemency or cruelty he has shown abundantly enough. As for us, let us appear before him, we or our subjects, clerical or lay, and let him trust us, if he has disdained to hear us; far be this madness from us. But we will make our faith, namely that of the Apostles and also that of the Fathers of the Nicene Council, plain before all princes, so that no one may be able to doubt the sincerity of our faith. We honour the clergy and the sacred places with especial reverence; we protect their temporal goods with sincere defence, nor does any bishop or prelate who lives under the temporal dominion of the Pope enjoy such liberty of person or property. Surely these cannot be signs of heresy or of suspicion in the faith, but unavoidable examples of good morals. Therefore, on account of those injuries, reproaches and insults of his, and on account of that erroneous summons and that injurious threat, we appeal and make protest, for ourselves and for our subjects, ecclesiastical and secular, saving nevertheless its nullity, and the continuing errors of his, both in faith and in law, to which we by no means assent; rather we profess the faith of Christ and his Apostles, declared also in the Nicene Synod, even if the Pope and Cardinal Cusanus think otherwise. For that faith itself is universal and common to all, and pertains not only to clerics but also to laymen, and to all Christians without exception.

units.la: Appellationis vero nostrae gradus facimus. Primo, si Papa causam, quam ipse & Cardinalis contra nos praesumunt, voluerit viro non suspecto delegare. Sunt enim plurimi praelati principes integerrimi per Germaniam, quibus status & conditio Brixinensis Ecclesiae, simul ac nostri ac ipsius Cardinalis mores & vita innotescunt: quorum arbitrium qui detrectauerit, suo se indicat iuri minime confidere. Alioquin ad futurum concilium, cuius praefinitum tempus, scilicet decennium, iamdudum elapsum est, prouocamus, cum stet per Papam, quominus celebretur. Similiter ad Romanum futurum Pontificem, absque omnibus modis & gradibus, prout in priori nostra appellatione in valvis ecclesiae Florentinae affixa continetur, quam Papa profitetur ad sui peruenisse notitiam, cum petitione Apostolorum, & protestationibus inibi comprehensis & contentis.
units.tr: We now set out the steps of our appeal. First, if the Pope should wish to entrust the case, which he and the Cardinal are presuming to bring against us, to a man who is not suspect. For there are very many upright princes and prelates throughout Germany, to whom the state and condition of the Church of Brixen, as well as the conduct and life of ourselves and of the Cardinal, are well known; whoever refuses their judgment shows that he does not trust his own cause at all. Otherwise we appeal to a future council, whose appointed time, namely ten years, has long since elapsed, since it is the Pope who stands in the way of its being held. Likewise we appeal to the future Roman Pontiff, without any restrictions or degrees, just as is contained in our earlier appeal posted on the doors of the church of Florence, which the Pope professes has come to his notice, together with the petition of the Apostles and the protestations included and contained therein.

units.la: DECLARATIO APOSTOLICA POENALIS contra Sigismundum Ducem.
units.tr: Apostolic Penal Declaration against Duke Sigismund.

units.la: PIVS Episcopus seruus seruorum Dei, ad futuram rei memoriam: Ineffabilis summi prouidentia Patris super gentes & regna, iuxta prophetae verbum, licet insufficientibus meritis constituti, officii nostri debitum vt tenemur exequimur, de vinea Domini Sabaoth euellenda euellimus, in eaque plantanda plantamus, ac recta regimus, & dirigimus indirecta, perfidosque ac facinorosos quosque, cum scandalo corpori ecclesiae sint, a fidelium coetu praescindimus. Nam sacro testante Euangelio, inutilibus membris a corporis compage diuisis, eis carere magis proficiat ad salutem, quam cum illis aeterna supplicia intoire. Nuper siquidem postquam nobis innotuerat, quod dilectus filius noster Nicolaus tituli sancti Petri ad vincula presbyter Cardinalis, & ex dispensatione sedis Apostolicae Episcopus Brixinensis, dum curae dictae suae ecclesiae Brixinensis intenderet, & in castro Brunegk, suae Brixinensis diocesis, ad ecclesiam curandam pleno iure spectantem resideret, per Sigismundum tunc Austriae Ducem hostiliter primo per suos in aurora diei Paschae in dicto castro obsessus fuerat; & quod castro ipso per eosdem nomine ipsius Sigismundi recepto, idem Sigismundus die sequente praefatum Cardinalem, missis ad eum duobus tubicinis, suo & omnium subditorum suorum nomine publice diffidauerat, atque cum magna armatorum copia, bombardis & aliis instrumentis bellicis, eundem Cardinalem, tunc in arce dicti castri existentem, minaciter valde & hostiliter fuerat persecutus, quousque ipsius Cardinalis personam in suam redegisset potestatem, & sic diebus multis tenuisset, & quod infra dies illos, quoddam castrum nomine Taufers, necnon notabilem quantitatem pecuniarum, obligationesque & literas plures ab eodem Cardinale & Capitulo Brixinensi extorsisset, ac damna multa sibi & suis intulisset, quae summam triginta quinque millium florenorum transcendere, ac in enervationem ecclesiasticae libertatis, totalemque exinanitionem priuilegiorum dictae ecclesiae vergere dicebantur. Et postquam praemissa & etiam certa alia ea concernentia in consistorio generali, promouente dilecto filio Michaele de Prato causarum camerae Apostolicae procuratore, per dilectum filium Andream de sancta Cruce, vtriusque iuris Doctorem, dictique consistorii & fisci nostri aduocatum, petendo Sigismundum ipsum, & alios culpabiles in praemissis etiam omnes & singulos, sententias ac poenas in constitutione felicis recordationis Bonifacii Papae VIII. praedecessoris nostri, quae incipit felicis, contentas, & alias in tales, a iure inflictas, & promulgatas incidisse declarari, & contra eos procedi, aliasque & alia fieri & decerni, prout in commissione tunc publice exposita continetur, nos tunc facinoris huiusmodi, (quod adeo notorium erat, vt nulla posset tergiuersatione celari) enormitatem, & gravitatem causae pensantes, antequam in ea quicquam ageremus, ad maiorem rei certitudinem & nostram informationem dicto procuratore ex suo officio promouente, dilecto filio nostro Iohanni tituli sanctae Priscae Presbytero Cardinali, ac venerabilibus fratribus nostris Iohanni Attrebatensi, & Dominico Torcellanensi episcopis, viua voce oraculo commisimus, vt se super expositis huiusmodi informarent, & nobis quae reperirent veritate subniti referrent. Postmodum vero facta per eosdem nobis relatione fideli, inuenimus quod dolenter referimus, praemissa & alia tunc exposita, veritate fulciri, habito tunc per nos cum eisdem commissariis ac aliis venerabilibus fratribus nostris sanctae Romanae ecclesiae Cardinalibus, super his maturo consilio, tantam Dei & ecclesiae offensam, tantamque temeritatis audaciam, inultam & sub dissimulatione pertransire nequeuntes, ipsum Sigismundum, ac omnes alios & singulos cuiuscunque, etiam pontificalis, dignitatis, status, gradus, ordinis vel conditionis forent ecclesiasticae vel mundanae, qui eidem Sigismundo in praemissis consilio, auxilium vel fauorem dederant, arma contra dictum Cardinalem suscepe rant, huiusmodiq; nefandum facinus facto reatu habuerant, seu Sigismundu & alios praedictos postea receptauerat, seu defensauerat, eosdem & eos qui diffidationi ipsu Sigismundu eide Cardinali factae adhaeserat, aut Cardinale ipsum p suas literas diffidauerant, aut indiffidatione ipsius Ducis coprehesi erat, ac eos q eide Cardinali defecerat, atq; ipsu Sigismundu suos contra eundem Cardinalem hostiliter venientes in castris & locis etiam ad praefatam ecclesiam Brixinensem, spectantibus admiserant; ecclesiasticos & seculares, eorum nomina & cognomina pro expressis habenda, per edictum publicum Apostolica auctoritate, per alias nostras certi tenoris literas ex abundanti moneri fecimus peremptorie & requiri, ut certa die per nos eis praefixa in consistorio generali, coram nobis personaliter comparerent, allegaturi causas si quas haberent rationes, cur ad declarationem poenarum tam in constitutione ipsa, quam dictis nostris literis monitorialibus contentarum, procedere non deberemus.
units.tr: PIUS, Bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the future memory of the thing: By the ineffable providence of the most high Father over nations and kingdoms, according to the word of the prophet, though we are set in office on insufficient merits, we carry out what the duty of our office requires of us. We uproot from the vineyard of the Lord of Sabaoth what must be uprooted, we plant what must be planted, we set right what is crooked and direct what is wayward, and we cut off from the assembly of the faithful all the treacherous and wicked, since they are a scandal to the body of the Church. For the sacred Gospel bears witness that it is better for useless members, cut off from the frame of the body, to lack them for salvation than to go with them into eternal punishments. Lately, after it had become known to us that our beloved son Nicholas, cardinal priest of the title of St Peter in Chains, and by dispensation of the Apostolic See bishop of Brixen, while attending to the care of his church of Brixen and residing in the castle of Bruneck in his diocese of Brixen, in order to look after the church which belongs to him by full right, had been attacked in hostile manner at dawn on Easter day in the said castle by Sigismund, then Duke of Austria, acting through his men; and that, once the castle had been taken by them in Sigismund's name, the same Sigismund, on the following day, sent two trumpeters to the aforesaid cardinal and publicly defied him, in his own name and in the name of all his subjects, and with a great force of armed men, with bombards and other war machines, pursued the said cardinal, then in the citadel of the said castle, very threateningly and hostilely, until he had reduced the person of the cardinal into his power and held him so for many days; and that within those days he had extorted from the same cardinal and the chapter of Brixen a certain castle called Taufers, a considerable sum of money, and many bonds and letters, and had inflicted many losses on him and his people, which were said to exceed the sum of thirty-five thousand florins and to tend to the weakening of ecclesiastical liberty and the total emptying of the privileges of the said church. And after the above matters, and certain other matters concerning them, had been set forth in a general consistory, by our beloved son Michael de Prato, procurator of causes of the Apostolic Chamber, and through our beloved son Andrew of Santa Croce, Doctor of both laws, advocate of the said consistory and of our treasury, asking that Sigismund himself and the others guilty in the above matters, all and each, be declared to have incurred the sentences and penalties contained in the constitution of Pope Boniface VIII of happy memory, our predecessor, which begins "Felicis," and the others inflicted and promulgated by law against such persons, and that proceedings be taken against them, and other and further steps be taken and decreed, as is contained in the commission then publicly read out; we, weighing the enormity and gravity of such a crime (which was so notorious that no evasion could conceal it), before we did anything in the matter, for greater certainty and our own information, at the instance of the said procurator acting in his office, committed by living voice and oral mandate to our beloved son John, cardinal priest of the title of St Prisca, and to our venerable brothers John, bishop of Arras, and Dominic, bishop of Torcello, that they should inform themselves about the matters so set forth and report to us the truth they found. Afterwards, indeed, by a faithful report made to us by the same commissioners, we found (as we report with sorrow) that the above matters and the others then set forth were supported by truth. Having then taken mature counsel on these things with the same commissioners and our other venerable brothers, the cardinals of the holy Roman Church, we could not allow so great an offence against God and the Church, and such rashness of audacity, to pass unavenged and under pretence of ignoring it. So we caused Sigismund himself, and all others, each and every one, of whatever pontifical dignity, status, rank, order or condition, whether ecclesiastical or secular, who had given counsel, aid or favour to Sigismund in the above matters, had taken up arms against the said cardinal, and had incurred guilt by such a wicked crime, or who had afterwards received or defended Sigismund and the others mentioned, or who had joined in the defiance of Sigismund made against the same cardinal, or who had defied the cardinal himself by their letters, or who were involved in the defiance of the said duke, and those who had defected from the same cardinal, and those who had admitted Sigismund's men coming hostilely against the same cardinal into camps and places even belonging to the aforesaid church of Brixen, to be warned and summoned peremptorily, by public edict under Apostolic authority and, abundantly, by our other letters of certain tenor, their names and surnames being considered as expressed, so that on a certain day fixed for them by us in a general consistory, they should appear in person before us, to allege whatever reasons they might have why we ought not to proceed to the declaration of the penalties contained both in that constitution and in our said letters of monition.

units.la: Alioquin quod tam ad declarationem ipsam, irritationemque omnium & singulorum vi & metu sic per ipsum Cardinalem gestorum, & ab ea extortorum huiusmodi, etiam iuramento validatorum, necnon restitutionem tam mobilium quam immobilium sic ab eodem Cardinale ablatorum, interdicti ecclesiastici in locis, in quibus praemissa commissa fuere, & omnibus aliis locis, ipsis Sigismundo & aliis praefatis subiectis etiam novam positionem, atque ad ulteriora, & ad omnia ea procedemus, quae nobis iuxta tanti excessus exigentiam, & rei notorietatem iusta viderentur fieri & decerni, prout haec & alia, literis nostris aliis desuper emanatis, quarum tenores, ac si de verbo ad verbum inserarentur praesentibus, haberi volumus pro sufficienter expressis, plenius continentur. Verum etsi dictum Sigismundum, quem antea semper speciali favore fuimus prosecuti, & in visceribus dilexerimus caritatis, cuiusque desideria quantum cum Deo licuisset fuimus exaudire parati, & etiam alios praedictos sperauremus pendente termino dicti monitorii ad cor redire, & tam grauem eorum reatum recognoscere, seque nobis tanquam Christi vicario, cuius vices quamuis immeriti in terris gerimus, totaliter submittere debuisse; ipsi tamen (de quo abintimis dolemus precordiis) diabolica fraude seducti, in profundum malorum se praecipitantes, animarum suarum salutem negligentes, & honorem suum pro nihilo habentes, in sathanica superbia perseuerauerunt. Sicque adueniente termino in ipso nostro monitorio expresso, & eis non comparentibus, comparuit dictus Michael de Prato, procurator noster fiscalis, & eo nomine in consistorio publico, per nos propterea celebrato, literasque monitoriales nostras antedictas, una cum earum executionibus in locis assignatis legitime factis, scripto producens, monitorum earundem contumaciam accusauit, & eos contumaces reputari, ac omnes & singulas poenas praedictas incurrisse ac incidisse, ac alias iuxta monitorii illius contumaciam declarari, vlteriusque contra eosdem monitos, prout iuris esset, procedi per nos debita cum instantia postulauit. Eoque facto, comparuit ibidem quidam Laurentius nomine, qui se Doctorem & dicti Sigismundi nuncium asseruit, ac eiusdem Sigismundi ex parte audiri petiit, quem etiam alias ad partem super his extense satis & saepius audiueramus, quam plura minus vera dicti Sigismundi & suorum complicum parte, nobis referentem; a quo tunc, ut mandatum, si quod in hac causa haberet, produceret, requisiuimus, & cum is nullum haberet mandatum, ad termino monitionis satisfaciendum, quoddam procuratorium ad nobis insinuandam quandam praetensam appellationem, tanquam a nobis male informato ad nos melius informandum exhibuit. Consideratesque autem quod Sigismundus ipse & alii praedicti ex abundanti, & de mera nostra gratia moniti fuerunt, ut si quid dicere vellent, cur iuxta monitorium per nos emissum declarari non deberent, tunc die lunae quarta mensis Augusti coram nobis personaliter comparerent, ita quod per aliud id facere eis concessum non fuerat; ut tamen omnis nostra mansuetudo appareret, procuratorium illud audire decreuimus, si forte ipse Sigismundus cum suis complicibus per procuratorem idoneum se nobis personaliter submittere & absolutionem a sententiis censuris & poenis incursis petere, aliasque iuxta canonicas sanctiones facere vellet; quo casu eundem Laurentium libenter vtique audiuissemus, sed cum audito procuratorio illo, quod ibidem publice alta & intelligibili voce legi fecimus, consideraremus etiam, quod ipse Laurentius solum ad nos illudendum, & obedientiam & correctionem fugiendum adu enerat, adidque mandatum haberet; quodque opus non erat, nos qui iam de notorietate commissi sacrilegii, & tam nefando actu huiusmodi, plene & plenius essemus informati, ita quod amplius nos informari opus non erat, praetensam & ineptam appellationem illam, de qua in dicto procuratorio mentio fiebat, ac quamcunque aliam contra praemissa interpositam forsan ac interponendam, friuolam & non admittendam, sed tanquam iniustam, reiiciendam esse decreuimus & reiecimus, ipsi Laurentio silentium imponentes. Venerabilibus vero Fratribus nostris Clusiensi & Ortonensi episcopis mandauimus, ut ad portas ecclesiae Senensis cum nuntiis ad hoc deputatis accederent, & per eosdem nuncios alta voce vicibus tribus ibidem vocari facerent, si adesset ipse Sigismundus aut alii praedicti per se aut procuratores legitimos, & iuxta dicti monitorii nostri continentiam aliquid dicere vellent, nam eos benigne audire parati eramus. Cumque episcopi ipsi mandatum nostrum huiusmodi exequentes, ad nos in eodem consistorio redissent, retulerunt, nec Sigismundum ipsum nec complices suos seu monitos huiusmodi aut eorum nomine aliquem procuratorem comparuisse seu adesse. Idcirco nos ad dicti procuratoris fiscalis instantiam Sigismundum, & alios monitos praefatos non comparentes reputauimus merito, prout erant quoad actum & terminum huiusmodi iustitia id exigente, contumaces. Et licet tunc contra monitos ipsos ad declarationem huiusmodi & alias, prout petitum fuerat, procedere potuissemus & debuissemus: Nos tamen, qui praemissa ea molestius fecimus, quo ipsum Sigismundum ab ineunte eius aetate dilexmus ad omnem nostram, ob eius specialem dilectionem, quae claraे & omni laude dignae domui Austriae, ex qua ipse Sigismundus originem traxit, coniungimur, mansuetudinem ostendendam, vtq; ipsi moniti penitus conuincerentur, dictum terminum vsq; in praesens continuauimus, mandantes ad ipsius Sigismundi & aliorum praedictorum malitiam, & cordis ipsorum duritiam conuincendum, eosdem iterum per edictum publicum in valuis dictæ Senensis Ecclesiæ affigendum vocari, quatenus die datæ præsentium coram nobis in consistorio publico, quod etiam propterea tenere decreuimus, personaliter comparerent, ad audiendum se pœnas, sententias & censuras in dicto monitorio nostro contentas incidisse declarari, vel causas cur id fieri non deberet, si quas haberent rationabiles, allegandum. Cùm autem facta executionem huiusmodi nostræ vocationis in dictis valuis, eaque reproducta hodie coram nobis, tanta fuerit ipsius Sigismundi & aliorum monitorum & vocatorum rebellio atque proteruia, vt nec hodierna die nefandissimum eorum excessum huiusmodi piis actibus humiliter recognoscere & expiare, nec se excusare, nec creatori omnium & Ecclesiæ sanctæ Dei satisfacere, nec alias iuxta canonicas sanctiones & sanctorum Patrum ac prædecessorum nostrorum Romanorum Pontificum instituta agere curarunt, cuncta interne rimantes, censuimus non dedecori, sed maximæ gloriæ & honori esse, ipsi inclitæ domui Austriæ, si contra dictum Sigismundum, eiusdem atque progenitorum suorum splendorem & famam denigrantem & scandalizantem, qui etiam honoris & dignitatis tam præclaræ domus, eius demeritis indignum se reddidit, armis iustitiæ insurgamus, ipsum tanquam palmitem, fructum non ferentem, & membrum putridum ab eadem domo resecemus. Ad Dei igitur laudem & gloriam, hac nostra summa in perpetuum valitura, de consilio eorundem fratrum decernimus, ac auctoritate Apostolica tenore præsentium declaramus, dictum Sigismundum ac eos omnes & singulos, qui dictum Cardinalem & Episcopum diffidarunt expresse, & cæteros quosque cuiuscunque etiam pontificalis dignitatis, status, gradus, ordinis, vel conditionis forent, ecclesiasticæ vel mundanæ, qui eidem Sigismundo & aliis prædictis in præmissis præbuerunt auxilium, consilium vel fauorem, & qui arma contra dictum Cardinalem susceperunt, huiusmodi quoque nefandum facinus ratum habuerunt, seu Sigismundum aliosque prædictos postea receptarunt, aut defensarunt, nec non eos qui diffidationi ipsius Sigismundi huiusmodi adhæserunt, aut in diffidationibus eiusdem Sigismundi & diffidantium aliorum prædictorum comprehensi sunt, atque eos qui dicto Cardinali in fidelitate & auxilio, cum potuerunt, eo tempore defecerunt, ipsumq; Sigismundum & alios prædictos contra præfatum Cardinalem hostiliter venientes in castris & locis etiam ad ipsam Ecclesiam Brixinensem spectantibus, & specialiter dictum castrum Brunegk & eius inhabitatores, qui ipsum Sigismundum & suos sic admiserunt, & eos qui præfata facinora rata habuerunt, ecclesiasticos & seculares, eorum omnium & singulorum nomina & cognomina, ac si de verbo ad verbum inserer entur præsentibus, pro sufficienter expressis habentes, ob præmissa sunt reos criminis læsæ maiestatis, anathematizatos, perpetuo infames, diffidatos, bannitos & intestabiles, atque ab omni successione expulsos, ædificia etiam eorum in ruinam danda, & eis de nullo debito respondendum seu responderi debere, omnia pacta promissa etiam Sacramento formata, & quæcunque fœdera etiam pacis seruandæ cum dictis, Sigismundo & aliis præfatis, inita fore irrita & inania, dictorumque Sigismundi & aliorum declaratorum huiusmodi bona quæcunq; mobilia & immobilia fisco nostro & Romanæ Ecclesiæ, cui in persona Cardinalis & Episcopi iniuriatum existit, penitus applicanda, & nostræ & Apostolicæ Sedis dispositioni totaliter reservanda, ita vt nihil de illis transmittatur ad posteros: ac eos omnesq; & singulos in præmissis culpabiles, siue Episcopi, Abbates, Præpositi, Decani, aut etiam Canonici Brixinensis, aut cuiuscunque alterius Ecclesiæ fuerint, in specie & in genere, omni honore & dignitate ecclesiastica seu seculari, omniq; feudo, locatione, officioq; & beneficio quocunque spirituali & temporali, quæ à quacunque Ecclesia, monasterio siue Prælato obtinent, priuatos. Quorum feudorum ad Ecclesiam devolutorum collationem & ordinationem ex certis causis animam nostram mouentibus, nostræ & Apostolicæ sedis dispositioni similiter reseruamus. Eorundem etiam filios & nepotes per rectam lineam descendentes, beneficiatos, quouis beneficio ecclesiastico, etiam pontificiali dignitate priuatos, eisq; omnis promotionis spem sublatam. Nobis etiam ipsorum filiorum atque nepotum ex virili sexu descendentium ab eisdem, alicuius dignitatis aut honoris ecclesiastici vel mundani, aut alicuius loci regiminis ianuam aperiendam, ac eis quodlibet officiu publicu seu ministerium interdictum, atque in iudiciis eorum dictis & depositionibus nihil fidei aut credulitatis contra quemcunque adhibendum, & ad testimonia perhibenda esse indignos: eisque ad beneficium & officium ecclesiasticum & ordines sacros negatum ascensum, & ad actus legitimos nullum eis patere aditum, absque omni spe dispensationis super aliquo præmissorum. Nec non omnes & singulos præfatos excommunicationis maioris sententiam, aliasque sententias, censuras & pœnas in tales à iure latas, inflictas & promulgatas, damnabiliter incidisse. Eosdem quoque Sigismundum & alios supradictos excommunicationis sententia innodamus, anathematizamus, bannimus: Infames, bannitos, intestabiles, honore & bonis ac successione priuatos esse, ac aliis omnibus pœnis supradictis cum terris per eos possessis siue occupatis subiacere decernimus per præsentes. Terras quoque & dominia per ipsum Sigismundum & alios prædictos occupata & possessa quæcunque, vbicunque & in quibuscunq; dioecesibus consistant, ac omnia alia loca, ad quæ eos aut eorum aliquem declinare, & quamdiu ibi moram trahere contigerit, ecclesiastico & strictissimo interdicto fore suppositæ declaramus, & etiam ipsum interdictum in prædictis locis Apostolica auctoritate de nouo ponimus. Mandantes omnibus & singulis Episcopis, Abbatibus, Prioribus, Præpositis, Decanis, Pro-
units.tr: Otherwise, we shall proceed to everything that seems just to us, given the magnitude of so great an offence and the notoriety of the affair: to the declaration itself, and to the annulling of all and each of the acts done by the Cardinal through violence and fear, and of the things extorted from them, even those confirmed by oath; to the restitution of both movable and immovable goods so taken by the same Cardinal; to an ecclesiastical interdict in the places where the aforesaid deeds were committed and in all other places; and to a fresh imposition of penalties upon Sigismund and the other aforesaid subjects. All this, and more, is set out fully in our other letters issued on this matter, whose tenor we wish to be held as sufficiently expressed in these present letters, as if it were inserted here word for word. Yet although we have always shown Sigismund special favour, have loved him with the bowels of charity, and have been ready to grant his desires so far as it was lawful before God, and although we hoped that during the term of the said monitory the others too would return to their senses, acknowledge the gravity of their guilt, and submit wholly to us as to Christ's vicar, whose office we hold on earth though unworthy of it; they nevertheless, to our heartfelt sorrow, led astray by diabolical deceit, plunged themselves into the depths of evil, neglecting the salvation of their souls and holding their own honour as nothing, and persisted in satanic pride. So when the day fixed in our monitory arrived and they did not appear, Michael de Prato, our procurator fiscal, came forward, and in the public consistory convened for that purpose presented in writing our said monitory letters, together with their lawful execution in the appointed places. He accused the summoned parties of contumacy, asked that they be held contumacious and to have incurred and fallen into all and each of the aforesaid penalties, that they be otherwise declared so in accordance with the contumacy of that monitory, and that proceedings be taken against them as the law required, with due urgency. When this was done, a certain Laurentius appeared there, who said he was a doctor and envoy of the said Sigismund, and asked to be heard on Sigismund's behalf. We had indeed heard him before, on the side of that party, at considerable length and often, when he reported to us many things that were not true on the part of Sigismund and his accomplices. We now required him to produce, as the command required, any mandate he had in this case; and since he had no mandate, he offered, in place of satisfying the term of the monition, a certain power of attorney to lodge with us a so-called appeal, as if we had been ill-informed, in order to inform us better. Yet since Sigismund himself and the others named had been summoned, out of abundant caution and of our pure grace, so that if they wished to say anything why they should not be declared according to the monitory we had issued, they were to appear in person before us on Monday the fourth of August, and since it had not been granted that this be done through another; nevertheless, so that all our gentleness might appear, we decided to hear that power of attorney, in case Sigismund himself with his accomplices should wish to submit themselves to us in person through a suitable procurator, and to ask absolution from the sentences, censures and penalties incurred, and to do the other things required by the canonical sanctions. In that case we would gladly have heard this Laurentius. But when we had heard that power of attorney, which we had read aloud there publicly in a loud and intelligible voice, we also considered that Laurentius had come only to mock us and to flee obedience and correction, and that he had no mandate. Moreover, there was no need for us to be better informed, since we were already fully and more than fully informed of the notoriety of the sacrilege committed and of such an abominable act. Therefore we decided that that supposed and empty appeal, mentioned in the said power of attorney, and any other appeal lodged or to be lodged against the aforesaid matters, was frivolous and not to be admitted, but to be rejected as unjust; and we rejected it, imposing silence on Laurentius. We further ordered our venerable brothers, the bishops of Chiusi and Orte, to go to the gates of the church of Siena with the messengers appointed for this purpose, and through those messengers to have them called three times there with a loud voice, to see whether Sigismund himself or the others named were present, either in person or through lawful procurators, and wished to say anything according to the content of our monitory; for we were ready to hear them kindly. When those bishops, carrying out our command, returned to us in the same consistory, they reported that neither Sigismund himself, nor his accomplices or the summoned parties, nor any procurator on their behalf had appeared or was present. Accordingly, at the instance of our procurator fiscal, we rightly held Sigismund and the other named parties, who did not appear, to be contumacious, as justice required in respect of that act and term. And although we could and should then have proceeded against the summoned parties to this declaration and otherwise, as had been asked, we nevertheless, who were the more troubled by these matters, wished to show mercy to all, both because we have loved Sigismund from his earliest age, and because of his special affection we are joined to the illustrious house of Austria, worthy of all praise, from which Sigismund himself derives his origin. We therefore extended the said term until now, so that the summoned parties might be utterly convicted. Now, to convict the malice of Sigismund and the others and the hardness of their hearts, we ordered that they be summoned again by a public edict, to be affixed to the doors of the said church of Siena, so that on the day of the date of these presents they should appear in person before us in the public consistory, which we also decided to hold for this purpose, to hear themselves declared to have incurred the penalties, sentences and censures contained in our said monitory, or to allege any reasonable causes why this should not be done. But when the execution of this our summons was made on the said doors, and when it was reproduced today before us, the rebellion and insolence of Sigismund and the other summoned and called parties was so great that they took no care, either on this day, humbly to acknowledge and expiate their most abominable offence by pious acts, or to excuse themselves, or to satisfy the Creator of all things and the holy Church of God, or otherwise to act according to the canonical sanctions and the institutions of the holy Fathers and of our predecessors the Roman Pontiffs. Weighing all these things within ourselves, we judged that it would be no disgrace but the greatest glory and honour to the illustrious house of Austria if we rose up with the arms of justice against the said Sigismund, who blackens and scandalizes the splendour and reputation of himself and his forebears, and who by his demerits has made himself unworthy of the honour and dignity of so distinguished a house; and if we cut him off from that house like a branch bearing no fruit and a rotten limb. Therefore, to the praise and glory of God, by this our sentence, which shall stand for ever, with the counsel of our brothers, we decree and by apostolic authority declare by the tenor of these presents that the said Sigismund, and all and each of those who expressly defied the said Cardinal and Bishop, and all others, of whatever pontifical dignity, rank, grade, order or condition, ecclesiastical or secular, who gave help, counsel or favour to the same Sigismund and the others named in the aforesaid matters, and who took up arms against the said Cardinal, and who also approved this unspeakable crime, or afterwards received or defended Sigismund and the others named, and likewise those who adhered to the defiance of Sigismund, or were included in the defiances of Sigismund and of the other defying parties named, and those who failed the said Cardinal in fidelity and aid, when they could have helped him at that time, and who admitted Sigismund and the other named parties when they came hostilely against the said Cardinal, in camps and places also belonging to the church of Brixen itself, and specially the said castle of Brunegg and its inhabitants who so admitted Sigismund and his men, and those, ecclesiastical and secular, who approved the aforesaid crimes: all of them, and each, by name and surname, as if inserted here word for word, we hold as sufficiently expressed; on account of the aforesaid matters they are guilty of the crime of high treason, are anathematized, perpetually infamous, defied, outlawed and incapable of giving testimony, and are expelled from all succession; their buildings are to be given to ruin; they are not to be answered for any debt, nor is any answer to be given to them; all pacts and promises, even those confirmed by oath, and all covenants, even those of keeping peace, entered into with the said Sigismund and the other named parties, shall be void and null; and all the movable and immovable goods of Sigismund and the others declared as above shall be wholly applied to our treasury and to the Roman Church, to which injury was done in the person of the Cardinal and Bishop, and shall be wholly reserved to the disposal of ourselves and the Apostolic See, so that nothing of them passes to their posterity. And all and each of those guilty in these matters, whether they are bishops, abbots, provosts, deans, or canons of Brixen or of any other church, we deprive, both specifically and generally, of every ecclesiastical or secular honour and dignity, and of every fief, lease, office and benefice, spiritual or temporal, which they hold from any church, monastery or prelate. The conferral and disposition of those fiefs that have fallen back to the Church, for certain causes moving our soul, we likewise reserve to ourselves and to the disposal of the Apostolic See. Their sons and grandsons descending in the direct line we render incapable of holding any ecclesiastical benefice, even one with pontifical dignity, and all hope of promotion is taken from them. Also, to us, the entrance to any dignity or honour, ecclesiastical or secular, or to the government of any place, is to be opened only by the male descendants of those sons and grandsons, and to them every public office or ministry is forbidden; in their judgments, their statements and depositions are to be given no trust or credence against anyone, and they are unworthy to bear witness; and the ascent to an ecclesiastical benefice or office and to holy orders is denied them, and no access to lawful acts lies open to them, without any hope of dispensation in any of the aforesaid matters. Moreover, we declare that all and each of the aforesaid have damnably incurred the sentence of greater excommunication, and the other sentences, censures and penalties laid down, inflicted and promulgated against such persons by law. We also bind Sigismund and the other named parties under sentence of excommunication, anathematize and outlaw them; by these presents we decree that they are infamous, outlawed, incapable of giving testimony, deprived of honour, goods and succession, and subject to all the other penalties mentioned above, together with the lands possessed or occupied by them. We also declare that all lands and dominions occupied and possessed by Sigismund and the other named parties, wherever they lie and in whatever dioceses, and all other places to which they or any of them may go, and for as long as they happen to remain there, are subject to the ecclesiastical and most strict interdict; and by apostolic authority we now lay that same interdict anew upon the aforesaid places. We command all and each of the bishops, abbots, priors, provosts, deans, pro-

units.la: Ssssss uinciauincialium, Ecclesiarum Rectoribus & Presbyteris aliis, vt ipsum Sigismundum & alios prædi-ctos etiā nominatim singulis diebus Dominicis & festiuis in diuinis, sic excommunicatos, anathematisatos, infames, diffidatos, priuatos & alias vt præfertur per nos declaratos in eorum ecclesiis denuntient, & denuntiari faciant, vniuersis & singulis Christi fidelibus districtius iniungentes, vt dictos excommunicatos, anathematisatos & declaratos vbilibet euitent & faciant euitari, nec cum eis aut eorum aliquo post spacium vnius mensis à data præsentium computando, quæuis commercia siue salis siue minerę argenti aut alterius generis cuiuscunque emendo vel vendendo quodlibet habeant, aut eis communicent, nec ipsis aliquod humanitatis opus aut solatium exhibeant, seu etiam victualia aut merces alias eis vendant, aut ab ipsis emant, sed eos omnes & singulos pro excommunicatis & anathematisatis ac pro diffidatis habeant inimicis. Et quoniam firmum esse nequit, quod vi & metu cōstat esse factum, harum serie dicta apostolica auctoritatem similiter pronuntiamus, decernimus, & declaramus, extorsionem & traditionem dicti castri Zauffers cum suis adhærentiis, nec nō sex millia florenorum Rhenensium, dicto Sigismundo per ipsum Cardinalem prompto & dicto tempore solutorū, promissionemq; de soluendo per eundem Cardinalem quatuor millium florenorum similium, ipsi olim Duci in terminis duobus; nec non quitantiam de tribus millibus florenorum eorundem eidem olim Duci per ipsum Cardinalem prius amicabiliter mutuatorum. Ac quod ipse Cardinalis Capitulum Brixinense ad regimen ciuitatis Brixinensis, castrorumque & oppidorum Ecclesiæ suæ Brixinensis ponere, castellanosq; nonnullos ipsi Cardinali & dictæ suæ Ecclesiæ fideles amouere. Et quod ipsum Brixinense Capitulum dicto olim Duci omnia castra & oppida Ecclesiæ præfatæ aperta tenere, nec in eis alios quam eidem Sigismundo gratos castellanos seu officiales instituere debeant seu teneantur, ac alia quæcunq; à dicto Cardinale, dum in ipsius Sigismundi potestate ac vt præmittatur, detinebatur, atque etiam, quæ tunc à dicto Capitulo per prefatum Sigismundum aut suos extorta, ac per ipsum Cardinalem seu etiam Capitulum antedictos tunc promissa seu literaliter facta, nec non sigillationem eiusdem literæ inter alia continentis, quod ipse Cardinalis eidem Capitulo omne regimen ciuitatis, castrorum & oppidorum suæ Ecclesiæ committeret, quam eodem tempore quidam se nominantes dictum Capitulum, à præfato Cardinale eorum Episcopo tunc angustiato & oppresso similiter extorserunt. Omnia quoque alia etiam inde secuta, cum non solum sint violenta & iniustissima, sed & contra omnem honorem & honestatem damnabiliter extorta, fuisse & esse nulla, irrita & inualida, nulliusque efficaciæ roboris vel momenti: Ipsumque Cardinalem ad ea obseruandum nunquam fuisse obligatum, neq; se sic in præiudicium Ecclesiæ obligare potuisse, eademque omnia & singula ad cautelam cassamus, irritamus & annullamus, ac ipsum Cardinalem ad ea obseruandum nullatenus obligatum fore, ac ipsum castrum Zauffers / cum suis adhærentiis vniuersis, & inde perceptis ab eodē tempore fructibus, ac sex millia florenorum prædicta, & damna illata alia, nec non literas sic extortas tam per olim Ducem quam Capitulum præfatos, nobis aut nostro Commissario infra duorum mensium spatium à die datæ præsentium computando, sub poenis antedictis liberè restitui debere decernimus. Quodque nisi ipsum Capitulum infra dictum spacium literas per ipsum à dicto Cardinale & Episcopo eorum sic extortas, ciuitatemque Brixinensem, castra & oppida eiusdem Ecclesiæ, amotis inde nouis iam positis castellanis, & repositis inibi illis, quos ipse Cardinalis ibidem posuerat, nobis aut nostro Commissario plenè restituerunt, ex tunc lapso duorum mēsium spatio huiusmodi omnes incorporationes quarumcunq; prouincialium Ecclesiarum, quas ipsum Capitulum obtinere dignoscitur, ad mensam episcopalem Brixinensem eo ipso reuertantur, & Capitulum ipsum huiusmodi incorporationibus Ecclesiarum, omnesque & singulas personas eiusdem Capituli in prædictis culpabiles, quorum nomina & cognomina præsentibus habere volumus pro expressis, vltra poenas iam dictas, omnibus & singulis eorum beneficiis ecclesiasticis cum cura vel sine cura, canonicatibus & Præbendis, dignitatibus, personatibus, officiis seu administrationibus, absque alia declaratione, quacunque priuatos esse volumus, atque priuamus per præsentes, eaque sic vacare decernimus. Per præmissa tamen, tam carissimo in Christo filio nostro Friderico Romanorum Imperatori, quàm dilecto filio, nobili viro Alberto Duci eius germano, ex eadem domo Austriæ, oriundis, & etiam omnibus iuribus, nec non etiam doti aut donationi propter nuptias dilectæ in Christo filiæ Eleonorae de Scotia, dicti Sigismundi conthoralis, quæ vt veridicè accepimus, præfatis facinoribus & nefandis nequaquam consensit, nolumus in aliquo præiudicare, sed ea sua bona sibi quoad vixerit, illæsa remanere. Nulli ergo omnino hominum liceat tam paginam nostræ reseruationis, innodationis, anathematis, bannimenti, constitutionis, positionis, mandati, iniunctionis, pronuntiationis, declarationis, cassationis, irritationis, annullationis, voluntatis, priuationis, & decreti infringere, vel ei ausu temerario contrauenire: si quis autem hoc attemptare præsumserit, indignationem omnipotentis Dei & beatorum Petri & Pauli Apostolorum eius se nouerit incursurum. Datum Senis Anno incarnationis Dominicæ M. CCCCLX. sexto Idus Augusti, Pontificatus nostri anno secundo.
units.tr: ...provincial Church Rectors and other elders, that they shall, on every Sunday and feast day during divine service, announce publicly in their churches that Sigismund and the others named above, having been so declared by us as excommunicated, anathematized, infamous, outlawed, deprived and otherwise as stated above, are to be avoided; and they shall have it announced, and they shall strictly enjoin on all and each of the faithful of Christ that they avoid the said excommunicated and anathematized persons, declared as such, wherever they may be, and cause them to be avoided. After a space of one month, counting from the date of these presents, no one is to have any dealings with them or any of them, whether buying or selling salt, silver ore, or goods of any other kind, nor is anyone to share anything with them, nor to give them any act of kindness or comfort, nor to sell them victuals or wares, nor to buy from them; rather, all and each of them are to be held as excommunicated, anathematized, outlawed enemies. And since what is done by force and fear cannot be firm, by the tenor of these presents we likewise pronounce, decree and declare by apostolic authority that the extortion and surrender of the said castle of Zauffers with its appurtenances, as well as the six thousand Rhenish florins paid to the said Sigismund by the Cardinal himself at the time stated, and the promise by the same Cardinal to pay four thousand similar florins to the said former Duke within two terms, and also the receipt for three thousand florins of the same, previously lent in friendship by the Cardinal to the same former Duke, are void. Likewise, that the Cardinal himself should place the Chapter of Brixen over the government of the city of Brixen and the castles and towns of his Church of Brixen, and remove certain castellans faithful to the Cardinal and his Church, and that the said Chapter of Brixen should keep open to the said former Duke all the castles and towns of the aforesaid Church, and should not or must not appoint in them any castellans or officials except those pleasing to the same Sigismund; and all other things demanded by the said Cardinal while he was held in the power of Sigismund, as stated above, and also whatever was then extorted from the said Chapter by the aforesaid Sigismund or his men, and whatever was then promised or formally made by the said Cardinal or the aforementioned Chapter, as well as the sealing of that letter which contained, among other things, that the Cardinal would commit to the same Chapter the entire government of the city, castles and towns of his Church, which at the same time certain men calling themselves the said Chapter similarly extorted from the aforesaid Cardinal, their Bishop, then distressed and oppressed: all these things, and everything else that followed from them, since they were not only violent and most unjust but also damnably extorted contrary to all honour and decency, we declare to have been and to be null, void and invalid, and of no force, strength or weight; and we declare that the Cardinal was never bound to observe them, nor could he so bind himself to the prejudice of the Church. For caution's sake we quash, annul and cancel all these things and each of them, and we decree that the Cardinal is in no way bound to observe them. Furthermore, we decree that the castle of Zauffers with all its appurtenances, together with all fruits taken from it since that time, and the aforesaid six thousand florins and the other damages inflicted, as well as the letters so extorted both from the former Duke and from the aforesaid Chapter, must be fully restored to us or to our Commissary, under the penalties stated above, within a period of two months counting from the date of these presents. And unless the said Chapter fully restores to us or our Commissary, within the said period, the letters so extorted from the Cardinal and their Bishop, and the city of Brixen and the castles and towns of the same Church, with the newly placed castellans removed and those whom the Cardinal himself had placed there restored in their place, then, once the said period of two months has passed, all incorporations of whatever provincial churches the said Chapter is known to hold shall, by that very fact, revert to the episcopal table of Brixen. And we will and decree by these presents that the said Chapter itself, and all and each of the persons of that Chapter who are guilty in the aforesaid matters (whose names and surnames we wish to be considered expressed in these presents), be deprived, beyond the penalties already stated, of all and each of their ecclesiastical benefices, with or without cure of souls, canonries and prebends, dignities, personages, offices or administrations, without any other declaration of any kind, and that these be vacant. Nevertheless, by the foregoing, we do not wish to prejudice in any way our most dear son in Christ, Frederick, Emperor of the Romans, nor our beloved son, the noble man Albert, Duke, his brother, sprung from the same house of Austria; nor do we wish to prejudice any rights, nor the dowry or donation made on account of marriage to our beloved daughter in Christ, Eleanor of Scotland, the wife of the said Sigismund, who, as we have truly learned, in no way consented to the aforesaid crimes and wicked deeds; her goods are to remain unharmed for her, as long as she lives. Therefore let no one at all be permitted to infringe or with reckless daring to contravene this page of our reservation, binding, anathema, proscription, constitution, placing, command, injunction, pronouncement, declaration, quashing, invalidation, annulment, will, deprivation and decree. If anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul. Given at Siena in the year of the Lord's incarnation 1460, on the sixth Ides of August, in the second year of our pontificate.

units.la: APPELLATIO DVCIS SIGISMVNDI A CENSVRA PII PAPÆ SECVNDI.
units.tr: THE APPEAL OF DUKE SIGISMUND AGAINST THE CENSURE OF POPE PIUS II.

units.la: Edita pro Cardinali de Cusa.
units.tr: Published on behalf of Cardinal of Cusa.

units.la: IN nomine Domini, Amen. Per hoc præsens publicum instrumentum cunctis pateat euidenter, quod Anno à natiuitate Domini millesimo quadringentesimo sexagesimo, Indictione octaua, die vero Mercurii decimo tertio Mensis Augusti, hora meridiei, vel quasi, Pontificatus sanctissimi in CHRISTO Patris ac Domini, Domini Pii, diuina prouidentia Papæ II. anno eius secundo, in oppido Isbruck, in mei Notarii publici testiumque infrascriptorum ad hoc specialiter vocatorum, rogatorum & requisitorum præsentia personaliter constitutus Illustrissimus Princeps & Dominus, Dominus Sigismundus Dux Austriæ, animo & intentione prouocandi seu appellandi, quandam papyrum vel schedam, notam prouocatoriam seu appellatoriam in se continentem, quam ibidem in manibus suis tenebat, & in medium produxit, mihi assignauit, nec non per me publicè legi fecit, ac sibi Apostolos seu literas testimoniales per me dari petiit & postulauit, nec non alia fecit, vt in prædicta prouocationis seu appellationis schedula continebatur, cuius tenor de verbo ad verbum sequitur, & est talis:
units.tr: In the name of the Lord, Amen. Let it be made evident to all by this present public instrument that in the year of the Lord's nativity 1460, in the eighth indiction, on Wednesday the thirteenth day of August, at about midday, in the second year of the pontificate of the most holy Father and Lord in Christ, Lord Pius II, by divine providence Pope, in the town of Innsbruck, in the presence of me, the public notary, and of the witnesses below written, specially summoned, asked and required for this purpose, there personally appeared the most illustrious Prince and Lord, Lord Sigismund, Duke of Austria. With the purpose and intention of appealing or lodging an appeal, he held in his hands and brought forward a certain paper or sheet containing a notice of appeal, handed it to me, and had it read aloud publicly by me. He also asked and demanded that letters of testimony be given to him by me, and did the other things contained in the said schedule of appeal, the wording of which follows word for word and is as follows:

units.la: Cùm æterni tribunal Iudicis illum reum non habeat, quem Iudex humanus iniquè condemnat, eo quod eius iudicium infallibili innititur veritati, humanum verò iudicium tum falsis suggestionibus, tum errore aut fragilitate humana, nonnunquam verò gratia & fauore perturbatur: Et idcirco prouocationis & varii recursus ac refugii remedia à maioribus nostris in subsidium oppressorum salubriter sunt inuenta. Nos itaque SIGISMVNDVS Dei gratia Austriæ, Stiriæ, Carinthiæ, & Carniolæ Dux, Comesq; Tyrolis, &c. oppressionem nostram cunctis CHRISTI fidelibus, præcipuè verò Principibus secularibus aduocatias & protectiones Ecclesiarum & Prælatorum habentibus, innotescere cupientes, hinc ordimur, quod Principatus noster vetustissimus & solidissimus ille Comitatus Tyrolis, ab antiquissimis annis, etiam antequam in nostrum & inclytæ stirpis Austriæ dominium seu ditionem peruenisset, inter varias suas aduocatias hereditario ac perpetuo iure sibi affixam habuit aduocatiam Ecclesiæ Brixinensis, cuius vigore potestatem habuerunt singuli Comites Tyrolis pro tempore in omnes fortias, castra, terras & homines ipsius Ecclesiæ, in dicto Comitatu & eius confiniis situatas, quantum ad ciuile (alias vniuersale) dominium attinet, scilicet tuitionem & protectionem omnium hominum ad Comitatum ipsum pertinentium, siue ipsi Comiti & Principi subiaceant immediatè, siue aliis personis Ecclesiasticis vel secularibus ad ipsum Comitatum spectantibus, coloniæ vel emphyteuseos, vel alio quouis iure attineant. Ipse quoque Episcopus Brixinensis, nunc existens Cardinalis tituli sancti Petri ad vincula, in exordio introitus sui in Ecclesiam Brixinensem, interueniente Domino Friderico Archiepiscopo Saltzburgensi, Metropolitano suo, nobis huiusce aduocationis ius recognouit, despondens sese erga nos gerere velle per omnia, sicuti prædecessores sui erga nos & antecessores nostros hactenus tenuissent. Quinetiam, vt ipsa aduocatia circa nos & principatum nostrum syncerius & solidius firmaretur, inter nos actum & conuentum (alias conditum) est, quod nos omnia Episcopalia & Capitularia ipsius Ecclesiæ castra, terras atque iura sub protectionis nostræ clypeo diligenter conseruare debemus, exceptis illis, quæ sub alieno & non principatu nostro consistunt. Sed etsi inter nos simultates & differentiæ suscitarentur, forma data est, quibus cognitionibus illæ discutiantur, nec alter alterum coercitiua interdictione distringere cogatur, sed coram arbitris receptis iuxta formam compromissi omnia determinentur. Cardinalis verò quietem publicam ipsius principatus ac propriam ferre nó valens (quo spiritu ductus, nescimus) nulla causa vrgente, sed nec vlla suspicione præuia, contra nos cōsinxit, qualiter vitæ suæ insidiati simus, & in quandam fortiam Ecclesiæ Brixinensis secessit, suggerens se inibi metu potentiæ nostræ latitate, & ob id Ecclesiasticum interdictum fulminandum esse censuit. Deinde Papa Calixtus suis delationibus permotus, edicta poenalia contra nos emisit: à quibus cùm prouocaremus ad eundem syncerius informandum, & tota prouincia Comitatus nostri Tyrolis status vtriusque, scilicet Ecclesiastici & secularis, nobis adhæreret, & interim annus, qui appellationi prosequendæ à iure præfixus est, laberetur; Papa ipse ex hac vita migrauit. Succedente postea Papa Pio, ipse nobis alterum fatale concessit, appellationem nostram per hoc tacitè admittendo. Deinde Cardinalis ipse prioribus iniuriis in nos renouatis, notas accumulauit, deferens nos, qualiter castra nostra, quæ in feudum ab Ecclesia Brixinensi dependerent, recognoscere nollemus, & metallarias seu mineras & salinas ad se spectantes detineremus. Itaque nos Mantuam applicuimus, Apostolico conspectui nos præsentantes, vbi ipsi Cardinali obtulimus omnia illa feuda recognoscere
units.tr: Since the tribunal of the eternal Judge does not hold guilty the man whom a human judge wrongly condemns, because his judgement rests on infallible truth, while human judgement is sometimes disturbed by false reports, by error or human frailty, and sometimes by favour and partiality, therefore the remedies of appeal and of various recourse and refuge have been wisely devised by our ancestors as a support for the oppressed. Accordingly, we, SIGISMUND, by the grace of God Duke of Austria, Styria, Carinthia and Carniola, Count of Tyrol, etc., wishing our oppression to be made known to all the faithful of Christ, and especially to the secular princes who hold the advocacies and protections of churches and prelates, declare as follows. Our principality, the most ancient and most solid county of Tyrol, from the earliest years, even before it came under the lordship or dominion of our house and of the famous stock of Austria, held among its various advocacies, by hereditary and perpetual right, the advocacy of the Church of Brixen. By virtue of this, each Count of Tyrol for the time being had power over all the forts, castles, lands and men of that Church situated in the said county and its borders, so far as civil (otherwise, general) lordship is concerned, namely the protection and defence of all men belonging to the county, whether they are subject immediately to the Count and Prince himself, or to other ecclesiastical or secular persons belonging to the county, whether by tenancy, emphyteusis, or any other right. Likewise the Bishop of Brixen himself, now Cardinal of the title of St Peter in Chains, at the beginning of his entry into the Church of Brixen, with the intervention of Lord Frederick, Archbishop of Salzburg, his metropolitan, acknowledged to us the right of this advocacy, promising that he would conduct himself towards us in all things just as his predecessors had hitherto done towards us and our ancestors.
