Moreover, so that this advocacy might be more sincerely and firmly established with regard to us and our principality, it was agreed and settled between us that we must diligently preserve under the shield of our protection all the episcopal and chapter castles, lands and rights of that Church, except those which lie under another lord and not under our principality. But if disputes and differences should arise between us, a method was given by which they might be settled through hearings, and neither party should be compelled to restrain the other by an order of prohibition, but all matters should be determined before arbiters chosen according to the form of the compromise. But the Cardinal, unable to bear the public peace of his principality and his own (by what spirit he was moved we do not know), with no cause pressing and no prior suspicion, invented charges against us, to the effect that we had plotted against his life, and withdrew into a certain fort of the Church of Brixen, claiming that he was hiding there for fear of our power; and for this reason he judged that an ecclesiastical interdict ought to be thundered forth. Then Pope Callixtus, moved by his denunciations, issued penal edicts against us. Since we appealed from these, so that he might be more sincerely informed, and since the whole province of our county of Tyrol, both ecclesiastical and secular estates, adhered to us, and meanwhile the year which the law prescribes for prosecuting an appeal was running out, the Pope himself departed from this life. Afterwards, when Pope Pius succeeded, he granted us another fatal period, by tacitly admitting our appeal in this way. Then the same Cardinal, renewing his former injuries against us, piled up accusations, charging that we were unwilling to acknowledge our castles which depended in fief from the Church of Brixen, and that we held back the mines and salt-works belonging to him. Therefore we came to Mantua, presenting ourselves before the Apostolic presence, where we offered to the same Cardinal to acknowledge and receive all those fiefs, and to render the due fealty for them, just as our late father had done toward his predecessors, with the added clause: that if we held any further fiefs, these also should be regarded as received and acknowledged.

units.la: Ssssss gnoscere & suscipere, ac fidelitatis debitum inde praestare, prout quondam genitor noster fecit erga praedecessores suos, cum adjectione clausulae: Quod si qua plura feuda teneremus, illa ipsa etiam suscepta & recognita habeantur: Cumque feuda huiusmodi particulatim fuerint declarata, nos etiam illa singulatim & expresse in feudum accipere vellemus, & de aliis simulratibus, si quae forent, iuxta compromissi formam iamdudum inter nos conuenti, omni cunctatione semota, experiri. Porro si quid differentiarum subesset, quae per viam compromissi decidi non possent seu deberent, illae per compromissarios ad competentem iudicem remitterentur. Quae omnia Cardinalis ipse refutauit, contra foedus pactum & conuentum, ut praefertur. Insuper aliarum Prouinciarum Principes (alias aliarum personarum potentiam) in nostrum Principatum accersire temptauit, offerens illis spontaneam inuestituram feudorum nostrorum. Sed (Deo propitio) neminem inuenit, qui sibi tantae factionis adiutor esse vellet. Ex aduerso autem innocentiam nostram super criminationibus ipsius Cardinalis ostendimus, quia cōstabat, Cardinalem ipsum tempore confiditmetus sui in monasterio Wiften, iuxta locum nostrae Ducalis residentiae, & aliis patulis locis, officium Pontificale palam exercuisse; vbi nemo inuitis nobis, ne momento quidem securus persistere posset. Et alias tam clare deteximus, quod Cardinalis ipse suam contra nos infamationem tam petulantem subterfugere volens, dixit se nostram praesentiam non deuitasse. Nos autem illico literam manu sua scriptam produximus, in qua nos palam nuncupauit: nec tamen ideo correptus fuit, nec reprehensus. Suam vero in nos sentiens audaciam impunitam, maiora molimina continuo in nos & subditos nostros saeuiendo est ausus, & fortias Ecclesiae variis machinis bellicis instruxit, arcibus suis custodes praefecit exteros audaciae plerumque assuetos, victualia ingessit, quorum visus in pace minime consuetus, sed obsidionis tempore plurimum aptus, & vrgente fame gratissimus est obsessis, quamquam nulla tunc esset hostilis incursionis suspicio, sed omnia tranquilla, praeter illa, quae inter nos & ipsum tunc amicabiliter tractabantur. quibus adhuc vehementius inhaerentes, misimus fidelem nostrum Barzefalem de Annenberg Consiliarium nostrum, hortantes, ne vllam nouitatem attemptarent, sed viam amicabilis tractatus ampleCeretur: & omnia prius per nos oblata renouauimus. Omni tandem via concordiae deficiente, obtulit idem Consiliarius noster treugas biennales, ad vltimum saltem annales, vt interea differentiae illae aut amicabili concordia terminarentur, aut saltem per viam compromissi arbitrali iudicio subiicerentur. Quae omnia Cardinalis ipse refutauit, spem ponens (vt creditur) in certis armigeris, qui tunc Comitatum Goriciae nobis finitimū inuaserunt. Et cum ipse Cardinalis a suis admoneretur, ne vllum adparatum hostilem ostenderet, ne publicam pacem perturbaret, contra iura prouinciae Comitatus Tyrolis, alioquin sibi exitium immineret, siquidem hostis patriae diiudicaretur: Respodit, nihil tale vereri, oportere sibi esse armigeros & homines, qui nedum vnam, sed plures valles replere valerent. Cum ergo ipse Cardinalis patientia nostra tam insolenter abuteretur, totusque populus Comitatus nostri audaciam eius fastidiret, ac nonnulli populi iam parerent ausus ipsius vi propria comprimere: nos veriti, ne furor popularis in ipsum indiscretius irruens maioris mali periculum afferret, tandem via regia & subordinaria disciplina, cohortes & turmas instructas misimus, adhaec omnia copescenda. Quibus applicantibus, subito Cardinalis ipse de Capituli Brixinensis Ecclesiae gremio, & alios de latere suo ad nos misit, pacem postulans. Illico pacis tractatores deputauimus, & pax subito conclusa est. Videns quippe Cardinalis, neminem audaciae suae fauere, nec quemquam a fide nostra deficere, spe sua fructratus omnia in manibus nostris reposuit. Sed absit a nobis, vt propter audaciam Praelati bona Ecclesiae vsurpemus. Omnia etenim castra ad manus Capituli tradidimus, ea lege, vt talibus rectoribus tutanda committantur, qui Ecclesiae, nobis, & Principatui vniuerso grati ac fideles conspicerentur, vt ita pax, tranquillitas, & vnanimis concordia per vniuersum Principatum, omnesque populos eius, in vtroque statu Ecclesiastico & seculari conseruaretur, euitaretur seditio, & omnis tumultuationis suspicio caueretur. Pro damnis autem & interesse nostro, castrum nostrum Transfers, (alias Taufers) quod ipse a nobis pro certa florenorum summa tenuit pignoratum, cum tenuissimis pecuniarum summulis, retinemus in recompensam: quae tamen omnia vsque mediocritatem expensarum, damnorum & interesse huiusmodi non attingunt. Hanc compositionem nedum ipse Cardinalis emologauit, verum etiam postea extra territoria nostra, & in vrbibus amplissimis degens ratificauit.
units.tr: And since such fiefs were declared one by one, we also wished to receive those particular ones singly and expressly as fiefs, and to settle any other disputes, if there were any, according to the form of the compromise agreed between us long before, without any delay. Moreover, if any differences existed which could not or ought not to be settled by way of compromise, these were to be referred by the arbiters to the competent judge. The Cardinal himself rejected all these things, contrary to the covenant, pact and agreement, as has been stated. Besides, he tried to summon the princes of other provinces (or the power of other persons) into our principality, offering them the voluntary investiture of our fiefs. But (God being favourable) he found no one who was willing to be his helper in so great a faction. On the other hand, we showed our innocence with regard to the Cardinal's accusations, because it was well established that the Cardinal, at the time of his fear, openly exercised the pontifical office in the monastery of Wiften, near the seat of our ducal residence, and in other open places, where no one could remain even for a moment in safety without our consent. And we exposed him so clearly in other ways that the Cardinal himself, wishing to escape the charge of having slandered us so shamelessly, said that he had not avoided our presence. We at once produced a letter written in his own hand, in which he named us openly; yet he was not on that account rebuked or reprimanded. But perceiving that his boldness against us had gone unpunished, he continually went on to greater enterprises against us and our subjects, raging, and fortified the Church's forts with various war-engines, placed over his strongholds foreign guards who were mostly accustomed to recklessness, and laid in provisions, a kind of men who are hardly used to peace but are very suitable in time of siege, and most welcome to the besieged when hunger presses; although at that time there was no suspicion of a hostile incursion, but all was quiet, except for those matters which were then being amicably discussed between us and him. Still more earnestly clinging to these, we sent our faithful Barzefal of Annenberg, our councillor, urging them not to attempt any novelty, but to keep open the way of friendly negotiation, and we renewed all the offers we had made before. At last, when every way of agreement failed, our same councillor offered a two-year truce, or at the least a one-year truce, so that meanwhile those differences might be ended either by friendly agreement or at least be submitted to arbitral judgement by way of compromise. The Cardinal himself rejected all these things, placing his hope (as is believed) in certain armed men who at that time invaded the county of Gorizia, which borders on us. And when the Cardinal was warned by his own people not to show any hostile preparation, lest he disturb the public peace, contrary to the laws of the province of the county of Tyrol, and otherwise destruction would threaten him, since he would be judged an enemy of the country, he replied that he feared nothing of the kind, for he ought to have armed men and people who could fill not only one valley but several. Since the Cardinal therefore abused our patience so insolently, and the whole people of our county loathed his audacity, and some communities were already preparing to restrain his attacks by their own force, we, fearing that popular fury rushing upon him too indiscriminately might bring the danger of a greater evil, at last, by royal authority and by the ordinary discipline, sent drawn-up cohorts and troops to check all these things. When they arrived, the Cardinal himself suddenly sent out of the bosom of the Chapter of the Church of Brixen, and others from his side, to us, asking for peace. At once we appointed negotiators for peace, and peace was quickly concluded. For the Cardinal, seeing that no one favoured his audacity and that no one was falling away from our allegiance, having been frustrated in his hope, placed everything in our hands. But far be it from us to seize the goods of the Church on account of the Prelate's audacity. For we handed all the castles over to the hands of the Chapter, on the condition that they be entrusted for safekeeping to such governors as should be seen to be pleasing and faithful to the Church, to us, and to the whole principality, so that peace, tranquillity and united concord might be kept throughout the principality and all its people, in both the ecclesiastical and the secular estates, and sedition might be avoided and every suspicion of tumult guarded against. For the damages and expenses incurred by us, we keep our castle of Transfers (otherwise Taufers), which he had held from us in pledge for a certain sum of florins, as a recompense, together with some very small sums of money; yet all these things do not come up to a moderate amount of such expenses, damages and costs. This settlement the Cardinal not only approved, but afterwards, living outside our territories and in very great cities, also ratified.

units.la: Post haec omnia Dominus noster sanctissimus Papa monitorium poenale contra nos emisit, quo praecepit, haec omnia rescindi, & in eum statum reponi singula, quo fuisset in vigilia Paschae. Nos rati sanctitatem suam male informatam, ad ipsum melius informandum misimus, alioquin ad prouocandū potestatem dedimus egregio vtriusq; Iuris Doct. Laurentio de Blumenow, Consiliario nostro, quem sanctitas sua recusauit audire, ipsumq; iterum audientiā postulantem, tandē prouocare volente, minis affecit, carcere cōminando sibi pro apostolis: ipsumq; ad nos redire parantem arrestari fecit, haeresis suspicione ipsum innocentissime maculare volens, eo quod Sanctitatem suam de facti qualitate (in qua etiā Romanus Pontifex saepe fallitur) de mādato nostro voluit informare. Demum ad nos proficiscente persequi fecit, hodieq; nobis incertū est, an persequentium manus aufugerit, an vero insidiatoris dicti laqueos inciderit. Hoc vero certum est, q; securitas experiendi (al. comparendi) in iure nobis & nostris in Curia Papali penitus adempta est. Cum itaque Sanctitas sua omnem spem consequendi iustitiam sustulerit a nobis, ideoque ad ipsum melius informandum prouocare non possumus, quia aures eius in nos obsurduerunt, & indignatio pro libitu succensa est, ideoque ad futurum Romanum Pontificem appellamus, qui de gestis antecessoris sui de iure habet cognoscere. Item ad generale Concilium instituendum, vel institutum, prout ex forma sanctorum & Catholicorum decretorum sacri Constantiensis Concilii, innouatorum per sanctissimum Basiliense Concilium, de tempore intempestiue praefinitum iure celebrari debet. Et ne quisquam putet, nos hanc nostram appellationem subterfugiendi iuris causa interposuisse, offerimus & protestamur, quod vias naturalis iuris nullo pacto volumus declinare. Et inprimis, si sanctissimus Dominus noster causam nostram, in qua se suspectum reddidit notorie, alteri non suspecto velit delegare, nos illius delegati constituendi iudicium subire non detrectabimus, uti vetustissima iuris ciuilis tradidit doctrina. Et hoc modo sedis Apostolicae illibata manebit auctoritas. Quia illius auctoritate manente, sola personae suspicionis causa terminabitur. Item si Sanctitas sua se putaret non esse suspectam, nos sub ... [illegible, ~3 letters] ... rentia compromittere parati sumus, ut iuris Canonici tradito docet. Sed & cum ... Cardinali simili via experiri offerimus, ne quis putet, nos transl[?]atiuam submittere constitutionem. Insuper ad ipsum eundem Romanum Pontificem, si adiungere sibi velit personas nobis non suspectas, quorum consilio causam agat, protestamur: ipsius iudicium, si in vniuersali Concilio praesederit, non declinabimus. Postremo quascunque vias, quibus nobis & nostris securitas causae prosequendae dabitur, & suspicionis metus auferetur, in huiusmodi causae prosecutione amplectemur. Quae omnia si nobis denegabuntur, tandem ad vniuersum Saluatoris & Domini nostri IESV CHRISTI populum & quicunque nostrae oppressioni misereri velint, aut iustitiam inferioris etiam contra superiores in ipsum incandescentes ament, omnesque iustitiae & innocentiae fautores appellamus & prouocamus, ac ad ipsos concurrimus, apostolosque primo, secundo & tertio instanter, instantius & instantissime petimus, si quis sit, qui dare velit aut possit: & a te Notario publico saltem testimoniales, pro nobis & subditis nostris, Ecclesiasticis & secularibus, ac adhaerentibus & fautoribus nostris: subiicientes nos & illos iurisdictioni & cognitioni illorum, quos supra nominauimus: & promittentes nos iuri modo praemisso, parere. Quae si nobis denegata fuerint, Deum aeternum iudicem, & omnes iustitiae ac innocentiae fautores contestamur, per nos non stare, quominus iustitia reddatur: nos vero oppressos esse. De quibus prosequendis protestamur, ac de appellatione nostra iuxta formam iuris propter metum coram vicinis insinuanda, & metu cessante, etiam coram Romano Pontifice, & vbi opus erit, & iuris ordo deposcit, vel persuadet aequitas rationis: saluo iure addendi, minuendi, mutandi, corrigendi, & aliam vel alias appellationem siue appellationes interponendi, & quolibet iuris beneficio: & protestamur, prout fuit & est moris atque styli.
units.tr: After all this, our most holy Lord the Pope issued against us a monitory with penalties, by which he ordered that all these things be rescinded and that each thing be restored to the state it was in on the eve of Easter. Believing that His Holiness had been ill informed, we sent Laurentius de Blumenow, Doctor of both laws and our counsellor, to inform him better; we also gave him authority to appeal. His Holiness refused to hear him. When he asked again for a hearing and was ready at last to appeal, His Holiness threatened him with threats and with prison as an apostate. When Blumenow was getting ready to return to us, His Holiness had him arrested, wishing to stain him most unjustly with the suspicion of heresy, because he had wanted to inform His Holiness, on our instruction, of the true nature of the facts (in which even the Roman Pontiff is often deceived). Finally, he had him pursued as he set out for us. Today we do not know whether he has escaped the hands of his pursuers or has fallen into the snares of that ambusher. What is certain is that the security of trying the case (alternatively, of appearing) in law has been utterly taken from us and ours at the Papal Curia. Since His Holiness has therefore removed from us every hope of obtaining justice, we cannot appeal to him to inform him better, because his ears have grown deaf to us and his indignation has flared up at will. We therefore appeal to the future Roman Pontiff, who ought to examine the acts of his predecessor under law. We also appeal to a general Council to be convened, or already convened, in the form of the holy and Catholic decrees of the sacred Council of Constance, renewed by the most holy Council of Basel, which must be lawfully celebrated at a time not untimely fixed in advance. And lest anyone think we have made this appeal in order to escape the law, we offer and protest that we do not in any way wish to decline the ways of natural law. And first, if our most holy Lord wishes to delegate our case, in which he has notoriously made himself suspect, to another who is not suspect, we will not refuse to submit to the judgment of a delegate so appointed, as the most ancient doctrine of civil law teaches. In this way the authority of the Apostolic See will remain unimpaired, since, while that authority remains, only the cause of the person's suspicion will be decided. Likewise, if His Holiness should think himself not suspect, we are ready to submit the matter to arbitration, as the doctrine of the Canon law teaches. But we also offer to try the case by a similar route with the Cardinal, lest anyone think we are submitting a transfer of the case. Moreover, we protest to that same Roman Pontiff that, if he wishes to join to himself persons not suspect to us, by whose counsel he may conduct the case, we will not decline his judgment, should he preside in a universal Council. Lastly, whatever ways may be given to us and ours for securing the prosecution of our cause, and by which the fear of suspicion may be removed, we will embrace them in the prosecution of this kind of cause. If all these things are denied us, then at last we appeal and summon the whole people of our Saviour and Lord Jesus Christ, and all who are willing to have pity on our oppression, or who love justice even from an inferior against superiors who burn against him, and all the supporters of justice and innocence; and we turn to them and join ourselves to them, and we ask the Apostles, first, second and third time, instantly, more instantly and most instantly, whoever there may be who is willing or able to give (help); and we ask you, public notary, at least for testimonial letters, for us and for our subjects, ecclesiastical and secular, and for our adherents and supporters, submitting ourselves and them to the jurisdiction and cognizance of those whom we have named above, and promising that we will obey the law in the manner set out above. If these things are denied us, we call to witness the eternal God as judge, and all the supporters of justice and innocence, that it is not through us that justice is not rendered, and that we are the oppressed. Concerning the prosecution of these matters we protest, and we protest that our appeal, according to the form of law, is to be made known before neighbours because of fear, and, once the fear has ceased, also before the Roman Pontiff, and wherever it is necessary, and as the order of law demands or fairness of reason persuades; saving the right to add, diminish, change, correct, and to lodge another appeal or other appeals, and to any benefit of law; and we protest as it was and is the custom and practice.

units.la: Qua quidem schedula per me expresse lecta praefato Illustrissimo Principi sic appellanti & prouocanti, ac apostolos petenti, in quantum de iure potui & debui, has literas testimoniales dedi & concessi. Acta sunt haec anno &c. praesentibus ibidem egregiis & honorabilibus viris, Dominis Georgio Heimberg vtriusque iuris Doctore &c.
units.tr: This schedule having been read by me in full, I gave and granted these testimonial letters to the aforesaid Most Illustrious Prince, who so appeals and summons, and asks for the Apostles, insofar as I was able and ought to do so by law. These things were done in the year etc., the following distinguished and honourable men being present there: Lords Georgius Heimberg, Doctor of both laws, etc.

units.la: Martinus Marquardi Notarius &c.
units.tr: Martinus Marquardi, Notary, etc.

units.la: MANDAT PAPA DENVNTIARI DVCEM SIGIS- mundum, & certos suos adhaerentes, per Breue Apostolicum.
units.tr: THE POPE ORDERS SIGISMUND, DUKE OF AUSTRIA, AND CERTAIN OF HIS ADHERENTS TO BE PROCLAIMED, BY AN APOSTOLIC BRIEF.

units.la: PIVS PAPA Dilecto filio N. Plebano Ecclesiae S. Stephani Constantiensis. Dilecte fili, salutem & Apostolicam benedictionem. Praesentium tibi tenore sub excommunicationis & depositionis ab ordine & officio latae sententiae poenis, districte praecipimus & mandamus, quatinus his literis acceptis, & continue in posterum, donec aliud tibi mandauerimus in contrarium, Sigismundum ex Austriae Principibus cum satellitibus suis, omnibus diebus festis, congregato populo ita denunties, vt in forma introclusa, quam tibi specialiter ad hoc mittimus, cernis contineri. Datum Romae apud sanctum Petrum, sub annulo Piscatoris, die 22. Ianuarii M.CCCCLXI. Pontificatus nostri anno tertio.
units.tr: PIUS POPE, to his beloved son N., parish priest of the Church of St Stephen in Konstanz. Beloved son, greetings and apostolic blessing. By the tenor of these presents, under the penalties of excommunication and of deposition from order and office, incurred by the sentence itself, we strictly command and order you that, on receiving this letter, and continually from now on until we order otherwise, you proclaim to the assembled people on every feast day Sigismund of the princes of Austria, together with his henchmen, in the form enclosed, which we send you specially for this purpose, as you see it set out. Given at Rome at St Peter's, under the Fisherman's ring, on 22 January 1461, in the third year of our pontificate.

units.la: Copia formae introclusae praetactae.
units.tr: Copy of the enclosed form mentioned above.

units.la: DE speciali districto & expresso mandato sanctissimi Domini nostri Papae, Sigismundum ex Austriae Principibus, ob hostilem insecutionem & sacrilegium in personam Reuerendissimi in Christo Patris & Domini, Domini Nicolai tituli S. Petri ad Vincula sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae Presbyteri Cardinalis, Episcopi Brixinensis, in Paschalibus festiuitatibus perpetratum, vobis omnibus, cum adhaerentibus & fautoribus suis, denuntio excommunicatum maiori excommunicatione, ac poenis criminis laesae maiestatis & perpetuae infamiae innodatum bannitum, diffidatum, & bonis & honore priuatum. Et cum hoc etiam itern[?] ... damnatam suam appellationem ad futurum Concilium, denuntio ipsum [illegible, ~12 letters] hematisa-tum, crimine laesae maiestatis & fautoriae haereseos irretitum: esseque etiam in [illegible, ~10 letters] dominiis, quae occupat, & ad quae ipse aut aliquis de suis adhaerentibus accedit, po[illegible, ~6 letters] Apostolica auctoritate strictissimum ecclesiasticum interdictum. Mandoque vobis, vt ipsum cum adhaerentibus, satellitibus & fautoribus suis, vt praeferatur, vitetis, & pro talibus habeatis. Simili modo denuntio excommunicatos & eisdem suprascriptis poenis irretitos, omnes & singulos, quos sanctissimus Dominus noster in suis Bullis tales esse exprimit: ex quibus sunt nominatim isti, qui sequuntur, scilicet Wolfgangus Neydlinger, Stephanus Steynhorn, asserti Canonici Brixinenses: Gregorius de Heymburg & Laurentius Blomenow, erronei Doctores: Parcifal Annenberger, Iacobus Traff, Turingus de Halwil, Baltasar de Weltzsperg, Christophorus Voxs, & Caspar Loubenberg, asserti milites: Happo [illegible, ~6 letters] Leonardus Weynecker, Oswaldus, Eghardus, Berchtoldus conditi Wolckensteyner [illegible, ~8 letters] trautson, Iacobus Tonner, Iohannes Kripp, Rolandus Glandensperger, Waltherus de [illegible, ~6 letters] ein, Leopoldus Spiess, Ioannes de Friberg de Astetten, Ioannes de Friberg de Pfaffenhusen, Georgius Burggraue, Georgius de Annenberg, Dionysius Heidelberger, Georgius Diepoltzkirchen, Caspar Spiess, Caspar Raminger, Paulus Rentel, Contadus Clammer, Wilhelmus Baldlouff, Vlricus Hont, Barbara de Sonnenberg, Georgius Ragant, Ioannes Rummer, Iacobus Frueger, Guntherus de Inspruck, Augustinus Teutsch cum illorum sociis & adhaerentibus, in Apostolicis literis [illegible, ~6 letters] genere aut quocunque modo nominatis & comprehensis.
units.tr: By the special, strict and express command of our most holy Lord the Pope, I proclaim to all of you, together with his adherents and supporters, Sigismund of the princes of Austria: excommunicated with the greater excommunication, bound by the penalties of the crime of high treason and of perpetual infamy, banned, outlawed, and deprived of goods and honour. This is on account of the hostile pursuit and sacrilege committed against the person of the Most Reverend Father in Christ and Lord, Lord Nicholas, Cardinal Priest of the holy Roman Church of St Peter ad Vincula, Bishop of Brixen, committed during the Easter festivities. And with this, having condemned his appeal to the future Council, I proclaim him [illegible] anathematized, entangled in the crime of high treason and in favouring heresy. Also, in the lands which he occupies, and to which he or any of his adherents goes, the strictest ecclesiastical interdict is in force by apostolic authority. I command you to avoid him, with his adherents, henchmen and supporters, as stated above, and to regard them as such. In the same way I proclaim excommunicate, and bound by the same penalties, all and each of those whom our most holy Lord in his Bulls declares to be such. Of these, the following are named: Wolfgang Neydlinger and Stephen Steynhorn, alleged canons of Brixen; Gregory de Heymburg and Lawrence Blomenow, erroneous teachers; Parcifal Annenberger, Jacob Traff, Turing de Halwil, Balthasar de Weltzsperg, Christopher Voxs, and Caspar Loubenberg, alleged knights; Happo [illegible], Leonard Weynecker, Oswald, Eghard, Berchtold, called Wolckensteyner [illegible], Trautson, Jacob Tonner, John Kripp, Roland Glandensperger, Walther de [illegible] ein, Leopold Spiess, John de Friberg de Astetten, John de Friberg de Pfaffenhusen, George Burggraue, George de Annenberg, Dionysius Heidelberger, George Diepoltzkirchen, Caspar Spiess, Caspar Raminger, Paul Rentel, Conrad Clammer, William Baldlouff, Ulrich Hont, Barbara de Sonnenberg, George Ragant, John Rummer, Jacob Frueger, Gunther de Inspruck, and Augustine Teutsch, together with their companions and adherents, and all others named or included in the apostolic letters under whatever genus or manner.

units.la: Intimo etiam, quod quicunque vadit per patriam illam Athesim seu vallis Eni, aut emit sal, argentum, vinum, aut alia de illis partibus, siue vendit illis quicquam, cadit in excommunicationem & perditionem bonorum secundum continentiam Apostolicarum Bullarum super hoc editarum.
units.tr: I further announce that whoever goes through that country called Athesis (the Etsch) or the valley of Eni, or buys salt, silver, wine or other goods from those parts, or sells anything to them, incurs excommunication and the loss of goods, according to the content of the apostolic Bulls issued on this matter.

units.la: Simile Breue diuersis Plebanis per dioecesim Constantiensem directum est.
units.tr: A similar Brief has been sent to various parish priests throughout the diocese of Konstanz.

units.la: QVOD EPISCOPVS BASILIENSIS, CON- tempta Papali Bulla, & interdicto excommunicatorio non curato, semper Sigismundum Ducem fouerit, ex sequenti patet epistola.
units.tr: That the Bishop of Basel, having scorned the papal bull and disregarded the excommunicatory interdict, always favoured Duke Sigismund, is clear from the following letter.

units.la: PIVS PAPA II.
units.tr: Pope Pius II.

units.la: Venerabili Fratri N. Episcopo Basiliensi.
units.tr: To our venerable brother N., Bishop of Basel.

units.la: VEnerabilis Frater, salutem & apostolicam benedictionem. Intelleximus displicenter, quomodo non obstante, quod Sigismundus ex Austriae Principibus propter infandum & notorium sacrilegium in personam dilecti Fratris nostri Nicolai tituli S. Petri ad vincula S. Rom. Ecclesiae Presbyteri Cardinalis, Episcopi Brixinensis, commissum in excommunicationis & alias iuris horribiles ac satis declaratas poenas, cum complicibus & satellitibus suis inciderit, per nosque talis (vt nolle debuisti) declaratus existat, positio, vt oportuit, Ecclesiastico interdicto omni in loco, ad quem accesserint: Tua tamen fraternitas eundem Sigismundum & suos (vt praefertur) sicut tenetur, non deuitet, nec etiam (proh dolor) interdictum seruet, ipsosque innodatos tremendis censuris non solum non denuntiet, quinimo se ad tractandum inter ipsum & dilectos filios confoederatos intromittat: non aduertens, quod per hoc maxime DEVM offendis, censuraque & huius Apostolicae Sedis auctoritatem contemnis, libertatem Ecclesiasticam paruipendis, & contra praestitum per te consecrationis tempore iuramentum venis, proprio honori non parcis, clerusque tuus profanans irregularis existens, diuinis contra Ecclesiae ordinationem se temere immiscet. Quam grauia quidem ista sint, non ignoras.
units.tr: Venerable Brother, greetings and apostolic blessing. We have learned with displeasure that, although Sigismund of the Austrian princes has incurred the excommunication and the other dreadful and well-declared penalties of law, together with his accomplices and henchmen, for his unspeakable and notorious sacrilege against the person of our beloved brother Nicholas, Cardinal Priest of the holy Roman Church under the title of St Peter in Chains and Bishop of Brixen, and has been declared such by us (as you ought not to have wished), an ecclesiastical interdict has been placed, as it should be, on every place to which they have come. Yet your fraternity, as it is bound to do, does not avoid this Sigismund and his people, as stated above, nor (alas) does it observe the interdict. Not only do you not denounce them, now bound by the dreadful censures, but you even intrude yourself into negotiating between him and our beloved sons in the confederation. You do not realise that by this you chiefly offend God, despise the censure and the authority of this Apostolic See, make light of ecclesiastical liberty, and act against the oath you swore at your consecration. You spare not your own honour, and your clergy, being irregular and profaning themselves, rashly mix in divine offices contrary to the Church's ordinance. You are not unaware how grave these things are.

units.la: Mandamus igitur per praesentes Tuae fraternitati, & districte per praestitum iuramentum requirimus, quatenus ab omni dicti Sigismundi & suorum conuersatione, atque tractatu inter ipsum & dictos confoederatos, prorsus abstineas. Interdictum autem iuxta nostrarum superinde literarum continentiam inuiolabiliter teneas, & teneri facias. Secus faciendo contra Tuam fraternitatem, tanquam fautricem dictorum sacrilegorum, & Apostolicae Sedis ac nostri, imo DEI contemptricem, nos iuste sentias prouocatos. Datum Romae apud S. Petrum sub annulo Piscatoris, die x. Ian. M.CCCCLXI. Pontificatus nostri anno III.
units.tr: We therefore command your fraternity by these presents, and strictly require you by the oath you have taken, that you hold yourself wholly aloof from all dealings with the said Sigismund and his people, and from any negotiation between him and the said confederates. You are to observe the interdict inviolably, according to the terms of our letters on this matter, and to see that it is observed. If you act otherwise, you may know that we shall justly regard you as provoked, as a supporter of the said sacrilegious men and a contemner of the Apostolic See, of us, and indeed of God. Given at Rome, at St Peter's, under the Fisherman's ring, on the 10th day of January 1461, in the third year of our pontificate.

units.la: Iacob. Papiensis.
units.tr: Jacob of Pavia.

units.la: GREGORII DE HEIMBVRG IVRISCONSVLTI, CONSILIARII Austriaci, TRACTATVS SVPER EXCOMMVNICATIONE PII PAPÆ II. IN DV- CEM Austriæ Sigismundum, & seipsum evulgata.
units.tr: Treatise of Gregor of Heimburg, Jurisconsult and Counsellor of Austria, on the Excommunication of Pope Pius II against Duke Sigismund of Austria and against Himself, Made Public

units.la: BREVE DOMINI PII PAPÆ SECVNDI ADVERSVS GRE- GORIVM Heimburg Vtriusque Iuris Doctorem.
units.tr: Brief of Lord Pope Pius II against Gregor Heimburg, Doctor of Both Laws

units.la: PIus Papa II. dilectis filiis, Burgimagistris & Consulatui oppidi Nurembergensis, salutem & Apostolicam benedictionem. Saluator humani generis in hunc veniens mundum, vt ex mortalibus genitos Dei filios, & sibi ipsi in summi Patris sui regno cohæredes efficeret, vnum ex omnibus fidelibus in eum credentibus regnum constituit, idque vnam ipsius Ecclesiam nuncupauit, cuius ipse caput esset, & regnator sempiternus. Visibilem vero humanis oculis præsentiam sui per admirabilem ad patrem omnipotentem ascensum mundo subtracturus, Petrum Apostolorum Principem, eiusque legitimos pro tempore successores, vicarios sibi cum plenitudine potestatis ad propriam gubernationem Ecclesiæ substituit, tribuens omnimodam per temporalem successionem vicariis ipsis in terris & in cœlis omnia ligandi soluendique potestatem, recipiensque; distincte ipsos audiri, & in eorum iussionibus permanari [al. permanere]. Quod si qui transgressores veneno imbuti eos non audirent, huiusmodi omnes exclusis à suo regno, electisque, à sancta Ecclesia inter Ethnicos & publicanos, cum perditionis & mortis filiis voluit computari. Cum enim nullum regnum (vt ipsius Domini nostri verbis didicimus) in se diuisum stare possit; quonam modo sacrosanctum stabit Ecclesiæ regnum, si illi, qui Christi supremi Regis vicario parere contemnunt, de regni non valeant sorte depelli? Aduersus hoc inquassabile fundamentum, & Ecclesiæ firmam petram, hæresis quædam à paruo tempore citra sensum visa suboriri pullulauit: quæ sub ouium vestibus lupos rapaces intrinsecus cælans, sub appellationis specie, Ecclesiæ satagit vnitatem conuellere. Nam si qua Christi vnicus vicarius canonibus sacris etiam & iuri scripto inhærendo decreuit, statuitque; & seruari (vt dignum est) præcepit, calumniatores maliuoli & peruersi, subterfugere iustitiam præsumentes, per ludibria friuolarum appellationum ad futurum Concilium (ceu ad id, quod nusquam est, ac super Christi vicarium esse aut reperiri nequit) obedientiam, quæ est de necessitate Ecclesiæ & salutis vniuersorum, improbè declinant, ac temere: Hac igitur de Diabolico spiritu & instinctu nouitatem exortam considerantes, in totius Ecclesiæ Catholicæ non tantum enerationem, sed euersionem in Mantuano conuentu sæpe multúque discussam, de venerabilium fratrum nostrorum tanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ Cardinalium, pluriumque aliorum psulum & peritorum, qui aderant, maturo consilio & consensu, illiusmodi appellationes damnauimus atque; ita appellantes, notariosque; ac testes & adhærentes eos excommunicauimus, læsæque Maiestatis & hæresis crimina & pœnas eo ipso illos diffinitiuimus indiciisse, put in Apostolicis litteris superinde cöfectis plenius cötinetur. Ceterum his omnibus nō obstantibus, quidā ex patre diabolo mendaciorum artifice natus, Gregorius de Heimburg nomine, auaritiae contaminatus illuuie, & superatus ardoribus, qui est seruitus Idolorum, de mense Augusti proxime præterito, à nostra solemni declaratoria sententia, qua Senis existentes, impiū Sigismundū ex Principibus Austriæ, ob notorium sacrilegium, propter hostile persecutionem in personam delicti filii nostri Nicolai tit. S. Petri ad vincula, S. Romanæ Ecclesiæ Presbyteri Cardinalis, & Episcopi Brixinensis, & rapinā bonorum Ecclesiæ illius perpetratum, iuris scripti pœnas declarauimus incurrisse; à nobis ad futurū Cócilium improbam, nefariam temerariam, seditiosam deniq; appellationem dictauit: & illius interpositionis p dictū Sigismūdū factæ, ipse dictator in originali instrumento Florentiæ ad valuas Ecclesiæ affixo, testis inscribit: Quod qa loquax ille, præsumptuosus & pceps, medix atq; turbulentus, temerarius, ob istud facinus excommunicatus existit, criminaq; & pœnas incidit læsæ Maiestatis atq; hæresis, adeo vt vltra execrationem honore omni & bonis iure sit priuatus: Deuotionem vestras in Domino requretes admonemus, vt huiusmodi pestiferū hominē, p tali excommunicato habeatis & priuato, à vestrisq; ciuib. omnib. haberi mädetis: ipsumq; nō solū vitetis, sed eiiciatis ab oppido & dominio vestro: & bona quæcunq; habet apud vos, tā mobilia qʒ et immobilia, fisco vestro applicetis, & alia omnia faciatis, q cōtra hereticos de iure Canonico fieri mādant. In quo vos vobis ostenderis, exhibebitisq; Catholicos (sicut plene cōfidimus) & Deo gratos ciues, in tale pniciosum Ecclesiæ Christi psecutore vos fideles. & S.R.Eccl. obedientes ostendendo. Nobisq; in hoc co magis deuotiones vestræ cöplacebūt, quāto scimus plurimū esse Deo charū, & Ecclesiæ suę putile, ac impias necessariū, ꝑ pfanusiste pestiferq; sacrorū conteptor ab omni expellat cōuersatione & cōsortio Christianorū. Facite nobis qd egeritis, p literas vestras describatur. Datū Romæ apud S. Petrū, sub annulo Piscatoris die XVIII. Octobr, M.CCCC.LX Pontificatus nostri anno tertio.
units.tr: Pius II, Pope, to his beloved sons, the Burgomasters and Council of the town of Nuremberg, greeting and Apostolic blessing. The Saviour of the human race, coming into this world so that he might make the sons of God, born of mortals, and co-heirs with himself in the kingdom of his supreme Father, established one kingdom out of all the faithful who believe in him, and called it his one Church, of which he himself is head and everlasting ruler. Intending to withdraw his visible presence from human eyes by his wonderful ascent to the Father Almighty, he appointed Peter, Prince of the Apostles, and his lawful successors in time, as his vicars, with fullness of power for the proper governance of the Church. He granted to these vicars, through temporal succession, the full power of binding and loosing in heaven and on earth, and he willed that they be heard distinctly and that people remain in their commands. But if transgressors, infected with poison, did not hear them, he wished all such persons, cut off and cast out from his kingdom, to be counted by holy Church among the pagans and tax collectors, among the sons of perdition and death. For since no kingdom (as we have learned from the words of our Lord himself) can stand divided against itself, how will the sacred kingdom of the Church stand, if those who scorn to obey the vicar of Christ the supreme King cannot be thrown from the lot of the kingdom? Against this unshakeable foundation and the firm rock of the Church, a certain heresy, unseen for a short time past, has sprung up and sprouted. Hiding rapacious wolves inside under sheep's clothing, it strives under the name of appeal to tear apart the unity of the Church. For if the one vicar of Christ has decreed, established and commanded, adhering to the sacred canons and also to written law, that these be observed as is fitting, malicious and perverse slanderers, presuming to escape justice, through the mockery of frivolous appeals to a future Council (as if to something that nowhere exists and cannot be found above the vicar of Christ), shamelessly and rashly decline obedience, which is necessary for the Church and for the salvation of all. Therefore, considering this novelty to have arisen from the diabolical spirit and instigation, and aiming at the overthrow, not merely the diminishing, of the whole Catholic Church, we condemned such appeals after frequent and lengthy discussion at the assembly of Mantua, with the mature counsel and consent of our venerable brothers, the Cardinals of the holy Roman Church, and of many other learned and experienced men who were present. We excommunicated the appellants, and likewise the notaries, witnesses and adherents, and declared that by that very fact they had incurred the crimes and penalties of treason and heresy, as is more fully contained in the Apostolic letters drawn up on this matter. Nevertheless, notwithstanding all these things, a certain man, born of the father the devil, the artificer of lies, named Gregor of Heimburg, stained with the filth of avarice and overcome by burning desire, which is the slavery of idols, in the month of August last past, after our solemn declaratory sentence, by which, while staying at Siena, we declared that the impious Sigismund, of the princes of Austria, had incurred the penalties of written law on account of notorious sacrilege, namely the hostile persecution of the person of our beloved son Nicholas, cardinal priest of the holy Roman Church, of the title of St Peter in Chains, and Bishop of Brixen, and the plundering of that Church's goods, dictated to us an appeal to the future Council, shameless, impious, rash and finally seditious. And of this appeal, made by the said Sigismund, the same dictator writes himself in as witness on the original instrument affixed at the doors of the church at Florence. Because that talkative, presumptuous, headlong, meddling and turbulent rash man has been excommunicated for that deed, and has fallen into the crimes and penalties of treason and heresy, so that, beyond execration, he is stripped of all honour and of every right, we, seeking your devotion in the Lord, admonish you to hold this pestilent man as excommunicated and deprived, and to cause all your citizens to hold him so. Not only are you to avoid him, but you are to cast him out of your town and dominion, to apply to your treasury whatever goods he has with you, movable and immovable, and to do all the other things which canon law commands to be done against heretics. In doing this you will show yourselves, and will prove yourselves, to be Catholic (as we fully trust) and citizens pleasing to God, showing yourselves faithful in opposing such a pernicious persecutor of the Church of Christ, and obedient to the Holy Roman Church. Your devotion will be all the more pleasing to us in this, since we know that it is very dear to God, useful to his Church, and necessary for the impious, that so profane and pestilent a despiser of sacred things be expelled from all Christian company and fellowship. Make known to us what you do, by your letter. Given at Rome, at St Peter's, under the Fisherman's Ring, on the 18th day of October 1460, in the third year of our pontificate.

units.la: Scholia Gregorii Heimburg in bre- ue Papale.
units.tr: Scholia of Gregory Heimburg on the Papal Brief.

units.la: Petrum Apostolorum Principem, eiusque legitimos successores] Non sacrilegos, auaros & amatores bastardorum.
units.tr: Peter, Prince of the Apostles, and his lawful successors] Not sacrilegious, greedy, and lovers of bastards.

units.la: Vicariis ipsius in terris ac in coelo omnia ligandi] Claue non errante. Non enim pro libito, sed pro ratione.
units.tr: To his vicars on earth and in heaven, with the power of binding all things] A key that does not err. For it binds not at pleasure but according to reason.

units.la: Eos non audirent] iusta iubentes.
units.tr: They would not hear them] Commanding what is just.

units.la: Vicario parere contemnunt] Dicit Gregorius: Nolite obedire Prælatis, vt eorum scelera approbetis.
units.tr: They despise obedience to the vicar] Gregory says: Do not obey prelates, lest you approve their crimes.

units.la: Christi vnicus Vicarius, canonibus sacris] Non dicunt sacri Canones, quod Episcopus debeat sibi vsurpare potestatem gladii contra Principem suum vniuersalem, ratione sui dominii particularis.
units.tr: Christ's sole Vicar, by the sacred canons] The sacred canons do not say that a bishop ought to usurp for himself the power of the sword against his universal Prince, on the ground of his particular lordship.

units.la: Supra Christi Vicarium esse aut reperiri nequit] Haec est haeresis in sacro Concilio Constantiensi & Basiliensi reprobata, tunc quando erat indubitatum.
units.tr: Cannot be above Christ's Vicar, nor found to be] This is the heresy condemned at the sacred Council of Constance and Basel, at a time when it was still undisputed.

units.la: Illiusmodi appellationes damnauimus] Tanto fuisti stultior, quia admonuisti nos quid timeres, & voluisti viam praecludere ad refugium, ratione oppressorum, quibus pro libito illusisti.
units.tr: We have condemned appeals of this kind] You have been all the more foolish, for you warned us what you feared, and wanted to block the way of refuge for the oppressed, whom you mocked at will.

units.la: Plenius continetur] Immo sacrilegius.
units.tr: More fully contained] Nay, sacrilegious.

units.la: Natus Gregorius de Heimburg] Probè & legitimè natus, qui non fouet adulterina coniugia, sicut Papa facit, qui fouet Fernandum bastardum contra heredem legitimum.
units.tr: Gregory of Heimburg, born] Honestly and lawfully born, he who does not foster adulterous marriages, as the Pope does, who fosters the bastard Ferdinand against the lawful heir.

units.la: Auaritia contaminatus illuvie] Parum recepi pro patrocinio iustitiae; sed Papa plurimum recepit pro fomento bastardiae, & nodum contentus quaerit talliam sub colore Turchino.
units.tr: Stained with the filth of avarice] I have received little for the patronage of justice; but the Pope has received much for fostering bastardy, and, not content with that, seeks a tax under the pretext of the Turkish war.

units.la: Impium Sigismundum] Magnificum, qui ausus fuit coripere factiones improbas Cardinalis.
units.tr: The impious Sigismund] Magnificent man, who dared to rebuke the wicked factions of the Cardinal.

units.la: Ob notorium sacrilegium] Ob magnificum & animosum factum.
units.tr: On account of notorious sacrilege] On account of a magnificent and spirited deed.

units.la: Iuris scriptiponas declarauimus incurrisse] Non auditum contra ius naturae, & obsurduerunt aures Papae tamquam aspidis, ita fuit incantatus amore Caesaris, cui vilissimè seruit.
units.tr: We have declared that he has incurred the penalties of the law] Not heard against natural law; and the Pope's ears were deaf like an asp's, so enchanted was he by love of the Emperor, whom he served most basely.

units.la: Sedicioso denique appellationem] O quantum times, miserrime Papa, qui non audes in publicum prodire, ne cognoscatur temeritas tua.
units.tr: Finally, an appeal of a seditious kind] O how much you fear, most wretched Pope, who dare not come out in public, lest your recklessness be recognized.

units.la: Et quia loquax ille] Quis te loquacior, qui tribus horis loquacitatem tuam protelasti pro bastardo Aragoniae arrogantissimè.
units.tr: And because that talkative man] Who is more talkative than you, who for the bastard of Aragon have arrogantly prolonged your chatter for three hours.

units.la: Laesae Maiestatis] Laesae maiestatis Papalis.
units.tr: Of injured majesty] Of injured Papal majesty.

units.la: Fisco vestro applicatis] Ita si vultis perdere mercantias vestras.
units.tr: Applied to your treasury] Yes, if you wish to lose your merchandise.

units.la: Quanto sanctius plurimum esse Deo carum] Iam fingit se in consilio Dei veri fuisse, ac si conscripsisset decreta Dei, & se reponit in numero ** sacrilegus ille, fingens se * socium, qui praeter * sacra & aniles fabulas nil habet doctrinarum.
units.tr: As much more holy, very dear to God] Now he pretends to have been in the counsel of the true God, as if he had written down God's decrees, and he places himself among the number of ** that sacrilegious man, pretending to be a * companion, who has nothing of teaching beyond * sacred and old wives' tales.

units.la: APPELLATIO GREGORII HEIMBVRG VTRIVSQVE IVRIS DOC- TORIS, à Domini Pii Papae Secundi Breui con- tra eum emisso
units.tr: APPELLATIO GREGORII HEIMBVRG, UTRIUSQUE IURIS DOCTORIS, à Domini Pii Papae Secundi Breui contra eum emisso

units.la: IS consilii expers mole ruit sua: vim temporatam in sublime prouehit Deus. Papa Pius iam pridem per breue non testatum, sed annulo Piscatoris obsignatum, fertur excommunicasse Gregorium Heimburg, nunquam euocatum, contra legem Dei, qui damnaturus protoplastum praevaricatorem, praemisit vocationem dicens: Adam ubi es? Similiter & Cain, fraterno adhuc sanguine madentem interrogans: Ubi est Abel frater tuus? Sodomorum quoque flagitia, antequam sulphuris exureret igne: Descendam, inquit, & videbo, an clamorem, qui ad me pervenit, opere compleuerint. Papa vero Pius, visoa fretus, omni consilio neglecto, quam tenuem telam orsus, qua debilem texit rationem, quaeso videte. Saluator, inquit, noster Petrum Apostolorum Principem ad gubernationem Ecclesiae substituit. Quis ignorat omnibus Apostolis a Iesu esse praeceptum, ut eant in orbem praedicaturi fidem, baptismum & salutem? Quis nescit passim omnibus esse permissum, ligatum esse in coelis, quod ipsi ligarent in terris; & soluturi esse, quod soluerent? Sed quod Cephas singulariter dictum est: Tibi dabo, &c. hoc ait D. Hieronymus esse factum, vt schismatu tolleretur occasio. Et Ambrosius in Pastorali suo dicit, quod nedum Petro trina rogatione interrogato, an amaret, ac terna responsione subsequente, amare se, teste ipso interrogatore Iesu, traditas sibi esse claues, sed & omnibus Apostolis una contradita. Apostoli quoq; post ascensionem Domini conuenisse, ac Petrum sibi Principem constituisse, & Antiochiae in cathedram collocasse referuntur: nihil tamen de potestate vniuersis Apostolis a Saluatore data & ipsorum omnium vniuersali missione diminuerunt. Ergo & hodie Catholica exorat Ecclesia, seseper Apostolos ipsos continuaprotectione custodiri, quos Saluator ipse vicarios tantis operibus constituit praefecipastores. Horum legitimos successores constat esse vniuersalia Concilia, Christianae fidei firmamenta, quae ta, quae Pontificum actiones pro tempore salubberrimis doctrinis instruxerunt, errores emendarunt De quibus summus ille Pontifex Gregorius scribit: Quisquis illa destruere tentaverit, seipsum destruit. Sed quorsum haec? Eo certe pertingunt, ut conuellatur illa superstitio, in qua Papa Pius factionibus Cardinalis Cusani adstruit, Concilium supra Papam non esse, dum dicit (ut eius verbis utar) ad futurum Concilium, quod supra Christi vicarium esse nequit. Videte ergo, quam vim omnis consilii expertem Papa inferre tentavit. Nam si omnes Apostoli missi sunt a Domino Iesu, dicente illis: Ite in orbem, &c. Quaecunque ligaveritis, &c. quos constat conciliariter postea esse congregatos ac ipsum Cepham in messem Domini misisse: quis dubitat, Concilia sacra vicem Christi gerere, quae & coetui Apostolico successisse comprobantur? Siquidem orbis maior est urbe.
units.tr: He who lacks counsel falls by his own weight; God raises a moderated force to the heights. Pope Pius, some time ago, by a brief that was not attested but sealed with the Fisherman's ring, is reported to have excommunicated Gregory Heimburg, who had never been summoned, contrary to the law of God. God, who was to condemn the first transgressor, first sent a summons, saying "Adam, where are you?" Likewise he questioned Cain, still dripping with his brother's blood: "Where is Abel your brother?" He also dealt with the crimes of the Sodomites before he burned them with brimstone: "I will go down," he says, "and see whether they have done according to the cry that has come up to me." But Pope Pius, relying on what seemed to be the case and disregarding all counsel, see how thin a web he has spun, and how weak a reason he has woven. "Our Saviour," he says, "set Peter, the prince of the Apostles, over the government of the Church." Who does not know that Jesus commanded all the Apostles to go out into the world to preach the faith, baptism and salvation? Who does not know that it was everywhere granted to all of them that whatever they bound on earth should be bound in heaven, and whatever they loosed should be loosed? But that the words spoken to Cephas alone, "I will give to you, etc.," were done, as Jerome says, so that the occasion of schism might be removed. And Ambrose, in his Pastoral, says that the keys were indeed handed to Peter, who was asked three times whether he loved him and answered three times that he did, Jesus himself, the questioner, being witness; yet the keys were handed over to them, but also to all the Apostles, one grant to all. It is also reported that the Apostles, after the Lord's ascension, met together and set Peter over themselves as chief, and placed him in the chair at Antioch; yet they did not diminish anything of the power given to all the Apostles by the Saviour, or of the universal mission of them all. So today too the Catholic Church prays that the Apostles themselves be kept under continual protection, whom the Saviour himself appointed as vicars and ministers of so great works. It is agreed that the legitimate successors of these are the universal councils, the pillars of the Christian faith, which have instructed the Church with the most wholesome teachings, and corrected errors, as the actions of the Pontiffs have required at various times. Of these that most eminent Pontiff Gregory writes: Whoever tries to overthrow them destroys himself. But to what end is all this? Surely it aims at overturning that superstition by which Pope Pius, under the influence of Cardinal Cusanus's party, maintains that a council is not above the Pope, since he says (to use his own words) "a future council, which cannot be above the vicar of Christ." See then what force, devoid of all counsel, the Pope has attempted to apply. For if all the Apostles were sent by the Lord Jesus, who said to them, "Go into the world, etc. Whatever you bind, etc.," and if it is established that they were afterwards gathered together in council and sent Cephas himself into the Lord's harvest, who can doubt that sacred councils represent the person of Christ, since they are shown to have succeeded the Apostolic assembly? For the world is greater than the city.

units.la: Subdit Papa Pius, Remillam in conuentu Mantuano saepe & multum esse discussam: quasi Concilium habuerit procerum, uti sacrae leges iubent in rebus nouis constituendis: quas tamen pro nudo libitu plus euomuit, quam edixit. Profecto siquidem ipse conuentum Mantuanum nuncupat, conuentum Regalium & Principalium Oratorum, illuc transmissorum, in illo certe nihil de hoc actum ne cogitatum quidem existit.
units.tr: Pope Pius adds that the matter of Remilla was often and at great length discussed at the Congress of Mantua, as if he had held a council of nobles, as the sacred laws require when new matters are to be settled. Yet he has spewn forth more from his own bare whim than he has decreed. Indeed, he calls it the Congress of Mantua, a gathering of royal and princely envoys sent there; but in that gathering nothing of this was done, nor even thought of.

units.la: Dicitur autem Papa Pius cum Cardinalibus suis ita decreuisse. Cur hoc? Nisi quia voluit Papa ipse abuti potestate sua, talliam imponendo, & sub velamento militaris expeditionis in Turcam instaurandae facultates Germaniae illius, quae est inter Coloniam Agrippinam & Austriam, ac rursus inter Daciam & Alpes, quae Germaniam ab Italia discriminant, medullitus exhaurire. Nam ex illis solis finibus Oratores Mantuae ad tractandum conuenere. Illi quippe soli videbantur apti Papae, quos luderet: Brabantia, Hollandia, Gelria, cum circumiacentibus reclamarunt, clam illis quos supra nominavi. Utcunque res acta sit, nullus illorum interfuit tractatibus nostris, ergo vim suam exsortem [al. exteriorem] esse voluit assensum illorum, quorum aera concupiuit. Hinc profecte non inepte, nec supine, Papa ipse, negatis sibi pecuniis, quas solas ardebat, suam ratus laedi Maiestatem, vim astri conceptam, sed totius Concilii expertem adhibuit: ac imprimis suam dimensus potestatem, simul & Imperatoris nostri splendorem ante oculos ponens, putavit neminem resistere posse, vel audere, conatibus eorum. Veruntamen suam potestatem stupendo, quae latior est quam hodie sit Imperii gratia Romani (quae quondam Caucasi montis limite coartata, dehinc facto Caucasi limite per totum orbem vires suas terra marique exporrexit, nunc autem Augustorum desidia angusto limite cingitur) nihil profecto suis machinationibus in hite partibus, quas Imperialis tituli splendor illustrat, obstare posse rebatur, nisi fortasse totius orbis Christiani conuentus cieretur, quod vniuersale Concilium nuncupamus. Hanc sanctissimam Christianorum conuentionem, libertatis alumnam, Papa velut iliacam horrens passionem, illam praevenire credens, vanissimo decreto, antequam nasceretur, condemnauit, sed condemnando potius indicauit. Cum enim sedulo vetat, profecto magis timere deprehenditur. Nam quod veteri silentio restinxit litura, hoc totum inuida damnatio viuificauit: non aliter quam qui latentes vires calcis, aquae rigentis & gelidae superfusione obruere cupiens, inuitus ac nolens exuscitauit. Prudentius Solon ille Atheniensis, legibus ordinatissime compositis, interrogatus; Cur nihil seuerius in parricidas statuisset, qui tamen sicariis longe immaniores essent? respondisse fertur: Ideo se reticuisse ne vetando admonuisse videretur. Hunc locum Praelati capessite, qui libertatis vestrae certissimum est refugium, dignitatisque firmamentum: infirmos rumpite casses, & inanes laqueos dissipate, qui scholasticis datis operam disciplinis. Seculi vero Principes & viri militares, ad bellaque doctiores, quibus est disciplina, si quando proficiscimini, editiora loca hostibus intercipere, hunc eminentissimum locum vniuersalis Concilii quaeso ante capite, unde vobis sit prospectus liberior, fortior & intentior propugnatio, tutelaque securior. Quod si Papa hoc tale tantumque asylum interceperit, hoc roboris vallum fortasse demolitus fuerit, seu obruerit, antequam emineat seu oriatur, vos abiecto clypeo exarmati tandem, precio venalitate, hoc est tributorum pensitatione, animas vestras geminii redimere: pecuniaque vestra, sub velamento militaris expeditionis aduersus Turcas instaurandae, in damnatum & scelestum vsum conuertetur, scilicet in subsidium Fernandi, ex damnato complexu quondam Alfonsi Regis Aragonum, connixi contra Renatum regni Siciliae heredem legitimum, & inclytum Ioannem Calabriae Principem, Christianae nobilitatis ac militaris gloriae decus & ornamentum, & exemplar imitabile. Et idcirco dicit Papa, Gregorii Heimburg ex diabolo natum: quia non ex damnato coitu, sed legitimo coniugio progenitus: quorum os of est Papa, fautor bastardorum, pro quibus longissimam, & fere trium horarum prolixam fecit orationem, dum Fernandi Bastardi laudes Mantuae peroraret.
units.tr: Pope Pius is said to have decided this with his Cardinals. Why so? Unless the Pope himself wished to abuse his power, by imposing a tax and, under the cover of a military expedition to be undertaken against the Turks, to drain to the very marrow the resources of that part of Germany which lies between Cologne and Austria, and again between Dacia and the Alps, which separate Germany from Italy. For it was from those very regions that the envoys met at Mantua to deal with the matter. Indeed, those alone seemed suitable to the Pope to be played with. Brabant, Holland, Guelders and the neighbouring lands protested, secretly from those I have named above. However the affair was conducted, none of them took part in our deliberations; so he wished his power to be without the consent of those whose money he coveted. Having therefore begun with this, and not without shrewdness or lack of diligence, the Pope himself, since the money alone which he burned for had been refused, thought that his Majesty was harmed, and applied a force conceived in the stars but devoid of the whole council. And above all, measuring his own power and setting before his eyes the splendour of our Emperor, he supposed that no one could resist or dare to oppose his attempts. Yet, stupidly marvelling at his own power, which is broader than the grace of the Roman Empire is today (which once was confined within the limit of Mount Caucasus, and afterwards, the limit of Caucasus having been overcome, extended its strength over the whole world by land and sea, but now, through the sloth of the Augustuses, is enclosed within a narrow boundary), he reckoned that nothing could stand in the way of his machinations in these parts, which the splendour of the imperial title illuminates, unless perhaps an assembly of the whole Christian world were summoned, which we call a universal council. This most holy gathering of Christians, the nursling of liberty, Pope Pius, shuddering as at a Trojan danger, and believing that he could forestall it, condemned with a most vain decree before it was born; but in condemning it he rather revealed it. For when he forbids it so earnestly, he is plainly found to fear it more. For what an erasure had quenched by long silence, all this envious condemnation has brought to life; not otherwise than someone who, wishing to crush the hidden power of quicklime by pouring cold, chill water over it, reluctantly and against his will has roused it. Solon the Athenian, that most prudent lawgiver, when asked why he had laid down nothing more severe against parricides, who were yet far more monstrous than assassins, is said to have replied that he had kept silent so that he would not seem to give warning by forbidding. Let the prelates seize upon this place, which is the surest refuge of your liberty and the firmest support of your dignity: break the weak nets and scatter the empty snares, you who devote yourselves to scholastic learning. And you, secular princes and military men, more skilled in war, whose discipline it is, whenever you set out to seize the higher ground from the enemy, I beg you first to occupy this most commanding position of a universal council, from which you may have a freer view, a bolder and more attentive defence, and a safer protection. But if the Pope should seize this so great and so powerful a refuge, he may perhaps have demolished or overthrown this rampart of strength before it rises or appears; and then you, having cast aside your shield and at last disarmed, will with your money, that is, by paying taxes, buy back your souls twice over; and your money, under the cover of a military expedition to be undertaken against the Turks, will be turned to a condemned and wicked use, namely to the aid of Ferdinand, who, sprung from the condemned embrace of the former King Alfonso of Aragon, has conspired against Rene, the lawful heir of the kingdom of Sicily, and against the renowned John, Prince of Calabria, the ornament and glory of Christian nobility and military renown, and a model worthy of imitation. And so the Pope says that Gregory Heimburg was born of the devil, because he was not born of a condemned union but of a lawful marriage; the Pope, the patron of bastards, whose mouthpiece he is, for whom he made a very long oration, nearly three hours long, while he extolled at Mantua the praises of the bastard Ferdinand.

units.la: Quod vero subdit Papa, Gregorium Heimburg auarum, mendacem & turbulentum nuncupando, benedictis si certaret, bona audiret: sed cum certat maledictis, alium quaerat, qui respondeat. Ego ex illo grege non sum, quippe cui facultates pro meritis minime respondent, qui plura suffragia liberaliter impendi, quam honoraria suscepepim: & libertatis amator plus semper fui quam blanditiarum: quae mendaciis & auaritiae minime conuenire possunt. Sed ipse aliquando audiet, quid gesserit, qualem vitam egerit, & quid apud Cumas.
units.tr: As for the Pope's further charge, calling Gregory Heimburg greedy, a liar and a troublemaker, if he were contending with good words he would hear good things in return. But since he contends with abuse, let him seek someone else to answer. I am not of that flock: my means by no means match my merits, I have given many votes freely rather than accepted fees for them, and I have always been more a lover of liberty than of flattery, qualities that can least of all agree with lying and greed. But he himself will hear someday what he has done, what sort of life he has led, and what he did at Cumae.

units.la: Sed comprimo me, pergens ad illius decreti vanitatem, in quo vetantur oppressi vel opprimendi ad Concilium prouocare, quod non est, & quod (ut aiat) supra Papam esse nequit. Iam supra ostensum est, cœtum Apostolicum fuisse supra Petrum: & nunc affirmo, quod sicut ad ean-dem Apostolicam vacantem appellari potest, sic ad Concilium, quod nondum est congregatum, rite appellatur. Quia potestas Ecclesiæ immortalis est, quemadmodum ipsa Ecclesia: quæ etsi nunc dispersa est, aliquando habet congregari. Et hoc nunc maxime opus esse, nemo dubitat, qui calamitates Ecclesiæ intelligit & cognoscit: cuius si se Papa partem esse fateatur, se vtique minorem illa fateri necesse est: siquidem orbis est maior vrbe. Papa autem hoc vetando, quid aliud agit quam quod causatur aduersus nos, qui eius imperium truculentissimum non sustinemus, quod facultates nostras, tam nostro quam maiorum nostrorum sudore & sanguine partas, in suas delicias effundere negamus: velut ille, qui ex vulneribus à se iniectis recreatum accusauit, quod telum parcius corpore suscepisset. Hoc dominicum in seruos extat imperium, quod in nos exercere cupit.
units.tr: But I restrain myself and turn to the emptiness of that decree, which forbids the oppressed, or those about to be oppressed, to appeal to a Council, a body which (so they say) cannot be above the Pope. I have already shown above that the Apostolic college was above Peter. Now I affirm that just as an appeal can be lodged to that same Apostolic body when it is vacant, so an appeal is rightly lodged to a Council which has not yet been convened. For the power of the Church is immortal, just as the Church itself is, and although the Church is now scattered, it will at some time have to be gathered again. Nobody who understands and knows the calamities of the Church doubts that this is now especially necessary. If the Pope admits that he is a part of the Church, he must necessarily admit that he is smaller than it, since the world is greater than the city. But in forbidding this, what else does the Pope do than what he charges against us, who will not endure his most savage rule and who refuse to pour our goods, won by our own and our ancestors' sweat and blood, into his pleasures? He is like the man who accused the one who had healed him of his wounds because the weapon had been taken too sparingly into his body. This is the lordly rule over slaves that he wishes to exercise over us.

units.la: Hoc est seruile seruitium, quod à nobis exigit: non filialis reuerentia, quibus certè nec peculium relinquere curat. Nemo sanæ mentis hoc non percipit, nullus emunctæ naris homo non olfacit, quorsum tendat hæc tam grauis exactio.
units.tr: This is the servile slavery he demands from us, not filial reverence, for which he certainly takes no care to leave even a private purse. No one of sound mind fails to perceive this, and no man with a keen nose fails to smell where such a grievous exaction tends.

units.la: Quod vero me loquacem facit, vir omni pica dicacior, quid dixerim? nisi Horatii verbo respondisse velim, dicentis: Ignoras te, an ignorum dare nobis verba putas? Cum tua peruideas oculis mala lippus inunctis, cur in aliorum vitiis tam cernis acutum, quam aut aquila, aut serpens Epidaurius? hinc tibi contra euenit, inquirant vitia ut tua rursus & illi. Fateor quippe me ventositati verborum pro tempore operam dedisse: at non ita vt ciuilis & Canonicæ traditionis præcepta contemserim: quæ ille nevnquam quidem olfecit, nuda verbositate contentus. Porro si quod tale vitium apud me deprehendit, inepte tamen id ipsum mihi exprobrauit, quo ipse potissimum turget. Mihi satis est, didicisse ciuiles sententias: & quicquid præcipuum habet ratio & industria, & quicquid sacra tradunt vtriusque iuris instituta, hisce literis & floribus exornare posse: & in illo grege me esse profiteor. Ipse in numero sit illorum, qui putant hæc omnia vi & artificio Rhetorum contineri. Ergo si Papa ob id facinus me excommunicatum dicit, quis erit eiectior ipso, qui præter verbositatem nihil habet in se virtutis?
units.tr: As for what makes me talkative, a man more chattering than any magpie, what shall I say? Unless I wish to answer with the words of Horace, who says: "Do you not know yourself, or do you think you can fool us with ignorance? When you, bleary-eyed, see your own faults clearly, why do you see the faults of others as sharply as an eagle or the Epidaurian serpent? Hence it happens to you the opposite way: let them search out your faults in turn." I confess that I have, for the moment, devoted some effort to windiness of words, but not so as to have despised the precepts of civil and canonical tradition, which he, content with bare verbosity, has never even smelled. Moreover, if he has detected such a fault in me, he has foolishly reproached me with the very thing in which he himself most swells. It is enough for me to have learned the civil opinions, and to be able to adorn with these letters and flowers whatever is chief in reason and diligence, and whatever the sacred institutions of both laws teach; and I profess that I am in that flock. Let him be among those who think all these things are contained by the force and artifice of the rhetoricians. So if the Pope says that I am excommunicated for this offence, who will be more cast out than he, who has nothing in himself of virtue apart from verbosity?

units.la: Subdit, & lasa Maiestatis crimine me irretitum. Credo eum culicibus & muscis has leges edidisse, aut animalibus quæ in tabidis corporibus nasci solent: vti aranearum telas in occursum fragiles, leges consilii exsortes æquauit: quas si culex, aut quod imbecillius animantium incideret, euoluere se nescit: si quid autem validiorum animantium inciderit, penetrat atque disrumpit. Neque enim rete sicedulis aut coturnicibus contextum aptum est vincire vulturem vel aquilam. Irretiat ipse Reatinos suos, & eos quos seruili metu constrictos habet: mecum erit (Deo duce) libertas Diogenis & Catonis. Nec satiatus est Papa conuiciis vulgaribus: quin etiam Hæreticum me audeat nuncupare. Siquidem hæresim voluit sectam vel sententiam nuncupare, vt Cicero noster Catonem recte appellat, hæreticus sum ego, qui aio; Concilium orbis Christiani sore supra Papam: hæreticus est Papa, qui contrariam sectam souet. Videte quod nihil grauius in eum dico, qui tamen abiecta rationis & consilii moderatione, cuncta in me pro libitu iussit scribi.
units.tr: He adds that I am entangled in the crime of treason. I believe he issued these laws for gnats and flies, or for creatures that are wont to be born in rotting bodies. Just as spiders' webs are fragile against an attack, so he has made laws that lack all counsel. If a gnat or some weaker creature falls into them, it does not know how to unroll itself; but if something stronger falls in, the web is pierced and torn apart. For a net woven for sparrows or quails is not fit to bind a vulture or an eagle. He entangles his own Reatines and those whom he holds bound by servile fear; with me, under God's guidance, will be the freedom of Diogenes and Cato. Nor is the Pope satisfied with common insults; he even dares to call me a heretic. For if by heresy he means a sect or opinion, as our Cicero rightly calls Cato, then I am the heretic, who say: a council of the Christian world will be above the Pope. The Pope is the heretic, who supports the contrary sect. See that I say nothing heavier against him, who nevertheless, casting aside all moderation of reason and counsel, has ordered everything to be written against me at his pleasure.

units.la: Postremò nec adhuc satiatus Papa conuitiis, mandat bona mea consiscari: quæ vtinam tanta essent, quod rapacibus viris hiatum pandere possent. Ego inter bonos conuersari volo, qui virtutes meas opibus suis foueant, & pluris faciant suffragia mea, quam locupletiuam, quam ex mea ruina sperare possent: maiori etiam vtentur consilio, quam Papa fretus in procacitate sua. Pollicetur tandem eis Papa, qui res meas inuaserint, Catholicorum hominum opetas impendisse. Maxime periculosum esset hoc verbum, nisi ipsius Papæ ineptia iam antea vobis comprobata esset, dum ipse incastuosos complexus, & vitia honestati publicæ inimica, Mantuæ tam copiosè & loquaciter personauit.
units.tr: Finally, not yet satisfied with insults, the Pope orders my goods to be confiscated. Would that they were so great that they could open a gaping maw for greedy men! I want to live among good men, who will foster my virtues with their resources and value my votes more than the wealth they might hope to gain from my ruin; they will also use greater counsel than the Pope, who relies on his own impudence. At last the Pope promises those who have seized my property that he has expended the means of Catholic men. This word would be most dangerous, were it not that the Pope's own folly has already been proved to you, since he, with incestuous embraces and vices hostile to public honesty, resounded so copiously and garrulously at Mantua.

units.la: Expugnatis nunc aranearum telis, & infirmorum retium vinculis nodisque dissolutis, ad remedium moribus introductum, quo aduersus superiorem truculentiam & amarissimas leges se tuetur innocentia, stylum conuertere depropero. Et in primis plane constat, semper & vbique ab inferiore ad superiorem rite prouocari. Nemo enim tam obtusi cordis est, qui non in seipso periculum fecerit, à sensualitatis fragilitate ad intelleCtualis potentiæ discursum prouocando. Sed & qui morbo aut vitio animi tenetur, vt nesciat cernere verum, si lapsus fuerit in vitium, defæcato tandem animo ad se rediens, ad animum ira, odio, gratiaque vacuum prouocat; quo certius de rebus dubiis consulret atque decernat, & vim suam grauitate consilii moderetur. Ideo laudata est illa mulier, quæ à temulento Rege Philippo ad eundem sobrium prouocauit. Sit ergo mihi gradus primus, ab irato Papa, qui me lacessit, ad eundem mitem saČtum appellare: & ab Oratore Topico ad eundem, si ventositate abdicata, si musis relegatis, ad sacras leges se conuerterit: vbi discet, Neminem indemnatum, rebus aut fama spoliare, nec quenquam inauditum condemnare. Deinde quia scriptum est, Papam omnes iudicare, ipsum au-tem à nemine iudicandum: quod & ego fateor verum, quantum attinet ad sedis ipsius & Papalis potestatis plenitudinem, sed non ita, vt sub inimico ac suspecto iudice quisquam cogatur samam aut res suas decertare: ad eundem itaque prouoco, si se iuxta boni viri arbitrium astrinxerit indicaturum. Et is sit appellationis mea gradus secundus. Si vero causam delegare malit viro non suspecto, rursus ad eundem Papam, seu quem deliget, prouoco & appello. Et hunc ter-tium. tium appellationis meæ modum offero, meque tali iudicio sisto. & in summa, Papali cognitioni ea lege me submitto, si suspicionis causa tollatur è medio. Et hic quartus ordo omnem tollit tergiversationis notam, quam mihi iniicere posset Cusana procacitas, cuius ductu hæc omnia diriguntur. Quæ omnia si Papa contempserit, quid restat, nisi ad vniversalem Ecclesiam provocare, prout à Senatu ad populum Romanum sæpe reperimus appellatum? Nec obiiciat mihi Papa, Ecclesiam non esse congregatam: quoniam idipsum factionibus suis impeditur & disturbatur. Apud me nulla mora, culpa nusquam, cum nō per me, sed per ipsum stet, quo minus fiat. Si quis enim in ius vocatum vi eximat, contumaciam remouet citato, sed omne vitium & crimen in se transfert. Papa metum intulit mihi, ipse sibi iustitiam indixit, qui se conuiciis suis aduersus me suspectum reddidit, qui se sapientis arbitrio adstringere declinauit, de suspicione experiri recusat, nec iudicem suspicione carentem delegare dignatur: quique vniversale Concilium concieri negat. Hic si aduersum me quidquam attentauerit, aduersus ipsum prouoco, gradatim atque alternatim, vt præmisi: & testimonium eius rei postulo, & de metu iusto protestor coram vicinis: Quo cessante, psequor, si opus erit, & opportunitas concedatur, prout iuris publici ratio poscit; saluo iure addendi, omnibusque remediis, moribus & lege introductis.
units.tr: Now that the webs of spiders have been destroyed, and the bonds and knots of weak nets dissolved, I hasten to turn my pen to the remedy introduced by custom, by which innocence defends itself against superior savagery and most bitter laws. And first it is quite clear that an appeal is always and everywhere rightly made from the inferior to the superior. For no one is so dull of heart that he has not tried this on himself, appealing from the frailty of the senses to the discourse of the intellectual power. And one who is held by disease or vice of the mind, so that he cannot discern the truth, if he has fallen into vice, returns to himself once his mind is cleansed, and appeals to a mind free of anger, hatred and favour, so that he may consult and decide more surely on doubtful matters, and temper his power by the gravity of counsel. Therefore that woman was praised who appealed from King Philip when he was drunk to the same king when he was sober. Let my first step then be to appeal from the angry Pope, who assails me, to the same Pope, mild and holy; and from the Topical Orator to the same man, if, having abandoned windiness and dismissed the Muses, he turns to the sacred laws, where he will learn that no one unconvicted should be stripped of goods or reputation, nor anyone condemned unheard. Then, since it is written that the Pope is to be judged by all, but is himself to be judged by no one, which I too admit is true so far as concerns the fullness of that see and of papal power, yet not so that under a hostile and suspect judge anyone is compelled to contend for his reputation or goods, therefore I appeal to the same man, if he binds himself to abide by the judgment of a good man. That will be the second step of my appeal. If indeed he prefers to delegate the case to a man who is not suspect, I again appeal and appeal to the same Pope, or to whomever he chooses.
