Et non esset verum q in duob. casib. Papa accusari posset, vt gl. ibi dicit, vnde sufficit q in secundo casu, scil. delicto notorio & scandaloso sit largo modo haeresis cum illa qualitate scandali. In haeresi vero proprie, et si delictum esset occultum Papa accusari potest, vt gl. ibi dicit, & ideo argumentum Theologorum factum s. in contrarium, non conuenit ad mentem & intentionem glo. si recte consideretur. Et ita dixi dum haberem sermone de hac re cum aliis Doctoribus in hac causa requisitis. Et per hoc et respondetur ad aliud, quo dicebatur, q Can.si Papa intelligitur de haeresi proprie, quia illud verum est qn Papa deberet accusari de haeresi simpliciter, secus si agatur de crimine scandaloso, quia ratione scandali, Papa accusari potest, licet non sit proprie haeresis, secundum gloss. in d. Can.si Papa, quae communiter approbatur: Non obstat q illa gloss. non probatur iure, qa immo probatur ratione scandali, vt s. dictū fuit: Non obstat q exceptio facta in Can.si Papa, de casu haeresis contra regulam q ibi ponitur, confirmare videtur regulā in casib. non exceptuatis, quia illud verum est in aliis casib. dissimilib. ab exceptuatis. Secus est in similib. casib. qa exceptio facta in vno ad nimilem casum porrigitur, vt notat Abb. per illum text. in c. cum d. literas, de confirm. vtil. & inutil. & idem Abbas, in c. iuranti, de probat. in c. ad audientiam de Cler. non residen. & nota Bald. per illum textum, in cap. post translationem, in verbo quanquam derenunt. Et hoc etiam procedit, si exceptio facta sit per dictionem taxatiuam tantum, vt notat Bartol. in l. si constante in princ. ff. solut. matr. in l.3. § cum Titio, ff. de adim. leg. Et tradit Ang. in l. si hominem § in Aedilitijs, ff. de Aedil. edict. in l. Paulus, § bares rogatus, ff. de usur. cum similib. vt Alex. scribit in l.1. Cod. de bonor. possess. contra tab. & in d.l. si constante, in 2. thar. & in Consilio 130. in causa, col. 3. lib. 4. & in proposito ratione scandali, casus videtur similis haeresi, secundum glossam in dicto Can.si Papa, quae communiter approbatur, vt s. dictum est. Et ad hoc bene facit, quod notat Salyc. in l. de crimine, in 2. oppos. Cod. qui acc. vbi per illum textum dicit, quod licet aliquid specialiter exprimatur, non per hoc videtur derogatum aliis casib. qui alia via & alio modo includuntur.
units.tr: The second is another notorious and scandalous offence, in which the Pope is incorrigible. For that incorrigibility or obstinacy is called heresy according to the gloss there, and in such a case it is not required that the offence be heresy properly, because then the second case would be reduced to the first, concerning heresy. Nor would it be true that a Pope can be accused in two cases, as the gloss there says. Hence it suffices that in the second case, namely a notorious and scandalous offence, it be heresy in a broad sense, with that quality of scandal. But in heresy properly, even if the offence were hidden, the Pope can be accused, as the gloss there says. Therefore the argument of the Theologians made above to the contrary does not agree with the mind and intention of the gloss, if it is rightly considered; and so I said when I discussed this matter with the other Doctors called into this cause. And by this it is also answered to the other point, where it was said that Can. si Papa is understood of heresy properly. That is true when the Pope is to be accused of heresy simply; otherwise, if the matter concerns a scandalous crime, the Pope can be accused by reason of the scandal, although it is not properly heresy, according to the gloss in the said Can. si Papa, which is commonly approved. It is no obstacle that this gloss is not proved by law, for it is rather proved by reason of scandal, as was said above. It is no obstacle that the exception made in Can. si Papa, concerning the case of heresy, against the rule laid down there, seems to confirm the rule in cases not excepted, because that holds in cases dissimilar to the excepted ones. It is otherwise in similar cases, because an exception made for one case extends to a similar case, as Abbas notes from the text in c. cum d. literas, de confirm. util. & inutil.; the same Abbas in c. iuranti, de probat.; and in c. ad audientiam, de Cler. non residen.; and note Baldus from the text in c. post translationem, on the words quanquam derelinquunt. This also holds if the exception is made only by a restrictive word, as Bartolus notes in l. si constante, in princ., ff. solut. matr., and in l. 3 § cum Titio, ff. de adim. leg. Angelus teaches it in l. si hominem § in Aedilitiis, ff. de Aedil. edict., and l. Paulus § bares rogatus, ff. de usur., with similar cases; as Alexander writes in l. 1 Cod. de bonor. possess. contra tab., and in the said l. si constante, in 2 thar., and in Consilium 130, in causa, col. 3, lib. 4. And in this matter, by reason of scandal, the case seems similar to heresy, according to the gloss in the said Can. si Papa, which is commonly approved, as has been said. To this well agrees what Salicetus notes in l. de crimine, in 2 oppos., Cod. qui acc., where, from that text, he says that although something is expressly stated, it is not thereby taken to be derogated from other cases which are included in another way and by another means.

units.la: XIV. Et facit etiam q dici solet, quod licet exceptio firmet regulam, non tamen videtur illa ampliare, ad ea quae aliàs sub regula non comprehenduntur, vt notat Bart. in l. generali, § vxoris ff. de vsufructu legat. Abb. in c. in nostra, de sepul. cum similib. quae nota sunt. Vlterius et considerandum est, quod textus in dicto Can.si Papa, dum excipit casum haeresis, non videtur loqui de haeresi proprie, vt supra dicebatur, cum vtatur verbis generalib. dum inquit, nisi fit a fide deuius, ista enim verba etiam in haeresi largo modo verificari videntur.
units.tr: XIV. And this agrees with the saying that is commonly repeated: although an exception confirms the rule, it does not seem to extend the rule to those cases which are not otherwise included under it, as Bartolus notes in l. generali, § vxoris, ff. de vsufructu legat., and Abbas in c. in nostra, de sepul., with similar authorities, which are well known. Further, it must be considered that the text in the said Can. si Papa, while it excepts the case of heresy, does not seem to speak of heresy properly, as was said above, since it uses general words when it says "unless he has departed from the faith"; for these words seem to be applicable even to heresy in a broad sense.

units.la: XV. Et ideo videntur habere locum in Simoniaco & schismatico, qa largo modo dicuntur haeretici, vt s. dictum est, & idem in similib. casib. vt in Can.omnes 22.dist. vbi in haeresin labitur, qui priuilegia Rom. Eccl. auferre conatur. Ad idem facit text. in Can.si 30 d.s.t. & 4. q.1. in Can.quod aut, 24.q.3. in Can. haeresis, in cau. contumacia, de haeretic. in VI. cum similib. Vltimo non obstat, quod text. in d. Can.si Papa, dum ponit regulam, quod Papa iudicari ab alio non posset, videtur etiam loqui in delicto scandaloso, vt s. ponderatur, quia loquitur ille text. quando Papa erat in suis operib. neglig ens & remissus.
units.tr: XV. And therefore they seem to apply to the simoniac and the schismatic, since in a broad sense they are called heretics, as was said above, and likewise in similar cases, as in Can. omnes 22 dist., where he who attempts to take away the privileges of the Roman Church falls into heresy. To the same effect are the texts in Can. si 30 dist. s.t., and 4 q. 1, in Can. quod aut, 24 q. 3, in Can. haeresis, and in cap. contumacia, de haeretic. in VI, with similar texts. Lastly, it is no objection that the text in the said Can. si Papa, while laying down the rule that the Pope cannot be judged by another, seems also to speak of a scandalous offence, as was weighed above, because that text speaks of a Pope who was negligent and remiss in his duties.

units.la: XVI. Et sic in delicto in non faciendo, in quo minor est culpa quam in faciendo, prout sequitur gl. in d. Can. si Papa. argum. gl. in l. si mora, ff. solut. matr. Et ideo non valet argum. in delicto quod fit in omittendo, ad id quod fit in committendo, ut not. Bart. in l. lucet, §. si. ff. depos. facit tex. in l. argentarius, §. cum autem. & quod ibi Bald. ff. de tedendo. Et satis est nobis, quod gl. ista in d. Can. si Papa communiter approbetur. Et sic remotis omnib. allegatis, s. in contrarium firmata remanet Conclusio, quod Papa accusari possit de notorio crimine in quo incorrigibilis sit & Ecclesia scandalizatur. Et ita primum dubium breviter absolutum sit.
units.tr: XVI. And so in an offence of omission, in which the fault is less than in an offence of commission, as the gloss on the said Can. si Papa follows, the argument from the gloss in l. si mora, ff. solut. matr., holds. Therefore the argument from an offence of omission to one of commission is not valid, as Bartolus notes in l. lucet, § si, ff. depos., and the text in l. argentarius, § cum autem, and what Baldus says there, ff. de tedendo, applies. And it is enough for us that this gloss on the said Can. si Papa is commonly approved. And so, with all the arguments on the other side set aside, the conclusion stands firm that the Pope can be accused of a notorious crime in which he is incorrigible and by which the Church is scandalized. And thus the first doubt is briefly resolved.

units.la: XVII. Venio ad secundum dubium, in quo quaeritur, an Papa qui post eius creationem iuravit & vovit ij. biennium celebrare Concilium, efficaciter obligetur, ita quod se absolvere non possit. Et prima facie videretur dicendum quod seipsum absolvere possit, ut in terminis volunt Petr. de Ancha. in c. venerabilem, in fi. de elect. dicens, quod ille qui non habet superiorem potest seipsum absolvere a iuramento. Et Pet. de Anch. refert novissime & sequitur Felinus in c. 2. de sponsal. col. 8. in verb. tertia declaratio. & in c. 1. in 4. char. in verb. sexta declaratio, de const. & ibi dicit, non obstare si dicatur quod debet esse distinctio personarum inter absolventem & absolutum. argum. s. fi. de inst. & c. per vestras, de iure patron. quia ipse respondet dupliciter: Primo, quod illa regula est de iure positivo, cui Papa non subiicitur, c. propositum, de con. eff. prab. Secundo, quod Papa poterit alteri suam absolutionem committere, iuxta gloss. in c. sane. Clem. 1. de offic. delegat. & talis absolutio non esset necessaria, si factum fuisset de missio ante ad Papatum promoveretur, quia non valuisset, ut notat Abb. in c. sicut nostris, mu. mirabili de iureiurando, ubi inquit, quod si Cardinales ante creationem summi Pontificis aliqua statuunt, & promittunt et cum iuramento illa observare, si contingit aliquem ipsorum ad Papatum promoveri, tale iuramentum non valet per illum textum.
units.tr: XVII. I come to the second doubt, in which it is asked whether a Pope who, after his creation, swore and vowed to hold a Council within two years, is effectively bound, so that he cannot absolve himself. At first sight it would seem that he can absolve himself, as Petrus de Ancharano holds in terms, in c. venerabilem, in fine, de elect., saying that one who has no superior can absolve himself from an oath. Petrus de Ancharano reports this most recently, and Felinus follows him in c. 2, de sponsal., col. 8, in the words "tertia declaratio," and in c. 1, in 4 char., in the words "sexta declaratio," de const., and there he says that it is no objection if it is said that there must be a distinction of persons between the one absolving and the one absolved, with the argument from s. fin. de inst. and c. per vestras, de iure patron. For he himself answers in two ways. First, that this rule is of positive law, to which the Pope is not subject, c. propositum, de con. eff. prab. Secondly, that the Pope can commit his absolution to another, according to the gloss in c. sane, Clem. 1, de offic. delegat.; and such an absolution would not be necessary if the thing had been done before the man was promoted to the papacy, because it would not have been valid, as Abbas notes in c. sicut nostris, mu. mirabili de iureiurando, where he says that if Cardinals before the creation of the supreme Pontiff decree something and promise with an oath to observe it, and one of them is afterwards promoted to the papacy, such an oath is not valid by that text.

units.la: Sed breviter his (ut j. apparebit) remotis, contrarium de iure in casu proposito concludendum est, videlicet quod ex tali promissione efficaciter Papa obligatur, nec se absolvere possit. Nam quod Papa tali casu obligetur, non videtur dubitandum, quia iuramentum & votum est de iure divino, ut per gloss. in c. quanto, de iureiur. cui Papa subiicitur: ut notatur in c. qua in Ecclesiarum, de consue. 17. q. 1. in Can. sunt quaedam. Et hac ratione Papa, qui est Princeps, ex suo contractu astringitur, ut notatur in c. 1. de probat. in c. 1. de natura feud. vbi Bal. not. Cyn. in l. digna vox, in verb. ultimo scias. Cod. de leg. cum similib. quod nota sunt. Nam & Deus ipse, ex eius promissione obligaretur, ut not. Bald. in l. r in princ. ff. de pact. vbi Magistrum sententiarum ita dicentem refert. Et in terminis in casu nostro hoc specialiter tradit Ant. de Butr. in c. 1. col. 2. in verb. ex quibus patet, de const. vbi refert casum qui fuit tempore Gregorij XII. Cum enim de eius electione tractaretur in conclavi, ante Papatum & etiam post, promisit, iuravit, & vovit renunciare Papatui pro sedando schismate, quod XXX annis duraverat: & eodem modo promisit non creare Cardinales, postea noluit implere quod promiserat, propter hoc quamplures Cardinales ab eo de civitate Lucana recesserunt, & se Pisas contulerant. Concludit Ant. de Butr. in d. c. 1. col. 2. in verb. & sic Papa, de const. quod in tali casu Papa efficaciter obligatur, adeo quod seipsum absolvere nullo modo possit. Et idem tenet Immol. ibi col. 3. quia debet esse distinctio personarum inter ipsum absolventem & absolutum, arg. c. si. de inst. & ad hoc facit quia in facto proprio quis seipsum absolvere non potest, ut de voto notat Abb. in c. Magna, in principio de voto.
units.tr: But, these things having been briefly set aside (as will appear below), the contrary must be concluded in law in the case proposed, namely that the Pope is effectively bound by such a promise and cannot absolve himself. For that the Pope is bound in such a case does not seem open to doubt, because an oath and a vow are of divine law, as the gloss in c. quanto, de iureiur. says, to which the Pope is subject, as is noted in c. qua in Ecclesiarum, de consue., 17 q. 1, in Can. sunt quaedam. And for this reason the Pope, who is a Prince, is bound by his own contract, as is noted in c. 1, de probat., in c. 1, de natura feud., where Baldus notes, and Cynus on l. digna vox, in the words "ultimo scias," Cod. de leg., with similar authorities, which are well known. For God himself would be bound by his promise, as Baldus notes in l. 1 in princ., ff. de pact., where he reports the Master of the Sentences saying so. And in the very terms of our case Antonius de Butrio delivers this specifically, in c. 1, col. 2, in the words "ex quibus patet," de const., where he reports a case which occurred in the time of Gregory XII. When his election was being discussed in conclave, both before and after he became Pope, he promised, swore and vowed to resign the papacy in order to end the schism, which had lasted thirty years; and in the same way he promised not to create Cardinals, but afterwards he was unwilling to fulfil what he had promised, and for this reason many Cardinals withdrew from him from the city of Lucca and betook themselves to Pisa. Antonius de Butrio concludes in the said c. 1, col. 2, in the words "et sic Papa," de const., that in such a case the Pope is effectively bound, so that he can in no way absolve himself. Immolanus holds the same there, col. 3, because there must be a distinction of persons between the one absolving and the one absolved, with the argument from c. si, de inst.; and this agrees, because in a matter touching himself no one can absolve himself, as Abbas notes concerning a vow in c. Magna, in principio de voto.

units.la: XVIII. Et quia hoc videtur duplex vinculum voti & iuramenti, quod potius ligat, ca. 1. de treug. & pace.
units.tr: XVIII. And because this seems to be a double bond of vow and oath, which binds more strongly, c. 1, de treug. et pace.

units.la: XIX. Et hoc bene facit, quia qui Princeps ex contractu obligatur, et de plenitudine potestatis contravenire non potest, ut notanter dicit Paul. de Castr. in d. l. digna vox, Cod. de legib. Et idem Bald. in c. 1. §. ad hae, col. 5. in verb. item notatur ex gl. de pace iuramento firmata: idem tenet Paul. de Castr. in Consil. 420. videtur, in antiquis. & hoc idem in terminis huius quaestionis tradit Petr. de Anch. in Consil. 65 pro declaratione dubiorum, col. 2. Et quod dictum est Papam seipsum absolvere non posse, maxime haberet locum qui Papa iam in periurium incidisset, quo casu, qui quis incidisset in periurium absolutio fieri non potest, ut not. Feder. in Consil. 100. factum tale est, debitor. & sequitur Abb. in cap 1. col. penult. de iureiur. Anthon. de Butr. & Immol. in cap. debitores de iureiur. Roman. in Consil. 426. in re praesenti, in princip. & idem Bald. in Authent. quod eis in sin. Cod. de nuptiis, in l. 1. in sin. Cod. si adversus rem iudicatam.
units.tr: XIX. And this agrees well, because a Prince who is bound by contract cannot, by the fullness of his power, go against it, as Paulus de Castro notably says in said l. digna vox, Cod. de legib. Baldus likewise, in c. 1, § ad hae, col. 5, in the words "item notatur," from the gloss de pace iuramento firmata; Paulus de Castro holds the same in Consil. 420, "videtur," in the old collection. And Petrus de Ancharano delivers this same thing in the very terms of this question in Consil. 65, pro declaratione dubiorum, col. 2. And what has been said, that the Pope cannot absolve himself, would especially apply where the Pope had already fallen into perjury; in which case, once a man has fallen into perjury, absolution cannot be granted, as Federicus notes in Consil. 100, "factum tale est, debitor.," and Abbas follows in c. 1, col. penult., de iureiur.; Antonius de Butrio and Immolanus in c. debitores, de iureiur.; Romanus in Consil. 426, "in re praesenti," in princ.; and Baldus likewise in Authent. quod eis, in sin., Cod. de nuptiis, and in l. 1, in sin., Cod. si adversus rem iudicatam.

units.la: XX. Praeterea dato, sine praeiudicio veritatis, quod absolutio fieri possit a summo Pontifice absoluendo seipsum, hoc intelligitur cum causa: sine causa vero nullo modo fieri potest, ut de summo Pontifice in casu nostro notat, Abb. in d. c. 1. de consil. col. 3. & idem Abb. in c. quanto, col. 4. in verb. ex quo infero, de iureiur. & in c. propositum, col. 3. de concess. prab. Nam et alios sine causa Papa absolvere non potest, ut per gl. in d. c. quanto. Talis enim absolutio debet fieri causa cognita, ut notat Innoc. in c. ad aures, quod metus causa, Abb. in c. 1. col. penult. de iureiur. Causa intelligitur qui iuramentum esset illicitum, ut notat Cardinal. in Clement. 1. §. sin. in 17. qu. ff. de iureiur. vbi allegat Innocent. in cap. debitores, eodem titul. de iureiurando, & idem tradit Paulus de Castro in Consil. 216. praesuppositio sine praeiud. cio, col. 2. vbi inquit quod absolutio a iuramento peti non potest, nisi quando iuramentum extortum fuisset dolo, vel metu, vel super re illicita, puta super usuris: ut per Innocent. in c. si vero, de iureiur. secus vbi licitum fuit iuramentum, quia debet efficaciter observari, nec absolutio peti potest, sicut in c. quamvis de pact. in 6. & in cap. cum contingat, de iureiur. & in similibus casibus, quia si licitum fuit iuramentum, absolutio fieri non potest, ut tenent Archid. Ioann. Andreas & Dominicus nicus in dicto cap. quamuis: Angelus in l. si quis pro eo in princip. ff. de fideiuss. Roma. in Consil. 427. in casu proposito, in sin. Paulus de Castro in dicto Consil. 226. & in Auth. sacramenta puberum col. 3. Cod. fiduciar. vendi. Alex. in Consil. 42. super premissa, col. penult. lib. 1. & in Consil. 51. visis, lib 3. cum similibus quae nota sunt. Et ideo cum in casu nostro licitum fuerit iuramentum, ut Concilium fieret, p reformatione Ecclesiae, Papa efficaciter debuit illud observare, & nullomodo absolvi potuit. Et ita et dixi superioribus diebus cum ad lectionem meam accessissent reverendissimi Cardinales S. Crucis & Cossensis. Non obstant allegata s. in contrarium, quia responsio colligitur ex supradictis, & et formaliter respondendo: non obstat dictum Petri de Anch. ind. c. venerabilem, quia non est verum saltem in casu nostro, & contrarium tenent Anton. de But. & Imol. in c. 1. de const.
units.tr: XX. Moreover, granting, without prejudice to the truth, that absolution could be given by the supreme Pontiff to himself, this is to be understood as holding only with a cause; without a cause it cannot in any way be done, as the Abbot notes concerning the supreme Pontiff in our case, in the said chapter 1, de consilio, col. 3, and the same Abbot in chapter Quanto, col. 4, under the words "ex quo infero", de iureiurando, and in chapter Propositum, col. 3, de concessione praebendae. For the Pope cannot absolve others without a cause either, as the gloss notes in the said chapter Quanto. Such an absolution must be granted with the cause known, as Innocent notes in chapter Ad aures, quod metus causa; the Abbot in chapter 1, penultimate column, de iureiurando. The cause is understood to be that the oath was unlawful, as Cardinal notes in Clementine 1, §. sin., in 17 qu., ff., de iureiurando, where he cites Innocent in chapter Debitores, under the same title de iureiurando; and Paulus de Castro hands down the same in Consilium 216, "praesuppositio sine praeiudicio", col. 2, where he says that absolution from an oath can be sought only when the oath was extorted by fraud, or fear, or concerning an unlawful matter, such as usury, as by Innocent in chapter Si vero, de iureiurando; otherwise, where the oath was lawful, it must be effectively observed, nor can absolution be sought, as in chapter Quamvis, de pactis, in 6, and in chapter Cum contingat, de iureiurando, and in similar cases, because if the oath was lawful, absolution cannot be granted; so hold Archidiaconus, John Andreas and Dominicus in the said chapter Quamvis; Angelus in l. Si quis pro eo, in principio, ff., de fideiussoribus; Romanus in Consilium 427, in the case proposed, at the end; Paulus de Castro in the said Consilium 226, and in Auth. Sacramenta puberum, col. 3, Cod., Fiduciae vendi; Alexander in Consilium 42, "super premissa", penultimate column, lib. 1, and in Consilium 51, "visis", lib. 3, with other similar authorities that are well known. And therefore, since in our case the oath was lawful, so that a Council might be held for the reformation of the Church, the Pope was bound to observe it effectively, and could in no way be absolved. And so I said the same some days ago, when the most reverend Cardinals of Santa Croce and Cosenza came to my lecture. The authorities cited to the contrary do not stand, because the answer is gathered from what has been said above, and also, answering formally: the saying of Peter of Ancarano in the said chapter Venerabilem does not stand, because it is not true, at least in our case, and Antonius de Butrio and Imola hold the contrary in chapter 1, de constitutionibus.

units.la: XXI.
units.tr: XXI.

units.la: Quia non videtur, q quis seipsum absolvere possit, c. sin. de inst. nec obstat q illa regula sit de iure positivo, quia imo videtur de iure naturali, quia sibi ipsi quis imperare nec se prohibere potest, l. pen. ff. de arbit. Non obstat q alteri Papae absolutionem committere possit, quia illius faceret nomine Papae, & sic videretur ipse Papa facere per alium, ut Abbas declarat in c. sin. de inst. Praeterea & secundo dato, q Papa seipsum posset absolvere, hoc esset intelligendum in his in quibus habet potestatem absolvendi: secus videtur in his q sunt de iure naturali, vel divino, vel ex contractib. in quib. efficaciter obligatur, ut s. dictum est. Vel tertio concludenter respondetur, q dictum Petri de Anch. habet locum, put etiam ipse loquitur, qn subesset iusta causa absolvendi, sed nulla causa subsistente, absolutio nullo modo fieri potest per supradicta. Et ista est clara responsio quae de plano & indubitanter procedit. Non obstat q notat Abb. in d. c. sicut nostris, quia in casu nostro nihil facit: nam ibi Abb. loquitur qn fuit facta premissio in conclavi ante electionem Pontificis, sed in casu opposito fuit facta premissio a summo Pontifice, post eius promotionem. Praeterea Abb. ibi loquitur qn premissio facta erat in iudicium dignitatis Pontificalis, q non est in casu isto, in quo premissio respicit honorem & dignitatem Ecclesiae universalis, ut Concilium congregetur p reformatione Ecclesiae, & cultus divini, qui debet augeri, c. exparte, de const. c. vasa, de cons. dist. 1. & ibi glos. & favor Ecclesiae respicit utilitatem publicam, ut notat. per gl. 24. q. 4. in Can. quod ergo: facit tex. in l. 1. §. huius studii, ff. de iust. & iur. & ex his satisfactu sit secundo dubio: & Conclusio est, q Papa ex tali premissione efficaciter obligetur, & non possit aliquo modo absolvi, & q ad observationem iuramenti & premissionis astringi possit.
units.tr: It does not seem that a man can absolve himself, c. sin., de inst., and it is no objection that this rule is of positive law, since it seems rather to be of natural law, for a man can neither command himself nor prohibit himself, l. pen., ff. de arbit. It is no objection that the Pope could commit the absolution to another, for that person would act in the Pope's name, and so the Pope himself would seem to act through another, as Abbas explains in c. sin., de inst. Moreover, even granting, secondly, that the Pope could absolve himself, this would have to be understood only in matters in which he has the power to absolve: it seems otherwise in matters that belong to natural or divine law, or to contracts, by which he is effectively bound, as has been said above. Or, thirdly, a conclusive answer is this: the saying of Peter of Ancarano holds, as he himself speaks, where there is a just cause for absolution; but where no cause exists, absolution can in no way be given, by the reasons given above. This is a clear answer, which proceeds plainly and beyond doubt. It is no objection what Abb. notes in d. c. sicut nostris, because in our case it has no bearing: for there Abb. speaks of a promise made in the conclave before the election of the Pontiff, whereas in the case opposed a promise was made by the supreme Pontiff after his promotion. Moreover, Abb. there speaks of a promise made to the judgement of the Pontifical dignity, which is not our case, in which the promise regards the honour and dignity of the universal Church, that a Council be assembled for the reformation of the Church and of divine worship, which ought to be increased, c. exparte, de const.; c. vasa, de cons., dist. 1, and the gloss there; and the favour of the Church regards public utility, as the gloss notes on 24 q. 4, in Can. quod ergo. The text in l. 1 §. huius studii, ff. de iust. et iur., also supports this. By these points the second doubt is satisfied, and the conclusion is that the Pope is effectively bound by such a promise, that he cannot be absolved in any way, and that he can be compelled to observe the oath and the promise.

units.la: XXII.
units.tr: XXII.

units.la: Accedo ad tertium dubium, in quo breviter & conclusive respondet, q licet regulariter Concilio generale Papam iudicare non possit, ut not. per gl. in Can. nemo, 9. q. 3. & in Can. mandatis, 2. q. 5. Tamen in casibus specialibus, in quib. s. dictum est q Papa accusari & conveniri potest, dicendum est & concludendum, q Concilium generale sit iudex: hoc expresse ocs dicunt in causa haeresis & fidei, gl. & Domin. in Can. Anastasius 19. dist. Archidi. & Domin. in c. De favorem de haeret. in VI. Abb. in c. proposuit, de concess. prebend. colum. penult. in c. significasti, in 7. duob. de elect. & in c. fraternitatis in princ. de haered. Archiep. Florentinus in tit. 23. 6. 2. §. 6. in 3. parte eius summae, Cardin. in Consil. 150. quaesitum fuit, in 4. dub. Et tali casu considerandum est, quia non est speciale quod concilium sit iudex contra Papam in causa haeresis. Licet enim sit speciale quod Papa in causa haeresis iudicari possit, dicto Can. si Papa, 40. distinct. hoc posito videtur quod de iure communi Concilii sit iudex in tali casu: quia parum esset iura condere, nisi essent Magistratus qui illa exequerentur. l. 2. §. post originem ff. de orig. iuris: ideo statim quod statutum specialiter fuit, quod Papa in causa haeresis iudicari possit, videtur quod ordinario iure ab ipso Concilio iudicari debeat. Et ideo pari ratione videtur, quod etiam in omnibus casibus specialibus, in quibus Papa iudicari poterit, quod Concilium generale sit iudex. Et ad hoc facit quod notat Card. in dicto Consilio 150. in primo dubio: & quod in crimine notorio & scandaloso Papa a Concilio iudicari possit, late probat Roma. in Consil. 23. quaestio discutienda, per totum: & idem Abbas dicit in c. proposuit, de concess. prebend. col. fi. & Doctores omnes in locis s. allegatis in primo dubio, qui tenent q Papa iudicari possit, intelligitur a Concilio: & faciunt istam consequentiam, q si Papa iudicari potest, quod Concilium sit iudex. Et ideo in hoc non videtur laborandum, & in ista conclusione resider Card. Alexandrinus in Can. Synodum col. 2. 7. distinct. & ita breviter tertium dubium expeditum sit, quod satis cum primo coniunctum videtur, ut supra dictum est.
units.tr: I come to the third doubt, on which he answers briefly and conclusively that although a general Council cannot regularly judge the Pope, as is noted by the gloss in Can. Nemo, 9 q. 3, and in Can. Mandatis, 2 q. 5, nevertheless in the special cases in which it has been said that the Pope can be accused and convened, it must be said and concluded that the general Council is the judge. Gloss and Dominicus expressly say this in a case of heresy and faith, in Can. Anastasius, 19 dist., Archidiaconus, and Dominicus in c. De favorem, de haeret. in VI; the Abbot in c. Proposuit, de concess. prebend., col. penult.; in c. Significasti, in the seventh of the two, de elect.; and in c. Fraternitatis, in the beginning, de haered.; Archbishop Florentinus in tit. 23, §2, §6, in the third part of his Summa; Cardinal in Consilium 150, quaesitum fuit, in the fourth doubt. And in such a case it must be considered that it is not special that a council is judge against the Pope in a case of heresy. For although it is special that the Pope can be judged in a case of heresy (the said Can. Si Papa, 40 dist.), given this, it seems that by common law the Council is the judge in such a case. For it would be pointless to make laws unless there were magistrates to carry them out (l. 2, §Post originem, ff. de orig. iuris). Therefore, as soon as it was specially enacted that the Pope could be judged in a case of heresy, it seems that by ordinary law he ought to be judged by the Council itself. And so by the same reasoning it seems that in all the special cases in which the Pope can be judged, the general Council is the judge. To this also pertains what Cardinal notes in the said Consilium 150, in the first doubt; and that in a notorious and scandalous crime the Pope can be judged by a Council, Romanus proves at length in Consilium 23, Quaestio discutienda, throughout; and the same Abbot says so in c. Proposuit, de concess. prebend., col. last; and all the Doctors in the places cited above in the first doubt, who hold that the Pope can be judged, are understood to mean by a Council; and they draw this consequence, that if the Pope can be judged, the Council is the judge. Therefore in this there seems to be no need for labour, and in this conclusion Cardinal Alexandrinus rests, in Can. Synodum, col. 2, 7 dist. And so the third doubt is briefly disposed of, which seems sufficiently bound up with the first, as was said above.

units.la: XXIII.
units.tr: XXIII.

units.la: Ultimo superest quartum dubium, presupposito quod Concilium generale sit iudex in casibus specialiter supradictis. Quaeritur de modo congregandi Concilii, & ad hoc et paucis respondetur, quod licet congregatio Concilii generalis regulariter debeat fieri a summo Pontifice, 3. distinct. § porro, & in Can. 1. & per totum 17. dist. tamen quando Papa ipse accusari & iudicari debet, auctoritas Papae in causa eius propria non requiritur, ut decidit Bald. in c. olim, circa finem, in verbo idem ait, de rescrip. & tali casu congregatio Concilii spectat ad Cardinales, & sufficit maior pars praesentium, & non habet locum q dicitur in c. licet de elect. & idem Bald. dicit in dict. Canonum, col. pen. & q dictum est de Cardinalib. idē sequit Card. in Conf. 150. s. allegato, in 3. dubio: & idē concordat Archiep. Flor. in tertia parte suae summae in tit. 23. 6. 2. § 7. & cum dictis concordat Abb. in c. p. licet, col. 3. de elect. in ver. quis autem, ubi ad hoc allegat Huguti. in Can. fidu forte, 79. dist. & dicit Abbas, ibi hoc practicatum fuisse Pisis: ubi Cardinales congregati scripserunt ad Principes & Praelatos. Et si Cardinales non concordarent in congregando Concilium: ad Imper. spectat talis congregatio Concilii, ut Cardin. concludit in dicto consil. 150. in quarto dubio, ubi inducit textum in can. sin. 65. distinct. & hoc latius prosequitur in Cardin. in consilio praeallegato, & Archiep. Flor. in 3. parte tit. 23. cap. 2. §. 7. supra allegato. & in hoc quia per alios plene fuerat tractatum est, vt nunc non insisto.
units.tr: Finally there remains the fourth doubt, presupposing that the general Council is the judge in the specially mentioned cases above. The question concerns the manner of convening a Council, and to this it is answered briefly that although the convening of a general Council should regularly be done by the supreme Pontiff (3 dist. §Porro, and in Can. 1, and throughout 17 dist.), nevertheless when the Pope himself ought to be accused and judged, the authority of the Pope is not required in a case concerning himself, as Baldus decides in c. Olim, near the end, in the words "idem ait," de rescript.; and in such a case the convening of the Council belongs to the Cardinals, and a majority of those present suffices, and what is said in c. Licet, de elect., has no place here. The same Baldus says so in the said Canons, col. last, and what has been said about the Cardinals, Cardinal follows in the said Consilium 150, cited above, in the third doubt; and Archbishop Florentinus agrees in the third part of his Summa, tit. 23, §2, §7. And with these statements the Abbot agrees in c. Licet, col. 3, de elect., in the words "quis autem," where he cites Hugutio in Can. Fidu forte, 79 dist.; and the Abbot says that this was practised at Pisa, where the Cardinals assembled and wrote to princes and prelates. And if the Cardinals did not agree in convening a Council, the convening of a Council belongs to the Emperor, as the Cardinal concludes in the said Consilium 150, in the fourth doubt, where he cites the text in Can. Sin., 65 dist.; and he pursues this more fully in the Cardinal in the Consilium cited before, and Archbishop Florentinus in the third part, tit. 23, cap. 2, §7, cited above. And since this has been fully treated by others, I do not dwell on it now.

units.la: XXIV. Vlterius tamen insistendum est, quia reuocatur in dubium & quaeritur, An minor pars Cardinalium, pro congregatione Concilij generalis maiorem partem requirere possit & prima facie videbat dicendum non, quia licet in casu a dicto talis congregatio petatur ad Cardinales, vt supradictum fuit, videtur illis competere vt Collegio, & non vt singulis. vt Bald. dicit in c. olim, col. pen. de rescript. & ideo maior pars ipsorum requiritur, vt etiam Bald. expresse dicit, in d. c. olim, col. pen allegat l. quod maior ff. ad munic. & subiicit, quod maior pars praesentium requiritur dummodo duae partes praesentes sint, l. nulli ff. quod cuiusque vni. Et hoc videtur procedere secundum regulam, quae est quod in actibus Collegij, maior pars attenditur: vt per glossam in cap. cum sit de causa in verb. tract. de reb. Eccl. non alien. in 6. cum simil. Ergo nullo modo videtur quod minor pars alios possit requirere: & hoc idem videtur velle Card. in consil. 150. 5. allegato, vbi in 3. & 4. tuto concludit, quod si Collegium Cardinalium, ad quod pertinet congregatio Concilij, sit divisum, & non concordet tali convocatione, ad Imperatorem potestas devoluitur. Ergo videtur, quod una pars Cardinalium hoc facere non possit, saltem si sit minor pars. Et est communis conclusio, quod in actib. Universitatis vel Collegij debeant duae partes interesse, & maior pars illorum sufficit, & ita intelligitur Lege maior, vt Abb. concludit in c. cum omnes de constit. & in c. 1. sur. sin. de bon. qua fiunt a maiore parte capituli, notat Barto. in d. l. quod maior, cum similib. quae notata sunt. Non obstat quod minor pars tota potestatem consequatur propter aliorum contumaciam, vt notat Abb. in d. c. cum omnes, & in c. ex literis in vlt. notabili de elect. & in c. cum nobis col. penult. eod. tit. & idem tradit Bald. in l. nisi sit sin. Cod. quando non pe. par. quia hoc haberet locum quando illi de Collegio vel Universitate citati & requisiti fuissent a superiore, qui haberet potestatem citandi, prout loquuntur Doctores in locis paßim. Secus quando Collegium vel Universitas per seipsam absque superiore debet congregari, quia tunc precise duae partes requiruntur, vt notanter Abbas dicit in dict. c. in causis: & ideo, cum in isto casu Collegium Cardinalium debeat absque superiore congregari, videtur quod duae partes omnino debeant interesse, vt Abb. specialiter dicit in dict. c. in causis. Similiter non obstat, quod minor pars instante termino, intra quem actus vtilis vel necessarius debet expediri, potest maiorem partem convocare, & in eius negligentiam actum expedire, vt notat Anton. de Butr. & Abb. post Io. And. in cum nobis, col. penult. & sin. de elect. & Pet. de Anch. in c. 1. de consti. in chart. 15. verb. videndum est, quia responderi potest, quod in casu isto non instat terminus congregandi Concilium ipsis Cardinalibus, licet enim summo Pontifici esset praefixum tempus biennij, & illud elapsum sit, tamen ipsis reuerendissimis Cardinalibus, ad quos potestas congregandi Concilium devoluitur, non est statutum tempus, intra quod hoc facere debeant. Et si dicatur, cum Domini Cardinales in casu videant supplere negligentiam Papae, tempus duorum annorum statutum Papae, videtur respectum illis qui habent negligentiam supplere. c. licet, de suppl. neglig. Prelat. c. 2. de concess. praeben. facit tamen l. si ius ex ff. de iudic. Respondetur, quod ex quo etiam tempus aliorum duorum annorum decursum sit, ad Imperatorem vel alios talis potestas devoluta videtur: ita quod etiam omnes Cardinales nomina berent vlterius potestatem, & ita prima consideratione dicendum videbatur.
units.tr: XXIV. Yet further it must be dwelt upon, because it is called into doubt and asked whether a smaller part of the Cardinals can require a majority for the convening of a general Council. At first sight it seemed that it must be said no, because although in the case in question such a convening is sought from the Cardinals, as was said above, it seems to belong to them as a College and not as individuals, as Baldus says in c. Olim, col. last, de rescript.; and therefore a majority of them is required, as Baldus himself expressly says in the said c. Olim, col. last, citing l. Quod maior, ff. ad munic.; and he adds that a majority of those present is required, provided two parts are present (l. Nulli, ff. quod cuiusque universitatis). And this seems to follow the rule that in the acts of a College the majority is what counts, as by the gloss in c. Cum sit, de causa, in the words tract. de reb. Eccl. non alien., in 6, with similar passages. Therefore it seems in no way that a smaller part can require others; and Cardinal seems to hold the same view in the Consilium 150, cited fifth above, where in the third and fourth points he safely concludes that if the College of Cardinals, to which the convening of a Council pertains, is divided and does not agree on such a convocation, the power devolves to the Emperor. Therefore it seems that one part of the Cardinals cannot do this, at least if it is the smaller part. And it is the common conclusion that in the acts of a University or College two parts must be present, and the majority of these suffices; and the law "Maior" is so understood, as the Abbot concludes in c. Cum omnes, de constit., and in c. 1, sur. sin., de bon., which are done by the majority of the chapter; Bartolus notes it in the said l. Quod maior, with similar passages that have been noted. It is no objection that the smaller part obtains the whole power on account of the contumacy of the others, as the Abbot notes in the said c. Cum omnes, and in c. Ex literis, in the last notable passage, de elect., and in c. Cum nobis, col. penult., same title, and Baldus teaches the same in l. Nisi sit, sin., Cod. quando non pe. par., because that would hold when those of the College or University had been summoned and required by a superior who had the power of summoning, as the Doctors speak in many places. It is otherwise when a College or University must be assembled by itself without a superior, for then precisely two parts are required, as the Abbot notably says in the said c. In causis; and therefore, since in this case the College of Cardinals must be assembled without a superior, it seems that two parts must altogether be present, as the Abbot specially says in the said c. In causis. Likewise it is no objection that the smaller part, when a term is running out within which a useful or necessary act must be carried through, can summon the majority and carry the act through in their neglect, as Antonius de Butrio notes, and the Abbot after Johannes Andreae, in c. Cum nobis, col. penult. and last, de elect., and Petrus de Ancharano in c. 1, de constit., in chart. 15, in the words "videndum est." For it can be answered that in this case no term for convening the Council presses on the Cardinals themselves; for although a period of two years was fixed for the supreme Pontiff, and that has elapsed, nevertheless for the most reverend Cardinals, to whom the power of convening a Council devolves, no time has been set within which they must do this. And if it is said that, since the lords Cardinals in such a case seem to supply the negligence of the Pope, the two-year period fixed for the Pope seems to have regard to those who have the negligence to supply (c. Licet, de suppl. neglig. Prelat.; c. 2, de concess. praeben.), yet this is answered by l. Si ius, ff. de iudic. It is answered that since the time of another two years has also run out, the power seems to have devolved to the Emperor or others, so that even all the Cardinals would lose the power further; and so at first consideration it seemed that this must be said.

units.la: XXV. Sed praedictis non obstantibus, saltem in casu proposito contrarium de iure suaderi posse hoc modo videtur, quia, vt s. dictum est, cum in isto casu agatur de interesse Papae in congregatione Concilij, auctoritas eius non requiritur. vt Bald. expresse dicit in d. c. olim de rescript. vt supra dictum est. Cum non sit verisimile quod ipse velit consentire, ex quo contra eum congregatio, vt dicit Card. Alex. in Can. Synodum 17. dist. & videmus in simili quod licet aliquo casu consensus Praelati requiratur, c. causam quae de iudic. tamen si agatur contra Praelatum, eius consensus non requiritur, vt Doctores tradunt in c. docere, de rescript. & notatur per glossam 2. q. 7. una cum Paulus, & facit glossa magna, in fine, in l. cum non solum. Cod. de bon. qua libe. Modo sic quod dicitur de summo Pontifice, idem dicendum videtur de Cardinalibus, qui sunt apud eum vel Romae, qui nutu ipsius Papae moventur, quia quando caput suspectum est, etiam alii qui verisimiliter capiunt sequuntur suspecti sunt, & de illis idem quod de capite iudicatur, vt notat Vincent. quem Abb. post alios refert, & sequitur in c. 1. de iud. & idem notat Bald. in l. 1. col. 1. Cod. si Rector provin. & facit text. in c. accedens selec. 1. & quod ibi Abb. vt lic. non contestata unde de talib. Cardinalib. idem dicendum est quod de summo Pontifice, isti enim adhaerentes sunt summo Pontifici, & de adhaerentibus idem iudicatur quod de principali. c. ad apostolica, de re iudicat. in 6. nota c. 1. depos. st. prelato & in l. qua religiosis, vbi Angel. in princ. ff. de rei vend. Sicut ergo in tali congregatione Concilij Papa ipse, contra quem debet Concilium congregari, excluditur, ita Cardinales qui cum eo sunt, excludi videntur, & potestas congregandi Concilium, quae ad Cardinales devoluitur, intelligitur de Cardinalibus qui non adhaerent summo Pontifici, quibus ista facultas competere videtur.
units.tr: XXV. But notwithstanding what has been said, at least in the case proposed, the contrary may be argued from law in the following way. As was said above, since in this case the matter concerns the Pope's own interest in the assembly of a Council, his authority is not required. As Baldus expressly says in the chapter Olim, on rescripts, as was said above. Since it is not likely that he himself would consent, when the congregation is held against him, as Cardinal Alexander says on the canon Synodum, distinction 17, and since we see in a similar case that although the consent of a prelate is required in some cases (c. causam, on judgments), yet if the action is brought against a prelate, his consent is not required, as the Doctors teach on the chapter Docere, on rescripts, and as the gloss notes at 2 q. 7, together with Paulus, and the great gloss at the end of the law Cum non solum, Code, on goods that are freely...; so what is said of the supreme Pontiff should, it seems, be said of the Cardinals who are with him or at Rome, and who are moved by the nod of the Pope himself. For when the head is under suspicion, those who likely follow him are also under suspicion, and about them the same is judged as about the head, as Vincentius notes, whom Abbas, after others, cites and follows on c. 1, on judgments; and Baldus notes the same on law 1, col. 1, Code, if the rector of the province; and the text in c. accedens, Select. 1, supports this, and what Abbas says there, that it is not contested. Hence the same must be said of such Cardinals as of the supreme Pontiff, for these are adherents of the supreme Pontiff, and of adherents the same is judged as of the principal: c. ad apostolica, on res judicata, in the Sixth Book; note c. 1, on deposing a prelate; and in the law Qua religiosis, where Angelus at the beginning, Digest, on the sale of a thing. Therefore, just as in such a congregation of a Council the Pope himself, against whom the Council ought to be called, is excluded, so the Cardinals who are with him seem to be excluded, and the power of calling a Council, which devolves upon the Cardinals, is understood to belong to those Cardinals who do not adhere to the supreme Pontiff, to whom this faculty seems to pertain.

units.la: XXVI. Secundo principaliter haec conclusio sic deducitur. Quia ego video quod vbi agitur de interesse Ecclesiae particularis, si Platus negligens sit, potestas agendi ad Capitulum devoluitur, & Capitulo et negligente, devoluitur ad particulares Canonicos Ecclesiae, vt notat Abb. in c. 1. olim. col. 4. de test. vbi ad hoc allegat Innoc. in c. dilecti de maior. & obed. & idem Abb. in dict. de datis, col. 3. post Hostiensem & alios, & idem tenent Anton. de But. Card. & Imola in dict. c. in omnibus, Lapus in allegatione 51. disputatur in effectu, in princip. & ad hoc facit quod notatur per glossam in cap. vt supra. vedera, in princip. in verb. Aliqui, de elect. in sexto. & quod habetur in cap. si qui Presbyterorum, de reb. Eccles. non alien. 12. quaest. 2. Can. non licet: & per glossam in Can. constitutum, in gloss. penult. 16. quaest. 1. & in Can. si sacerdotes, in verb. moriendo, 16. quaest. 1. & in cap. quia contingit, in verbo indebite, de relig. ol. dom. cum simil. & tali casu de negligentia Praelati & Capituli constare dicitur, si quam primum potuerunt, non fuerint persecuti iura Ecclesiae, ut notat Ant. de Butr. Abb. & Imol. post Innoc. ind. cap. cum olim, de restit. Et idem concludit Lapus in alleg. 51. supra alleg. & secundum eos, alia monitio non requiritur: quod maxime haberet locum, si factum esset notorium, ut notatur per gloss. in Clem. quia contingit, de rel. & sed. dom. in verbo, negligentia, ut probatur in cap. Romana, §. notoria, decens. in sexto. & tradunt Aret. & Mode. in d. cap. cum olim, & ista ad casum nostrum optime applicari potest, ubi agitur de interesse universalis Ecclesiae, & maiori periculo, & ideo cautius agendum est. Cap. ubi periculum, de elect. in sexto. & text. in cap. bona clericis. 1. de postul. Praelat. vide Paulum de Castro cons. 419. visa puncto. col. 2. in antiquis secundum novam formam, & cons. seq. ubi plura dicit, quae ad propositum conferunt. Et concludendum videtur, quod pro interesse universalis Ecclesiae Reverendissimi Dni Cardinales existentes in regali dominio, etiam ipsi particulares & singuli instare possint pro universali concilio, propter negligentiam Papae, & Collegii Cardinalium. nam negligentia Papae constat per lapsum biennii, infra quod Papa promiserat concilium congregare, quia ubi appositum est tempus, alia monitio non requiritur ad probandum negligentiam, ut notat Baldus in l. 2. C. de spons. & Pet. de Anch. in consil. 64. pro clariori decisione, circa sin. Dom. in cap. licet Canon. §. 1. perillum textum de elect. in 6. & de summo Pontifice in casu isto, non est curandum, quia cum concilium principaliter contra ipsum debeat congregari, eius auctoritas non requiritur, ut s. dictum fuit: & ideo tali casu congregatio concilii Cardinalibus incumbit, ut etiam s. dictum est, & licet videatur hoc competere Cardinalibus uti Collegio, tamen quia Collegium deprehenditur in negligentia, haec potentia ad Cardinales particulares deferri videtur, ut s. dixi in Ecclesia particulari, ut Dd. omnes tenent in d. c. cum olim de restit. & in cap. dilecti de maio. & obed. Non obstat, quod non videtur apparere de negligentia Collegii Cardinalium, quia ad probandum negligentiam in facto negativo, de quo agitur, monitio requiritur, ut est auctor Innoc. in cap. extirpande. de praeben. quem Dd. communiter sequuntur, & notat Bal. in lib. hoc amplius. col. 4. C. de fideic. Bald. & Imol. in l. si mirata. ff. sol. m. tr. cum si. ut tradit Alex. in lit. stipulatus. col. 5. de V.O. quia ad hoc respondetur, quod illa doctrina non habet locum in casu nostro, ut in terminis dicunt Ant. de Butr. Abb. & Imol. post Innoc. ind. cap. cum olim. & concludunt, quod absque alia monitione, negligentia praelati & capituli probatur, si quamprimum potuerunt non fuerint iura Ecclesiae prosecuti: & idem tenet Lapus in d. alleg. 51. ut etiam s. dictum est. Et ideo dictum Innocentii videtur procedere, prout loquitur, qui agitur, quod quis incurrat aliquam poenam extrinsecam: Secus ubi agitur de negligentia, quae aliter non punitur, prout Dd. loquuntur in dict. cap. cum olim. & ita dicit Felinus in cap. si autem. col. 3. de rescript. Vel secundo respondeti potest, quod in casu isto agitur de facto notorio, ubi monitio non est necessaria, ut supra dixi allegando gloss. in d. Clem. quia contingit, & text. in cap. 1. §. notorio. de cens. in sexto.
units.tr: XXVI. Second, this conclusion is principally deduced in this way. Because I see that where the matter concerns the interest of a particular Church, if the prelate is negligent, the power of acting devolves upon the Chapter, and if the Chapter too is negligent, it devolves upon the individual canons of the Church, as Abbas notes on c. 1, Olim, col. 4, on testimony, where for this he cites Innocent on c. Dilecti, on majority and obedience; and the same Abbas on the said decision De datis, col. 3, after Hostiensis and others; and Antonius de Butrio, Cardinal, and Imola hold the same on the said c. In omnibus; Lapus in allegation 51, disputed in its effect, at the beginning; and to this pertains what is noted by the gloss in the chapter Ut supra, vedera, at the beginning, under the word Aliqui, on elections, in the Sixth Book; and what is found in the chapter Si qui Presbyterorum, on the alienation of church goods, 12 q. 2, canon Non licet; and by the gloss on the canon Constitutum, in the penultimate gloss, 16 q. 1; and on the canon Si sacerdotes, under the word moriendo, 16 q. 1; and in the chapter Quia contingit, under the word indebite, on religious houses, with similar cases. And in such a case negligence of the prelate and Chapter is said to be established if, as soon as they could, they did not pursue the rights of the Church, as Antonius de Butrio, Abbas and Imola note after Innocent on the chapter Cum olim, on restitution. And Lapus concludes the same in allegation 51 above; and according to them no other warning is required, which would especially hold if the fact had been made notorious, as is noted by the gloss in Clementine Quia contingit, on religious houses, under the word negligentia, as is proved in the chapter Romana, §. notoria, on censures, in the Sixth Book; and Aretinus and Modernus teach this on the said chapter Cum olim. And this can be very well applied to our case, where the matter concerns the interest of the universal Church and a greater danger, and therefore one must proceed more cautiously: c. ubi periculum, on elections, in the Sixth Book; and the text in c. Bona clericis, 1, on the postulation of prelates. See Paulus de Castro, consilium 419, at the point seen, col. 2, in the old form according to the new, and the following consilium, where he says many things that serve our purpose. And it seems to be concluded that for the interest of the universal Church the most Reverend Lords Cardinals existing in the royal dominion, even each of them individually, can press for a universal council, on account of the negligence of the Pope and the College of Cardinals. For the negligence of the Pope is established by the lapse of two years, within which the Pope had promised to convene a council; for where a time has been fixed, no further warning is required to prove negligence, as Baldus notes on law 2, Code, on betrothals, and Pietro d'Ancarano in consilium 64, for a clearer decision, near the end; Dominus on the chapter Licet Canon, §. 1, on that text on elections, in the Sixth Book. And concerning the supreme Pontiff in this case, no care need be taken, because since the Council ought principally to be convened against him, his authority is not required, as was said above; and therefore in such a case the convening of the Council falls to the Cardinals, as was also said above. And although this may seem to belong to the Cardinals as a College, yet because the College is found to be negligent, this power seems to devolve upon the individual Cardinals, as I said above of a particular Church, as all the Doctors hold on the said chapter Cum olim, on restitution, and on the chapter Dilecti, on majority and obedience. It is no objection that the negligence of the College of Cardinals does not seem to appear, because to prove negligence in a negative fact, which is what is at issue, a warning is required, as the author Innocent says on the chapter Extirpande, on benefices, whom the Doctors commonly follow, and Baldus notes on the law Hoc amplius, col. 4, Code, on trust-bequests; Baldus and Imola on the law Si mirata, Digest, on the solution of money; as Alexander teaches on the stipulation Stipulatus, col. 5, on verbal obligations. For to this it is answered that that doctrine has no place in our case, as Antonius de Butrio, Abbas and Imola after Innocent say in terms on the chapter Cum olim; and they conclude that without any other warning, the negligence of the prelate and Chapter is proved if, as soon as they could, they did not pursue the rights of the Church; and Lapus holds the same in the said allegation 51, as was also said above. And therefore Innocent's statement seems to apply as he speaks, where it concerns someone incurring some external penalty; otherwise where it concerns negligence, which is not otherwise punished, as the Doctors speak in the said chapter Cum olim. And so Felinus says on the chapter Si autem, col. 3, on rescripts. Or, secondly, it may be answered that in this case the matter concerns a notorious fact, where a warning is not necessary, as I said above, citing the gloss on the said Clementine Quia contingit, and the text in c. 1, §. notorio, on censures, in the Sixth Book.

units.la: XXVII.
units.tr: XXVII.

units.la: Tertio principaliter hoc idem comprobatur, quia propter scandalum quod imminet, Ecclesia universalis opprimi videtur, & ut talis oppressio removeatur, Concilium generale debet congregari, & in hoc videtur tractari de defensione Ecclesiae universalis. unde sicut ubi agitur de defensione particularis Ecclesiae admittuntur Canonici particulares, etiamsi essent excommunicati vel periuri; ut est tex. in cap. dilecti. de excess. & gloss. ibi, in verbo, interlocutor, & notatur per gloss. in cap. cum Episcopus. de excess. & dicit Abb. post Hostiensem in dict. cap. dilecti, col. 2. quod ubi agitur de repellendo malo Praelato, dicitur defensio necessaria, ideo etiam excommunicatus admittitur, & facit gloss. in dict. cap. ut circa, in prin. de elect. in sexto. in verbo, Aliqui, cum similibus, sicut alleg. ita videtur, quod pro defensione universalis Ecclesiae, Cardinales singulares debeant admitti, & ex omnibus supradictis conclusio videtur.
units.tr: Thirdly, the same point is proved chiefly because, on account of the impending scandal, the universal Church seems to be oppressed; and so that such oppression may be removed, a general council ought to be convened, and in this matter the defence of the universal Church seems to be treated. Hence, just as where the defence of a particular Church is at issue, particular canons are admitted even if they were excommunicated or perjured, as is the text in cap. Dilecti, De excessibus, and the gloss there, s.v. "interlocutor", and it is noted by the gloss in cap. Cum Episcopus, De excessibus; and Abbas, after Hostiensis, says in the said cap. Dilecti, col. 2, that where the question is of removing a bad prelate, the defence is called necessary, and so even an excommunicate is admitted; and the gloss in the said cap. Ut circa, at the beginning, De electione, in sexto, s.v. "Aliqui", with similar passages, as cited, agrees. Thus it seems that for the defence of the universal Church individual Cardinals ought to be admitted, and from all the above the conclusion appears.

units.la: XXVIII.
units.tr: XXVIII.

units.la: Quod reverendissimi Dni Cardinales, qui in Regali dominio reperiuntur, convocare possunt concilium generale nomine Collegii Cardinalium, quia totum ius collegii in ipsis residere videtur, ex quo alii adhaerentes Papae simul cum Papa in casu isto excluduntur. Nam ius Collegii, etiam in uno solo conservari & residere potest, l. sicut. §. sin. ff. quod cuiusq; universit. Et ideo unus solus qui remanet de Capitulo, Praelatum eligere potest, ut per gl. & Dd. in c. gratia. de postul. praelat. & in uno solo Cardinali ius Collegii residere potest, & ipse poterit Papa eligere, ut notatur per gl. & ibi Abbas in Clem. ne Romani, §. porro, in verbo, Omnes, de elect. & non solum nomine Collegii, sed etiam uti singulares propter negligentiam Papae & Collegii debent admitti pro interesse universalis Ecclesiae, ut s. dictum est, & ex his iustificatur & comprobatur, quod in propositio notare voluit Petrus de Monte in libello de potestate Papae, colum. 16. in verf. 6. quaero, prout illum refert fidelis recitator Felinus in cap. super literis. in 5. charta, verf. an sua sit iurisdictio, de rescript. vbi inquit, quod in congregatione Concilii generalis minor pars eorum, qui debent interesse, potest citare maiorem partem, vel melius dicamus, quod minor pars eorum qui in generali Concilio interesse debent, potest requirere maiorem partem, quia citatio est actus superior, requisitio vero etiam inter pares fieri potest, ut notat Innocent. in cap. cum nobis. col. sin. de elect. & ibi Anton. de Butr. in col. penult. verf. venio ad secundum. & Abb. in fine col. & si alii requisiti non venerint, illa minor pars potest pronunciare, se constituere concilium generale, & apud eos esse totam iurisdictionem Concilii, ut Petrus de Monte concludit in loco prǣallegato: nam talicasu, cum Cardinales etiam particulares agere possint pro interesse vniuersalis Ecclesiæ, & defensionem vniuersalis Ecclesiæ suscipere, vt s. dictum est, & hoc debeat fieri apud Concilium (cum alius non sit iudex per supradicta) videntur alii requisiti, qui debent in Concilio generali interesse, tenentur coparere pro interesse vniuersalis Ecclesiæ. Et hoc clarum est, si nomine Collegii Cardinalium requisitio facta sit in stante, quod ius Collegij in dictis Cardinalibus resideret, vt s. dixi. Tali enim casu omnes, qui debent in Concilio interesse, citari possunt, & non venientes excluduntur propter eorum contumaciam: & ius totum Concilii in præsentibus resideret: quia citatio fuit facta per superiorem, i.e. per Collegium Cardinalium, cui hoc ius congregandi Concilium incumbit, vt s. dictum est, per ea quæ notat Abb. in d.c. cum nobis, in c. in causis, de elect. cum similib. s. allegatis. Et idem tamen videtur dicendum, si reuerendissimi Cardinales, suo nomine particulari instarent pro interesse Ecclesiæ vniuersalis, vt s. dictum est: quia, qua ratione propter interesse vniuersalis Ecclesiæ, ipsi etiam particulariter petere possunt, vt Concilium congregetur (cum alius non sit iudex) pari ratione, alii qui interesse debent in Concilio requisiti, propter hoc debent venire, pro ipso interesse vniuersalis Ecclesiæ: alias propter eorum negligentiam, potestas totius Concilii videtur in præsentibus tñ residere, prout dicit Pet. de Monte in loco s. allegato: & hoc etiam declarabitur respondendo ad allegatas. in contrarium. Nō obstat ergo, dum s. primò dicitur, q; potestas congregandi Concilium videtur competere Collegio Cardinalium, quia dato quod verum sit Collegium, videtur residere in istis: quia alii excluduntur simul cum summo Pontifice in isto casu per supradicta. Secundò respondetur, q; etiam dictis Cardinalibus (vt singulis) videtur hoc competere, propter interesse vniuersalis Ecclesiæ, vt supradictum fuit. Nō obstat, q; si Collegium Cardinalium diuisum sit, q; ad Imperatorem spectat congregatio Concilii, Cardin. dicit in d. cauf. 150. quia in casu nostro non videtur diuisum, ex quo ius Collegii residet in illis, qui à summo Pontifice recesserunt, vt s. dictum est. Vel secundò, dictū Cardinalis intelligitur, nisi aliqui particulares Cardinales hanc prouinciam suscipérent, quia possunt per ea quæ s. dicta sunt. Et per hoc tollitur, q; in contrarium dicitur de duabus partibus quæ requiruntur in actibus Collegii, quia hoc fieri à particularibus potest expediri, propter aliorum negligentiam, propter quam etiā ius Collegii vel vniuersitatis videtur residere in minori parte, vt s. dictum est. Non obstat q; maior pars non potest dici contumax, cum non sit citata per superiorem, quia sufficit q; sit requisita. Et in stante de præsenti interesse vniuersalis Ecclesiæ debuit comparere, aliter negligens videtur, & ad præsentes videtur rota potestas pertinere, sicut s. dixi de Prælato negligente prosequi iura Ecclesiæ, potestas defertur ad Capitulū: & Capitulo negligente, devoluitur potestas ad particulares Canonicos Ecclesiæ: & negligentia Prælati, & Capituli deprehenditur, si quamprimū possunt nō sequuntur iura Ecclesiæ: ita videtur in proposito, q; potestas remaneat penes minorē, ex quo maior pars requisita non venit, & non procurat interesse Ecclesiæ cum possit, & maximè in casu notorio, prout s. dictum fuit: & quia videtur minor trāgressio de una parte vniuersitatis ad aliam, quàm de Prælato vel Capitulo ad particulares: quia in habentibus similitudinem facilius est tramitis s.; §. item per acceptilationem, inst. quib. mod. toll. obl. l. sinrem. §. item quacunq;, ff. de rei vend. c. cum ab Apostolica, de statu, quæ fiunt à Prælatis. Vltimò non obstat, q; Collegio Cardinalium nec ipsis reuerendissimis Cardinalibus non sit præfixus terminus congregandi Concilium, vt s. dicebatur, quia stante interesse Ecclesiæ alius terminus non requiritur, & eo ipso q; non prouident, vt consulatur Ecclesiæ cum possint, dicuntur esse in negligentia, vt Dd. dicunt in d.c. cum olim, de testi. & supr. declaratum est. Non obstat, quod in casu isto Reuerendiss. Cardinales videntur habuisse terminum biennii in supplendo negligentiam Papæ, vt supr. dicebatur. Et illud tempus videtur etiam elapsum, quia responderi potest, quod dum essent Reuerendiss. Cardinales penes summum Pontificem, nō potuerunt talem congregationem facere, ideo ipsis impeditis tempus non currit, c. quia diversitatem, de constit. prob. Præterea non agitur hic de supplendo negligentiam Papæ, quia ex alio capite talis potestas congregandi Concilium ipsis reuerendissimis Cardinalibus immediatè concediuntur: quia cum sit Concilium congregandum contra ipsum summum Pontificem eius auctoritas nō requiritur, vt supra dictum est: & si hactenus hoc non fecerunt, excusati fuerunt, quia erant apud ipsum Pontificem, & hoc facere non potuerunt; Cardin. d. c. quia diversitatem. Et ita remotis omnibus allegatis supra in contrarium firmata remanet talis conclusio, quæ ad practicam, hoc modo reduci potest. Quod Reuerendiss. Cardinales congregentur in loco idoneo, pro Concilio prout eis videbitur, & ibi congregati (promouentibus serenissimo Imperatore & Christianissima Regia Maiestate) ipsi nomine Collegii Cardinalium, quod in eis representatur, & etiā nomine ipsorum particulariter omni meliori modo &c. faciant requirere omnes qui in Concilio generali interesse debent, vt veniant ad congregationem Concilii pro maximo & euidenti interesse Vniuersalis Ecclesiæ & totius Religionis Christianæ: quibus non venientibus, eorum negligentia deprehenditur, propter quam totum ius Concilii generalis residebit in præsentibus & ipsi pronuntiabunt se in effectu constituere Concilium generale, & apud eos esse totam iurisdictionem Concilii generalis, vt concludit Petrus de Monte in loco supra allegato, cuius decisio prima facie videbatur non esse secundum regulas iuris communis: sed tamen ex his, quæ supra dixi iustificari videtur. LAUS DEO.
units.tr: The most reverend lords the Cardinals, who are found in the royal dominion, can convene a general council in the name of the College of Cardinals, because the whole right of the College seems to reside in them, since the other adherents of the Pope, together with the Pope himself, are excluded in this case. For the right of a college can be preserved and can reside even in a single member, l. Sicut, §. sin., ff. Quod cuiusque universitatis; and therefore the one remaining member of a chapter can elect a prelate, as the gloss and the Doctors say on c. Gratia, De postulatione praelatorum; and the right of the College can reside in one Cardinal, and he may elect the Pope, as is noted by the gloss and Abbas there, in Clem. Ne Romani, §. Porro, s.v. "Omnes", De electione; and not only in the name of the College, but also individually, because of the negligence of the Pope and the College, they ought to be admitted on account of the interest of the universal Church, as has been said above. From this it is justified and proved what Peter of Monte wished to point out in the proposition in his book on the power of the Pope, col. 16, in the section "6. quaero", as the faithful reporter Felinus recites it in cap. Super literis, on the fifth page, section "an sua sit iurisdictio", De rescriptis, where he says that in the convocation of a general council, the lesser part of those who ought to take part can summon the greater part, or, to put it better, the lesser part of those who ought to take part in a general council can require the greater part, because a summons is an act of a superior, whereas a requisition can be made even between equals, as Innocent notes in cap. Cum nobis, at the end of the column, De electione, and there Antonius de Butrio in the penultimate column, section "venio ad secundum", and Abbas at the end of the column. And if the others who were required do not come, that lesser part can declare that it constitutes a general council, and that the whole jurisdiction of the Council resides with them, as Peter of Monte concludes in the place cited above. For in such a case, since even particular Cardinals can act for the interest of the universal Church and undertake the defence of the universal Church, as has been said above, and since this ought to be done before the Council (there being no other judge by the foregoing), the others who were required and ought to take part in the general council are held to appear for the interest of the universal Church. And this is clear if the requisition was made in the name of the College of Cardinals while the right of the College resided in those Cardinals, as I said above. For in such a case all who ought to take part in the Council can be cited, and those not coming are excluded on account of their contumacy, and the whole right of the Council would reside in those present, because the citation was made by a superior, that is, by the College of Cardinals, to whom the right of convening the Council belongs, as has been said above, by what Abbas notes in the said cap. Cum nobis, and in cap. In causis, De electione, with similar passages cited above. But the same seems to be said also if the most reverend Cardinals, in their own particular name, should press for the interest of the universal Church, as has been said above; for, on the same ground that because of the interest of the universal Church they themselves may individually ask that a Council be convened (there being no other judge), by the same reasoning the others who ought to take part in the Council, when required, ought to come, for that same interest of the universal Church; otherwise, on account of their negligence, the power of the whole Council seems in the present circumstances to reside still in those present, as Peter of Monte says in the place cited above. This will also be made clear by answering the arguments alleged to the contrary. It is no objection, therefore, when it is first said that the power of convening a Council seems to belong to the College of Cardinals, because, granting that the College is true, it seems to reside in these men, since the others are excluded together with the supreme Pontiff in this case, by the foregoing. Secondly, it is answered that this too seems to belong to the said Cardinals (taken individually), on account of the interest of the universal Church, as was said above. It is no objection that, if the College of Cardinals were divided, the convening of the Council belongs to the Emperor, as the Cardinal says in the said cause 150; for in our case it does not seem divided, since the right of the College resides in those who have withdrawn from the supreme Pontiff, as has been said above. Or, secondly, the statement of the Cardinal is understood to apply unless some particular Cardinals undertake this task, since they can do so by what has been said above. And by this is removed what is objected to the contrary concerning the two parts required in the acts of the College, because this can be accomplished by particular members, on account of the negligence of the others, on account of which also the right of the College or the university seems to reside in the lesser part, as has been said above. It is no objection that the greater part cannot be called contumacious, since it has not been cited by a superior, because it is enough that it has been required. And at the present moment, on account of the present interest of the universal Church, it ought to have appeared; otherwise it seems negligent, and the whole power seems to pertain to those present, as I said above concerning a prelate negligent in pursuing the rights of the Church: the power passes to the chapter, and if the chapter is negligent, the power devolves to the individual canons of the Church. And the negligence of a prelate and of a chapter is shown if, as soon as they can, they do not pursue the rights of the Church. So in the present case it seems that the power remains with the lesser part, since the greater part that was required has not come and does not look after the interest of the Church although it could, and especially in a notorious case, as was said above; and also because the transfer from one part of the university to another seems a smaller departure than from a prelate or chapter to individuals, since in things having similar likeness the path is easier, as in §. item per acceptilationem, Inst. Quibus modis tollitur obligatio; l. Sin rem, §. item quaecunque, ff. De rei vindicatione; cap. Cum ab Apostolica, De statu monachorum, which are done by prelates. Lastly, it is no objection that no fixed term has been set for the College of Cardinals, or for the most reverend Cardinals themselves, for convening the Council, as was said above, because while the Church's interest lasts no other term is required; and by the very fact that they do not provide, in order that the Church may be consulted although they can, they are said to be in negligence, as the Doctors say on the said cap. Cum olim, De testibus, and as was declared above. It is no objection that in this case the most reverend Cardinals seem to have had a term of two years for making up for the Pope's negligence, as was said above. And that time also seems to have elapsed, because it can be answered that while the most reverend Cardinals were in the presence of the supreme Pontiff, they could not hold such an assembly; therefore, while they were hindered, the time does not run, cap. Quia diversitatem, De constitutionibus. Moreover, we are not here treating of making up for the Pope's negligence, because on another ground such power of convening a Council is granted directly to the most reverend Cardinals themselves; for since the Council is to be convened against the supreme Pontiff himself, his authority is not required, as has been said above. And if hitherto they have not done this, they are excused, because they were with the Pope himself and could not do it, as the Cardinal says on the said cap. Quia diversitatem. And so, with all the arguments alleged above to the contrary set aside, there remains a conclusion which can be reduced to practice in this way: that the most reverend Cardinals assemble in a suitable place for the Council, as seems fit to them, and there assembled (with the most serene Emperor and the most Christian Royal Majesty promoting it), they themselves in the name of the College of Cardinals, which is represented in them, and also in their own names individually, by every better means, etc., cause all who ought to take part in the general council to be required to come to the convening of the Council, for the greatest and most evident interest of the universal Church and of the whole Christian religion. If they do not come, their negligence is shown, on account of which the whole right of the general Council will reside in those present, and they will declare that in effect they constitute a general council, and that the whole jurisdiction of the general Council resides with them, as Peter of Monte concludes in the place cited above; whose decision at first sight seemed not to accord with the rules of the common law, but nevertheless it seems to be justified by what I have said above. PRAISE BE TO GOD.

units.la: PHILIPPVS DECIVS PAPIÆ.
units.tr: PHILIPPUS DECIUS, OF PAVIA.

units.la: SERMO
units.tr: SERMON

units.la: SERMO DE EADEM MATERIA, EDITVS PER EXCELLENTISSIMVM VTRIVSQVE Iuris Doctorem Philippum Decium siue de Dexio, Medio- lanensem, pro justificatione Concilii Pisani, nunc Mediolani residentis.
units.tr: THE SAME SUBJECT, A SERMON PUBLISHED BY THE MOST EXCELLENT DOCTOR OF BOTH LAWS PHILIPPUS DECIUS, OR DE DEXIIS, OF MILAN, IN DEFENCE OF THE COUNCIL OF PISA, NOW RESIDING AT MILAN.

units.la: SVMMARIVM.
units.tr: SUMMARY.

units.la: 1 Non esse iudicandum de actionibus, priusquam causa illarum cognita fuerint.
units.tr: 1 Actions ought not to be judged before their causes have been known.

units.la: 2 Omnium hominum atque ipsius Iulii II. confessione, Ecclesia reformatione in capite & in membris indigebat.
units.tr: 2 By the confession of all men, and of Julius II himself, the Church stood in need of reformation in head and in members.

units.la: 3 Concilium tantum generalibus Ecclesia reformari potest.
units.tr: 3 The Church can be reformed only by a general council.

units.la: 4 An Concilium Pisis indictum sit legitimum.
units.tr: 4 Whether the Council called at Pisa was lawful.

units.la: 5 Congregatio Concilii generalis regulariter spectat ad summum Pontificem, tamen duobus de causis Concilium sine consensu Papae congregari potest.
units.tr: 5 The convening of a general council regularly belongs to the supreme Pontiff; yet for two reasons a council may be convened without the Pope's consent.

units.la: 6 Vbi caput suspectum est, etiam alii qui capiti sequuntur, suspectissimi, proinde duo aut tres Cardinales Concilium convocare potuerunt.
units.tr: 6 Where the head is under suspicion, those who follow the head are also most under suspicion; therefore two or three Cardinals were able to convene the council.

units.la: 7 Vbi agitur de interesse Ecclesiae particularis, si Prelatus fuerit negligens, potestas agendi ad Capitulum devoluitur.
units.tr: 7 Where the interest of a particular Church is at stake, if the prelate is negligent, the power of acting passes to the chapter.

units.la: 8 Responsio ad obiectiones bullae Iulii II. contra Concilii Pisani convocationem.
units.tr: 8 Reply to the objections in the bull of Julius II against the convening of the Council of Pisa.

units.la: 9 Papa correctioni fraternae subiicitur.
units.tr: 9 The Pope is subject to fraternal correction.

units.la: 10 Cardinalibus, ut se contra Iulii violentiam defenderent, praesidio armato uti licuit.
units.tr: 10 The Cardinals were permitted to use an armed guard to defend themselves against the violence of Julius.

units.la: 11 Falso Pisani Cardinales crimine falsi accusantur a Iulio II.
units.tr: 11 The Cardinals of Pisa are falsely accused by Julius II of the crime of forgery.

units.la: 12 Excusationes quibus Iulius II. persuadere vult se non fuisse obligatum ad Concilii convocationem.
units.tr: 12 The excuses by which Julius II seeks to persuade us that he was not bound to convene the council.

units.la: 13 Concilium Lateranense haberi non potuit Romae, propter violentiam Iulii II. a quo ratio vocationis sua tuto & libere exigi non poterat.
units.tr: 13 The Lateran Council could not be held at Rome, because of the violence of Julius II, by whom the reason for the summons could not be safely and freely demanded.

units.la: ANtequam perscruteris, non reprehendas, intellige prius, & tunc increpa. Verba sunt Salomonis, Damaso Papa referente in Can. eorum 11. quaest. 3.
