In labyrinthum enim erroris incidit, qui prius iudicat quam intelligat: ut legitur in Can. sciendum. 29. distin. & tale iudicium temerarium est, quod non nocet illi, de quo temere iudicatur, sed ei qui iudicat, Canon. temerarium 11. quaest. 3. nam cogitare & meditari quis debet, quid loquatur, 50. distinct. Can. ponderet. in princ. Virtus lenta est, & omnia percunctatur, iniquitas autem omnia praecipitat, de poenit. dist. 3. Canon. inter haec hircum. Non sum nescius, Reverendissimi Patres & supremi gradus Antistites, quam plurimos admirari, quod a Reverendissimis paternitatibus vestris Concilium Pisis indictum fuerit, & quidem a minori parte Cardinalium, cum talis facultas prius summo Pontifici competere videatur, & eo negligente ad Collegium Cardinalium deferatur. Sed illos rogatos quamplurimum esse velim, ne quod mature & legitime factum fuit, prius damnent & iudicent, quam singula recte intelligant, quia ex infra dicendis liquido apparebit, Concilium iuridice & legitime Pisis indictum fuisse, ad cuius rei evidentem demonstrationem sic proceditur.
units.tr: Before you examine, do not rebuke; first understand, and then reprove. These are the words of Solomon, cited by Pope Damasus in Can. eorum, 11 q. 3. For he falls into the labyrinth of error who judges before he understands, as is read in Can. sciendum, 29 dist.; and such a rash judgement does not harm the one about whom it is rashly made, but the one who judges, Can. temerarium, 11 q. 3. For a man ought to think and reflect on what he says, 50 dist. Can. ponderet, in princ. Virtue is slow and examines all things, but iniquity rushes headlong into everything, de poen. dist. 3, Can. inter haec hircum. I am not unaware, most reverend Fathers and bishops of the highest rank, that very many are amazed that the Council was convened at Pisa by your most reverend paternities, and indeed by a minority of the Cardinals, since such a power seems to belong first to the supreme Pontiff, and, if he is negligent, to pass to the College of Cardinals. But I would very much like those who ask this not to condemn and judge beforehand what was done in good time and lawfully, before they have understood each point properly; for from what will be said below it will clearly appear that the Council was convened at Pisa justly and lawfully. To demonstrate this matter plainly, we proceed as follows.

units.la: II. Constat enim & omnibus exploratum est, Ecclesiam universalem, quae congregatio fidelium dicitur, Can. Ecclesia. de consecr. distin. 1. indigere reformatione in capite & in membris, nam primo de capite, Leo Papa sanctissimus scribit, totius famulatus Domini status & ordo nitabit, si quod requiritur in corpore, non invenitur in capite, Can. miramur 61. distinct. ipse enim summus Pontifex maiorem zelum in cultu Dei habere debet, quam alii Christiani, ut dicitur in Can. officii 24 quaest. 1. & capite languescente caetera corporis membra inficiuntur, 6. quaest. 1. Can. ex merito. & in Can. sunt plurimi. §. verum. ead. causa & quaestione. Secundo idem de membris dicendum est, non solum enim Episcopi & Presbyteri, sed omnes Clerici, & omnes qui domui Dei inserviunt, magnopere praeuidere debent, ut totum populum sermone, conversatione, & operibus praecedant, quia vehementer Ecclesiam Dei destruit, meliores esse laicos quam clericos, Canon. qualis 8. q. 1. vita enim Pastoris debet esse exemplar subditis, 2 quaest. 7. Canon. cum pastoris, & non sufficit quod Praelatiae qualem vitam cum subditis ducant, Canon. sina. 8. quaest. 1. & Praelatus vilissimus reputatur, nisi sicut honore praestantior est, ita scientia & sanctitate praecellat, Canon. vilissimus 1. quaestio. 1. Delicta namque Praelatorum facile transeunt in exemplum subditorum: & scandalum generatur mentibus laicorum, dicentium, ubi est Deus clericorum, ut legitur in cap. magna, de voto: & sicut Praelati debent, quod si pervera perpetrant, tot moribus digni sunt quot ad subditos suos perditionis exempla transmittunt, Can. praecipue 11. quaest. 3.
units.tr: II. For it is established, and known to all, that the universal Church, which is called the congregation of the faithful, Can. Ecclesia, de consecr. dist. 1, stands in need of reformation in head and in members. For first, concerning the head, Pope Leo, most holy, writes that the state and order of the whole service of the Lord will falter if what is required in the body is not found in the head, Can. miramur, 61 dist. For the supreme Pontiff himself ought to have greater zeal in the worship of God than other Christians, as is said in Can. officii, 24 q. 1, and when the head languishes the other members of the body are infected, 6 q. 1, Can. ex merito, and in Can. sunt plurimi, §. verum, same cause and question. Second, the same must be said of the members. For not only bishops and presbyters, but all clergy, and all who serve the house of God, ought greatly to take care to go before the whole people in speech, conduct and works; because it greatly destroys the Church of God that the laity should be better than the clergy, Can. qualis, 8 q. 1. For the life of a pastor ought to be an example to his subjects, 2 q. 7, Can. cum pastoris; and it is not enough that prelates lead what kind of life with their subjects, Can. sina, 8 q. 1; and a prelate is regarded as most worthless unless, as he is more outstanding in honour, so he excels in learning and holiness, Can. vilissimus, 1 q. 1. For the faults of prelates easily pass into an example for their subjects, and a scandal is produced in the minds of the laity, who say, "Where is the God of the clergy?", as is read in cap. magna, de voto; and just as prelates ought, if they commit perverse acts, to be worthy of as many punishments as the examples of ruin they pass on to their subjects, Can. praecipue, 11 q. 3.

units.la: III. Ad talem igitur necessariam Ecclesiae universalis reformationem mediante salutari remedio Concilii procedendum est: in Conciliis enim velut in quadrato lapide sanctae fidei structura consurgit, & cuiuslibet vitae atque actionis norma constituit, ut inquit tex. in Can. sicut sancti 15. dist. & frequens Conciliorum generalium celebratio, agri Dominici praecipua cultura est, quae spinas, & tribulos haeresum, errorum, schismatum extirpat, excessus corrigit, deformata reformat, & vineam Domini ad frugem uberrimam fructus adducit: ut habetur in Canon. Constantiensis Concilii, in Canon. frequens: talis enim reformatio in Concilio generali maturius conficitur: quia ibi quamplures convocantur, & omnes in unum conveniunt, Can. Canones. §. Concilii vero, 15. distinct. unde firmius reputatur id quod a pluribus quam a paucioribus, cap. prudentiam, in princ. de offic. deleg. & facilius invenitur, quod a pluribus quaeritur, Can. sin. 20. distinct. Et magis integrum est iudicium, quod plurimorum sententia confirmatur, 64. distinct. can. extra conscientiam, cap. per hoc, §. verum. vbi domin. de haret. in sexto. Et ista ratione, quia factum in Concilio firmius reputatur, clausula generalis non tollit constitutiones conciliares, sed specialis derogatio requiritur, ut notat Archidiac. in cap. 1. de constitut. in sexto. Bald. in l. humanum, C. de legi. Et hac ratione Episcopus contra constitutionem conciliarem dispensare non potest, ut notatur per glossam in cap. cum dilecti. in verbo aetate, de elect. & in tali congregatione Concilii, quod omnino fieri debeat pro reformatione universalis Ecclesiae, omnes conveniunt, & fateri necesse est: Et ipse summus Pontifex non negat nec negare potest, cum ad hoc se cum voto & iuramento astrinxerit, & hac ratione Concilium Romae indixerit.
units.tr: III. Therefore, to such a necessary reformation of the universal Church, the Council must be undertaken as a salutary remedy. For in councils, as in a square stone, the structure of holy faith rises up and establishes the rule of every life and action, as the text says in Can. sicut sancti, 15 dist.; and the frequent celebration of general councils is the principal cultivation of the Lord's field, which uproots the thorns and thistles of heresies, errors and schisms, corrects excesses, reforms what is deformed, and brings the vineyard of the Lord to a most abundant harvest of fruit: as is held in the Canon of the Council of Constance, in Canon frequens. For such a reformation is more maturely brought about in a general council, because very many are summoned there, and all come together into one, Can. Canones, §. Concilii vero, 15 dist.; hence that which is sought from many is more firmly regarded than that which comes from fewer, cap. prudentiam, in princ., de offic. deleg., and what is sought from many is more easily found, Can. sin., 20 dist. And judgement is more whole when it is confirmed by the opinion of many, 64 dist., Can. extra conscientiam, cap. per hoc, §. verum, vbi Domin., de haeret. in sexto. And for this reason, because what is done in a council is more firmly regarded, a general clause does not annul conciliar constitutions, but a special derogation is required, as Archidiaconus notes in cap. 1, de constitut. in sexto. Baldus in l. humanum, C. de legibus. And for this reason a bishop cannot dispense against a conciliar constitution, as is noted by the gloss in cap. cum dilecti, in verbo aetate, de elect. And in such a gathering of a council, which must by all means take place for the reformation of the universal Church, all come together, and it is necessary to confess this. The supreme Pontiff himself does not deny it, nor can he deny it, since he has bound himself to it by vow and oath, and for this reason he appointed the Council at Rome.

units.la: IV. Sed difficultatem facit, quod Concilium praevalere debeat, vel hoc Pisanum a Reverendissimis Cardinalibus ob negligentiam summi Pontificis prius institutum, vel illud quod a summo Pontifice nuissime indictum fuit: & ideo pro vera resolutione videndum est de duob. Primo, an indictio Concilii facta a Reverendissimis Cardinalibus iuridice facta fuerit. Secundo, an impugnari possit ex his, quae in bulla summi Pontificis continentur.
units.tr: IV. But the difficulty is this: which ought to prevail, either the Council of Pisa, first instituted by the most reverend Cardinals because of the negligence of the supreme Pontiff, or that which was most recently appointed by the supreme Pontiff? Therefore, for a true resolution, two things must be considered. First, whether the indiction of the Council made by the most reverend Cardinals was lawfully made. Second, whether it can be impugned on the basis of what is contained in the bull of the supreme Pontiff.

units.la: V. Circa primum conclusive concedam, ponendo conclusiones, quae latius in Consilio edito habentur. Unde considerandum est, quod licet congregatio Concilii generalis spectare regulariter ad summum Pontificem (can. 1. in sin. Can. 2. per totum. 17. distinct. & 4. distinct. in §. porro, & absque auctoritate Papae congregatum Concilium dicitur Conciliabulum, Can. multi, in princip. 17. distinct.) hoc procedit regulariter, prout expresse dicitur in dict. Can. 1. 17. distinct. & secundum regulam loquuntur iura supr. allegata cum similibus: Sed praedicta regula fallit in duobus casibus, primus est quando Papa ipse accusandus fit, quia tunc auctoritas eius non requiritur, ut decidit Bald. in cap. olim, in sin. de rescript. & notat Dominic. in cap. ad Apostolicam, in princip. in not. de rendic. in sexto. & ad hoc facit, quia licet in aliquo casu consensus alicuius requiratur, tamen si contra eum agatur talis consensus remittitur, ut de Praelato notatur, cap. edocti, de rescript. & per glossam 2. quaest. 7. in can. cum pastoris. & facit glossa magna in fine, in l. cum non solum. C. de bon. qua liber. & ideo tali casu, quando contra Papam agitur, Concilium est supra Papam, & illum iudicare potest, ut notat Archidiac. & Domin. in cap. in Dei favorem, de haret. in sexto. Abb. in cap. signif. de elect. in cap. proposuit. de concess. prabend. & in cap. fraternitatis, in princ. de haret. Secundus casus est, quando Papa est negligens in congregando Concilium, quia tunc Concilium a seipso congregari potest, ut concludit Anton. de Roscl. in tract. de potestate Papae, in charta 52. colum. 3. vbi in tali casu dicit, cautelam esse, quod Concilium pronuntiet, Papam nolentem Concilium congregare, vel illi auctoritatem impertiri, suspectum esse de haeresi; & loco Papae Concilium habebit auctoritatem; & idem concludit de Turrecrem. Cardinalis sancti Sixti, qui fuit acerrimus defensor Papae, & tamen itatenet in Summa de Ecclesia, in 3. lib. cap. 8. in colum. 4. vbi inquit, quod tali casu Cardinales habent potestatem congregandi concilium. & hoc idem tradit Cardin. in consil. 150. quaesitum saepe fuit. in 3 dubio. Abb. in cap. licet. colum. 3. de elect. & Archiep. Florent. in 3 parte eius summae, in tit. 23. cap. 2. §. 7. Unde cum in isto casu agatur de reformatione, quae etiam in capite fieri debet in facto proprio summi Pontificis auctoritas sua exspectari non debet, ut dictum est: Similiter cum appareat de manifesta Papae negligentia in convocando concilium, Reverendissimi Domini Cardinales absque eo concilium congregare potuerunt per supradicta: Nam per lapsum biennii infra quod Papa promisit congregare concilium a die suae assumptionis, constat de negligentia: quia ubi est appositum certum tempus ad probandum negligentiam alia monitio non requiritur, ut notat Bald. in l. 2. C. de sponsal. Petrus de Anchar. in consil. 64. pro clarus declaratione, in sin. Dominic. in cap. licet canon, §. 1. de elect. in sexto. & sic pater, quod duplici ex capite Cardinales potuerunt absque summo Pontifice concilium in isto casu iudicere, & de hoc non videtur dubitandum.
units.tr: V. On the first point I shall concede conclusively, setting out the conclusions which are held more fully in the Consilium published. Hence it must be considered that, although the convening of a general council regularly belongs to the supreme Pontiff (Can. 1, in fin.; Can. 2, per totum, 17 dist.; and 4 dist., in §. porro), and a council assembled without the authority of the Pope is called a conciliabulum, Can. multi, in princ., 17 dist., this holds as a rule, as is expressly said in the said Can. 1, 17 dist., and the laws cited above, with similar ones, speak according to the rule. But the aforesaid rule fails in two cases. The first is when the Pope himself is to be accused, because then his authority is not required, as Baldus decides in cap. olim, in fin., de rescript., and Dominicus notes in cap. ad Apostolicam, in princ., in not., de rendic., in sexto. And to this it pertains that, although in some case the consent of someone is required, yet if action is taken against him such consent is remitted, as is noted of a prelate in cap. edocti, de rescript., and by the gloss in 2 q. 7, in Can. cum pastoris. And the great gloss in fine, in l. cum non solum, C. de bonis quae liberis. And therefore in such a case, when action is taken against the Pope, the Council is above the Pope and can judge him, as Archidiaconus and Dominicus note in cap. in Dei favorem, de haeret., in sexto; Abbas in cap. significasti, de elect.; in cap. proposuit, de concess. praebend.; and in cap. fraternitatis, in princ., de haeret. The second case is when the Pope is negligent in convening the council, because then the council can be convened by itself, as Antonius de Roscl. concludes in his tract de potestate Papae, folio 52, column 3, where in such a case he says that it is a safeguard that the council should declare that the Pope, unwilling to convene the council or to grant authority to it, is suspected of heresy; and in place of the Pope the council will have authority. And the same is concluded by Turrecremata, Cardinal of San Sisto, who was a most fervent defender of the Pope, and yet holds this in Summa de Ecclesia, book 3, cap. 8, column 4, where he says that in such a case the Cardinals have the power to convene a council. And the same is taught by the Cardinal in consilium 150, "quaesitum saepe fuit," in 3rd doubt; by Abbas in cap. licet, column 3, de elect.; and by the Archbishop of Florence in the third part of his Summa, title 23, cap. 2, §. 7. Hence, since in this case the matter concerns reformation, which ought also to be carried out in the head, in an affair concerning the supreme Pontiff himself his authority ought not to be awaited, as has been said. Likewise, since the manifest negligence of the Pope in convening the council appears, the most reverend Lord Cardinals were able to convene the council without him, by the aforesaid means. For by the lapse of two years, within which the Pope promised to convene the council from the day of his assumption, negligence is established; because where a fixed time has been appointed for proving negligence, no other warning is required, as Baldus notes in l. 2, C. de sponsal., Petrus de Ancharano in consilium 64, pro clarus declaratione, in fin., and Dominicus in cap. licet canon, §. 1, de elect., in sexto. And thus it is clear that the Cardinals were able, on a double ground, to judge the council without the supreme Pontiff in this case, and there seems to be no doubt about this.

units.la: VI. Sed maximum dubium facit, quod licet in praedictis casibus congregatio concilii spectaret ad Cardinales, ut dictum est, videtur illis competere ut Collegio, & non ut singulis, ut Baldus inquit in dict. cap. olim. colum. penult. de rescript. & ibi dicit, quod maior pars Cardinalium requiritur. Ergo videtur, quod minor pars, prout in casu isto fuit, hoc facere non potuerit. Ad hoc, in quo tota difficultas consistere videtur, responderi potest, & diligenter aduertendum est, quia sicut in proposito Papa ipse excluditur, cum de facto eius proprio agatur, ut supra dictum est, ita pariter excludi videntur alii Cardinales, qui sunt apud ipsum Pontificem, quia quando caput suspectum est, etiam alii qui caput verisimiliter sequuntur, suspecti sunt, & de illis idem quod de capite iudicatur, ut notat Abb. post Vincent. & alios, in cap. 1. de iudic. Bald. in l. 1. colum. 1. C. si Rector provin. facit textus in cap. accedens, el 1. & quod ibi Abb. ut lite non contestata. Nam tales adhaerentes sunt summo Pontifici, & de adhaerentibus idem iudicatur quod de principali, cap. ad Apostolicam, de re iudic. in sexto. cap. 1. de postul. praelato. l. qua religiosis. vbi Angelus ff. de rei vindicat. Sicut ergo in tali congregatione concilii Papa excluditur, ita Cardinales omnes qui apud ipsum resident,
units.tr: VI. But the greatest doubt arises here. Although in the cases above the calling of a council belongs to the Cardinals, as has been said, it seems to belong to them as a College and not as individuals, as Baldus says in the cited chapter olim, penultimate column, de rescriptis, where he also says that the greater part of the Cardinals is required. Therefore it seems that the lesser part, as was the case here, could not do this. To this, in which the whole difficulty seems to lie, it can be replied, and it must be carefully noted, that just as in the present matter the Pope himself is excluded, since his own deed is in question, as was said above, so likewise the other Cardinals who are with the Pope himself seem to be excluded. For when the head is under suspicion, those who probably follow the head are also under suspicion, and what is judged of the head is judged of them too, as Abbas notes after Vincentius and others, in cap. 1 de iudiciis; Baldus, in l. 1, col. 1, C. si Rector provinciae; the text in cap. accedens, and the el. 1; and what Abbas says there, ut lite non contestata. For such adherents are attached to the supreme Pontiff, and what is judged of the principal is judged of the adherents, cap. ad Apostolicam, de re iudicata, in sexto; cap. 1 de postulando praelato; l. qua religiosis, where Angelus, ff. de rei vindicatione. Therefore, just as the Pope is excluded from such an assembly of a council, so all the Cardinals who reside with him

units.la: {5} ... {55} ... {60} ... {50} ... {40} ... {45} ... {25} ... {15} ... {10} residēt, excludi videntur, & potestas congregandi Concilium, quæ ad Cardinales in supra dictis casibus devoluitur: intelligitur de Cardinalibus, qui non adhærent summo Pontifici, quibus facultas videtur competere: quia totum ius Collegii in ipsis videtur residere, cum etiam in uno ius Collegii conservari possit, l. sicut. §. sin. ff. quod cuiusque Universit. & ideo unus solus qui remanet de Capitulo, eligere potest Prælatum, ut per gl. & Dd. in cap. gratum. de postul. prælat. & etiam in uno Cardinali ius Collegii residere potest, & ille solus Papam poterit eligere, ut notatur per gloss. vbi Abb. in Clem. ne Romani porro. in verbo omnes, de elect.
units.tr: {5} ... {55} ... {60} ... {50} ... {40} ... {45} ... {25} ... {15} ... {10} reside, seem to be excluded; and the power of convoking the council, which in the cases mentioned above devolves upon the Cardinals, is to be understood of those Cardinals who do not adhere to the supreme Pontiff, to whom that faculty seems to belong, because the whole right of the College seems to reside in them. For even in one person the right of a College can be preserved, l. sicut, §. sin., ff. quod cuiusque universitatis; and therefore the one sole survivor of a chapter can elect a prelate, as the gloss and the Doctors say, in cap. gratum, de postulando praelato; and also the right of the College can reside in one Cardinal, and he alone will be able to elect the Pope, as is noted by the gloss where Abbas, in Clem. ne Romani porro, under the word omnes, de electione.

units.la: VII. Secundò principaliter respondere potest, quòd prædicti reuerendiss. Cardinales, etiā vti particulares, duo vel tres, dictum Concilium indicere potuerunt: quia videmus & vbi agitur de interesse alicuius Ecclesiæ particularis, potestas agendi in primis incumbit Prælato, & si Prælatus negligens sit, ad Capitulū devoluitur, & Capitulo etiā negligente devoluitur ad particulares Canonicos Ecclesiæ, ut not. Abb. in c. cum olim. de restit. col. 4. vbi ad hoc allegat Innoc. in cap. dilecti. de maior. & obed. vbi etiā Abb. post Hostiens. & alios, & idem tenent Ant. de Butr. Cardin. & Imol. in d. cap. cum olim, & Lapus alleg. 1. debebatur in effectu, in princ. & de tali negligentia Prælati & Capituli constare dicitur, si quàm primum potuerunt, non sunt prosecuti iura Ecclesiæ, & alia monitio non requiritur, ut concludunt Ant. de Butr. Imol. & Abb. post Innoc. in d. c. cum olim. de testib. & ista ad casum nostrum bene applicari possunt, vbi agitur de interesse Ecclesiæ vniuersalis, & de maiori præiudicio, ideo cautius agendum est, cap. vbi periculum, de elect. in 6. cap. bona, el 1. de postul. prælat. Vnde concludendum videtur, quod reuerendiss. Cardinales, etiam vti particulares, agere & instare possunt pro interesse vniuersalis Ecclesiæ, de quo agitur. Et hoc confirmatur, quia propter scandalum quod imminet, Ecclesia vniuersalis opprimi videtur, quia si agatur de repellendo malo Prælato, dicitur defensio necessaria, ut Abb. dicit post Hostien. in 2. col. in cap. dilecti. de excep. quo casu particulares, etiam si periuri sint & excommunicati, admittuntur pro defensione necessaria Ecclesiæ, d. c. dilecti, vbi gloss. in verbo interlocuti. & per gloss. in cap. cum Ecclesia sicca, de exception. Nec obstat si dicatur quod de negligentia Prælati & Capituli constare non videtur, quia ad probandum negligentiam quæ in facto negatiuo consistit, monitio necessaria est, ut est dictum Innoc. in cap. excurpanda, de prabend. Doctores communiter illud sequuntur. Bald. in Auth. hoc amplius col. 4. Cod. de fideicom. Bald. & Imola in l. si mora. ff. sol. matr. cum similibus vt tradit Alexand. in l. ita stipulatus, col. 5. de ver. obl. quia ad hoc respondetur, quod illa doctrina non habet locū, vbi agitur de interesse Ecclesiæ, vt in terminis dicunt Anton. de Butr. Imola, & Abb. post alios, in dict. cap. cum olim, & Lapus in allegat. praealleg. & dictum Innocentii videtur procedere, put loquitur, quando agitur quod quis incurrat aliquam poenam extrinsecam, puta vt priuetur beneficio, propter non residentiam, secus vbi agitur de negligentia simplici, quæ non punitur, prout loquuntur Doctores in dict. cap. cum olim, & ita Felinus dicit cap. si autem col. 4. de restit. Secundò responderi potest quod in isto casu agitur de facto scandaloso & notorio, quo in facto notorio non est monitio necessaria, vt per gloss. in Cle. quia contingit, in verbo negligentia, de religios. dom. facit text. in cap. Romana §. notoria de Censibus in 6. Et de his in Consilio prius dictum fuit: Et ita breuiter primum dubium absolutum sit.
units.tr: VII. Secondly, and principally, it can be answered that the aforesaid most reverend Cardinals, even acting as individuals, two or three of them, were able to call the said Council. For we see that where the interest of some particular Church is at stake, the power of acting in the first instance rests with the prelate, and if the prelate is negligent, it devolves upon the chapter; and if the chapter too is negligent, it devolves upon the individual canons of the church, as Abbas notes, in cap. cum olim, de restitutione, col. 4, where for this he cites Innocent, in cap. dilecti, de maioritate et obedientia, where also Abbas after Hostiensis and others; and Antonius de Butrio, the Cardinal, and Imola hold the same, in the said cap. cum olim; and Lapus, cited in the allegatio "1. debebatur in effectu," at the beginning. And such negligence of the prelate and chapter is said to be established if, as soon as they were able, they did not pursue the rights of the Church; and no other warning is required, as Antonius de Butrio, Imola and Abbas after Innocent conclude, in the said c. cum olim, de testibus. And these things can well be applied to our case, where the interest of the universal Church is at stake, and a greater prejudice, and therefore one must act with more caution, cap. ubi periculum, de electione, in sexto; cap. bona, el. 1, de postulando praelato. Whence it seems to be concluded that the most reverend Cardinals, even acting as individuals, can act and press on behalf of the interest of the universal Church, which is at issue. And this is confirmed, because on account of the scandal that threatens, the universal Church seems to be oppressed; for if it is a matter of repelling a bad prelate, a defence is called necessary, as Abbas says after Hostiensis, in the second column, in cap. dilecti, de exceptionibus. In which case individuals, even if they are perjured and excommunicated, are admitted for the necessary defence of the Church, d. c. dilecti, where the gloss, under the word interlocuti; and by the gloss in cap. cum Ecclesia sicca, de exceptionibus. Nor does it stand in the way if it is said that the negligence of the prelate and chapter does not seem to be established, because to prove a negligence which consists in a negative fact, a warning is necessary, as Innocent said in cap. excurrendum, de praebendis, and the Doctors commonly follow that. Baldus, in Auth. hoc amplius, col. 4, Cod. de fideicommissis; Baldus and Imola, in l. si mora, ff. soluto matrimonio, with similar passages, as Alexander sets out in l. ita stipulatus, col. 5, de verborum obligationibus. For to this it is answered that that doctrine does not apply where the interest of the Church is at stake, as Antonius de Butrio, Imola and Abbas after others say in terms, in the said cap. cum olim, and Lapus in the aforesaid allegatio. And Innocent's statement seems to hold when it speaks of a case where someone would incur some external penalty, for instance be deprived of a benefice on account of non-residence; otherwise where simple negligence is at issue, which is not punished, as the Doctors speak in the said cap. cum olim; and so Felinus says in cap. si autem, col. 4, de restitutione. Secondly, it can be answered that in this case the matter concerns a scandalous and notorious fact, and in a notorious fact no warning is necessary, as in the gloss in Clem. quia contingit, under the word negligentia, de religiosis domibus. The text in cap. Romana, §. notoria, de censibus, in sexto, supports this. And concerning these things it was said earlier in the Consilium; and so the first doubt is briefly resolved.

units.la: VIII. Venio ad secundum, videlicet ad ea quæ in bulla summi Pontificis dicuntur, quibus omnibus & singulis iuridicè & breuiter sic responderi potest. Primò enim reuerendissimis Dominis Cardinalibus obiicitur, quòd sine legitima causa à capite recedentes se Papam contulerunt.
units.tr: VIII. I come to the second point, namely to those things which are said in the Bull of the supreme Pontiff, to all and each of which a legal and brief answer can be given. First, it is objected to the most reverend Lord Cardinals that, withdrawing from the head without lawful cause, they betook themselves to the Pope.

units.la: IV. Sed respondetur, quòd id quidem consultò & iustissima ratione factum fuit: cum n. summus Pontifex charitatis officio secundum regulam Euangelii, cui et ipse subiicitur, ab eis sæpius monitus & requisitus fuisset, & non audiuerit, suamq; promissione cum voto & iuramento factam adimplere negligeret: licuit ipsis procurantibus reformationē vniuersalis Ecclesiæ, prout tali casu eorum officiū postulabat, in salutato hospite recedere, cū absq; periculo carceris & vitæ licentia peti non potuisset, & illam obtineri non posse illis satis constaret. De prædicta n. regula Euangelii, habetur in c. nouit. de iud. in can. si peccauerit 2. q. 1. & illam quilibet obseruare tenetur ex iniuncto, §. sin. de hæres. & illi et Papa subiicitur, 25. q. 1. in Can sunt quidam: & in terminis de Concilio, notat Abb. in c. propositū, col. 3. de concess. prabend. & Papa negligente congregare Concilium, ad reuerendissimos Cardinales pertinet congregatio Concilii, vt Cardin. tradit in Concilio 150. quæsitum sæpe fuit, in terto dubio. Abb. in c. licet, col. 3. de elect. & quia cum agendum sit contra ipsum summum Pontificem, non illi, sed Cardinalibus conuocatio Concilii videtur competere, vt Bald. concludit, in c. olim in sin. de rescript. & Doctor. in c. ad Apostolicam, in princ. not. de restit. in 6. & ipsis reuerendissimis Cardinalibus videtur competere vti Collegio, & et in ipsis particularib. vt in Consilio deductū & ostensum fuit. Et reuerendissimos Cardinales qui recesserunt, exemplū aliorū reuerendissimorū Cardinalium admonebat, qui hac de causa transgressionis voti & iuramenti à Gregorio XII. qui Lucæ morabatur, discesserunt, & Pisas se contulerunt, vt refert Anton. de But. in c. 1. col. 2. de const. & certè nulla ratio suadet quod summus Pontifex ex hoc tñ debeat commoueri: cùm ipse dum esset in minoribus sæpius ob minores & longè leuiores causas à plurib. summis Pontificib. absq; licentia recesserit, & reuocatus sub grauissimis censuris redire noluerit. Vnde incongruū est, quod in hoc reuerendissimi Domini Cardinales ab eo arguantur ; q. 7. in c. iudicet: Et legitur quod nihil obiicere debet Catilina Cethego, vt notatur per gloss. perillum text. in l. quoniam, Cod. de haer. facit text. in lege in arenam, Codice de inofficioso testam. cum similibus.
units.tr: IV. But it is answered that this was indeed done deliberately and for a most just reason: since the supreme Pontiff, by the duty of charity according to the rule of the Gospel, to which he himself is also subject, had been often admonished and requested by them, and did not listen, and neglected to fulfil his promise made with a vow and oath; it was permitted to them, working for the reform of the universal Church, as their office in such a case required, to withdraw from the host who had been greeted, since leave could not be sought without danger of imprisonment and life, and it was sufficiently clear to them that it could not be obtained. For the aforesaid rule of the Gospel is found in cap. nouit, de iudiciis; in can. si peccauerit, 2 q. 1; and everyone is bound to observe it by the injunction, §. sin., de haereticis; and the Pope himself is subject to it, 25 q. 1, in can. sunt quidam. And in terms concerning a Council, Abbas notes in c. propositum, col. 3, de concessione praebendae; and when the Pope is negligent in calling a Council, the convocation of the Council pertains to the most reverend Cardinals, as the Cardinal teaches in the Council, and it was often asked, in the third doubt, 150. Abbas, in c. licet, col. 3, de electione. And since the action must be taken against the supreme Pontiff himself, the convocation of the Council seems to belong not to him but to the Cardinals, as Baldus concludes, in c. olim, at the end, de rescriptis; and the Doctors, in c. ad Apostolicam, at the beginning, note, de restitutione in sexto; and it seems to belong to the most reverend Cardinals themselves as a College, and also to them as individuals, as was deduced and shown in the Consilium. And the most reverend Cardinals who withdrew were admonished by the example of other most reverend Cardinals, who for this reason of breaking their vow and oath departed from Gregory XII, who was staying at Lucca, and betook themselves to Pisa, as Antonius de Butrio reports, in c. 1, col. 2, de constitutionibus. And certainly no reason suggests that the supreme Pontiff ought on this account to be moved; since he himself, while still in minor positions, often withdrew without leave, for lesser and far lighter reasons, to several supreme Pontiffs, and when recalled under the gravest censures refused to return. Hence it is unseemly that the most reverend Lord Cardinals should be accused by him in this matter, q. 7, in c. iudicet. And it is read that Catiline ought to object nothing to Cethegus, as is noted by the gloss on that text in l. quoniam, Cod. de haeredibus; the text in l. in arenam, Codice de inofficioso testamento, supports this, with similar passages.

units.la: X. Nec, vt in secundo dicitur, argui & reprehendi reuerendissimi Domini Cardinales debent q; præsidio armatorum vsi fuerint, quia licet armorum vsus, pςrtim Ecclesiasticis, prohibitus sit, & vt Ambrosius inquit, arma Clericorum sint lacrymæ, Can. Conuenior, 23. q 8. & 36 dist. tam sin. tamen ad suam defensionem Clerici familiares armatos suscipere non prohibentur, cum leges omnes omniaq; iura vim vi repellere cuncti{que} se defendere permittat, c. dilectio, de pœn. dist. sent. excom. in 6. l. sciendum, §. qui cum aliter ff. ad l. Aquil. adeo q; etiam Cardinalem p; de defensione interficere permissum sit, vt notat Angelus in l. vt vim. ff. de iust. & iure, & monacho contra Abbatem in eum sæuientem armata manu resistere licet, vt Card. dicit in Cle. 1. in ver. prafata, de statu monach. & de Paulo legitur qui petijt milites à Prætore quorum præsidio illæsus seruaretur. 3. q 3. can. ex diff. rentia, in fine, & licitè Cardinales aufugiebant per ea quæ habetur 7. q 1. can. sicut aris, & can. ad uerfitas, eadem 7. q 1. Nec minus quoq; reuerendissimis Cardinalibus obstare videtur, quod falsò quidem tertiò asseritur illos voluisse ad summum Pontificem redire & desertionis suæ veniam petijsse. Quo enim spiritu de regressu ad eum cogitare debuerunt, cuius minis territi adniodum erant apud eum residentes, plurimumq; lætarentur è manibus eius euasisse, & Papiam saluos applicuisse, maximas Deo gratias agerent? Et licet forte nonnulli à seipsis pro concordia & compositione verba fecissent (eis etiam non prohibentibus id ex industria ab ipsis toleratum fuit) ne summus Pontifex cómotus in eos sæuiret: qa vt Hieronymus testatur, etiam homines iusti p; tempore aliqua simulare possunt, ob suam & suorum salutem, vt inquit text. in can. vtile, 22. q 2. facit text. in c. afferte, de præsump. in Can. si quelibet culpa. 22. q. 2.
units.tr: X. Nor, as is said in the second point, ought the most reverend Lords Cardinals to be accused and reproached because they made use of an armed guard. Although the use of arms is forbidden, especially to churchmen, and as Ambrose says, the arms of clergy are tears, Can. Conuenior, 23. q 8. and 36 dist. tam sin. nevertheless clergy are not forbidden to take armed household retainers for their own defence, since all laws and all rights allow everyone to repel force with force and to defend himself, c. dilectio, de pœn. dist. sent. excom. in 6. l. sciendum, §. qui cum aliter ff. ad l. Aquil. so much so that it has even been permitted for a Cardinal to kill someone in self-defence, as Angelus notes in l. vt vim. ff. de iust. & iure, and a monk may lawfully resist by armed force an abbot who rages against him, as the Cardinal says in Cle. 1. in ver. prafata, de statu monach. It is also read of Paul that he asked the praetor for soldiers, by whose protection he might be kept unharmed, 3. q 3. can. ex diff. rentia, in fine, and Cardinals fled lawfully, according to what is found in 7. q 1. can. sicut aris, & can. ad uerfitas, eadem 7. q 1. Nor does it seem to count any less against the most reverend Cardinals that it is falsely asserted, thirdly, that they wished to return to the supreme Pontiff and sought pardon for their desertion. For with what spirit ought they to have thought of returning to him, they who, terrified by his threats while they were residing with him, were very much afraid, and who rejoiced greatly at having escaped from his hands and, having reached Pavia safe, gave the greatest thanks to God? And although perhaps some of them, on their own initiative, spoke about agreement and reconciliation (and this was tolerated on purpose by them, the others not forbidding it), so that the supreme Pontiff, moved, would not rage against them: because, as Jerome testifies, even just men can at times feign for the sake of their own and their friends' safety, as the text says in can. vtile, 22. q 2. The text in c. afferte, de præsump. applies, and the text in Can. si quelibet culpa. 22. q. 2.

units.la: XI. Ad illud vero q; reuerendissimis Dominis Cardinalib. maximo animo impetu & exaggeritatis verbis de falsitate opponitur, ex eo q; nonnulli (ex his quorum nomine simul cum alijs Concilium Pisis indictu fuit) negant se vnq; in tali re consensisse. Respodetur q; hoc negare nullomodo possunt, qa per litteras eorum consensum præstiterunt, quib. literis et priuatis mandatum probatur, Clem. 1. de Procur. lib. 1. §. 1. ff. de Procur. & hoc q; plures reuerendissimi Cardinales attestant, quibus potius credendum est, quàm vni qui solus contradicit, vt sumo Pontifici reconcilietur, & eius gratia aucupetur, cap. in nostra de testib. c. licet causam, de probat. l. 3. §. 1. ff. de testib. & certè de tali falsitate nullo modo præsumendum videtur, cùm ille vel illi ex abundanti inscripti fuerint, & absque illis Concilium Pisis indici potuisset, vt in Consilio deducitur, quò casu vbi agit de modico interesse falsitas nunq; præsumitur, c. accedens, de crimine falsi, & cùm requisitio facta fuerit omni meliori modo quo fieri potuit, valet conuocatio ex personis illorum qui soli habebant potestatem: qa clausula illa omni meliori modo, operatur q; actus valeat ex isto capite q; potuit fieri, vt notat Bart. & Imola. in l. cum pater, §. filius matrem de l. 2. & Cardinal. & Imola. in c. ex literis de officio deleg. & notat. Bald. in l. quotiens, col. sin. Cod. de bared. inst. Paulus de Castro in Consilio 365. super puncto, col. pen. Fulg. in Consilio 90. in q. col. 2. cum similib. quæ nota sunt.
units.tr: XI. As for the objection, made with great vehemence and exaggerated words against the most reverend Lords Cardinals as false, that some of those in whose name the Council of Pisa was summoned together with others deny that they ever consented to such a matter: the answer is that they can by no means deny this, because through their letters they gave their consent, and by private letters a mandate is proved, Clem. 1. de Procur. lib. 1. §. 1. ff. de Procur. and because several most reverend Cardinals attest to it. They are to be believed rather than the one man who alone contradicts, in order to be reconciled to the supreme Pontiff and to win his favour, cap. in nostra de testib. c. licet causam, de probat. l. 3. §. 1. ff. de testib. And certainly such falsehood seems in no way to be presumed, since that person or those persons were named superabundantly, and the Council of Pisa could have been summoned without them, as is argued in the Consilium; in which case, where the matter concerns a slight interest, falsehood is never presumed, c. accedens, de crimine falsi. And when the summons has been made in the best possible way, the convocation is valid through the persons of those alone who had the power: because that clause "in the best possible way" has the effect that the act is valid on the ground that it could have been done, as Bartolus and Imola note in l. cum pater, §. filius matrem de l. 2. and Cardinal and Imola in c. ex literis de officio deleg. and Baldus notes in l. quotiens, col. sin. Cod. de bared. inst. Paulus de Castro in Consilio 365. super puncto, col. pen. Fulgosius in Consilio 90. in q. col. 2. and similar authorities, which are well known.

units.la: XII. Quod autem ad excusandū suam negligentiam sumus Pontifex longo verborū apparatu conatur ostendere q; cū esset in minoribus omni studio & diligentia procuravit vt generale Concilium celebraretur, & status Rom. Ecclesiæ in melius reformaretur: Responsio clara videt, nam licet sumo Pontifici credendum videatur vbi de facto eius attestatur, Clem. 1. de probat. hoc tamen non procedit in his, in quib. Papa liberam nō habet potestatem videlicet in præiudicium tertij, vt in casu isto videtur, & ita Abb. concludit in d. Cle. 1. infi & in c. cum nobis de testib. idem dicit Petrus de Anch. in Consil. 399. præmitto, infi. col. Paul. de Castr. in Consil. 156. riso & examinato puncto, col. fi. Et ideo prædictis verbis sumi Pontificis licet ornatissimis, nulla fides adhiberi debet, quia vt Augustin testatur in Can. sedulo 38. dist. melius est veriores quàm distortiores aud. re sermones, sicut ma è quis debet prudentiores quam formosiores habere amicos. Et certè nouum est, & hactenus inauditum fuit, sanctitatem suam, dum Cardinalatus officio fungeretur, operam præstitisse vt Concilium generale conuocaretur, & si tanto Concilij desiderio ipse summus Pontifex, vt asserit, concitatus fuisset, cur ad Pontificatum assumptus suum desiderium adimplere neglexit, et nulla habita ratione voti & iuramenti? Et fragilis & leuissima eius excusatio videtur, q; ex bellorū motib. causatur, quia et tempore assumptionis eius, superant huiusmodi bellorum impedimenta, vt et ipse confitetur: & tamen se celebraturum Concilium j. biennium cum voto & iuramento promisit, ideo propter hoc nō excusatur, vt notat Cyn. in l. ex conducto §. 1. ff. de loca. Bal. de pace Const. in verbo vassalli. el. 2. & in l. fi ea col pe. nult. Codice de vsur. Alex. in l. interdum §. quo ex naufragio, in fi. de acq poss ff. Et certè hac de causa potius Concilium accelerari debuisset cùm illud salutare sit remedium, vt bellis imminentibus consulatur: vt etiam ipse summus Pontifex in sua bulla attestatur, ex quo in tali excusatione repugnantia & manifesta contrarietas deprehenditur, quæ admitti non debet l. 1. Cod. de furtis. cap. fi. licitudinem de Appel. Et dum successiue allegatur quod à solis Romanis Pontificibus Concilia generalia congregari & indici debent, non negamus hoc esse verum regulariter vt canones dicūt: sed summo Pontifice, cui in primis talis cura incumbit, negligente, ad reuerendissimos Dominos Cardinales Pontifici non adhærentes potestas, ista defertur, vt supra dictum est. Et cùm in casu isto negligentia summi Pontificis, præsertim ex decursu temporis manifesta appareat reuerendissimi Domini Cardinales optimo iure Concilium Pisis indixerunt, & cùm agatur de euidenti & maximo interesse vniuersalis Ecclesiæ, hoc absq; alia monitione facere potuerūt, vt s. in Consilio dictū fuit, & hoc fauore Ecclesiæ permissū videt vt nauiculæ Pet. fluctuati succurrat hoc n. fauore fautore Ecclesiæ, sæpe numero à regulis iuris communis recedi itur, l. sum persone ff. de relig. facit text in l. sin. Cod. de sacrosanctis Ecclesiis, facit text in can. indignum, 18. dist. & in c. fidulo, & quod de baptismo dicitur in Can. retulerunt, de consec. dist. 4. Non obstat quod sanctitas Papæ velit & semper possit de æquitate canonica moram purgare, ut notat Bald. in l. qui crimen in 6. quæst. Cod. de accusa. Alexan. in l. si insulam col. 2. de verborum obligat. quia respondetur illud habere locum ad evitandum pœnam extrinsecam, quæ ab æquitate canonica est aliena, prout loquitur text. qui al legatur in cap. suant de pœnis; secus si agatur simpliciter de facultate faciendi actum quæ motoso competat, quia si in alium translata sit mora purgari non potest, ut notat Imola in dicta l. in sulam, quem Alexand. ibi refert col. 18. vers. 8. principaliter fallit. Et licet Alexan. dubitare videatur, tamen pro dicto Imo-la facit, & quod notat Bart. per illum text. in l. liberto, §. Lucius ff. de annu. leg. Bald. in lex. dictam. Cod. de condit. obtausam. Et hoc maxime videtur habere locum in isto casu in quo res non est integra, ideo videtur quod mora purgari non possit. Præterea nulla ratio purgationis morae habere debet ex eo quod de facto summi Pontificis agenda merit, in quo eius auctoritas minime requiritur, ut dictum est. Unde cum in tali causa facultas congregandi Concilium ad summum Pontificem non pertinet, purgatio morae in eo considerari non potest. Nec obstat quod dicitur de Concilio Constantiensi, quod contra Ioan. XXIII. eo auctore congregatum fuit, licet eius causa agi retur: quia hoc minime verum est, ut constat ex ipso Concilio Constantiensi, ubi in principio dicitur quod congregatio illius Concilij facta fuit ut perficerentur quæ ab Alexandro Quinto in Concilio Pisano inchoata fuerant, & ita patet quod à principio illud Concilium congregatum non fuit contra Ioannem XXIII; bene verum est quod postea Concilium insurrexit contra ipsum Ioannem XXIII. & voluit villicationis eius rationes perscrutari, & tunc ipse nedum auctoritatem non interposuit, sed aufugit, & propter fugam & contumaciam privatus fuit: Et dato quod ipse etiam in facto proprio auctoritatem interposuisset, ex abundanti illud fecisset, & non sequitur quod esset necessaria, & quod absque eo Concilium congregari non potuisset. Præterea, esto quod mora purgari à summo Pontifice potuisset: ex oblatione Concilij facta in loco notorie non tuto mora purgari non videtur, quia talis oblatio ad purgandam moram in loco congruo fieri debet, l. si soluturus ff. de sol. notatur in l. quæ decen. in primupo eodem titulo in l. accep-tam, ubi Bart. Cod. de ersur. in l. illud, ubi gloss. ff. de periculo & commod. rei vend. Nihil etiam obstare videntur quæ de breuitate temporis & inhabilitate loci ciuitatis Pisarum opponuntur, quia terminus arbitrarius est, cum à iure determinatus non repetiatur, ar. l. 4. ff. de iure delib. & etiam si ipsfixus fuisset propter periculum quod imminet, restringi ac moderari potuisset, qui regulariter quilibet terminus ex causa moderari potest. ut notat Bart. in l. 2. ff. de Jure inde. non in cap. cum sit Roma-na, de app. ubi Abb. cum similib. ut ibi dixi, in termino enim constituto providere poterit, ut futuris & imminentibus malis occurratur, in quibus periculum est in mora, deinde terminus prorogari poterit, prout Concilio videbitur: & alias cum minori dilatione, tempore Gregorij XII. Concilium Pisis congregatum fuit, & in hoc certe summus Pontifex reuerendissimos dominos Cardinales arguere non debet, cum ipse terminum Concilij, qui ut ab eo asseritur non minus anno à sanctissimis patribus constituebatur, ad nouem menses restrinxerit. Similiter ad illud quod de loci incommoditate allegatur, Responderi potest, quod cum alias Concilium ibi congregatum fuerit, ita & nunc pariter congregari potest, licet hactenus bello ciuitas Pisarum obsessa, à duobus annis citra nihil malihabuit, etiam fere restaurata & in pristinum statum re-stituta videtur, & omnia quæ ad victum necessaria sunt facile præparari possunt, propter agri fertilitatem. & quia mari propinqua est. Accedit etiam ciuitas Lucæ quæ illi vicina est, maxime adiumento illi esse poterit, & si Patribus Concilij videbitur, locus mutari poterit, prout in dictione Concilij dicitur, & sic patet leuissimam esse huiusmodi loci & temporis excusationem.
units.tr: XII. As for excusing his negligence, the Pontiff tries with a long display of words to show that, while he was still a minor cardinal, he took every care to have a general Council convened and the state of the Roman Church reformed for the better. The clear answer is this. Although the Supreme Pontiff's word is to be believed where he attests to a fact (Clem. 1, de probat.), this does not hold in matters where the Pope does not have free power, namely to the prejudice of a third party, as seems to be the case here. Abbas concludes this way in the said Clem. 1, below, and in c. cum nobis, de testib. Peter of Anchora says the same in Consil. 399, præmitto, below, col. Paul of Castro in Consil. 156, riso & examinato puncto, col. fin. Therefore, however elegant the Supreme Pontiff's words, no credit should be given to them, because, as Augustine testifies in Can. sedulo, 38 dist.: "It is better to have truer than more distorted words, just as a man ought to have wiser rather than more handsome friends." And certainly it is something new and hitherto unheard of that his holiness, while holding the office of Cardinal, lent his effort to have a general Council convened; and if the Supreme Pontiff himself was stirred by such a desire for a Council, as he asserts, why, once raised to the Papacy, did he neglect to fulfil his desire, with no regard for his vow and oath? His excuse seems feeble and very flimsy, that it is grounded on the movements of wars, since at the time of his election those hindrances of wars were overcome, as he himself confesses; yet he promised with a vow and oath that he would hold the Council within two years. For this reason he is not excused, as Cynus notes in l. ex conducto §. 1, ff. de loca; Bald. de pace Const. in the word vassalli, el. 2, and in l. fi, ea col. pe. nult., Codice de usur.; Alex. in l. interdum §. quo ex naufragio, in fin., de acq. poss. ff. And certainly for this reason the Council ought rather to have been hastened, since it is a salutary remedy for providing against impending wars, as the Supreme Pontiff himself attests in his bull. From this, a contradiction and manifest inconsistency is detected in such an excuse, which ought not to be admitted (l. 1, Cod. de furtis; cap. fin., licitudinem, de Appel.). And where it is argued in turn that general Councils must be gathered and summoned only by the Roman Pontiffs, we do not deny that this is true as a rule, as the canons say; but when the Supreme Pontiff, to whom this care chiefly belongs, is negligent, this power passes to the most reverend Lord Cardinals who do not adhere to the Pontiff, as was said above. And since in this case the negligence of the Supreme Pontiff appears manifest, especially from the lapse of time, the most reverend Lord Cardinals rightly summoned the Council at Pisa; and since it concerns the evident and very great interest of the universal Church, they could do this without any further warning, as was said above in the Consilium; and this seems to have been permitted out of favour to the Church, so that it may succour the little boat of Peter as it tosses on the waves; for out of this favour to the Church, one often departs from the rules of common law (l. sum personae, ff. de relig.; text in l. sin., Cod. de sacrosanctis Ecclesiis; text in can. indignum, 18 dist.; and in c. fidulo; and what is said of baptism in Can. retulerunt, de consec. dist. 4). It is no objection that the Holiness of the Pope wishes, and can always, to remove delay by canonical equity, as Bald. notes in l. qui crimen, in 6 quaest., Cod. de accusa.; Alexander in l. si insulam, col. 2, de verborum obligat. For the reply is that this has place for avoiding an external penalty, which is alien to canonical equity, as the text speaks which is read in c. suant, de poenis; otherwise, if it is simply a question of the power of doing an act which belongs to the one who is in default, delay cannot be purged if it has been transferred to another, as Imola notes in the said l. insulam, which Alexander there cites in col. 18, verse 8, "principaliter fallit". And although Alexander seems to doubt, nevertheless Imola's view is supported, and by what Bart. notes through that text in l. liberto, §. Lucius, ff. de annu. leg.; Bald. in the said lex, Cod. de condit. obtausam. And this seems especially to have place in this case, in which the matter is not whole, and therefore it seems that delay cannot be purged. Moreover, no reason for purging delay ought to arise from the fact that what is to be done concerns the deed of the Supreme Pontiff, in which his authority is in no way required, as has been said. Wherefore, since in such a cause the power of convening a Council does not pertain to the Supreme Pontiff, purging of delay cannot be considered in him. Nor is there any force in what is said about the Council of Constance, that it was convened against John XXIII, with him as its author, although the case was being pursued against him; for this is by no means true, as is clear from the Council of Constance itself, where at the beginning it is said that the gathering of that Council was made so that those things might be completed which had been begun by Alexander V at the Council of Pisa; and so it is plain that from the beginning that Council was not convened against John XXIII. It is indeed true that afterwards the Council rose up against John XXIII himself, and wished to scrutinise the reckoning of his stewardship; and then he not only did not interpose his authority, but fled, and because of his flight and contumacy he was deprived. And even if he had interposed his authority in his own affair, he would have done so superfluously, and it does not follow that it was necessary, or that without it the Council could not have been convened. Moreover, even if delay could have been purged by the Supreme Pontiff, delay does not seem to be purged by an offer of a Council made in a place notoriously unsafe, because such an offer ought to be made in a suitable place for purging delay (l. si soluturus, ff. de sol.; noted in l. quae decen., in principio, same title; in l. acceptam, where Bart. [notes]; Cod. de usur., in l. illud, where the gloss [notes]; ff. de periculo & commod. rei vend.). Nor do the objections about the brevity of the time and the unsuitability of the place of the city of Pisa seem to have force, because the term is arbitrary, since it is not fixed by law, ar. l. 4, ff. de iure delib.; and even if it had been fixed on account of the impending danger, it could have been restricted and moderated, since as a rule any term may be moderated for cause, as Bart. notes in l. 2, ff. de iure inde., not in c. cum sit Romana, de app., where Abbas with similar [authorities] (as I there said) notes. For within a fixed term provision can be made so that future and impending evils may be met, in which there is danger in delay; then the term can be prolonged as the Council thinks fit; and otherwise, with less delay, in the time of Gregory XII a Council was convened at Pisa. And in this matter the Supreme Pontiff certainly ought not to accuse the most reverend Lord Cardinals, since he himself reduced the term of the Council, which, as he alleges, had been fixed by the most holy Fathers at not less than a year, to nine months. Similarly, to what is alleged about the inconvenience of the place, it may be answered that since a Council was convened there at other times, so it can equally be convened now; although until now the city of Pisa, besieged in war, has suffered nothing bad for two years, and it seems almost restored and brought back to its former state, and all things necessary for sustenance can easily be prepared, on account of the fertility of the land and because it is near the sea. The city of Lucca, which is near it, will also be able to be of great help; and if it seems good to the Fathers of the Council, the place can be changed, as is said in the summons to the Council; and so it is plain that such an excuse of place and time is most flimsy.

units.tr: 4.
